Title: Thermal history and stress redistributions achieving reduced crack susceptibility in laser-directed energy-deposited Al2O3/GAP/ZrO2 eutectic ceramics by circular oscillation scanning
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Crack control remains a major challenge in laser-directed energy deposition (LDED) of oxide eutectic ceramics because of their intrinsic brittleness and thermal-stress accumulation. In this work, emissivity-calibrated in-situ infrared thermometry and thermo-mechanical simulation were used to reveal how circular oscillation scanning (COS) reduces the crack susceptibility of LDED Al2O3/GAP/ZrO2 eutectic ceramics. Compared with linear reciprocating scanning, COS produced a wider high-temperature zone, stronger interlayer reheating, and milder recooling. At the representative mid-height location, the average cooling rate from peak temperature to melting point decreased from 330.91 to 173.82 °C/s, while the reheating-induced temperature rise increased from 167.38 to 1076.03 °C. Stress analysis showed that COS reduced crack susceptibility mainly by weakening the continuous bottom-centered tensile-stress band and localizing higher-stress regions near the side areas, rather than by simply lowering the local stress peak. This stress redistribution was consistent with the observed transition from bottom-initiated vertical cracking to side-localized, laterally limited cracking. The COS parameter study further revealed a trade-off between thermal coverage and tensile-stress concentration. These findings provide guidance for scan-path design and crack control in LDED of oxide eutectic ceramics. © 2026

Title: A coupled oxidation-damage model for cross-layer ablation failure in HfC/SiC bilayer coatings on C/C composites
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: HfC/SiC bilayer coatings provide exceptional ultra-high-temperature ablation protection for Carbon/Carbon composites. However, the complex cross-layer chemo-mechanical interactions, specifically between the oxidation-induced cracking of the HfC outer layer and the active oxidation of the SiC inner layer, remain poorly understood. In this work, a comprehensive oxidation-damage coupling ablation model is proposed based on continuum damage mechanics and chemical reaction kinetics. Oxyacetylene ablation experiments were conducted to characterize the ablation depths and layer-specific damage evolution. To handle the severe material discontinuity at the bilayer interface, an interfacial node-decoupling method is implemented, ensuring multiphysics continuity while preserving the independent chemical kinetics. The proposed model is successfully validated against experimental results with an average relative error of 15.7%. The numerical results clarify a mutually exacerbating failure mechanism: Stress-driven HfC cracking creates preferential oxygen pathways that accelerate localized SiC depletion, while the resulting material loss undermines the mechanical support of the overlying HfC layer. Furthermore, parametric analysis uncovers a non-monotonic evolution of the anti-ablation performance when varying the SiC layer thickness (10–30 μm). A thicker SiC layer imposes a more severe mechanical constraint that prematurely drives outer-layer microcracking, whereas it provides a superior secondary oxygen barrier during extended ablation. This chemo-mechanical trade-off offers crucial guidelines for the structural optimization of advanced multilayer anti-ablation coatings. © 2026

Title: Determining the robust drivers of CO2 emissions in Africa: Machine learning and panel econometric evidence on the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis
Abstract: One of the primary greenhouse gases linked to global warming is carbon dioxide. This study investigates the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions in 29 African countries over the period 1990–2023 using a two-stage machine learning and econometric framework. In the first stage, Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms are employed to identify the most important drivers of carbon dioxide emissions. The results indicate that Random Forests provide the highest predictive performance among the machine learning models. In the second stage, the variables identified by the machine learning analysis are incorporated into second-generation panel estimators that account for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity. Specifically, long-run and short-run relationships are examined using the Common Correlated Effects Autoregressive Distributed Lag estimator, while Augmented Mean Group, Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimators, and Fixed Effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors are employed as robustness checks. The findings reveal that oil consumption is positively associated with carbon dioxide emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption is negatively associated with carbon dioxide emissions. The results provide limited but supportive evidence for the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis, with income and income-squared terms exhibiting the expected signs and the estimated turning point falling within the observed income range. Robustness analyses based on oil-exporting and non-oil-exporting country groups, as well as an alternative carbon-intensity measure, confirm the central role of fossil fuel dependence and renewable energy adoption in shaping environmental outcomes across Africa. These findings highlight the importance of accelerating renewable energy deployment, reducing reliance on fossil fuels, improving energy efficiency, and promoting sustainable development strategies to achieve long-term environmental sustainability in African economies. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Zuo H.; Liu L.; Luo R.; Hua S.; Zhang X.-B.; Zhang L.
Title: The perceived legitimacy of costly punishment in the evolution of cooperation under private reputation
Abstract: Indirect reciprocity promotes cooperation by allowing reputation to serve as a social currency for future benefits. However, the role of costly punishment under private reputation remains less understood. Under private reputation, independent assessments may lead observers and punishers to hold different views about the same recipient. This raises the question of how an observer evaluates punishment when the punished recipient appears to have a good reputation. We introduce the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment into a private-reputation model of indirect reciprocity. We first analyze the core dynamics among unconditional cooperators, unconditional defectors, and discriminating punishers, and then test whether the cooperative state is stable against the full set of action-rule mutants, including antisocial punishers. Our results show that costly punishment promotes cooperation only when its perceived legitimacy lies within an appropriate range. In this regime, discriminating punishers and unconditional cooperators can coexist stably, producing high cooperation and social payoff. However, insufficient legitimacy prevents punishers from disciplining defectors, whereas excessive legitimacy allows strategies that punish high-reputation individuals to invade, linking the model to antisocial punishment. Finite-population Markov analyses further confirm that the main qualitative dynamics are robust to small punishment execution and assessment errors. These findings show that, under private reputation, the perceived legitimacy of costly punishment determines whether punishment sustains cooperation or facilitates antisocial punishment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Family specific spatial borrowing in multimodal urban reconstruction: a leave one neighborhood out study of Cincinnati
Abstract: Urban spatial models often assume that nearby borrowing improves prediction across target variables, but this assumption is rarely tested across distinct urban feature families within a city. Ridge performs best for street structure, indicating that some spatially regular families are best reconstructed from local linear combinations. The local nonlinear masked autoencoder (MLP-MAE) holds the highest median for most families with positive transfer, though these differences are not statistically distinguishable from the graph models, indicating that local nonlinear multimodal fusion is often sufficient. Graph-based models help most clearly for topography, while the selective-gate graph model wins many individual neighborhood comparisons for several families despite lower medians, reflecting different error profiles. Graph models also produce more neighborhood-structured representations: contextual embeddings from the selective multimodal spatial autoencoder (SMSA) recover neighborhood structure better than raw principal components or local-only embeddings. Learned gates are stable across folds and provide interpretable diagnostics of context reliance, but not a universal ranking of borrowing regimes. Title: The effect of social robot authority on epistemic vigilance in early childhood
Abstract: Social robots are increasingly deployed as tutors and learning partners, yet their authority cues may discourage children from questioning or verifying information. We investigated whether robot authority influences Chinese children’s epistemic vigilance and which source of authority drives this effect. In Study 1 (N = 128, ages 4 and 6, Mage = 5.39 years, SD = 0.92, 66 girls and 62 boys), robots with high and low overall authority asserted that all aliens in a task had three eyes. Children’s verification behaviors were assessed in terms of the number of times they checked the information, the length of time they spent checking, and how much time passed between checks. Results showed that children engaged in significantly less verification in the high-authority condition, and 6-year-olds checked more often than 4-year-olds. Study 2 (N = 200, ages 4 and 6, Mage = 5.19 years, SD = 0.92, 97 girls and 103 boys) built on Study 1 by manipulating two sources of authority: role authority (teacher-like vs. peer-like) and cognitive authority (knowledgeable vs. unknowledgeable). The same task and outcome measures were used as in Study 1. The results showed that cognitive authority significantly decreased children’s verification behavior, but there was no significant effect of role authority or child age. Together, these findings suggest that authority cues can shape how much evidence children seek before accepting robot testimony, particularly when the robot is presented as knowledgeable. Title: Grinding Charcoal for Rock Painting: A Methodological Framework for Particle-Size Analysis in Rock Art Micro-Samples
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Research on the materiality of rock art has shifted attention from images as finished products to the technical and social processes involved in their making. Within this framework, pigment grinding is a crucial but still methodologically elusive aspect of painting production, despite its potential to inform technological choices, labor investment, and variability in painting practices. In this paper, we propose an experimental and archaeometric approach to the study of charcoal grinding in rock art micro-samples. By combining experimental archaeology, optical microscopy, and particle analysis, we develop a model linking charcoal particle area to grinding time. We apply this method to study black rock paintings from the Oyola archaeological site, in northwestern Argentina, where charcoal was identified as the main black pigment. The results show that microscopically measurable differences in particle areas make it possible to distinguish varying degrees of grinding among paintings that are macroscopically and chemically similar. Title: Driving sustainable development goal alignment through green consumption marketing and public mind
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable development demands synchronized efforts across socioeconomic and environmental domains, specifically targeting poverty alleviation, food security, and environmental stewardship. Although sustainable consumption patterns and ecological marketing act as established catalysts for environmental transitions, the specific socio-civic pathways translating micro-level pro-environmental behaviors into macro-level policy alignment remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, the study objectives were to evaluate the direct and indirect pathways through which green consumption behavior and green marketing drive local alignment with the sustainable development goals through the mediating role of the public mind among residents in Nonthaburi Province, Thailand. METHODS: A quantitative survey design was executed to gather data from 400 residents across administrative districts in Nonthaburi Province using proportionate stratified random sampling. The researchers collected primary data through structured questionnaires employing a 5-point Likert scale. Analytical procedures encompassed descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to validate construct relationships and assess overall structural model fit. FINDINGS: The results of structural equation modeling indicate that both green consumption behavior and green marketing significantly influence the realization of local sustainable development goals, operating through both direct pathways and indirect pathways mediated by public consciousness. The public mind demonstrated the strongest direct influence on sustainable development goals realization (β = 0.69, p < 0.01), followed by direct impacts from green consumption behavior (β = 0.35, p < 0.01) and green marketing (β = 0.28, p < 0.01). Additionally, green consumption behavior was the primary driver of public mind activation (β = 0.37, p < 0.01), surpassing green marketing (β = 0.27, p < 0.01). The validated structural model accounted for substantial variance in sustainable development goals alignment (R^2 = 0.97) and the public mind (R^2 = 0.77). CONCLUSION: Green consumption behavior and green marketing are critical precursors to cultivating a collective public mind, which bridges individual eco-conscious actions with macro-level alignment of Sustainable Development Goals. Municipal authorities ought to embed the mobilization of public ecological awareness into environmental governance policies. Furthermore, this structural framework offers a scalable model adaptable to other rapidly urbanizing provinces in Southeast Asia. Title: Explaining Strategies to Reduce the Occurrence of Medication Errors at Older Adults with Polypharmacy
Abstract: Objective: Age-related changes make the older susceptible to multiple chronic diseases and, consequently, an increase in the number of medications consumed. The present study aimed toexplain strategies to reduce the incidence of medication errors at illiterate and low-literate older adults with polypharmacy from the perspectives of the older, caregivers, and pharmacists. Method: The present study is a qualitative study that was conducted with 23 semi-structured interviews with three different groups of participants including illiterate and low-literate older adults with polypharmacy, caregivers of the older (informal caregivers of the older such as family members), and pharmacists from August 2022 to Murch 2024 in Tabriz, Iran. Participants were selected using purposive sampling method and interviews were conducted based on a designed interview guide. Conventional content analysis method was used to analyze the data. Findings: The inductive content analysis process extracted 6 main categories from 32 subcategories. The average age of the older participants in the study was 67.53 years. From the perspective of the study participants, strengthening self-care and health-oriented behaviors and beliefs, using techniques to optimize medication management, caregiver responsibility and support, effective education, effective interaction between the older and the physician-pharmacist, and an efficient healthcare system can be effective in reducing the incidence of medication errors in the older. Conclusion:Due to the multifactorial nature of medication errors, it is not the sole responsibility of health professionals to contribute to the reduction of medication errors, and integrated actions must be taken by health care providers, the pharmaceutical industry, insurers, educational providers, legislators, caregivers, and ultimately the elderly themselves. © (2027), (Negah Institute for Scientific Communication), All Rights Reserved.

Title: Meta-operation-assisted optimization for execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning
Abstract: Existing robotic disassembly sequence planning (RDSP) studies mainly optimize operation ordering under precedence constraints, whereas robot configurations and local operation parameters are typically treated separately or represented by fixed or simplified operation costs. To bridge this gap, this paper formulates an execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning (EP-RDSP) problem that jointly considers disassembly sequencing, robot configuration selection, and disassembly operation parameter optimization. In contrast to task-level RDSP, EP-RDSP evaluates a plan through the coupled effects of its operation sequence, selected inverse kinematics (IK) configurations, joint-space transitions, and local operation parameters. EP-RDSP contains heterogeneous and tightly coupled decisions, making direct optimization of the full mixed decision space computationally challenging. To address this challenge, a meta-operation-assisted (MOA) optimization framework is proposed to support multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA)-based search. The framework exploits meta-operation knowledge for operation-parameter generation before online optimization, allowing MOEA to focus on globally coupled planning decisions such as operation ordering, IK candidate selection, and joint-configuration and speed-ratio decisions. Experiments on 15 generated problem instances show that, across the four underlying optimizers and three instance scales, the MOA variants reduce the mean online runtime required to reach the target hypervolume (HV) by 16.45%–83.01%. Under fixed online time budgets, the MOA framework improves the mean HV by 31.13%–80.04% relative to five comparison methods and achieves the lowest mean inverted generational distance (IGD) on 14 of the 15 instances. Authors: Poorjangi I.; Farsi H.
Title: Dual-Objective Design of Broadband Rectenna and Anchor Node Optimization for Energy Harvesting and High-Accuracy UWB Localization
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Wireless sensor networks and portable devices face two major challenges: sustainable energy supply and high-precision indoor localization. While far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) offers energy solutions, it suffers from low power density and environmental sensitivity. To mitigate these drawbacks, the proposed system incorporates polarization diversity and a wideband impedance matching strategy. Simultaneously, GPS fails in indoor environments, driving the need for ultra-wideband (UWB) localization to achieve centimeter-level accuracy. This paper presents a dual-objective framework to tackle both issues. First, it designs a broadband antenna array (1–20 GHz) with multi-polarization reception, combined with an optimized matching network and Schottky-based rectifier to enhance RF-to-DC conversion under low power. Second, it introduces an anchor placement optimization algorithm for UWB that uses probabilistic target behavior models to minimize positioning errors. Simulation results confirm that the energy harvester remains effective across various incident angles and frequencies, while the localization error is consistently reduced to around one centimeter. The integrated approach provides a comprehensive solution for next-generation WSNs, overcoming power management bottlenecks while elevating localization accuracy to approximately one centimeter. © 2027 The author(s). Authors: He Z.; Deng N.; Guo S.; Xiong T.; Lu Z.Y.; Li X.R.; Chen R.
Title: TikTok as a stage: How short video creators’ identity performance drives engagement with tourism experiences
Abstract: Destinations are increasingly collaborating with short-form video creators to engage consumers. Through Goffman's dramaturgical lens, this study explores how creators' performed identities in travel videos relate to audience responses. Combining machine learning and AI-powered analyses of over 10k short-form videos and 176k viewer comments with a controlled experiment, we identified four identities that creators performed in these videos (the “showman,” “diarist,” “docent,” and “photographer”) and classified them at scale. Results showed that identity performance is associated with distinct configurations of audiences' behavioral engagement. The “docent” generated more audience engagement than other identities, including audiences' learning, endorsing, and intending to participate dimensions. Guided by the knowledge gap theory, a subsequent experiment showed that the “docent” identity increased engagement by sparking curiosity. These findings guide content creators in adopting effective identity performance strategies, destinations in partnering with well-aligned content creators, and platforms in using algorithmic curation to achieve desired marketing outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Recursive self-regulation in genAI-assisted experiential learning: A task-contingent model
Abstract: Existing literature on generative AI (genAI) in business education has examined students’ attitudes, motivation, and the ethics of genAI use, alongside ongoing debate about whether genAI over-reliance may diminish self-regulated learning (SRL). However, how students self-regulate their learning while working with genAI during authentic tasks remains under-explored. This study addresses this gap by examining (RQ1) how students' self-regulatory strategies manifest during genAI-assisted learning and (RQ2) how these strategies change through genAI interaction. A thematic analysis was conducted of 34 metacognitive reflections generated across two scaffolded, four-stage experiential learning activities in a Lean Startup unit. Findings inform a three-stage AI-mediated recursive loop model, comprising monitoring, strategic adoption, and limitation identification, that extends cyclical models of self-regulated learning by showing how regulation may be initiated within the task by genAI-generated suggestions. Within this structured, reflective learning context, students indicated evaluative judgement and metacognitive regulation, providing preliminary evidence that scaffolded genAI activities can elicit active rather than passive engagement. GenAI-supported cognitive deepening was task-contingent, emerging most strongly during applied refinement tasks. The model offers management educators a pedagogical process model for designing scaffolded genAI-assisted activities that elicit monitoring, selective adoption, and critical reflection. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Brazilian Expert Consensus on the Use of Equity and Acceptability in Health Technology Assessment: A Delphi Panel
Abstract: Objectives To achieve consensus among Brazilian experts on the concepts of equity and acceptability within the context of health technology assessment (HTA) in Brazil and to identify guidance for their practical application across assessment stages, operationalization methods, and strategies for evidence generation and use. Methods A 2-round online Delphi panel with Brazilian HTA experts assessed agreement on predefined literature-based concepts of equity and acceptability and explored perspectives on HTA stages, methods, and evidence generation and retrieval strategies. Reasons for disagreement and recommendations for further incorporating these dimensions were also qualitatively analyzed. Results Participants were experienced HTA professionals, and consensus on the concepts of equity and acceptability was reached in the first round, exceeding the predefined threshold of 80% agreement. These dimensions were considered cross-cutting throughout the HTA process, with priority given to technology assessment, clinical guideline development, and implementation stages. Evidence search methods and cost-effectiveness analyses were prioritized for equity, whereas qualitative evidence and mixed methods were prioritized for acceptability. Strategies including secondary data analysis, primary data collection, and standardized filter use were prioritized for both dimensions. Conclusions This study advances the conceptual understanding of equity and acceptability in HTA and provides methodological guidance across process stages, supporting the development of more comprehensive HTA that is sensitive to inequities and responsive to population needs. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Complex adaptive governance for sustainable tourism villages: Explanatory insights from combined polycentric and chaos theoretical perspectives
Abstract: Sustainable tourism villages face complex governance challenges because they must simultaneously support economic development, protect local culture, preserve ecological resources, and respond to changing social conditions. Existing studies have examined sustainable tourism governance mainly from administrative, community-based, or institutional perspectives, but less attention has been given to how distributed authority interacts with nonlinear adaptive dynamics in village-level governance systems. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated framework that combines polycentric governance theory and chaos theory. Using a quantitative explanatory design, survey data were collected from 590 stakeholders involved in tourism village governance across four regencies and one city in Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that institutional diversity has the strongest association with sustainable tourism village governance, followed by decentralization and local autonomy, bifurcation and cosmology, community participation, flexibility and adaptability, edge of chaos and the butterfly effect, and self-organization and strange attractors. The model yields a very high coefficient of determination, which suggests a close within sample fit between the proposed constructs and the observed perception data. This result is interpreted cautiously because the study is cross-sectional and several constructs are conceptually proximate. The study contributes to governance theory by showing that sustainable tourism village governance can be understood as both polycentric and complex-adaptive. Practically, the findings suggest that policymakers and tourism village managers should strengthen multi-actor coordination while maintaining flexibility to respond to uncertainty and local change. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Retreat in monastery stay tourism: the role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ connectedness and behavioural intention
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Monastery stay tourism is an emerging niche within spiritual and transformative tourism, offering immersive experiences that facilitate personal and emotional growth. Despite its rising popularity, limited research has explored how such experiences shape tourists' emotional bonds, identity formation, and revisit intention. Drawing on mindfulness theory, this study examines the role of mindfulness cultivated during Buddhist monastery retreats in influencing emotional solidarity, experience self-connection, place identity, and behavioural intention. Data were collected from 430 visitors and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The PLS-SEM results underscore the critical role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ social interactions, emotional attachment to the destination, and self-connection, all of which significantly impact their intention to engage in spiritual retreats. Emotional solidarity and self-connection are found to significantly influence place identity and future behavioural intention. The MGA findings indicate that generational and experiential segmentation reveals that Generation Z is more responsive to mindfulness and experience self-connection, while older cohorts are more influenced by emotional solidarity. Repeat visitors report stronger mindfulness effects across all outcomes, whereas first-time visitors rely more on emotional bonding. These insights underscore the value of tailoring mindful retreat experiences to foster deeper engagement and sustained support for religious tourism destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Emotion Regulation in Language Learning: Strategies for Managing Foreign Language Anxiety among Iranian EFL Learners
Abstract: This study employed a mixed-methods approach to examine the utilization of two emotion regulation strategies, namely cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression, among a group of Iranian learners of English as a foreign language (EFL) at universities in Isfahan, Iran. The investigation was based on the Process Model of Emotion Regulation, a psychologically-validated theoretical model proposed by Gross (2015). The study also investigated the correlation between emotion regulation and levels of foreign language anxiety (FLA), and as an additional area of investigation, the impact of emotion regulation on the association between FLA and motivation for learning a second language. A total of 295 learners were questioned using a quantitative questionnaire. The qualitative research involved the selection of thirteen respondents from three levels (high, medium, low) of FLA. The primary component employed in this study was a stimulated recall interview. Data collection was undertaken online due to scheduling constraints. The findings indicated a low frequency of utilization for the two emotion regulation strategies, with cognitive reappraisal being more commonly employed compared to expressive suppression. Learners with low English proficiency exhibited a lower prevalence and preference for cognitive reappraisal. There was a stronger positive correlation observed between expressive suppression and FLA. The study found a negative correlation between cognitive reappraisal and FLA. It provides evidence that understanding the inner workings of learners’ emotion regulation may inform pedagogical practices. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. All rights reserved.

Title: Exploring the acceptance of science teachers toward simulator-based technology
Abstract: Teacher acceptance of technology is crucial for enhancing the effectiveness of learning in the digital era. This study aims to explore the acceptance of simulator-based technology among science teachers and to compare the perspectives of experienced and inexperienced teachers. A quantitative descriptive approach was used, adopting the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology 2 (UTAUT2) model. The analysis was conducted to test the influence of Performance Expectancy (PE), Effort Expectancy (EE), Social Influence (SI), Facilitating Conditions (FC), Hedonic Motivation (HM), and Habit (HA) on Behavioral Intention (BI) and Use Behavior (UB). Data were collected through a survey of middle school science teachers in Surakarta, Indonesia. The results revealed positive acceptance of the simulator, with differences between the two groups. Perceived ease of use (EE) and facilitating support (FC) influence behavioral intention (BI), whereas habit (HA) and hedonic motivation (HM) play a significant roles in use behavior (UB), especially among experienced teachers. The results revealed positive acceptance of the simulator, with significant differences between the two groups. Overall, experienced teachers demonstrated higher mean scores across all UTAUT2 indicators. Performance Expectancy (PE) and Facilitating Conditions (FC) were found to consistently influence Behavioral Intention (BI) across almost all groups. However, Effort Expectancy (EE) and Social Influence (SI) were more significant for inexperienced teachers, whereas Habit (HA) significantly influenced BI only for experienced teachers. For Use Behavior (UB), Behavioral Intention (BI), Facilitating Conditions (FC), Hedonic Motivation (HM), and Habit (HA) emerged as strong predictors, particularly for the experienced group. These findings imply the need for adaptive implementation strategies; experience-based training, infrastructure enhancements, and user-friendly simulator design are recommended to enhance the acceptance and utilization of technology among science teachers. Title: Employee cybersecurity awareness impact on cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada
Abstract: This study investigates the impact of employee cybersecurity awareness on the cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada, as the prevalence of cyber threats, such as ransomware, phishing, and data breaches, continues to rise. The study adopts Servant Leadership (SL) theory as the analytical framework, with particular emphasis on SL’s attributes of employee empowerment, training, and organizational culture as factors in building resilience against cyber threats. A systematic literature review (SLR) methodology was employed, drawing on peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 from databases including Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science. The review process followed PRISMA guidelines, with rigorous application of inclusion and exclusion criteria, data extraction, and quality appraisal using the AMSTAR and CASP tools, resulting in 30 articles for the SLR. The findings reveal that organizations with strong servant leadership attributes, employee empowerment and training, combined with a cybersecurity-conscious culture, enhance employee cybersecurity awareness and training. The study further found that clear and consistently enforced policies are critical for guiding employee behaviour and fostering long-term adherence. The study recommends adopting targeted role-based and scenario-driven training approaches on cybersecurity for employees to improve their knowledge retention and threat response to cyberattacks for strengthening organizational cybersecurity posture in Canada. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

Title: Blowing Leaves in Archaeology—The Multidimensionality of Technological Complexity in Human Origins Research
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Technological complexity has been a continuous trope in archaeological research from its beginnings in the nineteenth century. Based on a concept of unidirectional cultural evolution, archaeological material was ordered along a linear progression from simple to complex. While creating hierarchies of extant populations based on the complexity of their tools is not overtly practiced in archaeology anymore, the same is not true for the deep past. The concept of behavioural modernity and research on human cognitive evolution is still partly founded on technological complexity. The turn away from technological complexity to symbolic behaviour in pursuing questions surrounding behavioural modernity and humanness was less a reaction to criticisms of the concept but served to maintain the hierarchical ranking between modern humans and extinct hominins. Here, we propose an alternative view on technological complexity that attempts to overcome linear hierarchies and lingering progressivist notions. By reviewing several measures of complexity alongside their analytical units and underlying definitions, we show that technological complexity is not suitable for creating a single hierarchy of artefacts, assemblages, or hominin species. The multitude of existing definitions, methods, and measures does not imply a fundamental flaw in these approaches but exemplifies the multidimensionality of technological complexity. We propose a new way of understanding multiple, justified measures for technological complexity through a heterarchical structure that allows various kinds of ranking to exist depending on context, need, scale, or function, including the potential for competing or even contradictory hierarchies. A heterarchical perspective on technological complexity asks ‘How were technologies or hominins complex?’ rather than ‘How complex were technologies and hominins relative to another?’ This approach can shed persistent historical bias and overcome simplistic dichotomies such as ‘us’ and ‘them’ in deep-time archaeology that hinder our ability to engage with questions about the becoming of humans in a meaningful way. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Multi-objective optimization and decision-making for renewable energy production and enhancement of wind turbine selection in Morocco
Abstract: Selecting an appropriate wind turbine for a specific location requires the simultaneous evaluation of energy output, cost, and site-specific deployment constraints. This research introduces a comprehensive framework that integrates simulation, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), and hybrid deep learning to enhance the selection of turbines for various sites. One year of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis version 5 (ERA5) reanalysis data and geographical information from satellite and elevation datasets was used to model the energy output of 40 commercial turbines in 15 Moroccan cities. A weighted scoring procedure was developed to evaluate turbines based on their capacity factor, annual energy production (AEP), capital and operating expenditures (CAPEX/OPEX), topographical constraints, and proximity to infrastructure. Two hybrid models, convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) and convolutional neural network-Transformer (CNN–Transformer), were trained on structured inputs that included meteorological, topography, and spatial data to enhance decision assistance. The CNN–Transformer model outperformed the CNN–LSTM model in predictions and closely aligned with the expert rankings derived from simulations. Constraint-aware filtering and cost-performance trade-offs were employed to enhance the final turbine suggestions. The findings demonstrate the efficacy of integrating physics-based simulation with machine learning for large-scale energy planning at specific locations. This framework supports future upgrades to renewable energy systems, including AI-based digital twins, real-time monitoring, and use across more locations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The influence of gender, socioeconomic, and domain competencies on students’ creative thinking across four high-performing educational systems
Abstract: This study explores the multidimensional construct of students’ creative thinking by analysing the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment data from four educational systems: Chinese Taipei, Hong Kong, Macao, and the Czech Republic. These jurisdictions are uniquely characterised by high student performance in reading, mathematics, and science, while their average creative thinking scores fall below the OECD benchmark. The study examines the predictive power of gender, socioeconomic status (SES), and academic proficiency in Reading, Mathematics, and Science on students’ performance across four creative thinking (CRT) domain contexts: Written Expression, Visual Expression, Social Creative Problem-Solving, and Scientific Creative Problem-Solving. Evidence shows that female students consistently outperformed male students across all four creative thinking domains, while SES demonstrated a modest but consistently positive association with creative thinking performance. Academic competencies also contributed significantly to CRT but exhibited distinct domain-specific predictive patterns. Reading competence was the strongest and most consistent predictor, particularly for Written and Visual Expression. Science competence showed stable positive associations across domains, whereas Mathematics contributed most strongly to Social and Scientific Creative Problem-Solving but was negatively associated with Visual Expression. These findings indicate that academic competencies contribute differently across creative thinking domains. Representative item-level analyses further illustrated task-specific predictive patterns, while the complete item-level analyses are reported in the Supplementary Material. These findings support a domain-sensitive view of creative thinking, in which academic competencies show differential associations with creative performance depending on the domain and task context, and further offer practical implications for creativity assessment and educational practice. Title: Measuring head motion across deceleration levels in automated driving: Quantifying comfort
Abstract: Passenger-centred comfort measures are needed to enable adaptive driving styles in automated vehicles, particularly where comfort begins to decrease. This study examined passengers' head motion during automated braking at a crosswalk. Data from thirty-four participants were analysed, who experienced three deceleration levels (−1.5, −2.5, −3.5 m/s2) and two pedestrian visibility conditions, reflecting how quickly the AV braked after the pedestrian appeared, rating comfort respectively. As expected, head pitch and translational acceleration increased with deceleration intensity, while pedestrian visibility had no effect on head motion, even though faster AV responses were previously found more comfortable, suggesting this reflects passengers' judgement of the AV's response rather than head stability. Head-motion measures did not add predictive value beyond vehicle kinematics, likely because comfort ratings were similar across conditions. In this scenario, head-motion mainly reflected physical response to braking rather than subjective evaluation. Title: Behavioral Economics as a Driver of Healthcare System Reform: Methodological Approach
Abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to develop and apply the Behavioral Economics in Health index as a methodological tool for assessing the role of behavioral strategies in healthcare reform, with particular attention to their impact on healthcare expenditure, life expectancy, and system-level adaptation in countries with varying levels of institutional maturity and economic capacity. Methods The research used system-dynamics-based simulation modeling using behavioral and economic parameters, followed by statistical analysis of the results. Results The AnyLogic simulation results showed that, under an intensive behavioral integration scenario for 2024 to 2034, per-capita health expenditure decreased by USD 200 in Ukraine and USD 190 in Poland. In these countries, the initial levels of behavioral integration were the lowest—0.51 and 0.59, respectively—and the 10-year increase was 0.30. This fact ensured a steady reduction in expenditure throughout the entire modeling period without significant fluctuations. In Denmark, where the initial behavioral integration level was higher (0.88), the decrease amounted to only USD 26 per person, indicating a limited effect of further behavioral interventions in an already prevention-oriented healthcare system. Conversely, in the United States, where the integration index was even higher (0.91), expenditure increased by USD 20.72 per capita. Conclusions These findings indicate that the maximum economic effect of behavioral strategies is achieved in countries with low initial levels of integration and limited resources. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: LMC-DETR: A lightweight detection model for foreign object detection on power lines
Abstract: To address the dual requirements of model lightweighting and detection accuracy in foreign object detection for drone-based power-line inspection, this paper proposes a lightweight multi-scale context-aware detection model, termed LMC-DETR. Specifically, a Context-aware Global Block (CGB) is introduced into the backbone network, which integrates multi-scale receptive field fusion with global context recalibration, thereby achieving significant reduction in parameters while enhancing feature extraction capabilities. In the neck network, a Multi-scale Context Fusion Framework (MCFF) is designed to construct an intelligent feature pyramid, wherein two cooperative submodules, Fusion-U and Fusion-D, collaborate. Attention-guided upsampling and downsampling mechanisms are employed to substantially improve the quality of multi-scale feature fusion. Furthermore, a Squeeze-and-Excitation Channel (SEC) module incorporates a lightweight Efficient Squeeze-and-Excitation (ESE) attention mechanism for adaptive channel-wise feature recalibration, effectively suppressing background noise while accentuating critical feature representations. Experimental evaluations on a public power line foreign object dataset demonstrate that the proposed LMC-DETR achieves a detection accuracy of 85.0% APIOU=50. Compared to the baseline, LMC-DETR reduces the number of parameters (15.1M) and computational cost (44.1 GFLOPs) by 23.7% and 22.5%, respectively, striking a favorable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Consequently, the model shows promise for real-time drone inspection scenarios, pending further validation on edge hardware. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Functional metagenomics yields insights into the adaptive mechanisms of microbial persistence in beef processing drains
Abstract: Selective pressures within beef processing environments drive the persistence of microbial communities capable of withstanding repeated sanitation, yet the functional mechanisms underlying this resilience remain largely uncharacterized. To address this knowledge gap, a metagenomic study was conducted on 21 drain samples collected across eight United States beef processing facilities, evaluating the effects of spatiotemporal factors (processing areas and the 2019 versus 2021 sampling years) on functional potential and resistome composition. Broad functional profiling identified significant enrichment of KEGG pathways governing biofilm formation, quorum sensing, bacterial secretion systems, ABC transporters, chemotaxis, and flagellar assembly, with Pseudomonas spp. emerging as the dominant driver across all enriched features. Differential abundance analysis revealed significant (Padj < 0.05) enrichment of these pathways and multidrug resistance determinants in carcass storage coolers and in 2021 samples. This temporal shift may reflect several non-exclusive factors, including changes in sanitation pressure, natural temporal drift, shifts in cattle microbiomes, or sample storage effects. Antimicrobial resistance profiling using AMRFinderPlus and DeepARG further demonstrated that the dominant Pseudomonas populations exerted a disproportionate influence on the facility resistome, primarily via multidrug efflux systems. This profile coincided with a nearly two-fold increase in beta-lactam resistance annotations between 2019 and 2021, suggesting that environmental pressures may select for clinically relevant resistance markers. These findings provide a functional framework for understanding microbial persistence in built food-processing environments and highlight the critical need to evaluate whether current sanitation strategies inadvertently promote resistant, biofilm-forming communities. © 2026

Title: Assessment of Drinking Water Security and Waterborne Disease Prevalence in Imphal East and West Districts of Manipur, India
Abstract: Integrated assessment of drinking water security and the prevalence of waterborne diseases in the Imphal East (IE) and Imphal West (IW) districts of Manipur, India, using the water poverty index (WPI). The seasonal prevalence of waterborne diseases was assessed with respect to climate variables, specifically rainfall and temperature. The systematic, structured household questionnaire survey and focus group discussions were conducted to assess socioeconomic parameters of the representative population. Based on the integrated assessment, the study reveals a poor-to-moderate WPI, highlighting a significant challenge for people in accessing potable water in the region. This underscores the need to improve rural drinking water supply to ensure public health safety. Title: Gaze aversion and emotional mimicry deficits in individuals with schizophrenia during naturalistic interaction
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Individuals with schizophrenia exhibit a range of verbal and nonverbal impairments during social interaction, which contribute to reduced interaction quality and broader social dysfunction. To optimize clinical interventions, it is essential to identify the mechanisms underlying these deficits. Building on previous findings demonstrating reduced emotional mimicry in schizophrenia, the present study examined whether gaze aversion is associated with instances of failed mimicry during naturalistic conversation. In a within-partner design, interacting partners (n = 20) each engaged in one conversation with an individual with schizophrenia (n = 20) and one with a matched healthy control (n = 20). Prior analyses using OpenFace-based video coding revealed diminished emotional mimicry in the schizophrenia group. In the present study, the same video recordings were reanalyzed using FaceReader to extract gaze direction. We specifically examined gaze aversion during the interaction and, more critically, during episodes of failed mimicry, defined as instances in which participants did not reciprocate their partner's smile. Results indicated that although individuals with schizophrenia did not display significantly greater overall gaze aversion across the entire interaction, they exhibited significantly greater gaze aversion when their partner was smiling. This pattern was associated with a higher proportion of failed mimicry accompanied by gaze aversion in the schizophrenia group compared to controls. These findings suggest that reduced visual attention may represent one mechanism contributing to emotional mimicry deficits in schizophrenia. Clinical implications are discussed, along with the potential role of stigma in exacerbating these processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Locked in: How formal institutional design sustains extractivism and ecological decline in Ghana’s mining–water sector
Abstract: Mining-related water pollution persists despite repeated legislative reforms and regulatory interventions. Yet, existing explanations largely attribute this persistence to weak enforcement, political patronage, or socioeconomic pressures driving artisanal small-scale mining (ASM). We argue instead that the problem is fundamentally one of institutional design. Drawing on institutional theory and institutional grammar analysis, we examine how Ghana's mining-water legislation allocates authority and embeds incentive structures that shape environmental governance. We find that the legislative framework privileges regulative over constitutive institutional elements, producing governance arrangements that are procedurally elaborate yet functionally weak. At the same time, it embeds economic and political incentives that favor extractivism while providing comparatively weak social and regulatory incentives for environmental stewardship, reinforcing fragmented authority, symbolic governance, and executive overreach. These institutional arrangements generate intertwined common-pool resource and public-bad dilemmas that lock Ghana's mining-water sector into a gilded trap, in which short-term extractive gains systematically outweigh long-term socioecological sustainability. The findings suggest that persistent mining-related water pollution is not simply a failure of enforcement but a consequence of institutional architectures that privilege extractivism while weakening environmental governance. In reconceptualizing the gilded trap as an institutionally produced condition, the paper demonstrates how imbalances between constitutive and regulative institutional elements generate symbolic governance and position the state as an active producer, rather than merely a failed regulator, of extractivist outcomes. © 2026 .

Title: Overcoming interlayer weakness in Ti2C MXene via 3D pillared nanostructures for enhanced compressive and shear resistance
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: The outstanding in-plane mechanical properties of two-dimensional Ti2C MXene nanosheets have made them promising candidates for advanced structural materials. However, the weak interlayer van der Waals bonding between MXene sheets limits the load transfer efficiency, leading to premature interfacial debonding and shear sliding under mechanical loading. Here, we propose a three-dimensional (3D) pillared MXene nanostructure consisting of Ti2C nanosheets covalently interconnected by Ti2C nanotubes, and systematically investigate its mechanical properties via molecular dynamics simulations. We examine the effects of nanotube diameter, inclination angle, atomic-scale vacancies, and multi-tube spatial arrangement on tensile, compressive, and shear responses. Under tension, the nanotube remains covalently bonded to the nanosheets and undergoes localized deformation. Under compression, an optimal diameter of 1.8 nm balances strength and deformability, while larger-diameter tubes show reduced sensitivity to point defects. A 15° inclination enhances compressive strain by 53.7% with only 19.3% strength loss. In multi-tube configurations, a systematic trade-off between strength and deformability emerges: Vertically aligned arrays maximize strength, staggered arrangements introduce progressive load release, and hybrid designs achieve the highest deformability. These findings suggest that 3D pillared nanostructures offer a promising route to overcome the interlayer weakness of Ti2C MXene assemblies with enhanced compressive and shear resistance, providing atomistic insights for the design of free-standing MXene-based structural architectures. © 2026

Authors: Liu Z.; Liu S.; Wang Y.; Chen Y.; Deng H.; Tan Z.; Zhao X.; Chen Y.; Zhu M.
Title: Broad-spectrum chromaticity and high color fastness of polyimide fibers via intrinsic coloration
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Due to the exceptional thermal stability, radiation resistance, and mechanical properties, polyimide (PI) fibers are widely used in various extreme environments. However, the intrinsic monochromatic golden hue and chemically inert surface of PI fiber give rise to a natural barrier to dyeing and low color fastness. Herein, a facile and transformative intrinsic coloration strategy for the dyeing of PI fibers is proposed by directly incorporating a perylene-based chromophore monomer into the backbone of PI. By tuning the concentration and categories of perylene derivatives, various intrinsic colors of PI fibers are afforded, constructing a diverse chromatic PI fiber library with a broad color gamut (spanning from warm tones to slate-grey). Significantly, the strategy successfully overcomes the long-standing trade-off between dyeing and mechanical integrity. Moreover, the incorporation of perylene-based chromophores exhibits excellent structural compatibility with the PI backbone, acting as reinforced components rather than stress-concentrating defects. Consequently, the fibers exhibit simultaneous enhancements in mechanical properties and exceptional color fastness against harsh environments. This work establishes a cost-effective and scalable paradigm for the functionalization of PI fibers, contributing to the expanding application of PI fibers in high-end textiles and smart wearables. © 2026

Title: How social status shapes U.S. children’s beliefs about social mobility
Abstract: Children grow up within social hierarchies that shape their everyday lives. Social mobility is a core mechanism through which societies either challenge or maintain existing inequalities. The present study examined how U.S. children’s social status—both experimentally manipulated and measured at the neighborhood level—shapes their beliefs about social mobility for themselves and their high- and low-status peers. Children ( N = 130; 3–8 years; 70 girls, 59 boys, 1 non-binary; 12.3% Asian, 6.9% Black, 11.6% Latine, 20.7% Multiracial, and 48.5% White) were randomly assigned to either experimentally advantaged or disadvantaged groups. They were then assessed on their (1) general expectations about social mobility, (2) effort-contingent expectations for mobility, and (3) post-hoc explanations for upward and downward mobility. We found that compared to experimentally-disadvantaged children, experimentally-advantaged children were more likely to have higher expectations for themselves and high-status peers, but lower expectations for low-status peers. With age, disadvantaged children (experimental and neighborhood) exhibited higher expectations for themselves and lower expectations for high-status peers, whereas advantaged children’s expectations remained stable. Older children were more likely to believe working hard leads to upward mobility and attribute upward/downward mobility to individual effort. This tendency was especially pronounced for their own upward (vs. downward) mobility, but less so when evaluating the upward mobility of high-status peers (vs. themselves). These results suggest that children’s beliefs about social mobility develop throughout childhood, differ by target, and are shaped by their own social status. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Electrical performance assessment of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid power system for EV charging applications
Abstract: The integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure with renewable-based autonomous power systems presents a promising approach for distributed energy deployment. This study evaluates the electrical performance of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid system designed to supply EV charging and lighting loads in Urla, Izmir, Türkiye. Optimal system sizing is performed using HOMER, followed by detailed electrical modeling and time-domain simulations in ETAP under realistic operating conditions. The system comprises photovoltaic arrays, a wind turbine, battery energy storage with bidirectional converters, supplying EV charging and lighting loads. A deterministic time-scheduled load profile is adopted to ensure reproducibility. Scenario-based analyses across multiple operating conditions, including reduced solar irradiance, wind turbine outage, and load curtailment, are conducted over three representative days corresponding to winter, summer, and transitional conditions. Results demonstrate sustained power balance and full supply reliability, achieving 0% unmet load across all scenarios. Voltage levels remain within tight operational limits, confirming electrical stability, while battery state-of-charge profiles indicate adequate energy availability and effective storage utilization. The findings validate the operational feasibility and electrical robustness of the proposed system under variable generation and dynamic loading conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zeng Y.; Liu Y.; Mei L.
Title: Curriculum greenwashing in business statistics education: Institutional decoupling in responsible management education
Abstract: Business schools increasingly state commitments to responsible management education (RME), yet institutional commitment may not be consistently reflected in pedagogical change. This study examines curriculum greenwashing as a possible divergence between RME language in curriculum artifacts and corresponding evidence in teaching practice and student learning, without assuming deliberate intent. Drawing on institutional theory and decoupling, we test whether signatory status in the Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME) is associated with declarative, procedural, and consequential integration in undergraduate business statistics courses. Longitudinal multilevel data were collected from 215 students and 45 faculty members across 30 institutions across three waves. PRME status was positively associated with RME content in syllabi, whereas associations with reported teaching and student learning gains were not detected. Faculty-reported practices were positively associated with student learning gains. The PRME status × faculty quantitative teaching self-efficacy interaction was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance; exploratory probing indicated a positive PRME association only at high self-efficacy. The study contributes a three-level audit framework for evaluating how institutional RME commitment is reflected across curriculum representation, reported teaching practice, and student learning, while underscoring the value of evidence beyond syllabus language alone. © 2026

Title: Recurrent and eroding challenges in creative tourism: A longitudinal study of entrepreneurial resilience among urban handicraft artisans
Abstract: Despite the growing importance of creative tourism in emerging economies, the temporal nature of the challenges facing artisans—and the resilience strategies they employ—remains poorly understood. Adopting a longitudinal interpretivist approach, the study examines the entrepreneurial resilience of urban handicraft artisans in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, across a period of compounding crises, including the pandemic, political instability, and socioeconomic volatility. Theoretically, the study introduces new typologies of entrepreneurial challenges and extends resilience theory in creative tourism. Title: Embodied cognition and the luxury hospitality experience of in-flight wine in premium cabins
Abstract: This study explores how first- and business-class passengers experience in-flight wine as luxurious, even though flying reduces taste and smell. Drawing on embodied cognition theory, we argue that passengers do not simply judge wine by its quality. They build a sense of luxury by noticing how the airline tries to compensate for sensory limits, by feeling that the service fits their bodily experience, and by responding emotionally. We surveyed 500 premium-cabin passengers and used two analytical approaches: structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis. The results show two related paths to luxury: a cognitive path, in which the service feels consistent with the passenger's bodily state, and an affective path, in which the service creates positive emotions. For first-class passengers, both paths had to reach a minimum level for luxury to emerge. For business-class passengers, the cognitive path was more important, and positive emotions were less essential. Title: Beyond participation: Creativity and entrepreneurial mindset across instructional modes and learner-level digital conditions in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: Entrepreneurship education is often examined as a uniform educational exposure, although its associations with student development may depend on instructional mode and learner-level digital conditions. Drawing on survey data from 1181 graduating students at a multidisciplinary university in Guangdong, China, we use propensity score matching to improve comparability between participants and non-participants on observed characteristics and estimate interaction models to assess conditional relationships. The results indicate that entrepreneurship education is more consistently associated with entrepreneurial mindset than with creativity. Business plan competitions, training programs, and practical workshops generally show comparatively strong associations, particularly relative to entrepreneurship courses, although public lectures are also notably associated with entrepreneurial mindset. Perceived digital literacy displays a selective and format-dependent moderating relationship with creativity but does not consistently moderate the relationship with entrepreneurial mindset. Functional social media use shows no stable moderation in the primary binary models, while supplementary continuous-measure models reveal some operationalization-sensitive patterns. Title: Optimal telepresence experience in heritage tourism: A multidimensional scale and its impact on tourist behavior

Title: Designing sustainability communication across behavioral effort levels: How AI-generated micro-videos shape pro-environmental intentions
Abstract: The sustainability communication literature treats communication formats as functionally substitutable, overlooking how effectiveness may depend on the effort required to perform targeted behaviors. Title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread
Abstract: The dissemination of epidemic-related information can effectively enhance public awareness of preventive measures and decrease infection risks. However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility. To address this gap, this study develops a three-layer metapopulation network coupled model that integrates online information dissemination, epidemic spreading, and offline information dissemination. The proposed model systematically investigates the patterns of information dissemination through both online and offline channels, as well as the epidemic reaction–diffusion process driven by individual migration. Furthermore, the social interactions dynamics of both information channels are influenced by migration, manifested as migrated individuals acquire offline information in destination patches and establish online connections with individuals residing there. Theoretical analysis using the Microscopic Markov Chain Approach (MMCA) derives epidemic thresholds, while Monte Carlo (MC) simulations validate the model and examine factors influencing propagation dynamics. Results indicate that migration enhances individuals’ offline information acquisition, and accelerates cross-patch online information dissemination. Both online and offline information interactions exert inhibitory effects on epidemic spread, effectively increasing the infection threshold and reducing the outbreak scale. Furthermore, increasing the connectivity and dissemination rate of online information, particularly the information dissemination via weak relationships between patches, can effectively inhibit epidemic outbreaks. Notably, when the suppression effect of information on the epidemic is weak, population migration facilitates epidemic spread. In contrast, when the suppression effect is strong, migration-driven information dissemination significantly reduces the probability of infection, thereby further suppressing the outbreak. Title: Analogy Versus Behavioral Ecology in the Study of Human Evolution
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: In a recent critique published in this journal (Ben-Dor, M. & R. Barkai, 2026, Paleolithic dietary flexibility? Methodological considerations in analogy-based reconstructions of Paleolithic energetic returns, Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory 33, article 47, pp. 1–27), the authors characterize behavioral ecology approaches to the study of foraging efficiency as being fundamentally constrained by their reliance on conventional analogy-based reasoning. This characterization, however, misrepresents the aims and theoretical and methodological foundations of these approaches. Rather than relying on simple analogies, behavioral ecology models evaluate how interactions among variables such as prey behavior, encounter rates and contexts, seasonal variation in the macronutrient composition of game tissues, technology, pursuit success rates, opportunity costs, and other ecological and economic factors influence foraging efficiency across diverse habitats and among a wide range of societies. By explicitly identifying and testing the mechanisms that generate variation in economic returns, these approaches provide a rigorous and theory-driven alternative to conventional analogy-based interpretations. We also identify several problems with Ben-Dor and Barkai’s claim that proboscideans constituted high-ranked prey during the Lower and Middle Pleistocene. These include a selective use of relevant data, assumptions that lack sufficient empirical support, methodological shortcomings in the treatment and interpretation of the available evidence, and reliance on inadequately controlled archaeological datasets. Given these limitations, we find little support for their claim that proboscideans represented a frequent and easily acquired prey resource during the Pleistocene. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Pastoral Belonging and Educational Opportunity for Mongolian Herder Women
Abstract: As part of the UN’s International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralism (2026) the Gender Working Group stresses the importance of equality in pastoralism. For herder women themes of family, work, schooling and marginality resonate across African and Asian drylands. As environmental, economic and development pressures impact herding women are essential to its continuity. In Mongolia, a prominent pastoralist nation, the role of rural women in household decision-making, livelihood production and community contributions has received little study. In a series of interviews in two rural districts this study explores the practice and knowledge of female herders with a focus on their daily lives. Findings reflect pastoralism in a time of social and livelihood transition. Nature, livestock and tradition were valued whilst family and work responsibilities were arduous. Reflecting perceived challenges and opportunities, experienced herders encouraged daughters to pursue education. Whether growing up in the socialist era or appreciating today’s conveniences, women’s commitment to herding is a vital part of the country’s past nomadic heritage and future direction. As social roles and environmental uncertainty reconfigure pastoralism, female herders are at the forefront of changing rural communities in Mongolia. Title: Distributed neuromorphic computing with temporal co-optimization of spiking dynamics
Abstract: Neuromorphic processors and event-based sensors enable always-on perception, yet training their computational building blocks, namely spiking neural networks (SNNs) across heterogeneous edge devices, is constrained by bandwidth, latency, and energy. This paper studies the systems problem of distributing continuous-time SNN training when computation and communication are driven by sparse spike events. Building on a previously developed exact event-driven single-device learner (ExactTrain) as a local training primitive, we develop distributed protocols, an AER communication abstraction, and the associated convergence, traffic, and system analyses. In particular, we formulate: (i) FedSNN, a federated protocol that matches centralized exact-gradient training under full participation and a one-full-local-gradient regime, (ii) SplitSNN, a split protocol that partitions a model across devices and exchanges address-event representation (AER) spike and error packets, and (iii) HybridSNN, a two-tier split/federated hierarchy that exposes an explicit accuracy-communication trade-off.Experiments on the N-MNIST and DVS Gesture benchmarks evaluate centralized equivalence, split and hybrid traffic, matched-configuration and byte-accounted baseline comparisons, scalability, sensitivity to non-IID data and partition location, and trace-driven network emulation with injected bandwidth limits, jitter, and packet loss. The results reveal that the proposed protocols preserve the timing benefits of exact event-driven local learning while replacing dense activation exchange with sparse spike/error traffic whose scaling is predictable from event rates and cut connectivity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Individual entrepreneurial orientation in Spanish university students: The role of critical thinking disposition and intellectual styles in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: This study proposes a model that links students' disposition toward critical thinking (DTCT), Type I intellectual styles (oriented toward creativity, cognitive complexity, and autonomy) and Type II intellectual styles (oriented toward structure, conformity, and rule adherence), and individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) in higher education. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 208 students enrolled in entrepreneurship-related courses at a Spanish public university, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that DTCT is a strong positive predictor of IEO; Type I intellectual styles are positively related to both DTCT and IEO, whereas Type II styles display negative relations with entrepreneurial orientation. DTCT improves the effect of Type I styles on IEO, but not with Type II styles. These findings suggest that strengthening DTCT is a central pathway through which entrepreneurship education can enhance students' IEO. Title: Integrated system dynamics modeling for sustainable fisheries provisioning services
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fisheries provisioning services deliver food production, livelihoods and ecosystem functions, but are increasingly under pressure from environmental degradation, declining fishery resources and socio-economic stressors. Traditional paradigms in fisheries governance often exhibit a deficiency in accounting for the multidirectional feedback loops linking ecological systems with socio-economic dynamics. The objectives of this study were to develop an integrated system dynamics model to assess interactions between these dimensions and identify management options to improve fisheries provisioning services through long-term scenario simulations. METHODS: A system dynamics model was integrated, consisting of social, environmental, and economic sub-models using primary and secondary data from 2018-2023. The model includes population, fishermen, floating net cages, alternative employment, willingness to be a fisher, water quality and aquatic conditions, fish restocking, capture fisheries production, fisheries productivity, fish processing innovations, income, costs, and fisher's income. The model was verified and validated using the mean absolute error and average variation error metrics. Subsequently, predictive simulations were projected to 2045 under current, moderate, and optimistic scenarios. FINDINGS: Actual capture fisheries production declined by 88.9 percent, from 588,100 kilograms in 2018 to 65,035 kilograms in 2023 and was projected to decline to 31,179 kilograms by 2045 under current conditions. Under the moderate and optimistic scenarios, the number of floating net cages was modeled with an annual reduction rate of 30% and 35%, respectively. Production recovery commenced in 2027 under the moderate scenario and in 2026 under the optimistic scenario. Furthermore, target water quality conditions were achieved by 2041 and 2037, respectively, while fisher's net income reached positive values by 2034. CONCLUSION: The integrated system dynamics model underscores the potential for the sustainability of fishery production services through coordinated actions across social, environmental, and economic dimensions. The faster realization of target outcomes under the optimistic scenario highlights that proactive, coordinated interventions effectively expedite ecological restoration, fisheries output, and socioeconomic progress. This model offers a decision-support framework for assessing long-term fisheries management strategies. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Teaching AI governance in management education: A serious game for accountable decision-making under uncertainty
Abstract: Management education increasingly needs ways to prepare students for AI governance, yet students have limited opportunities to practise the organisational judgement involved in deployment decisions. This paper presents “Leading in the Age of AI”, a card-based serious game in which student teams assume asymmetric C-suite roles, make AI deployment decisions under constraints, and document their reasoning in Model Cards adapted from AI documentation practice. Conceptually, the paper frames AI governance education as accountable decision-making under uncertainty: students negotiate competing priorities, allocate scarce safeguards, respond to disruption, and prepare written accounts for scrutiny. The paper contributes a reusable game design, a pedagogical adaptation of Model Cards as justification artefacts, and design patterns for management-education contexts involving accountable decisions under uncertainty. An exploratory evaluation across two undergraduate cohorts used matched pre-test/post-test data (N=67), post-session evaluations, and descriptive artefact analysis of team-produced Model Cards (n=15). Students evaluated the activity positively and reported immediate confidence gains across knowledge, ethics, and governance composites (dz=0.44 to 1.00), while quiz gains were modest and not statistically significant. Authors: Lehto X.; Lee Y.J.; Chen J.
Title: Dance as destination infrastructure: Toward a progress agenda
Abstract: Tourism destinations increasingly seek embodied, multisensory, and culturally meaningful experiences whose significance extends beyond immediate consumption. Yet tourism management still has a limited vocabulary for explaining how embodied cultural practices generate value across destination systems. This Progress paper uses dance as a focused and theoretically revealing case to address this gap. Rather than treating dance merely as entertainment, heritage representation, or event programming, we conceptualize it as relational, embodied cultural infrastructure through which patterned movement can organize encounters, carry cultural meaning across generations, and contribute to the character and capabilities of destinations. Drawing on tourism's anthropological lineage and interdisciplinary dance scholarship, we develop the Dance Ecosystem for Destinations—a seven-biome framework that distinguishes encounter-level value realization, portfolio-level accumulation and circulation, and cross-cutting technological mediation. The framework expands tourism management's conceptual and diagnostic capacity by linking these biomes to questions of experience design, stewardship, governance, value distribution, and evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
