Title: Lithium extraction and developmental embeddedness in Zimbabwe: Chinese-led investment and local development outcomes
Abstract: Zimbabwe’s rapidly expanding lithium mining sector, dominated by Chinese investment and integrated into global battery and electric vehicle value chains, presents significant opportunities for economic transformation. However, whether this investment generates development benefits for mining-affected communities remains uncertain. This paper examines the extent to which Chinese-led investment contributes to locally experienced development outcomes in Zimbabwe. Drawing on survey data from 230 respondents across six lithium mining sites complemented by stakeholder interviews, field observations, and documentary sources, this study assesses economic outcomes, social responsibility, environmental stewardship, governance and public participation, and physical infrastructure. The findings reveal limited local economic integration and infrastructure development, weak community participation, and significant environmental and social costs. These outcomes are shaped not simply by investor nationality, but by the interaction between corporate practices, globally integrated transition mineral value chains, and fragmented and weakly enforced governance frameworks. The article argues that Zimbabwe’s lithium sector remains weakly developmentally embedded despite rapid production and export growth. It advances the Community-Centered Developmental Embeddedness Framework as an analytical framework for assessing whether transition mineral extraction becomes developmentally embedded through inclusive governance and participation, local economic integration, and environmental and social accountability, supported by coordinated government action. The framework contributes to existing scholarship on transition mineral governance and resource-based development by placing community-level development outcomes at the center of assessing the developmental impacts of extraction. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Crops in Motion: Strontium Isotope Analysis of Cereal Provenance in a Foraging-Oriented Neolithic Economy
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Strontium isotope analysis offers a powerful tool for investigating mobility and provenance in prehistoric contexts, yet its application to archaeobotanical finds remains limited. This study applies ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr analysis to charred cereal grains from Molino Casarotto, an Italian Middle Neolithic wetland site characterised by a foraging-oriented subsistence strategy and unusually limited cereal use compared to contemporary Neolithic farming sites. A locally defined bioavailable ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr baseline was established through systematic sampling of modern plants across distinct lithological units surrounding the site. The isotope ratios of the archaeological cereals reveal a non-local and heterogeneous supply pattern, with values consistent with both regional fluvial units and more radiogenic extra-regional sources. These results provide direct evidence for a spatial decoupling between crop production and consumption and demonstrate the methodological viability of strontium isotopes for tracing cereal provenance. By extending isotopic provenancing to plant remains, this study contributes a new analytical framework for investigating crop circulation and provisioning systems in prehistoric societies. More broadly, it highlights the potential of archaeobotanical isotopic data to address fundamental questions concerning surplus, exchange, and the organisation of economic networks in non-state contexts. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Stage-specific expression and localization of ETRAMP4 during gametocyte development in the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum
Abstract: The early transcribed membrane protein 4 (ETRAMP4) is one of 14 predicted members of the ETRAMP family in the malaria parasite Plasmodium . All characterized ETRAMP proteins localize to the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM) and associated membranous structures during the early stages of parasite infection of erythrocytes; and are thought to participate in host-parasite material transport, which is critical for parasite development. In this study, we investigated the stage-specific expression and subcellular localization of ETRAMP4 during the asexual and gametocyte intraerythrocytic stages. Indirect immunofluorescence assays revealed that ETRAMP4 is prominently detected in immature stage I and II gametocytes; whereas no detectable signal was observed in stage III to V gametocytes or in asexual blood-stage parasites under our experimental conditions. Immunoelectron microscopy demonstrated that ETRAMP4 predominantly localizes to the PVM and PVM-derived membranous structures extending into the host erythrocyte cytoplasm, suggesting a potential role in membrane dynamics during early gametocyte development. Title: Worker-to-ergatoid differentiation is associated with reproductive maturation and DNA repair-related transcriptional remodeling in Reticulitermes chinensis
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: Termite reproductives provide a useful system for examining molecular changes associated with reproductive differentiation because secondary reproductives can arise from worker-like individuals. Here, we compared workers and worker-derived ergatoids of Reticulitermes chinensis to characterize transcriptional changes associated with the acquisition of reproductive status. Histological observations revealed developed gonads containing vitellogenic oocytes in female 10-day post-differentiation ergatoids and spermatids and spermatozoa in male 10-day post-differentiation ergatoids. Transcriptome sequencing, targeted gene set enrichment analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and RT-qPCR revealed caste-associated changes in the expression of genes annotated to DNA repair-related pathways. Gene sets associated with homologous recombination, p53/checkpoint signaling and mismatch repair were significantly positively enriched toward the ergatoid-associated end of the ranked gene list, whereas the Fanconi anemia-related repair gene set showed a positive but non-significant enrichment trend. Several mismatch repair genes, including MSH2, MSH6, and MLH1, showed higher transcript abundance in ergatoids, and MLH1 retained conserved sequence and domain features across representative insects. These findings indicate that worker-to-ergatoid differentiation is associated with reproductive maturation and coordinated transcriptional remodeling of DNA repair-related genes. This study identifies candidate genes and pathways for future functional investigations of genome-maintenance-related processes during reproductive differentiation in termites. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Assessment of a Role-Playing Game’s Effectiveness in Identifying Cattle Herding Strategies at a Wildlife-Livestock Interface in Zimbabwe
Abstract: Natural resource management at the interface between protected areas and communal lands varies across space and time, affecting wildlife and livestock movement patterns. In southern Africa, many communities bordering protected areas are partly agropastoral and rely on access to these areas to graze their cattle. However, farmers face complex decisions about whether to graze cattle inside protected zones or on communal lands, weighing factors such as increased predation risk or exposure to wildlife-borne diseases within protected areas. Social, economic, cultural, and climatic influences further complicate herding strategies and decision-making. We analysed data from a role-playing game co-designed and played by local farmers living near protected areas and communal lands in Zimbabwe to explore their cattle herding practices and the factors driving grazing choices at this wildlife-livestock interface. Multiple correspondence analysis revealed two primary herding strategies. The most prevalent involved grazing cattle inside protected areas during the farming season. The second was a mixed strategy, with farmers grazing cattle both inside protected areas and on communal lands in similar proportions during the transition between agricultural and dry seasons. Grazing decisions were mainly linked to the presence of crops or stored crop residues on communal lands. We observed variations in strategy use under different rainfall scenarios. Our findings can be integrated into an agent-based model to simulate cattle movements at this wildlife-livestock interface. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: IMPORTANCE OF STAKEHOLDERS AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS IN CAMPUS MANAGEMENT
Source title: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
Abstract: Campus managers need to balance the competing claims of different stakeholders of higher education institutions (HEIs). Previous studies in general management have indicated that the decision-making processes are highly related to stakeholders’ attributes (power, legitimacy and urgency). However, such studies have not yet been conducted in the field of campus management. Therefore, this paper aims to identify the importance of key stakeholders in campus development and relevant key performance indicators (KPIs) that are essential for decisionmakers in determining and explaining how their efforts are progressing towards achieving various stakeholders’ goals. To explore the underlying importance of campus stakeholders, a theory on stakeholder salience and a questionnaire survey among Polish public HEIs were employed. In turn, to identify various KPIs, the content analysis of institutions’ strategies was conducted. Empirical research suggests that in Polish public HEIs, authorities and academic staff continue to be regarded as the most important stakeholders (at different stages of the building’s life cycle, respectively). This contrasts with the growing market-oriented approach seen in higher education globally. Moreover, the KPIs presented in HEIs’ strategies are predominantly result-focused and rarely user-centric (which have begun to be perceived as the most significant with respect to building performance). © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Research Competence of a Modern Teacher as a Factor in Improving the Quality of Education and Supporting Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study examines teacher research competence as a factor in improving educational quality and supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Using theoretical analysis, survey data, and economic-mathematical modeling, the study clarifies the structure, conditions, and impact of research competence in modern teaching. Data from 10 secondary school teachers were collected through a questionnaire assessing professional competencies, temperament, motivation, stress resistance, and burnout. Communicative and methodological competencies were strongest, while research, managerial, digital, and inclusive competencies need further development. Research competence was positively related to intrinsic motivation and methodological competence. The study proposes a three-component model integrating research practice, professional communities, and motivational support to strengthen evidence-based teaching and sustainable educational improvement. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

Authors: Tian J.; Zhang Q.; Liu Y.
Title: Government subsidy policy and farmer’s live-streaming strategy in the fresh agricultural products supply chain
Abstract: Live-streaming serves as an effective means to promote the sales of fresh agricultural products. Farmers cooperate with streamers for live-streaming through the direct or resale live-streaming strategy. The third-party logistics service provider offers cold-chain services to maintain the freshness of agricultural products. Meanwhile, the government provides subsidies to farmers, streamers, or consumers. Motivated by this background, this study investigates a farmer’s choice of live-streaming strategy and its impact on other supply chain members. We find that, first, when streamer traffic is high, the farmer should adopt the resale live-streaming strategy. When streamer traffic is low, the farmer should adopt the direct live-streaming strategy if the government subsidizes farmers or consumers; if the government subsidizes streamers, the farmer’s decision on live-streaming strategy is also affected by unit subsidy. Second, the high-traffic streamer always prefers the resale live-streaming strategy, whereas the low-traffic streamer’s preference for the live-streaming strategy depends on the government subsidy policy. Finally, if streamer traffic is low (high) and subsidy is low, the government can promote the sales of fresh agricultural products, increase the farmer’s profit, and improve social welfare by subsidizing farmers (streamers); otherwise, subsidizing consumers may improve social welfare, but it is not conducive to the sales of fresh agricultural products or farmer’s profit. Furthermore, we conduct an extension study with an endogenous subsidy to verify the robustness of the main results. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Bone Surface Mapping: A New Method for Recording Detailed Human Bone Surface Variation
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Surface changes on bone can be indicative of a range of different processes affecting an individual, from palaeopathology and taphonomy to cultural modification. Mapping these changes is essential to understanding bioarchaeological context and compare the changes across an individual and between them. This paper presents a new method for mapping surface features on bone (e.g. erosion/abrasion, surface cuts and scratches, pathologies, modifications). It is an accessible and quantifiable alternative to photogrammetry or three-dimensional scanning. It breaks each bone down into a number of two-dimensional geometric faces that can be utilised in statistical analyses. The number of faces differs depending on the skeletal development of the individual. The recording method allows faces to be grouped by anatomical plane, bone type, side, and region of the body. These selective groupings facilitate flexible categories for hypothesis testing. The technique was developed to enable a detailed recording of taphonomic staining on human skeletal remains from Khok Phanom Di, Thailand. While the technique was developed for recording bone surface staining, it could also be used to map other variations on bone surfaces, such as in palaeopathological, forensic, or taphonomic contexts. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Carney M.
Author full names: Carney, Molly (57210151985)
Title: Archaeologies of Indigenous Foodways and Collective Capacities
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Recent archaeological scholarship has embraced food security and food sovereignty frameworks to connect past foodways to present-day crises. However, these studies require critical examination of the colonial origins and ideological foundations of these frameworks, which emerged from industrialized western economic paradigms that do not align with Indigenous worldviews. Drawing on food studies scholarship, I argue that archaeologists must move beyond the uncritical adoption of food security and sovereignty frameworks to embrace culturally grounded paradigms developed by and for descendant communities. This paper advocates for reframing North American archaeological investigations of foodways through Indigenous philosopher Kyle Powys Whyte’s concept of collective capacities: webs of relationships among humans, non-human beings, and landscapes organized together to support responses to change and continuance. As a linking tool, collective capacities help archaeologists carry out the material and analytical work that Indigenous Food Sovereignty movements call for. An archaeology of collective capacities shifts our focus to understanding how food systems functioned as relational infrastructures of care, responsibility, and reciprocity that sustained communities across millennia. In this contribution I outline an archaeological framework identifying key material signatures of collective capacities. Applying this framework to the Pend Oreille Valley in northeastern Washington State, I demonstrate how paleoethnobotanical and archaeological data from the last 1500 years reveal Indigenous food systems were sustained through active management, coordinated labor, and intergenerational knowledge transmission across climatic and sociopolitical changes. I also consider how contemporary practices of reciprocity and relationality mirror the archaeological record of stability and stewardship. By centering culture-specific terminology and philosophies, an archaeology of collective capacities offers a methodological and theoretical approach that supports, rather than imposes frameworks upon, past societies while documenting the enduring systems that enabled communities to thrive across deep time. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Pan B.; Bi X.; Liu Z.; Ma Y.
Title: Breaking the cycle of malice: Influence mechanism and intervention of social exclusion on malevolent creativity in adolescents
Abstract: Creativity is the core driving force for humans to break through existing boundaries and promote continuous social progress, and its positive impacts have been widely recognized. However, creativity also has a dark side, namely, malevolent creativity, which poses significant potential harm to society. Therefore, it is necessary and meaningful to conduct research on malevolent creativity to prevent its negative impacts. Based on the 4P model of creativity, this study explored the impact mechanism between social exclusion and malevolent creativity (Study 1) and the effectiveness of a group counseling intervention for self-concept clarity (Study 2). Study 1 conducted a field questionnaire survey (N = 1567). The results showed that social exclusion not only directly increased malevolent creativity, but also indirectly predicted it through the independent mediating effects of reduced self-concept clarity and heightened negative emotions, as well as through the serial mediating effect whereby reduced self-concept clarity led to increased negative emotions, which in turn predicted malevolent creativity. Trait mindfulness moderated the impact of social exclusion on self-concept clarity, with higher levels of trait mindfulness alleviating the negative effects of social exclusion on self-concept clarity. Study 2 utilized a group counseling intervention (N = 30) and demonstrated that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in self-concept clarity and a significant decrease in malevolent creativity after the intervention. The study's conclusions provide educators with references and insights for correctly understanding the impact of social exclusion and for offering interventions to enhance self-concept clarity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises: The roles of technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality in an ai-driven business environment
Abstract: The tourism industry is experiencing unprecedented transformation driven by digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, and the rapid evolution of smart tourism ecosystems. At the same time, tourism enterprises face growing pressure to enhance service quality while controlling operational costs and improving managerial responsiveness. In this context, management accounting effectiveness has become a critical capability for supporting strategic decision-making and maintaining sustainable competitiveness. Although previous studies have examined digital transformation and accounting systems separately, limited attention has been paid to how technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality jointly influence management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises operating in emerging economies. Addressing this research gap, the present study investigates the effects of these three determinants on management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism enterprises. Grounded in the resource-based view, contingency theory, dynamic capabilities theory, and sociotechnical systems theory, the study adopts a mixed-method research design consisting of expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. Data were collected from 315 tourism enterprises, with chief accountants, general accountants, and management accounting personnel serving as key respondents. The data were analyzed using SPSS through reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The empirical findings demonstrate that technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality all exert positive and statistically significant effects on management accounting effectiveness. Among these determinants, information technology infrastructure emerges as the strongest predictor, followed by technology readiness and data quality. These findings indicate that tourism enterprises equipped with integrated digital infrastructure, advanced technological capabilities, and high-quality accounting data are better positioned to generate timely, accurate, and strategically relevant management accounting information in AI-enabled business environments. This study extends the literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging economy and contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital transformation and management accounting. The findings also offer practical implications for tourism managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen digital accounting capabilities, improve managerial decision-making, and enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of tourism enterprises in the era of AI-driven business transformation. Title: An advanced integrated cross-sectoral model for formulating government strategies on energy consumption management to reduce greenhouse gas emissions toward achieving net-zero emissions in the future
Abstract: This study aims to develop a model that identifies alternative scenarios for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by examining the interrelationships among the circular economy, socio-cultural, and environmental sectors, with the ultimate goal of supporting Thailand's net-zero emissions target. Using a mixed-methods research design, the study provides a foundation for developing integrated national management strategies that promote long-term sustainability. A novel model, referred to as the Path–Probit–Logit–ARx Model (Path Analysis–Probit–Logit Model based on Autoregressive with Exogenous Variables), was developed to address the study objectives. The findings reveal that, during the period 1992–2025, the circular economy sector experienced continuous growth, which directly contributed to the steady expansion of the socio-cultural sector. The growth of both sectors also exerted a positive influence on the environmental sector. Furthermore, the environmental sector was found to have a direct positive effect on the socio-cultural sector, indicating a bidirectional relationship between these two sectors. This finding suggests that environmentally responsible societies can promote long-term ecosystem development and that environmental and social development should progress concurrently. Based on the analysis, the study identified the adoption of electric vehicles as the most sensitive and effective scenario for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Under this scenario, the growth rate of final energy consumption is reduced to 33%, while greenhouse gas emission growth decreases to 53.73%, remaining below the critical threshold of 590.05 Mt CO2 equivalent and thereby meeting the government's target. To enhance the policy relevance and credibility of the findings, a focus group consisting of 15 experts was conducted to validate the results. The experts confirmed the appropriateness and accuracy of the proposed scenario and agreed that it is suitable for promoting sustainable development in Thailand. However, they emphasized the need for immediate action and strong governmental support to ensure effective implementation. Therefore, the findings of this study can support evidence-based decision-making and strategic planning, contributing to the development of Thailand's long-term national strategies through 2065. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Examining primary students’ mathematical communication through the lens of de Bono’s practical thinking processes
Abstract: Mathematical thinking is a complex, multi-faceted process that typically involves both intra-personal and interpersonal communication. While it has been described as messy and difficult, it can also show growth and insight into conceptual understanding and knowing. This paper explores the application of Edward de Bono's practical thinking processes to examine the mathematical thinking processes that primary school students use. de Bono’s perspective is relevant as it foregrounds thinking as an active developmental process, providing the metalanguage to describe children’s communication of their mathematical thinking. The research was conducted in a small regional South Australian school where the entire school population (n = 36) was divided into two classes. The two-phase research first used participant (n = 23) drawings, written descriptions, and interviews about their drawings to document retrospective accounts of the processes students used to engage and to communicate their mathematical thinking. Analysis of the data from this phase was then used to inform subsequent class observations (n = 20) conducted to identify the processes of practical thinking used in-the-moment during mathematical learning experiences. By applying the foundations of de Bono's practical thinking, this paper offers insights into the potential benefits of integrating the tenets of practical thinking into mathematics education. The analysis identifies how primary students engage and use connect-up thinking, carry-on thinking, and porridge words as core processes which facilitate the communication and development of their mathematical understanding. Of note is the emergence of different forms of connect-up thinking, and students’ creative use of porridge words. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Examining the Prevalence and Impact of Sleep Disorders among Dental Interns, Postgraduates and Dental Staff
Source title: Pesquisa Brasileira em Odontopediatria e Clinica Integrada
Abstract: Objective: To assess the prevalence of sleep disorders among dentists in private and public tertiary care hospitals in Peshawar, Pakistan. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in four major hospitals, including two private and two government institutions. Dentists, including dental interns, postgraduates, and staff, participated in the study. Data were collected using the Epworth Daytime Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and analyzed in SPSS. This study used descriptive statistics, t-tests, multivariate regression, and chi-square tests to examine associations between sleep disorders and sociodemographic factors. Results: Among the 570 participants, the mean age was 27.67 ± 2.67 years. The prevalence of sleep disorders was 65%, with a mean ESS score of 11.80 ± 3.64. Dental postgraduates exhibited the highest levels of moderate to severe sleep disorders. No significant association was found between sleep disorders and gender or workplace. However, job designation was significantly associated with sleep disturbances (p = 0.007). Work output and efficacy, personal changes, workplace environment, and gender were significant predictors of sleep disorders. Conclusion: Addressing sleep disorders among dentists requires comprehensive strategies, including organizational changes, stress management support, and workload reduction. Future research should explore interventions to enhance sleep quality and assess the long-term impacts on dentists' well-being and patient care outcomes. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). Title: Human Factors and Safety Communication in Engineering Safety Performance: A Predictive PLS-SEM Model for Petrochemical Operations
Abstract: Petrochemical operations are complex engineering systems in which safety performance depends not only on technical safeguards and process controls but also on human and organisational factors that influence how workers perceive, interpret, and respond to safety requirements. Despite advances in engineering controls and occupational safety management systems, incidents continue to occur, highlighting the need to integrate human factors into engineering safety management. This study develops and evaluates a predictive model of engineering safety performance by examining the effects of two culturally embedded human factors, religiosity and fatalism, together with safety communication effectiveness in Malaysian petrochemical operations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 463 employees and contractors from major petrochemical facilities in Malaysia. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. The structural model showed that religiosity significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.442, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while fatalism significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.451, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.378, p < 0.001). In contrast, safety communication effectiveness did not directly predict safety performance (β = −0.006, p = 0.954). The model explained 74.7% of the variance in safety communication effectiveness and 61.2% of the variance in safety performance. These findings demonstrate that engineering safety performance in high-risk petrochemical operations cannot be addressed solely through technical controls and communication systems. Integrating culturally embedded human factors with organisational safety mechanisms provides a more comprehensive approach to engineering safety management and supports the development of human-centred safety interventions for complex industrial operations. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. Title: An Analysis of Interactive and Interactional Metadiscourse Markers in Applied Linguistics Webinars: The Case of Top-Tier Native vs. Non-Native Speaking Scholars
Abstract: Within the ecosystem of genres, audiences, and modalities, knowledge dissemination relies on metadiscourse markers that guide and engage academic audiences. Despite digital technologies reshaping communication after the pandemic, their use in academic webinars, especially regarding speakers’ linguistic backgrounds, remains an underresearched area of inquiry. Accordingly, this study aimed to comprehensively analyze interactive and interactional metadiscourse markers utilized by both top-tier native and non-native scholars in Applied Linguistics webinars. To this end, a corpus of 24 webinars (24 hours and 35 minutes) conducted by top-tier Applied Linguists over five years was purposively selected and analyzed using Hyland’s (2005) metadiscourse model, focusing on the frequency and distribution of interactive and interactional markers. The results showed that native scholars employed metadiscourse markers (both interactive and interactional) somewhat more frequently than non-natives, though both groups used them extensively to organize and engage audiences. While natives favored interactional markers over interactive ones, non-natives demonstrated the opposite trend, relying more on interactive than interactional markers. These findings highlight the need for EAP/ESP pedagogy to extend beyond accuracy, fostering non-native scholars’ interactional competence through training in hedges, boosters, attitude markers, and self-mentions, empowering them to communicate confidently, engage audiences, and sustain presence in global academia. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Pathways to peace: understanding the role of grassroots movements in countering radicalization and promoting stability in Jammu and Kashmir
Abstract: Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), long marked by political instability, economic deprivation, and socio-religious fault lines, has become a fertile ground for radicalization. While mainstream counter-radicalization strategies have relied on state-led top-down developmental initiatives, grassroots movements have emerged as transformative actors addressing the root causes of extremism. This paper investigates the efficacy of grassroots initiatives in countering radicalization in J&K through a multi-theoretical lens and supported by field interviews. Employing models such as Moghaddam’s Staircase to Terrorism, Wiktorowicz’s Theory of Cognitive Openings, and Relative Deprivation Theory, it evaluates the structural and psychosocial conditions that fuel extremism and how locally-rooted programs neutralize them. The paper argues that the fusion of youth engagement, women’s empowerment, economic inclusion, and digital literacy has yielded a resilient counter-narrative that deserves formal integration into national policy frameworks. By analysing field-based insights and contextualizing global peacebuilding precedents, the study proposes a strategic reorientation toward grassroots-led deradicalization. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

Title: Temporal water-quality variability and its implications for environmental management of sand lobster aquaculture
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable management of sand lobster aquaculture is often limited by monitoring approaches that summarize environmental conditions using long-term averages, obscuring short-term extremes and spatial variation. The study objectives were to characterize spatial and temporal variations in water quality within a floating net cage aquaculture system, identify their underlying physical drivers, evaluate whether longitudinal growth is governed more by culture duration, initial size, and stocking density than by environmental exposure alone, and translate these empirical relationships into a transferable environmental monitoring framework. METHODS: The study collected longitudinal growth and environmental data from floating net cage culture in Indonesia. Monitoring covered temperature, salinity, oxygen concentration, potential of hydrogen, and nutrient concentrations across three water depths and multiple sampling times. Non-parametric statistical tests were employed to evaluate depth-dependent variations in dissolved oxygen, while correlation and regression analysis assessed the relationships between wind speed, water temperature, and dissolved oxygen levels. Multivariate statistical ordination summarized dominant environmental gradients, and mixed-effects statistical models, compared through an information-theoretic model selection approach, captured longitudinal growth. FINDINGS: Dissolved oxygen concentration differed significantly among depths (test statistic 29.27, probability below 0.001), declining by close to a fifth from the surface to three and ten meters. Monthly wind speed closely tracked the concurrent decline in temperature closely (correlation coefficient -0.988, probability below 0.002) but exhibited no statistically significant association with dissolved oxygen, consistent with a wind-driven transition observed during this production cycle. Culture duration, initial size class, and stocking density together explained total length best, with an additive model carrying more than seventy percent of the statistical weight among six candidate models. Growth rate exhibited its strongest association with low-oxygen exposure, followed by temperature and potential of hydrogen condition, an interpretation that warrants caution given the limited independent exposure intervals available. CONCLUSION: Successful sand lobster aquaculture requires an adaptive environmental monitoring architecture that accounts for depth-related oxygen stratification and wind-driven seasonal variability, alongside coordinated management of culture duration, initial seed size, and stocking density. The analytical framework of integrated site assessment and management for lobster can be adapted to other marine aquaculture systems through the inclusion of species-specific biological indicators and management variables. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Integrated Waste-to-Energy Systems: A comprehensive review of Technologies, decision Frameworks, and sustainability metrics
Abstract: Rising waste generation and growing energy demand have driven global interest in Waste-to-Energy (WtE) systems as a pathway toward sustainable waste management and resource recovery. However, existing WtE reviews remain fragmented: most are technology-centric, focusing on individual conversion routes, while others address environmental performance, economic feasibility, or decision-making methods in isolation, without linking them to waste characteristics or site-specific conditions. This limits the ability of researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders to systematically select suitable WtE solutions for specific regional contexts. This review addresses this gap by first characterizing major waste streams—municipal solid, industrial, agricultural and forestry, sewage sludge, medical, e-waste, and construction and demolition waste—and evaluating their compatibility with thermal (incineration, gasification, pyrolysis), biological (anaerobic digestion, landfill gas recovery), and emerging hybrid conversion technologies. It then examines site-specific factors governing WtE deployment, including economic conditions, geographic and logistical constraints, regulatory and policy drivers, and social acceptance. Building on these dimensions, the review proposes a novel conceptual 3D matrix framework integrating waste type, technology suitability, and site characteristics into a unified selection platform, and synthesizes multi-criteria decision analysis approaches supported by case study synthesis. Environmental and economic performance is further consolidated through life cycle assessment, levelized cost of energy, and circular economy indicators to establish a holistic sustainability assessment methodology. Finally, the review identifies key challenges in emission control, investment uncertainty, resource recovery, and public acceptance, and outlines future opportunities in AI-assisted optimization, carbon capture integration, and circular economy-driven WtE systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Economic design of residential solar resources under uncertainty: An adaptive robust optimization approach for EV households
Abstract: The integration of residential PV systems with electric vehicles (EVs) offers significant opportunities to enhance self-consumption, reduce reliance on the grid, and lower household energy costs. Effective PV system sizing, however, is challenged by uncertainties in PV generation, household electricity demand, and EV charging behavior. While traditional approaches often ignore uncertainties or assume predefined values for uncertainties, this paper develops an adaptive robust optimization framework for sizing residential PV systems in EV-integrated households, explicitly accounting for operational uncertainties and calibrating the uncertainty parameters using a Genetic Algorithm. The proposed model explicitly incorporates multi-source uncertainty using a budgeted adaptive robust optimization approach. Investment decisions, such as PV capacity, are modeled as here-and-now variables, while operational variability is captured as wait-and-see decisions responding to uncertainty realizations. To mitigate the inherent conservatism of robust optimization and identify optimal uncertainty settings, a Genetic Algorithm–based calibration is integrated. The GA iteratively searches for the best combination of uncertainty parameters through simulation-based evaluation, balancing robustness and economic efficiency. The results show that calibrated uncertainty parameters provide a cost-effective and resilient system design, avoiding oversized PV capacities while improving household energy performance by reducing the cost of energy up to 18%. © 2026

Title: A Tale of Two Styles: Exploring the Compatibilities and Incompatibilities among Learning and Teaching Styles in Second Language Didactics
Abstract: The process of teaching and learning is a complex interplay of multiple factors, including teaching and learning styles. A mismatch between these styles can lead to negative outcomes. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the learning styles of non-Iranian Persian language learners and the teaching styles of their instructors. To explore the alignment and discrepancies between these variables, a quantitative method was employed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between them. This research was conducted with a sample size of 116 Persian language learners and 25 teachers, and data on learning styles were collected using the Perceptual Learning Style Preference Questionnaire (PLSPQ). The same questionnaire was adapted and validated to collect data on teaching styles. The study revealed no significant difference in the prioritization of visual, tactile, auditory, and kinesthetic learning styles between learners and teachers. However, a notable difference was observed in group and individual learning styles. Furthermore, academic background emerged as a crucial factor affecting teaching style, with teachers who had completed a teaching Persian program (AZFA) prioritizing group-style instruction. The outcomes of this research underscored the existence of discernible disparities between the teaching styles of educators and the learning styles of students. As such, it was recommended that teachers adjust their teaching styles to align with the learning styles of their students. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. All rights reserved.

Title: Offshore infrastructure decommissioning, just transitions, and the struggle for the right to the sea: Small-scale fishers’ perspectives from coastal Ghana
Abstract: Offshore petroleum infrastructure decommissioning is usually framed as a technical and environmental process requiring technical expertise. Yet, offshore infrastructure decommissioning could have deleterious consequences on adjacent coastal communities and livelihoods. Drawing on qualitative data from 65 respondents from Ghanaian coastal communities of Saltpond and Kormantse, this paper investigates small-scale fishers’ experiences of offshore oil and gas infrastructure decommissioning. The paper frames decommissioning as a critical phase of energy transition and interrogates its outcomes through the dual lenses of just transitions and the “right to the sea.” The findings reveal that decommissioning produces socio-ecological and economic disruptions. These include the creation of offshore safety zones leading to spatial exclusion of fishing activities, the erosion of socio-ecological knowledge systems, material precarity through asset loss, and ecological uncertainty linked to perceptions of pollution. While these processes are officially justified on grounds of safety and environmental protection, they are experienced locally as forms of livelihood dispossession and governance exclusion. The study argues that decommissioning represents an unjust transition, in which the challenges associated with post-extractive restructuring are disproportionately shifted onto vulnerable coastal communities. At the same time, it is a struggle over the right to the sea, as regulatory and security mechanisms reconfigure access to marine space in ways that privilege state and industrial actors over fisherfolk. The paper concludes that achieving socially just and sustainable decommissioning outcomes requires moving beyond technical compliance toward inclusive governance frameworks that recognise local knowledge, ensure equitable access to marine resources, and address the livelihood impacts of transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Transforming value of sustainability in urban development: Reconfiguring logistics service in the construction industry
Abstract: Urban development depends on construction activity to improve sustainability, yet the logistics required to move materials, equipment, waste, and workers remains insufficiently integrated into urban planning. This paper examines how construction logistics can be integrated into municipal urban planning by analysing how actor groups perceive its impacts and coordinate value creation across fragmented urban systems. The study applies a qualitative interactive research design based on a Swedish construction logistics project. Data were collected between August 2022 and March 2024 through eight semi-structured group interviews, joint workshops, actor-specific validation workshops, and a final synthesis workshop with developers, main contractors, suppliers, and trade organizations. The analysis combines iterative thematic coding with value configuration theory. The findings show that suppliers emphasize efficiency and climate savings, main contractors focus on project efficiency and safety, developers stress sustainability, accessibility and accountability, while trade organizations highlight knowledge-building and sector coordination. These differences create misalignment because societal benefits are often separated from project-level costs. Four conditions are identified as central: clearer procurement requirements, stronger logistics knowledge, scalable logistics service designs, and systematic follow-up of time, cost, and emission effects. The paper concludes that municipalities should use procurement, planning requirements and follow-up mechanisms to enforce construction logistics values in urban planning. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Self-report measures of mindfulness for children: convergent validity, predictive validity, and impacts of social desirability bias
Abstract: Mindfulness-based interventions have shown promise in supporting psychological well-being in children. However, mindfulness is commonly measured using self-report questionnaires, a method that might be problematic due to its reliance on children’s accurate self-perceptions of their own mindfulness and the potential influence of social desirability bias. In the current study, we examined the convergent validity, the predictive validity, and the influence of social desirability bias on three mindfulness self-report measures for children ages 9–13 years (N = 109). Results showed that children’s self-reported mindfulness demonstrated good convergent validity and predictive validity, as higher levels of self-reported mindfulness were positively associated with higher levels of parent-reported executive functioning. Self-reported mindfulness also covaried with social desirability bias. However, controlling for this bias did not substantively affect the convergent validity nor the predictive validity of self-reported mindfulness. These findings suggest that children’s self-reported mindfulness also captures social desirability bias, but this bias may not affect conclusions about mindfulness when assessed as a latent factor across multiple measures. Future work measuring children’s mindfulness with self-reports should account for social desirability bias when possible, as well as explore objective methods of assessing mindfulness in children. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Hot war tourism: The touristification of unresolved conflict
Abstract: This article conceptualises hot war tourism as the touristification of unresolved conflict: configurations in which conflict continues materially to shape civilian vulnerability, security and visitor access while conflict-affected places and experiences acquire experiential, representational or market value. A critical integrative review clarifies its boundaries with dark, battlefield, military, risk, recovery and solidarity-oriented tourism and identifies five dimensions: temporal immediacy, spatial proximity, commodification, moral and motivational ambiguity, and governance and responsibility. Ukraine and Syria illustrate contrasting active-war witnessing and recovery–normalisation configurations. A relational framework locates war-related tourism according to the degree of unresolved conflict and the intensity of touristification, while a multi-actor governance framework specifies responsibilities for access, risk disclosure, representation, consent, platform accountability, humanitarian non-interference and escalation. The concept links tourism value production to unresolved harm and provides a basis for analysing when conflict-related visitation requires facilitation, restraint or restriction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java: The roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, innovation capability, and ESG
Abstract: This study examines the determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java by analyzing the roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) implementation, innovation capability, and organizational performance. Social enterprises in emerging economies increasingly face challenges in maintaining long-term sustainability due to resource limitations, institutional uncertainty, and dynamic social demands. Although previous studies have explored intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, ESG practices, and innovation capability separately, limited empirical research has integrated these variables into a comprehensive sustainability model within the context of social enterprises in emerging economies, particularly Indonesia. Therefore, this study seeks to address this gap by developing and testing an integrated model of social enterprise sustainability. This research adopts a quantitative approach using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Data were collected from 200 owners and managers of social enterprises operating across six provinces on Java Island. Social enterprise performance also demonstrates a significant mediating role in achieving long-term sustainability. Title: Who fights best? Discovering winning personality pairings for LLM debate agents
Abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, most MAD systems employ personality-neutral agents and overlook the role of personality, which has been shown in psychology and behavioral science to influence reasoning styles and collaborative problem-solving. In this study, we introduce MBTI-DB, a debate framework for systematically studying the impact of personality in MAD. We design 16 distinct personality profiles and inject them into debates in a modular manner. Through experiments across four LLM families and 700 factual questions, we demonstrate that incorporating personality induces systematic and measurable accuracy shifts. Further analysis reveals that lexical density, personality-question similarity, and prompt perplexity influence these accuracy variations. We evaluate personality-pair selection strategies and find that retrospectively selecting the best-performing pair for each question yields significant gains as an oracle upper bound. However, automatically identifying the best configuration remains challenging with substantial cross-model variation, suggesting that while personality diversity offers meaningful performance benefits, its effects are complex and context-dependent. Title: Reflection quality and psychological safety as mechanisms of development in virtual management education
Abstract: This study examines the mechanisms linking behavioral participation in virtual management education to developmental learning outcomes. Drawing on experiential learning theory (ELT), this study investigates whether reflection quality mediates the relationship between behavioral participation and student development and whether team psychological safety moderates the participation–reflection relationship. Data were collected from an eight-week multicultural virtual leadership program involving 74 business students working in nine multicultural teams. To reduce common method concerns, this study integrated six independent sources of evidence: instructor activity logs, coded reflection reports, pre- and post-program competency surveys, psychological safety ratings, peer evaluations, and instructor-assessed team-performance scores. The findings indicate that higher behavioral participation is associated with deeper reflective responses. Reflection quality is more consistently associated with gains in cultural intelligence (CQ) and global leadership competency than participation alone. Furthermore, the relationship between participation and reflection is stronger in teams characterized by higher psychological safety, highlighting the importance of supportive learning environments in fostering reflective practices. Because reflection depth and post-program outcomes were assessed at the same measurement occasion, the mediation findings are interpreted as theory-consistent associative evidence rather than causal proof. Overall, the results are consistent with a sociocognitive extension of ELT, in which experiential learning is shaped not only by individual cognitive processing but also by the interpersonal safety of the team environment. For management educators, the findings emphasize three design priorities: systematic monitoring of behavioral participation, scaffolding and assessing reflection quality, and intentionally cultivating psychologically safe learning environments to enhance developmental outcomes in virtual management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From eco-signals to green trust: How tourists evaluate sustainability credibility through online reviews
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Growing sustainability claims in tourism have intensified concerns about credibility and greenwashing. This study examines how tourists interpret environmental practices by analyzing 138,683 online reviews from major Southeast and East Asian coastal and island destinations. Drawing on signaling theory and attribution theory, the study proposes that observable sustainability cues are associated with eco-authenticity inference, which is linked to green trust and, in turn, more positive review sentiment. Using natural language processing, topic modeling, regression analysis, mediation analysis, and robustness checks for sparse text-derived variables, the findings show a positive association between eco-signal richness and eco-authenticity inference, as well as a significant indirect association from eco-authenticity inference to sentiment through green trust. Eco-authenticity inference is not directly associated with more positive sentiment once green trust is included. Because the focal sustainability, authenticity, and trust expressions are infrequent and have median values of zero, the findings identify a consistent but sparse textual pattern rather than a large or pervasive psychological effect. Because the Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner (VADER) is English-oriented, VADER-based sentiment models were also checked using the English-language subset; the qualitative pattern remained consistent. Topic modeling provides supplementary contextual evidence that sustainability discourse in reviews is episodic and grounded in concrete visitor experiences. Abstract: This study investigates the simultaneous utilization of mineralized mass (MM) from Central Kyzylkum phosphorite waste and acidic wastewater (AWW) from the soapstock processing industry for efficient fluoride removal. The MM was chemically activated by AWW under controlled conditions, leading to surface modification, increased porosity, and enhanced active site heterogeneity. The chemical interaction between H⁺ ions from AWW and fluorapatite in MM resulted in ion exchange, dissolution of phosphate groups, and the formation of volatile HF. Adsorption experiments were conducted at various MM: AWW ratios to determine the optimal operating parameters. Equilibrium data were fitted to the Freundlich isotherm model, confirming multilayer adsorption on heterogeneous surfaces. Kinetic analysis indicated that the pseudo-second-order (PSO) model provided the best fit, suggesting that chemisorption is the dominant rate-limiting mechanism. The Weber–Morris intra-particle diffusion model revealed that pore diffusion contributes to fluoride uptake but is not the sole controlling step. The synergy between isotherm and kinetic results supports a two-stage adsorption process involving rapid surface chemisorption followed by slower intraparticle diffusion. The developed method offers a dual environmental benefit by valorizing two industrial waste streams and reducing their ecological footprint. The produced sorbent showed high fluoride removal efficiency under simulated operational conditions. The process is simple, cost-effective, and compatible with existing industrial infrastructures. Large-scale application has the potential to reduce operational costs and promote circular economy principles. Title: Can a transversal adaptation of teaching materials foster students’ entrepreneurial intentions? A quasi-experimental exploration in a statistics course setting
Abstract: We propose that a transversal integration of entrepreneurship content within other curricula may be an effective approach to foster students' entrepreneurial intentions. We embedded entrepreneurship content in an otherwise unrelated statistics course targeting the theory of planned behavior constructs of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms in relation to entrepreneurship. 350 Swiss students (193 intervention group, 157 control group) participated in a nine-week quasi-experiment to explore the effects of this intervention. Structural equation modeling suggests that being in the intervention group affected students' attitude toward entrepreneurship, which in turn was associated with higher entrepreneurial intentions by the end of the intervention. The intervention did not affect perceived behavioral control nor subjective norms and changes in these variables were neither associated with change in entrepreneurial intentions. Unexpectedly, the intervention did not improve students' attitude ratings but appeared to prevent their decline over time. A qualitative follow-up exploration with seven participants suggested that the data collection itself may have prompted students to reassess their attitude toward entrepreneurship. Title: Motivational Aspects of Teacher Feedback Practices: Development and Validation of a Questionnaire Based on Students’ Perceptions
Abstract: This study developed the Motivational Aspects of Teacher Feedback Practices Questionnaire (MATFP-Q), designed to examine students’ perceptions on six key types of teacher feedback—task-focused, specific, self-referenced, normative, next-step, and person-focused—from a motivational perspective. The instrument’s theoretical foundation integrates Hattie and Timperley’s (2007) feedback model with Koenka and Anderman’s (2019) principles for motivation-supportive feedback. Validation was conducted with a sample of 1,079 Chinese secondary school students. Student workshops were conducted to ensure ecological and cognitive validation, and expert reviews were used to establish content validation. Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to identify the underlying factor structure, and confirmatory factor analysis provided evidence for the structural validity of the proposed six-factor model (χ² = 902.49, df = 309, p < .001, CFI = .920, TLI = .909, SRMR = .059, and RMSEA = .042 [90% CI = .039, .045]). The internal consistency of the subscales (Cronbach’s α = .69–.86) ranged from acceptable to excellent. Furthermore, correlations among the MATFP-Q subscales indicated that the instrument captures related but distinguishable aspects of teacher feedback. In addition, the expected pattern of correlations with students’ perceptions of teachers’ goals and mindset belief provided evidence for convergent and divergent validity. Title: When static Volt–VAr control helps and when it does not: Operational and planning lessons from a weak radial distribution feeder
Abstract: Long radial distribution feeders are increasingly exposed to sustained undervoltage as electrification-driven load growth outpaces reinforcement. Static inverter Volt–VAr curves are attractive because they can be deployed through existing controller settings, but standard curves may be too conservative for electrically weak feeders. This paper evaluates the operational and planning value of feeder-specific static Volt–VAr settings under data conditions commonly available to distribution system operators: sparse voltage measurements, hourly feeder-level inputs, and offline parameter updates. The study applies the slope-selection procedure developed in [1] to a predefined BESS Volt–VAr curve and evaluates the resulting setting through quasi-static time-series power flow for a real 22 kV radial feeder in Northern Norway. During the constructed 168 h high-load/no-generation stress period, the model-based, condition-matched comparison produced 153 h within the adopted target band with the full feeder-specific setting, compared with 8 h under the IEEE 1547-type setting and 1 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. An independent 2025 operating period was used for quantitative comparison with field measurements. The model reproduced the average voltage and voltage-band occupancy, while the disagreement in hourly variation limits its use to comparative screening rather than point-by-point prediction. The transferred feeder-specific setting produced 0 h outside the target band, compared with 16 h under the IEEE-type curve and 55 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. Higher-resolution measurements from the BESS and hydropower plant were used separately to examine interaction between the two local controllers. Under the 59% industrial-growth stress scenario, 4 MVAr was the smallest tested reactive-power rating that kept all 168 hourly voltages at or above the lower limit of the adopted target band after feeder-specific slope selection. The results provide a practical DSO screening procedure: test static tuning first, then identify whether the remaining limitation is curve setting, VAr headroom, or interaction between independently controlled assets. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Human capital development through community digital centers for inequality reduction in Thailand
Abstract: Driving human capital development through community digital centers to reduce inequality requires multiple interrelated factors and components to ensure successful implementation. This study aims to examine the mechanisms of human capital development through community digital centers and to analyze the causal factors influencing human capital across various dimensions, with the goal of synthesizing practical recommendations for integrated community digital centers that support economic and social development. A mixed-methods approach was employed, consisting of quantitative research using questionnaires administered to 398 participants selected through accidental sampling with proportional allocation, along with qualitative research conducted through in-depth interviews with seven community digital center administrators selected using purposive sampling. The quantitative data were analyzed using Pearson's correlation coefficient and multiple regression analysis. The findings revealed that digital infrastructure, organizational management, personnel competency, and community participation were positively correlated with human capital development. The results of the multiple regression analysis indicated that digital infrastructure (B = 0.137), organizational management (B = 0.244), personnel competency (B = 0.225), and community participation (B = 0.303) significantly influenced human capital development through community digital centers to reduce inequality (p < 0.05). Title: Social and Spiritual Aspects Affecting Psychosocial Well-Being Among Early- and Late-Stage Oral Cancer Patients Presenting with Restricted Oral Functioning
Source title: Journal of Health Science and Medical Research
Abstract: Objective: There is increasing awareness of the diverse negative effects of cancer stage on the psychosocial well-being of patients with oral cancer. This study examined the role of social support and spiritual aspects in predicting psychosocial well-being among the early-and late-stage Malaysian oral cancer patients with restricted oral functioning, to inform a holistic model of cancer care. Descriptive analyses, including correlation, were performed, followed by a hierarchical multiple regression using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) Version 25.0. Results: The multivariate analyses indicated moderate-strong relationships between the mean scores for oral functioning, social support, spiritual aspect, and psychosocial well-being among a cohort of both early (n=31) and late-stage (n=65) patients attending three visits: pre-treatment, 1 month, and 3 months post-treatment. However, only oral functioning and social support were found to be significant predictors of patients’ psychosocial well-being; with social support being the most significant predictor for both groups. In addition, social support was a mediator of oral functioning at pre-treatment among the late-stage group. Title: Defect reconfiguration driven by transient vibration enables superior forging formability and cryogenic strength–ductility synergy in titanium
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Hexagonal close-packed metals such as titanium (Ti) are widely regarded as promising materials for cryogenic applications, where concurrently achieving high strength and ductility is crucial for extreme-service reliability. However, their intrinsically low symmetry crystal structures not only limit the formability of complex components but also make it difficult to achieve strength–ductility synergy through conventional deformation strengthening. Here, we developed a novel transient vibration-assisted forging strategy that achieved efficient forming of Ti and overcame its strength–ductility trade-off at cryogenic temperatures. The stress wave transmission induced by vibration assistance significantly strengthened the dislocation dynamic response in Ti, specifically manifested an enhanced dislocation multiplication rate through long-range migration ability and cross-slip. Besides, the unique dislocation mechanism efficiently activated a high-density nanotwinned structure, facilitating the uniform distribution of dislocations. As a consequence, the nanotwinned Ti exhibited a high yield strength of 841 MPa and remarkable ductility of 24.1% at −183 °C after simple stress-relief annealing. This exceptional strength originates from the combined effect of nanotwin boundary strengthening and vibration-induced grain refinement. Further, the strain-hardening ability and ductility are improved by nanotwin-mediated heterogeneous deformation-induced stress, <c+a> dislocation activity, and secondary twinning. These findings reveal a novel deformation mechanism in Ti induced by transient vibration, offering a novel defect-level microstructural reconfiguration to design high-performance Ti and its alloys for cryogenic applications. © 2026

Title: PC-TD3-based multi-objective adaptive dispatch method for microgrids guided by a meta-policy
Abstract: To address the dynamic multi-objective trade-off between economic performance and system safety in microgrid operation, this study proposes a meta-policy-guided PC-TD3-based adaptive multi-objective scheduling method for microgrids. The method uses a high-level meta-policy network to generate scheduling preferences online, while a lower-level preference-conditioned TD3 policy is trained over the full preference space so that a single model can approximate continuous economy-safety trade-offs. A two-layer safety projection mechanism is further introduced to embed local battery constraints and global voltage constraints into action execution. Long-horizon simulations based on real-world data show that PC-TD3 achieves the lowest average daily operating cost among the compared methods, at 111,405 CNY, and the lowest average number of voltage violations, at 22.1 counts/day. Across 100 test days, the cumulative economic benefit of PC-TD3 relative to the average baseline reaches approximately 0.56 million CNY. Ablation experiments further show that full-preference-space training, dynamic preference generation, and safety projection jointly improve dispatch adaptability: the complete framework maintains stable voltage responses under both normal-load and high-load scenarios, whereas removing safety projection leads to voltage violations and single-preference training weakens SOC regulation under high-load conditions. These results indicate that the proposed method can adaptively coordinate economic performance and operational safety under dynamic operating conditions, providing a practical reference for reinforcement-learning-based multi-objective microgrid dispatch. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Mining transitions in the Mid West of Western Australia: A regional transition knowledge system
Abstract: Mining transitions are typically understood as the shift from active mining to post-mining futures requiring technical planning and stakeholder consultation. This framing overlooks how mining regions experience continuous transitions throughout project lifecycles and marginalises the knowledge communities accumulate through navigating these changes. Drawing on social constructionism and knowledge systems, this paper argues communities in the Mid West of Western Australia experience mining transitions within a broader regional context. Through community-engaged methodology, semi-structured interviews were conducted with twenty-two participants, including First Nations community members, across diverse sectors and sub-regions. Analysis revealed three interconnected knowledge forms: contextual knowledge situating mining within regional systems; observed knowledge from direct experiences of the mining industry; and practical knowledge of mining transitions and strategies to manage them. These forms constitute a regional transition knowledge system that already exists within communities in mining regions, distinct from industry expertise. The paper's contribution is identifying this knowledge system. Title: Institutional underspending in a state university: Managerial constraints and implications for organizational development
Abstract: Understanding in public higher education institutions continues to pose a challenge and hinders the delivery of government-funded programmes and infrastructure, restricts organisational development and reduces the effective use of public resources. The study investigated the managerial constraints that resulted in institutional underspending of a state university in the Philippines and explored its implications to organizational development. The study employed a qualitative descriptive-exploratory single case study design and performed a retrospective analysis of the University's budget utilization for Fiscal Years (FY) 2014–2017. Documentary evidence, including budget reports, financial records, project implementation documents, and audit reports, was initially analyzed to identify the major areas of underspending. The emerging findings were subsequently validated and explained through interviews with 10 key informants representing the Budget Office, Accounting Office, Bids and Awards Committee, Procurement Office, Planning Office, Administrative Office, Internal Audit Office, and other administrative units involved in budget execution. Findings revealed that infrastructure projects consistently accounted for the largest proportion of unspent budgetary allotments. The primary causes of underspending were deficiencies in project planning and preparation, procurement delays, limited technical manpower, inadequate organizational coordination, leadership challenges, and weak monitoring and control mechanisms. These managerial constraints resulted in delayed infrastructure development, inefficient utilization of public funds, missed institutional development opportunities, and reduced absorptive capacity. The findings demonstrate that institutional underspending is not merely a financial concern but a manifestation of broader managerial and organizational capability constraints that affect the University's ability to translate appropriated resources into completed projects and strategic outcomes. The study further highlights the importance of strengthening project planning, procurement readiness, technical capacity, inter-office coordination, and institutional monitoring systems to improve budget utilization and organizational performance. Although limited to a single institutional case, the findings provide practical insights for strengthening budget execution and governance in public higher education institutions operating within similar public financial management and procurement systems. Title: Dynamic causal graph representation learning for neurological disorders recognition
Abstract: The effectiveness of dynamic brain networks in diagnosing neurological disorders, which represent a worldwide threat to human health, is increasingly recognized. Numerous Graph Neural Network (GNN) models have been created to autonomously detect aberrant integration patterns related to specific neurological conditions in brain graphs. Nevertheless, most existing approaches exhibit primary drawbacks. These methodologies typically either employ predetermined statistical metrics (e.g., Pearson correlation) or depend on static brain networks. Moreover, the process of constructing dynamic brain networks/graphs concentrates on static or temporally invariant effective connectivity, resulting in a substantial knowledge gap about the dynamic aspect of dEC. Although statistically-specific brain networks are extremely efficient in identifying certain disorders, their performance may lack robustness when applied to other neurological diseases. To address these issues, we introduce a novel model termed the Dynamic Causal Graph Inference Graph Neural Network (DCGI-GNN), which can estimate brain networks and learn graph representation within a two-stage pipeline, facilitating the optimization and interpretability of each stage. The term “causal” in this work refers to directed, time-varying functional influence relationships, not intervention-based causality. Our model initially deduces the task-relevant graph structures directly from the data and later utilizes them to improve downstream task performance. We conducted extensive experiments to diagnose three brain diseases: autism spectrum disorder (ASD), Alzheimer's disease (AD), and Parkinson's disease (PD) using data from the ABIDE, ADNI, and PDD datasets. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Title: The effects of risk perception based on local or global information in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: This paper aims to investigate the role of individuals’ perceptions of infection risk in suppressing the spread of infectious diseases. It also examines whether global or local information is more effective in preventing infections. We developed an agent-based model in which 100000 individuals are connected in a small-world network. Infection information for the entire population was classified as global information, and infection information for the surroundings of a specific individual was classified as local information. The degree of response to infection risk information was measured using a normalized tunable sigmoid function. Higher sensitivity to infection risk increases the implementation of preventive measures, which reduces the spread of infectious disease. The use of global information on infection risk has been shown to be more useful in suppressing infections in general. However, if infected people around us can be recognized immediately and personal quarantine is quickly followed, the use of local information has been shown to be the most cost-effective way to end infections. Our study emphasizes the importance of individuals recognizing and responding to infected people around them to effectively control the spread of infectious diseases. It demonstrates that higher sensitivity to infection risk leads to better adherence to preventive measures, which in turn reduces disease transmission. These findings suggest that individual awareness and behavior play a critical role in managing infectious diseases. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: Feedback-Free Photonic Reservoir Computing via Time-Concatenated Dimensional Expansion and Hybrid Pruning
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) offers an efficient framework for temporal processing by combining nonlinear mapping with short-term memory. However, conventional implementations are often hindered by the high hardware costs of spatial arrays or the speed and integration bottlenecks associated with feedback delay lines and input masking in time-delayed RC. In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a single-node photonic reservoir computing system without physical delay lines and input masking operations.
