Title: Think-pair-share strategy integrated with Google Classroom: Investigating its effect on students with different cognitive styles for learning about electrolysis
Abstract: While acknowledging that students organise, process and perceive information in different ways, empirical studies report that students perform poorly in chemistry, and the topic of electrolysis, in particular. Some of these studies suggest integrating technology into science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. A think-pair-share instructional strategy, integrated with Google Classroom (TPSISIGC) was useful for increasing students' achievement and active learning. This study examined the effect of the TPSISIGC on students' achievement in electrolysis for different cognitive styles and the challenges students encounter when electrolysis is taught using the TPSISIGC. The study involved secondary school chemistry students and used a quasi-experimental research design. Students in the experimental group were taught electrolysis utilising TPSISIGC, and the control group was exposed to the lecture method. Data were collected using the Electrolysis Achievement Test (EAT), Group Embedded Figure Test (GEFT), and a questionnaire titled Student Challenges When Taught Electrolysis Using Think-Pair-Share Integrated with Google Classroom (SCETPSIGC). The instruments were validated by three experts, and reliability indices of 0.88, 0.85, and 0.80 were established for EAT, GEFT, and SCETPSIGC, respectively. The data collected were analysed using mean, standard deviations and ANCOVA. The study findings reveal that TPSISIGC, compared to the lecture method, significantly improved students' achievement on the topic of electrolysis. Although no significant difference was found between students with field-dependent and field-independent cognitive styles when they were taught about electrolysis using TPSISIGC, there was a significant interaction effect between cognitive styles and treatment on secondary school students' achievement on the topic of electrolysis. Moreover, inadequate teacher training, too little time, unstable internet connectivity and unstable power supply were some of the challenges students encountered while using TPSISIGC. Title: Towards a digital skills framework for the energy sector: Evidence from the Australian LNG industry
Abstract: Digital innovations have become increasingly widespread in almost every industry, and Australia’s energy sector has not been immune to this. It therefore follows that the coordination of energy exports like liquified natural gas (LNG) across government, industry, and community stakeholders will be largely dependent on the ability of these constituents to share digital information between and among each other in useful timeframes. However, the success of these integrated data systems will hinge on the ability of the energy sector’s workforce to use these technologies effectively, but it is increasingly coming into focus that the industry’s workers have very uneven levels of proficiency with digital technologies. By synthesizing earlier digital skills frameworks from other industries and adding qualitative evidence distilled from 42 interviews with a broad range of employees throughout a midsize Australian LNG company, this paper puts forward a digital skills framework for the energy sector which identifies five skill areas that will be required in 2030: (1) data analytics, (2) digital communication and collaboration, (3) digital security, (4) digital ethical and social responsibility, and (5) digital innovation. The required level of proficiency that will be required in 2030 for each of these skill areas is then assessed for different discipline groups throughout the industry. We conclude by explaining how the presented framework can be used as an assessment tool for identifying skill gaps throughout the energy sector, and exploring the policy-related implications of the findings. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Heterointerface-grain boundary defect engineering enables high-performance and mechanically robust Bi2Te3-based thermoelectric nanocomposites

Abstract: The simultaneous optimization of thermoelectric (TE) performance, mechanical robustness, and device-level applicability remains a long-standing challenge for the practical deployment of Bi2Te3-based TE materials in power generation and solid-state cooling. Herein, we report a high-performance TE nanocomposite, Bi0.3Sb1.7Te2.99S0.01 + 0.7 wt.% ZrO2, which concurrently exhibits enhanced TE properties and mechanical strength, enabling reliable device fabrication. This defect-mediated transport modulation markedly enhances the Seebeck coefficient and power factor, while suppressing both electronic and lattice thermal conductivities, thereby effectively mitigating the intrinsic trade-off between TE efficiency and mechanical integrity. Title: Bridging governance and sustainability in the Global South: NGO-led urban transition pathways in Mashhad, Iran
Abstract: Urban areas in the Global South face growing challenges of centralized governance, rapid urbanization and environmental degradation, which demand more inclusive and sustainable planning approaches. This article investigates how civil society organizations, particularly professionally oriented NGOs, can influence urban governance and contribute to sustainability-oriented transitions. The study examines the case of CharTabaqeh, a non-governmental organization in Mashhad, Iran, that contested the construction of the Southern Beltway and played an important role in the policy process that ultimately contributed to the project's transformation into the Mountain Park. Drawing on document analysis and observation, the research adopts a qualitative case study approach. The findings reveal that CharTabaqeh acted as a transition intermediary by creating participatory spaces, mobilizing citizens, and connecting community concerns with formal decision-making processes. The organization also promoted a shift toward more sustainable and resilient urban development by advocating for the preservation of ecological assets and the development of public green space in place of a car-oriented infrastructure project. Moreover, the NGO's strategic use of digital platforms during the COVID-19 pandemic facilitated civic mobilization, strengthened coalitions and amplified advocacy efforts at local and national scales. These results demonstrate that NGOs can act as catalysts of sustainable urban transitions by bridging community interests with policy processes, reframing development trajectories and leveraging digital technologies within centralized governance contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Leveraging avatar fingerprinting: A multi-generator photorealistic talking-head public database and benchmark
Abstract: Recent advances in photorealistic avatar generation have enabled highly realistic talking-head avatars, raising security concerns regarding identity impersonation in AI-mediated communication. To advance this challenging problem, the task of avatar fingerprinting aims to determine whether two avatar videos are driven by the same human operator. However, current public databases in the literature are scarce and based solely on old-fashioned talking-head avatar generators, not representing realistic scenarios for the current task of avatar fingerprinting. We also conduct a comprehensive analysis under generator and dataset shift. Our results show that, while identity-related motion cues persist across synthetic avatars, current avatar fingerprinting systems remain highly sensitive to changes in the synthesis pipeline and source domain. Title: Cushioned but hollowed out: coal’s end and the demographic legacy of Spain’s mining communities
Abstract: Between 2018 and 2020 Spain closed almost its entire coal sector, abruptly and in a handful of mining districts, under a just-transition agreement that retired displaced miners early. I ask what the closures did to the population of the mining municipalities and whether the cleaner air they left behind drew anyone in Comparing the municipalities that the government classified as most affected by the mine closures with non-mining municipalities on the same pre-closure population path, I find that the two move together until the closures and then diverge: the mining municipalities lose about three percent of their population by 2022. The loss is larger where coal mattered more and survives randomization inference. It did not arrive as unemployment, which fell relative to controls because early retirement converted dismissal into pension, and it was not offset by newcomers: in-migration to the areas whose air improved most does not respond, an improvement that was small in this low-pollution setting. The transition therefore delivered justice to workers without securing the territory. Read through the lens of territorial justice, income protection for the displaced is necessary but not sufficient for the sustainable development of extractive regions, and the social and cultural costs of a hollowing community, together with the lagged effects on services and on the young, lie beyond what the quantitative record yet shows. Title: E-retailer channel selection in live-streaming commerce: balancing traffic attraction and information disclosure
Abstract: Live-streaming commerce allows e-retailers to attract new consumers, but it also provides valuation-relevant information that can make consumers more selective. This paper studies an e-retailer’s channel-entry and pricing decisions when a live broadcast channel simultaneously generates additional traffic and discloses noisy information about consumers’ true valuations for a new product. In our model, consumers in the original channel are initially uncertain about their match values and purchase based on their prior expected valuation. If the retailer opens the live broadcast channel, newly attracted consumers and informed consumers from the original channel can watch the live stream and update their valuations, whereas uninformed consumers remain in the original channel. We show that live-channel entry is governed by a tradeoff between traffic attraction and information disclosure. Although the live broadcast channel expands market reach, more accurate information induces low-valuation consumers to exit and weakens the retailer’s pricing power. Consequently, the retailer’s profit decreases with information accuracy, and entry is profitable only when the traffic-attraction effect is sufficiently strong. We further show that the retailer’s optimal price is non-monotonic in information accuracy because demand preservation, value exploitation, and convergence incentives dominate in different regions. Welfare analysis shows that live-channel entry always increases consumer surplus but may reduce social welfare when information disclosure is strong. Finally, channel-based differentiated pricing can improve both retailer profit and consumer surplus by separating prices across informed and uninformed consumers. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: How do Self-Compassion and Cognitive Flexibility Shape Pre-Service English Language Teachers’ Resilience? The Path from Self-Care to Strength
Abstract: The present study sought to examine the association between preservice second or foreign language (L2) teachers’ self-compassion (SC) and teacher resilience (TR), with the mediation of cognitive flexibility (CF). To accomplish this, a total of 353 participants voluntarily completed a set of scales. Results from a structural equation modeling analysis indicated that these three constructs are positively related. Specifically, SC was found to significantly predict TR, and CF significantly mediated the association between the constructs. The results also showed that the indirect effect of SC on TR through CF was significant, indicating that flexible cognition helps transform self-directed compassion into resilient professional functioning in L2 teaching. The findings imply that self-compassionate teachers of the English language are more likely to remain resilient in their profession, and this association is fostered when coupled with their flexible cognition in language teaching. Implications are offered for teacher education, including incorporating reflective practices that cultivate SC and activities that train flexible thinking and adaptive problem-solving. Title: Augmented reality as a digital scaffold for slow travel: The roles of cultural competence and tourist engagement at a heritage site

Abstract: Heritage sites are designed to foster in-depth cultural experiences for tourists at destinations and are well suited for promoting slow travel. Title: Enhancing communication competence and managerial skills through virtual reality based experiential learning in management education
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising pedagogical modality in higher management education, offering immersive, risk-free environments that simulate the complexity of real-world organizational interactions. This study investigates whether, and to what extent, VR-based experiential learning is associated with students' communication competence and managerial self-efficacy, drawing on Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory and Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory. Using a cross-sectional survey design complemented by platform-generated usage logs, we analyzed survey and behavioral data from 412 postgraduate and undergraduate management students across three program types at a research-intensive business school. Ordinary least squares regression served as the primary analysis, supplemented by instrumental-variable estimation (IV/2SLS), generalized method of moments (GMM), and propensity score matching to address potential endogeneity and selection bias. Bootstrap mediation analyses indicated that experiential learning depth and reflective practice partially mediate the associations between VR intensity parameters and both outcomes. Heterogeneity analyses revealed stronger associations among executive-education participants and where instructor facilitation quality was high. Findings were robust to alternative specifications and sample-trimming procedures. Title: Is green product trade a pathway to better air quality in China?
Abstract: This study evaluates whether green product trade can serve as an effective pathway to improving air quality in China. Using panel data for 28 provinces from 2010 to 2021, we are the first to jointly examine the impacts of green trade on six major air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NOx, and CO2) while simultaneously identifying both its temporal dynamics and spatial spillover effects within a unified empirical framework. We construct an integrated green-product trade database combining the APEC, OECD, and World Bank classifications and employ System GMM and the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) to address spatial-temporal dependence. The results show that a 1% increase in green trade reduces PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by approximately 1.1%. Moreover, green imports in neighboring provinces generate strong spatial spillovers, lowering local PM2.5, PM10, CO, and SO2 emissions by about 5%. We also find that green imports exert significantly stronger pollution-reduction effects than green exports, suggesting an import-driven technology-upgrade mechanism typical of developing economies. Title: Equity in print: Unveiling GEDSI construction in an Indonesian junior high school english textbook
Abstract: This study investigates how Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) are represented in English for Nusantara Grade Seven, an Indonesian government-issued English textbook developed under the Merdeka Curriculum. While previous textbook studies have predominantly focused on binary gender representation, limited research has examined disability and social inclusion through a multimodal critical discourse analysis (MCDA) framework. Addressing this gap, the present study analyzes how verbal and visual elements jointly construct meanings related to gender equality, disability, and inclusion. Using Kress and van Leeuwen's MCDA framework, the study examined the entire 264-page textbook and identified Chapters 1 and 2 as the only sections containing explicit GEDSI-related representations. The analysis focused on ideational, interpersonal, and textual meanings embedded in images, comic strips, and written passages. The findings reveal partial efforts toward inclusive representation. Female and male characters are portrayed in both domestic and public roles, indicating attempts to challenge traditional gender stereotypes. The textbook also includes characters with physical disabilities, particularly wheelchair users, and presents them as socially active participants in school and family life. However, representations remain limited in scope. Physical disabilities dominate the portrayals, while cognitive, sensory, and invisible disabilities are absent. In addition, female characters with disabilities are less visible and less empowered than male characters with disabilities, reflecting intersectional inequality. Title: When crowds converge: Link between events and crime
Abstract: This study draws on environmental criminology to conceptualize planned events as bounded opportunity contexts that temporarily reshape urban activity. Title: A hierarchical scheduling strategy for achieving multi-source energy complementarity in self-powered systems
Abstract: Ensuring long-term, stable operation of self-powered systems considering the stochastic and fluctuating nature of ambient energy remains a pivotal challenge, as existing multi-source harvesting architectures are confined to static, non-responsive paradigms. This work presents a self-powered wireless sensing system that transitions the field toward automatic, priority-driven management through a hardware-enforced, quadruple-buffered power scheduling strategy. The core of this strategy is a scheduling protocol that orchestrates energy flow in the following order: real-time photovoltaic (PV) energy, PV-stored energy, real-time thermoelectric-vibration hybrid energy, and auxiliary-stored energy. This is implemented via a dedicated circuit that enables automatic stored energy release and seamless source switching (<20 ms). A critical enabling feature is the electrical isolation between the primary and auxiliary power paths, which prevents mutual interference and resolves the impedance mismatch inherent in conventional static topologies. Experimentally, the system achieves 93 min of operation from a 10-min charge under controlled conditions, surpassing standalone PV-only and thermoelectric-only systems by 47.6% and 116.3%, respectively. Its practical viability is demonstrated by 75 min of stable field operation and consistent performance over a 10-day continuous test, with an overall system efficiency of 75%. Title: Energy security risks and democratic vulnerability in the European Union
Abstract: Over the past decade, growing vulnerabilities in the global energy system have affected both economic stability and the quality of democratic governance. The COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine war have intensified energy security risks, imposing new pressures on democratic processes and public accountability. Structural imbalances in energy markets, particularly within the European Union (EU), have necessitated the redefinition of energy policies and the reduction of external dependency. This study empirically investigates the impact of energy security risk on democratic governance using data from 25 EU countries for the period 2008–2023. The Voice and Accountability indicator from the World Bank’s World Governance Indicators serves as the measure of democratic governance, while dynamic interrelationships are analyzed through a Panel Vector Autoregression model estimated via the generalized method of moments (Panel GMM-VAR). The findings indicate that energy security risk has predictive precedence over democratic accountability. Granger causality analysis shows a unidirectional relationship running from energy security risk to Voice and Accountability, with no significant reverse effect. The cross-sectional association between the two is negative, although the dynamic responses are modest in magnitude and conditional on the identification ordering. At the policy level, energy supply diversification and resilience-building measures should be prioritised in efforts to protect democratic stability. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

Title: Underground movements: Zama Zama Mobility, Precarity, and community resilience in South Africa’s Platinum Belt
Abstract: This article examines the lived experiences of unregulated artisanal miners, locally known as Zama Zamas, who mine within and around abandoned platinum mines in South Africa’s North West province, a region rich in critical minerals. While artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) in abandoned gold mines has been the subject of considerable academic inquiry, similar activities in platinum mining areas remain understudied. This study seeks to address this gap by situating ASM within the broader discourse on Africa’s critical minerals agenda and contributing to both academic and policy debates on its strategic role. Drawing on a mixed-methods approach, the paper investigates how Zama Zamas navigate precarious and often dangerous working conditions, patterns of circular and transnational migration, and exclusion from formal mining economies. It further reveals the social and economic networks and adaptive local strategies that foster resilience and community cohesion amid institutional abandonment and uncertain regulation within the critical mineral extraction sector of derelict mines. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Enhancing graph link prediction with sequential latent variable diffusion models
Abstract: Predicting interactions between nodes, known as link prediction, is a fundamental task in graph machine learning. This task is critical due to its widespread application in domains such as recommendation engines, social network analysis, drug discovery, and sequential data analysis. Deep generative approaches, such as Graph Auto-Encoders (GAEs) and Variational Graph Auto-Encoders (VGAEs), along with their derivatives, have set benchmarks by addressing challenges related to edge partitioning during training, the complexity of prediction functions for node pairs, and the proficiency in reconstructing data through latent spaces. Despite the prominence of these models in link prediction, in this work, we reveal their limitations through analytically investigations. Specifically, their reliance on a single set of latent variables often fails to capture the full spectrum of complex interactions and potential links between nodes. Moreover, we mathematically demonstrate that integrating multiple latent variables can substantially enhance a model's expressive capacity. To address this, we propose a methodology that enriches model expressiveness by leveraging a sequence of latent variables to perform multi-step latent refinement. Our approach involves constructing a parameterized forward process and a reverse reconstruction model to optimize the probability of accurately reconstructing the adjacency matrix, which follows a diffusion-inspired multi-step refinement scheme. Evaluations on diverse datasets, both homophilic and heterophilic, supported by detailed visualization analyses, confirm that our approach significantly improves the detection of potential links and the handling of complex node features within graph structures. Authors: Wang T.; Tian Z.; Li H.; Wang Z.; Li T.
Title: Experimental comparison of dual-stage organic Rankine cycle and organic Rankine flash cycle for low-temperature geothermal power generation
Abstract: Organic Rankine cycle (ORC) has gained increasing attention in thermal power generation, but with a relatively low efficiency due to the irreversible loss of the evaporation process. In order to improve the performance of ORC, dual-stage ORC (DORC) and organic Rankine flash cycle (ORFC) were proposed. Previous numerical studies have demonstrated that DORC and ORFC can indeed enhance the system performance. However, experimental verification is lacking. This study designed and established an experimental setup to achieve the switching of the DORC and ORFC systems via valve start-stop operation, using R245fa as the working fluid. The power generation performance of ORFC is tested and compared with that of the DORC. Experimental results reveal that the working fluid of ORFC undergoes incomplete evaporation before entering the scroll expander, which can effectively reduce the irreversible loss of between the heat source and the working fluid. Compared with DORC, ORFC achieves a higher specific power output due to the further reduction the injection temperature. The thermal efficiency of ORFC is almost the same as that of DORC. Nevertheless, ORFC exhibits lower net power generation and exergy efficiency due to higher power consumption of the working fluid pumps. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Overcoming geothermal development barriers in Indonesia: A narrative policy review of sedimentary basin-based geothermal development
Abstract: Indonesia possesses the world's largest geothermal resource potential, yet its utilization remains disproportionately low. This study conducted a narrative policy review and strategic assessment using the SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) framework to identify the key barriers to geothermal development and formulate strategic recommendations using the TOWS (Threats, Opportunities, Weaknesses, Strengths) matrix. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach based on a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2011 and 2026. The analysis identified four major constraints to conventional volcanic geothermal development: high exploration risk and capital expenditure (CAPEX), land-use conflicts with protected forests, electricity tariff policies linked to coal-based generation costs, and persistent social resistance (NIMBY/Not in My Backyard syndrome). The findings indicated that diversifying geothermal development toward non-volcanic back-arc sedimentary basins, particularly through co-production with mature Oil and Gas (O&G) fields, provided a practical pathway to reduce exploration risk, lower infrastructure costs, minimize permitting conflicts and social resistance, and improve project economics. This approach could potentially reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) to below USD 0.07/kWh. Based on the TOWS analysis, the study recommended a dual-track geothermal development strategy combining continued volcanic exploration with accelerated sedimentary basin development, supported by binary-cycle technology, brownfield O&G infrastructure reuse, Feed-in Tariff (FiT) reform, and international green financing. Collectively, these strategies could strengthen investment attractiveness and accelerate Indonesia's transition toward its Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 target. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Career plateau and multifaceted turnover pathways in the airline industry: Evidence from full-service and low-cost carrier cabin crew
Abstract: This study examines how career plateau influences stress, burnout, and multifaceted turnover intentions among airline cabin crew members by comparing full-service carriers (FSCs) and low-cost carriers (LCCs). Career plateau was categorized into hierarchical and job content career plateaus, and their psychological and behavioral impacts were assessed. Data were collected through a survey of 382 Korean cabin crew members with at least three years of experience and in-depth interviews with 14 participants. Quantitative results showed that a job content career plateau significantly heightened stress, leading to burnout. LCC crew members reported stronger turnover intentions, whereas burnout among FSC crew members did not necessarily translate into turnover intentions, suggesting that its effects may be constrained by organizational and labor market conditions. Qualitative findings revealed coping strategies such as goal adjustment and highlighted carrier-specific interpretations of turnover. Social support moderated the burnout–turnover link, buffering negative outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: 'In Every River, in Every Lake': Impacts of Beaver Population Change on Indigenous Livelihoods and Wellbeing in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, Western Canadian Arctic
Abstract: Ecosystem transformation driven by climatic, environmental and societal factors poses interlinked ecological and social challenges for many Indigenous communities. For Inuvialuit communities in and around the lower Mackenzie Delta, in the western Canadian Arctic, recent changes in the population of beavers (Castor canadensis) have disrupted subsistence harvesting activities and travelling routes, exacerbating stresses linked to the cost of living and increasing the exposure of active harvesters to risk. Drawing on interviews with 25 Inuvialuit knowledge holders from the three communities of Inuvik, Tuktoyaktuk, and Aklavik, we investigated concerns around beaver population change in the western Arctic and the impact of this change on Inuvialuit livelihoods and wellbeing. Beyond the direct impact of beavers, the issues associated with ecosystem transformation pose challenges for Inuvialuit collective identity, the continuity of knowledge and connections to the land. While beaver population change was widely attributed to the local effects of a warming climate, participants also pointed to the effects of social transformations over recent decades. Ecological changes interact with social factors to produce complex and wide-ranging consequences for Indigenous communities. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A simulation-informed machine learning framework for integrated energy and thermal comfort assessment in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings under hot-arid climates
Abstract: Adaptive reuse of heritage courtyard buildings as boutique hotels creates a complex balance between energy performance, thermal comfort, and cultural conservation in hot-arid regions. However, existing studies commonly address energy performance and thermal comfort separately and often depend on computationally intensive simulation workflows. This study develops a simulation-informed machine-learning surrogate framework for simultaneous prediction of end-uses energy consumption and thermal comfort indicators in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings. A comprehensive hourly dataset was generated from full-year simulations of twelve heritage courtyard buildings modelled in DesignBuilder using representative meteorological data for the hot-arid climate of Kashan, Iran. Building-specific heat-transfer characteristics represented by overall heat-transfer coefficient values, geometric attributes, operational parameters, indoor environmental conditions and weather were used as predictors. Seven end-uses energy outputs, namely cooling electricity, heating gas, lighting, appliance energy, system fan energy, system pump energy, and auxiliary energy, were evaluated alongside three thermal comfort indicators: predicted mean vote, predicted percentage of dissatisfied, and comfort percentage. Twenty-eight machine-learning algorithms were attempted, of which 22 successfully converged and were assessed using a leave-one-building-out validation strategy to evaluate cross-building generalization. In addition, an independently simulated heritage building, excluded from all training and validation procedures, was used for external testing to further assess model transferability. Model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination, root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean squared error, and predictor importance was examined using a Shapley-value-based feature-importance analysis. Ensemble Bagged Trees achieved the highest predictive performance for eight of the ten evaluated outputs, while the two system-level end-uses, system fans and system pumps, were predicted less accurately (coefficients of determination of 0.397 and 0.839, respectively). Thermal comfort analysis revealed substantial seasonal discomfort, ranging from cold winter stress to severe summer overheating, while annual comfort levels remained below the adopted comfort benchmark. The Shapley-value-based analysis indicated that climatic variables (e.g., solar irradiation and outdoor temperature) and building-scale geometric/envelope variables (e.g., orientation, façade area, window-to-wall ratio, and envelope thermal properties) were among the most influential predictors across the evaluated outputs. Although courtyard-specific geometric parameters were not included as explicit inputs, building-scale variables partly reflect the influence of courtyard configuration. The independent test case further demonstrated the framework's ability to predict several energy and thermal comfort outputs for a previously unseen building, while indicating lower transferability for some system-level end-uses. Although the framework is based on simulation-generated rather than measured data, it provides a computationally efficient basis for preliminary retrofit assessment and scenario exploration. Overall, the framework enables integrated and interpretable assessment of energy performance and thermal comfort to support heritage-sensitive retrofit planning in hot-arid climates. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Zwitterionic Ionogels Resolving the Trade-Off Between Mechanical Strength and Autonomous Self-Healing for Iontronics
Abstract: Simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness and autonomous self-healing in ionogels remains a fundamental challenge for durable, skin-like electronics. Conventional approaches often improve mechanical strength by introducing rigid or densely cross-linked polymer networks, but such strategies inevitably restrict polymer chain mobility and hinder dynamic bond reconfiguration required for healing. Here, a zwitterionic side-chain engineered tough ionogel (ZESTI) is developed to overcome this trade-off through molecular-level design. Hydrophilic zwitterions are covalently grafted onto a hydrophobic polyurethane backbone to preferentially interact with the ionic liquid through ion–dipole interactions and thereby regulate its distribution. This architecture simultaneously facilitates dipole–dipole interactions for mechanical reinforcement and ion–dipole coordination for efficient self-healing under ambient conditions. As a result, ZESTI exhibits an exceptional combination of tensile strength (10.40 MPa), stretchability (1606%), toughness (56.03 MJ m−3), and ambient self-healing efficiency exceeding 83%, while maintaining high ionic conductivity via enhanced ion hopping. When constructed as a self-reporting packaging interface, ZESTI provides stable protection and state perception under sharp contact and restores signal output after mechanical damage through self-healing. This work offers a generalizable design strategy that reconciles mechanical toughness with dynamic functionality in ionogels, establishing a general design paradigm for next-generation self-sustaining iontronic devices. Title: Alginate-induced structural modification of high-moisture extruded soy and pea protein scaffolds for cultivated meat applications
Abstract: Producing plant-based scaffolds through high-moisture extrusion offers a promising approach for cultivated meat. However, the influence of hydrocolloid incorporation on scaffold structure and functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated alginate incorporation during high-moisture extrusion of pea and soy protein concentrates and evaluated its effect on structure, material properties, and cell distribution.Protein source was associated with differences in processing behavior and extrudate appearance, with soy exhibiting higher specific mechanical energy and darker extrudates than pea. Increased directional alignment was observed in pea extrudates upon alginate addition, whereas soy extrudates only showed moderate structural changes. Mechanical characterization of soy extrudates showed increased stiffness and cohesion compared to pea extrudates, while alginate-containing formulations generally reduced stiffness and increased deformability, potentially reflecting both alginate incorporation and the associated reduction in protein content. Protein extraction differed between pea and soy protein and was altered by alginate addition, indicating changes in protein accessibility, potentially reflecting both altered protein-polysaccharide interactions and the decreased protein content. Scaffold preparation altered surface morphology, with observed increased porosity upon ethanol treatment, especially in alginate-containing scaffolds. Cell experiments showed heterogeneous cell distribution, with observed localized cell accumulation in grooves and cavities.Overall, differences between protein sources were observed in processing behavior, structure, mechanical properties, and protein solubility, while alginate addition altered these properties to varying extents. These findings provide first insights into how formulation composition and scaffold preparation may influence scaffold architecture and cell distribution, for cultivated meat applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Global and Regional Prevalence of Areca Nut Consumption among Children and Adolescents – A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Source title: Pesquisa Brasileira em Odontopediatria e Clinica Integrada
Abstract: Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis (SRMA) aimed to pool the estimates of prevalence of areca-nut consumption among children and adolescents. Materials and methods: A comprehensive search was done in “PubMed”, “EMBASE”, “Scopus”, and CINAHL databases till 31st December 2024 using search terms “Areca nut” OR “Betel nut” OR “Areca catechu”, “Arecas” AND “Children” OR “Youth” OR “Juvenile” OR “Child” OR “Minor” OR “Teenagers” OR “Adolescent”. Cross-sectional and cohort studies that reported the prevalence of areca nut consumption among children and adolescents, and studies published in English were included. Variables extracted were year, country, age and sex, sample size, prevalence (maximum recall), sex specific prevalence, and type of population. Results: A total of 1447 publications were identified using a systematic search of various databases. Title and abstract screening were performed for 722 publications after removing duplicates (n = 725). Six publications were identified from other websites. Full text screening was performed for 106 publications, which yielded 66 estimates. Males have a significantly higher prevalence than females (OR: 2.6). The pooled prevalence of areca-nut consumption was 29.1 (95% CI: 23-35.3; n = 66) with high heterogeneity. Multiple meta-regression analyses were done, which showed no significant influence of age, male: female ratio, publication year, and the risk of bias score on the overall estimates. Sensitivity analysis showed that the overall estimates were not changed drastically when one study was eliminated successively. Conclusion: Three out of 10 children and adolescents had the habit of consuming areca nuts. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). All rights reserved.

Authors: Wu R.; Liu Q.; Zhang N.; Wang G.; Li X.; Wang H.
Title: Differentiated impacts of urban expansion patterns on ecosystem services and their socio-ecological drivers: Evidence from the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration in China
Abstract: Urban expansion can alter ecosystem services (ES), yet the effects of different expansion patterns and their socio-ecological drivers remain insufficiently understood. The study focused on the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration (PRD) to understand how different geometric expansion types influence regional ES. The Landscape Expansion Index (LEI) was used to identify interior-filling, edge-spreading, and leap-frogging expansion, while the InVEST model assessed changes in habitat quality, carbon sequestration, soil retention, water yield, and food production. A Random Forest model was further employed to identify the relative importance of ten socio-ecological drivers under different expansion patterns. The results showed a clear spatial gradient, with interior-filling concentrated in the urban core, edge-spreading dominant in the middle belt, and leap-frogging more common in peripheral areas. Carbon sequestration, habitat quality, and food production declined over 2000–2020, with net changes of −11.86 × 108 gC, −21.67 × 104, and −17.12 × 105 t, respectively, while soil retention decreased by 7.73 × 106 t. Water yield increased by 7.24 × 107 mm despite declines during the early periods. Edge-spreading generated the largest absolute ES losses because of its extensive spatial footprint, whereas interior-filling produced the highest ES loss intensity per unit area. The driving mechanisms also differed among patterns: edge-spreading was more sensitive to topography and precipitation, while interior-filling was more strongly associated with socioeconomic factors. Leap-frogging had smaller regional effects but may increase local risks such as habitat fragmentation, soil erosion, and reduced ecological connectivity. These findings suggest that urban growth should be managed according to expansion patterns, with ecological land around urban fringes protected during edge-spreading, ecological safeguards strengthened during interior development, and green infrastructure improved in areas affected by leap-frogging expansion. Title: The American touch: Evaluating the reach of U.S. soft power in India; [رویکرد آمریکایی در ارزیابی دامنة قدرت نرم ایالات متحده در هند]
Abstract: The study assesses the reach and effectiveness of U.S. soft power in India from 2010 to 2025. It also explores how cultural, educational, economic, and diplomatic tools have shaped Indian perceptions of the United States. In this study, using Joseph Nye's soft power theory, qualitative content analysis was combined with quantitative data from Pew surveys and secondary indicators, including educational exchange, aid flows, and trade figures. According to the findings, U.S. influence in India is impressive but unbalanced, with it being strongest in the areas of technology, education, and entertainment, but limited by historical mistrust, cultural sensitivities, and geopolitical complexities. Initiatives such as Fulbright exchanges, immigrant engagement and economic cooperation have fostered goodwill, but apparent inconsistencies in U.S. policy and moral messages continue to limit deep appeal. In conclusion, sustained and creative engagement – based on credit, equality, and shared prosperity – is essential to transforming U.S. cultural appeal into a lasting strategic influence in India's evolving multipolar fabric. © 2026, University of Tehran. Title: Bi-level coordinated day-ahead dispatch of an electricity–gas–heat–hydrogen integrated energy system with endogenous hourly vehicle-to-grid pricing interaction
Abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy and large-scale EV integration poses new challenges to the optimal scheduling of regional integrated energy systems (RIESs) by intensifying source-load uncertainty and affecting operational flexibility and economic performance. To address this issue, a bi-level optimal dispatch model is developed to coordinate the economic interaction between the RIES operator and EV users through price-based source-load interaction. The upper-level RIES operator minimizes its net operating cost, while the lower-level EV users minimize their net charging/discharging cost. Three EV participation modes, namely disorderly charging, orderly charging, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G), are compared to quantify their impacts on load smoothing, multi-energy coordination, and system-user economics. Scenario generation and reduction are used to construct expected renewable profiles, while Monte Carlo sampling provides heterogeneous EV travel inputs for the deterministic day-ahead bi-level dispatch. Under the zero-degradation-cost setting, the V2G strategy reduces the RIES operator net cost, EV user net cost, and combined resource cost by 5.56%, 47.74%, and 10.99%, respectively, compared with disorderly charging. When battery degradation compensation is considered, the EV-side economic benefit decreases but remains positive; for example, the EV user cost reduction decreases to 42.41% at a degradation cost of 0.10 CNY/kWh. The proposed strategy balances the interests of EV users and the RIES operator while improving load smoothing and flexible coordination of multi-energy flows. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chandran S.; Ramachandran T.; Sivakumar D.; Ambika A.
Title: The impact of environmental, economic, and social sustainability under intensive agriculture
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Intensive agriculture has substantially increased agricultural productivity but is increasingly associated with environmental degradation, resource depletion, and socio-economic challenges. The study objectives were to evaluate the sustainability impacts of intensive agricultural practices across environmental, economic, and social dimensions in Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu, India, with particular emphasis on resource utilization, ecological stress, and the factors influencing sustainable agricultural development. METHODS: Primary data were collected during 2025 from 663 eligible farmers selected through multistage stratified random sampling across eight taluks of Namakkal District using a structured questionnaire. Farms were classified as traditional or intensive based on cultivation practices. Relationships among the study variables were examined using correlation analysis, analysis of variance, regression analysis, and non-parametric statistical tests. FINDINGS: The findings revealed a strong positive relationship between landholding size and family size (correlation coefficient = 0.7214), indicating close structural and demographic linkages within farming systems. Intensive agriculture was significantly associated with land expansion (correlation coefficient = 0.658), environmental pollution (correlation coefficient = 0.519), and declining health conditions among farming communities (correlation coefficient = 0.412). Approximately 63 percent of respondents reported land degradation, while 65 –78 percent reported salinity and nutrient depletion, reflecting perceived ecological stress. The regression model explained 7.1 percent of the variation in agricultural production (coefficient of determination = 0.071), indicating modest explanatory power. Questionnaire reliability was satisfactory (Cronbach's alpha = 0.824), supporting the internal consistency of the survey instrument. Title: Competition-aware information fusion for cascade popularity prediction
Abstract: Estimating the final size of an information cascade from its early prefix is difficult on open social platforms, where concurrent cascades often compete for overlapping user attention. Existing methods have improved prefix-based prediction with structural, temporal, and continuous-time representations, but external diffusion information is still often treated as generic context. The target-specific competitive environment available at prediction time is therefore not explicitly represented. We propose COMPETE, a competition-aware information fusion framework for macroscopic cascade popularity prediction under historical observability. COMPETE constructs a leakage-free local competition field from cascades visible at the prediction time. It combines structural-anchor and dynamic-burst views to represent the target cascade, selects locally relevant competitors by representation similarity, user overlap, and temporal concurrency, and couples the resulting competitive representation with the endogenous state for popularity estimation. In this formulation, surrounding cascade activity is represented as a target-specific field rather than a coarse context vector. Experiments on four public datasets show that COMPETE outperforms representative baselines in most settings. Additional analyses show that local competition is useful mainly when the observable environment contains stable external signals, which makes prediction-time competition a practical information source for cascade popularity prediction. Title: Beyond green claims: a social-ecological assessment of cruise tourism sustainability
Abstract: Cruise tourism sustainability discourse prioritises vessel level innovation, marginalising destination level social ecological impacts. To address this, we develop a structured literature based conceptual model of cruise mobility as a coupled global and local social ecological system. Supported by AI assisted extraction and synthesis of multidisciplinary literature, this paper constructs a governance-oriented framework. The analysis identifies two interacting dynamics: a reinforcing expansion loop where revenues stimulate infrastructure and deepen dependency, and a degrading acceptance loop where cumulative stress erodes tolerance. Presented as heuristic formalisation devices, these loops help explain why vessel efficiency alone cannot prevent destination level degradation. We translate these findings into a five-pillar governance framework featuring capacity thresholds, social monitoring, economic diversification, power rebalancing, and multi-level coordination. This shifts attention from ship focused compliance towards destination embedded sustainability governance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Optimal planning of rooftop PV systems participating in local energy markets: evidence from Japan's electricity market
Abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems integrated into community-based local energy markets (CBMs) offer a promising solution for urban energy transitions by enabling local consumption of surplus energy. This study develops a comprehensive modeling framework to investigate (1) the impact of CBM dynamics on the optimal sizing and configuration of rooftop PV systems, and (2) the potential of the proposed system to mitigate feed-in-tariff (FiT)–related challenges, especially renewable energy curtailment due to limited grid capacity. The developed model is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) framework to identify rooftop PV configurations that maximize total social welfare in residential areas operating and trading within a CBM, distinguishing it from previous studies that primarily focus on technical, spatial, economic, or aesthetic aspects of rooftop PV planning. The developed CBM-based Rooftop PV system optimization model is validated using data from the Japan Electric Power Exchange (JEPX) market, combined with electricity load and meteorological data from Fukuoka City in Kyushu, a major island in Japan, which has frequently experienced challenges associated with FiT-induced renewable energy curtailment. Four market scenarios with varying FiT and CBM fees are considered to assess their impact on rooftop PV spatial deployment and electricity transactions. The results reveal that rooftop PV deployment is highly sensitive to FiT levels and CBM dynamics, and CBM further enhances local utilization. The results highlight that lower FiT levels combined with CBM can reduce subsidy burdens while promoting intra-community energy exchange and more efficient use of rooftop PV systems in urban systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Ethical reasoning and responsible use of ChatGPT in higher education: Integrating technology acceptance and moral cognition
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT into higher education has raised important questions about how students evaluate the ethical implications of AI-assisted academic practices and whether those evaluations are linked to intentions to use these tools responsibly. While previous research has largely focused on technology adoption and acceptance, it has paid less attention to the relationship between ethical reasoning and intentions to use these tools responsibly. This study develops and tests an integrated framework that combines the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and moral cognition theory to examine how technology perceptions and academic and cognitive factors relate to students’ ethical reasoning and intentions to use ChatGPT responsibly. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design among business and management students in Oman and analysed the data using structural equation modelling. The findings indicate that perceived ease of use, academic pressure, and moral disengagement are positively associated with ethical reasoning, whereas perceived usefulness is not significantly associated with ethical reasoning. Ethical reasoning is positively associated with behavioural intention to use ChatGPT responsibly. In contrast, ChatGPT usage does not significantly moderate the relationship between academic pressure and ethical reasoning. These findings suggest that students’ responsible-use intentions are associated with their ethical evaluations of ChatGPT-assisted academic practices, while conventional technology acceptance perceptions and usage frequency alone offer a more limited explanation of ethical reasoning. The study contributes to emerging research on responsible generative AI use by extending TAM beyond conventional adoption outcomes and integrating it with a moral cognition perspective. It highlights the relationship between ethical reasoning and responsible-use intentions while distinguishing ethical evaluation from technology acceptance and usage frequency. The findings also provide context-specific evidence from Omani higher education, while recognising the limitations of the cross-sectional design, self-reported measures, and a context-specific sample. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Social inequalities and occupational disease in Colombia: An ecological analysis of the 2021 ENCSST and associated determinants; [Desigualdades sociales y enfermedad laboral en Colombia: análisis ecológico de la ENCSST 2021 y determinantes asociados]
Abstract: Introduction. Occupational disease represents a growing public health challenge in Colombia, characterized by marked territorial inequalities associated with socioeconomic, organizational, and exposure-related factors. Objective. To describe the prevalence of occupational disease in Colombia and to identify the associated socioeconomic, organizational, and exposure-related factors across the country's six regions. Materials and methods. An exploratory ecological study was conducted using regional data from the 2021 National Survey of Working Conditions and Health (ENCSST) and socioeconomic indicators from DANE and DNP. Spearman correlations were estimated between occupational disease prevalence and variables related to exposure, organizational conditions, and structural determinants. A multiple linear regression model was developed to identify factors associated with regional variation. Results. The prevalence of occupational disease showed substantial disparities, ranging from 36 cases per 100,000 workers in the Pacific region to 2,289 per 100,000 in the Amazon region. Implementation of the Occupational Health and Safety Management System (SG-SST) was significantly inversely associated with prevalence ( β = -6.04 ; 95% CI: -7 to -5 ; p = 0.002 ). Exposure to biological hazards ( β = 6.29 ; 95% CI: 5-7.62; p = 0.002 ) and multidimensional poverty ( β = 1.06 ; 95% CI: 0.652-1.47; p = 0.008 ) were positively associated with higher prevalence. The model explained 50 of the regional variation. Conclusions. Occupational disease in Colombia reflects profound territorial inequalities driven by the interaction between social vulnerability, occupational exposure, and organizational capacity. Title: Supporting initial teacher education student creativity and critical thinking using active constraints in assessment: A scoping review
Abstract: Assessment design plays a critical role in shaping student learning in higher education, particularly in disciplines where creativity is both a learning outcome and a pedagogical approach. In Initial Teacher Education (ITE), this role is intensified, as assessment tasks often function as the primary site of learning for time-poor students and simultaneously model pedagogical practice for future teachers. While constraints are frequently embedded within assessment tasks, their role in supporting creativity remains under-theorised and inconsistently articulated in the literature. This scoping review examines how constraints are used within assessment tasks that aim to foster creativity and/or critical thinking in social sciences, humanities, education and creative arts courses in higher education in order to consider implications for enhancing creativity through assessment tasks in ITE. Using a scoping review framework, 28 empirical studies published since 2000 were identified and analysed thematically. Six key themes emerged: the role of prior experience, constraints as catalysts for creativity, task design and flexibility, rubrics and scaffolding as support structures, the domain-specificity of creativity, and the presence of “invisible architectures” in task design. Findings indicate that constraints function as powerful pedagogical mechanisms when they are intentionally designed, aligned with disciplinary practices, and calibrated to student readiness. However, many studies prioritise creative outcomes without sufficiently detailing the task conditions that shape them. Drawing on these findings, the paper positions constraints as active contributors to assessment design and introduces a design-oriented framework to support educators in making constraints explicit and pedagogically purposeful. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: From Herders’ Knowledge to Ecological Insight: Reindeer, Voles, and Food Caches in the Arctic
Abstract: This paper examines pistin, a little-studied forage resource for domestic reindeer previously mentioned only briefly in the scientific literature: underground stores of rhizomes made by voles on the Yamal Peninsula in the Russian Arctic. Drawing primarily on semi-structured interviews with reindeer herders and interpreting them alongside rodent trapping data, habitat descriptions, and genetic identification of rhizome samples from one available cache, we document a hidden trophic interaction among reindeer, voles, and tundra plants. Herders’ observations reveal reindeer’s seasonal use of pistin, its high attractiveness as forage, and its uneven spatio-temporal distribution across Yamal. Long known to Nenets herders in southern Yamal, pistin has only recently become visible in the peninsula’s northern part, where herders describe it as a new or still absent resource. We argue that pistin is both an overlooked seasonal forage resource and an indirect indication of vole presence across tundra subzones. Title: Artificial intelligence and generative AI in entrepreneurship education: A systematic review of competency development, entrepreneurial intention, and the sustainability disconnect
Abstract: Entrepreneurship education increasingly deploys artificial intelligence (AI), yet claims that it builds entrepreneurial competence and advances sustainability rest on an unexamined evidence base. This review asks what that evidence supports, and what it does not. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus and Web of Science searches yielded 21 empirical studies with approximately 7800 unique participants across 14 countries. Studies were stratified as generative, broader or analytical AI, quality was appraised item by item with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and every conclusion was tested by sensitivity analysis. CIMO logic specified the question; TCM-ADO organised the synthesis. AI was positively associated with entrepreneurial intention in every study that measured it, but its magnitude cannot be established: the largest estimates come from the lowest-quality studies, and few report uncertainty estimates. Competency development, the assumed mechanism, rests almost entirely on non-generative AI studies and is untested for generative systems. Self-efficacy operates as a boundary condition, raising an equity concern no study measures. Nominal relevance to the Sustainable Development Goals is widespread, yet none measured a sustainability outcome or named an environmental goal. It supplies a stratified, quality-weighted evidence base and shows that closing the sustainability gap requires theory and instruments, not more intention surveys. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Toward vulnerability-friendly destinations: A relational framework for inclusive destination governance
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourism research has generally located vulnerability in particular travelers and treated inclusion as an extension of accessibility provision. This paper reframes vulnerability as a relational destination-level condition produced, intensified, or reduced through interactions between heterogeneous human capacities and destination-system demands. A structured integrative conceptual synthesis connects public health equity, human factors engineering, and tourism management. The resulting framework explains how unequal exposure creates person-system mismatch, how destination arrangements produce vulnerability through recurring interfaces, and how inclusive-governance capability operates both preventively by shaping system properties and responsively by coordinating intervention. Risk redistribution is specified as a distinct mechanism that follows risk reduction and the allocation of responsibility, workload, and cost, and concerns the pooling, transfer, or absorption of residual risk by actors with greater capacity. Five recurring exposure interfaces and four intervention dimensions are organized in an analytical matrix. The framework distinguishes proximal outcomes (participation, safety, dignity, trust, and wellbeing) from conditional destination outcomes such as legitimacy, loyalty, and competitiveness. The paper extends relational vulnerability logic to the destination-system level and provides a research agenda for inclusive destination governance. © 2026

Title: Investigating the interplay between public art, urban design, and national identity: Case of the UAE
Abstract: Public art and culturally responsive urban environment play a crucial role in shaping national identity, particularly in culturally diverse and rapidly evolving societies like the UAE. This study examines how different forms of public art, their integration into urban spaces, and digital platforms influence perceptions of national identity. Grounded in Social Identity Theory, Place Attachment Theory, and Public Space Theory, it employs structural equation modeling (SEM) and thematic analysis using data from 543 respondents across UAE emirates. The SEM model explains 40.3% of the variance in Perceived National Identity (PNI), emphasizing the significant role of public art and digital platforms in cultural engagement. Mediation analysis highlights the importance of interactive experiences in strengthening cultural connections, while thematic analysis identifies cultural integration, community involvement, and sustainability as key themes. Findings suggest that combining traditional Emirati artistic elements with modern digital technologies enhances inclusivity and engagement. However, the limited direct impact of urban design on national identity highlights the need for culturally relevant elements to maximize its effectiveness. By integrating quantitative and qualitative insights, this study offers clear implications for policy and practice by recommending participatory planning, integration of heritage-based design elements and use of digital platforms to enhance cultural visibility and engagement. Title: AI-assisted interactive narrative as an integrative-learning design task: Student appraisal in preservice teacher education
Abstract: Research on generative AI in education often asks whether these tools improve learning outcomes. Collaborative design raises a prior question: how should teaching organize AI-supported work so that disciplinary knowledge, creativity, collaboration, and human judgment come together? Integrative learning names that aim: connecting disciplinary knowledge with situated experience and synthesizing insights across cases. Integration matters in teacher education, where preservice teachers must apply principles to ambiguous professional situations. We examined an AI-assisted interactive-narrative (AI-IN) assignment in which preservice teachers designed branching professional-ethics games through a whole-part-whole sequence: course-wide orientation, collaborative development of a focal case with AI-supported possibility generation, and cross-case reintegration. We used self-reports from a 480-person primary cohort and an independent 257-person same-course cohort to ask how students appraised the design, whether the learning ratings shared residual covariance in a one-factor model, and which conditions accompanied appraisal. Allowing residual covariance between the two perceived-learning ratings improved the one-factor model in both cohorts (scaled Δχ²(1) = 11.99 and 14.20, respectively; both p < .001); the localized association was stable across sensitivity analyses. This localized covariance may reflect perceived-learning content or shared-method influences, including wording and placement; it establishes neither learning gains nor a distinct latent domain. In the primary cohort, favorable appraisal accompanied clearer roles, efficient collaboration, greater contribution, better challenge-engagement balance, and positive AI attitudes. Students reported challenges in translating ethics into plots, selecting platforms, and managing workload. AI-IN offers a testable design proposition for integrative learning: AI supports possibility generation while students retain responsibility for selection, verification, ethical judgment, and synthesis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Experimental validation of an E-GOA-Based MPPT for PV-SEPIC systems under challenging irradiance conditions
Abstract: In photovoltaic systems, partial shading and rapidly changing irradiance create multiple peaks in the power-voltage (P-V) characteristic, making global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) challenging. The grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA) provides a population-based search mechanism for GMPPT but remains sensitive to search boundaries and algorithm parameters. This work establishes, through simulation and hardware experiments, an enhanced GOA (E-GOA) for MPPT of PV-SEPIC systems. In the proposed implementation, the search space is defined directly by the converter duty cycle, with each search agent corresponding to a candidate operating point within the prescribed limits. The search process is reinitialized when the relative variation in PV output power exceeds a predefined threshold. The search dynamics are re-tuned through the social-force parameters and a linearly decreasing control coefficient to balance exploration and exploitation. E-GOA was evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink using a 162 W PV array under ten uniform irradiance levels, ten mismatched patterns and four dynamic scenarios. The methods were benchmarked against PSO, GWO, FA and P&O over 1000 independent runs using tracking efficiency, RMSE, MAE and STD. E-GOA tracked the MPP at 1000 W/m2 in 0.33s, compared with 0.55 s for FA, 0.64 s for PSO and 0.91 s for GWO. Under mismatched irradiance, E-GOA achieved average tracking efficiencies of 94.21-97.25%, compared with 86.65-95.89% for PSO and 53.46-85.21% for P&O. Experimental validation showed that E-GOA achieved tracking efficiencies ranging from 98.99% to 99.95% across the tested scenarios. The measurement uncertainty of the experimental acquisition chain was also quantified. These results confirm the effectiveness of E-GOA for fast and reliable GMPPT. © 2026

Title: Motivations in Chinese costume travel photography: An evolutionary psychology perspective

Abstract: Tourist photography has shifted from passive sightseeing to active narrative construction. Title: The Acheulean Large Cutting Tool Assemblage from Rodafnidia, Lesvos: A 3D Morpho-technological Cross-regional Comparative Analysis
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The Acheulean, a key Lower Palaeolithic technocomplex characterised by iconic large cutting tools (LCTs), is one of the most extensively studied phenomena in prehistoric archaeology. Yet its vast chrono-spatial distribution, together with the persistent tension between technological homogeneity and variability, has hindered the construction of robust cultural phylogenetic scenarios for its evolution and dispersal. One way to address this challenge is to develop regional- and continental-scale syntheses of industrial traits based on standardised analytical protocols. Such protocols can help overcome differences in site context, artifact recovery, chronology and publication standards that reflect diverse geographic, chronological and academic traditions. In tune with this we integrate technological and computational archaeological analyses under open science principles to conduct a comparative study of Acheulean variability and cultural phylogeny at the Eurasian crossroads of the Aegean and the southern Levant. Our point of departure is Rodafnidia, a Middle Pleistocene locality on the island of Lesvos, Greece, where excavations have revealed stratified Acheulean knapped stone tool assemblages. We present a comprehensive morpho-technological analysis of an LCT assemblage composed of handaxes and cleavers from Rodafnidia. The analysis evaluates contextual integrity and examines the relationship between technological procedures and morphological features across well-provenanced stratified artifacts and surface finds. Given the scarcity of Acheulean assemblages in the Balkan Peninsula and western Anatolia, we compare the Rodafnidia material with five handaxe assemblages from ‘Ubeidiya, Gesher Benot Ya’aqov (GBY), Ma’ayan Barukh, Holon, and Nahal Hesi, as well as with nine cleaver assemblages from GBY. Together, these reference assemblages span different chrono-cultural stages of the Levantine Acheulean. The results reveal a high degree of homogeneity within the Rodafnidia assemblage, indicating consistent technological preferences and recurrent morphological outcomes. At the same time, the morpho-technological configuration identified at Rodafnidia differs from any pattern recognised among the studied Levantine assemblages. Our research protocol underscores the value of integrated comparative morpho-technological analyses for investigating the complex evolutionary and cultural dynamics of Acheulean hominin populations. More broadly, our findings contribute to a nuanced understanding of Middle Pleistocene Acheulean variability and cultural phylogeny in this part of the Mediterranean, while demonstrating a scalable approach that can be applied across the Acheulean world. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: From fragmentation to integration: Rethinking the measurement of responsible management education
Abstract: Responsible Management Education (RME) has become a central agenda within business schools, as institutions seek to prepare graduates capable of addressing complex sustainability and societal challenges. Despite its growing prominence, approaches to evaluating RME remain fragmented, with studies measuring diverse educational, institutional and societal outcomes using inconsistent conceptualisations and indicators. This study systematically reviews the contemporary literature to examine how RME is currently measured and develop a more coherent conceptual framework for evaluation. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature review of 62 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 using the Scopus database—an AI-assisted, human-in-the-loop thematic synthesis identified and consolidated 328 measurement-related concepts. The synthesis identified five complementary measurement domains: implementation, learning, behaviour, performance and impact, alongside five stakeholder groups: students, educators, institutions, industry and society. Building on these findings, the study proposes the Integrated Responsible Management Education Measurement Framework (IRMEF) as a multidimensional conceptual evaluation architecture that organises these domains and stakeholder perspectives. Rather than representing an empirically validated measurement model, the IRMEF provides a common conceptual vocabulary for organising existing approaches and guiding future evaluation and empirical validation. It provides a foundation for greater theoretical coherence and methodological consistency while supporting business schools, accreditation bodies, and policymakers seeking more balanced, multidimensional, and contextually appropriate approaches to RME evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Hierarchical contrastive learning for multi-modal representation in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis increasingly relies on the integration of multi-modal data, including structural magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. However, existing methods often inadequately explore the discriminative information within each modality and fail to fully capture complementary interactions between modalities. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical contrastive learning method which can fully utilize the intra-modal and inter-modal information, guiding the model to learn a well-structured feature space to improve the performance of diagnosis. Specifically, our method first introduces intra-modal alignment, which enforces supervised contrastive constraints within each modality, thereby effectively exploiting discriminative information between different clinically diagnosed groups. Secondly, we innovatively propose a clinical label-guided inter-modal alignment method to exploit the complementary interactions between modalities, leading to more discriminative and coherent representations. Furthermore, a dynamic learning strategy is employed between the intra-modal and inter-modal alignments to ensure the stability of the training process and achieve the comprehensive hierarchical contrastive learning. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches, validating its efficiency in learning discriminative multi-modal representations for AD related diagnosis. Title: Advancing family bonding: A conditional framework from immersion to communitas
Abstract: A gap still exists between mobile social media-embedded modern family tourism and family relationship improvement. From a communitas perspective, this study proposes a conditional immersion-communitas relationship improvement framework to address this gap. Evidence from multi-wave surveys, an eye-tracking experiment, focus group interviews, and multiple field experiments shows that: (1) social media notification management is a key precondition for relationship improvement; compared with notification-off, visual, or auditory models, haptic notifications better sustain relationship improvement through the full chain mediation of immersion and communitas; (2) happiness experience type (eudaimonia vs. hedonia) moderates the immersion maintenance mechanism, with hedonia family members relying more on notification management; (3) family structure (intragenerational vs. intergenerational) also moderates the process: the positive effect of communitas on family relationship improvement is stronger in intergenerational families than in intragenerational ones. This study advances understanding of modern family tourism and offers practical implications for both individual management and external intervention. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Combating human trafficking in Vietnam: How does the 3P+P framework influence policies and laws?
Abstract: Human trafficking remains among the greatest human rights violations globally, and Vietnam—as both a source country and a transit country—has undergone substantial legal and policy reform over the past fifteen years. This article systematically analyzes the development of Vietnam's legal and policy framework for the prevention and control of human trafficking from 2010 to 2025, applying the 3P+P theoretical framework (Prevention, Protection, Prosecution, and Partnership) as the primary analytical lens. Drawing on doctrinal legal analysis and policy analysis, this study examines domestic legislation, including the 2011 Law on Prevention and Combat of Trafficking in Persons, the 2015 Penal Code (as amended in 2017), and the landmark 2024 Law on Prevention and Combat of Trafficking in Persons, alongside international instruments—notably the Palermo Protocol and the ASEAN Convention Against Trafficking in Persons (ACTIP)—and empirical materials from UNODC, UNDP, and the U.S. Department of State's annual Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Reports. Analysis across three phases (2010–2015, 2016–2020, and 2021–2025) reveals a progressive trajectory from foundational criminalization toward a multisectoral, human rights-centered approach, reflecting both endogenous developmental priorities and exogenous normative pressures. Key findings indicate that while Vietnam has achieved meaningful normative alignment with international standards—particularly in victim protection, legal aid, and regional cooperation—critical implementation gaps persist, including inadequate victim identification, weak interagency coordination, the absence of corporate supply chain accountability, and delayed legal responses to emerging exploitation forms such as online scam operations. This study offers the first longitudinal 3P+P analysis of Vietnam's complete 2010–2025 legal and policy trajectory, including the 2024 Law, highlighting the persistent gap between normative progress and implementation outcomes. Accordingly, the article proposes concrete legal amendments: incorporating “abuse of a position of vulnerability” into Article 150 of the Penal Code, formalizing NGO legal status in specialized law, and establishing a corporate accountability regime for forced labor in supply chains. © 2027, Malque Publishing.
