Authors: Kumar A.
Title: From distraction to engagement: An applied examination of the IMPACT framework in technology-rich management education
Abstract: Student perceptions of instructional effectiveness in technology-rich management education remain actively studied amid concerns about classroom distraction in digitally mediated environments. This study introduces IMPACT—an integrative pedagogical framework composed of Incentive, Measurement, Project-based Learning, Accountability, Critical Reflection, and Technology. It presents an exploratory, multi-course demonstration across four management courses spanning the MBA, Executive MBA (EMBA), and Executive Postgraduate Diploma in Management (EPGDM–VIL) programs, delivered in face-to-face and synchronous online modes. Implementation was examined using institutional course-evaluation data (N = 202 of 203 enrolled students), and a thematic close reading of open-ended comments informed by reflexive thematic analysis. Across all four courses, student perceptions of instructional effectiveness were uniformly high on standardized nine-item instrument (weighted averages ≥ 6.0 on a seven-point scale). Qualitative themes aligned with the framework's design intent: practical relevance, structured project workflows, visible progress indicators, and technology-mediated tools, alongside integrative configuration as a framework-level property. Findings support consistent implementation across heterogeneous settings and association with positive student perceptions, but do not support causal claims about engagement. The study contributes design-oriented vocabulary identifying integrative configuration, operational workflow, and multi-mode portability as the framework's primary contributions. Limitations include single-institution, single-instructor, construct–measurement mismatch, and the absence of comparative or pre/post designs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xie T.C.; Wang X.L.
Title: The blind spots of in-situ upgrading: Rethinking social infrastructure
Abstract: In-situ upgrading has become a preferred strategy for improving informal settlements worldwide, yet its focus on physical infrastructure often obscures the social infrastructures that sustain everyday life. This study examines how communal spaces—alleyways, rooftops, and other informally produced environments—function as urban commons and how they become vulnerable during upgrading processes. Drawing on Schlager and Ostrom’s bundles-of-rights framework, document analysis, field observations, and 105 interviews, the research traces changes in access, use, management, and ownership of communal spaces during a comprehensive in-situ upgrading project in Nantou, Shenzhen. The findings show that social infrastructure in informal settlements is constituted through shared routines, tacit norms, and collective practices rather than formal design, making it particularly susceptible to enclosure when upgrading prioritizes aesthetic, commercial, or heritage objectives. The study identifies governance displacement as a mechanism through which upgrading reconfigures rights and responsibilities, producing non-physical forms of dispossession even without relocation. By conceptualising social infrastructure as urban commons, the paper advances a framework for recognizing and protecting these often-invisible systems. The findings offer transferable insights for upgrading practices globally, highlighting the need for governance-sensitive, participatory approaches that safeguard the social foundations of community life. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Building on sand: state capacity, livelihoods, and the limits of environmental governance in Cabo Verde
Abstract: Cabo Verde has built an extensive environmental policy framework, ratifying major multilateral agreements and enacting decree-laws that formally regulate the exploitation of natural resources. Yet on Santiago Island, small-scale illegal extraction of development minerals by low-income households continues to cause severe degradation of beaches, watersheds and hillsides. Drawing on fieldwork in two northern municipalities (São Miguel and Tarrafal) and 25 semi-structured interviews with community leaders and sand and gravel extractors, this article investigates why extraction persists despite a dense regulatory architecture. We find that extraction is a survivalist strategy primarily undertaken by women heads of household, for whom environmental regulation represents a direct threat to precarious livelihoods. Mobilising the "environmental state" framework and feminist political ecology (Nightingale, 2006). We argue that state intervention has tightened coastal enforcement but displaced extraction into riverbeds and hillsides, intensifying rather than reducing aggregate environmental pressure. We characterise this as "governing through precarity", an environmental state present in law and on highly visible beaches, though absent in inland sites where the poorest extractors work. By centring the politics of enforcement and social reproduction, the article contributes to global debates on artisanal extraction, gender, and informality in African Small Island Developing States (SIDS). © 2026 The Authors.

Title: “Whose Death Killed Death, and Took Away His Sting”: Aemilia Lanyer-s Subtle Art of Death in Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum
Abstract: Historically grounded approaches to the Renaissance “death arts” can be used to illuminate Lanyer-s mobilizing and transforming of standard rhetorical tropes and poetic conceits—most notably the blazon—to reconceptualize and represent the bliss-imbued chiastic movement from Jesus-s incarnation and death by crucifixion to the resurrected Christ-s making possible the prospect of eternal life. Consonant with Lanyer-s participation in the querelle des femmes (the longstanding controversy over women-s ontological and social status in a patriarchally organized world-system), Salve Deus partakes of earlier traditions of female piety like those popularized in The Golden Legend, and also the Christus Mortuus contemplative technique brought to prominence in Reformation England by Katherine Parr. Lanyer-s poem thus provides a rich case study in the death arts to promote a novel, reconfigured form of female piety predicated on a series of stunning memory images of the grotesquely maimed and blood-drenched male body. Title: A Holistic Framework for Paleolithic Projectile Studies: Insights from Swabian Gravettian Fléchettes
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Projectile technology and long-range weapons represent a major innovation in human evolution, shaping subsistence strategies, complex behavior, and advanced planning skills. Given the fast decay of organic remains, the Upper Paleolithic record is dominated by lithic implements, which are often classified as projectiles based primarily on morphological characteristics. However, such typological classifications frequently overlook macro- and microfractures that signal actual projectile use and may vary between different weapon systems. Here, we present the results of a detailed technological and functional analysis of 54 fléchettes from the Gravettian layers of the cave sites Hohle Fels, Brillenhöhle, and Geißenklösterle. Using a holistic approach including multiple analytical approaches spanning from lithic technology, traceology, projectile experiments, and statistics allowed a more comprehensive and robust analysis of possible wear patterns linked to projectile use. The technological analysis focused on the production sequence and morphological variability of the fléchettes, while use-wear analysis was employed to identify macro- and micro traces indicative of projectile use. The observed traces were tested against a reference assemblage of experimentally replicated fléchettes knapped from Jurassic chert and radiolarite, the two primary lithic materials used in the Swabian Gravettian. The experiments tested different propulsion modes, including spear-throwing and bow-and-arrow propulsion, as well as the influence of raw material variability on the formation of macro traces. The results reveal a high overlap of use-wear traces between Ach Valley fléchettes and fléchettes used in experimental spear-throwing while clustering with TCSA values of ethnographic arrowheads. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that fléchettes were likely adapted for projectile use in a long-range weapon system, complementing other Gravettian point types in a modular projectile design that reflects the versatile technological and subsistence organization in the Swabian Gravettian. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Speed-Resolved experimental and CFD evaluation of a Low-Power Intake-Air ionization retrofit for diesel combustion and emission control
Abstract: A low-power intake-air ionization attachment was experimentally and numerically evaluated as a retrofit strategy for diesel-engine performance and emission control without fuel reformulation or engine modification. A single-cylinder compression-ignition engine was tested under baseline and staged ionized-air conditions at 300–1500 rpm, with five repeated measurements at each operating point. Each negative-ion module operated at a fixed 12 V DC input (<1 W per module) with device-rated values of approximately −9.5 kV DC high-voltage output, 1.2 x 1013 ions s−1 negative-ion production, and 1.9 x 1012 ions cm−3 at a 2.9-cm reference distance. The staged strategy activated one to five modules as speed increased. At the fully load-matched 1500-rpm condition, brake power and torque remained 1.94072 kW and 12.35 N m in both modes, while fuel mass-flow rate decreased from 2.34 x 10-4 to 2.25 x 10-4 kg s−1. Using an LHV of 42.5 MJ kg−1, BSFC decreased from 0.4341 to 0.4174 kg kW-1h−1 and brake thermal efficiency increased from 19.51 % to 20.30 %. Across the speed range, mean exhaust-gas temperature decreased by 6.8–19.8 °C and CO, HC, and NOx analyzer concentrations were lower under the staged ionization-ON condition. Crank-angle-resolved in-cylinder pressure and ion-current signals were measured, and apparent net and cumulative heat release were derived from the pressure trace. A steady three-dimensional RANS model used displacement-consistent inlet conditions based on the 0.363-L swept volume and eta_v = 0.82. Grid refinement at 1500 rpm used approximately 1.6, 3.2, 6.3, 12.6, and 25.2 million cells; the 6.3-million-cell grid was selected as the production mesh after the monitored solution changed by less than 1 % with further refinement. Residual reduction, monitored-variable stability, and inlet–outlet mass conservation were verified before post-processing. The CFD results include velocity, pressure, recirculation, residence-time, turbulence/mixing, outlet-flow redistribution, and normalized scalar-transport fields for the solved operating points. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Adaptive energy management of storage-enabled microgrids using emission-aware demand-side flexibility aggregation
Abstract: Microgrids play a key role in distributed energy systems by facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, maintaining system reliability, and creating economic value. However, optimising their operation remains challenging, as it requires balancing conflicting objectives under operational constraints. This paper presents a novel customer-centric adaptive microgrid energy management framework using a two-stage ε-constraint multi-objective optimisation approach to balance competing objectives: minimising operational costs and emissions, enhancing technical performance through load factor improvement, and maximising customer benefits via dynamic reward allocation. The proposed two-stage response mechanism, formulated as a non-convex MINLP, exploits the flexibility of both economic- and comfort-oriented consumers within a coordinated system optimisation framework. The first stage models consumer participation using a coefficient of participation (CoP) and an incentive-based structure, enabling significant load adjustments. In the second stage, the microgrid operator exploits the aggregated flexibility of comfort-oriented consumers to solve the multi-objective problem and generate feasible optimal solutions. To improve computational efficiency, this paper reformulates the model as an MIQP using the Big-M method and McCormick relaxation. The framework is validated against real-world data from an Australian grid-connected microgrid. Results indicate that, relative to a no-flexibility baseline, economic-oriented consumers reduce individual energy consumption by up to 33%, with load factor improvements of up to 10%. The analysis also reveals clear trade-offs among the objectives by generating solutions with an average computation time of approximately 3 seconds per feasible solution, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated energy management in balancing technical, economic, and social objectives in microgrid operation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Traditional or simplified Chinese? Exploring the use of linguistic variants in tourism linguistic landscape
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: By employing a two-phase mixed-method research design (i.e. survey and interviews), this study investigates residents' and tourists' perceptions of the effectiveness of language variants of Chinese characters in public signage within Macao's tourism landscape. The findings reveal that while simplified Chinese may be favored for its practicality, traditional Chinese retains significant cultural and identity values among residents and enhances the travel experiences by signally authenticity. Additionally, the research highlights perceived cultural erosion among the local community and concerns over prioritizing tourists' needs at the expense of local identity. This study extends linguistic landscape scholarship by illustrating how script variants within a shared language carry distinct practical and symbolic meanings for different stakeholders. Finally, this research proposes an exploratory needs–affect–attachment framework and a theoretically informed model of tourism power relations to conceptualize these dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Uncovering creative metacognition patterns in TVET innovation education: insight from an epistemic network analysis of students’ self-reflective assessments
Abstract: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) increasingly position creativity as a teachable competence in innovation and entrepreneurship education, yet little is known about how Creative Metacognition (CMC) elements are structurally interconnected and activated to facilitate creativity in TVET learners. To address this gap, this study provides an exploratory epistemic network analysis on structural mapping of CMC in TVET innovation and entrepreneurship course. Forty TVET learners completed a three-stage authentic Creative Problem-Solving task focused on venture design for a remote region. Their self-reflective assessments were segmented into 1,506 theory-driven semantic fragments and coded into Creative Strengths (CS), Creative Restrictions (CR), and Creative Contextual Knowledge (CK). Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) was employed to model the co-activation patterns and relational intensity among CMC elements. Results show that students with high scores exhibited a stronger connection between CS and CK, suggesting that contextual knowledge was framed as creative affordances. In contrast, low-scoring students demonstrated a stronger connection between CR and CK, suggesting that situational reasoning was more often associated with perceived barriers and may reflect constrained idea development despite contextual awareness. The study also provides evidence of associations between reflective CMC configurations and creative performance, offering implications for reflective scaffolding and TVET entrepreneurship task design. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Synergistic strength-ductility in wire arc additive manufacturing of Al-Cu-Mg alloys via Sc microalloying and in-situ multi-scale precipitation
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) of high-strength 2xxx series Al-Cu-Mg alloys is severely restricted by the intrinsic strength-ductility trade-off, severe mechanical anisotropy, and inadequate microstructure control under non-equilibrium solidification. This work addressed these challenges by developing a novel Sc microalloyed 2024 Al alloy wire and systematically investigating its microstructural evolution and mechanical properties in both as-deposited (AD) and T6-treated conditions. The results indicated that the non-equilibrium solidification during WAAM induced the in-situ transformation of primary Al3Sc into the highly stable Al8Cu4Sc (W-phase) at grain boundaries. The introduction of Sc and Mn synergistically mitigated the conventional bimodal grain structure by inhibiting interlayer recrystallization, reducing the microstructural anisotropy to 9.1%. Following T6 treatment, the intergranular T-phase (Al20Cu2Mn3) networks were largely dissolved and reprecipitated as nanoscale rod-like intragranular T-phase, while the coarse W-phase remained thermally stable at the boundaries. This cross-scale hierarchical microstructure enables a remarkable synergy of strength and ductility. The ultimate tensile strength and yield strength reached 453.0 and 313.9 MPa, respectively, with an extraordinary elongation of 10.1% (a 115% increase compared to the AD conditions). Quantitative calculation indicated that Orowan strengthening from nano-scale T- and W-phases dominated the yield strength (108.2 MPa), while uniform distribution of non-shearable precipitates promoted homogeneous dislocation slip and delayed strain localization, accounting for the improved ductility. This work provides fundamental insight into Sc microalloying in high-Cu Al alloys for WAAM, and offers a facile strategy for developing high-performance additively manufactured aluminum alloys. © 2026

Title: Sequential patterns in turn durations of dynamic speech interaction
Abstract: People’s conversations follow distinct interaction patterns. We examine the role of time in these patterns by visualizing, analyzing, and identifying patterns in transitions between speakers using tools from dynamical systems theory. We map spontaneous conversational activities as paths in state space, calculate the likelihood of state transitions, and evaluate the correlation between the durations of subsequent turns. Our measurements demonstrate that the duration of consecutive turns follows a structured pattern: consecutive turns are highly correlated in length, except for pairs involving at least one short turn. These results advance descriptive knowledge of turn-taking dynamics and may help inform the design and evaluation of conversational systems. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Cognitive predictors of narrative retelling in early childhood
Abstract: This study examined the associations between inhibitory control, working memory, inductive reasoning, awareness, and children’s narrative retelling abilities in early childhood. A total of 212 children aged 4–7 years participated in the study. Executive functions were assessed through measures of verbal and visuospatial working memory and inhibitory control, inductive reasoning was assessed using a Raven-like matrix task, and awareness was assessed through perceptual and inferential awareness tasks. Narrative retelling was evaluated using a story retelling task that captured multiple aspects of narrative performance. Correlational analyses indicated moderate associations between inhibitory control, working memory, and several narrative retelling indicators. Narrative retelling performance also increased significantly with age, indicating clear developmental gains from the preschool to the early school years. Structural equation modeling further showed that inhibitory control and verbal working memory were significant predictors of the latent narrative retelling construct, whereas visuospatial working memory and inductive reasoning were not significantly associated with narrative retelling. Awareness showed small but significant associations with certain narrative retelling indicators. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Informal elder care in Malaysia: Cultural norms, motivations and family dynamics shaping adult children’s caregiving roles
Abstract: This qualitative study explores the cultural norms and motivational factors shaping adult children's involvement in informal elder care for ageing parents in Malaysia from a multidisciplinary perspective. Amid rapid population ageing, growing numbers of working adult children undertake informal caregiving responsibilities while balancing employment and family commitments, often in contexts of limited formal support. Within this setting, caregiving arrangements are largely negotiated within families and shaped by deeply embedded social expectations and moral obligations. Drawing on in-depth interviews with thirteen working adult children from middle- to high-income households, the study examines the motivations underpinning caregiving roles as well as the family dynamics and challenges encountered. Thematic analysis identified nine interrelated factors influencing the assumption of caregiving responsibilities: (1) rejection of institutional care, (2) siblings' inability or unwillingness to provide care, (3) a sense of responsibility and perceived capability, (4) parental selection, (5) caregiving as a natural family role transition, (6) religious motivation, (7) caregiving as an opportunity, (8) personal choice, and (9) intergenerational role modelling. Beyond motivational drivers, participants' narratives reveal the emotional, cultural and moral complexities of informal elder care within a collectivist social context, shaped by familial expectations, religious values and caregiving norms. The findings highlight the need for integrated support systems and responsive social policies to reduce caregiver burden and enhance quality of life among working caregivers. By conceptualising informal elder care as a culturally embedded and multidimensional family practice, this study offers insights relevant to counselling, public health, social policy and family studies, while contributing to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3: Good Health and Well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Liu Y.; An M.; Yang H.; Weng Z.; Li L.; Chen G.
Title: miRNAs: Current and future diagnostic biomarkers in liver fibrosis
Abstract: Liver fibrosis is an abnormal response of the liver to various pathogenic factors. It represents a critical stage in the progression from chronic liver disease to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Without timely diagnosis and intervention, liver fibrosis can significantly reduce patients' survival rates and quality of life. In liver fibrosis, microRNA (miRNA) plays a dual role in disease progression by regulating gene expression and signaling pathways. Some miRNAs have antifibrotic effects by inhibiting the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway or blocking the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). In contrast, other miRNAs accelerate fibrosis by activating the HIF-1α/VEGF pathway or promoting abnormal extracellular matrix deposition. This two-way relationship establishes a basis for investigating miRNAs as potential diagnostic markers. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on various miRNAs associated with liver fibrosis and their molecular mechanisms. It also evaluates their potential applications in serological testing. Research shows that miRNAs, because of their high stability and specificity, are likely to overcome the limitations of traditional methods for diagnosing liver fibrosis. Furthermore, this article evaluates the strengths and weaknesses of popular miRNA detection methods, such as real-time quantitative PCR, microarrays, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), emphasizing that optimizing standardized processes and high-throughput technologies is essential for facilitating the clinical use of miRNAs. In summary, miRNAs are promising non-invasive diagnostic tools for the early diagnosis and personalized treatment of liver fibrosis. Nonetheless, additional research is essential to improve the technology and clinical validation of miRNA detection for its widespread use in clinical settings. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A framework for transmission line ice thickness prediction integrating physics-informed feature engineering, attention networks, and causal inference
Abstract: Accurate prediction of ice thickness on transmission lines is essential for effective anti-icing and de-icing strategies. Existing methods predominantly rely on "black-box" models lacking physical interpretability, and correlation analysis alone cannot distinguish direct causal effects from mediated transmission among meteorological factors. This paper proposes a three-layer progressive analytical framework for high-altitude heavy-icing sites that integrates physics-informed feature engineering, an attention-based prediction network, and causal inference, progressively addressing prediction accuracy, feature-level interpretability, and causal mechanism discovery. A key finding is the synergistic effect between physics-informed feature engineering and the attention mechanism—neither component alone improves prediction accuracy, yet their combination yields a significant performance gain, with the proposed model achieving competitive performance among deep learning methods. Computational analysis further shows that the proposed model achieves a compact parameter count (12,321) and 40× faster inference than Random Forest, while providing interpretability. SHAP cross-model consistency analysis identifies humidity-related features as the dominant predictors across architecturally distinct models, a conclusion driven by data patterns rather than model bias. Causal inference further reveals that humidity exhibits a nonlinear inverted-U effect on ice thickness (peak at ∼82% RH), temperature serves as a necessary threshold condition, and wind speed exerts a modest direct effect (+0.21 mm/(m/s)) that is not mediated by temperature or humidity. Title: Topology-aware gap analysis for national DC fast-charging networks: The case of Türkiye
Abstract: This study evaluates the functional adequacy of DC fast-charging infrastructure using a network-based framework that moves beyond station counts to assess corridor continuity, traffic demand, and targeted expansion strategies. A graph representation of the national intercity highway system integrates public DC fast-charging stations as network seed nodes, and accessibility is quantified through multi-source shortest-path analysis. Minimum Viable Coverage (MVC) criterion and traffic-weighted metrics are used to reflect heterogeneous mobility demand across provinces. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity, highlighting a disconnect between nominal infrastructure availability and functional long-distance mobility. Inequality analysis shows that the top ten provinces account for approximately 72.8% of national traffic-weighted accessibility, while the bottom 40% contribute only about 2.2%. Sensitivity analysis across inter-charger distance thresholds indicates diminishing marginal gains beyond moderate spacing levels. A gap-based DC expansion scenario further demonstrates that a limited number of strategically placed stations can substantially restore consecutive coverage along previously disconnected highway corridors, yielding relative MVC improvements of up to 62% in structurally underserved provinces. At the national level, the targeted deployment raises primary-corridor MVC from 86.72% to 91.22%, recovering approximately 3,400 km of previously disconnected roadway. Title: Voltage fluctuation source localization in distribution systems using a signature-based approach with minimal monitoring points
Abstract: Reducing or eliminating voltage fluctuations, a key power quality issue that causes many problems such as flicker, hinges on accurately identifying their sources. The complexity of distribution systems adds further challenges to this task. On the other hand, there is a limitation in providing power quality measurement devices (PQMDs) compared to the number of buses in these systems. Therefore, this paper introduces a simulation-based approach for pinpointing voltage fluctuation sources (VFSs) in distribution systems, specifically for frequencies up to three times the network frequency, using a limited number of PQMDs. The proposed method simulates potential VFS locations and applies a trial-and-error approach, comparing a defined signature from the simulated system with that of the real system to find the closest match to the observed network behavior. Additionally, this method employs a novel carrier signal estimation technique for demodulation and a pulse-wave approximation method for decomposition of rectangular amplitude modulation. To validate the method, simulations were performed under various scenarios on the 15-bus system, the IEEE 33-bus standard test system, and the 70-bus test system. The simulation results demonstrate 99.4%, 97.8%, and 99.5% accuracy in identifying the VFS location in the 15-bus, 33-bus, and 70-bus test systems, respectively, while using only 3, 4, and 14 PQMDs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Li S.; Fu X.; Chen Z.; Pan L.
Title: Reasoning-aware fake review detection via contextual integration of large language model generated rationales
Abstract: Fake reviews on e-commerce platforms undermine consumer trust and distort fair competition. Their detection remains challenging due to the subtle linguistic cues and intentional mimicry of authentic reviews. Although neural models capture surface-level semantics effectively, they often struggle to infer deceptive intent or assess commonsense plausibility, which limits the reliability of fake review detection. This work introduces LLM-Augmented Rationale Integration Network (LLM-RIN), a rationale-aware hybrid framework that integrates motivational intent and commonsense plausibility rationales generated by a large language model (LLM) into a small language model (SLM) classifier. Through rationale-level auxiliary supervision, cross-attentive review–rationale interaction, and usefulness-aware fusion, the framework improves interpretability and strengthens the ability to detect subtle deceptive patterns. A contrastive review–rationale alignment objective is further incorporated to encourage instance-level grounding and enhance robustness to noisy or drifting rationales. Experiments on YelpZip and YelpNYC-20K show that LLM-RIN consistently improves fake-class detection over competitive baselines, while class weighting provides a more recall-oriented operating point. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: DensePSA: Robust image watermarking framework with cross-scale dense structure and patch-wise self-attention mechanism
Abstract: While recent architectural advances in image watermarking have yielded notable performance improvements, they often introduce substantial model complexity and computational overhead, thereby impeding real-world deployment. To address this trade-off, we propose a robust yet lightweight image watermarking framework that integrates cross-scale dense connection with a self-attention mechanism. Specifically, we design a multi-scale dense-connected encoder/decoder architecture that systematically reuses intermediate features across resolutions, enhancing both feature utilization and representational capacity for reliable watermark embedding and extraction. Complementing this design, we incorporate a Patch-wise Self-Attention (PSA) module between convolutional stages. By partitioning high-resolution feature maps into non-overlapping patches and applying an adaptive re-weighting strategy, PSA effectively captures global dependencies with reduced computational cost. This patch-based design preserves global contextual information without incurring the prohibitive complexity associated with conventional attention models on large tensors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both imperceptibility and robustness against common signal-processing attacks, all while supporting real-time inference. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: The reality of Dubai's property price index and a look at the foreseeable future; [تحلیل شاخص قیمت املاک دبی و پیشبینی آیندة آن]
Abstract: The real estate market serves as an important indicator of economic health, reflecting the complex interaction of numerous factors. The study provides a detailed assessment of the real estate sector in the United Arab Emirates, with a particular focus on the Dubai market. Using price data from 2012 to 2024 compared to a base index of 1.00 (equivalent to AED 934,524 for apartments and AED 1,646,567 for villas), the results show a steady upward trend in value. This growth will peak in 2024, when the index will reach 1.58 for apartments and 1.43 for villas. The study uses the Orange-ARIMA forecasting model, according to which the period of market stability will continue until 2028. At this stage, a slight correction is expected, with the forecast indices stabilizing at 1.57 for apartments and 1.37 for villas. As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, the apartment price index fell to a low of 0.99 in the second quarter of 2021, while the villa price index reached its lowest point in the first quarter of 2020, recording 0.99. The research confirms that the Dubai real estate market has remarkable resilience and great potential for sustainable growth. This stability is underpinned by solid economic fundamentals and a predictable political environment. Key drivers include the increasing adoption of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, which enhances operational efficiency and market transparency. Title: A solution approach for sustainable uncertain multi-objective 5D shortest path problem involving fixed-charge: Application to fish transport system
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Sustainability encompasses the interplay between environmental, economic, and social systems at multiple levels. Vehicles rely on various fuels to meet their energy needs in transportation systems. However, these fuels emit greenhouse gases, leading to environmental pollution. Considering this context, this study investigates a sustainable fixed-charge multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problem. The main goal is to identify the most efficient route that minimizes costs, time, risk, carbon emissions, and distance for travel between sources and destinations. In practical scenarios, the parameters of fixed-charge multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problems often involve uncertainties, which can be anticipated based on human judgment. Liu's uncertainty theory is widely accepted as a legitimate tool for handling such uncertainties. Therefore, zigzag uncertain variables are incorporated into the proposed model to represent uncertain parameters. The study develops the expected and optimistic value models of the fixed-charge uncertain multi-objective multi-route multi-conveyance multi-driver shortest path problem and provides their corresponding deterministic transformations. Moreover, two multi-objective genetic algorithms namely, aspiration level - based non-dominated sorting genetic algorithms -II and III are used to address the deterministic model. An application of the proposed model is demonstrated through a fish transport system problem. A comparison of the compromise solutions obtained from the mentioned techniques is presented with hybrid genetic algorithm, non-dominated sorting genetic algorithms-II, and III, along with a sensitivity analysis of the objective functions concerning the shape parameter and aspiration level. Finally, the coverage performance measure is calculated to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Sun D.; Mi X.; Hong J.
Title: From diagnosis to explanation: An integrated framework for examining spatially heterogeneous associations between temporary industrial-land use and neighborhood gentrification
Abstract: As Chinese megacities transition to post-industrialism, the socio-spatial consequences of temporary industrial land reuse—a pivotal urban renewal strategy—remain under-theorized. This study integrates Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR), Geodetector, and Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) to examine associations between four functional types of temporary use and a Standardized Gentrification Index (SGI) capturing changes in educational and floating-population composition across 134 Beijing subdistricts. The results reveal differentiated and context-dependent patterns. Technology-oriented use density exhibits a stable and spatially widespread positive association with SGI. Cultural-use area is positively associated with SGI across most subdistricts, whereas cultural-use density is predominantly negative. Production-service area is significant only in a limited set of locations, while consumer-service measures show no statistically significant local MGWR coefficients. Cultural and technology clustering recur as the principal correlates of coefficient heterogeneity, whereas production clustering, transport-accessibility growth, and housing-price change matter in specific relationships. These findings suggest a state-mediated, technology-oriented pathway of demographic upgrading and a more conditional cultural pathway. Methodologically, the framework moves from mapping spatial non-stationarity to interpreting its contextual correlates, providing evidence for differentiated urban-renewal governance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Foraging Theory and the Colonization of Unfamiliar Landscapes: Assessing Late Pleistocene Projectile Point Reduction Strategies
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: How humans perceive risk has long been of interest to the social sciences. The colonization of unfamiliar landscapes by Late Pleistocene hunter-gatherers is a valuable case study that required novel strategies of risk management, technological organization, and ecological knowledge acquisition. Here, we apply evolutionary theory to projectile point reduction in the Tennessee River Valley to model utility thresholds and assess resharpening versus replacement decisions. We evaluate attributes of Clovis and Cumberland points to quantify artifact use-lives and curation intensity using a dataset drawn from the Paleoindian Database of the Americas. Results indicate that Clovis groups practiced a more conservative lithic resource management strategy by resharpening points further to extract greater utility. By contrast, subsequent Cumberland groups more frequently discarded points with variable amounts of utility remaining, suggesting reduced emphasis on resource conservation. We interpret this difference as reflecting the resolution of landscape knowledge barriers. Clovis groups confronted higher search costs in raw material acquisition, whereas Cumberland groups inherited generational knowledge of local lithic resources and became more familiar with known resource distributions. More broadly, our study demonstrates that lithic artifacts, when modeled as patches of utility, provide archaeologists with rare opportunities to test predictions of optimal foraging theory and risk management. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Embedding ESG, sustainability and ethics in accounting assessment: Bridging global standards and educational practice
Abstract: The growing prominence of environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, sustainability, and ethical accountability is reshaping expectations of accounting and management graduates. While these competencies are increasingly embedded within global professional standards and competency frameworks, their translation into educational assessment remains underexplored. This study examines how ESG, sustainability, and ethics are embedded in documented assessment across global standards, professional competency frameworks, and Australian university accounting education. Using qualitative comparative document analysis, the study analyses the International Federation of Accountants’ International Education Standards, the competency frameworks of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, and assessment documentation from 104 undergraduate accounting units across 26 Australian universities. The findings reveal partial and uneven alignment. Although sustainability and ethics are explicitly articulated within global and professional frameworks, they are frequently embedded implicitly within technically oriented assessment tasks rather than explicitly assessed as judgement-focused competencies. To explain this pattern, the study introduces the concept of differential assessability, which explains why some professional competencies are more readily translated into assessment than others despite comparable prominence within professional standards. By reframing ESG integration as an assessment design challenge, the study extends assessment theory and offers practical implications for responsible management and accounting education. © 2026

Title: Designing ethical negotiation simulations for measurable metacognitive development: Boundary conditions in SCELM
Abstract: Ethical negotiation simulations generate strong engagement but often fail to produce measurable metacognitive development in students. This boundary condition design study argues that the problem is structural: many simulation formats are misaligned with the consolidation phase through which disruption becomes learning. We evaluated two implementations of Structured Cross-Cultural Ethical Leadership through Multilateral Negotiations (SCELM): a multicultural rotating format (N = 84 responses; matched n = 26) and a bilateral intercultural format (N = 39; Battle 1 n = 30) across four high-institutional-distance dyads in this study. Paired t-tests and thematic analyses of 124 reflections (κ = 0.81) were conducted in parallel. The rotating format produced no significant within-person changes across any metacognitive index (all d ≤ 0.17). In contrast, the bilateral format generated greater baseline assumption disruption, as indicated by a significant Welch's t-test (p = .028) and marginally higher role tension (p = .063). Qualitative findings showed that perspective revision occurred primarily during structured intra-team consolidation rather than during negotiations, indicating that immediate post-battle surveys underestimate learning. We propose four educator-facing design principles and a dual-timepoint Assurance of Learning protocol, recommending that perspective-shift outcomes be assessed after structured consolidation rather than immediately following negotiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From influence to empowerment: Unpacking capacity building and social learning in virtual communities
Abstract: This study explores how independent travel empowers women travel influencers and how meanings of empowerment are negotiated through interactions with their followers by examining the empowerment process at both individual and social levels. Title: Modern artisanal gold mining practices and livelihood dynamics in Shurugwi, Zimbabwe
Abstract: Artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) is increasingly central to rural livelihoods in Zimbabwe amid unemployment and declining agricultural viability driven by climate change. However, in a context characterised by uneven access to technology, capital, and contested resource governance, ASGM assumes a socially differentiated and politically contested character with far-reaching implications for livelihood trajectories. Drawing on qualitative data from interviews, focus group discussions, and archaeological surface survey walks in Shurugwi, Zimbabwe, this article analyses how everyday mining practices, technological adoption, and socio-political relations shape livelihood dynamics. Using a historical materialist lens, the study shows that differential access to processing technologies and means of production structures participation and reward within the mining economy. Informal arrangements function as adaptive governance mechanisms regulating access to labour, markets, and claims amid regulatory ambiguity. Authors: Continelli E.; Haskovec J.; Pignotti C.
Title: Consensus and flocking with transmission and reaction delays
Abstract: We investigate consensus formation and flocking behavior in multi-agent systems subject to two distinct types of delay: a transmission delay accounting for information exchange between agents, and a reaction delay representing the processing time before agents adjust their states. For a simplified linear two-agent system, we analyze how these delays affect asymptotic stability. We then derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic consensus and flocking in the general multi-agent setting with a nonlinear, globally positive influence function. These conditions require the delays to be sufficiently small relative to the initial data and the decay rate of the influence function. The analysis is based on a Lyapunov functional approach combined with a Grönwall–Halanay-type inequality. Our results establish rigorous sufficient conditions under which collective behavior emerges in delayed multi-agent systems where both communication and reaction lags are non-negligible, with applications to biological, social, and engineered systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Generative AI communications and firm value: Evidence from digital innovation in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms using deep learning
Abstract: This study examines whether firm-initiated generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) communications are associated with firm value in UK-listed tourism, travel, and hospitality (TTH) firms. Firm- and year-fixed-effects results show that implementation-weighted GenAI communication is positively associated with Tobin's Q and operating performance. Title: Assessing salinity intrusion risk from coastal flooding through a spatial multi-criteria approach in Satkhira district of Bangladesh
Abstract: Bangladesh's coastal zones face compounding threats from climate change, sea-level rise, and the resulting intensification of salinity intrusion, critically jeopardizing freshwater security, agriculture, and local livelihoods. Conversely, the Exposure analysis identified a substantial 28.19% of the land as highly and very highly exposed, reflecting the high density of valuable assets even in inland Upazilas. The final composite risk map reveals that 27.95% of the study area is subjected to either high or very high salinity intrusion risk, with the highest risk observed in Satkhira sadar. Title: Comparative assessment of distribution network robustness against wind and solar uncertainties using information gap decision theory
Abstract: To address the challenges posed by source‑load multiple uncertainties to the stable operation of power systems, this paper explores adaptive control strategies for energy storage system (ESS) and investigates differences in system sensitivity to uncertainties in wind and solar power generation. Title: Modeling the historical relationship between waterfront development and transport infrastructure: Evidence from Jeddah’s coastal transformation
Abstract: The redevelopment of waterfronts is increasingly perceived as a transport-mediated spatial process as opposed to a design or land-use process. Nevertheless, limited information exists on the impacts of transportation infrastructure on waterfront integration over time, nonlinear dynamics and temporal lag effects, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This paper examines the history of the relationship between the evolution of transport infrastructure and waterfront spatial integration along the Jeddah coastline in a longitudinal, GIS-based study. The analysis combines network accessibility, pedestrian permeability, land-use intensity gradients, and a composite Waterfront Mobility Integration Index (WMII) across three historical development phases. Normalized indicator trajectories, sensitivity tests, and counterfactual situations are used to analyze the concepts of threshold behavior and time lag. It has been found that accessibility to transport grows more rapidly than other spatial dimensions, and that substantial growth in pedestrian permeability and the continuity of public space is achieved only after accessibility becomes critical, with a time lag. The findings reveal that accessibility is sufficient, though not necessary in waterfront integration, and that pedestrian infrastructure is the mediating variable in the transformation of transport investment into continuous, publicly accessible waterfront environments. Title: EgoMamba: Fusing hand-guided spatial cues and multi-scale temporal context for efficient egocentric action recognition
Abstract: Egocentric action recognition requires modeling hand-object interaction regions and their temporal evolution while maintaining high computational efficiency. Existing methods are mainly based on CNNs or Transformers. CNN-based methods are limited in long-range dependency modeling, whereas Transformer-based methods often incur high computational and memory costs. Recent state space models such as Mamba offer an efficient alternative for sequence modeling, but directly applying them to video understanding remains insufficient for capturing action-critical spatial interactions and non-strictly causal temporal context in egocentric scenes. EgoMamba adopts a spatiotemporally decoupled architecture and introduces lightweight enhancement branches in both the spatial and temporal stages. In the spatial stage, a hand-guided global and local spatial reweighting module highlights core hand-object interaction regions. In the temporal stage, a multi-scale temporal context convolution branch supplements short-, medium-, and long-range temporal cues. We further incorporate a semantic-prior-guided masked pretraining strategy to improve representation learning for key egocentric regions. Authors: Li J.; Ge S.S.; Ji R.; Xu K.
Title: Singularity avoidance control of independently steerable and driven mobile robots
Abstract: This paper develops a coordinated singularity avoidance control framework for independently steerable and driven mobile robots by jointly regulating steering geometry and control allocation. A unified model is established by combining the common instantaneous-center-of-rotation consistency constraint with planar rigid-body dynamics, thereby relating steering configuration, chassis motion, and wheel actuation within a common formulation. In the steering layer, a manipulability-gradient correction is combined with a boundary-localized safeguarding mechanism. Positive invariance of a prescribed safe steering set is established under explicit initialization and guard-region regularity conditions, providing a sufficient condition for operational singularity avoidance under the nominal steering dynamics. In the chassis layer, an adaptive disturbance-compensating controller is integrated with a manipulability-dependent damped least-squares allocator. The resulting allocation mismatch is retained in the closed-loop dynamics, and uniform ultimate boundedness of the chassis tracking errors is established under a bounded total disturbance. Numerical studies on representative four-wheel and six-wheel configurations show that the proposed method preserves a positive manipulability margin and substantially limits singularity-induced actuator amplification while allowing a finite transient deviation from nominal geometric consistency. Under actuator, steering-rate, sensing, and steering-lag nonidealities, the four-wheel configuration maintains a minimum scaled manipulability of 0.1705 with a peak commanded wheel torque of 3.818 Nm, while the six-wheel configuration maintains a minimum value of 0.6326 with a peak commanded torque of 4.339 Nm. A gain-sensitivity study further quantifies the trade-off between manipulability preservation and geometric consistency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Hand clearances in ergonomic design: A scoping review of types, methods, and measurements
Abstract: Hand clearances, the space available for hand access and operation, are essential for manual workspace design. However, clearance types lack systematic characterization, unified methods, and standardized criteria for defining adequate space during manual tasks. This scoping review analyzed 26 records published between 1960 and 2026. Ninety-four unique clearances were identified and organized into four categories: Openings, Operational Clearances, Object-Specific Clearances, and PPE Allowances. Four methodological approaches and eight methodological gaps were identified, including reliance on static measurements, inadequate treatment of PPE, small or outdated samples, and limited reporting standards. Widely cited clearance values originate from small, demographically narrow 1960s studies and have propagated with limited re-validation. The review introduces the functional clearance margin as a conceptual proposition describing the additional space beyond hand dimensions required for functional operation rather than fit alone. These findings provide a foundation for developing more representative, dynamic, and standardized approaches to hand clearance design. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Modeling the propagation of risk in large-scale power outages: Integrating ETA, directed-weighted CN, and risk chain mining
Abstract: To understand the systemic propagation and interdependencies of various risk factors in large-scale power outages, a novel risk evolution framework is proposed, incorporating Event Tree Analysis (ETA), directed-weighted Complex Network (CN), and risk chain mining. A network comprising 37 nodes and 130 edges is constructed using data from 29 large-scale power outages spanning from 1965 to 2025. Topological analysis identifies critical propagation nodes, including power plant failures and grid instability. Robustness tests reveal the network's resilience to random disruptions but also expose its vulnerability to targeted attacks. Furthermore, high-risk causal chains are directly extracted and classified from the network, and path mining further uncovers 24 high-risk six-node chains, which are categorized into four distinct propagation patterns. Title: Students’ engagement with statements and their understanding of corresponding proofs by contradiction and contraposition
Abstract: Engagement has been shown to influence students’ understanding and achievement, yet little is known about how engagement with statements relates to students’ understanding of corresponding proofs. In this paper, we take a step towards addressing this gap by investigating whether engaging with statements is associated with better understanding of proofs by contradiction and contraposition. Eighty-seven Indonesian undergraduate mathematics education students, organized in four groups, participated in the study. Two groups (n = 43) were randomly selected to first engage with the statements—reflecting on their meaning, judging their truth, and attempting to prove or disprove them—before responding to an instrument designed to measure their understanding of given proofs for the same statements; the other two groups (n = 44) proceeded directly to the instrument. There were six statements overall, three proved by contradiction and three by contraposition. We found that students who engaged with the statements achieved significantly higher mean scores on measures of proof understanding than those who did not, with a medium effect size. Regression analyses confirmed engagement as a significant predictor of students’ understanding for both proof methods, and individual semi-structured interviews with 12 participants provided qualitative support for these findings. Overall, our findings identify engagement with statements as a meaningful factor in students’ proof understanding and suggests that selectively incorporating an engagement stage before introducing key proofs may enhance undergraduate mathematics instruction beyond the typical Definition-Theorem-Proof (DTP) approach. Title: Workplace management of musculoskeletal and mental health risks: translating evidence into practice
Abstract: There is a large body of research evidence identifying the biomechanical and psychosocial hazards that can affect work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and stress-related mental health problems (MHPs). The APHIRM Toolkit was developed to facilitate more effective translation of this evidence into workplace risk management practices. Using APHIRM survey data from three occupations in the healthcare sector, this project compared hazard ‘riskiness’ profiles: (a) at occupational versus local workgroup levels, and (b) using hazard constructs versus individual hazard items. It was concluded that effective risk management is likely to require: risk assessment and prioritisation of control actions separately for each local workgroup; assessment of specific hazards rather than the generic constructs used by researchers. Title: Do smiling faces change children’s minds? Testing evaluative conditioning in 3–6‑year‑olds
Abstract: This study examined whether preschoolers form preferences for shapes paired with happy or sad faces (evaluative conditioning) and whether the effect varies with age or with the number of different faces paired with each shape. Sixty-one children aged 3–6 years viewed four neutral shapes during a brief conditioning movie. Each shape was assigned to one of four conditions, in which it was paired with a single happy face, a single sad face, five different happy faces, or five different sad faces. Shape preferences were measured before and after the movie, along with memory for the pairings. Children showed clear pre-existing preferences for some shapes, and the pattern differed by age. After accounting for these starting preferences, two additive advantages emerged (for positive over negative faces and for multiple over single faces) and their combination in the shape paired with multiple smiling faces was the only condition to produce a reliable shift from zero. The other three conditions did not produce reliable change, and children’s exact age and memory for the pairings did not predict change. These findings suggest that evaluative conditioning in preschoolers is more selective than typically assumed, with the number of different faces paired with a shape emerging as a key factor. The results also highlight the importance of accounting for children’s pre-existing preferences when measuring acquired evaluative learning. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Urbanisation, gender vulnerability, and ecovocation among migrant women in prostitution
Abstract: This study examines how rapid metropolitan transformation in Jakarta produces structural vulnerability and social inequality among female migrants involved in covert sexual labour within the SPA industry. It investigates the relevance of the right to the city and an eco-vocational educational approach within Population and Environmental Education as critical frameworks for understanding exclusion, agency, and citizenship. Using a qualitative multi-sited case study design, the research draws on in-depth interviews, limited participant observation, and document analysis involving women workers, SPA managers, community actors, civil society representatives, and policymakers. The data were analysed thematically through critical urban studies and feminist perspectives. The findings show that women's involvement in covert sexual labour cannot be understood simply as an individual moral failure or fully voluntary decision. Rather, it reflects constrained agency shaped by unequal labour markets, limited educational capital, family economic responsibilities, debt relations, migration pressures, and regulatory ambiguity surrounding the SPA sector. Participants experienced layered forms of exploitation, symbolic violence, stigma, and disconnected citizenship: they contributed to the city's informal service economy but remained socially marginalised, politically unrecognised, and institutionally underprotected. Urban governance practices tended to intensify this vulnerability by emphasising surveillance, raids, and moral regulation rather than social protection, labour justice, and inclusive public policy. The study argues that the right to the city offers a useful analytical lens for revealing spatial injustice and the denial of substantive citizenship among marginalised women. It further proposes eco-vocational education as a transformative framework for restoring dignity, strengthening capabilities, expanding livelihood alternatives, and promoting more inclusive, just, and humane urban futures. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Energy transition materials, climate knowledge, and the imagined supply chain: Escaping the productive paradox of necessary mining
Abstract: Much scholarship, public discourse, and policymaking on ‘energy transition materials’ (ETMs) imagines a supply chain from material production to climate mitigation, despite the absence of any mechanism ensuring that mined materials will become an electrification technology, let alone replace fossil fuels or avoid warming impacts. Scholarship about energy transition material (ETM) discourse, including criticism, largely neglects this material-discursive contradiction and truncates final analyses to paradoxes productive toward extractive futures. Leveraging a review of 99 peer-reviewed articles published between 2013-2025, this article brings mining scholarship into conversation with climate knowledge politics. It charts the dematerialization of climate knowledge from warming impacts to values negotiated along three spectra (urgency, scale, and sacrifice) and rematerialization reflected in extractive rationales (developmental, Indigenous rights, nature, and futures). Most ETM discourse is enclosed in three narrative boundaries, which lean on the imagined supply chain and foreclose non-extractive possibilities: (1) The contingencies that link climate policy and mining, such as materials science, technological manufacturing and use, are taken for granted; (2) Scalar formulations separate and compare anthropogenic climate change and mining impacts; and (3) ETMs wield climate knowledge itself as a supply chain, dialectically illustrating a problem to its own solution. Pathways to overcome the boundaries can center the materiality of mining and climate change over the abstractions of supply chains and imagined climate benefits, critically reflect on the relationships between material production and technopolitical knowledge, and take seriously actually occurring alternative livelihoods. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: LLM-agent-based explicit-implicit interaction fusion for human-robot collaborative Assembly
Abstract: In human-robot collaboration (HRC), explicit and implicit interactions typically follow distinct workflows: explicit interactions are actively initiated by the operator to convey task objectives, while implicit interactions are continuously perceived and responded to by the system to adapt robot behavior to the current collaboration context. Existing HRC systems often handle these interaction types separately, lacking a unified cognitive and decision-making mechanism, which can lead to interaction conflicts, execution interruptions, or delayed safety responses in complex scenarios. Although large language models (LLMs) demonstrate tremendous potential in reasoning, they have yet to effectively integrate explicit and implicit interactions into robotic decision-making. To address this, this paper proposes an LLM-Agent-based framework for explicit-implicit interaction fusion, which models both types of input within a unified semantic space and incorporates a two-stage fusion decision mechanism in LLM reasoning. This framework helps robots maintain consistent responses to task objectives and mitigate potential collaborative safety risks. Preliminary small-scale experimental results on representative HRC tasks reveal favorable trends in task completion ratio, collaborative safety performance and decision consistency when compared with the baseline scheme without explicit-implicit fusion. The proposed method provides an interpretable and scalable approach for deploying LLM-based HRC systems in real-world settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Presidential Involvement in Legislative Processes in Indonesia: Constitutional Distinctiveness or Structural Anomaly Within a Presidential System?; [La participación presidencial en los procesos legislativos en Indonesia: ¿una particularidad constitucional o una anomalía estructural dentro de un sistema presidencialista?]
Abstract: The lawmaking process in Indonesia, as defined by the 1945 Constitution, features extensive presidential involvement in proposing bills, participating in deliberations, and enacting laws. This departs from most presidential systems, where the executive's role in lawmaking is more limited. This article examines whether Indonesia's model is a distinctive constitutional innovation or an anomaly that strains the separation of powers. Employing a normative legal methodology, it analyses constitutional provisions, implementing statutes, and comparative studies of presidential systems in the United States, South Africa, and Colombia. The analysis shows that Indonesia's model institutionalises intensive executive-legislative cooperation but also generates legal ambiguities, especially in agendasetting, budget formation, veto practice, and emergency legislation. These procedural uncertainties risk governance instability and blur classical boundaries between branches. The article argues that Indonesia represents a "colegislative presidency" that both departs from orthodox presidentialism and enriches comparative typologies of executive-legislative relations. Title: The Effect of Mindful Teaching on Job Satisfaction among L2 Instructors: Examining the Mediating Role of Teacher Self-Efficacy
Abstract: Teacher well-being has become an important concern in higher education due to increasing levels of occupational stress, burnout, and attrition, which may negatively affect instructional quality and student learning outcomes. These challenges are particularly evident in English as a foreign language teaching, where instructors frequently manage intensive workloads, diverse learner needs, and substantial emotional demands. Although previous research has linked mindfulness and self-efficacy to positive teacher outcomes, limited attention has been given to the psychological mechanisms through which mindful teaching contributes to job satisfaction in EFL contexts. Addressing this gap, the present study examined the direct effect of mindful teaching on job satisfaction and investigated the mediating role of teacher self-efficacy in this relationship. The participants consisted of 321 EFL instructors working in English-language preparatory programs in higher education in Türkiye. Data were collected using the Mindfulness in Teaching Scale, the Teacher Self-Efficacy Scale, and the Job Satisfaction Index. The findings revealed a statistically significant positive relationship between mindful teaching and job satisfaction. Teacher self-efficacy was also found to partially mediate this relationship, indicating that mindful teaching contributes to job satisfaction both directly and indirectly through stronger efficacy beliefs. These findings identify self-efficacy as an important psychological mechanism underlying the relationship between mindful teaching and job satisfaction. The study extends current understanding of teacher well-being in EFL higher education by providing empirical support for a mediation model linking mindful teaching, self-efficacy, and job satisfaction. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Fear of psychosis in an OCD analogue sample: Prevalence and associated factors
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) includes heterogeneous presentations, despite the disproportionate research and clinical attention on contamination and symmetry symptoms. Colloquially coined “schizophrenia OCD”, obsessional fears of having or developing a psychotic disorder (or “going crazy”) and associated compulsions have received growing recognition within psychoeducational contexts and patient communities. This preliminary study examined the prevalence and associated factors of fears of psychosis among a university student sample (N = 154). Participants completed an online questionnaire that included symptom checklists assessing psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviours, alongside a series of validated measures. Fears of psychosis were commonly endorsed: 77.9% endorsed lifetime unwanted intrusive thoughts, 70.1% endorsed associated compulsive behaviours, and 83.1% reported at least one psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thought or compulsive behaviour. Fears of losing control of your thoughts or actions was the most frequently endorsed intrusive thought (50.6%), whereas fear of developing a psychotic illness (18.3%) was rated most distressing. The most frequently endorsed compulsive behavior was replacing “bad thoughts” with better thoughts (53.2%). Supporting our hypothesis, individuals meeting OCD symptom cut-offs were more likely to endorse psychosis-related fears. Finally, hierarchical regression analyses indicated that health anxiety and negative beliefs about losing control predicted psychosis-related unwanted intrusive thoughts, over and above demographic factors, OCD severity, or other clinically relevant variables. Findings underscore the need for recognition of fears of mental health issues in individuals with OCD and suggest that interventions targeting health anxiety and perceptions of loss of control may be particularly relevant. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Numerical approximation in discrete portfolio optimization using DeFi as a new asset frontier: Risk contribution and correlation dynamics in a minimum-risk portfolio
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The introduction of decentralized finance (DeFi) as an innovative asset class necessitates a reevaluation of the conventional framework for portfolio optimization. Traditional continuous-time models are challenged by the complex and non-linear features of DeFi tokens, such as discontinuous trading, high volatility, heteroskedasticity, and regime-switching behavior. The use of numerical approximation is examined in this article, optimizing portfolios with discrete techniques, including DeFi assets in a framework with low risk. We use and compare several optimization techniques, such as mean variance, Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and a number of Risk Parity (RP) strategies are at the core of our analysis. We used a dataset of ten well-known DeFi tokens for our empirical investigation. DeFi tokens from 2021 to 2024 show a fundamental trade-off. Concentration-based models (mean-variance and CVaR) generate highly concentrated weights portfolios, leading to extreme volatility, large drawdowns, and prohibitively high portfolio turnover, which would be severely affected by real DeFi transaction fees, such as gas fees. In contrast, Risk Parity models consistently demonstrate superior practical performance. They produce well-diversified portfolios that deliver smoother results and significantly lower compound return paths and more stable rolling volatility and drastically reduced turnover. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Impact of Livelihood Capital on Farmers’ Adoption of Sustainable Crop Residue Management Practices: Empirical Evidence from Punjab Province, Pakistan
Abstract: Sustainable crop residue management can increase agricultural productivity and reduce farming-related carbon emissions, yet adoption of sustainable crop residue management practices (SCRMPs) remains limited. Although livestock feed remains the most common use, many farmers are willing to adopt alternatives such as biofertilizer production and biogas. These findings indicate substantial potential to expand sustainable residue management in the region. Title: Balancing the mechanical-corrosion performance via the in-situ alloying effects of commercial Al-Mg and Al-Zn powders during additive manufacturing
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Corrosion-mechanical performance trade-off is a key issue for engineering application of Al-Mg alloy. The main restriction is the contradicted performance variation and sensitization phenomenon. Current research has achieved prominent progress in performance optimization of casting Al-Mg alloy, by in-situ alloying, post treatment, etc. Whereas, the performance evolution in hot-spot additive manufacturing still needs systematic study. More importantly, the performance is vitally sensitive to microstructure variation, and their intrinsic mechanism still needs clearer elucidation. This work attempts to testify the influence of microstructure evolution on the strengthening-corrosion behaviors. Herein, an economic and efficient alloying approach is adopted by coupling commercial Al-Zn/Al-Mg system. The cooperation of Al3(Sc,Zr) and low-brittleness T-Mg32(Al,Zn,Cu)49 suppresses the sensitization effects and harmonizes the strengthen-deformation behaviors. Therefore, the novel Al-Mg-Zn-Cu alloy achieves a yield strength of 420.4 MPa and an elongation of 11.4%, and they retain 310.9 MPa and 29.4% at 200 °C, respectively. Moreover, the microstructure can restrain intergranular corrosion and promote pitting homogeneity. Zn addition promotes the passive film densifying, and T-phase shows a standard potential close to matrix, thus lowering the corrosion tendency. By regulating the plastic deformation-corrosion behaviors, the comprehensive performance is improved. The findings can provide a supplement for the performance regulation theory of Al-Mg alloy. © 2026

Title: Beyond Digitalization: A Conceptual and Institutional Framework for Digital Transformation in Higher Education
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Digital transformation in higher education has emerged as a strategic priority for universities worldwide over the past decade. Despite the rapid growth of scholarly interest in this field, the existing literature remains conceptually fragmented, disproportionately focused on technological aspects, and limited in providing integrated frameworks to guide digital transformation processes. This study aims to systematically synthesize the digital transformation literature in higher education, identify dominant trends, key dimensions, challenges, and research gaps, and develop an integrated conceptual framework to address these limitations. Using a systematic literature review approach in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, 145 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2026 were analyzed. Data were examined through systematic content analysis across multiple levels, including temporal and geographical trends, methodological characteristics, thematic classifications, and conceptual integration of findings. The results reveal a clear shift in the literature from technology-centered perspectives toward a multidimensional, institutional, and strategic understanding of digital transformation in higher education. Three interrelated dimensions, digital technologies and infrastructure, human resources and digital skills, and leadership, culture, and policy were identified as the core components of effective digital transformation. The findings further highlight persistent research gaps related to organizational readiness, institutional implications, change management, and the contextual localization of digital transformation frameworks, particularly in developing country contexts. In response to these gaps, this study proposes an integrated conceptual framework that conceptualizes digital transformation in higher education as a dynamic four-stage process encompassing readiness and assessment, pilot implementation, scaling and integration, and continuous optimization and innovation. The proposed framework offers both an analytical foundation for future research and a practical reference for university leaders and policymakers seeking to design and implement sustainable digital transformation initiatives. © 2027 The author(s). Author full names: Cocco, Edoardo (59001984800)
Title: Understanding situational fear of crime in context: a virtual reality interview approach to studying victimization avoidance strategies in nocturnal urban spaces
Abstract: Most research on the behavioral dimension of fear of crime captures broad avoidance habits through surveys or retrospective interviews, leaving the in-situ risk management behaviors people deploy while actually present in a threatening space largely unobserved. This study uses Virtual Reality Retrospective Thinking Aloud (VR-RTA) to access this underexplored dimension. Sixty-one participants navigated a 3D replica of nocturnal Lausanne in scenarios developed with police officers. Analysis identified two types of in-situ avoidance strategies: anticipatory scanning and route management; reactive symbolic distancing from perceived threats, modulated by personal familiarity with the area as a dispositional factor, alongside three vulnerability dimensions (self, environment, others) reflecting the core components of Routine Activity Theory. Crucially, many routing decisions proved habit-driven rather than fear-driven (a distinction surveys cannot detect) and several behavioral adjustments operated below conscious awareness, recoverable only through VR-RTA video review of participants’ own behavior. Findings point towards a sequential process model of situational FoC: behavioral adjustment begins as routine cognitive appraisal and escalates to full fear engagement only when perceived risk crosses a threshold. They confirm and nuance existing qualitative typologies of avoidance behavior while identifying specific gaps in survey instruments for measuring the behavioral dimension of situational FoC. Based on these insights, new survey items targeting in-situ risk management behaviors are proposed to strengthen the measurement of fear of victimization events. © The Author(s) 2026.
