Title: Populist urbanism and the speculation network: Discourse, conflict, and planning monopoly in Hamadan
Abstract: This article explores how populist discourse reshapes urban planning conflicts and legitimizes speculative development in Hamadan, Iran. Using post-structuralist discourse theory and qualitative analysis of 1248 local media texts (2017–2024), it shows how signifiers like “the people” and “justice” construct antagonistic narratives that erode planning authority. The study introduces the concept of a “speculation network” involving political, commercial, and media actors that exploit participatory rhetoric for elite gain. It finds that populism marginalizes expertise and reinforces monopolies, with media as a key discursive arena. The article advances agonistic planning theory and advocates media-aware, conflict-sensitive planning approaches. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zou Y.; Lei Z.; Hao F.
Title: When the sea remembers: Ritual, emotion, and identity at the Mazu Festival
Abstract: The study examines how ritual participation in religious festivals generates emotional energy and reinforces cultural identity, using the Mazu Festival in China as a case example. Findings reveal that ritual engagement fosters affective synchronization and reactivates collective memory, enabling participants to reconnect with heritage, culture and negotiate evolving identities. Emotional energy emerges as a central process linking symbolic system to identity formation. The research contributes to festival tourism studies by advancing an integrated emotional and symbolic framework and by highlighting the role of festivals as dynamic platforms for cultural continuity and identity renewal. The findings also offer practical insights for destination managers and policymakers seeking to enhance cultural meaningfulness of festival experiences. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kong K.; Wang D.; Li H.; Wang Z.; Liu G.; Yuan D.; Wang R.; Hu N.
Title: Hierarchically woven covalent organic framework hydrogels with programmable hydrogen-binding domains for adaptive human–machine interfaces
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Hydrogels are among the most promising materials for wearable sensors in human–machine interaction, but the pursuit of high mechanical strength and resilience in hydrogels often leads to a trade-off with conductivity, which significantly limits their practical applications; thereby, balancing energy dissipation and ion transport in hydrogels remains a critical challenge. Here, we develop molecularly woven hydrogels by non-covalently threading linear polymers into thiadiazole-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs), in which the thiadiazole dihydrazide units in the COFs function as hydrogen-binding domains, fostering multiple non-covalent interactions between the COFs and linear polymers. This unique configuration facilitates energy dissipation while simultaneously enhancing ion transport. The resulting hydrogels exhibit a tensile strength of 0.41 MPa, resilience of 99%, an ionic conductivity of 1.27 ± 0.18 S m−1, and limited crack propagation, ranking among the highest values reported for hydrogel materials. Furthermore, the hydrogel-based sensor demonstrates a rapid strain response of 12.5 ms, excellent cyclic stability, and superior environmental weatherability, enabling accurate monitoring of human activities and gesture recognition for dexterous robotic manipulation. This work holds great promise for developing intelligent human-machine interfaces to perform dangerous and high-precision tasks. © 2026

Author full names: Chinta, Gkentian (60757894100); Floros, George (57204851467); Kosmidis, Christoforos (7004476695); Kolomvatsos, Konstantinos (24829478600)
Title: A density-aware and overlap-driven framework for task allocation in distributed spatial data processing environments
Abstract: The increasing volume of data generated by distributed sensing and Internet of Things (IoT) devices and applications has intensified the need for efficient data and task management in edge and distributed environments. A key challenge in such systems is determining how to allocate tasks that require the processing of multidimensional data across distributed nodes while preserving data locality and limiting communication overhead. In this paper, we propose a density-aware and overlap-driven framework for task allocation in distributed data-processing environments. Tasks and node data regions are represented as multidimensional hyper-rectangles, while each node maintains information about its local data density. The proposed framework employs a scenario-based allocation mechanism based on strict spatial containment, tolerance-based containment, and external execution. Depending on the spatial relationship between a task and the available data regions, as well as the corresponding density conditions, the task can be executed locally, supported through neighboring-node collaboration, offloaded to another node, or reported as unserved when no suitable execution node is available. Candidate nodes for collaboration and offloading are selected using a scoring mechanism that considers spatial overlap and communication latency. To improve adaptability under heterogeneous data distributions, the framework additionally supports adaptive density thresholds and bounded tolerance expansion according to the observed node densities. The proposed approach is evaluated using three heterogeneous real-world datasets: OpenStreetMap (OSM) data from Greece, NYC Yellow Taxi data, and data derived from the National Ambulatory Medical Care Survey (NAMCS). The evaluation examines allocation behavior, execution success, communication requirements, decision overhead, scalability, parameter sensitivity, and deadline-aware admission. The results demonstrate accurate allocation decisions with low decision overhead while highlighting the trade-offs among local execution, neighbor collaboration, and external offloading. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and adaptive approach to multidimensional task allocation and offers a practical basis for distributed data processing in edge and IoT environments. Authors: Desrizal; Widigdo B.; Yulianto G.; Kurniawan F.; Sulistiono
Title: Sustainability assessment for multi-activity coastal areas using an integrated hierarchical decision-making framework
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainability assessments of multi-activity coastal areas generally evaluate each utilization activity independently, leaving interdependencies unaccommodated and risking biased contribution estimates under conventional hierarchical weighting. This constraint carries profound implications for settings where anthropogenic activities vie for finite ecological space, most notably within tropical coastal socio-ecological systems in developing countries. The study objectives were to develop an activity-based sustainability assessment framework integrating hierarchical and network-based multi-criteria weighting to estimate the relative contribution of three activities: small-scale capture fisheries, vannamei shrimp ponds, and coastal tourism, in the coastal area of Pariaman City, Indonesia. METHODS: Assessments covered 36 indicators across four sustainability dimensions: ecological, social, economic, and governance, with a 17-node interdependence network built from 14 indicators showing cross-activity dependencies through shared resources and identified causal pathways. Hierarchical weights for individual activities were derived independently by fifteen experts across three sectoral panels. Additionally, network-based weighting to account for inter-activity interactions was performed by a subset of five cross-sectoral experts. All pairwise comparison matrices satisfied the predetermined consistency threshold. The resilience of the regional index to weighting uncertainty was tested through sensitivity analysis. FINDINGS: Network-based weights ranked vannamei shrimp ponds above small-scale capture fisheries and coastal tourism, but far less dominantly than under hierarchical weighting, which treated ponds as an extreme outlier by ignoring their negative influence on shared water quality and spatial resources. With a near-uniform contribution value of 0.554 across all three activities, the regional index underscores that intervention prioritization requires integrating interdependent cross-activity contributions rather than relying exclusively on standalone activity assessments. The moderately sustainable category held consistently across sensitivity scenarios, although activity contribution order proved more sensitive to weighting uncertainty. CONCLUSION: Accounting for interdependence corrects the hierarchical approach's over-estimation of vannamei shrimp ponds and reveals a greater contribution from small-scale capture fisheries and coastal tourism than independent estimates suggest. The sustainability contribution of a given activity cannot be reliably determined in isolation from cross-sectoral interdependencies, highlighting the primary utility of this framework as a decision-support mechanism for coastal management. Author full names: Galindo-Domínguez, Héctor (57209238017); Campo, Lucía (56026747800); Delgado, Nahia (60518415700); Urruzola, María-Victoria (57212091708)
Title: Brains on copy-paste mode? A mixed-methods study on the relationship between generative artificial intelligence use and students’ critical thinking skills
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence tools, such as ChatGPT, into higher education has raised important questions about their relationship with students' critical thinking (CT) skills. This study explored these associations among 398 undergraduate students using a mixed-methods design. Quantitatively, participants completed validated measures of critical thinking and a survey assessing frequency of AI use in academic contexts. Correlation analyses indicated a significant negative association between AI use and Analyzing/Organizing skills. Moderation analyses revealed that academic achievement moderated this relationship for Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating, with higher achievers showing a stronger negative association. No significant effects emerged for gender and age on the remaining CT dimensions. Likewise, qualitative analyses of 200 open-ended responses identified three user profiles: (1) instrumental/uncritical, comprising younger low-achieving male students emphasizing AI speed and utility while reporting reduced verification effort; (2) stable/complementary, comprising older high-achieving students perceiving little change in their evaluative practices; and (3) ambivalent/skeptical-trusting, comprising women with medium achievement, divided between increased skepticism and greater reliance on AI outputs. Supplementary analyses linking Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating scores to these profiles showed that lower development of both skills consistently aligned with the instrumental/uncritical profile. The interpretive consistency between both analytical strands suggests that the relationship between generative AI use and CT skills is nuanced and profile-dependent, limited in scope to specific dimensions and student groups rather than reflecting a broad negative impact, while highlighting the risks of uncritical reliance and the potential of AI as a complementary academic tool when used reflectively. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Affective Dimensions of Spanish as a Foreign Language (SFL) Education: Exploring the Interplay of Anxiety, Motivation, and Self-Esteem among Secondary School Students
Abstract: This study probed the associations among Spanish as a foreign language (SFL) students’ anxiety, motivation, and self-esteem. Beyond mapping the connections between these affective factors, the research also examined the extent to which students’ motivation and anxiety predicted their self-esteem. The data were collected from 118 secondary school students through three validated instruments, namely the Foreign Language Classroom Anxiety Scale, Foreign Language Self-Esteem Scale, and Motivation towards Foreign Languages Survey. The analysis indicated clear patterns of association, with higher levels of anxiety linked to lower levels of both motivation and self-esteem. The results highlighted the importance of addressing emotional factors in foreign language education and suggested that interventions targeting anxiety reduction and the enhancement of self-esteem and motivation could foster a more supportive language learning environment. By demonstrating how affective factors shape SFL learning, the study offered practical insights for policymakers and language educators seeking to promote students’ emotional well-being and engagement. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Integrating local cultural values into deep learning pedagogy: A framework for teaching science fiction writing in Indonesia
Abstract: This study examines the integration of the Deep Learning curriculum with Javanese cultural values in teaching science fiction writing to high school students. The study is motivated by the importance of developing STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) competencies integrated with the strengthening of cultural identity in the era of globalization. A mixed methods research approach was applied involving 30 students and 2 Indonesian language teachers at SMA Negeri 9 Malang. Data were collected through structured observations, semi-structured interviews, and analysis of student work documents using rubrics developed based on the 6C's dimensions of Deep Learning (Critical Thinking, Creativity, Collaboration, Communication, Character, Citizenship). The research results revealed that the integration successfully actualized all dimensions of Deep Learning at a high level (scores of 4.3-4.8 on a 5-point scale), with the highest achievements in the Collaboration (4.8) and Creativity (4.7) dimensions. Qualitative analysis of student work identified five patterns of Javanese cultural integration, namely: (1) integration of technology with Javanese philosophy, (2) technology as an optimizer of local wisdom, (3) mythology as the basis of technology, (4) collaborative resolution of generational conflicts, and (5) culture as a value system regulating technology. As many as 55% of student works reached the very good category, showing a significant improvement in aspects of creativity and cultural integration. The research conclusion states that the integration of the Deep Learning curriculum with Javanese cultural values not only improves technical competence in writing science fiction but also develops contextual scientific literacy and strengthens students' cultural identity. This model represents a transformative synthesis between global education paradigms and local wisdom relevant to the Indonesian educational context. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Developing Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Gen Z accounting students: The roles of AI Competency, Systematic Thinking Ability, and Design Thinking Ability
Abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in accounting practices have significantly increased the complexity and uncertainty of professional work environments, making Dynamic Risk Management Skills a critical competency for contemporary accounting graduates. This study aims to examine the relationships between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Generation Z (Gen Z) accounting students, with Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability considered as mediating variables. A quantitative research design was employed, collecting data from 571 fourth-year accounting students across Thailand. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that AI Competency is significantly and positively associated with Systematic Thinking Ability, Design Thinking Ability, and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. Moreover, Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability significantly account for the indirect associations between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. These findings extend theoretical understanding of risk management skill development in accounting education and offer practical implications for curriculum design by emphasizing the integration of AI with higher-order thinking skill development to better prepare graduates for complex and rapidly changing professional environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Modelling Local Strontium Isotope Baselines from Human Isotopic Data Using Machine Learning: Implications for Past Mobility Studies
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Estimating bioavailable strontium isotope baselines is a critical step in archaeological mobility studies. Conventional proxy-based approaches, which rely on environmental samples, such as soils, fauna, plants, or waters, are not always feasible and may be affected by environmental, taphonomic, or sampling-related biases. Here, we introduce MobSr, a machine-learning-based model designed to estimate probable local 87Sr/86Sr baselines directly from human enamel isotope data. The model combines four first-layer classifiers—Naïve Bayes, k-nearest neighbours, support vector machine, and Random Forest—with a Bayesian ensemble layer that integrates classifier outputs and refines local/non-local probability estimates. MobSr was trained on a dataset of approximately 3000 human enamel samples from 86 archaeological sites, using published expert-derived local/non-local classifications. Local isotopic ranges are estimated by analysing posterior probabilities assigned to individual observations. Model performance was evaluated through general cross-validation and through site-specific case studies, including a La Tène period cemetery from the Czech Republic, an Early Medieval cemetery from Finland, and multi-period burial assemblages from Bahrain in the Arabian Peninsula. The results show 87–95% agreement with published local/non-local classifications, depending on the evaluation strategy and treatment of atypical cases. These values quantify concordance with the source-study labels. These findings demonstrate that MobSr can replicate and refine local baseline estimates without requiring additional environmental sampling. The model offers an efficient tool for preliminary mobility assessment and provides a complementary strategy to traditional baseline construction in bioarchaeological research. In addition, the use of a large training dataset enables broader exploration of expert-derived locality assignments across predominantly sedentary populations from different regions and periods. © The Author(s) 2026.

Author full names: Naseem, Muhammad Tahir (57733123500); Zaman, Wajid (57193825110); Ullah, Aziz (60723128600)
Title: Beyond copy number: circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA Fragmentomics and structural states in liquid biopsy
Abstract: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf-mtDNA) is commonly treated as a concentration-based biomarker, yet the measured signal is a composite of biologically distinct molecular states that are differentially affected by blood collection, platelet activation, centrifugation, storage, extraction, amplification, and sequencing. This analytical heterogeneity has become more consequential as cf-mtDNA research moves from copy-number assays toward fragmentomics, topology, heteroplasmy, oxidative lesions, and carrier-resolved measurements. Recent multi-cohort studies indicate that fragment size, 5′-end composition, motif diversity, and regional breakage patterns can support cancer detection and tissue-of-origin inference, while clinical chemistry studies demonstrate that routine preanalytical choices can markedly alter the mitochondrial fraction recovered from plasma. This review develops a laboratory-medicine framework in which cf-mtDNA is considered a multidimensional analyte rather than a single abundance variable. We integrate mitochondrial release biology with the extracellular carrier states of mtDNA; explain how TFAM, membrane pores, mitophagy, extracellular vesicles, platelets, and nucleases shape the observed fragmentome; evaluate preanalytical and analytical sources of bias; and assess translational evidence across oncology, critical illness, cardio-renal disease, metabolic inflammation, transplantation, and neuroinflammatory disorders. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing true biological variation from procedure-induced redistribution of cf-mtDNA between soluble, vesicular, platelet-associated, and cell-free mitochondrial compartments. We propose minimum analytical descriptors, quality-control priorities, and validation steps required before cf-mtDNA fragmentomic signatures can become transportable clinical tests. The central implication is that the next phase of cf-mtDNA diagnostics will depend less on measuring more DNA than on measuring the correct molecular fraction with traceable preanalytics, orthogonal characterization, and clinically locked computational models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Shala, Vjosa Jonuzi (58628802500); Shala, Hana (59008012300)
Title: Between criminalization and decriminalization: Homosexuality, gender norms, and sociolegal change in Kosovo
Abstract: Since the mid-nineteenth century, Kosovo has undergone significant social transformation and legal reform, particularly in relation to sexuality and state intervention in private life. This study provides a historical analysis of criminal legislation addressing homosexuality, examining both normative legal frameworks and prevailing social attitudes. At first glance, the fact that approximately 95 of the population of Kosovo identifies as Muslim might suggest the existence of a pronounced social resistance towards homosexuals, as seen in certain countries of the Eastern world. However, empirical research reveals a considerably more intricate social reality. While traditional attitudes toward homosexuality persist, there is no proportionally strong political or social mobilization against the rights of homosexual individuals. Indeed, a significant segment of the population endorses the civil rights of LGBT people in general. The main reason for these attitudes is that national identity often carries more social and political weight than religious affiliation. The research employed a mixed-methods design, integrating a literature review, historical and comparative analysis, two personal communications, and a structured questionnaire survey conducted with 1,050 respondents stratified into three age groups. The χ^2 test of independence was used to assess the associations between attitudes, gender, and age, while Cramer's V measured the strength of these relationships. The findings demonstrate that age exerts a statistically significant influence on attitudes, whereas gender differences are relatively small. The majority of the respondents (74.8%) recognize that homosexuals and lesbians often marry heterosexually to conform to tradition, while 77.3% believe imprisonment would not eliminate homosexuality. Furthermore, the results indicated that more than half (53.2%) oppose renewed punishment for homosexuals, and 52% acknowledge its timeless existence. The findings of this study suggest that attitudes toward homosexuality in Kosovo are shaped by a complex interplay of historical experience, legal change, cultural norms, and contemporary human rights discourse. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Risk perception and preventive control in indoor plant production: food safety practices among Swedish operators of leafy vegetables and microgreens
Abstract: Indoor plant production is often promoted as a controlled production system that can reduce some hazards associated with open-field cultivation. However, ready-to-eat leafy vegetables, herbs, microgreens and sprouts remain vulnerable to microbial contamination through seeds, water, nutrient solutions, growing media, surfaces and human handling. This study investigated how Swedish commercial indoor production operators perceive and manage food safety in their urban soilless production systems. A mixed-methods design was used, combining an online survey of 17 respondents with semi-structured interviews with representatives from eight indoor production operations. Fisher's exact tests showed no statistically significant association between awareness of applicable safety requirements and educational level, certification status, or previous safety training. Interview data showed that food safety management was shaped by three interrelated dimensions: risk perception, preventive control practices, and economic, spatial and regulatory constraints. Some operators interpreted controlled indoor production as inherently low risk, whereas others recognized system specific hazards and reported routines for seed treatment, water testing, cleaning, employee hygiene, documentation and certification. Resource limitations, testing costs, limited space, language barriers and unclear regulatory communication constrained implementation. Because the study did not include observation, audit or microbiological sampling, it addresses perceived safety and reported preventive control rather than verified food safety performance. The findings reinforce that indoor plant production modifies, but does not remove, the food safety risk landscape. Strengthening food safety in this sector requires practical, regulation-aligned training, scalable guidance, and verifiable preventive controls adapted to indoor production systems. © 2026

Title: From Individual Reasoning to Collaborative Engagement: Continuity of Student Problematic in Grade 1 Mathematical Problem Solving
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This qualitative study examined the continuity of student problematic from individual reasoning to collaborative engagement in a Grade 1 mathematics classroom within the Transformative Lesson Study Incorporating Open Approach (TLSOA) context. Seven Grade 1 students were followed across six lessons on addition and subtraction. Data were collected through video and audio recordings, students’ written work, field notes, and photographs, and analyzed using protocol analysis and analytic description. The findings show that student problematic remained observable when students re-engaged with the same mathematical problem in small groups. Student problematic appeared through proposing, questioning, explaining, checking, reconsidering, and coordinating mathematical ideas. The study contributes to understanding how young learners’ mathematical engagement continues across changing social contexts. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

Title: Beyond the final product: AI-Enabled Learner Traces as Assessment Evidence in Project Management Education
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in project management education (PME), especially in digital learning environments where learner activity can be captured as process data. This matters because project management learning involves collaboration, coordination, decision-making, reflection, and professional judgement, which are difficult to assess through final outputs alone. This systematic mapping review examines how AI-generated or AI-mediated learner data are collected, analysed, and used for assessment-related purposes, and identifies the educational implications reported in the literature. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches were conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, ERIC, and IEEE Xplore for studies published between January 2016 and November 2025. Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The review identified five categories of AI-enabled learner data and assessment-relevant evidence: human–AI dialogue and prompt-based interaction logs, adaptive and personalised learning process data, project artefacts and revision traces, reflective, self-report, and course feedback evidence, and standardised task, output, and scoring data. These categories are treated as different layers in the data-to-evidence process rather than as learner traces in a narrow technical sense. Future-oriented conceptual data systems were identified as an emerging possibility but were treated separately from reported learner data and assessment evidence. Across the included studies, data were analysed using natural language processing, machine learning, rule-based techniques, learning analytics, and generative AI/LLM-based prompting, and were used to generate feedback, indicators, recommendations, and scoring support. Reported benefits mainly relate to formative feedback, improved visibility of learning processes, and more timely instructional support. However, the evidence base remains limited and uneven, with important gaps in validity, fairness, transparency, and longer-term educational effects. Overall, AI in PME is used not simply to automate assessment, but to broaden how learner activity is captured, interpreted, and used to support process-oriented assessment and pedagogical judgement. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Optimizing renewable energy planning: a Monte Carlo–analytical hierarchy process framework for net-zero transitions
Abstract: As the world pursues net-zero emissions, selecting renewable energy technologies presents a complex challenge balancing technical, economic, environmental, and social factors. Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods support decisions by comparing alternatives against multiple criteria. However, traditional MCDM approaches, reliant on fixed inputs, often fail to capture real-world variability in energy planning, yielding less reliable outcomes. This study introduces a novel Monte Carlo–Analytical Hierarchy Process (MAHP) framework that integrates AHP's structured evaluation with Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) to model uncertainty in criteria weights and alternative scores. The MAHP framework was applied to support Sheffield's 2030 net-zero target by evaluating five renewable energy technologies: solar PV, onshore wind, biomass, hydropower, and geothermal. Thousands of simulations were conducted to reflect different stakeholder priorities, covering technical, environmental, social, economic, and equal-weighting scenarios. The analysis demonstrated that technology rankings are highly sensitive to stakeholder priorities, underscoring the need for adaptable planning approaches, and showing that no single technology consistently dominates when priorities are balanced. Overall, the results support a hybrid mix centred on solar PV, onshore wind, and hydropower for Sheffield. This framework strengthens renewable energy planning by moving beyond single deterministic rankings and instead quantifying how robust each recommendation is under uncertainty and shifting priorities. By making ranking stability and trade-offs explicit, MAHP enhances the credibility of technology selection and provides decision-makers with clearer evidence to support defensible net-zero strategies in dynamic urban contexts. More broadly, probabilistic ranking supports portfolio planning by identifying consistently competitive technologies, reducing over-commitment when stakeholder priorities and evidence are uncertain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Network science in sports
Abstract: Network science has become a central methodological framework for the study of complex systems, with applications across social, biological, and technological domains. Its strength lies in formalizing such systems as collections of interacting units, whose collective behavior depends not only on the properties of the individual components, but also on the structure, dynamics, and evolution of their interactions. In this Review, we analyze how this framework, rooted in statistical physics, is being applied to the study of sports systems. Sports provide a particularly suitable domain for network modeling, as performance emerges from interactions among agents, whose actions are constrained by spatial embedding and temporal ordering, and evolve under competitive, adaptive, and out-of-equilibrium conditions. We review the main network representations used in sports, from classical graph-based descriptions to more general frameworks, including spatial, temporal, multilayer, and higher-order networks. Particular attention is devoted to soccer, where network science has had its deepest methodological impact, while applications to other sports such as basketball, volleyball, American football, or badminton serve to illustrate the generality of the underlying principles. Network science provides sports analytics with a rigorous language for quantifying coordination, emergence, adaptation, and collective performance. At the same time, the availability of high-resolution event, tracking, and pose-estimation data makes sports an ideal testbed for validating and refining network models in realistic settings. As a result, the relationship between network science and sports, currently driven primarily by the application of network methods to sport, has the potential to become genuinely bidirectional. In this Review, we not only organize the literature on network methodologies and their applications to sports, but also discuss complementary concepts needed to capture the full picture, including entropy and complexity measures, as well as key ideas from statistical physics and nonlinear dynamics. Finally, despite the substantial progress made so far, the field remains under active development, and we highlight the main open questions that should be addressed in future research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Evaluating feasibility of an ACT group telehealth-delivered therapy intervention for adolescents with depression
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Increasing rates of adolescent depression call for efficient and accessible interventions that are well received by adolescents. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a third-wave psychotherapy that has been shown to be effective in treating depression in adolescents, delivered both individually and in group settings. Group therapy can help address service provider shortages by enabling a single provider to treat multiple individuals at once. Additionally, telehealth allows greater access to care for individuals who cannot readily travel to a clinic. Telehealth-delivered group therapy combines these two strategies to facilitate adolescents’ access to mental health treatment. We piloted a 10-week group intervention, adapted from ACT for Adolescents with Depression, and explored its feasibility. Adolescent patients with depression (N = 10) ages 14 to 18 (M = 16; SD = 1.49 years), seeking mental health services, participated in the program and completed pre and post assessments. The majority identified as female (70%) and White (60%). The groups were well attended; only one patient dropped out, and one was discharged. The patients reported overwhelmingly overall positive experiences with the program. Group means for depression and anxiety scores in this sample decreased from baseline to end of treatment, psychological flexibility increased by the end of treatment, and no changes were observed in flourishing scores. Overall, the intervention was well accepted. Well-powered research studies with randomized allocation to telehealth delivered ACT and control groups are needed to test this protocol’s effectiveness in treating depression in adolescents as an independent treatment or as adjunct treatment to individual therapy. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Authors: Jin B.; He B.; Zhao Y.; Liu Y.; Ding J.; Meng L.; Shi Y.; Han D.; Sun J.
Title: A multi-objective planning study of distributed photovoltaics based on candidate-node screening and an MO-ISSA method
Abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (DPV) siting and sizing in distribution networks is a high-dimensional discrete optimization problem with coupled objectives. Existing studies usually focus on optimizer improvement or full-bus-set planning, while the coordinated improvement of search-space reduction and Pareto-front quality remains insufficient. To address this issue, a DPV planning framework combining topology-aware candidate-node screening and a Multi-Objective Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (MO-ISSA) is proposed. A Node Comprehensive Importance Index (NCII), integrating inter-community connections, betweenness centrality, and active-power-loss improvement, is constructed to identify candidate nodes before optimization. MO-ISSA is then used to solve a three-objective model considering economic benefit, comprehensive grid vulnerability, and active power loss. Results on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed screening strategy reduces computation time while maintaining planning quality. Compared with NSGA-II, MOPSO, and SSA, MO-ISSA achieves better Pareto-front quality, convergence, and stability. Comparisons with the full-node-space heuristic result, an SOCP-representable deterministic surrogate reference model, and full-node-space standard algorithms further verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The IEEE 69-bus case confirms its applicability to larger distribution networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Efficient IP Lookup Using a B-Tree on Expanded Trie
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: As routing tables continue to increase in size, IP address lookup has become a critical performance bottleneck in packet forwarding. A fundamental challenge arises from the variable-length nature of IP prefixes, which requires longest prefix matching (LPM) to identify the appropriate next-hop router. This paper presents BTET (B-tree on Expanded Trie), an efficient data structure designed to support high-performance IP address lookup. BTET combines the hierarchical organization of B-trees with the Controlled Prefix Expansion (CPE) technique to achieve efficient lookup and update operations. The core of the proposed structure consists of a collection of B-trees, where each expanded prefix is partitioned into multiple segments, and each segment is stored in the B-tree corresponding to its expansion level. Before insertion, every prefix is expanded using the CPE technique. Experimental results demonstrate that BTET provides high memory efficiency while requiring only a small number of memory accesses during lookup operations. These characteristics make the proposed data structure a practical and scalable solution for deployment in modern routing environments. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Patient Characteristics Associated With Preference for 480-mL Oral Sodium Sulfate: A Prospective Clinical Study on Bowel Cleansing Efficacy and Taste Acceptability for Total Colonoscopy
Abstract: Background and Aims: Oral sulfate solutions (OSSs) are used for low-volume bowel preparation but have a distinctive bitter taste. This study evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of OSSs compared with polyethylene glycol plus ascorbate (PEG-ASC) and identified patient factors associated with favorable acceptability. Methods: In this prospective single-center study, patients undergoing colonoscopy using OSSs who had used PEG-ASC for a previous colonoscopy within 2 years were enrolled. Cleansing quality (Boston Bowel Preparation Scale [BBPS]), ingested volume, adverse events, patient preference, and taste acceptability were assessed. Outcomes were also compared between elderly (≥75 years) and non-elderly patients. Results: Among 263 patients, 98% achieved satisfactory cleansing (BBPS ≥ 6). Overall, 54% preferred OSS for their next procedure. Multivariate analysis identified favorable taste acceptability as the strongest predictor of preference (odds ratio [OR], 4.88). Favorable taste acceptability tended to be associated with male sex (OR, 1.58; p = 0.09) and age ≥ 75 years (OR, 1.69; p = 0.07). Older male patients showed significantly higher favorable taste acceptability than younger female patients (63% vs. 40%; p = 0.03). Elderly patients had lower total fluid intake (p = 0.04) and fewer adverse events (p < 0.01), particularly nausea, while maintaining cleansing quality equivalent to non-elderly patients. Conclusions: OSS provided high-quality cleansing with a reduced intake volume. Elderly patients tended to have favorable taste acceptability for OSS, and effective cleansing was achieved with even lower total fluid intake and fewer adverse events. Title: A tax-subsidy scheme for efficient investment in renewable generation capacity
Abstract: Electricity markets are central to the energy transition, but current market rules do not always deliver socially desirable outcomes. This paper studies two related inefficiencies in wholesale electricity markets. First, competitive market-clearing based on merit-order dispatch can ignore pollution damages, leading to inefficient spot-market outcomes. We address this distortion by deriving a Pigouvian tax that charges each generator for its marginal contribution to pollution damages. Second, because generation capacity affects future spot prices, producers may strategically distort their long-run investment decisions, particularly in systems with increasingly low-operating-cost renewable generation. To align private investment incentives with social welfare, we derive a generator-specific investment subsidy based on each producer's contribution to aggregate utility. We show that, under the stated behavioral and informational assumptions, the combined tax–subsidy mechanism aligns decentralized dispatch and generation-capacity investment decisions with the social-welfare benchmark while respecting operational constraints. Implementing this mechanism does not require producers to report their complete private cost functions; the tax and subsidy can instead be calculated using existing market submissions and settlement data, verified emission information, and generator-specific counterfactual market re-clearing outcome. An analytical example and numerical experiments illustrate the mechanism and show that strategic capacity investment can exceed the socially optimal level and reduce welfare. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Unbowed: Raiding and Hunting with Paracas Spearthrowers and Slings and the Conspicuous Absence of the Bow in Western South America
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: New weapons such as the bow and arrow often emerge alongside rising population densities and interpersonal conflict. We test this generalization in southern Peru during the violent Final Formative (400–1 BCE) with measurements of 200 obsidian projectile points anchored to precise Bayesian chronologies from Paracas sites in the Palpa valleys. Based on Bayesian regressions against hafted archaeological projectile points, we conclude all Paracas points were spearthrower darts. This agrees with the lack of bows in Paracas burials and in imagery on ceramics and textiles. Conflict was limited to small-scale raids, based on a compilation of sites with slingstones, mace heads, skeletal trauma, and walls. Hunting and herding were focused in the highlands, mapped with a MaxEnt predictive surface of modern prey location. Based on spatial correlations, conflict did not drive settlement patterns; the key factors were hunting grounds, herding pastures, and agricultural suitability. Pending future research, the notable lack of the bow in the region may include later Nasca, Moche, and Chimú populations. This invites us to rethink the conditions that drive and limit the adoption and invention of bows, a uniquely human and purportedly superior projectile technology that no one bothered with during these violent centuries. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: The Fragility of Collective Action in Community Forest Management: Social Feedbacks, Trust, and Cooperation Dynamics
Abstract: In community forest management, cooperation is rarely a one-time decision. It depends on whether local actors continue contributing time, labor, and resources year after year. We examine this problem with a system dynamics model that follows changes in trust, reputation, reciprocity, perceived benefits, and free-riding. The model adapts an earlier structure to the case of ejido La Loma, Mexico. The case material guided several modeling decisions, especially the choice of variables and the interpretation of the scenarios. It did not, however, provide enough information for full empirical calibration. The simulations show that trust and reputation may sustain cooperation even as participation declines. Over time, however, the loss of active members can weaken monitoring and place collective action at risk. One result is particularly relevant: a favorable starting point does not guarantee long-term stability. Title: Genetic engineering of cyanophages for harmful cyanobacterial bloom treatment—A mini review
Abstract: Harmful cyanobacterial blooms (HCBs) are a prominent worldwide environmental concern. Proliferation of HCBs outpaces the development of mitigation and management technologies. Recently, cyanophages began to emerge as a potential abundant resource that can be harnessed for target-specific HCB treatment. However, there exist two major technical barriers in applying cyanophage-based treatment to HCB mitigation: host specificity and lysogenic life cycle. This minireview attempts to parse documented studies that developed or applied genetic engineering approaches or technologies to tackle the barriers through expanding host range and bypassing or abolishing the lysogenic life stage. We summarized representative technical approaches that may be extrapolated from bacteriophage to cyanophage, discussed genes and pathways that regulate host binding and infection or determine the switch between lytic and lysogenic lifecycles, identified existing knowledge and technological gaps and challenges, and proposed some attainable solutions and future perspectives for this fast-growing field of engineered cyanophage-mediated HCB remediation. © 2026 .

Title: Re-imagining visions as shared societal statements– empirical insights from Indian cities
Abstract: Visions in Indian cities lack commitment from actors and possess low normative power. To address these concerns, we take up the task of examining vision-making with a focus on institutional settings across 31 million-plus populated cities. Ostrom's Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) framework and ADICO grammar tool are used for analysis. We ask how rules-in-use within the vision-making settings are organized and geared towards collective action, and how they affect outcomes, i.e., visions. The analysis underscores three commonalities that hinder collective action, i.e., bureaucratic hegemony and allegiance to sectoral mandates, fragmented actor constellation and weak regulatory power of visions. Within visioning settings, facilitators serve as key agents for ensuring a level playing field. We found that when facilitators are external (i.e., consultants), stakeholder coverage is wider and documentation is exhaustive. In large metropolises and megacities, the visioning process acknowledges stakeholder consultation responsibly. Perhaps fair information exchange and informal monitoring of visions by civil society actors contribute to the politicisation of vision-making. In institutional terms, visions are closer to being a strategy and less to norm-setting. The paper argues that participatory discussions in diverse and heterogeneous settings with the scope of repeat interactions will build homophily and address concerns of structural fragmentation. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Algorithms-Based Monitoring of Vaccine Coverage in Chronic-Disease Cohorts: A Population-Based Evaluation of Regional Immunization Policy in Emilia-Romagna, Italy
Abstract: Objectives This study aims at estimating uptake of risk-based recommended adult vaccinations among major chronic-condition subgroups in Emilia-Romagna Region (Italy) and at quantifying sociodemographic and territorial determinants of vaccine uptake. Vaccination histories were retrieved from the Regional Vaccination Registry-Real Time (2000-2024); uptake was defined as ≥1 recorded dose. Uptake was modeled via subgroup-specific multivariable logistic regression (sex, age group, citizenship, Local Health Authority). Results Pneumococcal uptake ranged from 28.4% in cancer to 40.7% in COPD and was markedly higher in anatomical asplenia (85.1%). Composite uptake mirrored these patterns (32.6% cancer; 42.0% COPD; 85.5% asplenia). Uptake of other risk-indicated vaccines was low in large subgroups, whereas asplenia showed high meningococcal uptake (MenACWY 67.5%; MenB 65.8%). Title: Territorializing the sea: fragmented operational control in offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia
Abstract: The expansion of offshore tin mining transforms the sea into a space of extraction, yet territorial claims over this space do not necessarily translate into operational control. Studies of territorialization have largely focused on the formation of claims rather than on the processes through which such claims are converted into operational control. This article examines the territorialization of offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia, through three interrelated analytical moments: territorial claims, securing access, and operational control. This qualitative study draws on fieldwork comprising interviews with 23 informants and observations, supplemented by a review of relevant literature and an analysis of regulatory documents, corporate reports, and news coverage. The findings show that exploration and regulatory arrangements produce epistemic and legal claims over marine space but do not, in themselves, enable mining operations. Companies and their local networks must still secure access by cultivating and representing support, engaging village institutions and local intermediaries, negotiating benefits, and making personal approaches to key actors. Their success varies across locations, shaped by local power relations, actor legitimacy, and fisher resistance. Consequently, operational control is contingent, partial, fragmented, and continuously negotiated: mining operations can proceed in some locations, whereas elsewhere territorial claims remain in force without being translated into operational control. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Loneliness trajectories and psychosocial, behavioral, and functional vulnerability among cancer survivors: A comparison of patients aged 50–64, 65–74, and ≥75 years
Abstract: Introduction Loneliness is common among older cancer survivors and may contribute to depressive symptoms, adverse health behaviors, functional decline, and loss of independence. National data on loneliness trajectories and survivorship-related vulnerability remain limited. Materials and methods The study cohort included cancer survivors aged ≥50 years from the 2022 Health and Retirement Study, with age categorized as 50–64, 65–74, and 75 years or older. Loneliness was the primary exposure; 2020–2022 data were used to classify survivors as never lonely, or as having incident, resolved, or persistent loneliness. Survey-weighted logistic and linear regression models were used to evaluate associations between loneliness and psychosocial, behavioral, and functional measures after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidity burden, and self-rated health, as applicable. Results Among 2331 cancer survivors aged 50 years or older, mean age was 72.4 years, 59.5% ( n = 1387) were female, and 18.6% ( n = 433) reported loneliness. In cross-sectional multivariable analyses, loneliness was associated with higher odds of elevated depressive symptom burden (aOR, 11.21; 95% CI, 7.44–16.90), loss of independence (aOR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.01–2.31), fair or poor self-rated health (aOR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.35–2.72), and current smoking (aOR, 2.37; 95% CI, 1.06–5.29). In a separate adjusted linear regression model, loneliness was associated with a 3.10-point higher continuous Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression score (β, 3.10; 95% CI, 2.82–3.39). In longitudinal trajectory analyses, persistent loneliness (aOR, 15.78) and incident loneliness (aOR, 8.32), but not resolved loneliness, were associated with elevated depressive symptom burden. Discussion Among cancer survivors aged 50 years or older in the United States, loneliness was associated with depressive symptom burden, worse self-rated health, current smoking, and loss of independence. Persistent and newly emergent loneliness identified survivors with the greatest depressive burden, supporting repeated loneliness assessment to guide targeted psychosocial, behavioral, and functional support. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Optimized machine learning models for identification of autism spectrum disorder
Source title: International Journal of Cognitive Computing in Engineering
Abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) relies heavily on identifying critical behavioral and clinical markers within high-dimensional datasets. However, standard feature selection methods frequently struggle with premature convergence and suboptimal feature identification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an approach based on an Improved White Shark Optimizer combined with Machine Learning classifiers (IWSO-ML). The proposed approach engineers a dynamic balance between global exploration and local refinement by integrating an adaptive PSO-WSO velocity update, differential evolution, and covariance-based exploitation. To ensure robust search space navigation and prevent local optima entrapment, IWSO-ML incorporates Sobol/Halton chaotic initialization, a shrinking search radius, and stagnation-aware population control. The algorithmic superiority of the approach is first validated against the complex CEC’2022 continuous benchmark suite. The proposed IWSO-ML evaluated clinically across four diverse ASD datasets including adult, children in UCI, and prediction, screening in Kaggle using five distinct classification models (SVM, K-NN, RF, DT, and GNB). Extensive statistical analysis confirm that IWSO-ML consistently outperforms state-of-the-art metaheuristics, including RUN, HHO, IMODE, PSO, SSA, WOA and MFO. Notably, the IWSO-SVM configuration achieved a peak classification accuracy of 99.5%, demonstrating superior convergence speed, narrowed error distributions, and exceptional solution stability. Ultimately, this hybrid architecture provides a highly generalized and computationally efficient feature selection mechanism, establishing a robust foundation for reliable clinical predictive modeling and advanced ASD diagnostics. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Cost-Effectiveness of Peripheral Neuropathy Screening in Patients With Thalassemia: A Hybrid Decision-Markov Model
Abstract: Objectives To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a systematic screening program for thalassemia-related peripheral neuropathy (ThalPN) compared with standard care in Malaysia. Methods A hybrid decision-Markov model was developed to simulate the lifetime health outcomes and costs for a hypothetical cohort of adult thalassemia patients (both transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent). The analysis was conducted from a healthcare provider perspective, utilizing the neuropathy symptomatic score and neuropathy disability score as screening tools. The model was populated with data from the Malaysian Thalassemia Registry, a clinical cohort study for prevalence and utility values, and published literature. Costs and health outcomes were discounted at 3% annually. Results The screening strategy for ThalPN was found to be highly cost-effective across all age cohorts compared with standard care. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was most favorable in the ≥40 age group at USD 2027 per quality-adjusted life-year gained. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratios for the 18 to 29 and 30 to 39 age groups were USD 2951 and USD 3209 per quality-adjusted life-year gained, respectively. Conclusions Incorporating a ThalPN screening program into standard care is a cost-effective strategy. By facilitating early intervention, screening can prevent or slow irreversible disease progression, thereby improving health-related quality of life and potentially reducing long-term costs for this patient population. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Graphitic-shell-mediated interfacial bonding and MWCNT-enabled electrical percolation in superhard cBN composites
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: Conductive superhard cubic boron nitride(cBN)-based composites are difficult to realize because conductive additives often weaken the covalent load-bearing framework. Here, we demonstrate a graphitic-shell-mediated interface/network strategy for integrating electrical transport with superhardness in cBN composites synthesized by high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) sintering at 5 GPa and 1400 °C. Surface-graphitized nanodiamonds and multi-walled carbon nanotubes were incorporated into a polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PcBN) matrix to couple robust cBN/diamond load bearing with carbon-network conduction. The optimized composite exhibits a Vickers hardness of 40.8 GPa, and an electrical conductivity of 1.33 × 104 S m−1, with rapid net mass loss observed near 1331 °C in air under the present thermogravimetric analysis conditions. Microstructural, Raman, and transport analyses reveal strongly bonded cBN/diamond interfaces and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-connected carbon-rich pathways. This interfacial/network architecture partially decouples mechanical and electrical functions, offering a practical route to overcome the hardness–conductivity trade-off in cBN-based superhard ceramic composites. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: AI-enabled cyberbullying detection from a cyber-physical-social-thinking space integration perspective: Theories, technologies, and challenges
Abstract: Cyberbullying has emerged as a pervasive threat to digital well-being, evolving into a multidimensional phenomenon that spans multiple interconnected spaces. Despite significant progress in detection techniques, existing approaches predominantly rely on textual analysis, limiting their ability to capture the full spectrum of cyberbullying behaviors and contextual dependencies. To address this limitation, this study presents a systematic review with qualitative synthesis of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection through the lens of Cyber-Physical-Social-Thinking (CPST) space integration. Based on 120 included studies, the review develops three principal outputs. First, it develops a fusion-mechanism taxonomy of AI-enabled cyberbullying detection research across cyber, physical, social, and thinking dimensions, organizing how content, contextual, relational, behavioral, and cognitive information is combined to support more comprehensive and context-aware detection. Second, it establishes a quantitative and descriptive landscape of the reviewed literature across CPST-space coverage, modalities, model families, publication trends, social media platforms, dataset characteristics, and evaluation metrics. Third, it develops a four-level conceptual taxonomy that organizes cyberbullying-related information into observable evidence, latent states, behaviors, and outcomes. Building on this evidence-based output, the study synthesizes a CPST-based conceptual reference architecture that organizes heterogeneous data sources, feature representations, information-fusion strategies, and decision-making processes, while distinguishing the differing empirical maturity of the four spaces. The review further synthesizes state-of-the-art AI technologies, including natural language processing, computer vision, network analysis, affective computing, and multimodal learning, in relation to their roles in cross-space information integration. The synthesis identifies key challenges, including data privacy, bias, and generalization, and highlights research opportunities involving explainable AI, federated learning, and human-in-the-loop systems. The resulting synthesis provides a structured evidence base for understanding existing fusion approaches and guiding future research on cross-space cyberbullying detection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Behavior of Children with Down Syndrome During Preventive Dental Care: An Observational Study

Abstract: Objective: To compare behavior guidance techniques (BGTs) applied to children with and without Down Syndrome (DS) during preventive dental care. Material and Methods: This observational, cross-sectional study included 40 children aged 2-6 years with and without DS. Heart rate and the dentist´s subjective evaluation were assessed in the waiting room, during the anamnesis, during the child's positioning, during the preventive procedure, and at the end of the preventive procedure. The Melamed´s Modified Behavior Scale was evaluated during the preventive procedure and the Frankl's Behavior Rating Scale (FBRS) was classified after dental care. The BGTs applied were evaluated by direct observation. Friedman and Mann-Whitney U tests and Spearman's Correlation Coefficient were applied. Results: A total of 76 attempts were required to perform the dental procedure for children with DS and 42 for children without DS. According to Friedman's test (p = 0.7385), there were no statistically significant differences in heart rate values across all children in the five situations analyzed. In the Mann-Whitney U test, statistically significant differences were found between the following variables: heart rate during anamnesis (p = 0.0166) and during the preventive procedure (p = 0.0009), and the highest values were obtained in children with DS in both cases. In Spearman's post-correlation coefficient, negative and statistically significant correlations were found between the values of the following variables: age, when compared with all heart rate during anamnesis (p = 0.016), in the child’s positioning (p = 0.018), preventive procedure (p = 0.027) and at the end of the procedure (p = 0.017). Conclusion: There was a difference between groups in relation to the behavior evaluated by the physiological method. Title: Dislocation network-induced multiple deformation mechanisms enabling a near-α titanium alloy with high strength-ductility synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Overcoming the intrinsic strength-ductility trade-off remains a central challenge in developing advanced titanium (Ti) alloys, as conventional strengthening strategies invariably sacrifice ductility. Here, we propose a dislocation engineering strategy that deliberately constructs ordered dislocation networks in the TA18 alloy, achieving exceptional strength-ductility synergy. These ordered geometric architectures are robustly stabilized by sessile jogs originating from specific crystallographic interactions between <a> and <c+a> dislocations. During early deformation, the networks subdivide grains into fine deformable units, providing massive initial strain hardening by impeding mobile dislocations via the dislocation jog dragging effect. With progressive strain, inhomogeneous local stresses drive the sweeping out of jogs, dynamically transforming the static networks into glissile dislocation arrays and dense dislocation walls. This critical structural evolution triggers a fundamental transition to a “transport-dominated” plasticity regime, activating potent hetero-deformation-induced strengthening and indirect slip transfer. These findings establish a scalable paradigm for designing high-performance Ti alloys via dislocation architecture control. © 2026

Title: Multi-level analysis of firearm reoffending: the importance of community and incident context
Abstract: Criminologists have long noted the exacerbated rates of firearm-related offending in the United States in comparison to other developed nations. There has been a renewed focus on gun crime in the wake of a recent dramatic reversal of the long-trending decrease in firearm-related violence. Although they provide valuable insights, explorations of the factors that contribute to firearm offending are often restricted to large metro areas like Chicago, New York City, and Philadelphia—which may have limited generalizability to more common small and medium sized cities in the United States. This study attempts to address this concern through examination of the factors that contribute to firearm re-offending among arrestees in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Specifically, multi-level analysis is used to explore the relative influence of neighborhood conditions, arrestee demographics, gang involvement, and offense characteristics on the odds of firearm reoffending among a sample of individuals arrested for gun crimes committed between 1/1/21 and 4/30/23 (n = 937). Our findings reveal null influence across contextual factors, while gang membership and juvenile status are each associated with increased odds in firearm reoffending. Title: Beyond positive attitude: What motivates stem undergraduates to engage in classroom discussions?
Abstract: Fostering active participation in classroom discussions remains a persistent challenge in higher education, particularly in STEM fields where lecture-based instruction remains prevalent. While positive attitudes are often considered an important predictors of participation in classroom discussions, this study examines a broader set of psychological factors associated with STEM undergraduates’ intention to participate in classroom discussions. We propose and test an integrated model incorporating attitude, subjective norms, perceived need, and self-efficacy. Using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) on data from 550 undergraduates from engineering-focused universities, the study examines the motivational factors associated with participation intention and willingness to recommend classroom discussions. Perceived need and self-efficacy showed the strongest statistical associations with both outcomes. Subjective norms were positively associated with participation intention but not willingness to recommend, whereas attitude did not demonstrate a significant unique effect in the full model. Additional analyses suggest that this pattern reflects the stronger explanatory role of perceived need when considered alongside students’ general evaluations of classroom discussions. These findings highlight the importance of perceived learning value and confidence in predicting students’ participation in classroom discussions and provide context-specific implications for discussion-based teaching in engineering education. Title: Landscapes of extraction: Youth, coal and contested livelihoods in Tinsukia, Assam
Abstract: The article explores the diverse and intersecting forms through which youth encounter, experience, and respond to coal mining in Tinsukia, Assam’s easternmost resource-rich district. Drawing on qualitative ethnographic fieldwork in the Ledo and Margherita coalfields, it examines how extractive economies reshape youth livelihoods, aspirations and vulnerabilities in a landscape marked by environmental devastation, informalization of labour, and uneven development The article focuses on three connected processes: the erosion of traditional livelihoods and ecological relations; entry into precarious and informal mining-related work; and the emergence of critique and resistance. Rather than treating youth as a homogeneous category, the article analyzes how their positions are not fixed but fluid. It shows how their positions differ according to access to land, labour, networks, and political resources, while also shifting between economic dependence, negotiation, and opposition. The article contributes to political ecology and extractive-frontier scholarship by foregrounding youth perspectives from a Northeast Indian coal belt and by showing how development is experienced simultaneously as livelihood opportunity and socio-environmental harm. Title: High-thermal-conductivity GFRP for dry-type air-core reactors: thermal-electrical performance and trade-off analysis
Abstract: Dry-type air-core reactors suffer from localized overheating due to the limited thermal conductivity of conventional glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) insulation. Enhancing the thermal conductivity of GFRP provides a potential approach for improving reactor heat dissipation; however, excessive incorporation of thermally conductive fillers may compromise electrical insulation reliability. This study establishes an integrated material-to-equipment evaluation framework to investigate the thermal-electrical trade-off of high-thermal-conductivity GFRP (HTC-GFRP) for dry-type air-core reactors. HTC-GFRP samples with different alumina contents were prepared, and their thermal conductivity, dielectric properties, AC flashover voltage, and breakdown strength were experimentally characterized. The results demonstrate that increasing alumina loading effectively enhances thermal conductivity by promoting the formation of thermally conductive pathways, whereas excessive filler incorporation leads to deterioration of insulation performance. Considering both thermal enhancement and electrical insulation reliability, a favorable thermal conductivity range of approximately 0.75–0.95 W/(m·K) was identified. Furthermore, multiphysics simulations of a 10 kV dry-type air-core reactor reveal that increasing the GFRP thermal conductivity from 0.35 to 1.3 W/(m·K) reduces the maximum operating temperature by approximately 3 °C. These results demonstrate the thermal-electrical trade-off of HTC-GFRP and provide quantitative guidance for balancing heat dissipation capability and insulation reliability in dry-type air-core reactors. © 2026

Title: Harnessing the power of AI in qualitative research: Role assignment, engagement, and user perceptions of AI-generated follow-up questions in semi-structured interviews

Title: Beyond transactions: Cultural role enactment, positive emotional response, and supportive behavioral intention in Northeast China

Abstract: Language learning strategies refer to deliberate behaviors, processes, and approaches through which learners receive, process, and use new information in a structured and purposeful manner, thereby promoting self-directed learning, self-regulation, and learner responsibility. Due to a lack of sufficient empirical research in this area, the present study aims to investigate the relationship between language learning strategies, learning engagement, and writing skills in an Arabic language writing curriculum. This study employed a descriptive-correlational design and included 70 female undergraduate students of Arabic Language and Literature at Kharazmi University in 2019. Data were collected using the Oxford Language Learning Strategies Scale (1990), the Learning Engagement Scale developed by Schaufeli et al. (2002), and a researcher-developed writing skills questionnaire. The data were analyzed using regression analysis.The results revealed a positive and significant relationship between language learning strategies, their components (except for the affective/emotional strategy), learning engagement, and Arabic writing skills. Furthermore, the findings indicated that language learning strategies and learning engagement together account for 17% of the variance in writing skills. These results suggest that the use of effective language learning strategies and higher levels of learning engagement can enhance students' writing performance.In practical terms, the findings of this study propose a pedagogical model for integrating language learning strategies and strengthening learning engagement within the curriculum. Title: Correlations between cerebrospinal fluid and plasma levels of GABA, glutamate, dopamine, and related metabolites, and their concentrations across neurological disorders
Abstract: Background Neurotransmitters play critical roles in both central and peripheral nervous system function. However, the correlation between cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma levels of neurotransmitters remains incompletely understood, limiting the interpretation of peripheral measurements as surrogates for central neurochemical changes. This study aimed to investigate the correlations between CSF and plasma levels of GABA, glutamate, dopamine, and related metabolites, and to explore their expressions across common neurological disorders in a real-world clinical setting. Methods A total of 181 paired CSF and plasma samples from patients with neurological disorders and 67 plasma samples from healthy controls were analyzed. Concentrations of GABA, betaine, L-DOPA, histamine, glutamine, glutamate, dopamine, and choline were quantified using LC–MS/MS. Correlations between CSF and plasma concentrations were assessed using Pearson correlation analysis. Age- and sex-related effects were evaluated in healthy controls, and differences among disease groups were analyzed after classifying patients into neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs), CNS demyelinating diseases (CNS DDs), CNS tumors, and CNS infections. Results GABA, histamine, betaine, glutamate, and choline exhibited higher concentrations in plasma than in CSF, whereas glutamine concentrations were higher in CSF. Except for betaine and glutamate, all other neurotransmitters showed statistically significant but weak CSF–plasma correlations ( r = 0.15–0.7, p < 0.05). In healthy controls, plasma histamine, betaine, glutamate, and choline levels were higher in males. Plasma GABA levels in all disease groups were consistently lower than controls, and plasma glutamine levels in NDDs, CNS DDs, and CNS tumors were significantly higher than those in controls. By contrast, there were no significant differences in CSF levels among different disease groups, except that glutamate was higher in the CNS tumor group than in the other disease groups. Conclusions Most plasma neurotransmitters and their metabolites do not reliably reflect their CSF levels, which may provide important context for interpreting peripheral neurotransmitter biomarkers in CNS diseases. Title: Environmental risks of pest management practices in smallholder coconut plantations
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: Oryctes rhinoceros, the coconut rhinoceros beetle, remains one of the most damaging pests of coconut (Cocos nucifera) across South and Southeast Asia, the Pacific, and increasingly, new invasion fronts in the Americas. Although climatic alterations may redistribute the geographic footprint of the hazard, predictive assessments underscore non-linear and variable outcomes. Regional expansions in vulnerable or suitable extents are largely contingent upon the analytical scenario and structural parameters of the model utilized. This reinforces the case for treating its management as an environmental, not solely agronomic, concern. The study objectives were to characterize how smallholder-level management choices translate into differentiated environmental and health risk. Smallholder coconut plantations, which supply most world coconut production, are disproportionately exposed because of fragmented land holdings, limited capital, and constrained extension access. This review evaluates the translation of management interventions into distinct environmental and health hazards by systematically reviewing evidence on coconut rhinoceros beetle biology, intervention efficacy, smallholder socioeconomic dynamics, and insecticide risk literature through a standardized four-tier risk framework. Smallholders commonly rely on chemical control options such as organophosphates and pyrethroids. These options carry documented risks: non-target toxicity, soil and water contamination, and occupational exposure. In the absence of beetle-specific metrics, elevated occupational exposure risks are inferred from prevailing normative practices in smallholder agriculture concerning the omission of protective equipment. Biological and cultural alternatives include O. rhinoceros nudivirus, Metarhizium anisopliae, Bacillus thuringiensis, botanical larvicides, and pheromone-based trapping. These present a substantially lower environmental risk profile: laboratory bioassays report 90 to 100 percent larval mortality for Metarhizium isolates from East Java, comparable to the up to 98 percent larval and 90 percent adult mortality reported for a granular carbamate alternative, indicating technical efficacy is not the limiting factor, with field-deployed monitoring documented in Jepara and Bengkulu. Uptake of these lower-risk options is nonetheless constrained less by technical efficacy than by production economics, extension access, and the fragmented governance of smallholder replanting and pest-management programs. The evidence suggests that attenuating this risk burden is predominantly constrained by the disparity between existing lower-risk technological interventions and their operational uptake, among other compounding determinants. Risk-management strategies must therefore be designed around smallholder economic and institutional realities rather than efficacy data alone. Title: Intervening Impersistence on the St. Johns River, Florida
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Across 9000 years, shells were a common medium of terraforming along the St. Johns River in northeast Florida. In this regard, shell mounds nicely match definitions of persistent place. However, close attention paid to shells and their itineraries highlights how impersistent these places were. Shell, as a construction medium and an index of history, provided opportunities for re-establishing place in the context of change, even when used by settler colonists to build out Florida’s road networks in the twentieth century. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Assessment of Pragmatic Disorders in Persian­Speaking Adults with Acquired Brain Injury; [ارزیابی بیماران آسیب دیده مغزی بزرگ سال فارسی زبان از منظر اختلالات کاربرد شناختی]
Abstract: This study investigates pragmatic communication abilities in Persian-speaking adults with acquired brain injury (ABI), focusing on patients with right-hemisphere damage (RHD) and left-hemisphere damage (LHD). Pragmatic competence, crucial for interpreting metaphors and speech acts, depends on distributed neural networks, with increasing evidence highlighting the right hemisphere's critical role in processing non­literal meaning, inferencing, and social cues. Despite extensive research in non-Persian populations, evidence on pragmatic impairments in Persian speakers with focal brain injuries is limited. This study evaluates and compares pragmatic performance across RHD and LHD groups using the Montreal Protocol for the Evaluation of Communication (MEC). Results indicated that 60% of RHD patients exhibited pragmatic deficits compared to 30% of LHD patients, though group differences were not statistically significant (P > 0.05). Lesions in temporal lobe regions and adjacent areas were consistently associated with pragmatic impairments, suggesting a significant role for these regions in higher-level communication.
