Title: Activating slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 on CeO2 with concentrated sunlight to enable ethylene and propylene synthesis
Abstract: Harnessing solar light to convert CO2 and H2O into multi-carbon (C2+) fuels constitutes a critical strategy toward achieving carbon neutrality. This necessitates the development of photocatalytic systems and catalysts capable of breaking the linear activity-selectivity trade-off, which ultimately rests on a fundamental understanding of the key factors controlling C1–Cn (n ≥ 2) coupling selectivity. Herein, with CeO2 and Pr6O11 selected as model catalysts, we clarify that the decisive factor governing C2+ production is interfacial CO2 adsorption strength/coverage, rather than interfacial photogenerated charge carrier density or H2O dissociation/adsorption. Therefore, a solar‑concentrating photocatalytic system was designed to activate slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 with high local coverage, ultimately achieving substantial generation of C2+ products by a *CO–free formaldehyde self–condensation pathway, whereas almost no multi‑carbon products were observed under conventional photocatalytic reaction systems. Intriguingly, within this system, CeO2, despite its inferior photoelectric response and H2O activation capability compared to Pr6O11 and the Pr6O11/CeO2 composite, delivered the highest C2+ yield and molar selectivity. Over 56 h, it produced 109.69 μmol of C2H4 (19.79%) and 31.0 μmol of C3H6 (5.59%). These findings establish that, in concentrated solar light catalytic systems, the formation of C1–Cn bonds is closely related to interfacial CO2 adsorption behavior, and that slightly stronger CO2 adsorption strength is clearly beneficial for the generation of C2+ products. This insight advocates a new design paradigm under concentrated solar catalytic systems, focused on modulating CO2 adsorption strength/coverage rather than that of the *CO intermediate, moving beyond the traditional practice of avoiding either strong or weak binding. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Cost-Utility Analysis of Sentinel Node Biopsy Versus Selective Neck Dissection for Node-Negative Early-Stage Oral Cancers: A Health Economic Evaluation from the Indian Healthcare System Perspective
Abstract: Objectives To conduct a cost-utility analysis comparing sentinel node biopsy (SNB) with selective neck dissection (SND) for clinically node-negative early-stage oral cancer from the Indian healthcare system perspective. Methods A hybrid decision-tree-Markov model compared SNB with SND over a 10-year horizon, incorporating 18 clinical pathways, time-trade-off utilities from an Indian population, and costs from Indian settings. Model and R code construction were assisted by a large language model (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) with author verification. Effectiveness was measured in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. The primary outcome was net monetary benefit at the India-specific willingness-to-pay threshold of INR 212 307/QALY. Results SNB yielded 6.145 QALYs versus 6.032 for SND (incremental 0.114) at INR 332 865 versus INR 336 433 (incremental −INR 3568). SNB dominated SND in the deterministic base case. Under probabilistic sensitivity analysis, SNB was cost-effective in 78.5% of iterations at the India-specific threshold (mean incremental net monetary benefit INR 15 944; 95% CrI −INR 22 141 to INR 54 287) and 81.8% at 1× gross domestic product per capita (INR 245 000/QALY). A lifetime-horizon scenario (cohort age 55-100; 45 cycles) confirmed SNB dominance with incremental cost −INR 5466 and incremental QALYs 0.1767. Results were robust across deterministic and scenario analyses. Conclusions SNB is a cost-effective alternative to SND for clinically node-negative early-stage oral cancer in Indian tertiary cancer centers with appropriate technical expertise, dominating in the deterministic base case and remaining cost-effective in 78.5% of probabilistic iterations at the India-specific threshold. Title: Stage-aware deep learning with adversarial data synthesis enables prospective season-scale A/H1N1 influenza forecasting in China
Abstract: Accurate influenza forecasting is essential for public health preparedness, yet many models require future covariates, provide limited interpretability, and degrade under post-pandemic regime shifts. We propose a Stage-Aware Multimodal Neural Network (SAMNN) that integrates multimodal temporal features using configurations adapted to heterogeneous transmission regimes and supports season-ahead scenario forecasting using adversarially synthesized covariates. Using 13 years of national A/H1N1 surveillance data from mainland China (2011∼2024), SAMNN was evaluated across three epidemiologically distinct seasons spanning ∼20-fold differences in peak intensity. SAMNN achieved R  2  values of 0.82–0.95, 0.82-0.97, and 0.55-0.97 for 1-week-, 2-week-, and 4-week-ahead forecasting, respectively, and generally maintained competitive performance relative to five baseline models across forecast horizons. SHAP attribution showed that epidemiological signals dominated predictions, with context-dependent contributions from climatic and social-context features. To support prospective scenario forecasting, we used an adversarial synthetic covariate-generation pipeline to produce season-ahead forecasts for 2024/25 using information available at the prespecified forecast origin. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: 40 years of equity sensitivity: A theoretical and meta-analytic review of relations, roles, and remaining questions
Abstract: Organizational scholars have studied equity sensitivity (ES) for nearly half a century. Yet, a lack of synthesis in the ES literature suggests important questions remain regarding our understanding of the concept, its nomological network, the theoretical role(s) it may play in shaping employee attitudes and behaviors, and its relations to adjacent theories of equity and organizational justice. In the current work, we address these questions via a theoretical and meta-analytic review of the ES literature encompassing 117 articles, 144 samples, and 36,177 participants. In synthesizing the literature, we (1) describe and alleviate existing tensions surrounding the construct's conceptualization, (2) provide empirical insights regarding the construct's associations and relative importance in the prediction of key workplace outcomes, and (3) present an integrative model of ES's potential theoretical moderating role in equity and justice relationships. Our work provides clarity regarding ES's nomological network and offers critical directions for future scholarship. Specifically, we draw special attention to opportunities for new work exploring ES's potential as a key linking mechanism among equity and organizational justice theories. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Microclimate shifts driven by Lake Urmia shrinkage and their implications for urban cooling demand and carbon emissions under future climate scenarios
Abstract: Lake Urmia, one of the world's largest hypersaline lakes, has experienced dramatic shrinkage over recent decades, raising concerns regarding its impacts on regional climate, urban thermal environments, and energy sustainability. This study investigates microclimate shifts driven by Lake Urmia desiccation and evaluates their implications for urban cooling demand and carbon emissions under future climate scenarios. An integrated framework combining multi-temporal remote sensing observations, climate data, urban thermal indicators, and energy-emission modeling was employed to quantify relationships among lake shrinkage, land surface temperature, urban heat island intensity, cooling demand, and carbon emissions. Results show that Lake Urmia's surface area declined from 5420 km2 in 1990 to 610 km2 in 2025, representing an 88.7% reduction. This hydrological decline was accompanied by substantial thermal amplification, with mean Land Surface Temperature increasing from 28.4°C to 36.4°C and maximum Land Surface Temperature rising from 34.8°C to 47.1°C. Vegetation degradation was also pronounced, with the mean Normalized Difference Vegetation Index decreasing from 0.46 to 0.23. Concurrent urban expansion intensified thermal stress, increasing surface urban heat island intensity from 1.8°C to 4.7°C in Urmia and from 2.1°C to 5.2°C in Tabriz. Correlation analysis revealed strong relationships between lake area and LST (R = −0.87), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and Land Surface Temperature (R = −0.81), Land Surface Temperature and Urban Heat Island intensity (R = 0.79), and LST and cooling demand (R = 0.84). Future climate projections indicate temperature increases of 1.4°C, 2.6°C, and 4.1°C by 2050 under the SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5 scenarios, respectively, resulting in projected increases in cooling demand of 18–36%. Given Iran's electricity sector's fossil-fuel dependence, rising cooling demand is expected to increase carbon emissions. These findings highlight Lake Urmia desiccation as a coupled hydro-climatic–urban-energy challenge requiring integrated restoration, climate adaptation, and sustainable energy strategies. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A review on model innovation and applications through network data envelopment analysis
Abstract: Over last 25 years, network data envelopment analysis (NDEA) provides effective framework for assessing efficiency in systems characterized by multiple interconnected stages and hierarchical levels. This review presents PRISMA 2020 based systematic review of NDEA literature by analysing studies sourced from multiple academic databases. The retained literature was used for bibliometric analysis and 260 selected studies were comprehensively synthesized to examine evolution in NDEA from conventional DEA models to network based formulation that capture internal structures, intermediate links, shared inputs and environmental interactions. Important methodological advancements in NDEA include slack-based measures, dynamic models, stochastic and fuzzy extensions. This study also discusses approaches that integrated undesirable outputs, time-dependent variables and hybrid AI/ML-based models, which enable more accurate and data-driven efficiency assessments as compared to traditional DEA. Bibliometric and qualitative analyses indicate substantial methodological advancement and increasing application of NDEA across diverse domains. Banking, healthcare, energy, transportation and supply chain applications demonstrate need of NDEA. Despite of recent progress, challenges associated with variable selection, data quality, model standardization and result robustness continue to exist. Future research should focus on harmonizing input–output structures, enhancing sensitivity analysis, strengthen model validation and integration of NDEA results with cost-effective assessments and policy oriented evaluations. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Ji L.; Chang Y.
Title: What prevents community gardens from long-term survival? A five-year case study in Suzhou, China
Abstract: Community gardens are increasingly recognised as important instruments of urban micro-regeneration, yet their long-term sustainability remains fragile under project-based governance. This study traces the five-year evolution (2021–2025) of maintenance barriers in a government-initiated community garden in Suzhou, China. Using a longitudinal mixed-methods design, this paper tracks the community garden across three stages (inception, growth and struggle) through three phases of Likert-scale surveys and semi-structured interviews, supplemented by Participatory Action Research (PAR). The findings reveal a marked divergence in barrier trajectories. Individual technical constraints declined as residents accumulated horticultural knowledge, with the mean score for ‘lack of gardening knowledge and skills’ falling from 4.00 in 2021 to 1.83 in 2025. By contrast, team and institutional barriers intensified: ‘lack of an internal leader’ rose from 4.07 to 4.83, ‘unclear garden tasks’ from 3.20 to 4.33, and ‘Inadequate support from local authorities’ from 3.53 to 4.83, reaching the ceiling value of 5.0 for several individual respondents in 2025. The withdrawal of external facilitators exposed a governance vacuum that residents themselves labelled the ‘Three-Ignores’ ( san-bu-guan ) condition, in which fragmented responsibilities among Residents’ Committees, Property Management Companies and Homeowners’ Committees, together with unfulfilled budgetary commitments, produced systemic deterioration. At the same time, a significant demographic shift towards a volunteer team composed exclusively of elderly residents weakened the garden’s collective resilience. Sustaining community gardens requires a shift in urban management from temporary ‘project logic’ to more durable ‘governance logic’, including formal exit strategies, clearer responsibility arrangements and the incorporation of community assets into established administrative and budgetary systems. Title: Hamiltonian dynamics of Boolean networks

Abstract: This article examines the impact of Hamiltonian dynamics on the interaction graph of Boolean networks. Three types of dynamics are considered: maximum height, Hamiltonian cycle, and an intermediate dynamic between these two. The study addresses how these dynamics influence the connectivity of the graph and the existence of variables that depend on all other variables in the system. Title: Modeling the Relationship Between Physical Activity, Mental Health, and Cognitive Abilities with the Mediating Role of Perceived Social Support in Older Adults
Abstract: Objectives: Aging is one of the most significant demographic phenomena of the twenty-first century, and identifying factors affecting the physical and mental health of older adults is crucial. This study aimed to examine the relationship between physical activity, mental health, and cognitive abilities with the mediating role of perceived social support in older adults. Materials and Methods: This correlational descriptive study with path analysis was conducted among older adults aged 60 years and above (Mean = 67.63, SD = 6.02) in Sanandaj, Iran, in 2024. Using a convenience sampling method, 280 participants were recruited. Data were collected using the Physical Activity Questionnaire, the Quality of Life Questionnaire (mental health domain), the Cognitive Abilities Questionnaire, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. Data analysis was performed using SPSS-24 and AMOS-24. Results: Path analysis indicated that physical activity (Mean = 10.32, SD = 5.26) had significant direct effects on perceived social support (Mean = 40.87, SD = 11.33; β = 0.378, P < 0.001), cognitive abilities (Mean = 69.09, SD = 15.34; β = 0.351, P < 0.001), and mental health (Mean = 18.86, SD = 5.53; β = 0.189, P = 0.002). Cognitive abilities and mental health also had significant direct effects on perceived social support. Mediation analysis confirmed the significant mediating role of perceived social support in the relationships of cognitive abilities (β range = 0.061-0.453, 95% CI range [0.022- 0.573], P < 0.001) and mental health (β range = 0.054-0.153, 95% CI range [0.010-0.224], P < 0.001) with physical activity. Conclusions: These findings confirm that strengthening perceived social support can serve as a key mediating pathway that enhances the impact of mental health and cognitive abilities on physical activity among older adults. Perceived social support plays an important mediating role in amplifying the effects of physical activity on mental health and cognitive functioning in this population. Accordingly, health-promotion programs and public health policies should simultaneously focus on fostering supportive social interactions and encouraging regular physical activity in order to improve the psychological well-being and cognitive performance of older adults. © (2027), (Negah Institute for Social Research and Scientific Communication). Title: Consumer awareness, participation, and accessibility in sustainable electronic waste management
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid increase in electronic waste has created increasingly complex environmental and health challenges, especially in developing countries like Indonesia. The study objectives were to examine how household awareness and accessibility of electronic-waste management facilities are associated with consumer participation, controlling for socioeconomic factors, demographics, and the region's spatial characteristics. METHODS: This study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design to examine household consumers living near electronic waste management facilities in Indonesia. To analyze the data, Spearman's rank correlation was employed to evaluate variable relationships, ordinary least squares regression to estimate the associations of awareness and accessibility with participation levels, Kruskal-Wallis test to examine group differences, and Geographic Information System-based spatial analysis to describe the spatial patterns of facility distance, accessibility, and electronic waste management participation. FINDINGS: Consumer awareness of the consequences of electronic waste showed a significant positive correlation with the intention to manage electronic waste, with a correlation coefficient of 0.340, but showed no significant correlation with actual behavior, with a correlation coefficient of only 0.067. Accessibility showed a significant positive correlation with both intention and actual behavior, with correlation coefficients of 0.197 and 0.416, respectively. Accessibility had the largest reported regression coefficient for actual behavior ( β = 0.449 ), followed by awareness of consequences ( β = 0.182 ). The Kruskal-Wallis test confirmed significant differences in intention and actual behavior across accessibility levels, with chi-square values of 11.67 and 35.91, respectively. Spatial analysis using the nearest neighbor method produced a nearest neighbor ratio of 0.60 with a z score of -10.01. Spatial analysis revealed that highly aware and active residents are significantly clustered rather than randomly dispersed, with the vast majority residing within a functional catchment area defined by 10 to 30 kilometer distances or 10 to 30 minute travel times from e-waste facilities. CONCLUSION: The findings underscore the need for electronic waste management policies that prioritise facility accessibility and spatially based approaches to strengthen community participation within a circular economy framework. Title: Comparative diagnostic utility of cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in multiple sclerosis
Abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis depends on clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data; the need for confirmatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers for differential diagnosis is a crucial step. Objective We aim to investigate and compare the diagnostic value of CSF markers (e.g., chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)) compared to the established supportive diagnostic oligoclonal bands test (OCBs) in MS. Methods We collected 62 CSF samples from suspected MS patients with T2-Hyperintense lesions and investigated OCBs and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for NfL, CHI3L1, and GFAP. Results The CSF levels of NfL ( p < 0.001) and CHI3L1 ( p < 0.001) were significantly elevated in the MS group compared to the non-MS group, in contrast to GFAP ( p = 0.17). Diagnostic criteria for MS diagnosis was excellent for OCBs (Area under curve (AUC) = 0.978, p < 0.001; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.929–1.000), good for CHI3L1 (AUC = 0.838, p < 0.001; 95% CI: 0.738–0.939), acceptable for NfL (AUC = 0.729, p = 0.003; 95% CI: 0.602–0.855) and poor for GFAP (AUC = 0.604, p = 0.173; 95% CI: 0.477–0.762). Conclusion Among the studied biomarkers, CHI3L1 showed potential as an adjunctive biomarker for discriminating MS from non-MS patients. Its diagnostic accuracy was higher than that of NfL in our cohort, but GFAP has limited diagnostic accuracy, which could restrict its use in MS diagnosis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Optimal timing for staged vaccination campaigns: Insights from scenario tree-based stochastic optimization
Abstract: We develop a mathematical modeling framework to address the challenge in launching an effective staged vaccination campaign during a typical viral infection season to avoid an overwhelmed healthcare system for the entire season. Using the COVID-19 pandemic following its acute phase as a motivating example, our model takes into account the willingness of the public to receive vaccines, as well as the uncertainty of vaccination delivery and administration, to achieve the objective of optimizing the timing and distribution of the vaccination campaign, subject to the constraint that hospitalized cases do not exceed healthcare capacity. The integration of a dynamic transmission model with a scenario tree–based stochastic optimization framework enables the evaluation of future scenarios characterized by uncertainty in vaccination rates, contact mixing, and public adherence to safety measures. Accounting for these future scenarios facilitates the identification of strategies to dynamically adjust the timing and scale of vaccine and contact mixing during distinct phases of the viral season. Our study demonstrates that a well–timed, well–phased vaccination campaign, along with other public health interventions, can prevent overcrowding in hospitalization in a typical viral infection season. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Analytic hierarchy process-based criterion weighting for water resources management projects
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Prioritizing water resources projects requires decision-makers to balance hydrological performance, engineering feasibility, environmental and social sustainability, and economic value under limited budgets and implementation resources. Conventional evaluation frameworks are frequently bound to specific project typologies or geographical contexts, thereby constraining their direct applicability across heterogeneous project portfolios. The study objectives were to develop an analytic hierarchy process-based multi-criteria decision-making framework for deriving criterion weights for water resources management project assessment, using Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as the empirical context. METHODS: The framework was developed by synthesizing water resources management principles, practical project-assessment considerations, and relevant multi-criteria decision-making literature. The evaluation model comprised four principal dimensions and 18 operational sub-criteria. The Analytical hierarchy process framework was employed to analyze expert judgments elicited from six senior water resources and irrigation specialists, each possessing a minimum of 20 years of professional experience. Individual judgments were subsequently evaluated for consistency and aggregated using the geometric mean. Local weights were calculated using the eigenvector method and combined with the corresponding main-dimension weights to obtain global priorities. FINDINGS: Engineering and Implementation Feasibility received the highest main-dimension weight (32.58 percent), followed by Economic performance (25.84 percent), Environmental and Social Sustainability (21.87 percent), and Water Resource and Hydrological Performance (19.71 percent). At the global level, cost effectiveness ranked first (13.99 percent), followed by Structural Scale (11.58 percent), Foundation Suitability (10.60 percent), and Storage and Hydrological Adequacy (8.93 percent). These four sub-criteria accounted for 45.10 percent of the total weight. Accounting for 81.88 percent of the total weight and encompassing elements across all four dimensions, the top 11 sub-criteria demonstrate that comprehensive assessment necessitates an integrated approach spanning technical, economic, hydrological, environmental, and social dimensions. CONCLUSION: By establishing a transparent architecture for criterion organization and context-specific priority derivation, the framework facilitates water resources project evaluation. Integrated with empirical performance data and explicit scoring protocols, it underpins the formulation of robust project screening, portfolio comparative analysis, and budgetary prioritization procedures. The reported weights represent the judgments of the study panel and should be recalibrated for other locations, project types, and stakeholder groups. Subsequent applications of this framework should formulate a structured operational scoring rubric while comprehensively evaluating parameter sensitivity, model robustness, and project-ranking stability. Title: Translation and Transcultural Adaptation of the Monitor-Blunter Dental Scale (MBDS) into Brazilian Portuguese
Source title: Pesquisa Brasileira em Odontopediatria e Clinica Integrada
Abstract: Objective: To translate and culturally adapt The Monitor Blunter Dental Scale (MBDS) into Brazilian Portuguese. Material and Methods: The MBDS assesses the extent to which children report using monitoring and blunting strategies and whether dental-specific coping styles can be identified. It consists of four scenarios. Children are asked to imagine each situation and tick all strategies that would apply to them. For each item, there are equal numbers of monitoring and inattention strategies (three each). Results: Most children interviewed in the pre-test were boys (65%), with ages equally divided between 8-9 and 10-12 years. Title: Coupling composition design with defect engineering: An oxygen-doped Ti-Zr-Nb strain glass alloy with enhanced high-temperature shape memory effect
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-temperature shape memory alloys (HTSMAs) are critical for temperature-sensitive applications, yet the trade-off between high transformation temperatures and large recoverable strains remains a long-standing challenge. This study addresses this limitation by deploying a composition control and defect engineering strategy to regulate the martensitic transformation in HTSMAs via a strain glass while preserving elevated transformation temperatures. By introducing 1 at.% oxygen as point defects, a Ti47Zr47Nb5O1 strain glass alloy with a freezing temperature of about 462 K was fabricated. The microstructure consists of a strain‑glass‑dominated β matrix with minor residual α″ martensite. The low Nb content destabilizes the β phase, enabling the alloy to retain a high transformation temperature of about 745 K. Enabled by the strain glass state and the remarkable theoretical transformation strain derived from the addition of high-content Zr with large atomic radius, this alloy exhibits nearly full recoverability for pre‑strains up to about 5%, and achieves a shape memory recovery strain of ∼5.7% at a pre‑strain of 10%, outperforming most reported HTSMAs. The underlying deformation mechanism is attributed to the stress-induced reversible β → α″ martensitic transformation together with martensitic variant reorientation, which cooperatively accommodate local strains within nanoscale domains. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

Authors: Nelson P.P.
Author full names: Nelson, Priscilla P. (7402246675)
Title: Adaptive stewardship of understanding: Artificial intelligence and intergenerational governance in mining
Abstract: Mining stewardship has traditionally focused on the governance of physical assets, operational performance, environmental impacts, and organizational decision-making. While these responsibilities remain essential, they assume that the understanding supporting stewardship is comparatively stable. In reality, understanding continually evolves as new observations emerge, assumptions are revised, stakeholders change, institutions adapt, and stewardship extends across increasingly long temporal horizons. Artificial intelligence further transforms this process by participating in how observations are integrated, interpretations are developed, assumptions are reinforced or challenged, and institutional knowledge is preserved and communicated. Stewardship must therefore address not only what decisions are made, but also how understanding itself is created, maintained, questioned, and renewed. This paper proposes adaptive stewardship as a framework for governing an evolving ecology of understanding throughout the mine life cycle and beyond closure. The framework distinguishes understanding from observation, examines the lifecycle of assumptions, introduces the concepts of time windows of understanding and observation boundaries, and argues that governance must preserve the conditions under which understanding can continue to improve across generations. Within this ecology, artificial intelligence is treated not as an autonomous decision-maker but as an evolving participant whose value depends upon transparent governance that maintains visibility of assumptions, uncertainty, evidence, and human judgment. The paper concludes that the long-term objective of stewardship is not to preserve today's knowledge, but to preserve society's continuing capacity to develop better understanding as mining systems, environmental conditions, technologies, institutions, and societal expectations evolve. Authors: Jin X.; Wang Y.; Li S.
Title: Robust incomplete multi-view clustering via adaptive similarity graph completion and dual-tensor decomposition
Abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering (IMC) is crucial for real-world applications such as image retrieval, text classification, and subtype recognition, where multi-modal data frequently suffer from missing values and severe noise due to acquisition limitations or transmission losses. However, most existing methods rely on raw data completion, single-tensor constraints, and isolated multi-step processing paradigms. These approaches not only struggle to simultaneously preserve cross-view consistent principal components and filter out view-specific variations, but their phased nature also introduces irreversible error accumulation. To overcome these bottlenecks, this paper proposes a novel unified framework named Dual-Tensor Graph Completion for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering (DTGC-IMVC). Specifically, to eliminate reconstruction noise at the data feature level, an adaptive similarity graph completion mechanism is introduced to directly recover the similarity graph within the self-representation. Meanwhile, a dual-tensor architecture seamlessly integrating the tensor nuclear norm and the Schatten-p norm is constructed to rigorously capture high-order cross-view consistent features and effectively sparsify noise and view-specific components. Furthermore, a unified multi-source denoising strategy constrained by the L2,1-norm is introduced. Comprehensive experiments on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of clustering performance and robustness. Title: Strategic deployment of seasonal thermal energy storage for decarbonizing remote northern communities in Canada: A multidimensional evaluation framework
Abstract: Remote northern communities face major energy-transition challenges due to extreme climates, prolonged heating seasons, geographic isolation, dependence on imported fossil fuels, and limited energy infrastructure. Seasonal Thermal Energy Storage (STES) can address the mismatch between renewable heat availability and winter heating demand, but technology selection must account for environmental, geological, logistical, economic, and socio-technical constraints alongside conventional engineering performance. This review evaluates seven STES technologies using a northern-specific multidimensional framework integrating thermodynamic performance, technical maturity, economic performance, constructability and logistics, permafrost compatibility, and community implementation capacity. The framework operationalizes this assessment through non-compensable feasibility screening and TOPSIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis using a literature-informed technology-performance matrix, an equal-weight reference, two contrasting northern deployment archetypes, and weight- and score-sensitivity analyses. Results show that suitability depends on the interaction between technology characteristics and deployment context rather than engineering performance alone. Tank Thermal Energy Storage (TTES) exhibits the most robustly favourable profile across the evaluated scenarios and sensitivity analyses, whereas Pit Thermal Energy Storage (PTES), Borehole Thermal Energy Storage (BTES), and Rock Thermal Energy Storage (RTES) are more context dependent. Phase Change Material (PCM) and Thermochemical Energy Storage (TCES) offer high theoretical storage potential but remain limited by large-scale operational validation, while Aquifer Thermal Energy Storage (ATES) is conditional on suitable hydrogeological conditions. The proposed framework shifts STES selection from performance-based ranking toward context-driven decision support, providing developers, utilities, engineering practitioners, and community decision-makers with a transparent and reproducible methodology for identifying robust candidates, context-sensitive alternatives, and critical deployment constraints before detailed site-specific assessment in northern Canada and other circumpolar regions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Two pathways at once: An investigation of how reactance and ethicality shape student learning with AI
Abstract: Generative AI tools promise to expand student agency in management education, yet the same tool can help and hurt learning inside a single classroom. We argue this contradiction is the signature of two psychological pathways running in parallel. Drawing on the cognitive-affective-conative framework, we develop a dual-pathway serial mediation model in which a cognitive pathway runs from psychological reactance through autonomy perceptions to effectiveness judgments, while an affective pathway runs from ethical perceptions through emotional engagement to effectiveness judgments. Ninety-seven undergraduate management students participated in two AI-enhanced activities with different chatbot tools across one semester. Both pathways operated as predicted. More surprising was how the cognitive pathway changed across exposures. At first use, reactance traveled through autonomy, consistent with self-determination theory. By the second activity, reactance bypassed autonomy and suppressed effectiveness directly. The affective pathway remained stable across exposures. For management educators, ethical framing before a student's first AI encounter may do more work than redesigning the tools themselves to preserve student choice. As a single-cohort study using two researcher-built chatbots, the results are preliminary and point to hypotheses for multi-site replication rather than population estimates. © 2026

Title: Resilience Optimization Strategy for Cyber-Physical Distribution Systems Under Coordinated Fake-Base-Station and Physical Attacks
Abstract: Driven by the deployment of intelligent terminals and advanced communication technologies, modern distribution networks have fundamentally evolved into cyber-physical distribution systems (CPDSs). Consequently, these systems face an escalating exposure to sophisticated, coordinated cyber-physical attacks. To address this critical vulnerability, a tri-level defender-attacker-operator optimization model is proposed in this paper to enhance CPDS resilience against coordinated fake-base-station (FBS) and physical attacks. The coordinated attack process is modeled by jointly considering physical line disruptions, cyber-induced RCS communication failures, and their coupled impact on post-attack self-healing. To render the resulting complex tri-level formulation computationally tractable, a hybrid framework is developed, which integrates an improved column-and-constraint generation method with M²SITRI. Comprehensive simulations conducted on modified IEEE 33-node and IEEE 123-node distribution test systems verify both the effectiveness of the proposed resilience-enhancement model and the computational efficiency of the hybrid solution method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Contrasting growth and spoilage traits combined with antagonistic core-periphery network organization reveal distinct ecological strategies among dairy-associated Pseudomonas subgroups
Abstract: Pseudomonas spp. is a taxonomically diverse genus causing dairy spoilage. Despite its high occurrence in dairy products, its ecology remains poorly understood. In this study, 89 Pseudomonas strains mainly isolated from dairy products were characterized using a high-throughput multi-trait approach that combines biotic and abiotic factors. The collection was dominated in equal proportions by the two subgroups P. fluorescens and P. fragi, followed by the P. gessardii subgroup. Under pH and NaCl stress, the P. fragi and P. fluorescens subgroups exhibited the lowest and highest growth capacity, respectively. The P. fluorescens subgroup contained a higher proportion of proteolytic and lecithinase-producing strains compared to P. fragi subgroup. Strains from P. gessardii subgroup displayed spoilage traits similar to P. fluorescens but with more variable growth behavior. The antagonism network exhibited a nested core-periphery architecture. The P. fluorescens subgroup formed the highly connected core, while P. gessardii and P. fragi occupied the periphery with marginal interactions. Overall, these results revealed that despite equal prevalence, P. fragi and P. fluorescens subgroups displayed markedly divergent ecological strategies. These findings pave the way for promising future investigations into the impact of ecological strategies on product quality. © 2026

Title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based predictive model for prognosis in cerebral hemorrhage patients after hyperbaric oxygen therapy
Abstract: (Figure presented.) Intracerebral hemorrhage is a common and critical neurological emergency, and the inconsistent results of hyperbaric oxygen therapy make predicting outcomes challenging. Therefore, a reliable predictive model for outcomes is needed to improve treatment plans. This study used interpretable machine learning to determine key risk factors linked to adverse outcomes in cerebral hemorrhage patient post-hyperbaric oxygen therapy. To improve prognostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making, we analyzed the data from 401 patients with intracerebral hemorrhage who received hyperbaric oxygen therapy at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jiaxing, China, using multivariate logistic regression and machine learning to develop predictive models, with model performance assessed via 10-fold cross-validation. SHapley Additive exPlanations values aided in model interpretation and in the development of a logistic regression-based nomogram. Based on the modified Rankin scale, patients were stratified into two prognostic groups: a good prognosis group (modified Rankin scale < 3, n = 265) and a poor prognosis group (modified Rankin scale ≥ 3, n = 136). Significant differences in various factors were observed between the groups. Independent risk factors identified included the Glasgow coma scale score, computed tomography hemorrhage volume, activities of daily living score, treatment modality, intraventricular bleeding, and rebleeding. Among the models tested, the random forest algorithm yielded the highest predictive performance (the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.99). The study identified key predictors, including activities of daily living score, computed tomography hemorrhage volume, and Glasgow coma scale score, as factors influencing hyperbaric oxygen therapy outcomes in intracerebral hemorrhage patients. Random Forest model demonstrated strong predictive capability, with SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis providing insights into individual risk factors. Overall, these findings are crucial for improving clinical decision-making and personalized treatment. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

Title: Spatial analysis of the 15-minute city concept in three historically distinct urban areas across metropolitan greater Cairo
Abstract: This paper explores how the 15-min city concept plays out in Greater Cairo by examining three neighbourhoods: Agouza, Madinaty, and Badya. To do so, it draws on a systematic approach that includes selecting case studies, identifying key service categories, extracting POI and street-network data, mapping service areas in ArcGIS, and presenting the results through service area analysis and thematic mapping. To complement this, accessibility was assessed through four measures: cumulative opportunities, land-use entropy, functional redundancy, and space syntax (integration) metrics. The findings show that access in Cairo depends not just on distance but also on the diversity of available services, the degree of proximity between services, and the way streets connect different areas. Cycling makes a clear difference in widening reach and reducing accessibility inequalities and fragmentation. The findings suggest that, in addition to clinics and schools, social anchors such as souqs, ahwa, and cultural places emerge as vital parts of daily urban life. The paper argues that in Cairo, the 15-min city concept, whether built from scratch or adapted to existing urban fabrics, should not be treated as a universal recipe but as a flexible framework. The concept is part of a longer lineage of planning ideals, adopted in the planning of several areas of Cairo, from the Garden City movement to New Urbanism. It should build on the city’s own urban vocabularies, shaped through layered urban planning and lived experiences, which continue to define how urban spaces and services are used and valued within the 15-min radius or beyond. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Ghost-ResDSCNet:lightweight residual depthwise separable convolution with spatial pyramid pooling for power quality disturbance classification
Abstract: The increasing complexity of power quality disturbances (PQDs) calls for lightweight yet accurate classification methods suitable for edge deployment. This paper proposes Ghost-ResDSCNet, a multi-scale deep network that first converts voltage signals into time–frequency spectrograms via short-time Fourier transform. A residual depthwise separable convolution backbone performs efficient feature extraction, Ghost modules reduce computational cost by cheap feature generation, and a spatial pyramid pooling module captures multi-scale contextual information. On a 21-class synthetic PQD dataset, Ghost-ResDSCNet achieves an average accuracy of 99.34% on clean signals, along with 99.26%, 99.11%, and 95.80% under 40 dB, 30 dB, and 20 dB SNR respectively, with only 0.12M parameters, outperforming MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet. On a real-world five-class dataset, it attains 100.00% accuracy on clean and 40dB signals, and 99.96% and 94.02% under 30dB and 20dB SNR. Grad-CAM++ visualization confirms that the model focuses on physically interpretable time–frequency regions. The results demonstrate an effective trade-off among accuracy, robustness, and efficiency for real-time PQD monitoring in edge computing. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Reconciling rheology, stretchability and thermal conductivity in thermal interface materials through dynamic polymer interactions and multimodal filler networks

Abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) used for heat dissipation of high-power electronics must combine good dispensability, high stretchability, and high thermal conductivity to maintain efficient heat dissipation during assembly and thermo-mechanical cycling. Here, we report a polyurethane-siloxane TIM that integrates dynamic polymer interactions with a multimodal aluminum filler network to overcome this trade-off. As a result, the TIM exhibits low viscosity (234.13 Pa s), pronounced thixotropic behavior, high stretchability (elongation at break of 304.58%), and high thermal conductivity (8.13 W m−1 K−1). Integrating the TIM into a chip, we demonstrate the reduced operating temperature and thermo-mechanical reliability of the chip under cyclic and prolonged operation. Title: Enhancing accounting students’ writing performance through problem-based learning: Evidence from a vocational higher education context
Abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) has gained momentum in English for specific purpose (ESP) education, yet little is known about how PBL functions in vocational higher education settings for accounting for students' writing. This study investigated the effectiveness, benefits, and challenges associated with accounting students' writing performance. This study employs a mixed-methods design involving 60 students from one of the state polytechnics in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. The experimental group (N=30) experienced PBL, and the control group (N=30) received conventional learning. Data were collected through writing tests to investigate students' improvement in their writing performance, and interviews to explore students' perceptions of benefits and challenges. The results of the writing test were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics via SPSS, and the interview results were analyzed using thematic analysis. The quantitative results reveal that there is a significant difference in the writing performance of accounting students who were taught by using PBL and those who were taught by using conventional learning, with PBL being better than conventional learning. It can be concluded that PBL is effective at enhancing accounting students' writing performance. The qualitative results of the interviews revealed that the accounting students mentioned the benefits of PBL, including improvement in students' writing skills, development of students' problem-solving skills, development of students' critical thinking, team collaboration, and real accounting problem connections. However, they listed the challenges of PBL, which include difficulty relating to the varied ideas and a lack of experience with the problems. Future research is recommended to extend the study duration to better capture the lasting impacts of PBL, offering a more comprehensive understanding of this approach. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Enhanced adaptive SRF-PLL-based robust synchronization and control of grid-integrated PV-battery systems for seamless mode transition under distorted grid conditions
Abstract: Synchronization problems, harmonic distortion, and power regulation problems are likely to occur in grid-integrated SPVA-BES microgrids serving nonlinear loads due to changing grid conditions. A dual-mode approach, EAFF-SRF-PLL, has been introduced for the grid-integrated SPVA-BES microgrid, which operates in both grid-connected and standalone modes. In the synchronization loop, adaptive gain scheduling, along with a frequency feed-forward estimation technique, has been used to maintain phase-locking capability under distorted, unbalanced, and nonlinear grid conditions. A supervisory energy management strategy controls the BDDC and grid-connected VSC based on the battery SOC status and BES availability. The performance of the controller is tested under harmonic distortion, varying loads, irradiation, unbalanced voltages, frequency deviations, PV unavailability, and mode transitions. The results of CHIL experiments employing an STM32F407G-DISC1 controller with an OPAL-RT OP4512 real-time simulator include the following: a synchronization time of 5 ms, a phase ripple of 0.78%, and a grid current total harmonic distortion of 2.7%. Compared with traditional SRF-PLL and DDSRF-PLL, the proposed algorithm achieves better synchronization accuracy and transient response. Harmonic voltage and current obtained from the test results meet the criteria of IEEE Std. 519. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Si L.; Li L.; Yuan W.; Ma Z.
Title: Link prediction in multiplex social networks based on information transmission graph neural networks
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: Social networks are omnipresent graph-structured data where entities and interactions between them can be modeled as nodes and edges, respectively. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have evolved as a mainstream and powerful model for handling graph data. Link prediction, which can foretell missing or potential links, is a crucial task in social network analysis. However, most existing methods focus on monolayer networks and usually ignore that multiplex networks have richer information, which often results in poor performance on link prediction. Therefore, this paper proposes an information transmission-based GNN (IT-GNN) model for link prediction in multiplex social networks. IT-GNN first learns the representation of each node in a multiplex network from itself and its neighborhood. Specifically, the neighborhood information of a node is learned from its 1-, 2- and 3-hop neighbors in combination with the three new ways of information transmission. Then, the embedding of a node pair is obtained based on these representations. In this regard, the final representations of potential links in the target layer, which are used to determine the existence of potential links, are generated by fusing their embeddings from all layers. Extensive experiments on seven real-world networks demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed model. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Authors: Hu R.; Chen J.L.; Li G.; Qin Y.
Title: Impacts of tourism development on residents’ quality of life: A dual spillover perspective
Abstract: Tourism development can influence residents’ quality of life through bottom-up spillover (i.e., mediation) across life domains and through spatial spillover across regions. However, existing research has not integrated these micro and macro perspectives. This study develops an innovative theoretical framework to account for both spillover effects simultaneously. Using a constructed panel dataset from England and Wales, which integrates national longitudinal survey data, tourism statistics, socioeconomic indicators and geographic information, we apply dynamic spatial lag X panel models to verify the above framework. Results indicate that tourism development affects overall life satisfaction only indirectly, through spatial spillover effects mediated by different life domains, depending on the tourism indicators employed, underscoring the complexity of its impacts and the need for multifaceted tourism policymaking. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Transformational entrepreneurship education in the AI era: Reframing entrepreneurial readiness through AI literacy and digital entrepreneurial capability
Abstract: Artificial intelligence integration is reshaping entrepreneurship education and increasing the need for pedagogical approaches that prepare students to act under digital uncertainty. Drawing on Transformational Learning Theory, Growth Mindset Theory, and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines how Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy contribute to Entrepreneurial Readiness directly and through Digital Innovation Skills and Digital Growth Mindset, the complementary dimensions through which Digital Entrepreneurial Capability is conceptually expressed. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. Survey data from 698 Indonesian university students were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, followed by semi-structured interviews with 24 students. The findings show that Transformational Entrepreneurship Education was positively related to AI Literacy, Digital Innovation Skills, Digital Growth Mindset, and Entrepreneurial Readiness. AI Literacy was also positively related to both capability dimensions and Entrepreneurial Readiness. Both dimensions significantly mediated the relationships of Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy with Entrepreneurial Readiness, while the corresponding direct effects remained significant. Qualitative findings showed that reflective AI engagement, iterative experimentation, feedback, and persistence supported capability development, whereas passive AI reliance and limited scaffolding constrained capability translation. The study advances entrepreneurship education and AI Literacy research by reframing Entrepreneurial Readiness as an action-oriented outcome. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Setyowati M.S.; Hanum R.K.
Title: The effect of agricultural taxes and local agricultural policies on enhancing food security and environmental sustainability
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Indonesia is currently working towards sustainability in line with Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger). Anticipated demographic growth to 10.8 billion by the year 2050 is expected to place unprecedented strain on global food security and production systems. The study objectives were to examine the biophysical factors, production inputs, economic conditions, socio-technological factors, agricultural business management, and agricultural tax policies regional agricultural policies and, ultimately, agricultural productivity. METHODS: This quantitative study employed structured questionnaires administered to a sample of 200 farmers in Surabaya. The instrument used a one-to-five Likert scale covering biophysical factors, economic factors, tax policy, tax morale, and agricultural productivity. Data was analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modeling version 3. The analytical procedure comprised three distinct phases: first, evaluating the outer model for convergent and discriminant validity; second, conducting reliability assessments; and third, testing the inner model via bootstrapping to determine the coefficient of determination, the effect size, and hypothesis significance. Hypothesis significance was determined using t-statistic values of at least 1.96 and p-values of no more than 0.05. FINDINGS: Four hypotheses were rejected: economic factor on regional agricultural policy (p-value 0.557), agricultural taxation policy on tax morale (p-value 0.072), tax awareness on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.058), and tax morale on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.208). The findings reveal that regional agricultural policies are substantially driven by three key dimensions: biophysical factors (beta coefficient of 0.251, probability value of 0.000), production inputs (beta coefficient of 0.253, probability value of 0.002), and agricultural business management (beta coefficient of 0.228, probability value of 0.007). Agricultural tax policy significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.229, probability value of 0.000), while tax administration efficiency also significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.345, probability value of 0.000) and tax morale (beta coefficient of -0.634, probability value of 0.000), since clarity on procedures, benefits, and regulations fosters public responsibility and awareness of taxpayer obligations and rights. CONCLUSION: Elevating agricultural output demands comprehensive frameworks characterized by active farmer participation, supportive regulatory policies, targeted outreach regarding tax frameworks, and enhanced coordination between industry stakeholders and governmental bodies. Regional agricultural policies and tax awareness significantly influence agricultural productivity. These findings offer practical insights for policymakers aiming to strengthen agricultural governance and tax compliance frameworks in support of sustainable rural development. Title: Moral responsibilisation in destination management: The strategic framing of civic practices by DMOs
Abstract: This paper examines moral responsibilisation as an emerging destination governance mechanism through which destination management organisations (DMOs) and local stakeholders mobilise visitors to support sustainability goals. Drawing on an intrinsic qualitative case study of the Danish DMO, Wonderful Copenhagen , we develop a practice theory-based model showing that responsibilisation extends beyond narrative persuasion to include the organisational and material reframing of civic conduct. Analysis of interviews, participant observation, documents, and netnography identifies four interrelated stages: interpellation, involvement, intervention, and institutionalisation. Together, these stages connect inspirational messaging with participatory experiences, reward schemes, and decentralised service design. The findings also reveal tensions around the relevance, inclusivity, and feasibility of emerging civic practices. Resistance to responsible subject positions stems from stakeholders’ differing interpretations, negotiations, and disengagement from DMO-prescribed roles. The study advances the understanding of responsibilisation as a practice-based mode of governance and offers insights that may inform destination managers in varied tourism contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Pastoral Nomads at a Crossroads: Investigating the Resilience of the Bakarwal Community to Climate and Socio-Ecological Challenges
Abstract: Environmental shifts influence the livelihoods of Bakarwal pastoral nomads as they traverse the varied terrains of the Western Himalayas. Climate fluctuations and socio-ecological stressors markedly affect their resilience. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study examines how environmental factors and livelihood pressures interact among these nomads. By integrating scientific analysis of long-term climate patterns with qualitative data from 239 Bakarwal families, the research investigates their adaptive strategies and internal capacity. Results show that a 1 °C rise in winter and early summer temperatures, coupled with decreased rainfall in winter and transit habitats, affects mobility and resource availability, including fodder and water. The study highlights the importance of traditional knowledge, flexible transhumance practices, and eco-friendly methods in enhancing resilience. However, socio-ecological challenges, including limited institutional support and marginalization, threaten the sustainability of their pastoral lifestyle. The research situates livelihood resilience within the dynamic interactions of environmental and cultural systems. By simultaneously evaluating climate and socio-ecological factors, it affirms the enduring value of traditional wisdom and the resilience of pastoral systems in preserving ecological integrity and fostering sustainable development. It underscores the need for inclusive, community-driven policies and adaptive strategies to strengthen resilience and sustain pastoral livelihoods. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Touchable cultural heritage: How alternative touch experience facilitates visitors’ cultural inheritance behavior
Abstract: Touch is a fundamental human need, yet in cultural heritage tourism, it is strictly restricted to protect fragile artifacts. While essential for preservation, touch restrictions limit multi-sensory experience and impede deeper cultural participation. This research addresses this touch dilemma by introducing alternative touch experiences, wherein tourists touch surrogate objects (e.g., artifact replicas) that simulate the haptic attributes of authentic artifacts. Across four studies with qualitative, experimental, and field evidence, we found that alternative touch experiences enhance tourists’ psychological closeness to heritage, which in turn fosters cultural inheritance intentions and actual behaviors (e.g., cultural learning, cultural knowledge sharing, and donation to protect heritage). However, this touch effect diminishes when artifacts carry negative (vs. positive) superstitious associations. These findings offer a new theoretical perspective on enabling embodied experience within the traditionally sensory-restricted context, and highlight the role of sensory engagement in facilitating heritage appreciation and cultural inheritance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Sustainable urban planning in conflict-affected cities: Governance, displacement, and hierarchical sustainability in Marib, Yemen
Abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. Drawing on a framing analysis of global sustainability frameworks, semi-structured interviews with 16 city stakeholders, and structured observations in seven neighbourhoods, the study identifies a structural mismatch between global sustainability paradigms and local planning practice. Whereas international models assume balanced domain integration, the evidence from Marib reveals a context-conditioned hierarchy in which governance capacity and essential service provision operate as preconditions structuring environmental management, economic activity, and technological uptake. Locally, environmental sustainability is reduced to basic service continuity; social sustainability is dominated by displacement-driven absorptive pressures; economic sustainability narrows to livelihood survival; and technological adoption is fragmented and institutionally constrained. The paper advances a context-conditioned, hierarchical model of urban sustainability that challenges the implicit universality of parallel-domain planning approaches and calls for planning paradigms that recognise institutional capacity as foundational in fragile urban contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Revisiting the Agropastoral Landscape of Çatalhöyük East Through Agent-Based Modeling (9100–8100 BP)
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Understanding the complex interplay between external climatic forcing and internal socioecological dynamics remains a major challenge in the study of early sedentary societies. While unilinear frameworks frequently link systemic shifts to external climate triggers, these perspectives tend to neglect the internal dynamics and non-linear feedback loops of complex socioecological systems (SES). This research sheds new light on established narratives by investigating the 1000-year coevolution of agropastoral practices and landscape dynamics at Çatalhöyük East (ca. 9100–8100 BP). We employ a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM), integrating the MedLanD (MML) platform with the Macrophysical Climate Model (MCM) via an original sequential simulation design. This methodological novelty allows us to quantify how cumulative land-use legacies and their environmental costs shaped the community’s later options. Our results indicate that while the agricultural strategy effectively sustained high population density, it simultaneously pushed the system toward a rigidity trap. The model demonstrates how short-term adaptive successes generate structural limits in landscape capacity. These findings suggest that the settlement’s eventual reorganization was not a simple response to external climatic forcing but rather an emergent outcome of internal socioecological stress. By reframing the trajectory of Çatalhöyük through a complex systems lens, this study emphasizes that resilience must be understood as a dynamic process shaped by the long-term interaction of human agency and landscape evolution. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Performing Power and Transitional Space: the Use of Acoustics and Multimodal AI in Etruscan Painted Tombs
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: This article presents a new multimodal AI and acoustic methodology using two 5th c. BCE Etruscan painted tombs at Tarquinia, Italy, the Tomba del Gallo and the Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri as case studies. Via the integration of AI computer vision–based visual saliency analysis, architectural affordance modelling, acoustic data, and agent-based perceptual trajectories, the study suggests that each tomb affords distinct experiential strategies. The Tomba del Gallo privileges visual sequencing, threshold control, and gaze discipline, whereas the Tomba dei Demoni Azzurri potentially induces perceptual disorientation and immerses the visitor into a sensory and spatial environment that has the possibility of inducing trance-like experiences. A central contribution of the study is the reinterpretation of subterranean funerary spaces as possible transitional spaces, where architectural and symbolic devices mediate between life and death, order and chaos, memory and transformation, and sensory manipulation operate as core ritual technologies. Ultimately, we argue that when combined with scientifically documented acoustic data, AI enables archaeology to move beyond representational interpretation toward the experimental modelling of ritualised experiences in the ancient Mediterranean. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children
Abstract: Theories of cognitive development propose that cultural values shape metacognitive skills. However, cross-cultural research on metacognition remains limited and often relies on verbal assessments that may lack validity across cultural contexts. The present study examined metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children (N = 95; 6–10-year-olds; 46% female) using a non-verbal problem-solving task in which children assembled objects according to a model. Across all three cultural contexts, children exhibited various monitoring behaviors (e.g., checking the model), and the frequency of these behaviors increased with age. Cross-cultural differences emerged in the specific monitoring strategies children used: Chinese children engaged in more thorough monitoring than Kenyan and U.S. children. Title: Adaptive ADMM-based optimal power flow for distribution systems via dynamic penalty strategy
Abstract: To mitigate voltage fluctuations caused by intermittent distributed generation (DG), this paper proposes a reactive power optimization strategy based on an Improved Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (I-ADMM). The model coordinates switchable capacitor banks (SCBs), on-load tap changers (OLTCs), and the reactive power capabilities of DGs to balance voltage quality and active power losses. Simulation results on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed I-ADMM reduces total voltage deviation by 18.71% and 25.94%, and decreases branch losses by 9.51% and 10.67% compared with T-ADMM and C-OPF, respectively. In addition, a multi-period validation under time-varying DG and load conditions shows that the proposed method maintains effective performance across representative operating periods while preserving voltage security. Additional validation on a modified IEEE 69-bus system further confirms the scalability of the proposed method. These results demonstrate improved computational efficiency and the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive penalty strategy for distributed OPF under representative time-varying operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang H.; Shan Q.; Zhang J.; Xiao P.; Liu A.
Title: An audio-visual fusion emotion generation model based on neuroanatomical alignment
Abstract: In the field of affective computing, traditional methods for generating emotions predominantly rely on deep learning techniques and large-scale emotion datasets. However, deep learning techniques are often complex and difficult to interpret, and standardizing large-scale emotional datasets are difficult and costly to establish. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel framework named Audio-Visual Fusion for Brain-like Emotion Learning(AVF-BEL). In contrast to conventional brain-inspired emotion learning methods, this approach improves the audio-visual emotion fusion and generation model through the integration of modular components, thereby enabling more lightweight and interpretable emotion learning and generation processes. The framework simulates the integration of the visual, auditory, and emotional pathways of the brain, optimizes the fusion of emotional features across visual and auditory modalities, and improves upon the traditional Brain Emotional Learning (BEL) model. The experimental results indicate a significant improvement in the similarity of the audio-visual fusion emotion learning generation model compared to single-modality visual and auditory emotion learning and generation model. Ultimately, this aligns with the fundamental phenomenon of heightened emotion generation facilitated by the integrated impact of visual and auditory stimuli. This contribution not only enhances the interpretability and efficiency of affective intelligence but also provides new insights and pathways for advancing affective computing technology. Title: Training and Institutional Guidelines in Teachers’ Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Bibliometric Analysis, Empirical Evidence, and Implications for Quality Education and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

Title: The role of creativity and imagination in scientific endeavour
Abstract: Creativity and imagination (C&I) are integral, but often overlooked, aspects of scientific endeavour. If scientists aim to innovate and develop new knowledge about the world around us, C&I are essential, yet how C&I are used in science is poorly understood. This lack of clarity about how C&I are defined, and how they are used, results in uninformed views about the nature of scientific endeavour. Here, we propose a conceptual Framework for an informed view of C&I to support the understanding of science through both research and teaching. We define our understanding of scientific endeavour, then define creativity in science through the generation of new thoughts, processes and products in intentional and unintentional ways which are effective in the context in which the creativity was applied. Imagination complements creativity and is defined as the ability to form mental images in the absence of the senses. During scientific endeavour, C&I work in conjunction with critical thinking and manifest as dispositions and actions when questioning, planning, doing and reflecting in science. Nineteen aspects of scientific endeavour are identified and the roles of C&I for each aspect are illustrated. The result is a characterisation of the role of C&I in scientific endeavour that makes creative and imaginative thoughts and actions explicit. This conceptualisation of an informed view provides a Framework for science educators who are tasked with researching, teaching and assessing, students’ understanding about the role of C&I in scientific endeavour. We close with implications for science education and research. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Authors: Pan A.
Title: The AI-augmented collaborative learning model: A conceptual framework for integrating generative AI in business and management education
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) amplifies four tensions in business and management education: the threat to pedagogical coherence, the literacy-to-competency gap, pervasive ethical risks, and the assessment crisis. A first wave of practice-oriented frameworks – including the Human-Centric AI-First (HCAIF) framework and the Leeds Model – offers actionable roadmaps but lacks the theoretical architecture needed to explain the systemic classroom dynamics GenAI introduces. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by developing the AI-Augmented Collaborative Learning (ACL) Model, a second-wave framework organised around three research questions: (RQ1) which theoretical lenses explain the classroom dynamics that generative AI creates in business and management education; (RQ2) how can these be synthesised into an integrated pedagogical framework whose pillars address the four systemic challenges; and (RQ3) how can human-AI collaboration be operationalised as an assessable pedagogical meta-skill. Using Socio-Technical Systems Theory, Activity Theory, Actor-Network Theory, Constructivist and Experiential Learning Theories, and the AI-TPACK framework, the ACL Model specifies four interlocking pillars – Pedagogical Intentionality, Developmental Scaffolding, Ethical Guardrails, and Authentic Assessment. The paper's primary theoretical contribution is to relocate the unit of analysis from the individual student to the student-AI network and to define collaborative intelligence as the resulting meta-competency. Author full names: Dirksmeier, Peter (22134520700); Göb, Angelina (57362109900)
Title: Why conversations constitute neighbourhood cohesion: A mixed-methods approach to substantiating cause and effect
Abstract: Communicating is a meaningful practice for building neighbourhood cohesion by fostering a sense of connection, mutual support and belonging among residents of a geographically defined neighbourhood. In our paper, we highlight the role of regular contact and conversations with neighbours for generating neighbourhood cohesion. Following a mixed-methods approach, we combine qualitative instruments from two case studies focusing on neighbourhoods in Hanover with quantitative data from a panel survey conducted in Hanover and Magdeburg, Germany. The residents’ statements clearly show that talking to each other influences their socio-spatial orientation towards the neighbourhood as a point of reference, thus promoting attitudes and practices to strengthen neighbourhood cohesion. Based on these results, the causal model confirms the effect of conversations on neighbourhood cohesion, which is mediated by the factor of trust. Combining the two types of data helps to understand and explain why neighbourhoods are relevant for peaceful coexistence: they enable low-threshold interaction and thus the experience of belonging and integration. It remains open whether and to what extent neighbourhood cohesion can be scaled up, which requires comparisons with other cities and city types as well as different neighbourhoods to identify regional and international differences. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Safi H.
Title: Conflict minerals, institutional failure, and the limits of transparency: Resource governance in post-2001 Afghanistan
Abstract: Why did the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) fail to generate accountability in Afghanistan, which was declared EITI-compliant in 2012 and suspended in 2019? This article treats Afghanistan's post-2001 extractive sector as an extreme case of resource governance under a contested political settlement and examines it through an embedded single-case design. Drawing on interviews with senior officials of the Ministry of Mines and Petroleum, the national EITI secretariat, and civil society, together with interviews with miners, community members, and academics, focus groups, and documentary sources, it traces how neopatrimonial governance and elite capture undermined transparency. Three mechanisms emerge: the colonization of mining institutions by patronage networks; the exclusion of mining communities from participation and benefit-sharing, which sustains customary and insurgent revenue channels; and the invisibility of artisanal, armed-group-controlled extraction to payment-reconciliation mechanisms. The article's main contribution is a sequenced governance framework, derived abductively from the conditional-transparency literature and the case evidence, which holds that in deeply captured, conflict-affected sectors, security provision, elite incentive restructuring, and community empowerment are preconditions for, rather than consequences of, effective transparency. The article specifies the framework's scope conditions and the evidence that would count against it. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
