Title: The dialectic of the carrot and the stick in the expansion of the extractive frontier in Oaxaca, Mexico
Abstract: The expansion of large-scale mining in Mexico since the 1990s has been accompanied by intensifying socio-environmental conflicts, particularly in rural and Indigenous territories. While existing literature has shown that extractive governance frequently combines coercive practices with strategies aimed at securing local legitimacy, this article argues that these mechanisms are mutually constitutive rather than simply simultaneous or complementary. It develops the concept of the dialectic of the carrot and the stick to explain how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and coercion recursively reshape the conditions under which one another operate over the life of an extractive project. The article examines the San José silver and gold mine in Oaxaca, Mexico, operated by Fortuna Silver Mines (FSM). Drawing on qualitative fieldwork conducted between 2023 and 2024, including interviews, field observations, corporate publications, media reports, and civil society sources, it traces extractive governance over more than a decade of conflict. It shows that community programmes and relationships with local institutions produced differentiated and conditional forms of legitimacy, while repression, intimidation, and violence increased the costs of dissent and weakened resistance networks. Coercion thus transformed the terrain on which legitimacy was subsequently cultivated, while persistent limits to legitimacy generated renewed pressures to contain opposition. The dialectic therefore describes a recursive process through which coercion and consent reshape one another, enabling extraction to persist despite sustained opposition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Navigating CSRD compliance: Challenges in sustainability reporting for the real estate sector
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the challenges faced by the Norwegian real estate sector in complying with the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), addressing a critical gap in understanding how these regulations impact sustainability reporting practices. The research seeks new insights into the barriers to implementing CSRD-compliant reporting, contributing to a deeper understanding of the sector's readiness and areas requiring improvement. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, utilizing a scoping literature review to map existing knowledge and semi-structured interviews with industry stakeholders to supplement findings. Data were collected from peer-reviewed articles, master's theses, and interviews with key stakeholders, and analyzed using thematic coding and qualitative analysis. The results reveal that the main challenges include limited knowledge of sustainability matters, difficulties in conducting Double Materiality Assessments (DMA), high costs, poor data systems, and administrative burdens. These findings provide evidence that while some companies proactively prepare for CSRD compliance, many, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), struggle due to resource constraints and a reliance on manual processes. This highlights significant implications for improving digital solutions and stakeholder collaboration. This research offers a novel perspective on sustainability reporting in the Norwegian real estate sector, providing valuable insights into the sector's preparedness and key barriers. The study's findings contribute to advancing digital reporting practices and support for SMEs, highlighting areas for future research and potential policy development to ease the transition to CSRD compliance. Authors: Liu L.; Li X.(.; Wang X.; Zhao Z.
Title: Can leisure travel help combat loneliness in later life?
Abstract: Loneliness is a growing public health concern, particularly among older adults. Tourism research on healthy aging has largely centered on positive well-being; limited attention has been given to whether travel can alleviate loneliness. Drawing on longitudinal data from China and the United States, this study conceptualizes leisure travel as a form of activation and examines its relationship with loneliness among older adults. The findings indicate that greater participation in leisure travel is associated with lower levels of loneliness among this group over time. Travel also offsets age-related declines in daily social participation and the accompanying increase in loneliness, highlighting travel's activating role in later life. Leisure travel further serves as a compensatory resource for older adults with relational deficits. This mechanism varies across cultural contexts. By moving beyond the focus on positive emotion, this study demonstrates tourism's therapeutic potential for reducing loneliness and promoting well-being in aging populations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Impact of heritage status on market prices of townhouses in Central Rio de Janeiro
Abstract: This study investigates the effects of differentiated heritage protection regimes on townhouse property values in central Rio de Janeiro, contributing original evidence to a largely unexplored field in Brazil. Based on a sample of 86 townhouses, it applies a traditional hedonic pricing model (OLS), a Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR), and a Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression with Spatial Autoregressive Error (MGWRSAR), which account for spatial heterogeneity and residual autocorrelation. To overcome data limitations, the analysis employs a bootstrap procedure to improve the robustness of inference. Results indicate that only properties under the least restrictive protection (“monitored”) display statistically significant price premiums. However, rather than reflecting a simple inverse relationship between restrictions and market value, this finding points to the importance of regulatory legibility, enforcement consistency, and perceived investment risks. The discussion highlights how flexible and intelligible protection regimes may foster market confidence, while ambiguous or overly rigid frameworks can undermine the effectiveness of heritage policy. The study also underscores a structural barrier to evidence-based policymaking: the lack of public access to transaction-level data in Brazil. Title: Beyond compliance: Community development committees and the transformation of resource governance in Tanzania
Abstract: Resource-rich countries worldwide often face persistent imbalances in the redistribution of resource wealth. Although mineral extraction generates substantial revenues, these funds are typically centrally managed and redistributed, leaving host communities, who bear the social and environmental burdens of extraction, impoverished and marginalized. In Tanzania, despite provisions allowing Local Government Authorities to levy a 0.3% service charge on mining revenues and receive Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions intended to support local development, means of engaging host communities remain a challenge. Community Development Agreements (CDAs) have been identified as potential instruments to safeguard the interests of host communities. However, despite their widespread promotion, a critical gap remains in understanding how communities can effectively engage in, negotiate, and implement CDAs, particularly in contexts marked by power asymmetries. Communities are often poor, with limited knowledge of mining and the broader extractive industry, and with no access to decision-making power. This study addresses the gap by examining Community Development Committees (CDCs) as an inclusive, participatory institutional mechanism through which communities can effectively articulate their development priorities. Using semi‑structured interviews with 36 key informants across the mining value chain, including central government officials, mining representatives, and local communities, the study finds the CDC model as an effective approach for strengthening community voice, enhancing transparency, improving negotiations, and monitoring project implementations. Although grounded in Tanzania’s mining sector, the study offers insights relevant to other resource dependent economies seeking to foster more equitable social contracts. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Connectivity in Written Personal and Fictional Narratives: The Study of Iranian EFL Learners and Native Speakers of Persian and English
Abstract: The present study aimed to examine the use of different levels of syntactic architecture in written personal and fictional narratives in both Persian and English across three discourse communities, namely Persian native speakers, English native speakers, and Iranian EFL learners. To this end, the participants of the study were selected based on convenience sampling and were asked to write one of their happiest memories. Also, an English fable from Aseop's fables and a Persian story, chosen based on comparative literature and having the similar plot, were given to them to read and write whatever they remembered; there was no limit on the number of words and paragraphs. To analyze the data, the Berman and Nir-Sagiv's (2009) model was followed. The findings showed that in fictional narratives written by both Persian and English native speakers, isotaxis, asymmetric parataxis, complement (CMP), and parataxis levels were frequently employed; however, personal narratives in Persian were dominantly isotactic, paratactic, and asymmetric paratactic, CMP, while isotactic, hypotactic, and paratactic levels were frequent in English written personal narratives. Also, after receiving explicit instruction on different types of English sentences, the use of adverbial and relative clauses (hypotaxis level) increased in Iranian EFL learners' written narratives. It can be concluded that explicit teaching of syntactic levels enabled EFL learners to arrange their sentences correctly to express their intended meaning. Teachers can benefit from the results to gain a more comprehensive understanding of narrative connectivity and help EFL learners elaborate clause linkage in their written narrative tasks. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Enhancement of power system steady-state stability through allocation of quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization algorithm-based multiple D-STATCOM Units
Abstract: Modern distribution networks suffer from power losses and voltage instability under various loading conditions. Mitigating these operational issues requires optimal allocation of custom power devices, such as Distribution Static Compensators (D-STATCOMs). To address this challenge, this study develops a quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization (QGWO) algorithm for allocating D-STATCOMs to ensure steady-state stability, improve bus voltage profiles, and reduce power losses. Distinct from existing variants, QGWO models search agents as probabilistic quantum state vectors, utilizing a fitness-driven amplitude scaling and dynamic phase angle adaptation. Using the backward-forward sweep (BFS) load-flow method, the performance is evaluated across base-load, load-increment, and single-phase fault scenarios on practical 44- and IEEE 69-bus test systems. The voltage stability margin (VSM) is utilized to determine maximum loading factors. For the 44-bus system, buses 22, 29, and 41 with capacities of 637.69 kVAR, 503.75 kVAR, and 351.01 kVAR are found as the optimal locations and sizes. With these units, power losses are reduced by 50.894% under the base-load scenario. For the IEEE 69-bus system, buses 11, 17 and 61 with capacities of 358.69kVAR, 254.02kVAR and 1206.75kVAR reduce power losses by 42.76% under the base-load scenario. Using VSM, the maximum loading factor is found as 1.53 and 2.65 for 44- and 69-bus systems. Statistically, the proposed QGWO achieves the lowest mean power loss, with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests confirming its advantage over PSO, APSO, GWO, and CGWO. Weight sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the optimal solution remains invariant to changes in objective-function weights. Economically, cost-benefit sensitivity analyses confirm the financial viability of the project. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy for flashforwards: Randomized multiple baseline single case experimental design in social anxiety disorder
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Background and objectives: Negative mental imagery in social anxiety is common and can involve memories of adverse events or catastrophic future anticipations (i.e., “flashforwards”). Laboratory research has shown that such imagery can be modulated by dual-tasking interventions, which is used in Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy. Methods: Using a replicated sequential single-case experimental design, we examined whether EMDR therapy for flashforwards reduces social anxiety and avoidance of fear-related situations, relative to baseline, in eight individuals with social anxiety disorder. Participants were recruited from a specialized treatment center after unsuccessful CBT or because of treatment complexity (e.g., comorbidity) and were randomly assigned to varying baseline durations before EMDR therapy. Outcome variables were daily social anxiety and avoidance. Randomization tests were conducted for each case separately to test whether EMDR therapy compared to a baseline phase resulted in less daily 1) social anxiety and 2) social avoidance for individual participants and for the total sample. Results: The preregistered randomization tests did not show statistically significant between-phase differences in daily social anxiety, daily social avoidance, or weekly social anxiety severity. Exploratory, unplanned permutation distancing tests, conducted to examine the possible influence of serial dependency, indicated lower scores during the intervention phase across all three outcomes. At the individual level, these exploratory analyses indicated reductions in daily social anxiety for six participants, in daily social avoidance for three participants, and in weekly social anxiety severity for five participants. Aggregated effect-size estimates were medium for daily social anxiety, small for daily social avoidance, and small to medium for weekly social anxiety severity. Limitations: Limitations include modest serial dependency, absence of an active treatment control condition, absence of long-term follow-up measurements, and inclusion of one participant without a clearly identifiable flashforward, although treatment adhered to the prespecified Stage 1 treatment protocol. Conclusions: The preregistered analyses did not provide confirmatory evidence that EMDR therapy for flashforwards reduced social anxiety or avoidance. However, the descriptive findings, effect-size estimates, and exploratory analyses showed a pattern consistent with possible reductions in social anxiety, while findings for avoidance were weaker and less consistent. Authors: Gan Q.; Kang Q.; Xu J.; Peng S.
Title: Dual-regime molecular restructuring in vacuum hot-pressed briquette coal: Closing the fidelity gap for gas outburst simulations
Abstract: Briquette coal (BC) is used extensively as a coal analog in the physical modeling of coal and gas outbursts. However, the intrinsically weak mechanical structure and elevated permeability of BC relative to natural coal introduce systematic biases. To close this fidelity gap, we report an integrated vacuum hot-pressing thermal conditioning protocol (150–450 °C) coupled with triaxial rock mechanics and seepage characterization. Correlative X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses are performed to decode the molecular engineering levers that govern BC evolution. Two distinct thermal regimes are identified. Below 300 °C, the selective scission of aliphatic C–C/C–H and oxygen-bearing side chains (C–O, C–OH, and COOH) generates plasticizing fragments that drive matrix densification and strength accrual, concurrent with intensified aromatic layer ordering (decreased d 002, increased L c and L a). Above 300 °C, accelerated polycondensation consumes these plasticizing moieties, triggering embrittlement and permeability rebound. The 300 °C optimum delivers the closest macroscopic parametric convergence in terms of the compressive strength and permeability. A uniaxial compressive strength of 7.79 MPa and permeability of 1.72 mD are achieved, which are comparable to typical ranges for natural coal specimens. This optimum is attributed to balanced depolymerization–condensation chemistry and optimized microcrystalline packing. These insights establish thermal processing as a quantitative molecular tuning strategy for coal analog fidelity, providing a mechanistic foundation to enhance the predictive reliability of gas outburst simulations. Title: Indonesian Teachers’ Perceptions About the Potential of Technology-Enhanced Language Assessment (TELA)
Abstract: Technology-enhanced language assessment (TELA) has significantly improved language evaluation by integrating digital tools to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility. Title: Effective algorithms for tensor-train decomposition via the UTV framework
Abstract: The tensor-train (TT) decomposition is widely used to compress large tensors into a more compact form by exploiting their inherent data structures. A fundamental approach for constructing the TT format is the well-known TT-SVD method, which performs singular value decompositions (SVDs) on the successive unfolding matrices sequentially. But in practical applications, it is often unnecessary to compute full SVDs. In this article, we propose the TT-UTV method, a general framework that incorporates the family of UTV-type algorithms to compute the TT decomposition. As an extension of TT-SVD, it can choose rank-revealing UTV factorizations for the extraction of core tensors, enabling more efficient handling of large-scale intermediate unfolding matrices. We further analyze the error propagation of each step within the TT-UTV framework, and derive a tight overall error bound. Based on this analysis, we recommend distinct sweep patterns for the ULV and URV cases, and formulate the rank-adaptive algorithms with prescribed accuracy. Title: Quasi-real-time degradation-aware energy management for standalone PV-battery microgrids under uncertainty
Abstract: Energy management in standalone photovoltaic-battery microgrids requires balancing supply reliability, forecast uncertainty, and battery degradation within tight computational budgets. This paper proposes an integrated, quasi-real-time energy management framework that couples nonlinear rolling-horizon model predictive control with three complementary mechanisms: (i) a variable-resolution dispatch layer that adapts the optimization granularity to system dynamics, (ii) an operating reserve formulation based on short-term energy-mismatch forecasts produced by dedicated Long Short-Term Memory recurrent neural networks (LSTM-RNN) for load, photovoltaic generation, and reserve estimation, and (iii) an online battery degradation assessment algorithm compatible with the optimization layer. The framework is evaluated on a standalone microgrid in Ouarzazate, Morocco, using one-second-resolution data over three representative weeks. The results reveal that the integrated degradation-aware framework does not uniformly improve dispatch performance, but rather establishes an explicit trade-off between supply reliability and battery lifetime. Under the tested configuration, the joint framework extends expected battery lifetime by approximately 218% compared to the uncertainty-only strategy (from 4.51 to 14.36 years averaged across three weeks), at the cost of a 50% relative increase in unmet load (from 19.22% to 28.78%), providing microgrid operators with a quantifiable, tunable mechanism to prioritize battery preservation when operationally justified. The proposed online cycle detection algorithm is cross-verified against pyLife's rainflow-based reference implementation across all 30 evaluated dispatch cases, showing a mean absolute cycle-count deviation of 2.68%, confirming its consistency with reference rainflow methods and its suitability for real-time embedded deployment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Dual-view contrastive learning for heterogeneous graph representation
Abstract: Representation learning on heterogeneous graphs relies on exploiting both diverse semantics and intricate structural relations. However, the common approaches struggle to simultaneously account for distant semantic interactions and fine-grained structural patterns. Therefore, we introduce a novel Heterogeneous Graph Representation Learning method via a dual-view contrastive structure (HGRL). Specifically, the Schema-aware Graph Abstraction Module (SGAM) captures relational dependencies using a type-aware graph neural network augmented with adaptive residual pathways to learn structural representations. Title: Enhancing Real-World Physics Problem-Solving Skills through Mind Map-Based Scaffolding: The Role of Metacomponents among Pre-University Students

Abstract: Physics problem-solving is essential in physics education, yet many pre-university students struggle to apply concepts to real-world contexts. This study examines the effectiveness of integrating mind map-based scaffolding with metacomponents to enhance real-world physics problem-solving skills (RWPPS). A quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test non-equivalent group design involved 253 students at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. The experimental group used mind maps to define problems, organize information, and plan strategies with guided scaffolding, while the control group received conventional lectures. Data from open-ended RWPPS assessments showed that the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group, with improvements across all metacomponent sub-skills, especially monitoring. Title: Declining cocoa and intensifying artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM): examining changing labour structures and livelihoods in rural Ghana
Abstract: Ghana’s cocoa frontier increasingly overlaps with mechanised artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), creating competition over land and labour. This article examines how declining cocoa production and intensifying ASGM reorganise a local labour regime and reshape rural livelihood pathways in Juaboso District, Western North Region. It draws on 40 semi-structured interviews with cocoa farmers, ASGM workers and institutional actors, alongside observations at four ASGM sites, conducted in 2024. The analysis combines the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework for the 21st Century (SLF-21) with a labour-regime lens. The findings show that cocoa decline and political arrangements governing access to land, machinery, finance and licences create uneven openings for mining. Landowners and operators can convert cocoa land and capture mining rents, while young, often migrant, workers enter hazardous and insecure work. At the same time, ASGM expansion reduces labour availability for cocoa production, increases labour costs for cocoa farmers and degrades land and water used by farming households. Mining income can meet urgent household needs and, in some cases, support farming, but these gains coexist with risks that are shifted onto workers, non-mining farmers and younger generations. These risks are unevenly distributed across generations, with younger people likely to bear a greater burden through depleted land and water resources, and the health and educational consequences of mining-centred livelihood pathways. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Urban transformation in heritage cities through the perceptions of experts- A case of Varanasi, India

Title: Severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS frequency regulation and SoC management
Abstract: This paper proposes a severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS-based primary frequency regulation (PFR) and state-of-charge (SoC) management. Conventional adaptive droop controllers commonly use decoupled gain structures, fixed nonlinear curves, or multi-parameter logistic functions, which complicate tuning and may increase unnecessary battery cycling. The proposed controller introduces a unified Δf–SoC map in which a single concavity parameter β shapes the frequency-severity response. A multiplicative SoC weighting function enforces dynamic participation limits, while a hybrid β-adaptation mechanism distinguishes sustained volatility from high-RoCoF events. A frequency-gated restoration loop is added to recover SoC without interfering with critical frequency support. The controller is evaluated through SFR-model simulations and IEEE 9-bus multi-machine studies, supported by sensitivity analysis, stability verification, and battery degradation assessment. Results show that the proposed method provides a balanced trade-off between frequency regulation and battery utilization. In the continuous stochastic case, it reduces BESS energy throughput and total degradation damage compared with the benchmark controllers. In the severe IEEE 9-bus step disturbance, it achieves the lowest RMS frequency deviation and maximum deviation among the tested methods. These results confirm that the proposed strategy improves large-disturbance frequency support while preserving battery lifetime and maintaining stable operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Intra-Matrix Flexible Optical-Electronic Configuration Algorithms for Energy-Efficient Large Language Model Inference
Source title: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
Abstract: Low-energy, low-precision inference is an important enabler for scalable deployment of large language models (LLMs). Optical-electronic computing offers high bandwidth, low latency, and potentially high energy efficiency, making it a promising approach for future LLM deployment. However, existing optical and hybrid optical-electronic inference systems typically use uniform hardware configurations, such as fixed optical power or a fixed electronic-photonic partition across layers. Fine-grained allocation of optical power and optical-electronic computation remains underexplored for photonic LLM inference. Here, we propose three flexible configuration algorithms: Flexible Optical Power Allocation (FOPA), Flexible Weak-Column Allocation (FWCA), and Joint Optical Power and Weak-Column Allocation (JOWA). Using a diagonal Hessian estimator without constructing the full Hessian matrix, these methods jointly optimize optical-electronic resources under predefined energy budgets. Evaluations on Llama 2-7B and DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Base show estimated energy savings of 40.11%-60.85% relative to FP16 inference on the NVIDIA H100 and 5.34%-38.12% relative to uniform optical-power and weak-column baselines, while maintaining an acceptable perplexity increase. Evaluations using a Tianshu-hardware-calibrated simulator show corresponding estimated energy savings of 39.91%-53.67% and 5.02%-26.76%, respectively. These results indicate that fine-grained resource allocation can improve the energy-accuracy trade-off of hybrid optical-electronic systems for LLM inference.  © 1995-2012 IEEE.

Title: Socio-ecological Landscape Contexts and Ecosystem Services in the Argentine Dry Chaco: From Agroexpansion to Inhabited Forests (2000–2020)
Abstract: Landscape transformation driven by agribusiness expansion in the Dry Chaco is among the most pressing socio-ecological challenges globally, yet biophysical, ecosystem-service (ES), and sociodemographic dynamics are typically analyzed separately, obscuring how territorial configurations shape landscape change. To address this gap, this study proposes the Socio-Ecological Landscape Context (SELC) framework — a spatially explicit approach that integrates biophysical metrics with sociodemographic variables to define territorial units and interpret how they mediate ES supply over time. We applied it to Santiago del Estero Province in the Argentine Dry Chaco, analyzing landscape transformation (patch count and edge density) and ES supply (a rapid multicriteria assessment assigning potential supply values to land-cover types) over two decades (2000–2020), using satellite imagery (MapBiomas Chaco Collection 4), deforestation records, and census data. Cluster analysis identified six SELCs: First Wave Agroexpansion, Second Wave Agroexpansion, Concentrated Population, Inhabited Dry Forest, Hilly Arid, and Alluvial Plain. Closed woody vegetation declined by 12.6% points (from 66.6% to 54.0%), while the number of forest patches rose by 44%, indicating progressive fragmentation. Two contrasting patterns emerge: dynamic SELCs (First and Second Wave Agroexpansion, Concentrated Population) show marked declines in key ES, whereas persistent SELCs maintain higher ES levels over time. A sparse rural population shows a modest but consistent positive association with ES supply. These findings suggest that similar land-cover compositions can yield divergent socio-ecological outcomes depending on landscape configuration and modes of inhabitation, supporting biocultural conservation approaches that recognize peasant and Indigenous communities as active contributors to landscape multifunctionality. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Blastocystis sp. in human populations: Pooled prevalence and subtype distribution from a systematic review and meta-analysis
Abstract: Blastocystis is widely detected in human populations, yet prevalence estimates vary substantially across geographic regions, population settings, and diagnostic approaches. We systematically reviewed cross-sectional surveys published from 2015 to 2025 that investigated non-disease-selected human populations. Across 137 eligible survey units from 47 countries, 562,327 participants and 26,697 positive detections were included. The crude participant-level positivity was 4.7%, whereas the random-effects pooled prevalence across published surveys was 17.9% (95% CI: 13.9%–22.6%; 95% PI: 0.7%–87.5%; I2 = 99.7%). Regional pooled estimates were 44.2% in Africa, 36.7% in the Americas, 8.4% in Asia, and 7.2% in Europe; however, these comparisons should be interpreted descriptively because substantial residual heterogeneity and study-level confounding remained. Population-group differences were not statistically significant ( P = 0.074), while the three broad diagnostic-strategy groups were summarized descriptively because multimodal protocols were heterogeneous. Sensitivity analyses restricted to population-based surveys and community/household surveys yielded pooled estimates of 15.8% and 13.0%, respectively. Among 62 studies reporting molecular subtype information, 5220 isolates were assigned single subtypes, while 658 mixed-subtype detections from 18 studies were summarized separately. ST3, ST1, and ST2 were among the predominant reported subtypes. These findings summarize available published surveillance data rather than a population-weighted global burden estimate and highlight the need for standardized sampling frameworks, harmonized molecular workflows, and integrated One Health investigations to clarify Blastocystis epidemiology and transmission ecology. Title: Business simulation games and ethical decision making confidence and intentions: The role of self-efficacy, reflective practice, and teamwork
Abstract: This study examines the potential associations between experiential learning via participating in a business simulation game and business students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. While simulation games have been widely recognized for their effectiveness in developing business competencies, their associations with ethical decision making confidence and intentions in a non-ethics related environment remain underexplored. Our findings suggest that participation in simulation games is associated with higher levels of students' teamwork and reflective practice capabilities that, in turn, were found to be positively associated with their ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Moreover, students who participated in simulation games reported higher self-efficacy which, however, was not found to have a significant relationship with ethical decision-making confidence and intentions. Title: Integrated assessment of the environmental and social impacts of bauxite mining in the Boké Prefecture
Abstract: Since the 2011 mining reforms, Guinea has experienced a rapid increase in bauxite extraction, particularly in the Boké Prefecture. While this growth has significantly stimulated the nation's economy, the aggregated socio-environmental and territorial consequences of bauxite extraction at the local level remain insufficiently documented in peer-reviewed literature, especially through comprehensive, community-level empirical analyses that links spatial transformations to residents’ experiences of displacement. This study argues that existing compensation and governance frameworks do not match the territorial extent of bauxite mining impacts, resulting in ongoing livelihood insecurity even in cases of formal resettlement. The research employs a mixed-methods approach, integrating field surveys, direct observations, interviews, and focus group discussions with 83 participants from four impacted communities. It also incorporates a diachronic analysis of land use and land cover (LULC) derived from Landsat imagery spanning 1973 to 2024. The study follows Cernea’s Impoverishment Risks and Reconstruction framework. Findings indicate a marked increase in mining areas (from 0 to 68 km²) and exposed soils near Sangarédi, accompanied by a substantial decline in vegetation cover (–28%). These spatial changes align with local perceptions of deteriorating air and water quality, farmland loss, and heightened livelihood insecurity, despite observable investments in social infrastructure. In Kanfarandé, the expansion of port infrastructure has precipitated significant territorial changes, even absent direct mining activities. Overall, the research shows that current compensation and governance mechanisms remain inadequate to address the cumulative and indirect impacts of bauxite exploitation, underscoring the need for integrated, participatory, and territorially informed governance frameworks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Seven Sisters tourism under siege: Hybrid neural insights into stakeholder resilience
Abstract: Tourism stakeholders in insurgency-affected destinations navigate persistent insecurity that shapes their perceptions, adaptive behavior, and support for tourism in nonlinear ways. This study investigates how security-related perceptions influence tourism support in Northeast India's Seven Sisters region, a politically fragile zone characterized by prolonged insurgency. Using a mixed-method hybrid design, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), artificial neural network (ANN) modeling, sensitivity analysis, and content analysis were applied to 584 stakeholder surveys and 25 in-depth interviews. ANN modeling revealed a nonlinear inverted-U relationship between security visibility and stakeholder support, interpreted as a “ security-skepticism dilemma” grounded in Prospect Theory. Security forces concern (35%) and moral panic (24%) were the most influential predictors. These findings advance tourism resilience theory and provide actionable governance guidance for conflict-affected destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Robust scheduling of a port power system with shore-power load uncertainty, dynamic shore-power pricing, and hybrid hydrogen–battery storage
Abstract: Shore-power demand in ports is highly dependent on vessel arrivals, departures, berthing duration, and vessel-type differences. These operating features make conventional aggregated load models insufficient for coordinated scheduling. This paper proposes a two-stage robust scheduling model for a port distribution network–multi-microgrid system considering vessel-behavior-driven shore-power load uncertainty, dynamic shore-power pricing, and hybrid hydrogen–battery storage. By combining vessel-type classification, vessel-level parameterization, arrival/departure perturbations, and microgrid-level aggregation, a shore-power load model and its uncertainty representation are developed to capture the overlapping berthing effect of multiple vessels and the time-varying uncertainty of shore-power demand. Dynamic shore-power pricing is used to better reflect practical port operation, while a hybrid hydrogen–battery storage system is incorporated to leverage the complementary characteristics of fast-responding batteries and long-duration hydrogen storage, effectively smoothing multi-timescale power fluctuations, facilitating efficient wind power accommodation, and enhancing the intertemporal regulation flexibility and economic efficiency of the port microgrid. The proposed model is solved through a hierarchical ATC–C&CG framework, which coordinates the distribution network and microgrids and optimizes recourse decisions under worst-case scenarios. Case studies show that the total social cost is 20,632.50 CNY, the served shore-power energy reaches 7078.64 kWh, and no load shedding or renewable energy curtailment occurs. Comparative results indicate that the proposed uncertainty model can describe practical port operation disturbances, dynamic shore-power pricing improves shore-power revenue without reducing the service level, and hybrid hydrogen–battery storage enhances microgrid intertemporal regulation flexibility under wind power fluctuations. © 2026

Title: Multi-Level collaborative optimization for Multi-Modal media manipulation detection and grounding
Abstract: The proliferation of manipulated multi-modal content threatens the credibility of social media. Although existing detecting and grounding multi-modal media manipulation (DGM4) methods exploit image-text complementarity, they optimize classification and localization largely independently, overlooking structured collaboration between the two tasks. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-level task collaboration (MLTC) framework that progressively promotes detection and grounding interaction at the feature, semantic, and decision levels. At the feature level, cross-modal alignment and interaction construct modality-specific bridge representations, enabling classification and grounding within each modality to reason over a shared multi-modal evidence space. At the semantic level, the proposed cross-granularity semantic fusion (CGSF) module learns shared semantic importance weights to coordinate global classification semantics and local grounding evidence, encouraging consistent manipulation-aware evidence selection across different granularities. At the decision level, focusing on the dense spatial nature of visual grounding, we introduce cross-granularity decision fusion (CGDF), which integrates image-level manipulation confidence and patch-level localization responses to produce a manipulation probability map (MPM). The manipulation-aware grounding refinement (MAGR) module further introduces the MPM as a bounded soft prior during query-based evidence aggregation, strengthening manipulation-relevant patch contributions while preserving the baseline visual evidence for robust bounding-box prediction. On the entire DGM4 test set, MLTC achieves an AUC of 94.94%, a multi-label mAP of 90.72%, an image-grounding IoUmean of 79.63%, and a token-grounding F1 score of 76.85%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Congestion management in electric distribution systems through flexibility services: a bibliometric and analytical review
Abstract: Electricity systems are rapidly evolving toward decentralized architectures with high shares of variable renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources (DERs), increasing congestion in medium- and low-voltage networks. This paper presents a structured mixed-source review combining bibliometric mapping and targeted analytical synthesis on flexibility services for congestion management in electric distribution systems. Analysis of the quality-controlled Q3 corpus (n = 1827) identifies China as the leading national contributor and substantial collective European participation, with 79.6% of records published from 2018 onward. Author-keyword mapping reveals five streams: distribution-network optimization, market-based congestion management, uncertainty-aware active-network operation, flexibility-service coordination, and demand-response smart-grid control. Novelty lies in keeping the validated bibliometric corpus separate from an independently assembled, question-driven evidence base until interpretation. The analytical synthesis shows that distributed locational marginal pricing (DLMP), particularly in iterative formulations, can internalize network constraints and provide locational signals for DER coordination, although its effectiveness depends on adequate network modeling, uncertainty treatment, and flexible-demand participation. The review also identifies converging trends toward multilayer coordination between transmission system operators (TSOs) and distribution system operators (DSOs), local flexibility procurement, and digital platforms for ancillary-service provision. Across jurisdictions, explicit remuneration, interoperable data, and coordinated governance recur, but uneven implementation precludes causal comparisons or effectiveness rankings. The paper concludes by identifying research gaps related to cost–benefit validation, regulatory standardization, data interoperability, and large-scale implementation in distribution systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Yao H.; Chen Z.
Title: How autonomy-supportive environments and growth mindset foster creativity efficacy in middle school students? Evidence from a large-scale survey in China
Abstract: This study examines the associations between multi-source autonomy-supportive environments, growth mindset, and creative self-efficacy among Chinese middle school students, with particular attention to the mediating role of growth mindset and individual heterogeneity in these associations. Using large-scale survey data from 6146 middle school students in Suzhou, China, and drawing on Bandura's (1997) social cognitive theory and Self-Determination Theory, we employed structural equation modeling and quantile regression to investigate these relationships. The SEM results indicate that teacher, parental, and peer autonomy support are all positively associated with creative self-efficacy, with teacher and peer support showing stronger total associations than parental support. Growth mindset mediated all three associations, with the indirect effect proportion being highest for teacher autonomy support, followed by parental autonomy support and peer autonomy support. Quantile regression analyses revealed meaningful heterogeneity across the creative self-efficacy distribution: teacher and parental autonomy support showed stronger associations at lower quantiles, peer autonomy support peaked at moderate quantiles, and all associations weakened at higher quantiles. These findings contribute to the cross-cultural understanding of how multi-source autonomy-supportive environments relate to creative self-efficacy in a collectivist educational context, and offer practical implications for differentiated educational interventions targeting students at different levels of creative self-efficacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Maiese K.
Author full names: Maiese, Kenneth (35546043800)
Title: Oxidative stress, aging, metabolism, SIRT1, and the gut microbiota: the neurocardiac basis of cognitive loss
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease and cognitive loss have a neurocardiac basis. Poor vascular perfusion can impair cognitive function in both Alzheimer’s disease and multiple sclerosis. However, a treatment gap exists because current approaches do not adequately address the shared underlying cellular mechanisms responsible for cognitive dysfunction in these conditions. Current treatments for cognitive impairment in diseases such as cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis, and diabetes often fail to fully address the shared underlying cellular mechanisms. Consequently, the prevailing precision treatment strategy, which focuses on managing symptoms and preventing disease progression, is insufficient. This highlights the urgent need for innovative approaches capable of targeting these common cellular pathways across these diverse conditions. Novel investigations into oxidative stress, cellular senescence, programmed cell death with apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and autophagy, cellular metabolism with apolipoprotein E and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonism, silent mating type information regulation 2 homolog 1 (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), mitochondrial dynamics, and the gut microbiome offer the potential to address the risk factors and clinical treatments for cardiovascular disease and cognitive loss. These pathways are exquisitely dependent upon one another and require in-depth knowledge of the modulatory cellular mechanisms for effective translation to clinical care. © 2026 Medical Gas Research

Title: Gullibility, loneliness, exploitation or just bad luck? Exploring older adults’ perceptions of fraud risks, protections and victimhood
Abstract: Exploring older adult victimisation of cybercrimes, perceptions of risk and protections using semi-structured interviews and a mixed interactional analytic approach, this paper assesses the implications of isolation, technical knowledge and trusted sources of protection advice. It explores perceptions of personal responsibility, fraud risk, fraud protections, the interconnected and dichotomous narratives of blame and empathy relating to victimhood, and how judgement rests on whether victimhood is perceived as acceptable (just bad luck) or not (gullibility). It highlights the importance social isolation and cognitive decline has in relation to older adults’ fraud victimhood, underscored by participants’ perceptions that youth, education and intelligence are key to resilience against threats. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Croes R.; Bąk M.; Suchanek M.

Title: When tourism competitiveness becomes human development: The conditioning role of institutional quality in Central and Eastern Europe
Abstract: Why do destinations with similar levels of tourism competitiveness experience different human development outcomes? Integrating Sen's Capability Approach with the Tourism Competitiveness Theory Hypothesis, this study examines the institutional conditions under which tourism competitiveness becomes meaningful for human development. Tourism competitiveness is conceptualized as a resource-generating capacity, while institutional quality represents a macro-level condition shaping its conversion into human development. Using annual data for eleven Central and Eastern European countries (2000–2023), we estimate heterogeneous panel autoregressive distributed lag models, error-correction dynamics, and Granger-type causality tests. Results show a positive long-run relationship between tourism competitiveness and human development, with stronger institutional quality associated with larger developmental returns. A trajectory analysis identifies four tourism–development pathways and interprets their differences through institutional quality. The study extends tourism competitiveness theory beyond destination performance by explaining why comparable competitive capacities can generate different human development outcomes across institutional contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ji X.; Zhang X.
Title: Can AI-generated images match human-generated images in inspiring travel? A visual feature analysis of audience perceptions and visit intention
Abstract: Generative AI tools can now create photorealistic destination images at low cost, yet whether such images motivate travel as effectively as human-generated images remains unclear. Drawing on the heuristic-systematic model, this research examines differences between AI-generated and human-generated tourism images through three studies. Study 1 shows that AI-generated images receive higher ratings of perceived aesthetics but lower ratings of perceived authenticity, narrative transportation, and visit intention than human-generated images. Study 2 identifies 19 computable visual indicators across three dimensions and finds that AI-generated images exhibit stronger visual schema characteristics, whereas human-generated images show richer visual structure. Study 3 uses XGBoost and SHAP analysis to identify the visual features associated with different psychological responses. These findings connect computational visual analysis with tourism consumer research by identifying differences in audience responses to AI-generated and human-generated images and the visual features associated with those responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Vivoda V.; Janjua R.; Borja D.
Author full names: Vivoda, Vlado (26647183600); Janjua, Ron (60818927800); Borja, Danilo (57193092324)
Title: Data centres and the new strategic infrastructure governance: From cloud ESG to compute sovereignty
Abstract: Data centres have moved from the background of the digital economy to the foreground of energy, climate, industrial and national-security politics. Artificial intelligence is intensifying this shift through growing demand for compute, electricity, cooling, land, hardware and critical materials. Yet governance remains largely organised around facility-level metrics that treat data centres as bounded technical assets rather than strategic infrastructure embedded in grids, water systems, supply chains, communities and security architectures. This article develops the CLOUDS framework—Coherence, Lifecycle materiality, Operational locality, Utility burden, Digital sovereignty, and Social licence and public purpose—as a diagnostic architecture for evaluating data centres as system-shaping infrastructure. It also develops capacity extraction: the process through which heterogeneous inputs such as electricity, water, land, permits, institutional trust and community tolerance are rendered as a single quantity called capacity and converted into compute whose higher-value layers may remain controlled elsewhere. The framework is developed through an integrative review and tiered empirical design spanning Chile, Australia, Querétaro, Ireland and Singapore. It is proposed for testing rather than presented as validated. Two findings are central. First, instrument incoherence can arise without regulatory capture when no institution can govern trade-offs across electricity, water, planning and public value. Second, hosting is not sovereignty: physical location alone creates no assured claim on compute access, workload priority, crisis continuity or higher-value layers. The policy implication is strategic infrastructure bargaining over both system capacity and the institutions governing its conversion into compute. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Puente-Díaz R.; Cavazos-Arroyo J.
Author full names: Puente-Díaz, Rogelio (56013548600); Cavazos-Arroyo, Judith (56102212300)
Title: Feelings of ease in generating ideas: My loyal companion that guides my mental action but does not help me generate more creative ideas
Abstract: The ability to generate creative ideas is an important skill for education. This study examined how feelings of ease in generating ideas act as a cue that allowed individuals to have information to monitor their mental action and make important metacognitive decisions while generating creative ideas. Participants were asked to generate four ideas to help deal with the problem of empty work offices during and after the pandemic of COVID-19. After generating each idea, participants reported their feelings of ease and evaluated the creativity of each idea. Participants then reported their confidence in the ideas generated and selected their most creative idea. Results showed negative, curvilinear trajectories of feelings of ease and self-evaluations of the creativity of each idea. Feelings of ease in generating ideas were positively related to self-evaluations and the decisions to continue generating ideas and negatively related to choosing the first idea as the most creative. In addition, feelings of ease were indirectly and positively related to post-task confidence through their relationship with self-evaluations. These findings provided initial, empirical evidence that feelings of ease acted as cues to inform relevant judgments and decisions in the process of ideation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bongo M.F.
Author full names: Bongo, Miriam F. (57190491240)
Title: Modified DEA-SBM efficiency-based diversion risk proxy assessment with peer similarity for decision support in aircraft diversion management
Abstract: Aircraft diversion is a critical component of aviation safety management, requiring close coordination among pilots, air traffic controllers, and airline operations teams. Although established procedures guide the process, diversions remain complex and time-sensitive due to operational and logistical constraints, and there is no universal framework for selecting the most suitable alternate airport. This paper proposes a decision support system to assist diversion decision-making through a modified data envelopment analysis–slack-based measure (DEA-SBM) efficiency-based proxy model. The model evaluates the efficiency-based diversion risk proxy (EDRP) index for airports using relevant input and output variables associated with the diversion process. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, three real diversion cases in the Philippines are used as baseline scenarios. The resulting model outputs are consistent with the actual diversion decisions implemented in operational practice. This alignment provides empirical support that the model can function as a reliable decision support tool for diversion management, particularly in replicating observed operational judgment under real-world constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Asare P.Y.
Author full names: Asare, Prince Yeboah (58089618800)
Title: Task value, effort regulation and critical thinking: Towards a unified learning configuration in financial management education
Abstract: Financial Management requires students to integrate motivational, behavioural, and cognitive competencies to solve financial problems. However, existing research has predominantly examined these learner characteristics independently, providing limited understanding of how they coexist to shape learning. This study adopted a person-centred approach to identify distinct learning configurations based on task value, effort regulation, and critical thinking among Business students studying Financial Management. A cross-sectional survey design was employed to collect data from 168 students using validated measures, and Latent Profile Analysis identified naturally occurring learning profiles. Four distinct learning configurations emerged: Low Learning Orientation (10.1%), Developing Learning Orientation (11.9%), Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation (31.0%), and Integrated Learning Configuration (47.0%). The Integrated Learning Configuration represented the largest group. Notably, the Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation profile reflected students with stronger task value and effort regulation relative to critical thinking. This finding suggests that valuing learning and regulating effort alone may be insufficient for developing higher-order financial reasoning. Profile membership differed by programme of study but not by sex or age. The study advances management education by conceptualising learning in Financial Management as an integrated configuration of motivational, behavioural, and cognitive dimensions rather than isolated learner characteristics, informing pedagogical connoisseurship in practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Serafin T.; Nitka W.
Author full names: Serafin, Tomasz (36180080500); Nitka, Weronika (57206777718)
Title: Data-driven calibration sample selection and forecast combination in electricity price forecasting: An application of the ARHNN method
Abstract: Calibration sample selection and forecast combination are two simple yet powerful tools used in forecasting. They can be combined with a variety of models to significantly improve prediction accuracy, at the same time offering easy implementation and low computational complexity. While their effectiveness has been repeatedly confirmed in prior scientific literature, the topic is still underexplored in the field of electricity price forecasting. In this research article we apply the Autoregressive Hybrid Nearest Neighbors (ARHNN) method to three long-term time series describing the German, Spanish and New England electricity markets. We show that it outperforms popular literature benchmarks in terms of forecast accuracy by up to 10%. We also propose two simplified variants of the method, granting a vast decrease in computation time with only minor loss of prediction accuracy. Finally, we compare the forecasts’ performance in a battery storage system trading case study and propose a new automated trading strategy. We find that using a forecast-driven strategy can consistently achieve a substantial share of theoretical maximum profits while trading, demonstrating business value in practical applications. © 2026

Authors: Mohammadi P.; Dahmardeh M.
Author full names: Mohammadi, Poune (61000718800); Dahmardeh, Mahdi (55897288900)
Title: Gender Representation and Intercultural Competence in Iranian EFL Coursebooks from the 1960s to 2020s
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the representation of gender and intercultural competence in the images and texts of 15 Iranian secondary school English coursebooks, published over six decades. Gender representation was investigated using the framework proposed by Dahmardeh and Kim (2020), and the scale developed by Solhaug and Kristensen (2020) was used as the criteria for investigating intercultural competence. The data were coded and counted using manifest content analysis. The results showed that Iranian English coursebooks mentioned males and females unequally in their texts across different decades, with one gender being represented more in each decade. Regarding gender representation in the images, males were represented more than females in almost all decades. The representation of males and females in the books published in the 1970s was almost equal, followed by extreme and sudden changes in gender representation in the 1980s. However, the books published in and after the 2000s presented a balanced picture of males and females. The coursebooks dealt with intercultural competence in their texts and images very rarely, limiting this concept to religious issues and neglecting other aspects. In fact, the coursebooks addressed only one category out of the 11 categories. Finally, the study ends with implications for coursebook authors, materials designers, teachers, students, and teacher trainers. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. All rights reserved.

Author full names: Haddad, Gloria Ghantous (56448133800); Merhej Sayegh, May (57207456370); Mekdessi, Selim (57156421500); Osta, Alain (57213164119)
Title: Perceived social entrepreneurship education and entrepreneurial intention in times of crisis: Where moral obligation matters
Abstract: Social entrepreneurship education is widely promoted; however, the reflection of students' educational experience in social entrepreneurial intention remains insufficiently understood, particularly in institutionally fragile contexts. Drawing on survey data from 299 Lebanese university students, this study tests a moderated mediation model grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). Specifically, it examines whether personal attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control mediate the relationship between students' perceived social entrepreneurship education experience and entrepreneurial intention, and whether moral obligation conditions these pathways. More positive perceptions of the educational experience are associated with stronger intention indirectly through personal attitude and perceived behavioural control, while subjective norms show no significant effect, reflecting weakened normative reference points under prolonged crisis. Moral obligation operates selectively, strengthening the attitudinal pathway while leaving the control and the normative pathways unchanged. This study extends the mediated view of educational influence to social entrepreneurship education in a crisis setting, suggests that moral obligation may function as a conditional ethical amplifier, and shows how institutional fragility can affect the salient dimensions of TPB. In fragile settings, such education should cultivate reflective attitudes and moral engagement alongside structural reforms that enable normative support for socially oriented careers. © 2026

Title: Reproductive numbers and traveling fronts in models of protest dynamics with police management
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: Protests often spread through social networks and across cities, a phenomenon that can be modeled using reaction–diffusion systems. Building on the model in [10] , which links protest activity and social tension, we study an extended model that also includes police protest management strategies. We focus on traveling wave solutions and examine how protest activity, social tension, and police density interact to shape the spread of protests [36] . Assuming the existence of traveling fronts in parameter regimes where the system is not monotone, we derive stability conditions for these traveling fronts, extending earlier results that assumed monotonicity. Through numerical simulations, we estimate how fast protests spread and identify threshold conditions, similar to epidemiological reproduction numbers, that determine whether protests grow or fade. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: The social acceptance of agrivoltaics: Exploring the cognitive and affective outcomes of technological, contextual, and personal beliefs
Abstract: Agrivoltaics -the co-siting of photovoltaic energy and agronomic production- has been promoted as a win-win solution to reconcile renewables expansion with food security, yet its deployment has raised ambivalence and public opposition. Existing studies have largely focused on farmers and experts, leaving lay citizens’ views underexplored. This paper addresses that gap by examining the determinants of agrivoltaics’ acceptance among non-experts. Acceptance was assessed through the integrated Sustainable Energy Technology Acceptance framework, further extended by introducing outcome evaluation as both a cognitive (perceived efficacy) and an affective (positive emotions) pathway to acceptability, and by incorporating anticipatory solastalgia, understood as present distress over anticipated landscape change. A convenience sample of Italian citizens (N = 849), mostly residing in urban or semi‑urban areas, completed an online questionnaire during the early phase of APV implementation in Italy, thus providing anticipatory evaluations. Hierarchical regressions and path analyses show that technological beliefs, especially perceptions of global and local sustainability, are the strongest predictors of agrivoltaics’ acceptability. Contextual beliefs, notably legitimacy, fairness, and trust in agrivoltaics’ technical-scientific actors, further enhance acceptability. Personal beliefs contribute as well: injunctive norms encourage acceptability, whereas anticipatory solastalgia significantly hinders it. The findings provide a quantitative baseline against which context-specific case studies can be interpreted as installations spread across the territory in the future. Findings suggest that policy and communication should highlight agrivoltaics’ environmental and socio-economic benefits and engage local experts rather than political actors; implications concerning landscape framing are advanced as hypotheses to be tested with affected populations. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Zhang R.

Title: Emotional preferences in LoRA-driven AI-generated urban vitality spaces: A study using discrete choice models
Abstract: China's transition toward urban stock renewal has heightened the focus on the emotional quality of urban vitality spaces. While AI generative design offers new approaches, whether AI-generated images as visual representations for specific spaces can meet people's emotional needs remains insufficiently examined. This study examines whether AI-generated visual representations of such spaces evoke image-based emotional preferences comparable to those for real photographs, and identifies which spatial attributes drive these preferences. Using THE BOX in Beijing as a case, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion models generated visual representations of seven chosen scenes. Emotional preferences were measured through validated scales completed by 115 participants. A discrete choice model was used to compare participants' preferences between photographs of the real space and AI-generated images and identified influential attributes. Results showed that participants with design-related backgrounds preferred real photographs. Positive affect toward AI-generated images was the strongest predictor of preference. Real-scene color, natural elements, and uniqueness reduced the odds of choosing AI-generated versions, whereas AI-generated form and structure, natural elements, and changeability increased them. The study contributes a replicable workflow linking generative AI with emotional preference measurement, offering a structured approach for evidence-based design review. The findings are preliminary due to the single case, modest sample, and reliance on static images. Future work should extend to diverse urban contexts and multimodal evaluation. © 2026 The Authors.

Author full names: Aguirre-Suárez, T. (60994559300); Pérez-Chiquito, M. (60994192400); Cochea-Tomalá, H. (60994192500); Escandón-Panchana, P. (57200918370)
Title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Although artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in smart tourism research, its application to geotourism remains fragmented, particularly regarding geoheritage conservation, geodiversity management, and territorial planning. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. An integrated bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review were conducted to evaluate scientific developments and empirical applications of artificial intelligence within geotourism contexts. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. The study objectives were to propose an integrated conceptual framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning to support the development of smart geotourism. © 2027 The author(s). Authors: Mohammadi V.; Sadeghi Bigham B.
Author full names: Mohammadi, Venus (57209109758); Sadeghi Bigham, Bahram (58450826800)
Title: Trust fusion: a weighted multi-perspective framework for ECG anomaly detection in IoMT
Abstract: Continuous electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments faces a fundamental precision–sensitivity trade–off. Standalone reconstruction–based detectors achieve high specificity but miss subtle anomalies, while geometric detectors capture rare patterns but generate excessive false alarms. This paper presents a hybrid Trust Fusion framework that resolves this trade–off through linearly weighted integration of an LSTM–Autoencoder, a 6–band Isolation Forest, and Z–score statistical validation, augmented by a clinically motivated Label–Free Adaptive Recovery mechanism that reclassifies borderline missed arrhythmias closest to the decision boundary. Evaluated on the MIT–BIH Arrhythmia Database under a strict inter–patient protocol (25 training records, 10 held–out test patients, 406,210 windows), the proposed method achieves 93.56% Accuracy, 86.96% Sensitivity, 96.15% Specificity, 89.86% Precision, 88.39% F1–Score, and an AUC–ROC of 0.9640, reducing missed arrhythmias by 74.5% compared to the standalone LSTM–AE baseline while maintaining a clinically acceptable False Positive Rate of 3.85%. The core detectors are trained without labeled data; only threshold calibration and recovery configuration use a small validation subset offline. Computationally, the framework operates at 7.93 ms per window with a throughput of 3,697 windows/s and a compact 350–400 KB footprint, making it well–suited for real–time, resource–constrained IoMT deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Han M.; Li J.; Xu L.
Title: MT-MNER: A multimodal named entity recognition model based on multi-view contrastive learning and two-stage feature fusion
Abstract: Multimodal Named Entity Recognition (MNER) is essential for extracting structured information from unstructured data, yet it faces challenges including insufficient coordination between multimodal alignment and fusion, as well as the difficulty of balancing fusion precision and information integrity in multi-granularity information integration. To address these challenges, We propose MT-MNER, an innovative model based on multi-view contrastive learning and two-stage feature fusion. Specifically, MT-MNER introduces a multi-view contrastive learning strategy that performs dual-granularity alignment: at the coarse-grained level, it aligns textual features with global visual features to unify the two semantic spaces. At the fine-grained level, it adopts a ranking-based contrastive learning strategy to promote fine-grained semantic alignment by prioritizing candidate image patches with higher semantic relevance to textual tokens. To further deepen cross-modal interaction, we design a two-stage feature fusion mechanism that incorporates a hierarchical feature fusion module and a global feature fusion module. This two-stage approach progressively integrates local visual cues with global semantic information, thereby ensuring precise entity detection. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that MT-MNER achieves micro F1 scores of 77.03%, 81.06%, and 92.06%, respectively, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. These results validate MT-MNER as a robust and efficient paradigm for MNER in complex scenarios. The main code is available at: https://github.com/Shy0418/MT-MNER.git . Copyright © 2026. Authors: Shen X.; Liu S.; Zhang Y.
Title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. Tourism demand is highly sensitive to external stimuli, often leading to abrupt and irregular fluctuations that are difficult to quantify using existing methods. To address this issue, we propose an event-aware dynamic spatiotemporal network (EAD-STN) that integrates large language model embeddings with dynamic spatiotemporal graph modeling. External factors are encoded into high-dimensional representations to capture their impacts on visitor demand. The model further incorporates both dynamic spatial adjacency and LLM-derived semantic adjacency among attractions, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of inter-attraction relationships. Experiments on real-world datasets from Beijing and Shanghai demonstrate that EAD-STN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. By leveraging large language models to quantify complex external influences and semantic relationships, this framework provides a new perspective for improving the accuracy and interpretability of tourism flow forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bisht A.
Title: Silent Valleys: Unraveling the Causes and Strategic Pathways for Reverse Migration in Hilly Regions of Uttarakhand
Abstract: This study examines out-migration and the prospects for sustainable reverse migration in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand, addressing three objectives: identifying the main drivers of migration, synthesizing reinforcement strategies to reduce distress migration and support return, and linking causes and responses within a human-environment systems perspective. We conducted a scoping review of 68 studies (2010–2025) using a structured screening and synthesis process. Findings show that migration results from interacting economic, infrastructural, geographical, policy, and social pressures rather than a single employment factor, with reinforcing feedback effects such as land abandonment, declining agricultural viability, weakened local services, and heightened human-wildlife conflict that can intensify future migration. Title: NOVEL INSECTICIDES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF LIVE WOOD EATING TERMITES IN TEA PLANTATIONS OF ASSAM
Abstract: Studies were undertaken to evaluate the efficacy of six insecticides having newer chemistry against termites infesting tea plantations in Assam, India during 2020-21 and 2021-22. Title: Experimental study on high-pressure constant-volume combustion of ultra-lean methane-air mixtures under different ignition delay times
Abstract: Low-concentration coal mine gas is typically characterized by low combustion rate and significant heat losses. Studies on ultra-lean methane-air combustion under high-pressure constant-volume and turbulent conditions remain limited. This study experimentally investigates turbulent combustion characteristics and heat losses under elevated initial pressures, where turbulence intensity is regulated by adjusting the ignition delay time t d. Results reveal that varying t d non–monotonically affects both flame development and rapid combustion stages. While turbulence plays a primary role in shortening the rapid combustion duration, its intensification does not monotonically reduce heat losses, since the flow field influences both the convective heat transfer coefficient and the temperature difference between combustion products and chamber walls. At t d = 1 s, weak turbulence attenuates the promoting effect of temperature rise on flame development, with the most pronounced effect observed at P 0 = 0.5 MPa and 0.7 MPa. Further turbulence intensification yields a greater reduction in combustion duration than that resulting from the combined effect of temperature rise and weak turbulence. Within initial pressures of 0.3–0.7 MPa, the coupled effects of temperature rise and turbulence reduce the combustion duration by 20.6%–54.0% and increase P max by 10.3%–19.2% relative to quiescent combustion. An initial pressure of 0.6 MPa is found to minimize heat losses for the 6 vol% methane–air mixture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mapping the intellectual structure of digital transformation research in SMEs: A decade of performance-oriented studies
Abstract: Despite their vital contribution to worldwide economic progress, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vulnerable to environmental fluctuations, resource limitations, and swift technological shifts. In this context, digital transformation has emerged as a critical strategic mechanism through which firms seek to enhance competitiveness, resilience, and organizational outcomes. Although this topic has attracted considerable scholarly attention in recent years, the available literature is dispersed across different academic fields, theoretical viewpoints, and methodologies, making it difficult to gain a holistic understanding of the area's intellectual organization and progression. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to examine digital transformation and firm-level outcomes in small business contexts from January 2016 to January 2026. Bibliographic data were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix through its Biblioshiny interface and VOSviewer. A final dataset of 186 peer-reviewed journal articles was examined using descriptive statistics, keyword co-occurrence analysis, bibliographic coupling, citation analysis, thematic mapping, and research trend analysis. The results indicate a strong and accelerating publication trend, with an annual growth rate of 17.46, particularly since 2020, highlighting the increasing strategic importance of digital technologies in response to economic disruptions and uncertainty. The analysis identifies four major thematic clusters: (1) performance-oriented outcomes, (2) technology - and capability-driven transformation, (3) organizational and sustainability-related performance, and (4) strategic and Industry 4.0-oriented transformation. In addition, emerging themes include digital readiness, dynamic capabilities, and business model innovation. While the literature frequently associates digital transformation with improved organizational outcomes, the findings also reveal persistent heterogeneity in results and highlight substantial risks and failure rates, especially among resource-constrained firms. By mapping the intellectual foundations, thematic structure, and evolution of this research domain, the study provides an integrative overview that supports theory development and informs future empirical research. The results also offer valuable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers who seek to understand and guide digital transformation initiatives in small business contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing.
