Authors: Ramkumar J.; Anand K.; Ramesh A.
Title: Development and experimental analysis of a novel impulse turbine compounded naturally aspirated High-Speed diesel engine
Abstract: Despite decades of research and development proving the technical advantages of turbocharging, several gasoline and diesel engines, especially the single-cylinder engines, remain naturally aspirated. Commercially available single-cylinder engines are rarely turbocharged due to inherent technical challenges and cost-to-performance trade-offs. The pulsating exhaust flow typical of single-cylinder engines causes efficiency losses in conventional turbocharger reaction turbines, which are designed for steady or near-continuous exhaust flow. Thus, the benefits of charging and exhaust energy recovery are not realised in many engines, especially single-cylinder engines. Even in the case of two-cylinder and three-cylinder engines, the benefit of charging is not fully realised, as adapting a turbocharger to these engines involves several compromises in energy extraction by the turbine due to the pulsated exhaust flow, in matching the turbine and the compressor, and in matching the turbine and the engine. Consequently, the best-suited compressor or the most effective turbine is not designed individually for these engines, since matching both to the engine compromises the system’s effectiveness. Thus, commercially available single-cylinder engines are rarely turbocharged, supercharged, or turbo-compounded. Therefore, neither the advantage of charging is realised nor the potential for exhaust energy recovery is capitalised, leaving these engines underutilised and underperforming despite their potential. In this work, a novel impulse turbine capable of extracting work from the pulsating exhaust flow typical of a single-cylinder engine was designed and developed for a commercially available single-cylinder diesel engine, based on simulations and theoretical calculations. Furthermore, a turbocompounding layout was developed to adapt the novel impulse turbine for the single-cylinder engine. Subsequently, an experimental analysis was conducted to evaluate the performance of the impulse turbine. Experimental results showed that the impulse turbine delivered 1.2 kW of power at 3000 rpm, increasing the naturally aspirated (NA) engine brake power output by 12 %. The turbine efficiency was about 80 %, and the net brake power output of the NA engine with the impulse turbine was 11.5 kW at 3000 rpm. The present study demonstrates the potential to improve the performance of single-cylinder engines by effectively extracting thermal energy from exhaust gas through impulse turbo-compounding. Author full names: Stephens, Melodena (55377683300); Kothari, Tanvi (8679142800); Khurshid, Sadaf (59957959300)
Title: International scaling of social innovations through digitalization: A 3D framework
Abstract: Social enterprises that embed social innovations (SIs) play a critical role in advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), representing an estimated US$12 trillion market opportunity. Yet, how SIs internationalize in the presence of institutional voids remains underexplored in international business research. Using a history-to-theory and history-in-theory approach, this study examines how dynamic capabilities and digitalization enable the international scaling of SIs. We find that international diffusion depends on capabilities such as boundary spanning, international sensing, legitimacy building, business diplomacy, and market shaping. Digitalization accelerates scaling, contingent on factors including timing, resources, intellectual property ownership, purpose, and technology scope. Our findings also suggest that traditional internationalization metrics—such as exports, FDI, subsidiaries, and foreign sales—do not adequately capture SI internationalization. Instead, internationalization is reflected in the cross-border diffusion of innovations and social impact, alongside the ability to attract international funding, partnerships, talent, and legitimacy while balancing social impact with financial sustainability. Title: An integrated framework for total nitrogen load allocation and multidimensional assessment reconciling equity and environmental efficiency in large river basins
Abstract: Total nitrogen (TN) load governance is crucial for safeguarding river and nearshore water environments. However, translating basin reduction goals into equitable and efficient spatial targets remains challenging due to socioeconomic, hydrological, and biogeochemical heterogeneities. This study develops an integrated framework coupling process-based water quality modelling (SWAT) with Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) to reconcile environmental efficiency with regional equity. Applying this framework to the Liao River Basin in China, this study generated multiple allocation schemes reflecting different socioeconomic priorities and evaluated their performance across TN compliance, abatement costs, food production, and social equality. Results show that under the 30% reduction target, schemes integrating efficiency reduced total basin abatement costs by 0.1%–6.5% and increased crop yields by 0.4%–2.4% relative to the equity-only scheme, although they widened regional disparities in economic and livelihood burdens. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the economic advantages of efficiency-integrated schemes weaken under the 40% reduction target due to nonlinearly escalating marginal abatement costs, and remain sensitive to source allocation within individual catchments. The scheme performance assessment accounting for multiple uncertainties reveals that the optimal schemes depend on the total reduction target and specific policy priorities, including objective weighting and policy-weighted scenarios prioritizing food security, cost control, or social equality. Ultimately, this framework explicitly quantifies multidimensional tradeoffs and provides a practical basis for formulating load management strategies across varying reduction targets and policy priorities. © 2026

Title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce student anxiety during the transition to middle school

Abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of a school-based intervention to reduce anxiety and related impairment during the transition to middle school. Thirty-eight students were randomly assigned to receive the Transitioning Emotionally and Academically to Middle School Successfully (TEAMSS, n = 20) program, a group cognitive behavioral intervention, or Enhanced Usual Care (EUC, n = 18), a study generated resource list and usual school counseling. Students (mean age 10.4; 85.7% White; 50% female) had elevated anxiety symptoms and/or a primary anxiety disorder. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed via recruitment, retention, attendance, intervention satisfaction, and intervention adherence. Exploratory student outcomes of anxiety and constructs targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., behavioral avoidance, academic organizational and social skills) were assessed at post intervention (10 weeks after the initiation of treatment) and at the end of the academic year (follow-up). Results revealed student recruitment challenges; enrolled participants found the intervention acceptable and helpful. Student attendance at the group meetings was high. Clinician adherence to the intervention indicated room for improvement. At post and follow-up assessments, students in both groups showed significant reductions in anxiety and improvements in functioning, but there were few statistically significant between-group differences. Within group effect sizes were medium to large and favored TEAMSS on several measures assessing changes in areas targeted in TEAMSS (e.g., maladaptive cognitions, social skills); however, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the overall absence of group differences on most measures. Authors: Zhao X.; Liu J.; Wang S.; Chen N.; Zhao J.; Zhang Y.; Li J.; Li H.; Li N.; Yang Q.
Title: Ginsenoside compound K inhibits complement C1qA/C3-CR3-mediated microglial synaptic pruning and neuronal pyroptosis
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Ginseng (Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer), a classic traditional Chinese medicine, has long been used for “calming the mind and enhancing intelligence” to combat cognitive decline. Its major metabolite, ginsenoside compound K (CK), exerts neuroprotection, but the molecular mechanisms against Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. Aim of the study: This study investigated the molecular mechanism by which CK attenuates microglial aberrant synaptic phagocytosis and neuronal pyroptosis via inhibiting the complement C1qA cascade. Materials and methods: APP/PS1 mice were used as AD models and treated with CK (20 or 40 mg/kg/d) or memantine (MH, 3 mg/kg/d) by gavage once daily for 14 weeks. Morris water maze and open field tests were used to assess cognitive function and anxiety-like behavior, respectively. HE, Nissl and Golgi staining detected neuronal damage and synaptic integrity. Immunofluorescence and ELISA measured microglial polarization, activation and synaptic phagocytosis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations analyzed the CK-C1qA interaction. Western blot, immunofluorescence and ELISA detected complement components (C1qA, C3, CR3) and pyroptosis-related proteins (NF-κB, NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-18). In vitro cellular experiments, including BV2 cell monoculture and BV2-HT22 transwell co-culture systems, were further performed to validate the causal role of C1qA. Results: CK improved cognitive and anxiety behaviors in APP/PS1 mice, attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage, increased Nissl-positive neurons, restored dendritic complexity and spine density, and upregulated PSD95 and SYP. CK induced microglial M1-like-to-M2-like polarization and reduced Iba1+/CD68+ microglia colocalization with PSD95+ synapses, indicating suppressed synaptic engulfment. CK was predicted to bind to the C1qA globular head domain, reduced C1qA deposition at synapses, inhibited C3, and CR3 expression, suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation, downregulated NLRP3, ASC, cleaved-caspase-1, and GSDMD-N, decreased IL-18 release, and alleviated neuronal pyroptosis. In vitro, CK suppressed C1qA expression in BV2 cells and reduced synaptic C1qA deposition in HT22 cells. Conclusion: CK ameliorated cognitive and synaptic deficits in APP/PS1 mice by inhibiting the C1qA/C3-CR3 pathway to suppress aberrant microglial synaptic phagocytosis and blocking NF-κB/NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated neuronal pyroptosis. These findings elucidate CK's neuroprotective mechanisms and provide scientific evidence for ginseng's traditional cognitive benefits. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Research trends and conceptual foundations of religious moderation: A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Although the concept of religious moderation has received increasing scholarly attention in recent years, comprehensive and globally integrative syntheses remain limited. In many Western scholarly traditions, similar ideas are often articulated through related concepts such as religious tolerance, pluralism, liberal pluralism, or collaborative secularism, resulting in fragmented conceptual discussions across disciplines and regions. This study therefore aims to map the development, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of research on religious moderation within global academic discourse. This study employs a hybrid approach combining Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database, where the keyword “religious moderation” was searched in article titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search identified 901 publications (2009–2026). After applying the PRISMA screening procedure, 235 articles met the inclusion criteria and were selected for analysis. Bibliometric mapping was conducted using VOSviewer to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, institutional affiliations, and thematic patterns within the field. The findings indicate that research on religious moderation has experienced gradual growth and increasing global visibility. However, the distribution of scholarly contributions remains highly concentrated in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia and Malaysia, suggesting that the concept has not yet diffused widely across Western, Middle Eastern, and African academic traditions. This geographical concentration reveals significant opportunities for comparative, cross-cultural, and interdisciplinary research. This study also, through an analysis of 235 articles indexed in Scopus, found several studies on the indicators and principles of religious moderation, which play an important role in fostering harmony amid social differences and diversity. In addition, the study proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework linking religious moderation to broader domains including social cohesion, conflict resolution, interfaith relations, family dynamics, and education, highlighting its relevance for sustaining inclusive and resilient communities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Biological effects of ionizing radiation combined with extremely low frequency magnetic fields among occupationally exposed X-ray technicians
Abstract: The human body is susceptible to ionizing radiation penetration resulting in cancer and other adverse health outcomes. One potent ionizing radiation source that has uses in medicine is X-rays. Globally, about 2.3 million and in Pakistan about 26,046 registered medical technicians are exposed to X-rays. Along with X-rays, these X-ray technicians are also potentially exposed to extremely low frequency magnetic field (ELF MF) from X-ray machines and other electrical devices. This study investigated the individual and combined effects of X-rays and ELF MF in the form of molecular mechanism including disruption of antioxidant enzyme activities, generation of reactive oxygen species, and the DNA damage. A total of 250 healthy workers were enrolled in this study; divided into ionizing radiation exposed and un-exposed groups. Along with exposure to ionizing radiation and ELF MF, information about exposure to potential confounding factors and effect modifiers was also collected. The results showed a statistically significant increased risk of DNA damage in the X-ray exposed group 20.3 ± 11.2 compared to un-exposed group 10.3 ± 5.85, p < 0.001. Also, antioxidant enzymes activities were statistically significantly higher in the exposed group Vs. un-exposed group for CAT: 12.1 ± 4.53 Vs. 9.67 ± 4.99; p < 0.001 and MDA: 9.36 ± 6.55 Vs. 5.92 ± 4.58; p < 0.001. However, the increase for SOD was not statistically significant (7.75 ± 5.58 Vs. 7.45 ± 4.83; p= 0.648). The combined exposure of ionizing radiation and ELF MF (≥0.4 μT) increased the impact for DNA damage only where changes in all the antioxidant enzymes were not meaningful. The age was statistically significantly associated with DNA damage and SOD activity. Also, the risk increased with dose-response (duration of employment) and highest DNA damage was observed in workers with work experience of ≥10 years. The study findings are useful in reporting the adverse health effects of exposure to occupational X-rays radiation and also in educating the laboratory technicians about the potentially harmful parts of their work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Meng S.; Zheng H.; Pu A.; Yan X.; Wei J.
Title: Multi-scenario CTR prediction with LLM-augmented semantic graphs and anti-polarization experts
Abstract: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction is a core task in recommendation systems. However, existing multimodal CTR methods still rely heavily on interaction-driven graphs, which are often too sparse to capture deeper semantic relations between users. To address this limitation, we propose APEX-GraphMoE, a unified framework centered on LLM-enhanced LightGCN (LLN). LLN introduces an LLM-as-graph-builder paradigm, in which fine-tuned large language models aggregate multimodal user behaviors and construct semantic user–user edges to enrich the graph beyond explicit interactions. Building on this core paradigm, we further introduce HUBM and APG to address two additional challenges caused by strong semantic graph signals. HUBM performs task-aware multimodal refinement to preserve the contribution of image and text features during downstream optimization, while APG stabilizes adaptive routing in MMoE and alleviates expert polarization. Experiments on the large-scale AntM2 C dataset, containing approximately 10 million samples across five scenarios, show that APEX-GraphMoE improves AUC by 2.89% and reduces expert-usage variance by 50.21% over strong baselines.We further conduct auxiliary validation on MM-CTR1 M to provide preliminary cross-dataset evidence, while keeping AntM2 C as the primary benchmark. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of LLN as the core source of semantic topology enhancement, with HUBM and APG serving as complementary supporting mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Li Z.; Ma M.; Yavuz M.
Title: Reservation-based intersection scheduling using dynamic programming with dominance pruning
Abstract: Scheduling connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) at reservation-based intersections faces a fundamental trade-off: existing methods sacrifice either optimality for computational efficiency or real-time applicability for optimal solutions. We bridge this gap by proposing a dynamic programming (DP) algorithm with dominance pruning ((Formula presented.)) that simultaneously achieves optimal batch formation, polynomial-time complexity, and superior solution quality. (Formula presented.) introduces a novel dominance rule that eliminates suboptimal child nodes by comparing analytically derived lower bounds, enabling batch-based processing of CAVs while guaranteeing optimality. Unlike existing approaches that assume predetermined batches or sacrifice optimality, (Formula presented.) integrates optimal batching decisions directly into the scheduling algorithm. The proposed method achieves a substantial improvement over existing exact algorithms with (Formula presented.) worst-case and (Formula presented.) best-case time complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that (Formula presented.) reduces computation time by 91% and 99% compared to a state-of-the-art DP algorithm and Gurobi solver, respectively, while consistently delivering superior performance in makespan, average delay, and maximum delay metrics across diverse traffic scenarios. Furthermore, (Formula presented.) outperforms heuristic algorithms in achieving better solution quality and comparative computational efficiency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that (Formula presented.) ’s dominance rule remains effective across varying mean headways, CAV counts, and batch proportions, with performance benefits extending beyond simple batch processing to complex traffic patterns. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Authors: Gao G.; Wang H.; Gan L.; Wei J.; Bi R.; Bi B.
Title: Effects of black soldier fly larvae meal on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis): Insights from non-targeted metabolomics
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: To investigate the effects of replacing fishmeal (FM) with black soldier fly larvae meal (BSFLM) on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis), six isonitrogenous and isoenergetic diets were formulated with graded replacement levels of 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% and fed to fish for 8 weeks. Intestinal antioxidant parameters, serum immune factors, hepatic free amino acids, and non-targeted hepatic metabolomics were analyzed. No significant differences were observed among groups in intestinal superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutaredoxin (GSH-PX), total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), or malondialdehyde (MDA) (ANOVA, all P > 0.05). Serum interleukin-10 (IL-10) showed a significant linear increase with increasing BSFLM inclusion (P = 0.021), indicating dose-dependent anti-inflammatory immunomodulation. Hepatic free amino acid profiling revealed that ornithine decreased significantly with increasing replacement (P = 0.012), S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) peaked in the H50 group (36.59 vs. 24.00 in H0, P = 0.006), proline decreased significantly (P = 0.030), taurine and cysteine were significantly elevated in the H50 group (P = 0.007 and 0.022, respectively), and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) declined significantly (P = 0.004). Non-targeted metabolomics revealed a three-phase metabolic trajectory: 10–20% replacement represented an adaptation phase characterized by decoupling of central nitrogen metabolism from anabolism; 30% constituted a transition phase with synergistic integration of energy metabolism, carbohydrate utilization, and glucuronidation detoxification; 40–50% represented a stress/dysregulation phase, marked by a coordinated stress module containing norepinephrine and pyroglutamic acid, with 2-furoic acid emerging as a potential stress biomarker at 50% inclusion. The number of differentially abundant metabolites increased from 7 in the H10 group to over 60 in the H50 group. KEGG pathway enrichment confirmed activation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis at low levels, while high levels enriched oxidative stress-related pathways including glutathione metabolism, ferroptosis, and ABC transporters. Collectively, these findings indicate that BSFLM replacement should not exceed 30% in juvenile southern catfish diets to balance sustainable protein utilization with maintenance of metabolic homeostasis and overall health. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Liu X.; Tian M.; Dong Z.; Ou X.; Shi F.; Lai J.
Title: Risk-based collaborative planning for cyber–physical–social distribution systems against extreme weather
Abstract: Extreme weather can simultaneously damage distribution lines and communication facilities, weakening coordinated resource operation and increasing load-shedding risk. Such disruptions are particularly consequential in cyber–physical–social systems (CPSS) supporting distribution system operation, where power delivery depends on cyber connectivity and prosumer participation. To address this interdependence, a risk-based collaborative planning framework traces fragility-based failures through communication service to prosumer market access and adaptive post-event operation. Within this framework, peer-to-peer (P2P) trading serves as a communication-dependent mechanism for energy exchange among accessible prosumers rather than as an independent planning objective. A two-stage mean–CVaR model coordinates the distribution system operator’s (DSO) investment in communication backup and active-power transfer capacity with prosumer investment in renewable generation and energy storage. As cyber–physical conditions deteriorate, the model shifts from grid-connected coordination to communication-supported island operation and ultimately to local self-supply. A nested progressive hedging and alternating direction method of multipliers (PH-ADMM) algorithm coordinates scenario decisions and the interfaces between the DSO and prosumers. Studies on modified IEEE 33-node and 123-node systems show that communication survivability materially affects investment decisions and feasible post-event energy coordination. The framework provides a scalable basis for resilience-oriented collaborative planning in communication-dependent distribution systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Fang L.; Liu H.; Tong B.; Zhao Y.; Gan X.; He C.
Title: Toward intelligent safety science: a paradigm-oriented framework for AI-enabled reconstruction of safety theories and models
Abstract: Modern socio-technical systems are increasingly interconnected, dynamic, and uncertain, which challenges safety research that relies mainly on retrospective accident explanation. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied to risk identification, fault diagnosis, early warning, and decision support, its role in safety research is still often fragmented and limited to tool enhancement. This paper proposes Intelligent Safety Science (ISS) as a paradigm-oriented framework for organizing AI-enabled safety research. The framework aims to explain how AI can help extend classical safety theories from post-accident analysis toward earlier understanding and management of evolving risks. To develop this framework, the paper identifies three AI-enabled extension paths for classical safety theories: dynamic upgrading, real-time enhancement, and proactive transformation. It then abstracts a Perception-Reasoning-Decision-Intervention (PRDI) structure as a conceptual-methodological framework for linking risk observation, risk analysis, safety response, and feedback. Based on PRDI, ISS is characterized by four capability dimensions—predictability, holism, adaptability, and generativity—and four supporting elements: data, model, knowledge, and interaction. Scenario-based analyses of complex industrial systems, urban critical infrastructure, and human-machine collaborative environments further illustrate how ISS can be adapted to different sectoral conditions. This study provides a theoretical framework for clarifying the role of AI in safety science and offers a basis for future empirical research on intelligent safety systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Y.; Nie L.
Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of an age-space structured epidemic model with partial immunity, nonlinear infection rate, and combined transmission pathways from hosts and environment
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: To account for the complex challenges of spatial heterogeneity, inevitable human mobility, and dual transmission pathways (human-to-human and environment-to-human) in epidemic dynamics, we propose a novel age-space structured model incorporating partial immunity and nonlinear incidence. The model explicitly includes the infection age structure of both infected individuals and environmental pathogens to capture variations in infectivity during the transmission process. First, the well-posedness of the model solution is rigorously established using the Banach fixed-point theorem. Next, by applying the Laplace transform, we derive the next-generation operator L, then the basic reproduction number is defined as its spectral radius. Furthermore, under a spatially homogeneous scenario, R0 is obtained in exact analytical form. The global asymptotic stability of the disease-free and endemic steady states is then established by analyzing the distribution of the roots of the characteristic equations and constructing appropriate Lyapunov functionals. Numerical simulations visually elucidate complex spatio-temporal-age dynamics and quantify the effectiveness of interventions. In particular, restricting the mobility of infected individuals and improving vaccine efficacy significantly curb transmission. Fitting to cholera case data from Somalia, we find that neglecting either age structure or spatial heterogeneity leads to significant biases in case number estimates, underscoring their indispensable role in accurate forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Shiny by Design: Establishing Diagnostic Criteria for Intentional Burnishing on Prehistoric Bone Artifacts
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The identification of intentional burnishing on prehistoric osseous artifacts remains a persistent methodological challenge. Bone surfaces are highly reactive and readily record microwear traces but are susceptible to taphonomic alteration. This study investigates how the use of different burnishing materials affects the morphology of bone surfaces and the formation of diagnostic microwear traces to develop a methodologically grounded classification for identifying intentionally burnished surfaces on archeological osseous artifacts. Experimental observations are evaluated in relation to existing knowledge of use-related, manufacturing, and postdepositional surface modifications. The analysis is based on a microwear framework that integrates multiscalar observations (low- and high-magnification microscopy and scanning electron microscopy) with quantitative three-dimensional surface texture analysis. Both microscopy and quantitative data derived from confocal microscopy reveal clear differences among bones burnished with different agents, highlighting agent-specific topographic patterns. The experimentally derived reference dataset was subsequently applied during microwear analysis of selected prehistoric bone points from Lake Lubāns (Latvia) and the Wiele 33 site (Poland) to assess the analytical applicability of the proposed protocol. The results of our study demonstrate the diagnostic potential of the created classification of wear traces to distinguish intentional burnishing on archaeological osseous artifacts and to discriminate between intentional, use-related, and taphonomic surface modifications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A dual-process motivational approach to understanding antisemitism: The role of authoritarianism, social dominance orientation, and conspiracy mentality
Abstract: Antisemitism remains a persistent challenge in contemporary societies, yet its psychological underpinnings are not well understood. Building on the dual-process motivational (DPM) model of ideology and prejudice, this study examined the extent to which antisemitism is rooted in broader ideological dispositions - right-wing authoritarianism (RWA), social dominance orientation (SDO), and conspiracy mentality. Using a nationwide online survey of German adults ( N = 457), bivariate and multivariate analyses indicate that conspiracy mentality is the strongest correlate of antisemitic attitudes, followed by individual differences in SDO. These findings support the view that antisemitism is embedded within a broader ideological belief system characterized by anti-egalitarian and conspiratorial worldviews. The role of conspiratorial worldviews as a potential distinct motivational pathway to prejudice within the DPM model is discussed. © 2026 The Author.

Title: Artificial intelligence systems distort upstream selection in human social learning
Abstract: Humans are social learners who depend on observing others to acquire knowledge, norms, and behaviors, a capacity that underlies cumulative cultural evolution. Social learning unfolds in two stages: upstream selection determines what information becomes visible, and downstream selection determines what learners copy from that visible sample. Downstream selection occurs through biases such as conformity bias (copying what appears common) and prestige bias (copying those who appear highly respected). These downstream biases can be adaptive when upstream selection yields a sample that reflects the population's true distribution, so that what appears common is actually common and those who appear respected are actually competent. We argue that digital technologies disrupt this condition, creating an upstream selection problem. Engagement-based algorithms amplify the tails of the distribution, surfacing rare and extreme content, whereas generative AI collapses it toward the mode (of the population or the user), erasing the surrounding diversity. Crucially, in each system the optimization signal shapes both visibility and prestige. For engagement-based algorithms, the signal is engagement: creators who post extreme content become more visible and, through the likes, shares, and followers, appear more prestigious. For generative AI, the signal is statistical typicality: it makes a modal answer dominant and, with no alternatives shown, makes the model that produced it appear more prestigious. These distortions can give rise to emergent group-level phenomena, including pluralistic ignorance and illusory consensus. Synthesizing evidence across psychology, cultural evolution, and computational social science, we provide a framework for how digital technologies disrupt social learning and outline interventions for restoring functional cultural transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Wang Z.Q.; Li X.T.; Yan J.X.; Qu Z.; Zhang Z.J.; Zhang P.; Zhang Z.F.
Title: Overcoming the strength–ductility trade-off of chemically complex alloys via local chemical fluctuations
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Tailoring the ordered structures within chemically complex alloys (CCAs), represents an effective strategy for addressing the strength-ductility trade-off dilemma in conventional metals, such as steels, aluminum alloys, and titanium alloys. In this study, a novel strategy is proposed in a CoCrNiAl dual-phase CCA, where prolonged low-temperature annealing is utilized to tailor local chemical fluctuations (LCF). This process promotes enhanced ordering degree of the matrix, resulting in an enhancement in strength without loss of uniform elongation. Comprehensive microstructural analysis reveals that LCF modulates dislocation activity and deformation mechanisms by altering local energy fluctuations (LEF). Specifically, the enhancement of atomic ordering increases the antiphase boundary (APB) energy, thereby increasing the resistance to dislocation glide. Meanwhile, elemental segregation reduces the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the matrix, enhancing its work-hardening capacity. These novel findings provide deeper insight into the influence of ordered structures on both the strength and work-hardening capacity of face-centered cubic CCAs at room temperature. © 2026

Title: More alike than unalike: Contextually aligned authority arguments amplify sustainable choices across cultures
Abstract: Most research is conducted in Western societies, with few studies from Latin America. This oversight has led to a narrow understanding of the effectiveness that various sustainability-oriented interventions have in countries with different cultural values. As consumers play a vital role in mitigating climate change issues, this behavioral field experiment investigates whether reliance on the authority and commitment-consistency principles from social influence increases individuals' inclination to choose sustainably, and whether the effectiveness of these principles is culturally contingent. Participants from Ecuador and Norway (N = 346) were randomized to one of three conditions (control vs. authority vs. commitment-consistency), with the latter two conditions containing a message tailored to its associated social influence principle. After replying to some survey items, participants made a choice between a more (vs. less) sustainable option. A chi-square test revealed that both social influence conditions jointly boosted choice likelihood of the more sustainable option relative to the control condition, supporting our initial preregistered hypothesis. However, contrary to our second preregistered hypothesis, a regression-based simple moderation analysis using the PROCESS macro (Model 1) showed no country moderation in the effectiveness of these social influence principles; instead, the results were largely attributable to the authority condition alone, which was considerably more effective than both other conditions across countries, regardless of participants' trust in authorities and their need for consistency. Our findings demonstrate the superiority of contextually aligned authority arguments as a viable way to foster pro-environmental behaviors. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Li Y.; Chen R.; Tran K.T.
Title: 2D time-domain SH-wave full-waveform inversion for geotechnical site characterization: a practical comparison of optimization strategies
Abstract: Engineering-geological site investigation requires reliable identification of shallow subsurface structures, interfaces, and weak zones, whereas conventional methods such as boreholes and coring remain spatially discrete. Two-dimensional time-domain SH-wave full-waveform inversion (SH-FWI) provides a nondestructive, in situ, and spatially continuous approach for recovering shear-wave velocity (Vs) and density, two parameters directly relevant to engineering-geological interpretation. This study presents a practical evaluation of steepest descent (SD), L-BFGS, and Gauss–Newton (GN) within a unified 2D time-domain SH-FWI framework, focusing on their effects on Vs and density recovery using one synthetic model and two representative engineering-geological field cases with contrasting near-surface conditions. In the field cases, the inversion-derived density results are quantitatively compared with laboratory-measured borehole core densities through depth-dependent and layer-wise statistical analyses, thereby providing practical evidence for assessing the applicability of different optimization strategies in engineering-geological site characterization. The results show that all three methods can recover the main engineering-geological framework, including shallow hard layers, weathered limestone transitions, localized weak intervals, and competent bedrock. GN provides the highest inversion resolution and fastest convergence but at substantially greater computational cost and memory demand. SD serves as a stable first-order baseline but tends to produce smoother models and slower convergence. L-BFGS provides a practical compromise among inversion reliability, borehole-density consistency, and computational affordability under the tested field conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate that SH-FWI can provide useful and spatially continuous information for shallow engineering-geological characterization, and the recovered Vs and density models can further support the derivation of stiffness-related parameters for subsequent engineering-geological analysis and application. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Transparent and mechanically robust fish gelatin hydrogels through covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation by dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers
Abstract: Polysaccharide reinforcement enhances the mechanical strength of fish gelatin (FG), narrowing its performance gap with mammalian gelatins (bovine and porcine gelatins). However, the improved mechanical strength is often accompanied by reduced optical transparency due to interfacial incompatibility-induced aggregation, phase separation, and light scattering. Herein, a covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation strategy based on dialdehyde carboxymethyl chitin nanofibers (dCMCh-NF) was developed to optimize protein–polysaccharide interactions in FG hydrogels. At a low loading of 0.1 wt%, dCMCh-NF effectively reinforced the FG network. The FG/dCMCh8-NF hydrogel exhibited a hardness of 695.52 ± 4.51 g, significantly higher than that of pure FG (497.30 ± 19.19 g) and comparable to that of mammalian gelatin. Meanwhile, its light transmittance reached 85.70 ± 1.32%, markedly exceeding that of FG/CMCh-NF (71.37 ± 0.47%). Structural characterization and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that aldehyde groups on dCMCh-NF formed Schiff-base linkages with FG as the primary interaction, while hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions served as secondary stabilizing forces. This dual crosslinking suppressed local aggregation, reduced phase separation, and facilitated the formation of a homogeneous and compact network, thereby minimizing light scattering. This work establishes covalent–noncovalent interfacial regulation as an effective strategy for overcoming the inherent transparency-strength trade-off in polysaccharide-reinforced FG hydrogels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A novel strategy for high conductivity and dimensional stability sulfonated polyimide proton exchange membranes for direct methanol fuel cells
Abstract: The trade-off between proton conductivity and dimensional stability of sulfonated polyimide (SPI) proton exchange membranes (PEMs) greatly limits their practical application in direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs). Herein, a strategy for regulating the proton conductivity and dimensional stability of copolymer membranes through the coupled regulation of the degree of sulfonation (DS) and fractional free volume (FFV) is proposed. By introducing bulky fluorene groups as side chains to regulate the FFV, a series of SPI PEMs with different DS and FFV were prepared. It is found that an appropriate balance between DS and FFV is critical for achieving high proton conductivity and dimensional stability. In particular, the BSPI-50 membrane achieves a proton conductivity of 113 mS·cm−1 at 80 ℃ while maintaining a low swelling ratio of 35.2 %. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that FFV can be tuned by adjusting the content of fluorene units, as increased side-group content weakens intermolecular interactions between polymer chains. An appropriate balance between DS and FFV facilitates the formation of well-connected hydrophilic nanochannels, thereby promoting proton transport while maintaining dimensional stability. The BSPI-50 membrane delivers a peak power density of 72.97 mW·cm−2 in single cells and exhibits durability over 100 h of continuous operation, with a minimal voltage decay rate of 0.7 mV·h−1. This work demonstrates that the combined regulation of DS and FFV provides an effective approach to balancing proton transport and dimensional stability, enabling the development of SPI PEMs with excellent overall performance for DMFCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Pang X.; Chen L.; Mu Y.
Title: Wedge-index based butterfly counting in bipartite graphs
Abstract: Butterfly counting is a key metric in the analysis of bipartite networks. Existing butterfly counting techniques are primarily classified into two categories: layer-priority-based and vertex-priority-based methods. Both approaches compute the number of butterflies in bipartite graphs by enumerating wedges from the neighbor lists of vertices. The state-of-the-art algorithms typically adopt vertex-priority-based techniques, where priorities are assigned to vertices, enabling the enumeration of fewer wedges during the butterfly counting process.In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient wedge-based index for bipartite graphs, referred to as the WB-index (Wedge-based Bipartite Index), designed to accelerate butterfly counting. We introduce two variants of the WB-index based on the two primary butterfly counting principles. By performing a single traversal of the WB-index, we can compute three types of butterfly statistics: the total number of butterflies in the bipartite graph, the number of butterflies for each vertex, and the number of butterflies for each edge. These three computations are implemented by the algorithms BFC-WB, VBFC-WB, and EBFC-WB, respectively. Furthermore, when the bipartite graph undergoes changes, butterfly counting can still be performed efficiently by maintaining the index without the need for reconstruction, especially for medium-scale graphs. Experimental results show that BFC-WB substantially improves butterfly counting efficiency compared with state-of-the-art vertex-priority algorithms, achieving speedups of 66× to 103×. © 2026

Title: Beyond decontamination: Investigating the effect of gamma irradiation on natural dyes in a historical wool carpet
Abstract: This study investigates the viability of gamma irradiation as a treatment process for historical textiles, focusing on the dyes of a 19th–century wool carpet. The effect of irradiation doses (1–10 kGy) on blue-, red-, and yellow-dyed fibers was evaluated by multiple techniques, including colorimetric, spectroscopic, chromatographic, thermal, and morphological analyses along with theoretical calculations. Colorimetric measurements showed that color changes were hardly perceptible (ΔE* < 3) for all samples after 10 kGy irradiation. XRF results indicated that the red and yellow fibers were mordanted with aluminum, whereas the blue dye was applied directly. Dye characterization using the LC-PDA-MS method revealed the presence of indigo carmine in the blue fibers, cochineal in the red fibers, and a mixture of weld and cochineal in the yellow fibers. The irradiation at 10 kGy significantly decreased the extractability of red and yellow color components. As no new peaks corresponding to degradation products were detected in the chromatograms, the reduced extractability was attributed to radiation-induced solid-state molecular reorganization, consistent with the Raman and SEM findings. The thermal characteristics of the dyed fibers were almost unaffected by irradiation. Furthermore, theoretical evaluations of the experimental findings were performed using global reactivity descriptors, charge distributions, and local reactivity regions obtained via optimized geometries, MEP mapping, and Fukui functions, respectively. The findings demonstrate that gamma irradiation up to 10 kGy is a safe treatment for historical wool carpets, causing no significant visual or molecular damage to the color components, while even enhancing the stability of certain dyes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Trustworthy artificial intelligence in advanced manufacturing
Abstract: Additive manufacturing is relying more and more on artificial intelligence for prediction, control, and real-time decisions. Deployment, however, is still difficult. The main reason is that the underlying thermal, flow, and microstructural behavior can shift as the process changes, which makes reliable model performance hard to maintain. This review examines how trustworthy artificial intelligence (TAI) can be used to close that gap in digital twins for additive manufacturing across both metallic and ceramic systems. It frames trustworthiness as a technical condition for deployment and translates it into an AM-specific operational framework. From that point onward, it examines how current workflows handle reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, explainability, robustness, generalizability, fairness, and transparency. A structured evaluation of sixty studies in metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing systems reveals a distinct trend. Robustness and generalizability receive much more attention than transparency, explainability, and fairness. The coverage is also stronger in metallic systems than in ceramic ones. To move beyond binary classification, the review further applies a structured evidence-depth rubric that distinguishes absent coverage, limited or implicit evidence, method-level evidence, and operational evidence for each TAI attribute. We further show that trustworthy deployment depends on more than predictive accuracy. It also depends on physically consistent models as well as updates that account for uncertainty. Decision support has to remain interpretable as well. Model transfer across machines and materials should be treated as controlled adaptation, where reusable physics, sensing, and validation elements are separated from material-specific features that require recalibration. The validation path must also support qualification and industrial deployment, leading to a more cohesive digital twin framework. It brings together physics-based models, reduced-order models, learning-based surrogates, multimodal sensing, and trust-aware evaluation. The main finding is that trustworthiness is the missing technical link between digital twins that can be confidently used in advanced manufacturing and promising AI-enabled demonstrations. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and risk factors of pulmonary tuberculosis in a high-altitude Tibetan region of China from 2018 to 2022: A Bayesian modeling analysis
Abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in high-altitude, resource-limited regions of western China. Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, situated on the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, consistently reports the highest TB notification rates in Sichuan Province, yet fine-scale spatial heterogeneity and localized risk factors remain underexplored. This study aimed to quantify county-level spatiotemporal dynamics of TB and identify associated contextual and individual characteristics of reported TB cases from 2018 to 2022. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 14,768 pulmonary TB cases reported in Ganzi Prefecture from 2018 to 2022. Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model incorporating structured and unstructured spatial effects, a global temporal trend, and county-specific temporal deviations was implemented using the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) framework. County-level covariates were evaluated within a Poisson log-linear structure, while individual characteristics associated with residence in high-risk counties among reported TB cases were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Results The average annual TB notification rates was 251.2 per 100,000 population and increased over the study period. Persistent hotspots were identified in northern areas (e.g., Seda and Shiqu), while elevated risks were also observed in southern counties (e.g., Litang). Seasonal peaks occurred in spring and early autumn. At the ecological level, ultrahigh altitude (≥3500 m; RR = 2.52), higher natural population growth (RR = 1.87), and greater urbanization (RR = 2.03) were associated with increased TB notification rates, whereas greater cropland coverage was inversely associated (RR = 0.84). Among reported TB cases, herdsmen (aOR = 1.72) and children under 14 years (aOR = 2.12) were more likely to reside in high-risk counties. Conclusions Substantial spatial heterogeneity and dynamic temporal variation in TB risk were observed across counties in Ganzi Prefecture. The findings support geographically differentiated TB control strategies and highlight the importance of addressing contextual structural vulnerabilities in high-altitude settings. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Evolution and lifecycle mapping of research methods based on the Boston Matrix in library and information science from 1995 to 2025
Abstract: Developing an evolution framework for research methods is essential for advancing Library and Information Science (LIS), but existing research method schemas remain fragmented and limited. This study proposes an automated framework combining AI-driven methods to mine, classify, and a temporal analysis based on the Boston Matrix to map the lifecycles of research methods. Using a comprehensive dataset of 31,913 articles from 21 LIS journals (1995–2025) as a validation corpus, the framework integrates semantic clustering for bottom-up entity extraction with generative top-down ontology mapping. This approach dynamically maps methods into a four-stage lifecycle schema: mainstream, emerging, marginalized, and mature, revealing distinct evolutionary trajectories and the broader computational turn within LIS. Validated through quantitative threshold testing and qualitative evaluation, the proposed framework significantly reduces manual coding subjectivity and enhances replicability. By empirically comparing the subfields of librarianship and information science, this study accounts for inherent thematic variations and uncovers their distinct paces of methodological adoption. Ultimately, this study offers a robust automated framework for longitudinal methodological tracking, theoretically demonstrating how diverse AI-driven and traditional methods synergistically coevolve and assume distinct scholarly roles within the emerging AI4Science paradigm. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Yuan L.; Zhu J.
Title: The security unlock: How rural social pension makes people more entrepreneurial?
Abstract: Previous literature on the determinants of entrepreneurship has not explored the role of social pension. Leveraging variation in the roll-out timing of a universal rural pension program across Chinese counties, our analysis, at both the individual and aggregate levels, reveals that pension provision led to an increase in entrepreneurship among the younger generation. We show that this effect operates through two primary channels: an intergenerational transfer channel and a local demand channel. Specifically, the pension program mitigates upward transfers from adult children to elderly parents, while boosting local consumer demand, which exerts a demand-side “pull” effect on enterprise establishment. Our findings may shed new light on the interplay between pension, intergenerational resource allocation, and entrepreneurial activity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Sex-divergent vulnerability to chronic peripheral LPS challenge in aged ApoE4 mice: Male systemic fragility versus female central neuroinflammation
Abstract: Inflammageing links chronic inflammation to biological aging, contributing to senescence and multimorbidity common in the elderly. In neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, inflammatory processes play a causal role in accelerating neurodegeneration. Interestingly, apolipoprotein E (APOE), particularly the APOEε4 allele, is a major genetic risk factor for neurodegeneration, acting as a key immunomodulator with sex differences. This is especially relevant given the lack of clear prevention strategies for APOEε4 carriers. Therefore, this study characterized the sex-specific neuroinflammatory and cognitive vulnerability of APOE4 genotype under a chronic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in senescence-transition stage. Male and female homozygous apoE4 mice (15–16 months old) were administered intraperitoneal doses of 0 or 0.25 mg/kg LPS three times per week for a total of 17 doses. Body weight was monitored, and behavioural assessments were conducted from the 12th injection until the 17th. Serum and tissues were collected to assess hippocampal, cortical and systemic markers of inflammation, antioxidant-related genes, genes implied in myelin dynamics, and neurotrophin-related transcripts. Findings revealed basal sex-dependent divergent phenotypes with specific responses under LPS challenge. Under LPS treatment, males exhibited higher systemic fragility, with significantly increased mortality, which may have conditioned cognitive outcomes. Females showed greater central alterations related to neuroinflammation along with altered expression of myelin-related transcripts. However, the results suggest a stablished tolerance to LPS. These results highlight how chronic systemic inflammation during ageing in an APOE4 genotype background shapes sex-divergent pathological trajectories, underscoring the need to address sex-specific therapeutic strategies. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Algorithmic fairness as a human–technology interaction problem
Abstract: Algorithms shape high-stakes decisions across society. While promising efficiency, algorithms also raise fairness concerns. This article proposes that algorithmic fairness is best understood as a human–technology interaction problem rather than a purely technical challenge. Algorithms can reproduce human biases, amplify them through feedback loops, or create new forms of unfairness through objectives, proxies, and seemingly neutral variables. Yet they can make decision processes more explicit, disparities more visible, and actively mitigate discrimination. Fairness depends not only on statistical properties but also on how algorithms are designed, used and experienced by those affected by their decisions. This article therefore offers an interdisciplinary perspective that integrates insights from social justice, psychology, computer science, judgment and decision-making, and management. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Solaja D.; Gustison M.L.
Author full names: Solaja, Dami (58965577200); Gustison, Morgan L. (54941181400)
Title: Structure, functions, and mechanisms of Rodentia vocalizations across the lifespan
Abstract: Vocalizations are an integral way that rodents and many other mammals communicate. Historically, research on rodent vocalizations focused on laboratory-derived strains of two species, house mice (Mus musculus), and brown rats (Rattus norvegicus). However, with over 2000 species, Rodentia is one of the largest vertebrate orders with many species available for communication research. In this review, we synthesize recent findings on lesser-studied species spanning five Rodentia families: Muridae, Caviidae, Cricetidae, Bathyergidae (including Heterocephalidae), and Sciuridae. First, we take an evolutionary perspective to compare adult vocalizations within and across these five Rodentia families. Then, we take a developmental perspective to characterize immature vocalizations and how they transition into mature vocalizations. Next, we explore the potential functions of rodent vocalizations by surveying the behavioural contexts in which they occur. Finally, we summarize recent work on the physiological mechanisms that underpin rodent vocalizations, from biomechanics to neuromodulator systems and neural circuitry. Together, this research shows that Rodentia is an excellent taxonomic group for exploring the diversity and evolution of vertebrate acoustic communication. © 2026 The Authors

Author full names: Jeong, Doyun (60001957800); Min, Seungjae (7202852272)
Title: Multi-material topology optimization of tunable multifunctional microstructures with nonlinear magnetic and thermal fields
Abstract: Multi-material microstructures provide a versatile means for tailoring multiple macroscopic properties beyond those of monolithic materials. Achieving reliable magnetic performance while ensuring efficient heat dissipation is essential for magnetic devices and motivates the concurrent design of magnetic and thermal responses. In this context, multifunctional material systems offer an expanded design space for meeting such combined requirements. However, most existing studies on magnetic fields remain limited to single-material systems. To address this limitation, a novel multi-material inverse homogenization framework is proposed to facilitate microstructure design by considering both magnetic and thermal fields. In this approach, micromechanics-based homogenization is employed to evaluate effective properties. A discrete-material-optimization-based interpolation scheme was adopted to represent the spatial distribution of two-phase ferromagnetic materials with inherent trade-offs between magnetic permeability and thermal conductivity and was further modified using exponential interpolation to improve numerical characteristics. To obtain balanced multifunctional designs, a global criterion method was introduced to integrate multiple physical performance criteria into a unified objective function. Several numerical examples were presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results showed that multi-material designs under multi-field conditions offer apparent benefits over their single-material or single-field counterparts and that considering magnetic nonlinearity leads to distinct design outcomes. Furthermore, systematic performance tuning was achieved through material volume fraction control, and directional magnetic responses were realized by introducing an additional orthotropy constraint. This study provides insights into the engineering design of hybrid material systems, highlighting the potential of multi-material and multi-field approaches for achieving controllable and application-relevant functional performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Sun M.; Lu G.; Huang Z.; Quan S.; Zhang Y.; Tan Y.
Title: Hybrid scheduling for serverless function workflows in edge computing system
Abstract: Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) computing paradigm enables fine-grained resource scheduling through decomposing complex workflows into a series of functions deployed in edge computing systems by a containerized manner. The temporal constraints of these workflows are required to be satisfied, where delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant workflows are scheduled through a priority-aware mechanism. We focus on resource-constrained edge nodes which are characterized by limited energy supply and computing capability. It is challenging to achieve the optimal trade-off between response delay and energy consumption through optimally deployed functions on edge nodes for scheduling unpredictable incoming workflows. This issue is formulated as an online deadline-aware function deployment model in terms of the Lyapunov optimization technique with efficient stability queues. A Markov decision process is formulated by continuously updating system states, selecting scheduling actions, and evaluating corresponding rewards. We develop a Deep Q-Learning based Workflow Scheduling (denoted as DQLWS) technique to achieve adaptive hybrid workflow scheduling, while considering long-term response delay and energy efficiency. Extensive experiments are conducted in terms of different proportions between delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant workflows, delay-energy weighting settings, scalability of edge node quantity and long-term scheduling performance. Evaluation results show that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in multiple comparison dimensions, including response delay, energy consumption, temporal violation rate, and algorithm stability, and thus achieves near-optimal scheduling solutions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: How have flight operations between China and Europe changed since the Russia–Ukraine war?
Abstract: This study examines how direct flight services between China and Europe changed during the COVID-19 pandemic and after the Russia–Ukraine war began in February 2022. We use monthly airport pair–airline data from January 2014 to September 2024. Our baseline model is a panel regression with route fixed effects. As a robustness check, we also estimate a two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) specification with route and period fixed effects. After February 2022, passenger traffic fell and yields rose on the sampled routes, and these changes differed between European and Chinese carriers. In the baseline route fixed-effects model, European carriers had approximately 32.7% lower revenue passenger miles and 14.4% lower yields than Chinese carriers during the war period, relative to pre-war differences. The TWFE specification gives interaction estimates of similar sign and magnitude. These differences arose at the same time as the closure of Russian airspace to European carriers and are consistent with the longer routings that other studies document, together with other concurrent factors. During the COVID-19 period, passenger traffic fell sharply. Yields rose in the pooled sample but not in either travel direction separately, which is consistent with unequal travel demand in the two directions. Taken together, these findings highlight persistent vulnerabilities in the China–Europe aviation market and point to potential airline strategies, including greater operational flexibility, service enhancements, code-sharing arrangements, and bilateral coordination, that may strengthen market resilience. Authors: Chen J.; Xia S.; Ma Z.
Title: The role of attention and norm perception in online comments’ impact on attitudes toward sunscreen: An eye-tracking approach
Abstract: Social media platforms have become a major source of health information, where user-generated comments often shape attitudes toward health behaviors. Yet, the mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. This study examines the role of selective attention and perceived norms in the influence of online comments on attitudes toward sunscreen use. Using a between-subject eye-tracking experiment (N = 177), participants viewed a simulated YouTube live-stream video promoting sunscreen misinformation accompanied by either pro- or anti-sunscreen comments. Attention to comments was measured objectively (time viewed, fixation counts) and subjectively (self-reported attention). Results reveal that prior attitudes and behaviors predict selective attention in distinct ways: individuals with more positive attitudes attended more to pro-sunscreen comments, whereas more frequent sunscreen use was associated with more attention to anti-sunscreen comments. Mediation analyses indicate that attention to comments influences perceived norms differently across conditions. In the pro-sunscreen condition, greater attention predicted stronger perceived proximal network norms, which were strongly associated with attitude change. In contrast, in the anti-sunscreen condition, attention predicted weaker perceived social media norms but did not alter proximal norms. Across models, changes in proximal network norms were the most robust predictor of attitude change. Findings highlight the importance of examining selective attention to better understand online comment effects and reveal nuanced normative pathways. The study advances selective exposure and social norm literature in online comment contexts and underscores the value of eye-tracking for objectively measuring visual attention to online comments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From design attributes to social life: Modelling conviviality in urban underground spaces
Abstract: From being infrastructure utilities, urban underground spaces (UUS) have developed into multipurpose public spaces that combine commercial, cultural, and transit functions. While their technical and spatial contributions to compact urbanism are evident, their capacity to foster conviviality, the experiential quality of inclusiveness, sociability, and shared belonging, is less understood. This study develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework that operationalizes conviviality in UUS by linking seven spatial-perceptual dimensions (safety and security, identity and meaning, accessibility, functionality, environmental comfort, aesthetics, and structure and form) to behavioral mediators of willingness to use and social interaction, culminating in perceived conviviality. Using the Theatre-Shahr underground complex in Tehran as a case study, data were collected through structured surveys and analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that although environmental factors generally have a positive indirect effect on perceived conviviality, social interaction emerges as the primary mechanism shaping conviviality in urban underground spaces, while willingness to use plays only a complementary and limited mediating role in this process. Among the environmental factors, accessibility, environmental comfort, and safety and security show the strongest effects. In contrast, some variables, particularly identity and meaning and structure and form, do not demonstrate statistically significant effects in certain pathways. These findings suggest that planning and design strategies for urban underground spaces should prioritize environmental qualities that support social interaction, to enhance perceived conviviality. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Enhancing combustion in an ethanol rotary engine via turbulent jet ignition: parametric study and mechanism analysis
Abstract: Enhancing the combustion of ethanol rotary engine (ERE) is crucial for carbon neutrality. This study systematically compares the effects of conventional spark plug ignition mode (CSPIM) and turbulent jet ignition mode (TJIM) on the performance of an ERE. This investigation employs a combined methodology of experimental validation and numerical simulation, systematically analyzes the combustion characteristics of both ignition modes across multiple equivalence ratio conditions. Furthermore, this research elucidates the effect of jet nozzle diameter (JND) on the combustion behavior of the TJIM. The results reveal that TJIM’s effectiveness is governed by the coupling between the energy of the jet flame and the concentration of the mixture in the pre-combustion chamber. It demonstrates superior flame propagation and combustion at equivalence ratios of 1.0 and 1.2 by generating highly turbulent jet flames, but underperforms CSPIM under an equivalence ratio of 0.8 due to reduced jet flame intensity. Furthermore, the optimal JND shifts with the global equivalence ratio — 3.5 mm for lean and 2.0 mm for stoichiometric combustion. The JND governs a trade-off between the mass of fuel in the pre-combustion chamber and the jet flame velocity. While TJIM significantly reduces CO emissions via more complete combustion, it increases NO formation due to higher temperatures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Unconventional plastic accommodation mediated by strain gradients in a multiscale heterostructured Mg alloy at room temperature
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Heterostructures are widely recognized as an effective strategy for achieving strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloys. However, their potential remains insufficiently exploited because most current approaches rely on single-scale structural regulation. In this work, a multiscale heterostructured Mg alloy with through-thickness gradients in grain size, texture, and dislocation density was fabricated via heterothermal rolling. The alloy exhibits a pronounced strength–ductility synergy, with ∼3.3 times higher ductility than that of conventional rolling while maintaining comparable strength. Microstructural characterization reveals that the multiscale heterogeneous architecture rapidly accumulates geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) at the early stage of deformation, establishing a pronounced dislocation density gradient that continuously generates strain gradients along the thickness direction during subsequent deformation. The coupled dislocation and strain gradients promote special boundary formation and activate micro-shear-dominated plasticity. Owing to the through-thickness microstructural heterogeneity, shear bands nucleate heterogeneously across different layers, activating multiple slip systems and accelerating dynamic recrystallization and texture weakening processes that are usually suppressed at room temperature. The recrystallized fraction reaches up to 80% in the necked region, suggesting that the strain gradient can activate high-fraction room-temperature recrystallization and thereby contribute to plastic accommodation in the present heterostructured Mg alloy. Meanwhile, the heterogeneous layers undergo a dynamic soft/hard-domain transition, which sustains strain accommodation and delays strain localization. These findings reveal a strain-gradient-mediated plasticity mechanism and provide a new structural design strategy for overcoming the strength–ductility trade-off in Mg alloys. © 2026

Authors: Chen W.; Liu B.
Title: Production decisions of a leasing-selling closed-loop supply chain under different authorization strategies
Abstract: Leasing or selling, when to choose which? This paper investigates the production decisions of a closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) considering authorized remanufacturing (royalty/fixed-fee authorization) under different business mode combinations. Furthermore, win–win authorization strategies for the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the third-party remanufacturer (TPR) are analyzed. The conclusion shows that: (1) Regardless of the business mode chosen by the OEM, the sensitivity of unit product authorization fee to consumer perceived value of remanufactured products (RPs) is always higher when the TPR chooses the selling mode than when it chooses the leasing mode. (2) For selling new products (NPs) and RPs mode and selling NPs and leasing RPs mode, the fixed-fee authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for selling is high and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range, and the royalty authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when this cost is low and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range. The win–win authorization strategies for the leasing NPs and selling RPs mode and leasing NPs and RPs mode are affected by the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for leasing and the fixed authorization fee. (3) Under the royalty authorization strategy, the TPR is more profitable when the OEM chooses the leasing mode, but the OEM is more profitable when the TPR chooses the selling mode. Under the fixed-fee authorization strategy, when one of the two players chooses the leasing mode, the other is always more profitable. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Teng J.; Cho S.
Title: Mental imagery and visuospatial processing in visual communication design education: Examining relationships with creative performance and academic achievement in university students
Abstract: This study investigated the relationships among mental imagery, visuospatial processing, creative performance, and academic achievement in university visual communication design students. A sample of 156 undergraduate students majoring in visual communication design completed the Mental Imagery Test (MIT), Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM), and Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT), while their academic performance in design studio, typography, digital imaging, and visual theory courses was assessed through course grades. Results indicated significant positive correlations between mental imagery abilities and both creative performance and academic achievement across all design-related courses. Visuospatial processing, operationalized here as figural-inductive visuospatial reasoning, partially mediated the relationship between mental imagery and academic performance in design studio and digital imaging courses, while creative self-efficacy emerged as an additional mediator for typography performance. Gender differences were minimal, with males showing slight advantages only in spatial transformation tasks. These findings underscore the importance of developing mental imagery and visuospatial skills within visual communication curricula and suggest that targeted cognitive training interventions may enhance both creative output and academic success in design education contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li X.; Lu C.; Li W.; Gao X.; Xu J.; Chen H.; Wei C.; Li L.
Title: Regulating metallurgical continuity and fracture-path selection through interfacial coupling in multi-material additive manufacturing
Abstract: The growing demand for multifunctional components requires structural and functional properties to be spatially tailored within a single architecture, a capability difficult to achieve using monolithic materials. Multi-material additive manufacturing offers a promising solution, yet its implementation is constrained by the difficulty of forming reliable interfaces between dissimilar alloys. Here, we reveal how interfacial melt-pool coupling governs interface evolution and fracture-path selection in 316L stainless steel/CuSn10 multi-material architectures fabricated by multi-material laser powder bed fusion. Four programmed coupling conditions were produced by varying the cross-boundary scan extension and were operationally classified as decoupled, partially coupled, stably coupled, and over-coupled according to the resulting interfacial morphologies. Stable coupling transformed the sharp and discontinuous boundary into a continuous, chemically heterogeneous transition zone with broadened Fe/Cu redistribution, refined interfacial grains, and locally identified BCC α-Fe within the Cu-rich matrix. This transition suppressed boundary-dominated failure and redirected fracture across both constituent materials, increasing the ultimate tensile strength by 61.7%, from 161.1 to 260.5 MPa, although the elongation decreased from 8.33% to 5.23%, indicating a strength–ductility trade-off. Insufficient coupling preserved lack-of-fusion defects, whereas over-coupling generated pore-bearing Cu-rich regions and shifted failure to a pore-assisted path. Time-resolved synchrotron X-ray imaging further revealed keyhole fluctuation, partial collapse, and pore retention as a plausible pore-formation pathway. Application-oriented multi-material demonstrators with complex geometries were successfully fabricated, supporting the geometric implementation of interface-controlled MM-LPBF. These findings establish a coupling-dependent interface-control principle for balancing metallurgical continuity against defect-assisted damage in multi-material additive manufacturing. © 2026 The Authors. Title: On flat production surfaces associated with Cobb-Douglas-type production models exhibiting variable returns to scale
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: We prove that the flatness of the production surface associated with a Cobb–Douglas-type production model exhibiting variable returns to scale forces the local return-to-scale index to be constant, thereby establishing a rigidity result for this class of production functions. Consequently, every flat production model in this class is homogeneous, and its local classification follows directly from the classification theorem established in [8] . Title: Benchmarking operational spatial plausibility and temporal compatibility of EEG inverse solutions in the visual P300 network
Abstract: Background: EEG source localization is ill-posed, and competing inverse priors may yield different spatial, temporal, and reliability profiles for visual P300 source estimates. Methods: We benchmarked nine inverse solutions across four families (RAP/TRAP, LCMV/DICS, MNE/dSPM/sLORETA/eLORETA, and Bayesian sparse/hierarchical inference) in 31 participants, 63 sessions, and 2520 trials. Analyses were repeated under an fsaverage template BEM and an alternative spherical conductor model. Outcomes included continuous nearest-ROI distance, 20 mm ROI coverage, 5–40 mm tolerance sensitivity, P3b-window temporal plausibility (300–500 ms with ±25 ms shifts), cross-session reliability, computational cost with setup-versus-inference timing, and source-method×head-model interaction testing. FDR-corrected contrasts, TOST equivalence tests, subject-level bootstrapping, and Aligned-Rank-Transform checks were used. Results: Under fsaverage, LCMV had the highest 20 mm ROI-proximal coverage (21.7%). However, the head-model interaction was significant (p=9.8×10−8), and MNE was the most probable top performer under the spherical model. Cross-session dispersion showed no significant method effect (p=0.866). P3b-timing conclusions were sensitive to the shifted windows, and cross-method agreement was low (mean κ about 0.13). Computational cost ranged from 17.2 to 191.1 s per trial under fsaverage and reached 974.0 s for spherical DICS. Conclusions: The results support uncertainty-aware, multi-constraint method selection rather than a single fixed ranking. © 2026
