Title: Mapping Healthy Days Scores to EQ-5D-5L Utilities: Development and Validation of an Algorithm Using Population Survey Data
Abstract: Objectives To develop and validate an algorithm for estimating EQ-5D-5L utility scores from the nonpreference-based Healthy Days (HD) instrument using direct and indirect mapping approaches. Methods Data were drawn from the Queensland Preventive Health Survey for 2022 ( N = 12 491) and 2023 ( N = 12 679). Survey-weighted ordinary least squares (OLS), Tobit, beta, majorize-minimize, and ordinal logistic regression models were evaluated. Algorithms were developed using an 80% random training sample from the 2022 data, tested in the remaining 20%, and externally validated using 2023 data. Predictive performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, differences between predicted and observed mean utilities, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, body mass index, smoking status, and utility quartile. Results Moderate correlations were observed between unhealthy days measures and EQ-5D-5L utilities (Pearson’s r: −0.53 to −0.56). Predictive accuracy was broadly similar for the OLS, beta, and ordinal logistic models. The OLS model including physically unhealthy days, mentally unhealthy days, activity limitation days, self-rated health, age, and sex was selected as the preferred algorithm. It demonstrated strong and stable predictive performance across samples (root mean square error ≤ 0.117 and mean absolute error ≤ 0.066 in validation samples). All models overestimated utilities in the lowest utility quartile. Conclusions The HD instrument can be mapped to the EQ-5D-5L with favorable predictive accuracy in population survey data. The proposed algorithm provides a pragmatic approach for estimating mean utilities for quality-adjusted life-year calculation when only HD data are available, although caution is warranted in populations with very low baseline health status. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Yang Y.; Li J.; Li Y.; Zhang S.; Guo K.
Title: Facilitator or hallucination trap? A social-cognitive account of AI-generated misinformation handling in GenAI-assisted L2 writing
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has demonstrated remarkable potential in second language (L2) learning, yet it is prone to hallucinations. Empirical research on how GenAI-generated misinformation is handled in educational contexts remains scarce. Accordingly, little is known about how these practices shape learning processes and outcomes. Guided by social cognitive theory, the current study frames students' GenAI-assisted L2 writing (using a tailored GenAI writing agent) in a hallucination-prone context in which misinformation was implanted. We examine AI literacy, higher-order thinking resources (i.e., critical thinking and creativity), L2 writing resources (i.e., L2 writing grit and self-regulatory writing strategies), English writing self-efficacy (EWSE), AI-generated misinformation detection (AI-MD), and L2 writing performance within this framework. Using a multi-method approach, combining a qualitative interview study (N = 35), two lab experiments (N = 140), and a large-scale questionnaire survey (N = 406), we find that critical thinking positively predicts GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance via AI-MD, and that negative priming on AI hallucinations significantly improves students’ AI-MD and their GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance, relative to neutral or positive priming. Furthermore, the cross-sectional survey focuses on personal factors and shows that AI literacy significantly predicts EWSE both directly and indirectly through a cognitive–generative pathway involving higher-order thinking resources and a motivational–regulatory pathway involving L2 writing resources. These findings extend social-cognitive accounts of GenAI-assisted L2 writing and inform instruction that helps learners evaluate AI outputs, manage misinformation risks, and sustain their own writing processes. © 2026

Authors: Xu S.; Li M.; Huang Q.; Tian Y.
Title: Decoupled reverse Kullback–Leibler: Rethinking knowledge distillation loss for bridging GNNs and MLPs
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel at handling graph-structured data but are often prohibitively expensive for low-latency applications. Cross-architecture graph knowledge distillation (GKD) addresses this by training efficient Multi-layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to mimic GNN performance. Interestingly, while existing methods predominantly use forward Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, we find that the two terms of reverse KL exhibit optimization properties that are better matched to the GKD objective. However, its conventional form suffers from tightly coupled fitting and regularization terms with fixed weights, limiting its flexibility. To overcome this, we propose Decoupled Reverse KL (DRKL), which introduces hyperparameters to independently adjust the weight of each term, enabling more effective adaptation to diverse prediction scenarios. Title: Beyond topology-driven graph convolution: Node patch convolutional network for node representation learning
Abstract: Attributed graph node representation learning is crucial for tasks such as node classification in attributed networks. Conventional GNNs, whether coupled or decoupled, are mainly topology-driven and struggle to capture attribute correlations among non-neighboring nodes. Existing CNN-based graph methods alleviate this limitation by selecting relevant nodes but remain sensitive to node ordering and often fail to integrate attribute and topology views effectively. In this paper, we propose a CNN-based graph representation learning framework namely node patch convolutional network (NPCN) that constructs node-centric patches from both attribute and topology perspectives. Moreover, a tailored patch augmentation and the corresponding readout mechanism are adopted to enhance the node representation learning. A patch consistency constraint further stabilizes the learned representations. Experiments on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms representative approaches. Moreover, computational efficiency analysis shows that NPCN achieves competitive performance with lower training overhead compared with Transformer-based graph representation learning methods, making it a practical solution for attributed graph node classification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Self-disclosure to intelligent virtual agents: A scoping review and the disclosure affordance–actualization–governance framework
Abstract: Intelligent virtual agents (IVAs) have become digital social objects to which people disclose personal, emotional, health-related, and other sensitive information. Yet similar cues—including anthropomorphism, social presence, empathy, gaze, anonymity, and structured questioning—are associated across studies with greater disclosure, refusal, impression management, socially desirable responding, or discomfort. Searches covered four bibliographic databases without publication-year restrictions through March 17, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar searching on May 20, 2026. This review, reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), maps 88 empirical studies and introduces the Disclosure Affordance–Actualization–Governance (DAAG) framework as a middle-range account linking specific empirical findings with broader explanations of IVA-mediated disclosure. DAAG distinguishes sociotechnical interaction ecology; perceived safety from judgment, relational receptivity, expressive latitude, and boundary agency; disclosure actualization; affective, relational, and functional consequences; governance; and evidential reach—the extent to which studies observe perception, behavior, consequences, time, and governance. The literature is most developed for disclosure onset, sensitive reporting, emotional expression, and immediate system acceptance, but remains thin on persistence, reciprocity, subjective–behavioral divergence, correction, revocation, and downstream data use. Recurrent patterns are consistent with IVA cues being interpreted through evaluation risk, partner responsiveness, observability, topic sensitivity, competence, privacy, and control. DAAG is not presented as a validated causal model, but as a framework for explaining when digital social interaction supports, redirects, or appropriately constrains self-disclosure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Taylor-sparsified differentially private federated learning with support-consensus robust aggregation
Abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative training without sharing raw data, but sparse private updates may still leak information through both support masks and noisy values, while remaining vulnerable to Byzantine attacks. We propose TDP-SRA, a Taylor-sparsified differentially private federated learning framework with support-consensus robust aggregation. Clients select supports using a privatized Taylor utility criterion and release clipped sparse values with Gaussian perturbation, providing client-level privacy accounting for the complete sparse release. The server maintains a temporally smoothed support frequency vector, estimates a consensus support, scores uploads by support agreement and privacy noise normalized residuals, and aggregates server clipped sparse updates via a weighted geometric median in the consensus subspace. We establish client-level Rényi differential privacy and provide sufficient or conditional analyses for support recovery and robust aggregation under explicit support stability, support separation, and effective Byzantine weight assumptions. Experiments on multiple vision datasets under standard, data poisoning, and adaptive support-aware attacks show that TDP-SRA achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among accuracy, privacy, robustness, and uplink communication efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Zhang Y.; Qian H.; Luo X.; Liang Y.; Lu P.; Liang Z.; Chen J.; Chen Y.
Title: Life cycle analysis and multi-objective optimization of CCUS-integrated methanol reforming PEMFC-CCHP systems
Abstract: Distributed methanol steam reforming (MSR)-proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems have attracted attention due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. Coupling these systems with combined cooling, heating, and power (CCHP) configurations further enhances energy utilization. However, their strong reliance on fossil fuels leads to substantial carbon emissions. Although integrating carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) mitigates operational emissions, it introduces additional energy penalties, economic costs, and complexity, while its full life cycle environmental benefits remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, conventional single-objective optimization is inadequate to simultaneously balance energy, economic, and environmental performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel distributed MSR-PEMFC-CCHP system integrated with CCUS and develops a comprehensive evaluation framework combining life cycle assessment (LCA) and multi-objective optimization. Three configurations—CCHP-C (without carbon treatment), CCHP-S (with CCS), and CCHP-M (with CCUS)—are systematically analyzed to quantify full life cycle environmental impacts and identify optimal trade-offs. Results show the operation stage dominates life cycle emissions, contributing over 80 % in all configurations. Under the adopted inventory assumptions and system boundary, CCHP-M has the lowest total pollutant emissions and global warming potential, whereas CCHP-C has lower acidification and respiratory effect potentials. For CCHP-M, the selected compromise solution, Point D, achieves an energy efficiency of 85.61 % and an LCOE of 0.2463 $/kWh. Compared with the energy-optimal solution, Point K, Point D reduces the LCOE by 2.84 % and lowers life-cycle CO2-equivalent emissions by 2.816 t, or 4.14 %, to 65.153 t, while decreasing energy efficiency by 1.79 %. These results identify the environmental trade-offs among the three carbon-management configurations and the operating compromise within CCHP-M. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effect of CO2 concentration on carbon sequestration and mechanical strength of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill
Abstract: Coal production generates large quantities of coal-based solid wastes (coal gangue, blast furnace slag, and fly ash) and significant CO2 emissions, creating severe ecological challenges in mining regions. This study integrates coal-based solid waste cemented backfilling with CO2 mineral sequestration to manage both solid wastes and CO2. The CO2 uptake and uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) of coal-based solid waste cemented backfill (CSCB) were investigated after 14 days of mineralization curing at CO2 concentrations of 0–10 vol%. Thermogravimetric analysis (TG), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were used to examine the sequestration mechanism and the associated strength reduction. CO2 uptake increased with CO2 concentration: raising the concentration from 1.5 to 10 vol% increased the uptake from 2.42 to 4.05 wt% (a 67.4% increase), based on a single TG measurement per group. In contrast, UCS decreased from 6.05 MPa (0 vol%) to 0.72 MPa (10 vol%), an 88.1% reduction. Microstructural and mineralogical analyses indicate that CO2 reacts with alkaline phases and hydration products (CH, MH, C-S(A)-H gel, and AFt) to form calcite, gypsum, and possible Mg-bearing carbonate (XRD peaks tentatively assigned to dolomite). The strength loss is attributed to weakening of the alkaline environment, decalcification of C-S(A)-H gel, and carbonation of AFt to gypsum. A concentration of 1.5 vol% provided a reasonable balance, with 2.42 wt% uptake and a 13.2% strength loss. These results show a clear trade-off between carbon uptake and mechanical performance in CSCB. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Pu Y.; Chen H.; Guo Y.
Title: Autonomy-supportive mediation and scam susceptibility: The role of literacy among middle-aged and older adults
Abstract: Although online scams increasingly threaten middle-aged and older adults, existing research has largely focused on individual literacy and short-term interventions, leaving the development and application of scam literacy in everyday contexts less understood. Drawing on parental mediation theory and self-determination theory, this study conceptualizes autonomy-supportive mediation (ASM) as a family-based socialization context for developing aging parents' scam-related literacy. It also considers face concern, a personal orientation reflecting individuals’ motivation to protect their social image from potential social judgment. This study tested two complementary models that distinguish between the foundation of scam literacy (scam knowledge) and its activation (cyber-risk beliefs). Data were collected through a cross-sectional vignette-based survey of 404 middle-aged and older adults in China between February 13 and February 27, 2025, using a volunteer-assisted convenience sampling strategy. The results indicated that higher levels of ASM were linked to lower scam loss, with this association mediated by scam knowledge and moderated by face concern. Moreover, ASM was positively related to cyber-risk beliefs, which were subsequently linked to greater systematic information processing and suspicion toward potential scams. These findings suggest that effective scam prevention depends not only on what individuals know, but also on whether they recognize and respond to risks in real-world situations. This study highlights the importance of autonomy-supportive family communication in combating online scams. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Multidisciplinary design, analysis, and optimization (MDO) for co-designed transmission & distribution electric grid planning

Title: Integrating fatty acid signatures through machine learning for traceability and nutritional profiling of wild and farmed gilthead sea bream (Sparus aurata)
Abstract: Fatty acid composition of seafood can provide insights into its nutritional value and tools for traceability analysis. In this study, the fillet fatty acid compositions of wild-caught gilthead sea bream and specimens produced under cage-reared and pond-reared aquaculture regimes in Northeast Atlantic waters were evaluated to (i) assess nutritional quality using lipid quality indices and (ii) test the traceability discrimination potential of fatty acids using machine-learning classification (Random Forest) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis. Distinct fatty acid profiles and total lipid contents were observed between all groups. Although wild-caught fish exhibited higher relative abundance of nutritionally important marine fatty acids EPA and DHA, the greater total lipid content of farmed specimens yielded comparable or higher absolute levels of these omega-3 fatty acids. Mid-Atlantic cage-reared fish contained the highest total fatty acid and EPA + DHA contents, whereas coastal cage-reared specimens displayed favorable cardiovascular health indices. The traceability model achieved high accuracy during the training (100%) and validation phases (99.1%), with higher classification accuracy for wild-caught and pond-reared specimens, followed by coastal and Mid-Atlantic cage-reared specimens. Notably, this methodological approach identified key fatty acids, driving discrimination between groups, providing biologically meaningful markers likely linked to feeding regimes and production practices. Overall, fatty acid profiling coupled with machine learning provides a highly accurate framework for discriminating the production groups examined while delivering consumer-relevant nutritional information and supporting future seafood traceability applications. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Dependent development at the energy transition: placing lithium imaginaries in Neoliberal and Contentious Peru
Abstract: We examine lithium and development imaginaries in mining-dependent Peru, asking: What are these imaginaries? What narratives underpin them? Who articulates and shares them, and from where? What forms of state (in)action are envisioned in relation to them? The case study elucidates how alternative “imagined futures” coexist within a natural resource–dependent economy. The ruling national elites in Lima have a neoliberal imagination, treating lithium like any other mineral resource in the country. In contrast, professional elites in the mineral-rich but peripheral region of Puno adopt a resource nationalist view, advocating for direct state involvement in lithium industrialization and the transformation of the domestic energy system, shaped by beliefs on Bolivia's developmental pathway. Among rural community leaders as well as political and social leaders in the districts near lithium and uranium deposits, however, the prevailing idea is that of a social license. In this view, each community has the capacity to negotiate development terms with mining companies independently. In the broader imagination at the resource periphery of a peripheral national economy, the state is perceived primarily as a minimalist governmental actor, necessary only to oversee and ensure the enforcement of mine-community agreements and to provide basic infrastructure. Thus, elites at the political center and communities near expected resource developments converge in their immediate pursuit of rents promised by resource commodification. In the dominant discourses, environmental concerns are often subordinated to economic development goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Semi-Asynchronous Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning for heterogeneous resources
Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of cloud–edge–device collaborative computing, Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) has become a promising paradigm for large-scale distributed model training. However, existing HFL systems still struggle with device heterogeneity, Non-IID data distributions, and substantial communication overhead, leading to inefficient training and unstable convergence. To overcome these limitations, we propose SAEHFL, a Semi-Asynchronous Efficient Hierarchical Federated Learning framework designed for heterogeneous environments. SAEHFL leverages a heterogeneity-aware device grouping strategy that clusters devices based on computational capability and data distribution, reducing intra-group imbalance and mitigating Non-IID-induced bias. A circular ring-sequential aggregation mechanism further restructures device–edge communication, reducing communication overhead and improving bandwidth utilization. At the edge–cloud level, a hybrid synchronization strategy enables synchronous group updates while incorporating semi-asynchronous buffered aggregation, reducing waiting time and reducing global waiting time while maintaining stable convergence behavior. Extensive experiments on MNIST, FEMNIST, and CIFAR10 show that SAEHFL achieves a favorable time–accuracy trade-off. At the target accuracy for each dataset, SAEHFL reduces the average training time by 55.61%, 56.91%, 63.45%, 62.99%, and 61.54% compared with SFedAvg, SAFedAvg, Random, FedProx, and HFLCHFL. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SAEHFL in enabling efficient and communication-aware hierarchical federated learning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Hydrazo Bridging Combined with Multiple Hydrogen-Bonding Network: A Strategy for Regulating Energy and Safety in Pyrazinyl Energetic Molecules
Abstract: Hydrogen bonding plays a pivotal role in the crystal engineering of energetic materials and provides an effective strategy for the synergistic regulation of structural stability and energetic properties. In this work, we used polysubstituted pyrazine as the parent skeleton, other six-membered aromatic rings as building blocks, and a hydrazo group as a bridging module to construct a series of symmetric and asymmetric hydrazo-bridged bicyclic pyrazinyl energetic molecules. A systematic evaluation of their geometric structures, electronic properties, detonation performance and safety was conducted by integrating theoretical calculations with experiments. Experimental and theoretical calculations have revealed a clear structure-property rule: as the number of ortho-NH2/NO2 modules increases, the hydrogen bond network gradually becomes more continuous and abundant, leading to improved detonation performance (Dv: 8023∼8414 m·s⁻¹), reduced mechanical sensitivity (IS: 8∼20 J) and improved thermal stability (Td: 223∼283 °C). It is worth noting that the enhancement of hydrogen bonding networks effectively eliminates the long-standing trade-off between energy and safety, while additional conjugation enhancement helps to improve thermal stability. This work establishes hydrazo-mediated multiple hydrogen bond network engineering as a universal and scalable strategy for achieving triple synergistic optimization, providing clear design principles for the next generation of high-performance, insensitive and thermally stable energetic materials. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Patient education for older adults with cancer and their caregivers: A scoping review
Abstract: Introduction Patient education is essential for older adults with cancer and their caregivers to support understanding of diagnosis and treatment. However, the evidence describing patient education interventions has not been comprehensively mapped. Our objective was to characterize the features, delivery approaches, and outcomes of patient education interventions developed for older adults with cancer and/or their caregivers across any study design, and to identify gaps in the evidence. Materials and methods A scoping review was conducted using the Arksey and O’Malley framework and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guideline. MEDLINE, EMBASE, EMCARE, CENTRAL, PsycINFO, and Scopus were searched on January 23, 2025. Studies published from 2000 onward were included if they evaluated healthcare professional-delivered patient education. Results From 26,898 records screened, 93 studies met inclusion criteria. Most interventions were delivered pre-treatment (n = 63), with surgery the most common context (n = 31). Common aims included side-effect prevention (n = 32) and supporting treatment decision-making (n = 26). Caregiver involvement was limited. Outcomes were clustered into 20 domains. Frequent reported domains were satisfaction/acceptability (52 occurrences) and knowledge/understanding (46 occurrences), while caregiver outcomes and clinical endpoints were rarely assessed. Discussion Patient education interventions generally improved knowledge and satisfaction, but evidence for clinical or system-level impacts remains limited. Key gaps include minimal integration of geriatric assessment, limited adaptation for cognitive impairment, sparse caregiver-specific outcomes, and inconsistent reporting of unintended effects. Future research should better integrate caregiver needs and geriatric principles into patient education design. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Multi-omics profiling of muscle tissue reveals metabolic signatures associated with size variation in redclaw crayfish (Cherax quadricarinatus)
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: The rising market demand for large, premium grade redclaw crayfish (Cherax quadricarinatus) highlights the need for improved production efficiency, yet the molecular characteristics associated with body-size variation remain poorly understood. This study employs an integrated multi-omics approach (untargeted metabolomics, targeted taurine analysis, and transcriptomics) to characterize the metabolic signatures associated with crayfish size variation. Untargeted analysis of 18,204 metabolite features identified 229 differentially abundant metabolites, including a 28-fold higher level of sucrose in large individuals (p = 0.025). Targeted analysis confirmed that taurine, a key osmolyte and antioxidant, was significantly elevated in larger crayfish. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed metabolic features associated with carbohydrate and purine metabolism that correlated with body-size variation. In contrast, smaller crayfish exhibited elevated purine turnover (xanthine/uric acid) and reduced levels of key anabolic metabolites. These findings provide a multi-omics characterization of metabolic states associated with growth phenotypes and identify candidate biomarkers for future studies investigating the potential of nutritional strategies to improve crayfish production. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Online direct-to-consumer channel introducing and ordering strategies of fresh supply chain considering disruption risks and yield constraints
Abstract: The rise of online direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels expands fresh producers’ distribution networks while intensifying competition with traditional retail channels. Meteorological disasters threaten the DTC channel's reliability, dynamically reshaping the coopetition between fresh producers and retailers. This study develops a theoretical framework to examine strategic interactions within a fresh supply chain, comparing a traditional monopoly model with an integrated distribution system that incorporates both DTC and traditional retail channels. Disruption risks and yield constraints faced by producers are considered. The findings suggest producers should introduce DTC channels during yield contraction but exercise caution in surplus periods. Despite disruption risks, DTC channels pressure retailers to accept higher wholesale prices and increase orders, enhancing the sales revenue of fresh produce with limited yield. Title: Events under fire: Developing an urgent anthropology for events during armed conflicts
Abstract: This conceptual and methodological research note addresses event industry dynamics during armed conflicts, proposing an urgent anthropology approach to document transformations in real time. Using Ukraine as an example, we illustrate how event organizations have adapted to existential threats since the 2022 Russian invasion, demonstrating resilience through cultural initiatives, charitable events, and creative repurposing of resources. We argue that these practices have the potential to sustain cultural identity and to contribute to economic development, social cohesion and morale in conflict settings. To overcome the methodological and ethical challenges of traditional ethnography in war zones, we propose a novel citizen science framework within the urgent anthropology paradigm, leveraging digital technologies, social media, and participatory methods. This approach can decentralize knowledge production, mitigate researcher risk, and create longitudinal archives of industry adaptations. Title: EPIPTrack: Rethinking prompt modeling with explicit and implicit prompts for multi-object tracking
Abstract: Multimodal semantic cues, such as textual descriptions, have shown strong potential in enhancing target perception for tracking. However, existing methods rely on static textual descriptions from large language models, which lack adaptability to real-time target state changes and prone to hallucinations. To address these challenges, we propose a unified multimodal vision-language tracking framework, which leverages explicit and implicit prompts for dynamic target modeling and semantic alignment. Specifically, explicit prompts transform spatial motion information into natural language descriptions to provide spatiotemporal guidance. Implicit prompts combine pseudo-words with learnable descriptors to construct individualized knowledge representations capturing identity-related semantic attributes. Both prompts are dynamically adjusted through a pretrained vision-language text encoder to respond to changes in target states. Furthermore, we design a Discriminative Feature Augmentor to enhance visual and cross-modal representations. Extensive experiments on three public multi-object tracking benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing trackers across diverse scenarios, exhibiting robust adaptability and superior performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Development and experimental evaluation of common rail direct injection methanol (MD97) fuelled compression ignition engine
Abstract: Methanol has emerged as a promising alternative to fossil fuels for powering internal combustion (IC) engines due to its higher fuel-to-oxygen ratio and lower tendency to form soot. Given the widespread use of compression-ignition (CI) engines in heavy-duty applications, there has been significant interest in adapting methanol for their operation. However, methanol’s inferior autoignition characteristics and longer ignition delay (ID) compared to diesel make its direct use in CI engines challenging. To overcome these limitations, engine modifications are essential to optimise the engine performance and ensure stable combustion. In this experimental study, a single-cylinder, four-stroke CI engine was modified by increasing its compression ratio (CR) and by incorporating an intake air preheating system to improve methanol ignition. The engine’s mechanical fuel injection system was replaced with a custom-built common-rail direct-injection (CRDI) system, and an in-house developed controller was utilised to inject methanol supplemented with an ignition improver (MD97: 97 % w/w methanol and 3 % w/w catalyst). The performance, combustion, and emission characteristics of MD97 were analysed and compared with baseline diesel (FIP 600 bar, SoI 14° bTDC). MD97 achieved stable ignition with a minimum ID of 7° CA, compared to the baseline diesel’s 7.5° CA. Injection timing was further optimised to achieve a balanced trade-off between the engine performance, combustion, and emission characteristics. Under optimised conditions (FIP 500 bar, SoI 13° bTDC), MD97 exhibited ∼40 % higher brake thermal efficiency (BTE), ∼88 % reduction in nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions, and almost negligible exhaust smoke; however, hydrocarbons (HC) and carbon monoxide (CO) emissions increased by ∼23 % and ∼52 %, respectively, compared to baseline diesel. Title: Co-firing of upgraded biomass towards flexible CO2 reduction for coal-fired power plants in China
Abstract: The increasing trend in CO2 emissions from fossil fuels has accelerated the renewable energy development, especially in China, the world's largest CO2 emitter, which targets carbon peaking by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Co-firing of raw biomass is a promising carbon–neutral energy option in China, but its application is limited to only 10% incorporation with stable combustion performance. Therefore, in this study comprehensively assessed biomass upgrading methods, including torrefaction, pelletization, pyrolysis, and gasification, demonstrated that upgraded biomass exhibited significant potential as an attractive, feasible, and sustainable alternative fuel for a low-carbon approach to co-firing in existing PC power plants. The existing research work revealed that the recent Chinese energy policies support the co-firing of biomass, while biomass upgrading technologies are under development and need bioenergy-supported policies. The results showed that upgraded biomass enables higher co-firing ratios in PC boilers, achieving up to 50% substitution on an energy basis and reducing net CO2 emissions by up to 50% compared with full coal combustion. Co-firing of the upgraded biomass not only maintains the high efficiency of PC and CFB furnaces, but also has the potential to lower their carbon footprint and NOx emissions. Additionally, the effectiveness of the co-firing strategy for achieving carbon neutrality is evaluated. This review paper can assist in identifying the potential methods that can increase the biomass-to-coal ratio during direct co-firing in existing PC furnaces without requiring large modifications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Oxygen recovery in a long channel PEM fuel cell using side injection: Balancing uniformity, power density, and pressure drop
Abstract: Increasing the length of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell channels attracts a lot of attention due to benefits such as enhanced reactant residence time, increased contact area and mass transfer path, and reduced edge effects. However, increasing the channel length may lead to a non-uniform distribution of the reactant along the flow path, which can result in performance degradation in the downstream regions. To compensate for this defect, the effect of side air injection into the cathode channel on the performance and oxygen concentration uniformity in a long PEM fuel cell is numerically investigated. A parametric study evaluating the impacts of the number and arrangement of injection ports on reactant distribution and overall cell efficiency of PEMFC was conducted and compared with case of without injection to finding the optimal configuration from point of view of power density and performance index. Results demonstrate that side injection effectively compensates for the oxygen concentration decline resulting from increased PEMFC channel length. Depending on the injection port arrangement, the power density enhancement relative to the no-injection case ranges from 27% to 158.96%. The highest power density was achieved with the eight-injection configuration (ports 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9), corresponding to a 158.96% increase. Furthermore, the six‑injection configuration (ports 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 9) emerges as the global optimum based on the performance index, which accounts for the trade‑off between hydrodynamic resistance and electrochemical performance, thus maximizing efficiency while avoiding excessive pressure drops. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Does artificial intelligence improve social stability risk performance in China?
Abstract: This paper examines whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to improving the social stability risk level in China. Against the backdrop of rapid digital transformation and increasingly complex governance challenges, AI has been widely adopted in areas such as public security, social management, and risk monitoring. However, its actual effectiveness in mitigating social stability risks remains underexplored. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions in China, this study constructs an empirical framework to evaluate the impact of AI policy on social stability risk levels. The analysis integrates indicators of technological capacity, governance performance, and socio-economic conditions, and applies quantitative methods to identify both direct and indirect effects. The findings suggest that AI policy significantly reduces social stability risks by promoting digital economy development, increasing wage levels and investment in education. At the same time, the results reveal notable regional heterogeneity. The AI policy significantly reduces social stability risk in the central and western regions, and areas with moderate digital economy development, but has no statistically significant effect in economically developed and digitally advanced areas. The study also highlights potential challenges, including data governance concerns and uneven technological access, which may offset some of AI's benefits. This research contributes to the literature by linking technological innovation with social governance outcomes and provides policy implications for leveraging AI to promote social stability. It suggests that policymakers should not only invest in AI infrastructure but also address institutional and regional disparities to ensure inclusive and effective risk management. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Duration of depressive symptoms prior to a cancer diagnosis and post-cancer memory function and decline: A longitudinal analysis of the US Health and Retirement Study
Abstract: Introduction Depressive symptoms are associated with increased risk for cognitive decline in the general population, but less is known about how depressive symptoms might influence cognitive aging after a cancer diagnosis in mid-to-later life. We aimed to determine if the duration of depressive symptoms before a cancer diagnosis is associated with post-cancer diagnosis memory function and decline. Materials and methods Data were from 425 adults aged ≥50 with an incident cancer diagnosis from 2004 to 2020 and three waves of depression data prior to their diagnosis in the US Health and Retirement Study. Depressive symptoms were measured biennially using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D; range 0 to 8); a score of ≥3 was considered clinically relevant depressive symptoms. Duration of pre-cancer diagnosis clinically relevant depressive symptoms was categorized as never, 1 time point, or ≥ 2 time points. Episodic memory was assessed from the time of cancer diagnosis as a composite of immediate and delayed recall scores. Multivariable adjusted linear mixed-effects models estimated the association between pre-diagnosis depression duration and post-diagnosis memory function and decline. Results The mean baseline age was 68.9 years (SD: 8.6) and 52.7% were female. In the three survey waves (~6 years) prior to diagnosis, 56.7% (241/425) had no depressive symptoms, 20.0% (85/425) had depressive symptoms at 1 time point, and 23.3% of participants (99/425) had depressive symptoms at ≥2 time points. The mean follow-up time after cancer diagnosis was 6.2 years (SD = 4.7). A longer duration of pre-diagnosis depression was associated with a faster rate of memory decline post-diagnosis (−0.12 SD units/year, 95% CI: −0.22, −0.02). Discussion Increased duration of depressive symptoms prior to cancer diagnosis is associated with faster memory decline post-cancer diagnosis and may be a salient risk factor for accelerated memory aging among older cancer survivors. Authors: Zhang T.; Liao H.; Zhang J.; Bai L.; Li Y.
Title: Cross-modal vision transformer with energy-system priors for interpretable operational pattern discovery
Abstract: The identification of the repeating operating conditions for energy assets — namely, the limited range of states through which any turbine or building passes — forms an essential component of condition monitoring; however, since operating labels are seldom available at scale, the process has to be unsupervised. Progress is hampered by two issues: one-dimensional sequence encoders do not explicitly represent pairwise lag, recurrence, and transition structures that can separate states with similar marginals; moreover, physics-blind clustering can collapse into trivial magnitude groups that lose temporal coherence. We present PRISM, a cross-modal vision transformer that reads the operational segment both as a smoothed picture derived from the signal via the vision transformer branch and as an unprocessed sequence of signals through the selective state-space branch, connecting the two derived perspectives using cross-attention with prior biasing. We present an idealized conditional identifiability result under explicit multi-view and bounded-switching assumptions, while the envelope prior provides only a qualitative complexity rationale. On five public benchmarks involving buildings (the Building Data Genome 2 and REFIT) and wind turbines (Kelmarsh, Penmanshiel, CARE-to-Compare), PRISM brings fault and anomaly detection to a mean AUROC of 0.922 and exceeds the leading contrastive baseline by 0.031 (3.1 percentage points), while improving silhouette from 0.489 to 0.571. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhao Z.; Wu S.; Liu Y.; Cao Y.
Title: Biomass densification-assisted pyrolysis for bio-oil production: structural regulation, product distribution, and fuel-quality trade-offs
Abstract: Biomass pyrolysis is a promising route for producing bio-oil and value-added chemicals, but its practical application is limited by the low bulk density, unstable storage and transportation, poor feeding behavior, and structural recalcitrance of lignocellulosic feedstocks. Biomass densification provides an effective strategy to overcome these supply-chain constraints while also functioning as a structure-regulating pretreatment for subsequent pyrolysis. This review summarizes how compression-induced particle rearrangement, lignin softening and redistribution, pore reconstruction, hemicellulose disruption, and cellulose crystallinity variation affect heat transfer, volatile release, product distribution, and bio-oil quality. The synergistic roles of torrefaction, hydrothermal carbonization, steam explosion, biological and chemical pretreatments, and reactive co-densification are further discussed. These coupled strategies can improve feedstock uniformity and alter product distribution and bio-oil characteristics during subsequent pyrolysis. Their performance varies with feedstock properties, treatment intensity, densification conditions, and reactor operation, so the preferred route also depends on the desired product. Route selection must balance gains in liquid yield, bio-oil quality, or phenolic enrichment against the additional energy input and chemical or solvent recovery required by the process. This review highlights densification-assisted pyrolysis as an integrated pathway linking biomass supply, structural regulation, product-oriented conversion, and sustainable system design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Microbial contamination and hygiene practices in small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses in Vietnam: The effects of two interventions
Abstract: Foodborne diseases impose major health and economic burdens on low- and middle-income countries. In Vietnam, bacterial contamination is common along pork supply chains, particularly within traditional slaughterhouses. These facilities therefore represent key intervention points for improving food safety. This study evaluated the effects of interventions on microbial contamination and hygiene practices across small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses in four provinces of Vietnam. A controlled trial was conducted in 16 small- and medium-scale pig slaughterhouses. Eight slaughterhouses were first randomly assigned to receive a ‘Technique’ intervention (low-cost equipment and training), while the remaining eight served as no ‘Technique’ group. Within both groups, four slaughterhouses additionally received an ‘Incentive’ intervention (practice-rating program with monetary rewards). Microbiological and behavioral data were collected pre- and post-intervention through swabs of workers' hands (n = 128), pig carcasses (n = 192) and structured observation checklists (n = 192). The main effects of the ‘Technique’ and ‘Incentive’ interventions were evaluated using difference-in-differences mixed-effects models. The results revealed that Salmonella prevalence and mean total bacteria count on carcasses did not significantly change (37.5% and 5.4 log10 CFU/cm2 at baseline to 35.4% and 4.7 log10 CFU/cm2 at endline, respectively). Coliforms and Escherichia coli counts decreased across all groups, including the control, a pattern more consistent with seasonal and operational factors than the interventions. Neither intervention was associated with lower carcass contamination, and hygiene practice scores were not associated with contamination. Temperature, slaughtering capacity and workforce size showed mixed associations with microbial indicators. The ‘Technique’ intervention produced measurable improvements in hygiene practices, while the ‘Incentive’ intervention improved practices only in the short-term. While neither intervention reduced contamination, the study documents real-world slaughterhouse conditions and suggests that durable improvement will require sustained, multi-level strategies that combine behavioral change with structural and environmental upgrading. Title: Assessing the techno-economic performance of membrane-based carbon capture and storage in South African coal-fired power plants
Abstract: South Africa relies heavily on coal for electricity generation, making its power sector a major contributor to carbon dioxide emissions. Carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies have been proposed as pathways to mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and environmental impacts. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture system tailored for a South African coal-fired power plant. This study presents a techno-economic evaluation of a membrane-based carbon dioxide capture from a South African coal-fired power plant. The work involves firstly simulating a supercritical coal power plant with a capacity to produce a gross power of 804 MW. Coal characteristics and local ambient conditions in a specified region of South Africa are considered. The resulting flue gas composition and state are determined from the simulation. In a second stage, a membrane system is proposed for carbon capture from the power plant flue gas. To optimise the process, a superstructure-based model is applied. The capture efficiency is set at 90% whilst the product stream consists of 95% carbon dioxide. The cost of the membrane process, transport and storage and ultimately the cost of electricity, is determined. The study shows that an optimal membrane-based carbon capture and storage system in South Africa would result in an additional 10.6% efficiency penalty. The cost of electricity would increase by 131.9% to 152.5 US$/MWh. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Exposing rumor in online networks: A CP tensor-based detection framework
Abstract: With the proliferation of social media, the speed and scope of rumor dissemination have grown exponentially, posing significant challenges to information security and public governance, thus necessitating the development of robust rumor detection methods to address the increasingly complex online environment. Conventional rumor detection approaches, primarily relying on natural language processing or single-modal feature analysis, struggle to capture the complex user interactions and multi-dimensional contextual correlations in social networks, while graph neural network (GNN)-based methods, despite exploiting structural information, remain vulnerable to malicious manipulations and adversarial perturbations, resulting in limited generalization and detection performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes an adversarial training-based rumor detection framework, which integrates posts, authors, users, and comments into a fourth-order rumor feature tensor, leverages a multi-graph regularization joint optimization mechanism within the CP tensor decomposition framework, and incorporates four camouflage strategies under a min-max optimization framework to enhance the model's capability to model heterogeneous relationships and resist adversarial attacks. Experimental results on the PHEME and Weibo datasets show that the proposed framework achieves strong performance and improved robustness compared with the considered baselines. © 2026

Authors: Zhang Y.; Xu Q.; Li Y.
Title: LENS: A graph-based ciphertext semantic retrieval scheme with lightweight representations
Abstract: With the rise of cloud outsourcing and pre-trained language model-driven semantic retrieval, high-quality semantic search over encrypted data remains challenging. Existing schemes either depend on keywords or coarse representations that cannot capture complex semantics, or use high-dimensional dense vectors with linear scanning, causing prohibitive computation. Although tree indexes reduce latency, their rigid partitioning may miss neighbors. Meanwhile, encrypted graph indexes still lack explicit leakage characterization and security adaptation. To address these issues, we propose a ciphertext semantic retrieval scheme that jointly integrates robust semantic representation learning, lightweight vector compression, and graph-based navigation. Specifically, we construct low-dimensional compact semantic vectors for encrypted computation through hard-negative-driven sample construction, global-local collaborative optimization, and multi-level self-distillation. We then build an encrypted graph index whose retrieval workflow is isomorphic to hierarchical navigable small world graph (HNSW) search. We further characterize the leakage boundary of graph-based retrieval and prove chosen-keyword attack security under an IND-CPA secure inner-product primitive. Experiments on the TREC corpus demonstrate a better trade-off among query efficiency, retrieval quality, and scalability than scan-based and tree-based baselines. These results suggest that high-performance ciphertext semantic retrieval requires the joint design of representation learning, index topology, and security modeling. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: A perception-oriented framework for assessing wind turbine aerodynamic noise and operating-parameter effects with normal amplitude modulation
Abstract: To evaluate the effects of wind turbine operating parameters on residents’ perceived annoyance from aerodynamic noise in open rural areas, this study proposes a perception-oriented engineering framework that explicitly accounts for normal amplitude modulation (NAM). Initially, the ISO 9613–2:2024 propagation model is combined with empirical corrections to characterize attenuation across different azimuthal directions around the turbine. A directionally corrected Quasi-AM factor is then introduced to quantify variations in modulation depth under diverse propagation conditions and turbine operations. To better capture subjective human response, a power-law saturation penalty model is developed to adjust the conventional sound pressure level (SPL) by incorporating the contribution of NAM. The resulting NAM-corrected A-weighted sound level is subsequently employed in an annoyance model to evaluate residents’ perceived disturbance. The framework is validated through representative case studies in open rural areas, examining the effects of yaw angle, pitch angle, and rotational speed on the Quasi-AM factor, NAM-corrected A-weighted sound level, and perceived annoyance. Results demonstrate that the framework accurately captures the principal azimuthal variation of NAM, with a mean absolute error of approximately 0.38 dB, NAM-related corrections reach up to 3.60 dB in the main radiation region, indicating that NAM can substantially amplify perceived annoyance even when overall SPL changes are limited. The power-law saturation penalty model exhibits strong fitting performance (R2 = 0.9461), confirming its ability to represent the nonlinear contribution of NAM to annoyance. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that yaw angle, pitch angle, and rotational speed exert distinct effects on the spatial distribution of perceived annoyance. Overall, this framework provides a robust and practical tool for noise-oriented optimization of wind turbine operation and environmental assessment in rural wind farm settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Design of piezoelectric energy harvester with low frequency vibration via multiscale topology optimization

Title: Transforming noncooperative behavior with dynamic trust and weight incentives mechanism in social network group emergency decision making
Abstract: In emergency disaster response, resource allocation conflicts stemming from functional specialization often trigger noncooperative behaviors that severely compromise group decision-making efficiency. Existing social network group decision-making methods face two critical limitations: static trust models fail to capture the dynamic evolution of decision-makers’ credibility, and penalty mechanisms tend to provoke psychological resistance in high-pressure environments. To address these issues, this study develops an incentive-driven consensus framework. The approach integrates subjective trust relationships with objective behavioral similarity to construct a dynamically updated composite trust scoring mechanism, which enables adaptive allocation of decision makers’ weights. Furthermore, it introduces a harmony degree-based feedback mechanism incorporating a maximum individual cooperation willingness detection model to accurately identify noncooperative decision-makers. The core contribution lies in its weight incentive mechanism, which stimulates cooperation by increasing the decision weights of noncooperators, thereby transforming the traditional penalty paradigm into a reputation-based incentive paradigm. Case studies and comparative analyses demonstrate that the framework not only achieves consensus at lower adjustment but also effectively transforms noncooperative behavior into proactive collaboration while ensuring fairness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Granular-ball graph coarsening for graph representation learning
Abstract: Graph coarsening provides an effective approach for improving the computational efficiency of Graph Neural Networks; however, existing paradigms often suffer from a connectivity-semantics gap, where rigid partitioning leads to a resolution mismatch that compromises structural integrity. To resolve these challenges, we propose GBC-GL, a novel granular-ball-based coarsening framework designed for high-fidelity graph representation learning. GBC-GL initiates with a connectivity-driven decomposition to safeguard the global topological skeleton. Building on this, we develop a structure-aware partitioning strategy that synergistically fuses PageRank-derived centrality with multi-scale features to map nodes into optimal granules. Crucially, a dynamic granularity control mechanism adaptively modulates aggregation scales based on local structural complexity, effectively mitigating information collapse in critical motifs while maximizing redundancy reduction. Extensive experiments across 16 benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of GBC-GL: it consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, yielding a 95.94% accuracy on Physics for node classification, 84.80% on YEAST for graph classification, and a 0.628 mean absolute error on ZINC for graph regression. Notably, GBC-GL delivers a 50-fold to 60-fold acceleration compared to spectral-based methods on representative graph classification benchmarks, effectively bridging the gap between high-efficiency graph compression and high-precision predictive modeling. Title: FedLoop: Personalized federated learning with closed-loop feature rectification
Abstract: While Personalized Federated Learning (pFL) has emerged as a promising solution to statistical heterogeneity, existing methods predominantly rely on static client-level adaptation. However, uniform adaptation ignores instance-level heterogeneity, inevitably leading to the under-fitting of outliers and the catastrophic forgetting of well-aligned samples. To address this, we introduce FedLoop, a novel paradigm that shifts from static parameter tuning to dynamic, instance-aware feature rectification. FedLoop establishes a closed-loop feedback mechanism that explicitly decouples rectification into direction and magnitude, utilizing prediction uncertainty as a real-time feedback signal to dynamically modulate the rectification intensity. Notably, our method adds personalization through a local rectifier that is excluded from aggregation, so instance-level adaptation does not alter the aggregated global backbone. Extensive experiments across computer vision, time-series, and NLP benchmarks demonstrate that FedLoop significantly outperforms state-of-the-art pFL methods. Crucially, it achieves rapid convergence with negligible computational overhead and maintains superior robustness even under sparse client participation, effectively resolving the long-standing dilemma between local personalization and global utility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Tian H.; Chen W.; Cheng Y.; Li K.; Lv D.
Title: Mechanism-guided soft sensing of NOx emissions in CFB boilers under heterogeneous noise and multiscale dynamics
Abstract: Accurate soft sensing of NOx emission concentration in coal-fired boilers is important for clean combustion control. However, real CFB operating data contain heterogeneous noise, multiscale dynamic responses, and stage-dependent dominant variables, which hinder extraction of NOx-formation dynamics and degrade soft-sensing accuracy. To address these issues, a NOx emission soft sensing method is proposed. First, training samples consistent with practical disturbances are constructed from differences in the statistical distributions of process variables. Representation consistency between noisy and original data is then constrained in the latent space to reduce abnormal-disturbance effects on basic features. After obtaining basic representations, a variable-scale prior weight matrix is designed using data characteristics and CFB combustion mechanisms. This matrix is combined with data-driven scale weights to fuse multiscale features and extract dynamic information better matched to the actual combustion process. To capture dynamic changes in variable effects, learnable proxy vectors aggregate NOx-related key segments with reduced sequence interaction cost. Variable gating then generates variable weights from proxy temporal representations, dynamically identifying dominant process variables across operating stages. Experiments on practical operating data from a 350 MW CFB unit show that the proposed method achieves an R2 of 0.953 on the test set. Under compound disturbances comprising random, abnormal, and drift noise, the R2 remains 0.896, indicating strong noise robustness. SHAP analysis and internal-weight visualization show that the identified key variables and their time-varying effects are generally consistent with CFB combustion mechanisms. Overall, the proposed method improves the accuracy, robustness, and interpretability of NOx emission soft sensing, and provides a practical auxiliary tool for NOx emission monitoring in CFB boilers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Semantic drift-resistant learning for robust multimodal sentiment analysis with incomplete information
Abstract: With the rapid growth of multimodal user-generated content, multimodal sentiment analysis in real-world applications is increasingly challenged by missing modality information. Existing methods mainly focus on missing information reconstruction or representation completion, while paying less attention to the disruption of cross-modal semantic consistency caused by incomplete information, which leads to latent representation shifts and further induces semantic drift. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Semantic Drift-Resistant Learning framework (SDRL) from the perspective of semantic drift mitigation. Specifically, SDRL models the representation relationship between complete and incomplete states through semantic consistency constraints to restrict the semantic deviation caused by missing information. Meanwhile, a reliability-aware proxy compensation mechanism is introduced to generate proxy semantic representations from non-text modalities and dynamically adjust the contribution of textual and proxy representations, thereby reducing the interference of unreliable information during cross-modal representation learning. Furthermore, a hierarchical consistency optimization strategy is designed to constrain the propagation of semantic drift from multiple perspectives, including local representations, global structures, and task responses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SDRL consistently outperforms existing methods under different missing rates and various missing modality patterns on the MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS datasets. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in mitigating semantic drift and preserving semantic information in incomplete multimodal scenarios. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Shi P.; Chow C.-O.; Wong W.R.
Title: IAEF: Illumination-adaptive event-frame fusion framework for autonomous driving object detection
Abstract: Object detection for autonomous driving degrades under varying illumination. Traditional RGB cameras lose information in extreme brightness and darkness, and existing RGB-event fusion methods do not adapt to how information distribution shifts between modalities as lighting changes. We propose the Illumination-Adaptive Event-Frame Fusion Framework (IAEF), which combines RGB frames and event camera streams through three modules: an Adaptive Multi-modal Feature Extraction Network that cross-enhances features between modalities at multiple scales; an Illumination-aware Complementary-Unique Fusion module that separates unique and complementary features and weights them according to local illumination; and an Event-Frame Fusion Dynamic Detection Architecture that routes scenes through a lightweight or heavy detection path based on learned scene difficulty. On the DSEC-Det dataset, IAEF achieves 82.6% mAP50 and 52.3% mAP50:95, outperforming SFNet by 2.6% in mAP50 among RGB-Event methods and TSD-DETR by 4.2% among RGB-only methods. The gain is largest at night, where IAEF exceeds YOLO-FSE by 6.6% in mAP50, confirming that illumination-conditional fusion provides the greatest benefit when RGB features degrade most. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Tourism's temporal pathways: A deceleration framework
Abstract: This research introduces Tourism Deceleration as a theoretically grounded framework for understanding temporal recalibration in tourism. Building on social acceleration theory and consumer deceleration framework, we conceptualize tourism deceleration as a situated temporal negotiation through which travelers recalibrate pace, attention, mobility, digital connectivity, and presence. Using hybrid deductive-inductive qualitative content analysis supported by LLM-assisted coding and human validation, we analyze 367 unique Reddit posts and 21,554 comments related to slow travel and long-term travel. The findings show that decelerated travel is often negotiated through practical, social, and personal constraints rather than simply chosen as a preferred travel style. Episodic deceleration remains the most explicit form of decelerated travel, while extended duration often intersects with embodied practices, reduced mobility pressure, and selective negotiation of digital technologies. The research note contributes by distinguishing tourism deceleration from slow tourism and explaining how travelers manage time under conditions of choice, context, and constraint. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Design implications of ground properties and operating conditions for geothermal cooling in hot-humid and arid regions: A case study of Bahrain
Abstract: This study assesses the feasibility of geothermal cooling for residential buildings in hot-humid and arid regions, using Bahrain as a representative case. Unlike studies relying on commercial software, this evaluation utilizes a fundamental analytical approach based on ASHRAE guidelines to explicitly demonstrate how individual parameters influence system sizing. Vertical borehole ground-coupled heat pump systems were modeled using local climatic data and subsurface thermal properties. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis was performed to isolate the impact of ground thermal conductivity, diffusivity, borehole spacing, system operating duration, and circulating water temperature on the required heat exchanger length. The analysis identifies ground thermal conductivity and circulating water temperature as the primary drivers for minimizing system footprint, yielding borehole length reductions of up to 46%. The study also quantifies the competing long-term effects on the ground heat exchanger: localized thermal buildup expands the required heat exchanger length by 39% over time, whereas natural groundwater flow provides a stabilizing 36% reduction. Techno-economic analysis indicates that despite elevated capital expenditure driven by drilling cost, geothermal cooling can substantially reduce power consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, while mitigating local ambient temperatures by rejecting heat into the ground. The findings provide a transparent, physics-based design framework that demonstrates the technical viability of geothermal cooling in high-ambient-temperature regions, provided that long-term ground thermal saturation is managed. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Ecological mechanisms and bifurcation dynamics in a mathematical model of African wild dogs
Abstract: The African wild dog (Lycaon pictus) is an endangered species, they live in cooperative packs led by alpha males and females, responsible for breeding and hunting. Young members disperse to maintain genetic diversity, while integration from other packs is welcomed. Pack size is crucial for survival: small packs struggle to hunt and face extinction, whereas large packs face challenges in feeding and raising pups. A mathematical model of predator–prey dynamics includes three roles within the predator population: pups and breeding helpers, active hunters, and dispersing individuals. The study demonstrates the fundamental role of social structure and cooperation in predator–prey dynamics. By incorporating Allee effects and dispersal, the model provides a more realistic representation of population viability in social carnivores and offers quantitative guidance for conservation of endangered cooperative species such as African wild dogs. Bifurcation analysis identifies critical thresholds separating steady and oscillatory regimes: Allee effects lower the threshold for oscillatory onset and amplify their intensity. At the same time, dispersal acts as a stabilizing force, delaying oscillatory behavior and enhancing population persistence. Numerical simulations reveal that Allee effects lengthen and amplify population cycles, particularly during socially dependent life stages, thereby increasing vulnerability at low densities. The existence of stable limit cycles confirms the persistence of oscillatory dynamics and enables detailed characterization of their periods. Furthermore, employing bifurcation analysis, which includes both Hopf and transcritical bifurcations, reveals critical transitions in system behavior as key parameters change. This analysis offers insights into the conditions necessary for stability. © 2026 International Association for Mathematics and Computers in Simulation (IMACS).

Title: Multiscale engineering of lignocellulosic materials: from hierarchical deconstruction to genetic reprogramming
Abstract: The widespread reliance on fossil-derived materials has enabled modern manufacturing but has also driven plastic pollution, carbon emissions, and end-of-life waste challenges. Lignocellulosic biomass offers a renewable and biodegradable alternative, yet its intrinsic heterogeneity has historically limited precise materials design. In this Review, we present a unified multiscale engineering framework for lignocellulosic materials, using wood as an archetypal system to illustrate how structure–property–function relationships can be deliberately programmed from the molecular to the macroscopic scale. We synthesize recent advances in hierarchical deconstruction (top-down processing of cell-wall polymers into micro-, nano-, and molecular building blocks) alongside emerging hierarchical assembly strategies enabled by genetic reprogramming of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin biosynthesis. This convergence enables unprecedented control over composition, anisotropy, interfaces, and transport pathways, yielding biomass-derived materials with tailored mechanical, optical, barrier, and electrochemical performance. We further discuss how these approaches reduce feedstock heterogeneity, improve process efficiency, and align materials development with circular-economy principles, carbon sequestration, and low-impact manufacturing. By linking molecular-level design and genetic modification to scalable processing routes and device-level functionality, this review positions engineered lignocellulosic materials as credible, high-performance alternatives to fossil-based plastics and composites, with transformative implications for energy, environmental, and sustainable manufacturing applications. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: The effects of resilience-oriented workspace interventions: combining social network analysis and organizational quality indicators
Abstract: Although it is known that workspace influences the performance of healthcare teams, there is scarce evidence regarding how to evaluate its implications for resilient performance. Notably, reciprocity between teams, which is crucial for resilience, increased substantially – e.g., RRT↔MOC increased from 57.5% to 80.0%. Changes in collaboration patterns and quality indicators provided complementary evidence that the conditions supporting resilient performance were enhanced. Title: Chemical proximity governs open-world infrared identification of microplastics using dual-evidence calibration

Abstract: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) classifiers can assign familiar polymer labels to spectra outside their training domain. We developed SPARC-FTIR to couple class-conditional conformal prediction with a calibrated distance gate for binary high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP) identification with rejection. Five spectral views were combined in a training-derived principal-component representation. The two gates distinguished label-set uncertainty from departure from the known feature domain and produced four evidence states. After auditing sample identifiers, 776 spectra were retained from an open ATR-FTIR collection; 689 HDPE/PP spectra supported training, calibration and testing, while 87 non-target spectra were withheld. On the primary test partition, closed-set balanced accuracy was 100%, 124 of 139 known spectra were accepted correctly, and 37 of 87 unknown spectra were rejected. Rejection was 29.4% for low-density polyethylene, 33.3% for mixtures and 100% for the 14 remaining unknown spectra. Across 30 group-preserving splits, mean known acceptance and unknown rejection were 92.8% and 36.3%, respectively. Matched spectral-library comparisons showed different subgroup trade-offs in acceptance and rejection. Frozen-model evaluation on two additional libraries showed acquisition-dependent acceptance and rejection. Authors: Wu J.; Chen H.; Long R.
Title: Exploring the evolution of public cognition toward generative AI through sentiment-topic mining and community detection in social graphs
Abstract: The swift advancement of Generative AI(GAI) improves content production efficiency and generates commercial value, yet it presents complex governance issues, including misinformation and technological misuse. To investigate the cognitive evolution of the public and the characteristics of the online opinion ecosystem regarding GAI, this study collected 105,384 GAI-related posts and comments from Sina Weibo between 2023 and 2026. A semantic-topological social graph(ST-Graph) was constructed from textual semantics, engagement feedback, and user profile features, and a Contrastive Learning-based Graph Neural Network(ConGNN) was employed for node representation learning and community detection. Additionally, StructBERT-based sentiment classification was combined with DeepSeek-based key attribute and trigger-word extraction to analyze emotional orientations and cognitive focuses across communities. Experimental findings indicate that ConGNN achieved the highest Silhouette, ARI, and NMI values among the compared methods, while the yearly community partitions yielded Silhouette coefficients ranging from 0.4002 to 0.4476. These results indicate relatively clear separation in the learned representation space and consistent clustering under the evaluated settings, supporting the effectiveness of ConGNN for the constructed ST-Graph. Sentiment analysis shows that public attitudes toward GAI are generally positive, but vary across publishing entities. Public figures garner the greatest number of remarks, with positive feedback from Enterprises constituting the predominant share(49.3%). Government mainly garner neutral feedback(70.9%), however Media and Organizations/Institutions observe a greater share of negative remarks(38.9% and 41.2%). Aspect-level analysis further indicates that public cognition is shifting from early technological expectations and substitution anxiety toward institutional concerns, especially demands for anti-counterfeiting, content credibility, and digital governance mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: The evolving science of negotiation alternatives: New contexts, new perspectives
Abstract: We review the past decade (2016 – present) of empirical research on negotiation alternatives across multiple disciplines, including dyadic bargaining, international trade, and civil conflict interventions. Three themes emerged in our analysis: First, research has focused on how the effects of a negotiator's BATNA (best alternative to a negotiated agreement) are not person-invariant but are instead moderated by the characteristics of the party who “holds” the BATNA. Second, studies are establishing the conditions under which negotiation alternatives can backfire and hurt a negotiator's performance. Third, an emerging stream of research challenges our conventional understanding of BATNA by highlighting its perceptual nature and the possibility that it may exist on multiple levels within a given negotiation. Title: EV-PV-capacitor integration in distribution systems with reliability-cost trade-off: A utility-prosumer perspective
Abstract: This paper proposes a generalized framework for the integrated planning of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS), Photovoltaic (PV) systems, and capacitors in distribution networks using a sequential optimization strategy aligned with practical planning dependencies. The three-stage approach addresses multi-stakeholder economics and reliability–cost trade-offs. To establish the planning baseline, Stage-1,determines EVCS locations that minimize total network losses using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Stage-2 employs Multi-Objective PSO (MOPSO) to size PV systems by jointly optimizing conflicting utility and prosumer Net Present Values (NPVs), considering bill savings, export revenue, lifecycle costs, loss reduction, interruption savings, deferral benefits, FiT expenses, and PV degradation, with the optimal solution selected using Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Stage-3 applies a similar framework to co-optimize capacitor number, size, and placement, balancing investment costs with reliability. Validation on the 33-bus system under probabilistic uncertainties in load, solar irradiance, and EV charging shows reduced losses, improved economic performance, and enhanced stability and reliability. Results demonstrate that the coordinated EV-PV-capacitor solution reduces active power losses by 59.0%, improves minimum voltage by 6.2%, and reduces SAIFI, SAIDI, and AENS by 17.9%, 20.4%, and 30.3%, respectively. Title: Nodding of virtual humans does not necessarily increase customer trust: a temporal analysis
Abstract: Virtual humans can potentially facilitate engaging customer interactions, but remain rarely used in customer service. Their embodiment enables virtual humans to use non-verbal listening cues like nodding. Nodding is theorized to increase trust in virtual humans, but literature on this effect is scarce, inconsistent, and only uses measurements after interactions. This study therefore aims to research how nodding of virtual humans influences customer trust, by (1) studying the following hypothesized mediation: nodding (social cue) triggers perceived responsiveness (social signal), which subsequently increases trust (social response); and (2) studying temporal trust dynamics within a customer interaction using exploratory analyses. An online experiment (N = 429) was performed, using a between-subjects design with two conditions: a virtual human either nodded during listening or did not. To isolate nodding optimally, participants watched a video of a customer interaction: a virtual human advised a customer on a wardrobe. While watching, participants used a slider scale to keep updating their temporal trust in the virtual human. Afterwards, participants answered questionnaires on trust and perceived responsiveness. Results showed that nodding did not increase trust or perceived responsiveness, nor did nodding build temporal trust. Temporal trust was built throughout the customer interaction, mostly when the virtual human was speaking. Exploratory analysis found that nodding increased anthropomorphism. Possibly, nodding did not influence trust because other social cues already caused trust-building. Virtual human developers should therefore be aware that nodding does not necessarily build customer trust. The temporal trust scale was useful for visualizing trust-building throughout customer interaction videos. © 2026 The Authors
