Title: Aquilaria leaves (Thymelaeaceae): A comprehensive review of ethnobotany, traditional applications, phytochemistry, pharmacological activities, toxicity and quality evaluation
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Aquilaria species are well known for agarwood, while their leaves are also used in regional folk medicine and consumed as herbal teas in southern China and Southeast Asia, mainly for inflammatory conditions, infections, and stress-related symptoms. Aims of the review: This review summarizes the ethnobotany, taxonomy, traditional applications, phytochemistry, pharmacology, toxicity and quality evaluation of Aquilaria leaves, and identifies gaps that warrant further investigation. Materials and methods: Relevant literature was collected from Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, PubMed, CNKI, and Wan Fang Data, including journal articles, books, and dissertations. Flora of China and Plants of the World Online were consulted to verify species distribution and accepted botanical names. Chemical structures were drawn using ChemDraw 22.0.0. Results: A total of 185 compounds have been recorded from Aquilaria leaves. Phytochemical and pharmacological studies mainly involve three species, A. sinensis, A. crassna, and A. malaccensis. The major compound classes include flavonoids, terpenoids, benzophenones, organic acids, xanthones, and 2-(2-phenylethyl)chromones, with flavonoids (39) and terpenoids (43) predominating. Pharmacological studies have largely focused on crude extracts, with relatively few investigations of isolated compounds, and have demonstrated anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antibacterial, antidiabetic, laxative, and neuroprotective activities. Available toxicological studies generally indicate low acute toxicity within the tested dose ranges, although evidence on long-term safety remains limited. Quality evaluation has mainly relied on chromatographic profiling and multi-component determination, while standardized quality criteria remain to be established. Conclusions: This review highlights Aquilaria leaves as a renewable and underexplored medicinal resource by integrating evidence from traditional applications, phytochemistry, pharmacology, toxicity, and quality evaluation. However, current evidence is still limited by crude-extract-based studies, insufficient active-constituent characterization, and limited long-term safety and clinical data. Title: Why skilled migrants stay or leave host countries: A belongingness theory perspective
Abstract: While skilled migrants have a high propensity to quit their jobs and leave host countries, little is known about why some skilled migrants leave while others stay. This paper draws on belongingness theory to examine the mediated effects of work and non-work sense of belonging between skilled migrants’ local language proficiency and host country exit, and the moderated effects of work and non-work social support from locals between local language proficiency and both belonging types. Regression analyses of time-lagged, multisource data collected from 159 foreign academics in Japan suggest that local language proficiency was positively related to work sense of belonging, which was subsequently negatively related to host country exit. Furthermore, the positive relationship between local language proficiency and work sense of belonging was stronger when work and non-work social support were high. This paper contributes to the literature by providing a novel perspective on skilled migrants’ host country experiences, shifting the focus from withdrawal cognitions to belongingness and host country exit, and integrating language proficiency into the theory of belongingness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chen Z.; Liao H.; Chen J.; You D.
Title: Complementary recommendation with abductive correction in incremental development
Abstract: Complementary cloud API recommendation, which suggests APIs frequently co-invoked with a given set of APIs, plays a crucial role in enabling efficient incremental development. Existing approaches primarily model API complementarity from co-invocation behaviors but often overlook weak complementary relationships revealed through functional co-occurrence. Moreover, most methods follow a one-step paradigm, directly generating recommendations from learned relationships without further abductive refinement, thereby limiting accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a Complementary Recommendation method with Abductive Correction, named CRAC. CRAC is built on three key ideas: (1) developing a path-based modeling approach that unifies both strong complementary (from co-invocation) and weak complementary (from functional co-occurrence) relations into a unified framework; (2) introducing complementary projection and higher-order reasoning modules that capture complementary and non-substitutable relationships while enforcing complementary-but-not-substitutable constraints; (3) designing an abductive correction mechanism that refines recommendation results through abductive tasks and losses, with an over-correction strategy to ensure effective correction. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that CRAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Further ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of weak complementarity modeling and abductive correction in enhancing complementary recommendation performance. Title: Vulnerable narcissism outperforms grandiose narcissism as a predictor of social comparison orientation, motives, and affect
Abstract: Narcissism is often characterized by feelings of superiority over others, yet little research has directly tested its relationship with social comparison. Existing work has focused mostly on grandiose narcissism, leaving the role of vulnerable narcissism largely unexplored. Thus, it remains unclear how the two dimensions of narcissism contribute to social comparison processes. Across four correlational studies, we tested how facets of narcissism predict frequency of making social comparisons (Study 1, N = 176; Study 2, N = 217), motives for making comparisons (Study 2), tendencies to make upward and downward comparisons (Studies 3, N = 228; 4 N = 300), and affective responses to upward and downward comparisons (Studies 3 & 4). We also explored whether associations between narcissism and social comparison varied across measurement approaches, using three measures of narcissism. Across studies, vulnerable narcissism consistently predicted greater social comparison orientation, self-enhancement motives, higher directional comparison tendencies, and more negative affect following upward comparisons. In contrast, associations involving grandiose narcissism were weaker, inconsistent, and dependent on measurement approach. These findings indicate that vulnerable narcissism is a more robust predictor of social comparison processes than grandiose narcissism and should be centrally incorporated into future research on narcissism and self-evaluation. Title: When imperfect food meets joint consumption: a social influence perspective
Abstract: Drawing on social influence theory, this research examines the interaction effect of food appearance (imperfect vs. perfect) and consumption context (solo vs. joint) on consumers' preferences. Across five experiments, we show that a joint (vs. solo) consumption context exacerbates the reduction in consumers' purchase intention toward imperfect food. In addition, perceived risk and purchase embarrassment mediate this interaction effect on both purchase intention and willingness to pay (WTP). We further identify self-construal and discount information as boundary conditions. Regarding self-construal, for consumers with an interdependent self-construal, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. In contrast, for those with an independent self-construal, these amplifying effects are not significant. In terms of discount information, when it is displayed, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. When it is absent, however, only the effect on purchase intention remains, albeit attenuated. Finally, the presence of discount information shifts the underlying mechanisms of the interaction toward greater reliance on indirect pathways. This research offers practical guidance for promoting suboptimal food in joint consumption contexts. © 2026

Authors: Liang J.; Jin Z.; Li G.; Cheng S.; Luo H.
Title: A JSCC framework with temperature-guided rate learning and multi-domain joint compensation for underwater image transmission
Abstract: Underwater acoustic image transmission faces a mismatch between transmission-cost control and distortion mitigation. Although recent DeepJSCC schemes support variable code lengths, they often rely on auxiliary predictors, fixed temperatures, or simplified fading models, limiting their ability to couple rate adaptation with underwater multipath and frequency-selective fading. To address this problem, we propose an end-to-end JSCC framework that integrates temperature-guided rate learning with latent-domain composite-distortion compensation. The key design is to condition the relaxation temperature on channel state and jointly use retained-count bias and score calibration to learn adaptive code-length selection. Specifically, the framework performs pre-encoding feature recalibration through dynamic channel–spatial coupling and introduces progressive multi-domain latent compensation that integrates physical channel-memory priors with learned spectral and noise-robust calibration for transmission over composite acoustic channels. By coupling this channel-conditioned temperature with a retained-count bias and SNR-aware score calibration, the framework jointly shapes the training relaxation and code-length preferences, enabling content- and channel-state-dependent prefix selection without an external quality predictor or a manually specified SNR-to-rate lookup table. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves superior reconstruction performance and a better quality–bandwidth trade-off than representative separation-based and neural JSCC baselines under dynamic underwater conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: How homophily and sociality propensity influence stakeholder diversity in wildfire risk management networks: an ERGM analysis
Abstract: Recent wildfire management strategies emphasize stakeholder engagement in risk management and prevention as a means of enhancing systemic safety and operational reliability. Despite its growing importance, guidance on how to effectively implement such engagement remains limited. This study addresses this gap by combining Social Network Analysis (SNA) and Exponential Random Graph Models (ERGMs) to examine a sample of 256 stakeholders across seven wildfire management networks in different European countries. The objective is to identify the propensity of stakeholders to form ties, network diversity and structural dependency within wildfire risk management networks. The results make two key contributions to risk and resilience in crisis and emergency management body of knowledge. First, we show that sociality – the propensity of stakeholders to establish connections – is shaped by stakeholder profiles. Second, we find that homophily – the propensity of stakeholders to connect with similar others – emerges across multiple categories alongside structural network effects. We discuss the dual role of these mechanisms that facilitate engagement while simultaneously constraining the diversity of stakeholder types. The findings invite policymakers promoting stakeholder engagement and stakeholder diversity as strategies in risk management and crisis response to critically reflect about the mechanisms through which such engagement can be effectively fostered. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Performance assessment and multi-objective optimization of a novel vehicular power system integrating a direct borohydride fuel cell with an organic Rankine cycle
Abstract: In this study, a novel vehicular direct borohydride fuel cell (DBFC) power system integrated with an organic Rankine cycle (ORC) is proposed. The ORC subsystem recovers the waste heat generated by the onboard DBFC stack to produce additional electrical power. Given the limited engineering maturity of vehicular DBFC systems and low-temperature ORCs, the proposed system is investigated through steady-state theoretical and numerical analyses. The principal contribution of this work is the development of a DBFC-ORC system-level framework for vehicle-oriented power assessment, incorporating comprehensive 4E evaluation and multi-objective trade-off analysis in terms of energy, exergy, economic, and environmental performance.Numerical results show that the integration of the ORC subsystem effectively enhances system performance. At operating temperatures of 70, 75, and 80 °C, the maximum net output power of the integrated system is increased by 9.0%, 8.5%, and 8.0%, respectively, compared with that of the standalone DBFC stack. Moreover, the parametric analysis reveals that the 4E performance indicators cannot be simultaneously optimized through parameter adjustment alone. Therefore, multi-objective optimization is performed to obtain the Pareto-optimal solution set and the corresponding optimal operating parameters. Compared with the baseline case(current density of 10500 A/m2, an operating temperature of 353.15 K, a NaBH4concentration of 1 mol/L, an inlet pressure of 2 atm, anode stoichiometric ratios of 1.2 and cathode stoichiometric ratios of 1.2), the selected Pareto-optimal solution yields an 18.22% increase in net output power, a 14.52% reduction in the levelized cost of energy, and a 97.27% increase in exergy efficiency. Authors: Yan Y.; Wu X.
Title: Can bigger cities be safer? Evidence from criminal indictment data in China
Abstract: This paper examines how city size affects the criminal indictment rate, drawing on panel data from Chinese cities spanning 2014-2021. The results show that bigger cities are associated with significantly lower criminal indictment rates. This finding remains robust after accounting for endogeneity concerns and conducting a series of robustness checks. Further analyses provide suggestive evidence that larger cities may reduce criminal indictments through higher opportunity costs, stronger punishment-related deterrence, and greater moral and social costs of crime. However, this crime-reducing effect is weakened by the presence of migrants, and supplementary evidence suggests that lower levels of migrant social integration in larger urban settings may help explain this moderating pattern. These findings highlight the importance of not only supporting urban development, but also ensuring stronger institutional capacity, effective public security governance, and more inclusive public-service provision. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Xu H.; Nguyen U.; Yang T.
Title: Bubble-cell native fluorescence imaging for high-sensitivity label-free protein quantification
Abstract: Quantification of low-abundance proteins is critical for biopharmaceutical development, proteomics, and biochemical research; however, existing methods often require trade-offs among sensitivity, sample consumption, and workflow simplicity. Ultraviolet (UV) absorbance at 280 nm remains the most widely used method for routine protein quantification because it is rapid, label-free, and reproducible, but its intrinsic sensitivity limits the analysis of dilute samples, particularly when only microliter sample volumes are available. Here we present a high-sensitivity, label-free method for protein quantification based on native fluorescence imaging (NFI) using a bubble-cell capillary, in which a short, enlarged section is incorporated into an otherwise uniform capillary to enhance fluorescence detection. The enlarged bubble-cell increases the optical interrogation volume, generating a localized fluorescence peak that enables robust peak-based quantification, signal-to-noise analysis, and direct visualization of proteins near the detection limit. Using only 1–2 μL of sample, the method achieved experimentally validated limits of detection of approximately 0.005 mg/mL for bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 0.0025 mg/mL for monoclonal antibodies, representing detection limits approximately one order of magnitude lower than literature-reported values for NanoDrop UV spectrophotometry, while preserving the simplicity of a rapid, label-free, and reagent-free workflow. Method validation demonstrated good reproducibility, satisfactory spike-and-recovery performance, negligible carryover, and reliable quantification over the validated working range. The method was further applied to monitor low-abundance fractions collected during monoclonal antibody charge-variant fractionation, enabling detection of minor protein populations that were not reliably detected using a conventional fluorescence plate reader. The combination of high sensitivity, validated analytical performance, minimal sample consumption, and simple peak-based detection demonstrates the potential of bubble-cell NFI as a practical platform for routine protein quantification and characterization, particularly when sample availability is limited or low-abundance protein species must be analyzed. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Arora L.; Jain S.
Title: Seeing through the mind: Explainable multimodal AI for depression detection—A review
Abstract: Depression detection using multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving, transitioning from traditional machine learning techniques to deep learning architectures built on pre-trained transformer encoders. These systems integrate textual, acoustic, visual, and physiological signal streams through early, intermediate, late, and hybrid fusion strategies to improve predictive performance. However, a significant gap persists in model interpretability: post-hoc attribution frameworks (such as SHAP and LIME) dominate recent work, accounting for over 70% of studies published in 2024–2025, while clinician-centered validation is reported in only about 18% of the full reviewed corpus. Consequently, existing explanations are rarely validated for explainability quality dimensions; for example, SHAP attributions are known to degrade under inter-modality collinearity, and reported systems frequently lack alignment with established diagnostic criteria (e.g., DSM-based or PHQ-9 symptom structures). To close the gap between predictive accuracy and clinical utility, this review jointly synthesizes multimodal datasets, feature extraction strategies, machine learning and deep learning taxonomies, fusion strategies, and explainability techniques across 72 included studies. Finally, we outline critical future directions, emphasizing standardized XAI benchmarks, clinician-in-the-loop validation studies, and knowledge-driven neuro-symbolic reasoning. © 2026

Title: Extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods promotes animal-friendly food choices
Abstract: Plant-based foods are essentially animal-friendly, yet they are rarely labelled as such. We examined whether extending animal welfare labels from only being displayed on animal-based foods, towards also being placed on plant-based products, would better integrate plant-based products into the set of options consumers consider animal-friendly. Across two studies in a simulated online supermarket, we hypothesised that extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods would promote animal-friendly choices via increased perceptions of physical opportunity to choose animal-friendly (i.e. availability of animal-friendly foods) and social opportunity to choose animal-friendly (i.e. social norms for choosing animal-friendly foods). We show that extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods not only promoted animal-friendly choices within the animal-based category, but also significantly increased the number of plant-based foods chosen by 28% compared to the control condition, and 33% compared to the condition in which only animal-based products were labelled. Furthermore, we show that the positive effects of extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods persisted even when consumers were exposed to multiple sustainability messages presented through a multidimensional label, which displayed animal welfare, biodiversity, and climate scores. The studies confirmed that label effects on animal-friendly choices were driven by increases in perceived physical and social opportunity to choose animal-friendly. Extending animal welfare labels to plant-based foods is an effective strategy for encouraging animal-friendly food choices. Labels, it turns out, do more than inform: They reshape the physical and social context into a more supportive environment for plant-based choices. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Multi-objective design and optimization of modular methanol production systems integrated with renewable hydrogen and direct air capture
Abstract: A unified multi-objective optimization framework integrating renewable energy generation, electrolyzers, hydrogen-driven electrochemical CO2 capture systems (HECCS), methanol synthesis, and multiple storage technologies is developed to enable joint optimization of capacity configuration, operational scheduling, and flexibility allocation amid coupled electricity-hydrogen-carbon-methanol flows. The evolving roles of HECCS under supply-driven and demand-driven operating modes are evaluated. Under the supply-driven scenario, CO2 storage enables carbon-side buffering and partial temporal decoupling between carbon capture and methanol synthesis. At the minimum-total-annualized-cost Pareto solution, S2 with CO2 storage reduces the total storage requirement by approximately 41.3% relative to S1 without CO2 storage, while maintaining a nearly unchanged total annualized cost. This indicates that CO2 storage primarily restructures the inter-temporal regulation pathway rather than directly reducing system cost. Under the demand-driven scenario, HECCS achieves the lowest total annualized cost relative to conventional thermally regenerated direct air capture (DAC) technologies, demonstrating advantages in energy consumption and system integration. Further analysis shows that the fast response capability of HECCS does not necessarily lead to frequent dynamic operation. Under the economically optimal conditions, the system preferentially employs lower-cost storage to absorb renewable fluctuations and maintain stable operation of capital-intensive process units, whereas HECCS flexibility is activated mainly under storage-constrained conditions. The system-level process flexibility is thus governed by system constraints, economic trade-offs, and coordination among multiple flexibility resources rather than by intrinsic dynamic capability alone. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Sequentially coupled numerical modeling of liquid-propellant-induced in-situ pyrolysis of oil shale
Abstract: The low thermal conductivity of oil shale restricts heat propagation during in-situ pyrolysis, while reservoir stimulation and heating are commonly treated as separate processes, making it difficult to capture the dynamic alteration of heat-transfer pathways after fracture creation. To address this issue, a sequentially coupled numerical framework integrating liquid-propellant deflagration pressure release, main-fracture propagation, discrete fracture-network construction and mapping, reservoir heat transfer, and kerogen pyrolysis was developed. Deflagration pressure was described using the JWL equation of state, main-fracture growth was driven by net pressure, and the resulting main and statistically generated branch fractures were mapped into a three-dimensional reservoir domain. Subsequent thermal and pyrolysis responses were calculated using Robin-type gas–rock wall heat transfer, bedding-anisotropic heat conduction, and distributed activation energy model (DAEM) kinetics, together with sensitivity analysis of the key thermal-boundary parameters and numerical verification of the heat-transfer implementation. For a single 3 kg charge, the peak gas and net pressures reached 83.78 and 77.73 MPa, respectively, and the main-fracture half-length stabilized at 1.49 m within approximately 0.3 s. The fracture network promoted preferential heat transfer from the hot gas into the reservoir, yielding 138.88 kg of cumulative primary shale-oil generation after 1800 s. Three-stage sequential deflagration substantially increased the axial thermal influence. Increasing the stage spacing from 2 to 8 m expanded the axial extent of the T ≥ 310 °C region from 12.12 to 24.12 m, whereas cumulative primary shale-oil generation decreased from 467.33 to 389.33 kg, demonstrating a trade-off between spatial coverage and inter-stage thermal overlap. These results reveal the sequential mechanism of short-duration fracturing, fracture-enhanced heat transfer, and early-stage pyrolysis, and indicate that liquid-propellant deflagration is better suited as a pre-fracturing and thermal-startup technique coupled with subsequent sustained heating rather than as an independent long-term heat source. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: How to move you? The persuasive effects of influencer narrative styles in recommending tourism activities
Abstract: Influencers exert significant promotional effects in tourism marketing; however, few empirical studies have examined how different types of tourism activities can strategically leverage these effects through influencer narrative style. The study analyzes secondary data from 1187 social media posts and conducts three scenario-based experiments with 1438 participants. Results show that personal narrative style is more persuasive for relaxing activities, whereas professional narrative style works better for challenging activities. Moreover, experience resonance and knowledge acquisition are identified as key underlying mechanisms. Title: Should I “stay” or should I “go”? Influence of an anticipated stop on cortical correlates of overground walking
Abstract: Real-world walking frequently requires pedestrians to maintain proactive inhibition to safely navigate unpredictable environments. While cortical modulations occurring during locomotion under environmental uncertainty are well-established, the specific proactive mechanisms underlying this state of inhibitory anticipation remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the behavioral and cortical shifts associated with anticipating a stop during overground walking. Cortical activity and trunk acceleration were recorded using a 32-channel mobile electroencephalography and an integrated accelerometer. Step-1 latency and step-interval variability were calculated via heel strike detection. Gait-phase-related power modulations were computed, and spectral principal component analysis was applied to attenuate artifacts. The results revealed that cautious walking significantly increased step-interval variability, whereas step-1 latency remained unaffected. At the cortical level, left frontotemporal areas exhibited an attenuated and delayed theta desynchronization during the swing phase. Furthermore, centroparietal regions demonstrated an altered temporal profile of alpha and beta synchronization, characterized by enhanced late-stance synchronization and reduced swing-phase synchronization. The present findings suggest that anticipating a potential stop may alter the rhythmic consistency of gait and reorganize phase-specific cortical dynamics. Title: Physics-informed neural network for predicting high-temperature flow stress of 3Cr-1Si-1Ni ultra-high-strength steel
Abstract: In this work, a first application of physics-informed neural network (PINN) to predict the high-temperature flow stress of an ultra-high strength steel is proposed, in which the accuracy, robustness and data efficiency are enhanced. Physical embedding and physical constraints are incorporated into the PINN as guiding physical principles, enabling superior generalisation ability and accuracy compared with the conventional artificial neural network (ANN) and the Johnson–Cook (J–C) model. The PINN also demonstrates significantly improved data efficiency when only small amounts of training data are available, requiring only three datasets for training. In terms of robustness, the PINN is shown to tolerate higher levels of random noise than the ANN. When the standard deviation of added random noise increases from 0 % to 10 %, the absolute prediction error of the PINN rises by only 5.5 MPa, compared with a 30.0 MPa increase for the ANN. These results demonstrate that PINNs provide a powerful framework for the development of constitutive models for metals with improved accuracy, data efficiency, and robustness. Title: Unified task profiling and performance interference-aware Makespan and energy scheduling for cloud robotics tasks driven by an improved genetic algorithm
Abstract: Cloud robotics systems offload heterogeneous, computation- and data-intensive tasks to shared cloud nodes, yet suffer from severe performance interference caused by co-located contention for shared physical resources. Such interference renders idealized execution times unreliable and degrades both Makespan and energy efficiency in conventional schedulers. To enable interference-aware scheduling, it is first necessary to quantitatively characterize the resource demands of diverse tasks and to measure how co-location affects their execution. Therefore, this paper proposes a unified task profiling approach that characterizes CPU, I/O, and memory demands and other key differentiating attributes of eight representative cloud robotics tasks spanning perception, planning, control, and execution. Lightweight, tunable benchmarks are then designed to emulate these resource-access patterns, enabling controlled co-location experiments that construct a quantitative interference-sensitivity matrix. On this foundation, an interference-aware integer programming model is formulated to minimize the weighted sum of Makespan and energy consumption. The main novelty lies in connecting task profiling, benchmark-calibrated interference measurement, and joint Makespan-energy scheduling into a unified interference-aware optimization method. To solve the resulting NP-hard problem, we propose an Improved Genetic Algorithm for Cloud Robotics Task Scheduling (IGA-CTS), which jointly searches task allocation and execution order over the interference-aware scheduling model. In benchmark-calibrated simulation experiments against seven evaluated baselines, no baseline simultaneously achieves lower median Makespan and energy consumption than IGA-CTS at any scale; although some baselines perform better on an individual objective, these advantages are accompanied by inferior performance on the other. Authors: Wang L.; Guan B.; Zhu T.; Zhuang Z.; Chen J.; Bai Y.; Gao J.; Huang Z.
Title: Green methanol production under carbon constraints: pathways, system integration, and deployment conditions
Abstract: Green methanol links low-carbon carbon sources with renewable electricity while retaining liquid-fuel handling advantages. We reviewed 155 publications covering genuinely green routes based on renewable hydrogen and sustainable carbon (CO2 hydrogenation with renewable H2 and biomass- or waste-derived methanol), transitional low-carbon retrofits of fossil-based plants, and less mature electrochemical, photocatalytic, or methane-conversion routes. Retrofits are treated as transitional, not genuinely green, because their carbon remains fossil-derived unless the feedstock is replaced. Authors adopt different system boundaries and functional units, and assumptions about electricity, CO2 supply, plant scale, and cost are rarely identical. Our comparison places each pathway in its operating conditions and avoids ranking isolated performance values. It considers technical maturity, energy demand, life-cycle emissions, levelized methanol cost, feedstock supply, infrastructure, and operating flexibility, and examines when power-hydrogen-carbon integration is justified. The review provides four outputs: a protocol for checking the comparability of techno-economic assessment and life-cycle assessment (TEA/LCA) evidence, conditional rules for evaluating integration, a qualitative regional pathway-selection matrix, and a dynamic-validation gap analysis linking demonstrated performance to availability, load-following, capacity factor, and degradation. No route is universally preferred; a defensible choice depends on consistent accounting and on regional electricity, carbon resources, industrial assets, and end use. The integration comparison distinguishes H2-to-CO2 power-to-methanol (PtM), H2-enhanced biomass/waste conversion, retrofit/carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) in fossil methanol hubs, and multi-source industrial symbiosis, and shows that no archetype is universally superior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhai P.; Su Y.; Cao Y.; Wu L.; Zhang F.; Teng C.
Title: Delay-aware feasibility control for quadrotor path following
Abstract: Safe quadrotor path following under input delay is formulated here as a quantitative feasibility problem in which delayed actuation directly reduces the transverse acceleration authority available for path recovery. The proposed framework establishes an explicit chain from bounded thrust-channel delay and rotor-level actuator limits to a recoverability margin, a curvature-aware path-speed law, and a second-order Lyapunov invariant tube. A delay-matched nonlinear disturbance observer is incorporated to reduce the disturbance-related residual, while a command-rate-limited closed-form speed governor regulates path progression only when curvature demand and delay-induced authority loss approach the available recovery budget. The resulting controller requires no online optimization and is implemented through the same full SE(3) plant, rotor allocation, thrust–attitude mapping, and actuator constraints used in the numerical benchmarks. Across four simulation scenarios, including a certification-oriented case and more demanding nominal, stress, and curvature-varying conditions, the proposed method preserves the implemented feasibility margin while avoiding unnecessary uniform speed reduction. In the stress case, with a delay reserve of 0.703 m/s2 and a certified transverse acceleration radius of 5.724 m/s2, the proposed controller maintains zero negative-margin duration, whereas the fixed-speed disturbance-observer controller and the delay-ignorant proportional–derivative controller exhibit negative-margin durations of 12.76% and 20.56%, respectively. The proposed controller attains a root-mean-square transverse error of 0.195 m at a mean path speed of 3.682 m/s, illustrating the intended safety–progression trade-off rather than minimizing tracking error at the expense of recoverability. These results demonstrate that input delay can be treated not merely as a stability perturbation but as a quantifiable loss of rotor-backed recovery authority that can be compensated through explicit feasibility-based progression regulation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Wang Y.; Liu X.; Deng Y.; Xiao H.; Zhang Y.
Title: Gendering conversational AI in human–AI interaction: The role of interaction context and sexist ideology in shaping user evaluations
Abstract: As human–AI interaction becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, users often infer social identities from AI systems, including gender. Moving beyond the conventional view of AI gender as a static, designer-assigned attribute, this study conceptualizes AI gender as a user-constructed perception shaped by contextual cues. Integrating social role theory, the stereotype content model, and ambivalent sexism theory, we conducted a 2 (AI gender cues: male vs. female) × 3 (interaction context: service-oriented, warm-authoritative, vs. serious-authoritative) between-subjects experiment with Chinese participants (N = 833) to examine how interaction context, perceived AI gender, and sexist ideology jointly shape evaluations of AI competence, warmth, and trustworthiness. The results showed that interaction context significantly influenced gender attribution, with the serious-authoritative condition eliciting stronger gender categorization and a masculinization bias regardless of assigned gender cues. The evaluative consequences of perceived AI gender were also context-dependent: perceived femininity consistently linked with warmth, but was associated with competence and trustworthiness primarily in the serious-authoritative condition. Hostile and benevolent sexism further moderated these relationships in distinct ways. By shifting attention from designed gender to perceived gender, this study offers a more process-oriented account of AI anthropomorphism and demonstrates the value of integrating the stereotype content model with ambivalent sexism theory to explain bias in human–AI evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Adaptive loss-based random Fourier filtering with complementary adaptation: Algorithm design and performance analysis
Abstract: Random Fourier features (RFF) based adaptive filtering provides an efficient tool for nonlinear modeling by approximating kernel mappings with finite-dimensional feature representations. However, existing RFF-based filters typically rely on quadratic loss functions and fixed adaptation strategies, making them vulnerable to non-Gaussian disturbances and limiting their ability to balance convergence speed and steady-state accuracy. To address these issues, a new adaptive filtering framework in the RFF domain is proposed. The framework incorporates an adaptive loss function with an adjustable shape parameter to improve robustness under non-Gaussian and impulsive noise environments. In addition, two RFF-based filters with complementary adaptation characteristics are combined through a convex combination strategy, providing a favorable trade-off between convergence rate and steady-state performance. The steady-state performance analysis of the proposed filtering framework is presented, which characterizes its steady-state behavior under mild assumptions. Simulation results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method under various noise conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Li Y.; Yang M.; Liu S.; Liu L.-B.; Ouyang B.; Bian L.; Sun Y.; Luo J.-L.; Liu S.
Title: Phase-resilient in situ exsolution via thermal pre-stabilization of a double perovskite for high-efficiency solid oxide CO2 electrolysis
Abstract: Metal in situ exsolution endows perovskites with highly active and strongly anchored catalytic sites for high-temperature CO2 electrolysis. However, the concomitant lattice oxygen loss and B-site cation reduction often trigger detrimental phase transitions that compromise long-term durability. Here we demonstrate a chemically non-invasive thermal pre-stabilization strategy that fundamentally resolves this activity-stability trade-off. By elevating the calcination temperature of the double perovskite (DP) Sr1.95Ce0.05Fe1.3Ni0.2Mo0.5O6−δ (SCFNM) from 1100 to 1250 °C, we induce lattice contraction and enhanced BO6 octahedral ordering, which increase B-site cation oxidation states and metal-oxygen bond strength. This robust structure effectively suppresses the DP phase of perovskite transitioning to Ruddlesden-Popper phase during in situ exsolution, while preserving uniformly exsolved NiFe nanoalloys and retaining a higher oxygen vacancy concentration and a stronger CO2 adsorption capacity. As a result, the phase-pre-stabilized NiFe@SCFNM-1250 achieved a current density of 1.72 A cm-2, a maximum CO Faraday efficiency of 98.63% at 1.5 V and 850 °C and a markedly reduced degradation rate of 2.06 mA cm–2 h–1 over 100 h, which outperforming its non-stabilized counterpart by nearly twofold in durability. This work establishes thermal pre-stabilization as a universally applicable paradigm for balancing catalytic activity with structural stability in perovskite-based electrodes, offering a chemical-doping-free route toward durable CO2 electrolysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Hutchinson J.
Author full names: Hutchinson, Joy (60337137000)
Title: The therapy room is not a classroom: Why emotional safety in therapy belongs to the client
Abstract: Emotional safety in the therapy room is a clinical resource that belongs to the client. A growing number of clinicians, particularly those trained in social justice frameworks, feel empowered or obligated to correct clients' use of language deemed offensive. This paper argues that such practices are ethically indefensible and clinically counterproductive. Drawing on meta-analytic evidence on the therapeutic alliance, countertransference management, and core conditions of change, the evidence indicates that corrective responses to client language damage the alliance quality, increase the risk of premature termination, and suppress the very kind of honest disclosure that therapy requires. This paper further examines structural ideological bias in the profession, the contradictions between activist training frameworks and foundational ethics codes, and the misapplication of harm-speech theory to the clinical context. The fiduciary obligation of the therapist, the clinical evidence base, and every major professional ethics code converge on the same conclusion: the counseling room is not a classroom, and the client's psychological safety is not the therapist's to withdraw. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhou Y.; Wang J.; Gao J.; Wang K.; Lu H.
Title: An integrated analytical framework for natural gas pricing: combining multi-source drivers, forecast enhancement, and model interpretability
Abstract: With the global pursuit of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), accurate forecasting and mechanistic interpretation of natural gas pricing have become increasingly important. As a transition fuel in the shift toward a low-carbon energy system, natural gas plays a vital role in balancing energy accessibility and environmental sustainability. However, rising economic uncertainty and geopolitical risks present significant challenges to effective price forecasting and policy formulation. In response, we develop a data-driven analytical framework for natural gas pricing that integrates feature engineering and forecast enhancement to achieve accurate point-interval forecasts and investment timing. Leveraging advanced explainability techniques, the framework systematically uncovers the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in global gas market drivers. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional models in predictive accuracy and reveals important lag effects and interaction mechanisms among influencing factors. These findings validate the framework's ability to support pricing decisions and risk hedging for energy enterprises, and to provide scientific evidence for regional energy policymaking through quantification of heterogeneity. Ultimately, it offers key support for improving resource allocation efficiency and advancing the achievement of SDG targets. © 2026

Title: An agenda for plastics crisis research in the synthetic age
Abstract: This survey synthesizes insights from environmental social sciences to recast the plastics crisis as a structural feature of growth-dependent economies instead of a problem solvable by consumer choice or incremental technologies. Rather than a within-field review of ecological economics, it maps adjacent literatures to specify what this field could study and how, clarifying researchable questions, suitable methods, and tractable indicators. The synthesis foregrounds connections between expansionary political-economic dynamics, globally uneven socio-ecological burdens across the plastics life cycle, and the power and knowledge relations that shape what is produced, measured, and governed. It calls for comparative, mixed-methods, multi-scalar work and for open, standardized data on plastics flows to strengthen causal inference and comparability. Shifting attention upstream—from end-of-pipe fixes to the transformation of provisioning systems—the paper charts lines of inquiry capable of aligning social metabolism with biophysical limits and human needs, providing a roadmap for ecological economics to organize and accelerate research beyond consumer or techno-managerial framings. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Deep sea mining, think tanks, and the politics of expertise
Abstract: Deep sea mining (DSM) is being contemplated in an environment of heightened geopolitical tensions. A confluence of factors has led to securitised framings of DSM, including the centrality of the Pacific as both a potential mining location and a perceived frontline of strategic competition, and the desire of western states to “derisk” from China when it comes to critical minerals. One of the factors shaping how strategic competition is understood and responded to is the role of experts. Within western states such as the US and Australia, think tanks play an important role in shaping narratives, perceptions, and policies relating to defence and foreign affairs. In this paper I will investigate how western security-related think tanks are approaching DSM.I will argue that think tanks are playing a significant role in contributing to narratives of necessity regarding DSM, and that security and strategic competition are the dominant framing of these narratives of necessity. Title: Trade-offs and transitions: A scoping review of structural and discursive power in post-growth interventions
Abstract: The dialectic relationship between the production of post-growth knowledge and ongoing construction of social reality is a complex one, but one that warrants attention. In this scoping review, we respond to the emergent interest in post-growth politics and theories of change. We aim to complement existing reviews of post-growth policy proposals and recommendations with an analysis of peer-reviewed studies on interventions – deliberate attempts by one state, market or civil society actor to influence another. Drawing on a socio-ecological systems leverage points perspective embedded within a political economy inspired mapping of social forces, we develop a conceptual framework for explaining strategic trade-offs made by actors to achieve various forms of depth.Our findings point to asymmetrical relationships between actors-executor pairs and a pattern of neoliberal subjectification in both intervention design and analytical focus. We also find that whilst post-growth interventions can readily achieve discursive depth, it is often accompanied by institutional shallowness and temporal fragility. We conclude with reflections on strategic implications for post-growth researchers and movements. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Hu X.; Li H.; Zhu H.; Zhang J.
Title: Decoding interfacial differences between regioisomeric organic dyes: The role of alkyl-chain conformational accessibility
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Long alkyl chains in dye-sensitized solar-cell sensitizers are commonly regarded as aggregation-suppressing substituents, although their conformational accessibility may influence interfacial organization. Here, DFT, TD-DFT, CREST/xTB conformational sampling, and projected density-of-states (PDOS) analysis were combined to examine the regioisomeric dyes T5-1 and T5-2, for which IPCE maxima of approximately 60% and 85%, respectively, have been previously reported. The T1–T4 reference series shows that π-extension red-shifts absorption while introducing trade-offs in adsorption and charge-transfer descriptors. For T5-1/T5-2, frontier-orbital energetics and alkyl-free dye–TiO₂ coupling are comparable; however, the low-energy T5-1 ensemble favors syn-type chain dispositions, whereas T5-2 has a thermally accessible anti conformer. Thus, conventional backbone-centered electronic descriptors alone do not fully account for their distinct interfacial behavior. Selected interface models associate the T5-2 motif derived from the anti-conformer with more-upright adsorption, stronger local chain-mediated contacts, and larger LUMO resonance broadening. This organization provides a structural basis for reduced electrolyte accessibility and a lower propensity for interfacial charge recombination, while retaining strong dye–TiO₂ electronic coupling. These findings highlight alkyl-chain conformational accessibility as an important factor linking molecular connectivity to interfacial behavior in the T5-1/T5-2 regioisomeric dye pair. Title: Intersectional justice as a guiding principle for feminist ecological economics
Abstract: Ecological economics focuses on provisioning for a good life for all within planetary boundaries. Feminist ecological economists have long highlighted the relevance of unpaid care work, times beyond linear clock time, and social-ecological provisioning towards this same end. In this article, we explore why and how intersectional justice should be a guiding principle for (feminist) ecological economics. Intersectional justice involves recognizing and redressing the discrimination that individuals or groups face due to overlapping social identities, which give rise to structural injustices that undermine the provisioning for a good life for all within planetary boundaries. Through three examples (global care chains, hidden ableist assumptions about ‘work’, and inequitable water access in India) we show that while many areas of feminist ecological economics lend themselves to intersectional analysis, operationalizing intersectional justice as a guiding principle is far from easy in practice. Learning from Black feminisms, disability studies, and feminist standpoint theory, we show how intersectional feminist perspectives can help challenge power structures and institutions that sustain injustices on both epistemic and material levels. This enables the kinds of collaborative action that can bring (feminist) ecological economics into broader acceptance, uniting struggles against various forms of oppression while building economic systems that prioritize the sustainability of life. Title: Designing wave farms to support mangrove restoration: A coupled hydro-morphodynamic and habitat suitability modelling approach
Abstract: Wave farms are increasingly proposed for hybrid coastal infrastructure, offering both renewable energy generation and shoreline protection. However, their potential to enable ecological restoration, particularly for mangrove restoration, remains underexplored. This study presents a novel framework for evaluating how wave farms can precondition coastal zones for mangrove restoration by attenuating wave energy, reducing erosion, and expanding areas of hydrodynamic suitability. Using a schematized coupled depth averaged (2DH) hydrodynamic, spectral wave and morphodynamic model in Delft3D, six wave farm configurations were tested under idealized conditions to quantify wave attenuation, sediment retention, and habitat suitability. Mangrove survivability was assessed through a novel drag-based (Type II) erosion-adjusted uprooting threshold. K-means clustering was applied to field-collected morphological traits to define three distinct seedling groups, enabling species-specific resistance modelling based on frontal area and anchorage. The results show that array layout strongly influences ecological and engineering performance. Some configurations enhanced erosion reduction and created more contiguous planting zones while others expanded the total area suitable for restoration. The proposed framework identifies zones preconditioned for restoration, which can be made viable for planting through interventions such as mud nourishment or raised platforms. This study provides a transferable methodology to support hybrid infrastructure design for climate resilience, ecosystem recovery, and local socioeconomic benefit. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Rapid microwave-assisted synthesis of ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes for cancer catalytic immunotherapy
Abstract: Catalytic nanomedicines face a persistent trade-off between structurally defined active sites and rapid synthesis. A microwave-assisted salt-flux conversion is developed that transforms a bimetallic metal-organic framework precursor within 3 min into nitrogen-doped carbon-supported ZnMn dual-atom nanozymes (ZnMn DAzymes). Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and dual-edge X-ray absorption fine structure analyses support adjacent Zn-Mn sites with an N-dominated ZnMn-N6-like coordination motif. Steady-state kinetics and density functional theory calculations suggest cooperative catalysis: Zn modulates H2O2 adsorption and O-O bond activation, whereas Mn provides stronger H2O2 chemisorption and redox flexibility, jointly enhancing catalase-, peroxidase-, and oxidase-like activities. The resulting cascade decomposes H2O2, relieves hypoxia, generates reactive oxygen species, and depletes glutathione, inducing mitochondrial dysfunction, immunogenic cell death, cGAS-STING-associated signaling, dendritic-cell maturation, and effector T-cell infiltration. Glutathione-responsive Mn2+ release additionally enables activatable T1-weighted magnetic resonance contrast. Combined with αPD-L1, ZnMn DAzymes suppress primary and distal tumors by approximately 90%, reduce lung metastases by 92%, and prolong survival in 4T1 models. Title: Coupled design of a bamboo-shaped cathode flow field and hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer for enhanced performance and multiphysics transport in open-cathode PEMFCs
Abstract: The bamboo-shaped cathode flow field can enhance heat-mass transfer and improve the performance of open-cathode proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, its further engineering application faces two prominent challenges: 1) the effects of the key design parameters on cell performance and multiphysics transport remain unclear; 2) geometry-induced local convection enhancement may aggravate the inherent spatial nonuniformity of the physical fields within the porous electrode assembly and increase the risk of local degradation. To address these challenges, this study first studies the impacts of two key design parameters, the number of bamboo-joint units ( N ) and bamboo-joint indentation depth ( W ), on PEMFC performance and the associated heat and mass transfer in porous electrodes. Furthermore, the flow field is coupled with a hybrid-porosity GDL to improve physical field uniformity while retaining enhanced transport. The results show that moderate increases in N and W strengthen the periodic contraction–expansion effect of reactants within the bamboo-shaped configuration, thereby enhancing shear disturbance and lateral mixing. This promotes faster renewal of the thermal and concentration boundary layers in the flow field and porous electrode, thereby increasing the net water and oxygen transport fluxes and improving heat dissipation. Adjusting N and W contributes to superior open-cathode PEMFC performance by up to 8.10 % and 18.85 %, respectively. Increasing N and W also increases the ideal cathode air-supply power due to the relatively larger pressure drop under otherwise identical operating conditions, indicating a greater relative air-supply penalty. Accordingly, the flow field design requires a trade-off among performance improvement, ideal air-supply penalty, and the uniformity of key physical fields within the MEA. Guided by these mechanistic insights, a coupled design is developed by integrating the bamboo-shaped flow field with a hybrid-porosity gas diffusion layer (GDL). This novel design retains the transport and performance advantages of the bamboo-shaped flow field while further alleviating the inherent limitation of the non-uniform distribution of key physical fields within the porous electrode. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Age-related emergence of behavioral deficits and amyloid pathology in the J20 mouse model of Alzheimer's disease
Abstract: Transgenic mouse models carrying familial Alzheimer's disease mutations are widely used in preclinical research, yet phenotypic variability across age and sex can complicate experimental design and interpretation. Here, we performed an age-stratified behavioral and pathological phenotyping of the hAPP-J20 mouse model using independent cohorts of female and male mice at 3, 6, and 9 months of age (n = 5–21 per group depending on the assay). In parallel, amyloid pathology was quantified using ELISA measurements of Aβ1–40 and Aβ1–42 levels and histological assessment of hippocampal plaque burden. J20 mice exhibited early behavioral alterations detectable at 3 months, including impaired working memory, increased locomotor activity, and alterations in self-care behaviors. Spatial learning alterations were detectable from 3 months, whereas robust spatial-memory deficits became more consistently evident at later ages. Soluble and insoluble Aβ species increased progressively with age, whereas hippocampal plaque pathology was minimal at 3 months and rose markedly at 6 and 9 months. Analyses including sex as an independent factor identified endpoint-specific sex-related effects but did not support a consistent sex-specific trajectory. Overall, non-cognitive and working memory deficits emerge early, while spatial memory impairment and amyloid pathology dominate at later stages. Authors: Quan J.; Guo C.; Wang X.
Title: Collective reinforcement learning and human–machine cooperation in multi-state stochastic games
Abstract: With the growing deployment of artificial intelligence agents in collaborative systems, understanding how they jointly shape cooperative behavior with humans under dynamic environmental conditions becomes essential. Stochastic games provide a natural framework for capturing how environmental feedback shapes behavioral choices and supports the emergence of cooperation. Building on this framework, we incorporate collective reinforcement learning dynamics (CRLD) into a multi-state stochastic game and develop a mixed human–machine population model to examine the emergence and stability of cooperation. Unlike existing models that mainly consider homogeneous learning populations or externally determined environmental states, this framework explicitly captures the feedback interaction among human behavioral responses, environmental state transitions, and machine learning dynamics. Our results show that environmental vulnerability, public-goods incentives, human cooperative inclination and its population share, as well as machine discounting, jointly determine the evolutionary path of cooperation. Cooperative humans increase the likelihood of favorable environmental states, lowering the threshold for machines to learn cooperative strategies. In contrast, defect-prone humans can disrupt numerically stable cooperative states and induce cooperation collapse. Increasing the proportion of cooperative humans also reduces the critical discount factor required for machines to sustain cooperation. These findings demonstrate that human behavior reshapes environmental state transitions and alters machine value evaluation, exerting essential influence on learning and strategy evolution. Overall, this study reveals the mechanisms that sustain cooperation in human–machine systems with variable environmental states and provides theoretical insights relevant to coordination in mixed-agent systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Rural occupational health in Colombia: policy–practice gaps among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca
Abstract: This study examines policy–practice gaps in occupational safety and health (OSH) protection among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca, Colombia. A multi-method design combined 14 semi-structured interviews and two focus groups with an adapted ILO Vision Zero Fund survey administered to 200 agricultural workers. Survey data were analyzed descriptively and through exploratory Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA), and qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated during interpretation. Findings showed multidimensional patterns involving occupational protection, working conditions, health-service availability, agricultural practices, and productive autonomy. These patterns coexisted with informal, seasonal, short-term, day-labor, and subsistence work, limited occupational risk coverage, discontinuous prevention and training, and fragmented institutional coordination. Qualitative findings further highlighted women’s combined productive and care roles, local and traditional knowledge, community participation, and heterogeneity across territorial settings and agricultural practices as relevant to prevention and decision-making. Conventional social protection and occupational risk arrangements centered on formal, contributory employment may not fully respond to dispersed and unstable rural work. Strengthening rural OSH requires integrated, territorially adapted, gender-sensitive strategies linking prevention, social protection, sustained training, institutional coordination, community participation, and productive autonomy. The findings support assessing differentiated and progressive protection pathways, including the feasibility of subsidized occupational risk coverage for more vulnerable workers and small productive units, combined with contributory mechanisms where work arrangements are more stable. By linking worker-level realities with institutional and policy-implementation gaps, this study provides evidence to inform more equitable rural OSH policies responsive to diverse territorial realities in Colombia. Title: Broken bodies in Domestic Spaces: Direct and Structural Violence in an Atypical Mortuary Dataset from Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: A major challenge for the understanding of violence in the past is that our main source of evidence comes from cemeteries, but a significant proportion of the victims of violence are not buried in cemeteries. Iron and Viking Age Scandinavia (c. 500 BCE–1050 CE) is infamous for its emerging warrior ideology and hegemony of violence. Yet, somewhat counter-intuitively, trauma rates have typically been found to be relatively low in cemetery populations. Not everyone was afforded formal burial in cemeteries, however. The BODY-POLITICS project examines a previously neglected mortuary dataset: disarticulated and semi-complete human remains deposited in and around domestic spaces such as longhouses, pits, wells, postholes, and hearths. We report on 12 individuals inscribed with 19 ante- and perimortem traumatic injuries, analysed through osteological, bimolecular and digital imaging methods. The unusual post-mortem history of these individuals, set within a historical context of raiding, enslavement, and ritual violence including potential ‘human sacrifice’, allows us to explore multiple scenarios for inflicted injuries: war-like events (extra-community violence), interpersonal and domestic violence (intra-community violence), and ritual violence. Finally, by integrating trauma patterns, mortuary treatment, and contextual information, we discuss the broader life histories of these individuals and argue that some may have been vulnerable to structural, ‘slow’ violence that compounded over the lifecourse. This study thus contributes to broader discourse on direct and structural violence towards potentially marginalised people, as well as connections between ritualised violence and divergent mortuary pathways. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Masculine honor, social visibility, and safety non-compliance: intentions and approval judgments in high-risk sectors in Turkey
Abstract: Unsafe work in high-risk sectors cannot be explained only by knowledge deficits or weak safety management; workers may also attach reputational meaning to visible compliance. Drawing on honor theory and occupational-safety research on risk perception and social context, this study examined whether masculine honor values (hereafter honor values)—the belief that a man’s worth depends partly on a publicly defensible reputation—were associated with unsafe work intentions, lower perceived risk, and greater approval of safety-rule non-compliance among male workers in Turkish construction and shipbuilding. A worker survey (N = 244) was combined with a within-person vignette experiment in which the focal hazard was held constant while visibility was manipulated and audience identity and prior social comment varied orthogonally. Honor values were positively associated with unsafe work intentions (H1a) and approval of others’ violations (H1b), and negatively associated with perceived risk (H2). Perceived risk partially accounted for the honor–intention association (H3). The association between honor values and approval of non-compliance was stronger when the violation was public rather than private (H4), consistent with a reputational, visibility-contingent account. These findings identify a micro-level sociocultural pathway that complements knowledge- and risk-based accounts of safety decisions. They also suggest that safety communication and supervisory practice should address the social meaning of compliance, while the cross-sectional mediation and judgment-based vignette outcome limit causal and behavioral inference. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Teaching Through Making: |xam and !xun Material Culture of the Bleek and Lloyd Collection
Abstract: At Wits Art Museum (University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa) is a small collection donated to the former Wits Museum of Ethnology by Percival Kirby in 1952. A note in the accession register ties the items into the context of the renowned ‘Bushman researches’ of Wilhelm Bleek and Lucy Lloyd in Cape Town in the 1870s and 1880s, an unusual cross-cultural collaboration with a small group of |xam- and !xun-speaking people against the backdrop of the extreme oppression of San peoples across the southern African region. These objects represent a rare instance of historical material culture of San (‘Bushman’) origin in museum collections being associated with named persons or specific communities of origin. We examine them according to object type—spoon, head ornament, firestick, plaything, arrow and bullroarer—to assess their provenance and approach them ‘biographically’, exploring their community origins and coming into being as specific things, and their being gifted to Kirby by Wilhelm's daughter, Dorothea Bleek. Our ‘relocation’, documentation and contextualization of the Bleek-Kirby collection enables some of the material linkages to be restored, complementing the better-known narratives, making the case for the objects as active participants in the conversations, and enriching understanding of the Bleek and Lloyd Collection as a whole. We examine the significant cultural know-how embedded in these objects and emphasize the creative agency of the |xam and !xun people—|hanǂkass'o, !nanni, Tamme among others—as primary authors and producers of knowledge within the broader intellectual project. The bullroarers in particular reveal some of the affordances of this detailed work, assisted by the ongoing digitization and digital curation of the archive. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Differential frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics and behavioral flexibility in autism like VPA-exposed mice
Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) involves social impairments, repetitive behaviors, and behavioral inflexibility, defined as an inability to adapt behavior to changing contingencies, and is linked to frontostriatal dysfunction. How behavioral training modulates these circuits is unclear, but ΔFosB, a marker of sustained neural activity, may be useful to establish their relationship. The aim was to evaluate frontostriatal ΔFosB expression following prenatal exposure to valproic acid (VPA) and to determine how experience in the midsession reversal (MSR) task modulates posterior ΔFosB expression. CD-1 mice were prenatally exposed to VPA (500 mg/kg) or vehicle. Brains from postnatal day (PND) 30 mice were analyzed to quantify baseline ΔFosB + cells in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), dorsal striatum (DS), and ventral striatum (VS). In the second experiment, mice performed the MSR task for 13 days. Then, ΔFosB was re-evaluated at PND43 to assess experience-dependent changes. At PND30, VPA-exposed mice showed a significant increase in ΔFosB + cells in mPFC, OFC, DS, and VS, suggesting sustained activity-dependent engagement of the frontostriatal circuit. In the MSR task, mice adapted to contingency shifts using mixed strategies, including win-stay/lose-shift behavior and temporal estimation, whereas VPA mice showed less consistent strategy selection after reversal. After MSR, ΔFosB expression in the OFC and striatum of VPA mice normalized to control levels and remained persistently elevated in the mPFC at PND43. Thus, prenatal VPA induces long-term increases in neuronal transcriptional changes, suggesting activity-dependent plasticity in the frontostriatal circuit. Despite these neural alterations, behavioral flexibility was preserved, suggesting circuit-level adaptations underlying ASD-related strategies. Future studies could broaden these results by examining sex differences and characterizing the cellular and molecular changes dependent on frontostriatal ΔFosB dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Negotiation across the social sciences: An interdisciplinary review
Abstract: Psychological investigations have generated numerous insights into how two parties bargain. To build on this literature, we review recent research across multiple disciplines, focusing on aspects of negotiation that have received relatively little attention, namely individual differences, multiparty negotiations, and contextual factors. Insights into individual differences are observed in the developmental psychology, artificial intelligence, and social psychology literature. Investigations in these domains show that young children can think strategically about exchange, that individual differences shape the information negotiators obtain and how they utilize information, and that situational factors can constrain or facilitate the expression of individual differences. Insights into multiparty negotiations emerge from the social networks and political science literature. Investigations in these domains explore novel multiparty dynamics, highlighting the importance of structural position in bargaining, and demonstrating that relationship history can shape coalition formation. Insights into contextual factors emerge from the economic and public health literature. Investigations in these domains challenge assumptions about core negotiation concepts such as power and alternatives. Overall, an interdisciplinary perspective on negotiation complements and enriches psychological understanding, and provides implications for interventions, future theoretical development, and empirical research. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Effects of a design thinking education program for kindergarteners: A mixed-methods study
Abstract: Children as young as three can engage in oral and visual planning when creating tangible objects from materials, yet it remains unclear whether such design competencies can be systematically strengthened in early childhood to cultivate future design thinkers and innovative creators. To evaluate a research-informed design thinking (DT) education program, we conducted a mixed-methods study. The quantitative component involved a quasi-experiment with 133 children ( M age = 5.22, SD = 0.86) from a Chinese kindergarten (intervention group: n = 68; business-as-usual comparison group: n = 65), where the intervention group received an eight-week DT program. Each child’s DT competence was assessed immediately before and after the intervention, followed by play-based interviews with 12 children (six per group). Child-level analyses indicated a statistically significant improvement in overall DT competence favoring the intervention group (Cohen’s d=0.38). However, gains were uneven across specific DT dimensions. Children showed more apparent gains in Empathize, Define, and Prototype, whereas no significant gains were observed in Ideate and Test. Furthermore, the youngest children appeared to show larger gains, whereas gender did not significantly moderate the intervention effects. Qualitative interviews provided insight into the cognitive processes underlying these developmental variations. Together, these preliminary findings may inform DT education research and practice in early childhood settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Han Z.; Zhao F.; Xu H.; Zhang Z.; Wu J.; Zhang Y.; Pan J.; Li M.; Hao Z.; Guan W.; Jiang P.; Luo Y.; Ma X.; Kuang H.; Liu Y.
Title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research
Source title: Spectrochimica Acta - Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: SR-MCUR: A scalable and robust CUR decomposition method for large-scale matrix approximation
Abstract: Matrix decompositions are powerful tools for analyzing and processing large-scale data in computer vision and pattern recognition applications. In particular, CUR decompositions offer several advantages over other factorizations, such as interpretability and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a robust and scalable CUR matrix decomposition, called SR-MCUR, based on deterministic sampling of rows and columns. It addresses the main limitations of a recently developed deterministic CUR method based on the discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM), as it does not require seeing the whole data matrix and only requires computing the singular vectors of a few observed data samples. Two versions of SR-MCUR, SR-MCUR(1) and SR-MCUR(2), are proposed based on selecting the rows and columns simultaneously and sequentially, respectively. We demonstrate that SR-MCUR(2) provides a more stable performance than the existing deterministic CUR methods and is less subject to ill-conditioning. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods. SR-MCUR methods dramatically outperform the existing deterministic CUR methods in terms of computational efficiency, enabling the handling of large-scale datasets on a single machine with limited computing and storage resources. Title: How social media content shapes enrollment intention: Distinguishing firm-generated and user-generated effects through TPB and self-identity
Abstract: The increasing reliance on social media has transformed how prospective students gather and evaluate information when selecting universities. This study examines how firm-generated content (FGC) and user-generated content (UGC) influence students' behavioral intention to enroll in private universities through psychological mechanisms grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and self-identity. Specifically, the study investigates both direct and indirect effects of FGC and UGC on behavioral intention, mediated by attitude toward behavior, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and self-identity. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed, with data collected from 295 final-year high school students in Banten, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that FGC has a significant direct and indirect effect on behavioral intention, whereas UGC does not have a significant direct effect but appears to operate primarily through indirect pathways. Among the mediators, subjective norms emerge as the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, followed by attitude toward behavior and self-identity. In contrast, perceived behavioral control does not significantly influence behavioral intention. The findings suggest that FGC and UGC function through distinct mechanisms. While institutional content can directly shape behavioral intention, user-generated content primarily influences intention through social and psychological processes. These results highlight that the effectiveness of social media communication depends not only on information exposure but also on how information is cognitively evaluated, socially validated, and integrated into individuals' self-concept. This study contributes to the literature by distinguishing between different types of social media content and extending the TPB framework with self-identity in the context of higher education decision-making. The findings provide insights for understanding how digital communication influences complex behavioral decisions in contemporary educational environments. © 2027 Malque Publishing, All rights reserved.
