Title: Extremely lightweight salient object detection in optical remote sensing images
Abstract: Existing salient object detection models in optical remote sensing images (ORSI-SOD) struggle to achieve a trade-off between saliency performance and computational efficiency. To address this issue, an extremely lightweight ORSI-SOD model is designed which operates independently of pre-trained weights. The proposed model incorporates an extremely lightweight trainable backbone, i.e. Octconv Backbone Network (OctNet) that is able to capture high-quality features. Different from commonly used lightweight ORSI-SOD models that introduce the MobileNet series as their backbone, the OctNet achieves this without relying on pre-trained weights. The high-quality features are subsequently fed into a multi-scale feature extraction module (MFEM) and a boundary enhancement module (BEM). The MFEM improves the feature extraction capability for multi-scale salient objects by introducing convolutions with diverse receptive fields. The BEM strengthens the capability in capturing intricate object boundaries within a dual-branch structure. The experimental results on three datasets consistently demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the existing state-of-art salient object detection models in terms of saliency performance and computational efficiency without relying on pre-trained weights. Furthermore, when the input data size is 288 × 288, the proposed model comprises merely 0.93 million parameters and requires only 3.25 billion floating-point operations (FLOPs). Title: Speech-driven dialogic question generation for preschool picture book reading: a cognitive-level-aware spoken interaction system using pre-trained language models
Abstract: The quality of preschool children's language development depends largely on the cognitive level of questioning strategies employed during shared reading interactions; however, existing intelligent dialogic reading systems predominantly rely on fixed question scripts and lack the capacity for dynamic adaptation to narrative context and children's cognitive needs. This study proposes a speech-driven, cognitive-level-aware dialogic question generation system targeting preschool picture book reading scenarios. Title: Cross cultural patterns of linguistic aggression and aggressive combat content enjoyment: A computational study of PUBG reviews across six continents

Abstract: This study explores global patterns of linguistic aggression and appreciation for aggressive combat content as expressed in reviews of PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds (PUBG), analyzing over 18.7 million Google Play Store English language reviews from over 80 countries. Title: EGCG accelerates wound healing in diabetic mice by Notch pathway to enhance epidermis formation
Abstract: Keratinocyte proliferation delay was a prominent clinical manifestation of diabetes, significantly impeding the wound healing process in diabetic mice. The potential therapeutic role of (−)-epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) has been recognized due to its ability to enhance wound healing under diabetic conditions, but the underlying mechanism remained unclear. This study elucidates that EGCG expedited wound healing in diabetic mice by accelerating re-epithelialization and collagen deposition. Remarkably, we observed that EGCG promotes epidermal cell proliferation and enhances wound healing process in diabetic mice. We also discovered an overexpression of the Notch pathway in the epidermal cells of diabetic mice. Interestingly, EGCG effectively suppresses this overexpressed Notch pathway, suggesting a targeted mechanism for its therapeutic effects. Furthermore, the experiments with human immortalized keratinocytes (HaCaT) confirmed that high glucose levels activated the Notch signaling pathway, which was subsequently inhibited by EGCG treatment. In conclusion, our study reveals that EGCG improves wound healing in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mice by targeting the Notch pathway in epidermal cells. These findings offered novel insights into therapeutic strategies for diabetic wounds and highlight EGCG as a promising candidate for treating chronic wounds. © National R&D Center for Edible Fungus Processing Technology 2026.

Title: Environmental performance of hydrogen production via eucalyptus biomass gasification and natural gas steam reforming: A life cycle assessment approach
Abstract: A life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted to compare hydrogen production via steam methane reforming (SMR) of natural gas and eucalyptus biomass gasification under Brazilian conditions. Three scenarios were evaluated for the production of 1 kg of hydrogen: (i) SMR, (ii) SMR with carbon capture and storage (SMR-CCS), and (iii) Gasification-WGS (eucalyptus gasification with water–gas shift reaction). The ReCiPe 2016 midpoint method was applied, with normalization used to identify the most relevant impact categories. Global warming potential (GWP) was confirmed as the most critical category by both midpoint and endpoint results. SMR generated 10.13 kg CO2-eq, SMR-CCS 6.40 kg CO2-eq, and Gasification–WGS 1.30 kg CO2-eq per kg of hydrogen, corresponding to reductions of 36.8% and 87.2% relative to conventional SMR, respectively. Carbon capture reduced the climate impact of the fossil route but did not result in net-negative emissions. SMR-CCS showed higher burdens than conventional SMR in seventeen of the eighteen impact categories assessed, most markedly in water consumption (14.1-fold) and land use (8.5-fold), the latter arising from the biomass-fired cogeneration supplying MEA regeneration heat. Gasification-WGS achieved the lowest climate impact but did not dominate across all indicators: it outperformed conventional SMR in nine of the eighteen categories and underperformed in the remaining nine, most notably in land use (37-fold), water consumption (3.8-fold), marine eutrophication (2.3-fold) and freshwater ecotoxicity (2.2-fold). The comparison therefore describes a trade-off in which the biomass route exchanges carbon and fossil resources for land, water and nutrient pressure. Overall, the results indicate that the preferred pathway depends on which environmental priority dominates in a given region: eucalyptus gasification offers the largest climate and fossil-resource benefit, while carbon capture on the fossil route delivers a smaller climate gain at the cost of increased impacts in nearly every other category. By addressing both climate mitigation and resource sustainability, this study provides guidance for policymakers and industry in developing low-carbon hydrogen pathways adapted to regional conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: How do sustainability capabilities create retail performance over time? dynamic evidence from U.S. and Chinese retailers
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how sustainability-oriented technological innovation, sustainable supply chain management, and corporate social responsibility relate to environmental and manager-reported organisational performance in retail firms over time. Drawing on the natural resource-based view, institutional theory, and stakeholder theory, the study analyses a 12-wave monthly panel of 2410 retailers in the United States and China, comprising 26,998 firm-month observations. A multi-group hierarchical Bayesian continuous-time dynamic structural equation model estimates within-firm relationships, effects over one-, three-, and six-month intervals, time-varying mediation, and country differences. Technological innovation predicts environmental performance in both countries, but it strengthens sustainable supply chain management only in China. Sustainable supply chain management predicts organisational performance in both countries. Corporate social responsibility predicts environmental performance in both countries, while its direct short-run organisational effect is positive in the United States and negative in China. Environmental performance converts into organisational performance, and all three proposed indirect effects emerge, only in China during the focal six-month window. Exploratory analysis identifies integration-driven accelerators, evidence-driven pragmatists, and weakly-coupled drifters. The findings characterise retail sustainability as a dynamic conversion system with country-specific pathways to environmental and organisational outcomes; implications for individual customer responses require separate empirical testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Synergistic non-thermal plasma-catalytic reforming of toluene over hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 catalysts for efficient syngas production
Abstract: Biomass tar reforming is generally constrained by the high energy demand of conventional thermal processes because of the chemical stability of aromatic compounds. In this work, dielectric barrier discharge plasma was coupled with hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 catalysts for the steam reforming of toluene as a representative biomass tar compound. The effects of Ni loading, reaction temperature, and discharge power on toluene conversion, syngas formation, carbon recovery, and energy efficiency were systematically investigated. Among the catalysts, 15 wt% Ni/mHZSM-5 exhibited the best performance because of its favorable Ni dispersion, high proportion of surface chemisorbed oxygen, enhanced reducibility, and balanced acidity distribution. Among the operating conditions investigated, the best overall reforming performance was obtained at 75 W and 525 °C, achieving a toluene conversion of 99.2%, an H2 yield of 48.3%, a CO selectivity of 36.0%, and a gaseous carbon balance of 60.1%. In comparison, conventional catalytic reforming required substantially higher temperatures to achieve lower conversion and syngas production, demonstrating the promotional effect of plasma excitation on aromatic activation and subsequent surface reforming. The highest toluene conversion energy efficiency of 6.5 g·kWh−1 was obtained at 30 W, indicating a trade-off between conversion performance and energy input. The catalyst also maintained high activity during a 48 h stability test, although gradual deactivation occurred because of carbon deposition. Identification of reactive species and by-products suggests the involvement of plasma-generated species in toluene and steam transformation, while Ni-containing sites may contribute to the subsequent conversion of intermediates toward H2 and CO. These results demonstrate that hierarchical Ni/mHZSM-5 is a promising catalyst for energy-efficient plasma-assisted biomass tar upgrading. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Xiao P.-Y.; Li H.; Marwick B.
Title: Characterizing Core Morphology and Scar Patterning Within a Unified Spherical Harmonic Framework
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Lithic cores preserve the most direct evidence of past reduction strategies, yet their analysis still relies largely on typological classifications that are subjective and difficult to reproduce. Recent 3D methods quantify core attributes more precisely, but morphology and scar organization are handled in separate mathematical frameworks, precluding joint analysis of how the two relate. Here we present a unified framework based on spherical harmonics that encodes both core morphology (M-SPHARM) and scar patterning (SP-SPHARM) within a single rotation-invariant, landmark-free space, the latter being the first application of spherical harmonics to scar orientation data. Co-inertia analysis examines their covariation, and harmonic reconstruction renders statistical axes back into interpretable three-dimensional forms. While the methods are complementary, validation on ideal models and experimental cores shows that the scar pattern descriptor resolves finer distinctions among core types than existing metrics, most clearly the radial subtypes others cannot separate. The exploratory analysis on experimental and archaeological assemblages reveals no detectable covariation between morphology and scar organization. We identify core type as the principal factor structuring variation at Sandinggai (Hunan, China). The methods are released as an open-source R package (spharmlithic) with a fully reproducible workflow. More broadly, the framework supports understanding core variability as a continuous techno-morphological space rather than a set of discrete types. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Towards effective multimodal emotion recognition in conversations via joint multi-graph learning and self-distillation
Abstract: Emotion Recognition in Conversation (ERC) is a crucial component of empathetic dialogue systems, enabling conversational agents to comprehend users’ expressed emotions and respond appropriately. In recent years, ERC has increasingly evolved toward multimodal approaches, particularly graph-based ones, that leverage complementary signals to enhance effectiveness. Although these approaches show promise, they face challenges in effectively modeling relational structures, computing the contribution of each modality during fusion, and regularizing unimodal representations to prevent modality bias. In this study, we propose DiGemo, a novel multimodal ERC framework that employs Transformer-based contextual modeling and graph-based learning to jointly capture both sequential dependencies within conversations and complex inter-utterance relational structures across modalities. To effectively balance and exploit multimodal information, we employ an adaptive fusion approach based on the Gated Multimodal Unit to estimate the contributions of each modality. In addition, we integrate a self-distillation training strategy to regularize unimodal representations, allowing each modality to learn from the fused multimodal representation and achieve more stable learning. DiGemo achieves Weighted F1-scores of 74.44% and 65.92% on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness of jointly modeling conversational context, cross-modal interactions, the adaptive contributions of modalities, and self-distillation for multimodal ERC. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: EIMa: Efficient and robust local feature matching with interleaved Mamba
Abstract: The trade-off between accuracy and efficiency remains a fundamental challenge in feature matching. Although recent Mamba-based detector-free matchers such as JamMa achieve remarkable performance in outdoor scenes with low inference latency, their lightweight parameterization and reliance on purely sequential modeling constrain generalization capabilities, leading to significant degradation in complex indoor environments. To address this limitation, we propose EIMa, a novel feature matching framework that effectively balances accuracy and computational efficiency. First, we propose an interleaved scan strategy that spatially interweaves tokens from both views at the feature level to promote high-frequency cross-view interactions. Second, we design a sparse omnidirectional scan scheme coupled with a lightweight global aggregator, which substantially reduces the scan sequence length while preserving a global receptive field. Finally, we introduce an aggregated attention mechanism that synergizes with these scan paradigms to strengthen cross-view global modeling, thereby significantly enhancing generalization in challenging scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EIMa achieves a superior performance-efficiency trade-off, providing an efficient and robust solution for lightweight local feature matching. Title: A bi-objective optimization model to plan vaccination campaigns aided by temporary centers
Abstract: Vaccination campaigns have saved thousands of lives and reached even the world's most remote areas. However, the COVID-19 pandemic significantly changed the strategies for such campaigns. It is now crucial to rigorously consider new factors when planning the operational aspects of these campaigns, particularly for last-mile vaccine dispensing. First, a large share of the population must be vaccinated, with emphasis on vulnerable groups at higher risk. Second, if the virus is highly contagious and capable of asymptomatic transmission, implementing public health measures at vaccination sites becomes paramount. To address these challenges, we propose a bi-objective optimization model to support healthcare decision-making. It defines a schedule for locating temporary vaccination centers and assigning populations to permanent and temporary sites over a planning horizon. Moreover, we formalize and validate a minimum set of properties for a function-based prioritization mechanism to ensure consistent prioritization. One objective prioritizes vaccinating vulnerable groups according to our novel function-based approach, while the other minimizes the operational costs of temporary centers. In the complex environment of a pandemic, the strategic integration and use of temporary and permanent vaccination centers is vital for creating a robust and responsive vaccination strategy. Temporary centers, whose locations are determined by the model, improve access for hard-to-reach groups, contribute to minimizing crowding at permanent sites, and lower infection risks. Our results, demonstrated through a case study, show that the model effectively allocates resources and generates various vaccination plans that cater to different priority levels assigned to each objective, thereby offering valuable decision support. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: ThreatNet: A multi-class dataset and LLM-based framework with class-imbalanced fine-tuning for life threat detection
Abstract: Detecting life-threatening intent in online text is an increasing challenge as social media increasingly influence public conversation. Current models often face challenges related to insufficient data, class imbalance, and domain variability between platforms. This study proposes ThreatNet, a manually annotated multi-class dataset that contains a variety of linguistic indicators and different intensities of threats sourced from multiple online sources. Using this benchmark, we perform a comprehensive empirical evaluation of seven instruction-tuned LLMs (Flan-T5, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-3-4B-IT, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-Instruct-7B, Zephyr-7B-Alpha, Phi-3-Mini-3.8B) and four transformer baselines (BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, DeBERTa). We analyze the impact of class imbalance mitigation strategies, few-shot prompting (0, 4, 8, 16 shots), and model scale. Experimental results, reported with standard deviations over five runs, show that Flan-T5 achieves 85.67% ± 0.81% macro-average F1 on ThreatNet, while LLaMA-3.1-8B attains 97.12% ± 0.38% accuracy on the YouTube-Threat-Corpus. These results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its usefulness for life-threatening intent detection. Title: Current research on catalysts and deactivation mechanisms for methane catalytic oxidation
Abstract: Focusing on the complex marine exhaust conditions with high water vapor, trace sulfur compounds and fluctuating operating loads, this work systematically summarizes the structure–activity relationships and anti-deactivation characteristics of mainstream catalysts for marine methane total oxidation. Among noble metal materials, Pd-based catalysts exhibit remarkable low-temperature catalytic activity, while Pt-based catalysts deliver superior sulfur tolerance under harsh flue gas environments. By contrast, the performance advantages of Rh catalysts are mainly effective for partial oxidation of methane. Beyond noble metals, low-cost transition metal oxides, perovskites, zeolites, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have also been comprehensively analyzed, with emphasis on their modification strategies tailored to improve low-temperature activity, hydrothermal stability and sulfur resistance. This review highlights the rational design and directional optimization of multifunctional catalysts targeting the actual demanding marine working conditions, providing theoretical guidance for the development of efficient and durable marine methane emission control technologies. Title: Social media reading engagement and critical reading proficiency among Vietnamese EFL learners: A correlational study
Abstract: Social media has become a routine source of English reading for university students, yet its contribution to critical reading proficiency remains empirically under-specified in EFL contexts. This study examines the extent to which social media reading engagement and learners’ critical reading orientation are associated with performance-based critical reading proficiency among Vietnamese undergraduate English majors. Adopting a cross-sectional correlational design, data were collected from 100 third-year English majors at a public university in Vietnam using a questionnaire measuring social media reading engagement and critical reading orientation, alongside a performance-based critical reading test targeting inference making, evaluative judgment, and credibility assessment. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson and Spearman correlations, and hierarchical regression. Results showed a moderate positive association between social media reading engagement and critical reading proficiency (r = 0.42), with engagement alone explaining 17.6% of the variance in test performance. When critical reading orientation was added to the model, the explained variance increased modestly to 20.7%, representing a small incremental gain (ΔR² = 0.031). Regression coefficients indicated that engagement accounted for the larger unique share of variance, whereas the contribution of orientation was statistically weaker and sensitive to threshold criteria. Overall, the findings suggest that social media reading functions as a supportive but conditional literacy environment: engagement with English texts on social media is associated with higher critical reading performance, yet its explanatory power remains bounded and insufficient to account for substantial individual differences. The study underscores the need for restrained pedagogical expectations regarding informal digital reading and highlights the importance of instructional mediation in fostering critical reading development in digitally saturated EFL contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: “How can I help you learn?” Incorporating emotions into parents' support of young children's self-regulated learning at home and school during prolonged crisis
Abstract: Background: Parents apply their knowledge of cognition, emotion, and behavior (metacognition, metaemotion, and metabehavior) to provide children external regulation to achieve learning goals. Aims: Two studies examined how parents' metaprocesses shape children's self-regulated learning (SRL) strategies through external regulation (other-regulation and co-regulation) in distance and in-school learning. Study 1 Method: Mothers (N = 357) were surveyed regarding their own and their 1st–3rd graders’ SRL in three cohorts: Cohort 1 (in-school learning; pre-COVID-19); Cohort 2 (distance learning; COVID-19 first lockdown); and Cohort 3 (in-school learning; post-lockdown). Results: Mediation coefficients were estimated for parent metaprocesses associated with their children's SRL, mediated through external regulation. In distance learning, parental metaemotion, metabehavior, and co-regulation were positively associated with their children's SRL. Co-regulation was positively associated with emotion SRL-reappraisal for Cohort 2 and Cohort 3. Study 2 Method: Parents (n = 311; 49% fathers) were surveyed while their 1st-3rd grade children were in distance learning (Time 1: COVID-19 third lockdown) and in routine in-school learning (Time 2) in a repeated-measures design. Their children (n = 143) reported on social, math, and language abilities at Time 2. Results: Cross-lagged models investigated Time 1 and Time 2 associations within- and across-time effects using complex mediation models. Metaprocesses were linked to SRL, math, and language skills through other-regulation, whereas metaprocesses were associated with SRL strategies and social skills through co-regulation. Conclusion: Parent metaprocesses were positively associated with prompts guiding their children's SRL strategies and learning outcomes. Findings highlight links between metaprocesses and child emotion SRL-reappraisal through co-regulation. © 2026

Title: Breaking the NOx-soot trade-off in compression ignition engines at mid-load with high-percentage n-Pentanol blends through charge cooling and oxygenation
Abstract: The quest for sustainable and environmentally friendly fuel alternatives has significantly increased interest in exploring higher alcohols, particularly n-pentanol, as a promising oxygenated biofuel option for internal combustion engines. This study meticulously analyzed the combustion, performance and emission characteristics of a 60% n-pentanol/40% n-dodecane blend, designated P60D40 , and n-dodecane, D100, utilizing computational fluid dynamics simulations. Here, n-dodecane was used as a surrogate for diesel fuel. The analysis was conducted under a variety of engine operation control parameters to ensure a thorough understanding of their behaviors. The results showed that under identical operating conditions, the indicated thermal efficiency of the P60D40 blend was 47.94%, which is higher than the 44.32% for D100. Furthermore, the equivalent indicated specific fuel consumption for the P60D40 blend was 169.89 g/kWh, in contrast to the 183.77 g/kWh of D100. This represents a 7.55% reduction in fuel consumption, highlighting the efficiency benefits of using n-pentanol as a fuel component. In addition to the performance improvements, the study also found significant reductions in harmful emissions. Specifically, emissions of soot, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide were reduced by 91.46%, 86.18% and 12.91%, respectively, compared to D100. The utilization of a 60% n-pentanol blend demonstrates considerable potential, as it not only meets the selected Euro VI reference limits of 0.4 g/kWh and 0.01 g/kWh for NOx and soot, respectively, but also offers excellent performance characteristics. Moreover, it shows the capability to effectively address the common trade-off between NOx and soot emissions, particularly under mid-load operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A dynamic fusion enhanced trajectory distillation framework for multi-view classification
Abstract: Multi-view classification incorporates multiple views to improve classification performance. However, in real-world scenarios, different views often exhibit unequal informativeness, which poses challenges to learning discriminative representations. Existing fusion methods mainly rely on weighting or attention mechanisms, which can mitigate redundancy but still lack explicit semantic guidance for discriminative representation learning. To address this issue, we propose a novel dynamic fusion enhanced trajectory distillation method for multi-view classification. Specifically, we develop a dynamic fusion module that enhances discriminative learning and adaptive multi-view fusion by incorporating label embeddings as explicit semantic guidance. Furthermore, we propose a trajectory distillation strategy to prevent the risk of inference-time label leakage while ensuring effective knowledge transfer, thereby enabling the student model to inherit the representation capability of the teacher model without relying on label information during inference. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently achieves superior performance and learns more discriminative representations for multi-view classification. Title: Acceptability-driven adaptive migration promotes cooperation in human–machine hybrid population
Abstract: Sustaining cooperation in social systems is persistently challenged by the destabilizing influence of selfish behavior. In human–machine hybrid networks, interactions between artificial agents and human participants introduce both new obstacles and new opportunities for maintaining sustained cooperation. Social interactions are strongly influenced by individuals’ affective assessments of peer strategies. Here, “acceptability”—the degree to which an individual's strategy is supported by neighbors—drives emotion-based migration toward more favorable positions. By contrast, cooperative robots are unaffected by such emotional evaluations and instead base their migration decisions on either success-driven movement or random exploration. Inspired by this notion, the Acceptability-Driven Adaptive Migration (ADAM) model is proposed. Monte Carlo (MC) simulations demonstrate that the proposed ADAM model effectively fosters the emergence of cooperative strategies. In populations where ordinary nodes migrate according to acceptability, increasing the proportion of cooperative robots markedly enhances cooperation, while node density exerts minimal influence except at extremely high or low levels. When a greater share of robots follow the success-driven rule rather than random exploration, cooperation is further reinforced. Network-level average acceptability improves when robots constitute either a minority or a majority of the population. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Compitus K.
Author full names: Compitus, Katherine (57209096834)
Title: Categorical exclusion: Speciesism as a neglected dimension of prejudice in cognitive behavioral therapy
Abstract: While CBT and ABA have recently begun to grapple with their own internal biases, the field's ethical framework remains stubbornly anthropocentric. Scholarship increasingly addresses systemic prejudice in research, yet speciesism—the hierarchical valuation of life based on biological category—is still largely ignored as a socio-political ideology. This is a significant oversight: psychometric evidence suggests that speciesism is not a fringe belief, but is cognitively rooted in Social Dominance Orientation (SDO), much like racism and sexism. Consequently, the discipline's human-centricity should not be viewed as a neutral default, but as an active ideological framework that prioritizes control over clinical insight. This is visible in the pathologization of vystopia. By framing the profound distress caused by industrialized animal exploitation as a cognitive distortion, clinicians commit a form of microaggression that can fundamentally weaken the therapeutic alliance. Title: THE VALUE OF RECOMMENDATIONS FROM SOCIAL MEDIA ANALYSTS IN ONLINE INVESTMENT COMMUNITIES
Abstract: This study examines the informational value of stock recommendations issued by social media analysts through the lens of Self-Determination Theory (SDT). Using comprehensive data from Seeking Alpha, we demonstrate that these recommendations significantly predict abnormal stock returns over a two-month horizon, with no subsequent reversal, suggesting that they convey incremental information not captured by sell-side analysts or textual sentiment. Guided by SDT, we further show that predictive accuracy varies systematically with analysts’ motivational contexts. Recommendations are more informative when issued by analysts identified as traders, whose direct financial stakes deepen the internalization of extrinsic incentives, and by analysts with high comment-section engagement, where interactive feedback supports needs for competence and relatedness. Conversely, predictive ability declines with longer platform tenure, consistent with motivational saturation as psychological needs become satisfied, and with higher posting frequency, where cognitive overload undermines need satisfaction. Finally, we find that both editorial selection and user-driven engagement effectively identify recommendations with greater ex-post informativeness. In an era of information abundance in online investment communities, our SDT-grounded analysis offers investors guidance for signal extraction and provides platform designers with principled insights for fostering higher-quality content ecosystems. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. Title: Advanced oxidation pretreatment of biomass for preparation of carbon-based adsorbents with high CO2 capture performance
Abstract: The advanced oxidation system composed of FeSO4·7H2O/K2S2O8 was adopted to pretreat pear tree branches, before carbonization and KOH activation, successfully producing porous carbon materials with excellent CO2 adsorption performance. The sulfate radicals ((Formula presented) ) produced in the pretreatment process were capable of effectively breaking the chemical bonds between cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin, leading to a decrease in the degree of polymerization. Concurrently, they convert the raw biomass into a loose, rough, lamellar architecture, accompanied with abundant oxygenic functional groups introduced. After 10 regeneration cycles, the material maintained 98.7 % of its initial adsorption capacity, demonstrating excellent cycling stability. Mechanistic analysis indicated that physical adsorption played a primary role in the uptake process, with pore filling playing a key role. The pretreatment strategy significantly reduced the amount of activator required, while achieving synergistic optimization of the microporous structure and surface chemical properties and also markedly enhanced the CO2 adsorption performance of the resulting adsorbent. Title: Obsessive compulsive disorder and depression change in a residential setting with the added role of quality of life
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Co-occurring depression is a common aspect of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) presentation, however, there are mixed conclusions on how depression influences treatment outcomes. Many studies lack accounting for temporal precedence, and do not account for both within person and between-person effects. This study utilizes a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model to examine changes in OCD and depression over the course of intensive/residential treatment for OCD in a sample of 311 adults. We build on past research by including quality of life in the model as well. Autoregressive paths reflected OCD symptoms predicting future OCD symptoms across time, and depression symptoms predicting future depression symptoms in the context of treatment. Contrary to past research on OCD and depression, there were no significant cross-lagged effects in either model except for a positive relationship between quality of life at week 1 and OCD at week 2. Limitations include constraints on generalizability given the unique nature of the study sample and patient population from which it is drawn. Future studies examining the nature of the relationship between OCD and depression with newer statistical models, examining other constructs involved in the OCD and depression relationship, and utilizing holistic and recovery-focused outcome measures are indicated based on these findings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: High-efficiency near-infrared TADF OLEDs with dipole moment selective matching and exciton management strategy for polar hosts
Abstract: Near-infrared organic light-emitting diodes (NIR-OLEDs) based on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) are promising for optical communication, bioimaging, and biomedical sensing, but face a persistent trade-off between long-wavelength emission and device efficiency. Here, the previously reported NIR-TADF emitter APDC-DTPA is used to examine a dipole-moment-selective host-screening strategy together with energy-level matching and device-level exciton/charge management. Changing the host from BCP to PPF and DPEPO shifts the film PL maximum from 690 to 724 and 729 nm, while the corresponding photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY) are 28.87%, 24.89%, and 15.17%, respectively. These results show that host polarity can stabilize the charge-transfer excited state, whereas HOMO/LUMO alignment, triplet energy, and transport properties jointly determine device suitability. PPF therefore provides the most practical spectral-photophysical compromise and is selected for device optimization. Transient electroluminescence further reveals intermediate carrier-response dynamics for the PPF-based device. Subsequent insertion of CzSi/TSPO1 blocking layers and optimization of the hole-injection/transport architecture improve exciton confinement and charge balance. The optimized MoO3/TAPC:MoO3/TAPC device exhibits EL centered near 730 nm, a maximum luminance of 220 cd/m2, a maximum radiance of 4.86 W/sr/m2, and a measured peak EQE of 5.81%, corresponding to an approximately 175.4% increase relative to the initial PPF-based Pristine device (2.11%). Title: Structure-aware optimization of recurrence thresholds for multi-sensor kinematic time-series image representations
Abstract: Recurrence plots (RPs) provide a nonlinear representation of time-series dynamics, but their structural characteristics are highly sensitive to recurrence-threshold selection. Conventional fixed-threshold and fixed-recurrence-rate strategies prescribe the recurrence condition without explicitly evaluating the structural properties of the resulting representation. To address this limitation, this work proposes a structure-aware recurrence-threshold optimization framework for multi-sensor kinematic time-series image representations. Rather than directly optimizing the absolute threshold ε, the target recurrence rate (RR) is formulated as a representation-design variable and evaluated using a normalized and regularized multi-metric Recurrence Quantification Analysis (RQA) objective. A kinematics-aware recurrence representation is constructed from acceleration magnitude, angular-velocity magnitude, jerk magnitude, and angular-acceleration magnitude to characterize both steady and transient motion dynamics. Experiments on UP-Fall show that the proposed formulation identifies a stable, non-boundary recurrence-density regime around the prior-informed RR≈0.08 region and produces systematic structural differences relative to fixed, nearest-neighbour, and stability-based threshold-selection methods, with large effect sizes for several RQA descriptors. Independent validation on SisFall confirms systematic RR dependence of the evaluated recurrence structures under different sensing and acquisition conditions, while demonstrating that the numerical operating regime is dataset-dependent rather than universally fixed. Downstream fall-versus-ADL validation further shows that the complete kinematics-aware representation achieves 85.58% accuracy, 88.89% recall, and 84.83% F1-score using RQA features, while direct KA-RP image classification achieves 0.9609±0.0089 accuracy and 0.9902±0.0044 AUC. Overall, these results support recurrence-rate selection as a structure-aware representation-design problem and provide a data-dependent framework for constructing density-controlled recurrence representations for wearable kinematic time series. © 2026

Authors: Wen J.; Pu Q.
Title: Integrative genetic analyses of circadian chronotype and autism highlight regional co-association at 17q21.31
Abstract: Chronotype and sleep problems are common in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but their genetic relationship remains uncertain. We integrated published cross-trait LD score regression (LDSC), brain eQTL-based summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), SNP-based two-sample MR, two-step mediation MR, secondary parallel SMR, and Bayesian colocalization using UK Biobank chronotype GWASs, the iPSYCH/Psychiatric Genomics Consortium ASD GWAS, and GTEx v8 brain eQTLs. The published LDSC estimate was negative for morningness-coded chronotype and ASD (rG = −0.199). Primary ASD-outcome SMR identified 50 gene-tissue pairs representing 24 genes at the exploratory multi-SNP PSMR < 0.001 threshold; none met Bonferroni significance. Fifteen candidates occurred in the LD-rich 17q21.31 inversion and are not independent gene discoveries. Secondary eveningness-outcome SMR tested all 24 candidates in matched tissues; 22 had PSMR < 0.05, but GTEx reuse made this descriptive. At 17q21.31, the prespecified p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁵ favored distinct variants (PP.H3 = 0.785) over one shared variant (PP.H4 = 0.126). H3 dominance strengthened at p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁶ and reversed only at the permissive p12 = 1 × 10⁻⁴, equal to p1 and p2. Eveningness-oriented IVW MR was positive (β = 0.270, P = 0.008), whereas robust estimators were attenuated; no mediation was detected through sleep duration or insomnia complaints. These analyses prioritize exploratory regional associations without proving shared causality or mechanism. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: An investigation of the neglected serial mediators and moderators of green inclusive leadership in the hospitality industry
Abstract: Using social exchange and social identity theories as the theoretical umbrella, our paper proposes and tests the neglected serial mediators and moderators of green inclusive leadership (GIL) using time-lagged data gathered from hospitality employees. Authors: Yuan B.; Sun Y.; Sun H.
Title: RAGM-track: Typed graph memory for reliability-conditioned identity reasoning in RGB-T multi-object tracking
Abstract: Identity errors in RGB–thermal MOT can persist beyond the degraded frame because unreliable associations committed to memory distort later matching and identity recovery. Existing trackers encode history as homogeneous queues, prototypes, or track queries, limiting control over evidence retrieval and updating. We propose Reliability-Aware Graph Memory Tracking (RAGM-Track), which represents each identity as a persistent typed graph of identity, appearance, motion, reliability, occlusion, and hard-negative evidence. Reliability-derived degradation adapts the candidate-retrieval budget, while modality reliability and cross-modal conflict modulate association scores and protect memory writing, limiting error propagation and supporting re-entry recovery. On VT-MOT, RAGM-Track achieves 41.37 HOTA, 43.19 DetA, 42.76 IDF1, 50.83 MOTA, and 1124 identity switches. Among published results reproduced in our benchmark comparison, it reports the highest HOTA, DetA, and MOTA and the lowest identity-switch count, while its cross-pipeline IDF1 remains below PFTrack (47.25) and ACNTrack (48.04). Memory-slot-controlled ablations support the benefits of typed organization. On UniRTL-MOT, RAGM-Track improves AssA and IDF1 over untyped attention memory by 1.42 and 1.67 points with shared MCTrack detections, and 3.28 and 2.58 points with oracle boxes. These results show that governing memory evolution complements the interpretation of current observations in robust multimodal tracking. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Multiple pathways to social bonding through music
Abstract: Music is widely recognized for its ability to foster social bonding. Yet, while research has largely focused on interpersonal movement coordination, other ways in which music can connect people have received comparatively less attention. We argue that music-related social bonding extends beyond coordinated movement and emerges through multiple forms of imagined and shared social experience. We propose a conceptual framework comprising three interrelated pathways: interpersonal coordination, shared social experience without explicit behavioral coordination, and imagined social experience during solitary listening. Across these pathways, music recruits interacting mechanisms of temporal prediction, self-other integration, reward processing, and social-cognitive alignment that together promote social closeness, affiliation, and prosocial orientation. We further highlight how musical features and individual differences shape these processes. By integrating evidence from music psychology, cognitive neuroscience, and social psychology, this framework broadens current perspectives on how music promotes social bonding and identifies conceptual and methodological directions for future research. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Novel starch/agar smart bioplastic incorporated with dual-encapsulated anthocyanin for shrimp freshness monitoring
Abstract: A dual-encapsulation strategy for anthocyanins (as the active core) was proposed, using chitosan hydrochloride and carboxymethyl chitosan (90, 160, and 240 kDa) as the external shell and β-cyclodextrin as the internal shell. Authors: Qiao H.; Feng S.; Wang J.; Zhang F.; Li F.
Title: THDiff: Joint modeling of social and temporal factors in hyperbolic space for time-aware information diffusion prediction
Abstract: Information Diffusion Prediction (IDP) aims to forecast how information spreads among users on social platforms at a micro level. Most existing methods emphasize social relations while overlooking fine-grained temporal dynamics, even though both factors are essential to diffusion. Moreover, both social and temporal factors exhibit hierarchical and imbalanced structures, posing challenges for effective modeling via conventional Euclidean methods. In particular, our analysis of real-world diffusion data reveals highly irregular and heavy-tailed time-interval distributions, suggesting the need for refined representations that can accommodate such imbalanced patterns. While hyperbolic geometry has demonstrated strong capability in capturing hierarchical social influence, its potential for modeling temporal imbalances remains largely unexplored. Motivated by these observations, we propose a novel time-aware hyperbolic diffusion prediction model (THDiff) that jointly models social and temporal factors within a unified hyperbolic framework. Specifically, THDiff uses a rotation-assisted hyperbolic embedding to construct user representations that encode global hierarchical social influence. Building on these representations, it leverages hyperbolic attention to construct cascade representations from both social and temporal perspectives and fuses them through a hyperbolic Hawkes process, enabling comprehensive modeling of complex dynamic diffusion dependencies. By jointly modeling social and temporal factors, THDiff effectively predicts not only who will be activated but also when diffusion events are likely to occur. Extensive experiments across four real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing methods, achieving up to 8.2% and 10.9% improvements in Hits@1 and MRR, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Multifunctional polyurethane enabled by halloysite nanotubes: Combining robust self-healing, high recyclability, and superior wear resistance
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Developing advanced intelligent materials that integrate long service life, high reliability, and sustainable recyclability remains a critical unresolved challenge in the field of high-end equipment. Conventional polyurethanes, constrained by their intrinsic molecular structures, struggle to reconcile mechanical performance with self-healing capability. Guided by a molecular-nanoscale multiscale structural design paradigm, this study designs and fabricates a novel polyurethane composite through a ternary synergistic strategy involving dynamic covalent bonds, multiple hydrogen bonds, and rigid nanotubes. Title: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COIN: CLICKBAIT’S INFLUENCE ON CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION IN SOCIAL MEDIA
Abstract: As social media increasingly operates within algorithm-driven attention economies, clickbait has become a pervasive engagement tactic. However, prior research has not fully explained the psychological mechanisms linking clickbait to downstream consumer behavior. Existing studies have also largely treated clickbait as an isolated persuasive cue, overlooking its dynamic interactions with other elements in social media ecosystems. Drawing on psychological reactance theory (PRT) and uses-and-gratifications theory (UGT), this study develops an integrated framework to examine when clickbait harms versus facilitates consumer responses. Across four experiments, we test a sequential mediation model in which perceived intrusiveness and advertising avoidance transmit the effects of clickbait on purchase intention. We further introduce message appeal congruence as a key boundary condition. The results indicate that clickbait does not uniformly produce negative outcomes. When headline-induced motivations align with the gratifications delivered by the content, perceived intrusiveness and reactance are attenuated. When they are misaligned, advertising avoidance increases and purchase intention declines. Title: Semantics-aware truth discovery based on semi-supervised representation refinement
Abstract: Data scientists are facing the urgent need to build a robust data integration pipeline for heterogeneous data from multiple sources. Existing truth discovery algorithms consider textual values as categories, ignoring semantic ambiguity. This work seeks to answer the Semantics-aware Truth Discovery problem: How to incorporate semantic information into truth discovery methods? We tailor an off-the-shelf tabular representation method for multi-source observations as a Basic Representation Model (BRM). However, as an unsupervised model, BRM falls short in dealing with inadequate local semantic information in multi-source observations. To mitigate this issue, we construct a semi-supervised hyperparameter search strategy for representation refinement. We also propose warm start and pruning strategies to accelerate hyperparameter search. Empirical evaluation on three real world datasets shows that S3TD outperforms existing truth discovery state-of-the-art algorithms by 3.07% on average, and can enhance the performance of existing truth discovery algorithms by up to 8.17%, both in absolute error rate. Title: Stepwise salting-out and freeze-thaw strategy enables robust conductive polyvinyl alcohol hydrogels via interfacial synergy for multifunctional wearables

Abstract: To address the intrinsic trade-off between mechanical robustness and ionic conductivity in polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogels arising from structural heterogeneity, this work presents a stepwise salting-out and freeze-thaw cycling strategy to fabricate high-performance composite hydrogels with synergistic interfacial interactions. Title: Social consequences of emotional expressions in negotiation
Abstract: Negotiation is integral to social life. Whether we focus on exchanges between individuals, groups, organizations, or nations, negotiation is the most common and constructive way of making deals and solving disputes. Negotiations can spark intense emotions, which in turn shape negotiation processes and outcomes. Here, we review research on the social consequences of emotional expressions in negotiation. We summarize evidence regarding specific single emotions (e.g., anger, happiness, disappointment, sadness, fear, guilt, shame, pride, hope) as well as alternative (patterns of) emotional responses (e.g., empathy, emotional ambivalence, mixed emotions, alternating emotions, indifference) across levels of analysis (interpersonal, intragroup, intergroup). Our review indicates that emotions can have both favorable and unfavorable consequences, depending on critical moderators (e.g., information processing, perceived appropriateness) and the focal criterion (e.g., monetary gains, social outcomes). The richness of the empirical record underlines the importance of investigating discrete emotions (rather than positive vs. negative affect) and defies simple conclusions about the (dys)functionality of emotions. Emotional expressions can help or hurt negotiators’ outcomes depending on goal prioritization (e.g., maximizing individual outcomes vs. maintaining positive relations) and the social context. We call for research outside the lab to gain insight into real-world consequences of emotional dynamics in (intergroup) negotiation, mediation, and diplomacy. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: ASD-FCGCN: A biologically interpretable graph convolutional network for ASD diagnosis from rs-fMRI
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition traditionally diagnosed through subjective behavioral assessments. Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) provides a potential pathway for objective neuroimaging biomarker discovery; however, existing deep learning methods often struggle to integrate neurobiological priors with data-driven representations. This study aimed to address these limitations by developing a biologically interpretable graph-learning framework for rs-fMRI-based ASD classification. Methods: We propose ASD-FCGCN, a biologically informed graph convolutional network validated on 871 subjects from the ABIDE dataset. The method systematically integrates neurobiological priors with graph learning. Specifically, prior-weighted functional connectivity matrices are constructed to generate hemisphere-specific representations. Title: Machine Learning-Assisted optimization of acetylene Dual-Fuel combustion using Copper oxide (CuO) Nano-Enhanced waste Plastic Oil in Compression Ignition (CI) Engine
Abstract: In this study, an experimental and machine learning-assisted investigation was conducted on a modified single-cylinder direct-injection Compression Ignition (CI) engine operating in acetylene dual-fuel mode using copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticle-enhanced waste plastic oil (WPO) blends. The proposed approach integrates waste-to-energy fuel utilization, catalytic nano-additives, high-reactivity gaseous combustion, and data-driven predictive modelling within a unified sustainable combustion framework. Experimental investigations were performed using WPO10 and WPO20 blends containing 50 and 100 ppm CuO nanoparticles under acetylene flow rates of 5 and 10 LPM. Among all tested fuel combinations, A5WPO10Cu100 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a maximum brake thermal efficiency of 33.12 %, corresponding to an 8.27 % improvement over diesel, together with a 21.03 % reduction in brake specific energy consumption. The optimum fuel also reduced HC, CO, and smoke opacity by 41.46 %, 47.62 %, and 43.58 %, respectively, while A10WPO10Cu100 produced the highest combustion intensity with a peak heat release rate of 68.9 J/°CA, maximum cylinder pressure of 90.5 bar, and minimum ignition delay of 8.75 °CA, indicating enhanced premixed combustion and catalytic oxidation. Although NOx emissions increased under higher acetylene induction due to elevated combustion temperatures, the overall combustion efficiency and emission trade-off were significantly improved. To further establish predictive capability, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models were developed using the experimental dataset. Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy with R2 values ranging from 0.995 to 0.999 and prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, confirming its robustness in predicting nonlinear combustion, performance, and emission characteristics. The integrated experimental and machine learning framework demonstrates that CuO nano-enhanced WPO coupled with acetylene induction is a promising strategy for improving CI engine efficiency while simultaneously advancing intelligent combustion optimization for sustainable transportation applications. To further enhance predictive capability and intelligent engine diagnostics, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) were developed using experimentally measured combustion, performance, and emission parameters. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior nonlinear prediction capability with prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, coefficient of determination (R2) approaching 0.995–0.999 for major engine responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The Influence of Tswana Cosmological worldview and Sacred Beliefs on the Spatial Organization of Traditional Settlements: A Study of the Setswana Traditional Space kgotla
Abstract: This study examines how Tswana cosmology and sacred beliefs shaped the spatial organization, social structure, and geography of traditional settlements, focusing on the Setswana kgotla as the central sociopolitical, ritual, and spiritual space. Although the kgotla has undergone substantial functional and physical transformation through colonization, modernization, and contemporary planning, its historical development provides important insight into the principles underlying Tswana settlement planning. Using an interpretive qualitative approach based on historical documents, classic ethnographic literature, comparative spatial analysis, field observations, and oral accounts from six historically significant Tswana villages in Botswana—Kanye, Mochudi, Molepolole, Maun, Serowe, and Ramotswa—this study investigates the sacred and social principles governing settlement organization, including the location of the kgosi’s ward, the centrality of the kgotla, geographic setting, cardinal orientation, hierarchical ward structure, spatial configuration, and threshold treatments. The findings show that traditional Tswana settlements were shaped not only by practical and defensive needs but also by a cosmological order in which authority, ancestry, community, environmental relationships, and protection were expressed through space. Rather than serving solely as a traditional court, the kgotla functioned as the symbolic center where the moral, political, and sacred dimensions of Tswana society converged. The study argues that Tswana spatial organization is best understood as a dynamic system shaped by cosmology, environmental knowledge, and historical change rather than as a fixed symbolic structure. It further demonstrates that precolonial Tswana settlement planning embodied an Indigenous system of spatial knowledge rooted in concepts of hierarchy, enclosure, ecology, and social affiliation. Reconsidering the cosmological foundations of the kgotla therefore provides valuable insights into Indigenous settlement planning and contributes to broader discussions of culturally grounded, context-responsive approaches to spatial organization. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: The viral deviation: a quantitative analysis of social media engagement metrics on non-compliant flight deck behaviors
Abstract: Background Normalization of Deviance (NoD) is a well-documented organizational failure mode in aviation, yet its propagation through digital ecosystems remains unexplored. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) highlights a critical mentorship vacuum due to pilot retirements, and social media platforms increasingly serve as informal training environments. This study introduces the concept of Algorithmic Normalization of Deviance- ANoD, hypothesizing that recommendation algorithms systematically reward and amplify “gray-zone” cockpit behaviors that erode sterile flight deck protocols. Method We conducted a stratified netnographic analysis of 150 high-visibility aviation videos (N = 150) across Instagram Reels, split between algorithmically recommended content (n = 100) and curated influencer content (n = 50). A novel coding framework operationalized compliance (Compliant vs. Gray Zone vs. Deviant) and incentive structures. Engagement metrics were analyzed to quantify the algorithmic advantage of non-compliant behavior. Results The analysis reveals a directionally consistent “Viral Deviation” pattern rather than a statistically decisive one. Gray-zone recordings (i.e., technically legal but procedurally borderline) comprised 57% of the sample and attracted higher engagement than compliant content, although this difference was small and did not reach conventional significance (d = 0.24, p = 0.11). The clearest signal emerged between content sources: algorithmically surfaced posts showed significantly higher interaction rates than curated influencer posts (d = 0.31, p = 0.029), a small but statistically significant per-view advantage for content promoted directly by the recommendation system. Structural incentive analysis further indicates that monetization pressures co-occur with increased gray-zone production, structurally analogous to a parallel, shadow curriculum associated with conditions that may facilitate drift. Conclusion The study identifies statistical associations, not causal relationships, and the downstream behavioural impact on pilots is hypothesised from the algorithmic-pattern evidence rather than directly measured. Within those bounds, social media algorithms constitute a structurally unmonitored distribution channel whose observed associations with gray-zone content amplification are consistent with a normalisation-of-deviance feedback mechanism operating beyond current regulatory oversight — an association that warrants urgent empirical validation and proactive governance. We propose a shift from prohibition to risk-stratified governance, recommending that regulators distinguish between handheld (high-risk) and mounted (managed-risk) devices, and integrate digital algorithmic literacy into ab-initio pilot training to counter this new systemic threat. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Automatic design of flow channel for PEMFC based on space-weighted topology and multi-objective optimization
Abstract: To address the severe concentration polarization in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) under high current density, caused by oxygen transport limitation and water management imbalance, this study proposes a three-dimensional automatic flow channel design framework integrating topology optimization and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). A multi-physics coupled model is established, with average current density, current density variance, and pressure drop selected as optimization objectives. The weight space is systematically explored through Latin hypercube sampling combined with simplex mapping, and a BP neural network surrogate model is trained based on COMSOL-MATLAB high-fidelity simulation data to enable efficient global optimization. The results reveal a pronounced nonlinear trade-off among the three objectives. Single-objective optimization improves current density but significantly increases pressure drop, while conventional empirical weighting schemes fail to achieve balanced performance. The optimal compromise solution (w1 = 0.571, w2 = 0.286, w3 = 0.143), identified using the TOPSIS decision-making method, achieves a 5.04 % increase in peak power density compared to the conventional structure, while significantly enhancing oxygen distribution uniformity and water management capability. Furthermore, the lateral flow intensity ratio demonstrates a fundamental transition of oxygen transport from diffusion-dominated to convection–diffusion coupled mechanisms. This study provides a systematic and data-driven optimization framework that eliminates empirical bias in weight selection, enables automatic generation of complex flow channel structures, and the optimal structure’s discovery mechanistically reveals the embryonic form of single-channel optima, offering new insights for designing high-performance PEMFC flow fields. Title: Spectral graph filter bank fusion for multimodal rumor cascade representation and detection
Abstract: Rumor detection on social media is inherently a multi-source information fusion problem that involves heterogeneous signals from textual content, user interactions, and temporal dynamics. Existing approaches often underexploit the global structural patterns encoded in rumor propagation graphs. In this work, we propose a unified multimodal fusion framework, termed Rumor Graph Filter Net (RGFN), which integrates multimodal representations with learnable spectral graph filtering. Specifically, post content embeddings derived from a pre-trained language encoder, user social relation representations obtained via self-supervised contrastive learning, and propagation timestamps are jointly transformed into the graph spectral domain using the Graph Fourier Transform (GFT). To adaptively capture discriminative propagation characteristics, we design channel-wise graph filter banks based on Chebyshev polynomial approximations, enabling frequency-selective enhancement and noise suppression. The filtered spectral responses are projected back to the spatial domain through the inverse GFT, followed by a simplified hierarchical multi-view graph pooling mechanism to obtain robust graph-level representations across scales. The final classifier operates on fused multilevel features for rumor identification. Experiments on two real-world rumor datasets, Twitter and Weibo, show that RGFN achieves the highest F1-score among the baselines and performs competitively on other metrics. Specifically, RGFN outperforms the best baselines on Twitter and Weibo by 4.9% and 1.4% on F1-score, respectively. The proposed framework offers a principled integration of graph signal processing and multimodal information fusion for social media credibility assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning for drug–drug interaction prediction
Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–drug interactions (DDIs) is vital for patient safety and therapeutic efficacy. Recently, DDI prediction methods based on graph neural networks and multi-source heterogeneous drug information have made progress. However, most existing multimodal DDI prediction methods still fail to fully integrate multi-source heterogeneous drug information and effectively exploit the complementary information across different modalities, making it difficult to fully capture the sequential, structural, and semantic characteristics of drugs, thereby limiting the quality of drug representations and DDI prediction performance. To address these limitations, we propose MHGCL, a Multi-source Heterogeneous Data Fusion with Graph-Aware Dual Contrastive Learning framework, designed for DDI prediction. Initially, we construct a comprehensive drug representation by integrating four modalities: drug SMILES sequences, protein target sequences, molecular graphs, and a biomedical knowledge graph (KG) to holistically capture and incorporate the sequential, structural, and semantic information of drugs. Next, we design a graph-structure-aware adaptive subgraph extraction strategy that selects the optimal sampling method based on the structural properties of the KG, and propose a dual contrastive learning mechanism to enhance the quality of feature representations for both molecular graphs and KGs. Finally, we construct a cross-modal self-attention fusion module that achieves dynamic interaction and deep integration of heterogeneous modality features. Experimental results on three real-world drug datasets demonstrate that MHGCL significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, validating its effectiveness for DDI prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Ensemble of deep architectures for SWARM AI-based decision-making
Abstract: This work studies how an artificial agent can participate in swarm-based decision-making alongside human experts by learning collective decision dynamics. We formulate this problem as a multimodal sequential prediction task that combines two complementary sources of information: (i) spatiotemporal interaction traces generated by experts through the HANS web platform and (ii) the corresponding image. We propose a hybrid architecture with an LSTM branch for interaction sequences and a WideResNet branch for image encoding, followed by feature fusion and joint optimisation. The model predicts the evolution of the collective decision at each time step, thereby acting as an autonomous swarm AI agent that receives the same evidence as a human participant. We evaluate the approach on four use cases from environmental microscopy and biomedical imaging: diatoms, cyanobacteria, HER2 and Ki67. The analysis considers interaction-level prediction error, measured by RMSE, and decision-level metrics, including precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score and balanced accuracy under Top-k settings. Across the datasets, the model achieves low interaction error and strong balanced accuracy, while the temporal analysis shows that it captures meaningful convergence patterns in expert consensus. These results support the feasibility of hybrid multimodal models for embedding artificial agents in collaborative decision environments. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: HAD-TAM: Health insurance anomaly detection via truncated affinity maximization with degree-normalized scoring
Abstract: Substantial financial losses are incurred annually as a result of medical insurance fraud, driven by subtle behaviors such as false diagnoses and over-prescription. Although heterogeneous graph structures can be exploited by existing graph neural network-based methods, they often rely on manually selected meta-paths, and the identification of structural anomalies remains a persistent challenge. To address these challenges, Health insurance Anomaly Detection via Truncated Affinity Maximization (HAD-TAM) is proposed as a health insurance fraud detection method, wherein degree-normalized anomaly score-guided meta-path selection is first combined with dual-threshold edge pruning to capture structural anomalies. First, the meta-graph with the highest degree-normalized anomaly score is selected by the model to highlight structures potentially indicative of fraud. Second, non-homophily edges are iteratively pruned by the model using both global and local thresholds to suppress noise and preserve meaningful structure. Finally, the neighborhood affinity of normal nodes is maximized by the model to better separate them from anomalies and improve fraud detection accuracy. Experimental results show that HAD-TAM outperforms eleven advanced baseline methods on two real-world medical insurance datasets, achieving a 2.41% improvement in AUROC and a 1.06% improvement in AUPRC. Furthermore, it exhibits good generalization to public datasets such as Amazon and Reddit. © 2026

Title: Overcoming Digital Twin Blindness: An event-triggered edge–cloud architecture using quantized TinyML
Abstract: Maintaining synchronization between physical assets and their Digital Twin (DT) typically requires continuous data transmission, which becomes challenging in bandwidth- and energy-constrained Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. Continuous data transfer introduces a trade-off between update frequency, state accuracy, and communication overhead. To address this challenge, an edge–cloud cooperative architecture is proposed for event-triggered DT synchronization using a quantized Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) model. An ultra-lightweight INT8-quantized separable convolutional autoencoder is deployed at the edge. This model performs on-device sensor fusion and triggers synchronization when significant deviations in the physical state are detected. During periods without edge transmissions, a cloud-hosted forecasting model predicts and maintains the DT state. The proposed approach is evaluated using the SKAB, CMAPSS, and MNIST datasets. Micro-benchmark results show that the TinyML gatekeeper is compressed to 10.77 KB and consumes only 0.0058 mJ per inference, resulting in an 11.9 times reduction in memory footprint and a 45 times improvement in Age of Information compared to conventional synchronization methods. Cloud-side experiments further show that predictive state reconstruction preserves DT fidelity while reducing communication overhead by more than 85%. End-to-end evaluations show that the proposed framework significantly extends the Pareto frontier of DT synchronization. The system operates at a low bandwidth utilization of approximately 54.2%, reduces univariate synchronization error by over 71%, and achieves a perfect synchronization for multivariate anomaly tracking with RMSE of zero for 8-dimensional data. Overall, the framework mitigates the Digital Twin Blindness problem inherent in static polling approaches and provides a scalable synchronization strategy for next-generation IIoT systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Achieving superior piezoelectric temperature stability in Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3-based piezoceramics via mixed phase boundary engineering
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: A long-standing challenge for Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3 (BNT)-based ceramics is that constructing a single morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) makes it difficult to simultaneously achieve high piezoelectric constant d 33 and superior piezoelectric temperature stability, which hinders their industrial applications. Herein, a novel strategy is proposed to mitigate the above trade-off by designing a mixed phase boundary strategy that integrates the multi-MPB components (abbreviated as M-BNT) to construct polymorphic polar domains. By this strategy, the M-BNT ceramic not only possesses a high d 33 of 180pC/N and a large depolarization temperature T d of 145°C, but also exhibits outstanding thermal stability of in-situ d 33. The competitive residual stress related to the mismatch of shrinkage rate and coefficient of thermal expansion during sintering and cooling, provides the driving force for the development of polymorphic polar domains. Our work offers a viable strategy for developing BNT-based piezoceramics that simultaneously exhibit a high d 33 and superior piezoelectric temperature stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Determination of discount rates in business valuation and public project evaluation: A systematic review from the perspective of international finance and financial theory
Abstract: The discount rate plays a central role in business valuation and public project appraisal because it links risk to the valuation of future cash flows and guides the efficient allocation of resources. However, the global literature lacks methodological consensus and shows significant divergences between private and social approaches, as well as between developed and emerging economies. The present study aims to synthesize the main theoretical and empirical approaches used to determine discount rates from the perspective of international finance. A systematic literature review was conducted following the prisma protocol. Searches were conducted in scopus, web of science, sciencedirect, ssrn, and jstor, using boolean search strings related to “discount rate”, “wacc”, “capm”, “social discount rate”, and “country risk premium”. Studies published from 2000 to 2025, in english and spanish, were included. Only studies with a clear methodological foundation in finance and economics were considered. The analysis was carried out through a qualitative thematic synthesis. The reviewed literature indicates the predominance of the wacc and asset pricing models as the primary references for estimating private discount rates, and reports the increasing use of multifactor models and country risk premiums in the international context. For public projects, the literature identifies two main approaches: the social rate of time preference and the social opportunity cost of capital. The studies also suggest substantial heterogeneity across countries, with generally higher discount rates in emerging economies. No single discount rate is universally applicable; instead, its estimation depends on the local institutional context, the objectives of the investment, and the nature of the risks being evaluated. Title: BCF-CDAN: bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network for multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition with EEG-fNIRS
Abstract: Emotion recognition is essential for affective brain-computer interface (BCI), yet poses significant challenges. Specifically, emotion processing involves complex temporal dynamics and spatial brain networks. Therefore, it’s difficult to decode human emotions. Furthermore, individual differences limit the generalizability of cross-subject emotion recognition. In addition, the feasibility of EEG-fNIRS for fine-grained emotion recognition remains underexplored. To address the above issues, this study proposed an interpretable multimodal cross-subject emotion recognition model—the bidirectional cross-modal fusion and conditional domain adversarial network (BCF-CDAN). The proposed framework explicitly exploited the high temporal resolution of EEG and the high spatial resolution of fNIRS. Specifically, modality-specific convolutional neural networks were first employed to emphasize the temporal information of EEG and the spatial information of fNIRS. A multi-stream module and a one-stream module were then designed to achieve cross-modal fusion. The multi-stream module employed bidirectional cross-attention to capture interactive correlations between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features, while the one-stream module used self-attention to learn a global discriminative representation. Subsequently, a conditional domain adversarial network (CDAN) combined with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss was applied to achieve cross-subject distribution alignment. Results on the two self-collected EEG-fNIRS datasets, TMVED3 (three-class task) and TMVED8 (fine-grained eight-class task), showed that BCF-CDAN achieved cross-subject accuracies of 80.14% and 53.13%, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, the interpretability analysis revealed cross-modal dependencies between EEG temporal features and fNIRS spatial features. Overall, the approach leveraged modality-specific strengths, offering a generalizable and interpretable strategy for brain signal integration.
