Title: Effect of walking slope on cognitive performance. Electrophysiological evidence of dual-task interference
Abstract: The neural basis of cognitive–motor dual-tasking (CMDT), which involves the simultaneous performance of motor and cognitive tasks, has received increasing attention. However, the electrophysiological impact of walking complexity on concurrent cognitive performance remains unclear. This study examined how walking slope modulates cognitive performance and event-related potentials during a visuomotor discrimination task requiring a simple manual keypress response to target stimuli while walking on a treadmill. Twenty healthy adults (20–36 years) completed the task under three slope conditions (downhill −11%, flat 0%, uphill +11%) while electroencephalogram was recorded. Behavioral results showed preserved accuracy across conditions, with slower response times during downhill walking relative to uphill walking. Early sensory processing was strongly affected by locomotor complexity: both uphill and downhill walking elicited larger P1 amplitudes and reduced N1 amplitudes relative to flat walking. In contrast, late cognitive processing indexed by the P3 was largely preserved, although the differential P3 was selectively reduced during uphill walking, suggesting selective redistribution of resources under the highest energetic and cognitive load, consistent with a possible capacity-sharing account. Uphill walking was perceived as the most physically and cognitively demanding condition, while the lowest mean state-anxiety score was observed after uphill walking. Overall, these findings indicate that locomotor complexity selectively modulates early sensory and attentional processing during CMDT, while higher-order decision processes appear relatively preserved. The results are consistent with models of flexible resource allocation and provide insights relevant to the design of motor–cognitive training and rehabilitation protocols. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chen W.; Yuan H.; Li S.; Ye M.
Title: DMoA: Dynamic Mixture of Adapters with Feature-Enhanced Fusion for UAV Visible-Infrared Object Detection
Abstract: Visible-infrared (RGB-IR) object detection has attracted significant attention in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based applications, such as disaster search and rescue, intelligent surveillance, and battlefield target tracking. However, the quality of RGB and IR modalities may vary substantially under different environmental conditions, causing one modality to become unreliable and leading to suboptimal feature enhancement and fusion. To address this challenge, we propose the Dynamic Mixture of Adapters (DMoA), a novel modality-aware enhancement framework that dynamically refines multi-modal features before semantic fusion through a Mixture of Experts (MoE) mechanism. Applied across multi-scale feature layers, DMoA consists of three key components. First, a Cross-Modality Feature Pre-Enhancement (CMFPE) block exploits complementary information to compensate for weak modality features. Second, the Dynamic Feature Enhancement (DFE) block employs separate four-expert pools and gating networks for RGB and IR at each scale, with no parameter sharing across modalities or scales. Each gating network sparsely activates the top two lightweight experts for input-adaptive feature refinement, thereby limiting computational overhead. Finally, a Semantic Information Fusion (SIF) block promotes cross-modal semantic consistency through mutual information optimization while suppressing redundant feature responses. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that DMoA consistently achieves competitive detection performance and a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, highlighting its effectiveness for UAV-based RGB-IR object detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Generating synthetic citation networks with communities
Abstract: Generating realistic synthetic citation, patent, or component dependency networks is essential for benchmarking community detection, graph visualisation, and network data mining algorithms. We present a systematic comparison of generators of directed graphs that are nearly acyclic and have a ground-truth community structure. We evaluate 12 methods across 7 real citation networks and 26 metrics. We propose the practice of reversing the directions of edges in static generators to break cycles and induce a citation-like flow, which markedly improves the performance of a degree-corrected Stochastic Block Model. Our methodological approach to evaluating community detection benchmarks distinguishes between endogenous and exogenous mesoscopic similarities, with the latter proving more important. This distinction reveals that high-parameter models gain much of their advantage by memorising planted community statistics, which limits their fidelity when the evaluation is blind to those labels. Finally, we introduce the Citation Seeder (CS) algorithm, an iterative generator grounded in the Price-Pareto model of citation networks, with interpretable parameters and O(N+E) generation. CS achieves competitive results against the best-performing baselines while using up to four orders of magnitude fewer parameters, providing an interpretable account of a network's structure and, on a temporal hold-out, extrapolating its future in-degree distribution more faithfully than descriptive baselines. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Development and validation of an ICD-11–based problematic social media use scale
Abstract: The present study aimed to address conceptual and measurement challenges in assessing problematic social media use by developing a scale grounded in the ICD-11 diagnostic framework for behavioral addictions. Item generation was based on core features including impaired control, prioritization of the behavior, continuation despite negative consequences, and functional impairment. Following expert review and pilot testing, data were collected in multiple phases. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a multidimensional structure consistent with ICD-11 criteria. Measurement invariance was established across gender (female vs. male) and age groups (emerging adults vs. adults) in separate Multigroup Confirmatory Analyses. Item Response Theory analyses showed that the scale demonstrates higher discrimination at low to moderate levels of problematic use, highlighting its sensitivity for early detection. Overall, the findings suggest that the scale is a theoretically grounded and psychometrically sound instrument for assessing problematic social media use, with potential applications in research, screening, and early intervention contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Compressive payoff-to-signal transduction can separate the start and sustain thresholds of cooperation
Abstract: Cooperation is often difficult to start but easier to sustain once established. We ask whether this asymmetry can arise from payoff-to-signal transduction before objective payoffs enter action comparison. In a minimal contribution-sharing game, at a given return factor, cooperation has a net objective disadvantage relative to defection that does not vary with the local cooperative environment. When compressive transduction is applied separately to the two action payoffs, however, the transduced cooperation–defection comparison gap can vary across local environments. Population reweighting aggregates these environment-dependent local gaps into a state-dependent mean comparison signal, whose slope is governed by the environment–gap covariance. In the baseline response map, two branch points satisfy fixed-point self-consistency, tangency, and non-degeneracy, yielding distinct start and sustain thresholds. Analytical derivations, controls, and finite-population tests support this mechanism. The contribution lies in identifying and verifying the conditional cross-level chain linking compressive encoding, population reweighting, and adaptive updating. They also show that whether the deterministic threshold structure is clearly expressed in finite-time trajectories depends on whether the update process reads out the same-environment action gap. These results identify a cross-level mechanism in which payoff-to-signal transduction, population reweighting, and adaptive updating jointly separate the start and sustain thresholds of cooperation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Geospatial Analysis of HIV Prevalence and Cervical Cancer Screening Coverage in Sub-Saharan Africa: Opportunities and Gaps for Integrated Care
Abstract: Objectives Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality among women in sub-Saharan Africa, with HIV infection amplifying risk through immunosuppression. This geospatial analysis examines the alignment between HIV prevalence and cervical cancer screening (CCS) coverage in 4 high-burden countries (South Africa, Kenya, Mozambique, and Lesotho) using recent Demographic and Health Survey data (2016-2023/24). Methods Using nationally representative Demographic and Health Survey data sets from South Africa (2016), Kenya (2022), Mozambique (2022/23), and Lesotho (2023/24), this study used geospatial hotspot analysis to identify areas with high and low CCS coverage and their overlap with high HIV prevalence hotspots. RStudio was used to map and analyze spatial clusters. Results Substantial geographic heterogeneity was observed within and across countries. In South Africa, HIV hotspots were concentrated in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, with strong alignment between HIV and CCS in metropolitan centers; however, high screening intensity in the Western Cape contrasted with relatively lower HIV burden. In Kenya, the most pronounced convergence occurred in the Lake Victoria basin (Kisumu, Homa Bay, Siaya, and Migori), whereas central counties demonstrated high CCS activity despite lower HIV prevalence. Mozambique showed the clearest spatial concordance, with near-complete overlap of HIV and CCS hotspots in Maputo City, Maputo Province, and Gaza, alongside limited screening presence in central and northern high-burden areas. In Lesotho, HIV and CCS hotspots were largely colocated in Maseru and border districts, with additional moderate overlap in Mokhotlong and southern districts. Conclusion The analysis highlights where service integration might be working (overlap of HIV prevalence and CCS hotspots) and where urgent alignment is needed (HIV hotspots without CCS). Policymakers should invest in region-specific strategies, with greatest integration potential in Mozambique south, South African metros, and Kenya’s Lake Victoria basin, while urgently addressing CCS gaps. Geographically tailored interventions are critical to accelerate progress toward World Health Organization’s 90-70-90 cervical cancer elimination targets in high-prevalence settings. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: ECG-based NSR, CHF, and ARR classification: Tradeoff between classical feature engineering and TCN-based deep features
Abstract: Accurate and efficient automatic classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for scalable cardiac monitoring and timely clinical decision making. Herein, we focus on classifying Arrhythmia (ARR), Congestive Heart Failure (CHF), and Normal Sinus Rhythm (NSR). In particular, this study compares a classical feature-based pipeline that includes time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-scale features with a modern deep feature extractor employing the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). For this, MATLAB simulations were conducted on ECG signals from the MIT-BIH database to evaluate the classification performance and quantify practical trade-offs by reporting wall-clock training times, inference latency, and hardware requirements. The results showed that the Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved classification accuracies of 88%, 91%, and 100% for ARR vs NSR, ARR vs CHF, and NSR vs CHF, respectively, when trained and tested on the classical features. On the other hand, the TCN achieved an overall accuracy of 99.4% to distinguish between the three classes. Furthermore, the TCN yielded superior raw predictive performance but offered reduced interpretability compared with the classical feature-based pipeline, at the expense of requiring substantially greater computational resources. These results demonstrated that well-engineered classical descriptors remain competitive for low-resource deployment, while data-driven TCNs deliver higher accuracy when computational budgets permit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yu Y.; Zhang S.; Xu Y.; Wang P.
Title: DMJP: Diffusion and multi-model joint perturbation for enhanced facial privacy
Abstract: Face recognition technology has been adopted in public safety, social platforms, and other domains. However, unauthorized identity recognition poses privacy risks, exacerbating concerns about the misuse of personal data and thus calling for robust privacy protection methods. Current face privacy protection techniques often encounter challenges such as limited transferability or noticeable image distortion. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces DMJP, a framework that integrates Latent Diffusion Models with a multi-model joint perturbation optimization mechanism. The method encodes an input image into the latent space, applies gradient-based multi-model perturbations, and generates a protected image via Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model sampling. Gradients from multiple white-box face recognition models are combined to guide common feature manipulation, while different adversarial attack algorithms are merged to form a unified perturbation direction, enhancing transferability against black-box FR models. In addition, an adaptive perturbation strategy dynamically adjusts perturbation strength according to the diffusion timesteps and reconstruction errors, balancing protection effectiveness and image quality. Experiments on CelebA-HQ and FFHQ demonstrate a favorable trade-off between Protection Success Rate and image quality, with competitive PSNR/SSIM and substantially improved Fréchet Inception Distance. Further experiments evaluate computational efficiency through sparse injection and demonstrate target-free anonymization and robustness to preprocessing and DDIM purification. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Sun Y.; Zhang H.; Xu Z.; Guo Z.; Yuan L.; Zhang R.; Liu C.; Li T.
Title: STR-LBSN: Spatio-temporal Role-based Heterogeneous Hypergraph Embedding for location-based social networks
Abstract: Location-based social networks (LBSNs) contain rich social, spatial, and temporal information. However, most existing embedding methods overly simplify the underlying hypergraph structure, represent each user with a single static embedding, and fail to model the coupling between social relationships and mobility behaviors. To address these limitations, we propose STR-LBSN, a Spatio-temporal Role-based Heterogeneous Hypergraph Embedding framework for Location-Based Social Networks. STR-LBSN models users’ temporally evolving behavioral roles as hidden states in a Hidden Markov Model and constructs a role-centric hypergraph from the decoded role assignments. Based on this structure, STR-LBSN learns multi-role representations through biased random walks and heterogeneous sampling in cosine space, while balancing social contexts and spatio-temporal mobility patterns. Extensive experiments on seven real-world LBSN datasets demonstrate that STR-LBSN achieves the highest mean performance among twelve state-of-the-art baselines in nearly all settings. Specifically, for friend recommendation, STR-LBSN achieves substantial relative improvements across four evaluation metrics, including Precision, Recall, F1-score, and NDCG, with particularly large gains on sparse datasets. For POI recommendation and activity recommendation, it delivers average performance gains of about 5% to 30% in terms of Hit@5, Hit@10, and Hit@20. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation studies and parameter sensitivity analyses support the effectiveness of the main modeling components and examine the robustness of STR-LBSN to key hyperparameters. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Understanding conflict in protected areas: integrating justice considerations with economic perspectives
Abstract: Despite broad agreement on the urgency of sustainability transitions that protect biodiversity, conservation conflicts continue to rise. This paper examines environmental conflicts in protected areas (PAs), highlighting the overlooked link between conflict and justice. Existing frameworks often fail to distinguish between conflict manifestations and determinants, or to integrate justice theories with economic perspectives. This study provides a comprehensive review of the literature to support the analysis of PA conflicts and develops a robust framework that integrates justice considerations with the economic perspective. Conflicts are viewed as inherent to complex social–ecological systems, shaped by social relations and rights over ecosystem services. The framework is structured around three analytical axes: substance (what the conflict is about), process (how it unfolds), and relation (who is involved with-whom). It differentiates between how conflicts appear (i.e., manifestation) and what causes them (i.e., determinants), framed through distributive, procedural, and recognition justice. This perspective challenges linear assumptions that conflicts always stem from injustices, emphasizing their potential to drive institutional change. The framework offers a novel approach to assessing justice-conflict dynamics in PAs governance, providing comprehensive toolkit for promoting equitable conservation strategies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Scenario-based robust optimization for the design of a resilient and sustainable power supply chain network using energy storage system
Abstract: The increasing demand for electricity, along with the growing reliance on intermittent renewable energy sources, presents significant challenges for building resilient and cost-efficient power supply chains. This study introduces a hybrid multi-objective mathematical modeling framework that integrates renewable and non-renewable power generation units, multi-level substations, and strategically located energy storage systems. A scenario-based robust optimization model is developed to jointly minimize total system costs and maximize the performance of selected energy storage system technologies. The latter is quantified through a hybrid hierarchical group decision-making method combining the best‒worst method and the technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution and is incorporated into the model as a secondary objective via the improved weighted augmented ε-constraint technique. To strengthen system resilience, the model includes strategies such as diversification of generation technologies, capacity expansion of substations and lines, deployment of redundant transmission paths, and optimal siting of energy storage systems. A real-world case study from an Iranian province is conducted to evaluate the model’s effectiveness under disruption scenarios. The results demonstrate the framework’s ability to provide robust infrastructure planning under uncertainty. Title: From half-cell to heavy-duty: a critical review of MXene catalysts for PEMFC cathodes
Abstract: MXenes have emerged as promising cathode catalyst supports for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) due to their high conductivity and tunable surface chemistry. However, despite numerous reports of exceptional half-cell oxygen reduction reaction activity, MXene-based catalysts have not yet been demonstrated to translate into practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performance, especially under combined heavy-duty automotive conditions. This review critically evaluates the gap between the rotating disk electrode and single-cell performance of Pt/MXene, MXene-carbon, non-precious, and single-atom catalysts. We systematically benchmark MEA-level metrics, peak power density under H2/air, high-current–density polarization, electrochemical surface area retention under accelerated stress tests, and Pt utilization against commercial Pt/C and heavy-duty targets. We identify key unresolved barriers: MXene oxidation under acidic and oxidative cathode conditions, nanosheet restacking-induced oxygen transport resistance, and the lack of standardized MEA validation. Finally, we provide an engineering-oriented roadmap that integrates termination engineering, hybrid architectures, and AI-assisted design to bridge the half-cell-to-heavy-duty gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Significantly enhancing the strength of aluminum while preserving excellent electrical conductivity via single-walled carbon nanotubes reinforcement
Abstract: The inherent trade-off between the strength and electrical conductivity has long constrained the development of advanced aluminum (Al) conductors, and the potential of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) to break this dilemma remains critically underexplored, largely due to their dispersion difficulties. Herein, SWCNTs reinforced Al matrix nanocomposites are fabricated via friction stir processing (FSP) and followed by hot extrusion, and the strength-electrical properties are systematically evaluated. Microstructural analysis confirmed the well dispersion of SWCNTs without micro-sized aggregations. The smaller diameter and much higher specific surface area of SWCNTs enables the formation of a greater number of clean and strong bonded interfaces with the Al matrix under the thermo-mechanical conditions of FSP, which is the key for enhancing strength and maintaining electrical conductivity of Al. As a result, the ultimate tensile strengths of the SWCNTs/Al nanocomposite reached 201.1 MPa, representing an increase of 113.0% over the unreinforced Al. Remarkably, the SWCNTs/Al nanocomposite retained a high electrical conductivity (∼62.3% IACS) and good elongation (∼12.5%). This combination of more than doubled strength with uncompromised conductivity highlights the advantage of SWCNTs over conventional CNTs reinforcements in achieving strength-electrical conductivity synergy. Our findings establish that SWCNTs, despite their processing challenges, serve as exceptionally efficient reinforcements for overcoming the long-standing strength-conductivity trade-off, positioning them as a highly promising reinforcement for next-generation high-performance Al conductors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Synthesis-structure-property-performance economic value creation relationships in biomass-derived carbon materials for hydrogen storage: Implications for green finance and sustainable development
Abstract: The transition toward a hydrogen-based economy requires innovative storage materials that simultaneously enhance hydrogen performance, promote resource efficiency, and generate long-term economic value. Biomass-derived porous materials have emerged as a promising solution by transforming abundant agricultural, forestry, and industrial biomass residues into high-value hydrogen storage media, thereby supporting the principles of the circular bioeconomy and sustainable resource management. This study examines the economic value creation potential of biomass-based hydrogen storage technologies and evaluates their implications for green finance, low-carbon investment strategies, and sustainable development. It highlights how biomass valorization reduces dependence on expensive conventional storage materials while creating new revenue streams through waste utilization, carbon reduction, and renewable energy integration. The analysis demonstrates that biomass-derived activated carbons, biochars, carbon aerogels, and hierarchical porous carbon nanostructures possess favorable physicochemical properties, including high specific surface area, tunable pore architectures, lightweight characteristics, and excellent adsorption performance, making them attractive candidates for efficient hydrogen storage systems. From an economic perspective, these technologies improve supply-chain resilience, lower production costs, stimulate rural economic development, and encourage investment in sustainable manufacturing industries. Furthermore, biomass-based hydrogen storage aligns closely with green finance mechanisms by attracting environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investments, facilitating access to green bonds and climate finance, and supporting national decarbonization policies designed to achieve net-zero emissions. The study also discusses the integration of biomass-derived storage materials within emerging hydrogen value chains, emphasizing their contribution to carbon neutrality, renewable energy storage, and energy security. Despite challenges related to commercialization, feedstock standardization, scalability, and investment uncertainty, continued advances in material engineering, policy incentives, and financial innovation are expected to accelerate industrial deployment. Overall, biomass-derived hydrogen storage represents a strategically important intersection between sustainable materials science, green finance, and circular economic development, offering significant opportunities to create environmental, economic, and social value while supporting the global transition toward resilient and sustainable energy systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Fast semi-supervised graph clustering by directly solving pairwise constrained problem
Abstract: Pairwise-constrained graph clustering has been widely studied in semi-supervised learning. Most existing methods incorporate pairwise constraints indirectly, either as penalty terms in the objective function or through modifications to the similarity graph, and subsequently obtain cluster results via relaxation strategies. Such approaches may not sufficiently enforce the given constraints and often involve costly eigendecomposition, which limits their efficiency on large datasets or in the presence of numerous constraints. To address these limitations, we propose a novel optimization framework that directly solves the original discrete constrained graph clustering problem. Specifically, a block coordinate descent (CD) method is formulated to exhaustively evaluate all feasible assignments of the two-row associated with each cannot-link pair yielding an exact solution to the corresponding discrete subproblem. Furthermore, connected components induced by must-link constraints are merged during anchor graph construction, effectively shrinking the problem scale. Crucially, a two-row incremental update mechanism is developed to accelerate the joint optimization process. Extensive experiments across twelve benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior clustering performance and exhibits high computational efficiency. © 2026

Title: From alignment to decision: Page-matching supervision and consistency-shaped fusion for phishing detection
Abstract: With the widespread adoption of online services, phishing detection based on URLs and HTML must handle heterogeneous evidence sources whose representations may be misaligned, incomplete, or dominated by one modality. This paper proposes a URL–HTML multimodal detection framework that connects representation alignment with decision-level stability. First, a page-matching auxiliary task constructs matched and mismatched URL–HTML pairs to strengthen page-level cross-modal correspondence, while a controlled same-domain different-page variant examines whether the learned signal extends beyond coarse domain or topical differences. Second, a class-aware consistency loss imposes a “legit-close/phish-far” constraint on normalized cross-modal similarity, shaping a more discriminative shared space. Third, a sample-adaptive gating network dynamically balances URL, HTML, and fused features to reduce modality dominance and preserve complementary evidence. Experiments on the Mendeley dataset, a CompPhish-derived cross-dataset evaluation set, and a joint URL–HTML obfuscation setting show that the proposed method achieves the best performance among the evaluated reproducible URL/HTML baselines, especially under low-FPR operating points. Ablation studies and diagnostic visualizations further verify the complementary roles of page matching, consistency shaping, and adaptive gating. A sample-level gate analysis demonstrates reliability-aware weight reallocation under joint URL–HTML obfuscation, while a same-domain hard-negative evaluation reveals both improved fine-grained correspondence discrimination and its trade-off with the primary phishing-detection objective. © 2026

Authors: Wu Y.; He Z.; Wang S.
Title: Carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS): From technology advances to carbon neutrality pathways in energy and industrial sectors
Abstract: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is critical for hard-to-abate sectors including steel, cement, chemicals, and power generation. This review systematically synthesizes recent advances across the full CCUS chain, covering emerging electrochemical and membrane-based direct air capture (DAC), AI-enhanced monitoring, verification, and risk management with digital twins, and synergistic coupling with green hydrogen and power-to-liquid synthetic fuels. Mature capture technologies and utilization pathways are assessed alongside geological storage in saline aquifers, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, and coal seams. Operational data from million-tonne demonstration projects are distilled to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial implementation. The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects CCUS playing a key role in global emissions reductions by 2050, while the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) emphasizes its critical role in ambitious climate stabilization pathways. A conceptual system integration framework is proposed to clarify the distinct roles of CCUS in energy conversion versus industrial production. Despite persistent challenges, including high costs, energy penalties, infrastructure deficits, and regulatory gaps, future directions prioritize low-energy materials, AI-driven optimization, industrial clustering, cross-border networks, and policy incentives. Through innovation and cooperation, CCUS is transitioning from demonstration to commercial-scale deployment to support global climate goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A graph-based direct association strategy with fuzzy interpretability for linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality
Abstract: Existing coke quality prediction methods mainly rely on a two-stage prediction strategy, where blended coal properties are first estimated from individual coal properties and then used for coke quality prediction. This process inevitably introduces information loss and accumulated prediction errors, which limit the prediction accuracy and reliability of these models in practical coal blending applications. To address this challenge, this study proposes, for the first time, a graph-based direct association strategy linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality. Each coal blending scheme is transformed into a graph structure, where individual coal samples are regarded as graph nodes and their corresponding coal properties together with blending ratios are used as node features. Different graph neural network models are further investigated to directly learn the relationship between individual coal properties and coke quality indicators, namely Coke Reactivity Index (CRI) and Coke Strength after Reaction (CSR). A total of 306 coal blending schemes are used for model development and evaluation. Experimental results show that the proposed one-stage graph-based framework outperforms traditional two-stage prediction methods. Among different graph neural network models, the graph attention network achieves the best overall prediction performance, obtaining mean absolute errors of 2.06 and 2.60 for CRI and CSR prediction, respectively. The t-SNE visualization further demonstrates that the proposed one-stage framework can learn more discriminative feature representations than the traditional two-stage framework. In addition, the proposed framework demonstrates good robustness under blending conditions with different numbers of coal types and can provide interpretable analysis through feature importance and node importance visualization. Furthermore, fuzzy interpretability is introduced at the feature level to characterize the gradual contribution levels of different coal properties. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: SUGARS AND POLYOLS IN HONEY OF APIS LABORIOSA AND OTHER BEES FROM ARUNACHAL PRADESH AND NAGALAND
Abstract: Honey bees and stingless bees produce honey not only as nourishment for their broods but also as an essential product associated with pollination. The composition of honey varies with bee species, floral sources, and climatic conditions, and it primarily consists of sugars and polyols that determine its sweetness. However, limited information is available on the honey composition of the biodiverse eastern Himalaya. This study investigated the sweetener profiles of honeys from four honey bee species (Apis laboriosa, A. dorsata, A. cerana, and A. florea) and two stingless bees (Lepidotrigona arcifera and Tetragonula iridipennis) collected from northeast India. Sugars were qualitatively identified using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) and quantified by High-Performance Liquid Chromatography with Refractive Index Detector (HPLC-RID). Across species, 24 sugars and eight polyols were detected. A. laboriosa and A. dorsata honeys each contained 13 sugars and three polyols, while A. cerana and A. florea honeys had 13 and 14 sugars, respectively. L. arcifera honey showed the highest diversity, with 18 sugars and three polyols. Notably, A. laboriosa honey contained maltitol, which was absent in other samples. The findings demonstrate species-specific variation in honey sweeteners, reflecting the diverse floral resources and environmental conditions of the eastern Himalaya. © 2027, The Entomological Society of India. Title: Wideband active noise control for open-ear headphones via low-delay acoustic design with a coaxial loudspeaker
Abstract: Open-ear headphones preserve environmental awareness but provide little passive attenuation, so broadband feedforward active noise control (ANC) is required. This paper presents a controlled measured-path offline study of a wideband ANC design using one device in one dummy-head wearing configuration, based on a design-oriented secondary-path delay budget. A coaxial offset 2-way secondary source with a tweeter placed in front of a woofer is used, and the control bands are assigned on the basis of frequency-dependent delay characteristics, where the woofer is favored at low frequencies because of its smaller mechanical delay, while the tweeter is favored at higher frequencies because of its shorter acoustic propagation delay. We investigated two implementations: one for a dual-filter setup and the other for a single-filter setup. In this idealized linear measured-path evaluation under controlled assumptions, the two-driver configurations increased band-limited noise-power reduction for broadband pink noise relative to the unfiltered single-driver baselines. At the nominal controlled virtual electronic delay of 104 µs, the background dual-filter condition Du-BpHp-Bg and the single-filter condition Xo-BpHp achieved 8.01 and 7.58 dB reductions from 100Hzto2000Hz, respectively, compared with 5.94 dB for Wf-Bp and 5.02 dB for Tw-Bp. For the tested device and wearing configuration, these results indicate that a design-oriented delay budget can support driver-band allocation for broadband feedforward ANC in open-ear headphones. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Safety concepts through a memetic lens
Abstract: Within safety practice and science there are countless ideas, approaches and concepts to manage safety. Some of these safety concepts are picked up, discussed widely and spread, while others do not. Little is known about this subject. This paper provides a unique perspective on the development and adoption of safety concepts by using an evolutionary framework to explore reasons why. As a case, this paper traces the historic development of one of safety’s most influential and iconic safety concepts, the accident triangle, over nearly a century through successive cycles of replication, variation, and selection. Knowledge of factors that influence the adoption of safety concepts can contribute to the design of more effective concepts that attract attention and of social and organisational environments that are receptive of these concepts. In the end, provided the concepts in question are useful, this can contribute to enhancing safety and reducing harm. In addition, the insights gained in this paper can help safety professionals and academics to critically reflect on the development of safety concepts, to help them better understand how safety concepts evolve and can change meaning leading to various interpretations and reflect on what this means for their own adoption of concepts and eventually their practice. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Jia X.; Du J.; Wei H.; Chen J.; Zhu H.; Zhou J.T.; Wang Z.
Title: Collaborative multi-instance feature aggregation for visual privacy protection
Abstract: The rapid advancement of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) has dramatically shaped numerous domains of modern society. With the increasing emphasis on high-quality and personalized data, safeguarding visual privacy and preventing information leakage have become urgent research priorities. Traditional privacy-preserving strategies predominantly rely on isolated instance-level manipulations, such as artificial noise injection or pixel-level obfuscation, to achieve de-identification. Yet, these independent sample-level approaches inevitably face an inherent trade-off: slight alterations provide inadequate protection, whereas aggressive modifications severely distort task-relevant semantics and compromise downstream accuracy. To overcome this dilemma, we introduce a novel visual privacy protection framework driven by multi-instance feature-level aggregation. Unlike conventional methods that perturb a single isolated instance, our approach constructs anonymized representations by collaboratively aggregating identity-discriminative feature fragments drawn from multiple data instances. Instead of relying on external noise to conceal identity, this collaborative aggregation synthesizes protected data, effectively weakening the deterministic link between the original identity and the visual representation. Comprehensive experiments on diverse visual identity recognition benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework delivers superior results, achieving both robust perceptual anonymization and high downstream task utility compared with prior state-of-the-art techniques. © 2026

Title: Gut-joint axis mediates susceptibility to osteoarthritis in female adult offspring rats with prenatal caffeine exposure
Abstract: Prenatal caffeine exposure (PCE) is closely associated with the susceptibility to adult osteoarthritis, but the mechanisms underlying the gut microbiota remain unclear. In this study, the postnatal weeks (PW) 12 and 36 PCE female offspring rats showed decreased articular cartilage mass, increased modified Mankin's score, decreased matrix synthesis, elevated local inflammatory factors in articular cartilage, and increased matrix degradation. Furthermore, the gut microbiota of PCE female offspring rats was disturbed, which was primarily characterized by decreased butyric acid-producing bacteria (such as Butyricimonas and Romboutsia). The short-chain fatty acid metabolic profile also confirmed that decreased serum butyric acid levels in the PCE group were significantly correlated with the expression of essential genes of the osteoarthritis phenotype. The fecal microbiota transplantation experiment confirmed that the altered gut microbiota in PCE offspring rats induced osteoarthritis phenotype. Supplementation with sodium butyrate can alleviate the osteoarthritis phenotype caused by PCE in female adult offspring rats. © 2026

Title: Beyond the lecture: Creative and innovative pedagogies in management education – An integrative conceptual review
Abstract: Management education has been criticised for over-reliance on transmission-oriented pedagogies poorly suited to developing the competences contemporary business graduates require. The case for moving beyond the lecture is strengthened by generative artificial intelligence, which performs the analytical and reproductive tasks underpinning conventional assessment, shifting educational value toward judgement, situated decision-making, and reflection. This integrative conceptual review of creative and innovative pedagogies draws on literature published principally between 2013 and 2026, organising the field into six clusters: experiential and simulation-based learning; game-based and gamified approaches; arts-based methods; design-based pedagogies; problem-based learning; and student-generated multimodal artefacts. For each cluster it examines theoretical foundations, evidence strength, and implementation challenges, distinguishing outcomes with stronger evidence (engagement, motivation) from those with weaker evidence (durable transfer). Three cross-cutting themes are identified: the centrality of learner agency, the neglect of structured reflection, and institutional conservatism as a barrier to change. The review contributes a typology of creative pedagogy organised by locus of creation and mode of engagement, which is used to make explicit the trade-offs each configuration entails and where institutional conservatism constrains change, together with implications for programme design, assessment and facilitation, and a research agenda spanning longitudinal measurement, equity, programme-level integration, and generative AI. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Hu G.; Jiang Z.; Ma J.; Wang M.; Han Y.; Du W.; Qian F.
Title: Modelling, intelligent optimisation and techno-economic analysis of post-combustion carbon capture for ethylene production under variable loads
Abstract: Thermal cracking furnaces in ethylene plants are the dominant source of CO2 emissions in the petrochemical industry, making the integration of carbon capture plants critical for decarbonization. However, the coupling behaviours between the thermal cracking furnace and the capture plants, particularly under different operating conditions, pose significant challenges to system optimization. To address this, this study proposes a comprehensive integrated simulation and intelligent optimization framework for a 60 kt/yr industrial thermal cracking furnace coupled with a Monoethanolamine (MEA)-based carbon capture process. Firstly, a high-fidelity coupled thermal cracking furnace model (based on Zone Method and COILSIM1D) is established to accurately predict flue gas characteristics under varying fuel gas flowrates. Secondly, a rate-based post-combustion carbon capture plant model is developed in Aspen Plus®, validated against pilot scale experimental data from the Technology Centre Mongstad (TCM), and scaled up to match the flue gas from the industrial scale thermal cracking furnace. Genetic Algorithm (GA) is implemented in MATLAB to interact with process simulations, enabling the global optimization of energy consumption and carbon capture costs. Optimization results reveal a previously unidentified divergence between technical and economic performance: the lowest specific reboiler duty occurs at 82–84% capture level, whereas the lowest cost consistently lies at 86–90%. We demonstrate quantitatively that this 4–6 percentage point gap arises from the trade-off between the change of capital cost caused by economies of scale and the exponential rise in regeneration energy, which is established for the first time for low carbon ethylene plants—— the optimal capture level shifts towards higher values as fuel gas flowrate decreases. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Z.; Yin Y.; Wei F.; Wu J.; Lv H.; Yang W.
Title: Psy-DMTL: Psychology-guided dynamic multi-task learning for LLM-based personality detection
Abstract: Personality detection aims to infer individuals’ psychological traits from user-generated text and has broad applications in user profiling, personalized services, and human–computer interaction. Recent LLM-based methods have shown strong potential for this task by providing rich semantic representations. However, most existing methods still face three limitations: coarse-grained long-history encoding may dilute sparse personality cues, shared user representations may entangle heterogeneous evidence across personality dimensions, and cross-dimension dependencies are often modeled implicitly without psychology-inspired structural guidance. To address these issues, we propose Psy-DMTL, a psychology-guided dynamic multi-task learning framework for LLM-based personality detection. Psy-DMTL first encodes posts independently with a frozen LLM and uses a gated hierarchical context encoder to capture user-level dependencies while preserving fine-grained cues. It then introduces orthogonal dimension-attention pooling to extract dimension-specific representations for different MBTI dimensions. Finally, a psychology-guided dynamic modulation decoder models directional cross-dimension interactions through FiLM-based feature modulation. Experiments on the Kaggle and Pandora benchmarks show that Psy-DMTL achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of average Macro-F1 on both datasets. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for long-history personality detection. Supplementary experiments on the Italian Personal-ITY dataset further support the model's competitive performance. Our model is publicly available at https://github.com/qaswzh/Psy-DMTL. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Pan S.; Zhan P.; Chen W.; Wu L.; Cai R.
Title: Causal-inspired knowledge tracing via class-conditioned latent representation learning
Abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) plays a foundational role in smart education by modeling students’ evolving knowledge states from historical learning interactions. Existing deep KT architectures predominantly mine statistical correlations from individual interaction sequences, neglecting group-level educational contexts (e.g., class). Such contextual heterogeneity forces models to rely on spurious correlations, leading to error next-response predictions. Guided by advanced educational philosophies, causality offers a principled lens to characterize the underlying data-generating process of student learning. Nevertheless, comprehensive contextual signals are inherently complex and largely latent. To bridge this gap, we propose CLR4KT, a causal-inspired plug-in framework for Class-Conditioned Latent Representation Learning in KT. CLR4KT introduces an identifiable Variational Autoencoder (iVAE) style architecture to capture the data-generating mechanism, leveraging class-level contextual information as an observed group-level conditional signal to assist in identifying and resolving the complex, latent context representations. By conditioning both the latent prior and the variational posterior on class labels, CLR4KT learns class-conditioned latent representations. These enhanced latent states are seamlessly integrated into mainstream KT backbones via temporal modeling. Extensive experiments across four benchmark datasets demonstrate that CLR4KT consistently boosts predictive capability. Ablation and visualization analyses confirm the effectiveness of class-conditioned latent representation learning module of our method. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Debiasing scene graph generation with Context-Aware Peer Networks
Abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects and infer their pairwise relationships, but long-tailed predicate distributions cause models to over-predict frequent predicates and under-recognize informative tail relations. We propose Context-Aware Peer Networks (CAPN), a plug-and-play framework for unbiased SGG. CAPN replaces a single relation predictor with multiple collaborative peers and introduces a context-aware encoder with Context-to-Peer (CPE) and Context-to-Predicate (CPR) modules. CPE adaptively weights peer contributions according to scene context, while CPR modulates predicate logits to improve context-consistent prediction and alleviate head-predicate dominance. Experiments on Visual Genome and Open Images V6 show that CAPN improves the mR-R trade-off across Motifs, VCTree, and Transformer backbones, achieving a weighted score of 45.1 on OI-V6 and a mean score of 49.0 on VG PredCls. Title: Fatigue crack growth behavior of additively manufactured aluminum alloys: A comparative investigation
Abstract: This study investigates the fatigue crack growth (FCG) behavior of three aluminum alloys, namely AlSi10Mg, QuesTek Al, and Scalmalloy, using compact tension specimens fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF). Among these, AlSi10Mg specimens are manufactured with two feedstocks from different suppliers. The materials exhibit different fracture surface roughnesses due to variations in their microstructures which correlated with threshold stress intensity factor range, ΔKth . Scalmalloy exhibited the highest ΔKth , followed by QuesTek Al, with both AlSi10Mg materials being comparable but the lowest. Vertical specimens had higher ΔKth values (except Scalmalloy), while higher R resulted in lower ΔKth due to reduced crack closure effects. Stable crack growth behavior was comparable among both AlSi10Mg materials and Scalmalloy although their microstructures were different. However, QuesTek Al had significantly higher FCG rates due to its limited ductility. In the unstable region, the maximum stress intensity factor at failure, Kmax,failure correlated broadly with ductility obtained from tensile tests. Scalmalloy exhibited the highest Kmax,failure whereas QuesTek Al exhibited the lowest due to its limited plastic deformation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Toward a relational typology: Mapping social entrepreneur-resident interactions in community-led tourism social entrepreneurship
Abstract: Research on tourism social entrepreneurship has focused on exogenous models while overlooking host communities' agency. The aim of this study was to examine interactions between social entrepreneurs and residents in the context of community-led tourism social entrepreneurship. The exploratory qualitative study design involved three fieldwork phases. We used two dimensions—the initiator's primary motivation and the embeddedness forms in the responder's actions—to identify four relationship types: traditional bonding ties, instrumental ties, patron–client ties, and value-congruent alliances. The social action and embeddedness theories guided our examination of relational formation. Findings further reveal a model of power shift and relationship dynamics. This model suggests that a power shift involves three principal stages centered around dependence. In summary, we provide here a typological framework for analyzing social entrepreneur–resident interactions and offer practical insights into sustainable community development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A bibliometric review of farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia: A two-decade study
Abstract: Farmer livelihood resilience is crucial given the sector's contribution to the national economic resilience, particularly in Indonesia. Despite its importance, a comprehensive synthesis of how this field has evolved over the past two decades remains limited. The objectives of this study are to provide an overview of the circumstances and challenges related to farmer resilience by examining research on farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia. Employing a hybrid methodology that combines bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review (SLR) guided by PRISMA protocols, this research analyzed 184 articles, 94 conference papers, and 2 review papers indexed in the Scopus database from 2005 to 2025. VOSviewer software was utilized to visualize co-occurrence networks and publication patterns. The results demonstrate a substantial increase in academic interest over the last decade, with a significant peak in publications after 2015. The analysis identified five dominant thematic clusters: (1) Smallholder Farmers’ Climate Change Adaptation in Indonesia; (2) Sustainable Agriculture and Land Conversion Policy; (3) Social Capital and Collective Action for Sustainable Agriculture; (4) Livelihood Strategies of Oil Palm and Agroforestry Farmers; (5) Sustainability of Palm Oil Smallholders. This study fills a critical research gap by bridging quantitative mapping with qualitative insights, offering a strategic roadmap for future scholarly inquiry. The findings emphasize that strengthening farmer resilience in Indonesia requires integrated policy frameworks that prioritize institutional support and optimized social capital. Ultimately, these results provide vital evidence for policymakers to design more inclusive and sustainable agricultural development strategies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Ma C.-X.; Peng F.-L.; Li Z.-J.; Qiao Y.-K.
Title: Spatial cognitive patterns of underground public spaces from a stimulus-organism-response perspective: evidence from LLM-empowered social media data mining
Abstract: Current underground public space (UPS) renewal prioritizes engineering-oriented physical upgrades, neglecting users’ multidimensional cognitive experiences. Existing studies on underground space perceptions rely on small-sample surveys and fail to capture joint co-occurrence patterns among multiple stimuli. This study integrated the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework with large language models to decode spatial cognitive patterns. It drew on 76,078 social media reviews from 64 UPSs in 19 Chinese cities (2005–2024). DeepSeek extracted 27 spatial stimuli and their sentiments, serving as public perceptions. Generalized ordered probit regressions showed that management quality, environmental conditions, and atmospheric experiences exhibited the strongest associations with overall ratings. Negative perceptions showed stronger negative associations with ratings than positive perceptions showed positive associations. Association rule mining uncovered co-occurrence patterns across genders, city clusters, and review periods. Dissatisfaction was associated with shorter, more concentrated patterns of negative stimuli, whereas satisfaction was associated with the co-occurrence of positive functional and experiential perceptions. Co-occurrence patterns varied markedly across organismic attributes. Males showed simpler, function-oriented networks, while females displayed more complex, multi-dimensional ones. Regional expectation thresholds differed across contexts. Temporal patterns shifted from physical defects to operational management. Title: The psychology of AI-mediated communication across languages
Abstract: Communication across languages is increasingly mediated by artificial intelligence (AI). This creates opportunities for people with different language backgrounds to communicate in their respective native languages. AI-mediated communication can therefore reduce cognitive effort, disfluency, and social stigma associated with speaking a non-native language. At the same time, non-native language use influences cognitive, emotional, and social processes that go beyond the accurate transmission of meaning. By affecting these processes and introducing new cues, AI-mediated communication could also have unintended effects on communication effectiveness and social evaluations between interlocutors. We examine the conditions under which these effects may help or hinder cross-linguistic interactions and identify directions for research on the psychology of cross-linguistic communication as AI language tools become prevalent. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Beyond Technology Readiness Levels: Developing and Evaluating an Industry 5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework for Regulated Life Sciences Manufacturing
Abstract: Purpose: Regulated life sciences manufacturing organisations face increasing pressure to adopt Industry 5.0 (I5.0) innovations while maintaining patient safety, product quality, data integrity, and regulatory compliance. Existing assessment models provide useful perspectives on technical maturity, expectation dynamics, and organisational innovation capability, but do not fully assess whether an innovation is ready to progress responsibly in a regulated, multi-stakeholder environment. This paper develops an I5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework and presents a preliminary practitioner-informed evaluation of its use in regulated life sciences manufacturing. Methods: This paper uses design science research structured through the Double Diamond process. The framework was developed through literature review, advisory feedback, subject matter expert input, practitioner workshops, case-based application, surveys, and thematic analysis. Evaluation was conducted with a small, purposively selected cohort of 16 practitioners from a single educational-industry programme. Results: The framework comprises three linked tools: the Innovation Maturity Assessment, Innovation Maturity Rubric, and Innovation Readiness Levels. Across two exploratory workshops involving 16 experienced practitioners, participants reported that the framework supported clearer discussion of readiness and improved visibility of adoption risks. In Workshop 2, descriptive feedback indicated that 91% of respondents viewed Innovation Readiness Levels as clearer than Technology Readiness Levels, 82% found the framework useful for comparing innovation timelines, and 75% would recommend it. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary practitioner feedback rather than sector-wide validation. Conclusion: The findings support the conceptual distinction between innovation readiness and technology readiness and indicate the need to assess technical, regulatory, organisational, stakeholder, and societal dimensions together when evaluating I5.0 innovation in regulated manufacturing. Further evaluation with broader industry cohorts, quality and regulatory professionals, and regulatory stakeholders is required. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Li F.; Chang J.; Zhu C.; Bai H.; Huang W.
Title: Tuning donor–acceptor interactions via electronic modulation in Ga-doped ZnO for carbon chain growth from syngas
Abstract: Higher alcohol synthesis from syngas over conventional CuZn catalysts often encounters a trade-off between total alcohol selectivity and C2+ distribution. Here, we show that Ga-doped ZnO enables precise electronic modulation to balance donor and acceptor reactions through controlled Ga doping. Electron-deficient Znδ+ sites serve as key active centers, facilitating non-dissociative CO adsorption and CO insertion for carbon chain growth. At low doping, substitutional Ga acts as a donor, promoting C-O bond activation. At 1 mol% Ga, substitutional Ga and the resulting electron-deficient Znδ+ sites effectively balance the electron donation-acquisition relationship, achieving 63.5% liquid C2+ alcohol content. Excessive doping (13 mol%) causes Ga clustering and electron-rich states, over-dominating acceptor reactions and suppressing CO insertion. This work establishes that balancing donor–acceptor reactions via electronic modulation is key to overcoming this trade-off, offering a design principle extendable to other electronically tunable catalytic systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Gravity-inspired key node identification in complex networks using entropy-weighted shortest path analysis
Abstract: Identifying influential nodes is an important issue in analyzing complex networks. This paper proposes Gravity-Inspired Entropy-Weighted Shortest Path Analysis (GEWSP), a multidimensional strategy for identifying influential nodes in complex networks. GEWSP can consider node interactions as gravitational forces based on the law of gravity, providing a more faithful representation of structural influence. A network weighting strategy is introduced to account for path diversity and structural heterogeneity. Meanwhile, GEWSP integrates multiple weighted shortest-path features to characterize node importance from different structural perspectives. Information entropy is then employed to adaptively determine the weight of each dimension, enabling a more balanced integration of different structural influences. In addition, GEWSP adopts a semi-local perspective by jointly considering the intrinsic properties of each node and the characteristics of its nearby neighborhoods within a predefined range. This configuration enables the model to exploit information from different structural scales without imposing substantial computational overhead. The proposed framework is evaluated on several networks by the Susceptible–Infected–Recovered (SIR) spreading model. Experimental results show that GEWSP consistently outperforms existing methods in epidemic spreading simulations. It achieves higher identification accuracy and stronger discrimination among influential nodes, demonstrating its effectiveness for key node identification in complex networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Do workers value formal jobs? Evidence from Brazil
Abstract: Informal employment, and the resulting lack of social insurance coverage, remains widespread in low- and middle-income countries. This paper contributes to the debate on the determinants of informality by estimating workers’ willingness to pay (WTP) for a formal job using a sample of 4997 Brazilian dependent workers. On average, workers are willing to forgo 15.1% of their wages for a signed work card, with higher WTP among formal and highly educated workers. Predicted eligibility for non-contributory social assistance lowers WTP, while predicted eligibility for contributory social insurance increases it. A simple calculation suggests that workers’ WTP may not fully offset employer contributions if passed on through lower wages. Providing additional information on formality raises WTP, but mainly among those already having a higher valuation of formality. © 2026 The Author

Title: A comprehensive review on ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion technology for engine applications: a utopia or still a challenge?
Abstract: Amid the global pursuit of carbon neutrality and energy transition, the decarbonization of engines has become an inevitable trend. Ammonia, featuring zero-carbon content and high hydrogen density, offers advantages such as easy storage and transport, a mature industrial chain and low cost, making it a promising alternative fuel for carbon–neutral energy systems. However, the inert combustion of pure ammonia severely limits its direct application in engines. Given the physicochemical differences between hydrogen and ammonia, blending highly reactive hydrogen can create novel combustion schemes for ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels. Notably, a critical gap remains between current fundamental reaction kinetics of ammonia-hydrogen systems and their engineering application in macro-scale engines. Therefore, this paper systemically reviews the latest technological advancements in ammonia-hydrogen synergistic fuels for internal combustion power systems, focusing on reaction kinetic mechanisms, mixture formation, advanced combustion mode adaptability, and emission generation and control strategies. In engineering applications, the realization of online hydrogen production through vehicle-mounted catalytic cracking is essential for establishing a single-fuel ammonia power system. New combustion methods, such as jet ignition and spark-assisted compression ignition, show great promise in improving the efficiency of ammonia-hydrogen combustion and reducing nitrogen-based emissions. However, ammonia-hydrogen combustion systems still face several challenges, including incomplete combustion mechanisms, unreliable materials in the injection and cracking systems, low catalytic cracking efficiency and the difficulty of controlling nitrogen-based emissions. In summary, ammonia-hydrogen synergistic combustion is a vital technical approach to achieving zero-carbon combustion in engines, but its commercial application necessitates continuous technological innovation and development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A trustworthy evidential transformer with linear fusion and Gram-matrix distillation for efficient optic disc and cup segmentation
Abstract: Accurate glaucoma screening relies on the vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR), but automation remains challenging. A critical trade-off between computational efficiency, segmentation accuracy, and model trustworthiness hinders clinical deployment. Vision Transformers offer global context but suffer from quadratic complexity (O(N2)), while standard Convolutional Neural Networks lack explicit mechanisms for uncertainty quantification (UQ). To bridge this gap, we propose EviG-Former (Evidential Gram Transformer), a highly efficient student network trained via Teacher-Student distillation. Our framework combines Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) with Linear Multi-Scale Token Fusion (L-MSTF). We designed an Uncertainty-Gated Feature Fusion (UGF) module that uses epistemic uncertainty to guide gradient flow, focusing on ambiguous regions like faint vessel boundaries. Additionally, Gram-Matrix Consistency Distillation ensures the lightweight student maintains topological integrity. We validated EviG-Former on RIM-ONE-r3, Drishti-GS, ORIGA, and REFUGE datasets. It achieved highly competitive Optic Cup segmentation Dice scores (0.9004, 0.9423, 0.8916, and 0.9005, respectively) when evaluated against thirteen leading baselines. Crucially, this performance requires only 0.69M parameters (up to 178× fewer than recent high-capacity networks) while sustaining real-time processing (≈60.7 FPS). Furthermore, the estimated VCDR mean absolute error falls below the 0.05 clinical threshold on three datasets. By uniting diagnostic precision, edge efficiency, and calibrated uncertainty mapping, EviG-Former effectively addresses the traditional capacity-accuracy-trustworthiness trade-off. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Examining perceptual spillover effects in social media influencer marketing effectiveness: A PLS-SEM and fsQCA approach
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Social media influencers (SMIs) play a pertinent role in shaping brand evaluations, yet how influencer-level perceptions translate into brand-level evaluations and SMI marketing effectiveness remains unclear. Drawing on spillover effects as a theoretical lens, a two-stage quantitative approach was adopted. Results from the Stage 1 serial mediation model suggest that SMI social attractiveness is directly associated with purchase intention and indirectly associated with purchase intention through brand attitude. Contrary to prevailing assumptions, perceived SMI authenticity does not mediate the relationship between social attractiveness and purchase intention. Consistent with a spillover interpretation, perceived SMI authenticity serves as an evaluative facilitator associated with brand-level evaluations rather than directly with purchase intention. Title: When passion breeds silence: How coworkers’ work passion elicits envy and employee silence in hospitality workplaces
Abstract: While work passion is well-studied as an intrapersonal motivational construct, its interpersonal consequences for coworkers remain underexplored. Drawing primarily on the Social Functional Theory of Emotions, we examine how employees' observed work passion functions as a social signal that elicits coworker envy and, in turn, shapes silence behaviors. Across four studies (three experiments and a multi-source dyadic field study with hotel employees), we find a robust asymmetric pattern: harmonious passion primarily elicits benign envy, which is associated with prosocial silence, whereas obsessive passion primarily elicits malicious envy, which is associated with deviant silence. Cross-path effects were weaker and less consistent across studies. An exploratory field-study finding suggests that obsessive passion may occasionally relate to benign envy, although this association did not emerge in the experiments and warrants replication. This research extends passion theory by highlighting its interpersonal signaling effects and reframes silence as a strategic emotion-regulation response. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: How punishment sensitivity affects delay discounting: The mediating role of functional connectivity between the left dorsal medial prefrontal cortex and right postcentral gyrus
Abstract: Punishment sensitivity refers to an individual's tendency to perceive and respond to punishment and other negative outcomes. Delay discounting refers to that an individual tends to devalue the subjective worth of future rewards as the waiting time increases. Previous findings suggest that punishment sensitivity may be related to delay discounting, but direct evidence for this association and the neural mechanisms underlying this relationship remain unclear. To address this question, we combined behavioral measurements, voxel-based morphometry (VBM), resting-state fMRI, and mediation analysis to investigate their brain-behavior mechanisms. Behaviorally, punishment sensitivity negatively correlated with delay discounting. Furthermore, VBM analysis found that the gray matter volume (GMV) of the left dorsal medial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC_L) is positively associated with punishment sensitivity, and neuroimaging results revealed that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC_L and the right postcentral gyrus (PCG_R) was positively associated with punishment sensitivity. More critically, mediation analysis showed that this functional connectivity exhibited a partial mediation with a statistical suppressor effect in the association with delay discounting. These results suggest that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC_L and PCG_R may represent a neural correlate of this association, providing new insights and a neurobiological interpretation for this association. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Federated knowledge graph-driven multimodal neuroinformatics for early diabetes-related cognitive risk prediction
Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to cognitive decline and neurodegeneration through intertwined metabolic, vascular, and neuroinflammatory mechanisms. Despite growing clinical evidence, early identification of diabetes-related cognitive risk remains challenging due to the heterogeneous, longitudinal, and distributed nature of healthcare data. Existing predictive models typically rely on centralized, static learning paradigms, which limit scalability, privacy preservation, and adaptability to evolving patient trajectories. In this paper, we propose CNEC, a Continual federated knowledge graph-driven multimodal Neuroinformatics framework for Early diabetes-related Cognitive risk prediction. CNEC integrates heterogeneous multimodal data–including EHRs, metabolic biomarkers, lifestyle factors, and IoMT signals–into a diabetes-aware knowledge graph that explicitly models metabolic, vascular, and neurocognitive interactions. A relation-aware graph neural network is employed to learn interpretable representations, while continual learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting under longitudinal data shifts. Federated learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative training across distributed healthcare institutions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CNEC consistently outperforms various baselines, achieving up to a 6.1% improvement in AUC and significantly enhanced robustness under continual updates, with less than 1.5% performance degradation in federated settings. These results indicate that CNEC provides an effective, scalable, and interpretable solution for proactive cognitive risk assessment in populations with diabetes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: From rejection sensitivity to phubbing: Self-compassion and self-uncertainty as serial mediators and a self-compassion writing intervention
Abstract: Phubbing—attending to one's smartphone in another person's presence—is widespread, yet its dispositional and intrapersonal correlates remain poorly understood. Drawing on the cognitive-affective model of rejection sensitivity (RS) and a self-regulatory resource framework, we examined whether RS is associated with phubbing through two intrapersonal processes: reduced self-compassion and heightened self-uncertainty, operationalized as low self-concept clarity. Across three studies with Chinese university students, we combined a cross-sectional survey (Study 1, N = 1202), an experiment crossing measured high- versus low-RS groups with a social-context recall manipulation (Study 2, N = 197), and a four-week randomized self-compassion expressive-writing intervention with one-month follow-up (Study 3, N = 87 completers). In Study 1, RS was positively associated with phubbing, with statistical indirect associations via self-compassion, self-uncertainty, and their serial combination. Study 2 replicated these indirect associations and showed that social context moderated the indirect pathway through self-compassion: relative to a neutral condition, it was larger after rejection recall and smaller after acceptance recall. In Study 3, self-compassion writing, relative to neutral writing, produced larger gains in self-compassion and larger reductions in phubbing, sustained at follow-up. The findings identify intrapersonal responses to rejection as correlates of phubbing and provide preliminary evidence for a targeted writing intervention. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: RFEP-SI-Fed: Fuzzy risk-entropy prediction safety island with federated reinforcement learning for low-carbon dispatch of nitrogen-hydrogen-ammonia coupled multi-park integrated energy systems
Abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy requires multi-park integrated energy systems (IESs) to coordinate electricity, heat, cooling, hydrogen, ammonia, and nitrogen while retaining local operational data and screening safety-critical actions before execution. This study proposes RFEP-SI-Fed, which integrates a six-carrier N2-H2-NH3 dispatch model, risk-weighted fuzzy-entropy assessment with Green/Yellow/Red Safety Island control, and FedProx-based PPO coordination. In the original three-park representative-day benchmark, aggregate operating cost decreased from 46,640 to 38,960 CNY/day (16.5%) and aggregate carbon-trading cost decreased from 5460 to 3590 CNY/day (34.2%) relative to the NoMonitor baseline. Warning coverage ranged from 92.1% to 94.7%, the average warning lead time was 22.4 min, and the complete configuration achieved a 96% survival rate in the reported ablation evaluation. The extended evaluation used three independent training seeds, six program-generated out-of-distribution scenarios, 3-, 6-, and 12-park systems, communication-delay and client-dropout tests, optimizer comparisons, and parameter screening. From 3 to 12 parks, mean server-side aggregation latency increased from 11.45 ± 2.92 to 40.79 ± 6.62 ms, while mean cost per park increased by 2.42%. One- to three-round aggregation delays increased paired mean cost by 4.57–5.66%. Title: The Integration of Islamic Religious Values in the Ritual Mantras of Pinisi Boat-Making as Instructional Material for Literature Learning in Islamic Schools

Abstract: This study aims to integrate Islamic religiosity values embedded in the ritual mantras of Pinisi boat-making into literary learning materials for madrasah education. Title: Fusion techniques of time frequency-based images to predict the outcome of rTMS depression therapy
Abstract: Depression is a mental condition that can lead to suicide and self-harm. Predicting the outcome of depression treatment is one of the most difficult tasks for clinicians. Among various treatment options, repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is a widely used non-invasive method. Predicting rTMS response using Electroencephalogram (EEG) data is difficult because of high inter-subject variability and limited features from single-domain analysis. We introduce two fusion techniques, montage and blending, to overcome these limitations and extract richer features from EEG-derived Time-Frequency (TF) images. We then propose a lightweight custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on fused TF representations. We use a primary dataset of 15 patients and a secondary dataset of 46 patients. We run two sets of experiments. The first set uses segment-level 10-fold cross-validation. In this setup segments from the same patient can appear in both training and testing. The Montage CWT_ST fusion reaches 99.90% accuracy on the primary dataset and 91.90% on the secondary dataset. The second set uses strict subject-disjoint cross-validation. All segments of a patient stay in one fold and no patient appears in both training and testing. Performance collapses. We test four time–frequency methods, six fusion mechanisms, and fourteen model architectures. With one exception, every configuration on both cohorts falls between AUC 0.31 and 0.54 and every 95% confidence interval contains 0.5. A patient-level permutation test on the best standalone method returns p = 0.703. The best subject-level result is Montage CWT_ST on the primary cohort, which reaches AUC 0.874 ± 0.183 and 82.7% accuracy. The same fusion strategy on the same pair of methods reaches 0.514 on the secondary cohort, so the mechanism behind this difference is not yet established and we identify it as the main target for follow-up work. The gap between the two experimental setups is the main result. Segment-level validation raises accuracy from chance to near-perfect on this data. Similar figures in the EEG literature should therefore be read together with the fold construction used to produce them. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
