Title: Wuwei Huanglian Wan inhibits Helicobacter pylori and alleviates associated gastritis: host metabolic remodeling and altered IL-6/STAT3 signaling
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Wuwei Huanglian Wan (WWHLW) is a traditional Tibetan medicine formula developed by Tibetan physician Takpe Pingcuo and officially documented in the Ministry of Health Drug Standards for Tibetan Medicines (Volume I, 1995). It has long been used for the treatment of gastrointestinal disorders, particularly conditions associated with gastrointestinal discomfort and inflammation. Given the overlap between its traditional indications and the clinical manifestations of H. pylori-associated gastritis (HAG), WWHLW represents a promising candidate for the management of H. pylori infection and related gastric inflammation. In addition, several constituent herbs of WWHLW have demonstrated anti-H. pylori and anti-inflammatory activities, providing a pharmacological basis for further investigating its therapeutic effects. Aim of the study: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the therapeutic effects of WWHLW against H. pylori infection and HAG, and to explore the biological processes associated with these effects through integrated multi-omics and experimental validation. Materials and methods: The therapeutic effects of WWHLW were evaluated through in vitro antibacterial assays and an H. pylori-infected mouse model. UHPLC-HRMS/MS was employed for chemical profiling and identification of serum-absorbed constituents. Serum metabolomics, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, network pharmacology analysis, molecular docking analysis, and molecular biological analyses were integrated to investigate the metabolic, microbial, and signaling changes associated with its therapeutic activity. Results: WWHLW exhibited anti-H. pylori activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of 0.2-0.5 mg/mL against both standard strains and multidrug-resistant clinical isolates. At MIC concentrations, WWHLW treatment altered the expression of multiple virulence-associated genes and reduced gastric H. pylori colonization by 93.8% in infected mice. UHPLC-HRMS/MS analysis putatively annotated 121 compounds in the WWHLW extracts, of which 10 prototype constituents were detected in serum after oral administration. Integrated metabolomics and network pharmacology analyses revealed alterations in lipid and amino acid-related metabolic pathways following WWHLW treatment. Gut microbiota analysis showed that WWHLW was associated with less pronounced alterations in microbial diversity and composition than antibiotic treatment. Correlation analysis further revealed statistical associations between microbial taxa and lipid and amino acid-related features. Experimental validation showed that WWHLW reduced inflammatory cytokine expression and suppressed STAT3 phosphorylation, consistent with altered IL-6/STAT3-related molecular changes. Conclusions: WWHLW exhibits therapeutic potential against H. pylori infection and HAG through combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory effects. Title: From facial synchronization to social conformity: A computational analysis of emotional contagion in online co-viewing
Abstract: This study examines emotional contagion and social conformity in online co-viewing environments, where viewers can observe one another's facial expressions during shared media experiences. Using a 2 (group size: 3 vs. 8) × 3 (emotional valence: happy, neutral, mixed) between-subjects experiment, we applied deep learning–based facial expression analysis (DeepFace) to capture participants' emotional responses on a frame-by-frame basis. Emotional contagion was operationalized as frame-by-frame facial expression synchronization between participants and co-viewers. The results showed that facial expression synchronization was significantly higher in smaller groups and in the happy-valence condition, suggesting that emotional contagion occurred even without direct interpersonal interaction. Contrary to predictions based on classic conformity research, synchronization was stronger in smaller groups, indicating that visual social cues may operate differently in online co-viewing than in face-to-face settings. Time-lag analyses further showed that facial expression synchronization was strongest with no temporal delay and declined as the lag increased, suggesting that emotional contagion emerged rapidly during online co-viewing. These findings extend current understanding of emotional contagion and social conformity in video-mediated communication by showing that visually mediated emotional cues can shape shared affective responses in ways that differ from established patterns of face-to-face social influence. Methodologically, this study illustrated the usefulness of AI-based facial expression analysis for examining dynamic emotional processes during shared media experiences. The findings also provide practical implications for designing online co-viewing platforms that leverage visual social cues to enhance shared viewing experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Fu H.; Dong Q.; Ye P.; Cui X.; Chai Q.; Zhang Y.; Feng R.; Song C.; Jiang H.
Title: hnRNPU regulates the sorting of exo-miR-125a-5p in colon epithelial cells and its role in realgar-induced central nervous system toxicity
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Elucidating the mechanisms underlying realgar-induced toxicity is essential for the early prevention and treatment of arsenic-related adverse effects and for reducing the associated healthcare burden. Aim of study: Owing to its poor solubility, realgar preferentially accumulates in the intestine after oral administration. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which realgar regulates exosomal miR-125a-5p (exo-miR-125a-5p) sorting in colonic epithelial cells and to investigate the role of exo-miR-125a-5p in realgar-induced central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Materials and methods: A chronic realgar-exposed mouse model was established and combined with AAV9-mediated hnRNPU knockdown, miR-125a-5p-enriched exosome administration, and probiotic intervention. Complementary in vitro studies were performed using YAMC cells subjected to hnRNPU silencing or co-treatment with realgar and L-cysteine sulfinic acid (LCSA). Small RNA sequencing, 16S rDNA sequencing, quantitative proteomics, untargeted metabolomics, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), miRNA pull-down, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), Western blotting, and other molecular biological approaches were integrated to systematically investigate the molecular mechanism underlying realgar-regulated exo-miR-125a-5p sorting in colonic epithelial cells and its contribution to realgar-induced CNS toxicity. Results: Realgar exposure induced dose-dependent colonic injury, altered the exosomal miRNA profile of colonic epithelial cells, and significantly reduced the secretion of exo-miR-125a-5p. Mechanistically, the RNA-binding protein hnRNPU directly bound mature miR-125a-5p, enhanced its post-transcriptional stability, and promoted its nuclear retention, thereby limiting its loading into exosomes. Realgar-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis reduced the abundance of Lactobacillus and the level of its metabolite, LCSA, resulting in aberrant upregulation of hnRNPU. The consequent reduction in circulating exo-miR-125a-5p relieved repression of the STAT1 signaling pathway, leading to activation of the microglial STAT1–NLRP3 inflammasome axis and exacerbation of realgar-induced CNS toxicity. Conclusion: Realgar induces both colonic and central nervous system toxicity. Mechanistically, realgar disrupts gut microbial homeostasis, depleting Lactobacillus-derived LCSA, which promotes hnRNPU expression and enhances the nuclear retention of mature miR-125a-5p. This process suppresses miR-125a-5p sorting into exosomes, reduces circulating exo-miR-125a-5p levels, and consequently activates the microglial STAT1–NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, thereby aggravating CNS toxicity. These findings identify a previously unrecognized gut microbiota–metabolite–RNA-binding protein axis governing exosomal miRNA sorting and establish exo-miR-125a-5p as a critical mediator linking intestinal injury to neuroinflammation. This study provides new mechanistic insights into realgar-induced colonic and CNS toxicity and expands our understanding of gut–brain axis-mediated toxicological mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chain performance, ripple effects, and viability
Abstract: We simulate impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chains (SCs). First, we articulate the specific features that frame a global energy crisis as a unique type of SC large-scale systemic shocks characterized by a long-term disruption existence, disruption propagations (i.e., the ripple effect), a combination of immediate and delayed effects, cross-industry ripple effects, and mutual interrelations of SC and economic impacts. Second, we demonstrate how simulation-based methodology can be used to examine and predict the impacts of global energy crises on SC performance using the example of the Strait of Hormuz blockage and anyLogistix software. The major observation from the simulation experiments is that global energy crisis impacts resemble the COVID-19 pandemic patterns and ripple effects in 2020–2022 with reduced logistics capacities, delivery delays, and production shutdowns, supplemented by inflation effects observed in tariff turbulences in 2025. Other important factors influencing the shock impacts and propagation mechanisms are the duration of the energy crisis and SC viability. We observe that viable SCs with greater variety in production, supply, logistics, and energy structures are better able to absorb shocks. The outcomes of this research can be used by decision-makers to predict the operational and long-term impacts of global energy crises on SCs and to develop viability strategies. Our models are readily available to be used in practice for SC stress testing. They offer recommendations on proactively building adaptability and reconfiguring in response to disruptions to survive in a world without a reliable energy supply, incorporating large-scale systemic shocks into operational models. © 2026 The Author(s). Author full names: Hong, Binsheng (59005012100); Hu, Jinchang (57205501604); Qu, Yubin (57203360707); Lu, Jiangtao (59815998200); Huang, Song (55608828500); Zheng, Changyou (36652245300)
Title: Cross-language vulnerability migration in the rust supply chain: A survey of mechanisms, risks, and countermeasures
Abstract: Rust is widely adopted in system software and critical infrastructure due to its ownership model and compile-time memory-safety guarantees. However, modern Cargo-based software systems frequently combine unsafe Rust code, foreign-function interfaces, wrapper crates, generated bindings, native C/C++ components, build scripts, and transitive dependencies. These mechanisms create cross-language vulnerability paths through which upstream vulnerabilities or vulnerability-relevant assumptions may become reachable, transformed, or amplified in Rust software. In this survey, we use cross-language vulnerability migration (CLVM) as an analytical term for tracing such paths, rather than as a vulnerability class independent of unsafe-Rust safety, FFI safety, or software supply-chain security. Following Kitchenham's guidelines for systematic literature reviews, we analyze 168 studies published between January 2021 and April 2026. Using an evidence-layered synthesis, we distinguish Rust-specific evidence from upstream, comparative-ecosystem, and general supply-chain governance evidence and examine how security-relevant conditions cross unsafe, FFI, migration, and native-component boundaries before being propagated or amplified through Cargo dependencies. Once a vulnerability or security-relevant assumption has crossed a language or native-component boundary, its impact may be amplified or obscured through transitive dependencies, incomplete metadata, delayed remediation, and limited supply-chain visibility. The evidence is strongest for individual mechanisms: translation studies mainly assess correctness and unsafe-surface reduction, while complete sequences from a foreign or native origin to Rust-side reachability, dependency-level propagation, and downstream remediation remain rarely analyzed. These findings reveal the limits of language-centric security approaches and highlight the need for boundary-aware, reachability-aware, native-aware, and governance-aware defenses for Rust supply chains. © 2026

Authors: Li Z.; Zhao Q.; Xu J.; Jiang J.; Zhang J.; Li J.
Title: Identifying key regions in spatial networks via regular hexagonal grids
Abstract: Spatially embedded complex systems are often disrupted at the regional level rather than by isolated node or edge failures, making key region identification a challenging combinatorial problem. Existing partition-based approaches either suffer from overlap and coverage trade-offs with circular regions or rely on square grids that may inadequately capture spatial influence and accessibility in real-world settings. We adopt a non-overlapping regular hexagonal grid and propose Key Region Identification with Graph Neural Networks using Regular Hexagonal Grids (KRIG-H). The framework treats each grid cell as a region node and constructs a region graph through geometric mapping between original edges and grid cells. Trained on synthetic spatial networks, KRIG-H generalizes to unseen real-world networks. Using the fraction of removed regions as a normalized evaluation scale, we compare KRIG-H with six region-centrality baselines under both hexagonal and square decompositions, with random region removal as a control. On real-world networks, KRIG-H reduces AUC by 24.88 % relative to its square counterpart, while hexagonal partitioning lowers the overall average AUC across methods by 21.77 %. Results on synthetic and real infrastructure and road networks show that KRIG-H achieves effective, robust, and transferable region-based vulnerability analysis with limited additional computational cost. © 2026

Title: Sociotechnical imaginaries and acceptance of artificial intelligence in education: A longitudinal social media analysis
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a site of public debate on social media concerning the future of education, raising broader societal questions about human behavior, judgment, and accountability. However, how educational AI is publicly interpreted and contested in everyday digital discourse is still underexplored. Addressing this gap, this study examines how AI in education is publicly discoursed through a longitudinal mixed-methods analysis of user comments responding to TED Talk videos on YouTube that circulate influential public narratives about technological and educational futures between December 2022 and November 2025. The study traces changing public orientations towards educational AI and the future visions underpinning them. Multilingual sentiment analysis reveals a fluctuating three-year trajectory, with sentiment becoming more positive in the middle period before negative sentiment rose again in 2025. Thematic analysis of the public discourse further identifies three sociotechnical imaginaries through which commenters articulate competing visions of educational futures: (1) human-centered education in an age of cognitive displacement, where concerns focus on preserving critical thinking and human judgment; (2) educational transformation through literacy, governance, and accountability; and (3) teachers as mediators of competing AI-powered educational futures. The study contributes to existing scholarship by demonstrating how acceptance and resistance toward AI in education are socially and discursively constructed through competing visions of desirable educational futures in digital public spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Sung Y.
Title: Translanguaging as an epistemic mechanism in Korean immigrant parents’ mediation of mathematical meaning
Abstract: This study investigates how Korean immigrant parents draw on translanguaging practices to mediate mathematical meaning with their elementary-aged children during home mathematics interaction. Using video-based, ethnographically informed observations of six sessions across three parent-child dyads, the analysis examines how parents coordinated Korean and English alongside gesture, diagrams, and tools to make mathematical relationships more visible, interpretable, and open to negotiation in real time. In this study, translanguaging is conceptualized as the epistemic mechanism through which mathematical meaning is mediated. The findings suggest that parents used translanguaging to diagnose procedural and structural mismatches, make unfamiliar terminology more accessible, bridge semantic and structural relationships across concepts, reorganize algebraic representations, and coordinate geometric action through multimodal guidance. The most salient form of this mechanism appeared in diagnostic interactions, where bilingual contrast and multimodal coordination made otherwise implicit mismatches visible and available for repair. The study contributes to translanguaging research in mathematics by respecifying translanguaging not only as a resource for participation but as an epistemic mechanism through which mathematical structure is made visible and available for reorganization. The study also suggests that Korean-English interaction provides an analytically productive context for examining how typologically associated linguistic resources become interactionally available in mathematical activity. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Author full names: Rebesco, Pierre (60572824700); Akimowicz, Mikaël (55675511700)
Title: Know its worth? Factors affecting the social acceptability of water reuse: A mixed methods planned behavior model
Abstract: Due to strong demographic pressure, rapid urban development, and climate change, water demand is increasing while usable freshwater supplies are being depleted. The reuse of treated wastewater (RTWW) is one of the avenues currently being explored to ensure the quantitative and qualitative security of the water supply. The interests for social acceptability emerged with risk management approaches and the subsequent debates on the role of technical progress, the implementation of major development projects, and their consequences for the environment between the late 1970s and early 1980s. The purpose of this article is to identify the factors that influence the building of RTWW acceptability. This study was carried out in southern France. It combines a quantitative survey on behavior related to engaging in RTWW, based on Ajzen's theory of planned behavior, with a qualitative socioeconomic study aimed at understanding representations and beliefs regarding RTWW. The findings show that a lack of knowledge about RTWW and the implementation of only a few RTWW projects result in a normative gap and a perceived lack of control. In addition, trust in managers and public authorities, the quality of treatments, as well as risks perceptions – particularly those relating to health – significantly influence intentions to engage in RTWW. Lastly, several factors such as emotions, types of uses, and environmental awareness play an underlying role by helping build perceptions of water reuse, trust in relevant stakeholders, and more accurate perceptions of risks. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Assessing the viability of urban rooftop photovoltaic systems under new regulatory frameworks in Brazil via an evolutionary real options approach
Abstract: The transition towards decentralized and sustainable urban energy systems requires robust decision-making frameworks that account for policy changes, market uncertainties, and investment flexibility. This study applies an Evolutionary Real Options Approach (EROA) to evaluate the economic viability of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems in Brazil under the New Mark of Distributed Generation (NMDG), a regulatory change that alters incentives for net metering. By incorporating stochastic volatility models, such as the Heston model and Geometric Brownian motion (GBM) with jumps, this work quantifies the impact of regulatory changes on investment timing and system sizing decisions. Results indicate a significant reduction in financial returns and a delay in investment decisions under the new regulation. The introduction of the new regulation has led to reductions in returns of approximately 18% and 23% for the Heston and GBM with jumps models, respectively. In terms of decision sequences, the Heston model presents increased opportunities for phased investment due to its greater flexibility. On the other hand, the GBM with jumps model encourages immediate investment in a complete solar system. The new regulation results in a delay of 6 to 12 months at entry points, regardless of the chosen model. These findings contribute to the understanding of urban energy transitions, policy impacts on decentralized generation, and investment dynamics in sustainable urban infrastructure. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Lean limit extension Aspects of gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine with hydrogen fraction
Abstract: An experimental investigation was conducted on a spark-ignition gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine equipped with hydrogen port fuel injection (PFI) to investigate the effects of hydrogen enrichment on combustion characteristics, thermal efficiency, and exhaust emissions under lean-burn operation. Gasoline–hydrogen blends with different hydrogen mass fractions were tested at varying equivalence ratios, while spark timing was adjusted between 14° and 35° bTDC to compensate for hydrogen’s higher flame speed. The results showed that hydrogen addition accelerated combustion, shortened combustion duration, and significantly extended the lean operating limit. However, hydrogen enrichment generally increased nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions because of higher in-cylinder combustion temperatures. Under homogeneous combustion conditions, hydrogen was supplied through port fuel injection (PFI) in the intake manifold with a start of injection (SOI) of 210° during the suction stroke, while the gasoline direct injection (GDI) SOI was set at 330° during the engine suction stroke. With a spark timing of 22° bTDC, 5.17% hydrogen by mass fraction reduced nitric oxide emissions by 0.29 g/kW-h and improved the hydrocarbon–NOx emission trade-off. Stable engine operation was achieved at an equivalence ratio of 0.55. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The Filipino attitudinal framework for academic success and well-being: Exploring the role of attitudes toward lesbians and gay men and social interest on psychological well-being and perceived academic performance
Abstract: Extant knowledge has established associations among the psychological constructs attitudes toward lesbians and gay men (ATLG), social interest (SI), psychological well-being (PW), and perceived academic performance (PAP). However, these studies for the most part have been compartmentalized. Very few, if not none, have explored the plausible complexity underlying the interactions among these constructs. Using a correlational cross-sectional research design covering 932 students (between 16 to 26 years old) in a public university, I hypothesized that ATLG, SI, and PW interact to play an enabling role in the pursuit of academic excellence. I likewise hypothesized that sex (SE), sexual orientation (SO), gender identity (GI), and gender expression (GE) as possessing moderating effects on ATLG and SI. A structural equation model (SEM) on the interaction of all of the aforementioned variables was posited. The results of the SEM revealed that ATLG and SI are directly associated to PW and PAP. Moreover, PW mediates the relationship between ATLG and PAP, and that of SI and PAP. However, SE, SO, GI, and GE were found to have no moderating effects on ATLG and SI. Likewise, SI does not mediate the relationship between ATLG and PW, and that of ATLG and PAP. Consequently, a proposed model is derived, referred to as Parreño’s Filipino Attitudinal Framework for Academic Success and Well-being or PAFIFAB, with model fit indices APC = 0.199, P < 0.001 and ARS = 0.136, P < 0.001. The present study contributes to integrative theory building as it underscores the importance of employing a gendered lens and having progressive attitudes and compassion in achieving positive mental and academic outcomes, thus allowing academic institutions to bring to fruition the global mandate of promoting well-being, advocating gender equality, and advancing quality education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: A novel tetrafluoroborate with giant birefringence assembled from biocompatible adenine
Abstract: Birefringent crystals with large optical anisotropy are indispensable for the achievement of optical devices miniaturization. Due to structural diversity, organic-inorganic hybrid crystals have emerged as promising platforms for modulating birefringence. However, achieving ultraviolet (UV) transparency and large birefringence simultaneously still remains a challenge due to intrinsic trade-off. Herein, a strategy that combines a biocompatible planar π-conjugated cation with non π-conjugated anion is proposed. Adenine (ADE, C5H5N5) is employed as a new birefringence-active unit and assembled with tetrafluoroborate [BF4]− anions, yielding a new fluoroborate crystal (C5H6N5)BF4 (ADE-BF4). The anhydrous two-dimensional structure, sustained by intermolecular hydrogen bonding and π-π interactions, endows ADE-BF4 with high thermal stability up to 213 °C. It features a giant birefringence of 0.439@546 nm, and the limited electron delocalization of ADE and [BF4]− endows it with a wide transparency range extending into the UV region (cutoff edge at 289 nm). Theoretical calculations disclose that the coplanarity of the planar ADE moieties contribute to the significantly enhanced birefringence. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Chen J.; Wang S.; Ke W.; Zhang J.
Title: When culture speaks through E-commerce chatbots: How collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles shape impulsive buying
Abstract: E-commerce chatbots increasingly provide product advice during online shopping, yet it remains unclear how culturally framed recommendation language shapes impulsive buying. Drawing on cultural dimensions theory, cultural priming theory, and constructivist interpretation, this study conceptualizes collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles as message-level cultural language cues rather than as measures of consumers’ stable cultural orientation. Across four experiments with 880 participants, we show that a collectivistic persuasive style increases impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as socially supported and behaviorally acceptable choices, which strengthens social conformity. By contrast, an individualistic persuasive style reduces impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as choices requiring confirmation against personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit, which strengthens self-referencing. The findings further identify two boundary conditions. Human labeling strengthens the collectivistic pathway through social conformity by making group-oriented language more likely to be treated as socially relevant advice, whereas AI labeling shifts source perception toward algorithmic advice and strengthens the individualistic pathway through self-referencing by increasing attention to personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit. Low algorithm accessibility strengthens the collectivistic pathway, whereas high algorithm accessibility strengthens the individualistic pathway. These findings show that chatbot recommendations do more than transmit product information. They shape how consumers interpret the perceived source, social relevance, and personal applicability of recommendations, thereby influencing whether recommendations are quickly accepted as purchase decisions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: High-performance thin film nanocomposite membrane prepared from 2D ZIF-67 nanosheets and Pebax for natural gas dehydration
Abstract: Thin film nanocomposites (TFNs) fabricated with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are considered as promising alternatives for natural gas (NG) dehydration. However, it remains difficult to realize both high water permeance and selectivity at the same time. The ultrathin selective layer of the TFN structure inherently provides higher permeance than traditional membranes. In this research, TFN membranes were fabricated via incorporating ultrathin ZIF-67 nanosheets into a Pebax 1657 polymer matrix with polyacrylonitrile (PAN) porous support. The 2D ZIF-67, characterized by their leaf-like morphology, create well-defined molecular sieving channels while maintaining excellent interfacial compatibility. A key innovation of this work is the achievement of exceptionally high separation performance. The optimized membrane with 12.5 wt% ZIF-67 loading demonstrated exceptional separation capabilities, a remarkable 38,356 GPU in water vapor permeation along with H2O/CH4 separation factor of 18,235 was documented, which surpasses most reported membranes for NG dehydration. The synthesized membranes also exhibited exceptional stability of 10 days. This work demonstrates that 2D MOF nanosheets can overcome the typical permeability-selectivity trade-off, advancing membrane based NG dehydration toward practical applications. Copyright © 2026. Title: The rise of religious influencers and their impact on social communication in Asia: A systematic review of Da’wah, preaching, and public discourse
Abstract: This systematic review examines how digital platform ecosystems have reshaped Islamic da’wah, contemporary preaching practices, and public-facing religious engagement in Asian contexts through the growing prominence of online faith-based opinion leaders. The review synthesizes studies indexed in Scopus covering the period 2020–2025. Using a qualitative thematic synthesis approach, the article analyzes recurring patterns related to authority transformation, platform-specific communication strategies, credibility and authenticity, youth engagement, religious moderation, gender participation, ethical risks, media literacy, and institutional adaptation. The findings show that religious authority in digital environments is increasingly negotiated through visibility, engagement, relatability, and algorithmic circulation rather than through formal institutional credentials alone. Religious communicators successfully expand access to religious learning by adopting short-form video, live interaction, collaborative content, and personalized storytelling, particularly for younger audiences. At the same time, the review identifies substantial risks, including interpretive oversimplification, misinformation, commercialization pressures, gendered constraints on legitimacy, and the amplification of polarizing content by platform logics. The study further demonstrates that sustainable digital religious communication requires hybrid governance arrangements that combine theological stewardship, operational content standards, media literacy interventions, and strategic collaboration between scholars, institutions, and digital communicators. Overall, the review highlights that the digitization of da’wah is not merely a technological shift, but a structural transformation in how religious authority, trust, and public moral discourse are produced, circulated, and contested across Asian societies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Development of an immersion-type hydrogel-integrated microfluidic glass fiber-based analytical device and its application to smartphone-assisted glucose colorimetric assay
Abstract: Microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) are attractive platforms for on-site analysis; however, quantitative analysis remains challenging because sampling strongly influences analytical performance. Existing sampling methods often require precise volumetric sampling or operator-dependent handling, which involves an inherent trade-off between analytical simplicity and quantitative reliability. To overcome this limitation, herein, we propose the concept of a quantitative assay using an immersion-type hydrogel-integrated microfluidics glass fiber-based analytical device (IHμGFAD). The IHμGFAD consisted of a reagent-encapsulated hydrogel for reaction/detection with a glass fiber channel for sampling. The combination of the hydrogel with the glass fiber channel was realized by exploiting the self-adhesive property of hydrophobic patterns fabricated using a liquid crystal display 3D printer. The immersion-based quantitative assay using the IHμGFAD was demonstrated with a glucose oxidase/horseradish peroxidase-based glucose colorimetric assay as a model system. The limit of glucose detection (3σ) was estimated to be 68 μM. The immersion-based assay was also applied to the quantification of glucose in human serum controls and pooled human serum, demonstrating its potential applicability to real-sample analysis. The immersion-based assay provides a μGFAD-based analytical method that achieves both practical user-friendliness and reliable quantitative performance, and it contributes to the advancement of on-site quantitative analysis in a wide range of fields, including healthcare, environmental monitoring, and food safety. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Ng Y.M.M.; Maslowska E.
Author full names: Ng, Yee Man Margaret (56957717900); Maslowska, Ewa (56830422700)
Title: Platform abandonment through push–pull–mooring: Trust, commitment, and generational patterns in U.S. social media
Abstract: Generational frameworks frequently explain platform adoption, but rarely platform abandonment. Through a stratified survey of 990 U.S. adults, this study examines how age cohorts (digital natives vs. digital immigrants) respond to platform change and what predicts abandonment across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, and TikTok. Using the push-pull-mooring (PPM) framework, we found that cohort labels did not predict exit in pooled models. Distrust was the strongest pooled push predictor. Affective and normative commitment reduced abandonment odds, whereas need-based commitment increased them. Generation did, however, structure post-exit destinations: among Twitter/X leavers, digital natives were more likely to name Instagram and TikTok, and older cohorts were more likely to name Facebook. Abandonment is better explained by institutional distrust and multidimensional attachment than by cohort labels, but generation remains consequential for where users go next. Platforms seeking retention should repair credibility and cultivate wanted attachment rather than relying on lock-in or age targeting alone. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zeng L.; Wu S.; Yin X.; Lu W.
Title: Plug-and-play watermarking method for diffusion models via distribution alignment
Abstract: Generative models are widely distributed to multiple users, raising significant concerns about tracing malicious content dissemination. While watermarking is a common solution, existing methods struggle to support scalable multi-user scenarios and maintain watermark integrity under adversarial manipulations. To address these issues, we propose a plug-and-play watermarking method for diffusion models based on distribution alignment, enabling effective detection and per-user traceability. Specifically, watermarks are embedded directly into latent representations without altering diffusion model parameters, allowing seamless deployment and replacement across different users. Our method leverages the connection between latent representations and generated images to ensure high watermark accuracy. Furthermore, we enforce distribution constraints to couple watermark integrity with image utility. This mechanism ensures that generated content inherently carries the watermark while neutralizing malicious bypass attempts. Experimental results demonstrate our method’s high effectiveness, achieving average true positive rates exceeding 95% for both detection and traceability under various complex distortions. Crucially, the framework thwarts Quality-Constrained Evasion (QCE) by forcing the semantic quality of tampered images to drop to unusable levels (CLIP score < 0.2). Collectively, our method provides a robust and secure plug-and-play framework for tracing the source of generated content in generative AI deployment scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Author full names: Kwon, Deuksin (57193776885); Lee, Elena Hayoung (60135822800); Lucas, Gale M. (56176552700); Gratch, Jonathan (6701390206)
Title: Artificial intelligence in negotiation research: From computational negotiators to psychological evidence
Abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence are reshaping how negotiation is conducted and studied. AI systems increasingly enter negotiation research in two broad roles: as part of the negotiation process, either as negotiators or as support for human negotiators, and as research instruments that annotate, standardize, and simulate negotiation at scale. As negotiators, these systems range from theory-driven agents to data-driven and hybrid agents, each embedding different assumptions about negotiation. As instruments, they promise scale, consistency, and control, but also raise risks of circular inference, in which AI appears to reveal patterns in human negotiation while actually reproducing patterns learned from its own training data. This review organizes emerging work on AI and negotiation around these two roles and argues that their scientific value depends on psychological grounding. Used naively, AI becomes a mirror of its own assumptions. Used carefully, with grounding in theory and calibration against human evidence, AI can become a transformative tool for advancing negotiation science. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Tian W.; Lan B.; Wu H.; Yu R.; Cui Z.
Title: Hierarchical diagnosis and operating-condition tracing of energy-efficiency abnormalities in crude oil distillation units
Abstract: Dynamic energy-efficiency abnormalities in crude oil distillation unit (CDU) are difficult to diagnose because process variables are strongly coupled and abnormal operating conditions may affect multiple process sections. This study develops a hierarchical diagnostic framework that progressively narrows the diagnostic scope from process-level abnormality monitoring to process-section localization and finally to operating-condition tracing. First, slow feature analysis (SFA) is employed to monitor the dynamic energy-efficiency state and detect deviations from normal operation. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is then used for process-section classification to narrow the diagnostic scope to a specific process section. Subsequently, a convolutionally encoded heat-map strategy based on sliding-window feature extraction is applied to characterize temporal deviations among variables within the localized section and trace the associated abnormal operating condition. Eight abnormal operating conditions are simulated for the CDU, with 2400 samples generated for each condition at a 2-min sampling interval. Using 21 selected process variables, the CNN achieves average precision, recall, and F1 scores of 99.84 %, 99.90 %, and 99.87 %, respectively, under the reported experimental setting. SFA achieves an average recall of 99.54 %, a false-positive rate of 0.39 %, and a fault detection delay of 7 min, compared with 98.79 %, 2.26 %, and 15.25 min for PCA. Two industrial operating cases are further analyzed to examine the practical applicability of the proposed diagnostic workflow. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework for hierarchical energy-efficiency abnormality detection and operating-condition tracing in CDU processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Lin K.; Coutellier L.
Author full names: Lin, Katrina (59806784200); Coutellier, Laurence (24075442900)
Title: Impact of parvalbumin interneuron inhibition during adolescence on social behaviors
Abstract: Adolescence is an important period for the maturation of prefrontal circuits and the complex behaviors it regulates, including social interactions. A major component of this developmental process is the maturation of parvalbumin-expressing (PV) interneurons, which regulate excitation-inhibition balance and contribute to the refinement of cortical networks. Although PV neurons have been implicated in social behaviors, their role during adolescence in shaping social behavior development remains unclear. To address this question, we chemogenetically inhibited prefrontal PV interneurons in male and female mice during either adolescence or adulthood and assessed long-term changes in PV network characteristics and social behavior. Adolescent PV inhibition produced persistent reductions in detectable PV neurons and increased PNN labeling surrounding PV cells, as well as reduced social motivation in males following prolonged food deprivation. In contrast, adult inhibition did not alter detectable PV neurons or PNN association, but reduced cFos expression in PV-targeted cells in the prelimbic cortex in response to a social interaction and produced changes in female social interaction patterns and sex-dependent changes in anxiety-like behavior. These findings suggest that PV interneuron activity contributes to the regulation of prefrontal inhibitory circuitry and social behavior, with disruption during adolescence producing lasting changes in PV network characteristics and social motivation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Alexithymia and everyday interpersonal emotion regulation
Abstract: Alexithymia, a multifaceted personality trait characterized by difficulties identifying and describing feelings and an externally oriented thinking style, is linked to social difficulties. Drawing on the extended process model of extrinsic interpersonal emotion regulation (IER), we examined whether higher (vs. lower) levels of alexithymia are associated with differences in how people regulate others' emotions, a pathway that may help explain why alexithymia is linked to social dysfunction. Across two ecological momentary assessment studies (Study 1: Germany, n = 129; Study 2: United States, n = 220; 6028 observations), results revealed distinct patterns of association across alexithymia facets. In both studies, the direction of associations suggested that greater difficulties identifying feelings were associated with higher IER strategy use, with this pattern most apparent for more cognitive and problem-focused strategies versus more emotion-oriented IER. In contrast, greater difficulties describing feelings were consistently linked to lower IER strategy use, whereas externally oriented thinking showed no consistent directional pattern. These findings suggest that alexithymia is associated with differential patterns of IER strategy use, underscoring IER difficulties as an interpersonal process that may contribute to links between alexithymia and social dysfunction. Our results emphasize the importance of considering the multifaceted nature of alexithymia in IER. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Fu H.; Liang J.; Liang F.; Zhang G.; Han J.
Title: FEDS: Feature and Entropy-Based Distillation Strategy for efficient learned image compression
Abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) offers strong rate–distortion performance, but many high-performing models remain too heavy for deployment. This paper introduces Feature and Entropy-based Distillation Strategy (FEDS), which transfers knowledge from a strong offline teacher to a lightweight student through output supervision, intermediate feature alignment, and entropy-guided latent supervision. The latent objective ranks teacher channels by entropy and transfers the channels with the largest expected coding cost under the student's limited channel budget. On Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC, the student stays close to the teacher, with BD-rate gaps of only 1.24%, 1.17%, and 0.55%, while reducing parameters by 63% and decreasing encoding/decoding time by about 73%. Additional channel-selection, alignment, bit-rate robustness, and transformer-family ablations confirm that FEDS provides an effective compression–efficiency trade-off. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Pore-confined synthesis of ultra-small Pt nanozymes on gold nanobipyramids for electrochemical detection of cancer cell-derived H2O2
Abstract: Accurate quantification of H2O2 released by tumor cells is important for characterizing cancer-associated oxidative stress, yet conventional biosensors often face an intrinsic trade-off between catalytic activity and structural stability. Herein, we present a rational strategy for real-time electrochemical monitoring of cancer-associated oxidative stress species through the in-situ fabrication of ultrasmall Pt nanozymes confined within the mesoporous silica shell of gold bipyramids (AuPt@SiO2). In this architecture, the Au core provides conductive nucleation and anchoring sites, the mesoporous SiO2 shell regulates Pt growth and affords structural stabilization and molecular-sieving protection, and Pt serves as the catalytic center for H2O2 reduction. The resulting AuPt@SiO2 nanozyme exhibited pronounced peroxidase-like activity with a favorable Michaelis-Menten constant (Km) of 6.08 mM toward H2O2. After integration into a Nafion-based sensing interface, the enzyme-free sensor provided complementary linear ranges of 0.25-60 mM by cyclic voltammetry and 1-2100 μM by amperometry with a detection limit at 0.3 μM of H2O2. The electrochemical sensor based on AuPt@SiO2 also demonstrated excellent repeatability and exceptional stability, retaining over 85% of its initial response after 30 days. Importantly, this platform enabled label-free monitoring of phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-triggered H2O2 efflux from MGC-803 gastric cancer cells and differentiated their oxidative-stress phenotype from that of normal gastric epithelial cells. The apparent H2O2-equivalent response normalized to cell number was approximately 1.72 × 10−13 M per cell. This work highlights the potential of confined nanozymes for high-performance H2O2 sensing and precise pathological profiling at the single-cell level. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Lin H.; Zhou T.; Guo J.; Liu Z.; Liu J.
Title: Federated multi-view information fusion based on prototype and feature distillation: A privacy-performance tradeoff method for data heterogeneity
Abstract: With the rapid development of distributed intelligent systems, federated learning has become a crucial research direction. Federated distributed training frameworks enable collaborative optimization of global models, while the ubiquitous data heterogeneity across clients severely degrades model accuracy. Although existing information sharing strategies can alleviate heterogeneous bias, they are prone to incurring privacy leakage risks. Achieving an effective trade-off between privacy preservation and model performance has thus become a core challenge. To address the privacy-performance trade-off problem in heterogeneous federated scenarios, this paper proposes a federated multi-view information fusion method based on prototype and feature distillation, termed FedTPF. Before the local model training on clients, FedTPF first trains a distillation model, and constructs dual feature views consisting of latent features derived from the distillation model and local prototypes. By minimizing the constrained distance in the latent space, dual-view feature fusion is implemented to extract minimal features with superior global generalization capability and filter redundant information. Each client leverages the well-trained distillation model for feature filtering and generates generalized features combined with differential privacy. The generalized features are further constructed as a globally shared view, which is integrated with the local data view for multi-view fusion training to mitigate data heterogeneity. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that FedTPF improves the global model accuracy without disclosing clients’ private information. Under the same privacy budget, it achieves a 3.7% performance gain compared with state-of-the-art methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Chi Y.; Zhao Y.-P.
Title: Urea revisited: Isopropyl substitution for a balanced nonlinear optical performance
Abstract: Organic nonlinear optical (NLO) materials represent a promising class of NLO crystals. Compared with inorganic NLO crystalline materials, they often exhibit stronger second-harmonic generation (SHG) responses. However, many organic NLO crystals suffer from excessively large birefringence, and there is an inherent trade-off between achieving a large SHG coefficient and maintaining a moderate birefringence. In this work, by substituting some of the hydrogen atoms in urea with isopropyl groups, we obtained the compound N,N’-diisopropylurea (DIU), which exhibits a strong SHG effect (∼0.9 × urea) and a large optical bandgap (5.91 eV), while achieving a dramatic reduction in birefringence (a 60% decrease compared to urea). The resulting birefringence is very close to that of the most classic inorganic NLO crystal, KH2PO4 (KDP), which is of great importance for the application of NLO crystals. Furthermore, using the atomic space tessellating (AST) method, we explored, at the atomic and electronic levels, the evolution pattern of the contributions of different structural motifs to the SHG coefficient and birefringence induced by the structural changes in this series. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Fast and accurate node-level hosting capacity estimation in distribution networks using graph neural networks
Abstract: This paper presents a fast and accurate method for estimating node-level hosting capacity in distribution networks using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). A large open dataset of synthetic networks, representative of Italian distribution grids, was created, and hosting capacity values were computed using AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) simulations, which are computationally expensive. This dataset was used to train a GNN regressor based on the Graph Isomorphism Network architecture, integrating path-based electrical features to capture both local and global grid dependencies. The proposed GNN is compared to a fast physics-based estimation method, showing a reduction in mean absolute error of about 30%, highlighting its ability to capture the spatial and electrical relationships embedded in the network topology and to produce physically consistent estimates. In terms of efficiency, the model achieves an inference speed over 11,000 times faster than AC-OPF, enabling hosting capacity estimation in milliseconds. This significant speed-up allows real-time applications such as interactive hosting capacity maps, large-scale scenario analysis, and decision support for distribution system operators. The model's robustness is also evaluated under out-of-distribution conditions, where some performance degradation is observed, particularly for small networks, emphasizing the importance of representative training data. Importantly, the GNN remains operational even when traditional power flow methods fail to converge, providing stable and reliable estimates without requiring manual intervention. Overall, the approach demonstrates strong potential for scalable, real-time hosting capacity assessment to support the integration of distributed energy resources. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Hand-in-river: Design of direction-dependent virtual cues of assistive/resistive force via auditory displacement and pitch variation
Abstract: This paper investigates the role of sound-only manipulations in eliciting pseudo-force perception during lateral hand movements within a virtual river environment. Building on prior formative and exploratory studies, a pseudo-force feedback design is refined, leveraging two mechanisms: (i) auditory displacement, a spatial shift in the virtual, binaural position of the hand-in-river sound, creating a conflict between where the hand is felt and where it is heard; and (ii) pitch variation, making the sound splashier or calmer by raising or lowering its pitch, relying on learned touch–sound associations. No physical force is actuated and no haptic or kinesthetic response is measured; the manipulation is entirely auditory and the dependent measure is a forced-choice judgment. A within-subjects psychophysical experiment used a two-interval forced-choice (2IFC) protocol with a 2 × 2 factorial design, evaluating pitch variation and displacement for resistance (leftward movement against the flow) and assistance (rightward movement with the flow). Results showed that both restricting displacement and pitch increase reliably biased participants toward perceiving resistance, with pitch variation being the dominant factor—suggesting that spectral content carries more perceptual weight than localization—and no interaction between cues, indicating an additive effect. Conversely, aiding displacement and pitch decrease did not reliably bias participants toward perceiving assistance—though displacement exhibited a positive trend—revealing a potential direction-dependent asymmetry. These findings refine the design space of sound-based pseudo-force feedback for inclusive immersion among visually impaired users. Resistive cues can be tuned modularly to create pseudo-haptic boundaries for navigation, while assistance likely requires strategies beyond simply inverting resistive cues. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Network-mediated information–behaviour coupling drives collective decision-making in crowd evacuation
Abstract: Emergency evacuation in real buildings is governed not only by physical interactions but also by the propagation of warnings, misinformation, and corrective cues through social and local communication channels. Cellular automaton (CA) models are widely used in crowd-evacuation modelling because their discrete transition rules enable computationally efficient simulation and large stochastic ensembles. Conventional CA formulations nevertheless often represent pedestrians as geometry-driven agents, leaving information transmission and route revision exogenous; standalone information-propagation models describe communication pathways but omit embodied route adaptation in space. Here, we develop a network-mediated cellular automaton framework to investigate information–behaviour coupling in crowd evacuation. The model integrates a floor-field CA with a dynamic small-world social network and a questionnaire-informed random utility formulation for local information acceptance, thereby coupling crowd motion, social topology, and heterogeneous behavioural response within one simulation framework. Simulations show that information–behaviour coupling accelerates route correction, weakens congestion near the failed exit, and improves both individual and collective evacuation performance relative to a geometry-driven CA. Systematic analyses further uncover the mechanisms underlying these improvements. Moderate network rewiring accelerates the spread of collective awareness via long-range shortcuts, while increasing local interaction range enhances performance up to a saturation threshold. Notably, increasing the average social degree produces an onset-and-plateau pattern in which fragmented local responses gradually become coordinated global egress. Two-parameter explorations further show that evacuation performance emerges from compensatory interactions among network topology, transmission fidelity, local interaction scale, and initial information composition, rather than from any single parameter in isolation. These findings establish information–behaviour coupling as a fundamental mechanism governing collective evacuation under uncertainty and provide a theoretical foundation for communication-aware evacuation design and management. More broadly, this work highlights the critical role of information-driven interactions in shaping collective dynamics in complex adaptive systems. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhou Y.; Lyu Y.; Wu L.-Z.; Chen M.
Title: Why and when customer-related social stressors impair service performance: A conservation of resources perspective
Abstract: Building on the conservation of resources theory, we investigate how customer-related social stressors impact service performance among hospitality employees. To explore this, we gathered data from 350 supervisor-employee pairs across twelve hotels in China through a three-wave survey. The results show that customer-related social stressors detrimentally affect work engagement, which in turn reduces service performance. Furthermore, job social support and employees’ social skills emerge as two key moderators, buffering both the direct impact of customer-related social stressors on work engagement and the indirect effect on service performance via work engagement. These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the interactions among customer-related social stressors, work engagement, and service performance, offering significant implications for both theory and practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Gai P.J.

Title: How AI amplifies, mitigates, and creates social biases: A tripartite framework
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in social life, shaping how individuals perceive themselves and others and influencing social dynamics that bear directly on equality and collective welfare. Yet its relationship to social bias is paradoxical: the very systems that can entrench and amplify long-standing prejudices may also be leveraged to challenge them, and may simultaneously generate entirely novel forms of bias. This review synthesizes recent empirical literature within a tripartite framework organized around the core pathways along which AI shapes social biases: AI design, lay beliefs about how AI operates, and processes of social evaluation and attribution. Drawing on these pathways, I outline three corresponding avenues for intervention: more equitable AI design, targeted adjustment of lay beliefs about AI capabilities, and redesign of social evaluation processes to account for the attribution biases that AI introduces. Together, these findings underscore the urgency of a socially informed approach to AI development and governance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Spectral clustering based on neighborhood relationships and the number of nearest neighbors k
Abstract: Spectral clustering has become a mainstream method for clustering complex data due to its strong adaptability to non-convex distributions, high-dimensional data, and manifold structures. The performance of spectral clustering is directly determined by the quality of the similarity matrix, yet conventional methods often rely on globally fixed parameters, making it difficult to accommodate local structural variations in the data, which can easily lead to degraded clustering results. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel spectral clustering algorithm based on neighborhood relationships and the number of nearest neighbors k(SC-k). The algorithm constructs an ε-neighborhood graph that integrates mean and variance, uses the average distance between a sample and its k nearest neighbors as a local scaling parameter, and designs a new Gaussian kernel similarity measure. This ensures both sparsity and reasonableness of the similarity matrix while reducing sensitivity to the parameter k. Finally, extensive numerical experiments are conducted to compare the proposed algorithm with existing advanced methods, demonstrating that our approach achieves more efficient clustering performance. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática Aplicada e Computacional 2026.

Title: Too many humilities: Construct proliferation and the measurement of a consequential trait
Abstract: Humility is among the most morally and socially consequential traits in individual-differences research, yet it is measured by more than 20 instruments spread across four traditions that differ in theoretical level and have developed largely on separate tracks: intellectual, relational, and cultural humility, and the Honesty-Humility factor of HEXACO. Two recent papers bring the costs of this fragmentation into focus. Costello et al. (2023) report that widely used intellectual humility self-reports track confidence more than error recognition, a failure of criterion-related validity against metacognitive calibration and error recognition. Pärnamets et al. (2026) show that consolidating measures within a tradition is feasible and clarifying. We argue that cross-tradition integration should become a priority for individual-differences science, and we outline what it requires: multitrait-multimethod designs; comparison of correlated-factor, higher-order, and bifactor models; attention to discriminant and incremental validity, and to measurement invariance; and validation against distinct classes of external criteria that have psychometric support of their own. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Sym-SKAN: Symbolic spiking Kolmogorov–Arnold learning for interpretable hyperspectral land-cover classification
Abstract: Accurate hyperspectral land-cover classification is increasingly needed in precision agriculture, urban mapping, wetland monitoring, disaster assessment, and satellite/UAV-based Earth observation. However, many recent deep hyperspectral classifiers improve accuracy by relying on dense spectral–spatial representations whose decision mechanisms are difficult to interpret and whose computational cost limits deployment on resource-constrained remote-sensing platforms. This study proposes Sym-SKAN, a Symbolic Spiking Kolmogorov–Arnold Network for interpretable and energy-aware per-pixel hyperspectral classification. The framework first maps each normalized hyperspectral pixel to a compact scalar representation using a narrow Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) spectral encoder with learnable spline functions. The encoder is explicitly regularized for symbolic distillation, allowing its learned spectral response to be converted after training into closed-form analytic spectral-index expressions that can be inspected by remote-sensing practitioners and evaluated in conventional GIS or band-math workflows. The learned representation is then processed by a Leaky Integrate-and-Fire spiking classifier, providing a sparse inference path suitable for low-power edge, UAV, and on-orbit hardware. Sym-SKAN therefore supports two complementary deployment modes: a full spiking mode for energy-aware classification and a symbolic-only mode that evaluates the discovered analytic index without specialized neural hardware. Experiments on six public hyperspectral benchmarks, Indian Pines, Salinas, Pavia University, Pavia Center, Kennedy Space Center, and Botswana, show consistent performance across vegetation, urban, and wetland scenes, with Mode A overall accuracies of 87.1%, 95.7%, 88.8%, 98.1%, 91.7%, and 92.9%, respectively. The study further reports the discovered symbolic indices, symbolic residuals, decision-threshold ranges, ablation results, and energy estimates. The results indicate that Sym-SKAN provides a practical trade-off between classification accuracy, analytic interpretability, and deployment efficiency, offering a remote-sensing-oriented route toward auditable and hardware-aware hyperspectral inference. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Visualizing multiphase flow and vapor dynamics during microwave reheating of food
Abstract: Microwave reheating of water-rich, deformable porous media, such as cooked meat, can produce abrupt vapor-release and sample-deformation events; however, the coupled thermal, transport, and mechanical processes underlying these events remain difficult to access experimentally. Here, cooked chicken was treated as a water- and lipid-containing deformable porous medium, and kitchen-scale experiments were combined with high-speed imaging, fluorescent fiber-optic temperature measurements, photogrammetric reconstruction, and coupled electromagnetic–thermal–granular–poroelastic simulations. Non-metallic fiber-optic probes recorded an above-surface temperature near 372–373 K during sustained vapor release and a distinct subsurface thermal transition near 20 s, from approximately 360–374 K to 348–365 K. The simulations identify contrasting dispersed-lipid and lipid-clustered regimes: open pathways support vapor percolation, whereas local hydraulic choking promotes pressure buildup and stress localization. Authors: Liang J.; Wang X.; Du F.; Zhang H.; Wang Y.; Rong Y.; Lin K.; Xia D.; Tao B.; Zhang J.; Yang Y.
Title: Breaking the performance trade-offs of nano-metal fuels: ammonium perchlorate-mediated high-performance energetic microspheres
Abstract: Simultaneously achieving high energy density, rapid reaction kinetics, and practical processability remains a fundamental challenge for metal fuels in next-generation solid propellants. Here, high-performance energetic microspheres (HPEMs) are established as a particle-level energetic composite by integrating nano-aluminum, nano-boron, and ammonium perchlorate into individual energetic microspheres, enabling intrinsic property complementarity to evolve into combustion synergy. The optimized HPEMs (Al:B = 7:3) simultaneously achieve high energy density, rapid reaction kinetics, and excellent processability. Specifically, the optimized HPEMs deliver a combustion heat of 24.0 kJ g−1, 1.86 and 1.48 times higher than those of the Al@AP and B@AP counterparts, respectively. They exhibit the shortest ignition delay (577.2 ± 31.6 ms), accelerated flame propagation, and a balanced combustion duration (88.3 ± 5.0 ms), demonstrating efficient kinetic coupling between rapid Al oxidation and sustained boron combustion. The particle-level architecture suppresses nanoparticle aggregation, reducing slurry viscosity of propellant from 138.380 to 61.596 Pa·s while maintaining superior combustion performance in propellant formulations. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that rapid Al/AP combustion establishes a self-sustained high-temperature oxidizing environment, which promotes the dynamic evolution of the molten B2O3 layer, facilitates oxygen transport to the boron core, and continuously activates boron oxidation. Consequently, the rapid reaction kinetics of nano-aluminum are effectively transferred into sustained boron oxidation, establishing a synergistic combustion pathway that combines rapid reaction kinetics with continuous high-energy release. More importantly, this work establishes the coordinated integration of complementary energetic constituents as a general design strategy that shifts material optimization from overcoming the limitations of individual components toward synergistic optimization of multicomponent performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Negotiating the contested: A framework for studying social issue negotiations
Abstract: Negotiation research has yielded useful insights on how to manage economic and business interactions by highlighting the importance of information sharing, trade-offs, and integrative solutions in achieving mutually beneficial outcomes. However, these approaches inadequately explain why negotiations over social issues such as immigration reform and climate change can remain deadlocked despite sustained efforts to reach agreement. Drawing upon recent research, we introduce an organizing framework that identifies three common features of such negotiations: moralization, identity threat, and public contestation. Moralization frames issues as matters of right and wrong, reducing willingness to compromise; identity concerns transform policy disagreements into threats to group membership and self-concept; and public scrutiny increases reputational risks and constrains flexibility. Together, these dynamics hinder engagement, value creation, and the quality of agreements. We review emerging interventions—including moral reframing, perspective sharing, high-quality listening, informal dialogue, and third-party mediation—that may mitigate these barriers. We conclude by highlighting the need for research examining how moral, identity, and public pressures interact across levels of analysis to shape social issue negotiation processes and outcomes. © 2026 The Author(s)

Author full names: Cofsky, Nicole I. (59717626900); Binder, Matthew S. (57196064288)
Title: Atypical early-life ultrasonic vocalizations disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad in the BTBR model of autism spectrum disorder
Abstract: Alterations in early-life communication are a defining feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). While these deficits are well conserved in mouse models, few studies have assessed how aberrations in neonatal vocalizations affect maternal behaviors and disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad. To better elucidate the consequences of altered communication in ASD models, we assessed ultrasonic vocalization (USV) production in pups and the corresponding retrieval behaviors in dams using C57 and BTBR (autistic-like) mice. We first used the pup's dam as the retriever and found that BTBR dams retrieved significantly fewer pups than C57 dams. We then used a novel C57 dam as the retriever and found that BTBR pups were retrieved significantly slower than C57 pups. Follow-up analyses detected positive correlations between call duration and retrieval time and amplitude and retrieval time in BTBR pups. Similarly, we found that C57 mice that were retrieved the fastest had calls of a lower amplitude than slowly retrieved mice. In the BTBR model, we found that faster retrieved mice produced shorter calls with a higher pitch than slowly retrieved mice, displaying call characteristics more similar to C57 pups. Lastly, we found that a more diverse call type repertoire was associated with a faster retrieval time. Overall, our study demonstrates that altered USV production significantly affects the pup-dam communication dyad. Furthermore, we identified the USV duration, amplitude, and a more diverse call type repertoire as being critical factors underlying maternal retrieval. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yin C.-C.; Do K.-M.; Liu Y.-L.
Title: From image to action: How social proof turns brand image into repurchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how social proof shapes the relationship between brand image and repurchase intention in an emerging digital marketplace, distinguishing three forms that operate through different mechanisms: user-generated content, brand ambassadors, and testimonials. Because online markets involve considerable information overload, consumers rely heavily on others' evaluations to reduce decision risk; however, forms of social proof vary in authenticity and persuasive effectiveness, and prior research has largely treated them as a single, uniformly positive construct. A two-study, mixed-methods design set in Vietnam addresses this gap. Study 1 applies a Vietnamese-optimized RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach) model to social media comments to surface authentic consumer sentiment, providing exploratory, triangulating context without constituting a direct hypothesis test. Study 2 tests the proposed relationships using moderated regression on survey responses from 394 active Vietnamese online shoppers. Results show that brand image exerts a strong positive direct effect on repurchase intention. User-generated content significantly strengthens this relationship, with the largest effect among consumers holding moderate brand-image perceptions. Brand ambassadors moderate the relationship but show a bounded pattern, with diminishing influence once brand image is already strong. Testimonials exert a dual effect: they amplify the brand image-repurchase link when perceived as credible, but, when seen as commercially motivated, they independently trigger skepticism and weaken repurchase intention. By conceptually and empirically distinguishing ambassadors from testimonials, this study shows that social proof is not a uniformly positive force but a context-dependent mechanism conditioned by authenticity, with implications for transparency-oriented digital marketing strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhao H.; Ye J.; Lv S.; Xu W.
Title: Robust subband adaptive filters: A review
Abstract: Due to its outstanding decorrelation ability, the normalized subband adaptive filter (NSAF) algorithm has been widely used in scenarios involving highly correlated input signals. Under Gaussian noise, the NSAF algorithm based on the mean square error (MSE) criterion has attracted extensive attention due to its low computational complexity and excellent performance for correlated signals. However, practical environments often contain impulsive noise instead of ideal Gaussian noise. Since the MSE criterion is sensitive to outliers, impulsive noise will seriously deteriorate the convergence and steady-state performance of the NSAF algorithm. To suppress impulsive interference, robust subband adaptive filter (RSAF) algorithms usually adopt nonlinear saturation-based loss functions (e.g., Lp-norm, Huber function, correntropy) to weaken the impact of outliers. Beyond this core anti-impulsive capability, techniques derived from the RSAF framework for fixed step-size implementation, sparse system identification, nonlinear tasks, censored regression (CR) models, errors-in-variables (EIV) models, and distributed network problems have also attracted considerable scholarly interest. Overall, despite the rapid development of RSAF algorithms in recent years, there remains a lack of comprehensive reviews that systematically summarize their design principles, performance characteristics, and application scopes. Addressing this research gap, this paper presents a systematic overview of RSAF algorithms and proposes several promising future research directions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Wang Y.; Chen Y.
Title: Logit-guided feature denoising distillation for model compression
Abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective strategy for compressing deep models by transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a lightweight student network, which is particularly valuable for reliable deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments. Traditional distillation methods usually align features as a whole, ignoring that they often contain background activations unrelated to the target as well as scattered noisy responses. To address this problem, Logit-Guided Feature Denoising (LGFD) distillation is proposed, which integrates the logit discriminative encoder (LDE) and the feature denoising mask (FDM) into a novel framework to guide the student toward acquiring the truly discriminative feature of the teacher. Specifically, the LDE encodes the teacher’s logit discriminability for feature denoising, thereby aligning features along semantic directions. Based on the LDE, the FDM highlights the attentive regions related to label class, which can help suppress redundant and noisy activations in the feature maps. Comprehensive experiments covering CIFAR-100, ImageNet, MS-COCO, and RTE confirm both the effectiveness and wide applicability of LGFD to classification, detection, and natural language inference. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Wen H.; Liu Y.; Luo Y.
Title: Symptom network structures of social media addiction and internet gaming addiction among school-aged youth: Undirected and Bayesian directed graph analyses
Abstract: Social media addiction (SMA) and internet gaming addiction (IGA) are increasingly recognized as important behavioral concerns among children and adolescents. However, little is known about whether their symptoms occupy similar structural positions across digital behavior contexts. This study compared the symptom structures of SMA and IGA among school-aged children and adolescents using network and Bayesian graph analyses. A school-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 11,638 students aged 10–18 years from six public schools in Chongqing, China. SMA was assessed using the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale, and IGA was measured using the Game Addiction Scale. Regularized partial correlation networks, Network Comparison Tests, and Bayesian Directed Acyclic Graphs were estimated to examine symptom associations, gender differences, and probable directional pathways. Both networks were densely connected but organized around different hubs. Tolerance emerged as the most central symptom in SMA, whereas Withdrawal occupied the central position in IGA. No significant gender differences were observed in the SMA network. In contrast, the IGA network showed significantly greater global strength among females, although no individual edge difference survived correction for multiple comparisons. Bayesian analyses yielded no directionally interpretable pathways for SMA, whereas the IGA network showed a small number of interpretable pathways, with Tolerance and Withdrawal both pointing toward Mood Modification. These findings revealed the different symptom structures of SMA and IGA, with implications for more targeted school-based assessment and intervention. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhancing computational thinking through unplugged activities in elementary education: A systematic literature review
Abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of unplugged activities in enhancing computational thinking (CT) skills among elementary school students through a systematic literature review. Using the systematic literature review design guided by the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework, the study examines 34 relevant empirical studies. Data collection involved literature searches in multiple electronic databases using keywords related to unplugged activities and CT concepts. The data were analyzed using a coding scheme covering methodological characteristics, subject area, types of unplugged activities and tools, contextual factors, challenges and suitability. The findings indicate that unplugged activities can support the development of computational thinking skills, particularly in resource-limited environments. Reported contextual factors associated with variation in outcomes include learner age, year level, curriculum and school support. However, challenges such as inadequate teacher training, difficulties in curriculum integration, and the lack of standardized assessment tools persist. The implications of this study suggest that unplugged activities can serve as an inclusive and cost-effective pedagogical tool for teaching CT skills in elementary education. © 2026 The Authors.
