Title: Spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network for traffic flow prediction
Abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a critical task in intelligent transportation systems. The main challenge lies in the existence of complex, intertwined and dynamically evolving spatio-temporal dependencies in real-world traffic networks. Existing methods often rely on inherent static road network graph structures, lacking focus on the key time nodes and effective interaction mechanisms of spatio-temporal dimension information. To address this limitation, we propose a traffic flow prediction model named spatio-temporal cross attention involved dual graph convolution network. Our method adopts a parallel framework to synchronously extract features from both spatial and temporal dimensions. It spatially achieves enhanced learning of global and local dynamic dependencies through a dual graph convolution module, and temporally, it combines a long short-term memory network with a temporal attention module to capture continuous temporal correlations. Then through a cross attention fusion module, it dynamically integrates spatio-temporal information and establishes an interaction mechanism between them. Extensive experiments on four real-world traffic datasets from the Caltrans performance measurement system (PeMS03, PeMS04, PeMS07 and PeMS08) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average performance improvement of 2% to 15% compared with existing baseline models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Preschoolers use exploratory approaches to selective social learning
Abstract: Preschoolers evaluate many cues when making inferences about others (Harris et al., 2018). It is unclear whether children’s understanding of inference-making is sophisticated enough that they also seek out the most relevant cues for making specific inferences. Here, we tasked 4- and 5-year-olds and adults with a modified epistemic trust paradigm in which they were told to select one of two informants to help them learn about novel objects. However, before doing so, participants were told that they could learn up to three pieces of information about the informants: what they know (epistemic cue), how they play with their friends (benevolence cue), or what they look like (appearance cue). Of particular interest was which cue participants prioritized (picked first) and what strategies they used for seeking information. In Study 1, adults prioritized learning epistemic information and tended to employ efficient information-seeking strategies (selecting the fewest cues possible to make their inferences). Children, on the other hand, chose each cue first at relatively equal rates and tended to employ exploratory strategies for information-seeking (sampling broadly from the available information). This was even the case in Study 2, in which the informativeness of the appearance and benevolence cues was reduced. These studies raise questions about the way in which children make inferences about others and point to a tendency for children to employ exploratory strategies for learning about others (Gopnik, 2020). © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Analysis of medical isotope yield based on 232Th(p, x)225Ac reaction
Abstract: Actinium-225 (225Ac) has emerged as a premier medical isotope for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), yet its large-scale production remains impeded by multiple technical challenges. Title: Piezoelectric sensor based on MWCNTs/SEBS stretchable composite electrode for human motion monitoring
Abstract: Wearable piezoelectric electronics promise self-powered sensing for health monitoring and human-machine interfaces, yet their practical deployment is hampered by a long-standing trade-off between stretchability and output performance. Here, we report a co-engineered strategy that simultaneously optimizes both electrodes and active layers. A MWCNTs/SEBS composite electrode forms a stiff, percolating network with metal-like conductivity, high tensile compliance, and hydrophobic stability, enabling robust charge transport under sweat and strain. Concurrently, BaTiO₃ nanoparticles induce a β-phase-rich P(VDF-TrFE) matrix, supplying a high density of switchable dipoles. The hybrid delivers open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current of ~20.1 V and ~4.33 μA, respectively. Demonstrated in a 4 × 4 sensor array, the system decodes joint motions and gait patterns in real time. This design offers a promising pathway toward soft-electrode-integrated, durable, and high-performance piezoelectric skins for next-generation wearable electronics. © 2026

Title: Motivation for cyberhate among Ukrainian youth
Abstract: While research on cyberhate has focused largely on prevalence and exposure, motivation underlying cyberhate perpetration remains under-researched. Guided by the general aggression model, social identity theory, and social cognitive theory, we explored the mediating roles of revenge and proactive motivation in the association between cyberbullying victimization and cyberhate perpetration. Title: Optimization of process variables for CO2/CH4 and CO2/N2 binary gas separation using dual-layer hollow fiber mixed-matrix membrane
Abstract: Membrane based carbon dioxide removal from methane, biogas, and process modified streams, such as flue gas recycling, oxy-fuel combustion with air ingress, and industrial exhausts remained a pivotal strategy to curb greenhouse gas emissions and support sustainable energy development. Dual-layer hollow fiber mixed-matrix membranes (DLHFMMMs) have recently garnered substantial attention for CO2 separation, however, optimization of separation variables for such process is still imperative. In this study, design of experiment framework was adopted to perform process optimization of binary gas separation involving CO2/CH4 and CO2/N2 via DLHFMMM. The influences of feed pressure (2–10 bar for CO2/CH4; 5–10 bar for CO2/N2), temperature (30–50 °C), and CO2 feed composition (30–70 vol.% for CO2/CH4; 10–50 vol.% for CO2/N2) on DLHFMMM performance were evaluated. A response surface methodology (RSM) coupled with central composite design (CCD) was utilized to develop predictive models correlating these variables with CO2, CH4 and N2 permeances, along with the corresponding CO2/CH4 and CO2/N2 separation factors. Title: Optimizing melt–stretch properties in yeast protein vegan mozzarella analogues through protein–starch interactions
Abstract: The role of yeast protein (YP) in structuring Mozzarella-type vegan cheese analogues was investigated through its interactions with tapioca starch in composite gel systems. YP exhibited a lower water-holding capacity and smaller particle size (measured in 1%, w/w protein dispersions) than conventional plant proteins, which significantly influenced subsequent gel formation and functionality. Cheese analogues were formulated at varying YP:starch ratios (9:12, 12:9, 15:6, and 18:3), and their physicochemical rheological, microstructural, and functional properties were systematically evaluated. The YP:starch ratio critically governed the network structure, water distribution, lipid organization, and phase stability. At low YP levels, a starch-dominated matrix containing a high proportion of loosely held water lacked a continuous protein network, resulting in limited meltability and stretchability. An intermediate YP:starch ratio (15:6) produced a homogeneous co-continuous protein–starch network with balanced water immobilization and controlled lipid distribution, resulting in the greatest meltability and stretchability. At the highest ratio (18:3), elevated intermolecular β-sheet content was associated with protein aggregation, structural heterogeneity, water over-immobilization, and enlarged lipid domains. These findings demonstrate that the thermo-mechanical functionality of vegan cheese analogues is governed primarily by the structural integration of protein, starch, water, and lipid phases, rather than by protein content alone, providing mechanistic insights for the rational design of high-protein vegan cheese analogues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: The social embeddedness of learning: Social network formation and academic achievement in an undergraduate student community
Abstract: Background: Students play an active role in developing their social learning environment and peer relationships. Meanwhile, their academic behaviors are likely to be affected by their integration and individual positions in social networks. Despite the clear importance of social aspects on learning, the mechanisms shaping students’ social networks and the impact of emerging social ties on students’ academic performance remain underexplored. Aims: We investigate (1) the development of undergraduate students’ friendship and co-learning relationships, and (2) the influence of social embeddedness on students’ academic achievement. Sample: The sample consists of first-year students from two large STEM cohorts at a Swiss university: NA=225, NB=625. Methods: With longitudinal network data, we applied stochastic actor-oriented models to simultaneously examine the (co-)evolution of friendship and co-learning networks for each cohort while controlling for other network mechanisms on relationship formation. Furthermore, we implemented network autocorrelation models to examine the influence of social embeddedness on students’ first-year qualification exam GPAs. Results: The results revealed a mutual sustainability of co-learning and friendship ties, which were initially bridged by more generic positive social interactions. Furthermore, we found a significant association between students’ first-year grades and the average grades of their co-learners. This grade interdependency may be a joint outcome of peer selection and peer influence processes. Conclusion: Our study contributes to a deeper understanding of the co-dynamic processes of undergraduate students’ co-learning and friendship networks and highlights the importance of social embeddedness in students’ academic performance. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Zhou Z.; Wu Y.; Fei Y.; Chu J.; Jiang S.; Xu W.; Zheng X.; Wang H.
Title: Hyperuricemia, circulating metabolites, and the risk of cardiometabolic multimorbidity
Abstract: Background The role of hyperuricemia in cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) needs to be further confirmed. We aimed to investigate the impact of hyperuricemia on cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and to explore the metabolic mechanisms. Methods We conducted a prospective cohort study using data from 422,058 participants in the UK Biobank. Cardiometabolic multimorbidity was defined as having two or more cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs) identified from linked primary care, hospital, and death registry records. Cox and multistate model was used to examine the role of hyperuricemia in the progression of CMM. Elastic net regression was employed to identify metabolites associated with hyperuricemia, and a weighted hyperuricemia metabolic score was calculated to assess its association with CMM. Results During a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 55,092 developed CMDs, 6484 progressed to CMM, and 2234 died with CMM. Compared with participants without hyperuricemia, those with hyperuricemia had increased risks of any CMDs (HR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.20–1.26, P < 0.001), and CMM (HR = 1.32, 95% CI: 1.23–1.42, P < 0.001). Mendelian randomization confirmed causal effects of hyperuricemia on CMDs and CMM. Furthermore, hyperuricemia metabolic score composed of 126 differential metabolites was significantly associated with CMDs (HR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.21–1.27) and CMM (HR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.28–1.44). In multi-state analyses, the metabolic score was associated with higher risks of transition from health to CMD (HR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.22–1.28) and from CMD to CMM (HR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.07–1.22). Conclusions In this large cohort study, hyperuricemia was both observationally and genetically associated with increased risk of cardiometabolic diseases and subsequent progression to cardiometabolic multimorbidity. Hyperuricemia-related metabolic signatures may provide additional insights into the biological processes underlying cardiometabolic disease progression. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: The regulatory roles of the medial septum and hippocampus in spatial memory impairment of PTSD mice
Abstract: This experiment was based on the establishment of an analogue of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in mice, aiming to explore the regulatory effects of the medial septum (MS) and the hippocampus (HIP) on spatial memory impairment in mice, and to establish a theoretical foundation for revealing the pathological basis of PTSD-related spatial memory impairment. The PTSD mouse model was prepared, behavioral testing, FluoroGold (FG) retrograde tracing technique, viral tracing technique, in vivo fiber photometry recording technique, chemogenetic technology and in vivo electrophysiological recording techniques were applied to observe and analyze the changes in spatial memory ability and the central regulatory mechanism. PTSD mice showed heightened anxiety, impaired spatial memory, suppressed Sch-CA1 long-term potentiation, and hyperactivity of MS-CA1 cholinergic neurons; chemogenetic inhibition of this pathway rescued both the behavioral and synaptic plasticity deficits. The regulation of spatial memory impairment in PTSD mice involves MS-resident cholinergic neurons. We found a cholinergic pathway connection between MS and CA1, and this pathway may regulate murine spatial cognition by influencing the synaptic plasticity of Sch-CA1. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Authentic or strategic ESG? Motive attribution, consumer–company identification and purchase intention in retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Against the backdrop of widespread greenwashing skepticism, consumers are increasingly scrutinizing corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) motives rather than simply accepting ESG disclosures at face value, creating a fundamental ethical dilemma in which ESG investment may fail to translate into market returns if corporate actions are attributed to strategic calculation rather than genuine values. Drawing on attribution theory and social identity theory, this study examines how Chinese retail consumers internalize ESG perceptions, through sincere versus strategic motive judgments, into consumer-company identification (CCI), and how this psychological process ultimately drives purchase intention, using a multi-study design in which Study 1 (N = 226) employed a cross-sectional survey of Chinese retail consumers to test the associative pathways and mediation effects among the key variables, while Study 2 (N = 156) employed a single-factor, two-level between-subjects experiment with structural equation modeling (SEM) and 5000-resample bootstrap estimation to examine the proposed direct and indirect effects. Three core findings emerge. First, corporate ESG performance exerts a robust positive effect on purchase intention even in skeptical environments. Second, CCI serves as the critical psychological bridge linking ESG performance to market response. Third, experimental causal evidence reveals that sincere motive attribution is the key trigger for activating CCI, with the indirect effect through identification accounting for 38.3% of the total effect, revealing a “dual-channel structure” in which a direct effect and an indirect, identification-mediated effect coexist. These findings offer actionable implications for ESG communication strategy in China's retail sector and provide a basis for future comparative research in other Asia-Pacific emerging markets. © 2026

Title: Faunal Evidence and the Duration of Occupation: A Statistical Approach to Neanderthal Archaeological Sites
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: The duration of Neanderthal occupations of caves and rock shelters is one of the most debated issues in prehistoric archaeology. Several disciplines, including lithic analysis, micromorphology, zooarchaeology, taphonomy, and spatial archaeology, have proposed criteria to estimate occupation length, but their reliability varies. This study focuses only on indicators derived from faunal assemblages and evaluates their effectiveness through statistical testing. Four features were analysed: number of taxa, hunting spectrum, anthropogenic modifications, and evidence of carnivore activity. These characteristics were applied to a dataset from Late Mousterian sites in Spain and south-eastern France (70–40 ka) that have previously been examined through multidisciplinary approaches. The results indicate that the four features do not provide equally robust signals. Anthropogenic modifications and the number of exploited taxa show the strongest correlation with occupation duration. In contrast, the number of taxa and carnivore activity, when considered alone, are less reliable indicators. Multivariate analyses reveal a clearer structuring of the faunal assemblages. Brief stopping places are consistently distinguished from longer occupations. However, long-term occupations and repeated short-term occupations tend to overlap, largely because of palimpsest effects. Overall, these findings demonstrate both the potential and the limits of faunal criteria. They highlight the need for integrated, high-resolution approaches to reconstruct the duration and intensity of Neanderthal occupations. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Cura: The case for institutionalizing health and well-being in the arts & culture sector
Abstract: A convergent body of evidence from clinical trials, epidemiological cohort studies, mechanistic science and emerging economic analysis demonstrates that arts and cultural engagement is a meaningful determinant of health. Yet the organisational infrastructure of arts and cultural institutions has not kept up with this science. Drawing on the historical example of how education became a permanent institutional vertical in arts and cultural organisations during the twentieth century, this paper argues that the evidence base for arts and health now meets a reasonable threshold for a parallel structural change: the creation within arts and cultural organisations of a permanent, staffed and resourced health and well-being vertical. The argument is normative in its institutional commitments, but deliberately pluralist in form. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Identifying and prioritizing key factors influencing electric vehicle fast-charging infrastructure planning in China: A Delphi study
Abstract: The rapid expansion of China's new energy vehicle market has intensified demand for a coordinated, equitable fast-charging infrastructure system. Despite substantial growth, regional disparities, technical incompatibilities, and fragmented governance arrangements continue to constrain the efficiency and long-term sustainability of network deployment. This study systematically identifies and prioritizes the key determinants shaping the planning of fast-charging infrastructure in China. A two-round Delphi process was conducted with 30 experts drawn from government, industry, and academia to establish consensus on critical influencing factors. Anchored in diffusion of innovation and institutional theory, the analysis integrates technological, economic, spatial, social, environmental, and governance dimensions into a coherent evaluative framework. Six principal factors emerged: governance and institutional coordination; economic and financial viability; technological integration and standardization; social equity and user-oriented considerations; spatial and urban planning; and environmental sustainability. Governance and institutional coordination ranked highest in importance, with strong consensus among participants (Kendall's W = 0.696, p < 0.001). The findings underscore the central role of policy coherence, sustainable financial models, and interoperability in accelerating the diffusion of infrastructure and reducing regional inequality. The study advances a theoretically informed prioritization framework to support strategic infrastructure planning in rapidly electrifying economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Feng J.; Li Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Payroll taxes, firm dynamism, and aggregate productivity
Abstract: This study examines the impact of payroll-tax enforcement on firm dynamism and its implications for aggregate productivity. We exploit China's Social Security Collection Agency Reform, which transferred responsibility for collecting social-insurance contributions from local social-insurance agencies to tax authorities, thereby strengthening enforcement. We show that the reform increased firms’ social-insurance contributions, shifted workers toward informal employment without reducing overall nonagricultural employment, and reduced new firm entry while weakening incumbent firms’ profitability and investment. Overall, the reform reduced measured aggregate productivity in China's registered, above-scale industrial sector by 3.3 percent, with entry into the above-scale industrial sector accounting for about 45 percent of the estimated decline. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Synergistic structure-microenvironment design of polyamide membranes for efficient extraction of lithium from brine
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Polyamide (PA) membrane has become a promising material for direct lithium extraction from salt lake brine, but it faces the trade-off between permeability and Li+/Mg2+ selectivity. Here, we propose a strategy to resolve this limitation by synergistic regulation of the crosslinked structure of the PA layer and the internal hydrogen-bonding environment. The pre-crosslinking of tannic acid (TA)-modified montmorillonite nanosheets (MMTNS) and polyethyleneimine (PEI) promoted the formation of a PA composite layer with narrow pore size, thereby enhancing Mg2+ rejection. Their synergistic effect also achieves precise regulation of PEI: MMTNS inhibits PEI diffusion in the bulk phase, while TA facilitates its interfacial diffusion. The resulting heterogeneous polymerization dynamics forms a thin and dense PA layer, which enables high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity and ultrafast water transport. In addition, MMTNS and TA construct a rich hydrogen-bonding network that improves the water transport environment and further enhances transport efficiency. The optimized membrane achieves a permeance of 10.08 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 and a Li+/Mg2+ separation selectivity of 49.5, exceeding most currently reported selective Li+ extraction membranes. This work provides insights into the control of the PA layer structure and mass transfer environment, facilitating the design of next-generation selective ion separation membranes. © 2026

Title: Approximate minimization of interpretations in fuzzy description logics under the Gödel semantics
Abstract: The problem of minimizing fuzzy interpretations in fuzzy description logics (FDLs) is important both theoretically and practically. For instance, fuzzy or weighted social networks can be modeled as fuzzy interpretations, where individuals represent actors and roles capture interactions. Minimizing such interpretations yields more compact representations, which can significantly improve the efficiency of reasoning and analysis tasks in knowledge-based systems. We present the first algorithm that minimizes a finite fuzzy interpretation while preserving fuzzy concept assertions in FDLs without the Baaz projection operator and the universal role, under the Gödel semantics. The considered class of FDLs ranges from the sublogic of fALC without the union operator and the universal restriction to the FDL that extends fALCreg with inverse roles and nominals. Our algorithm is given in an extended form that supports approximate preservation: it minimizes a finite fuzzy interpretation I while preserving fuzzy concept assertions up to a degree γ∈(0,1]. Its time complexity is O((mlogl+n)logn), where n is the size of the domain of I, m is the number of nonzero instances of atomic roles in I, and l is the number of distinct fuzzy values used in such instances plus 2. Methodologically, our approach fundamentally differs from existing ones, as it avoids quotient constructions traditionally employed for minimizing fuzzy interpretations and fuzzy automata. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: PG-DCA: prototype-guided knowledge transfer for imbalanced and heterogeneous data collaboration
Abstract: Collaborative analysis of distributed data requires fusing information from multiple sources whose raw data cannot be centralized, whose label distributions may be highly skewed, and whose local feature mappings may be incompatible. Data Collaboration Analysis (DCA) can align heterogeneous client representations after local dimensionality reduction, but traditional DCA relies on anchors that often lack task-specific semantic structure and are used only after biased local mappings have already discarded important discriminative components. This paper formulates this limitation as Non-IID component loss and proposes Prototype-Guided Data Collaboration Analysis (PG-DCA), a heterogeneity-robust framework based on prototype-guided knowledge transfer. PG-DCA constructs a task-relevant reference by extracting class-level knowledge from client-side statistics, translating it into the observation space, and rebalancing it without moving raw client data. Crucially, this reference is used as a knowledge carrier to guide local mapping before DCA alignment begins. A local-first guidance interface incorporates prototype knowledge into each client’s mapping while retaining the native objective of its chosen structured linear algorithm. The guided representations are then aligned in a common collaborative space to support server-side model training. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 under severe statistical and algorithmic heterogeneity show that PG-DCA reduces component loss and improves collaborative utility, with gains driven by prototype-mediated reference quality and guidance of local mapping. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Hidden dissatisfaction after agreement: Post-negotiation perceptual alignment
Abstract: Negotiations continue to have consequences after an agreement or impasse. When parties reach a deal, value is often created only later, as they implement commitments, adapt to uncertainty, or decide whether to negotiate again. This review introduces post-negotiation perceptual alignment, how accurately a negotiator understands the counterpart's post-negotiation experience. Integrating research on subjective value, interpersonal perception, and post-agreement outcomes, I distinguish four states: recognized satisfaction, recognized dissatisfaction, overestimated dissatisfaction, and hidden dissatisfaction. Hidden dissatisfaction is consequential because it creates a false sense of success where one party treats agreement as evidence that the negotiation went well while the counterpart carries forward negative appraisals that remain unrecognized and unaddressed. Recent research suggests tactics that appear successful at agreement can impose unrecognized social and relational costs. I review why misalignment arises, emphasizing how negotiators’ imperfect inferences about counterparts’ experiences can combine with social pressures that discourage dissatisfied parties from speaking up. I conclude by outlining directions for measuring alignment and testing how negotiators can recognize and respond to dissatisfaction after negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Precision forensic toxicology: Leveraging Toxicogenomics, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence for next-generation poisoning investigations
Abstract: For much of its history, forensic toxicology was built on a core analytical question: what poison or drug is present, and at what concentration? That question still matters, but modern casework increasingly shows that it is no longer sufficient on its own. The field grew from the nineteenth-century chemical toxicology of Mathieu Orfila and the arsenic-detecting Marsh test into a discipline central to medicolegal death investigation, overdose certification, and exposure reconstruction. Yet contemporary practice must now contend with novel psychoactive substances, highly potent synthetic opioids, complex polysubstance deaths, delayed reporting, postmortem redistribution, matrix degradation, and incomplete toxicological context. These pressures are pushing forensic toxicology beyond simple compound detection toward mechanism-aware, data-rich interpretation. This review develops the idea of precision forensic toxicology as a proposed, forward-looking conceptual framework for that transition rather than a description of established or routinely implemented forensic practice. In this model, classical analytical chemistry remains essential, but it is connected to toxicogenomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, proteomics, metabolomics, exposomics, microbiomics, and spatial multi-omics, then integrated through systems toxicology and artificial intelligence. Recent literature shows that toxicogenomics can reveal early molecular perturbations before overt phenotype, that postmortem metabolomics can assist cause-of-death screening, that RNA- and miRNA-based markers may improve postmortem interval estimation, and that machine learning can strengthen high-resolution mass-spectrometry workflows and multi-omics interpretation. At the same time, routine implementation remains constrained by standardization, validation, explainability, privacy governance, and regulatory uncertainty. None of these components is yet part of routine forensic casework; each remains at a research or early-validation stage, and their translation into daily practice will require dedicated feasibility, validation, and regulatory work, which this review discusses explicitly. Taken together, the evidence suggests that the future of poisoning investigation will depend less on any single assay and more on interoperable workflows that connect toxicant detection with biological response, individual susceptibility, and transparent decision support, and that these workflows are intended to complement, not replace, classical toxicological and medicolegal interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: HAPO: Hierarchical affinity aware propagation for unsupervised graph anomaly detection
Abstract: Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify nodes that deviate from normal structural or semantic patterns and is critical in security-sensitive applications. Existing unsupervised anomaly detection methods based on anomaly scoring are largely grounded in the local homophily assumption and are limited by feature smoothing to aggregating one-hop neighborhoods. Consequently, they lack a global perspective for detecting globally anomalous nodes and tend to misclassify structurally peripheral yet normal nodes as anomalies. Moreover, most existing approaches are not readily applicable to multi-view settings, limiting their effectiveness in graphs with heterogeneous relational semantics. To address these challenges, we propose Hierarchical Affinity-Aware Propagation (HAPO), a unified framework for single-view and multi-view GAD. HAPO combines multi-hop affinity-aware propagation with affinity-guided residual connections to enlarge the receptive field while mitigating over-smoothing, and a multi-classifier hierarchical affinity module to construct robust global affinity representations. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. In particular, HAPO outperforms state-of-the-art methods by more than 10.11% on the single-view Amazon dataset and 9.69% on the multi-view IMDB dataset in terms of AUPRC. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Informal urban regeneration through social capital: The Anousheh Street experience in a developing city
Abstract: While underprivileged neighborhoods are often seen as obstacles to urban development, their regeneration is essential for achieving sustainable urban development. Understanding the factors that influence successful regeneration experiences can guide action in similar neighborhoods. This study examines how the local community drove the informal regeneration of Anousheh Street in Ahvaz, Iran, transforming an underprivileged neighborhood into a vibrant street food hub. This study employed a Straussian Grounded Theory approach based on 24 in-depth interviews, triangulated with secondary socioeconomic data, to explain how the regeneration of Anousheh Street emerged. The findings show that vendor solidarity, rooted in social capital, acts as the central driving mechanism. This solidarity enabled informal creativity in attracting customers, supported by gradual institutional involvement from local authorities. This sequential process drives social, economic, and physical regeneration, evidenced by a 31-fold increase in commercial units and a halving of the local unemployment rate (from 35.27% to 16.81%) between 2011 and 2016. Unlike top-down models, this informal approach preserves cultural authenticity, fostering local identity and economic opportunities. This study develops a novel empirical model demonstrating how urban regeneration in developing cities can be achieved without reliance on large-scale physical investment, instead leveraging social capital and street food-based economies. The model contributes to theory by addressing a key gap in Middle Eastern urban studies and extends the application of Grounded Theory within urban regeneration research. From a practical perspective, this study proposes a context-sensitive yet scalable and transferable model based on three key conditions: vendor solidarity, vendor informal creative practices, and gradual institutional support. While the model demonstrates potential for application in other developing cities, its success depends on local socio-cultural and institutional contexts. These findings provide new policy-relevant insights for advancing inclusive and low-cost urban regeneration in the Global South. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Interface-engineered titanium matrix composites with silicon-segregated boundaries for high-temperature strength-ductility synergy
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: High-temperature titanium alloys are approaching intrinsic performance limits, while discontinuous TiB whisker-reinforced composites provide a possible route to higher service temperatures. The central challenge is to improve strength without sacrificing ductility, especially because deformation and fracture are strongly governed by reinforcement interfaces. Here, a hot-extruded TiB/Ti65 composite is developed with ultimate tensile strengths of 1342 MPa at room temperature and 570 MPa at 800 °C. The composite also retains 21.5% ductility at 800 °C, showing a superior strength and ductility combination compared with most reported high-temperature titanium materials. By combining three-dimensional tomography, atomic-resolution microscope, in-situ micromechanical testing, and first-principles calculations, we reveal a Si-segregated TiB/α-Ti interface with enhanced adhesion work. This interface strengthens load transfer to aligned TiB whiskers and promotes pyramidal 〈c+a〉 slip in adjacent α-Ti, thereby improving local deformation compatibility. As a result, interfacial decohesion is suppressed, and ductile fracture is maintained at elevated temperature. These results demonstrate that atomic-scale chemical tailoring of reinforcement interfaces is an effective strategy for overcoming the strength and ductility trade-off in titanium matrix composites designed for extreme environments. © 2026

Title: Corporate social responsibility and socio-economic impacts in the mining sector: A bibliometric review of local community empowerment and sustainable development
Abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the scholarly literature on corporate social responsibility (CSR) and its socio-economic implications in the mining sector, with a focus on local community empowerment and sustainable development outcomes. Using the Scopus database, a systematic search yielded 217 documents published between 2015 and 2025, which were then refined into 182 articles and reviews through structured inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study covers three main dimensions: (1) the evolution of mining-related CSR publication trends over the period 2015–2025; (2) the identification of dominant countries, institutions, and authors along with evolving collaboration patterns; and (3) thematic clusters that shape the intellectual architecture of the field, specifically how these clusters reflect the tension between corporate interests and stakeholder rights as theorized by Stakeholder Theory. The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer and the Bibliometrix package in R to map publication trends, author productivity, international collaboration networks, and thematic keyword clusters. The findings show a progressive growth in publications, reaching a peak of 37 documents in 2023, reflecting increasing academic and regulatory attention to corporate accountability in the extractive industries. Five thematic clusters were identified: CSR and indigenous peoples, economic sustainability and the resource curse, artisanal mining and local livelihoods, coal mining and occupational health, and a methodological cluster related to data mining in computer science. The United States and Australia lead in publication volume, while Ghana records the highest citation-per-document ratio. Indonesia, while present in the corpus, exhibits limited citation visibility, indicating significant room for increased global research engagement. The study identified critical gaps, including a dearth of longitudinal CSR assessments, limited multinational accountability research, and underrepresentation of Southeast Asian perspectives as urgent research priorities for advancing equitable mining governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Electrochemical sensing of promethazine: A critical review of detection strategies, sensor architectures, and analytical challenges
Abstract: Promethazine (PMZ) is a widely used phenothiazine drug whose accurate determination is important in pharmaceutical quality control, clinical monitoring, forensic toxicology, food analysis, and environmental surveillance. Although chromatographic and spectrometric methods remain valuable for confirmatory analysis, their dependence on sophisticated instrumentation and extensive sample preparation has encouraged the development of faster electrochemical alternatives. This review critically evaluates PMZ electrochemical detection studies published from 2010 to 2026, covering voltammetric methods, direct electrocatalytic detection, molecularly imprinted and DNA-mediated recognition, adsorptive stripping, and extraction-integrated electroanalysis. Particular attention is given to the effects of nanostructured materials, conductive composites, porous interfaces, and recognition layers on analytical performance. Comparative analysis indicates that nanostructured electrodes generally enhance sensitivity and electron transfer, whereas molecularly imprinted and DNA-modified interfaces offer greater potential for selective recognition. However, important trade-offs remain because high-surface-area and adsorption-based platforms are susceptible to fouling, affinity-based sensors often require complex fabrication and regeneration, and ultra-low detection limits frequently depend on prolonged preconcentration or sample pretreatment. Major research gaps include inadequate discrimination from structurally related phenothiazines, limited validation in authentic complex samples, poor inter-electrode and batch-to-batch reproducibility, and insufficient assessment of robustness, operational stability, total assay time, and cost. Future research should prioritize matrix- and fouling-resistant interfaces, simplified scalable fabrication, rigorous validation, and integrated sample handling. Combining reproducible disposable electrodes with microfluidics, portable potentiostats, and connected readout systems may facilitate reliable field-deployable and point-of-care PMZ analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The dynamics of climate change skepticism sharing on social media: Social identity, partisanship, and the impact of negative public opinion cues
Abstract: Social media has facilitated the rapid spread of incorrect information, including climate change skepticism. Drawing on Social Identity Theory, we investigated why individuals adopt skeptical views and disseminate them on social media. Study 1 (N = 316) revealed that Republicans were more likely to endorse climate change skepticism and that those with strong partisan attachments were particularly likely to share these views actively as a manifestation of their social identity. Furthermore, Study 2 (N = 120) designed through the lens of the Spiral of Silence theory revealed that explicit social media cues signaling opposition to climate skepticism (e.g., high number of “dislikes” on posts about climate change skepticism) effectively discouraged climate change skeptics from sharing their skepticism. The findings of the two studies highlight the psychological drivers of climate change skepticism dissemination on social media and demonstrate that explicit cues (e.g., number of “dislikes”) can reduce the spread of climate change skepticism in digital spaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Naseem M.T.; Zaman W.
Author full names: Naseem, Muhammad Tahir (57733123500); Zaman, Wajid (57193825110)
Title: From curated datasets to social-media reality: In-the-wild, multimodal, and generalizable deepfake detection
Abstract: Deepfake detection has advanced rapidly alongside progress in generative adversarial networks, diffusion models, neural rendering, and multimodal synthesis. However, strong performance on curated benchmark datasets does not necessarily translate into reliable performance in real-world environments, where manipulated media are affected by platform compression, reposting, post-processing, multimodal inconsistency, temporal drift, and evolving generation pipelines. This review examines deepfake detection from the perspective of in-the-wild robustness, multimodal reasoning, and cross-domain generalization. It first clarifies the conceptual foundations of in-the-wild and generalizable deepfake detection, then reviews the data ecosystem, including benchmark datasets, real-world media conditions, multimodal data gaps, annotation quality, and benchmark aging. The review further analyzes the major causes of detector failure under realistic deployment conditions, including generator shift, platform-induced degradation, modality mismatch, language and speaker variation, and broader contextual diversity. It then compares major methodological families, including artifact-based methods, deep representation-based approaches, transfer-based learning, domain adaptation, domain generalization, and multimodal detection strategies, with emphasis on their relevance to real-world robustness. Finally, the review discusses evaluation practices, external validation, realistic benchmarking, and future directions such as continually updated benchmarks, missing-modality-robust systems, uncertainty-aware detection, provenance integration, and foundation-model-based approaches. Overall, the review argues that reliable deepfake detection requires a shift from benchmark-centered optimization toward robust, multimodal, and deployment-oriented evaluation and design. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Generative AI as a social partner for young adults: Dual pathways to resilience and AI dependence
Abstract: This study examines LLM-based AI chatbots as social interaction partners. It identifies young adults’ support-seeking motivations and models their associations with two interaction processes (Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity) and two psychological outcomes (Resilience and AI Dependence). In Study 1, we developed the Motivation Scale for Generative AI (MS-GAI) through theory-driven item generation and interviews and validated it with a survey of Korean young adults (N = 300). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported an eight-factor, 40-item structure grounded in four social-support domains and supplemented by context-specific motivations. In Study 2, structural equation modeling showed that Emotional Support and Self-Enhancement were positively associated with both Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity. Objective Advice Seeking was positively associated with Perceived Authenticity, whereas Learning Assistance, Daily Problem-Solving, and Entertainment/Mood Diversion were positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Perceived Authenticity was also positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Both interaction processes were positively related to self-reported Resilience and AI Dependence, with Interaction Intensity showing the stronger association with AI Dependence. These findings identify distinct but overlapping interaction pathways through which support-seeking motivations are associated with adaptive and maladaptive outcomes. The study extends understanding of social support in human–AI interaction by providing a validated motivation measure and showing how shared interaction processes relate to both short-term perceived recovery and dependence. The findings are consistent with the Paradoxes of Technology perspective and highlight the need for emotionally supportive yet balanced design and policy safeguards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From hostile feedback to withdrawal: Emotional exhaustion as a barrier to social media misinformation correction
Abstract: User-driven misinformation correction is essential for sustaining the integrity of democratic discourse on social media, yet the emotional costs that discourage engagement remain understudied. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how the emotional tone of other users' feedback affects correctors' emotional exhaustion and subsequent willingness to engage in future corrections in a social media environment. In a cross-national experiment (N = 2001) across Austria, Bulgaria, Denmark, and Poland, utilizing a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design, participants corrected misinformation and received feedback varying in valence and arousal. Results show that angry, high-arousal feedback uniquely depletes emotional resources, producing higher exhaustion than civil disapproval or positive feedback. This indicates that critical feedback does not inherently exhaust correctors, but it is the hostile tone, not the negativity itself, that drives depletion. Emotional exhaustion, in turn, predicts avoidance of future corrective engagement. This exhaustion-driven withdrawal is amplified rather than buffered by correction confidence, suggesting that individual motivation alone is insufficient in hostile environments. These findings highlight emotional exhaustion as a key psychological constraint on citizen-led fact-checking and suggest that platform-level moderation targeting hostile comments is critical to protect the emotional resources required for a resilient democratic debate in digital environments. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Hydrogen production from municipal solid waste via oxygen–steam gasification for a Riyadh application: process simulation, sensitivity analysis, and techno-economic screening
Abstract: This study develops an Aspen Plus thermodynamic screening framework for hydrogen production from municipal solid waste (MSW) in a Riyadh application through oxygen–steam gasification, staged water–gas shift (WGS), surrogate contaminant removal, and surrogate pressure swing adsorption (PSA). MSW was represented on an as-received basis using literature-derived proximate and ultimate analyses. Gasification was modeled using an equilibrium reactor coupled adiabatically to decomposition, with the industrial-purity oxidant flow solved for the target temperature. The 100 kg h−1 reference case produced 6.775 kg h−1 of product hydrogen (67.75 kg H2 per metric ton of as-received MSW). Hydrogen production decreased across the 10–60 kg h−1 steam sweep at 900 °C. Response-surface analysis of 15 distinct simulations ranked 25 kg h−1 steam, an 800 °C gasifier temperature, and a 180 °C low-temperature WGS temperature highest within the studied domain; two cases excluded from regression showed interpolation errors below 0.074 %. A comparison case at 27 kg h−1 steam, 800 °C and 180 °C (Case A) produced 7.083 kg h−1 hydrogen, with specific compressor work of 5.911 kWh kg-H2−1 and an oxidant demand of 36.841 kg h−1. A 1200 °C refuse-derived fuel benchmark with reconstructed steam input reproduced four major wet-gas fractions within 0.76 percentage points. Two fluidized-bed comparisons at 850 °C showed substantial departures in gas ratios, and hydrogen yields at 800–900 °C remain unvalidated. Under three capital scenarios, the preliminary minimum hydrogen selling price for Case A was US$4.10–5.51 kg-H2−1. The results define conditional operating trade-offs and priorities for local feed characterization, kinetic, separation, heat-integration, and equipment-level studies. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Uncovering heterogeneity in students’ metacognitive ability within social-emotional learning: A rasch measurement analysis
Abstract: This study aims to uncover the heterogeneity of students' metacognitive ability within the framework of Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) using the Rasch measurement model. While previous studies have tended to treat metacognitive ability as a homogeneous construct, limited attention has been given to latent individual variability through modern psychometric approaches. This study employed a descriptive quantitative design involving 536 secondary school students in Bali, Indonesia. Data were collected using a metacognitive ability scale and analyzed using the Rasch Rating Scale Model to estimate individual abilities and item difficulty on a common logit scale. In addition to person and item calibration, the analysis included reliability indices, rating scale diagnostics, principal component analysis of residuals, differential item functioning by gender, and person-item mapping through the Wright Map. The findings indicate that students' metacognitive ability is heterogeneously distributed and forms multiple distinct ability strata. The instrument demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and was capable of differentiating levels of student ability meaningfully. Visualization through the Wright Map shows that student abilities are continuously distributed from low to high levels, without clustering in a single category. Furthermore, some students exhibited ability levels that exceeded the difficulty of most items, suggesting the need to develop more challenging items to enhance measurement precision. This heterogeneity may reflect variations in self-regulation development, learning experiences, and socio-emotional factors. In addition, some observable gender-related patterns emerged, although these tendencies should be interpreted cautiously and within their sociocultural context. Overall, the findings highlight the contribution of Rasch measurement in revealing latent variations that are often obscured by aggregate scores and provide empirical support for differentiated learning strategies aimed at fostering reflective, autonomous, and adaptive learners. Title: Designing the future of consciousness: A components framework and speculative implications
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: As technologies increasingly converge with users’ psychophysiology and mental states, perception and mind-altering are emerging as plausibly designable components of user experience. This gives rise to emergent phenomena of digitally induced altered states of consciousness (DIAL) that find application not only in therapeutic and mental health contexts but also in communication and leisure. Modern consciousness-altering technologies primarily exist as early prototypes, and their empirical research tends to constrain the context of use to instrumental functionality. Fictional narrative analysis proposes to push these limitations by considering concepts of technology in imaginary contexts, thereby examining the experiences, social rituals, and ethical issues associated with their use far beyond traditional technical scenarios. This article employs a reflexive thematic analysis of popular science fiction narratives to expand our understanding of how ASCs are integrated into HCI, considering broader sociocultural and sociotechnical contexts. As a result, we identify key aspects of interaction (purpose and context) and combine their subcategories into a framework that facilitates rethinking traditional HCI, revealing potentials that remain inaccessible within clear consciousness. This framework was used to construct five themes, highlighting that the benefits of mitigating cognitive load and deepening technology-mediated communication with DIAL might entail sacrificing identity and autonomy and increasing the pressures of the modern, overcompetitive, hyper-individualistic lifestyle. Thus, the article contributes to the HCI agenda by expanding existing paradigms of interaction with mind-altering technologies and by demonstrating the use of science fiction as a powerful avenue for exploring the design space and critical inquiries about these types of interactions. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Mental Health and Neurodivergence Disclosure Risk Mitigation in Private Higher Education Institutions: An Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to Support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study examines mental health and neurodivergence disclosure risk mitigation in private higher education institutions through an Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 297 academic and non-academic staff from selected private higher education institutions in Selangor, Malaysia. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Structural power asymmetry, institutional trust deficit, stigma anticipation, and absence of safeguards reduce psychological safety in disclosure. Perceived enforceability of protection moderates these relationships and strengthens the explanatory power of the model. This study highlights perceived enforceability of protection as a key risk mitigation mechanism for developing inclusive, psychologically safe, and sustainable higher education governance. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

Title: AWCRL: Adaptive Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reliability Learning for resource-constrained proxy-state recognition
Abstract: Multimodal pattern recognition can support the characterization of affective and behavioral states by integrating complementary visual and physiological evidence, but real-world deployment is challenged by unreliable modalities, limited annotations, and constrained computation. We propose Adaptive Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Reliability Learning (AWCRL), a resource-aware framework for recognizing ontology-derived affective proxy states under incomplete or unreliable multimodal evidence. AWCRL estimates modality reliability from unimodal predictions and a lightweight pre-routing pooled consensus, then uses a budget-conditioned router to retain informative tokens before low-rank cross-modal fusion. An explicit weak ontology maps affective and engagement-related cues to four ordinal proxy states — stable, disengaged, cognitive overload, and acute stress — while confidence- and affinity-weighted prototype refinement reduces the influence of uncertain weak labels. Under subject-independent five-fold evaluation on K-EmoCon and AMIGOS, AWCRL achieves 78.6% and 76.2% macro-F1 with mean computation of 0.78 and 0.82 GFLOPs per segment, respectively. Compared with full-token inference at 1.95 GFLOPs, the budgeted setting reduces computation by 60.0% and 57.9%, with macro-F1 decreasing by only 0.8 and 0.7 percentage points. On K-EmoCon, AWCRL also achieves the highest descriptive macro-F1 among the compared methods under complete, missing-modality, and single-modality corruption conditions. These results indicate a favorable recognition–efficiency trade-off under weak supervision and variable multimodal evidence. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: HeRaKT: Heterogeneous bidirectional modeling for response-aware knowledge tracing
Abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) aims to predict future performance of learners by modeling the evolving knowledge states from historical interactions. Existing methods typically do not distinguish the semantic roles of responses and encode them in a unified structure, thereby overlooking the heterogeneous semantics between correct and incorrect interactions. In this paper, we conduct empirical analyses revealing that responses with the same correctness label as the prediction target contribute positively to performance, whereas those of the opposite type introduce semantic noise. Motivated by this finding, we propose a novel Heterogeneous bidirectional modeling framework for Response-aware Knowledge Tracing (HeRaKT). To explore the underutilized semantic heterogeneity of learner responses, we design a path-separated architecture for handling heterogeneous signals with distinct inductive biases. To further enrich each path with broader bidirectional response-level signals, we devise a cloze-style training strategy which aggregates both past and future responses without label leakage. Extensive experiments on multiple public KT benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, validating the importance of explicitly modeling response heterogeneity and leveraging bidirectional response contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Sex-dependent habenular dysregulation across the continuum of stress exposure and depression severity: A systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence
Abstract: Background: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is diagnosed at roughly twice the rate in women as in men, yet sex is still routinely treated as a covariate rather than a biological variable of primary interest in depression research. The habenula (Hb), particularly the lateral habenula (LHb), is an increasingly implicated substrate of depression, but two recent systematic reviews found sex-stratified habenula data sparse and reported sex effects inconsistent in direction. Objective: To determine whether sex-related effects on habenula structure and function are patterned by stress intensity or chronicity in preclinical models, and by depression severity or chronicity in clinical populations, rather than arbitrary. Methods: This review builds on two parent systematic reviews (Cameron, Weston-Green and Newell, 2024; Fortin et al., 2025), extracting eligible sex-stratified studies and supplementing them with an independent, two-phase search (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) for comprehensive coverage of sex- and stress-related terms. Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by stressor chronicity (preclinical) and illness chronicity or severity (clinical), without meta-analysis. Results: Seventeen studies met eligibility criteria (10 preclinical, 7 clinical). In preclinical models, acute stressors produced modality-dependent, sometimes opposite-direction sex effects, while chronic stressors more consistently interacted with, and sometimes abolished, pre-existing baseline sex differences. In clinical populations, sex-dependent habenula abnormalities were largely absent in first-episode presentations and became more pronounced, often specifically in women, with greater illness chronicity, treatment resistance, or symptom severity. Conclusions: Sex-dependent habenula dysfunction in depression shows a patterned, chronicity-linked structure in both literatures, though the evidence base remains small and several conclusions rest on a single study. These findings are hypothesis-generating rather than establishing sex as a confirmed driver of habenula dysfunction. Estrous cycle stage, baseline circuit-level sexual dimorphism, and sociocultural confounds are identified as testable moderators for future research. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Renewable energy infrastructure in desert-gobi-arid zones: A review of physical-ecological transformations and ecosystem resilience
Abstract: Desert-Gobi-Arid (DGA) zones are key regions for large-scale photovoltaic and wind-energy development and represent fragile dryland ecosystems with strong water limitation and slow ecological recovery. This paper critically reviews the ecological impacts of renewable-energy infrastructure in DGA-type landscapes, using China’s DGA bases as the main empirical context and evidence from ecologically comparable drylands for comparison. It examines how photovoltaic and wind facilities affect surface environments, ecological processes, and carbon cycling. Existing studies indicate that these facilities influence local microclimate, soil conditions, vegetation dynamics, and carbon exchange through shading, surface disturbance, airflow alteration, and hydrothermal redistribution. These impacts are site- and scale-dependent and are jointly controlled by facility layout, disturbance intensity, surface substrate, vegetation background, climate conditions, and management practices. Under low-disturbance design and effective management, they may support soil moisture retention, vegetation recovery, soil carbon accumulation, and ecosystem resilience, while higher disturbance may increase ecological risks such as water stress and habitat fragmentation. This review links direct emission reductions with indirect ecological effects and governance considerations and provides a case-based reference for assessing renewable-energy development in fragile dryland environments. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Li C.; Xi Z.; Yu B.; Yu X.; Wang H.; Dong R.; Zhao S.; Yang S.
Title: Dynamic temporal modeling and distribution-calibrated fusion for multimodal sentiment analysis
Abstract: Existing multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) methods still lack dynamic modeling of unstable emotional information. Emotional expressions in audio and visual modalities often exhibit different temporal rhythms, while most existing recurrent state update mechanisms propagate hidden states at fixed temporal progression scales. In addition, some cross-modal associations merely reflect statistical co-occurrence patterns, and such incidental correlations do not always correspond to genuine emotional dependencies. Moreover, the reliability and contribution of each modality may dynamically vary across real-world scenarios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multimodal sentiment analysis framework based on dynamic temporal modeling and distribution-calibrated fusion. Specifically, adaptive temporal modeling is performed on audio and visual sequences through dynamic temporal granularity selection, enabling the model to capture both short-term emotional fluctuations and long-range emotional dependencies while estimating temporal confidence. Furthermore, Gaussian distribution modeling and perturbation consistency constraints are introduced to characterize uncertainty in modality representations, thereby preventing over-reliance on unreliable associations during fusion. Temporal confidence and distributional uncertainty are further combined into a unified modality confidence, which dynamically regulates cross-modal fusion and representation alignment to improve semantic consistency of fused representations. Experimental results on the CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Extending the operating range of HCCI engines with the rhombic drive mechanism: A novel concept
Abstract: Homogeneous charge compression ignition (HCCI) engines offer high thermal efficiency and very low nitrogen oxides (NOx) and soot emissions, but they have significant challenges such as a limited operating range, knocking at high loads, and misfiring at low loads. In this study, the use of a rhombic drive mechanism as an alternative to the conventional crankshaft mechanism was numerically investigated for the first time to extend the operating range of HCCI engines. A total of 301 computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed using CONVERGE CFD, employing an HCCI engine model validated with experimental data. The simulations were conducted at engine speeds of 800–2600 rpm, within a λ range of 1.3–3.4, using fuels with research octane numbers of 20 and 40 (RON20 and RON40). The results showed that the rhombic drive mechanism extended the compression phase, allowing the piston to remain near top dead center (TDC) for a longer duration. This increased the average cylinder temperature, facilitating auto-ignition and enabling stable HCCI combustion near the low-load limit at higher engine speeds. With the rhombic drive mechanism, heat release was more concentrated around TDC, the combustion duration was shortened, and the combustion process approached a constant-volume character. The principal contribution of the rhombic drive mechanism was extending the upper engine-speed limit of naturally aspirated HCCI operation. The low-load improvement was secondary, while higher MPRR under identical engine-speed and lambda conditions showed no direct extension of the high-load limit at a fixed speed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Exploring socioeconomic associations of crisis information processing via large language models and explainable AI
Abstract: Social media evolution has restructured corporate crisis communication, yet extracting regional intelligence from unstructured data remains a significant computational challenge. This study proposes an integrated AI-Spatial Information Framework to analyze provincial-level discourse patterns during a major corporate crisis. Using the DeepSeek R1 671B model with few-shot learning, we classified 225,515 social media comments from Douyin into five theory-driven categories and an “Other” category, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.67% against stratified human reference labels (Cohen’s kappa = 0.828). We then employed LASSO-based feature selection and FDR-corrected OLS regression to examine associations between provincial-level socioeconomic indicators and consumer discourse patterns across 31 Chinese provinces. Statistical results suggest that provincial socioeconomic factors account for a substantial portion of the observed variation in digital discourse. Life expectancy was positively associated with brand anthropomorphism, while tertiary education showed a tentative negative association with health risk perception. More importantly, these associations suggest that regional variation in brand-supportive discourse is closely related to socioeconomic conditions and is theoretically consistent with cognitive buffering processes. By integrating theory-driven LLM classification with spatial analysis, the proposed framework connects computational linguistics and spatial social computing, providing a replicable approach for examining regional heterogeneity in digital crisis discourse. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Interface-aware adaptive layer-wise physics-informed neural networks for multilayer large-strain consolidation: a benchmark of architectures, training strategies, and trade-offs
Abstract: Multilayer large-strain consolidation in stratified soils involves nonlinear pore-pressure dissipation, evolving deformation, and material discontinuities, which pose significant challenges for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). This study develops a layer-wise adaptive PINN framework in which soil layers are represented by neural subnetworks coupled through pore-pressure and Darcy-flux continuity conditions. A controlled three-layer benchmark is used to evaluate MLP and KAN architectures, adaptive activation, adaptive weighting, and parameter sharing over three independent random seeds. The framework is further extended to four- and five-layer profiles using Shared MLP, layer-wise MLP, and KAN. Results demonstrate that no single architecture is optimal across all physical responses: parameter sharing improves mean global and settlement accuracy, KAN-based models better control selected local errors, and adaptive strategies alter pressure, settlement, and interface behavior in a metric-dependent manner. The successful four- and five-layer calculations further support the applicability of the same physical formulation as the number of internal interfaces increases, although the preferred architecture changes with the layer arrangement. Overall, pore-pressure accuracy, settlement prediction, interface consistency, and computational cost involve distinct trade-offs, so model selection should reflect the target physical quantity and profile complexity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Technological paths for enhancing renewable energy integration: Modeling, optimization, and practical prospects
Abstract: Against the backdrop of global dual-carbon goals and China's energy transition, the large-scale integration of wind and solar power faces an integration bottleneck due to their inherent intermittency and insufficient grid flexibility. This paper systematically reviews mainstream modeling methods for renewable energy integration-including system constraint modeling, time-series production simulation, and optimal scheduling-with a comparative analysis of their core logic, applicable scenarios, and solution strategies. From five key dimensions-power-side regulation, grid-side flexible interconnection and grid-forming control, energy storage coordination, multi-energy complementarity, and market-oriented mechanisms-this study analyzes the optimization pathways and technical achievements in enhancing renewable energy integration. It also summarizes typical domestic and international practices and identifies core challenges such as limited model adaptability, trade-offs between system security and integration efficiency, weak grid support, and regional imbalances. Future research directions are proposed, including AI-assisted dispatching, digital twin applications, distributed integration technologies, localization of international experiences, electricity-carbon market linkage, and differentiated urban-rural development paths. This review aims to provide theoretical and practical insights for overcoming integration bottlenecks and advancing the construction of new power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Understanding work well-being: A systematic review and future research agenda on multilevel influences
Abstract: Work well-being has become an important topic in organizational research, as it is beneficial to employee performance and job satisfaction. Although studies on work well-being have increased recently, existing literature remains fragmented, with prior reviews predominantly focusing on general employee well-being or single-level analyses. This limitation constrains both theoretical clarity and the development of targeted organizational interventions. In particular, there is a need to systematically review how individual, group, and organizational factors shape employees’ well-being at work. To address this gap, the present study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from 53 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. This study has two key implications: It identifies knowledge gaps in the literature and supports evidence-based decision-making. By synthesizing findings across the individual, group, and organizational levels, this review develops a broad and integrated understanding of the drivers of work well-being. The findings suggest that work well-being is driven by the dynamic interaction between individual and social resources, and broader organizational conditions. These factors operate in combination rather than independently, shaping employees’ psychological experiences across work contexts. This study contributes to the literature by providing a structured and integrative multilevel framework, clarifying conceptual boundaries of work well-being, and identifying underexplored research areas. It also offers a more analytically grounded synthesis that advances theoretical development and informs evidence-based organizational practices. In addition, the study highlights directions for future research, offering valuable insights for policymakers, managers, and scholars seeking to promote work well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Cities under pressure: Tourism intensity and the erosion of social capital in Italy
Abstract: This research note reconceptualizes tourism intensity as a structural stressor capable of undermining the social capital that sustains urban life. Drawing on a 15-year longitudinal panel data of 42 Italian cities (2009-2023) and employing a dynamic System GMM estimator, our study analyses how varying levels of tourism intensity affect social capital, operationalized through a multi-indicator civic engagement index. The results reveal a non-linear erosion process, where social capital remains stable at low and moderate levels of tourism intensity but declines sharply once cities surpass high-intensity thresholds. Our findings provide a quantifiable basis for understanding overtourism as a threshold-based social phenomenon, extending beyond resident perceptions to the structural weakening of civic cooperation, trust, and engagement. The present study advances theoretical debates by positioning tourism intensity as a civic destabilizer and highlights the need for governance models that protect social capital as a critical urban asset. Without such safeguards, cities risk transitioning from vibrant, participatory communities into socially depleted Non-places. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Science takes more than belief: Epistemic and cognitive predictors of scientific reasoning
Abstract: Belief in science and scientific reasoning represent related but conceptually distinct aspects of individuals' engagement with science: the former reflects an epistemic orientation toward science, whereas the latter concerns the ability to evaluate evidence, methods, and inferences. We examined actively open-minded thinking (AOT) and cognitive reflection (CRT) as theoretically complementary characteristics, representing an epistemic disposition and a reflective cognitive component, respectively. In a sample of 333 Italian participants, we examined the incremental associations of belief in science, AOT, and CRT with scientific reasoning and whether AOT and CRT showed similar or differentiated associations with belief in science and scientific reasoning. Belief in science was positively but weakly associated with scientific reasoning. AOT and CRT accounted for additional variance in scientific reasoning beyond sociodemographic characteristics and belief in science. AOT was associated with both belief in science and scientific reasoning, whereas CRT was associated with scientific reasoning but not significantly with belief in science. Overall, the findings indicate partly differentiated patterns of association across the two constructs. Authors: Guan Y.; Cao S.
Title: A dynamic graph query-based data pricing method via multi-armed bandits
Abstract: Graph query-based data pricing is promising for pricing answer subgraphs in graph databases according to diverse buyer queries. However, existing methods provide limited support for adaptive price updates when the broker must balance transaction revenue with transaction success rate under incomplete buyer-valuation information. To bridge this gap, we propose GQPRM, which includes: (1) a vertex-edge pricing mechanism that prices a first-time queried answer graph through non-negative atomic prices; (2) a multi-armed bandit (MAB)-based strategy that discretizes repeated-query prices into candidate actions and uses historical acceptance/rejection records for exploration and exploitation; (3) an entropy-weighted feedback update that allocates the observed subgraph-level price variation to vertices and edges in a demand-sensitive manner, rather than assuming that binary feedback uniquely identifies a single overpriced element; and (4) a smart contract-based incentive allocation mechanism that records ownership and supports auditable reward allocation between the data broker and data owners. Experiments on three typical datasets demonstrate that GQPRM improves cumulative transaction value and transaction success rate over the static baseline under the evaluated settings. © 2026

Authors: Xu Y.; Hao Q.; Li X.; Niu L.; Xia C.
Title: Reinforcement learning with experience sharing promotes collective cooperation on higher-order networks
Abstract: As a central form of prosocial behavior, collective cooperation is the cornerstone of social prosperity, and elucidating how it emerges among the self-interested population is of significant theoretical and practical importance. However, existing research of cooperative evolution on higher-order networks typically assumes that agents update decisions exclusively based on their own experiences, overlooking the pervasive diffusion of information within groups. In reality, decision-making is shaped not only by individual experience, but also by experiences acquired from neighboring agents. To this end, we develop a hypergraph-based reinforcement learning framework that integrates individual and neighborhood experiences to investigate how information sharing affects cooperation under higher-order interactions. Specifically, we utilize hypergraphs to characterize the interaction topology, within which agents update their strategies according to the Q-learning algorithm. Extending the standard learning paradigm, we introduce an experience sharing mechanism, where neighborhood information is aggregated to form a shared experience and subsequently fused with individual experience to guide decision-making. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that an intermediate level of experience sharing can significantly enhance the collective cooperation, particularly under severe social dilemmas, increasing the final cooperation level by up to approximately 0.43. In contrast, excessive experience sharing leads to behavioral homogenization among agents, thereby undermining the relative advantage of cooperation. Moreover, higher learning rates coupled with moderate discount factors are most conducive to cooperation. These findings shed new light on how experience sharing shapes cooperative dynamics in higher-order networks. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.
