Title: Efficient stability-preserving model order reduction for vibro-acoustic systems with complex configuration of porous and poro-elastic materials
Abstract: Recent developments in digital twins have led to a renewed interest in efficient transient vibro-acoustic finite element simulations, which can be combined with limited measurements to bridge the gap between the model and the physical world. To this end, stability-preserving model order reduction (spMOR) is a rapidly emerging topic to enable large-scale finite element models, which can reduce the size of these models but preserve their high fidelity and stability. Notably, the spMOR for vibro-acoustic systems with different porous materials was recently addressed by introducing additional variables. The trade-off is that the size of the resulting full-order models increases significantly with the complexity of porous materials, such as the frequency range and dimensions. Consequently, substantial computational resources are required for the offline generation of the reduction basis. Hence, an efficient approach is proposed in this paper to improve the offline stage efficiency of the spMOR for vibro-acoustics with a complex configuration of porous and poro-elastic materials, which adopts a two-step strategy to generate stable reduced-order models. Firstly, a higher-order Krylov subspace method based on Taylor’s theorem is applied to the frequency-domain model, leading to an intermediate reduced-order model. This process ensures the preservation of system matrix properties and positive realness of the frequency-dependent parameters. Secondly, leveraging these key properties, the spMOR for vibro-acoustics with porous and poro-elastic materials is applied to the intermediate reduced-order model to give a compact time-domain model. The proposed method is demonstrated on a simple cubic cavity and a more involved sedan car cabin. The proposed method significantly accelerates the calculation of the reduction basis and reduces memory usage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: An adaptive-problem structure framework for survival relevance in temporal processing
Abstract: Research on survival-relevant cues and subjective time often groups stimuli into immediate-survival, reproductive, and social categories. These labels do not explain why cues within one category recruit different temporal processes across contexts and perceivers. The Adaptive-Problem Structure (APS) Framework characterizes the adaptive problem indicated by a cue through two separable appraisals: ecological urgency, the time sensitivity and cost of delaying a response, and interpretive indeterminacy, the extent to which adaptive meaning and the appropriate response remain unresolved. APS predicts when these appraisals recruit established arousal, attention, information-sampling, and memory processes, how diagnostic context changes those links, and which personality differences strengthen them. Temporal consequences depend on the timing paradigm, interval, and response format. We outline independent ratings, selective within-domain manipulations, process measures, and staged construct validation. Five predictions specify task conditions, personality mappings, comparison baselines, and non-supporting outcomes. APS offers testable constraints on mechanism recruitment and prediction for new stimuli; the framework itself remains to be empirically validated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Efficient optimal scale combination selection via granular sequential three-way decision
Abstract: Optimal scale combination (OSC) selection is crucial for knowledge extraction in multi-scale decision systems (MDSs). However, existing multi-scale rough set models typically represent the three regions as unions of equivalence classes, losing the structural information of equivalence classes and hindering rule extraction. Moreover, most OSC selection algorithms adopt a fine-to-coarse backward search strategy, which not only contradicts the human coarse-to-fine cognitive mode but also is inefficient on large-scale datasets due to scale combination explosion. To address these issues, a granular sequential three-way decision model for MDSs (GrS3WD-M) is developed, and then an efficient forward optimal scale combination selection algorithm (FOSC) is designed. First, a two-step trisecting strategy is proposed to accelerate boundary region reduction, and then GrS3WD-M based on granular rough sets is developed to preserve the structural information of equivalence classes. As a result, rules can be directly extracted from equivalence classes in the positive region, while redundant computation during granulation is avoided. Second, the core scale combination is defined, an equivalent computational formula is derived, and an efficient algorithm based on GrS3WD-M and attribute grouping is proposed for its computation. Finally, the outer significance of attributes in MDSs is defined, and an efficient method for computing it is presented. Furthermore, the FOSC algorithm is proposed, which starts from the core scale combination and uses the outer significance as a heuristic to guide a coarse-to-fine forward search. Title: QLRUN: Integrating Q-learning and covariance matrix learning into Runge–Kutta optimization for engineering design problems
Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid metaheuristic Q-learning Runge–Kutta Optimization (QLRUN) for solving complex, high-dimensional, rotated, and constrained engineering optimization problems. The proposed framework integrates the gradient-guided search mechanism of the Runge–Kutta Optimization (RUN) algorithm with the adaptive decision-making capability of Q-learning to achieve dynamic regulation of exploration and exploitation behaviors during the optimization process. In QLRUN, the optimization state is characterized using convergence and population-diversity indicators, while the Q-learning agent adaptively selects search operators according to a fitness-improvement-driven reward policy that is iteratively updated throughout the search process. To further enhance rotational robustness and maintain population diversity, a lightweight Covariance Matrix Learning (CML) mechanism is incorporated to construct adaptive eigen-coordinate systems aligned with the fitness landscape's geometry. Unlike the full covariance adaptation employed in CMA-ES, the proposed CML strategy acts as an efficient coordinate-transformation mechanism with low computational overhead. The effectiveness of QLRUN is comprehensively validated using the 23 classic standards, the CEC2020, and CEC2022 benchmark suites, which include unimodal, multimodal, hybrid, composition, shifted, and rotated functions, as well as seven constrained engineering design problems. Comparative evaluations against the original RUN and nine state-of-the-art metaheuristics demonstrate that QLRUN consistently achieves competitive convergence accuracy, improved solution stability, and faster convergence characteristics. Quantitatively, QLRUN achieves the top Friedman mean rank across all three benchmark suites, attaining scores of 1.70 on 23 classic standards, 1.40 on CEC2020, and 1.17 on CEC2022, thereby substantially outperforming the original RUN and the competing optimization methods. Moreover, on constrained engineering design problems, QLRUN obtains highly competitive best-known solutions, including a pressure vessel design cost of 5.88536×103 and a tension/compression spring weight of 1.26660×10−2. Beyond p-value-based significance, practical superiority is further confirmed through consistent top-one Friedman rankings and Wilcoxon Rank-Sum win/tie/loss results against RUN of 17/5/1, 8/1/1, and 9/2/1 for the 23 classic standards, CEC2020, and CEC2022 benchmark suites, respectively. Statistical analyses using the Wilcoxon Rank-Sum, Friedman, ANOVA, and Kruskal–Wallis tests confirm the robustness and practical significance of the proposed approach. Authors: Halali E.
Author full names: Halali, Eliran (55835015500)
Title: Two automatic motivations, two control systems: A neuroscience framework for negotiation
Abstract: Negotiation often involves a recurring tension between self-interest and social preferences such as fairness, trust, honesty, and reciprocity. A central debate concerns which motive, self-interest or social preferences, constitutes the automatic default and which requires cognitive control to be expressed. Understanding these automatic processes is important because negotiations often tax cognitive resources, increasing reliance on automatic responses. Yet, the evidence remains contradictory: in some contexts, self-interest appears spontaneous and social concern effortful, whereas in others the reverse holds. This review argues that the inconsistency stems from a flawed premise. Drawing on converging evidence from social, affective, and decision neuroscience, I propose that both self-interest and social preferences are automatic motivational processes, driven by distinct motivational systems and regulated by separate prefrontal control mechanisms. The right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (rDLPFC) is proposed to regulate reward-seeking motivation, facilitating prosocial behavior such as fairness and reciprocity, whereas the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (rVLPFC) is proposed to regulate socio-emotional responses, facilitating self-interested choice, together forming a proposed double dissociation within this motivational conflict. This dual-control framework reframes the central question from which motive is automatic to which automatic motivational system dominates a given context. It reconciles conflicting findings and explains why subtle situational shifts can reverse the apparent automatic response. Title: The role of citizen science in engaging older adults with age-friendly green spaces
Abstract: This project addresses the global challenges of an ageing population and rapid urbanisation by exploring how citizen science can support the engagement of older adults in shaping age-friendly green spaces. Conducted in the City of Unley, South Australia, the study engaged 30 older residents (aged 60+) as citizen scientists to trial a multi-format audit tool and co-reflect on its use in practice for creating age-friendly environments, generating practical insights for future research and design practice. Integrating audits into participants’ daily routines and everyday life spaces ensured that findings reflected lived experiences. Citizen science was not merely a data collection tool but a sustained dialogue, with regular workshops and informal café sessions supporting motivation, peer learning, and collaborative analysis. Participants reported challenges such as sustaining long-term motivation, but also highlighted opportunities for empowerment, confidence-building, and strengthened community ties. Importantly, many older adults described shifts in how they experienced their environments—becoming more observant, extending their walking habits, and growing more confident in voicing ideas. Several participants continued their civic engagement beyond the project, illustrating the lasting impact of participation. The study contributes methodological insights into designing inclusive citizen science initiatives, offering guidance on recruitment, tool development, and engagement strategies tailored to older populations. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of citizen science not only to generate grounded data but also to empower older adults and co-produce inclusive urban knowledge. Findings provide process-focused insights into age-friendly engagement and illustrate the broader potential of citizen science in shaping equitable, community led public spaces. Overall, this research demonstrates how citizen science can move beyond data collection to become a co-creative process that empowers older adults and informs age-friendly urban transformation. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Herbal medicine among vulnerable populations in Cameroon: a systematic review and meta-analysis with clinical, mechanistic, and global health perspectives
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Herbal medicine (HM) is widely used in Cameroon, yet its prevalence, clinical evidence, and the pharmacological mechanisms supporting its use among vulnerable populations have not been comprehensively synthesised.Aim of the study: To systematically review and meta-analyse HM use among women, adolescents, and children in Cameroon, summarise the available clinical and mechanistic evidence for commonly reported medicinal plants, and identify challenges relevant to policy and global health. Materials and methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, multiple databases were systematically searched. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled HM proportion. Also, a PubMed search for clinical evidence (randomised controlled trials, RCTs) and bioactive compounds/mechanistic insights was conducted to support the folkloric use of the identified plants. Results: Sixteen studies involving ∼15,000 individuals were included. The pooled proportion of HM use was 46.9% (95% CI 30.7 – 63.4%), with subgroup estimates of 52.1% (95% CI 33.6 – 70.4%) in women and 26.4% (95% CI 0.0 – 85.0%) in children. A total of 93 plant species belonging to 79 genera and 44 families were identified. Anaemia, digestive problems, labour, and cancer were the main reasons for HM. Cordia platythyrsa and Entandrophragma candollei were classified as vulnerable/endangered by the IUCN. RCT evidence was available for only 19 plant species, including 6-shogaol (Zingiber officinale) and annonacin (Annona muricata) for cancer, quercetin-3-rhamnoside (Alchornea cordifolia) for anaemia, and oleic acid (Phoenix dactylifera) for labour. Mechanistic studies indicated that these bioactive compounds act through multiple pathways (e.g., shogaol - upregulated STAT3 pathway, reactive oxygen species generation, and cell cycle arrest in cancer cells). Conclusions: Nearly one in two individuals in these vulnerable populations reported HM use, despite limited high-quality clinical evidence supporting most medicinal plants. Strengthening epidemiological surveillance, clinical research, conservation of threatened medicinal species, and integration of traditional medicine into health systems could improve the safe and evidence-based use of HM in Cameroon and similar settings. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Anchoring sustainability: A new paradigm for maritime clusters
Abstract: The environmental footprint of maritime transport, combined with growing social and regulatory pressure to tackle pollution, has brought the shipping industry to the forefront of the sustainability agenda. The role of industry clusters is becoming increasingly relevant to this discourse, given their influence across all dimensions of sustainability. Surprisingly, although this profound relationship is well documented, it has not received sufficient scholarly attention. This study analyses the highly fragmented literature on maritime clusters and sustainability using a novel combination of bibliometrics and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven thematic analysis. On this basis, a framework is developed that captures the interaction between clusters and the key components of sustainability. The findings suggest that sustainability should not be treated as an isolated strategic initiative or the outcome of regulatory pressure, but as a key dimension of cluster competitiveness. Additionally, it emerges that digital innovation acts as a cross-cutting enabler of sustainability in maritime clusters, linking the economic, social/governance, and environmental pillars of the proposed framework. Title: Techno-economic analysis of biogas production: a literature review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: The accelerating global energy transition and the development of the circular economy have established biogas as a key renewable energy source that can reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve waste management, and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals. From this perspective, the techno-economic performance and sustainability of biogas systems have attracted growing attention in both academic and policy domains. This review aims to provide a comprehensive assessment of global research on biogas production and its techno-economic analysis, focusing on scientific dynamics, technological advances, analytical methods, and methodological challenges. An integrative review approach was applied, combining a systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis. A total of 287 Scopus-indexed publications were analyzed using VOSviewer to identify key research trends, collaborations, and thematic clusters. The qualitative synthesis explores advancements in anaerobic digestion technologies, biogas upgrading, and techno-economic analysis frameworks, with an emphasis on key performance indicators, cost metrics, modeling approaches, and uncertainty analysis. The results indicate a substantial increase in publication activity, from 3 publications in 2015 to 64 in 2024, accompanied by expanding international research collaboration. The analysis also reveals a methodological evolution from conventional cost-based evaluations toward integrated frameworks that combine technical, economic, environmental, and uncertainty assessment components. Recent studies reflect progress in co-digestion optimization, microbiological enhancement, life cycle-based assessments, and AI-driven modeling. However, significant gaps remain, including limited data reliability, regional inconsistencies, and the absence of harmonized methodologies for techno-economic analysis. The review highlights the need for standardized, transparent, and policy-oriented frameworks to strengthen the role of biogas in sustainable energy transitions. Future efforts should concentrate on improving the robustness of data, integrating environmental and socio-economic dimensions, and aligning techno-economic analysis practices with national and international energy strategies. Bibliometric analysis identified 5 major thematic research clusters covering anaerobic digestion, feedstock and waste management, environmental assessment, process engineering, and resource recovery. The review further demonstrates that recent advances in co-digestion, pretreatment technologies, microbiological enhancement, and biogas upgrading have contributed to improved methane yields and enhanced process performance. In order to increase the efficiency of the production system, careful consideration must be given to the choice of feedstocks, the production processes, and the legal framework for biogas production. Efforts must be focused on improving the technological and commercial efficiency of biogas to ensure good sustainability. In this context, appropriate investments and policies could play a key role in energy diversification. © 2026 The Authors. Publishing services by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of KeAi Communications Co. Authors: Wang L.; Jia J.; Zhou L.; Li S.
Title: Perceived placeness in creative tourism: Conceptualization, scale development and implications for transformative experiences
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Creative place-making combines cultural heritage, spatial design, creative symbolism, and experiential affordances to cultivate distinctive destinations, yet what tourists holistically perceive in these places remains underexplored. Drawing on atmospheric aesthetics theory, this study conceptualizes perceived placeness in creative tourism as tourists' holistic perception of the environmental and atmospheric qualities that make creative tourism destinations experientially distinctive. To operationalize this construct, content analysis was used to identify its dimensions and initial items. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses refined these items into a 20-item, five-dimensional scale comprising environmental qualities, historical-cultural embeddedness, creative-symbolic ambiance, restorative affordance, and emotional affordance. The nomological relevance of the scale was further established by examining its implications for transformative experiences via authenticity. Theoretically, this study positions perceived placeness as an integrative perceptual field between place-making and tourists’ psychological responses, and contextually elaborates atmospheric aesthetics theory in creative tourism. Practically, the scale provides a timely tool for evaluating and planning creative place-making efforts and curating meaningful tourist experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhou T.; Liao Y.; Cheng X.; Liu L.; Chen W.
Title: From growth mindset to social-emotional skills in early and mid-adolescence: A educational-cultural examination of an integrated mind-body-behavior framework
Abstract: Background: Social-emotional learning (SEL) is a core educational goal, yet little is known about how adolescents’ cognitive beliefs, body-related self-perceptions, and everyday health behavior jointly relate to social-emotional skills across diverse cultural contexts and school stages. Objective: Based on mindset theory and self-regulation perspectives, we examined an integrated Mind-Body-Behavior framework in which growth mindset, positive body image, and health behavior show a theoretically specified pattern of associated with adolescents’ social-emotional skills. Sample: Participants were 62,105 adolescents from 15 regions where data were drawn from the OECD 2023 Study on Social and Emotional Skills. Methods: A two-stage quantitative design combined structural equation modeling and machine learning. Results: Growth mindset was associated with social-emotional skills both directly and indirectly associations via body image and health behavior. The direct association was substantially stronger than the combined indirect associations, indicating partial rather than complete support for the full proposed pattern. Scalar invariance across the seven clusters was not supported, so cluster-level comparisons were treated as descriptive. Associations differed between cohorts: the association between growth mindset and body image was stronger in the younger cohort, whereas the association between health behavior and social-emotional skills was stronger in the older cohort. Conclusions: The study contributes an integrated view of how beliefs, body-related self-perception, and health behavior relate to social-emotional skills. The framework shows that cognitive, body-related, and behavioral domains each relate to adolescents’ social-emotional skills and that these relations change between school stages. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Lexicon-guided representation learning with self-attentive transformer models: Enhancing offensive language detection in low-resourced languages
Abstract: Detecting offensive language in online social platforms is essential yet challenging in low-resourced, morphologically rich languages such as Turkish. This study presents an engineering-driven and innovative approach for offensive language detection in Turkish. The proposed method directly injects offensive lexicons collected from local sources by domain experts into transformer self-attention mechanisms. In particular, it leverages lexicon-guided representation learning within Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) variations to enhance attention toward offensive linguistic cues. DistilBERT and XLM-RoBERTa are enhanced with a lexicon mask that reweights attention toward lexicon-matched tokens by a factor of five, while maintaining end-to-end fine-tuning without architectural modifications. Using the OffensEval Turkish dataset (35,284 annotated tweets), the proposed method is evaluated against traditional baselines (MLP, CNN, SVM, LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU) as well as vanilla transformer models. The proposed Lexicon-Guided XLM-RoBERTa achieves an F1-score of 0.87, while Lexicon-Guided DistilBERT attains 0.85, outperforming vanilla XLM-RoBERTa (0.78), DistilBERT (0.76), and non-transformer baselines (0.66–0.72). Additionally, LIME is employed to provide local and model-agnostic explanations for both offensive and non-offensive predictions, demonstrating that lexicon-guided attention enhances the detection of morphologically complex and implicit offensive cues while reducing false positives in neutral contexts. The proposed method offers practical and multidisciplinary contributions through a lightweight plug-in attention mechanism based on linguistic resources, achieving state-of-the-art performance in Turkish offensive language detection while providing interpretable outputs beneficial for content moderation, human-centered AI, and computational social science. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Sounding different: Exploring attitudes towards digital voice personalization in a conversational setting
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of voice generation and conversion technologies, the application of voice personalization in everyday communication is becoming increasingly possible. However, current studies on voice personalization have largely focused on tool design, while relatively little is known about the impact of these technologies on self-presentation and social interaction. To explore this, we conducted a qualitative study with 14 pairs of participants (28 in total, 15 females and 13 males) that integrated a voice personalization tool into natural conversation. In pairs, participants first engaged in a conversation using their original voices, and then reflected on this experience. After that, they personalized their voices using a voice modification tool and took part in a second conversation with the same partner in which they heard each other’s modified voices in real-time. Finally, they participated in follow-up interviews. Our findings show that voice personalization prompted participants to reflect on their original and modified voices, to negotiate between authenticity and desired traits, and to consider both benefits and risks of voice personalization in different contexts. These insights indicate that voice personalization is intricately linked to self-perception while simultaneously functioning as a malleable social signal. Overall, this study contributes empirically grounded findings on how voice modification affects self-perception and impression management, and offers design directions for future personalization tools. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Greenhouse gas emission under a dual-disposability approach: Assessing environmental technical efficiency in the airline industry
Abstract: This study provides a robust analysis of environment-adjusted airline efficiency under a dual-disposability assumption for undesirable output. It employs also a two-stage methodology to investigate the complex and heterogeneous relationships between airline operational profiles and their environmental efficiency. Technical efficiency is estimated in the first step using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) based on the Directional Distance Function (DDF) under both assumptions of the technological characterization of gas emissions, contractible versus non-contractible. In the second step, to analyze the factors influencing the estimated efficiency scores, a Tobit second-stage regression is employed. Results show that efficiency scores under strong disposability are systematically and significantly higher than those obtained under weak disposability, with an average difference of 11.9 percentage points. The findings also indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between the LCC variable and technical efficiency, implying that airline groups with LCC subsidiaries achieve higher efficiency levels. Based on their specific trade-off between operational and environmental inputs, the analysis of technical efficiency elasticities classifies airlines into five groups. These range from “Strong Proactive Environmental Performers” to “Low Efficiency High-Cost” groups, whose efficiency improvements are structurally linked to either an optimization or a deterioration of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions performance. The technical efficiency elasticity with respect to revenue share and to fuel efficiency are parallel across all airlines, while the elasticity for GHG consistently exhibits the opposite sign. We provide one of the few systematic comparisons of efficiency scores under weak versus strong disposability. This comparison allows us to quantify the systematic contraction in measured efficiency that occurs when greenhouse gas emissions are modeled as a technologically costly output rather than a costless byproduct. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Nitrogen-doped graphene composite with optimized pyridinic/pyrrolic configurations for high-performance NH4+ storage
Abstract: Graphene has emerged as a crucial class of electrode materials for aqueous ammonium-ion batteries (AAIBs). However, pristine graphene suffers from severe restacking and lacks sufficient redox-active sites, fundamentally limiting its practical application. Herein, we employ a two-step temperature-controlled pyrolysis strategy using melamine as both a nitrogen source and a self-sacrificing template to synthesize a nitrogen-doped graphene/g-C3N4 composite (g–CN@G-700) that features both a high proportion of redox–active pyridinic and pyrrolic nitrogen configurations and an optimal graphitization degree, thereby resolving the trade-off among conductivity, specific surface area, and active nitrogen content. Consequently, the material demonstrates a high reversible NH4+ storage capacity of 202 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, favorable rate capability, and satisfactory long-term cycling stability with no significant capacity decay after 5,500 cycles at 4 A g−1. By using X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, we reveal a highly reversible synergistic charge storage process involving the active nitrogen species and carbonyl groups with NH4+. Finally, combined with theoretical calculations, we propose a synergistic NH4+ storage mechanism where pyridinic-N and pyrrolic-N provides primary redox-active sites, and graphitic-N maintains structural integrity. This work provides a pathway to design and synthesize high-performance carbon-based materials for AAIBs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Graphene and MXenes: performance–scalability trade-offs and application-driven materials selection in two-dimensional technologies
Abstract: Graphene and MXenes are leading two-dimensional (2D) materials, yet their selection for emerging technologies remains limited by the lack of quantitative comparison between intrinsic performance, scalability, and cost. This review introduces a practical performance–scalability assessment framework based on a multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) approach. In this regard, material-performance, synthesis-scalability, and techno-economic indicators were normalized and integrated to calculate the final material-selection score. The evaluated criteria include electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, mechanical strength, electrochemical capacitance, synthesis yield percentage, maturity status, price per unit mass of precursors, specific energy utilization, and oxidation resistance capability. Graphene exhibits higher thermal conductivity (2000–4000 W m⁻1 K⁻1), mechanical strength (∼130 GPa), and oxidation stability, supporting its use in performance-critical electronics and structural applications. MXenes provide higher electrochemical capacitance ( 300–1500 F g⁻¹), higher reported synthesis yields (80–99%), tunable surface chemistry, and lower estimated laboratory-scale cost (US$10–50 g⁻1), favoring energy storage, sensing, electromagnetic interference shielding, and water-related applications. The novelty of this review lies in combining property-level performance, synthesis maturity, scalability indicators and cost-performance mapping, into a single comparative framework, enabling rational, application-specific selection of graphene, MXenes, and their hybrid systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Zhang P.; Yang Z.; Chen R.
Title: Going green to compete: Male-biased operational sex ratio, status motivation, and men's relative green product preference
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Motivating men to choose environmentally preferable products remains an important challenge. Across six studies, this research examines how operational sex ratio (OSR), defined as the ratio of reproductively available men to women, is associated with men's relative preference for green products over conventional alternatives. OSR can characterize a broader demographic environment or serve as a population cue in a local social setting. A cross-level analysis in China showed that men living in provinces with more male-biased OSRs assigned greater priority to environmental protection, whereas women showed no corresponding association. Randomized experiments showed that perceived male-biased OSR increased men's relative green product preference; perceiving a female-biased OSR did not produce a corresponding increase among women. Among men, the subsequent studies provided complementary evidence consistent with mediation by status motivation, linked male-biased OSR cues more closely to intrasexual competition motivation than to mate-attraction motivation, and showed that audience publicness moderated the indirect effect through status motivation. Title: Laser etching of flattened copper mesh for fabricating continuous capillary channels in flexible heat pipe with high durability
Abstract: Flexible heat pipes suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between heat transfer performance and bending durability. Although thinning the flexible section can effectively reduce bending stress and improve durability, it generally compromises capillary-driven liquid transport across the wick, thereby limiting heat transfer performance. To overcome this conflict, this study proposes laser etching of flattened copper mesh for constructing continuous capillary channels in ultrathin flexible heat pipes. Ultrafast laser processing was used to generate continuous capillary channels on the surface of flattened copper mesh, and a liquid transport model was established based on three-dimensional surface topography to clarify the relationship between laser-induced morphology and capillary behavior. The results show that flattening a 200-mesh copper mesh reduced its thickness by 50% and increased wire width by 56%, creating favorable conditions for continuous channel fabrication. By regulating laser parameters, continuous V-shaped capillary channels with a depth of 35 μm and a width of 30 μm were achieved, exhibiting strong capillary pumping capability with a maximum wicking coefficient of 17.94 mm/s0.5. When applied in a flexible heat pipe, the etched flattened copper mesh enabled an ultrathin flexible section of 261 μm and a low thermal resistance of 0.84 °C/W at 5 W. A bending test platform was further developed to quantitatively evaluate durability degradation during cyclic deformation. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Masson SAS.

Authors: Zhang G.; Cui X.; Liu H.; Wang Y.; Zhao S.
Title: ResGAT: A residual graph attention network for technology transfer prediction in Chinese universities
Abstract: University patent transfer in China remains sparse, and only a small fraction of university patents are licensed or assigned. Technology-transfer offices must still judge which patents are worth promoting and which enterprises are plausible recipients. Existing matching methods rely on content similarity, collaborative filtering, or shallow heterogeneous graphs. They rarely model patent–patent, patent–entity, and entity–entity relations together with patent attributes when positive transfer labels are extremely scarce. This study proposes a residual graph attention network (ResGAT) for technology-transfer object recognition. Built on three meta-paths, ResGAT uses relation-specific attention together with a shared feature transformation. It stacks residual graph-attention layers on the homogeneous branches to limit over-smoothing, and it uses a shallow cross-type branch to pass entity information to patents. A two-stage procedure then estimates transfer probability and ranks candidate transferees by dot-product similarity. On a civil-engineering patent graph from a Chinese university, and on seven strategic-emerging-industry subsets, ResGAT outperforms heuristic, linear, and multi-relational graph baselines under the same 10-fold protocol. The model also returns ranked enterprise lists for high-potential patents, so transfer offices receive a concrete shortlist rather than only a transfer score. © 2026

Title: Energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impact assessment of an ethyl acetate–diesel dual-fuel engine under different EGR rates
Abstract: This study experimentally investigates the energy, exergy, and direct engine-out emission impacts of ethyl acetate (EA)–diesel dual-fuel operation under exhaust gas recirculation (EGR). Tests were conducted on a single-cylinder direct-injection diesel engine at 1800 rpm and 25–100% loads. EA injection durations of 1, 2, and 3 ms and EGR rates of 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20% were investigated. Energy and exergy balances were established, and direct emission impact was calculated from CO, CO2, HC, and NOx mass-flow rates derived from the measured exhaust-gas concentrations and intake-air flow. At full load, EA(2 ms) + 20% EGR increased energy and exergy efficiencies by 39.1% and 38.4%, respectively, and reduced exergy destruction by 42.5% relative to diesel operation without EGR, representing the thermodynamically preferred condition. Title: Descriptive or injunctive? The interactive effects of influencer type and social norms on alternative protein purchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As alternative protein products attract increasing attention, understanding how social norm messages and influencer type jointly shape consumers’ purchase intention has become increasingly relevant. Drawing on schema congruity theory, this study conducted three scenario-based experiments with Chinese panel participants. The studies manipulated influencer type (human vs. virtual) and social norm framing (descriptive vs. injunctive), with regulatory-mode message priming introduced in Study 3. The results showed significant interactions between influencer type and norm framing. In Study 1, human influencers elicited higher purchase intention than virtual influencers under injunctive framing, whereas virtual influencers elicited higher purchase intention under descriptive framing. However, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention than injunctive framing within both influencer conditions. Study 2 provided evidence of moderated mediation through information processing fluency: the conditional indirect effect was significant for virtual influencers but not for human influencers. In Study 3, injunctive framing generated higher purchase intention than descriptive framing for human influencers under assessment-oriented priming, whereas this difference was not significant under locomotion-oriented priming. For virtual influencers, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention under both priming conditions. These findings extend research on influencer marketing and social norms by identifying how influencer type and norm framing interact, highlighting information processing fluency as a potential explanatory mechanism and regulatory-mode priming as a boundary condition. They also provide practical guidance for selecting influencers and designing social norm messages in alternative protein marketing. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Orgs G.
Title: The neuroaesthetics of liveness
Abstract: Live theatre, dance and music pervade to human culture. Building on a rich theoretical debate within theatre, performance and media studies, this review sketches out a psychological approach to understanding live experiences. It distinguishes physical liveness (presence in a here and now) from social liveness (sharing experiences with others). Recent mobile EEG studies on live dance performances and music concerts demonstrate that audience engagement during live performances is measurable as dynamic brain synchrony between co-present audience members or between audience members, music and movement. Differences in audience engagement between live and recorded performances (physical liveness) are measurable as looser or tighter slow wave neural synchrony. Conversely, social liveness can increase audience arousal, indexed by reduced power in the EEG alpha band during collective viewing of both live and recorded dance. These findings suggest that variable performance content and stable performance context engage dissociable neural mechanisms, attention and arousal respectively. Research on liveness originates in the performing arts but can be extended to the visual arts and to sport events. Physical and social liveness may facilitate those rare, memorable and transformative aesthetic experiences that are difficult to produce in lab-based environments. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Tuberculosis Patients’ Preferences for Improving Tuberculosis Care in Chitwan District, Nepal: A Discrete Choice Experiment
Abstract: Objectives Patient-preferred tuberculosis (TB) care is integral for the patient-centric approach to TB care delivery. This study aimed to ascertain the aspects of TB care that people with TB value most, to inform improvements in TB care in Chitwan District, Nepal. Methods A discrete choice experiment (DCE) survey was developed to elicit the care preferences of TB patients in Chitwan District. The DCE included 6 attributes (patient card, sex of healthcare worker, transport incentive, provision of psychosocial support, waiting time, and type of TB care provider), which were developed through literature review, expert consultations, and patient interviews. Participants were randomly selected from the TB care centers and interviewed face-to-face to complete the survey. Six choice sets were presented to each participant and asked to choose preferred option from 2 hypothetical TB care models labeled as TB Care A and TB Care B. A conditional logit regression model was used to quantify the preference of TB patients. Results Among 133 patients who participated in DCE (97% response rate, mean age of 47 years, 71% male), 83% had pulmonary bacteriologically confirmed TB, and 32% were in the intensive phase of treatment. Patients highly valued TB care services that have the provision of psychosocial support (β = 0.62, P < .001), followed by improved patient card (β = 0.50, P < .001), and the waiting time for TB care within half an hour (β = 0.25, P = .002). Conclusions People with TB preferred to be supported by psychosocial interventions, improved patient card, and reduced waiting time in current TB treatment strategy. This study provides evidence for current/future TB control program package to align with the patient’s preferences. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Meaning in the age of AI: Experiencing less, needing more
Abstract: What does it mean to be human when artificial intelligence (AI) can simulate human thought and creative labor with increasing fidelity? Unlike AI, humans experience meaning in life. Yet AI may create a paradox for meaningfulness. AI may reduce people's ability to experience meaning by disrupting selfhood (loss of effort and self-efficacy), social relationships (reduced mattering and connection), and culture (erosion of value and stability). At the same time, it may heighten people's need for meaning by challenging human exceptionalism and increasing the need for coherence amidst upheaval. This paradox—experiencing less while needing more—is what we term the AI Meaning Gap. Yet meaninglessness is not inevitable. If developed and used intentionally, AI could become a tool for reflection, understanding, and self-growth, thereby enhancing meaning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Experimental Study on Smart Sloped Rolling-Type Bearings Integrated with Early Prediction of Peak Velocity
Source title: International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics
Abstract: The use of sloped rolling-type bearings (SRBs) to protect critical equipment from seismic damage has been widely adopted. However, maintaining SRB displacement responses within safe limits often requires a large damping force, which results in unacceptable accelerations. This highlights the trade-off in seismic isolation: reducing displacement typically comes at the cost of increased acceleration, and vice versa. Although previous numerical studies have shown that adjusting the SRB damping force based on peak velocity (PV) predictions from an earthquake early warning (EEW) system enables better control over acceleration and displacement responses, experimental validation is necessary. This study employs magnetorheological (MR) dampers to apply the damping force determined by the predicted PV. Performance tests are conducted to characterize the physical properties of the MR dampers and develop their mathematical representation. Numerical simulations incorporating the MR damper and SRB models under seismic conditions are used to establish a control law that correlates PV with the voltage required by the MR dampers. To predict PV, the first few seconds following primary seismic wave (P-wave) detection undergo a multi-scale short-term Fourier transform (STFT) to generate a spectrogram. After feature enhancement, it is fed into a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model, which predicts the impending earthquake’s PV. This prediction, alongside the established control law, enables rapid adjustment of the SRB damping force shortly after P-wave detection. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated through shake table testing. Results indicate that the approach significantly mitigates isolation displacement responses under major earthquakes, demonstrating its potential for improving seismic isolation performance. 2026 © The Author(s)

Title: Synthesis, physicochemical characterization, and alkyd-enamel performance of cobalt phthalocyanine pigment
Abstract: Cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc)-containing pigment was prepared by heating phthalic anhydride, urea, and cobalt(II) chloride with boric acid and magnesium acetate tetrahydrate at 200 °C for 2 h and evaluated in PF-115 alkyd enamel. A 40.000 g portion of the crude product yielded 16.400 g of dry pigment-containing material after acid treatment, neutralization, washing, and drying (41.0% purification mass recovery); the chemical yield and purity of CoPc were not established. Powder X-ray diffraction showed changes after acid treatment but did not permit an unambiguous α/β polymorph assignment. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) bands supported a phthalocyanine-related framework, whereas absorptions at 1772 and 1722 cm−1 indicated possible residual carbonyl-containing compounds. Ultraviolet–visible absorption of a sample prepared in dimethyl sulfoxide showed features in the 600–700 nm region. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) showed an unresolved signal near 337.9 mT (effective g = 1.9996) without uniquely identifying its origin; scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy provided local, semi-quantitative elemental information. Enamels containing 4.5 wt% pigment matched the reported first-grade GOST 6465-76 numerical limits, with gloss values of 54% and 50% and hiding-power values of 60 and 40 g m−2 for light-blue and blue coatings, respectively. Title: STGCM: Sign-aware triple graph collaborative model for recommendation
Abstract: Recommendation systems, as a core technology for mitigating information overload, play a crucial role across many fields. In recent years, graph neural networks (GNNs) have significantly improved recommendation performance by modeling user-item interactions as a graph structure. However, most existing sign-aware methods directly partition the user-item interaction graph into separate positive and negative graphs for modeling. While this local modeling approach can distinguish different feedback types, it disrupts the global topology of the original graph. This impairment exacerbates data sparsity and weakens the propagation of signed information. To address this, we propose STGCM, a Sign-aware Triple Graph Collaborative Model for Recommendation. STGCM employs a multi-perspective graph convolution embedding learning framework, which preserves the complete topology of the original graph while thoroughly excavating local preference features from both positive and negative feedback. Building on this, a two-stage hierarchical attention fusion mechanism is designed to achieve a global-information-supplemented, synergistic fusion of multiple perspectives, thereby enhancing the model's information complementarity capability. The experimental results provide compelling evidence that STGCM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across three real-world datasets. Title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Anamorelin and Olanzapine for Cancer Cachexia in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients in Japan
Abstract: Objectives Cancer cachexia significantly impacts quality of life and prognosis in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Anamorelin and olanzapine have demonstrated efficacy in improving appetite and body weight in clinical trials. However, their cost-effectiveness within the Japanese healthcare system is unclear. This study assesses the cost-effectiveness of anamorelin and olanzapine for cancer cachexia in patients with non-small cell lung cancer from the perspective of Japanese healthcare payers. Methods A Markov model with 7 health states was developed using clinical trial data (ONO-7643-04 for anamorelin and OlAnCa for olanzapine) and real-world cost and survival data from the Japan Medical Data Center claims database. The time horizon was 60 months, with 4-week cycles (65 cycles). Costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were discounted at an annual rate of 2%. One-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted using 1000 Monte Carlo simulations. Results The incremental cost-effectiveness ratios were 7 405 419 Japanese yen (JPY)/QALY for anamorelin and 6 737 715 JPY/QALY for olanzapine compared with placebo. Both exceeded the willingness-to-pay threshold of 5 million JPY/QALY. At the 7.5 million JPY/QALY threshold, cost-effectiveness probabilities were 63.7% for anamorelin and 93.2% for olanzapine. One-way sensitivity analysis identified utility values and healthcare costs as the most influential parameters. Conclusions Both anamorelin and olanzapine exceeded conventional cost-effectiveness thresholds in Japan. Given the limitations of pharmacotherapy in improving physical function, multimodal cachexia management incorporating nutritional counselling, exercise therapy, and rehabilitation warrants consideration. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Fear of missing out, entertainment, and social presence: A stimulus-organism-response model of impulse buying in Chinese live-stream commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines the drivers of impulse buying behavior in China's rapidly expanding live-stream e-commerce environment. Building on a Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, it investigates how key live-stream features — including entertainment value, host interactivity, perceived scarcity of product offers, and social presence — influence consumers’ internal reactions (emotional arousal and fear of missing out) and ultimately their impulse purchase intentions. Survey data were collected from a representative sample of 580 Chinese consumers with recent live-stream shopping experience. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the results show that entertainment and scarcity stimuli significantly increase arousal and FOMO, both of which in turn are associated with higher impulse purchase intention, while social presence relates directly to impulsive buying. Multi-group analyses indicate significant demographic differences in some pathways. The fsQCA reveals distinct configurations of conditions associated with high impulse purchase intention, highlighting the crucial roles of scarcity cues and community engagement. The findings offer new theoretical insights into digital retailing and practical guidance for designing engaging live-stream shopping experiences that balance consumer excitement with brand objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Use of Social Network Analysis for community-led area-based fisheries management: The case of tropical lobster fisheries
Abstract: Co-management is essential for successful community-based fishery reserves such as Mexico’s Fishing Refuge Zones (FRZs), but they can be hindered by gaps in institutional capacity that undermine collaborative governance. This study analyzes the governance networks underpinning FRZs in Punta Allen and Maria Elena, two small-scale fishing communities within the Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve, Mexican Caribbean. Using a social-ecological system lens and social network analysis, we analyzed the structure, cohesion, and resilience of the governance networks of both communities, using semi-structured interviews and a weighted interaction index that integrates communication frequency and quality, trust, and collaboration. Results show structural differences between governance networks. Punta Allen exhibits a more decentralized, cohesive, and diversified network that links community actors, civil society organizations (CSOs), and government agencies, fostering multiple pathways for collaboration. María Elena presents a more centralized and segmented configuration, with strong dependence on CSOs and limited integration of governmental actors. Resilience simulations further demonstrate that decentralized structures maintain coordination under disturbance more effectively than centralized ones. Although FRZs are formally established by federal authorities, their local-level operational governance is sustained by informal social relationships that enable trust, reciprocity, and local coordination. Our findings show that FRZs can function as effective co-management instruments within MPAs, but their long-term viability requires strengthening institutional coordination, diversifying actor participation, and ensuring consistent governmental presence to reduce fragmentation. By diagnosing governance gaps and highlighting structural strengths, this study provides a transferable framework for improving the design, implementation, and policy uptake of community-based conservation and small-scale fisheries management initiatives. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: When ads look worth keeping: Screenshotable design increases ad saving and Facebook ad liking
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media advertising increasingly competes in fast-scrolling feed environments, an important but understudied question is whether some ads succeed by functioning less as transient persuasive messages and more as saveable information objects. Drawing on affordance theory and uses and gratifications reasoning, this research examines whether screenshotable ad design increases preservation-oriented engagement by making ads seem useful for later use. Across five studies, including controlled online experiments and a naturalistic simulated-feed experiment, screenshotable ads were associated with higher ad saving intention and Facebook ad liking relative to non-screenshotable ads. The results are consistent with perceived future utility as a mediating mechanism: screenshotable design increased perceived future utility, which in turn was associated with higher saving-related responses and Facebook ad liking intention. The process was stronger when consumers anticipated a future rather than immediate need, such that perceived future utility translated more strongly into ad saving and liking under future-need conditions. In addition, screenshotable design more strongly increased perceived future utility when information density was high rather than low, indicating that saveable structure is most effective when the ad contains enough substantive content to justify preservation. The findings contribute to consumer research on digital advertising response by identifying screenshotable ad design as a distinct visual structure that can shape consumers’ interpretation of an ad as a later-use resource, and they offer guidance for managers designing social media ads intended to be kept, revisited, and positively engaged with over time. © 2026

Title: The benefits of reading narrative fiction
Abstract: The benefits of reading are well-known and have been well-established by research. But does it matter what we read? Are there unique benefits to reading narrative fiction: stories about people, their goals, challenges, emotions, and interactions? Focusing on research published in the past few years, we review the empirical evidence of the benefits associated with reading fiction. This includes a wide range of domains, including language abilities, our ability to understand others, early social development, intergroup prejudice, meaning in life, cognition, longevity, and well-being. Title: A long-term time series prediction model based on dynamic-order polynomial fuzzy information granules
Abstract: Navigating the big data landscape, information fusion and data mining have become essential tools for extracting meaningful insights from complex datasets, particularly in the domain of time series prediction, which is crucial for fields such as finance, power systems, and environmental studies. Traditional methods often fall short due to poor interpretability, high computational costs, and an inability to capture complex patterns. Fuzzy information granule (FIG) has emerged as a solution, but current FIGs, especially Gaussian polynomial fuzzy information granules (GPFIGs), still face challenges in accurately representing data and adapting to varying trends. To address these limitations, a novel long-term time series prediction model based on dynamic-order GPFIGs is proposed. This model combines a Savitzky-Golay filter and autocorrelation function (ACF) for time series segmentation, effectively filtering noise and identifying periodicity. Subsequently, during the construction of GPFIGs, this study proposes an FMDL polynomial order selection criterion inspired by the trade-off principle of MDL. The proposed criterion employs nonparametric entropy based on the empirical distribution of residuals to measure the fitting uncertainty and introduces a parameter-number-based penalty to quantify model complexity, thereby adaptively selecting an appropriate polynomial order for different information granules. Hierarchical clustering is integrated into the fuzzy inference system (FIS) to reduce the impact of redundant rules and improve prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on eight datasets demonstrate the model’s superior performance, achieving lower RMSE, MAE, and SMAPE compared to advanced models. For example, on the chaotic time series dataset, the model attains an RMSE of 0.0286, MAE of 0.0224, and SMAPE of 2.72% for a prediction length of 500. These results validate the model’s effectiveness and robustness in long-term time series prediction. Title: Effect of source azimuth on the perceived annoyance of domestic sounds
Abstract: Although noise-induced annoyance has been extensively studied, the influence of spatial factors on annoyance perception remains underexplored. A listening experiment was conducted to assess the effect of sound source azimuth on perceived annoyance, for a variety of common domestic sounds. 54 participants graded the perceived annoyance caused by seven sound sources presented binaurally, situated at 45∘ azimuth intervals around the listener. The results indicated that in most cases, laterally placed sources caused the highest level of annoyance, and rear sources were the least annoying. A significant effect of source azimuth was identified. However, the type of sound source and acoustic condition also affected annoyance levels. Conventional psychoacoustic annoyance (PA) models are computed using omnidirectional audio signals, so although they may accurately predict the effect of sound source, they cannot account for the effect of azimuth. As a result, a binaural PA metric is suggested demonstrating the potential to predict the effects of source azimuth and acoustic condition. Following further experimentation, these findings will inform the future development of an improved PA model, that considers the spatial features of annoyance, with applications in optimisation of room acoustics and annoyance reduction. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: On linkage-based metamaterials with inertial regulation: benefits of using asymmetry for superior low-frequency broadband vibration suppression
Abstract: Lightweight and compact structures in aerospace, automotive, and precision instrumentation are increasingly demanding vibration suppression solutions that are effective at low frequencies and over broad frequency range. However, conventional locally resonant metamaterials with symmetric linkage configurations for inertial regulation face a fundamental limitation: a persistent trade-off between achieving low-frequency vibration suppression and obtaining a wide broadband gap. To overcome this limitation, this study develops a generalized theoretical linkage-based metamaterial model for inertial regulation and derives two new key inertial regulation factors, which are related to geometric parameters and mass distribution. The analysis first reveals the inherent constraints imposed by symmetric models on these two factors, which restrict their bandgap tunability. Then, an asymmetric inertial regulation model is proposed. Remarkably, this asymmetric model not only achieves an ultra-wide bandgap approaching a relative width of 2, but more importantly, resolves the trade-off between low-frequency suppression and broadband width, exhibiting a resonant bandgap that is 1000 times wider than that of the symmetric model at lower frequencies. Furthermore, an innovative nested linkage mechanism is introduced, which significantly enhances the bandgap control capability of the asymmetric model under strict spatial constraints, a feature from which the symmetric model derives only limited benefit. Collectively, this study demonstrates the multiple advantages of asymmetric inertial regulation: it establishes a new design paradigm beyond traditional symmetry-based approaches, delivers superior performance compared to its symmetric counterparts, and offers a promising non-intuitive strategy for wide and low-frequency vibration suppression in engineering applications where lightweight and spatial compactness are essential. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Corporate environmental credit rating and social stability: Evidence from capital-labor conflicts in China's polluting industries
Abstract: Mitigating capital-labor conflicts is essential for maintaining social stability. Using China's Enterprise Environmental Credit Evaluation System (EECES) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the impact of corporate environmental credit rating on capital-labor conflicts. The results indicate that EECES reduces capital-labor conflicts in polluting industries by approximately 17.63%, although its effect weakens over time. Channel tests show that EECES mitigates capital-labor conflicts by reducing workers' pollution exposure risk, improving corporate environmental information transparency, and enhancing social trust in corporations. Moreover, in cities with weaker social governance capacity, EECES exerts a stronger restraining effect on capital-labor conflicts, suggesting that it effectively compensates for deficiencies in social governance. Further analysis reveals that although EECES reduces industrial output, it significantly promotes economic transformation. Authors: Wei M.; Zheng G.; Xia B.; Zhou H.; Ding L.; Du Y.
Title: A comparative investigation of physics-driven machine learning architectures for consolidation analysis
Abstract: Physics-driven machine learning has emerged as a powerful framework for forward and inverse modeling of partial differential equations (PDEs), with increasing applications in geotechnical engineering. However, the relative performance of different physics-driven learning strategies remains problem-dependent, and their suitability for typical geotechnical problems has not been systematically established. This study systematically compares four physics-driven machine learning paradigms for consolidation analysis by combining Multi‑Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) with physics-informed neural networks (PINN) and the discrete-time deep energy method (DTDEM). The paradigms are evaluated for forward and inverse consolidation problems in one and three dimensions, with particular attention to convergence, computational cost, parameter inversion, accuracy, and robustness to noise. For forward problems governed by PDEs, although the energy-form DTDEM converges in fewer epochs than the strong-form PINN under both MLP and KAN architectures, its higher per-epoch cost results in a longer total wall-clock training time. A similar trade-off applies to KAN relative to MLP where the higher per-epoch cost can offset the benefit of faster convergence in terms of epochs. In terms of solution accuracy, replacing MLP with KAN improves both accuracy and training-loss convergence under the strong-form PINN framework, while under the DTDEM framework this advantage is not consistent. For parameter inversion, the DTDEM-based energy formulation is ineffective for parameter inversion because treating material parameters as additional optimization variables make the functional unbounded from below, resulting in divergent training. In contrast, within the strong-form framework, KAN substantially improves parameter-inversion accuracy and robustness to noisy data compared with MLPs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: UHPLC-HRMS-based untargeted lipidomics for differentiating halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages
Abstract: The integrity of the halal food supply chain is continually challenged by fraudulent adulteration, particularly in processed meat products where visual identification of ingredients is impossible. This study used untargeted lipidomics based on ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-HRMS) combined with chemometric analysis to differentiate halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages. Five sausage formulations were prepared: 100% beef, 100% pork, 100% dog meat, and 50:50 mixtures of beef–pork and beef–dog meat. Lipid profiles were acquired in both positive (ESI+) and negative (ESI−) ionization modes. Principal component analysis (PCA) clearly separated the five sausage formulations, indicating distinct lipidomic profiles. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) further differentiated the sample groups and identified several putative lipid biomarkers based on variable importance in projection (VIP) scores. Among these, PG(16:0/18:2) and PE(6:0/14:1) + H detected in pork samples were consistent with previous reports and may serve as candidate biomarkers for halal authentication, while PC(18:0p/17:1) + H and PC(13:0/21:2) + H were identified as putative lipid biomarkers characteristic of dog meat sausages. These findings highlight the potential of UHPLC-HRMS-based untargeted lipidomics for differentiating halal and non-halal meat species in processed sausages. However, the proposed biomarkers require further validation by targeted MS/MS analysis and independent sample sets before broader application. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Subsample averaging for non-periodic microstructures: Bias reduction, dispersion increase, and practical trade-offs in computational micromechanics
Abstract: The computation of effective properties of random microstructured materials via representative volume elements (RVE) is affected by both bias and dispersion. For non-periodic microstructures (snapshots), which naturally arise in experiments and imaging-based studies, the bias decays slowly, rendering standard homogenization approaches inaccurate, significantly biased, and therefore unreliable. Recent theoretical results suggest that subsample averaging – evaluating the apparent properties only on a strictly interior subdomain – can significantly reduce the bias. In this work, we investigate the practical performance of subsample averaging for linear elastic particle-reinforced composites using large-scale numerical experiments and FFT-based computational micromechanics. We first demonstrate that subsample averaging must respect the Hill–Mandel condition to improve the convergence behavior of the bias, i.e., both stress and strain fields must be subsample averaged. In particular, the naive approach of subsample averaging the apparent stress alone may reduce the magnitude of the bias, but does not improve its convergence rate. When applied consistently, subsample averaging reduces the magnitude of the bias and produces a more favorable decay trend for the investigated non-periodic microstructures. However, this bias reduction comes at the cost of an increased dispersion due to the reduced sampling domain, resulting in only marginal improvements of the total error when used in isolation. To overcome this limitation, we combine subsample averaging with variance reduction via optimized volume fraction (OVF), which significantly improves overall accuracy and reliability for matrix-inclusion composites. The presented strategy is straightforward to implement and can be readily applied within existing computational frameworks without modifying the underlying solver. These results reveal a fundamental bias–dispersion trade-off associated with subsample averaging and provide practical guidance for computing the effective properties from non-periodic microstructure samples, including samples obtained experimentally. © 2026

Authors: He X.; Choi Y.; Su Y.; Fan D.; Cui L.; Lei J.
Title: Beyond the accession event: Joint regional membership duration and completion of cross-border acquisitions
Abstract: Cross-border acquisition (CBA) completion is often hindered by institutional barriers, imposing substantial costs on deal participants. While regional integration aims to reduce such barriers, prior research predominantly treats regional integration as a discrete accession event, leaving post-accession adaptation dynamics and their underlying mechanisms underexplored. Drawing on new institutional economics and social learning theory, we argue that joint regional membership duration increases CBA completion likelihood, with country-dyadic M&A stock serving as the mediating carrier via the sequential pathways of institutional alignment and social learning. We further examine how initial regulatory distance and cultural distance condition this mechanism. Using a sample of 8009 announced CBAs across the European Union (2010–2022), we find support for the mediation pathway and show that both regulatory and cultural distance weaken this indirect effect. This study advances the literature by moving beyond discrete event-based integration framing and refines the understanding of cross-national distance within integrated regional blocs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
Abstract: Hierarchical text embedding models offer variable-length representations, while quantization reduces numerical precision; both aim to improve computational efficiency. This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact. We evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) using four transformer-based embedding models, covering 1D and 2D hierarchical representations combined with 32-bit, 8-bit, and binary quantization, for 168 configurations per task. We report each efficiency dimension separately: theoretical per-vector storage and end-to-end evaluation time. Under a Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis, int8 quantization is statistically indistinguishable from float32 for pair classification and re-ranking and costs at most 1.5 percentage points overall, whereas binary quantization is significantly worse across every task category. Halving the embedding dimension once is not statistically detectable above m=16; two successive halvings always are. Combining an 8× dimensionality reduction with int8 yields a 32× reduction in per-vector storage at 94.4% of baseline effectiveness. Because evaluation times were measured once, we treat them as indicative: we find no evidence that quantization speeds up evaluation, whereas sampling from intermediate layers shortens it substantially. Retrieval degrades far faster than every other category, so we report findings per task category. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Chen M.; Li R.; Hu T.; Dong J.
Title: Community participation intensity on asynchronous biodiversity and human well-being responses to ecological restoration in global drylands
Abstract: Ecological restoration serves as a key strategy for addressing desertification and ecosystem degradation in global drylands. However, achieving synergistic benefits for both biodiversity and human well-being remains a significant challenge for sustainability. Although community participation is increasingly promoted, quantitative evidence remains limited on how participation intensity is associated with measured ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. A dataset encompassing 744 effect sizes from 41 independent studies across global drylands was constructed to conduct a meta-analysis. The synthesis indicated positive benefits relative to degraded baselines, while composite biodiversity and composite human well-being showed asynchronous responses across community participation intensity. For composite biodiversity, the pooled mean estimate corresponded to an average increase of 122.11% relative to degraded baselines. Limited community participation was associated with long-term positive patterns in the composite biodiversity (159.35%) and composite human well-being (130.71%), whereas extensive community participation showed an evidence-limited and marginally supported positive tendency in composite human well-being in the short term. Eventually, we propose an adaptive framework in which livelihood-support components may be emphasized during early restoration, followed by lower-disturbance stewardship considerations as biodiversity recovery stabilizes. Overall, our findings provide exploratory quantitative evidence for discussing how community participation may affect asynchronous ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Mapping the evolution of communication research in aquatic conservation: A systematic literature review of emerging patterns and research opportunities (2015–2025)
Abstract: This review examines the development of communication research in aquatic conservation through a systematic literature review. Although communication is increasingly recognized as crucial for environmental governance, promoting aquatic conservation remains underexplored and often treated instrumentally. Using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, this review analyzed eleven articles (n = 11) published between 2015 and 2025, drawn from Scopus and Web of Science databases. Findings indicate that existing studies are predominantly presented in the Global North and tend to emphasize media representation, message framing, and individual behavioral change. These patterns suggest that communication is often conceptualized as a tool for disseminating information rather than as a broader social process. Most of the research described is qualitative, further strengthening the exploratory nature of the evidence. This review identifies limited engagement with systemic perspectives in understanding how communication shapes environmental responses. To address this, this study introduces Niklas Luhmann's social systems theory as an analytical lens for reinterpreting communication in aquatic conservation. From this perspective, communication is understood as a process of systemic resonance in which environmental issues are selectively interpreted across different social systems. This study contributes to the field by providing an exploratory synthesis of existing research and highlighting the need for more methodologically robust, geographically diverse, and theoretically grounded studies. The findings also underscore the importance of shifting from instrumental approaches to a more systemic understanding of environmental communication. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Maternal diet and offspring ASD and ADHD: A critical narrative review of dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures
Abstract: Maternal diet may influence fetal neurodevelopment through nutrient availability, placental function, and maternal–fetal metabolite signaling. This critical narrative review used a structured, purposive search to organize human evidence on prenatal dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures according to outcome directness: diagnosed autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), related dimensional traits, and general neurodevelopment. Whole-diet studies provide the most direct human evidence, but diagnostic findings are cohort-dependent and vulnerable to residual familial and genetic confounding. Choline trials and cohorts mainly address attention-related traits or general cognition; they do not establish prevention of diagnosed ASD or ADHD. Polyphenol evidence is limited to food proxies and one trimester-specific cohort of estimated intake, without diagnostic or biomarker-based studies. Preclinical data support biological plausibility—particularly for choline in BTBR, maternal immune-activation/CHRNA7, and Ts65Dn models and for resveratrol in valproate-exposed rodents—but remain model-specific. The evidence is therefore best treated as an organizing framework rather than a confirmed causal hypothesis. Clinical translation should prioritize achieving recommended dietary adequacy and balanced dietary patterns; evidence does not support high-dose single-nutrient or concentrated-polyphenol supplementation for ASD/ADHD prevention. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
