Title: Resurgence of large-scale influenza A (H1N1) outbreaks: Modeling the interplay of transmission, loss of immunity, and vaccination
Abstract: Influenza is a highly transmissible respiratory virus that can cause devastating pandemics. The 2009 influenza pandemic, caused by a strain of A(H1N1) virus, resulted in millions of cases and hundreds of thousands of deaths worldwide. In the following years, many regions experienced waves driven by environmental conditions, waning immunity, and other factors. More dramatically, several locations saw unpredicted large resurgent outbreaks, yet the mechanisms behind these severe resurgences remain poorly understood. Despite an extensive literature of epidemic models aimed at explaining and predicting H1N1 dynamics, mathematical frameworks specifically designed to address why these large outbreaks recur years after an initial epidemic are still lacking. Here we address this gap by proposing a mechanistic model with time-varying rates of infection, loss of immunity, and vaccination. In particular, we explore two mathematical functions to model dynamic loss of immunity, capturing how viral evolution may reduce the duration of immune protection. Numerical simulations show that the model reproduces key features of H1N1 case data, and that delayed resurgence is associated with longer immunity periods and higher vaccine efficacy. We also fit the model to data from Brazil, Turkey, Iran, New Zealand, the United States, Colombia, South Africa, and Croatia, demonstrating its ability to capture resurgence patterns. Fitted infection rates exhibited a wide range of temporal profiles, from regular annual cycles to higher-frequency oscillations and gradual changes, suggesting that transmission is driven by factors beyond seasonal influences. The model also inferred dynamic loss-of-immunity rates, representing different effects of antigenic drift. To our knowledge, this is the first mechanistic modeling study specifically aimed at investigating large resurgent H1N1 epidemics across multiple locations. Our findings highlight the need for context-specific models and surveillance systems that account for the complex interplay among environmental drivers, population immunity, and viral mutation driving H1N1 dynamics. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Extracts of Coriaria nepalensis ameliorate MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behaviors via regulation of neurotransmitter imbalance and neuroinflammation
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Coriaria nepalensis Wall. is a traditional ethnomedicine used by the Dong ethnic group in Guizhou Province, China, for the treatment of schizophrenia. However, its pharmacological effects and the bioactive constituents responsible for its therapeutic efficacy remain largely unknown. Aim of the study: To evaluate the anti-schizophrenic effects of C. nepalensis extracts and investigate their underlying mechanisms and potential bioactive constituents. Materials and methods: An MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like Sprague–Dawley rat model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects in the blank control group, model group, positive drug group, and different dose groups of C. nepalensis extracts (EA-H, EA-M, EA-L, SJ-H, SJ-M, and SJ-L). Schizophrenia-like behaviors were assessed using the open-field, Y-maze, three-chamber social interaction, and prepulse inhibition (PPI) tests. Neurotransmitter levels in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex were determined by LC-MS, inflammatory cytokines were quantified by ELISA, and the expression of signaling pathway-related proteins and glutamate decarboxylase 67 (GAD67) was analyzed by Western blotting. Plasma-absorbed constituents of the active extract were characterized using HPLC-MS/MS. Results: C. nepalensis extracts alleviated MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities to different extents, including altered locomotor activity, impaired spatial working memory, and social deficits. Among all treatments, the low-dose ethanol extract (EA-L) produced the most pronounced effects. EA-L significantly improved sensorimotor gating deficits in the PPI test and showed a stronger ameliorative than risperidone under the present experimental conditions. Mechanistically, EA-L restored neurotransmitter homeostasis in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, attenuated neuroinflammatory responses, regulated the abnormal activation of inflammation-related signaling pathways, and normalized GAD67 expression. These changes were associated with improvements in schizophrenia-like negative symptoms, cognitive deficits, and sensorimotor gating impairment. Chemical profiling identified 251 constituents in the ethanol extract, of which 57 were detected in rat serum after oral administration, suggesting that these absorbed compounds may contribute to the observed pharmacological activity. Conclusion: Extracts of C. nepalensis, particularly EA-L, ameliorated MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities by restoring neurotransmitter homeostasis and suppressing the aberrant activation of neuroinflammation-related signaling pathways. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Multimodal fusion for precision livestock behavior monitoring: A systematic review of deep learning, pose estimation, and sensor integration strategies
Abstract: Animal behavior analysis is a cornerstone of precision livestock farming, providing non-invasive insights into health, welfare, and productivity through continuous behavioral monitoring. Traditional approaches, including manual observation, sensor-based systems, and rule-based modeling, are limited by labor intensity, observer subjectivity, and low temporal resolution. This systematic review (PRISMA 2020; 2020-2026 literature) presents a comprehensive synthesis of deep learning and multimodal artificial intelligence approaches for animal behavior recognition in precision agriculture. Deep learning architectures, including convolutional, recurrent, and transformer-based models, achieve reported accuracies of 85-99% across livestock species, with transformer-based models reaching a mean of 94.4% (95% CI: 91.96-96.76%). Critically, multimodal fusion systems demonstrate a mean accuracy gain of 10.3 percentage points over single-modality baselines in an exploratory analysis of four independent source-level comparisons (95% CI: 4.9-15.8%; paired t(3) = 6.01, p = 0.009, Cohen’s d = 3.01), with peak detection sensitivities exceeding 90% for health-critical conditions, including lameness and metabolic disorders. This review evaluates early, late, and hybrid fusion strategies; the role of pose estimation in fine-grained movement analysis (with 94-100% accuracy in lameness detection); and the contribution of wearable and environmental sensors to continuous monitoring. Explainable AI methods are assessed for their role in improving model transparency and stakeholder trust. Key challenges, including data scarcity, annotation heterogeneity, multimodal synchronization, and limited cross-domain generalization, are critically discussed, along with six directions for future research. This review uniquely positions adaptive multimodal fusion as the central paradigm for next-generation, deployable precision livestock behavior monitoring systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Expand or carve up? Evaluating market dynamics of premium airline entry with extended synthetic control methods: Evidence from STARLUX airlines
Abstract: This study examines the effects of STARLUX Airlines' entry as a newly established premium full-service carrier on Taiwan's international air transport market. Using the synthetic control method (SCM) and an extended SCM framework, the analysis evaluates changes in passenger demand following the airline's entry, encompassing both single and multiple treated units, including individual routes and interconnected markets. A conditional growth model was subsequently employed to distinguish market expansion from demand redistribution. Results indicate that although only 9 out of 24 treated markets showed statistically significant expansion, STARLUX's entry still revealed latent demand and contributed meaningfully to overall market growth despite the relatively small size of STARLUX as compared to its primary competitors, China Airlines and EVA Airways. This effect was particularly evident in business-oriented and transfer-focused segments, while some tourism-driven and politically sensitive markets saw limited or negative responses. This study contributes to the literature by highlighting the demand-side influence of premium airline entry, extending SCM to multi-unit and network-based applications, and providing a replicable framework for evaluating airline market interventions in liberalized environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: DRNet: Parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for color image steganalysis
Abstract: Image steganalysis is a hot topic in the field of information security, and researchers have recently proposed a series of methods. However, existing color image steganalysis methods tend to extract features indiscriminately from different channels and regions, which fails to focus on steganographically relevant channels and texture-rich areas where stego signals are concentrated. In addition, most methods lack effective mechanisms to aggregate and amplify steganographic information across the three color channels, leaving weak stego signals dispersed and undetected. To address these issues, we propose a parallel two-branch network with fusion-enhancement and channel-pixel attention for universal color image steganalysis. In the main branch, we design a stego signal fusion-enhancement block that performs multi-channel information fusion and first introduces detail-enhanced convolution to amplify weak stego signals. In the auxiliary branch, we design a channel-pixel attention mechanism that jointly performs attention across channel and pixel dimensions, enabling precise localization of steganographic regions via multiplication-based fusion with main branch features. Experiments on the Alaska II dataset demonstrate that the proposed network achieves superior detection accuracy and generalization over state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component, and visualizations confirm that the channel-pixel attention mechanism effectively guides the model to focus on steganographic regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Mobile internet connectivity and climate change literacy in Africa
Abstract: Addressing climate change requires individual behavioral shifts and a deep understanding of its impacts, yet the role of information and communication technologies (ICT), a powerful driver of social movements and cultural shifts, in shaping climate change literacy remains underexplored. This study addresses a critical gap by exploring how ICT, particularly mobile Internet connectivity, influences climate change literacy in Africa. I provide the first systematic evidence on the impact of mobile Internet connectivity on climate change literacy by exploiting variations in peer-based Internet connectivity in an instrumental variable strategy. Using newly georeferenced individual-level data on climate change literacy from over 42,000 respondents across 31 African countries, I show that mobile Internet connectivity has a modest yet robust effect on climate literacy, raising it by approximately 0.57 points for a typical adopter. Heterogeneity analysis shows that mobile Internet access primarily enhances the knowledge-based dimensions of climate literacy, particularly climate awareness and understanding, while also improving risk perceptions to a lesser extent. This suggests that mobile Internet contributes to climate literacy mainly by expanding access to factual information and knowledge about climate change. Title: HCl emission prediction in municipal solid waste incineration using a Transformer–XGBoost hybrid model with deep feature extraction and SHAP-based interpretation
Abstract: Accurate prediction of hydrogen chloride (HCl) emissions plays an important role in efficient control of deacidification systems in municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) plants. However, accurate prediction remains challenging due to the dynamic nonlinearity, multivariable coupling and time series characteristics of MSWI process. This study proposes a Transformer–XGBoost hybrid model to predict HCl emissions in MSWI process. Firstly, a feature extractor based on Transformer model is designed to capture target-relevant temporal dependencies and complex interactions among process variables, extracting features and generating auxiliary prediction. Subsequently, a weighted feature fusion strategy is introduced to integrate the extracted features with auxiliary prediction result, thereby enhancing the representational capacity of features. Finally, the fused features are input into the XGBoost predictor to predict the HCl emissions at time t + 3. The proposed model is trained, validated, and tested using real industrial data from the MSWI plant. Additionally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis reveals model behavior and the importance of combustion air distribution and deacidification operating variables to HCl predictions. Comparative experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves optimal prediction performance, with an R2 of 0.974, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.388 mg/m3, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.262 mg/m3, and a symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) of 8.14 % on the testing set. These results indicate that the proposed method achieves accurate and robust HCl emission prediction in MSWI process, thereby providing critical data support for the precise, stable and cost-effective control of HCl emissions in MSWI plants. Title: A graph-based friend recommendation system in social networks using Q-Deep Learning Network
Abstract: The growth of social networks heavily depends on effective user connectivity. In such networks, users typically establish connections through cascading diffusion models. This allows them to expand both their friend circles and the overall reach and scalability of the network. However, due to the overwhelming number of users, identifying potential friends with similar interests and experiences can be challenging. To address this, friend recommendation systems aim to suggest similar users based on individual features and activities on social platforms. This task becomes even more difficult under the “cold start” condition, where no prior user information is available. Given the dynamic nature of social networks, user preferences are continuously changing. For this reason, using adaptive machine learning models is essential. Reinforcement learning, which adapts through interaction with the environment and user behavior, presents a promising solution for dynamic friend recommendation. In this paper, we propose a Graph-based Friend Recommendation system using a Q-Deep Learning Network (GFRQLN). Our method leverages standard social network datasets stored as adjacency matrices. It uses graph centrality metrics—degree, closeness, and betweenness—as input features. Each state in the proposed model includes a user and their immediate friend circle, while the action corresponds to adding a new user to this circle. The reward mechanism is based on modularity: if the modularity increases, a positive reward is given; otherwise, a penalty is applied. Experimental results demonstrate that GFRQLN outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, it shows improvements in accuracy and precision of approximately 12 % and 24 % on the Facebook dataset, 10 % and 13 % on DBLP, 11 % and 10 % on IMDB, and 20 % and 17 % on Yelp. Additionally, our model achieves significant reductions in MAE and RMSE, with improvements of about 43 % and 48 % on the Ciao dataset, and 35 % and 28 % on the Epinions dataset, respectively. © 2026

Title: A Malatya Centrality-based algorithm for optimal solutions to maximum independent set and minimum vertex cover problems in lattice graphs
Abstract: A lattice graph constitutes a fundamental graph type utilized across various domains and for addressing distinct challenges. The literature acknowledges a plethora of lattice graphs, each characterized by unique structures and attributes. Among the problems defined on lattice graphs are the Maximum Independent Set Problem (MISP) and the Minimum Vertex-Cover Problem (MVCP). MISP entails identifying the largest set of vertices in a graph that are not adjacent via edges. Conversely, MVCP involves determining the smallest set of vertices necessary to encompass all edges between nodes. Numerous methodologies have been suggested to resolve these issues within the context of lattice graphs. This research introduces an algorithm to address both MISP and MVCP on lattice graphs, leveraging the Malatya centrality algorithm. The algorithm calculates the centrality values of nodes within a lattice graph based on their degrees. Initially, it identifies the optimal solution set for MISP by employing the Malatya centrality values of the nodes. Subsequently, it ascertains the optimal solution set for MVCP based on the solution derived for MISP. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm was verified through its application to sample lattice graphs of varying sizes and configurations. It offers an efficient and robust solution in polynomial time across different lattice graph categories. Mathematical analysis and empirical studies on prevalent lattice graphs in the literature affirm that the algorithm yields optimal and effective resolutions for MISP and MVCP. Moreover, it generates solutions that are not contingent on constraints such as the number of iterations or initial conditions, and it produces effective outcomes in scenarios where integer linear programming methods fall short. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Fat body transcriptomic responses to dietary macronutrient balance and Metarhizium infection in the desert locust, Schistocerca gregaria
Source title: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology - Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
Abstract: Dietary macronutrient balance influences immunity and disease outcomes in most organisms, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. We investigated how dietary protein-to-carbohydrate ratio shapes the fat body transcriptomic response of an insect, the desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria), following infection with the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium robertsii. Our earlier research showed that a carbohydrate-biased diet extends better survival from infection. We hypothesized that this was due to enriched immune functions, potentially due to more readily accessible energy to support immune responses, and/or because the fungal growth was slowed due to reduced availability of protein or other nutrients. RNA sequencing of fat body tissue collected 96 h post-infection followed by differential expression analysis showed that infection elicited a core transcriptional response, whereas direct dietary effects remained limited. Infection substantially enriched all immune pathways (humoral, cellular, and recognition and signaling) regardless of diet. These results provide support against the hypothesis that differences in survival among dietary treatments are due to differences in host immune pathway activation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: A cross-disciplinary reflection on the role of Indonesian traditional fermented foods in strengthening sustainable science education
Abstract: Traditional fermentation practices in Indonesia embody biocultural knowledge by linking food production, microbial processes, ecological adaptation, and community traditions. Nevertheless, industrialization, urbanization, and diminished intergenerational knowledge transfer have increasingly marginalized these practices, resulting in the underutilization of their educational potential for sustainable science learning. This study argues that the deliberate incorporation of Indonesia’s traditional fermentation practices into sustainability-focused STEM education, guided by culturally responsive pedagogy, can directly foster scientific literacy, promote sustainability, and strengthen local cultural connections. Such integration addresses the underutilization of biocultural knowledge in fermentation and underscores its unique potential at the intersection of science and culture. A systematic narrative literature review was conducted utilizing Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Publications from 2000 to 2025 were included. Eligible sources comprised peer-reviewed articles or academic works addressing fermentation, science education, sustainability, and indigenous knowledge. Studies were analyzed using thematic content analysis and inductive-deductive coding. The review further assessed conceptual clarity, empirical rigor, contextual depth, and educational relevance. The findings indicate that traditional fermentation serves as a living laboratory, connecting microbiology, biochemistry, ecological knowledge, and sociocultural practice. Five themes emerged: indigenous ecological knowledge; microbiological and nutritional aspects; cultural transmission and identity; food security and sustainability; and STEM pedagogy integration. Although many studies provide strong cultural and conceptual insights, fewer offer robust empirical evidence regarding classroom implementation or measurable outcomes. This study presents a framework for incorporating traditional fermentation into science education. By prioritizing contextual, interdisciplinary, and community-based approaches, the framework demonstrates how local knowledge can enhance scientific literacy, sustainability, and cultural resilience. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Politeness negotiation in English refusals: Evidence from Javanese EFL learners and Native Speakers of English
Abstract: This study examines how politeness is negotiated in English refusal speech acts produced by Javanese Learners of English (JLEs) and Native Speakers of English (NSEs) across situations characterized by variations in power relations and social distance. Data were collected through a set of written discourse completion tasks (WDCTs) consisting of nine scenarios representing interpersonal, academic, and professional contexts. The study employs a comparative qualitative design, with refusal strategies identified using an established taxonomy and systematically coded using Atlas.ti. The results show that refusal is consistently realized as a sequence of pragmatic moves rather than a single illocutionary act. Among JLEs, the most frequent pattern is layered mitigation, characterized by the combination of apology, appreciation, and indirectness prior to the main refusal. This pattern becomes more prominent in situations involving greater interlocutor power and greater social distance. In contrast, NSEs tend to employ concise mitigation combined with clearer expression intent, often limiting negotiation and reducing ambiguity. Indirectness in JLEs frequently functions to maintain relational harmony and prolong interactional openness, whereas in NSEs, it operates within a more bounded and situationally oriented framework. The study also revealed that direct refusal emerges selectively in equal-power relationships, with differing orientations toward politeness marking between the two groups. Theoretically, this study contributes to the literature on interlanguage pragmatics by positioning politeness in refusal as a dynamic negotiation process shaped by the interaction of cultural orientation, social variables, and sequential organization of speech. These findings highlight the need to conceptualize refusal not as a fixed strategy type but as a context-sensitive pragmatic practice. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: A systematic review of emerging bioenergy pathways: Comparison of economic viability and greenhouse gas emissions
Abstract: To capture the recent technology improvements in advanced biofuels, this review conducted a systematic review of post-2015 publications and synthesized 116 techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), and social LCA studies to analyze the economic viability and environmental and social impacts. Capital costs, feedstock prices, operational expenses, and minimum fuel selling prices (MFSPs) were benchmarked alongside carbon emissions to enable direct comparison. This review finds key technical advancements emerged from new catalysts, enzymes, and chemicals, and optimized processes in pretreatment, conversion, and integrated system models. Results indicate that biomethane from anaerobic digestion of agriculture waste is the most cost-effective and climate-friendly option, with capital investments often below $10 million, MFSPs under $2/gal, and WTW emissions consistently below 30 g CO2-eq/MJ. Biodiesel from waste oils can achieve MFSPs below $2/gal when co-products (e.g., electricity, glycerol) are valorized, though emissions vary with feedstock and land use change impacts. For cellulosic ethanol, advances in pretreatment, enzyme efficiency, and lignin valorization have reduced MFSPs to $2.3–$3.2/gal and achieved 70–90% GHG reductions relative to gasoline. Overall, waste-based feedstocks consistently outperform crop-based systems in cost and emission metrics. Process optimization and co-product valorization help with improving resource efficiency, reducing production costs and lowering environmental impacts. The social LCA studies find advanced bioenergy deliver broad societal benefits, with employment as the most consistently reported positive outcome. The review highlights the importance of standardized TEA/LCA/social LCA frameworks, recommending targeted policy incentives to accelerate the deployment of low-carbon bioenergy technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Deterministic modeling of infection dynamics under Far-UVC irradiation: a cumulative-exposure framework and its mathematical relation to infectious quanta
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: Far-UVC irradiation (200–235 nm) is a promising photonic intervention for suppressing the environmental transmission of airborne pathogens in occupied spaces. However, establishing a robust physical and mathematical framework to quantify these dynamic pathogen-host interactions remains challenging, as direct verification using mammalian models is experimentally demanding and cost-prohibitive. Here, we present a controlled in vivo biophysical model system—utilizing zebrafish and Yersinia ruckeri —to quantitatively examine the macroscopic survival dynamics of a host population under varying environmental pathogen loads. We observed a distinct, threshold-like transition in macroscopic host survival near a critical pathogen density (106 CFU/mL for a 0.25-day exposure duration), above which infection-induced mortality sharply increased. Far-UVC irradiation reduced the viable pathogen density as a function of UV dose, systematically driving the system below this critical threshold and demonstrating effective physical pathogen attenuation. To elucidate the underlying dynamics, we introduced a deterministic, multistep Susceptible-Infectious-Removed (SIR) model governed by a system of coupled differential equations. The theoretical model revealed that the final macroscopic state of the system is governed by a cumulative exposure parameter, Λ=β0ρτ, where β0 is the infectivity coefficient, ρ is the bacterial density, and τ is the exposure duration, rather than by instantaneous bacterial density alone. Crucially, the cumulative exposure parameter Λ derived from this aquatic infection model shares the same exponential cumulative form with the infectious quanta in the Wells-Riley model for predicting airborne transmission. Therefore, this in vivo platform validates a quantitative physical framework specifically for evaluating ultraviolet (UV) disinfection dynamics. These findings provide a theoretical basis for designing precise photonic irradiation algorithms that maintain cumulative environmental exposure below critical pathogenic thresholds. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Art as a scaffold for social cognition
Abstract: The idea that art connects us to others is culturally compelling, yet empirical evidence linking art engagement to social cognition remains mixed across paradigms, methods, and timescales. We develop the thesis that art functions as a scaffold for social cognition, rather than a direct intervention on social-cognitive abilities. From this perspective, art structures the conditions under which social cognition unfolds by shaping whether individuals engage with socially meaningful content, how deeply they become involved, and whether they return to similar experiences over time. The scaffold model identifies three interrelated components: a motivational gate, qualities of engagement, and reinforcement and habit formation. By integrating previously disconnected literature, the scaffold model reframes art's social-cognitive impact as a recursive process that creates repeated opportunities for social-cognitive practice across contexts, media, and timescales. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Ultrasonic vocalizations in mice and rats: New applications and recent developments from sender to receiver
Abstract: Mice and rats emit ultrasonic vocalizations (USV) above the human hearing range. Such USV are widely regarded as reliable indicators of the animal's affective state. Moreover, USV serve important communicative functions. Given their prominent role in social communication, this review adopts a reciprocal framework that considers both sender and receiver, with particular emphasis on the production and perception of USV. The review focuses on sex differences and subtype variations in the sender, and explores the communicative value of USV through playback studies, revealing their role in regulating social interactions from the receiver's perspective. It also examines recent applications, including the use of isolation-induced USV during the homing test, USV as measures of expectation, and their relevance in modeling mania and emotional contagion. Furthermore, this review takes into account advancements in sender identification and live tracking in semi-natural environments, which have enhanced our understanding of USV. Title: Neural and endocrine correlates of extinction of conditioned sexual incentive salience in male rats
Abstract: Conditioned sexual arousal (CSA) can develop when initially neutral social cues acquire sexual incentive value through associative learning. Here, we examined how this response changes following repeated nonreinforced exposure to the conditioned social cue. Adult male rats underwent three conditioning trials followed, in the extinction-training groups, by three additional drug-free exposures to the almond-scented juvenile male. Conditioned responding was subsequently assessed toward both a receptive female and the juvenile male. QNP-Paired males showed robust juvenile-directed non-contact erections (NCEs), whereas QNP-Extinction males showed markedly reduced NCE responding. Genital investigation also showed a significant Partner × Treatment interaction, while the remaining behavioral measures did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Free testosterone did not differ significantly among treatments. Exploratory Fos-immunoreactivity (Fos-IR) analyses revealed treatment-related differences in several brain regions; however, no direct QNP-Paired versus QNP-Extinction regional comparison remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Title: Mitigating feature degradation in deep Forward–Forward networks
Abstract: The Forward–Forward (FF) algorithm is a promising alternative to Backpropagation (BP) using layer-wise optimization. Specifically, Cross-layer Gradient Momentum (CGM) propagates cross-layer gradient momentum to enrich the learning signal, and Local Feature Reconstruction (LFR) reconstructs local features to compensate for information loss. Title: Mapping the intellectual structure of floating photovoltaics research, trends and emerging frontiers: a hybrid bibliometric review and content analysis
Abstract: This study presents a hybrid bibliometric–content analysis integrating scientific publications, patent activity, and deployment statistics to map the evolution, intellectual structure, and emerging research priorities of floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems. A dataset of 1716 publications spanning 2004–2025 was analysed using Bibliometrix, and the resulting thematic structure was used to organize a technical synthesis. Four interconnected domains were identified. Structurally, FPV deployment spans three aquatic environments, three principal floating concepts, and four station-keeping families, confirming that design requirements vary fundamentally with site conditions and environmental loading. Reported FPV energy-yield differences relative to land-based PV range from −3.84% to +19.68%, demonstrating that thermal benefits are strongly dependent on climate, geometry, and ventilation. Environmental studies commonly assess approximately 10% reservoir coverage, while scenarios reaching 25–30% indicate increasing trade-offs between water conservation and ecological uncertainty. Techno-economic evidence reports FPV capital-cost premiums of approximately 25–30%, with operating-cost estimates commonly 2–4% higher than land-based PV, although assumptions vary substantially. These findings demonstrate that FPV is a coupled water–energy–infrastructure system whose reliability, environmental sustainability, and bankability cannot be evaluated independently. Title: The role of mnemonic discrimination in symptom severity and treatment response of obsessive-compulsive disorder

Abstract: Mnemonic discrimination, the ability to differentiate novel stimuli from highly similar past ones, has been evidenced as a compelling factor for fear overgeneralization in anxiety disorders. Title: A production-ready machine learning system for inclusive employment: Requirements engineering and implementation of AI-driven disability job matching platform
Abstract: Employment inclusion of people with disabilities remains critically low in Italy, with only 3.5% employed nationally despite mandatory hiring quotas. Traditional manual matching processes require 30–60 min per candidate, creating bottlenecks that limit service capacity. Our goal is to develop and validate a production-ready machine learning system for disability employment matching that integrates social responsibility requirements while maintaining human oversight in decision-making. We employed participatory requirements engineering with Centro per l'Impiego di Villafranca di Verona professionals. The system implements a seven-model ensemble with parallel hyperparameter optimization using Optuna. Qualitative expert validation with employment center professionals suggests potential for 60%–100% capacity increases for employment centers. The LightGBM ensemble shows optimal performance with 94.6-second training time. Our findings indicate that advanced AI systems can successfully integrate social responsibility requirements without compromising technical performance. Authors: Lu T.; Liu H.; Wang T.; Sun K.; Lin T.; Jia Z.; Wang H.; Yu S.; Song Y.; Zhang X.
Title: Toward ammonia-to-NOx ratio control in an ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection engine under low-load conditions
Abstract: An excessive ammonia-to-NOx ratio (ANR) under low-load operation poses a challenge to the efficient operation of aftertreatment systems in ammonia-fueled engines. In this study, experiments were conducted on a single-cylinder ammonia/diesel dual direct-injection (DDI) engine to investigate the effects of ammonia substitution ratio (ASR), intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing (−28 to −12°CA ATDC) on NH3 emissions, NOx emissions, and the ANR under a low-load condition of 4 bar indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP). The results show that increasing ASR is the dominant factor driving the increase in the ANR. When the ASR was maintained below 60%, coordinated optimization of intake pressure, dual-fuel injection pressure, and injection timing under the late diesel injection strategy reduced the ANR to 1.1–1.25 while maintaining a high indicated thermal efficiency (ITE), thereby reducing the ANR to a level compatible with the efficient operating window of the aftertreatment system, and engine-out N2O emissions showed no evident deterioration. Furthermore, by substantially advancing diesel injection timing (−340 to −220°CA ATDC) to establish a thermally favorable in-cylinder environment before ammonia combustion, the ANR could be further reduced to below 1.0. However, a trade-off between ASR and ITE together with a marked increase in engine-out N2O emissions was observed under this strategy. The study systematically elucidates the regulation characteristics of key combustion control parameters on the ANR under low-load conditions and proposes practical ANR control strategies for ammonia/diesel DDI engines. The findings provide new insights into the optimization of ammonia utilization and energy conversion efficiency, and offer useful guidance for in-cylinder combustion control with aftertreatment requirements in ammonia-fueled engines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Jiang Q.; Zhao X.-L.; Zhang H.; Wu W.-H.; Ng M.K.
Title: A convolutional low-rank continuous tensor representation for multi-dimensional data recovery
Abstract: Convolutional low-rank methods have been widely used in image processing and computer vision due to their ability to capture local spatial structure. However, existing convolutional low-rank methods are limited to rectangular meshgrids at a fixed scale, which restricts their applicability to emerging real-world spatial-irregular data, such as semantic spatial sub-regions and spatial transcriptomics. To overcome this limitation, we propose a convolutional low-rank tensor representation for spatial arbitrary-shape multi-dimensional data. Specifically, by representing the latent tensor through an implicit neural representation, we impose a new tensor nuclear norm (low-rank regularization) on the sampled domain by inferring the inside/outside data entries and develop a new ARbiTrary-shape Convolutional Tensor Nuclear Norm (ART-CTNN). Compared with classic convolutional low-rank tensor representations, ART-CTNN offers two key advantages: it unifies the exploration of the convolutional low-rank prior for spatial arbitrary-shape data, and it can exploit convolutional low-rankness at arbitrary resolutions beyond the original sampling grid, allowing regularization at a suitable scale. Extensive experiments on both regular and irregular datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the recovery performance of complex spatial details and structures, while further enhancing downstream clustering performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Res-PGDnet: A time frequency fusion model with physiologically constrained adversarial training for PPG-based valence–arousal state classification
Abstract: Accurate valence–arousal assessment is crucial for affective computing applications. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is a promising, practical modality for this task, but it poses challenges: signals are noise-prone, the physiological affect mapping is complex and subject-specific, and models generalize poorly. Existing methods often focus narrowly on temporal features, employ physiologically unconstrained robustness strategies, or suffer from a severe performance–efficiency trade-off. We propose Res-PGDnet to address these issues via synergistic time frequency fusion and physiologically constrained adversarial training. Its core innovations are (i) applying adversarial perturbations constrained by physiological priors to model parameters to ensure robust, plausible learning and (ii) hierarchically integrating DCT attention modules to jointly enhance temporal and spectral feature representations. On the DEAP-PPG dataset, Res-PGDnet achieves 93.47% intra-subject accuracy and 92.46% Macro-F1 score, with strong robustness (metric: 0.920) and 85.1% cross-subject accuracy. The model is efficient (12.5 M parameters, 1250 FPS), demonstrating potential for wearable-based valence–arousal classification in settings like mental health monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Urine culture contamination in a tertiary hospital: Demographic predictors and direct economic impact
Abstract: Background Pre-analytical sample contamination is a significant pre-analytical error that hinders diagnostic efficiency and increases laboratory costs. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical-demographic factors associated with contamination and quantify its direct economic impact in a tertiary hospital. Methods An observational, retrospective study was conducted on 2835 urine cultures processed between January and June 2025. Contamination was defined according to CLSI PRE05 guidelines. Direct costs (reagents and consumables) were calculated. Data normality was assessed using Q–Q plots, and cost distributions were compared using the non-parametric Kruskal–Wallis test. Results Of the total samples, 31.4% were positive, 64.7% negative, and 3.8% contaminated. Multivariable analysis identified age ≥ 60 years and female sex as independent predictors of urine culture contamination. Patients aged ≥60 years accounted for 44.9% of all contaminated samples. ESKAPE pathogens represented 81% of positive isolates. The total cost for urine cultures was $37,728 USD, with contamination representing a direct loss of $873 USD (2.3% of the urine culture budget). Kruskal-Wallis analysis confirmed that contamination costs constitute a significant and avoidable financial burden ( p < 0.0001). Conclusions Older adults (>60 years) and female patients had a higher risk of urine culture contamination. Although the absolute cost of contamination may appear marginal, it reflects a preventable diagnostic inefficiency that delays treatment in a clinical setting dominated by ESKAPE pathogens. Implementing assisted collection protocols for geriatric patients is a necessary cost-effective strategy to optimize institutional resources and patient safety. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Gong T.; Xu H.; Sui X.; Han Z.; Gan R.; Yuan L.; Liu Y.; Qiao H.; Zheng Y.; Wang Z.
Title: Riveted Fe–N5 moieties confined in curved graphitic carbon enable a triple-protection mechanism for robust acidic oxygen reduction electrocatalysis
Abstract: Fe–N–C exhibits exceptional catalytic activity and stands as a prominent representative of single-atom catalysts (SACs). However, the activity and, especially, the stability of its active sites pose a formidable challenge for practical applications. Therefore, we first performed DFT predictions on active site structural models featuring curvature and axial coordination, revealing that the curved Fe–N5 configuration simultaneously boosts both the activity and stability. Then we adopt an O-Tolidine molecular-induced strategy to construct the curved graphitic carbon layers, which anchor Fe single atoms in a bent and axial N-coordinated configuration. The molecular-assisted effect facilitates micropore formation, accelerates the graphitization process, and simultaneously provides additional nitrogen coordination sites, ultimately achieving the curved Fe–N5 configuration. The curved Fe–N5 motifs establish a triple protection mechanism: resistance to Fe dissolution, suppression of carbon corrosion and shielding against H⁺ attack, thus alleviating the long-standing activity–stability trade-off in SACs. Benefiting from these structural merits, the as-obtained catalyst delivers outstanding durability in H2-O2 fuel cell, achieving a high peak power density of 1.37 W cm−2 with only 10.2% performance degradation after 10,000 square-wave cycles—far lower than the 29.8% loss of conventional Fe–N–C. Under H2-Air conditions at 0.65 V, it retains 74.3% of its initial current density over 200 h. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang X.; Tinacci L.; Giusti A.; Kang H.; Deng W.; Li Y.; Sun Z.; Peng H.; Zou L.; Armani A.; Wen J.
Title: DNA authentication of shark meat products from a major Chinese e-commerce platform reveals trade-name opacity and traceability limitations
Abstract: Shark meat products are subject to a variety of regulatory and conservation frameworks, yet their characterization at the retail level is often constrained by the use of umbrella terms and limited species-specific information. In this context, the present study was designed as an exploratory case study examining shark meat products commercialized through a major Chinese e-commerce platform within a defined sampling period. Product descriptions, labeling information (including trade name, processing type, product presentation, declared production origin, and price), and molecular species identification obtained through DNA barcoding were jointly examined to characterize shark-derived products marketed through the platform. A total of 63 products were screened, and 165 tissue samples were analysed using COI and cytb markers. All products were marketed under generic umbrella terms, without scientific nomenclature, and prepackaged products showed variable labeling completeness. Molecular analyses detected at least one shark taxon in 61 of the 63 products examined, whereas the remaining two products contained billfish and batoid taxa. At the tissue level, 160 of 165 samples (97%) were assigned to shark taxa. Across all analysed samples, molecular identification revealed 12 species-level taxa, comprising 10 shark species (Alopias pelagicus, A. superciliosus, Carcharhinus brevipinna, C. limbatus, C. sorrah, Galeocerdo cuvier, Isurus oxyrinchus, Mustelus griseus, Prionace glauca, and Sphyrna lewini), one batoid species (Rhynchobatus australiae), and one billfish species (Istiophorus platypterus), together with three genus-level assignments including shark and billfish taxa (Scoliodon sp., Carcharhinus sp., and Kajikia sp.). The identified taxa include species listed as Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, and Critically Endangered according to the IUCN Red List. The two products containing non-shark taxa represented cases of non-conformity between molecular identity and the available product information and therefore warrant discussion in relation to labeling practices. Overall, the findings illustrate the utility of molecular approaches for documenting species composition in online retail settings and provide an exploratory baseline for future investigations into species-level transparency, product information practices, and shark product commercialization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: An AI-driven clinical decision support system for coronary artery disease prediction in T2DM patients using clinical laboratory parameters and deep fusion learning
Abstract: This article presents an intelligent clinical decision support system that integrates graph-based modelling and deep fusion learning for coronary artery disease (CAD) risk prediction using a clinical Laboratory and validated dataset. A Graph-Based Multivariate Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) imputation approach is proposed to handle the missing values, while latent class analysis (LCA) is applied for outlier detection. The framework further incorporates with the graph-based directional risk scoring and the comorbidity network analysis to identify significant clinical attributes and capture complex relationships among risk factors. For prediction, the Enhanced TabNet and Enhanced Residual MLP (ResNet) architectures are then combined through the probabilistic fusion with XGBoost as a meta-learner. Title: Ultrasonic vocalizations as markers of anxiety and depression in rodent models of neurotrauma
Abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) and traumatic brain injury (TBI) are severe events that cause lasting sensorimotor and autonomic impairments. Both injuries often also lead to psychological and somatosensory dysfunctions such as anxiety, depression, or pain. Preclinical assessment of anxiety and depression in rodents often relies on locomotion-based behavioural tests confounded by motor deficits and pain-related changes. Because rodents cannot self-report sensory or emotional experiences, behavioural outcomes are limited to observable proxies of anxiety and depression. Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) offer a complementary, non-locomotor tool that may capture anxiety- and depression-relevant context not detected by behavioural tests. Despite extensive USV research in stress, reward, and social behaviour, applications to neurotrauma remain underexplored, with no studies directly examining USVs in relation to anxiety- or depression-like outcomes after SCI. Even so, evidence from related fields and the limited neurotrauma literature suggests that USVs warrant further exploration as affective readouts after TBI and particularly SCI. USVs may complement behavioural testing by providing socioaffective context without relying on locomotor performance, potentially helping distinguish post-injury anxiety- and depression-like phenotypes from pain-related and other injury-associated changes. By integrating behavioural, neural, and pharmacological evidence, we highlight how USV features may reflect affective dimensions relevant to post-injury anxiety- and depression-like states and outline methodological considerations for validity and specificity. Machine-learning approaches further enable high-throughput, objective detection of subtle affective shifts. With development of collaborative datasets, these methods could reveal consistent affective vocal patterns and lay groundwork for a rudimentary ‘lexicon’ of rodent affect. Integrating USV analysis into neurotrauma and CNS disease research may refine preclinical models of affective dysfunction and improve triangulated evaluation of treatments targeting chronic mental health outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

Author full names: Zawada-Tomkiewicz, Anna (6507550999)
Title: A unified micro–macro stochastic framework for tool wear evolution and lifetime prediction
Abstract: Tool wear results from the interaction of numerous micro-scale contact regions subjected to mechanical, thermal and tribological loading. This paper proposes a physics-informed micro–macro stochastic framework linking contact-scale degradation processes with engineering-scale prediction of wear evolution and tool life. At the micro-contact level, tool degradation is represented by a population of interacting contacts undergoing wear, load redistribution and local instability. Model reduction leads to a state-dependent stochastic differential equation whose drift and diffusion terms describe macroscopic flank-wear evolution, while a jump component represents intermittent degradation events. Abrasion/ploughing, adhesion/BUE, thermal–oxidative and diffusion–chemical wear are represented as dominant degradation mechanisms, whereas coating protection and edge instability are treated as latent degradation states. Tool life is formulated as a first-passage problem with respect to a prescribed wear limit. Model parameters are identified from experimentally reconstructed wear increments, with different tribological systems represented using the same stochastic formulation through coefficient calibration. Validation is performed at three complementary levels: predictive assessment of wear evolution, statistical evaluation of degradation dynamics and independent physical validation. The framework reproduces nonlinear wear evolution and increasing degradation variability, while the inferred mechanism hierarchy and latent degradation states are qualitatively supported by independent experimental evidence. The proposed methodology bridges tribological processes at the micro-contact scale and stochastic reliability assessment at the engineering scale, integrating wear evolution, mechanism interpretation and tool-life prediction within a unified physics-informed framework. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Li X.; Meng H.
Title: The allure of imperfection: How ugly-cute aesthetics drive purchase intentions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The rise of social media has increased both aesthetic diversity and consumer attention to product appearance and emotional appeal. This research examines the commercially successful yet under-researched “ugly-cute” aesthetic, exemplified by products like Pop Mart's LABUBU. Moving beyond traditional approaches that treat beauty (or ugliness) and cuteness as separate dimensions, we investigate their interactive effects through four studies: one field experiment and three online experiments, involving participants from both China and the United States. Our findings show that the combination of ugly-cute configurations can attenuate the purchase-intention disadvantage associated with ugliness-related aesthetic deviation, with this effect explained by perceived social value and moderated by consumption setting (public vs. private). Specifically, this effect is more pronounced in public consumption settings, where consumers are more likely to seek social approval and positive evaluation from others, thereby amplifying perceived social value in purchase decisions. These results advance the literature on product design and consumer aesthetics by identifying a psychological explanation underlying consumer responses to atypical aesthetics, and provide practical insights for designing products that generate perceived social value (e.g., feeling accepted, gaining approval, or being positively regarded by others). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Beyond the hotspots: Identifying public opinion blind spots and agenda-setting dynamics in crisis information generation
Abstract: During sudden crises, a structural mismatch between social media attention and governance value often marginalizes key crisis issues, creating public opinion blind spots that undermine effective emergency management. Using the 2021 Henan rainstorm as a case study (N = 40,160), this study proposes an integrated framework to identify public opinion blind spots and examine their agenda-setting dynamics. Bootstrap estimation further assesses the association between blind spots and agenda-setting effects. Results show that blind spots vary dynamically across the 4R phases, with Prevention Education, Disaster Causation, and Review and Improvement recurring most frequently. Bidirectional agenda-setting effects can emerge at a 1-hour resolution, and stronger agenda guidance from authoritative users is associated with blind-spot mitigation. Ultimately, these findings offer practical implications for optimizing crisis information supply and strengthening social resilience. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Gas-solid interfacial photoelectrocatalysis for toluene mineralization with concomitant hydrogen peroxide generation

Abstract: The abatement of gaseous volatile organic compounds (VOCs) such as toluene is constrained by sluggish mass transfer and the trade-off between adsorption and oxidation activity in conventional liquid-phase systems. Herein, a solid-state paired photoelectrocatalytic system that operates at the gas-solid interface is proposed for enabling simultaneous anodic toluene mineralization and cathodic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) generation under ambient air feed. Comprehensive analyses reveal that MXene and EDTA synergistically modulate the band structure of SnO2 for promoting ∙OH generation, while MXene further amplifies this through photoelectric synergy and photothermal effects. In situ tests confirm the complete mineralization without accumulation of toxic intermediates, and theoretical calculations elucidate the increased electron density near the Fermi level, which significantly enhances the adsorption of both toluene and O2. Hence, this dual enhancement boosts the anodic oxidation kinetics but also facilitates the cathodic reduction reaction, offering a promising pathway for sustainable environmental remediation. © 2026

Title: Adsorption performance of radial-flow contactors for direct air capture: A computational study
Abstract: The need for efficient direct air capture (DAC) is increasing as the global mean temperature continues to rise and a large fraction of CO2 emissions cannot be addressed by conventional CO2 capture technologies. For adsorption-based DAC, the geometry of the gas-solid contactor is an important design parameter because it determines pressure losses, sorbent utilisation, and the efficiency of the process. This study investigates the adsorption stage in a centripetal Z-type radial-flow adsorber for DAC. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model is adopted to simulate the gas flow through the porous bed of adsorbent particles adsorbing CO2 from the gas with the help of the linear driving force model and the Toth isotherms. The material properties are experimentally obtained for a commercial amine-functionalised resin. Twelve different configurations of the contactor are analysed with various bed aspect ratios and radius ratios while keeping the bed volume constant. The simulations indicate that the geometry strongly affects the flow distribution, pressure drop, and adsorption time, which affect the specific energy requirement and productivity of the adsorption stage of the DAC process. Configuration selection represents the trade-off between low energy requirements (at high bed aspect ratio and radius ratio), low space requirements, and construction material costs (at low bed aspect ratio and radius ratio). Title: Multi-modal knowledge-level representation learning for structure-oriented patent citation prediction
Abstract: Patent citation prediction aims to identify prior patents that challenge the novelty of new patent applications. A citation is valid when the technical components in the new application are functionally and structurally similar to those disclosed in the prior patent. This component structure is conveyed through two modalities: the claim text and the patent figures. Existing methods predominantly rely on text and struggle to capture the graph-structured nature of patent components. We propose a Multi-Modal Knowledge-Level Patent Representation Framework. First, we construct a multi-modal component graph that links text-derived triples with figure-derived visual components via reference numerals. Second, we introduce a knowledge-level attention mechanism operating at the triple level, coupled with cross-modal attention that injects figure-grounded structure into token embeddings, jointly aligning the modalities and suppressing noise arising from legal characterizations in patent text. Finally, we introduce a re-ranking module that performs structure-oriented similarity reasoning over the fused representation. We introduce PatCite, the first citation dataset categorizing samples into “tree-structured” and “graph-structured” types. Under the dynamic full-corpus protocol, our method achieves macro Recall@1/Recall@10 of 14.4%/43.8% on PatCite, with a Recall@1 gain of 5.0 percentage points over the strongest fine-tuned baseline. © 2026

Title: Deep spectral unmixing unfolding network for multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion
Abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) comprise tens to hundreds of contiguous narrow spectral bands, imposing substantial computational demands on HSI processing. However, the strong similarity between adjacent bands creates considerable redundancy, whose reduction is essential for computationally efficient processing. We propose a multispectral and hyperspectral image fusion (MHIF) framework, termed the Deep Spectral Unmixing Unfolding (DSUU) network, from a matrix factorization perspective. DSUU exploits sparsity priors through a spectral unmixing model to reduce information redundancy. It then applies proximal gradient optimization and unfolds its iterations into a deep network, improving the efficiency of conventional model-driven optimization. The proximal operators for endmembers and abundances use 1D- and 2D-DWT-based blocks to mitigate errors arising from inaccurate initialization. To capture spatial-spectral correlations overlooked by matrix factorization, we introduce a Spatial-Spectral Refinement Block (SSRB) comprising a multiscale spatial module and a spectral attention module. Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that DSUU achieves a more favorable trade-off between fusion quality and computational complexity than state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Title: Gaussian Splatting for real-time scene reconstruction: Methods, systems, and trade-offs
Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) allows for high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis. Since its inception in 2023, its explicit and highly configurable scene representation has been extended toward sparse-view generation, dynamic reconstruction, efficiency and compression, streaming, and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Although Gaussian Splatting can provide real-time rendering, rendering an existing representation is distinct from constructing, updating, or maintaining the scene itself. In this survey, we synthesize current literature, categorize them and provide a connection of current approaches and tools towards an end-to-end pipeline. Explicitly, we categorize GS scene reconstruction into five overlapping families: single-shot generation, dynamic representations, efficiency and compression, streaming and immersive systems, and Gaussian Splatting SLAM. We distinguish render-only throughput from task-specific scene generation, update, tracking, mapping, and optimization costs, and combine controlled sparse-view benchmarking with native evaluations to identify cross-family quality, latency, memory, and update-cost trade-offs. © 2026

Title: Breaking selectivity-conversion trade-off for CO2-glycerol carbonylation via constructing ternary active-sites in zeolite-based catalyst
Abstract: Directly converting glycerol (GL) and CO2 into glycerol carbonate (GC) offers a pivotal solution to valorize biodiesel by-products while mitigate greenhouse gas emmissions. However, the chemical inertness of CO2 and the inherent complexity of GL molecular structure pose a significant challenge in balancing activity and selectivity for this reaction. Herein, Lewis and Brønsted acid sites were constructed on the inherent Lewis basic sites within ETS-10 zeolite, leading to the formation of a ternary-active-sites Zn(Otf)x/ETS-10 catalyst for overcoming the long-standing trade-off between activity and selectivity in CO2-GL carbonylation. The tailored Lewis and Brønsted acid sites synergistically anchor GL molecules and provide a novel mode for their targeted activation, resulting in an intriguing 11-membered ring-shaped Zn-GL* intermediate. Subsequently, the direct cyclization with the adjacent bi-COO* species formed by CO2 activation on Lewis basic sites promotes GC production while suppressing the side reactions that consume both GL and GC. Ultimately, by using CaC2 as a solid dehydrating agent, a 95.2% of GC selectivity and 40.9% of GL conversion were achieved within the regular and enlarged 12-membered ring (12-RS) of the ETS-10 framework. This work offers valuable insights into the rational design of active sites for highly active and selective carbonylation catalysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Multi‑objective optimisation and experimental validation of a compact energy‑efficient active regeneration burner for diesel particulate filter regeneration
Abstract: Active regeneration burners are essential for diesel particulate filter (DPF) regeneration. However, they are often constrained by low flow utilisation, excessive gas velocity, and inadequate mixing between combustion products and exhaust gas, leading to poor thermal efficiency and degraded regeneration performance. To tackle these challenges, this study focused on achieving a compact and lightweight burner design via iterative and dimensional optimisation. A multi‑objective optimisation framework incorporating Response Surface Methodology (RSM), Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was then established to enhance the combustion performance. The effectiveness of this optimisation approach was verified through regeneration experiments. The optimised design reduced burner volume and mass by 57.7 % and 39.5 %, respectively, while maintaining outlet velocity uniformity above 97 % across three investigated exhaust-flow conditions. Outlet temperature uniformity increased from 82.8 % to 92.2 %, the maximum measured outlet temperature at the five-point thermocouple plane increased from 865 °C to 970 °C, and thermal efficiency increased from 38.8 % to 51.1 %. The time required for the DPF upstream temperature to reach 600 °C decreased from 200 s to 172 s, while the regeneration efficiency increased from 92 % to 94 %. Smoke opacity, HC, and CO decreased from 3.9 % to 3.1 %, 28 ppm to 8 ppm, and 0.205 vol% to 0.100 vol%, respectively; however, NOx increased from 104.5 ppm to 117.0 ppm, indicating a trade-off between oxidation completeness and NOx formation. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the burner for compact and energy-efficient diesel aftertreatment systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Automated analysis of prosodic and conversational speech markers for autism spectrum disorder screening and severity estimation
Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with clinically meaningful differences in speech, prosody, and reciprocal communication; however, these markers are difficult to quantify consistently during routine screening. This study investigates whether automatically extracted acoustic, prosodic, and conversational speech markers can support objective ASD screening and severity estimation. We present SpectrumNet, a speech-marker modeling framework designed to analyze communication-relevant features rather than replacing clinical diagnosis. The framework combines a multi-scale acoustic encoder, a prosody encoder, and a conversational-dynamics encoder to represent voice quality, rhythm, intonation, speech rate, pause behavior, and turn-taking patterns. A cross-domain feature disentanglement module separates ASD-relevant communication markers from speaker identity and emotional variation, while a hierarchical attention mechanism identifies patterns across short-, medium-, and longer-range temporal scales. The model was evaluated using five publicly available datasets, with ASDSpeech serving as the primary clinical benchmark and ADOS-2 scores used for severity estimation. On ASDSpeech, SpectrumNet achieved 93.10% accuracy, 92.80% F1-score, and 95.50% AUC for ASD versus typically developing classification. Severity estimates were strongly associated with ADOS-2 scores, including a Pearson correlation of 0.891 for the total score. Cross-dataset testing on AV-ASD showed 78.43% zero-shot accuracy and 85.20% accuracy after minimal fine-tuning, suggesting partial generalizability across recording settings. These findings support the potential value of speech-based computational markers as an adjunctive screening aid for communication-disorder assessment, while highlighting the need for larger, clinically diverse, and prospectively validated cohorts before diagnostic deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Polyethylene gasification in a bubbling fluidized bed: Operating-parameter effects on syngas, tar and soot formation
Abstract: Plastic gasification offers a route to recover polymer carbon as synthesis gas; changes in operating conditions affect both syngas properties and the partitioning of carbon among gaseous, condensable, and solid products. This study investigates these effects during polyethylene gasification in an electrically heated lab-scale bubbling fluidized bed. Experimental series varied temperature (750–850 °C), equivalence ratio (ER; 0.20–0.30), and steam-to-carbon ratio (S/C; 0.25–0.75), with additional tests assessing the influence of feed rate and oxygen enrichment. Raising temperature increased H2 and CO yields, doubled gas yield from 0.90 to 1.74 Nm3/kgdaf, and raised carbon conversion efficiency to 93%, while shifting condensables from aliphatics toward aromatics/PAHs. Increasing ER to 0.30 lowered condenser-collected tar but increased soot sixfold and produced less favourable methanol-relevant stoichiometry, showing a trade-off between tar reduction, soot formation, and syngas quality. Steam addition suppressed soot by almost one order of magnitude, but H2, CO, and gas yields peaked at S/C = 0.50, with limited further conversion benefit at higher S/C. Oxygen enrichment from 30% to 72%, with additional steam moderating bed temperature, maintained gas-phase carbon conversion with only a minor reduction in cold-gas efficiency. Paired in-reactor and downstream sampling tracked gas evolution through the freeboard, showing continued olefin conversion and H2 formation consistent with kinetic-model predictions at an imposed 850 °C. C2H4 in the product gas accounted for 25–35% of feed carbon under all conditions. Title: Proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cells with La0.5Sr0.5Fe0.75X0.25O3 (X=Co,Ni, Cu) cathodes: a comparative study

Abstract: To enhance the cathode performance of La0.5Sr0.5FeO3 (LSF) in proton‑conducting solid oxide fuel cells (H‑SOFCs), different transition metal elements (Co, Ni, Cu) are introduced at the Fe site, forming the composition La0.5Sr0.5Fe0.75X0.25O3 (X = Co, Ni, Cu). Furthermore, the Ni-doped LSF material is evaluated in composite cathodes. A trade-off exists between the ORR activity of the Ni-doped LSF cathode and the proton conduction provided by the proton conductor. Title: A learning-based robust framework for chest X-ray pneumonia classification: Privacy-preserving deep learning with adversarial training
Abstract: Chest X-ray classifiers must protect patient data without sacrificing diagnostic utility or robustness to adversarial perturbations. Title: Encountering the “familiar stranger”: Activating latent cultural identification among Vietnamese tourists in China
Abstract: Tourism studies have largely examined cultural identification through encounters with difference, while paying less attention to culturally proximate travel contexts. Drawing on schema theory, this study examines how latent cultural identification (LCI) emerges when sedimented cultural meanings become perceptible and interpretable during travel. Based on interviews with 41 Vietnamese tourists traveling in China, the findings indicate that material, social, and mediated cues make routinized meanings noticeable, while internalized cultural schemata help tourists interpret them in relation to their cultural self-understanding. Affective resonance amplifies this process by intensifying the salience and self-relevance of interpreted meanings. Behavioural responses vary across compliance, inquiry, reinterpretation, and co-creation, reflecting different degrees of self-reflection and social embeddedness. By highlighting the role of cultural schemata in LCI, this study extends tourism identity research and shows how LCI can help tourists locate their own culture within the wider world-cultural landscape, enrich personal meaning-making, and foster intercultural exchange. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mn-doped polysaccharide-derived calcium-based sorbents with enhanced CO2 capture and cyclic stability
Abstract: Rapid CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel combustion have intensified the demand for efficient carbon-capture technologies. Calcium looping (CaL) is considered a promising option because of its high theoretical capacity and low material cost; however, severe sintering of CaO-based sorbents during repeated carbonation–calcination cycles results in rapid performance degradation. Mn-doped polysaccharide-derived CaO-based sorbents (Mn-PDCA) were prepared through a microtitration–wet-impregnation route to improve their cyclic CO2-capture performance. Among the prepared sorbents, 15Mn-PDCA exhibited the best overall performance, achieving an initial CO2 uptake of 0.474 g/g and retaining 0.417 g/g after 15 cycles under mild conditions, corresponding to a capacity retention of approximately 87.97%. Its initial uptake was 65.73% higher than that of Mn-free 0Mn-PDCA. Comprehensive experimental characterization indicated that the enhanced performance originated from the coordinated effects of Mn-associated surface regulation, Ca–Mn mixed-oxide pinning, XG-directed porous-structure formation, and residual-carbon confinement. Mixed Mn valence states and defect-associated oxygen species contributed to favorable surface chemical environments for CO2 adsorption, while thermally stable CaMnO3 and Ca4Mn3O10 phases acted as interfacial or grain-boundary barriers that restrained CaO crystallite migration and coalescence during cycling. Meanwhile, XG directed precursor nucleation and promoted the formation of porous microspheres, with the retained carbonaceous species providing an additional spatial-confinement effect. Excessive Mn loading at 20% caused Mn-rich aggregation, partial pore blockage, and dilution of active CaO, revealing a capacity–stability trade-off. These findings demonstrate a coordinated template–metal regulation strategy for developing sintering-resistant CaO-based sorbents for calcium-looping CO2 capture. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Experimental investigation of different CO2 injection schemes to enhance oil recovery in sandstone reservoir
Abstract: Application of carbon dioxide injection to enhance oil recovery is one of the best strategies to achieve a balance between energy security and reduced atmospheric emissions. Several injection schemes can be adopted to implement carbon dioxide-enhanced oil recovery. Injected CO2 mobilizes trapped oil by developing partial or full miscibility through diffusion, oil swelling, and viscosity reduction, but mechanisms such as viscous fingering, gravity override, and early gas breakthrough limit recovery efficiency. This study presents an experimental investigation of four different CO2 injection schemes, including continuous gas injection (CGI), cyclic injection (huff-n-puff), water-alternating-gas (WAG), and polymer-assisted WAG (PWAG) for enhancing oil recovery. Core was characterized for mineralogy, porosity, permeability, and wettability, while density, API gravity, rheology, and safety–critical properties of crude oil were evaluated. Core-flooding experiments were conducted at 70 °C and 800 psi overburden pressure, beginning with secondary waterflooding followed by tertiary CO2-EOR. Waterflooding recovered 47.47 % of the original oil in place (OOIP), leaving 52.53 % OOIP as the target for EOR method. CGI, cyclic, WAG, and PWAG injection schemes using CO2 resulted in significant incremental recovery. The results highlighted the critical role of mobility control in improving sweep efficiency, incremental oil recovery, and effective CO2 utilization by establishing a clear performance hierarchy: PWAG ' WAG ' CGI ' cyclic injection. Title: Unlocking reversible hydrogen storage in penta-hexa-hepta graphene through lithium functionalization
Abstract: A newly proposed two-dimensional carbon allotrope, penta–hexa–hepta graphene (PHH-Gr), is systematically investigated as a potential hydrogen storage medium using first-principles calculations. The thermodynamic, dynamical, and thermal robustness of PHH-Gr are verified through cohesive energy evaluation, phonon spectrum analysis, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Lithium decoration is found to be energetically favorable, with Li atoms strongly anchored at heptagonal hollow sites and minimal clustering tendency due to large Li–Li separations and high diffusion barriers. Electronic structure analysis demonstrates substantial charge transfer from Li to the PHH-Gr substrate while preserving metallic characteristics. Hydrogen adsorption on pristine PHH-Gr is weak, whereas Li functionalization markedly enhances H2 binding through polarization and charge-transfer effects. Each Li species can adsorb up to four hydrogen molecules, yielding a maximum gravimetric and volumetric hydrogen storage capacities of 10.75 wt% and 91.2 g L−1, respectively. Thermodynamic analysis using differential adsorption energies reveals that while the maximum storage capacity requires cryogenic temperatures or elevated pressures, a practical working capacity of approximately 6–8 wt% is achievable under reversible cycling conditions (298 K, 30 bar for uptake; 373 K, 3 bar for release). AIMD simulations also verify that the weakly bound fourth H2 molecule per Li site desorbs at room temperature under ambient pressure. Title: Positive emotion dispositions and human values in a Brazilian sample: Structural evaluation and exploratory network analysis

Title: Between indeterminacy and intervention: A field-based typology and design framework for interstitial Urban voids
Abstract: Urban voids are increasingly discussed as opportunities for urban transformation, yet they are often treated as a homogeneous category despite their diverse spatial, perceptual, and social characteristics. This study adopts a field-based qualitative research design that combines walking-based observation, standardized field coding, photographic documentation, and matrix-based comparative analysis to examine interstitial urban voids as heterogeneous spatial conditions. Using this research design, 61 interstitial micro voids were documented across four dense urban corridors in Istanbul. Data were recorded through a standardized protocol integrating morphological features, visibility and accessibility, informal use traces, sensory conditions, and perceived safety. The coded variables were then comparatively analysed to construct a typology and to support context-sensitive transformation decisions. Based on the combined evaluation of these variables, six void types were identified: circulation leftover, back-of-house void, residual structural gap, visual relief void, unintentional social pocket, and infrastructure-related void. Findings indicate that transformation potential differs across types and cannot be interpreted through a single factor. Unintentional social pockets and selected visual relief voids were associated with observed social or perceptual value, supporting preservation or light-touch intervention as analytically derived options rather than intensive formalization. By contrast, back-of-house voids and infrastructure-related voids combined poorer maintenance, negative sensory conditions, weaker public integration, and lower observer-based perceived safety, indicating a stronger need for safety-oriented redress before public activation.
