Title: Green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins system: SHAP-coupled entropy-energy-economic analysis and ANN-assisted multi-objective optimization
Abstract: A green hydrogen-enhanced coal-based methanol-to-aromatics and olefins (MTA/MTO) system offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization and reduce emissions in coal-based chemical production. However, the key variables and subsystem-level contributions affecting overall performance are not fully understood, and achieving efficient, feasible multi-objective optimization is challenging. This study develops an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted multi-objective optimization approach based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-coupled entropy-energy-economic (3E) analysis. The approach integrates ANN-based Pareto region identification with hierarchical Aspen Plus re-evaluation and repair to improve both optimization efficiency and solution feasibility. SHAP-coupled 3E analysis clarifies the roles of decision variables and subsystems in thermodynamic, economic, and energy performance, and highlights trade-offs among entropy generation rate, annual energy cost, and net present value. Results indicate that methanol-related and proton exchange membrane electrolyzer operations primarily influence overall 3E performance, while electrolyzer operation and methanol separation variables are most significant for objective trade-offs. Utilizing an ANN-assisted parallel NSGA-II, a promising Pareto region is identified in surrogate space within 132 s. Following rigorous re-evaluation and SHAP-coupled 3E-informed repair, all ANN-guided solutions converge in the rigorous model, with the relative errors between rigorous objective values and ANN predictions below 1.00 %. Compared to the baseline, the selected compromise solution increases the net present value by 28.48 %, while reducing the overall entropy generation rate by 1.52 % and the annual energy cost by 0.13 %. This study provides an interpretable, efficient, and reliable optimization framework for the low-carbon upgrading of highly integrated coal-based chemical processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Contesting Interests Between Institutional Pluralism and People-Centred Development in Natural Resource Management: Lessons from Selous Niassa Wildlife Corridor in Tanzania
Abstract: The debate on institutional pluralism (IP) in relation to natural resources management and people-centred development has become significant in Tanzania and many other developing countries. Mostly, the debates are related to the challenges of balancing conservation goals with people-centred development pathways in natural resources management. The theory of Self-Governance explains how the central government manages resources in community-owned areas. Data were gathered from national- and local-level government, non-governmental, and private-sector institutions relevant to the study, particularly those predominantly involved in natural resources management. The study utilized key informant interviews (KIIs), focus group discussions (FGDs), and household surveys in villages within the Selous-Niassa wildlife corridor (SNWC). The KII and FGD data were analysed using content analysis, and descriptive statistics were computed for the household interview data using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS). The results indicate that the evolution of institutional pluralism progressed through distinct stages, both before and after independence. During the pre-independence period, indigenous knowledge and practices for managing natural resources were destroyed, giving the colonial government power, even though it did not ensure sustainable management. This remained the same until the 1990s, when decentralization and Community-Based Resource Management were established (1990s - present). Tanzania saw increased recognition of the role of institutional pluralism in natural resource management. However, the increased recognition did not align with the current management status of natural resources in the SNWC, where degradation is accelerating due to increased human development. This paper concludes that natural resource management under institutional pluralism is influenced by communities’ development ambitions. This paper calls for strategies that balance the goals of natural resource management and development and recommends natural recovery measures. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Liu L.; Medaglia A.; Xie H.; Zanella M.
Title: Multi-fidelity methods for kinetic models of epidemic dynamics with uncertain contact structure
Source title: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
Abstract: In this work, we develop a multi-fidelity strategy for kinetic models in epidemiology with uncertain contact dynamics. Assessing and controlling the population-level effects of contact dynamics requires the development of models for understanding observable effects of heterogeneous contact structures, whose formation depends on complex social phenomena. These can be captured taking into account high-dimensional uncertain quantities. The proposed approach combines high-fidelity kinetic solvers with a hierarchy of low-fidelity surrogates, including reduced macroscopic models and coarse kinetic descriptions, remaining applicable even in regimes where a macroscopic closure is unavailable. This hierarchical framework identifies representative parameter samples and reconstructs full solutions via projection-based techniques, enabling efficient uncertainty propagation while drastically reducing computational cost. Numerical experiments in high-dimensional stochastic settings demonstrate that accurate statistical estimates of epidemic observables can be obtained with significantly reduced computational costs compared to standard approaches. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Gao B.; Gao S.; Wang X.; Xiang L.; Yuan Y.; Liu Y.
Title: A SIQOR dynamical model for rumor propagation in online social networks with coupled banning and debunking
Abstract: Online social networks (OSNs) often face a counterintuitive challenge during rumor outbreaks: regulatory suppression, such as node-level banning, can paradoxically amplify dissemination. Existing models largely neglect these cascading behavioral responses. To accurately simulate this dynamic and provide a mechanistic interpretation of the Streisand effect, the SIQOR rumor propagation model is proposed in this paper. Moving beyond traditional frameworks, the SIQOR model captures the interaction between platform-level intervention and user behavioral responses, specifically emphasizing how banning stimulates a state of heightened willingness to disseminate the rumor and curiosity among neighboring users. Following theoretical analysis of the system’s dynamic behavior, the model is validated through numerical experiments on synthetic scale-free networks and empirically verified using four real-world Twitter datasets. The results faithfully reproduce the peak scale and long-tail decay of actual rumor outbreaks. Crucially, while raising the baseline banning rate monotonically suppresses the peak scale of active spreaders, aggressive early-stage interventions subject to capacity limits conditionally trigger a non-monotonic surge in propagation desire among neighboring users, demonstrating that raising the banning probability mechanically triggers a non-linear surge in propagation desire, thereby proving that the Streisand effect is a predictable dynamical outcome rather than a mere behavioral anomaly. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Zhao X.; Huang H.; Bai N.; Chen Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang M.; Lu Y.
Title: From perceived attractiveness to visitation: Multi-scale measurement and influencing factors across 143 Chinese historic cities
Abstract: Effective tourism management requires understanding how attraction attributes and supporting factors shape tourists’ perceived attractiveness, and how these in turn translate into visitation. We develop a tourist-centered framework using 610,136 reviews across 2128 heritage attractions in 143 cities, measuring multi-scale perceived attractiveness with a large language model pipeline and visitation with review volume, then identifying the factors that influence both metrics using XGBoost and SHAP. Results show that (1) perceived attractiveness and visitation share a multi-core spatial structure, while visitation displays a polarized long-tail distribution; (2) attraction attributes, especially official designation, visual quality, and ticket pricing, dominate both metrics but shape them differently; (3) positively perceived social, economic, scientific, historic and aesthetical values increase visitation, whereas political value is negatively associated; and (4) accessibility and spatial agglomeration also contribute positively. Practically, multi-scale benchmarking identifies underperforming attractions, while attraction-scale value profiles and the identified influencing factors guide targeted strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effect of hemp protein isolate on the quality and in vitro digestion of high moisture plant-based meat
Abstract: Plant-based meat (PBM) offers high protein, low fat, and cholesterol-free benefits, yet optimizing its nutritional and functional quality remains a challenge. This study incorporated hemp protein isolate (HPI) into soy protein–wheat gluten blends to produce PBM via high-moisture extrusion, examining HPI effects on quality, structure, digestibility, and bioactivity. Results showed that HPI improved mechanical properties, color, and fiber formation; at 40% HPI, disulfide bonds peaked, enhancing water-holding capacity and network density. During in vitro digestion, HPI reduced α-helix/β-sheet ratios and increased random coils, facilitating enzyme access. Protein digestibility peaked at 30% HPI (48.47% gastric, 84.52% intestinal), yielding more small peptides. Although total peptide counts dropped, 28 unique HPI-derived peptides appeared, with six predicted in silico as potential α-glucosidase inhibitors. Moderate HPI addition thus improves PBM quality and digestibility while offering potential bioactivity, providing a theoretical basis for functional PBM development. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Rapid inter-individual vocal interactions in freely behaving rats revealed by acoustic source localization
Abstract: Ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) in rodents have been widely used as indicators of affective states; however, their role in rapid temporal exchange between individuals remains largely unexplored, primarily due to technical limitations in identifying vocalizing individuals during free social interactions. Here, we combined acoustic source localization (USVCAM) with markerless multi-animal tracking to examine the temporal structure of vocal interactions in freely behaving rat dyads. In three dyads with sufficient vocal output, inter-individual vocalization intervals exhibited a clear peak at approximately 50–250 ms, indicating fast temporal exchanges of vocalizations between individuals. To test whether this pattern could arise from independent vocal production, we performed Monte Carlo randomized simulations based on empirically observed intra-individual intervals. The simulated distributions failed to reproduce the empirical peak and instead showed a concentration at shorter intervals, resulting in a significant distributional difference. These results reject the null hypothesis of independent vocal generation and suggest that the observed temporal structure reflects the influence of one individual's vocalizations on those of the other individual. Together, these findings extend the potential applications of rodent USVs, in addition to their established use as affective indicators, by providing a proof-of-principle demonstration of rapid inter-individual vocal exchanges and a tractable experimental framework for investigating the temporal dynamics of social vocal communication. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Shared regulatory systems in memory suppression and fear extinction: An ALE and MACM meta-analysis
Abstract: Memory suppression and fear extinction both reduce the influence of past experiences on current cognition and behavior, but they are typically studied within separate research traditions. The present study examined whether these two processes recruit partially overlapping neural systems involved in the regulation of unwanted memories and previously threat-associated cues. We conducted a preregistered coordinate-based meta-analysis of fMRI studies using activation likelihood estimation (ALE) and meta-analytic connectivity modeling (MACM). The analysis included 63 experiments involving 1452 participants and focused on contrasts commonly used to index retrieval suppression in the Think/No-Think paradigm and threat-cue processing during extinction learning. ALE revealed convergent activation in bilateral inferior frontal gyrus/anterior insula and right inferior parietal lobule. MACM further showed that these regions were embedded within broader executive-control and attention-related coactivation networks. These findings suggest that memory suppression and fear extinction partially converge within broader control- and attention-related systems involved in controlling task-relevant memory and threat representations. At the same time, partly distinct medial temporal and affective-learning patterns point to important domain-specific differences between intentional episodic retrieval suppression and extinction-based threat–safety updating. Overall, the findings help bridge research on memory control and fear extinction by identifying partially overlapping regulatory systems while preserving important theoretical distinctions between the two processes. This framework highlights how control- and attention-related neural systems may contribute to the regulation of unwanted memories and conditioned fear responses through their interactions with memory, threat-learning, and contextual updating processes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Bi-level optimization of harmonic mitigation and energy trading in distribution networks with connected microgrids using PV-inverters and active power filters
Abstract: The widespread deployment of power electronic-based devices in modern distribution networks introduces significant power quality challenges, necessitating effective mitigation strategies at the distribution level. This paper proposes a novel bi-level optimization framework that coordinates a Local Energy Market (LEM) and a Local Harmonic Market (LHM) for interconnected microgrids (MGs), enabling simultaneous energy management and collaborative harmonic mitigation using PV inverters and Active Power Filters (APFs). The proposed framework is validated on modified IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 123-bus distribution systems. Simulation results demonstrate compliance with the IEEE 519 harmonic standard while establishing an incentive-based harmonic market that transfers the economic responsibility for harmonic mitigation to the Distribution System Operator (DSO), increasing its expenditure by 15.3% while creating additional revenues for participating MGs. Moreover, the distributed optimization achieves solutions within 4.86% of the centralized optimum while reducing computational time by approximately 60%, confirming its computational efficiency and scalability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Comparing neural signatures of risky decision-making and guaranteed reward processing using a modified Balloon Analogue Risk Task and multi-echo imaging
Abstract: Risky decision making is a fundamental human behavior involving multiple cognitive processes. Understanding how these processes are represented in the brain offers critical insights into decision-making, development, and vulnerabilities to psychopathology. However, functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) research of decision-making under risk and reward often does not clearly distinguish between risky decision processes and response to guaranteed reward and has limited sensitivity to deep subcortical regions, constraining our contributions. In this study, we present a modified Balloon Analogue Risk Task completed under a multi-echo fMRI protocol meant to enhance subcortical signal. Forty-eight participants inflated virtual balloons across three conditions: risky reward, guaranteed reward, and neutral. GLM analyses revealed increased signal in orbitofrontal cortex, anterior insula (AI), striatum and a brain stem nuclei, ventral tegmental area (VTA), during risky reward decision versus guaranteed rewards conditions. Multivariate analysis identified the AI as a key predictor of the risky decision condition, outperforming striatal and VTA contributions. These results suggest risky decision-making shows greater recruitment of reward-relevant regions and illuminates putative neurobiological mechanisms associated with risky decision making relative to guaranteed and non-contingent reward. The study also provides a new tool to enhance the resolution of human neuroscience research on risk-taking across the lifespan and vulnerabilities to psychopathology. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Miyagawa, Hiroshi (7102604041); Suzuoki, Tetsunori (6602517476)
Title: Exhaust emission control strategies for lean-burn NH3/H2-fueled spark ignition engines
Abstract: Ammonia-fueled engines are attracting increasing interest as a carbon-free energy conversion technology; however, their exhaust typically contains unburned ammonia (NH3), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and nitrous oxide (N2O), and achieving their simultaneous removal under oxygen-rich conditions remains a major challenge. This study investigates emission control strategies using SCR catalyst for a NH3/H2-fueled spark-ignition engine, with emphasis on the linkage between engine-out exhaust characteristics and SCR performance. Engine experiments demonstrate that the engine-out ammonia-to-NOx ratio (ANR) can be systematically controlled through mixture composition, specifically via the equivalence ratio and H2 energy fraction, providing a practical control index for aftertreatment. Using Fe- and Cu-zeolite SCR catalysts, ANR-dependent conversion characteristics are quantified over a wide temperature range. Both catalysts exhibit a temperature-dependent optimal ANR at which near-complete simultaneous removal of NH3 and NOx is achieved, reflecting competition between SCR reactions and NH3 oxidation. To address sensitivity to ANR variability, two complementary and distinct approaches are demonstrated: (i) a control-based strategy employing periodic ANR swing to exploit NH3 storage in zeolite catalysts, and (ii) a catalyst-design-based strategy using a tandem Fe/Cu SCR configuration. Both approaches achieve catalyst-out NH3 and NOx concentrations below 10 ppm. For the tested Fe/Cu tandem system at a nominal catalyst-inlet gas temperature of 450 °C, simultaneous high NH3 and NOx conversions were observed at all tested ANR points between 1.25 and 1.62. In addition, the effects of catalyst configuration and temperature on N2O formation and decomposition are clarified, highlighting trade-offs between operational robustness and greenhouse gas mitigation. The results present proof-of-concept emission-control approaches under the selected steady-state conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Effects of ambient temperature on flame propagation characteristics of methanol spray-hydrogen explosions
Abstract: Methanol-hydrogen fuel forms explosive spray droplet clouds during storage and transport. Therefore, understanding the propagation characteristics of spray flames is crucial for safe application. This study systematically investigates the impact of ambient temperature, methanol concentration, and hydrogen addition on flame propagation characteristics and reaction kinetics. A spray combustion model was developed and validated against experimental data. The results indicated that hydrogen addition played a dominant role in the variations of flame structure and explosion intensity. Compared with pure methanol spray combustion, the flame with 10.0 % hydrogen addition exhibited a smooth and symmetric structure, resembling that of a premixed gas‑phase flame. Its average propagation speed reached 3.04 times that of the pure methanol case, and the explosion index increased by 223.38 %. Ambient temperature had a non‑monotonic effect on flame propagation. At excessively high temperatures, the evaporative cooling of methanol suppressed combustion. Chemical kinetic analysis showed that the H-abstraction pathways R84 and R85 dominated methanol consumption, while R1 and R30 had the strongest inhibitory effect on flame temperature. This paper clarifies the combined effects of ambient temperature and hydrogen addition on methanol spray explosions, providing a theoretical basis for the safe storage and risk management of blended fuels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Interface-tuned Janus-type high-entropy heterostructures for cascade electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Abstract: High-entropy materials (HEMs) hold great promise for electrocatalytic applications owing to their tunable electronic structures, particularly in complex reactions involving multiple intermediates. However, HEMs prepared by conventional methods often suffer from a trade-off between site diversity and reaction specificity, resulting in limited catalytic efficiency. In this study, we address this challenge by developing a Janus-type high-entropy alloy/high-entropy layered hydroxide (HEA/HELH) heterostructure with synthetically controllable interfaces via Fe3 +-mediated topochemical reconstruction with precisely controlled reconstruction times of 30–120 min. Leveraging the Fe3+/Fe2+ redox-driven carbon-confined galvanic replacement reaction, we achieved epitaxial interfacial growth and formed a built-in electric field (BIEF) with a work-function difference of 0.54 eV, which lowered the potential required to reach 10 mA cm⁻² by 240 mV. The optimized HEA/HELH heterostructure delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 93.5% for FDCA at 1.55 V vs. RHE and retains more than 90% of its current response over 100 h, comparing favorably with recently reported HMFOR electrocatalysts. Mechanistic studies suggest that interfacial charge redistribution associated with the BIEF facilitates the formation and utilization of high-valence Co/Ni/Fe species, thereby promoting cascade oxidation from HMF to FDCA. Furthermore, the controllable HEA/HELH demonstrates significant potential for broader adaptability in multistep electrocatalytic oxidation. This work provides an interfacial engineering strategy for designing high-entropy catalysts for electrocatalytic biomass valorization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Evaluating Mild Cognitive Impairment using large language models: A comparative analysis
Abstract: This study evaluates whether fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support preliminary screening of Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) from transcribed Chinese speech. Using the Chinese subset of the TAUKADIAL/TalkBank connected-speech dataset, we compared Llama3, Gemma, Qwen, and Qwen1.5 models under supervised fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, different quantization settings, automatic speech recognition systems, and prompt styles. The experiments were evaluated with subject-level five-fold cross-validation and reported with mean and standard deviation for accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall. Among the tested configurations, Llama3-8B with 4-bit QLoRA achieved the strongest performance, with accuracy and F1-score of approximately 0.86. To place these results against transparent alternatives, we added the official TAUKADIAL feature-based benchmarks, which use acoustic eGeMAPS features and interpretable linguistic measures such as token count, type count, type–token ratio, lexical density, and verb and pronoun ratios. Because the official benchmark uses a different multilingual train/test protocol, it is treated as an external reference rather than a head-to-head ranking. The findings suggest that LLM-based transcript analysis may be useful as a low-cost prescreening aid, but the small, language-specific dataset and lack of matched external validation require cautious interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xie F.; Huang X.; Chen Z.; Xu Z.; Wu Z.; Li Y.; Bai S.; Yang R.; Xue J.; Yang Z.; Xiong X.
Title: Unraveling the multi-stage damage evolution in architected SiC/SiC composite claddings via quasi-in-situ X-ray computed tomography
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: While multi-layered SiC/SiC composites are essential for accident-tolerant fuels, linking structural architecture to damage evolution remains critical. This study evaluates hoop tensile failure across single-layer, duplex, and triplex claddings using quasi-in-situ XCT, Raman, and EBSD. Results reveal that macroscopic failure is governed by spatial defect distribution, residual stresses, and interlayer. Single-layer claddings exhibit flaw-sensitive failure influenced by the distribution of radially aligned pores. Duplex claddings achieve the highest strength via disrupted defect continuity, favorable compressive residual stresses, and polymorphic (6H/2H-SiC) boundaries that force tortuous crack pathways. Conversely, the triplex architecture exhibits a distinct mechanical trade-off: inner tensile stresses and a thickened PyC interlayer slightly reduce peak strength but trigger extensive interfacial debonding, yielding remarkable pseudo-ductility and damage tolerance. These insights highlight that managing structural architecture and residual stress is critical for optimizing multi-layered SiC/SiC composite claddings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Birdsong with gentle wind selectively benefits stimulus interference but not response or multisource interference: Evidence from EEG
Abstract: Despite the growing threat of urban noise pollution to cognitive health, empirical evidence regarding the cognitive benefits of natural sounds remains mixed. The Specificity Hypothesis addresses this by proposing that such benefits are selective, benefiting only those cognitive functions that are highly matched with directed attention. Interference control is a cognitive function closely linked to directed attention and comprises three types: stimulus interference, response interference, and multisource interference. These types differ in their relationship with directed attention. However, whether natural sounds produce differential effects on distinct types of interference control remains unclear. The present study employed electroencephalography to examine the effects of natural sounds such as birdsong with gentle wind on distinct types of interference control. Thirty-nine participants performed the multi-source interference task while listening to either birdsong with gentle wind or an urban sound dominated by machine noise, with electroencephalography recorded simultaneously. Behavioral results showed no significant differences between the two sound stimuli across any type of interference control. Neurophysiological results revealed that birdsong with gentle wind significantly enhanced alpha oscillations, N200, and N450 amplitudes in the stimulus interference condition, whereas no significant changes in any neural measure were observed in the response interference or multisource interference conditions. Exploratory correlation analyses suggested that the enhancements of N200 and N450 were correlated with behavioral improvement in stimulus interference. These findings indicate that birdsong with gentle wind selectively supports the resolution of stimulus interference, while it does not significantly modulate response interference or multisource interference in the current experimental conditions. This finding suggests that future soundscape design should reconsider the general utility of this type of natural sound and pay more attention to the alignment between the cognitive demands of the task context and its benefits. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang Y.; Li X.
Title: Adaptive PSO for consensus optimization oriented to trust-consensus inconsistency correction and personalized guidance
Abstract: In social network group decision-making (GDM) based on fuzzy preference relations (FPR), trust among decision-makers (DMs) dominates the efficiency of opinion convergence. Traditional particle swarm optimization (PSO) has inherent drawbacks when applied to the consensus reaching process (CRP), and existing research has three limitations: static trust weights lack quantitative correction methods for trust-consensus inconsistency, unified consensus guidance fails to generate differentiated adjustment targets based on preference similarity and dynamic consensus contributions, the personal historical optimum of classical PSO becomes invalid, and undifferentiated global guidance easily traps the algorithm in local optima. This paper adopts PSO instead of other algorithms because of its one-to-one particle-DM correspondence, interpretable updating rules and good compatibility with multi-round CRP iterations. To retain PSO’s strengths and address the local optimum problem, a three module collaborative optimization framework is proposed, including the trust-consensus inconsistency correction mechanism, consensus-oriented adaptive weighted aggregation mechanism, and reconstructed improved PSO. The first module identifies inconsistent trust via bidirectional ranking of trust degrees and consensus levels to ensure trust weights match the consensus reliability of DMs. The second module constructs a dual aggregation structure driven by similarity and consensus to produce exclusive personalized guiding opinions for each DM. The third module reconstructs the PSO updating paradigm and adopts consensus progress adaptive inertia weights and learning factors to balance global exploration. The three modules operate in closed-loop collaboration: calibrating trust weights, generating customized guidance, and adaptively updating preferences. Experimental results indicate that the proposed framework achieves faster consensus convergence and lower adjustment costs under the tested settings, providing a promising intelligent solution for complex decision-making tasks in social network analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Opportunities for mathematical reasoning within teacher-student interactions in a Thinking Classroom context
Abstract: Developing students’ capacity to reason mathematically is a key aim of mathematics teaching. However, how such reasoning is supported remains complex. This study examines teacher-student interaction and students’ opportunities for mathematical reasoning in a Thinking Classroom context. While Thinking Classroom is designed to increase student engagement and mathematical thinking through substantial changes to classroom organisation, relatively little is known about how teacher-student interaction unfolds within this instructional context. The study draws on 34 video recordings from five upper secondary mathematics classrooms implementing the first three practices of the teaching approach Thinking Classroom, which concern task selection, random group formation, and work at vertical non-permanent surfaces. A thematic analysis of 124 teacher-student interactions identified four recurring patterns of interaction. Drawing on selected concepts from a complex dynamic systems perspective, these patterns are interpreted as relatively stable. The analysis further examines the students' opportunities for reasoning within these patterns. Opportunities for mathematical reasoning differed across the four patterns and often remained brief, even in interactions where reasoning was most visible. Authors: Wang L.; Wu X.; Sun Z.; Dou Y.
Title: Physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling for temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals
Abstract: Temporal localization in structured multichannel acoustic signals, such as first-arrival picking in geophysical logging, is a fundamental yet challenging task. Traditional signal processing methods rely heavily on manual heuristics, while existing data-driven deep learning approaches often overlook the inherent physical priors of multichannel arrays, resulting in a trade-off among accuracy, stability, and real-time performance in field applications. To address these challenges, we propose FA-Picker, a physics-constrained spatiotemporal modeling framework for first-arrival picking. This model explicitly incorporates the depth dimension to construct a three-dimensional input data volume, enabling the capture of joint spatiotemporal features across multiple receivers and consecutive measurements. Moreover, an end-to-end multi-task architecture is designed, where coarse first-arrival segmentation guides continuous arrival-time regression. A dual-constraint mechanism is introduced, combining soft loss-based guidance with hard physical constraints, ensuring that the localized temporal points strictly comply with the underlying wave propagation laws. Furthermore, to alleviate the scarcity of high-quality labeled data, we exploit the highly structured characteristics of multichannel acoustic arrays to develop a comprehensive synthetic data generation workflow that simulates diverse formation variations and acquisition environments. Experimental results on field datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed modeling and data augmentation strategies, showing the superior performance of FA-Picker in practical first-arrival picking tasks. Title: Non-progressive influence maximization in temporal social networks
Abstract: The influence maximization (IM) problem involves identifying a set of key individuals in a social network who can maximize the spread of influence through their network connections. In this paper, we focus on the temporal non-progressive IM problem, which considers the temporal nature of real-world social networks and the special case where the influence diffusion is non-progressive, i.e., nodes can be activated multiple times. While influence diffusion in many real-world social network scenarios is non-progressive, such as in marketing campaigns promoting updated products and public health campaigns promoting healthier lifestyle choices, this problem has received limited attention in prior research. We first extend an existing diffusion model to capture the non-progressive influence diffusion in temporal social networks. We then propose a method, named TNIMRL, which employs deep reinforcement learning and temporal graph embedding to solve the temporal non-progressive IM problem. In particular, we propose a novel algorithm that effectively leverages temporal graph embedding to capture the changes in temporal social networks and seamlessly integrates with deep reinforcement learning. The extensive experiments on different types of real-world social networks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Acierno S.G.; Apuzzo C.; Lancia A.; Erto A.
Title: Critical assessment of the multifaceted impact of in-situ water removal on CO2 hydrogenation to methanol in membrane reactors
Abstract: The thermodynamic limitation of CO2 hydrogenation to methanol remains a bottleneck for intensified e-methanol production. A kinetic–thermodynamic analysis assessed the potential of in-situ water removal for enhancing methanol synthesis and whether the theoretical benefits of selective dehydration can be preserved under realistic membrane-separation conditions. A catalytic packed-bed reactor (PBR) was adopted as a reference system, followed by an idealized point-wise water-removal benchmark and zeolite membrane-assisted reactor configurations with different transport characteristics. The reaction system was described using a one-dimensional pseudo-homogeneous plug-flow coupled with the Vanden Bussche–Froment kinetic model for methanol synthesis over a Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalyst. Membrane-assisted configurations combined reaction kinetics on the retentate side with permeance-based membrane transport. A highly water-selective NaA membrane and a steam-selective SOD-type membrane with appreciable reactant co-permeation were considered to evaluate the impact of non-ideal permeation and reactant losses. The reference PBR exhibited the trade-off between increasing CO2 conversion and enhanced CO formation at higher temperatures. The idealized benchmark showed that selective dehydration can relax equilibrium constraints and enhance methanol yield, particularly at high water-removal levels. However, comparison with realistic membrane-assisted systems revealed that these gains depend on the balance between water removal and reactant retention. The NaA membrane provided the best performance, achieving a methanol yield of 23.8% at 250 °C and ΔP = 30 bar, whereas SOD-based configurations suffered from H2 and CO2 co-permeation losses that partially offset benefits of water extraction. Overall, membrane-assisted methanol synthesis is advantageous only when water-removal capacity is balanced by sufficient reactant retention within the catalytic environment. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Evolution and Uses of Rock Art Sites: Contribution of Morphogenic Mapping of Rock Walls
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: In this article, we present a new method for investigating rock art within the framework of site morphogenesis. Although numerous surveys of paintings and engravings have been conducted in archaeology since the twentieth century, few have taken into account the geomorphological characteristics of rock surfaces and their morphogenic evolution. Yet the processes responsible for these transformations directly interact with rock art. This approach therefore raises several questions: have the sites and their rock surfaces always been accessible? If not, from when until when were they accessible? Beyond parietal paintings and engravings, are there other traces of human activity? How are these related to the rock art? The method developed, based on the general geomorphological ground mapping’s codes, has been adapted for the analysis of painted and engraved rock walls at different spatial scales. The results demonstrate the relevance of such morphogenetic analysis of rock walls for the understanding of painted and engraved archaeological sites. At Rocher du Château (France, Savoie), phases of the rock wall’s evolution have been identified, which enable discussions about Neolithic and proto-historic frequentations contemporaneity with rock paintings, and their accessibility through time. At Bruguier rock shelter (France, Gard), seven phases of human activity, that are not visible on the ground, and numerous modifications were identified on the rock wall. The methodological and cartographic framework presented in this paper is grounded in an integrative approach to the study of evolving rock walls. Geomorphological analysis sheds light on the physical changes affecting the rock wall before, during, and after (pre)historic human occupation, while the cartographic framework is intended to be further developed through interdisciplinary collaboration. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Adaptive time-period discretization for multi-period scheduling of gaseous energy systems in steel enterprises
Abstract: Multi-period scheduling of gaseous energy systems in steel enterprises commonly relies on Equal Time-Period Discretization (ETPD), which involves an inherent trade-off between discretization accuracy and computational efficiency. Coarse discretization may accumulate storage deviations and cause safety violations, whereas fine discretization significantly increases the computational burden. To address this issue, this study proposes Adaptive Time-Period Discretization (ATPD), a time-representation and inventory-safety enhancement framework that adaptively partitions continuous-time supply–demand parameters based on cumulative storage deviation. Specifically, ATPD decouples the adaptive parameter grid from the uniform decision-variable grid and incorporates the deviation bound as a compensation margin in the storage safety constraints, thereby directly linking discretization accuracy to physical safety. The proposed method is validated through a case study on oxygen and byproduct gas scheduling using real-world data from a steel enterprise. Compared with ETPD, ATPD achieves more accurate parameter fitting, eliminates storage safety violations via deviation-bound compensation, and improves computational efficiency by over tenfold while maintaining a comparable model size. The results demonstrate that ATPD effectively balances discretization accuracy, storage safety, and computational efficiency in gaseous energy scheduling. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Beyond technological determinism: A multidimensional framework and research agenda for consumer trust in blockchain applications
Abstract: Blockchain technology is increasingly integral to domains such as finance, supply chain, commerce and tourism, yet consumer trust remains a pivotal barrier to its widespread adoption. Studies on trust in blockchain contexts have significant conceptual and contextual limitations that inhibit a holistic understanding of trust formation. In this study, we draw on the antecedents, decisions, outcomes and theory, context, methods (ADO-TCM) framework to systematically review 53 high-quality multidisciplinary studies. We identify three critical issues: (1) technological determinism that conflates technical capability with consumer trust, marginalising psychological, social and institutional factors; (2) theoretical convergence around acceptance models that obscures blockchain-specific trust phenomena; and (3) a narrow geographic and domain scope that creates self-reinforcing knowledge hierarchies limiting generalisability across applications and cultures. To address these gaps, we propose a multidimensional trust framework integrating three dimensions: technological architecture trust, information source trust and social actor trust, reflecting blockchain's sociotechnical structure. Central to this framework is a four-paradigm typology that classifies trust into interpersonal, technology, institutional, and sociotechnical perspectives, revealing that the prevalence of technological determinism reflects theoretical inertia rather than genuine consensus. We complement this with three research themes: multi-level theoretical integration, innovative methodologies and contextual expansion. This study contributes to the information systems discourse by providing a theoretical foundation for understanding trust in complex sociotechnical systems beyond acceptance models. By conceptualising consumer trust as a dynamic, multidimensional construct shaped by interactions between users, technology, and institutions, we offer a research agenda with actionable directions for advancing blockchain trust theory and practice. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Leveraging concept-cognitive learning to identify maximum s-defective cliques in network systems
Abstract: Detecting maximum s-defective cliques and cohesive subgraphs tolerating up to s missing edges is crucial for analyzing noisy and dynamic networks, but due to its NP-hardness, it remains challenging, leading to poor time efficiency and difficulties in dynamic scenarios. To address this problem, this study introduces a novel framework that leverages Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) under the paradigm of Concept-Cognitive Learning (CCL). This paper presents a theoretical proof that any maximum s-defective clique can be derived by expanding an equiconcept, which refers to a clique structure with equal intension and extension, and with at most s vertices, thereby ensuring detection completeness. Based on this, we develop two algorithms: a static method SFDC and an incremental method IFDC. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach typically achieves 10x to 100x speedups over state-of-the-art methods in both static and dynamic settings, with particularly strong performance in high-defect and dynamic environments. A case study further illustrates the practical utility of our method in extracting meaningful cohesive structures from real networks. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Highly active Ni-Co catalyst on hybrid MWCNT-Graphene nanoplatelet catalysts for ammonia decomposition
Abstract: Ammonia decomposition offers a promising route for on-demand hydrogen production. However, the large-scale use of non-noble metal catalysts is limited by their low activity and poor stability at low temperatures. In this study, a series of monometallic Ni, Co and bimetallic Ni-Co catalysts supported on a hybrid multi-walled carbon nanotube-graphene nanoplatelet were synthesised via impregnation. This study examined how changes in the Ni-Co ratio affect the properties and performance of the catalysts. The catalysts were carefully analysed using XRD, N2 physisorption, CO chemisorption, H2-TPR, H2-TPD, N2-TPD, NH3-TPD, SEM, and TEM. They were then tested for NH3 decomposition at a weight hourly space velocity of 12,000 mL/gcat.h. The results showed that increasing Co content increased the surface area, metal dispersion, and reducibility, while lowering the adsorption and desorption energies for H2, N2, and NH3. The 2.5Ni-7.5Co catalyst had the highest surface area (166.8 m2/g), the best metal dispersion (8.39%), the smallest crystallite size (7.27 nm), and the lowest desorption temperatures and energies for H2, N2, and NH3. It reached 78% NH3 conversion at 500°C and 99% at 550°C, and remained stable for 24h. These findings show that the combination of Ni and Co, along with conductive carbon supports, is important for making efficient, long-lasting, non-noble-metal catalysts for low-temperature NH3 decomposition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Intellectual overconfidence and susceptibility to anti-science misinformation
Abstract: Anti-science misinformation can undermine trust in science, and understanding who is most susceptible is important for combatting its influence. One relevant trait is Intellectual Humility (IH), associated with greater understanding of science and the reasoning skills required to reject misinformation. Three pre-registered experimental studies (total N = 1604) examined IH and susceptibility to anti-science misinformation in the context of consumer genetic testing. A central subscale of IH – Lack of Intellectual Overconfidence – emerged as the strongest predictor, with intellectually overconfident individuals most susceptible to misinformation, though effect sizes were modest. The final study introduced a warning-label intervention that had a small positive effect on reduced susceptibility to misinformation about genetic testing companies, but only for participants with less intellectual overconfidence, suggesting that those who would benefit most from such interventions may be least likely to do so. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Registered Report Stage I: Signaling green, securing greenbacks: Sustainability claims and venture funding in hospitality & tourism start-ups
Abstract: Tourism's sustainable transition increasingly depends on startups capable of scaling credible innovations. Yet to lead this transformation, they must convince investors that sustainability claims reflect genuine commitment rather than symbolism. This study tests whether, and under what conditions, startups' sustainability communication on X (Twitter) attracts external funding. Integrating signaling and legitimacy theory, we argue that costly, externally validated messages (e.g., stakeholder collaborations or investment-backed actions) enhance pragmatic legitimacy and capital inflow. Analyzing 3869 startups across 94 countries, we link few-shot-classified social-media posts with Crunchbase funding data using a multilevel hurdle model. Title: The adopter's conundrum: Institutional drivers and performance outcomes of innovation in travel distribution
Abstract: This paper investigates the link between institutionally driven innovation and firm performance within the travel distribution sector. Focusing on the adoption of the New Distribution Capability (NDC), we employ a Difference-in-Differences (DID) methodology on a proprietary dataset of travel agency sales spanning four years. The results provide causal evidence that adoption leads to improved sales performance. Moreover, we identify a clear premium for early adoption, with dynamic effects accelerating over time, indicating that firms faster to adopt obtain superior results. Title: The social implications of classroom seats: replicating and extending previous findings on seating arrangements and peer status
Abstract: This preregistered replication study examined how physical proximity in the classroom is associated with peer perceptions of social status, specifically likeability and popularity. We aimed to replicate and extend the study by van den Berg and Cillessen (2015) using data from 719 students across 33 elementary classrooms (grades 4–6; Mage = 10.27; 51.6% boys). We applied the Social Relations Model and mixed-effects modeling to examine (1) whether proximity between classmates is concurrently associated with likeability and popularity, (2) whether longitudinal changes in proximity lead to changes in likeability and popularity, (3) whether these findings differ for friends versus non-friends, and (4) whether they depend on how proximity is operationalized. We replicated previous findings by showing that classmates seated closer together concurrently rated each other as more popular and likeable. Furthermore, when given the opportunity to create their own seating arrangements, students placed classmates they found likeable and popular closer to themselves. We extended previous findings by showing that increased proximity between two classmates over time led to an increase in mutual liking, but not perceived popularity. Further, findings did not differ significantly between friends and non-friends. Finally, because extant studies differ in how proximity is measured, we tested an operationalization of proximity in terms of desk clusters. This alternative operationalization produced similar results to its continuous counterpart, highlighting the conceptual and practical value of the current operationalization for future research. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Inside and out: Exploring how internal and external CSR perceptions influence hospitality employees’ service sabotage
Abstract: Although corporate social responsibility (CSR) has been shown to exert positive effects on hospitality organizations and their stakeholders, the interactive effect of internal CSR (ICSR) and external CSR (ECSR) perceptions on employees’ subsequent service behaviors remains unclear. Drawing on social cognitive theory and cue consistency theory, this study aims to explore how the interaction between ICSR and ECSR perceptions influences employees’ service sabotage. Time-lagged data were collected from 366 hotel employees at two time points and analyzed using hierarchical regression. The results indicate that the ICSR × ECSR interaction has a significant effect on employee service sabotage. Specifically, ECSR perceptions suppress service sabotage only when ICSR perceptions are high. This relationship is mediated by perspective taking. Furthermore, corporate reputational identification strengthens the negative effect of perspective taking on service sabotage. This study offers valuable insights for CSR practices in the hospitality industry and points to promising directions for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Handedness, psychological characteristics, and social adaptation among Chinese college students
Abstract: Handedness may be associated with individual differences in information processing, but its implications for social adaptation remain unclear. This cross-sectional study examined associations among handedness type, openness, cognitive flexibility, multitasking preference, and social adaptation in 3798 Chinese college students. Mixed-handed students reported higher openness (η2 = 0.013), cognitive flexibility (η2 = 0.030), and multitasking preference (η2 = 0.007) than right- and left-handed students, with the largest group difference observed for cognitive flexibility. Left- and right-handed students showed broadly similar scores across these characteristics. Social adaptation was positively associated with openness ( r = 0.20), cognitive flexibility ( r = 0.32), and multitasking preference ( r = 0.23). Mixed-handedness was positively associated with openness ( r = 0.11), cognitive flexibility ( r = 0.17), and multitasking preference ( r = 0.08), whereas its association with social adaptation was weaker ( r = −0.04). Overall, these findings suggest that mixed-handedness is associated with a differentiated pattern of adaptation-relevant psychological characteristics, particularly cognitive flexibility and openness. The results highlight modest but potentially informative individual differences linked to handedness and indicate that these differences are more evident in specific psychological characteristics than in overall social adaptation. Title: Structural Determinants of Household Resilience in Earthquake-Affected Communities: A Case Study from Bawean Island
Abstract: This study examines the socioeconomic impacts of the March 2024 earthquake on household resilience in Bawean Island, East Java, Indonesia. Data for this study were collected through a survey with a snowball sampling technique, with a total of 221 valid respondents from affected regions. Using a household survey across 12 affected villages and partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), the study identifies critical factors contributing to household resilience, namely social, economic, human, and physical capital assets. The findings can be explained in two ways. First, the result confirms social, economic, human, and physical capital as critical resilience determinants. Second, higher household resilience could reduce the impact of natural disasters. This study can be an input for policymakers to strengthen household resilience in disaster-prone areas to support sustainable development goals (SDGs). © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: The structure and properties of the solid solution of high temperature piezoelectric ceramics: (1-x)Li0.5Bi2.5Nb2O9-xBi3TiNbO9
Abstract: Bismuth layer-structured piezoelectric ceramics have long faced an inherent trade-off between piezoelectric performance and Curie temperature. A novel solid solution (1-x)Li0.5Bi2.5Nb2O9-xBi3TiNbO9 (denoted as (1-x)LBN-xBTN) was designed and fabricated via a conventional solid-state reaction method to achieve a synergistic improvement in both properties. The (1-x)LBN-xBTN series of ceramics achieved optimal overall performance when x = 0.5: TC = 861 °C, d33 = 13.0 pC/N, ρdc (at 500 °C) = 2.39 × 107 Ω·cm, demonstrating its promise for high-temperature applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Participatory short film production and student well-being: A narrative review from media literacy and sociocultural perspectives
Abstract: In an AI-driven media ecology, short-form video platforms have intensified interest in participatory filmmaking (PFM) as a learner-centered practice in higher education. However, the relationship between student-led short-film production and holistic well-being remains conceptually scattered and methodologically uneven. This narrative review examines how PFM may support student well-being through media literacy and sociocultural learning processes, with particular attention given to the transferability of these mechanisms to Chinese higher education. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2014 and 2025 were searched in Scopus, Web of Science, and CNKI using combinations of “participatory video,” “filmmaking,” “higher education,” and “well-being.” A total of 238 records were screened. Studies were excluded if they focused on non-higher-education settings, addressed media consumption rather than student production, contained no interpretable well-being-related outcomes, or lacked peer-reviewed empirical content. Title: Renewable electricity penetration and retail price dynamics: Global evidence on transitional costs of the energy transition
Abstract: The global expansion of renewable energy represents a structural transformation with profound macroeconomic and financial implications. This study investigates the impact of renewable electricity penetration on retail electricity prices using a multi-country panel. The study employs a comprehensive multi-layered empirical framework to address endogeneity, dynamic adjustment, and cross-country structural heterogeneity. The results reveal that renewable penetration is associated with statistically significant short-to medium-term increases in residential electricity prices. However, this effect is nonlinear and conditional on fossil fuel dependence. Once fossil reliance falls below a critical threshold, the marginal price impact weakens substantially. Distributional evidence shows that renewable price effects are amplified in high-price electricity markets. These findings suggest that renewable expansion generates transitional system costs rather than permanent inefficiencies, highlighting the importance of structural conditions in shaping energy transition outcomes and broader economic stability. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Choi Y.; Choi J.; Shin H.; Lee Y.; Kim C.; Kim C.-K.
Title: Dynamic sequential recommendation via lag-aware graph learning
Abstract: Most existing sequential recommenders implicitly assume that feedback is observed immediately after it occurs. This assumption is often violated in production pipelines, where interaction logs can arrive late due to client buffering or downstream feature computation. As a result, the model input at decision time is frequently a censored and temporally misaligned history. In addition, the delay process is rarely stationary in online services, where it can change across users, items, devices, traffic regimes, and time periods. In this paper, we propose DynaLag, a dynamic framework for sequential recommendation via lag-aware dynamic graph learning. DynaLag represents observed user-item interactions as a time-evolving graph and introduces a learnable time-lag adjacency tensor that explicitly routes information across multiple temporal lags. Our method is designed as a lightweight local architecture: dynamic graphs are updated by event-driven insertion into bounded user and item buffers, and inference uses only adaptive local neighborhoods. Experiments on benchmark sequential recommendation datasets under heavy-tailed simulated logging latency show that DynaLag outperforms strong Transformer and graph-based baselines. Title: Genetic inference in social insects: the continued utility of microsatellites in the sociogenomic era
Abstract: Social insects differ from many other biological systems because colonies function as integrated reproductive, ecological, and evolutionary units, often conceptualized as superorganisms. This organization makes genetic inference inherently hierarchical, often requiring genotyping across multiple biological levels: the colony, the population, the individual, and, in some cases, the cellular level. Although whole-genome sequencing and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based approaches are now widely used in population genomics, microsatellites or short tandem repeats remain a useful approach for cost-effective, low-input, and highly replicated genotyping, particularly in the hierarchical sampling designs common in social insect studies. Here, we review the utility and limitations of microsatellites in social insect research using a three-tiered framework spanning colony-, population-, and individual- or cellular-level analyses. Across these scales, microsatellites are especially valuable for colony delimitation, kinship inference, diagnostic screening of known reproductive systems, and low-input genotyping. By comparing the suitability of microsatellites with that of SNP-based and broader genomic approaches across these applications, this review links marker choice to biological scale, sampling design, and inferential goal in studies of social insects. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: AC-UKAN: An enhanced U-KAN framework integrating modulated deformable convolution and mixed pooling
Abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is pivotal for clinical diagnosis. Segmentation targets in medical images differ in appearance, geometric morphology, and contextual organization, which motivates complementary architectural choices rather than a single universal mechanism. We propose AC-UKAN, a depth-specialized extension of U-KAN that assigns modulated deformable convolution (MDConv) to the shallow encoder for input-conditioned geometric sampling, tokenized Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (Tok-KAN) blocks to the low-resolution semantic stages for an alternative nonlinear parameterization, and a mixed pooling module (MPM) to the bottleneck for combined isotropic and anisotropic context aggregation. AC-UKAN was evaluated on the three heterogeneous two-dimensional binary segmentation benchmarks used by U-KAN: BUSI (breast ultrasound), GlaS (gland histopathology), and CVC-ClinicDB (colonoscopic imaging). For a controlled comparison, eight representative segmentation architectures were trained locally under an identical protocol. AC-UKAN achieved an average IoU of 80.78% and DSC of 88.86% with 6.66 M parameters, improving IoU over the U-KAN baseline by up to 4.04 percentage points on the evaluated splits, with its largest gains on BUSI and CVC. Component ablations showed that MDConv and MPM each provided incremental improvements in overlap-based metrics relative to the baseline and to each other's single-module configuration, whereas their combined effect and boundary-distance behavior varied across datasets. Under the official U-KAN protocol, AC-UKAN therefore offers a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off among the evaluated representative architectures, rather than uniform superiority across all three datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Epistemological bridges: A systematic review of virtual reality for ethnoscience and culturally responsive learning
Abstract: This research is motivated by the increasing use of VR media in science learning. Therefore, this literature review aims to identify, collect, and analyze scientific publications on the use of VR in the context of culture-based science learning and ethos to answer questions regarding the state, trends, and potential of research, as well as its implications for science learning. Following the PRISMA protocol, the literature published between 2016 and 2025 was searched across four primary databases: Google Scholar, CrossRef, Scopus, and ERIC. Among the initial 535 identified records, 12 peer-reviewed articles met the rigorous inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis. The results demonstrate that VR serves as an epistemological bridge, connecting abstract scientific concepts with concrete, indigenous practices. The analysis reveals that the level of VR immersion significantly affects the research methodology: fully immersive VR is predominantly utilized in small-scale qualitative studies focusing on deep experiential learning, whereas semiimmersive and nonimmersive formats offer broader accessibility for larger-scale classroom implementations. Despite persistent technical hurdles and high implementation costs, the findings indicate that VR consistently enhances students' affective and cognitive domains. It fosters heightened cultural awareness, greater appreciation for traditional knowledge, and a sophisticated understanding of the intersection between science and heritage. However, the review highlights a significant geographic concentration of research and a lack of long-term longitudinal data. This study concludes that while the field is currently a specialized niche, there are substantial opportunities for future research to utilize VR as a medium for integrating diverse knowledge systems into science curricula. These findings suggest that integrating ethnoscience through VR can fundamentally improve the quality and inclusivity of global science education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Hemisphere-aware Graph Convolution and 3D Structural Fusion for multi-modal fMRI brain-disorder classification
Abstract: Multimodal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data is a valuable source of information for precisely classifying neurological disorders, which is why it is widely used in the diagnosis of these diseases. However, traditional methods struggle to capture the spatiotemporal dynamics of the brain and single-modality approaches overlook voxel-level structural information. This limits the accuracy of imaging diagnoses of neurological diseases. This study therefore selected resting-state fMRI samples from the Autism Spectrum Disorder (ABIDE) and Parkinson's Disease (PPMI) datasets, proposing the multi-modal half-brain perception framework MSHAGL. This comprises a shared-weight half-brain–whole-brain graph convolutional network (CHW-GCN) and a three-dimensional structure encoder (GBConvNet3D). These are combined with multi-head gated fusion and redundancy suppression loss for joint optimization. Specifically, dynamic maps of the left and right hemispheres and the whole brain are constructed, cross-scale functional connectivity features are extracted, and 3D fMRI volumes are utilized to capture spatial structural patterns. Gating mechanisms achieve dynamic alignment and weighted fusion of temporal-structural features. In classification experiments on the ABIDE and PPMI datasets for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), the results demonstrate that hemispheric perception modelling and multimodal fusion effectively enhance diagnostic sensitivity and robustness while revealing abnormal connectivity and spatial activation patterns related to disease. Title: Dynamic Diffusion of Legal Compliance and Ethical Conduct among Construction Project Owners: An Epidemiological Modeling Approach
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Construction industries worldwide face persistent challenges of ethical misconduct, contractual violations, and regulatory noncompliance, imposing substantial legal liabilities and undermining sustainable development. Although legal frameworks exist to govern owner behavior, their dynamic enforcement effects and interactions with market-driven compliance mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study pioneers the application of epidemiological modeling to legal compliance and ethical behavior diffusion among construction project owners. An extended susceptible-exposed-infected-removed (SEIR) model was developed to analyze how statutory enforcement and voluntary market adoption jointly drive compliance diffusion, simulated via MATLAB. Three findings emerged: (1) the diffusion of ethical behavior exhibits S-shaped evolution with global asymptotic stability, providing a predictable basis for legal intervention design; (2) resistance parameters demonstrate positional asymmetry, revealing where legal safeguards are most needed; and (3) government-mandated enforcement and voluntary adoption generate superlinear synergistic effects, suggesting compliance frameworks achieve maximum efficacy when paired with market incentives. Authors: Zhang Y.; Ye Z.; Cui Z.; Hou Y.
Title: When AI ads violate expectations: the interplay of AI character, product type, and advertising appeal of AI ads on consumer attitudes
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping video advertising production. Using expectancy violations theory as an interpretive lens, this study develops a framework in which ad appeal (rational vs. emotional), product type (high-tech vs. low-tech), and AI character embodiment (no character vs. animal-like vs. human-like) jointly relate to ad attitude and to two appraisals: perceived novelty and perceived uncanniness. This study tests the framework in five between-subjects experiments with consumers recruited from an online panel. Results show that rational appeals outperform emotional appeals in AI-generated ads, especially for low-tech products. Novelty is positively and uncanniness negatively associated with ad attitude, and the indirect effects through both appraisals are consistent with the proposed process. Human-like AI characters amplify uncanniness in emotional low-tech executions. In one rational low-tech execution, an animal-like character lowered uncanniness relative to a no-character baseline, but ad attitude did not differ significantly. The findings extend expectancy-violation theorizing in AI advertising and offer configuration-level design guidance for brands deploying disclosed AI-generated advertising. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The relationship between product-based creativity and ADHD traits in children and the associations with later well-being
Abstract: Creativity is increasingly recognized as a positive aspect among adults with ADHD and those with high ADHD scores, but evidence in youth is limited, particularly regarding product-based creativity. It also remains unclear whether higher creativity benefits the lower well-being typically associated with ADHD traits. This study investigated associations between ADHD traits and product-based creativity in children, as well as longitudinal associations with well-being. Data were sourced from the Twins Early Development Study, a population-based sample of twins. ADHD traits (age 8), product-based creativity (age 9, writing task), and well-being (age 16) of 1,170 children were assessed. Correlation and regression analyses were used to explore the associations of ADHD trait dimensions (inattentiveness and hyperactivity/impulsivity) with writing-based creativity. Moderation analyses were conducted to examine whether this writing-based creativity moderated the association between childhood ADHD traits and later well-being. Additionally, we conducted exploratory analyses on children meeting screening criteria for suspected ADHD. We observed a small negative correlation between inattentiveness and writing-based creativity, which remained significant after controlling for hyperactivity/impulsivity, sex, IQ, reading, and writing. The writing-based creativity did not moderate the negative association between ADHD traits and well-being, nor did we observe differences in well-being between high-creativity and low-creativity groups among children meeting screening criteria for suspected ADHD. Future research utilizing diverse creativity measures beyond writing tasks is warranted to explore the developmental relationship between ADHD traits, creativity, and well-being. Additionally, our results highlight that taking both a creativity-domain-specific and a lifespan perspective is needed when studying and understanding ADHD-related positive aspects. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Emotions in flipped and lecture-based math courses
Abstract: Background: Emotions play an important role in learning. Activating teaching methods, such as flipped learning, can provide positive learning experiences but also pose emotional challenges to students. Aims: This intensive longitudinal study investigated 1) how students’ emotional valence before a learning event, learning mode (individual, peer, teacher-led), teaching implementation (lecture-based vs. flipped), and physiological arousal (electrodermal activity, EDA) during the learning event related to emotional valence after a learning event, and 2) how EDA varies across within-event segments and teaching implementations during learning events. Sample: Participants were 69 students enrolled in an engineering mathematics course implemented either as lecture-based (n = 34) or flipped learning (n = 35). Methods: Students reported their emotional states via a smartphone application and wore smart rings to measure EDA. A series of multilevel binomial logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were analyzed across 546 learning events, totaling 827 h of data. Results: Positive pre-event emotional valence predicted positive post-event emotional valence. Teacher-led events were associated with more positive post-event emotional valence than individual events, particularly in the lecture-based group. The main effect of the teaching implementation was not significant. EDA did not show robust associations with post-event emotional valence; however, lecture-based events showed a clearer decline in EDA across event segments than flipped learning events. Conclusions: The results highlight the importance of supporting social and individual learning processes and examining physiological arousal as a temporal learning-event process rather than a simple proxy for post-event emotional valence. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Newcomers help most after being helped, veterans do not: Evidence from Stack Overflow
Abstract: Whether people who receive help online go on to help others is an open question. Prior observational studies report mixed results, and designs that ignore prior user activity may overstate reciprocity. We develop a matched difference-in-differences survival analysis of over 21 million Stack Overflow questions, comparing users whose questions were answered with propensity-score-matched users whose questions were not. We don't ask broadly whether reciprocity works in general, but locate the narrow conditions under which it affects user behavior. Users whose questions were answered helped others slightly more often (increment at answer arrival, hazard ratio [HR] = 1.049, 95% CI [1.044, 1.054]). The response depended on tenure: new users responded most (HR = 1.071 in the first week, 95% CI [1.056, 1.086]), while the longest-tenured users did not respond measurably. The tenure gradient is the most robust pattern we find. Timing mattered too, though far more fragilely: users answered within 30 to 60 min responded most strongly, while answers under 30 min show no elevation. Most of our data predate 2020, and the generalized reciprocity effect among new users does not survive a split at 2020, so these estimates largely reflect a pre-generative-AI baseline. We review gratitude, moral obligation, social expectation, and incentive displacement as possible psychological mechanisms but cannot measure them. On Stack Overflow, generalized reciprocity is less a general driver of cooperation than a recruitment channel for contributions from new users: designers gain most by getting newcomers’ questions answered. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Mechanism of Dexmedetomidine Regulating the HDAC2/GPX4 Axis in Neurological Deficits in Rats with Acute Cerebral Infarction
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the molecular mechanism by which dexmedetomidine (Dex) alleviates neurological impairment in rats with acute cerebral infarction (ACI) by regulating the HDAC2/GPX4 signaling axis. Methods: An ACI rat model was established using the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) method. Model rats were treated with Dex, the HDAC2 inhibitor SAHA, oe-HDAC2, or the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3. Neurological function was evaluated using neurological deficit scores, while cognitive function was assessed via open field test, three-chamber social interaction test, and novel object recognition test. The enrichment of histone H4K12ac at the GPX4 promoter region was examined by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay. Results: ACI rats exhibited aggravated neurological deficits, severe cognitive impairment, and increased cerebral infarction area, accompanied by a significant upregulation of HDAC2 expression in brain tissues. Dex intervention markedly downregulated HDAC2 expression, suppressed inflammatory cytokine release, alleviated brain injury, and improved cognitive dysfunction in ACI rats. Inhibiting HDAC2 activity exerted protective effects similar to those of Dex, whereas HDAC2 overexpression partially reversed the beneficial effects of Dex on cognitive function in ACI rats. Mechanistically, Dex downregulated HDAC2 to increase H4K12ac enrichment at the GPX4 promoter region, thereby promoting the transcriptional expression of GPX4 and suppressing ferroptosis. Moreover, the protective effects of Dex against brain injury and cognitive impairment in ACI rats were partially abrogated by RSL3. Conclusion: Dex attenuates neurological impairment and reduces ferroptosis in ACI rats by inhibiting HDAC2 expression, which in turn upregulates H4K12ac enrichment at the GPX4 promoter and facilitates GPX4 transcription. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Factors associated with installed photovoltaic capacity in Australia across small, medium, and large-scale systems
Abstract: Australia, as a global leader in photovoltaic deployment, has attracted significant research attention, has attracted significant research attention into factors associated with PV installation patterns. Previous studies have highlighted the role of early adopters, family wealth, and education, and have identified financial parameters (such as investment cost, internal rate of return, and net present value), social parameters (including household income and demographics), and environmental factors as relevant correlates of PV adoption. The results indicate that different system-size categories exhibit distinct association patterns. Small-scale adoption shows higher correlations with electricity prices and unit costs, medium-scale systems are more correlated with income and affordability indicators, and large-scale systems are more correlated with long-term financial returns and market incentives.
