Title: Efficacy of group-based acceptance and commitment therapy in reducing anxiety and improving mental health among adults recovering from COVID-19: a quasi-experimental interventional study
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Background: Survivors of COVID-19 frequently encounter persistent psychological distress. While Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) aims to enhance psychological flexibility, its clinical utility and underlying mechanisms in post-pandemic recovery within diverse cultural contexts require further empirical investigation. Objective: This study evaluated the efficacy of a group-based ACT intervention in alleviating anxiety and promoting psychological well-being and mental health among COVID-19 survivors in Iran. Methods: This study employed a quasi-experimental interventional design with a pretest–posttest and 6-week follow-up assessment, including a control group. Individuals meeting the preliminary eligibility criteria were screened using the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) and the General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28). A total of 40 adults who had recovered from COVID-19 and exhibited clinically significant anxiety and reduced general mental health were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the ACT intervention group (n = 20) or the control group (n = 20). The intervention consisted of eight weekly 90-minute sessions focusing on the core processes of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). Outcomes were assessed using the BAI and GHQ-28 at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at a 6-week follow-up. Results: Analysis of the 36 participants who completed the protocol revealed that the ACT group demonstrated significant and sustained reductions in anxiety and somatic symptoms, alongside marked improvements in social functioning and overall mental health compared to the control group (p < 0.001). These gains were maintained at the 6-week follow-up. High intervention fidelity (90%) and attendance (87%) suggest the feasibility and acceptability of this approach in a post-viral clinical context. Conclusions: Group-based ACT is an efficacious and feasible intervention for addressing the long-term psychological sequelae of COVID-19. The findings support the integration of ACT into rehabilitation programs to enhance resilience and quality of life in survivors. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

Title: A network approach to mapping responsibility in wildfire risk mitigation
Abstract: As wildfire risk escalates in the wildland urban interface/intermix (WUI), creating defensible space clear of flammable fuels is important for wildfire risk mitigation and management. By definition, defensible space is constrained to the property parcel's boundaries and wildfire risk assessments generally focus on individual parcels, but this overlooks any risk in neighboring properties. If we imagine defensible spaces as buffers that cross property boundaries and overlap, neighboring properties may share wildfire risk in the overlapping spaces. However, homeowners may not recognize these overlapping regions and spillover effects of mitigating risk, jeopardizing their properties and, ultimately, the entire neighborhood. To address this issue, we propose a novel paradigm to rethink defensible space management by mapping the homeowner's responsibility to mitigate wildfire risk in overlapping defensible space buffers with respect to their neighbors who may share or owe responsibility to mitigation. First, we develop three new spatial metrics (Personal Responsibility (PR), Shared Responsibility (SR), and Owed Responsibility (OR)) for each homeowner, computed as the product of wildfire risk and the corresponding area of responsibility. Here, we use a fire behavior model to generate rate of spread (ROS) as a measure of wildfire hazard and compute each responsibility metric. Second, we build the metrics into spatial responsibility networks, modeled using all the houses in a given neighborhood with nodes characterized by average PR and with links weighted by average SR (or OR) that are directed to designate who is responsible between neighboring properties. In our study site, we find that SR and OR networks are composed of multiple sub-networks. This information is important to inform homeowners about their individual responsibilities, identify properties with greater responsibility, and gather neighbors with interconnected responsibility. Subsequently, we simulate different mitigation strategies by iteratively removing network links and monitoring how the total responsibility may change in the neighborhood. We use three strategies (random, localized, and targeted) for link removal. Results demonstrate that the targeted strategy (removing links in descending order of highest responsibility) reduces the total responsibility most rapidly and fragments the network into smaller components, concentrating mitigation on the highest-responsibility links. Through this study, we provide a framework for wildfire risk management, which can be used with different metrics and for various neighborhood layouts. Ultimately, the spatial responsibility metrics and networks provide a scalable and spatially-explicit approach to map complex wildfire risk in the WUI, which can help inform defensible space inspections, guide efficient resource allocation, improve neighborhood-level planning, and empower individual homeowners to make more risk-informed decisions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Negotiation and relationships: Insights from adjacent, psychologically-grounded literature
Abstract: Negotiations often unfold within ongoing relationships, making relationships integral to negotiation processes and outcomes. Yet, despite repeated calls for greater attention to relational dynamics, behavioral negotiation research has largely relied on paradigms that minimize the role of relationships. We review research from adjacent, psychologically-grounded literature (e.g., on close relationships, marketing, strategy, and operations) that conceptualize negotiation as embedded within ongoing relationships. We show that negotiations in relationships unfold under distinct starting conditions that shape negotiators’ interpretations, judgments of appropriateness and risk, and the interplay between negotiation processes, outcomes, and the longer-term relationship. As a result, negotiations in relationships often involve managing both objective and relational interests simultaneously, producing beliefs, behaviors, and outcomes that differ from dominant findings in behavioral negotiation research. We conclude by encouraging more dynamic, relationally embedded perspectives and methods that capture how negotiation unfolds across ongoing relationships and repeated interactions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Registered Report - Stage II: Do good, feel luckier: How cause-related marketing in unpredictable tourism products boosts tourists’ purchase intention?
Abstract: Marketing unpredictable tourism experiences like aurora or wildlife viewing poses distinct challenges due to their inherent uncertainty, yet research on effective strategies remains limited. In Stage I of this Registered Report, we proposed that cause-related marketing (CRM) would boost purchase intention for unpredictable tourism products more effectively than traditional discounts by activating a karmic investment mechanism (i.e., self-luck expectancy), especially under consumer-focused framing. Through an eye-tracking experiment, a quasi-experimental field study, and three scenario-based experiments, we found no conclusive evidence that CRM outperforms discounts in increasing purchase intention, nor support for the mediating role of self-luck expectancy. Although a moderating influence of protagonist focus was observed, its effect contradicted our hypothesis. However, an unexpected finding emerged: luck primes significantly elevate self-luck expectancy and enhance purchase intention. These results suggest that practitioners should either exercise caution in deploying standard CRM from a cost-benefit perspective or enhance its utility by fostering deeper consumer moral engagement. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Mapping distribution system operators for electricity and gas around the world

Title: Political elites and access to economic opportunities in China's rural market transition
Abstract: Understanding whether political elites maintain advantages in accessing economic opportunities during market transitions is crucial for assessing the distributional consequences of market-oriented reforms. This study examines whether political status provides rural households with advantages in accessing production resources and income opportunities during China's recent wave of marketization, and how these advantages vary with the degree of market development. Using three waves of the China Family Database spanning 2015–2019 and employing an instrumental variable approach, we find that political elites maintain persistent advantages in accessing economic opportunities. Relative to non-elites, cadre households exhibit 20.1 percentage points higher rates of receiving agricultural subsidies, 38.8 percentage points higher rates of owning agricultural machinery, and 9.7 percentage points greater likelihood of operating nonfarm businesses. As marketization advances, the sources of elite advantage shift from agriculture to commercial activities. While advantages in agricultural production weaken, reflecting reduced state-controlled resource allocation channels, advantages in business operations strengthen consistent with elites converting political capital into entrepreneurial opportunities. Our findings suggest that rural marketization in China reallocates rather than reduces opportunity gaps. This pattern indicates that even as market reforms diminish traditional avenues for political privilege, they simultaneously open new market-based opportunities that preserve elite advantage. These findings have broader implications for understanding how political power influences access to opportunities during market transitions in developing economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Engaging youth in end-of-life care: The 3 Wishes Project experience
Abstract: Background Citizen engagement can create a community of compassion for dying hospitalized patients. Objectives To describe a family co-designed end-of-life intervention engaging schoolchildren, and characterize dying hospitalized patients and their terminal wishes. Methods This cohort study partnered a healthcare organization and educational institution to voluntarily engage students attending senior, middle, junior, and Montessori schools in an end-of-life care program. The 3 Wishes Project involved hospital staff and family members eliciting and implementing wishes to honor dying patients. Age-appropriate engagement involved student-led acts of compassion. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results From June 2024–May 2026, 481 patients were enrolled, aged 65.4 (16.8) [mean (standard deviation)] years. The most common diagnoses were neurologic or neurosurgical (175, 36.4%), cardiovascular or vascular (97, 20.2%) and trauma (59, 12.3%). Of 2305 elicited end-of-life wishes, 2280 (98.9%) were implemented. Personnel eliciting wishes included nurses (169, 35.1%), social workers (152, 31.6%) and the project coordinator (99, 20.6%). Common wishes were tributes and keepsakes (820, 35.6%), acts to humanize the patient (374, 16.2%) and facilitating connections (248, 10.8%). Conclusions Community engagement in this adaptation of the 3 Wishes Project involved family member co-design and student partnership to help with terminal wishes for dying hospitalized patients. Title: International supply chain drivers of forage-livestock conflicts in pastoral China
Abstract: China aims to eliminate forage-livestock conflicts (FLCs) in pastoral areas by 2035 to restore degraded grasslands and address related environmental, social, and economic issues. International trade affects grazing-induced FLCs in pastoral China through global economic supply chains. Here, we examine the crucial foreign consumption drivers, international supply chain paths, and global socioeconomic factors influencing FLCs in pastoral China from 2010 to 2020. The results show that foreign consumption caused two million tons of FLCs in pastoral China in 2020. During 2010–2020, foreign consumption contributed 0.1%–10.4% of FLCs in each pastoral province of China. Inner Mongolia, one of the vital ecological barriers against sandstorms in Asia, underwent a significant increase (92.0%) in its FLCs caused by foreign consumption over the decade. The final production sectors in critical international supply chain paths moved from non-pastoral provinces to foreign economies during 2010–2020. In addition, foreign economic structure transitions led to 660 kt of FLC increments during the decade, where foreign production structure transitions contributed 66.8%. Our findings highlight the importance of optimizing foreign production structures and fostering international cooperation to realize China's goal of FLC elimination. © 2026

Title: Using emojis to uplift emotion: Effects on mental health chatbots’ performance

Abstract: As AI-based chatbots increasingly expand access to mental health support, understanding how text-based systems convey emotional attentiveness without face-to-face nonverbal cues is important. Emojis may serve as lightweight paralinguistic cues, yet their effects in mental health support remain unclear. Drawing on the Stereotype Content Model and psychological ownership theory, this study examines associations between emoji use and users’ emotional well-being, satisfaction, and continuance usage intention. Two scenario-based online experiments were conducted in China using random sampling through Credamo, yielding 459 valid responses (59 in the pretest and 400 in the main study). Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics 26 and the PROCESS macro. Across the experiments, emoji use was associated with more favorable emotional well-being, satisfaction, and continuance usage intention. Mediation analyses supported an indirect pathway through perceived warmth and psychological ownership, whereas the corresponding competence-based pathway was not supported. AI literacy strengthened the perceived warmth–psychological ownership association but, contrary to predictions, weakened the perceived competence–psychological ownership association. Moderated mediation analyses provided preliminary support for AI literacy strengthening the warmth-based indirect effects of emoji use on emotional well-being and continuance usage intention. The corresponding effect on satisfaction was not supported. These findings extend research on AI-mediated mental health support by identifying a warmth–psychological ownership pathway and the differentiated role of AI literacy. Title: How media narratives shape public sentiment toward electric micromobility: Stronger effects for e-scooters than e-bikes
Abstract: Public sentiment toward electric micromobility, particularly e-scooters and e-bikes, is increasingly shaping safety debates and regulatory responses; yet, these attitudes and perceptions have not been systematically evaluated within a unified framework, nor is it clear to what extent they reflect stable judgments versus sensitivity to external narratives. This study addresses these gaps by quantifying public sentiment toward e-bikes and e-scooters and evaluating their responsiveness to controlled negative media narrative exposure. A unified survey framework was developed to enable consistent evaluation, combining statement-based measures with image-based scenario assessments. Two complementary studies were conducted with Australian participants. Study 1 (N = 1027) established baseline sentiment in the absence of media exposure, and Study 2 (N = 1025) examined how responses shift following controlled exposure to negative news headlines. The results showed that public sentiment is multi-dimensional and mixed. While both modes received moderate recognition in terms of sustainability and legitimacy, practical acceptance remained lower, particularly for e-scooters. Exposure to negative media narratives produced broader and more consistent shifts toward less favorable sentiments for e-scooters, especially in perceptions of rider behavior and public-space interaction, whereas e-bike responses remained comparatively stable and more robust to media narrative exposure. In contrast, evaluations of concrete negative situations showed no systematic change following exposure, indicating that these evaluations are grounded in situational interpretation rather than external framing. The findings suggest that public sentiment should be used cautiously to inform policy development. While consistent concerns linked to observable safety issues justify targeted interventions, broader sentiment shifts may reflect narrative influence rather than actual conditions. Effective policy should therefore be informed not only by public sentiment but also by objective evidence on behavior, exposure, and risk. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Professional identity as the missing link: Understanding motivational pathways among hotel employees
Abstract: Hospitality research has often viewed motivation as the primary mechanism linking managerial practices to employee behavior. However, less attention has been paid to how employees interpret such practices before motivational responses emerge. Drawing on professional identity research, this study examines Professional Identity as an interpretive mechanism linking employees’ perceptions of Rewards and Transformational Leadership to Motivation and Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB). Using survey data from 325 frontline hotel employees in South Korea, we test an individual-level model connecting Developmental Rewards, Material Rewards, Transformational Leadership, Professional Identity, Intrinsic Motivation, Extrinsic Motivation, and OCB. The results show significant indirect associations between Developmental Rewards and Intrinsic Motivation and between Transformational Leadership and Intrinsic Motivation through Professional Identity. Developmental Rewards and Transformational Leadership were also indirectly associated with OCB through Professional Identity and Intrinsic Motivation. Title: Spatial optimization of land use for synergizing economic development and carbon neutrality based on an efficiency-driven PLUS model
Abstract: Optimizing land-use allocation is important for achieving regional carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality targets. Existing land-use simulation studies generally incorporate carbon objectives through ex-post assessment or macro-level land-demand optimization, leaving historical grid-level carbon–economic performance disconnected from future spatial allocation. To further address this limitation, we developed LUCE-PLUS, a framework that links grid-scale land-transition accounting and efficiency evaluation with PLUS-based spatial simulation. Using Jiujiang City, China, as a case study, we quantified conversion costs, economic-output changes, and carbon emissions induced by observed land-use transitions from 2010 to 2020 at a 30-m resolution. A single-stage mixed-integer linear programming super-efficiency range-adjusted measure (Sup-RAM) model treated carbon emissions as a weakly disposable undesirable output and enabled discrimination among efficient grid-level transition units while ensuring Pareto-efficient projections. The resulting surfaces of economic efficiency and carbon–economic synergy efficiency were incorporated into PLUS as scenario-specific predictors of land-use expansion probabilities. Land-use patterns in 2030 were simulated under natural-development, economic-dominant, and carbon–economic dual-objective scenarios while aggregate land demand and planning constraints were held constant. Mean carbon–economic synergy efficiency was 20.5% lower than mean economic efficiency, indicating that economic efficiency alone may understate the carbon-related environmental costs of land-use transitions. Compared with the dual-objective scenario, the economic-dominant scenario increased the projected GDP increment by only 0.04% but raised land-use-change-induced carbon emissions by 7.3%. Impervious-land expansion under the dual-objective scenario also showed a stronger tendency toward locations associated with lower carbon-stock losses. LUCE-PLUS therefore provides a performance-informed approach to low-carbon spatial allocation under fixed land-demand targets. From an environmental impact assessment perspective, the framework could support alternatives analysis in strategic environmental assessment of territorial spatial plans by enabling ex ante comparison of projected land-use patterns, carbon-stock changes, and economic outcomes under consistent planning constraints. © 2026

Title: Dynamic engagement patterns during collaborative reasoning discussions and their relations to adolescents’ individual reasoning
Abstract: Background: Collaborative Reasoning (CR) is a dialogic, learner-centered instructional approach shown to promote learners’ higher-order thinking. However, existing research has paid less attention to how learners engage in CR processes and how the temporal dynamics of engagement relate to the development of individual reasoning. Aims: To address this gap, this study investigated the temporal development of behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement during CR discussions and examined how evolving engagement patterns were associated with subsequent individual reasoning. Sample: The participants were 29 seventh-graders from a middle school in China. The students formed four discussion groups, and each group participated in seven CR discussions. Methods: The 28 discussions were video-coded for cognitive, emotional, and behavioral interactions (6868 codes). Process mining and epistemic network analysis were used to model shifts in engagement patterns. Individual reasoning was assessed through post-discussion essays. Results: Engagement patterns shifted dynamically over time, moving from socially shared regulation to sustained knowledge co-construction. Groups differed in the timing and trajectory of this transition: some groups shifted earlier, whereas others engaged in prolonged regulatory exchanges. The group characterized by later transitions produced fewer basic argumentative elements but more advanced elements in their individual essays. Conclusions: This study highlights dynamic engagement patterns as an important link between collaborative processes and learning outcomes and underscores the importance of understanding temporal configurations of regulation and knowledge co-construction in collaborative learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From rules to reasoning: A systematic review of agent-based and LLM-empowered simulation of public collaboration
Abstract: Agent-based simulation of public collaboration is consolidating into a distinct research pathway, with rule-based agent-based modeling (ABM) and large language model (LLM)-empowered simulation emerging as two technological lineages. Whether they are competitive, substitutive, or complementary has not been systematically examined. Drawing on 1,064 public collaboration simulation studies, we apply a “2 × 4” framework to compare the two lineages across research agendas, theory–model relationships, simulation paradigms, and knowledge contributions. The comparison reveals a pronounced divergence: rule-based work concentrates on outcome explanation (79.5%) and policy evaluation (64.4%), whereas LLM-empowered work is overwhelmingly methodological (98.5%) and foregrounds deliberation and consensus building (35.8%), with meta-theoretical inquiry at 38.8% versus 7.5% in rule-based work. These headline differences persist under temporally controlled comparison against same-period, early-stage, and more strictly matched rule-based windows, with support attenuating in the smallest window, and they are consistent with paradigm expansion rather than substitution: simulation instruments not only answer research questions but shape the questions that can be asked. For information processing and management, the review supplies the evidence base and reporting standards needed to evaluate generative simulation as an instrument for studying collective information behavior, and identifies hybrid ABM–LLM architectures, behavioral validation protocols, and dynamic-network modeling as priority agendas. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Life history strategy and the Dark Triad: A meta-analysis of trait-specific associations
Abstract: Life History (LH) Theory has been increasingly employed as an evolutionary framework for understanding individual differences in the Dark Triad. However, findings remain inconsistent regarding trait-specific associations between LH strategy and the Dark Triad. This meta-analysis synthesized 41 effect sizes from 18 independent samples reported in 16 articles. A three-level random-effects model showed a significant positive overall association between faster LH strategy and Dark Triad traits (Pearson's r = 0.26, 95% CI [0.19, 0.33], p < 0.001). Moderator analyses revealed significant differences among the three traits, with psychopathy showing the strongest association ( r = 0.36), followed by Machiavellianism ( r = 0.25), whereas narcissism showed the weakest association ( r = 0.11). Title: Building sustainable influencer partnerships within the creator economy
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Influencer marketing has become an integral part of retail branding strategies. As the creator economy continues to expand, influencer collaborations are now viewed as strategic partnerships rather than promotional activities. Despite this transition, sustaining authentic and long-term brand-influencer partnerships remains a significant yet underexplored challenge. Combining Social Exchange Theory (SET) and Self-Determination Theory (SDT) into a unified motivational-exchange framework, this research focuses on how brand practices operate simultaneously as relational exchange resources and as psychological need-satisfying inputs within influencer–brand partnerships. With a mixed-methods two-phase approach, this study exmains how brand ethical–purpose alignment, autonomy support, and AI co-creation are linked to influencers' sense of ownership and thriving, as well as citizenship behaviours and partnership continuity. In Study 1, 22 semi-structured interviews were conducted with professional influencers across four regions, intended to understand their lived partnership experiences. In Study 2, responses from 422 influencers were analysed using structural equation modelling and moderation analysis. The study also examines serial indirect pathways through which brand practices are associated with voluntary citizenship behaviours and partnership continuity via Collaboration Ownership and Influencer Thriving. The findings suggest that autonomy support, purpose alignment, and AI co-creation enablement are positively associated with influencers' ownership and thriving. Authors: Li S.; Li X.; Du X.; Xin Z.
Title: How local–global identity shapes physical-digital preferences through convenience preference
Abstract: Despite the functional advantages of digital products, consumers’ preferences between digital and physical formats remain highly heterogeneous in a marketplace where globalization and renewed localism coexist. Drawing on identity-based motivation theory, this research examines how local versus global identity influences consumers' preferences for physical versus digital products through convenience preference. Across three studies (five sub-studies), we demonstrate that a relatively stronger local-over-global identity is associated with greater preference for physical over digital consumption formats. Further analyses reveal an asymmetric effect that local identity drives stronger preferences for physical products, whereas global identity does not produce a corresponding increase in preference for digital formats. We further identify convenience preference as the underlying mechanism, showing that stronger local identity reduces convenience preference, thereby increasing preference for physical products. These findings reconceptualize physical versus digital preferences as identity-consistent choices rather than purely functional evaluations. By identifying convenience as an identity-contingent motivational preference, this research advances identity-based motivation theory and provides timely insights into how identity orientations shape consumer preferences amid ongoing digital transformation and heightened societal attention to globalization–localism dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Natural Hazards, Critical Infrastructure Systems, and Resilience Enhancement: A Structured State-of-the-Art Review and a Synthesis-Based Rapid Assessment Framework
Abstract: Critical infrastructure systems (CISs) are increasingly exposed to natural hazards whose impacts are amplified by infrastructure interdependence, urban complexity, and the growing prevalence of compound and cascading events. Existing research provides valuable insights into individual hazards, infrastructure components, modeling methods, and resilience metrics, but these insights remain difficult to translate into preliminary decision support because they are organized across different hazard types, sectors, analytical scales, and decision contexts. This article presents a structured state-of-the-art review of natural hazards, CIS impacts, and resilience enhancement. A two-pathway review strategy was adopted. A Web of Science (WoS) core search was used to characterize the bibliometric landscape and identify WoS-sourced core synthesis studies, while a targeted anchor-search pathway was used to verify foundational concepts, hazard mechanisms, methodological approaches, resilience frameworks, and authoritative institutional sources. The review clarifies the conceptual distinction among dependencies, interdependencies, compound hazards, cascading failures, service disruption, and resilience; synthesizes cross-hazard infrastructure impact mechanisms; compares major method families for hazard-impact and resilience assessment; and develops a synthesis-derived rapid resilience assessment framework for preliminary screening and prioritization under constrained data and time conditions. The synthesis indicates that future CIS resilience assessment would benefit from moving beyond isolated asset-damage analysis toward integrated workflows that link hazard loading, component vulnerability, network functionality, service consequences, recovery capacity, uncertainty, and feasible intervention choices. The article contributes a more transparent evidence-source structure, an evidence-to-decision bridge, and a bounded decision-oriented framework for organizing future research and practical resilience screening.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Imperfection in motion: Implied motion reduces negative associations of imperfect produce
Abstract: Food waste remains a major sustainability challenge, with imperfect fruits and vegetables often rejected due to their appearance. Prior studies suggest that food choices are mostly automatic, implicit, and habitual, rather than made through deliberated choice. Such insights suggest why explicit messaging to increase consumers' imperfect food purchasing has shown limited effectiveness and highlight opportunities for behaviour change via less mindful means. This study investigates the extent to which negative implicit associations for “imperfect” (vs. “perfect”) exist, and whether implied motion (e.g., fruit splashing into water) can mitigate these evaluations. In a pre-registered study, participants (N = 145) completed an in-person multi-dimensional Implicit Association Test (IAT) to examine their implicit attitudes in static and motion contexts. Results showed that participants' implicit associations were positive for perfect produce and negative for imperfect produce, suggesting an “Ugly = Bad” association. However, exposure to implied motion imagery significantly reduced this negativity effect toward imperfect fresh produce, while having no significant effect on perfect produce. Our findings link implicit attitudes to sustainable food acceptance and demonstrate the potential of visually-based interventions, such as implied motion, to reduce negative aesthetic biases and support behaviour change aimed at increasing acceptance of imperfect produce and reducing food waste. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Examining the layered veil of pay transparency: Implications for perceived ambiguity, sensemaking, and negotiation
Abstract: In the last decade, pay transparency—making pay information more accessible and understandable—has become a defining workplace reform. We examine the common assumption that pay transparency reduces pay disparities by improving negotiation outcomes. Our cross-disciplinary review suggests that pay transparency's effects on negotiation hinge on three factors: (1) how transparency is operationalized (i.e., what type of pay information is shared); (2) how people interpret the information provided; and (3) whether transparency alone can motivate and equip individuals to leverage that information to negotiate effectively. Title: Governing Indigenous territories: trust, moral economy, and the legitimation of Indigenous territorial authority in the Honduran Moskitia
Abstract: Formalizing Indigenous land rights is critical for environmental justice and sustainable development. Yet legal recognition often creates new territorial governing bodies tasked with managing collective lands, whose legitimacy cannot be assumed. This study examines how trust in Indigenous territorial authorities is built, contested, and withdrawn following the formalization of collective land rights in the Honduran Moskitia. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork and household interviews in three villages across diverse socio-ecological settings, the study analyzes how residents assess their territorial authorities. The analysis treats trust as multidimensional and relational. The study examines different forms of trust—dispositional, rational, affinitive, and procedural—to identify the rationales that drive assessments of authority in each village. These rationales are interpreted through the lens of a Miskitu moral economy, framing trust assessments in terms of what residents expect of a territorial authority to be considered legitimate. A moral economy lens contributes analytically to a multidimensional trust framework by explaining why certain forms of trust feel more salient when evaluating authority performance and how they interact with one another. The central finding is that the socio-spatial configuration of land conflicts shapes which evaluative dimensions of trust become most salient. A multidimensional and relational trust analysis contributes a more granular understanding of this process: it shows how different forms of trust interact and shift through everyday encounters with authority, identifying the specific points at which legitimacy is strengthened, strained, or quietly lost. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Explaining deceptive language in topical discourse: Integrating transformer models and explainable AI using LIME and SHAP for transparent text-based deception detection
Abstract: Detecting deception in textual communication is an important challenge in online environments where misleading information and deceptive narratives are increasingly prevalent. This study investigates the integration of fine-tuned transformer models, prompt-based large language models (LLMs), and explainable AI (XAI) techniques for interpretable deception detection. Its contributions include a statistically validated comparison of six BERT architectures, a factorial prompt ablation across five GPT models, and a quantitative evaluation of LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) explanation quality and stability. Experiments were conducted on two domain-specific datasets totaling 500 statements, with 264 related to climate change and 236 related to COVID-19. The results show that transformer models are effective for deception classification even when trained on relatively small datasets, with DeBERTa achieving 88.87% and 87.92% accuracy on topical datasets. LIME and SHAP were applied to analyze word-level attribution patterns in the best-performing model. The two XAI methods exhibited substantial aggregate-level agreement, converging on similar sets of influential words associated with deception across domains, whereas agreement on individual predictions was more limited. These findings align with prior research on recurring patterns in deceptive language and provide supportive evidence that linguistic patterns identified through explainability techniques remain consistent across topics, even under limited data conditions. Authors: Zheng L.
Title: Teaching by example? Teacher ICT use and middle school students’ computer and information literacy across China and the United States
Abstract: Background: In the digital era, Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) has become a crucial educational outcome. While teacher Information and Communication Technology (ICT) use is widely promoted to enhance student digital skills, its effectiveness may vary significantly across different national education systems. Aims: This study investigates the impact of teacher ICT use on middle school students' CIL in China and the United States. It aims to compare these cross-national effects and examine the mediating roles of school ICT resources and institutional support in shaping these relationships. Methods: Using nationally representative data from the International Computer and Information Literacy Study (ICILS) 2023, this research employs regression models and instrumental variable (2SLS) methods to address potential endogeneity. Mediation analyses further explore how school-level factors transmit teacher ICT effects. Results: The analysis reveals striking cross-country differences: in China, all dimensions of teacher ICT use significantly improved students' CIL, whereas these effects were statistically insignificant in the United States. School ICT resources and support fully mediated teacher ICT effects in China but only partially mediated ability effects in the U.S. Additionally, student background factors consistently influenced CIL across both countries. Conclusion: While teacher ICT experience demonstrates universal importance, the broader impact of instructional ICT practices depends critically on national context and institutional support systems. The findings highlight the complex interplay between teacher practices, school resources, and national educational environments in shaping digital literacy outcomes. © 2026

Title: CasHyper: Modeling multi-factor interactions and asymmetric influence in cascade prediction via hypercomplex algebra
Abstract: Cascade prediction aims to forecast the future evolution of information diffusion and is an important task in social network analysis. Most existing methods represent users and cascades in real-valued Euclidean spaces, which may offer limited capacity to model multi-factor interactions and asymmetric influence in complex diffusion processes. To address these challenges, we propose CasHyper, a hypercomplex-based cascade prediction framework that integrates hypercomplex algebra with graph neural networks and Transformers. CasHyper organizes user and cascade embeddings into multiple hypercomplex components, with each component encoding distinct latent factors, and uses structured algebraic operations to model cross-component interactions. The non-commutative hypercomplex product further yields order-dependent interaction representations, enabling the model to learn asymmetric influence among users. In the network encoding stage, a static heterogeneous graph channel captures user-user and user-cascade relations, while a Neural ODE-based dynamic channel models the continuous evolution of node states and edge weights. A hypercomplex Transformer with norm-preserving rotary transformations is then introduced to incorporate relative positional information into cascade sequence modeling. Finally, an interaction-aware module and a linear projection module are combined to estimate the probability of each candidate user participating next. Experiments on four real-world datasets show that CasHyper achieves competitive or better performance than the compared methods under the evaluated settings, including relative improvements of up to 43.24% on Android and 18.43% on Christianity in Hits@50. Additional analyses of architectural variants, graph incompleteness, computational efficiency, and different Cayley–Dickson algebras further demonstrate the empirical effectiveness of the proposed framework and reveal dataset-dependent behaviors of different hypercomplex structures. Title: SecuLEx: A secure limit exchange market for dynamic operating envelopes

Title: (Dis)trust in tap water: Consumer perceptions and behavior in California
Abstract: Tap water is not universally trusted in high-income countries, leading to tap avoidance and reduced public support for urban water infrastructure. Title: PLRA-KG: Pattern-derived latent relation augmentation for knowledge graph-based recommendations
Abstract: Knowledge graph (KG)-based recommendation has emerged as an effective solution to data sparsity by incorporating structured semantic information into user and item representations. However, existing KG-based recommendation approaches still face two core challenges: (i) over-reliance on explicit relations while insufficiently capturing latent connections between items, and (ii) feature degradation during high-order propagation, which leads to the dilution of informative signals in learned representations. To this end, we propose PLRA-KG, a pattern-derived latent relation augmentation framework for KG-based recommendation. PLRA-KG uncovers implicit item associations by generating syn-relations and syn-entities from global user preference patterns and relational structures. Specifically, PLRA-KG first performs relation-aware clustering via self-training to group items with strong association patterns. It then introduces a discernment-aware relation-pair selection mechanism to identify relation combinations that significantly influence user decisions. Based on the selected relation-pairs, a pattern-derived syn-relation generation strategy is designed to construct latent relations by jointly modeling global user preferences and relational value interactions. These generated syn-relations and syn-entities are subsequently integrated into the original KG, resulting in an augmented graph that better captures hidden semantic connectivity. Finally, PLRA-KG is optimized in a unified framework that jointly considers recommendation learning, KG embedding, and clustering objectives, enabling seamless integration with various KG-based recommendation models. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that PLRA-KG consistently improves both recommendation accuracy and diversity, achieving average improvements of approximately 6.64% in Recall, 7.83% in AD, 5.56% in Coverage, and 6.20% reduction in ARP. Title: Models for risk management in the procurement process within organizational contexts: A systematic literature review
Abstract: Over the past decade, supply chain management has faced extreme volatility, culminating in the unprecedented disruptions of the COVID-19 pandemic. Consequently, resilience in procurement has transitioned from a secondary attribute to an indispensable requirement for operational continuity. This study classifies the state of the art in procurement risk management within the post-pandemic landscape (2021–2025). It analyzes the transition from reactive approaches toward predictive and prescriptive perspectives to address supply chain volatility. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 protocol. Based on a structured search in the Scopus and Web of Science databases, an initial pool of 1,109 records was screened. This resulted in a final sample of 107 high-impact peer-reviewed articles. These studies were evaluated using thematic content analysis and classified into ten technical categories based on their functional orientation. The evidence reveals a fragmented methodological ecosystem where Hybrid Models (21.5%) and Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM, 16.8%) techniques predominate. A shift is observed from static approaches toward the integration of robust optimization, tail risk metrics like Conditional Value at Risk, and Machine Learning. However, a gap is identified between algorithmic complexity and corporate adoption. The study establishes that Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) and Blockchain are indispensable governance requirements to overcome the black box problem in strategic decision-making. This research contributes a functional classification of tools based on their diagnostic, predictive, or prescriptive orientation. Furthermore, it provides managers with a tiered roadmap to achieve analytical maturity. Title: Perceived control and stress reactivity in algorithm-supported hiring decisions

Title: Negative and positive emotional eating and food cravings related to weight loss during weight management
Abstract: Emotional eating and food cravings are common among adults living with overweight or obesity. This study investigated these in relation to weight-management success and reports on strategies for managing emotional eating. A quasi-prospective study design was used including an online survey completed by 3834 adults on a community weight management programme. Measures included negative and positive emotional eating (BEES) and food craving (CoEQ). Additionally, objectively measured body weight over the previous 12 weeks was obtained and participants were grouped into Higher (>10%, N = 962), Moderate (5-10%, N = 2156), and Lower (<5%, N = 716) weight loss groups. Open questions were used to explore strategies for managing emotional eating. Between-group differences were tested using univariate ANOVAs, with Tukey post hoc comparisons where significant effects emerged. Open ended responses were analysed using inductive thematic analysis and mapped onto the Behaviour Change Taxonomy. Respondents were mostly female (92.0%), mean age = 57.2 years, and BMI = 32.1 kg/m2. Results showed participants had lost 3.7 BMI units over the previous 12 weeks. Higher weight loss was strongly associated with lower negative and positive emotional eating, fewer food cravings and eating control difficulties. Prominent themes for managing emotional eating were distraction (31.7%) and physical activity along with healthier food substitutions, planning and positive mindset. Group social support was also highlighted. These data highlight the perceived importance of psychological and group-based social support in weight management. Authors: Zhang C.; Li J.; Fu H.; Shao S.
Title: The road to hell is paved with good intentions: How does the construction of low-carbon cities affect corporate low-carbon technological innovation in manufacturing?
Abstract: Low-carbon technological innovation (LCTI) is crucial for decarbonization and global climate change mitigation. Taking China's Low-carbon City Pilot (LCCP)—a pioneering exploration for low-carbon development through policy innovation—as an exogenous policy shock, this study utilizes a staggered difference-in-difference-in-differences model and the data of China's manufacturing firms to examine the causality between the voluntary carbon regulation and LCTI. For the first time, the results indicate that the LCCP enactment significantly hinders corporate LCTI, contradicting the predictions of the Porter hypothesis. Mechanism analysis reveals that under the LCCP framework, local governments are authorized to design innovative policies tailored to their specific conditions and are responsible for their own assessment. Using a two-stage LLM-based approach to construct a climate policy uncertainty perception index, we confirm that this “bottom-up” approach introduces significant policy uncertainty faced by firms and weakens their motivation for LCTI involvement. Furthermore, the compliance costs associated with the policy crowd out the funds for LCTI, further hindering firms from engaging in LCTI. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the adverse impact is more evident among firms exhibiting high risk aversion, ones with high artificial intelligence (AI) technology exposure, ones situated in non-resource-based cities, and state-owned ones, and that the adverse impact is significant for emission reduction technologies and zero-carbon technologies, but not for negative-carbon technologies. Additionally, all three pilot batches negatively impact corporate LCTI, suggesting that institutional modifications have not led to intended positive outcomes. This empirical research offers novel evidence regarding the efficacy of the LCCP and yields valuable policy insights—stable policy expectations and robust supervision mechanisms are crucial for achieving policy goals. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Mitochondrial-derived peptides in female reproduction: Emerging regulators of oocyte competence and novel therapeutic opportunities for infertility
Abstract: Female infertility affects approximately 17.5% of adults worldwide. Mitochondria are central to oocyte developmental competence, and a novel class of mitochondrial genome-encoded peptides, mitochondrial-derived peptides(MDPs) comprising MOTS-c, Humanin and small Humanin-like peptide2(SHLP2), regulates cellular metabolism, oxidative stress and apoptosis. This hypothesis-driven perspective aims to:(i) synthesize indirect evidence to construct a mechanistic framework for MDP involvement in oocyte physiology and female infertility;(ii) propose prioritized research questions; and(iii) delineate translational paths toward MDP-based biomarkers and therapeutics in assisted reproductive technology(ART). PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched up to May 2025 using terms related to MDPs, oocytes, follicular fluid, ovarian aging and IVF. Bibliographies were hand-searched. The search yielded 312 records, of which 87 were retained. The three principal MDPs decline with age in humans, mirroring the age-related deterioration of oocyte quality. The reduced MOTS-c in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; formerly polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS) (a 56% reduction in serum concentration versus controls, P < 0.001), provides preliminary evidence, albeit unreplicated and without ovarian sampling. Mechanistically, MDPs activate AMPK(MOTS-c), sequester pro-apoptotic Bax(Humanin), and reduce mitochondrial ROS while enhancing electron transport chain activity(SHLP2). Humanin is already known to be present in human follicular fluid and to associate with ovarian reserve and PMOS-related insulin resistance; we propose that this extends to MOTS-c and SHLP2, that composite MDP levels correlate with oocyte-specific quality parameters, and that a composite biomarker panel could improve IVF outcome prediction beyond AMH alone. MDPs(MOTS-c,Humanin,SHLP2) decline with age, regulate AMPK, suppress oxidative stress and inhibit apoptosis; processes that drive oocyte quality decline. Reduced MOTS-c in PMOS provides an initial, unreplicated clinical link. Convergent biology positions MDPs as promising candidates to improve IVF outcomes. Direct empirical testing, starting with quantification of MDPs in human follicular fluid and granulosa cells, is now warranted. © 2026

Title: Exploring Italian consumer perceptions and acceptance of innovative foods and food technologies: insights from a national survey
Abstract: Innovative foods and food technologies face barriers to adoption in Italy, where food plays a central role in identity and social life. This study investigates Italian consumer responses to seven innovative food products and technologies using a consumer survey (N = 2000), stratified by age, gender, and geographical region. The survey included psychometric scales assessing food neophobia, food technology neophobia, disgust sensitivity, trust, sensation seeking, and health interest. It measured perceptions of risk, benefit, familiarity, and emotions associated with each product. Findings indicate that Italian consumers show high levels of food and technological neophobia, coupled with low trust and strong health concerns. Acceptability varied significantly across sociodemographic groups: higher education and income were associated with higher trust and sensation seeking and lower neophobia, whereas female and older respondents exhibited higher disgust sensitivity and greater resistance to innovation. Exploratory clustering identified two broad clusters of aggregated consumer profiles. One cluster was associated with younger age, higher educational attainment and household income, together with greater trust and sensation seeking, whereas the other was associated with older age, lower educational attainment and household income, together with greater food and food technology neophobia and disgust sensitivity. Emotional responses emerged as correlates of acceptability, with curiosity most positively and disgust most negatively. Products most aligned with product ideals were plant-based proteins, algae, and unusual fruits, while insect-based proteins and cultured meat faced the greatest barriers. These findings highlight the importance of reinforcing trust and curiosity while addressing disgust to promote sustainable Italian food innovation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Women-Led Wildfire Disaster Adaptations within and from Indigenous Knowledge Perspectives
Abstract: This study examines Indigenous women-led wildfire disaster adaptations through traditional environmental knowledge and community-led strategies. Centering Indigenous traditional story sharing, intergenerational learning, and land stewardship, Indigenous women serve as key leaders in wildfire prevention and forest management. The research highlights the role of Indigenous fire governance in sustainable land management and the critical intersection between traditional knowledge and Western scientific tools in Chang Mai, Thailand. Using decolonial methodologies, the study highlights the necessity of Indigenous women leadership in climate-resilience efforts. Findings reveal that Indigenous women's practices contribute significantly to biodiversity conservation, climate adaptation, and community-led disaster response. The study calls for stronger academic engagement with Indigenous knowledge and policy reforms that center Indigenous women's expertise into global forest fire governance. The research provides a foundation for future transdisciplinary collaborations, advocating for Indigenous women's leadership in sustainable wildfire management.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Not naive, just gullible: psycho-cognitive vulnerability and fraud victimization in Italy
Abstract: Fraud represents a growing and complex threat in contemporary societies, with consequences that extend beyond economic losses. Despite increasing international evidence, limited research has examined the psychological and cognitive factors associated with fraud victimization in the Italian context, particularly in relation to online scams. This study examines individual differences and fraud experiences among 600 Italian adults through an online survey assessing sociodemographic characteristics, fraud experiences, personality traits, gullibility, financial literacy, and financial self-efficacy. Results revealed that more than half of the sample (n = 416) reported exposure to scam attempts, most of which occurred through remote channels (either exclusively online or in combination with offline channels). A smaller subset (n = 115) reported actual fraud victimization. A binomial logistic regression was conducted to identify individual factors associated with fraud victimization among exposed individuals. Gullibility emerged as the only statistically significant predictor, indicating that higher gullibility was associated with a greater likelihood of victimization, whereas sociodemographic characteristics, personality traits, financial literacy, and financial self-efficacy were not significantly associated with victimization. These findings highlight that fraud prevention strategies may benefit from considering psycho-cognitive vulnerability factors alongside traditional financial and digital literacy initiatives. © 2026

Title: Sensing the path forward: AI as amplifier in sensory and consumer science
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how sensory and consumer data are collected, analyzed, and used. A common fear is that algorithms will displace trained panels and that predictive models will replace expert judgment. We argue the opposite: as AI automates what is easy to formalize, the value of what only humans can do (embodied sensing, cultural interpretation, ethical judgment, and meaning-making) rises. This paper is not a systematic review. It advocates a particular perspective (AI as amplifier of sensory expertise), informed by on-the-ground experience through the recent rise of large language models, including what has worked and what has not in practice. Three industry case studies from PepsiCo, Danone, and Kenvue support that perspective. The principles (knowledge management, automation, predictive modeling, people-centered adoption; humans in the loop; culture before algorithms) are meant to apply beyond large companies, including academia and smaller groups. That perspective also guided a selective literature reading focused on Food Quality and Preference and related journals, mainly from 2022 to early 2026. We clarify what AI is and is not, trace the path from chemometrics to neuromorphic sensing, and describe a four-pillar framework from a Pangborn 2025 industry workshop. Self-reported case outcomes include up to 50% faster analysis and a 75% reduction in reporting time; calculation details were not disclosed to us and the figures are not independently validated. The three organizations built the same capabilities in different orders and met the same barriers (culture, talent, IT collaboration). We also propose narrative-driven analysis with large language models and a near-term research agenda. Central message: when machines predict, humans must decide. © 2026

Title: Explaining the relationship between urban land use per capita and residents’ perceived accessibility using a spatial justice approach: A case study of Tehran metropolis
Abstract: Land use per capita remains one of the most widely used quantitative indicators in urban planning for evaluating the provision of urban services. Despite its normative significance, its validity as a proxy for accessibility has received limited empirical examination. This study investigates the extent to which land use per capita provision corresponds to accessibility outcomes across seven neighborhoods in District 20 of Tehran. Using a spatial evaluation model, spatial equity is evaluated through observed service distributions and survey-based accessibility data. Accessibility is operationalized as a measurable variable derived from standardized survey responses. Statistical analyses and spatial diagnostics, including Global Moran’s I, are employed to explain the relationship between six categories of service-related land uses and reported accessibility levels. The findings reveal that higher land use per capita provision does not consistently translate into improved accessibility. The relationship is weak and spatially unstable, while service distribution exhibits a fragmented and non-clustered pattern across neighborhoods. These results suggest that land use per capita standards provide only a partial representation of accessibility outcomes. Spatial configuration and distributional structure emerge as key dimensions influencing the effectiveness of service provision. The study highlights the need for more robust, evidence-based evaluation models that integrate spatial and behavioral dimensions of accessibility. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Identification of novel skin/sweat-specific CpG sites and development of a skin/sweat identification multiplex system for forensic analysis
Abstract: Identification of the biological origin of forensic stains provides critical contextual information for crime scene reconstruction and evidence interpretation. Among forensic biological materials, skin/sweat is particularly important for distinguishing intimate from social contact in sexual assault investigations. Although DNA methylation-based body fluid identification has advanced considerably, reliable CpG sites for skin remain scarce. Here, we systematically screened skin/sweat-specific CpG sites using Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC (850 K) array data from five body fluids and developed a multiplex DNA methylation assay for forensic skin/sweat identification. Following site prioritization and assay optimization, a 10-CpG multiplex panel based on amplification refractory mutation system PCR (ARMS-PCR) was established. The assay was comprehensively validated using single-source samples, simulated degraded samples, and mixed body fluid samples representative of forensic casework. The limit of detection of the 10-CpG panel was 0.25 ng. Integration of a random forest classifier enabled robust interpretation of methylation profiles and achieved 100% accuracy in distinguishing skin/sweat-containing from non-skin/sweat samples, including degraded, mixed, and casework specimens. This study represents a promising addition to the forensic epigenetic toolbox for body fluid identification, particularly in cases involving trace or degraded skin/sweat evidence. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Empowering leadership in educational contexts: A bibliometric analysis to guide management in the framework of SDG 4
Abstract: Empowering leadership (EL) has emerged as a critical leadership approach in educational contexts, particularly in response to increasing demands for innovation, teacher autonomy, and sustainable institutional development. However, despite the rapid growth of studies in this field, the intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, thematic evolution, and contribution to Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) remain fragmented and insufficiently synthesized. Therefore, this study aims to provide a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of EL research in educational settings indexed in the Scopus database from 1999 to 2026. A total of 84 publications were analyzed using bibliometric performance indicators and science mapping techniques, including co-authorship analysis, keyword co-occurrence, three-field plot visualization, citation analysis, and thematic clustering, supported by Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. The results reveal a strong upward publication trend with a coefficient of determination of R² = 77.54%, particularly accelerating after 2018 and reaching the highest output in 2025. Citation influence remains concentrated in foundational studies published in high-impact journals such as Journal of Applied Psychology, Journal of Knowledge Management, and Leadership Quarterly. China and Indonesia emerge as major international collaboration hubs, while Indonesia shows the strongest author–keyword linkage. Keyword analysis identifies dominant themes related to psychological empowerment, teacher autonomy, innovative work behavior, job satisfaction, and distributed leadership. Notably, 74 out of 84 publications (88.1%) are aligned with SDG 4, highlighting the strong integration of EL research with global educational sustainability agendas. This study offers the first structured intellectual map of EL in education, identifies influential contributors and emerging research directions, and provides evidence-based guidance for educational leadership development aligned with quality education and sustainable transformation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Research on the sensitivity of key factors influencing evacuation in building stairwell based on simulation
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: With more people clustering in buildings, evacuation in high-rise buildings has become a challenge in urban safety. Despite the identification of key influencing factors in existing studies, quantitative analyses of their impacts remain inadequate, and there is a lack of a systematic evaluation framework. To address this gap, the present study employs a multi-factor-aware pedestrian evacuation agent model, coupled with parameter sensitivity analysis, to investigate the effects of evacuation parameters on evacuation time. The research proceeds as follows: first, a Perception-Decision-Operation (PDO) framework for occupant movement is proposed and integrated into the pedestrian evacuation model; second, the proposed model is validated by using evacuation experimental data collected from different floors; third, the sensitivity of evacuation time to four critical parameters — pedestrian number, expected speed, step depth, and stair width — is analyzed, and the degree of influence of each parameter is quantified. The results demonstrate that expected speed exerts the most significant impact on pedestrian evacuation time, followed by step depth, while stair width has the least influence. The sensitivity quantification method adopted herein overcomes the limitations of traditional empirical approaches. These findings not only provide a data-driven basis for optimizing key building evacuation parameters but also facilitate a paradigm shift in emergency evacuation design from qualitative assessment to quantitative evaluation. Ultimately, this study offers valuable insights for emergency management in complex built environments. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: The role of personal norms in farmers’ safety practices: Protective equipment use in pesticide handling
Abstract: Farmers’ use of personal protective equipment (PPE) during pesticide handling has been studied, but factors shaping this behavior can vary considerably. Farmers’ intention to use PPE in pesticide handling and observed protective behavior were studied using the norm activation model (NAM). Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, multiple linear regression, and binary logistic regression models. Almost fifty-nine (58.9%) of farmers showed unsafe behavior regarding PPE use. Intention to use PPE was low (mean: 2.415 on a 1–5 scale) and positively associated with observed protective behavior. Regarding NAM constructs, farmers showed moderate personal norms (mean: 3.027), slightly lower awareness of the consequences associated with not using PPE (mean: 2.888), and relatively weak ascription of responsibility (mean: 2.741) for reducing those consequences. Personal norms significantly predicted both intention and observed protective behavior (P < 0.01). In turn, awareness of consequences and ascription of responsibility were significant positive predictors of personal norms, supporting the applicability of NAM for understanding PPE-related behavior. Further analysis indicated that personal norms were negatively associated with age and farm size (P < 0.01), suggesting weaker norms among older farmers and those managing larger farms. Conversely, education was positively correlated with personal norms (P < 0.01). Overall, personal norms played a central role in shaping PPE use, with their relationship influenced by recognition of the risks of non-use and acceptance of responsibility for mitigating them. Enhancing communication about pesticide risks and emphasizing the importance of PPE may help strengthen personal norms and promote safer PPE-related practices. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Prioritizing configuration relevance via compiler-based refined feature ranking
Abstract: Modern programming languages, most notably Rust, offer advanced linguistic constructs for building highly configurable software systems as aggregations of features—identified by a configuration. However, they pose substantial challenges for program analysis, optimization, and testing, as the combinatorial explosion of configurations often makes exhaustive exploration infeasible. In this manuscript, we present the first compiler-based method for prioritizing configurations. Our approach consists of four main steps: (1) extracting a tailored intermediate representation from the Rust compiler, (2) constructing two complementary graph-based data structures—a feature dependency graph capturing inter-feature code-level dependencies weighted by predicate structure, and an atom dependency tree encoding the extent of code governed by each feature—, (3) using centrality measures to rank features, and (4) refining the ranking by considering the extent of code they impact. A fixed number of most relevant configurations are generated based on the achieved feature ranking. The validity of the generated configurations is guaranteed by using a SAT solver that takes a representation of feature dependencies in conjunctive normal form. We formalized this approach and implemented it in a prototype, RUSTYEX, by instrumenting the Rust compiler. An empirical evaluation on higher-ranked open-source Rust projects shows that RUSTYEX efficiently generates user-specified sets of configurations within bounded resources, while ensuring soundness by construction. The results demonstrate that centrality-guided configuration prioritization enables practical exploration of large configuration spaces, and we discuss the implications and open challenges for future configuration-aware analysis and optimization. © 2026 The Authors

Title: “Feminine” strengths, “masculine” costs: Rethinking gender gaps in negotiation research
Abstract: The impact of gender on negotiation outcomes has been an important aspect of the negotiation literature for decades. This literature has primarily focused on “masculine” attributes, such as assertiveness, as ideal negotiator characteristics, manifesting in gender research focused on men's economic advantages in negotiations, to the detriment of both women and men. Yet recent research has begun to examine gender gaps in “feminine” attributes, highlighting women's strengths in negotiations, particularly in relational outcomes. Future work is needed to fully unpack these results, understand the impact of intersecting identities, and explore partner effects. Title: Narratives of workplace conflict: A mixed-methods analysis of HEXACO and Dark Triad personality predictors
Abstract: Workplace conflicts are common, yet most evidence links personality to broad conflict management styles rather than to how concrete episodes unfold. We used a mixed-methods design to examine whether Dark Triad and HEXACO traits predict the content and course of real conflicts. Hungarian employees ( N = 318, 31.1% male, 68.9% female, M age = 35.24, SD = 10.34) completed personality measures and provided written narratives of a workplace conflict in which they were directly involved. Narratives were inductively coded into indicators of conflict context, process, outcomes, and narrative structure, and binary logistic regressions were used to examine associations with personality traits. Personality traits were more strongly related to how conflicts unfolded and were interpreted than to their structural features, such as who was involved or what triggered the conflict. Interpersonal traits from the HEXACO model showed the most consistent associations with conflict dynamics, emotional responses, and relationship outcomes. Dark Triad traits showed selective but limited associations with conflict processes, offering little evidence for broad predictive advantages beyond broader personality dimensions. Overall, the findings suggest that workplace conflict is not only enacted but also interpreted through the lens of personality, highlighting the importance of integrating dispositional and situational perspectives in research on organizational conflict. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: The neglected dimension: Arousal, emotions and product choices
Abstract: This article presents an overview of the ways in which arousal may be an important influence on consumer product choices. It is recognised that the recent emphasis on measures of emotions in consumer studies has its origins in the limitations of measures of liking to predict choices, and that there is evidence that such measures have added value to traditional hedonic ratings. The possibility that this improvement derives from the fact arousal is implicitly included in emotion measures is considered. In addition, measuring arousal may avoid some of the uncontrolled aspects of measuring emotions, including those related to individual variability in language use. The research evidence for arousal being directly involved in consumer decision making is discussed. Finally, there is an overview of the ways in which arousal can be assessed in consumer studies. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Hu J.
Title: Hero products and the value of position in live streaming commerce evidence from Douyin
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Every livestream sales session has one product that sells best, and the minutes in which it is shown are when the broadcast's audience peaks. This paper asks what that moment is worth to the products around it: can the items that follow the hero, or those shown just before it, turn the traffic it attracts into sales of their own? Using 260,252 product–session observations from 8123 Douyin sessions and an event-study design with session fixed effects, we find conversion highest in the slot immediately after the hero, exceeding products more than five positions away by 0.0177. The advantage is not borrowed traffic. It appears before the hero as much as after it, and only the adjacent slot breaks that symmetry; when the same product is compared with itself across sessions in which it sat at different distances, most of the advantage disappears except beside the hero. The running order therefore reveals mainly which products a streamer places near the featured item, and we report a positional association rather than an attention spillover. What survives is conditional. Scoring each product's own listing title with a large language model, we find that credibility signals attenuate the advantage while informativeness moves it in both directions, and the advantage exists only where the hero appears in the first third of the running order, vanishing when it is held until the end. For managers, the slots flanking an early-placed hero are worth allocating deliberately; positions further down the lineup are not. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: How they collaborate matters: collaboration modes and task fit in human-AI recommendations
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Human-AI collaboration is increasingly used in online product recommendation, yet it remains unclear how consumers interpret different role configurations and when such configurations facilitate adoption. Drawing on mind perception theory, we argue that collaboration mode signals the collaborative system's task-relevant capability profile, and that its effectiveness depends on whether this profile fits the judgment-support requirements of search versus experience goods. Evidence from one field experiment and two scenario-based experiments indicates that AI-dominant collaboration is more effective for search-good recommendations, whereas human-dominant collaboration is more effective for experience-good recommendations, and that this fit effect is mediated by perceived diagnosticity. In addition, AI empathy functions as a compensatory interaction cue, improving consumers' evaluations of AI-dominant collaboration in experience-good contexts by enhancing perceived diagnosticity and recommendation adoption intention. Overall, this research moves product recommendation research beyond simple comparisons between human and AI sources toward a consumer-centered understanding of visible collaboration modes, while also offering implications for the design of more effective human-AI collaborative recommendation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A systematic method for designing aging-resilient nuclear balance-of-plant systems: Theoretical foundations
Abstract: Maintaining service continuity is a fundamental requirement for nuclear plants, especially when supplying industrial heat users without access to a buffering thermal network. In such settings, gradual performance losses in balance-of-plant components can translate directly into curtailed thermal and electric delivery. This paper introduces PRIORITY (Probabilistic Ranking for Improving Operational Reliability through degradatIon-aware miTigation strategY selection), a computationally lightweight, design-stage framework that (i) identifies which component degradations most strongly limit productive capacity and (ii) ranks candidate mitigation portfolios (e.g., redundancy, oversizing, bypasses, dedicated control schemes). Long-horizon degradation trajectories are replaced by an ergodic Monte Carlo formulation in which multi-component health states are sampled from bounded distributions informed by Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), defined over the admissible range between nominal performance and the maintenance threshold. For each sampled state, a steady-state performance model evaluates a degraded power-capacity metric combining delivered process heat and net electric output expressed in thermal-equivalent units. Because all design variants are evaluated on the same set of sampled states, their performance distributions can be compared using probability of outperformance and synthesized into a global ranking (Bradley–Terry). The framework makes modeling assumptions explicit (stationarity, approximate independence, exclusion of common-cause effects) and outlines extensions to dependent degradations and cost-aware selection. A companion paper applies PRIORITY to a representative cogeneration configuration and quantifies the value of specific mitigation portfolios. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.
