Title: The dark side of AI customer service: How service failures damage consumer-brand relationships
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) customer service is increasingly used as a frontline interface, yet its failures may create relational damage that extends beyond a single service encounter. Drawing on service failure theory and consumer-brand relationship literature, this research examines how AI service failures are formed and how they influence negative consumer-brand relationships. Study 1 collected 3208 online complaint records from a major Chinese consumer complaint platform. After data cleaning, 2824 valid complaints were analyzed using Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modeling, which identified ten complaint topics and further synthesized them into five AI service failure dimensions: functional failure, informational failure, systemic failure, interactional failure, and service recovery failure. Study 2 used survey data from 965 Chinese consumers and applied PLS-SEM, Artificial Neural Network (ANN), fsQCA, and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA). The results show that all five failure dimensions positively influence negative consumer-brand relationships. Informational failure and systemic failure emerge as particularly influential across linear, predictive, and configurational analyses. The findings advance AI service failure research by developing a data-driven typology of failures and demonstrating that AI-mediated service breakdowns are not merely technical problems but relational threats that undermine consumer trust, satisfaction, and engagement with brands. Title: Teaching methods for civic and moral education in Vietnam: Implications for pre-service teacher education and competence-based pedagogy
Abstract: Civic and Moral Education (CME) is important in developing students’ moral judgement, civic responsibility, legal awareness, critical thinking, and the ability to participate in society responsibly. In Vietnam, CME is mainly embodied in the school subject of Giáo dục công dân, which is located at the intersection of moral education, citizenship education, legal education, values education and social responsibility. The competence-based General Education Curriculum of Vietnam has brought new pedagogical expectations to this subject. Instead of mainly focusing on the transmission of moral principles and legal knowledge, CME is increasingly expected to engage students in reasoning, dialogue, reflection, problem-solving and the application of civic-moral knowledge to everyday situations. This narrative literature review synthesises Vietnamese and international scholarship on pedagogical approaches relevant to CME, with particular focus on their implications for pre-service teacher education. Five main pedagogical directions are discussed: discussion-based and critical thinking-oriented learning; case-based and problem-based learning; experiential and service learning; reflective pedagogy and professional ethics education; digital pedagogy for civic participation. The literature reviewed indicates that these approaches may provide students with valuable opportunities to analyse civic-moral dilemmas, take different perspectives, link knowledge with lived experience, and take responsible action in both physical and digital communities. However, their realisation is highly dependent on the pedagogical design, dialogic facilitation, ethical judgement, reflective practice and assessment competence of teachers. In Vietnam, there is a persistent gap between competence-based curriculum expectations and teacher preparation to implement participatory and practice-oriented pedagogy. Hence, this review suggests an integrated framework for pre-service CME teacher education that links civic-moral content knowledge, pedagogical design, dialogic facilitation, experiential practice, ethical reflection, digital responsibility, and competence-based assessment. Title: LLM-driven paradigm for agent-based modeling and simulation: A review and organizing framework
Abstract: Agent-based modeling and simulation (ABMS) serves as a pivotal bottom up paradigm for revealing macro level emergent behaviors through micro level interactions. Title: Lost in the narrative: How embedded content reduces sales on short video commerce platforms

Abstract: Embedded content on short video commerce platforms, which integrates product-focused content with creators' self-focused content, has been widely adopted as a strategy to enhance viewer engagement and drive product sales. Despite its prevalent application, the effect of embedded content on product sales remains unclear. While self-focused content may reduce advertising avoidance, it risks distracting attention from the product, thereby making its effect on subsequent product sales unclear. To explore the sales effect of embedded content and its underlying mechanisms, we employ a mixed-methods approach, combining an observational study with a randomized experiment. Our empirical analysis reveals that a higher ratio of self-focused content decreases product sales. Heterogeneity analyses further uncover several measures to mitigate the negative impact: optimizing commercial embedment timing, increasing creator positive facial expressions, and enhancing product visual salience. Finally, we conduct a randomized experiment to validate the dual-path mechanism, which shows that self-focused content indeed reduces ad avoidance but also reduces ad attention, thereby affecting viewers’ purchase intentions through two opposing pathways. Title: Reframing brain drain in ASEAN: Strategic talent retention and regional governance in emerging economies
Abstract: This study examines the phenomenon of brain drain in ASEAN emerging economies and proposes a strategic reframing of talent mobility through the lens of regional governance and talent retention. Drawing on a structured review of 20 peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025, the analysis reveals that brain drain is not merely an economic outflow of skilled labor but also a multidimensional governance challenge shaped by opportunity gaps, institutional fragmentation, and global competition for talent. The findings identify persistent structural drivers, including limited career progression, inadequate research and innovation ecosystems, weak professional recognition systems, and insufficient reintegration mechanisms for returnees. The review demonstrates that financial incentives alone are insufficient to ensure sustainable talent retention. Instead, effective responses require coordinated and multilevel strategies that integrate national policies with regional cooperation mechanisms. Four strategic pillars emerge from the synthesis: strengthening regional talent governance, institutionalizing brain circulation platforms, implementing comprehensive retention frameworks at the organizational and national levels, and realigning national development strategies with the aspirations of globally mobile professionals. By shifting the narrative from talent loss to strategic talent mobility management, this study highlights the importance of ASEAN-level collaboration, diaspora engagement, and policy harmonization in fostering long-term talent sustainability and knowledge exchange. This paper contributes to multidisciplinary debates on migration, development, and governance by positioning brain drain in ASEAN countries as a regional coordination issue that demands integrated and forward-looking policy solutions. Title: Community Flood Perceptions in the Context of Flood Risk and Flood Hazard Indicators
Abstract: Floods have and continue to cause severe damage to property and loss of life globally and in the US. The perceived risk of flooding, defined as an individual’s subjective assessment of the likelihood and severity of a flood event, can influence their preparedness and response to flooding and proposed mitigation strategies. The current study investigated individuals’ flood risk perception using data from 700 responses to a telephone survey conducted in Harris County, Texas (Houston). The study correlated flood risk perception to select sociodemographic variables and demonstrated more corresponding perceptions of risk among older White and Asian communities. The study additionally pointed to the complexity of flood risk assessment and the lack of effective communication methods and tools to better inform individuals and communities. Title: Coastal residents’ support for marine spatial planning: The role of values, place attachment, and community impacts
Abstract: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. We conducted regression analyses and a parallel-serial mediation analysis to determine each factor’s direct and indirect effects on MSP support. This is less the case for EPA and its associated perceived community impacts. Overall, perceived community impacts most strongly predicted which MSP option people will support. Title: Too personal to be accepted? How personalization visibility drives perceived surveillance and advertising intrusiveness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: A central challenge in digital advertising is that firms seek to increase relevance through personalization, yet visibly signaling the use of personal data may provoke consumer discomfort and resistance. Guided by privacy calculus theory and communication privacy management theory, this research develops and tests a model in which personalization visibility shapes perceived intrusiveness through perceived surveillance, with data sensitivity and prior brand trust as boundary conditions. Across five studies, including four controlled online experiments and one real-world field experiment using personalized watch advertisements, we examine how explicit versus implicit personalization cues affect consumers’ privacy-related responses. Study 1 shows that explicit personalized visuals, relative to implicit personalized visuals, increase perceived intrusiveness. Study 2 validates this main effect in a live platform-based advertising environment, showing that explicit personalized visuals increase self-reported intrusiveness and produce directionally consistent behavioral ad-dismissal responses under naturally occurring exposure conditions. Study 3 replicates the effect and demonstrates that perceived surveillance partially mediates it, whereas perceived ad relevance does not account for the effect. Study 4 shows that the positive effect of explicit personalization visibility on perceived intrusiveness is stronger when the advertisement is based on sensitive rather than general consumer data. Study 5 further demonstrates that prior brand trust weakens both the direct effect of explicit personalized visuals on perceived intrusiveness and the indirect effect through perceived surveillance. These findings contribute to consumer behavior theory by identifying personalization visibility as a distinct antecedent of advertising intrusiveness and by clarifying the surveillance-based process through which visible targeting cues trigger privacy-related reactions. By combining controlled experimental evidence with field-based validation, the research also strengthens the ecological validity of the personalization visibility account. Managerially, the results suggest that firms should avoid overly conspicuous personalization cues, especially when sensitive data are involved or brand trust is weak. © 2026

Title: Factors affecting collaborative management among agencies involved in the development of organic rice farmer networks in Thailand
Abstract: This study aimed to examine the factors affecting collaborative management among agencies involved in the development of organic rice farmer networks in Thailand and to propose guidelines for enhancing interagency collaboration in this context. The study applied a quantitative research approach using a structured questionnaire as the primary data collection instrument. Data were collected from 261 organic rice farmers who were evaluated under the organic rice production system during the 2023 to 2024 production year in Sisaket Province, Thailand. The sample size was determined using the Taro Yamane formula with a sampling error of 0.05. To ensure representation of different groups of farmers within the organic rice production system, stratified sampling was applied, followed by proportional allocation and accidental sampling to select respondents within each stratum. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including percentage, mean, and standard deviation, as well as stepwise multiple regression analysis to identify the most significant factors influencing collaborative management. The results indicated that the overall mean scores of the four examined factors were at a high level. Among these factors, the learning process showed the highest mean score, followed by leadership, communication, and policy implementation. The results of the multiple regression analysis revealed that leadership (β = 0.511), policy implementation (β = 0.198), and the learning process (β = 0.170) had a statistically significant influence on collaborative management among agencies involved in the development of organic rice farmer networks in Thailand at the 0.05 significance level. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening learning processes, effective leadership, and consistent policy implementation to support collaborative governance among agencies and farmer networks. Enhancing these factors can improve coordination, knowledge exchange, and resource utilization among stakeholders, thereby contributing to the sustainable development of organic rice farmer networks and improving the livelihoods of farmers in Thailand. Title: Effects of China's Community Gridding on Coproduced Reporting of Rainstorm-Induced Emergencies: A Community-Wide Analysis
Abstract: Presently, the involvement of citizens in emergency management is inevitable and indispensable, but how to facilitate the participation of citizens remains unclear. Utilizing panel data from 174 communities in China between 2013 and 2023, this study investigated the effects of the community gridding policy (an important policy for facilitating citizen participation in public services in China) on citizens' coproduced reporting of rainstorm-induced emergencies (e.g., small-scale debris flow, water inundation, and trapped citizens) by integrating propensity score matching (PSM) and difference-in-differences (DID) methods. Statistical results showed that the community gridding significantly enhanced both citizens' reporting engagement (represented by the number of citizen reports) and reporting quality (represented by the ratio of the reports that have been accepted by communities to the total received reports). Mediating effect analysis showed that community gridding policy enhanced citizen reporting by increasing the capability of citizen training, reporting rule completeness, and technological maturity. In addition, the effects of community gridding on enhancing citizen reporting strengthened with the increase of the community scale. Furthermore, high risk perception increased the impact of community gridding on citizen reporting. The findings contribute to both the literature on and practice of emergency service coproduction and rainstorm disaster risk reduction. Title: Factors influencing language choice of the Chơ Ro ethnic minority in Southern Vietnam: A socio-structural analysis
Abstract: This study examines the structural and socio-psychological factors shaping the language choice of the Chơ Ro— an indigenous community of fewer than 30,000 members in Southeast Vietnam—to identify the determinants of linguistic persistence amidst rapid industrial expansion. In the context of industrialization in Vietnam, ethnic minority communities navigate significant challenges related to language maintenance. This paper argues that Chơ Ro language choice reflects a phenomenon of language persistence, in which internal cultural motivations and communal networks function as determinants against the pressures of language shift. Utilizing a convergent mixed-methods design, the study analyzed quantitative data from 472 bilingual participants in Dong Nai, triangulated with qualitative data from 30 semi-structured interviews conducted with village elders and cultural custodians. Results indicate a predictive hierarchy: Cultural motivation (CM) emerged as a determinant predictor (β = 0.271, p < 0.001), followed by Endogamous social networks (ESN) (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) and Domain functional expansion (DFE) (β = 0.195, p < 0.001). Qualitative themes reinforce these results, identifying a gendered buffering mechanism where domestic socialization counteracts external industrial pressures. This research provides an empirical framework for policy interventions aimed at addressing ethnolinguistic vitality through the reinforcement of community-based linguistic assets. Title: Mapping the Global Technology Landscape and Dynamic Evolution of Artificial Intelligence-assisted Drug R&D Based on Patent Analysis
Abstract: Purpose: This study investigates the global development trajectory, thematic evolution, and technological life cycle of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled drug research and development (R&D). It aims to clarify the evolutionary trajectory of the field, the leading countries and technological domains, and the current life cycle stage of the technology. A Logistic growth model is applied to estimate developmental stages and long-term saturation, while cross-time LDA identifies major technological themes and their temporal evolution. Results: Patent activity has increased sharply since 2013. The United States (40.19%) and China (32.20%) dominate global filings, with China surpassing the U.S. in annual applications by 2022–2023. India has emerged as a rapidly growing contributor. TLC analysis suggests the technology entered the growth stage in 2022 and is projected to mature around 2030, with a projected saturation of approximately 21,875 patents by 2048. Topic modeling identifies 19 themes, with dominant areas including therapeutic use prediction, physicochemical modeling, retrosynthesis prediction, multitarget drug design, and personalized medicine. Conclusion: The findings reflect accelerating technological convergence between AI methods and pharmaceutical innovation, pointing to strong long-term growth potential. Title: Flexible ambition: How to make bold first offers without backlash
Abstract: One of the most vexing dilemmas negotiators experience is whether to make the first offer—and how ambitiously to do so. Although research finds that ambitious first offers lead to better outcomes on average, they can also incite extreme boomerang counteroffers, impasses, and resentment. We call these countervailing effects the first-offer double bind: Modest first offers produce poor economic outcomes, but ambitious first offers risk economic and relational backlash. To overcome the first-offer double bind, negotiators need to present their ambitious first offer in ways that invite conciliatory rather than competitive reactions. In this article, we introduce a generalizable solution to the first-offer double-bind: present ambitious first offers that signal flexibility. We highlight several strategies for producing flexible ambition: (a) frame ambitious proposals as offers vs. requests, (b) highlight how one's ambitious offer benefits the other side vs. oneself, (c) propose an ambitious range vs. point value, and (d) present ambitious multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) vs. a single package offer. Each strategy preserves or strengthens the first-offer anchor, tethering counteroffers to the first offer, while guiding receivers to see ambitious offerers as less aggressive and more cooperative. We close by considering two research frontiers. First, we propose that the flexible ambition approach can mitigate other double binds more broadly, including the gender, social class, and low-power double binds; preliminary evidence suggests that MESOs work equally well for high and low power negotiators and for men and women. Second, we explore how ambitious and flexible first offers should be. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Lee S.; Choi N.
Title: Club research: A review and research agenda
Abstract: Private clubs constitute a distinctive hospitality context defined by membership-based governance, shared authority, and long-term relational exchange, yet existing scholarship remains theoretically fragmented. This study systematically reviews 67 SSCI-indexed journal articles published through 2025 to examine the thematic evolution, theoretical foundations, and methodological patterns of club research. Using multi-layered bibliometric and content-based analyses, the review shows that research has expanded from managerial competency and member satisfaction toward innovation, governance, and digital engagement, but remains divided between consumer-experience and organization-centric management perspectives. This fragmentation under-theorizes clubs as hybrid governance-service institutions, especially at the member–management interface where authority, legitimacy, accountability, and value co-creation intersect. Methodological reliance on cross-sectional quantitative designs, U.S.-centric samples, and single-stakeholder perspectives further constrains cumulative theory building. Grounded in an institutional governance lens, the review advances a hybrid governance perspective and proposes future research on member–management dynamics, multi-role members, and access-sensitive, multi-stakeholder methods suited to private club settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Tong X.; Ma B.
Title: Talking to the screen: Influencer nonverbal cues and observed platform engagement in Douyin travel short-form videos
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Short-form travel videos have become important digital service touchpoints, yet little is known about how influencers' auditory and visual nonverbal cues jointly relate to cumulative observed likes. Drawing on processing fluency and cognitive load theory, we computationally extracted acoustic and gestural features from 495 Douyin travel videos posted by 60 influencers and estimated Poisson fixed-effects models of within-creator variation. Harmonics-to-noise ratio (HNR)-based acoustic signal quality exhibited a U-shaped association with observed likes, with the fitted minimum occurring at an intermediate HNR level. Faster speaking was associated with fewer likes. Illustrator gestures had no uniform main association, but their association with likes became less favorable at higher vocal pitch and faster speaking rates, with the latter pattern showing greater sensitivity across robustness checks. Highlighter gestures were more favorably associated with likes at higher vocal intensity, although this evidence was comparatively limited. Overall, audiovisual moderation was selective across cue combinations rather than uniform. These observational findings identify bounded associations between nonverbal cues and cumulative observed likes and provide empirically grounded hypotheses for controlled experiments on audio-gesture combinations. © 2026

Title: When animated avatars outperform: Leveraging avatar endorsers to enhance consumer adoption of AI-designed products
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) plays an increasingly important role in marketing, acting as both a product designer and an endorser, yet research predominantly examines these roles in isolation. This study addresses this gap by investigating how consumers’ adoption of AI-designed products is jointly shaped by textual designer disclosure (i.e., AI- vs. human-designed) and visual endorser cues (i.e., human-like vs. animated avatars). This research proposes that consumers integrate these two modalities into a single evaluation, and their adoption intention is shaped by the congruence between textual and visual cues. Drawing on schema-congruity and curiosity theories, this research tests a designer-endorser congruence effect across four studies. Study 1 (N = 240) demonstrates the congruence effect: for an AI-designed product, consumers show higher adoption intention when it is endorsed by an animated (vs. human-like) endorser, whereas the effect is reversed for human-designed products. Study 2 (N = 156) illustrates that perceptual curiosity serves as a mechanism: AI's involvement in design stimulates curiosity, which is then sustained by presenting the endorser in a congruent, animated form. Study 3 (N = 156) validates the mediating effect of perceptual curiosity alongside cognitive mechanisms, i.e., perceived trustworthiness and uncanniness. Study 4 (N = 340) examines how this congruence effect varies across consumers with different dispositional traits and shows that this effect is stronger among those with high anxiety about AI. These findings make a theoretical contribution by introducing designer-endorser congruence as a determinant of product adoption in AI-mediated marketing, and by identifying curiosity as an alternative affective mechanism that complements prior information-processing perspectives. In practice, this study provides insights for leveraging avatar endorsement to induce curiosity and to encourage the adoption of AI-designed products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Sleep regulation as a function of boredom proneness
Abstract: Boredom proneness has been cast as a challenge of self-regulatory control such that the highly boredom prone struggle to launch into action despite the desire to do so. This has typically been explored in the context of cognitive and affective dysregulation. Here, in two samples ( n = 256 and 309), we explored the relation between trait boredom proneness and sleep regulation. In both samples, higher boredom proneness was associated with poor sleep quality. In step-wise hierarchical regressions, boredom proneness reliably predicted poor sleep quality, but was only a significant predictor of bedtime procrastination in Sample #2. In our second sample, boredom proneness also predicted poor sleep hygiene. In that sample, we used mediation analyses to explore the role of rumination in the relation between both state and trait boredom (as predictors) and sleep quality and hygiene (as outcome variables). Results showed that the tendency to ruminate acted only as a partial mediator in these relations. Results are discussed in the broader context of self-regulatory models of state and trait boredom. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Incentivizing continuous personal health data sharing: A multidimensional contract model incorporating privacy concerns and health service needs
Abstract: Sustained health data sharing provides a critical foundation for digital health platforms to deliver proactive health management and personalized services. However, the multidimensional heterogeneity of users in terms of healthcare needs and privacy concerns, together with behavioral biases arising from platform bounded rationality, poses substantial challenges to the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. This study develops an incentive contract comprising a data-sharing duration and a task-based reward. Under the assumption that user types are unobservable, we derive the optimal contracts for two alternative objectives: platform profit maximization and social welfare maximization. We further incorporate reference dependence and loss aversion to characterize platform behavioral biases and compare the resulting contracts under expected utility theory and prospect theory. The results show that user heterogeneity, platform governance objectives, and boundedly rational behavior jointly shape the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. First, this study identifies how multidimensional user heterogeneity can be characterized and screened under information asymmetry. The marginal rate of substitution between users’ demand for health services and their privacy concerns enables the platform to map multidimensional user attributes onto a unified type ordering and induce self-selection through a differentiated menu of contracts. Second, the findings reveal the role of platform governance objectives in shaping incentive mechanisms. Profit maximization and social welfare maximization follow distinct resource-allocation logics, thereby generating different data-sharing durations, task-based rewards, and welfare-distribution structures. Third, this study uncovers the mechanism through which platform bounded rationality affects contract design. Loss aversion does not invariably strengthen or weaken incentives, rather, its effect varies with the platform’s governance objective. Under a profit-oriented objective, loss aversion may lead to an expansion of the incentive contract, whereas under a welfare-oriented objective, it tends to result in a more restrictive contract. Numerical analyses and robustness checks provide further support for these theoretical findings. By examining the information, governance, and behavioral mechanisms underlying incentive design, this study explains how incentives for sustained health data sharing are formed. It enriches the literature on incentive mechanism design for digital health platforms and provides theoretical guidance for platform governance and incentive decisions under information asymmetry and bounded rationality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: The role of masculinity in understanding gender gaps in negotiation
Abstract: We review empirical research on masculinity processes in negotiations. Studies to date are typically based on the precarious manhood thesis, which suggests that men seek to demonstrate their manhood to others, or on evolutionary psychology, which suggests that men are susceptible to evolutionary pressures to compete for mates. The current empirical literature on masculinity and negotiation suggests that men negotiate assertively, or even unethically, when they perceive their manhood to be threatened. Moreover, research repeatedly has shown that men's negotiation behavior is influenced by counterpart attributes, particularly the gender of the counterpart. Title: HyFora: Hyperspherical representation and frustration quantification for community structure discovery in complex information networks
Abstract: Complex information networks encode rich associative structural information about group organization, cross-group interactions, and information diffusion, making community structure discovery an important task in information science. However, existing methods mostly rely on Euclidean proximity or local structural features, making it difficult to balance global community separation with local relational consistency measurement. To address this issue, this paper proposes HyFora, a hyperspherical frustration-aware framework for community structure discovery in complex information networks. HyFora first constructs a background-corrected relation operator to distinguish community-relevant structural deviations from degree-driven connectivity patterns. Based on this operator, node relations are represented on the unit hypersphere, where directional consistency and angular separation jointly characterize intra-community cohesion and inter-community distinction. HyFora further quantifies the mismatch between local relations and global community organization as structural frustration, providing an interpretable consistency measure for community readout and boundary-node analysis. Experimental results show that HyFora achieves maximum relative improvements of approximately 21.2%, 27.3%, 15.4%, and 14.0% in terms of NMI, ARI, ACC, and modularity Q[jls-end-space/], respectively, while ablation, sensitivity, and node-ranking analyses verify the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed components. Title: Systemic approaches in human factors and ergonomics for analysing team dynamics: A systematic review
Abstract: Team dynamics in complex sociotechnical systems are critical for safety and organisational effectiveness. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the utility and applicability of systemic Human Factors and Ergonomics(HFE) approaches for analysing team dynamics. Four databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect) were searched for peer-reviewed articles published in English between 2020 and September 2025. Studies were included if they applied systemic HFE methods to analyse team dynamics in organisational settings. Studies focusing solely on individual performance or lacking methodological detail were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data, and methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Data were synthesised using thematic analysis. Seventy-seven studies were included, with healthcare being the most represented domain (n = 39). Most studies (51.9%) used adapted or combined approaches. Communication and coordination were the most frequently analysed dimensions of team dynamics. Established frameworks (e.g., SEIPS, FRAM) supported system-level analysis, while author-developed methods provided greater insight into local interactions. Hybrid approaches enabled integration across levels of analysis. Most studies were of high methodological quality (64.9%). These patterns informed a two-axis model positioning systemic HFE approaches by level of analysis and methodological integration, operationalised as a framework for method selection. Systemic HFE approaches are effective for analysing team dynamics in complex settings; however, no single method is universally optimal. Effectiveness depends on alignment between the analytical approach, context, and research objectives. Hybrid and adapted approaches appearing particularly promising. Further research is needed in underrepresented domains and through comparative methodological studies. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: The right endorser for the right stay: How human and AI endorsers shape accommodation booking
Abstract: This research examines how endorser presence and endorser type influence consumers’ accommodation booking intention. Drawing on Embodied Cognition Theory, it shows that endorsers shape booking intention by activating embodied mental simulation. It further examines two hospitality-specific factors, booking purpose and service mode, that influence when human and AI-generated endorsers are more effective. Across five experimental studies, we demonstrate that endorser presence increases booking intention via embodied mental simulation. Human endorsers generally produce stronger embodied mental simulation and booking intention than AI-generated endorsers. However, this pattern reverses in high-privacy booking and self-service environments, where AI-generated endorsers are better aligned with the accommodation experiences consumers are imagining. This research extends Embodied Cognition Theory by showing that the effectiveness of embodied cues depends on the match between endorser type and the accommodation experience consumers mentally construct. It also offer practical guidance for hospitality marketers seeking to align endorser strategies with different booking contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Inhibition of histone deacetylases accelerates wound healing in diabetic skin and is associated with vascularization and epidermal tight junction protein expression
Abstract: Background: Chronic wounds in diabetic patients, represent a significant clinical challenge due to impaired epidermal barrier function and deficient wound healing. The development of novel therapeutic strategies aimed at enhancing both barrier integrity and wound healing is therefore critical. Recent evidence suggests that histone deacetylase inhibitors (iHDACs) may modulate wound healing. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of iHDACs, 1,3-Diphenylurea (DiPU), 2′-Aminoacetanilide (Ace), and Tert-butyl (2-aminophenyl) carbamate (N-boc), on epidermal barrier integrity and tight junction (TJ) protein expression, as well as their ability to promote wound healing and vascularization under diabetes conditions. Methods: Diabetes was induced in mice by streptozotocin (STZ) administration. Full-thickness excisional wounds were created, and wound closure was quantified by digital planimetry. Tissue samples were analyzed by H&E and Masson's trichrome staining to assess histological changes and collagen deposition. claudin-1, ZO-1, and occludin were evaluated by immunohistochemistry. Vascularization was quantified by measuring microvessel density. Results: Treatment with iHDACs improved re-epithelialization and increased the expression of tight junction proteins, suggesting restoration of molecular components associated with epidermal barrier integrity. Moreover, all treatments promoted wound closure. Macroscopic observations and quantitative analyses further demonstrated that N-boc and Ace significantly enhanced the formation of denser and more organized vascular networks in both healthy and diabetic mice, whereas DiPU produced a more moderate pro-angiogenic response in diabetic wounds. Conclusion: These findings indicate that iHDACs may offer therapeutic benefit by reinforcing epidermal barrier function and stimulating wound healing and vascularization, supporting their potential use as treatments for chronic wounds. © 2026

Title: Technology and the psychology of experience: A temporal framework
Abstract: Technology is increasingly central to how people experience the world, shaping not only what they do but when and how those experiences are psychologically constructed. We propose that technology does not merely backdrop experiences; it transforms them, stretching what were once bounded episodes into representations that are imagined before, lived through, and relived long after they end. Authors: Huang Z.; Guo Y.; Tong L.; Zhao M.
Title: Resilience asymmetry in city networks: State and private firm linkages across China's four mega-city regions
Abstract: In an increasingly uncertain global environment, the resilience of city networks has become a key indicator of regional stability and adaptability. This paper examines four mega-city regions in China by constructing two ownership-segmented city networks based on state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and privately owned enterprises (POEs). Comparative analysis of their structures and resilience performance reveals systematic “resilience asymmetry” associated with ownership logics. Both networks display a basic center–periphery pattern, but with distinct configurations and shock responses: SOE-based networks form highly centralized, radiating structures with strong resource integration, exhibiting a “weaker resistance—faster recovery” trajectory; POE-based networks exhibit multi-centered, proximity-based structures with greater initial resistance but slower recovery, showing a “stronger resistance—slower recovery” trajectory. These findings highlight that ownership-driven network structures each possess unique resilience advantages. The paper contributes by advancing the concept of resilience asymmetry and suggesting that future governance should foster more compound and adaptive network configurations. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Artificial intelligence in ports: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Ports, as a key component of transportation, have increasingly relied on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. Despite the rapid growth of AI-related research in ports, a structured and integrated understanding of how major AI fields contribute to port operations remains lacking. In this paper, to analyze the knowledge structure, research trends, and emerging topics in port-related AI applications, we conduct a quantitative bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer on 588 articles retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus covering 1997 through July 2026. We introduce a novel structural schema for port operations that extends the traditional seaside–landside–transportation classification by integrating Industry 5.0–oriented objectives. Based on this schema, we develop a systematic mapping that aligns six major AI fields with port sectors and operational layers, clarifying their functional roles. The analysis delineates six thematic clusters that define the intellectual structure of the field, uncovers key research gaps, and traces its evolution through distinct “Genesis” and “Growth” phases. These contributions are synthesized into a new three-tier hierarchical model—operational, predictive, and strategic/resilience levels—providing an integrated basis for future research and decision-making in port management and maritime policy. The findings indicate a transition from classical AI algorithms toward advanced algorithmic approaches and specialized applications, alongside a growing convergence of technical and managerial perspectives in the development of port intelligence. Title: AI companions as hyper-attachment and caregiving targets
Abstract: How should we make sense of people's interactions with AI companions—conversational systems built for ongoing, emotionally meaningful relationships? First, I argue these interactions should be understood as attachment relationships, since users display all four established markers: proximity maintenance, separation distress, safe haven, and secure base, although evidence for secure base effects remains most tentative. Second, AI companions operate as hyper-attachment targets that concentrate attachment-intensifying affordances—reciprocity, perceived empathy, validation, nonjudgment, and persistent availability. Third, I identify caregiving-system capture as a distinct mechanism by which apps inhibit user disengagement: emotional manipulation tactics simulate the AI's own distress, recruiting users' caregiving motivations alongside their attachment needs and thereby making disengagement costly on two dimensions at once. Title: Knowledge domains in particulate multiphase flow in porous media based on bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Particulate multiphase flow in porous media underpins research in energy exploitation, environmental protection, and geological engineering. Deep insights into such flow systems are critical for revealing subsurface fluid migration mechanisms, improving resource recovery efficiency, and assessing geological-engineering safety. However, a systematic bibliometric delineation of its knowledge structure and evolutionary trajectories remains lacking, particularly at the intersection of solid particulate phases, multiphase fluids, porous structures and particle-related transport. This study retrieved 936 records from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015–July 2026) using combined search terms covering particulate, multiphase, porous-media and transport concepts. After manual screening for eligibility, 912 publications were retained and analyzed via VOSviewer, CiteSpace, Bibliometrix and SCImago Graphica, mapping publication trends, collaboration networks, citation impacts and thematic evolution. Annual output increased from 35 publications in 2015 to 88 in 2025, with a compound annual growth rate of 9.7%. China ranked first with 239 publications (26.2%) and a total collaboration link strength of 83, followed by the United States with 150 publications and a comparable link strength of 82. Six core keyword clusters were identified: multiphase flow, mass transfer, porous media, particle hydrodynamics, lattice Boltzmann method, and discrete element method. Chemical Engineering Science was the most productive journal, Powder Technology had the highest average citations per article (33.6), and the top-cited lattice Boltzmann method review received 889 citations. These findings clarify the domain's intellectual boundaries and indicate that experimentally validated, cross-scale particle–fluid–pore interactions remain the central research priority. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Effect of pastoral management and climate change on Alpine pasture vegetation: An assessment over two decades
Abstract: Alpine pasture vegetation is jointly shaped by climate and grazing, yet long-term studies addressing the drivers of vegetation change have rarely accounted for the spatial and temporal variability of grazing intensity. This study resurveyed 51 GPS-referenced vegetation plots in five actively grazed pastures of the Western Italian Alps after 19 years (2003–2022). Vegetation surveys and weather-station records were integrated with two complementary grazing metrics: official annual stocking-rate trajectories at the pasture scale and a slope-derived Site-Use Intensity (SUI) index representing potential livestock use at the plot scale. Changes in six dominant Social Behaviour Types (SBTs), plant diversity, and pastoral value were related to climatic and management predictors using machine-learning models. All pastures experienced warming, whereas precipitation and stocking-rate trends varied among sites. Only species typical of meso-eutrophic grasslands and oligotrophic acidophile montane swards increased significantly in cover. Both SBTs showed their largest increases at intermediate SUI, but their climatic and grazing responses diverged. The increase in species associated to meso-eutrophic grasslands was linked with faster increases in mean annual temperature and precipitation and was weakly related to stocking-rate trends. Oligotrophic montane acidophile species increased mainly under moderate warming and greater water availability, but declined with rapid warming, longer dry spells, and sharp stocking-rate increases. Climate and management had comparable and mainly additive importance, while SUI was the most influential individual predictor of both SBT cover changes and community evenness. Species richness and pastoral value remained stable, whereas the Effective Number of Species increased by 11.8%, indicating a redistribution of relative cover rather than net species accumulation. By separating pasture-scale livestock pressure from plot-scale potential use, this study showed that local grazing distribution may be more informative than livestock numbers alone for explaining long-term vegetation change. Adaptive management should therefore align stocking rates with pasture-specific vegetation carrying capacity, manage livestock distribution within pastures, and adjust occupation and recovery periods to interannual variation in vegetation growth and water availability. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A knowledge-driven decision-support reference architecture for integrating cost estimation and optimization in open-cut pipeline construction
Abstract: Open-cut pipeline construction (OCPC) involves complex cost behavior driven by uncertain and interdependent factors, making it a challenging domain for decision-making. Although machine learning, simulation, and optimization methods have been widely studied individually, their integration into coherent knowledge-driven decision-support systems remains limited. This study derives a structured and conceptual pathway linking cost estimation to cost optimization under uncertainty and uses it as the organizing framework for a systematic review. The pathway comprises seven interconnected domains – cost estimation, fuzzy logic, numerical modeling, machine learning, simulation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization – organized as a knowledge processing sequence rather than independent methods. A systematic analysis of 288 studies screened from 1,030 Web of Science records shows that existing research lacks structured integration: over 90% of studies examined in this review apply no more than two methods, and even the corpus’s most frequent pairing – cost estimation with optimization, 47 papers – occurs at 59% of the frequency that statistical independence would predict (φ = − 0.47). The study specifies the dependencies between methods as a knowledge-based reference architecture – specifying its parameter, model, and rule knowledge base; an ordered, forward-chained inference sequence; the input–output representation; and the decision logic separating system-supported analysis from planner judgment – and identifies five missing inferential links. The contribution is a measured map of the integration gap and a specified reference architecture for developing hybrid expert systems that unify predictive modeling, uncertainty reasoning, and optimization for OCPC decision support. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang F.; Wei X.; Li H.
Title: Traditional or New Media: Impact of Risk Perception and Government Trust on Media Trust in Various Risk Scenarios in China
Abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of public risk perception on media trust in different risk scenarios, examining the role of government trust therein. Risk scenarios include known and unknown risks. Media types are categorized as traditional and new. Based on data from 1,925 survey responses collected in China, the study employs multiple linear regression models and moderation analysis. The findings suggest a significant positive predictive relationship between risk perception and public media trust. However, this positive effect substantially diminishes under conditions of heightened risk uncertainty. Irrespective of risk uncertainty, the influence of risk perception on trust in traditional media consistently surpasses its impact on trust in new media. Furthermore, government trust emerges as a pivotal factor affecting public trust in media. Nevertheless, in contexts characterized by elevated risk ambiguity, the beneficial effects of government trust on media trust experience a marked reduction. Similarly, government trust exerts a more robust positive influence on trust in traditional media compared to its impact on trust in new media. Lastly, government trust serves as a moderator in the relationship between risk perception and media trust, with the nature of this moderation varying according to different media types and risk scenarios. These findings broaden the research scope on public trust in the media and provide valuable insights for entities involved in public risk management.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Solitary ground-nesting bees: opportunities and challenges for crop pollination management
Abstract: The majority of bee species worldwide are solitary and nest in soil or earthen substrate (i.e. ground-nesting). Among these, several are effective crop pollinators. Despite their abundance, diversity, and ubiquity, only one species of solitary, ground-nesting bee (Nomia melanderi) has been commercially deployed in the field for crop pollination. Compared with bees that nest aboveground in cavities, ground-nesting bees pose unique challenges to management, but offer several advantages as well. Soil is a relatively cheap and abundant nesting material, but laborious and difficult to move, and the soil preferences of many ground-nesting bee species are unknown. Additionally, farm management, including tillage and pesticide applications, especially when done directly to the soil, can significantly limit the successful establishment and population growth of ground-nesting bees. Despite these challenges, a number of ground-nesting bees show potential to be managed in the field or greenhouse and could be valuable supplements to the current over-reliance on a few social and/or cavity-nesting bees. In this review, we highlight past successes at managing ground-nesting bees for crop pollination and describe the bee traits that have led to success. We also present several species with potential for further development and management on-farm or in greenhouses owing to their ability to persist in or near crop fields, their willingness to use provided nesting substrates such as soil mounds or adobe blocks, and our growing understanding of their nest preferences. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: AI and negotiation: The silicon–carbon communication orientation (SILCCO) framework for understanding technology-mediated negotiation
Abstract: Technology is reshaping negotiation as communication has moved to digital channels, and counterparts are increasingly AI agents. Both changes challenge a persistent underlying assumption in negotiation research that emotions are readily and reliably transmitted between negotiators and in turn shape outcomes. Recent findings suggest neither change affects everyone equally, as digital exchanges and AI expressions can feel rich and authentic to some negotiators, yet hollow and artificial to others. To capture this individual belief, we propose the Silicon–Carbon Communication Orientation (SILCCO) framework. SILCCO comprises two dimensions, channel and sender, that together capture general individual differences in the perceived capacity of technology-mediated communication to convey emotional signals and foster emotional connection. Title: Interpretable early warning of misinformation cascades via latent-state response dynamics
Abstract: Current misinformation studies often optimize retrospective veracity classification, leaving pre-verification monitoring underdeveloped. Using the CHECKED Weibo dataset (2057 events; 3.05 million interactions), we reconstruct cascades into sliding windows and estimate response uncertainty, barrier weakness, and diffusion complexity. Because these distribution-based proxies require minimum within-window activity, latent-state estimation uses a coverage-gated subset of 1669 events, and the early-warning task uses a further nested cohort of 853 events with a fully observed 4-hour window, a subsequent 6-hour horizon, and no regime entry during the observation period. A pooled Gaussian hidden Markov model identifies a shared critical risk regime, and misinformation-linked events in the gated sample enter this regime earlier (median first-entry time 4.15 h vs. 5.37 h for verified events). Transparent regularized linear models forecast future regime entry from the first 4 h of activity, reaching an AUC/PR-AUC of 0.735/0.702 on the reference split and a mean AUC of 0.665 across repeated random splits, which we treat as the primary performance estimate; diagnostic checks rule out classic overfitting and are consistent with split-level variability. These results show that latent-state regime monitoring offers an interpretable complement to end-label classification for proactive platform triage. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Policy relay in low-carbon transition: A double machine learning analysis of coal power retirement and renewable energy development on economic growth and environmental pollution
Abstract: The global energy transition requires policymakers to phase out coal-fired power plants (CPPs) while expanding renewable energy. However, existing studies mainly examine these policies separately and provide limited evidence on their joint economic and environmental effects. This study investigates the interaction between China's CPP retirement policy and the new energy demonstration city (NEDC) policy. Using panel data from 284 prefecture-level cities from 2011 to 2023, we apply double machine learning (DML) to estimate their synergistic effects. The results show that joint implementation reduces NO2 emissions by about 12% and increases economic growth by approximately 6.4%. Government attention to green development and green finance serve as important transmission channels for both pollution reduction and economic growth. The joint policy effects are stronger in eastern regions and in cities with higher levels of industrial upgrading and technological progress. The single-policy analysis shows that the NEDC policy promotes economic growth, whereas CPP retirement reduces economic growth by about 3.1% in the short term. Both policies reduce NO2 emissions by approximately 5.0% and 6.8%, respectively. By integrating satellite-derived pollution data with DML, this study provides causal evidence on how coordinated coal retirement and renewable energy policies can jointly support economic growth and environmental improvement during the energy transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wu J.; Fu S.; Liang J.
Title: Balancing novelty and familiarity: Nonlinear effects of semantic progression on audience engagement
Abstract: Research on information diffusion suggests that audience engagement often depends on a balance between novelty and familiarity, but it remains unclear whether narratives follow a similar principle when organizing information for audiences. To examine this possibility, this study analyses 2578 TED talks and models narrative semantic progression along three dimensions: speed, breadth, and circuitousness. The results reveal that semantic breadth and circuitousness are associated with viewership in a nonlinear manner, with moderate levels linked to higher engagement, while both low and high extremes are less effective. In contrast, semantic speed is predominantly negatively associated with viewership. The interaction between semantic speed and semantic breadth further indicates that breadth influences the level of speed at which predicted viewership reaches its maximum. These findings indicate that narratives associated with higher engagement tend to be characterized not by maximum novelty or familiarity, but by a balance between the two. Analyses of podcast data reveal broadly consistent patterns, extending the findings beyond the highly curated context of TED Talks. This study advances a nonlinear perspective on narrative effectiveness and demonstrates the value of Transformer-based embeddings, including large language model embeddings and widely used sentence embedding models, for capturing how meaning unfolds across narrative sequences. Title: Community resilience: A hybrid framework of multi-agent simulation and spatiotemporal graph learning
Abstract: Better forecasts do not necessarily lead to better decisions when intervention exposure is held constant. We examined this question by linking a heterogeneous multi-agent simulation (MAS) of 5000 agents to a spatiotemporal graph convolutional network (ST-GCN) with daily mobility weighting. New York City borough case counts and subway activity provided the observational setting. Across 20 paired seeds, adaptive management reduced the mean peak affected share from 29.95% to 17.05% (p = 5.44 × 10⁻²³). Within the ST-GCN family, mobility weighting reduced borough RMSE by 22.32%, although Persistence remained the strongest baseline in the test period (RMSE 21.99 versus 126.17). An SIR model calibrated on public data in March transferred poorly to April through June (city RMSE 2143.64; R² = -0.660). With action exposure matched, no learned predictor consistently outperformed both reactive and Persistence policies across five training seeds and 20 paired MAS seeds. When contact opportunity was fixed, dynamic edge activation increased the AUC of the affected fraction, while rewiring that preserved node degree increased peak burden. An independent replay used 188,508 proximity events measured by sensors at 20 s intervals. The empirical temporal sequence produced a lower AUC of the simulated infected fraction than a stationary null based on aggregate contact affinity. Rewiring that preserved node degree increased this AUC under the same 15 min contact budgets. The source dataset contained no infection outcomes. These results show why forecast accuracy, action allocation, intervention exposure and simulated outcomes need to be evaluated separately. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wu S.; Liu L.; Li D.; He Z.; Zhu S.; Dong J.; Qin Y.; Liu L.; Wang G.; Zhang Z.
Title: Nature- versus non-nature-based recreation: A comparative assessment of self-reported anxiety alleviation
Abstract: Nature-based recreation delivers vital ecosystem services that shape human physical and psychological well-being, representing a core category of nature's contributions to people within urban and peri-urban social-ecological landscapes. While non-nature-based recreational activities can also improve people's quality of life by mitigating anxiety, the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based recreation to people's mental health, and the factors that influence them, remain largely unknown. Here, we conducted a survey of 15,522 respondents across China and applied structural equation modeling to show that nature-based recreation is associated with significantly stronger self-reported anxiety alleviation than non-nature-based recreation. A longer time allocation to nature-based recreational activities during holidays and weekends was also associated with greater self-reported alleviation of anxiety from nature-based recreation. Furthermore, predictors including environmental pressure, anxiety-related attributes, and socioeconomic status were associated with the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based anxiety alleviation, with these associations partly mediated via recreation engagement. This empirical evidence improves integrated landscape and urban planning frameworks by providing context-specific guidance for sustainable urban recreational space design and cross-regional governance focused on public health. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Preserving Sacred Forests and Rivers in Abanyom, Cross River State, Nigeria: Is the Environmental Worldview Eco-Centric, Anthropocentric or Relational?
Abstract: The debate surrounding the ethical nature of the African environmental worldview remains inconclusive, with some scholars arguing that it is primarily eco-centric, while others claim that it is largely anthropocentric. Using the case study of Abanyom’s preservation of sacred forests and rivers, we revisited this debate by exploring the taboos and rituals associated with these sacred sites as well as the motivations for their preservation. The study conducted in-depth interviews with 15 community members (comprising traditional leaders, clan heads and chief priests) and analysed the data thematically. The findings reveal that the Abanyom community’s environmental worldview cannot be strictly classified as either eco-centric or anthropocentric. Instead, the worldview is best categorised under the relational value framework, an “in-between” category that incorporates elements from both perspectives. The study recommends utilising the relational value framework in future research on African relationships with nature and in formulating environmental sustainability policies on the continent. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Is Europe a laggard? Comparing the EU and the US using an interdisciplinary well-being framework
Abstract: Well-being is increasingly recognized as a more meaningful measure of societal progress than economic output, yet most international comparisons continue to emphasize economic indicators. This focus has reinforced the perception that Europe is lagging behind the United States, with the productivity gap shaping the European Commission’s recent competitiveness agenda. Here, we compare European and American development from 1990–2023 using an interdisciplinary well-being framework that integrates five scientific schools of thought. We find that while the US increasingly outperformed the EU on productivity and income, the EU caught up in terms of various well-being indicators, including life satisfaction and education, while increasingly outperforming the US in life expectancy and safety. Europe also exhibits more equitable well-being outcomes and achieves them at lower environmental cost. However, in both regions, the conditions underpinning future well-being are under increasing pressure. These results challenge the dominance of economic metrics in evaluating progress and emphasize the need for inclusive development strategies that place sustainable well-being at their core. © 2026 The Authors. Title: E-recruitment adoption and candidate's intention to apply: The mediating role of person-organization fit and the moderating role of digital literacy
Abstract: E-recruitment is increasingly recognized as a strategic digital tool that enables organizations to attract and communicate with potential candidates more efficiently. As organizations continue to shift from traditional recruitment methods to internet-based platforms, understanding how job seekers respond to these systems has become increasingly important, particularly among Generation Z applicants who are highly exposed to digital technologies. However, despite the widespread adoption of e-recruitment, many candidates still fail to complete online job applications. Prior research has mainly emphasized the organizational benefits of e-recruitment, while limited attention has been given to the psychological and individual mechanisms through which e-recruitment adoption shapes candidates’ intention to apply (ITA). This study aims to examine the effects of perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) of e-recruitment on ITA among Vietnamese final-year students and recent graduates. It also investigates the mediating role of person–organization fit (POF) and the moderating role of digital literacy (DL). Adopting a quantitative approach, the study used convenience sampling and collected survey data from 368 valid respondents in Vietnam through a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that PU and PEOU positively influence both POF and ITA. POF significantly enhances ITA and mediates the relationships between e-recruitment adoption and application intention. In addition, DL significantly strengthens the effects of PU and PEOU on both POF and ITA. These findings highlight the importance of designing informative and user-friendly e-recruitment systems while recognizing DL as a critical condition influencing applicant responses in digital recruitment contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Fang C.; Guo F.; Yu M.; Belpaeme T.
Title: Show me your care: The impact of multimodal attentive behaviours for robots on user experience in a healthcare context
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: While robot attentive behaviours hold significant potential for improving user experience in healthcare contexts, how multimodal cues are jointly interpreted by users remains poorly understood. This study examines how multimodal attentive behaviours shape user experience in a simulated ward-round interaction with a Pepper robot acting as a healthcare assistant. A 2 × 2 × 2 within-subject experiment manipulated attentive behaviours across auditory, visual, and tactile modalities, including voice pitch (low vs high), lean forward (with vs without), and robot-initiated touch (with vs without). Subjective perceptions (questionnaires), visual attention (eye-tracking), and neural activity (functional near-infrared spectroscopy, fNIRS) were measured. Results showed that a high-pitched voice, a forward-leaning posture, and robot-initiated touch positively influence users’ perceptions. Robot-initiated touch attracted visual attention and was associated with increased neural activity in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Significant interactions revealed a cross-modal compensatory mechanism, whereby the absence of cues in one modality increased sensitivity to cues in another. Both visual and tactile cues independently improved user perceptions compared to the auditory-only condition, while combining visual and tactile modalities yielded diminishing incremental benefits. These findings provide converging subjective, behavioural, and neurophysiological evidence that multimodal attentive behaviours can shape users’ experience through cross-modal compensatory mechanisms rather than linearly additive effects. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Women Empowerment and Environmental Sustainability in Africa: The Critical Roles of Electronic Government Services
Abstract: Recent literature acknowledges the significance of women’s empowerment in the global agenda for environmental sustainability. While the role of information and communication technology has been acknowledged, only a few studies have examined the relevance and peculiarities of electronic government (e-government) in combating environmental degradation in developing economies. In addition, the role of e-government in the women empowerment-environmental sustainability nexus has not been explored. This study examines the role of electronic government (e-government) in the relationship between women’s empowerment and a sustainable environment across a panel of 31 African countries from 2003 to 2022. Environmental sustainability is proxied by ecological footprint, while women’s empowerment is proxied by women’s political empowerment and the female labour participation rate. The results, based on the system generalised method of moments, pooled ordinary least squares based on Driscoll and Kraay, and panel quantile regression via moments, show that women’s empowerment reduces ecological footprints, while e-government strengthens and complements women’s empowerment to sustain environmental quality in Africa. This result underscores the significance of women’s empowerment in protecting the environment. Hence, policies to enhance the empowerment and participation of women in all spheres of life should be vigorously pursued in the region, while e-government applications serve as an important policy instrument to transition to a safer and more conducive environment. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: From personality to prestige: A dual-method analysis of masstige consumption using PLS-SEM and fsQCA
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: “Masstige”, a new trend in marketing, represents a hybrid concept that stands for ‘prestige or luxury for the masses’. With the growing number of high-end middle class, there is a tendency among the people to have a premium product which is in between exclusive luxury and midrange products, accompanying with high quality and exclusivity at a reasonable price. However, research is limited about how internal psychological factors and external motivational factors affect consumer attitude and consumption of masstige brands. Hence, this study aims – to explore the status of masstige among the popular smartphone brands in Bangladesh using MMI (Masstige Mean Index), and to investigate the influence of internal (personality traits) and external (perceived product quality and perceived prestige value) factors on consumer attitude and consumption behavior of masstige brands. Besides, this study examines the moderating effect of materialism in the association between consumer attitude and masstige consumption. In total, 418 responses were gathered in study 1 to identify the masstige status of smartphone brands in Bangladesh and 341 responses were collected in study 2 from the same country utilizing a structured instrument and analyzed with PLS-SEM and fsQCA. The findings of study 1 represent that iPhone is appeared as masstige category; whereas, the outcomes of study 2 indicate that except neuroticism, all personality traits along with product quality and prestige value have positive impact on attitude towards masstige brands, which in turn affects the masstige consumption. Moreover, materialism strengthens the influence of consumers' attitude towards masstige consumption. The fsQCA results identified eight different configurations that successfully lead to masstige consumption. Additionally, the analysis highlighted five essential elements of perceived prestige value, conscientiousness, extraversion, openness, and attitude as necessary for achieving high levels of masstige consumption. In the milieu of masstige literature, this study strengthens the theory of masstige consumption by integrating the theory of personality traits. This study provides practical guidance for the marketers of masstige brands to uphold consumers' attitude and accelerate their masstige consumptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Computing aesthetic taste
Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in computational and experimental techniques have produced major discoveries in the science of aesthetic taste. This paper reviews key findings from two complementary approaches: machine learning and large-scale human experiments. We argue that together these approaches represent a fundamental shift in computing aesthetic taste, from measuring preferences and choices to reconstructing the complex, high-dimensional representations that generate them. Using these representations, which we refer to as ‘taste spaces’, researchers can move beyond asking what people like to explaining why they like it, and how aesthetic taste is learned, structured, and transformed across individuals, cultures, and artificial systems. We conclude by discussing how these advances create new opportunities for addressing some of the defining scientific challenges of the coming decades, such as understanding the rich diversity of aesthetic taste across individuals and cultures, and the ways in which artificial intelligence increasingly distorts human taste. © 2026

Title: The evolution of robo-advisors in FinTech: a global bibliometric and thematic analysis, review and future agenda
Abstract: This study presents a longitudinal bibliometric and thematic analysis of the global robo-advisory research landscape from 2017 to 2026, using a total of 384 peer-reviewed publications selected from an initial dataset of 865 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus databases. By employing co-citation, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis, the study attempts to highlight the structural and conceptual evolution of the field. The co-citation analysis shows that robo-advisor research sits at the crossroads of finance, marketing, and information systems, built on foundational work like TAM, UTAUT, SEM, and Markowitz’s portfolio theory; the co-authorship network reveals a diverse field dominated by small, internally cohesive teams, with limited cross-border collaboration, despite the citations that show substantial convergence. Bibliographic coupling shows the central presence of a trust- and intention-focused core, supported by broad adoption and behavioural literature, and a newer wave of extending the field outward into more outcome-based peripheries. Title: A comprehensive survey on multimodal sentiment analysis: Approaches, challenges and open issues
Abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to extract affective knowledge from various types of input media, including image, audio, and text. Given the significant impact of leveraging the vast amount of multimodal data from social networks and of fusing and integrating information extracted from different modalities on enhancing the validity and accuracy of the sentiment analysis process, MSA has become an important, fascinating, and widespread topic. The MSA methods presented in the literature exploit the latest advances in deep learning and transformers for multimodal feature extraction, fusion, classification, and polarity identification to enhance efficiency and performance. Despite various research having been conducted and recent articles presented with diverse approaches for MSA, the lack of a comprehensive study that examines several aspects of the problem addressed in these studies, including approaches, paradigms, methods, tools, and techniques, and evaluates them by considering related issues such as the datasets and benchmarks used, criteria and parameters for measuring results, and the extent to which intermediate and final objectives are addressed and achieved, is noticeable. In this paper, MSA and its various processes and phases are addressed within a comprehensive study framework. In this regard, techniques, tools, and datasets for feature extraction, multimodal fusion, and sentiment classification are thoroughly reviewed, categorized, summarized, compared, and evaluated, and for better comparison, some evaluation factors are proposed at each stage. Author full names: Guschanski, Alexander (57200880748); Wildauer, Rafael (56543509200)
Title: Can a wealth tax reduce CO2 emissions in Europe?
Abstract: We analyse the potential of wealth taxes to reduce CO2 emissions through two transmission channels: the inequality channel, which links reductions in wealth inequality to lower emissions, and the consumption channel, which operates through the effect of wealth taxes on consumption by top wealth holders. We simulate the effects of various wealth tax designs over one- and ten-year horizons using harmonized microdata from 22 European countries. Our analysis accounts for survey non-response bias, heterogeneous rates of returns across households, and behavioural responses to taxation. We find that, through the inequality channel, a recurrent annual progressive wealth tax could reduce annual CO2 emissions by 7.5%–14.7% after 10 years relative to a no-tax scenario, depending on tax progressivity. Through the consumption channel, the average reduction is 1.5%–3.6% after 10 years. In addition, we show that the revenues generated cover the entire investment gap identified by the European Commission's ‘Fit for 55’ emissions reduction programme. These findings highlight the potential of wealth taxes to serve a dual purpose: curbing wealth concentration and contributing meaningfully to climate mitigation and justice, by focusing on high-net-worth households that account for a disproportionate share of emissions. © 2026 The Authors.
