Authors: Zhou J.; Zhang Q.
Author full names: Zhou, Jing (60913028900); Zhang, Qingfang (35338644100)
Title: Semantic comprehensibility modulates the time course of prosody-syntax interactions in poetry: An ERP study
Abstract: The present study investigated whether syntactic processing in classical Chinese poetry is modular or interacts with prosodic processing, and whether semantic comprehensibility modulates this effect. Classical Chinese poetry, with its fixed rhythmic framework and flexible syntax, is ideal for examining this issue because it permits a dissociation between syntactic and rhythmic boundaries. Each poetic line had a 4 + 3 or 2 + 5 syntax, read with a conventional 4 + 3 or unconventional 2 + 5 rhythm. Syntactic structure effects were operationalized as differences between the 4 + 3 and 2 + 5 syntax. Participants listened to seven-character quatrains with high or low semantic comprehensibility and completed a word recognition task, with accuracy and reaction times recorded. EEG was recorded during listening, and the 2nd, 4th, and 7th characters of each line served as keywords. Behaviorally, reaction times showed only a Semantic Comprehensibility × Syntactic Structure interaction. Cluster-based permutation tests on EEG data revealed a significant three-way interaction (Semantic Comprehensibility × Rhythmic Pattern × Syntactic Structure) at the 2nd and 4th keywords. Within the conventional 4 + 3 rhythm, syntactic processing varied with semantic comprehensibility. Under high comprehensibility, the 2 + 5 syntax elicited a more negative N100 than the 4 + 3 syntax at the 2nd keyword. Under low comprehensibility, the 2 + 5 syntax elicited a larger P300 at the 2nd keyword, and the 4 + 3 syntax elicited a larger post-CPS negativity at the 4th keyword. These findings indicate that semantic comprehensibility modulates the temporal dynamics of the rhythm-syntax interaction, providing neural evidence from classical Chinese poetry for an interactive, rather than a modular, account of language comprehension. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Effectiveness of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for individuals with premenstrual syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Background: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a common condition affecting women of reproductive age, characterized by a variety of physical, emotional, and behavioral symptoms that can significantly disrupt daily life and overall well-being. Given the limitations of traditional pharmacological treatments, there is a growing interest in exploring non-pharmacological interventions. Objective: The present systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the effectiveness of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) in reducing PMS symptoms and enhancing psychological health. Methods: The review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed across eight academic databases to identify studies evaluating the impact of MBCT on PMS-related outcomes. The eligibility criteria were developed based on the PICOS framework, focusing on women diagnosed with PMS who underwent MBCT. Of the 1,213 papers initially identified, five randomized controlled trials and one before-after feasibility study met the inclusion criteria, involving a total of 384 participants. Meta-analyses were performed using a random-effects model, and effect sizes were reported as standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Meta-analysis of three randomized controlled trials showed a significant reduction in PMS symptoms (SMD = -1.74, 95% CI: −2.13 to −1.35; I2 = 0%). Meta-analysis of two randomized controlled trials showed significant improvement in health-related quality of life (SMD = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.51 to 1.27; I2 = 29.96%). Narrative synthesis of secondary outcomes (depression, anxiety, health-promoting behaviors, work-related quality of life, PMS impact in daily life, and mindfulness) also suggested potential benefits of MBCT. Conclusion: Preliminary evidence suggests that MBCT may alleviate PMS symptoms and improve psychological well-being. However, the limited number of studies, methodological limitations (particularly lack of blinding and inadequate randomization procedures), and restricted geographical representation (five of the six studies were conducted in Iran) warrant cautious interpretation. Larger, methodologically rigorous, and geographically diverse randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive

Authors: Zhang S.; Lyu H.
Title: Sound temporal personality and perceived posttraumatic growth: Positive affect as a prospective indirect pathway in a half-longitudinal design
Abstract: Posttraumatic growth (PTG) is crucial for individuals' psychological well-being and development after adversity. While personality traits have been associated with perceived PTG, the processes linking personality to perceived PTG remain poorly understood. This study examined whether positive affect (PA) constitutes a prospective indirect pathway linking Sound Temporal Personality (STP) with perceived PTG. Employing a two-wave longitudinal design over a six-month interval, we assessed 312 college students and tested a half-longitudinal mediation model. The half-longitudinal indirect effect through PA was statistically supported. Specifically, T1 STP was prospectively associated with T2 PA, and T1 PA was prospectively associated with T2 perceived PTG. These findings extend previous work on STP by providing preliminary longitudinal evidence for PA as a potential affective pathway linking STP with perceived PTG. Copyright © 2026. Title: Personality traits add incremental value beyond food choice motives in predicting food-group consumption
Abstract: Background: Big Five personality traits and food choice motives are well-established correlates of dietary behavior, but they are rarely examined together. If motives are the mechanism through which traits operate, trait effects should largely disappear once motives are controlled; if traits also act through channels people do not report as reasons, dispositional variance should survive. This study tested these competing accounts. Methods: In a Brazilian adult sample (N = 449), participants completed the NEO-FFI-R, the Food Choice Questionnaire (FCQ), and single-item weekly frequency measures for six food groups (meat, fish, dairy, eggs, vegetables, and fruits). We estimated Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control and hierarchical regressions entering sociodemographics, then food choice motives, then Big Five traits. Results: Openness to experience and conscientiousness were the most consistent trait correlates, in the direction reported meta-analytically. Food choice motives accounted for most of the explained variance, yet personality contributed small but reliable increments for five of the six groups: meat, fish, dairy, eggs, and vegetables (ΔR2 = 0.025–0.038). This incremental explained variance was driven mainly by openness, extraversion, and conscientiousness, with no reliable increment for fruit consumption. Conclusions: By controlling proximal motives, the findings indicate that broad dispositions are not fully reducible to the reasons people give for their food choices. The single exception, fruit, was also the group most tightly governed by explicit motives, suggesting that the division of explanatory work between traits and motives is food-specific. The trait–consumption pattern replicated meta-analytic estimates in an under-represented context. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Artificial intelligence-based employee selection in tourism and hospitality: Justice, inclusion, and gender differences in resume screening and interviews
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in human resource management, its role in tourism and hospitality hiring remains underexplored. This study investigates job applicants’ perceptions of AI in employee selection, focusing on resume screening and interviews. Drawing on fairness heuristic theory and social role theory, we examine how AI affects perceived justice, inclusion, and organizational attractiveness. Four scenario-based experiments and one qualitative study were conducted with job applicants comparing AI-based and human-based selection methods. Results show that human recruiters are generally perceived as more just and inclusive, enhancing organizational attractiveness. However, gender moderates these effects: females favor AI-based resume screening, whereas males are more receptive to AI-based interviews. These findings provide insights for organizations seeking to integrate AI into employee selection while maintaining justice and inclusion. As AI becomes more prevalent in hiring, organizations should prioritize human oversight, ensuring that AI supports rather than replaces human. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Driving police engagement through talent management: Evidence from Abu Dhabi
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between talent management practices and employee engagement, as well as the moderating role of business analytics and the subsequent impact on employee performance within the Abu Dhabi Police. Specifically, the research explores how talent attraction, retention, learning and development, and career management influence employee engagement, which in turn affects job performance. Drawing on social exchange theory, dynamic capability theory, and Aon Hewitt's employee engagement model, a quantitative research design was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to senior officers across various departments. A total of 383 valid responses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 3.3.9. The findings reveal that all four dimensions of talent management (talent attraction, talent retention, learning and development, and career management) have significant positive effects on employee engagement. Furthermore, employee engagement strongly and significantly influences employee performance, underscoring its pivotal role in organizational effectiveness. The results of the moderation analysis indicate that business analytics significantly strengthens the relationships between talent attraction, learning and development, and career management and employee engagement, with learning and development and talent attraction showing the strongest moderating effects, whereas the moderating effect on talent retention is statistically insignificant. The model explains 53.8 of the variance in employee engagement, indicating satisfactory predictive power. These findings contribute to the literature by integrating business analytics into the talent management—engagement—performance nexus, particularly within a public sector policing context. Practically, the results highlight the strategic importance of leveraging data-driven and analytics-enabled HRM practices to personalize talent management interventions, enhance perceived fairness, and improve engagement outcomes. Overall, the findings demonstrate that while business analytics enhances most talent management dimensions, its influence is not uniform across all practices, particularly in the case of talent retention. This study provides actionable insights for policymakers and HR leaders seeking to build agile, high-performing, and engaged workforces in dynamic environments. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Authors: Zhang C.; Hu J.; Bi Z.; Wang Y.
Title: Designing the waiting experience: How order tracking shapes consumer engagement and loyalty
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The post-purchase waiting period is an important yet underexamined stage of the digital customer journey. Consumers increasingly interact with order tracking systems during this phase, yet research has treated tracking primarily as a logistics tool rather than an experiential touchpoint. This study examines how tracking experience design shapes consumer engagement and loyalty through two psychological mechanisms: perceived control and anticipation. Drawing on perceived control theory and anticipatory utility theory, we develop a framework proposing that richer tracking interfaces enhance consumers' sense of predictability and forward-looking excitement, which in turn strengthen post-purchase engagement and loyalty. We test this framework using a three-study design combining scale validation (N = 240), a between-subjects experiment (N = 180), and structural equation modeling with a large field sample (N = 920) of online shoppers. Across all studies, richer tracking experiences consistently increase perceived control and anticipation, both of which stimulate engagement during the waiting period and contribute to customer loyalty. Engagement further mediates the effects of perceived control and anticipation on loyalty. These findings extend customer experience research, contribute to the psychology of waiting literature, and provide actionable guidance for retailers designing post-purchase interfaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Benefit-principle accounting of CO₂ emissions in the global textile and clothing value chain
Abstract: Existing emission accounting frameworks assign CO₂ responsibility to producers or final consumers but do not identify factor-provider beneficiaries within bilateral trade flows. This study extends benefit-principle emissions (BPE) accounting by introducing a trade-pattern decomposition for the global textile and clothing (T&C) value chain. Using the multi-regional input-output table, the framework distinguishes producers, factor providers, final producers, and consumers, and separates final-goods, intermediate, and global value chain (GVC) trade. Consumer economies retain the largest single shares of their own T&C BPE. Developed-economy providers generally receive BPE above the consumption-based emissions (CBE) in their economies, while production-linked developing providers fall below. Bangladesh, the world's second-largest garment exporter, accounts for only 0.13% of EU-27 consumer T&C BPE despite its assembly role. Foreign factor-provider attribution rises in GVC-related trade, where assembly economies face higher CO₂ per dollar of factor-provider value added than in direct final-goods trade. Although final demand targets T&C products, emitted BPE concentrates in electricity, gas, and water, separating the consumer product from the emitting sector. Aggregate BPE-CBE ratios sit near parity for Bangladesh and selected developing-country pairs, while GVC-specific BPE exceeds CBE in most bilateral pairs. Bangladesh's economy-wide BPE exceeds its territorial emissions by 19%, showing that sectoral value capture and economy-wide balances can classify the same economy differently. Border carbon instruments based only on emission location or final-product origin can place compliance costs on actors capturing limited factor-provider benefit. Benefit-principle metrics give an additional diagnostic for border adjustment design, product-level disclosure, revenue recycling, and climate finance allocation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Can liking be instructed? Evaluations of familiar and unfamiliar food following Go/No-Go instructions and training
Abstract: Go/No-Go (GNG) training can influence food evaluations, yet the processes underlying these effects remain debated. Associative accounts propose that evaluative change emerges through repeated stimulus-response learning, whereas inferential accounts emphasise the evaluative meaning individuals derive from stimulus-response relations. This research examined whether instructions about stimulus-response contingencies can influence food evaluations before the corresponding responses are performed. Across two preregistered studies, participants received either detailed contingency instructions or general task instructions. In both conditions, go responses were framed as selecting a food and no-go responses as rejecting a food. The detailed instructions additionally specified which food category was associated with each response. Detailed instructions also framed go responses as selecting a food and no-go responses as rejecting a food. Food evaluations were assessed after instruction but before training (T1), and after GNG training (T2). Study 1 (n = 54) used familiar food stimuli, whereas Study 2 (n = 63) used novel, unfamiliar food stimuli. At T1, evaluations of go- and no-go-associated foods did not differ between instruction conditions in either study. Following GNG training, go-associated stimuli were evaluated more positively in both studies, whereas no-go devaluation was observed for familiar foods in Study 1 but not overall for unfamiliar foods in Study 2. Exploratory analyses in Study 2 indicated stronger no-go devaluation among participants higher in trait impulsivity. These findings suggest that providing information about stimulus-response contingencies before training was not reflected in differences in food evaluations. The observed changes in evaluations following training suggest that the evaluative impact of these stimulus-response assignments may depend in part on how responses are experienced and interpreted during task performance, although this possibility requires further investigation. © 2026 The Author. Title: Forecasting Approaches to Pharmaceutical Supply Management Across Healthcare Settings: A Scoping Review
Abstract: Background: Drug shortages remain a persistent global issue affecting essential medicines across healthcare settings. In healthcare settings, inadequate pharmaceutical forecasting and inventory management may lead to suboptimal medicine availability, treatment disruption, and patient harm. Despite advances in automated inventory systems, forecasting practices remain fragmented across healthcare contexts with varying demand conditions and implementation requirements. Objectives: This scoping review aimed to map forecasting methods used in pharmaceutical supply management and examine their application across operational contexts. Methods: Studies reporting forecasting or prediction models in pharmaceutical healthcare settings were included. Studies unrelated to pharmaceutical forecasting, non-healthcare logistics, qualitative designs, editorials, and inaccessible full texts were excluded. Searches were conducted in Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. Extracted data on forecasting methods, implementation contexts, and operational outcomes were synthesised narratively. A proposed conceptual framework integrating forecasting approaches and contextual triggers was developed through interpretive synthesis. Results: Twenty-four studies (2007–2026) were included, representing 13 identified countries. Four forecasting approaches were identified: rule-based, traditional/statistical, machine learning/artificial intelligence (ML/AI), and hybrid approaches. Traditional/statistical methods were most frequently reported (n = 8), followed by ML/AI approaches (n = 7), hybrid approaches (n = 5), and rule-based approaches (n = 4). Forecasting approaches were reported across operational contexts with differing demand patterns, data availability, and implementation requirements. Conclusions: ML/AI and hybrid approaches were also reported in studies involving uncertainty and demand variability. However, comparative superiority cannot be established, and the proposed conceptual framework remains an interpretive evidence synthesis structure requiring empirical validation. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

Authors: Shen X.; Kong J.; Shen X.; Dai F.
Title: Parks as behavioral climate adaptation infrastructure: mechanisms and limits under extreme heat
Abstract: Urban parks are increasingly positioned as critical nature-based solutions for mitigating extreme heat. However, while their physical cooling capacity is well-documented, their role as infrastructure for behavioral climate adaptation remains underexplored. This study examines urban parks as behavioral climate adaptation infrastructure by integrating event-based mobility analysis, park-level adaptation performance assessment, and neighborhood-scale accessibility analysis in the City of Las Vegas. Using anonymized mobility records, extreme heat episodes were identified and linked to changes in visitation intensity, dwell time, and nighttime use. Event-level behavioral responses were summarized using the Park Behavioral Adaptation Index (PBAI), while longer-term park performance was evaluated using the Park Adaptation Performance Score (PACS). Accessibility to higher-performing parks was subsequently assessed in relation to neighborhood social vulnerability. The results reveal three key findings. First, adaptation occurs primarily through temporal reallocation. Second, adaptation performance varies substantially across parks and cannot be explained by park size, morphology, vegetation greenness, or amenity provision alone. Third, access to higher-performing parks is unevenly distributed across the city. Adaptation deficit zones are concentrated in lower-income, renter-dominated, and minority neighborhoods, indicating that opportunities for park-based adaptation are socially unequal. By linking behavioral responses, park performance, and adaptive accessibility within a unified framework, this study shifts attention from the cooling potential of parks to their role in enabling realized adaptation under extreme heat. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wen C.; Long Y.
Title: Modular microgrids and their deployment: Aligning technological interoperability with integrators’ customization
Abstract: Modularity is recognized as a strategic instrument for advancing microgrid deployment and development. However, this potential is often constrained by a complex interplay of factors, including fragmented standards and site-specific requirements. In addressing these challenges, practitioners have taken different positions or priorities, which may lead to different paths and outcomes in microgrid deployment. This study employs Q methodology to explore practitioners’ subjective perspectives on this issue, aiming to reconcile the inherent tension between standardization and customization in leveraging modular microgrids. Drawing on insights from 17 Chinese experts with extensive experience in microgrid deployment, four distinct viewpoints were identified: (1) prioritizing the establishment of interoperability, (2) demand-oriented customization, (3) techno-economic optimization, and (4) industrial synergies. The findings suggest that aligning interoperability with customization can facilitate the deployment of modular microgrids. The proposed framework provides practitioners with a strategic tool to optimize negotiations and mitigate microgrid deployment risks, while offering policymakers a basis for formulating policy guidance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Staff interactions and individual influences on complaint behaviour in restaurants
Abstract: This study examines the influence of early staff interactions and individual characteristics on customer complaint behaviour during restaurant dining. Title: Navigating Sustainability of Fisheries in Pulicat Lagoon: An Indicator-Based Multidimensional Assessment
Abstract: Sustainable management of lagoon fisheries requires an integrated assessment of ecological and human dimensions. Pulicat Lagoon, India’s second-largest brackishwater lagoon, supports diverse fisheries and livelihoods but faces threats from anthropogenic activities and environmental degradation. This study applied the modified Rapid Appraisal for Fisheries (RAPFISH) framework to evaluate the sustainability status of Pulicat Lagoon fisheries using a multi-dimensional, indicator-based approach. The ten major fisheries were assessed across five dimensions: ecological, economic, social, technological, and governance based on 34 indicators. Sustainability scores were estimated using multi-dimensional scaling, supported by leverage analysis to identify influential indicators. The overall sustainability score of Pulicat Lagoon fisheries was 47.50%, classifying the system as ‘less sustainable’. Ecological (65.81%) and governance (53.35%) dimensions exhibited relatively better performance, while economic (46.39%), social (43.70%), and technological (28.26%) dimensions remained weak. Title: Striking the right balance: How sanctions and consequences of customer misbehavior shape hotel guests’ fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions
Abstract: Customer misbehavior in hospitality has attracted attention, yet little is known about how observer guests interpret sanctions imposed on misbehaving guests as rule-enforcement signals. Because observers often outnumber offenders and judge a hotel's response, their reactions may shape fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions. We investigate this through a scenario-based online experiment with U.S. participants (Study 1) and a scenario-based framed field experiment with hotel guests in Senegal (Study 2), manipulating sanction severity and observer guest impact. Across studies, moderate sanctions were judged fairer on average than no or severe sanctions, suggesting that observers do not simply prefer stronger sanctions. Effects on rebooking intentions were more mixed: in Study 1, moderate sanctions produced higher rebooking intentions than no sanction but did not differ significantly from severe sanctions; in Study 2, moderate sanctions produced higher rebooking intentions than severe sanctions but did not differ significantly from no sanction. Title: Towards ethical, co-produced and justice-oriented research with small-scale fishing communities: a multi-scalar call to action
Abstract: Small-scale fisheries underpin food security, livelihoods and cultural identity for hundreds of millions of people worldwide, yet remain marginalised within dominant ocean governance and research agendas. Recent shifts toward justice-, equity- and rights-based approaches in ocean governance and policy signal important progress, but their rapid uptake risks remaining largely rhetorical if not grounded in meaningful changes to research practice. This paper draws on the experiential knowledge of researchers working across diverse geographical and institutional contexts to critically examine the structural conditions that shape research with small-scale fishing communities. We identify seven tensions that are recurring and cross-cutting within funding architectures, institutional incentive systems, and global policy agendas that constrain the ability of researchers to conduct ethical, co-produced and justice-oriented work. These include misalignments between global priorities and local realities, knowledge hierarchies, rigid funding models, and academic metrics that undervalue relational and collaborative processes. In response, we propose six principles to enable and guide more equitable research practices with small-scale fishing communities. We emphasise the need for the recognition of diverse knowledge systems and creative outputs, institutional reforms that value long-term partnerships and local impact, and strengthened training in reflexive and ethical research approaches. Framed as a multi-scalar call to action, this paper highlights the shared responsibilities of research funders, academic institutions, policy agencies, NGOs, and researchers in reshaping the systems that govern knowledge production that inform ocean governance. Advancing ocean sustainability requires not only new ideas but structural transformation to ensure that research with small-scale fishing communities is inclusive, accountable and just. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Digital finance momentum and indonesian government bond yields: Evidence from an augmented affine term structure model
Abstract: This study examines the determinants of the Indonesian government bond yield curve by incorporating a digital finance momentum (DFM) factor into an augmented affine term structure model (ATSM). The study is motivated by the persistent inflation puzzle in Indonesia, where conventional inflation indicators frequently exhibit a weak empirical relationship with government bond yields despite their central role in macrofinance theory. To address this issue, the study introduces a novel DFM index constructed using principal component analysis (PCA) from high-frequency indicators of digital financial activity, including QRIS transaction values, fintech peer-to-peer lending, and e-money transactions. The first principal component explains 82.3% of the total variance across these indicators, supporting the validity of the DFM index as a unified single-factor measure of digital financial expansion. The empirical analysis uses monthly Indonesian data from January 2015 to December 2024 and estimates the model using Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques. The results show that the DFM factor significantly affects both the level and slope of the Indonesian yield curve and explains a substantial share of forecast error variance, particularly for medium- and long-term bond yields. In contrast, core inflation remains statistically weak in explaining yield dynamics. Impulse response analysis further indicates that shocks originating from digital financial activity generate persistent increases in government bond yields comparable to those produced by monetary policy shocks. These findings suggest that digital financial development has become an important transmission channel influencing macroeconomic expectations, liquidity conditions, and systemic risk in Indonesia. Under the rational expectations hypothesis, investors incorporate high-frequency digital financial signals into expectations of future inflation more rapidly than conventional macroeconomic indicators. Title: Strategic decision-making in negotiation: Lessons from behavioral game theory
Abstract: Game theory provides a language and a set of tools for analyzing behavior in a wide range of strategic interactions, including negotiation. Here, we illustrate behavioral game theory's contributions to the study of negotiation, with a particular focus on the role that communication and emotion play in negotiation. We explain how researchers can use games to study various negotiation phenomena, including the effects of power, information asymmetry, and identity on negotiation processes and outcomes. Title: Enhancing customer decision-making through 3D body-scan-enabled personalization in brick-and-mortar stores: The moderating roles of human support and technology intrusiveness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Brick-and-mortar stores remain vital in today's retail landscape. To stay competitive, they must deliver experiences that go beyond what online retailers offer, increasingly relying on technology-driven personalization and convenience. Although retailers are investing in technology-enabled personalization (TEP), empirical evidence of its effectiveness remains limited. Across three scenario-based experiments and one field experiment in two product categories (lingerie and jeans), we demonstrate that TEP, specifically 3D body-scan technology, enhances decision convenience and subsequently fosters word-of-mouth (WOM) intentions, but only when human-enabled personalization (HEP) is absent. However, when HEP is present, TEP does not seem to offer additional customer benefits in this study's context. Although we hypothesized that perceived intrusiveness would further qualify the interaction between TEP and HEP, this three-way interaction was not supported. Instead, the findings indicate that perceived intrusiveness directly qualifies the effectiveness of TEP. Specifically, when technology intrusiveness is perceived as low, TEP enhances decision convenience, which in turn fosters WOM intentions. Conversely, high perceived intrusiveness of the technology used reverses this effect, diminishing convenience and indirectly reducing WOM intentions. These findings advance retail personalization research in brick-and-mortar stores by identifying when the examined form of TEP, a 3D body-scanning technology, is most effective in a fashion retail setting and offer managerial guidance for strategically implementing this technology alongside HEP to optimize in-store experiences while safeguarding retailers' cost efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Exploring livelihood assets among inland fishing communities: Evidence from the Sungai Pahang, Malaysia
Abstract: The Inland fishing community consisted of Inland fishermen and cage fish farmers. They are among the vulnerable rural groups that require economic assistance. Their dependence on natural resources results in unstable income and increased vulnerability. The vulnerability affects their well-being and livelihoods. Therefore, this study helps by addressing livelihood assets that help minimise vulnerability among the inland fishing community. This paper aims to identify and explore the livelihood assets of inland fishermen and cage fish farmers along the Sungai Pahang. The study employs the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (SLF) to identify five livelihood assets: human, natural, financial, physical, and social assets. A survey was conducted among 521 respondents, including 261 inland fishermen and 260 cage fish farmers, using a structured questionnaire. The study was conducted in five districts along the Sungai Pahang Jerantut, Temerloh, Bera, Maran, and Pekan. The data was then analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to identify the main dimensions of the five livelihood assets within the inland fishing community groups. The data were also checked with reliability coefficients (Cronbach’s alpha). The findings show that inland fishermen depend heavily on financial assets 79.53% variance and physical assets 76.48% variance, highlighting the importance of access to credit and fishing gear for their livelihoods. In contrast, cage fish farmers mainly rely on social assets, accounting for 77.96% of the variance, and human assets, accounting for 69.67 of % variance. This reflects the cage fish farmers' reliance on relevant government institutions for support, training & skills, health, and experience to sustain cage fish production. Although both community groups share the same river ecosystem, their needs is differ, highlighting the diverse in main livelihood assets within riverine communities. However, both communities identify natural assets as a weak livelihood dimension, reflecting their shared vulnerability. Policy interventions in Malaysia should therefore prioritise river conservation, stricter pollution control, sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and community-based environmental awareness programmes. Relevant agencies, including the Department of Environment Malaysia, should collaborate with inland fishing communities to implement integrated, participatory environmental management strategies that enhance livelihood resilience and ensure the long-term sustainability of the Sungai Pahang ecosystem. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Faking feelings: Emotional deception in negotiation

Title: Urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity under extreme heat: Evidence from 550 global cities
Abstract: Extreme heat has become a key factor affecting urban residents’ quality of life, existing studies on urban forest have focused on their average cooling effects, overlooking whether and how variations in cooling efficiency affect heat exposure inequity. To address these gaps, this study selected 550 cities worldwide with a main urban area exceeding 100 km2 to analyze the relationship between urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity over the past 24 years. We found that although tree coverage increased in most cities, the enhanced vegetation index (EVI) deteriorated in nearly half of them, revealing a polarizing pattern: “High coverage turning green, low coverage turning brown.” Notably, tree coverage and EVI were particularly fragile in tropical climates and low Human Development Index (HDI) cities. We found that each 1 % increase in tree coverage reduces the average land surface temperature during extreme heat by 0.31 °C. However, this cooling efficiency is distributed extremely unevenly. The study utilized the population-weighted temperature Gini coefficient to represent the inequity of urban heat exposure. About 25.2 % of cities experienced increased heat exposure inequity, particularly in developed cities, as increasing tree coverage unintentionally exacerbated spatial inequity. At the same time, about 5.6 % of cities even exhibit a forest warming effect, especially in the desert climate zones and low HDI areas. About 66 % of the cities showed that as the cooling efficiency of urban forest increased, there was a corresponding increase in heat exposure equity. The study proposed the concept of the equity potential index and compared the possibility of achieving equity potential for the cooling efficiency of urban forest under the three scenarios: SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP3-7.0. The study showed that SSP1-2.6 is more favorable for temperate climate zones and low-HDI cities, whereas SSP2-4.5 is more beneficial for tropical, continental climates, and very high HDI cities. This study provides a scientific, equity-oriented framework for designing place-specific urban forest strategies that enhance thermal resilience and social sustainability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Luo Q.; Zhang S.
Title: Development and validation of a game-based assessment tool for computational thinking practices in lower primary students
Abstract: Computational thinking (CT) is a core problem-solving competence that originated in computer science and now applies across disciplines and to everyday life. It has been widely integrated into K–12 curricula, which creates an urgent need for valid assessments of students’ performance. However, instruments targeting CT practices remain scarce for lower primary learners, and many tools depend on specific programming platforms, capture limited process evidence, or lack adequate psychometric evaluation. This study addresses this gap by developing and validating a game-based assessment tool for CT practices in lower primary students, named CT Practices Quest for Lower Primary (CTPQ-LP). The tool was developed using an Evidence-Centered Game Design (ECGD) framework, with coherent student, task, and evidence models designed to operationalize five practices: pattern recognition, abstraction, problem decomposition, algorithmic thinking, and debugging. The content was validated through expert review and cognitive interviews, followed by a pilot study (n = 74) and a main study (n = 510) administered to students in Grades 1–3 at a Chinese primary school. We examined reliability, item characteristics, and factor structure using classical test theory (CTT) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). We further investigated performance differences across background characteristics and analyzed gameplay records to identify challenges encountered in solving CT problems. The study contributes an assessment tool and a transparent development procedure that can inform CT classroom practice, guide future assessment design, and support evidence-informed improvement of early primary instruction. © 2026

Title: Artificial intelligence and public sector transformation: A systematic literature review on applications, governance and acceptability factors
Abstract: The public sector is undergoing a profound digital transformation characterised by the increasing integration of artificial intelligence into its management control practices. Concurrently, the optimisation of public performance and accountability has emerged as a central concern among scholars, particularly within the broader context of digital transition. This period of structural change calls for renewed forms of governance and organisational steering grounded in innovative and adaptive approaches. Research on artificial intelligence in public administration has developed significantly since the early 2020s, although the effective adoption of these technologies continues to present substantial challenges. This article offers a systematic review of the literature published between 2020 and 2025, conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines to ensure methodological rigour and reliability. The content analysis is based on a corpus of twenty-five selected articles. The findings indicate that the adoption of artificial intelligence in public management control remains a critical issue. AI has contributed to innovation across five principal domains: financial auditing, budget forecasting, operational optimisation, public health, and legal support. These developments open promising avenues for enhancing the quality of public management, particularly through the effective implementation of technological innovations, the strengthening of institutional adaptability and resilience, the development of essential digital competencies, the cultivation of critical engagement with algorithmic systems, and the reinforcement of digital literacy among public officials. Nevertheless, significant ethical challenges persist, including algorithmic opacity, discriminatory bias, and tensions between efficiency and equity. Addressing these concerns requires the establishment of appropriate governance frameworks and the consolidation of broader societal acceptance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Shi Y.; Jiang F.; Ma Y.
Title: Quantifying the prestige of scientific awards: A network-bibliometric framework
Abstract: Scientific awards play a central role in recognizing excellence and shaping research trajectories, funding priorities, and disciplinary visibility. Yet despite their importance, scalable and reproducible quantitative frameworks for assessing award prestige remain limited, with prior efforts relying largely on small-scale or perception-based evaluations. This study introduces a data-driven framework for quantifying the prestige of scientific awards by integrating network centrality measures derived from inter-award linkages with bibliometric indicators of prize-winners’ research profiles. Using a dataset of 1352 research-related award records across seven disciplines, we treat award prestige as a latent construct approximated by two external reference dimensions: public attention (crowd-sourced engagement) and professional reputation (expert survey responses). Across three complementary modeling approaches and repeated cross-validation, the framework recovers rankings that are broadly consistent with conventional perceptions of scientific prestige, with awards such as the Nobel Prize, Abel Prize, and Turing Award consistently appearing near the top across external reference dimensions. Among the examined features, network prominence, as measured by eigenvector centrality, emerges as the most consistently important signal, followed by recent bibliometric activity and authorship leadership. The proposed framework offers a scalable and transparent approach to quantifying scientific recognition, providing empirical insights into the structure of academic prestige and informing future evaluations of emerging or underrecognized awards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: When do sustainability-related fashion reviews become helpful? The credibility role of verified purchase in online retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online reviews are an important source of information in digital retailing, yet not all reviews are equally useful to consumers. This study examines whether sustainability-related content is associated with online review helpfulness and whether verified purchase status conditions this relationship. Using 1,680,956 Amazon Fashion reviews, sustainability-related content is identified through a two-stage procedure combining a keyword pre-filter with large language model–assisted semantic classification and is integrated with review-, product-, and reviewer-level information. The main analysis employs a full-sample Negative Binomial model with product-level clustered standard errors, review-age exposure and review-specificity controls, and an empirically estimated NB2 dispersion parameter. Sustainability-related content is negatively associated with expected helpfulness among unverified reviews (β=−0.763), whereas verified purchase status is positively associated with helpfulness (β=0.596). The interaction between sustainability-related content and verified purchase status is positive and statistically significant (β=0.958). A formal linear-combination test shows that the combined sustainability effect among verified reviews is positive (β,=0.195p=0.023), corresponding to approximately 21.5% more expected helpful votes. Binary Logit and OLS models, year and month fixed effects, and product-type proxy fixed effects support the same credibility-contingent pattern. Title: The influential first offer: How to advance a negotiation classic by integrating features, mechanisms, and outcomes
Abstract: Six decades of research and hundreds of effects have identified robust first-offer advantages and disadvantages. Too assertive an offer can alienate the opposing negotiator, elevate the impasse risk, as well as impair the relationship and outcome satisfaction. In contrast, first offers can also beneficially anchor negotiation outcomes in the first mover's favor. This advantage is particularly strong when first movers effectively apply the first offer's moderating features precision, framing, ranges, and rationales. Despite more than six decades of research, existing studies on first-offer effects tend to isolate specific mechanisms or outcomes, thereby capturing a comparably narrow slice of the underlying complexity. We argue that future research can (and should) advance this field by further integrating first-offer features, psychological mechanisms, and separate measures of negotiation outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Trust in algorithmic governance: How algorithmic control and fairness shape justice perceptions and employee voice in luxury hotels
Abstract: Algorithmic management is increasingly embedded in hotel operations, raising questions about how employees interpret managerial authority and voice concerns. Drawing on organisational justice and trust perspectives, this study examines relationships among perceived algorithmic control, perceived algorithmic fairness, and employee voice intention. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design combined structural equation modelling with semi-structured interviews. Title: How information format, climate attitudes, and trust shape consumer response to food carbon emission information
Abstract: Consumers often underestimate the carbon emissions associated with their food choices, and carbon-emissions information is increasingly proposed as a way to close this knowledge gap. Yet evidence remains limited regarding how alternative information formats affect intended dietary choices and whether responses vary across consumers. We conduct a randomized online experiment comparing personalized carbon-emissions totals, generic food-category rankings, and their combination. We also examine heterogeneity in treatment effects by climate attitudes and explore whether reported trust and information internalization are associated with these differences. On average, all three formats produce negative estimated effects on projected emissions, with the largest point estimate observed for the ordinal ranking. Effects are highly heterogeneous: individuals with greater concern about climate change reduce projected emissions, whereas those with low concern show little response. Climate-concerned individuals also report greater trust in the personalized information and update their self-assessed emissions more closely toward the displayed estimates. The association between climate attitudes and information internalization is substantially attenuated after accounting for reported trust. Together, our findings demonstrate that responses to carbon-emissions information depend on both the format of the information and consumers' pre-existing climate attitudes, underscoring the importance of clear, credible, and actionable carbon-emissions information and of accounting for heterogeneity in consumer receptiveness when designing information interventions. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Halo or horn? The role of prior attitudes in shaping consumer responses to high-protein food labels
Abstract: Front-of-pack nutrition claims can shape consumers' perceptions of food products by triggering inferences about their overall healthfulness. Among these claims, “high-protein” labels have rapidly expanded across food categories, yet their influence on consumers' nutritional judgments remains underexplored. The present study investigated whether a high-protein label induces a health halo effect and examined the role of product characteristics and individual differences in shaping these perceptions. In an online experiment (N = 218), participants evaluated five food products presented either with or without a high-protein label. For each product, participants rated perceived calories, healthiness, sugar content, additives, level of processing, and purchase intention. Individual differences in drive for muscularity and attitudes toward protein products were also measured. Linear mixed-effects models revealed that the high-protein label did not produce a generalized positive halo effect: it did not significantly affect perceived healthiness, caloric content, sugar content, or purchase intention. However, products labeled as high protein were perceived as containing more additives and as being more industrially processed, consistent with a horn effect. The influence of the label on calorie and sugar estimations was moderated by the caloric content of the product, with effects emerging primarily for high-calorie products. Attitudes toward protein products moderated the label's effect across nutritional judgments, whereas drive for muscularity did not moderate labeling effects. These findings highlight the central role of individual predispositions in shaping responses to nutrition claims and suggest that high-protein labels may generate complex and sometimes contradictory perceptual biases, with implications for dietary behavior and public health. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Informing users about LLMs' environmental costs encourages ethical consumption
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming deeply embedded in everyday human-AI interaction. However, the environmental costs associated with using those tools remain elusive. Here, we address the question of whether providing users with information about the environmental costs of using LLMs tempers their use. Such information highlights an ethical tension: acting pro-environmentally requires people to forgo some of the benefits AI tools provide. We study how people solve this trade-off in tasks that are relatively easy to tackle without using LLMs and further assess if the impact of providing such information has a stronger effect on people who have stronger environmental concerns. In two preregistered experiments (total N = 1200), we studied participants' use of ChatGPT in a text-editing task after they learned about the tool's environmental costs. Results revealed that (i) raising awareness of ChatGPT's environmental costs reduced its use and usage volume; (ii) interacting with a sycophantic model, one that encourages continuous use, did not attenuate the awareness effect, although it led to greater overall use; and (iii) raising awareness was especially effective among people with high environmental concerns. Title: Cognitive forecasting: How intuitive theories of attention shape anticipated risk preferences
Abstract: How do people forecast their own and others' risk preferences? Although it is well established that affective forecasts shape decision-making, less is known about where these forecasts come from. Five studies demonstrate that people rely on intuitive theories of attention when forecasting future affect—such as dread and savoring while waiting for a risk to be resolved—with these affective forecasts in turn shaping willingness to take such risks. In Study 1, forecasts of the participant's own expectations and attention were systematically related to forecasts of positive and negative affect during a waiting period, which in turn predicted risk preferences. Studies 2a and 2b demonstrate substantial heterogeneity in intuitive attention–affect theories: some participants believed attention amplifies the emotional consequences of expectations, whereas others believed attention is uniformly affectively negative. These differences led to sharply divergent predictions about when attention should increase or decrease risk-taking. Study 3 shows that attention is also informative about expectations: participants differed in whether they believed attention signals optimism or pessimism, producing downstream consequences for affective forecasts and risk-taking. Finally, Study 4 reveals that many people endorse asymmetric causal models, viewing optimism as a cause of risk-taking, but risk-taking as a cause of attention. Together, these findings show that forecasts of risk preferences depend critically on people's intuitive theories about how cognition shapes affect and how affective utility is generated over time. By integrating affective forecasting, attention, and decision-making under uncertainty, this work highlights the role of metacognitive beliefs in shaping economic preferences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Do narcissistic personality traits and immature defense mechanisms hinder communication and cooperation in pilots?
Abstract: This study examines the safety operation behaviors of pilots within the framework of communication and cooperation, compares how these behaviors are affected by narcissistic personality traits, and compares the results for the correct evaluation and management of immature ego defense mechanisms, which are thought to be a factor triggering this relationship. The data were collected from 150 pilot participants working at airlines in Turkey using a survey data collection tool. It was observed that the participants frequently used the defense mechanisms of rationalization, isolation, and acting out. This result shows that pilots continue to exhibit the same behavior by providing acceptable reasons rather than trying to eliminate negative situations by discussing them realistically. It was also observed that they tend to focus only on the objective aspects of events and avoid discussing the parts that negatively affect them psychologically. In addition, it was found that narcissistic personality traits negatively affect the communication and cooperation behaviors of pilots, and immature ego defense mechanisms are a precursor that strengthens the narcissistic personality. It is thought that examining narcissistic personality traits within the framework of immature ego defense mechanisms and managing these mechanisms effectively will contribute greatly to aviation psychology research to prevent risks related to the human factor, which airline companies and authorities view as an important risk within safety management systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cao J.; Zhang R.; He J.; Wang Y.; Zhang X.; Xing Y.; Sun Y.; Li D.
Title: Digital transformation policy and production efficiency in state-owned electric power enterprises: Evidence from China
Abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly used to modernize public utilities, but its efficiency effects remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effect of China's 2020 digital transformation policy for state-owned enterprises on the production efficiency of listed electric enterprises. Treating the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a super-efficiency data envelopment analysis model to measure production efficiency and a difference-in-differences model to examine the policy effect. The results show that the policy significantly improves the production efficiency of state-owned electric enterprises relative to non-state-owned enterprises. Heterogeneity analysis shows stronger effects among utilities in eastern China, labor-intensive firms, and large firms. Mechanism analysis further shows that increased R&D investment is an important channel through which the policy generates efficiency gains, while managerial equity incentives strengthen policy effectiveness. The findings provide policy implications for utility digitalization, differentiated policy support, innovation incentives, and governance reform. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Martínez J.J.
Author full names: Martínez, Joan J. (58034445800)
Title: The long-term effects of teachers’ gender stereotypes on labor outcomes
Abstract: This paper links a teacher-level measure of gender-stereotyped grading — validated against their Implicit Association Test (IAT) scores — to the later schooling and labor-market outcomes of 1.6 million Peruvian students. Exposure to a more stereotyped teacher widens the gender gaps in high-school completion, formal-sector employment, and earnings, driven by boys’ lasting gains rather than by girls’ smaller, short-lived losses. A single year with a math teacher one standard deviation more stereotyped than average raises boys’ on-time graduation by 0.9 percentage points and lowers girls’ by 0.6. Over the five years after high school (ages 17–22), it raises boys’ formal employment by 4%–12% of the mean employment rate and widens the gender pay gap by about 11% in the first two years, while girls’ losses fade thereafter. These effects run through high-school completion, not test scores or college enrollment. The widening gap in male-dominated industries mainly reflects men's entry rather than women's exit, and students show little sign of adopting the stereotypes themselves. Where structural barriers already constrain access to higher education, teachers’ stereotypes shape who finishes school and their early labor-market outcomes, rather than who reaches college. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Muthoifin; Anwar S.
Author full names: Muthoifin (57211791356); Anwar, Sholihul (59144319000)
Title: Transformative leadership models and styles to improve the quality and development of Muhammadiyah school education in Blora Indonesia
Abstract: This study aims to investigate models and leadership styles that are effective in improving the quality of education in Muhammadiyah Schools in Blora, Indonesia. The research method used is a case study with a focus on qualitative data analysis, including interviews, observations, and analysis of related documents. This research identifies various leadership models that have been applied in Muhammadiyah Schools, including transformational, transactional, and participatory leadership. In addition, this study explores stakeholder preferences and perceptions of the most effective leadership styles in the context of Islamic education in the Muhammadiyah school environment in Blora. The results showed that transformational leadership models and styles play a key role in designing strategic vision and driving educational innovation in Muhammadiyah Schools. The implementation of transactional and participatory strategies has also proven important in day-to-day management and consensus-based decision-making. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for policymakers and education leaders in Muhammadiyah Schools, to optimize leadership strategies to improve the quality of Islamic education in Blora. The novelty of this study lies in the identification of a combination of transformational and participatory leadership as an optimal leadership model in the context of Islamic education. This research also adds a new perspective on stakeholder preferences in the implementation of leadership styles in Muhammadiyah schools. The implication of this study is the need for educational leaders in Muhammadiyah Schools to consider the application of a combination of flexible and innovative leadership models, in order to achieve continuous improvement in the quality of Islamic education. This can be a reference for policymakers to formulate more effective leadership strategies in facing future educational challenges. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: A survey of information retrieval and recommender systems in the era of large language models: Two sides of the same task
Abstract: The fields of information retrieval and recommender systems have long evolved as distinct disciplines, each with its own methodologies and theoretical foundations. This survey provides a perspective on the convergence of these fields, a transformation catalyzed by the advent of large language models. We maintain that this convergence is far from a trivial overlap of tools, but it embodies a substantial conceptual and architectural unification. Our central contribution is a novel three-part taxonomy that explains the mechanisms of this merger leveraging large language models as (1) an embedded engine, (2) a semantic re-ranker, and (3) a response generator. We show how this trajectory culminates in a paradigm inversion, from weak to strong inversion, where the information-seeking task itself is reshaped. The unification is structurally consolidated through joint search and recommendation architectures and contextually curated by retrieval-augmented generation frameworks. This hypothesis is substantiated by a rigorous, quantitative analysis of scholarly publication trends, which provides empirical evidence of this rapid evolution. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a convergence operating at different velocities dictated by domain-specific latency constraints, while acknowledging critical operational vulnerabilities regarding hallucination and bias. A companion GitHub repository is publicly available and offers the complete data collection methodology, dynamic trend analyses, and a comprehensive, categorized list of the surveyed papers, which will be actively maintained as a living resource for the research community. We conclude that the distinction between retrieval and recommendation is becoming a historical artifact and call for the formal recognition of a new, integrated science of information discovery. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Constructing a time-varying network to observe the spatiotemporal evolution characteristics of intra-city migration
Abstract: Studying the long-term migration network within cities effectively reveals changes in urban spatial structures. This paper focuses on intra-city migration activities, introducing a method for dynamic network construction and analysis based on spatiotemporal data, offering a new perspective for examining the dynamic characteristics of residential migration within cities and their relationship to urban development. Migration behaviors are aggregated at the community level in the form of migration flows, and a time-varying network model of migration flows is constructed. Community detection and dynamic evolution analyses are conducted to uncover migration behavior characteristics. Using Shenzhen, a megacity in China, as a case study, a migration network spanning six consecutive years (2018–2023) was constructed using mobile phone signaling data. Our findings reveal that the gravitational pull of communities in the northern and eastern sub-center areas has increased. The dynamic evolution of community structures is closely related to the city's polycentric structure. Smaller network communities are more susceptible to changes, while strengthened regional connections have led to community mergers. The time-varying migration network proposed in this study provides an effective method for observing the development patterns of urban spatial structures from a mesoscopic perspective by tracking and analyzing migration flow patterns between different areas within a city. © 2026 The Authors.

Author full names: Vaheddoost, Mahsa (60518097800); Özbay, Ahmet (57055742000)
Title: Personality, resilience, and educational recovery after disaster: A 12-month longitudinal analysis of mediation and cross-lagged associations
Abstract: Individual differences in personality may shape educational adaptation following natural disasters. This 12-month longitudinal study examined Big Five personality traits, academic resilience, and four adaptation outcomes among 884 Turkish university students following the February 2023 earthquake. Latent growth curve models indicated that conscientiousness (β = 0.34) and emotional stability (β = 0.28) showed the strongest associations with adaptation trajectories. Academic resilience accounted for approximately 32–38% of these associations, although concurrent T1 assessment of personality and resilience precludes causal interpretation of the indirect effects. Confirmatory factor analyses and the Fornell–Larcker criterion supported the empirical distinctiveness of personality and academic resilience. Cross-lagged analyses showed prospective associations between resilience and subsequent adaptation across academic performance, online learning adaptation, psychological well-being, and life satisfaction, with resilience-to-adaptation paths generally stronger and more consistent than reverse paths. These associations should be interpreted cautiously because traditional CLPMs do not separate within- and between-person variance. A robustness analysis using verified pre-earthquake GPA records ( n = 648) indicated that the principal personality associations with academic recovery persisted when performance was modeled relative to pre-earthquake achievement. Person-centered analyses supported three prototypical trajectories: Resilient Adapters (63.7%), Gradual Improvers (26.7%), and Struggling Students (9.6%). The findings are organized using the Dynamic Personality–Resilience–Adaptation framework as a heuristic, educationally specific extension of existing personality-adaptation accounts rather than as an independently validated theory. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cui B.; Zhang Y.; Jin T.
Title: Study on the effects of ditching behavior on emergency evacuation behavior in large civil aircraft
Abstract: Large civil aircraft ditching evacuations face operational uncertainties driven by unquantified interactions between dynamic fluid environments and passenger behaviors. To investigate these mechanisms, an extended cellular automata model was developed using an A320neocase study, integrating aircraft floating attitude, leakage, passenger dimensions, anxiety, and overtaking behaviors. Simulations evaluated varying wave conditions, pitch angles, and passenger compliance. Results indicate high-frequency, short waves amplify pitch disturbances, increasing evacuation time to calm water. Initial fuselage pitch angle exerts a non-linear effect on efficiency, as large angles induce aisle congestion due to gravity and friction. Additionally, non-compliant behaviors (luggage retrieval, premature life jacket inflation) generate negative synergistic effects: at a 50% overlap probability, the model yields a 47.3% reduction in average cabin movement speed. Under leakage scenarios, an improved Tanimoto-EW-TOPSIS model demonstrates that a door selection strategy, reconfiguring routes only upon substantial exit failure, optimizes system adaptability by controlling evacuation time, exit density, stagnation frequency, and water-exposure time. This research provides quantitative references regarding multidimensional environmental constraints and human factors for aircraft airworthiness verification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zeng Z.; Wu J.; Zhang X.; Kong X.; Wan H.; Li G.; Lin Q.; Luo M.; Cambria E.
Title: Learning from incomplete signals: Multi-view knowledge distillation for robust harmful micro-Video detection
Abstract: As hateful and misleading content continues to proliferate on social media platforms, detecting multimodal harmful content in micro-videos has become increasingly important. While recent advances in this area have shown promise, existing methods often assume complete access to all modalities, including video, audio, and textual descriptions. This assumption fundamentally limits their robustness in real-world settings, where micro-videos are frequently modality- and segment-incomplete due to upload artifacts, platform-level compression, or missing metadata. To bridge this gap, we introduce three real-world benchmarks that systematically capture varying degrees of incompleteness at both the modality and segment levels. We further propose MVKD , a multi-view knowledge distillation framework tailored for robust harmful micro-video detection under incomplete and uncertain conditions. MVKD (1) adaptively distills modality-specific knowledge through confidence-aware guidance, (2) enhances sample- and domain-level representations via contrastive alignment, and (3) integrates complementary cues using a multi-view mixture-of-experts strategy. Extensive experiments show that MVKD consistently outperforms strong baselines in both accuracy and robustness across diverse missingness patterns, and generalizes effectively to previously unseen domains. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Strengthening strategic environmental assessment through ecosystem service valuation and public preferences: evidence from Ireland
Abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a key instrument for integrating environmental considerations into plans and programmes at an early stage of decision-making. However, effectiveness reviews highlight a significant gap in the systematic quantification of SEA benefits, particularly regarding non-market values and ecosystem services (ES). To address this deficiency, this study, conducted in the Republic of Ireland, adopts a sequential research design in which expert workshops and focus groups were used to develop a nationally representative discrete choice survey (n = 970) to estimate willingness to pay (WTP) for environmental improvements and to enhance the effectiveness, legitimacy, and practical uptake of SEA. Our findings reveal strong public support for planning scenarios that include greater public participation, substantial increases in local green space (10–30%), and acceptance of short procedural delays (1–2 years) in SEA processes to ensure comprehensive environmental assessment. Model estimates indicate that respondents expressed a WTP of approximately €48–€63 per year for a 30% increase in green space, with the lower estimate derived from the multinomial logit (MNL) model and the higher estimate from the random parameters logit (RPL) model. Results also indicate limited public familiarity with SEA instruments and relatively low trust in governmental environmental decision-making. The study presents a methodological framework for integrating ecosystem service valuation and measurable forms of public participation into SEA processes to support more effective and legitimate environmental decision-making. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Adult-only: When excluding children reveals a flaw in hospitality management approach
Abstract: This research note explores social servicescape in hospitality settings, considering recent regulatory debates questioning the exclusion of children. Although children are often positioned as either sovereign consumers or a marginalised group, their impact on guest satisfaction remains largely unexplored. Drawing on 90,045 TripAdvisor reviews from 72 international resorts, we applied advanced natural language processing techniques, including BERT-based sentiment analysis and child-reference classification using a local Large Language Model to examine whether references to children influence customer evaluations. By comparing satisfaction scores across reviews that mention or omit children, we explore whether these differences reflect broader managerial, academic, and policy-related challenges. This study contributes to ongoing debates on adult-only vs inclusive hospitality by highlighting how children's presence is addressed in guest feedback, and by raising questions about the potential limitations in current hospitality management practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xiao M.; Tian J.; Chen Y.; Dai W.; Zheng A.; Chen X.; Liu X.; Han J.; Liu Y.; Chen H.
Title: How is self-defeating humor associated with perceptions of the physical self? A large-sample resting-state fMRI study
Abstract: Self-defeating humor (SDH), characterized by self-ridicule to gain social approval, has been consistently linked to the body-image disturbance. However, its neural underpinnings remain poorly understood. The present study investigated the neural mechanisms linking SDH to negative physical self-perceptions in a large sample ( N = 1668). Participants completed measures of humor style and negative physical self, and resting-state functional MRI. Behaviorally, SDH was positively correlated with all dimensions of negative physical self. Whole-brain fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations analyses revealed that SDH was associated with decreased activity in the right parahippocampal gyrus, left caudate, right posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), and right precuneus (PCUN), but increased activity in the right postcentral gyrus (PoCG). Resting-state functional connectivity analyses showed SDH was negatively associated with caudate–occipital and PCC–PCUN connectivity but positively associated with PCC–occipital and PCUN–occipital connectivity. Mediation analyses identified a negative indirect effect through PoCG activity, and a positive indirect effect through PCUN activity in the associations of SDH with negative evaluations of general appearance and fatness, respectively. These findings highlight the role of brain regions involved in self–other information processing in linking SDH to maladaptive self-perceptions, thereby advancing our understanding of the neural pathways through which humor styles influence psychological health. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu Y.; Lv X.; Yuan R.; Fu X.; Hu L.
Title: Fixed or flexible: How product formats affect consumer redemption behavior for live-streamed food and beverage (F&B) products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: With the rapid growth of live-streaming e-commerce in the food and beverage industry, low redemption rates despite high sales volumes have become a critical challenge for merchants. This research investigates how product formats and familiarity affect consumer redemption behavior and identifies the underlying psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions. Through five studies using one archival-data study, three scenario-based experiments, and one field experiment, we find that: product formats and familiarity interact significantly: set meals yield higher redemption under low familiarity, while vouchers perform better under high familiarity. This relationship is mediated through a dual-pathway mechanism: at low levels of familiarity, a loss-avoidance pathway prevails through perceived risk, whereas at high levels of familiarity, a gain-seeking pathway dominates through perceived preference fit. Purchase type further moderates this interaction, such that the effect emerges only under impulse purchase conditions. This research extends the theoretical understanding of the “purchase-redemption” process in live-streaming commerce and offers actionable insights for F&B firms to optimize product strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Marine ecosystem extent accounting in a deep-sea-dominated nation
Abstract: The global economy is heavily reliant on healthy ecosystems, which provide humanity’s foundation for prosperity, resilience, and well-being. This interdependence has driven growing international interest in developing frameworks to assess and account for the value of natural capital to humanity, society, and the economy. In response to this need, the United Nations developed the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting - Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA EA), and, in late 2024, the European Parliament adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/3024, which establishes ecosystem accounts as a core component of the European Union’s environmental-economic accounting system. This Regulation mandates Member States to compile data for three key physical accounts: ecosystem extent, ecosystem condition, and ecosystem services flows, covering both their terrestrial and marine territories. It provides a comprehensive framework that allows countries to move beyond GDP, enabling a systematized and coherent assessment of Member States' natural capital. Marine ecosystem accounting represents an innovative and data-driven approach for integrating ecological, economic, and social information into decision-making processes. This paper presents the methodological approach and preliminary results of Portugal’s Marine Ecosystem Extent Account, which showed that 99% of the Portuguese maritime space is deep-sea (' 200 m). Results show that, particularly for deep-sea dominated nations, greater detail is needed, beyond classes defined solely by depth and slope, in order to support useful and actionable ecosystem accounting. The paper also discusses the methodological challenges encountered during the compilation of Portugal’s marine extent account and highlights its policy relevance as a decision-support tool for evidence-based marine management and sustainable ocean governance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Trust patterns in food chain actors in the European region over a six-year period (2019-2024): an exploratory analysis
Abstract: We analyse consumer trust in food chain actors, both commercial and authorities, in 12 European countries and Israel over a period of 6 years, including the years of the Covid-19 pandemic, based on data from the EIT Food TrustTracker® yearly data collection. While we find considerable differences in consumer trust between countries, an analysis over time shows that trust levels have been remarkably stable. However, in some countries there was a change in trust level during the Covid-19 years. In some countries, trust in commercial actors increased slightly during Covid-19, and stayed at this higher level after the pandemic. Also, trust in authorities increased slightly in some countries during Covid-19, but mostly regressed to pre-Covid levels afterwards.
