Authors: Hu Q.; Pan Z.
Title: Helpfulness and enjoyment in eWOM: A dual-value perspective for hedonic digital products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As the digital economy increasingly pivots toward the experience sector, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) serves not merely as a decision-support tool but as an intrinsic source of entertainment. Yet, the literature remains overwhelmingly anchored to a unidimensional metric: review helpfulness. Challenging this utilitarian bias, this study establishes a dual-value evaluative paradigm that encompasses both diagnostic helpfulness and enjoyment to decode peer evaluations of hedonic digital product reviews. Grounded in processing fluency theory, we investigate how cognitive stimuli (product informativeness) and affective stimuli (emotional richness) synergistically yet distinctly drive these dual dimensions. Leveraging a dataset of 12,823 reviews from Steam, we deploy a rigorous methodological triangulation: extracting deep semantic features via Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and VADER sentiment analysis, estimating causal mechanisms via Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) regressions, and validating predictive robustness using Random Forest algorithms. The empirical findings reveal that review breadth and thematic distribution divergence concurrently enhance both outcomes. Review thematic density exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship across both dimensions. While the negative sentiment rate enhances utilitarian risk-mitigation but severely disrupts hedonic gratification. The study advances eWOM literature by establishing a dual-value evaluative paradigm, providing actionable guidelines for digital platforms to optimize content distribution for review helpfulness and enjoyment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Political activism and indulgent preferences: Perceived moral contribution and deservingness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Political activism is commonly conceptualized as a form of collective action that promotes individual empowerment, collective efficacy, and societal well-being. However, this research demonstrates that activism focused on the pursuit of a collective goal can also have paradoxical consequences by increasing subsequent indulgent preferences. Drawing on moral licensing theory, when high-effort, in-person activism is grounded in moral conviction, actors may interpret their effortful involvement as a morally meaningful contribution to a collective cause, enhancing a sense of perceived moral contribution, which heightens perceived deservingness and, in turn, indulgence. Across four experimental studies (n = 852) in emerging and developed economies, the results highlight that participants exposed to high-effort, in-person activism scenarios subsequently demonstrated higher levels of indulgence than those in low-effort online actions or the control condition. These effects are moderated by consumer type in emerging markets, with the effect of high-effort activism on indulgence being stronger among bottom-of-the-pyramid (BOP) consumers. Our findings caution advocacy organizations against assuming that effortful civic participation consistently reinforces prosocial behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Fan G.; Deng Z.; Fang H.
Title: EXPLORING THE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE CO-CONSTRUCTION ON SHORT VIDEO PLATFORMS
Abstract: Short video platforms have become an important channel for doctors to conduct health science popularization. This study aims to explore the factors influencing health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms. Based on arousal theory, we develop an empirical model to examine the effects of video vividness, video complexity, emotional attitudes, and doctor popularity on health knowledge co-construction. We collected data from the largest short video platform in China, comprising a total of 4,009 videos and 1,040,230 comments for empirical analysis. This study combined machine learning, large language models, and econometric models to test the theoretical model. The results show that: (1) video vividness has a significant positive effect on health knowledge co-construction; (2) video complexity has a negative effect on health knowledge co-construction; (3) there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between emotional attitude and health knowledge co-construction; (4) doctor popularity positively moderates this curvilinear relationship. Title: Mapping the research landscape of generative artificial intelligence in education with implications for teacher education: A bibliometric analysis
Abstract: The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models, has significantly transformed educational research and practice, resulting in a rapidly expanding yet fragmented body of literature. This study aims to systematically map the research landscape of GenAI in education and examine its implications for teacher education through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. Using the Scopus database, 16,250 documents published from 2021 to 2025 were analyzed through performance analysis and science mapping techniques, including keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship network analysis, and citation analysis to capture the structural and intellectual development of the field. The findings reveal a sharp increase in publication output beginning in 2023, indicating a transition from an emergent to a high-growth phase of research development. Research productivity and scholarly influence are concentrated among a limited group of authors, institutions, and countries, particularly the United States and China, reflecting uneven global participation. Collaboration networks exhibit a multi-clustered structure, suggesting active yet fragmented research communities with limited cross-group integration. Citation patterns indicate that a small number of recent publications exert strong influence and serve as foundational references in the field. Thematic analysis further identifies three dominant and interconnected areas: core technological developments, educational applications, and domain-specific implementations, highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of GenAI in education. The field is expanding rapidly but remains structurally fragmented and is still undergoing intellectual consolidation. These findings emphasize the need for more cohesive research efforts, stronger international collaboration, and greater integration across thematic domains. Implications for teacher education include the integration of AI-related competencies into pre-service programs, the adoption of pedagogically grounded and context-sensitive approaches, and the provision of continuous professional development to support teachers in AI-enhanced learning environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Food souvenir SMEs performance: Digital marketing, branding, innovation, and Hexa Helix moderation
Abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly in the food souvenir sector, play a vital role in supporting local economic development. However, increasing competition and rapid digital transformation require SMEs to strengthen their strategic capabilities in order to maintain their marketing performance. Previous research has largely examined digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation separately, with limited attention to the combined effects of these three factors and the moderating role of collaborative ecosystems such as the Hexa Helix model. This study aims to analyze the influence of digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation on marketing performance, while also examining the moderating role of Hexa Helix collaboration. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from 335 SMEs owners, and the data were analyzed using Warp Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (WarpPLS-SEM). The results indicate that branding has the strongest positive effect on marketing performance ( β = 0.318, p < 0.001 ), followed by digital marketing capabilities ( β = 0.289, p < 0.001 ) and product innovation ( β = 0.117, p = 0.015 ). Regarding the moderating role, the findings indicate that the Hexa Helix does not significantly moderate the relationship between digital marketing capabilities and marketing performance, nor between branding and marketing performance. However, the Hexa Helix significantly strengthens the relationship between product innovation and marketing performance ( β = 0.217, p < 0.001 ). These findings suggest that while internal strategic capabilities are the primary drivers of SMEs performance, external collaborative support through the Hexa Helix is highly effective in amplifying the impact of product innovation rather than uniformly strengthening all strategic relationships. This study contributes to the literature by providing a deeper understanding of the conditional role of collaborative ecosystems in SMEs performance. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Unequal sanitation in the Global South: infrastructure and governance shortfalls in northern Minas Gerais, Brazil
Abstract: The universal provision of public utilities, such as basic sanitation, remains a critical challenge in the Global South, where infrastructure disparities and governance failures perpetuate the exclusion of vulnerable populations. This article analyses the disparities in the provision and management of water, sewerage, solid waste and drainage services in the Brazilian semi-arid region, comparing a regional hub (Montes Claros) with 19 peripheral municipalities in northern Minas Gerais. Using microdata from the National Sanitation Information System (SINISA – 2024), the study develops a matrix of institutional compliance and integrated indicators of coverage and inefficiency. The results confirm the persistence of a deep centre-periphery infrastructure divide and identify severe ‘statistical invisibility’ — characterised by an absence of official data — in localities with lower governance capacity. Furthermore, the study highlights the lack of coordination between sanitation policy areas, with a serious historical neglect of stormwater drainage and solid waste management. It is concluded that current funding metrics and the expansion of privatisation in the sector are insufficient without a regulatory framework that addresses territorial inequalities. The study provides recommendations for improving public policies, highlighting the need to review federal coordination mechanisms and subsidies to ensure water and sanitation security in peripheral regions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Does AI encourage lax thinking, or does the human preference for validation make it that way?
Abstract: We offer a different perspective on whether AI encourages lax human thought. Specifically, we propose an “enjoyment-engagement tradeoff”: the type of chatbot that people most enjoy interacting with may be the type that encourages less cognitive engagement. We examined this possibility in the context of chatbot congeniality, expecting that people would prefer interacting with a congenial chatbot (one that consistently validates their views) over an uncongenial chatbot (one that consistently challenges their views); furthermore, we expected that people would show greater signs of enjoyment when interacting with a congenial chatbot but would show greater signs of cognitive engagement when interacting with an uncongenial chatbot. We tested this idea in an experiment wherein participants (N = 438) interacted with either a congenial chatbot, an uncongenial chatbot, or a default-model baseline chatbot that exhibited the default behavior of a popular AI chatbot. Results, based on self-reports and linguistic analyses of conversation transcripts, suggested that participants who interacted with the congenial (vs. uncongenial) chatbot showed greater attraction toward the chatbot (e.g., desire to interact again) along with signs of greater enjoyment (e.g., more positive affect) while participants who interacted with the uncongenial (vs. congenial) chatbot exhibited various signs of greater cognitive engagement (e.g., enhanced perceived learning, higher word counts). The default-model baseline chatbot closely resembled the congenial chatbot in its effects on attraction, enjoyment, and cognitive engagement. Findings suggest a novel perspective on whether AI chatbots encourage lax human thought: People's preference for congenial (vs. uncongenial) chatbots may, ultimately, undermine cognitive engagement. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Large language model-based carbon emission forecasting: A sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework with transformer-long short-term memory networks
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of carbon emissions from coal, oil, natural gas, cement, and total CO2 is critical for formulating effective emission reduction strategies and carbon trading policies. However, existing models are plagued by overemphasis on total CO2 prediction, overreliance on single-task learning that overlooks cross-source correlations, neglect of sentiment information in carbon-related texts, and the absence of domain-adapted large language models (LLMs) for carbon sentiment extraction, which severely impairs their prediction accuracy and generalization ability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a novel sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework for carbon emission forecasting, which integrates an LLM with a Transformer-long short-term memory (LSTM) network. First, a domain-adapted LLM is developed based on DeepSeek-R1 and a multi-level fusion attention mechanism, enabling efficient sentiment feature extraction from carbon emission reports (e.g., policy, transaction, social awareness) with few-shot data. Second, a Transformer-LSTM-based multi-task learning model is designed to synergistically predict emissions from the five aforementioned sources by exploiting shared features and the complementary strengths of parallel computing and long-term dependency capture. Finally, a strengthened blood-sucking leech algorithm with Cauchy chaotic mutation and chaotic mapping is proposed to optimize the hyperparameters of the multi-task model, thus avoiding local optima and enhancing convergence stability. Validated on real-world data from the International Energy Agency, the proposed framework reduces the root mean square error by 11.14 tons compared with benchmark models. Meanwhile, the developed LLM achieves a sentiment classification accuracy 0.145 higher than baseline methods, which fully verifies the effectiveness of integrating sentiment information in carbon emission forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Creative thinking ability: A hybrid systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: This study explores the development of creative thinking ability over the past few decades using a interdisciplinary approach in a global context. Various studies have investigated creative thinking ability over the past several decades, but the search is still fragmented in each field. Therefore, there is a significant gap in our understanding of how these concepts of creative thinking overlap and interact across disciplines. So that, in-depth research on this subject remains necessary. This study is a systematic literature review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis of creative thinking ability based on empirical studies that have been conducted. The methodology used in this study is a systematic literature review using term “creative thinking ability” in the article title, abstract, and keywords from the Scopus database, resulting in 4,487 publications from 1968 to 2025. The evaluation was conducted on January 5, 2026. The collected data were analyzed bibliometrically using the VOS (visualization of similarities) viewer. This study found that creative thinking intersects various disciplines, including psychology, education, and business, which holistically intersect with the cognitive dimension, the affective dimension, and the socio-cultural dimension. In psychology, an individual’s creative capacity can be optimized through cognitive stimulation aligned with their personality characteristics. In the business sector, a climate of innovation is encouraged through structured training programs adaptively designed based on employee perceptions and needs. Meanwhile, in the educational context, students’ creativity can be effectively cultivated through the implementation of transformative learning models supported by practical instructional strategies in the classroom. By integrating insights from these fields, it will be able to improve educational practices and foster a conducive environment for creativity that can lead to innovative teaching strategies. Title: Rethinking institutional support for migrant businesses in Sweden: A strategic management– oriented scoping review
Abstract: Migrant entrepreneurship has become an increasingly important contributor to Sweden’s economic and social landscape; however, the institutional environment supporting migrant-owned businesses remains fragmented and difficult to navigate. This study conducts a scoping review to map existing knowledge on the opportunities, barriers, and systemic gaps affecting migrant entrepreneurs in Sweden. The review draws on peer-reviewed journal articles, policy reports, and grey literature published between 2020 and 2026, identified primarily through the Scopus database and complementary manual searches. A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using a thematic synthesis approach. The findings reveal that migrant entrepreneurs contribute significantly to job creation, innovation, and regional development, particularly in sectors such as retail, hospitality, and services. However, they face persistent barriers including limited access to finance, bureaucratic complexity, language constraints, and weak integration into institutional support networks. The analysis further shows that although Sweden possesses a wide range of support mechanisms, these are often poorly coordinated, resulting in duplication, inefficiencies, and limited accessibility for migrant entrepreneurs. Guided by the resource-based view (RBV) and contingency theory, this study develops a strategic pathways model consisting of three interrelated pillars: resource mobilization, adaptive strategy, and collaborative alignment. The model provides a conceptual framework for enhancing institutional effectiveness and improving the inclusiveness of entrepreneurial support systems. The study highlights the need for a more integrated, flexible, and strategically coordinated support ecosystem. It also identifies critical gaps in empirical research and calls for future studies to test the proposed model in real-world institutional settings. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Adaptive Learning-based Semantic Enhancement for Multimodal Dialogue Discourse Parsing
Abstract: Dialogue Discourse Parsing (DDP) aims to identify dependency structures and relation types among utterances in conversations. Existing multimodal DDP methods often directly fuse low-level audio-visual features, making it difficult to establish explicit semantic links between nonverbal behaviors and discourse relations and potentially introducing irrelevant modality noise. To address these limitations, we propose ALSE-MDDP, an Adaptive Learning-based Semantic Enhancement framework for Multimodal Dialogue Discourse Parsing. Experiments on DraDDP and MODDP show that ALSE-MDDP achieves 56.79 and 57.50 Link&Rel F1, outperforming the strongest multimodal baseline, LLaMIPa* (Qwen2.5-Omni-7B), by 3.45 and 5.23 points, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Turning climate concern into climate courage: Female parliamentarians, environmental taxation and SDG13
Abstract: Environmental issues, including climate change, biodiversity loss, and air pollution, have received heightened international attention following the adoption of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which aim to promote global sustainable development. The presence of women in parliament has proven to be highly effective in advancing environmental tax policies that help reduce vulnerability to climate change. Using panel data from G20 and N11 economies between 2002 and 2022, this study provides evidence that women's presence in parliament is a critical determinant of achieving environmental sustainability. The models' results show that female parliamentarians with significant representation are more effective, and they reach the ‘Climate Action’ goal by reducing CO2 and GHG emissions, among other environmental targets. Notably, the country's ecological achievements can be intensified by implementing more efficient environmental taxation policies. We mitigate endogeneity by using Lewbel-IV and GMM estimation. Title: The health effects of genetically modified crops
Abstract: Public debates on genetically modified (GM) crops center on environmental and health risks, yet evidence remains limited and focuses largely on herbicide-tolerant varieties or on local exposure, leaving the broad consequences of insect-resistant crops unclear. Insect-resistant crops can reduce pesticide use and generate health effects beyond directly exposed farmers. Yet their net effects are ambiguous, as any environmental gains may be offset by crop substitution, pest resistance, industrial expansion, and land-use change. We exploit the staggered approval of Bt cotton across China, combined with river networks that link cotton-growing areas to downstream residents. Bt cotton approval leads to significant downstream reductions in under-five mortality by 4.2%, driven by reduced pesticide use and improved water quality. In aggregate, Bt cotton approval reduces national pesticide use by 3.2%. The findings show that the social value of insect-resistant GM crops can be significantly underestimated, as they generate positive health externalities through environmental spillovers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: GLP-1 medication use is associated with stronger implicit preferences for healthy foods based on enjoyment and taste
Abstract: The present study examined whether GLP-1 medication use was associated with differences in implicit and explicit evaluations of healthy and junk foods. Implicit preferences were measured using the Implicit Association Test in two separate conditions employing different types of evaluative terms. One condition used evaluation terms related to food enjoyment and taste, whereas the other used terms related to food desirability. Explicit preferences were assessed via ratings of healthiness, tastiness, and irresistibility. The results revealed stronger implicit preferences for healthy foods when evaluations were based on enjoyment and taste among medication users relative to non-users. Further analyses revealed stronger enjoyment-based implicit preferences for healthy foods among semaglutide users than among non-users, whereas no corresponding difference was found between tirzepatide users and non-users. No significant differences were found when evaluations were based on food desirability. Moreover, explicit ratings did not differ by medication status, suggesting that semaglutide users may be unaware of their implicit preference for healthy foods. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: A reciprocal perspective on internationalization and ESG in EMNEs: The role of digitalization
Abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) has become a critical measure of multinational enterprises’ global competitiveness, yet emerging market multinational enterprises (EMNEs) face distinct legitimacy challenges due to weak home-country ESG regulations, known as the liability of home origin. Although prior studies have examined the relationship between internationalization and ESG, they have largely treated the two directions separately, leaving unclear whether they operate as competing explanations or as mutually reinforcing processes. Drawing on legitimacy theory, this study conceptualizes internationalization and ESG performance as exhibiting mutually reinforcing associations over time. Using longitudinal data from 2460 Chinese listed firms between 2009 and 2020, we examine the reciprocal relationship between internationalization and ESG performance, and the moderating role of digitalization. Findings indicate that internationalization is consistently associated with stronger ESG performance, suggesting EMNEs use ESG to mitigate liabilities of origin and build legitimacy abroad. The reverse association is weaker but most robust for foreign-country scope, indicating that ESG performance may support international expansion by signaling alignment with international sustainability expectations. The moderating associations of digitalization are uneven and are concentrated in visible foreign organizational and geographic presence, such as overseas subsidiaries and foreign-country scope, rather than overseas revenues. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Colors of perfectionism - How experimental feedbacks change physiology using Mandalas
Abstract: Although the link between perfectionism, performance, and feedback has been widely studied, findings remain inconclusive, partly due to the lack of objective assessment methods. Biological correlates, such as heart rate variability, may help clarify these relationships. This study investigates physiological responses to performance feedback during a coloring task and examines the association between perfectionism and task performance. Eighty-three participants (Mage = 20.74, SD = 3.41), including 64 females, completed the study, with perfectionism assessed using the Short Almost Perfect Scale (SAPS). Higher High Standards scores were significantly associated with fewer correctly colored pixels (τ = −0.161, p = .036) and reduced overall coverage (τ = −0.153, p = .046), and these associations remained significant after controlling for age and gender. Higher Discrepancy scores were also significantly associated with fewer correctly colored pixels (τ = −0.153, p = .046) and reduced overall coverage (τ = −0.150, p = .049), although these associations were no longer significant after controlling for age and gender. Neither perfectionism dimension was significantly associated with HRV responses to evaluative feedback. Exploratory analyses revealed associations between HRV responses to evaluative feedback and overall coloring performance. The results suggest that different dimensions of perfectionism are associated with task performance, while physiological responses to evaluative feedback are related to overall coloring performance. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Contextual stroke embedding for Chinese sequence labeling
Abstract: Sequence labeling is a fundamental while challenging task in natural language processing. In this paper, we propose a language model with a stroke-based scheme, called contextual stroke embedding (CSE), for Chinese sequence labeling. The proposed scheme, which is based on the inner structure of Chinese characters, aims to extract rich internal semantic information from Chinese stroke sequence as well as contextual syntactic information among Chinese characters. The scheme works by first decomposing Chinese character into stroke sequence. The resulting sequences are then used to train a stroke-level language model, which contains a two-layer BiLSTM network architecture to produce character representations. The resulting method has been evaluated on various Chinese sequence labeling tasks, including named entity recognition, Chinese word segmentation and part-of-speech, and compared with related methods. The results confirm the significance of the devised CSE. Specifically, the CSE is able to capture Chinese semantic structural information, thus greatly improving the performance of proposed method on various Chinese sequence labeling tasks. Further, the results also show that our method could achieve the best performance among non-BERT methods for Chinese sequence labeling and work well with BERT. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Visions, narratives and numbers: How roadmapping enables industrial transformation toward decarbonisation
Abstract: The transformation to a low-carbon industry requires different actors to work together and align their strategies. To support this process, policy and industry in many European countries have been driving the development of industry technology roadmaps at sectoral and national levels. However, limited attention has been paid to how visions, narratives and quantitative modelling work together within roadmapping to enable alignment and transformation across organisational, industry and policy levels. We examine industry technology roadmaps in six selected European countries, using secondary material, survey responses and two focus groups. The analysis is based on a conceptual framework that integrates the design and process elements considered important for roadmap development and implementation, complemented by the requirements for promoting industrial transformation rooted in the literature on socio-technical change. While most roadmaps included sophisticated modelling techniques and quantified scenarios, the study shows that a well-articulated narrative is equally important in mobilising stakeholders toward long-term industrial decarbonisation goals. Title: What motivates landowners to use prescribed fire in a wildfire prone landscape? Evidence from California, USA
Abstract: The use of prescribed fires on private lands is important to achieving landscape and community resilience goals, yet private landowner adoption remains low. This study examines the factors shaping non-industrial private forest and rangeland owner intentions to use prescribed fire in California. Using the Theory of Planned Behavior framework and Likert scale questions, we administered a survey to 4000 landowners, yielding 509 usable responses. We used multinomial logistic regression to model adoption intention (yes, maybe, and no) and binary logistic regression to examine preferred implementation approaches among landowners open to burning. Results indicate that 27% of respondents were willing to burn, 42% remained uncertain, and 31% were unwilling. Social norms were the strongest predictor of adoption intention. Past wildfire exposure, perceived wildfire risk, landholding size, perceived benefits of prescribed fire, and attitudes toward cultural burning positively impact adoption likelihood. Capacity to conduct burns strongly differentiated the willing adopters from uncertain ones, while prohibitive cost was the most consistent barrier across groups. Among landowners open to burning, community cooperative burning was the most preferred implementation approach, followed by agency-assisted burning, with preferences shaped by trust, liability concerns, and landholding size. Findings suggest that in California, making prescribed fire more visible may matter as much as making it feasible. Effective outreach should prioritize peer-based demonstration strategies, reduce cost and liability barriers, and build local burning capacity to bridge the gap between interest and action. Policy interventions supporting community burn networks and technical assistance could accelerate prescribed fire adoption on private lands. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Recognition of individual angry versus happy faces in 6- and 9-month-old infants
Abstract: With mixed evidence from adults, children, and infants suggesting either anger or happiness superiority in emotion detection, emotion recognition, and recognition of individual faces posing emotional expressions, the current research was undertaken to determine if one or the other emotion would result in higher recognition of individual faces by 6-month-old and 9-month-old infants. The infants were familiarized with an angry or happy face and then given a novelty preference test pairing the familiarized face with a novel face posing the same emotion. Recognition performance of both age groups in each emotion condition was above chance; however, recognition of angry faces was reliably higher than for happy faces. A simple exposure-frequency account of the findings is unlikely because infants experience more happy than angry faces. In addition, lower-level interpretations based on differences in salience, complexity, and discriminability were not supported by image analyses, infant looking times during familiarization, or adult ratings. An account based on the processing of facial expressions as social or communicative signals by infants is discussed, with a possible role for an early negativity bias. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Digitalising waqf for sustainable development growth: Investigating user intentions through technology readiness and ethical commitment
Abstract: The digitalisation of cash waqf represents a promising avenue within Islamic social finance, offering substantial potential to enhance the welfare and socio-economic development of Muslim communities. Through digital platforms, cash waqf can be collected, managed and distributed more efficiently, transparently and widely compared to traditional methods. Despite these advantages, the level of public participation and contributions to digital cash waqf platforms remains significantly below expectations. This gap highlights the need to better understand the factors that influence individuals’ willingness to adopt digital channels for charitable giving. This study aims to explore the determinants that influence individuals’ intentions to contribute to cash waqf via digital platforms by employing the Technology Readiness framework. Specifically, the study examines the roles of optimism, innovativeness, insecurity, discomfort, and moral obligation in shaping users’ behavioural intentions toward online waqf contributions. Data were collected through an online survey involving 211 Muslim respondents in Malaysia who have experience with digital financial services. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings reveal that optimism, insecurity, and moral obligation have a positive and significant influence on individuals’ intentions to donate cash waqf through digital platforms. In contrast, discomfort demonstrates a significant negative effect, indicating that feelings of technological anxiety and lack of confidence in using digital systems may discourage adoption. Given the limited empirical research on digital cash waqf, this study contributes valuable insights into the psychological and behavioural factors influencing online donation behaviour. The findings provide practical implications for waqf institutions and policymakers to design strategies that reduce technological barriers while strengthening moral and religious motivations, thereby encouraging wider adoption of digital cash waqf platforms, particularly in developing countries with similar socio-economic environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Experiential and symbolic pathways to luxury fashion brand equity: The contingent role of brand attachment and subjective norm
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The study develops and tests an integrated moderated mediation model to explain how emotional attachment, shaped by experiential and symbolic brand stimuli, is associated with consumer-based brand equity (CBBE) in the luxury fashion context, and the role of consumers’ social environment, drawing on Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Data were collected from 544 luxury fashion consumers and were analysed using Hayes' PROCESS Model 15. Both brand experience and brand mystery were positively associated with brand attachment. Brand attachment was also positively associated with CBBE and significantly mediated the indirect associations between experiential and symbolic brand resources and CBBE. Furthermore, subjective norm moderately weakens the positive relationship between brand attachment and CBBE, indicating that while subjective norm weakens the relationship between emotional attachment and consumers' evaluations of luxury fashion brands, it does not replace it. This study advances luxury branding research by showing how an identity-based relational mechanism is associated with broader CBBE, with experiential encounters and symbolic meanings relating to brand equity through emotional attachment. By integrating Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour within a unified framework, the study shows that experiential and symbolic brand resources are associated with luxury brand equity through complementary relational pathways. © 2026

Title: Balanced Risk Assessment and Management in Development of Hard-To-Recover Reserves Using Example of Heavy Oil
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technological complexity, high energy intensity, and multifactor uncertainty. This study proposes a balanced risk assessment framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system. Quantitative project parameters are modeled as random variables, while poorly formalized geological, technical, operational, environmental, social, and political-regulatory risks are aggregated into an integral fuzzy risk index. The proposed framework is tested using open data for a heavy oil project and four integration variants: a baseline Monte Carlo model without fuzzy risk adjustment, a model with risk-adjusted mean values, a model with risk-adjusted standard deviations, and a combined model. The fuzzy inference system produced a high integral risk index, Rhtr = 0.782. In the baseline model, expected NPV was -1.79 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV was 66.52%. When the integral risk index was incorporated through shifts in expected values, expected NPV decreased to approximately -6.76 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV increased to 89.90%. The combined model produced a similar central shift, with expected NPV of -6.75 billion USD and P(NPV < 0) of 89.44%, while also reflecting increased distributional uncertainty. The results show that the main economic effect of integral risk is associated with systematic changes in expected CAPEX, OPEX, production rate, and decline rate, whereas variance-only adjustment has limited influence on central project metrics. The proposed approach provides a transparent tool for linking qualitative risk assessment with probabilistic economic evaluation and supports more conservative investment decision-making in heavy oil development projects. © 2026 The author(s). Title: Teachers’ language-promoting questions in primary classroom discourse: Relations with teacher expectations and student learning
Abstract: Background: Enhancing student learning with the use of cognitively and linguistically challenging questions is considered key for fostering student learning in classroom discourse. Theoretical models suggest that teachers’ use of questions is related to their achievement expectations for students. However, evidence for the interplay of teacher expectations, teacher questions, and student learning is scarce. Aims: This study (1) describes the use of teacher questions in whole-classroom discourse, (2) examines relations between teacher expectations and teacher questions, (3) and investigates the effects of teacher questions on student achievement in reading, vocabulary, and mathematics. Sample: The sample includes 329 first grade students and 17 teachers (nschools = 13) from 15 German language and 14 mathematics classrooms in Germany. Methods: First, we coded the language-promoting quality of teacher questions based on video recordings of whole-classroom discourse. Second, we employed multilevel modeling to examine links between teachers’ (inaccurate) expectations, teacher questions, and later student achievement. Results: Teacher questions were mostly of low language-promoting quality. Teachers asked significantly more questions in mathematics, including more open-ended questions. For mathematics, (inaccurately) low expectations were linked with higher frequencies of questions that promote elaboration and description. A positive effect on vocabulary emerged from questions that motivate students to hypothesize and conclude. Conclusions: Overall, language-promoting questions occur comparatively rarely in content lessons. Evidence for class-level expectancy effects on teacher behavior was limited. Our findings suggest that the effectiveness of teacher questioning is domain-specific. © 2026 The Authors

Author full names: Gunasekara, Suwani (59907279900); Pareek, Saumya (58996028600); Kelly, Ryan M. (23488976000); Kostakos, Vassilis (6508135447); Goncalves, Jorge (7103326186)
Title: Auditing TikTok’s recommendations: Understanding the prevalence of misinformation on the platform
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Short video platforms have rapidly increased in popularity, bringing forth a concerning trend: widespread dissemination of misinformation partially owing to the persuasive nature of the rich media these platforms support. However, little research has systematically investigated the role of algorithmic recommendations in this phenomenon. Our study addresses this gap by auditing the recommendation algorithm of TikTok, the leading short video platform, through four experiments. We explore the prevalence of misinformation in TikTok’s auto-complete suggestions, search results, and For You Page (FYP) recommendations. Our audits yielded a novel dataset comprising 8535 auto-complete suggestions, 1606 search queries, and 2893 videos labelled by stance (promoting misinformation, neutral in nature, or debunking misinformation). Our analysis reveals that TikTok’s algorithm exhibits sensitivity to user behaviours, often in unexpected ways. We find the algorithm recommends substantially more misinformation to newly created accounts lacking search histories, potentially shaping the tone of the content these accounts engage with. We also find that watching and engaging with videos (e.g., liking and favouriting) dynamically influence misinformation prevalent on the platform, potentially reinforcing existing beliefs and contributing to echo-chambers. Further, we emphasise how engaging with misinformation on one topic serves as a gateway, prompting the algorithm to recommend misinformation spanning both related and unrelated topics. Our work stands as the first large-scale, systematic, and empirical assessment of misinformation in TikTok’s recommendations, contributing valuable insights on the dynamics of misinformation dissemination on TikTok and also underscoring the pressing need for responsible auditing practices across digital platforms. © 2026 The Authors. Author full names: Bagies, Taghreed (57224616972)
Title: Automatic binary security classification of arabic mobile app reviews using transformer models and active learning
Abstract: Mobile application user reviews provide valuable insights into user-reported issues, including security concerns that are critical for software engineering activities such as requirements analysis and system design. However, existing research has largely focused on English reviews and lacks systematic approaches for identifying security-related feedback in Arabic, a low-resource language in this domain. In this paper, we address this gap by developing an integrated approach for automated binary classification of security-related versus non-security-related Arabic mobile app reviews, grounded in a structured set of security requirement categories derived from software engineering literature. We collected 14,667,283 reviews from 56 mobile applications across multiple domains, including government, finance, and social platforms. Using natural language processing techniques and sentiment-based filtering, positive reviews were removed as a dataset-reduction step, while neutral and negative reviews were retained for subsequent analysis. To construct a high-quality labeled dataset, we developed an annotation approach combining keyword-guided sample selection, expert annotation, and iterative dataset refinement using active learning. During the active learning phase, semantic feature representations were generated using Low-Rank Adaptation-enhanced sentence transformers and combined with machine learning classifiers within an agreement-based active learning strategy to identify candidate samples for expert validation. The process was conducted over ten iterations, starting with 300 expert-annotated reviews and terminating when classifier performance stabilized. Following the stopping criterion, the final classifier-agreement samples were expert-validated and used to construct a held-out test set rather than being added to the training data. The active learning process resulted in a final training dataset of 10,632 expert-validated reviews. In addition, 1000 expert-validated reviews were reserved as a held-out test set and excluded from model training. The training dataset was used to fine-tune three transformer models, namely CAMeLBERT, MARBERT, and Paraphrase, for binary classification of security-related and non-security-related reviews. CAMeLBERT achieved the highest performance among the fine-tuned models, with 95.76% accuracy and 95.77% F1-score under 10-fold cross-validation and 91.20% accuracy and 91.16% F1-score on the held-out test set. To support practical adoption, we developed a web-based interface integrated with a large language model to enable real-time classification and provide interpretable explanations. The resulting dataset and developed approach contribute to advancing security-aware analysis of Arabic user-generated content and support software engineers in identifying security-related concerns in mobile application reviews. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Fu Y.; Meißner M.
Title: Personalizing AI voice agents: How voice agents with similar voices shape trust, self-congruency, and behavior
Abstract: As voice agents become embedded in products as well as service interactions, firms increasingly seek personalization strategies that strengthen consumers' acceptance and engagement. This research examines whether voice agents that sound more similar to users' own voices elicit more favorable behavioral responses. Moreover, we investigate through which psychological mechanisms these effects occur. Across two experiments, we manipulate voice similarity using (1) pretested similar versus dissimilar AI voices and (2) individualized voice cloning that replicates users' voices. Results consistently show that higher voice similarity increases purchase intention, use intention, and willingness to disclose personal information. Mediation analyses indicate that voice similarity operates via two parallel mechanisms: self-congruency and trust. Our research advances research on voice agent-consumer relationships and demonstrates that increasing voice similarity is a robust personalization strategy that enhances consumers’ behavioral responses. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Liu T.; Liu Y.; Wei Q.
Title: Time, cognition, and culture: A three-dimensional self-system model of subjective well-being and interdependent happiness
Abstract: This research proposes a “time–cognition–culture” self-system model to examine whether and under what conditions Future Self-Continuity (FSC) is associated with well-being among Chinese undergraduate students across three studies (N = 1010). Study 1 experimentally showed that increasing FSC enhanced both Subjective Well-Being (SWB) and Interdependent Happiness (IH). In Study 2, PROCESS analyses showed that Self-Concept Clarity (SCC) moderated the associations between FSC and both well-being outcomes, such that the positive associations were stronger among individuals with higher SCC; however, the corresponding latent-variable interaction for SWB was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance. Study 3 showed that self-construal qualified the FSC × SCC interaction. The clearest conditional patterns were observed for independent self-construal in relation to SWB and interdependent self-construal in relation to IH. Overall, these findings suggest that the association between FSC and well-being may vary as a function of SCC, with this moderation pattern further qualified by self-construal. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Bai Z.; Cao B.; Chen T.
Title: When plateware shape matters: The congruence effects between food pungency and plateware shape on food preference
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Although considerable attention has been paid to enhancing the visual appeal of food, less is known about how plateware design should align with the sensory characteristics of food. Drawing on shape-taste correspondence research and processing fluency theory, this research examines the congruence between plateware shape and food pungency. Across four online experiments with Chinese participants, we obtained 754 valid responses covering all seven major geographic regions of China. The results show that pungent foods elicit more favorable consumer responses when served on angular rather than round plateware, whereas mild foods are evaluated more favorably when served on round rather than angular plateware. Processing fluency mediates the effects of plateware shape and food pungency congruence on food evaluation and ordering intention. These findings extend research on shape-taste correspondences and demonstrate that simple, low-cost plateware design can improve consumer responses to foods with different sensory profiles. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Defining the relationship between housing characteristics, household demographics, and time-of-use demand response participation
Abstract: As major energy consumers connected to the electric grid, the participation of residential buildings in demand-side management (DSM) programs, including time of use (TOU) rates, can help utilities with load management and support decarbonization goals. However, participation in these programs is influenced by a combination of household demographic and housing characteristics, which are often examined separately despite their potential interactions. To address this gap, this study develops and analyzes a linked dataset that combines demographic and housing characteristics at the household level, together with respondents' interest in adopting smart technologies (ST) and willingness to adjust thermostat settings. Separate and combined predictive models were developed to evaluate the influence of these factors on DSM related behaviors. Results revealed that combined demographic and housing models outperformed separate models (χ2 = 14.48–24.99, p < 0.001), indicating that jointly considering these factors better captures the complex drivers of DSM participation. Age, education level, tenure and dwelling type emerged as important predictors for ST technology adoption, while home size, dwelling type, and tenure status more effectively explained respondents' willingness to adjust thermostat setpoints throughout the day. Although 81.7% of respondents reported willingness to adjust setpoints at least sometimes during the day, only 11% were willing to do so during evening peak periods. Household income also seems to predict interest and willingness, indicating that financial resources may influence households’ ability to adopt and participate in DSM/TOU programs. These findings can help utilities tailor DSM and TOU programs to different household contexts, for example, by aligning incentives and outreach with housing types and tenure patterns, to improve participation and load-shifting outcomes. They can also guide policymakers in developing more equitable energy policies that expand access to ST across diverse income and housing groups. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The underestimated role of effort in ability self-concept formation: Preliminary evidence for another major comparison process
Abstract: Background: Early studies found that, among individuals with equal achievement, those perceived to exert less effort were rated as having greater ability (i.e. there was a negative relationship between effort and ability), leading to proposals that effort-achievement comparisons are highly influential in forming ability self-concepts. We argue that effort-achievement comparisons have been neglected in recent research due to large-scale studies failing to confirm the early findings. However, this may be because these studies have shifted their focus to a different type of effort: goal-driven effort, meaning perceived effort an individual actively chooses to invest. Aims: This study examines whether the negative relationship between effort and ability self-concepts among individuals with equal achievement can be confirmed when effort is operationalized more similarly to the earlier studies, as so-called data-driven effort, meaning perceived effort resulting from task requirements. Sample: Participants were 448 ninth-grade students from Germany. Method: Data-driven effort, achievements (school grades) and ability self-concepts in the domains of STEM and languages were assessed. We used structural equation modeling to test our hypotheses. Results: There was a strong negative relationship between data-driven effort and ability self-concepts in the two domains when controlling for achievements in the domains. Conclusions: In line with older self-concept research, these findings suggest that there is another influential comparison process, in which data-driven effort is compared with achievements, a topic that merits further investigation in future research. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Assessing the applicability of existing design recommendations to AI companion design: A multi-method study
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of large language model (LLM)-based systems, AI companions have emerged as conversational agents designed to cultivate emotional connection rather than primarily to support humans in instrumental tasks. Because engagement with AI companions involves relational, emotional, and potentially long-term interactions, their design is consequential. Prior work has offered guidance for designing trustworthy and relational AI systems and has begun to examine design for AI companionship. However, while such work provides insights into possible design solutions, less is known about what makes AI companion design difficult as a design problem. To examine this challenge, we assessed the applicability of existing design recommendations from adjacent domains in the context of AI companion design. Our multi-method investigation unfolded across four phases: literature review, practitioner co-analysis, internal heuristic evaluation, and external expert assessment. Throughout this process, we synthesized nine design principle areas that surfaced tensions in the applicability of existing recommendations to AI companion design. Our findings show that ethical and UX-oriented considerations are deeply intertwined and often require context-sensitive application. We document a systematic, multi-method problem analysis that uses these principle areas as an analytic artifact to examine why existing recommendations cannot be directly transferred to AI companion contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Integrating syntactic and semantic features for dual-task extraction in Arabic aspect-based sentiment analysis using graph convolutional networks
Abstract: Arabic aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) remains underexplored, particularly end-to-end dual-task learning that jointly performs aspect term extraction (ATE) and aspect sentiment classification (ASC). Most existing Arabic ABSA approaches are pipeline-based or restricted to single-task identification, which weakens task synergy, constrains performance, and rarely leverages explicit syntactic structure. To address this gap, we propose a structure-aware, end-to-end model that integrates contextual semantics with linguistic structure to perform ATE and ASC tasks simultaneously. Our architecture builds on contextual representations from an Arabic BERT, augmented with token-level attention and sequential modeling via a BiLSTM. A gated fusion module then learns adaptive weights to combine these features into a unified representation. To incorporate linguistic relations, we introduce a dual-branch graph convolutional network that captures (i) dependency-based syntactic relations and (ii) part-of-speech relational patterns. Both branches use attention-weighted adjacency matrices to reduce sensitivity to parser noise and to emphasize sentiment-relevant links. The proposed model is evaluated on three Arabic ABSA datasets (Hotel, News, and HAAD). It achieves ATE and ASC accuracies of 95.29% and 90.87% on Hotel, 91.85% and 82.15% on News, and 90.96% and 75.06% on HAAD, respectively. Under strict end-to-end exact-match evaluation of aspect–sentiment pairs, the model achieves F1-scores of 71.12%, 64.98%, and 33.81% on the Hotel, News, and HAAD datasets, respectively. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Fu X.; Li J.; Zhong H.; Wang D.; Chen W.; Li F.
Title: A comprehensive survey of federated learning for intrusion detection systems in Internet of Things environments
Abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into Internet of Things (IoT) is bringing unprecedented conveniences to daily life, but it also introduces severe cybersecurity challenges due to the widespread deployment of IoT devices. Federated learning, with its distributed nature and privacy-preserving characteristics, has emerged as a powerful framework for building Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) in IoT environments. It enables collaborative model training across distributed devices without centralizing sensitive data. In this paper, we systematically present typical federated learning-based IDS architectures in IoT environments, along with optimization algorithms that enhance their performance and robustness. We explicitly define a threat model that distinguishes two fundamentally different security layers. The first layer consists of external network intrusions that federated learning-based IDSs aim to detect. The second layer comprises internal model-layer attacks, such as poisoning, backdoors, and gradient leakage, which target the federated learning training process itself. Our review methodology involves retrieving literature from major academic databases (Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Springer Link, and ScienceDirect) and Google Scholar, with selection based on strict criteria. This survey contributes a structured synthesis and taxonomy of existing federated learning-based IDS literature, a comparative experimental analysis of datasets, and a detailed discussion of optimization strategies organized around the defined threat model. We conclude by discussing current challenges and outlining future research directions, including the critical need for lightweight model design and robust defenses against adversarial attacks on the federated learning. Title: Integrated cognitive processing model of phishing detection: Mood state as moderating factor in the mindful cognition mediated detection process
Abstract: Previous studies have shown that security awareness alone is not consistently associated with phishing detection accuracy, yet the processes through which awareness is associated with detection remain underexplored. Existing phishing research has also predominantly adopted a cognitive perspective, despite the interdependent nature of affect and cognition in decision-making. To address these gaps, this study adopts an affect-integrated cognitive processing perspective and examines a proposed cognitive process involving security awareness, domain mindfulness, cognitive processing, and mood state, with particular attention to the conditional role of positive mood in performance-focused phishing judgments. Our findings show that security awareness is not directly associated with phishing detection accuracy; rather, a significant indirect association is observed through domain mindfulness and cognitive processing. Although temperament is not directly associated with detection accuracy, it is positively associated with mood state. Positive mood is negatively associated with detection accuracy, and the estimated beneficial indirect associations involving domain mindfulness and cognitive processing are weaker at higher levels of positive mood. Together, the results are consistent with a phishing-detection process involving both cognitive and affective factors. This study extends cognition-focused phishing-detection models by integrating affective boundary conditions into the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Same prevalence, different futures: Protective appraisal and fatigue in seasonal influenza dynamics
Abstract: Behavior-disease models have established that awareness, risk perception, compliance, fatigue, and other behavioral processes can shape epidemic spread, and several existing frameworks already represent more than one behavioral mechanism. However, it remains unclear whether populations matched on both their current influenza state and their current realized protection can still experience different future trajectories because the hidden behavioral composition of that protection differs. We examine this question by distinguishing protective appraisal from accumulated fatigue.We developed an influenza transmission model coupled to appraisal and fatigue. The disease component was calibrated to weekly Hong Kong influenza case data from 5 January 2020 to 22 March 2020, yielding (Formula presented). The behavioral component was parameterized using contextual early-2020 respiratory-risk proxies combining survey-derived protection, Google-search intensity, influenza case intensity, and positivity. Because this window overlapped with the emergence of COVID-19, we repeated the analysis under alternative proxy specifications that removed Google-search and survey inputs. We then conducted prevalence-controlled and equal-current-protection experiments, epidemic-stage and fatigue-parameter robustness analyses, numerical-convergence and uncertainty checks, social-reinforcement ablation, and a direct comparison with an aggregate one-state behavioral model.In the principal equal-current-protection experiment, future peak magnitude ranged from approximately 0.099 to 0.109, time to future peak from 8.8 to 9.3 days, and cumulative post-snapshot incidence from 0.517 to 0.527. The qualitative ordering was retained under alternative proxy definitions, parameter perturbations, epidemic-stage changes, and removal of social-reinforcement feedback. However, the aggregate one-state and two-state models had similar short-window empirical performance. The two-state model reduced in-sample proxy RMSE by only 0.7% and had a 4.8% higher rolling one-week-ahead RMSE. Its demonstrated advantage was instead structural: once current protection was fixed, the one-state model produced one future by construction, whereas the two-state formulation retained future-peak and cumulative-incidence ranges of approximately 0.0100 and 0.0104.The contribution is therefore not the introduction of multiple behavioral states or a claim of superior short-window forecasting accuracy. It is a data-anchored matched-state framework showing that observationally equivalent current protection can contain distinct appraisal–fatigue compositions associated with different counterfactual epidemic futures. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Lin Y.; Zheng X.; Jiang B.; Chen Z.; Liu M.
Title: The perspective of artificial intelligence for NMR
Abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is an indispensable analytical technique in chemistry, biology, and medicine, offering molecular-level structural and dynamic insights for metabolite identification and biomarker discovery in biological and clinical research. However, its broader application in metabolite research is constrained by inherent limitations such as low sensitivity, severe peak overlap, and the trade-off between portability of low-field instruments and spectral resolution and sensitivity, as well as the difficulty of mining valid biological information from high-throughput metabolite big data. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), have contributed to addressing these core challenges, reshaping the capabilities of NMR technology in metabolite research. This perspective overviews NMR's core role and existing metabolite-specific bottlenecks, and traces the evolutionary progress of AI in NMR. Then it focuses on three interrelated and technologically innovative directions of AI-powered NMR for metabolite, including (1) improving the spectral resolution of low-field spectra to match that of high-field spectra, or directly extracting high-field-like NMR information from low-field spectra; (2) mitigating spectral congestion via optimizing pure shift spectra of complex metabolic mixtures, which simplifies complex spectra by converting multiplets into singlets; and (3) identifying metabolites and biomarkers (including lipoprotein-related metabolic markers in hyperlipidemia) in metabolomics. The synergy of AI and NMR is poised to unlock unprecedented analytical capabilities for metabolomics, extending its impact across scientific discovery, precision medicine, food science, and other related fields. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Store coolness in luxury fashion: Antecedents, outcomes, and the moderating role of price consciousness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: In the context of luxury fashion stores, this study investigates the mediating role of the dimensions of store coolness (extraordinary, subcultural, iconic, and high status) in linking service quality of employees, store display, and store creativity with customers' behavioral intention and positive word-of-mouth (WOM). Additionally, the study examines whether price consciousness moderates any of these relationships. To gain a deeper understanding of how coolness is perceived in luxury fashion stores, we collected customer insights through interviews with 16 frequent store visitors. We then tested our proposed model using a survey administered to shoppers immediately after they visited luxury stores (N = 213). Our results indicate that the extraordinary and subcultural dimensions of coolness positively mediate the effects of store display and creativity on behavioral intention and positive WOM. However, the iconic dimension did not play a mediating role, while the high status dimension negatively mediated these paths, including those involving service quality. Finally, we found that price consciousness weakens the path from store creativity to the studied outcomes via the extraordinary dimension. Building on these findings, we provide managerial insights for designing luxury fashion store experiences that foster store coolness and positive customer responses. © 2026 The Author(s)

Author full names: Fukubayashi, Nao (57316065100); Fuji, Kei (35848550100)
Title: From overloaded to unsatisfied: The short- and long-term effects of online career media exposure
Abstract: The contemporary career landscape is increasingly influenced by digital technologies. The widespread availability of online career information and the daily exchange of content via social media not only facilitate autonomous career development but also expose individuals to a vast array of career options. Although this abundance reflects greater self-determination, it may also lead to psychological challenges through choice overload. In this study, the possibility that online exposure to career information and options increases career choice overload, which, over time, may reduce overall career satisfaction, is examined. Using a combined contemporaneous and cross-lagged effects model, we found that greater online exposure to career information was associated with increased career choice overload, which was captured across three dimensions: career choice avoidance, disengagement from one's current career, and impatient career idealism. Longitudinally, elevated career choice overload predicted lower overall career satisfaction, and conversely, lower satisfaction contributed to greater overload, which suggests a potential negative spiral. Our findings provide empirical evidence that routine online media exposure can generate both conscious and unconscious career choice overload, which highlights the occurrence of choice overload in high-stakes career contexts and its multidimensional nature. © 2026

Title: Unveiling research trends in artificial intelligence adoption based on the UTAUT: A bibliometric analysis supporting SDGs and future outlook
Abstract: The development of AI adoption across disciplines has become a major global concern, especially with the UTAUT model that runs concurrently. This study aims to map research trends on AI adoption within the UTAUT model in conceptual, intellectual, and social structures. The research utilises a bibliometric approach from the Scopus database for the period 2018-2025 on related topics. Data analysis was conducted descriptively using Biblioshiny (Rstudio). The study found a very positive and significant development in research on AI adoption within the UTAUT model across various disciplines, aligning with the SDGs, particularly points four, nine, and seventeen. The countries that contributed most were China and the USA. Interesting themes for studying the development of UTAUT model implications include social influence, performance expectancy, behaviour, perceived risk, digital literacy, and AI anxiety. In SDG 4, the adoption of AI in higher education is crucial by incorporating perceived risk and digital literacy to achieve effective personalised learning. In SDG 9, organisational and corporate levels within managerial structures are important for combining structural and psychological factors that influence AI adoption. AIMDSS in the healthcare sector is essential for supporting health innovation and infrastructure. Meanwhile, for SDG 17, discovering best practices for AI adoption across various fields needs to be accelerated, particularly in Africa, South America, and most of Eastern Europe. The implications of this research point to the development of institutional guidelines for AI adoption and the exploration of the UTAUT model. By highlighting the evolving role of contextual, ethical, and governance-related factors, this study provides a foundation for aligning AI adoption strategies with sustainable development objectives and informs future empirical and policy-oriented research. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Tell me the truth: Consumer responses to feedback solicitation with robots versus humans
Abstract: Advanced technologies enable service robots to handle a broader range of tasks than ever before. Among these, this research examines the potential of service robots to solicit and collect high-quality consumer feedback. This research, comprising four experimental studies, including a field study in a hotel, demonstrates that unsatisfied consumers are more likely to provide honest feedback to service robots than to human employees. Drawing on the theory of mind perception, the present research finds that such an effect is attributed to consumers’ concern for others' feelings (i.e., empathetic concern). Moreover, the proposed effects are diminished when the robot has a high (vs. low) level of emotional capability but are more pronounced among consumers with interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal. This research offers practical insights that enable advanced robotic technologies to be useful beyond simple physical tasks: consumer feedback management. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: CONSENT IS NOT JUST ABOUT ASKING: HOW YOU REQUEST CONSUMERS’ AGREEMENT TO COOKIES MATTERS
Abstract: Website cookie notices influence consent decisions by configuring multiple design cues within the privacy calculus consumers apply when evaluating data disclosure. Results of an online experiment (N = 776) suggest that freedom of choice and cookie notice placement influence consumers’ perceived power. In addition, technical language influences perceived risk. Authors: Cao Z.; Ling L.; Li S.; Chen X.; Robinson G.M.
Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of rural human settlement quality in China: Based on a Kernel-Driver analytical framework
Abstract: Improving rural human settlements is essential for enhancing rural residents' well-being and achieving SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). This study develops a Kernel-Driver analytical framework to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, driving mechanisms, and future trajectories of rural human settlement quality (RHSQ) in China from 2005 to 2024. Results show that: First, RHSQ improved substantially, with an average annual growth rate of 6.10%, exhibiting a stable east-central-west gradient and gradually narrowing regional disparities. Second, rural development investment, farmers' income, rural industrial upgrading, urbanization, and rural digitalization promoted RHSQ improvement, although their marginal effects weakened over time. Rural hollowing and terrain slope constrained RHSQ, while rural population aging showed a weak positive effect overall, with declining intensity and negative effects in some regions. These drivers exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Third, RHSQ is projected to improve under all scenarios, with the enhanced rural revitalization scenario generating the greatest improvement. However, spatial equity remains challenging, as policy strengthening has limited capacity to reshape long-standing regional disparities. By revealing the dynamic mechanisms underlying RHSQ evolution, this study provides insights for developing more targeted and adaptive rural governance strategies to promote equitable and sustainable rural development. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Aggregate convergence and constituent divergence in incel-related online communities: A mentalizing-theory lens on cross-platform linguistic patterns
Abstract: The “incel” (involuntary celibate) subculture comprises an online ecosystem spanning mainstream-hosted, independent, and recovery-oriented communities. Using Fonagy's mentalizing framework, we derived four community-level Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC-22) patterns: rigidity–flexibility (Psychic Equivalence-inspired), goal–affect balance (Teleological Mode-inspired), cognitive-affective elaboration (Pretend Mode-inspired), and counter-positioning–curiosity (Epistemic Mistrust-inspired). Study 1 compared 2261 incels.is discussion-thread documents with 15 LIWC-22 Test Kitchen reference corpora and the overall benchmark. Incels.is generally showed higher Psychic Equivalence-inspired scores and consistently higher Epistemic Mistrust-inspired scores; Teleological Mode-inspired differences were reference-dependent, whereas Pretend Mode-inspired results were heterogeneous across reference genres. Excluding text from the top 1% of identifiable contributors retained 61 of 64 comparison directions. Study 2 analyzed 28,980 platform-specific user aggregates across five communities. Although platform differences were supported, their magnitude was modest (η2 = 0.037–0.055), with most user-level linguistic variation remaining within platforms. Relative to IncelExit, active-incel platforms generally scored higher on the Psychic Equivalence- and Teleological Mode-inspired patterns and lower on the Pretend Mode-inspired pattern. IncelExit had the highest Epistemic Mistrust-inspired score despite high curiosity, showing that the composite did not isolate epistemic closure from counter-positioning. Across all four patterns, community means showed a consistent ordering, although adjacent contrasts were not uniformly supported. The three-platform portion of the ordering persisted in temporally matched and year-adjusted analyses. Evidential support was clearest for PE, partial for TM, limited for EM and PM. The latent ecological or psychological basis of the ordering remains unresolved, and the linguistic patterns are descriptive rather than validated measures of mentalizing. © 2026

Title: Beyond openness: Mapping need for cognition across Big Five domains and facets in university students
Abstract: Need for cognition (NFC) is closely associated with openness-related personality traits, but broad domains may obscure a more selective facet-level pattern. We examined NFC in 1551 university students using the Big Five Inventory–2 and a split-sample discovery–validation design. In discovery, three domains (Open-Mindedness, Conscientiousness, and Extraversion) and four facets (Productiveness, Intellectual Curiosity, Assertiveness, and Creative Imagination) met the selected magnitude threshold. In held-out validation, all three domains remained independently associated with NFC, whereas at the facet level only Assertiveness, Intellectual Curiosity, and Productiveness did so. Complementary latent models indicated positive associations of NFC with both Intellectual Curiosity and Assertiveness, although a bifactor decomposition of Open-Mindedness was inadmissible and correlated-factor model fit was mixed. Overall, the findings support the particular importance of intellectual openness while indicating that NFC is also embedded in a selective cross-domain configuration involving agentic and goal-directed characteristics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
