Title: Deployment conditions for biomass value chains on marginal lands: Evidence from a multi-case stakeholder survey
Abstract: Biomass from marginal lands is increasingly considered as a feedstock for European bio-based value chains, particularly where biomaterials, bioenergy, and other bio-based products can support decarbonisation without directly competing with food production. This study examines stakeholder-assessed deployment conditions across seven biomass value-chain cases, with a primary focus on Europe and additional evidence from Argentina and South Africa that broadens the empirical scope. Using a mixed-methods analysis of stakeholder survey data from 133 respondents, the study examines perceived risks, sustainability priorities, implementation challenges, enabling measures, and expectations regarding bio-based products and bioenergy. The findings show that implementation does not follow a single generic pattern. Instead, stakeholders identified different combinations of environmental, regulatory, market, technological, and coordination conditions associated with different biomass value chains. Fibre- and material-oriented pathways were characterized by stakeholder emphasis on product standards, certification, and market development; wetland biomass pathways with ecological compatibility, land-use clarity, and regional logistics; biofuel-oriented pathways with policy stability, quality assurance, and secure demand; biogas- and substrate-related pathways with supply coordination, infrastructure, and predictable incentives; and restoration-linked woody biomass pathways with institutional coordination, land-tenure clarity, and local value creation. Across cases, stakeholders indicate deployment conditions of biomass conversion and utilisation depends not only on feedstock availability or technological potential, but on how environmental safeguards, regulatory conditions, market structures, and coordination arrangements align in practice. The study contributes stakeholder-based evidence on the conditions shaping the deployment of biomass for bioenergy and bio-based products primarily in Europe and highlights why value-chain-specific support conditions matter for implementation. © 2026 The Authors. Title: When does AI design help or hurt? Brand positioning and the dual effects of homogeneity and trend relevance in fashion retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in fashion design to generate product aesthetics and forecast trends. While prior research has separately examined algorithmic homogeneity risks or efficiency gains, how consumers simultaneously process these opposing signals, and whether this processing differs from human-generated design, remains unclear. This study investigates how the attribution of design to AI (vs. human) influences consumer evaluations via dual pathways—perceived homogeneity and trend relevance—and examines brand positioning as a boundary condition. A 2 (design source: AI vs. human) × 2 (brand positioning: avant-garde vs. mainstream) between-subjects experiment with 412 consumers reveals that AI-attributed designs simultaneously heighten both perceptions. Multi-group analysis demonstrates that these perceptions operate through perceived manipulative intent, a mechanism significantly stronger for AI- than human-attributed designs. The two pathways exert opposing effects on brand sincerity and purchase intention. Brand positioning moderates these effects asymmetrically: the negative homogeneity pathway is amplified for avant-garde brands, while the positive trend-relevance pathway is strengthened for mainstream brands. These findings identify perceived manipulative intent as the core mechanism translating AI design attribution into consumer responses, and demonstrate that aligning AI adoption with brand positioning can either help or hurt brand sincerity. For fashion retailers, the implications are clear: communicate AI usage as value-creating rather than cost-cutting, and tailor AI strategies to brand positioning—avant-garde brands should emphasize human-AI collaboration, while mainstream brands should leverage AI's trend-sensing capabilities while guarding against stylistic sameness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Hu Z.; Zheng Y.-H.; Zhang W.; Sun J.
Title: Who eats matters: How eating-agent identity in short-form retail videos influences consumers’ purchase intentions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Short-form retail videos frequently depict food consumption, yet little is known about whether the identity of the visible eater shapes how consumers evaluate the product. We conceptualize eating-agent identity as a contextual product cue and develop a cue-based inference account in which a pet eater makes nature-related meaning salient and, through visible consumption, connects that meaning to the focal food. Consequently, consumers infer greater product naturalness and greater healthiness, increasing purchase intention. This inference depends on how the consumption episode is structured: visible human assistance attenuates the pet advantage by altering the product-use relationship, whereas sponsorship disclosure changes the surrounding commercial context without necessarily disrupting that relationship. Five preregistered online experiments with 2462 retained participants from Chinese consumer panels support this account. Study 1 establishes the effect and examines alternative explanations. Study 2 demonstrates the sequential pathway through perceived naturalness and perceived healthiness. Study 3 manipulates naturalness information to provide causal evidence for the perceived naturalness component of the proposed pathway, Study 4 identifies eating autonomy as a boundary condition, and Study 5 shows that the focal pathway remains evident in the sponsorship disclosure context. The findings distinguish visible product users from promotional sources and reveal a scene-based route through which the contextual features of consumption episodes shape food attribute judgments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhanced DNMF-graph integrated multilevel semantic factorization for contextual named entity recognition
Abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) has undergone considerable changes in the recent past driven by the growing demand for models that are more robust, context aware and capable of generalizing across diverse textual domain. However, existing state of the art approaches primarily rely on local contextual representations, and often fails to capture corpus level semantic structures, particularly in noisy or low resource settings. To address these limitations, a unified NER system is proposed in the present work, that utilizes a Deep Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (DNMF) integrated with token level graph community discovery and a Transformer- Conditional Random Fields (CRF) model. The proposed model, named as DNMF-Graph-Transformer CRF, can utilize the strengths of various representation levels. By applying DNMF to the token-context matrix, several interpretable, low-rank latent semantic factors are obtained that not only complement neural representations but also help to improve the model's generalization when it has to work with a small amount of noisy data. Next, a token interaction graph is generated to represent the global relationships among tokens. Thus, community embeddings can be extracted that give structural priors at the corpus level. These features represent semantic neighbourhoods and functional groupings of tokens. Finally, the Transformer- CRF is adapted to learn the contextual aspects of the text. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated by conducting comprehensive experiments on CoNLL-2003, OntoNotes 5.0, and WNUT 2017. The results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms existing baseline models. It is observed that the performance gains are especially significant for noisy social media text. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Contrastive semi-supervised clustering based on pairwise constraint for identifying influential nodes in complex networks
Abstract: Identifying influential nodes is crucial for understanding the functional dynamics of complex networks. However, existing approaches face significant limitations: centrality-based methods capture only specific topological aspects, while supervised techniques require abundant labeled data, hindering their practical applicability. To overcome these issues, we propose PCGCN, a contrastive semi-supervised graph clustering framework that integrates limited node labels with structural information through pairwise constraints. Our method leverages regular equivalence-based (RE) similarity to define pairwise constraints between unlabeled nodes, which are jointly used with labeled data to guide the learning process. By combining a graph convolutional network (GCN) encoder with a pairwise constraint-based contrastive loss, PCGCN learns discriminative node embeddings under limited supervision. Extensive experiments show that PCGCN generally achieves better performance than the centrality-based and unsupervised/semi-supervised methods, while remaining competitive with the supervised methods adopted for comparison. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Mapping the global landscape of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship: A bibliometric review (2000–2025)
Abstract: Mentorship is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of women’s entrepreneurial participation and success. However, existing scholarship remains fragmented, conceptually inconsistent, and unevenly distributed across global contexts. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship, examining peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2025 globally. To enhance methodological robustness and address limitations associated with narrow keyword selection, a multi-stage search strategy was employed using the Scopus database. A total of 878 records were identified through the Scopus database. The final dataset includes 621 articles, allowing for a detailed analysis of publication trends, geographic distribution, authorship patterns, and thematic development within the field. The findings reveal a significant concentration of research output in the Global North, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom, with comparatively limited representation from developing regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa. Thematic analysis indicates strong clustering around mentorship, coaching, entrepreneurial ecosystems, and capacity building, highlighting both conceptual convergence and fragmentation. Furthermore, the results show that mentorship is frequently embedded within broader entrepreneurial support frameworks rather than examined as a standalone construct. In response, this study advances a Gendered Social Capital and Learning framework to provide a more integrated understanding of mentorship processes in women’s entrepreneurship. The study contributes to the literature by offering a robust, data-driven overview of the field, identifying key gaps in geographic and theoretical coverage, and highlighting the methodological implications of keyword selection in bibliometric research. Title: Psychological control and parent–child attachment in relation to adolescent delinquency and externalizing behaviours: A systematic review
Abstract: Adolescent delinquency and externalizing problem behaviors continue to represent major psychosocial concerns affecting adolescents across different cultural contexts. Growing evidence suggests that parenting practices, particularly parental psychological control, together with the quality of parent–child attachment, play important roles in shaping adolescent behavioral outcomes. The present systematic literature review aimed to synthesize recent empirical evidence on the relationships among parental psychological control, parent–child attachment, and adolescent delinquency. This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed using five electronic databases, namely Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, PubMed, and Embase. Studies published between 2019 and 2025 involving adolescents aged 10–19 years were included. A total of 1,421 records were initially identified, and after screening and eligibility assessment, eight empirical studies met the inclusion criteria and were systematically analyzed. The findings consistently demonstrated that parental psychological control, characterized by intrusive parenting behaviors such as guilt induction, emotional manipulation, and love withdrawal, was positively associated with adolescent delinquency, aggression, rule-breaking behavior, and other externalizing problems. In contrast, secure parent–child attachment was consistently associated with lower levels of delinquency and maladaptive behavior, functioning as a significant protective factor. Several studies further revealed that attachment quality mediated or moderated the relationship between psychological control and adolescent behavioral outcomes, indicating that adolescents exposed to high psychological control were more likely to engage in delinquent behaviors when attachment security was low. Conversely, secure attachment reduced the negative impact of psychologically controlling parenting practices. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of family relational dynamics in understanding adolescent delinquency. This review emphasizes the need for family-based interventions that promote supportive parenting practices, reduce psychological control, and strengthen secure parent–child attachment to prevent maladaptive developmental outcomes and promote healthy adolescent adjustment. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: WISE: An interpretable word intensity framework for emotion-aware conversational systems
Abstract: Emotion-aware conversational systems are increasingly adopted in healthcare, yet most emotion detection approaches rely on sentiment polarity, which fails to capture emotional nuance and intensity in short, informal chat messages. To overcome these limitations, this study develops an interpretable emotion-aware framework called Word Intensity Scoring Engine (WISE) that explicitly models emotional intensity in short-form conversational text. Grounded in Plutchik's Wheel of Emotions, WISE integrates lexicon-based emotion labeling, synonym expansion, semantic similarity using word embeddings, and negation-aware feature extraction to calculate intensity-weighted emotion scores at the word level. The WISE framework is evaluated through experimental benchmarking and an expert review involving practicing healthcare professionals. Results show that WISE enhances the performance of ML and LLM-based classifiers. Further, expert evaluations indicate that WISE-derived responses are perceived as professional, contextually appropriate, and empathetic. Title: Human behaviour in wildfire emergencies: insights from evacuation decision-making and timing across Canada, Australia, and the United States
Abstract: Wildfires often require rapid evacuation to save lives, leading residents to make quick and context-specific transportation decisions that may differ across countries and cultures. This study examines intended evacuation behaviours during wildfires, focusing on promptness, departure time, and cross-country differences. Surveys were conducted across Canada, the United States, and Australia (with sample sizes of 1,366, 1,490, and 1,173, respectively), and the data were used to run advanced choice modelling techniques to estimate factors influencing time-related decisions. The findings emphasized the importance of preparedness, reasons for evacuating, and risk perception in shaping responses to emergencies. Moreover, results identified country differences and similarities in evacuation preparedness time. For instance, employment, age, and income were factors relevant only in the U.S. context, while gender was significant exclusively in the Australian context. For all three countries, households with older adults were less likely to evacuate promptly, while households with children were more likely to evacuate promptly. The study also revealed that complex models showed minimal or no improvement in fit relative to simpler models. These insights on evacuation decisions and departure times, especially across jurisdictional boundaries, can assist in improving generalized wildfire evacuation plans and implementing more inclusive emergency communication strategies. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Shared value vs plural values. Contesting renewable energy projects of the Enel Group
Abstract: The energy transition triggers urgent questions about what values are important, who controls transitional processes, and who has the power to define the answers to the climate crisis. Energy companies claim their central role in the development of renewable energy as the ultimate solution. However, communities affected by large-scale renewable energy projects have extensively raised environmental and social justice concerns and denounced the industry's poor practices and abuses.In this article, we analyse 15 socio-environmental conflicts around renewable energy projects owned by the Enel Group, one of the world's largest energy utilities, through the values and valuation languages of the affected communities. We map them onto five dimensions: environmental, health-related, socio-economic, ontological, and political. We build on environmental justice and ecological economics literature on valuation languages and employ counter-accounting to gather bottom-up evidence of grievances.We argue that, while the company claims that RE is the ultimate solution and the ‘Creating Shared Value’ approach is beneficial to all parties, those impacted by Enel's projects question the corporate model of energy transition and defend a plurality of values embedded in relational worldviews that are systematically misrecognised. We eventually criticise the corporate self-attributed moral and value-centred mandate in the energy transition and call for inclusive research about desirable energy futures rooted in plural and relational value systems. Title: X-MCB-Net: Explainable multimodal Cyberbullying Detection Network using Swin Transformer
Abstract: Cyberbullying on social media represents a persistent digital safety concern, often conveyed through the interplay of offensive text and images. Existing detection systems largely treat visual and textual modalities independently and offer limited interpretability, hindering deployment in accountable content-moderation workflows. This study presents X-MCB-Net, an explainable multimodal cyberbullying detection framework that integrates the Swin Transformer for visual feature extraction with XLM-RoBERTa and a bidirectional GRU for textual analysis. A dynamic intermodal attention mechanism fuses visual and linguistic representations to capture implicit and context-dependent cues for abuse. The core novelty lies in the joint design of adaptive cross-modal fusion and explainability-aware attribution, enabling both high detection performance and transparent decision support for human moderators. Evaluated on 5790 annotated image–text pairs from the Multimodal Cyberbullying Detection Dataset, X-MCB-Net achieved 98.8% accuracy and 96.6% F1-score under stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Explainable AI (XAI) visualizations identify the image regions and text tokens that drive each classification decision, supporting auditability and moderator trust in automated online safety systems. Authors: Li X.; Guo X.
Title: Dynamic configurations and ecological fit: A fuzzy-set QCA analysis of effective data security governance in summer olympic games (1992–2024)
Abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating digital transformation, Summer Olympic Games have become mega‑temporary events generating massive volumes of data, where data security governance is critical to smooth event delivery. Nevertheless, existing scholarship mostly adopts fragmented technology‑centric or management‑centric perspectives, overlooking the synergistic interplay among multi‑dimensional factors. Drawing upon information ecology theory, this study applies fuzzy‑set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to nine Summer Olympic Games held between 1992 and 2024. We examine how five antecedent conditions—data asset sensitivity, organizational management maturity, technological maturity, security deployment intensity, and external regulatory pressure—jointly shape high‑level data security governance. Necessary‑condition analysis shows that no single factor is indispensable for sound governance. Three equifinal configurational paths are identified: the Full‑Element Driven path, the Management‑Technology Dual‑Driven path, and the Low‑Risk Baseline path. Our findings demonstrate that effective Olympic data security governance arises from nonlinear multi‑element synergy rather than isolated single‑factor advantages, while governance failures stem from ecological mismatches among information‑ecology components. Building on these patterns, we derive a path‑contingent investment framework specifying what budget‑constrained hosts can compress and what they must prioritize. This paper extends information ecology theory to the temporary governance context of mega‑sporting events and delivers differentiated, resource‑constrained managerial insights for future Olympic host cities under the ecological‑fit principle. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From precarious work to occupational health outcomes in hotel housekeepers: a narrative review with meta-synthesis
Abstract: Introduction: Hotel housekeepers sustain the core functioning of the hospitality industry yet perform demanding, repetitive, and undervalued work associated with substantial physical and psychosocial risks. Understanding how working conditions shape health, motivation, and lived experience is essential for informing prevention strategies and promoting decent work. Methods A sequential narrative review and qualitative meta -synthesis were conducted to integrate and reinterpret evidence across disciplines and study designs. Searches covered five academic databases and gray literature without year or language limits. Studies were screened using predefined criteria, appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and synthesized through narrative, tabular, and meta -analytical thematic analysis, with findings interpreted through the JD-R framework. Results Findings revealed employment precarity, work intensification, musculoskeletal pain, chemical and biological hazards, and elevated stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Time pressure fostered coping strategies such as skipping meals and delaying bathroom use. Gendered labor divisions, discrimination, and negative supervision contributed to invisibility and limited autonomy. Workers also expressed pride, intrinsic motivation, and collective action to make their contributions visible. Conclusions This review demonstrates that housekeeping is characterized by structural precarity and cumulative health burdens alongside resilience and emerging activism. Improving occupational health requires organizational and policy transformations: realistic workloads, safer equipment, secure contracts, participatory risk management, and leadership practices grounded in dignity and fairness; rather than reliance on individual coping. Structural change is essential to advance safer, more equitable, and sustainable workplaces in the hospitality sector. The JD-R framework highlights the need to reduce demand and strengthen resources. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: GCN-T: A fusion prediction model for GCN-Transformer optimized using an improved sine cosine algorithm
Abstract: Air quality forecasting serves as a critical foundation for public health protection and environmental management decisions. Accurate forecasts provide a scientific basis for pollution warnings and effectively mitigate the adverse effects of polluted air. However, traditional models struggle to integrate the temporal and spatial correlations of pollutant data effectively. While standalone graph convolutional networks (GCNs) can capture spatial correlations, they fall short in mining temporal dynamic features. Conversely, Transformer models are adept at capturing temporal dependencies but lack effective modeling of spatial correlations. Furthermore, parameter tuning for both types of models often relies on empirical settings, making them prone to overfitting and stuck in local optima, which results in prediction accuracy and model stability that do not meet practical application requirements. To address these issues, this paper deeply integrates GCN and Transformer to construct a new air quality prediction model. In this model, the Transformer uses a multi-head self-attention mechanism to calculate the dependency weights between the features of various pollutants. After symmetric normalization, these weights directly serve as the adjacency matrix for the GCN. The two components iterate alternately at each layer, with attention guiding graph convolution and the graph convolution output fed back to the attention mechanism at the next layer, thereby achieving cross-layer collaborative modeling of feature relationships and graph structures. To enhance model performance, this paper employs an improved sine cosine algorithm (SCA) for adaptive parameter optimization. First, multiple population mechanisms are introduced to expand the search range of SCA, effectively accelerating the algorithm’s convergence. Second, random parameters are incorporated to ensure that SCA favors global search during the initial iterations, thereby preventing the algorithm from getting trapped in local optima. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, experiments were conducted using eight datasets containing air quality data, comparing the proposed model with seven existing mainstream prediction models. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the comparison models across all evaluation metrics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Spatial wildfire risk assessment for Oahu, Hawaii, using swarm-intelligence-optimized CatBoost and the analytic network process
Abstract: Wildfires in the Hawaiian Islands are an increasing concern due to climate change and the spread of invasive species. This study thus assessed the wildfire risk on Oahu, Hawaii. Wildfire susceptibility was modeled using the categorical boosting (CatBoost) algorithm. To improve model performance, its hyperparameters were optimized through a comparative analysis of two swarm-intelligence (SI) metaheuristics: the pathfinder algorithm (PFA) and the sparrow search algorithm (SSA). These SI approaches automatically explored the hyperparameter space and maximized the prediction accuracy for the validation set, resulting in two optimized models (PFA-CatBoost and SSA-CatBoost). Socioeconomic vulnerability was then quantified using the analytic network process (ANP), based on eight socioeconomic and demographic indicators that were weighted, fuzzified, and integrated into a composite index. The wildfire susceptibility results showed that the hybrid PFA-CatBoost and SSA-CatBoost models outperformed the baseline CatBoost model, with SSA-CatBoost achieving the best performance, reaching an accuracy of 0.984 on the testing set. The ANP analysis identified annual household income, population density, and education level as the primary socioeconomic indicators associated with wildfire vulnerability. According to the resulting wildfire risk map, 11.7% of Oahu fell within the high or very-high risk categories. The high-risk areas were primarily concentrated in densely populated corridors such as Makaha, Waianae, Maili, Nanakuli, Ewa Gentry, Waipahu, and the Honolulu–Waialae-Kahala corridor. Overall, the proposed framework provides a robust approach to spatial wildfire risk assessment, supporting risk-informed decision-making for wildfire mitigation, land-use planning, and emergency management on Oahu Island. © 2026

Title: ACOPI-QGen: Implicitness-aware joint quintuple extraction for aspect-based sentiment analysis via contrastive and graph-based modeling
Abstract: In social media and online reviews, sentiments are often expressed implicitly through contextual, figurative, or indirect language, making them difficult to capture using traditional Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) techniques. Many prior studies on ABSA treat implicit aspects and opinions as auxiliary cases or evaluation subsets, limiting their role during learning. To address this limitation, we propose ACOPI-QGen, a joint structured framework that extracts a five-element sentiment quintuple (Aspect Term, Aspect Category, Opinion Term, Polarity, Implicitness). Rather than treating implicitness as a post-hoc attribute, we model it as a supervised four-class variable: EAEO, EAIO, IAEO, and IAIO, where A/O denote aspect/opinion and E/I denote explicit/implicit realization. The proposed framework combines BERT-based contextual encoding, Supervised Contrastive Implicit Learning, and a Relational Graph Attention Network guided by a Surrogate Aspect-Opinion Dependency Tree to support implicit sentiment modeling when aspect or opinion spans are missing. A non-autoregressive set decoder uses parallel tuple queries to predict multiple candidate sentiment quintuples while preserving aspect-opinion alignment. We curate three datasets for quintuple extraction (Restaurant-ACOPI: 2584; Laptop-ACOPI: 4376; and Shoes-ACOPI: 3896 instances). ACOPI-QGen achieves Exact Match F1 scores of 55.68, 48.43, and 60.49 on Restaurant-ACOPI, Laptop-ACOPI, and Shoes-ACOPI, respectively, with corresponding improvements of 2.92, 2.53, and 5.45 absolute F1 points over the best-performing state-of-the-art models across the three domains. Title: Material use and its relationship with per capita income. A panel data analysis at the global level
Abstract: Global use of materials has significantly increased over recent decades, causing a wide range of environmental and social concerns. In this study, we use the latest available data from the UN database on global material flows to investigate the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis for two widely used material flow indicators, Domestic Material Consumption and Material Footprint, for a dataset of 147 countries. Using both semiparametric and parametric methods over a longer period than any previous study (1970–2019), we find no evidence in support of the EKC hypothesis. A concerning result is that material-income elasticities are higher after 1989, implying that the situation has not improved. We conclude that major changes have not yet occurred in the income-material use relationship and that strong policy measures remain necessary to reduce material consumption. Title: Personality engineering with AI agents: A new methodology for negotiation research
Abstract: According to canonical negotiation theory, people's success in a negotiation depends on how well they balance competing demands—empathizing and asserting, demonstrating concern for other and concern for self, being soft on the people and hard on the problem. Yet people struggle to manage these tensions, so researchers have lacked the ability to rigorously test the field's prescriptions under controlled conditions. AI agents do not face the same limitations, and their precision, repertoire, consistency, and scalability enable a new class of experiments to contribute to negotiation theory. In this article, we introduce personality engineering—a methodology that precisely parameterizes the personas of AI agents based on established personality frameworks—and propose how this method can be used to study the traits and behaviors of negotiators. Given its relevance to negotiation theory, we propose the interpersonal circumplex—and its two core dimensions of warmth and dominance—as a foundational coordinate system for the field. This approach offers both a rigorous methodology for testing classic negotiation theories and a practical guide for designing the personas of AI negotiation agents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Probable alcohol use disorder in the U.S. Veteran population: Results from the 2025–2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans study
Abstract: Background Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a pervasive public health problem in the United States, and military veterans are at elevated risk. A prior wave of the National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study (NHRVS) estimated the prevalence of past-year probable AUD at 10.5 % in 2019–2020. Updated national surveillance data are needed given demographic shifts in the veteran population and evolving drinking patterns in the post-pandemic era. Methods Using data from the 2025–2026 NHRVS (N = 2,620), we estimated the weighted prevalence of probable AUD and compared it to that of the prior NHRVS wave. Multivariable analyses examined sociodemographic, military, trauma and mental health characteristics associated with probable AUD. Results The weighted prevalence of probable AUD in 2025–2026 was 12.1 %, compared with 10.5 % in 2019–2020 (difference, 1.6 percentage points; 95 % CI, −0.6 to 3.8), a difference that was not statistically significant. Independent correlates of probable AUD included younger age, unpartnered status, homelessness history, higher household income, and more adverse childhood experiences. When all lifetime psychiatric diagnoses were examined simultaneously, self-reported provider-diagnosed attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remained significantly associated with probable AUD (OR = 2.40). Veterans with probable AUD also had significantly greater odds of past-year suicidal ideation (OR = 2.02; 31.6 % vs. 11.7 %) and lifetime suicide attempt (OR = 1.67; 11.8 % vs. 4.0 %). Conclusions The prevalence of probable AUD among U.S. veterans remains elevated and is characterized by early adversity, co-occurring psychiatric conditions, and elevated suicide risk. Enhanced screening for social determinants of health and psychiatric concerns, including routine ADHD assessment in AUD treatment settings, alongside targeted outreach and integrated approaches are essential to address this complex and important problem. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Management of Disputes in the Construction Industry during COVID-19: Contractors' Takeaways for Future Pandemics
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic intensified construction disputes. While dispute management has been widely studied, limited research has examined pandemic-induced disputes globally, especially within the Sri Lankan construction context. Hence, this study aims to investigate how to manage the disputes due to COVID-19 in the Sri Lankan construction industry, considering the contractors' perspective. The study adopts an interpretivist philosophy and employs a qualitative Delphi technique involving two iterative rounds of semistructured interviews, thereby making a methodological contribution. The data were analyzed through manual content analysis. The findings reveal six positive impacts and 12 negative impacts of COVID-19 on the construction industry, along with suitable preventive measures to manage the 12 important causes of disputes arising from the pandemic. This is positioned as one of the limited studies identifying both positive and negative impacts and suitable preventive measures in managing the identified causes. The findings can be applied for developing contexts of a similar nature, particularly in managing disputes during future pandemics.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: From sound to resonance: Club anthem attractiveness and fan–brand relationships
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Auditory branding plays an increasingly important role in sensory service experiences; however, limited research has examined how recurring auditory brand cues relate to consumer–brand relationship outcomes. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework as an organizing logic, this study examines associations among club anthem attractiveness (CAA), positive emotion (PE), post-exposure brand cognition (BC), and fan–brand resonance (FBR) in sports leisure services. Data were collected from a screened nonprobability online sample of 468 respondents in China. Participants listened to one of three standardized 90-s club anthem excerpts before evaluating CAA, PE, BC, and FBR. CAA was positively associated with both PE and BC, and these responses were positively associated with FBR. The two prespecified coefficient products were positive, whereas the residual direct CAA–FBR association was not significant. A separate balanced validation study (N = 450) supported CAA's empirical distinction from simple anthem liking, PE, BC, FBR, and prior brand attitude. CAA explained additional variance in PE and BC beyond simple liking and pre-exposure controls, while its incremental association with FBR was small. The findings indicate that evaluations of recurring auditory brand cues covary with consumer–brand relationship outcomes alongside affective and cognitive responses. This study extends auditory branding and sensory service literature by conceptualizing recurring branded sound as a service-embedded cue and examining theoretically ordered affective and cognitive associations. Because CAA was measured and the focal constructs were self-reported within one session, the findings support an association-based interpretation and do not establish temporal mediation or causality. © 2026

Title: Evaluating role-prompted LLM responses on autism-related Theory-of-Mind tasks
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can perform well on social-reasoning benchmarks, but it remains unclear whether role prompting can produce distinguishable response patterns on autism-related Theory of Mind (ToM) tasks. This question matters for developing neurodiversity-aware AI evaluation, but any such work must distinguish behavioral output patterns from claims about autistic cognition or lived experience. In this paper, we introduce a ToM evaluation covering 11 established task types and four instructional personas: neurotypical and ASD Levels 1–3, labeled using DSM-5 support levels as heuristic anchors rather than validated clinical profiles. We curate 460 multiple-choice items and test state-of-the-art LLMs of varying scales. Baseline results show that in the original experiments, even detailed persona prompts do not yield reliable accuracy differentiation across model families, with smaller models often failing to meaningfully distinguish the imposed personas. A prompt-specificity ablation shows that explicit speech, cognitive-style, and response constraints substantially strengthen persona differentiation. Native-thinking configurations enlarge full-profile accuracy gaps and improve role-only accuracy, while some role-only conditions retain weaker, model-dependent ordering. To improve role fidelity, we implement an actor–critic workflow in which the actor produces in-character answers and the critic enforces persona constraints. After actor–critic, higher ASD levels exhibit lower accuracy on advanced ToM tasks and produce shorter utterances with fewer mental-state terms, matching the prompt-specified profile constraints. We further examine scale and alignment: larger models tend to increase overall accuracy while preserving role fidelity in our experiments, whereas general alignment tuned for helpfulness via preference optimization raises average correctness but reduces persona separability, collapsing the prompt-induced gradient. Title: The dark side of disrespect: How workplace incivility breeds service sabotage and turnover
Abstract: This study examines how different sources of workplace incivility affect frontline hotel employees. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory and Social Identity Theory, Study 1 compares the effects of employee incivility (originating internally) and customer incivility (originating externally) on emotional exhaustion. Based on a scenario-based experiment with 263 participants, the results show that employee incivility causes greater emotional exhaustion than customer incivility. Using survey data from 302 respondents, the findings reveal that same-level colleague incivility has the strongest negative impact, followed by supervisor, subordinate, and customer incivility. Title: ViLID: Multimodal misinformation detection with complementary input- and rationale-level inconsistency signals
Abstract: Multimodal misinformation on social media platforms often exploits subtle inconsistencies between text claims and accompanying images, such as repurposing authentic images out of context. We evaluate ViLID on Fakeddit and MMFakeBench. The full model achieves the strongest overall performance, while the ablation results indicate that rationale-derived signals primarily improve error balance and the preservation of truthful samples by reducing the over-flagging of benign mismatches. Title: Defisherization: The political ecology of small-scale fisheries decline in Indonesia
Abstract: In many coastal areas, the decline of small-scale fisheries is a daily reality for fishers. However, it is still framed as a technical issue, leaving unaddressed the power relations in marine governance that gradually erode fishers' livelihoods. This article develops the concept of defisherization to analyze how conservation-oriented coastal governance and ecological pressures cumulatively erode the livelihoods of small-scale fishers. Based on research in fishing communities along the coast of Buton, Southeast Sulawesi, the study employs observation, in-depth interviews (including a structured household questionnaire), and focus group discussions to examine the dynamics of this transformation. The findings suggest that defisherization occurs through the interplay of four main mechanisms: the narrowing of fishing spaces through permanent conservation zones; ecological pressures that drive household adaptation strategies without fully exiting the fisheries sector; symbolic persistence without adequate material reproduction; and the cumulative interaction between the three that gradually consolidates fisheries as a cultural identity but increasingly marginalizes it as a livelihood. This article offers defisherization as an analytical lens to move beyond explanations that view the decline of small-scale fisheries as an unintended consequence of conservation or environmental crises, demonstrating that environmental governance is vulnerable to undermining the material foundations of livelihoods. In this context, successful ecosystem protection often comes at the cost of compromising the sustainability of small-scale fishers' livelihoods. By offering an analytical lens to understand fisheries decline as a cumulative political-ecological process, this study emphasizes the importance of linking conservation agendas to the sustainable social reproduction of coastal communities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Sensitive determination of mandelic acid in urine samples by D-μSPE using an H-ZSM-5@UiO-66 composite
Abstract: A zeolite@metal–organic framework composite, H-ZSM-5@UiO-66, was synthesized and applied as a novel adsorbent for the rapid and sensitive dispersive micro-solid phase extraction (D-μSPE) of mandelic acid (MA) from human urine samples, followed by HPLC-UV analysis. The synthesized composite was characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM). Under the optimized conditions (sample volume: 8.5 mL; pH: 5.75; adsorbent mass: 35 mg; extraction time: 5 min; elution with water–methanol (5:5, v/v), 7 mL; desorption time: 5 min), the method exhibited high sensitivity, with limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) of 0.04 and 0.09 μg mL−1, respectively. Excellent extraction efficiency (93.8%), a wide linear dynamic range (0.30–120 μg mL−1, R2 > 0.9992), and satisfactory precision (RSD <3.9%) were achieved. The developed D-μSPE:H-ZSM-5@UiO-66–HPLC-UV method proved to be a reliable and effective approach for the determination of trace levels of MA in real urine samples. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wang K.; Pan Z.; Lu Y.
Title: Incompetence or deception: Unraveling the asymmetric mechanisms of AI hallucinations on trust and distrust
Abstract: Reliance on generative artificial intelligence (AI) for knowledge work is increasing, yet confidently presented hallucinations can elicit strong negative user reactions. Existing literature frames hallucinations as technical failures that reduce trust, conflating the decline of trust with the emergence of distrust. However, trust and distrust are theoretically distinct constructs rather than opposite ends of a single continuum. Drawing on information manipulation theory (IMT), this study reconceptualizes AI hallucinations as violations of conversational norms. It proposes a model linking hallucination cues to perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially related to trust and distrust. It further examines whether perceived AI autonomy moderates the relationship between hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The model was tested using a sequential mixed-methods design that combined qualitative semi-structured interviews with a two-wave survey of 506 GenAI users. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA). The findings revealed that hallucination cues were differentially associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, with the former more strongly associated with trust and the latter with distrust. Perceived AI autonomy moderated the associations between some hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The PLS-SEM–NCA analysis provided complementary evidence on net effects and necessary conditions that neither method could offer alone. Overall, this study extends research on AI hallucinations by conceptualizing them as distinct forms of conversational norm violations and explaining how different hallucination cues are associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially linked to trust and distrust. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: GRL-DDC: A data-driven paradigm for sustainable governance of online information propagation
Abstract: Online information governance is not merely a problem of predicting diffusion outcomes, but an information-fusion-driven dynamic decision problem that requires balancing credible-information promotion, risk-oriented suppression, and benign-discussion preservation under limited resources. This paper proposes Graph Reinforcement Learning for Dual-Track Diffusion Control (GRL-DDC), a graph reinforcement learning framework for dual-track diffusion control on dynamic graphs. The core innovation of GRL-DDC lies in integrating temporal graph learning, model-based reinforcement learning, constrained intervention, influence maximization/minimization, and misinformation suppression into a unified two-stage framework for online information governance. In the first stage, a temporal graph state-transition predictor fuses observable network structure, node-level semantic states, and user behavioral features to learn short-horizon propagation-state transitions from observational graph snapshots. In the second stage, the trained transition predictor remains fixed and supports a constrained reinforcement learning policy learner that evaluates model-based counterfactual estimates and allocates promotion or suppression actions under explicit budget and action constraints. Experiments on real-world social media data show that GRL-DDC learns an interpretable asymmetric resource-allocation pattern: it prioritizes nodes that contribute to credible or constructive information diffusion while selectively suppressing negative-risk propagation at relatively low cost. These results demonstrate that GRL-DDC provides a feasible data-driven decision-support approach for resource-constrained intervention in dynamic online information diffusion. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Creating markets for under-utilised fish species: Consumer valuation of a co-created fish finger
Abstract: It is common practice to discarded under-utilised fish species that are caught as bycatch because of their low market value. In this paper, we examine whether locally co-created and produced fish fingers, made from locally sourced under-utilised fish species are valued by consumers by employing a discrete choice experiment (DCE). A novel feature of this study is that we consider three versions of the fish finger, sourced from three UK ports: Plymouth, Lowestoft and Grimsby. Our DCE employs a novel set of attributes to capture the unique characteristics of product design and development of the fish finger. Results reveal that all attributes are positively valued, with the largest for fish that are sustainably caught. We also find that distance to the product locality does not materially affected consumer valuation. Location comparisons indicate limited differences overall for the three versions of the fish finger. These results indicate that sustainability information is a primary driver of demand for processed seafood using species with historically low market uptake, while local cues add value without substituting for sustainability. Our findings can help inform efforts to reduce discarding of under-utilised fish species that remains a significant issue in many fisheries. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Mai Pieper M.; Hornborg A.
Author full names: Mai Pieper, Maximilian (60935162700); Hornborg, Alf (6507077000)
Title: The fantasy of digital immateriality: AI, ecologically unequal exchange, and appropriation of lived human time
Abstract: The purported immateriality of AI technologies is as illusory as the general understanding of conventional technologies as simply the application of politically neutral knowledge to nature. The materiality of technologies and their foundation in global inequalities has been illuminated by studies of ecologically unequal exchange (EUE). The aim of this article is to extend the applicability of EUE theory to digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) by highlighting how even the data that they process have an inevitably biophysical history. AI technologies represent a novelty mainly in the sense that, in addition to exploiting extractive areas through EUE, they are based on the appropriation of data from the public. We argue for understanding the materiality of data as derived from lived human time. AI's dependence on data can thus be regarded as representing and embodying biophysical processes and asymmetric transfers implicating issues of justice. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. Title: Exemption or backfire? The double-edged effect of AI attribution strategy on brand trust in digital content moral crises
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Human-AI collaboration has become central to brand content production, but AI's black-box nature obscures responsibility in digital content moral crises. When such content is perceived as violating widely shared social values, brands increasingly attribute such incidents to AI errors. Prior research has mainly emphasized the responsibility-exemption role of AI attribution strategy, offering limited insight into its moral risks, mixed consequences, and underlying mechanisms. Drawing on the fact-value model, this study conducts five scenario-based experiments to examine how AI attribution strategy affects brand trust in this crisis context. The findings reveal a double-edged effect. At the factual level, this strategy increases consumers' perceived responsibility reduction, thereby producing an exemption effect that supports trust repair. At the value level, it also triggers perceived moral indifference, thereby producing a backfire effect that damages trust. This double-edged effect is moderated by public opinion and consumer traits. High negative electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) dispersion strengthens the perceived responsibility reduction path, whereas low negative eWOM dispersion strengthens the perceived moral indifference path. AI literacy strengthens the exemption effect by helping consumers understand AI-related technical limitations, whereas hostile attribution bias strengthens the backfire effect by leading consumers to question the moral motives behind the brand's technical explanation. This study advances crisis attribution research by examining AI attribution as a proactive brand communication strategy under attribution ambiguity and shows how it can reduce factual blame while raising value-based moral concerns. The findings offer guidance for using AI attribution carefully and reducing ethical communication risks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The organic halo effect: A systematic review of the influence of organic labels and claims on healthiness perceptions
Abstract: Food labels and claims play an increasing role in shaping consumer perceptions in complex food environments. While claims about nutrients are known to influence judgements of food healthiness, less is known about whether organic cues can lead to similar halo effects. We performed a systematic review to examine how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. We searched Web of Science and PubMed for experimental studies examining the effect of organic cues on food healthiness perceptions. Studies were included if they compared products with and without organic cues and reported outcomes related to perceived healthiness or perceived nutritional content. Of the records screened, 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. We conducted a narrative synthesis following SWiM guidelines, examining differences by cue type and outcome. Most studies found that organic cues increased perceived food healthiness. This effect was observed across both general health evaluations and specific calorie or nutrient judgements. Effects were more consistent for certified organic labels, whereas unofficial claims showed somewhat greater variability across products. A smaller number of studies reported mixed or null results, often depending on consumer characteristics or informational context. This review provides a synthesis of evidence on how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. By clarifying how consumers translate this information into health- and nutrition-related judgements, it contributes to a coherent understanding of the mechanisms underlying health halo effects. These findings suggest that organic cues may simultaneously act as signals of production practices and triggers of broader inferences about healthiness. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: The impact of reverse wording on cross-cultural comparisons of food-related attitudes
Abstract: Reverse-worded items (RWIs) are commonly used in multi-item scales to reduce acquiescence bias, yet their implications for cross-cultural food attitude measurement remain underexamined. This study compared positively worded items (PWIs) and RWIs across four established food-related attitude scales using data from 6300 adult consumers across ten countries. RWIs generally showed lower internal consistency and weaker inter-item correlations than PWIs. Items showing the largest cross-country variation in standardized loadings from multi-group confirmatory factor analysis were predominantly reverse-worded. RWIs also produced lower mean scores and generally greater response dispersion than PWIs. These wording-related differences varied by construct and country, followed no uniform pattern across measurement indicators, and may reflect the combined influence of item content, linguistic structure, and culturally patterned response tendencies. Across these indicators, PWI and RWI subsets did not consistently function as psychometrically equivalent components of the same scale. The findings suggest that the use of RWIs in cross-cultural food attitude measurement may introduce wording-related measurement instability, and that wording-direction effects require explicit consideration in the design and evaluation of international consumer research instruments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Cao S.; Yang J.; Xu L.; Li X.; Zeng Y.; Wu G.
Title: Upward movement of pedestrian groups on stairways under different urgency levels
Abstract: Efficient vertical evacuation through stairways has become a challenge for underground and high-rise buildings. The patterns and behavioral mechanisms of upward movement of pedestrian groups on staircases remains unrevealed, particularly under emergency conditions. In this paper, upward movement characteristics of pedestrians including monads, dyads, triads, and tetrads on a double-turn staircase with a divergent platform are investigated under normal and emergency conditions. A self-organized two-lane pattern is formed during turning, while the stair–platform transition induces rapid configuration reorganization. Dyads increasingly adopt chain configurations near the junction, whereas triads and tetrads shift toward triangle and quadrangle configurations. Moreover, emergency conditions enlarge interpersonal spacing and walking dissimilarity. The splitting probabilities of dyads, triads, and tetrads increase from 23%, 41% and 62% under normal conditions to 50%, 53% and 100% under emergency conditions respectively. Average speed decreases with group size and increases by 0.25–0.38 m/s under emergency conditions. At the individual level, monads generally maintain higher average speed, whereas group members tend to exhibit a larger increase under emergency conditions. These findings clarify the combined effects of stair–platform geometry, group size, and urgency level on group behavior and evacuation dynamics, providing empirical evidence for group evacuation modelling and stairway design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Text-driven causal mapping of PET/rPET circularity in Australia: A dynamic factor–network analysis
Abstract: PET circularity is often evaluated by recovery volumes, although performance ultimately depends on whether recovered material can be converted into quality-assured outputs and absorbed by viable end markets. Yet the mechanisms connecting policy, markets, technology, and stakeholder behavior remain dispersed across heterogeneous evidence. We developed a source-attributed, time-stamped causal-network approach using 750 Australian government, industry and NGO, corporate, and media documents published during 2010–2025. Causal extraction, semantic normalization, sentiment assignment, and graph construction yielded 2794 factor nodes and 1588 unique causal edges. The network was strongly externalized: policy, market, and social factors were more numerous and highly connected than internal technical and operational factors. Persistent barriers combined cost and price volatility, inconsistent recyclate quality, infrastructure gaps, and weak policy implementation. Positive mechanisms clustered around standards and measurement, design for recyclability, operational capacity, and end-market development; their circular value depended on retained material quality and the end use reached. Source attribution revealed systematic framing differences, with media coverage concentrating negative implementation narratives. Temporal and regional analyses indicated a shift from limited attention to rapid expansion and subsequent consolidation, alongside national structural hubs and differentiated state pathways. A full-text academic shadow corpus preserved the broad problem domains but changed their hierarchy: academic evidence foregrounded material and processing mechanisms, whereas the primary corpus foregrounded institutional coordination and market implementation. The contribution is therefore not a universal ranking of Australian interventions, but an auditable framework for identifying how technical feasibility becomes, or fails to become, operational circularity under different institutional conditions. © 2026 The Authors

Title: A transferable methodological framework for using EIA documentation as a data source for sector-level environmental footprinting
Abstract: Sector-level environmental assessment of mining is frequently constrained by the limited availability of consistent and publicly accessible operational inventory data. Although Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) documentation contains detailed engineering information on mining projects, its potential as a source of life cycle inventory (LCI) data has received little attention. This study develops and demonstrates a transferable bottom-up methodological framework that uses EIA documentation as a source of operational inventory data for sector-level environmental footprinting. The framework integrates project-level information extracted from publicly available EIA studies with official national mining statistics to estimate extraction-stage greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, land-use intensity, and water use. Croatia was selected as the demonstration case because publicly available EIA documentation can be systematically linked with official production and concession data. A total of 68 EIA studies describing 75 mining operations prepared between 2015 and 2024 were analysed. The estimated extraction-stage GHG emissions of the Croatian mining sector amount to 0.164 Mt. CO₂-eq, corresponding to approximately 2–3% of industrial GHG emissions. Construction stone and aggregates dominate total emissions because of their production volume, whereas dimension stone quarrying exhibits the highest specific GHG emissions and land-use intensity. The results further demonstrate that production scale primarily determines total environmental burdens, while extraction technology exerts a stronger influence on specific environmental intensities. Beyond the presented case study, the principal contribution of this research lies in demonstrating how publicly available regulatory documentation can be systematically transformed into operational inventory data suitable for sector-level environmental assessment. The proposed framework complements conventional LCA and national environmental inventories by improving the visibility of extraction-stage impacts and provides a transferable methodological approach for jurisdictions where comparable regulatory and statistical data are available. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: The processing of word order is affected by verb subcategorization frequency: Evidence from electrophysiology
Abstract: This study investigated the influence of verb subcategorization preferences on sentence processing in Standard Indonesian. We examined how verb biases affect the processing of active and passive sentences by utilizing event-related potentials. Our findings revealed that passive sentences with active-bias verbs elicited a significant late positive shift (P600) relative to active sentences, which indicated increased processing difficulty. No such effect was detected for passive sentences with passive-bias verbs. The cost was observed only where the verb's preference conflicted with the passive structure, suggesting that verb-specific statistics, rather than word order alone, contribute to the difficulty of passive sentences. We highlight the need for a nuanced understanding of sentence comprehension that incorporates both structural and lexical influences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yan J.; Zhao B.
Title: MVRFDet: Malicious package detection in PyPI ecosystem using multi-view representation fusion
Abstract: The widespread use of the Python Package Index has made it a primary target for malicious package poisoning attacks, seriously threatening software supply chain security. However, existing detection methods often rely on single-view features, making it difficult to cope with increasingly complex and covert attack methods, and it is difficult to achieve an effective balance between detection performance and efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel malicious package detection method called MVRFDet, based on multi-view representation fusion. Specifically, this method fuses features from three views: package metadata, global API call graph of source code and fine-grained control flow graph, and code semantic features of suspicious API code context snippets. To reduce runtime overhead, a centrality analysis and large language model are used to automatically extract a list of sensitive APIs offline, accurately locating suspicious API code context snippets. Finally, a channel attention module is designed to adaptively fuse representations from three views to achieve accurate classification. Extensive experiments on mixed datasets from multiple sources demonstrate that MVRFDet achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to eight baseline methods, with improvements in precision ranging from 2.5% to 24.8% and recall from 4% to 18.3%. Ablation studies and parameter sensitivity analyses validate the effectiveness of the model’s component design and the optimal selection of hyperparameters. Furthermore, detection efficiency evaluations show that it achieves a better trade-off between runtime overhead and detection performance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: SDE-IG: A robust malware family classification method based on graph invariance learning
Abstract: While existing malware family classification methods achieve high performance on in-distribution data, they often overfit mutable features when subjected to different compilers, optimization levels, and advanced code obfuscation. This vulnerability significantly degrades their generalization under complex distribution shifts. Furthermore, applying existing graph invariance learning methods, which typically rely on random topological sampling, disrupts the strict semantic dependencies inherent in binary code. Additionally, a naive concatenation of dynamic and static features introduces underlying system call noise, adversely affecting the model's ability to identify core family logic. In response, this paper proposes SDE-IG, a robust malware family classification framework based on invariant subgraphs. A cross-environment invariant subgraph extraction mechanism is designed from a static perspective. By integrating binary semantic priors with parameterized graph neural networks, this mechanism decouples the program call graph into an invariant subgraph representing core semantics and an environment subgraph capturing noise. This separation is designed to reduce reliance on environment-dependent structures that may vary across compilation, linking, and obfuscation settings. To address potential static topology failures caused by extreme obfuscation, SDE-IG incorporates a dynamic behavioral view as auxiliary semantic evidence. During end-to-end joint optimization, a collaborative mixup strategy is applied to simulate unknown variants and broaden the distribution boundary. Coupled with an asynchronous two-stage optimization and a gated residual calibration mechanism, this approach effectively minimizes the interference of dynamic behavioral noise on the static backbone representation. Experimental results show that SDE-IG achieves improved cross-period classification stability under the chronologically separated temporal distribution shifts evaluated in this study. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Physics-Inspired hybrid AI framework for mechanistic process model development
Abstract: Modern chemical engineering requires robust physical modeling and data analysis to uncover laws in complex phenomena. While traditional regression methods are highly interpretable, they often struggle with complex, non-linear data structures. Conversely, pure artificial intelligence solutions, such as deep learning, provide immense predictive power but often lack the transparency and physical consistency necessary for reliable mechanistic discovery. This study integrates advanced techniques, including deep neural networks and graph attention networks, thereby improving the framework’s accuracy in real-world applications. We also introduce a user-friendly graphical interface to simplify interactions with complex models. Title: Developing a cyber-resilience framework for UAVs: insights from expert interviews on addressing cybersecurity challenges
Abstract: Rapid technological advances have greatly enhanced the development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their potential for beneficial uses. Such uses, however, have been limited by cybersecurity concerns. Despite considerable research attention, threat levels are increasing, and this is likely to further inhibit UAV use. A different approach is therefore required, one that marks a change from reactive mitigation to proactive prevention. This study proposes a holistic cyber-resilience framework for UAVs based on five resilience features, which are redundancy, flexibility, modularity, diversity, and tightness of feedback loops. Such a change, called for by several authors but yet to be achieved, can come through the components of a framework that are supported by expert perspectives. The study employs a mixed-methods design with in-person interviews of 32 expert professionals across eight sectors (aviation, military, security, insurance, aerospace, cybersecurity, logistics, and academia). A total of 261 vulnerabilities ranging across five threat categories are identified, with those related to communication facilitating a point of entry for cascading attacks. Drawing on expert evaluations of five resilience features, the novelty of this study is its proposed lifecycle-based framework that shifts UAV security from mitigation to embedded resilience. Title: Does fast mapping accelerate lexical integration? Evidence from spoken and written novel words
Abstract: Fast mapping (FM) is an encoding paradigm in which a novel label is learned incidentally by inference. Some studies have interpreted FM training as capable of bringing forward the integration of novel words into existing lexical networks relative to typical consolidation timelines, although the evidence is mixed. We conducted three experiments to investigate whether FM promotes faster lexical integration compared to explicit encoding (EE). Experiments 1 and 2 extended prior orthographic fast mapping work, testing whether the rapid lexical integration claim generalises to the auditory (spoken) domain. Participants learned novel spoken words through either FM or EE training. Lexical integration was assessed using a pause detection task immediately after learning, one day later, and one week later (Experiment 1 only). Neither experiment found evidence that FM led to more rapid lexical integration compared to EE. Experiment 3 was a direct replication of previous orthographic fast mapping research ( Coutanche and Thompson-Schill, 2014 ), using a semantic categorisation task to assess integration of visually presented novel words. Again, we found no advantage for FM in promoting rapid lexical integration. Across all experiments, EE consistently produced superior explicit memory for the novel words compared to FM. These findings fail to support claims that FM-based training allows novel words to bypass time-dependent consolidation processes and become rapidly integrated into the mental lexicon. The results are consistent with complementary learning systems accounts positing that lexical integration typically benefits from offline consolidation, regardless of encoding method. Authors: Sattar M.A.; Hosen M.A.; Johnstone M.
Title: A review on hydrogen energy in the transportation sector: progress, challenges, and prospects in aviation, marine, and land
Abstract: The transportation sector emits large amounts of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, necessitating the adoption of a cleaner energy sources to reduce emissions. Hydrogen energy is considered as a cleaner energy source, offering zero emission during combustion, possessing the highest heating value and energy-to-weight ratio among conventional fuels. Therefore, hydrogen can be a better option for the transportation sector, including aviation, marine, and land transport. A thorough overview of the present status of hydrogen energy in the transportation sectors, assessing progress, challenges, and prospects for its application in different modes of transport considering hydrogen storage system is presented in this paper. Furthermore, the paper provides a full analysis of the current challenges impending the practical application of hydrogen in transportation sector and provides recommendations to overcome the challenges. This study also reviews current and future research on hydrogen fuel by different automakers such as Toyota, Honda, BMW, MAZDA, and Mercedes-Benz, aviation companies like Boeing and Airbus as well as marine vessels developed by China, Japan, France, Norway, and United Kingdom. This paper presents and discusses Commercial Readiness Index (CRI) and the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of hydrogen production processes, providing valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders. The authors identified key challenges that must be addressed to incorporate hydrogen in transportation sector, including the development of a convenient, safe, and cost-effective storage of hydrogen, reduction of hydrogen production cost, development of infrastructure, and the establishment of the formulation policy and regulatory framework. Authors: Yan R.; Wang S.; Shi D.; Ren X.
Title: CloudTrip: Exploring physiological data-enabled multisensory metaphorical narratives for everyday stress management
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: In modern society, an increasing number of people are suffering from the harmful effects of chronic stress, while data-enabled reflection has been shown to be an effective approach to stress management. However, most existing human–data interaction designs primarily focus on retrospective data review, often failing to foster engaging and meaningful reflection. In this paper, we present CloudTrip, an immersive application that represents the users’ data throughout a day as an experiential and interactive digital story for mental health self-reflection. Specifically, CloudTrip metaphorically conveys users’ daily stress-related physiological data into narrative experiences by dynamically mapping the data onto changes in visual and auditory elements of characters and virtual environments. Users can record reflective content during the experience and receive responsive feedback generated by a large language model, thereby forming an interactive narrative loop that further deepens reflective engagement. We conducted a 14-day within-subject study with 20 participants, comparing CloudTrip with a traditional line-chart visualization using a mixed-methods evaluation to assess its impact on the reflection experience and reflection support. Results show that CloudTrip was associated with a cardiac autonomic pattern compatible with higher arousal, increases in self-reported valence, arousal, and dominance, more favorable motivational ratings for the experience, stronger perceived support for reflection, and promise for repeated use. Finally, we discuss design implications for integrating data-enabled multisensory storytelling techniques into human–data interaction systems to promote everyday reflective behavior for mental health management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Explainable spatiotemporal modeling in crime analytics: Robbery prediction via graph neural networks
Abstract: Urban crime prediction is a critical task for ensuring public safety, yet it faces challenges related to model accuracy and transparency. While crime is an inherently temporal phenomenon, its embedding within the city’s structure suggests that integrating spatiotemporal dependencies via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can improve model robustness, particularly in data-sparse environments. Traditional grid-based methods often fail to capture the complex network topology of cities, while the “black-box” nature of advanced models raises ethical concerns for predictive policing. This study proposes an explainable spatiotemporal framework to predict robbery risk by uniquely integrating three elements: (1) fine-grained, citizen-sensed data from a public safety application in Santiago, Chile; (2) a tailored graph neural network to learn how to represent the urban environment as a graph; and (3) an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) component using Integrated Gradients to ensure transparency. We evaluate the model’s performance against traditional classifiers across various prediction horizons (1, 3, and 7 days) and spatial granularities. The results show that the tailored architecture dramatically improves predictive accuracy (average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve -AUC-  ≈  0.85) compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, the XAI analysis provides novel empirical evidence that citizen reports of “suspicious activity” are highly significant predictors of future burglaries, often more so than prior robbery incidents themselves. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
