Title: Quantifying Regulatory Bottlenecks in South Korea’s Clinical Trial Approval Process Through an Analytic Hierarchy Process Framework
Abstract: Purpose: Drug lag is a critical issue limiting South Korea’s pharmaceutical competitiveness and patient access, and it has been linked to delays in the Investigational New Drug (IND) review process. This study aimed to identify key barriers affecting IND review efficiency in South Korea by analyzing real-world industry experience and to propose concrete strategic actions to mitigate drug lag. Methods: We employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. First, we used grounded theory to identify problematic factors within the IND process through semi-structured interviews. We then applied the Analytic Hierarchy Process to evaluate these factors, followed by a quadrant analysis of importance and urgency to identify top-priority tasks. Results: Three core categories (rationality and patient-centricity, professional review, and operational efficiency), were identified as key domains for enhancing IND efficiency. Rationality and patient-centricity emerged as the most important and urgent criterion, followed closely by professional review. Within rationality and patient-centricity, four sub-criteria placed in the first quadrant (highly important and highly urgent): integration of patient needs into evaluation, global regulatory harmonization, acceptance of scientific evidence for new modalities, and adoption of overseas regulatory standards. Two sub-criteria within professional review (expert team review and standardized review guidelines) were also pinpointed in the first quadrant. Although operational efficiency ranked lowest, simplified Korean translation requirements stood out as the most critical factor within this category. Conclusion: Transitioning from focusing on procedural speed toward embracing regulatory flexibility to enhance scientific rationality and patient access is a viable pathway for mitigating drug lag in South Korea. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial
Abstract: Introduction: Treadmill exercise may improve gait and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain (CMLBP), but the additional effects of vertical traction and partial body weight support remain unclear. This study compared treadmill exercise combined with vertical traction and partial body weight support (VT+TE), treadmill exercise alone (TE), and core stabilization exercise. Methods: Forty-five patients with CMLBP were randomly assigned to VT + TE, TE, or control groups (n = 15 each). All groups received conventional physical therapy and completed 24 sessions over 8 weeks. Body weight support in the VT + TE group was reduced from 50% to 30%. The TE group performed pain-tolerable treadmill walking, whereas controls performed self-directed core stabilization exercises. Outcomes included Timed Up and Go (TUG) performance, self-selected and fast gait speeds, pain intensity, pressure pain threshold, disability, trunk repositioning error, and depressive symptoms. Assessments were conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and 4-week follow-up. Results: Significant time-by-group interactions occurred for all outcomes. Both treadmill groups showed greater improvements than controls in TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, pain intensity, and depressive symptoms. Compared with TE, VT + TE produced greater improvements in TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, disability, and flexion and extension repositioning errors. VT + TE also improved fast gait speed more than both comparison groups at post-intervention. Improvements in pain intensity and depressive symptoms were maintained at follow-up in both treadmill groups. Conclusions: Adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise may provide additional benefits for gait performance, disability, and trunk repositioning accuracy in patients with CMLBP. Interpretation is limited by the small sample size and the inability to distinguish the effects of vertical unloading from those of harness support. © 2026

Title: Biofeedback in musicians: A systematic review and meta-analysis of its effects on muscle activity, musculoskeletal health, and performance
Abstract: Musicians are at high risk for playing-related musculoskeletal disorders (PRMD) and playing- or performance-related pain (PRP), which can severely interfere with their practice routine, rehearsals, and performance. Although biofeedback offers a promising approach to address these problems, it has not been widely implemented into music education or practice, underscoring the need for a comprehensive assessment of its efficacy for physiological, health, and performance outcomes. We conducted a pre-registered systematic search of 9 electronic databases, yielding 3041 published works, and included 49 studies on biofeedback in musicians that reported outcomes related to muscle activity, musculoskeletal health, or performance. After extracting relevant data, we performed a meta-analysis of 36 studies using Bayesian mixed-effects models to evaluate effects across time (pre- vs. post), condition (biofeedback vs. comparator conditions, including traditional practice), and type of outcome. Across the selected studies, we found compelling evidence that biofeedback improves muscle activity (primarily reflected as reductions in activation), performance, and musculoskeletal health, indicating its potential to address PRMD and PRP symptoms, while also targeting relevant risk factors and supporting overall performance quality. These findings suggest that biofeedback-driven body awareness and physiological regulation can form the foundation for effective and sustainable performance. Successful implementation, however, will require collaboration between scientists, educators, and musicians to integrate biofeedback into pedagogical practice, supporting both performance and physical wellbeing. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Natural capital: the boom and bust of a metaphor? Insights from Scotland
Abstract: Despite a fifty-year academic history, the concept of ‘natural capital’ has only been translated into national policy and practice more recently. Since the early 2000s, global initiatives like The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity and the UN System for Environmental Economic Accounts have spurred country-level adoption of natural capital approaches around the world. To examine the implications of this uptake, we traced the concept’s evolution in Scotland through a discourse analysis of 14 interviews, supplemented by key documents and events. Natural capital entered the Scottish context in the early 2010s, intended to make nature visible to decision-makers through economically valuing the environment. By the 2020s, concerns over insufficient public funding for ecological restoration, conceptualised as a nature finance gap, shifted focus to making nature financeable by the private sector. Subsequently, natural capital became emblematic of emergent nature markets, particularly carbon-based mechanisms, precipitating a boom in private sector interest. As the risks of operationalising these markets became apparent to investors, confidence in natural capital faltered by 2023. This prompted the public sector to assume responsibility for de-risking market development. We argue natural capital has facilitated a discursive slide from advocacy for valuation towards commodification practices, framing environmental crises as apolitical market opportunities. This trajectory tends towards privatisation of potential returns while socialising risk through public mechanisms. While natural capital may enhance aspects of nature’s legibility within existing political and economic systems, we caution that its discursive dominance constrains more transformative ambitions to reconfigure the structures that harm nature and its restoration. Title: A hybrid ABM-PDE framework for real-world infectious disease simulations
Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid modelling approach that couples an Agent-Based Model (ABM) with a partial differential equation (PDE) model in an epidemic setting to simulate the spatial spread of infectious diseases using a compartmental structure with seven health states. The goal is to reduce the computational complexity of a full-ABM by introducing a coupled ABM-PDE model that offers significantly faster simulations while maintaining comparable accuracy. Our results demonstrate that the hybrid model not only reduces the overall simulation runtime (defined as the number of runs required for stable results multiplied by the duration of a single run) but also achieves smaller errors across both 25% and 100% population samples. The coupling mechanism ensures consistency at the model interface: agents crossing from the ABM into the PDE domain are removed and represented as density contributions, while surplus density in the PDE domain is used to generate agents with plausible trajectories derived from mobile phone data. We evaluate the hybrid model using real-world mobility and infection data for the Berlin-Brandenburg region in Germany, showing that it captures the core epidemiological dynamics while enabling efficient large-scale simulations. These results demonstrate that the proposed ABM-PDE framework provides a robust and computationally efficient alternative to full-scale agent-based simulations, making it suitable for realistic epidemic modelling and scenario analysis. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Dynamic risk assessment and emergency response effectiveness analysis for hazardous chemicals explosion based on dynamic Bayesian network and cloud model
Abstract: Hazardous chemical explosion accidents are characterized by multifactor coupling, time-dependent risk accumulation, and cascading consequence escalation. However, existing studies provide limited quantitative analysis of dynamic accident-risk evolution and the risk-reduction effectiveness of emergency safety barriers. To address these limitations, this study proposes a dynamic risk-assessment and emergency-response effectiveness analysis method for hazardous chemical explosions by integrating a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) with a cloud model (CM). First, a DBN incorporating explosion-related risk events, emergency safety barriers, and accident consequences is constructed based on accident investigation reports, accident evolution mechanisms, and expert knowledge. Second, the CM and an expert confidence index are used to quantify linguistic expert judgments and convert them into the prior and conditional probabilities required by the BN. Finally, Bayesian inference, sensitivity analysis, and safety-barrier scenario simulation are performed to identify the critical causal factors and quantify the risk-reduction effects of emergency measures. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can dynamically predict accident risk, diagnose critical contributing factors, and quantitatively evaluate the effectiveness of emergency safety barriers. It therefore provides quantitative decision support for hazardous chemical safety management and emergency-resource allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Development and test-retest reliability of a laboratory-based shipboard firefighting simulation for controlled performance testing
Abstract: Understanding shipboard firefighting performance is critical for improving crew safety and vessel preservation during damage control events. While prior research has been conducted in naval spaces, controlled simulations that assess performance without requiring naval vessels, personnel or specialised equipment are lacking. This study was designed to both develop and test a laboratory-based shipboard firefighting simulation. Consistent with shipboard firefighting activities, the simulation included walking, stair climbing, hose dragging, simulated boundary cooling, extinguisher carrying and casualty dragging tasks, completed within 8 min. Twenty-seven participants (22 males, 5 females) performed the simulation twice, with good test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.78; SEM = 17.6 s). Compared to Session 1, time-to-completion was 2.6% faster, RPE was 12.2% higher, HR was 5% lower, and core temperature estimate was 0.8% lower in Session 2 (all p < 0.05). Title: Effectiveness of exposure-based therapy through inhibitory learning via virtual reality in electronic gambling machines: Multiple baseline single-case experimental design
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Context: Electronic gambling machines (EGMs) can harm individuals and contribute to gambling disorder (GD). Empirically supported cognitive-behavioral interventions are effective yet associated with high relapse rates. One avenue for improvement is to target the urge to gamble through exposure. In the exposure approach based on the inhibitory learning model, the perceived self-efficacy (PSE) to refrain from gambling despite the urge serves as a proximal factor for change. The goal is to create a new learning association that overrides the pre-established link between gambling stimuli, urge to gamble, and PSE to refrain from gambling. Exposure can be done in virtual reality (VR) to promote self-control and reduce gambling behaviors. VR is a relevant exposure method because it allows reproduction of ecologically valid, realistic environments. Furthermore, researchers have more control over the course of the immersion experience than during exposure in vivo. The single-case, multiple-baseline experimental design includes six intervention sessions with VR exposure and daily journaling to measure PSE, urges, and gambling behaviors. This approach emphasizes building PSE to resist from gambling despite the urge. Four adult males who wanted to stop their gambling behavior participated in this study. Results: Statistical analyses demonstrate a significant increase in PSE across participants and a significant reduction in the urge to gamble in three of the four participants. This study highlights the potential benefits of using of such an exposure model. Title: Racialized psychotherapy: Understudied risks and the case for empirical scrutiny
Abstract: Racialized psychotherapy, a cluster of approaches centering race, racial identity, and racism in clinical work, emerged from legitimate concerns about cultural incompetence and minority underservice. The field has not tested the assumption that race-centering benefits racial minority clients. This paper identifies four mechanisms by which racialized therapy may harm clients: therapist-imposed racial salience that overrides client-defined concerns; hypervigilance induction through attributional training toward racial threat; externalized locus of control that undermines agency; and therapeutic deference that reduces the productive challenge clients from stigmatized groups may most need. The validation argument for racialized therapy is partly right but justifies responsive rather than proactive race-framing. The evidence base for culturally adapted interventions is modest, adverse effects go unreported, and the most explicitly race-focused protocols lack randomized trial evidence. Systematic research on conditions under which race-centered approaches benefit or harm clients is overdue. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Empirical Stage-Damage Functions for SME Content Losses in Australian Flood Vulnerability Assessment
Abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) dominate Australian business activity, yet empirically calibrated functions for nonresidential flood-related contents losses remain limited. Postevent surveys of 185 SMEs across 12 business types and 14 towns affected by the February-April 2022 Northern Rivers floods were used to derive stage-damage functions for stock, equipment, and fit-out. Contents-specific damage indices combined peak internal flood depth (0-6 m, relative to finished-floor level) with self-reported losses and preevent replacement values. Pooled curves were fitted using LOESS and a beta-family generalized additive model (Beta-GAM); a hierarchical Beta-GAM (HBGAM) generated business-type functions under partial pooling, while random forest and XGBoost provided depth-only predictive benchmarks. Across the pooled models, performance on the corresponding within-event 25% holdout sets was moderate (R2=0.57-0.69; RMSE=0.23-0.27), and neither machine-learning benchmark consistently improved performance. The Beta-GAM was retained because it provided smooth, bounded, interpretable relationships, model-based and bootstrap uncertainty intervals, and extractable threshold depths. The fitted mean damage index reached 0.50 at 1.03 m for stock, 1.09 m for equipment, and 1.27 m for fit-out, with uncertainty generally increasing above 3 m as data density declined. HBGAM-derived D50 values ranged from 0.66 to 1.18 m for stock, 0.81 to 1.18 m for equipment, and 1.09 to 1.48 m for fit-out, indicating model-derived sector variation. These event-calibrated functions support screening-level relative SME contents-loss assessment and evaluation of loss-reduction options in comparable settings; application elsewhere requires external validation or local recalibration.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Towards a datafication framework for higher education institutions student success: A systematic review
Abstract: Customer success is key to customer retention. Seemingly, this is equally true in the higher education space, as students are customers of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and, therefore, the primary reason for HEIs' existence. In view of this, it is important to understand and improve student success, which is dependent on different data indicators. Being guided by student success data indicators in HEI administration is necessary as it’s beneficial to both HEIs and their students, as through it, students can complete their qualification on time, and HEIs generate revenue. In the South African context, with its high unemployment rate and high dropout rates, understanding HEI student success is vital. However, HEIs are accustomed to collecting data rather than utilizing it for transformational activities, there has been an increase in research/publications on student success datafication frameworks in higher education in South Africa. However, these studies in isolation do not give the complete picture. This paper aims to systematically review the South African-based HEI student success data-related frameworks, including their underlying principles, trends, challenges, gaps, and future opportunities for improvement. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses method was used. Based on a clearly outlined search strategy, 508 publication abstracts were considered for review. Of these abstracts, 40 were selected for further review based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, and thereafter, 16 publications were included in the final review. The systematic review findings indicated that mostly data point indicators exist as compared to datafication frameworks. Furthermore, limited studies have been conducted on private higher education institutions in South Africa. Additionally, public sector studies have focused on first-year students; therefore, no segmentation. Title: An efficient convolutional neural network model for classifying positive affective states from EEG data considering sleep condition
Abstract: Background The recognition of affective states from EEG recordings considering the sleep condition can be an important supporting tool in therapy and in the treatment of psychological or psychiatric disorders. New method Since sleep deprivation changes EEG characteristics, a two-stage framework is developed for affective state classification. First, a classification between "Normal Sleep" (NS) and "Sleep-Deprived" (SD) is conducted using resting-state EEG data. The data are then fed into one of two newly proposed, lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize four affective states. Results In the first stage, CNN-BiLSTM achieves 95.96% accuracy under window-level splitting and 70.46% under subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, while in the second stage the proposed models achieve 93.40% (NS) and 90.95% (SD) under window-level splitting, and 38.98% (NS) and 38.97% (SD) under cross-validation. The lower subject-independent accuracies reflect the class imbalance and the clustering of scores near the class boundaries, which make cross-subject four-class generalization challenging. Comparison with existing methods As existing studies mostly classify momentary emotions without addressing sleep conditions, direct comparison with prior work is difficult; we therefore benchmarked our framework against several established baseline models, including SqueezeNet, EEGNet, ShallowConvNet, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. Conclusions This study suggests that considering physiological states can improve multi-class classification of affective states from time-varying neurophysiological signals such as EEG. The framework performs strongly under window-level evaluation, whereas its performance under the stricter subject-independent setting is more limited and should be interpreted accordingly. It can nonetheless contribute to more comprehensive research in affective neuroscience. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Followership, teamwork, and wellness among nursing students: A cross-sectional study
Abstract: Background: Effective followership is progressively acknowledged as an essential professional competency in healthcare. However, nursing education has traditionally emphasized leadership development, resulting in a limited understanding of how followership relates to teamwork and wellness during professional preparation. Evidence regarding effective followership among nursing students remains scarce. Objective: To examine the relationships among effective followership, teamwork, individual wellness, and organizational wellness among nursing students and to identify factors associated with effective followership. Methods: A cross-sectional correlational study was conducted among 325 nursing students recruited from universities in Jordan. Participants completed an online survey comprising measures of effective followership, teamwork perceptions, individual wellness, and organizational wellness. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression were used to examine the data. Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to evaluate the construct validity of the investigator-developed measures. Results: Students reported moderate levels of effective followership and teamwork perceptions. Effective followership demonstrated strong positive associations with teamwork perceptions (r = 0.66), individual wellness (r = 0.59), and organizational wellness (r = 0.59). Multiple linear regression showed that teamwork (β = 0.576, p < 0.001), GPA (β = 0.210, p < 0.001), and academic level (β = 0.083, p = 0.041) were significant predictors of effective followership, with the model explaining 47.10% of the variance (R2 = 0.471). Students demonstrating greater active engagement, accountability, and independent critical thinking reported more positive collaborative and wellness experiences. Conclusion: Effective followership appears to be an important professional competency associated with teamwork and wellness among nursing students. The results support consideration of the inclusion of followership development alongside leadership preparation within nursing curricula. Educational strategies that promote active engagement, accountability, constructive communication, and shared responsibility may better prepare students for interprofessional healthcare practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Lörch L.; Bonawitz E.; Brod G.
Author full names: Lörch, Lucas (57203911205); Bonawitz, Elizabeth (19933641800); Brod, Garvin (54917165400)
Title: The power of varying more than one thing at a time
Abstract: Background: Varying one thing at a time (VOTAT) is considered a universal approach for designing informative experiments. Its core idea is that controlled experiments can be designed by manipulating a single variable. However, we show that this single-manipulation heuristic can produce misleading evidence in contexts involving interrelated variables. We argue that varying more than one thing at a time (MOTAT) can be more informative when learners’ prior beliefs render alternative explanations implausible. Aims: To test these claims, we compared single-manipulation to MOTAT experiments in a Bayesian learning simulation and a pre-registered empirical study on children's learning about water displacement. Sample: Participants in the empirical study were 185 children aged 6–9. Methods: Learners predicted which of two spheres would displace more water and then observed an animation of the spheres being submerged. In the single-manipulation experiments, the spheres differed either only in size or only in material, leading to a confound of these dimensions with mass. In the MOTAT experiments, both size and material were manipulated such that the larger sphere was lighter. We investigated the formal informativeness of single-manipulation and MOTAT experiments (simulation study) and their effect on children's learning, as measured via a post- and transfer test (empirical study). Results: MOTAT experiments were most informative and led to the highest transfer test performance. Conclusion: These findings provide initial evidence that VOTAT's core heuristic has a narrower scope than is commonly assumed. When variables are interrelated, deliberately varying more than one variable may be the better choice. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Fuel transition pathways: assessing hydrogen blending in canadian household natural gas supplies
Abstract: Decarbonizing residential energy systems is essential for Canada to achieve its net-zero emissions target by 2050, particularly in regions where natural gas remains the dominant fuel for space heating. This study presents a techno-economic assessment of blending green hydrogen into residential natural gas distribution networks in Alberta, Ontario, Saskatchewan, and British Columbia using grid-connected hybrid energy systems integrating solar photovoltaics, wind turbines, battery storage, and electrolyzers. Hydrogen blending ratios of 10%, 15%, and 20% by volume are evaluated for a representative cluster of 500 households under province-specific demand and renewable resource conditions. The novelty of this study lies in developing a province-specific techno-economic framework that integrates hybrid renewable energy systems, residential hydrogen blending scenarios, and multi-parameter sensitivity analysis to evaluate hydrogen integration within existing Canadian gas infrastructure. Annual hydrogen demand increases from 9.5 t/year in British Columbia at 10% blending to 25.8 t/year in Alberta at 20% blending. At a 20% hydrogen blend, residential CO2 emissions decrease from 2,820 to 2,200 t/year in Alberta (∼22%), from 2,610 to 2,100 t/year in Ontario (∼20%), from 2,358 to 1,900 t/year in Saskatchewan (∼19%), and from 2,081 to 1,600 t/year in British Columbia (∼23%), corresponding to reductions of up to 620 t CO2/year. Net present costs range from $0.54 M to $1.33 M, while the levelized cost of hydrogen varies between $1.53 and $2.60/kg H2, primarily governed by renewable resource availability and electricity prices. Electricity demand for electrolysis increases with hydrogen blending, raising grid electricity contributions from approximately 34–45% at 10% blending to 58–66% at 20%, particularly during winter periods with limited solar generation. Sensitivity analysis shows that increasing solar irradiation from 2 to 5.2 kWh/m2/day can reduce hydrogen production costs by up to 24%, while higher grid electricity prices may increase total system costs by more than 150%. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Machine learning surrogate models for Thermo-Elastohydrodynamic Lubrication in line contacts: Full-field prediction and reduced-order modelling
Abstract: Conventional Thermo-Elastohydrodynamic Lubrication (TEHL) solvers for line contacts require solving coupled Reynolds–elasticity–energy equations, which typically take minutes per operating point. This limits their use in optimisation and system-level simulations. Moreover, accurate prediction of full-field quantities is essential: pressure profiles are required for fatigue analysis, film thickness distributions enable the proper translation of capacitance in measurements, and the heat fluxes are used in thermally coupled multiscale simulations. In this work, we develop and benchmark full-field surrogate models that generate 1D pressure and film thickness profiles and a 2D temperature-rise field using four architectures: MLP, generative CNN, POD-NN (linear reduction), and DLROM (autoencoder-based non-linear reduction). The models are trained on approximately 36,000 converged TEHL solutions spanning a twelve-dimensional input space of operating and material parameters, utilising robust outlier removal. All surrogates achieve a global R2>0.99 on the test set and compress inference times into the microsecond regime, delivering speed-ups of up to O(106) on CPU and O(107) on GPU relative to the numerical solver. Out-of-distribution testing demonstrates robust extrapolation capabilities, with maximum temperature errors below 1 °C and an RMSE below 0.8 °C when predicting beyond the training boundaries. The benchmark highlights clear trade-offs: the MLP and CNN are strong baselines on a fixed spatial grid; the POD-NN is particularly stable and fast for the high-dimensional temperature field but may smooth highly localised extrema; and the DLROM offers compact non-linear representations but exhibits higher extrapolation variance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Toward climate-responsive higher education: A HeatReady framework for state universities and colleges in the National Capital Region in the Philippines
Abstract: Extreme heat events have increased risks and threats to the education sector in urban areas across the Philippines. This study developed a HeatReady Framework for State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) in the National Capital Region (NCR) of the Philippines for climate-responsive educational management. The method that was employed in this study is the explanatory sequential design with 180 participants from seven SUCs in NCR. Findings revealed that all five HeatReady key action areas must be present in crafting a framework because of the high level of agreement of importance of the stakeholder in these components. Based on the inferential analysis using the Kruskal-Wallis H test revealed significant differences across SUCs (χ2 (6, N = 180) = 15.045, p = .010). The Ordinal logistic regression analysis confirmed that the five domains collectively predicted the importance of these key action areas in building the framework (χ2(11) = 22.265, p = 0.014), indicating the integration rather than isolation of these factors' impact. The goodness of fit is not significant, which indicates that the model fits the data very well (Pearson χ2 (446) = 269.623, p = 1.000; Deviance χ2 (446) = 243.014, p = 1.000). Qualitative findings revealed that the major challenges experienced by stakeholders included inadequate ventilation and cooling facilities, poorly ventilated classrooms, and the absence of formal institutional heat policies during extreme heat events. Stakeholders recommended the development of standardized HeatReady policies, flexible learning modalities during high heat index conditions, and the improvement of campus infrastructure through cooling systems, shaded spaces, and heat-safe areas. The HeatReady framework offered a model to safeguard welfare, ensure academic continuity, and improve the adaptive capacity of SUCs in NCR for climate-responsive educational management. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Cultural value configurations and guests’ evaluations of AI-enabled service technologies
Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence reshapes hospitality service delivery, understanding how culturally diverse guests evaluate AI-enabled encounters is critical. This study examines how cultural value configurations shape evaluations of service robots in hotels. Cultural value configurations are coherent combinations of orientations that jointly influence how individuals interpret and assess service encounters. Using more than 3000 robot-related hotel reviews from guests across 77 countries, we integrate Hofstede's dimensions with Schwartz's value theory to explain cross-cultural differences in sentiment. Masculinity and uncertainty avoidance predict more negative sentiment, individualism shows a positive association that is sensitive to model specification, and power distance shows no direct effect. One configuration is robust: masculinity combined with uncertainty avoidance amplifies dissatisfaction, and this interaction holds under multilevel and combined estimation and survives correction for multiple testing. Two further configurations remain suggestive: power distance combined with uncertainty avoidance attenuates risk aversion, and individualism combined with masculinity increases tolerance for imperfection. Both are marginal and do not persist under multilevel or joint estimation, so we report them as patterns for replication rather than as established effects. Hofstede's indices provide the measurement, while Schwartz's value theory serves as an interpretive lens rather than as a measured individual-level construct. Findings position culture as a configurational system and provide guidance for AI service design and communication. © 2026 The Authors

Title: A three-stage interpretable linguistic group decision-making model: A perspective of combining concept lattice and adversarial interpretive structure modeling
Abstract: In complex decision-making environments, linguistic group decision-making (GDM) often faces the challenge of high decision complexity as well as ensuring transparency and interpretability of decision results. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes an interpretable linguistic GDM model based on formal concept analysis (FCA) and adversarial interpretive structure modeling (AISM), which provides a three-stage framework for revealing the hierarchical relationships and directed dependencies among alternatives. Linguistic truth-valued lattice implication algebra is first utilized to represent the decision-maker’s linguistic evaluation information, which can handle both comparable and incomparable linguistic information. Second, the incorporation of Pareto frontier facilitates the identification and filtering of lower-ranked alternatives, reducing computational complexity and improving scalability in large-scale GDM scenarios. In addition, the integration of FCA and AISM enhances the interpretability of the decision-making process. Finally, a case study and experiments demonstrate the advantages of the proposed model in reducing decision complexity and improving decision interpretability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zheng Y.
Title: Understanding grey sheep users in recommender systems: A systematic and critical review of detection, modeling, and evaluation
Abstract: Grey sheep users (GSUs), characterized by weak or unstable alignment with the broader user population, remain a challenge in collaborative filtering-based recommender systems. Despite extensive efforts devoted to their detection and treatment, a clear and consistent understanding of GSUs is still lacking. Existing studies typically adopt model-dependent definitions and often assume that GSUs necessarily reduce recommendation quality. This paper presents a systematic and critical review of GSUs, covering their definition, detection strategies, modeling paradigms, and evaluation practices. We revisit the classical similarity-based interpretation and show that the effect of GSUs depends on model design rather than being inherently harmful. Based on this observation, we introduce a refined conceptual perspective that describes GSUs as users with consistently misaligned preference patterns, and further propose a dynamic view that distinguishes between short-term irregular behavior and stable preference differences. We then provide a comprehensive taxonomy of existing approaches, including detection-dependent methods and detection-free strategies, and analyze their underlying assumptions and limitations. We further show that the form in which a detection result is expressed constrains which handling strategies are available, and that this correspondence is rarely exploited in practice. A key finding of this study is that current research is limited by weak evaluation practices. In particular, the absence of ground truth, inconsistent definitions, and dependence on aggregate performance metrics lead to circular reasoning and unreliable conclusions. Finally, we outline future research directions toward more robust modeling frameworks and user-centered evaluation protocols, with the aim of establishing a clearer conceptual foundation and guiding the development of more reliable and inclusive recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Understanding event tourism competitiveness: From stakeholder-constructed attributes to visitor valuation
Abstract: This study examines event tourism competitiveness by integrating stakeholder-constructed competitiveness attributes with visitor valuation. Using Hong Kong as the primary empirical context and London as a validation context, the study combines thematic analysis, confirmatory composite analysis (CCA), and a discrete choice experiment (DCE). The thematic analysis identifies six competitiveness dimensions, including Resource Synergies, a novel dimension capturing cross-sector and cross-boundary integration. The DCE results show that Resource Synergies functions as a direct destination selection criterion for MICE participants, whereas its direct effect is not significant among leisure-event visitors. Professionalism and Facilities emerges as a universal competitiveness driver for both groups, while leisure-event visitors prioritise experiential distinctiveness and international content. These findings advance event tourism competitiveness research by explaining how competitiveness attributes are constructed by stakeholders and differentially valued in the event tourism context. Title: When is plant-based meat close enough? A multiplicity- and selection-aware non-inferiority reanalysis of sensory-parity claims
Abstract: Claims that a plant-based meat alternative has reached sensory parity can depend on the product designated as the category leader, the endpoint and margin examined, and whether multiple comparisons and product selection are considered. We reanalyzed the public respondent-level exports from a blinded consumer benchmark covering 14 meat categories. Primary products were fixed from the source metadata rather than re-selected from the reanalysis outcomes. We reported paired raw differences, standardized effect sizes, rating-based same-or-better shares, one-sided non-inferiority tests, and an inverted confidence-bound summary termed the minimum data-supported margin. The focal family comprised 14 Overall Liking tests at a 0.5-point margin and was adjusted using Holm's procedure. Chicken Nuggets and Unbreaded Chicken Filets met the nominal criterion, but neither remained non-inferior after familywise adjustment. Across the 70 source-roster contrasts, nine nominal findings were reduced to four after a conservative global Holm adjustment: Texture, Appearance, and Similarity for Chicken Nuggets and Appearance for Meatballs. At 0.5 points, no candidate-product Overall Liking conclusion survived within-category Holm adjustment. Source-designated and export-sample-best leaders differed in two categories, with an additional exact tie in Bacon. The public exports contained no city/site identifier or product-specific purchase, willingness-to-pay, or choice outcome; consequently, the analyzed margins cannot be interpreted as behaviorally validated acceptance thresholds. These findings reposition non-inferiority as one component of a transparent robustness audit: sensory-parity claims require an explicit decision margin, effect-size reporting, multiplicity control, and separation of product screening from confirmation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Throughput and energy efficiency optimization in cooperative IoT systems with multi-level adaptive vacation and delay strategies
Abstract: This paper addresses the trade-off between throughput and energy efficiency in Internet of Things (IoT) systems. A joint multi-level adaptive vacation and delay strategy is proposed for relay assisted Short Packet Communication (SPC). The relay is modeled as operating in four states: transmission, delay, vacation, and idle. Based on this model, closed-form expressions are derived for steady-state queue length, average durations of different system states, average throughput, and energy efficiency. Numerical results show that the benefit of delay strategy is condition dependent and is jointly affected by transmission reliability, system load, and vacation parameters. Research shows that the delay-assisted vacation strategy exhibits stronger robustness in improving throughput than in enhancing energy efficiency, with its performance gains jointly constrained by system load and link reliability. The strategy is only stably effective under high-load and high-reliability scenarios; thus, it should be deployed differently according to specific system conditions and optimization objectives rather than being enabled globally without distinction. Further comparison with multi-vacation strategies in the literature demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves a better balance between throughput energy efficiency over a broad feasible load–reliability range under the evaluated vacation settings. Title: Expansion toward risk: China's urban growth reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures
Abstract: Rapid urban expansion is altering the distribution of environmental benefits and risks. As cities grow outward, newly developed areas may face elevated exposure to multiple environmental pressures, raising concerns about whether urbanization is inadvertently exposing population toward more adverse environmental conditions. To investigate this, we use population-weighted exposure model to quantify three key environmental exposures in China's newly built-up areas from 2000 to 2018: blue-green space exposure (BGE), PM2.5 exposure (PME), and heat stress exposure (HSE). By integrating SOM–K-means clustering and Bayesian Networks, we identify the evolution of typical environmental exposure combinations and examine their conditional dependencies. Results show that, from 2010 to 2018, BGE slightly improves, PME shows greater balance but persistent risks, while HSE intensified significantly. Clustering analysis identifies three distinct environmental exposure types: Ecological Deficiency (ED), High Environmental Cost (HEC), and Eco-Advantaged under Heat (EAH). In 2010, ED is the most prevalent type (1133 counties; 55.5%), followed by HEC (792 counties; 38.8%) and EAH (115 counties; 5.6%). By 2018, EAH increases to 386 counties (18.4%), while ED and HEC decline to 1052 (50.1%) and 664 (31.6%) counties, respectively. Notably, 466 ED counties transition to HEC, making ED-to-HEC the largest single transition. 146 counties transition from ED to EAH, indicating ecological improvement accompanied by greater heat stress. Together, these changes reveal a pattern of urban expansion toward risks. Bayesian Networks further reveal a reconfiguration in the conditional dependency structure of environmental exposures, moving from a relatively constrained dependency pattern toward a more interconnected configuration, with BGE becoming more centrally embedded in the network. This study contributes a novel integrative framework for understanding how urban expansion reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures and provides insights to inform risk-aware and equitable urban governance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: From the couch to the arena: Prefrontal cortex network dynamics of reward and loss processing during gameplay across internet gaming disorder symptom severity
Abstract: This study employed functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) to investigate how gameplay contexts differing in sense of agency are associated with prefrontal cortex (PFC) network dynamics during reward and loss processing, and how these dynamics relate to Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) symptom severity. Data-driven clustering identified three recurrent PFC connectivity states across active gameplay (higher-agency) and passive viewing (lower-agency) conditions. Furthermore, IGD symptom severity was associated with context-dependent changes in the occurrence probability and network topology of PFC network states during reward and loss processing, with differential patterns emerging across gameplay conditions differing in agency. Authors: Li D.; Tao X.; Shen J.; Wang Z.
Title: Memory-augmented dual-pathway model for temporal speech emotion recognition
Abstract: Speech emotion recognition requires not only identifying salient local emotional cues, but also incorporating broader temporal context to better interpret the overall emotion of an utterance. To address this issue, we propose Dynamic-MEM, a dual-pathway framework that jointly models short-term contextual information and long-term accumulated emotional context. Specifically, the short-term pathway focuses on capturing emotionally informative local patterns and sequential context from speech representations, while the long-term pathway employs a dynamically updated external memory to progressively retain historical emotional information across an utterance. In addition, a multi-scale classification module is introduced to integrate temporal features at different receptive fields and enhance emotion discrimination. By explicitly coordinating immediate emotional evidence with accumulated contextual information, the proposed framework provides a more effective way to model temporally informative cues than conventional sequential encoding alone. Title: How does empowering leadership shape employee service innovation behavior? The roles of employee adaptability and job crafting
Abstract: Based on conservation of resources theory, this paper examines how empowering leadership (EL) predicts service innovation behavior (SIB) through employee adaptability. Title: Intelligent molecular design of working fluid and multi-objective optimization of system for ocean thermal energy conversion
Abstract: To address the critical challenges of working fluid selection and low efficiency in ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems, a phased collaborative framework is proposed in this paper, integrating working fluid inverse design, intelligent variable screening, and multi-objective system optimization. First, computer-aided molecular design (CAMD) is employed to inversely identify high-efficiency, environmentally acceptable working fluids, balancing thermodynamic performance and basic safety considerations. Second, convergent cross mapping (CCM) combined with a knowledge graph is used to identify the key system variables that most significantly influence turbine power, reducing the dimensionality of the optimization problem from eight variables to four critical decision variables: evaporation temperature (Te), condensation temperature (Tc), superheat degree (Ts), and pump outlet pressure (Pp). Finally, the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) is applied to perform multi-objective optimization of exergy efficiency and levelized cost of electricity (LCOE). The results indicate that propane is the optimal working fluid, and the optimal solution achieves an exergy efficiency of 41.0% and LCOE of 0.146 $/(kWh). This framework effectively addresses the bottlenecks associated with low-temperature working fluids and high-dimensional optimization, offering a practical and efficient paradigm for the intelligent design and optimization of OTEC systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Prevalence and correlates of GenerativeAI chatbot use for mental health concerns in higher education students
Abstract: Background: Large language model chatbots are increasingly used for mental health help-seeking, with general-purpose systems like ChatGPT becoming popular among young adults despite concerns about accuracy and misinformation. High rates of mental distress in higher education attending emerging adults make them an important focal population to characterize and contextual the use of generativeAI models for mental health in. Methods: Data were collected from the 2024-2025 Healthy Minds Study at a large, public 4-year university. Of 12,000 students invited, 2071 participated; 896 bachelor-level students aged 18–24 years were randomly selected to complete a module with generativeAI questions, and 809 (90.2%) had complete data. Measures included chatbot use for mental health support, perceived AI trustworthiness, AI knowledge, mental health diagnosis, perceived need for help, past-year mental health treatment, barriers to care, other forms of informal help-seeking, and demographics. Weighted logistic regression models examined associations between these variables and chatbot use for mental health support. Results: 15.4% of students reported using generalized chatbots for mental health help-seeking. Significant correlates included greater perceived need for help, experiencing more barriers to clinical care use, higher perceived trust in AI for mental health information, lower AI knowledge, and identifying as Asian. Specific barriers of financial constraints, limited time, fear of clinician mistreatment due to identity and privacy concerns were linked to chatbot usage. Conclusions: GenerativeAI chatbots are a notable source of mental health support for college students, especially among those facing access barriers and who perceive AI as trustworthy. Future initiatives should educate young adults about chatbot capabilities and limitations and promote equitable mental health support. © 2026 The Author

Title: Teaching people to draw is teaching people to look
Abstract: Artists have long observed that drawing facilitates a way of looking at the world more attentively. Psychological research has sought to evaluate this claim by investigating the association between drawing abilities and training, and performance on visuospatial tasks. This body of research literature has shown that some visuospatial abilities are enhanced in those that have better drawing abilities, specifically those that require integration of stored perceptual and cognitive schemas, and flexible visual attention. Longitudinal research has further shown that learning how to draw leads to changes in the way that visuospatial tasks are approached, suggesting that drawing involves strategies designed to circumvent the limits of perception. Such insights are valuable in the context of an environment that often precludes looking slowly and closely, and suggest that teaching drawing may be an effective way of teaching people how to look. © 2026

Title: Neuro-swarm intelligence-based dynamic offloading framework for heterogeneous IoMT in edge–cloud healthcare environments
Abstract: The growing need for real-time, energy-efficient processing in intelligent healthcare systems highlights the limitations of traditional medical devices and distributed computing systems. Existing computational offloading methods are often costly or require substantial architectural changes and additional hardware, thereby limiting their scalability and practical deployment in large-scale healthcare environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid edge-cloud offloading framework specifically designed for the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT). The proposed framework dynamically adapts to heterogeneous computing environments and execution contexts, thereby improving system responsiveness and reducing energy consumption. Its key contributions include the use of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for predictive load balancing and task scheduling, the integration of Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) for intelligent path discovery and resource allocation, and the Least Connection Method (LCM) for minimizing latency by assigning tasks to resources with the fewest active connections. By combining these techniques, the proposed framework enables efficient offloading of computation-intensive tasks, supports real-time processing, and optimizes resource utilization across heterogeneous edge-cloud infrastructures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces latency, improves energy efficiency, and enhances overall system performance for time-sensitive IoMT applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Engaging consumers with varying budgets for battery electric vehicles in the post-subsidy era
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: China's BEV market must now engage the early majority to sustain broader penetration in the post-subsidy era. However, existing research inadequately explores how manufacturer-led strategies and psychological factors differentially shape the adoption decisions of this emerging consumer segment, particularly across varying budget levels. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated choice and latent variable (ICLV) model to jointly examine the effects of psychological determinants and multiple manufacturer-led strategies on BEV adoption. The analysis draws on 1200 stated-preference responses from prospective BEV buyers in Beijing and Shenzhen. Findings indicate that budget level significantly drives consumer heterogeneity in psychological drivers, while the relative effectiveness of manufacturer-led strategies remains consistent across groups: bundled insurance packages yield the largest marginal effects, followed by advanced intelligent driving services and lottery-based discounts, with price discounts being the least effective. Title: RealTalk: Real-time audio-driven face generation with 3D prior-guided identity alignment
Abstract: Person-generic audio-driven face generation remains a formidable challenge in multimedia and computer vision, primarily due to the trade-off between high-fidelity lip synchronization and real-time inference speed. Existing methods often struggle to preserve unique individual traits or suffer from high computational latency. To bridge this gap, we propose RealTalk, a novel generalized framework composed of an Audio-to-Expression Transformer and a high-fidelity Expression-to-Face Renderer. In the first stage, we introduce an improved facial prior mechanism that incorporates both 3D facial shape and historical expression data. By leveraging cross-modal attention, our model effectively captures intra-personal motion variations, ensuring precise alignment between lip movements and audio signals. In the second stage, we design a lightweight Facial Identity Alignment (FIA) module equipped with a learnable facial mask. This module achieves high-quality texture generation and identity preservation using a single reference image, bypassing the computational bottleneck of complex feature warping used in prior arts. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that RealTalkoutperforms state-of-the-art methods in both lip-sync accuracy and visual quality while maintaining real-time efficiency (e.g., 30 FPS on a V100 GPU), making it highly suitable for practical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Investigation of tyre pyrolysis enhanced by inorganic additives
Abstract: The high sulphur content of end-of-life tyres restricts the use of pyrolysis products. In-situ desulphurisation using waste-derived additives is a promising solution. However, comparing additives across different studies is unreliable due to varying experimental setups and conditions. In this work, we established a systematic screening framework for fifteen distinct materials under identical reactor configuration, heating rate, and operational conditions. We evaluated dolomite, eggshell, alginite, mussel shell, zeolite, bone meal, deposited ash, fly ash, red mud, and their calcined counterparts. Experiments were carried out in the same batch reactor at 500 °C and 900 °C using a 1:1 tyre-to-additive mass ratio. At 500 °C, calcined Ca- and Mg-rich additives reduced the sulphur content of the pyrolysis oil from 1.3 to 0.6 wt%. However, this caused a product trade-off, as the oil yield decreased from 47.8 to 35.0 wt%. Bone meal increased the oil yield to 69.6 wt% but did not capture sulphur. At 900 °C, the thermal cracking intensified and shifted the sulphur into the gas phase. Calcined zeolite produced up to 40.0 wt% gas. Higher temperatures diminished the effect of liquid-phase desulphurisation, keeping oil sulphur levels between 0.9 and 1.3 wt%. Deposited ash retained the most sulphur in the solid phase (77.9 wt% at 500 °C) but increased the char ash content to 72.3 wt%. These results quantify the necessary trade-offs between oil quality, product yields, and multi-phase sulphur distribution. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhou M.; Gao X.; Wu X.; Zhang N.; Zhao Z.; Zhang H.; Liu Q.
Title: Navigating the unspoken: A qualitative study of how clinical nurse educators transmit tacit knowledge to nursing students
Abstract: Background: In nursing education, a significant body of knowledge essential for professional practice is tacit—difficult to articulate, yet crucial for clinical judgment, ethical comportment, and professional identity formation. Understanding how clinical nurse educators perceive and transmit this tacit knowledge is critical for optimizing student preparation. Objective: This study aimed to explore the experiences of clinical nurse educators in identifying, conveying, and cultivating tacit knowledge among nursing students. Design: A descriptive qualitative study. Methods: The study involved in-depth, semi-structured interviews with 20 clinical nurse educators who were purposively sampled from 15 Chinese provinces and possessed ≥5 years of teaching experience. Data were collected from July to October 2025 and analyzed using thematic analysis, from which the key themes and subthemes were derived. Results: Four themes and 12 subthemes were extracted. The themes were The nature and expression of tacit knowledge in clinical nursing education, Strategies for transmitting tacit knowledge, Challenges in tacit knowledge transmission, Organizational support and cultural nurturing. Conclusions: Tacit knowledge is fundamental, not optional, to nursing practice. Its effective transmission hinges on deliberate pedagogy, supportive structures, and a reflective mentoring culture. These findings provide a foundation for developing clinical education frameworks and faculty policies dedicated to cultivating competent, compassionate, and ethically aware nurses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Liu Z.; Li B.; Yan Y.; Han C.; Guo T.; Nie X.
Title: IBCL: Information Bottleneck Contrastive Learning with minimum sufficient augmentation and generalized representations
Abstract: Contrastive Learning (CL) has established itself as a dominant paradigm in self-supervised representation learning. However, its efficacy can be limited by discriminative information overfitting, where models learn overly specialized features for instance discrimination while insufficiently preserving semantic and structural information needed for downstream generalization. In this work, we re-examine CL through the lens of the Information Bottleneck (IB) principle and propose Information Bottleneck Contrastive Learning (IBCL), an IB-inspired framework that characterizes contrastive representation learning as a compression–preservation trade-off. Specifically, IBCL introduces two conceptual criteria: minimum sufficient augmentation, which encourages compact contrastive views by reducing redundant input information, and information-generalized representations, which aim to preserve useful semantic and structural information beyond pretext discrimination. Guided by this perspective, we propose Masked Reconstruction Contrastive Learning (MRCL), a plug-and-play instantiation of IBCL for classical contrastive learning frameworks. MRCL uses random patch masking as a controllable view-level compression mechanism and incorporates a lightweight reconstruction objective as an auxiliary semantic-structural regularizer to mitigate excessive information loss caused by masking. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MRCL consistently improves conventional CL baselines across ImageNet classification, ADE20K semantic segmentation, and COCO detection/instance segmentation. Notably, MRCL shows favorable scalability on large Vision Transformers and achieves competitive transfer performance on dense prediction benchmarks. These results suggest that the proposed compression–preservation design provides a practical and effective way to improve the generalization ability of contrastive representations. © 2026

Authors: Jiang L.; Liu Y.; Zhao H.
Title: Spatial trajectories and land-use potential of China's utility-scale photovoltaic expansion toward 2035
Abstract: China aims to reach 3600 GW of combined wind and solar capacity by 2035, requiring substantial expansion of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) deployment. Quantifying the geospatial footprint of this expansion is essential for sustainable land-use planning and ecological protection. This study develops a nationwide assessment framework that integrates multi-source remote sensing observations, Random Forest (RF) suitability modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for model interpretation, and scenario-based spatial allocation. Historical PV data from 2000 to 2025 show that China's utility-scale PV farms expanded to 13,800 km2, with growth concentrated in northwestern mega-bases and emerging decentralized installations in central-eastern regions, indicating a dual-track spatial trajectory. Scenario projections suggest that Scenario B (NDC Update-Aligned Pathway) requires an additional 21,420 km2, whereas Scenario C (Wind-Slowdown Compensation) increases land demand moderately to 24,405 km2. Scenario A (Business as Usual) could require up to 63,990 km2 and would disproportionately affect croplands and forests. However, China retains more than 206,000 km2 of high-potential land, indicating that ecological conflicts are driven mainly by spatial mismatch rather than absolute land scarcity. These findings underscore the need for integrated spatial governance, optimized ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission, and distributed PV deployment. By linking observed spatial trajectories, interpretable suitability modeling, and capacity-to-land translation, this study provides a transferable framework for assessing the land-use potential of utility-scale PV expansion toward 2035. © 2026

Authors: Wang M.; He J.
Title: An accelerated recursive decomposition algorithm for dynamic seismic reliability analysis of large-scale networks with complex component dependencies
Abstract: Accurate dynamic seismic reliability assessment of lifeline networks is critical for seismic design optimization and post-earthquake emergency response, however it faces challenges from complex internal network dependencies and computational inefficiency for large-scale networks. To calculate the dynamic seismic reliability of large-scale network systems with component dependencies, this paper proposes an accelerated recursive decomposition algorithm (RDA). Through a comparative analysis, a two-level nested joint cumulative distribution function (CDF) is developed and incorporated into the RDA to accurately capture complex dependencies while avoiding the curse of dimensionality. This joint distribution model is constructed by first reducing the dimensionality of high-dimensional variables via grouping based on k -medoids clustering, and then coupling the grouped variables using multiple Gumbel copulas. Based on the joint CDF (jCDF), this paper introduces an improved Dijkstra’s algorithm for the most reliable path search in the RDA to accelerate convergence of system reliability bounds. Moreover, a subgraph decomposition strategy based on real-time updated importance rankings is developed to identify fewer disjoint shortest paths and cuts while satisfying the requirement on system reliability bounds, thereby enabling rapid convergence of reliability bounds. The accuracy, efficiency, and applicability of the proposed accelerated RDA are demonstrated through two numerical examples. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Toward a greater understanding of profound and complex experiences during engagement with art
Abstract: This review focuses on two contemporary trends in the psychology of art. Title: Tracing locations from pixels: A survey of worldwide image geo-localization
Abstract: Worldwide image geo-localization (WIGL) estimates the geographic coordinates of a photograph from its visual content, without metadata on the query image and without a known search area. This capability supports practical applications, including cybercrime source tracing, disaster response, and autonomous navigation. In this manuscript, a comprehensive review of WIGL is presented, in which current methods are systematically organized into four paradigms: classification-based, retrieval-based, generation-based, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). For each paradigm, representative approaches and core design principles are examined, with their strengths and limitations compared. Training, testing, and fine-tuning datasets are also reviewed in depth. A spatial distribution analysis of these datasets reveals notable coverage biases in existing benchmarks. Standard evaluation metrics are consolidated, and the reported results on six test sets are aggregated, providing a common basis for comparison across methods. The comparative analysis of reported results indicates that RAG approaches currently achieve the highest accuracy on major benchmarks, though this advantage is partly confounded by larger backbone models and training data while generation-based approaches offer a promising alternative for zero-shot location inference. Finally, several under-explored research challenges that are rarely discussed in prior surveys are identified and outlined. These include the difficulty of disambiguating visually similar images captured at distant locations, as well as other open problems to guide future work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Evaluating SHAP feature selection guided by a biomechanical prior for offline knee angle estimation from sEMG
Abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) supports continuous knee-angle estimation, but predictive feature importance can diverge from expected patterns of muscle activity. This study evaluated a literature-informed biomechanical prior as a guide for feature selection and quantified its relation to predictive performance and agreement between model attribution and the prior. The proposed offline framework combines window-level sEMG descriptors with phase-stratified Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). A muscle-level Bio-Consistency Score (BCS) quantifies prior–attribution agreement, whereas a feature-level Phase-Profile Concordance (PPC) term guides selection alongside global importance and redundancy. Trajectory-cycle bins were assigned retrospectively from synchronised knee-angle records. Evaluation used 15 participants in an outer leave-one-subject-out design, with feature selection confined to an inner training–validation split. Cross-dataset analyses used a common four-channel, 48-feature candidate space and six target participants. The prior-guided selector retained 10.20 of 132 features on average, with a mean root mean squared error of 14.15∘, compared with 13.14∘ for the complete feature set. Selected subsets had a mean pairwise Jaccard similarity of 0.162. Prior guidance produced a less negative mean BCS, but no method-by-fold permutation test provided evidence of a statistically significant departure from the muscle-label reference. In cross-dataset analyses, none of the multiplicity-adjusted paired comparisons was statistically significant for prior-guided selection versus matched controls, warm-start adaptation versus from-scratch fitting, or teacher-target blending versus observed-target training. The results quantify the trade-off among input dimensionality, attribution concordance, and predictive accuracy under the evaluated protocol. Title: Identifying and Mitigating Legal and Contractual Risks in BIM-Enabled Construction Projects: A Conceptual Framework
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Building information modeling (BIM) is accelerating across Saudi Arabia's construction sector in support of Vision 2030, yet its legal and contractual integration lags behind technical adoption. This study investigates the legal and contractual risks associated with BIM-enabled project delivery and proposes a conceptual framework to guide risk mitigation in the Saudi context. A total of 21 BIM-related legal risk factors were identified from a comprehensive literature review and refined through a pilot study. An online questionnaire survey was administered to construction practitioners (consultants and contractors), yielding 87 valid responses for analysis. Principal component analysis revealed two latent dimensions: legal and regulatory ambiguities and BIM model management and technical risks. Mean-rank analysis identified the lack of coordination and control over the BIM model, lack of clarity regarding BIM standards and processes in the contract, and unclear rights and responsibilities related to BIM were ranked as the top risk factors. Synthesizing the empirical findings with mitigation strategies identified through an extensive literature review, the study developed a seven-pillar conceptual framework for risk mitigation: (1) standardization and legal infrastructure; (2) contractual clarity and enforceability; (3) roles, responsibilities, and liability; (4) ownership and intellectual property; (5) confidentiality and security; (6) data integrity and interoperability; and (7) collaboration and dispute resolution. The findings extend the limited scholarship on BIM's legal and contractual risks in Saudi Arabia and offer context-aware guidance for policymakers and practitioners to embed BIM-specific provisions aimed at mitigating dispute propensity in BIM-enabled construction projects.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Surrogate-free deep reinforcement learning for multiphysics geometric optimization of PEM water electrolyzers
Abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are inherently constrained by complex multiphysics trade-offs among electrochemical kinetics, two-phase mass transport, and thermal management. The geometric configuration of internal components plays a pivotal role in regulating these coupled processes, yet systematic optimization remains challenging due to the highly nonlinear design space and the substantial computational cost associated with three-dimensional multiphysics simulations. In this study, a surrogate-free optimization framework is developed by directly coupling a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning agent with a high-fidelity finite element multiphysics solver. A designed multi-objective reward function is employed to simultaneously enhance current density while constraining pressure drop and peak temperature. This direct interaction enables adaptive exploration of the design space without relying on intermediate approximations. The optimization results demonstrate that the identified configuration improves the average current density from 19,837 A/m2 to 20,354 A/m2 (a 2.61% increase), while promoting a more uniform pressure distribution and maintaining thermal conditions within acceptable operational limits. Furthermore, the results provide insights into the underlying trade-offs among transport processes, highlighting the role of geometric parameters in balancing electrochemical performance and system efficiency. This work demonstrates the feasibility and potential of integrating reinforcement learning with high-fidelity multiphysics simulations for the geometric optimization of PEM water electrolyzers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Too much of a good thing? The curvilinear effects of job clarity on career satisfaction and creativity among hospitality employees
Abstract: This study challenges the assumption that greater job clarity always benefits service employees. Drawing on self-determination theory and the Too-Much-of-a-Good-Thing framework, we test a moderated curvilinear mediation model linking job clarity, career satisfaction, and creativity, with career calling as a boundary condition. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 164 supervisor–employee dyads in Chinese hotels, results reveal inverted U-shaped relationships between job clarity and both career satisfaction and supervisor-rated creativity. Career satisfaction mediates this curvilinear effect. Title: Learning to coordinate: A knowledge-distilled agent for adaptive multi-agent code generation
Abstract: Code generation powered by large language models (LLMs) faces substantial challenges due to the variability of task difficulty, ranging from simple string-manipulation tasks to complex algorithmic implementations. Current approaches, including many multi-agent frameworks, typically employ uniform processing strategies across all tasks. This leads to systematic resource misallocation: over-processing simple tasks while providing insufficient reasoning and verification support for complex ones. To address this inefficiency, we propose an adaptive multi-agent framework driven by a knowledge-distilled Coordination Agent. By distilling posterior behavioral signals from a high-capacity teacher model into a specialized dataset, Code-PBD, our lightweight student agent learns to assess task difficulty and route tasks to appropriate execution workflows. Based on the predicted difficulty, the framework dynamically orchestrates specialized agents into three differentiated workflows: streamlined, standard, and enhanced; the enhanced workflow incorporates an Abductive Chain-of-Thought (D-CoT) mechanism for deep logical diagnosis. Empirical evaluations on HumanEval and MBPP demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 73.8 % and 77.3 % Pass@1, respectively. Compared with the Fixed-Enhanced baseline, the proposed approach reduces token consumption by 67.2 % and 70.0 % on HumanEval and MBPP, respectively, while achieving Pass@1 scores that are 2.4 and 3.4 percentage points lower. On HumanEval, the method further improves Pass@1 by 16.6 percentage points over the Fixed-Standard baseline with only a small increase in API calls, demonstrating a more favorable quality–cost trade-off. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Lu J.; Guo J.; Xiao J.
Title: An intelligent spectrum-aware trajectory data reduction approach for maritime decision support systems
Abstract: High-quality Automatic Identification System (AIS) data is the cornerstone of modern Maritime Expert Systems and Intelligent Decision Support Systems (IDSS). However, the exponential growth of AIS data challenges the real-time situational awareness and storage capabilities of these systems. Conventional compression strategies face a dichotomy: offline algorithms ensure fidelity but suffer latency, while online methods support streaming but often exhibit “geometric blindness,” neglecting kinematic variations like speed changes along linear paths. This study proposes a novel online method, Frequency-Aware Improved Open Window (FA-IOPW). FA-IOPW uses localized spectral information within an evolving Opening Window to adapt the PED–TED weighting during online compression. To support the evaluation, we developed a visualization platform for trajectory query, compression, comparison, and adaptive-weight display. The platform was tested with historical AIS records and controlled application-level replay; live satellite AIS feeds, production Vessel Traffic Service environments, and shipborne hardware were not included in the present validation. Results demonstrate that FA-IOPW achieves a Pareto-optimal trade-off between compression ratio and reconstruction accuracy. Under high-compression regimes, it significantly reduces position and speed errors compared to mainstream methods. Furthermore, we integrated an AI agent module into the platform, lowering the usage threshold for regular users. As a robust online method, FA-IOPW offers a high-fidelity solution for real-time maritime monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Guo Y.
Title: Scaffold-shift uncertainty calibration in molecular activity prediction: A multi-target benchmark of coverage, efficiency, and risk-aware selection
Abstract: Uncertainty estimates are increasingly used to prioritize molecules, yet their reliability under chemical scaffold shift is poorly characterized. We benchmarked prediction intervals and downstream selection policies across six human protein targets using 20,327 target-specific ChEMBL 37 compound records (19,972 globally unique ChEMBL molecule identifiers) and 7731 target-specific Bemis–Murcko scaffold instances, two model classes, and 20 scaffold-disjoint train/calibration/test partitions per target. We compared raw random-forest ensemble intervals, standard split conformal intervals, similarity-normalized conformal intervals, and similarity-binned local conformal intervals. Raw nominal 90% ensemble intervals achieved only 9.5%–11.4% molecule-weighted coverage. Conformal methods generally restored average coverage toward 90%, but results depended on target, partition, model, and whether molecules or scaffolds received equal weight. Conditional coverage averaged 82.3% in the least training-similar quartile and 78.7% in the highest-activity quartile. Similarity-adaptive methods did not uniformly improve the coverage–width trade-off. Across 240 matched target–partition–model comparisons, lower-confidence-bound selection reduced mean observed activity by 0.107 pActivity units, reduced top-decile hit rate by 0.063, and increased false optimism by 0.012, while selecting 2.16 additional scaffolds on average. Marginal calibration, conditional reliability, and decision utility are therefore distinct properties. Conformal calibration can repair severe interval undercoverage, but it does not automatically provide reliable extrapolation or a superior molecular-ranking policy. © 2026 The Authors
