Title: Welfare analysis of electricity distribution: The Dignity Tariff in Bolivia
Abstract: We conduct an analysis of the demand functions associated with electricity distribution in Bolivia, focusing on the implications of price fluctuations on consumer welfare. This analysis requires the estimation of demand functions, which we achieve through the application of panel data with fixed effects and the use of instrumental variables. Additionally, we apply propensity score matching (PSM) to compare electricity expenditures between beneficiary and comparable non-beneficiary households, providing an independent welfare estimate grounded in observed household behaviour rather than structural demand parameters alone. In 2006, the Bolivian government introduced the Dignity Tariff, aimed at regulating electricity distribution costs for both urban and rural households. This tariff offers a 25% reduction in electricity prices for households that consume up to 70 kWh per month. Our key findings indicate that the Dignity Tariff effectively acts as a subsidy for electricity consumption. Estimates derived from demand functions suggest an average monthly welfare gain ranging from Bs 17.98 to Bs 21.12 (USD 2.58 to USD 3.03), while propensity score matching yields an average monthly saving of approximately Bs 47 (USD 6.75) for beneficiary households, providing significant financial relief to economically vulnerable populations. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Hong Z.; Hou Y.
Title: A BO-based method for parameter tuning in voltage controlled DERs to improve flexibility area at TSO-DSO interface
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of aggregated flexible resources in active distribution systems (ADSs) calls for accurate estimation of the flexibility area (FA) at the transmission system operator-distribution system operator (TSO-DSO) interface to improve operational coordination. Meanwhile, voltage control plays a critical role in maintaining both economic and secure grid operation. However, the relationship between voltage control parameters and the FA metric is highly nonlinear and analytically intractable, as inverter droop coefficients and other control parameters interact with network constraints and distributed energy resource (DER) operating conditions in a coupled manner. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Bayesian optimization (BO)-based framework that systematically tunes voltage support parameters to maximize the FA potential. The main contributions are threefold: (1) a cross-layer optimization paradigm that links inverter-level droop control with system-level FA characteristics, revealing how voltage control curves shape interface power flow dynamics; (2) a reformulated FA estimation process in which the Interval-Constrained Power Flow (ICPF) model, embedded with droop-control operations, is cast as a Bayesian black-box problem solved efficiently via Gaussian process surrogates with a tile-coding kernel; and (3) a composite performance index, namely the Secure Area-Cost Flexibility (SeCoF), which jointly quantifies the trade-off between flexibility enhancement and operational cost. Case studies on modified IEEE 13-bus and IEEE 37-bus distribution systems demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, and scalability of the proposed method in improving both technical flexibility and economic performance under realistic operational constraints. © 2026 The Authors

Title: An interpretable multi-task TabNet framework for predicting multidimensional railway accident severity
Abstract: Accurately predicting the multidimensional severity of railway accidents is critical for risk assessment and safety management. Existing studies usually treat fatalities, injuries, and property damage as independent prediction tasks, failing to capture the dependence among these correlated outcomes caused by the same accident. Additionally, railway accident data are heterogeneous tabular data with severe class imbalance, making it difficult to balance prediction accuracy, rare-event learning, and model interpretability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes an interpretable multi-task learning framework for jointly predicting three severity dimensions using the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) rail equipment accident database. The framework consists of a joint-label-stratified Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) augmentation strategy for supplementing underrepresented outcome patterns, a Multi-Task TabNet for shared representation learning, and a mask-aware gradient projection (MAGP) strategy to alleviate task-gradient conflicts in the feature-routing process. Model interpretability is achieved by analyzing sequential feature masks combined with SHAP local attributions, which provide complementary evidence from encoder-level feature routing and task-specific prediction attribution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive overall performance and improves the recall-oriented detection of sparse fatality cases compared with several single-task and multi-task baselines. However, the class-wise evaluation also indicates that minority fatality prediction remains challenging, due to the extreme imbalance of fatal accidents. The interpretable results provide explanatory evidence consistent with engineering knowledge, supporting practical railway risk identification and safety decision-making as a screening-oriented decision-support tool. Title: From clinician to coach: Immediate learning and experiences of mental health nurses following a coaching for clinical nurses (C4CN) workshop
Abstract: Background: Coaching is increasingly used to strengthen nursing leadership and reflective practice, yet limited evidence describes how workplace coaches are prepared or how coaching education supports capability and role clarity in healthcare environments. Aim: To explore mental health nurses' experiences of a Coaching for Clinical Nurses (C4CN) workshop and examine immediate learning in developing workplace coaching capability and emerging coach role. Design: Exploratory qualitative analysis of a preparatory workshop within a constructivist embedded case study. Methods: The two-day workshop was delivered to 13 clinical leaders working in a single adult inpatient mental health unit in Queensland, Australia, in preparation for a six-month workplace coaching intervention. Workshop material included written reflections and group discussions, anonymous real-time responses and facilitator reflective session notes. Inductive reflexive thematic analysis was used to examine immediate learning and understandings of workplace coaching. Results: Four themes captured participants' learning: personal and leadership commitment to coaching; integration of coaching into daily routines; practical application of coaching; and self-development and confidence building. Subthemes reflected an emerging coaching mindset, coaching in the moment, structured coaching processes, developing coach identity and role clarity, and self-reflection and self-management. Participants described clearer coaching purpose and boundaries and growing confidence in coaching conversations. Experiential practice, peer dialogue and structured frameworks supported movement from technique towards a developmental leadership approach. Implications for nurse education: Workplace coach preparation should combine experiential skills development, reflective learning, role-boundary clarification and opportunities to practise coaching. Continuing development and organisational support are important for translation into practice. Conclusions: The C4CN workshop showed how experienced mental health nurses began developing workplace coaching capability and making sense of their coach role alongside other nursing and leadership responsibilities. The findings support workplace coach preparation as an experiential, reflective developmental process and provide a foundation for subsequent examination within the broader case study. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The increasing sensory richness of digitally-mediated experience
Abstract: Digital interfaces were once sensorially sparse. Contemporary technologies have changed this dramatically, expanding the sensory richness of digital interfaces across visual, auditory, haptic, olfactory, and even gustatory modalities, collectively narrowing the perceptual gap between digital and physical worlds. We present findings from a growing, multidisciplinary body of evidence examining how these evolving sensory affordances shape individuals' perceptions, judgments, and behaviors. Title: Forecast-guided multi-task scheduling for autonomous electric ride-hailing fleets under charging and maintenance constraints
Abstract: Autonomous electric ride-hailing fleets require real-time coordination among passenger dispatching, proactive repositioning, charging, and maintenance. This paper proposes a forecast-guided rolling framework that combines an attention-based spatial-temporal graph convolutional network (ASTGCN) with Enhanced Kuhn-Munkres (EKM) multi-task assignment. ASTGCN predicts grid-level demand, while a virtual-node (VN) mechanism converts forecasted regional shortages into bounded point-level relocation tasks at feasible points of interest (POIs). Passenger orders, VN-based repositioning, charging, and maintenance are then coordinated in a common vehicle-task graph after infeasible vehicle-task pairs are filtered according to battery, health, time-window, charging-capacity, and maintenance-capacity constraints. A residual-based search mechanism reduces the computational burden introduced by graph expansion. Experiments using real-world ride-hailing data show that the proposed framework achieves a system matching rate of 79.76%, which is 5.52 percentage points higher than the classical Kuhn-Munkres matching baseline. It reduces average passenger waiting time to 6.68 min, corresponding to a 14.41% reduction compared with the non-predictive scheduling variant. It also improves spatial supply-demand balance, reducing the normalized demand-supply difference to 0.128, and completes each rolling scheduling decision within 1.42 s on average. The incremental ablation study further shows that virtual-node-based forecast conversion mainly improves service quality and spatial balance, while the residual-based search mechanism reduces computation time from 22.45 s to 1.42 s without observed degradation. These results indicate that the main value of the proposed framework lies in converting demand forecasts into executable multi-task assignments for real-time autonomous electric fleet operation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: EFL teachers’expectation and recommendation: Intercultural curriculum implementation
Abstract: This study examines EFL teachers' expectations and recommendations for the intercultural dimension of Emancipated Curriculum, understood as the curriculum's emphasis on linking English language learning with local culture, global communication, respect for diversity, student agency, differentiated learning, and project-based tasks. Responding to concerns about uneven curriculum enactment across Indonesian schools, the study used a convergent mixed-methods design. An online questionnaire generated 172 valid responses from secondary English teachers in 11 provinces, while the regional focus was placed on East Java and West Nusa Tenggara because these two provinces contributed the largest survey clusters and all focus group discussion data. FGDs involved 27 teachers in East Java and 32 teachers in West Nusa Tenggara. Open-ended questionnaire responses and FGD transcripts were coded into meaning units, producing 308 coded items: 178 expectations and 130 recommendations. The findings show that teachers generally supported the reform and associated it with improved educational quality, better student futures, critical thinking, creativity, independence, and more contextual learning. However, their support was conditional on clearer operational guidance, practical and sustained teacher training, improved infrastructure, reduced administrative burden, curriculum evaluation, and stronger stakeholder collaboration. Regional and school-type comparisons indicated similar priorities across contexts, but West Nusa Tenggara teachers more often emphasized detailed training and infrastructure support, while East Java teachers more often highlighted administrative alignment and school-level coordination. The study contributes to curriculum implementation research by showing that teachers' expectations and recommendations provide diagnostic evidence for refining reform. Successful enactment requires not only policy dissemination but also locally responsive professional development, equitable resources, and feedback mechanisms that position teachers as central agents in intercultural EFL curriculum implementation. Title: Exploring Technology Probe applications in software engineering practice
Abstract: Background: The development of software systems relies on user feedback, which can be captured with Validation Sessions (VS); however, VS are often conducted in an ad hoc manner. Technology Probe (TP) offers a participatory design method for capturing user perception; however, its application in software engineering lacks structure. Aim: This study consolidates evidence on TP applications in software engineering and identifies practices that support the systematic use of TP. Methods: A Literature Study, inspired by Rapid Reviews, was conducted in Scopus using backward and forward snowballing, screening 530 studies and selecting 53 primary works across the trials that support the results. Thematic analysis was employed to extract motivations, outcomes, and challenges associated with the use of TP in software engineering. Results: Through thematic analysis and open coding, 11 evidence-based characteristics were identified describing the use of TP in software engineering. These characteristics formed the foundation of an evidence-based checklist developed to assess and guide the development of TP techniques. Conclusion: It was found that TP has been applied across a variety of domains, with diverse techniques being crafted. Therefore, the checklist developed in this research aims to assist future researchers in crafting their techniques and supporting their decisions. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Milking consumers' willingness to pay for greener dairy: Udderly important or a moo-t point?
Abstract: In an effort to combat their environmental footprint, leading associations in the United States dairy industry have committed to implementing new technology in manure management and achieving Net Zero production by 2050. These pledges can increase the cost of producing milk, but it is unclear if these production changes can garner price premiums from consumers. This study uses a choice experiment to analyze consumers' preferences for a gallon of milk described by four attributes: organic production, GHG emissions reduction, nutrient runoff reduction, and price. An online survey was administered across four U.S. regions to individuals who regularly purchase milk from grocery stores. We find evidence of heterogeneity in preferences and conduct several market segment analyses. A consumer segment characterized by higher socioeconomic status and environmental attitudes shows substantially higher WTP for organic production and GHG reductions than a lower-socioeconomic-status, less environmentally engaged segment, which actually exhibits disutility from organic production. A secondary analysis suggests that education is the main determinant of increased WTP for organic production, while environmental attitudes likely drive WTP associated with GHG reductions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Accounting for the risk of restoration failure in ecosystem service valuation
Abstract: While ecosystem recovery is widely recognized to vary, valuations of ecosystem services often assume guaranteed outcomes. We examine whether omitting information on restoration failure risk causes bias in the utility estimates of ecosystem services. Further, we examine how two personal attitudes (connectedness to nature and place attachment) influence risk perception. In comparison to previous studies, we integrate both risk (known outcomes and their probabilities of ecosystem service provision following grassland restoration) and uncertainty (unknown outcomes and probabilities) within a single framework. We find that omitting information on risk leads to overestimation of the utility derived from ecosystem services. Controlling for subjective uncertainty and risk aversion using a hybrid choice model, we find no influence of connectedness to nature on risk perception, whereas the negative effect of high restoration failure risk on utility becomes weaker when place attachment is high. Both latent attitudes decrease the utility of uncertainty, i.e., of the opt-out alternative no restoration. Given the substantial utility implications of restoration failure risk, the EU should complement Member State-level monitoring under the Nature Restoration Regulation with project-level monitoring, open data sharing, and transparent reporting of restoration outcomes to the public. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Mittal S.; Jha K.N.
Title: Emotional Factors in Quality Negligence: A Study of Residential Real Estate Construction Professionals
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Quality negligence in the construction industry, a significant originator of legal crises, is predominantly attributed to technical and procedural failures. However, the pivotal role of construction professionals' emotions as a precipitating factor remains a critically unexamined research area. This study addresses this gap by investigating the influence of specific emotions on quality negligence and its subsequent escalation into legal crises for construction firms. The research employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. Initially, a comprehensive literature review and unstructured interviews with industry experts identified seven prominent emotions (anxiety, guilt, pride, shame, elevation, injustice, and gratitude). Subsequently, a quantitative phase involved distributing a self-administered questionnaire to 162 Indian construction professionals within the Indian residential construction sector to assess their emotional states and quality negligence levels. Data analysis using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) indicated a statistically significant positive relationship between quality negligence and five emotions. The effects, in descending order of magnitude, were elevation (β=0.406, p<0.001), shame (β=0.405, p<0.001), gratitude (β=0.321, p<0.001), pride (β=0.261, p=0.009), and anxiety (β=0.179, p=0.047). In the final phase, consultations and brainstorming sessions with industry experts were used to identify the resulting legal crises and to establish a novel emotion-quality negligence-crises framework. This framework models the pathway from emotional antecedent to quality negligence and its culmination in a legal crisis. The study provides a critical diagnostic tool for practitioners in the real estate sector to mitigate risk and offers a new theoretical model for academics analyzing this psycho-legal connection.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: A broad learning model with dual-path feature encoding for robust and expedient incremental fault diagnosis
Abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) models that rely on one-shot learning often struggle in dynamic mechanical systems because they exhibit limited knowledge stability and high computational cost under incremental learning (IL). Title: A physics-cognitive proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing collaborative framework for offshore wind farms under extreme met-ocean conditions
Abstract: Reliable offshore wind operation requires maintenance decisions that account for multi-source uncertainty including stochastic degradation, environmental shocks, and incomplete condition information. Extreme met-ocean conditions also restrict maintenance access, coupling uncertainty in asset health with fragmented vessel operating windows and high operation and maintenance costs. To address these uncertain issues, this study proposes a proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing strategy. A marginal-benefit-driven opportunistic maintenance strategy is introduced to exploit short and variable weather windows. A continuous weather filtering module proactively schedules critical tasks before adverse conditions, integrated with a bi-level mixed-integer non-linear programming model, which is solved by a bi-stage collaborative solution algorithm to co-optimize multi-vessel routing and maintenance bundling. Simulations on a 78-turbine offshore wind farm over a 90-day period show that the proposed strategy reduces total O&M costs by 96.4%, 46.4%, 19.4% and 46.2% compared to corrective, condition-based, non-opportunistic baselines and sequential scheduling and routing strategy, respectively. Title: Firefighter turnout gear limits the ability to reach down for an object without flexing the spine
Abstract: The restrictive nature of firefighter turnout gear may influence firefighter's ability to lift low-lying objects using strategies aimed at mitigating low back disorder risk. This study examined the influence of each component of firefighter turnout gear on how far they could reach down for an object with their spine physically restricted from forward flexion. Wearing any component of fire gear restricted reach depth ( p < 0.001). The greatest amount of restriction, compared to wearing station fatigues, occurred when firefighters wore full gear with boots (12 cm, 95% confidence interval = [10, 14]). There was no statistical difference in restriction when firefighters wore only fire pants versus wearing only fire jacket and oxygen tank. Wearing boots only had a significant impact when firefighters wore full gear (average difference = 2 cm, 95% confidence interval = [1, 3], p < 0.001). Title: Emotion-aware retailing: Using biometrics to decode consumer experience in physical–digital environments
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The physical retail space, when blended with digital touchpoints, has created a multi-sensory consumer experience that cannot be fully measured in real time using legacy survey-based approaches. The work examines the opportunities offered by biometric technologies, such as electrodermal activity (EDA), facial action coding, eye-tracking, and heart-rate variability (HRV), to decode shoppers' affective experiences in a phygital retail space. The study is based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and affective computing theory, and has a mixed-methods experimental design that involved 312 study participants, who were offered four types of retail formats: department store, grocery hypermarket, experiential flagship store, and click-and-collect hub. All participants were given biometric sensors to wear and were monitored across three consecutive stages: browsing, assessment, and purchase decision. Behavioral and transactional data were used in real time and fused with multimodal biometric responses to create emotion maps for spatial retail areas. The findings show statistically significant positive relationships among high EDA arousal, positive facial affect, and conversion rates at digital interface points. Quantitatively, an optimal engagement window was identified at moderate stimulation levels (EDA = 2.10 μS), yielding a peak conversion rate of 41.2%. In contrast, HRV suppression was associated with decision paralysis at higher stimulation levels. Demographic cohorts and segmentation analysis showed that younger consumers reacted with much more emotion to augmented reality features and individualized digital signs. Eye-tracking and facial action coding confirmed that younger shoppers (<35) sustained an 8.42-s fixation duration with high positive affect (0.74) in flagship zones, whereas older cohorts (≥35) exhibited severe sensory avoidance. The article contributes to the theoretical understanding of emotion-behavior relationships in the store setting and offers practical guidance for store designers, digital experience architects, and consumer psychologists. Embargoes on biometric retail analytics that protect privacy are also discussed. The updated structural framework successfully bridges the gap between environmental retail inputs and transactional behavioral choices through intermediate biometric telemetry. Phygital spaces with heavy digital footprints create pronounced shifts in physiological processing, where elevated electrodermal activity predicts transaction completion up to an threshold point, beyond which severe heart-rate variability suppression signals choice paralysis. © 2026

Authors: Liu Q.; Li M.; Fan Y.; Qiao J.; Li B.
Title: Progressive resource allocation outperforms uniform strategies in enhancing urban vegetation growth offset: Evidence from DSTFormer-SHAP modeling across China's 19 urban agglomerations
Abstract: Urbanization degrades vegetation through direct land conversion while simultaneously stimulating residual vegetation growth through indirect environmental modifications. The growth offset coefficient (GO), measuring the degree to which indirect enhancement compensates for direct loss, serves as a key indicator of vegetation-growth compensation capacity; however, the nonlinear response, temporal lag structures, and optimal management strategies governing GO remain poorly understood. This study develops DSTFormer, a spatiotemporal Transformer integrated with SHAP analysis, and applies it to panel data from 227 cities across China's 19 major urban agglomerations from 2001 to 2022. Results indicate that GO increased at 0.0043 yr−1, with indirect enhancement (Ind) strengthening (0.0065 yr−1) faster than direct loss (DI) deepening (−0.0021 yr−1), although the net urbanization effect on vegetation remained negative throughout the study period. SHAP attribution identified forest landscape cohesion (FLCOHESION) as the leading positive predictive factor and impervious patch number (IMNP) as the main fragmentation-related constraint associated with GO variation. Temporal lag structures differed systematically across agglomeration types: the full sample and Optimization-Upgrading Agglomerations showed stronger recent contributions, whereas Cultivation-Development Agglomerations retained stronger historical contributions. Under identical total adjustment budgets, progressive temporal allocation was associated with larger predicted GO gains than uniform allocation. Spatial clustering further identified three regulatory regimes requiring differentiated interventions: a landscape-composition and infrastructure-environment mixed regime, a connectivity-fragmentation constraint regime, and a built-environment morphology and management-environment coupling regime. These findings suggest that improving GO is associated with harnessing nonlinear leverage effects, pursuing synergistic co-optimization, and adopting temporally progressive, agglomeration-specific greening strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: When do hedonic appeals backfire? Credibility, scepticism and the disconnect between emotional engagement and pro-environmental intention
Abstract: This study examines why emotional engagement with hedonic sustainability communication does not always translate into pro-environmental behavioural intention. Drawing on the Persuasion Knowledge Model and Truth-Default Theory, it investigates consumer responses to pleasure- and comfort-based hotel food-waste messages. A sequential mixed-method design combined a laboratory experiment, projective interviews, and a follow-up online experiment testing green scepticism. Findings show no robust statistically significant physiological differentiation across message types, but substantial differences in perceived credibility, sincerity and emotional meaning. Pleasure-based appeals were interpreted as enjoyable but superficial and less trustworthy; comfort-based appeals were warmer and more relational, yet both hedonic appeals produced lower behavioural intention than the control message. Green scepticism strengthened this negative effect, particularly for comfort-based appeals. The findings suggest that hedonic sustainability communication operates less through heightened physiological arousal than through interpretive credibility evaluation, particularly among sceptical consumers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Nanocellulose-reinforced κ-carrageenan/gluten films with Ardisia elliptica anthocyanins: structure-property balance for freshness-related colour response
Abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable alternatives to petroleum-based packaging has stimulated the development of intelligent materials capable of providing visual information on food quality during storage. In this study, soil-burial-disintegrable biopolymer films based on κ-carrageenan, wheat gluten, cellulose nanofibrils (CNF), and anthocyanin extract from Ardisia elliptica fruits were prepared by the solution-casting method and evaluated for their structural, optical, water-related, mechanical, and colourimetric properties. Anthocyanin incorporation conferred a clear pH-dependent colour response across the tested pH range, while CNF-containing formulations exhibited reduced UV transmittance, increased surface wettability (lower water contact angle), and modulated tensile performance and water-related properties in a formulation-dependent, non-monotonic manner. Among the CNF-containing formulations, the film containing κ-carrageenan, gluten, anthocyanin extract, and 20% CNF (κCG-GL-ANT-CNF20) exhibited the lowest water solubility and swelling, coupled with low UV transmittance, with water vapour permeability remaining a formulation-dependent trade-off rather than the primary selection criterion. Soil burial assays showed progressive disintegration, reaching more than 93% weight loss by day 35. Proof-of-concept applicability was assessed using rose apple, apple, and a sardine-based model system, where visible film colour changes were observed during storage. Within the tested series, κCG-GL-ANT-CNF20 provided the most balanced formulation, combining improved resistance to liquid-water-induced disintegration, low UV transmittance, lower short-term anthocyanin release, and qualitative food-model colour responsiveness. The developed films therefore show potential as colour-responsive hydrocolloid materials for qualitative freshness-related assessment. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Title: Multi-source observational data fusion for imputing missing confounders in debiased recommendation
Abstract: In recommender systems, selective interactions between users and items introduce selection bias. This leads to distributional shifts between training and test data, hindering the learning of users’ true preferences. When features that influence both the user selection mechanism and the feedback, referred to as confounders, are unobserved, hidden confounding arises and further complicates debiasing. In this study, we first highlight that unobserved confounders introduce errors in both outcome modeling and propensity estimation. Existing solutions primarily neglect the former issue, address the latter topic, and thus lead to inaccurate recommendations. Moreover, current methods often rely on untestable assumptions about hidden confounding or require costly auxiliary data, which limits their practical applicability. To address these challenges, we propose a two-stage debiasing framework leveraging multiple observational datasets. These datasets contain both shared confounders (e.g., mandatory information) and source-specific confounders (e.g., optional inputs). In the first stage, we identify each sample’s adaptive neighborhood to impute missing confounders. We aggregate these confounders using weights that incorporate spatial structure and neighbor reliability. In the second stage, we enhance the classical IPS debiasing method with a differentiable expected calibration error (DECE) loss. This loss mitigates potential imputation errors from the first stage. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate that our framework effectively alleviates selection bias under hidden confounding and consistently outperforms existing approaches. Copyright © 2026. Title: BBZS glass-ceramics for sealing to 4J33 Kovar alloy: crystallization behavior and sealing mechanism
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: To resolve the trade-off between low sealing temperature and high-temperature insulation in lead-free sealants, a novel Bi2O3–B2O3–ZnO–SiO2 (BBZS) glass-ceramic system was developed for sealing to 4J33 Kovar alloy. The influence of the Si/B mass ratio on the network structure and crystallization of the parent glasses was systematically investigated. The resulting BBZS glass-ceramics exhibited coefficients of thermal expansion (CTEs) tailored from 7.01 to 7.37 × 10−6 K⁻¹ , closely matching that of the Kovar substrate. An optimal joint was achieved at a moderate sealing temperature of 750 °C for 30 min, yielding an average shear strength of 4.70 MPa. Notably, the sealant retained an outstanding bulk resistivity of 107.99 Ω⋅cm at 500 °C. Interfacial analysis revealed that the bonding is driven by elemental interdiffusion, forming a stable transition layer. This work presents a promising strategy for designing environmentally friendly, highly insulating heterogeneous packaging sealants operable at moderate temperatures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Identification of subgroup causal effects in randomized trials under nonignorable missingness of covariates and outcome variables simultaneously
Abstract: Randomized experiments are widely regarded as the gold standard for causal inference. However, identifying subgroup causal effects becomes particularly challenging when pretreatment covariates and outcome are subject to simultaneous nonignorable missingness. The study investigates the identifiability of subgroup causal effects under five increasingly complex missing data mechanisms, ranging from an ignorable mechanism to nonignorable mechanisms in which missingness depends on different combinations of treatment, covariates, and outcome. Identification is established under several nonignorable mechanisms without imposing restrictive parametric assumptions. For the most challenging mechanism, identification is established under a parametric model with specific assumptions on the outcome distribution and the missingness mechanism. For estimation and inference, a fractional-imputation Expectation-Maximization algorithm is developed to maximize the observed-data likelihood. Simulation studies compare the proposed estimator with complete-case analysis, multiple imputation, and a full-data oracle estimator, demonstrating satisfactory finite-sample performance across the considered missingness mechanisms. The practical utility of the proposed method is further illustrated using data from the Oregon Health Insurance Experiment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Multi-field coupling mechanism of internal fin radial length on two-phase flow in gravity-assisted heat pipe
Abstract: Aiming at the unclear regulatory mechanism of internal fin parameters in the evaporation section of gravity-assisted heat pipes (GAHPs) and the insufficient systematic interpretation of the physical nature behind non-monotonic heat transfer behavior in industrial waste heat recovery, this paper establishes a three-dimensional numerical simulation framework coupled with the VOF-Lee-CSF model. Validated by bench-scale experiments, it quantitatively analyzes how circumferential internal fins with radial lengths of 1–8 mm affect in-tube gas-liquid two-phase flow and phase-change heat transfer. The results show that fin radial length exerts bidirectional nonlinear regulation on heat pipe performance through the synergy of vortex evolution and nucleate boiling modulation, with 6 mm as the optimal radial dimension. Under this condition, the heat transfer coefficients of the evaporation and condensation sections rise by 27.27% and 24.67% respectively compared with the 1 mm baseline, and the relative deviation between simulation and experiment stays within 12%–20%. Title: Workplace responses to perpetration of family and domestic violence: a global scoping review
Abstract: Introduction Family and domestic violence (FDV), which includes intimate partner and family violence, affects workplace safety through spillover impacts on workers, organisations, and occupational health systems. To date, workplace interventions addressing the issue of FDV have predominantly concentrated on providing support to victim-survivors, while there is limited research regarding employer responses to employees who perpetrate such violence. Method A scoping review was conducted following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines, which examined existing evidence from workplace policies, practices, and organisational mechanisms addressing FDV perpetration by workers. Peer-reviewed studies and high-quality grey literature on workplace responses to perpetration of FDV were systematically searched across multiple databases and online sources, and 28 documents on workplace responses to FDV perpetration were analysed. Results Findings from the scoping review reveal four dominant insights across the literature: 1. Perpetration of FDV is a major workplace problem, yet responses are under-researched; 2. Workplaces employ wide-ranging and varied responses, from zero tolerance dismissal of perpetrators to responsibility avoidance; 3. Responses lack a solid evidence-base and regulatory frameworks to address the problem remain weak; 4. Practical strategies are provided to better manage risk, strengthen safety, and reduce violence. Conclusion Our findings underscore the need for clearer organisational guidance, evidence-based strategies, and robust regulatory frameworks to strengthen workplace responses to FDV perpetration and improve occupational safety outcomes. Practical applications Effective workplace responses to perpetration of FDV should consider work design factors, referral pathways and confidentiality protections which are guided by graduated accountability models and regulatory frameworks. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A hybrid framework of LLM-based interaction generation and adaptive sampler for recommendation enhancement
Abstract: Data augmentation (DA) is a critical technique for addressing data sparsity. Existing DA methods suffer from several limitations: extensive parameter tuning, dependency on specific types of data, and the tightly coupled DA network in the backbone recommendation model. Consequently, there remains a notable absence of universal data augmentation frameworks capable of adapting to diverse recommendation tasks and backbone models. To address these issues, we propose a hybrid framework to mitigate data sparsity via DA in a more flexible and universal paradigm. Notably, we disentangle the data augmentation process into two modules, data generation and data fusion. Firstly, we prompt LLMs to learn collaborative filtering information from raw user–item interaction data in a CSV format, generating new reliable interactions. Specifically, we devise clustering-based data grouping and multi-round shuffling strategies to enable LLMs to capture comprehensive collaborative filtering information through limited context. Secondly, we design an adaptive sampler to obtain personalized fused data for backbone recommendation models dynamically, making the fused data satisfy the different data demands of diverse downstream recommendation models. Experiments on various recommendation models across distinct datasets demonstrate that our framework can consistently improve vanilla recommendation models and facilitate existing DA methods. Compared with vanilla recommendation models, our framework achieves an average performance gain of 7.10%, 23.54%, and 24.55% on MovieLens-100k, Book-Crossing, and Toys and Games datasets, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of our proposed framework in mitigating data sparsity in recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Effects of orifice diameter and initial state on flashing, depressurization and cooling during liquid CO2 pipeline leakage
Abstract: High-pressure liquid CO2 pipelines are integral to carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS), but accidental leakage can cause rapid depressurization, intense flashing and severe cooling. Such cooling may increase the risk of fracture and crack propagation, with implications for pipeline integrity. We investigated how phase-transition evolution and these transients vary with orifice diameter in a fully liquid-filled horizontal pipeline. Releases through 1, 2 and 3 mm circular orifices were tested under different initial pressures and temperatures, with synchronized pressure, temperature and high-speed imaging. Larger orifices were associated with greater resolved discharge capacity and faster depressurization. As diameter increased from 1 to 3 mm, release duration decreased from approximately 70 to 13 s. The maximum resolved depressurization rate increased from 16.9 to 45.7 MPa/s. The maximum measured degree of superheat ranged from 0.4 to 4.9 °C. Faster depressurization coincided with deeper pressure–temperature excursions into the metastable region, stronger visible flashing and larger in-pipe fluid-temperature drops. Within the observation window, the first persistent visible bubbles occurred in the bulk liquid for the 1 mm case and earlier in the upper visible region for the larger orifices. Higher initial pressure was associated with a longer single-phase stage for the smaller orifice, whereas higher initial temperature was accompanied by later persistent bubble onset. These results characterize associations among orifice diameter, initial state, flashing and cooling, and provide data relevant to safety assessment of liquid CO2 pipelines. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: The value of lost load in electricity intensive industry – combining and comparing stated and production value approaches
Abstract: The value of lost load (VoLL) is a monetary metric quantifying the cost of unsupplied energy (€/kWh) during outages, providing valuable insights for policymakers, utility providers, and industrial stakeholders. Leveraging a mixed-method approach that integrates and compares survey data with publicly available microeconomic data insights, results show how value-added based measures significantly underestimate the financial impact of power outages. Shorter outages are found to be disproportionately costly, primarily due to high fixed costs associated with initial disruptions. Businesses report that the effects of a 1-h outage could linger for months, with some unable to fully recover even 12 months after the event. These extended disruptions underscore the enduring consequences of power outages, particularly for electricity-intensive industries. In a regression type of approach, the cost of power interruptions is not significantly influenced by the type of industry. Instead, the economic impact of an outage is more closely tied to the volume of electricity consumed, duration and production hours. Highlighting sectoral aspects and methodological sensitivities, the paper offers relevant insights for setting reliability standards, designing compensation schemes, and for guiding infrastructure investment. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Cold plate with orifice-type manifolds and 3-pass channels for high temperature uniformity in battery packs
Source title: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
Abstract: Flow maldistribution in liquid-cooled cold plates is often overlooked in battery thermal management system (BTMS) design, despite its critical influence on cell-to-cell temperature uniformity at the pack level. This study proposes a novel bottom-cooled liquid cold plate that integrates orifice-type manifolds with a parallel 3-pass channel configuration to systematically address coolant flow maldistribution and temperature gradients in battery packs. First, the effects of flow maldistribution in parallel-straight-channel cold plates are quantified, revealing a flow maldistribution factor of up to 99.6%, which results in a row-to-row cell temperature difference of 3.03 °C at 2-C discharge. By introducing orifice-type manifolds, the flow maldistribution factor is reduced to 18.8%, leading to a 72.4% reduction in temperature variation across cell rows. A parametric study identifies an optimal manifold-to-port area ratio of approximately unity, providing the best trade-off between flow uniformity improvement and pressure drop penalty. To further mitigate temperature non-uniformity in the battery pack along the overall streamwise direction, a parallel 3-pass channel configuration is introduced, which reduces the temperature variation across cell columns by 67.8%. Furthermore, a parametric study reveals that the spanwise temperature uniformity in the battery pack decreases with the channel pitch for the parallel 3-pass channel configuration and the optimal 3-pass channel pitch is found to be 47.6 mm. Finally. compared with a conventional-serpentine-channel design, the proposed cold plate achieves a 53.3% reduction in overall cell-to-cell temperature difference (from 5.89 °C to 2.75 °C) while simultaneously reducing pressure drop by 75.7% at 2-C discharge and total flow rate of 23 L/min. Comparable improvements in thermal-hydraulic performance are also achieved under higher thermal loads of 3-C discharge and larger total flow rate of 35 L/min. The proposed design is lightweight, scalable, and compatible with conventional manufacturing processes, offering practical design guidelines for high-performance liquid cooling systems in battery packs. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A biophysically-inspired framework with spatiotemporal graph diffusion for EEG-based mental workload assessment
Abstract: Ensuring operational safety in high-stakes environments necessitates the precise assessment of mental workload via electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. However, conventional data-driven deep learning models are often impeded by the inherent non-stationarity of EEG signals and typically neglect the biological topology of the brain. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel biophysically-inspired framework that leverages spatiotemporal graph diffusion for robust workload assessment. We establish a computational surrogate model designed to mirror the dynamic cognitive state of the user. In contrast to traditional approaches, we integrate biophysical priors derived from volume conduction and functional connectivity directly into the learning process, thereby ensuring biologically consistent feature extraction. Specifically, we employ a spatiotemporal graph diffusion mechanism that treats EEG channels as nodes within a dynamic graph. This process effectively denoises the signals and captures complex, long-range dependencies across both spatial brain regions and temporal sequences. By reconciling biophysically-inspired constraints with data-driven graph learning, the proposed model enhances robustness against the low signal-to-noise ratio characteristic of EEG data. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior accuracy compared with other state-of-the-art baselines, offering a reliable solution for the real-time monitoring of mental workload. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Arévalo-Vásquez D.A.; Ramírez-Pizango K.K.
Author full names: Arévalo-Vásquez, Dino Armando (60900972800); Ramírez-Pizango, King Klaus (60819419800)
Title: Perceived influence of the principle of confidentiality in extrajudicial conciliation: A quantitative study among conciliators in the Peruvian Amazon
Abstract: This study aims to determine the perceived influence of the principle of confidentiality on the practice of extrajudicial conciliation from the perspective of conciliators in a city of the Peruvian Amazon, considering its relevance for effective dispute resolution and the strengthening of trust between parties. Methods: A quantitative approach was adopted, with a nonexperimental cross sectional design; the sample consisted of 80 conciliators selected through nonprobabilistic convenience sampling based on strict active procedural eligibility criteria, and data were collected through a 15 item Likert scale questionnaire assessing relational, institutional, and ethical dimensions, demonstrating high and uniform internal reliability with a total Cronbach's alpha coefficient of 0.75. Furthermore, the instrument allowed for a comprehensive assessment of perceptions associated with procedural integrity and professional conduct. Results: The findings show that 77.5 of participants perceive a high level of influence of confidentiality in conciliation processes; moreover, the relational dimension reached a unanimous 100 high rating, while institutional (65) and ethical (67.5) dimensions also showed elevated levels, although with identifiable margins for improvement. Additionally, the nonparametric Wilcoxon signed rank test evaluated against a theoretical neutral midpoint of 3.0 confirmed statistically significant differences with respect to the baseline (Z = 7.874; p < 0.001), yielding a very large overall effect size (r = 0.88) that reinforces the practical magnitude and robustness of the results. Conclusions: Therefore, confidentiality constitutes a structural pillar in conciliation practice; however, its full consolidation requires institutional strengthening, regulatory clarity, and specialized ethical training, providing empirical evidence from a subnational Latin American context and proposing a replicable three dimensional model for future research in alternative dispute resolution mechanisms and professional practice, as well as informing public policy and institutional decision making processes, particularly in decentralized justice systems and emerging governance frameworks. Author full names: Fofanah, Abdul Joseph (57217155104); Wen, Lian (14057317200); Chen, David (55724946100); Zhang, Shaoyang (12782310800); Kamara, Alpha Alimamy (59483574700)
Title: CL3E-GNN: Three-phase attention with feature fusion based on curriculum implementation strategy for class imbalanced node classification
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) often struggle with node classification under class imbalance because standard methods fail to adequately leverage graph topology. Specifically, majority nodes dominate message passing, causing the aggregated information from minority nodes to become statistically diluted, which masks relational signals associated with under-represented classes. Traditional techniques such as oversampling and cost-sensitive learning mitigate data skew but typically neglect structural dependencies, leading to under-representation of minority classes or overfitting to local graph substructures. We propose CL3E-GNN , a novel curriculum learning framework that addresses class imbalance through three synergistic phases: Engage, Enact , and Embed . The Engage phase employs multi-head attention to identify critical node and edge connections, generating enhanced feature representations via dual graph convolution network (GCN) and graph attention network (GAT) aggregation. The Enact phase refines minority class representations through three complementary mechanisms, each targeting a distinct source of imbalance: importance sampling for active feature learning, metapath propagation for knowledge transfer across heterogeneous relations, and anomaly detection for identifying structural irregularities. The Embed phase introduces a memory-augmented reinforcement learning mechanism that progressively refines node embeddings via reward-modulated updates. A dual-loss optimisation strategy combining cross-entropy with adaptive curriculum loss ensures gradual difficulty progression, offering a principled alternative to simple loss functions or data augmentation alone. Extensive evaluations on eight benchmark datasets, with results averaged over five independent runs, demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods. These results establish CL3E-GNN as a new benchmark for imbalanced node classification, effectively preserving topological integrity while mitigating class distribution skew. Authors: BAKIRCI A.E.
Author full names: BAKIRCI, Ahmet Erhan (59221544700)
Title: Regulatory exclusion and occupational health risk in Turkish firefighting: a legal-epidemiological policy analysis
Abstract: Article 2(2)(b) of Turkey’s Law No. 6331 on Occupational Safety and Health excludes the intervention activities of disaster and emergency units from that statute’s scope. The exclusion concerns duties performed during response operations; it does not establish that firefighters lack every protection under other legal or administrative instruments. This evidence-informed legal and policy analysis combines a structured, non-systematic occupational-health evidence synthesis, doctrinal analysis, a review of 43 Turkish judicial decisions issued from 1997 to 2024, and a functional comparison with the United Kingdom. International evidence identifies occupational firefighting as carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 1), links fire suppression with sharply elevated risk of fatal coronary events, and documents substantial psychological and musculoskeletal burdens. In the official sources examined, no nationally binding firefighter-specific instrument was identified that prescribed post-incident decontamination, detailed health-surveillance content, personal protective equipment performance monitoring, or structured psychological support. The judicial corpus was coded across eight analytical categories; its holdings concentrated on pay, personnel status, compensation, procedure, and jurisdiction rather than concrete preventive OSH duties. We interpret these findings through a structural accountability gap model, under which the statutory exclusion may constrain investigation, data generation, standard-setting, and regulatory learning. The model is interpretive, not a tested causal finding. United Kingdom law provides an illustrative comparator because it retains general employer and enforcement duties without a categorical operational exclusion. The article proposes eight evidence-linked policy options. Their effectiveness, feasibility, and cost-effectiveness require prospective evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Cui, Xining (57463112900); Sun, Yanteng (60260950900); Tang, Xincheng (60261010700); Zhang, Biao (56303891700); Meng, Leilei (57192211382)
Title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven adaptive search algorithm for emergency rescue routing
Abstract: Following natural disasters, emergency rescue route planning becomes substantially more challenging due to damaged transportation networks, urgent rescue demands, and the operational complexity of heterogeneous rescue resources. Efficient rescue decision-making under constraints including time windows, regional accessibility, and casualty survival risk is therefore of considerable practical significance. However, existing studies often suffer from inadequate modeling of casualty survival dynamics, excessive reliance on manually designed operator control strategies, and limited search robustness in highly constrained environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning-assisted iterated greedy algorithm for heterogeneous rescue and route planning, termed Dueling Double Deep Q-Network Iterated Greedy (D3QNIG). First, a disaster rescue routing optimization model integrating casualty evacuation and relief material distribution is developed, where an injury-adaptive survival-risk mechanism is incorporated alongside capacity, time-window, and accessibility constraints. Second, a reinforcement learning-assisted iterated greedy framework is designed to adaptively control operator selection and destruction intensity during the destruction, reconstruction, and local search stages. Third, a state representation approach based on set attention pooling is constructed for variable-length and heterogeneous routing solutions, together with a hierarchical Dueling Double DQN decision architecture to enhance policy-learning stability and search effectiveness. Finally, a two-stage reward–acceptance decoupling strategy is introduced to alleviate the credit assignment issue and improve training stability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed D3QNIG achieves superior solution quality, faster convergence, and stronger robustness than benchmark methods, indicating its effectiveness for heterogeneous rescue route optimization in complex disaster scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: CAST-DRO: Cognition-aware service triage with configurable risk adjustment for resource-constrained AI information services
Abstract: AI information service platforms must allocate heterogeneous requests across models, memory, clarification, and human review under joint resource constraints. We develop CAST, a cognition-aware five-action service-triage framework; CAST-ERM learns group-level empirical allocations, and CAST-DRO adds a configurable mean-plus-variability adjustment. Using sequence-grouped train/evaluation splits for 520 LifeSim-derived evaluation requests across 20 repeated splits, CAST-DRO improves over rule-based CAST in quality (0.679 to 0.743), failure rate (0.617 to 0.350), and final satisfaction (46.35 to 56.51), while reducing normalized high-value resource cost (0.087 to 0.081). CAST-ERM reaches quality 0.738, confirming that cognition-group empirical allocation explains most of the average gain. The risk adjustment changes 12 of 104 eligible group-seed action selections and sharply reduces selected-action loss variability in the medium-risk group. A LinUCB comparison warm-started with full-information simulator outcomes reaches quality 0.744 with high-value cost 0.092. A strict budget audit finds zero human, memory, or total-spend violations for all four hard-budget policies across all 20 splits. Resource-price and capacity tests retain a positive quality advantage over CAST, although high-value resource use depends on the bottleneck. In a two-layer stress test, separate mandatory safety-review capacity of 30% reduces latent-reference high-risk miss from 0.788 to 0.230, with 0.035 overflow and 0.398 total escalation. Real-model evaluation on 100 requests and anonymized 1–5 ratings of 50 request–response pairs provide supporting, not production-level, validation. CAST-DRO is best interpreted as an auditable middle-layer allocator after mandatory safety filtering. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Mao Z.; Wang X.; Lei Q.; Fu K.; Shen J.; Liu B.; Lou H.; Zhu L.
Title: Soft-Hard interfacial engineering for optimized mechanical properties of magnesium alloy/polylactic acid films
Source title: Composites Part A: Applied Science and Manufacturing
Abstract: The clinical translation of poly (lactic acid) (PLA)-based bioresorbable scaffolds (BRS) is severely hindered by a strength-thickness trade-off and the inevitable physical aging of the matrix. To improve the overall mechanical properties of the PLA matrix, we fabricated magnesium (Mg) alloy/PLA composite structural films via magnetron sputtering. The results demonstrate that, compared with the pristine matrix, the elastic modulus and yield strength of the unaged PLA-based composite films increased by 306% and 363%, respectively. For composite films based on aged PLA, the modulus and strength still increased by 21.2% and 20.1%, respectively, while maintaining favorable ductility. By coupling a time-dependent physical elasto-viscoplastic constitutive model with a finite element cohesive zone model, this study reveals an aging-induced anomalous mechanical transition mechanism driven synergistically by matrix structural relaxation and interfacial mechanical evolution. It is found that in the unaged state, the sputtering energy dissipates deeply into the PLA matrix with high free volume, forming a strongly constrained interfacial transition zone (ITZ) and a robustly anchored interface, triggering premature brittle fracture of the material. In the intermediate aging stage, the intrinsic densification of the matrix shrinks the ITZ and weakens the interfacial bonding strength. This interfacial debonding effect relieves the geometric constraints imposed by the metal layer, thereby releasing the intrinsic ductility of the matrix, enabling the composite structural films to avert brittle failure while simultaneously enhancing their modulus and strength. Furthermore, the quantitative analysis framework for multi-mechanism synergy established herein elucidates the intrinsic coupling correlations among the aforementioned multi-physical mechanisms, which will facilitate the design and development of high-performance biodegradable scaffolds based on polymer/metal composites. Authors: Hu X.; Lima M.F.
Title: Urban park biodiversity preferences and trade-offs: A comparison between residents and professionals using Adaptive Choice-Based Conjoint analysis
Abstract: Urban parks are important biodiversity hotspots as well as recreational spaces in cities. It is desirable for urban residents to derive pleasure from parks that also embody biodiversity values due to their ecological and health benefits. Despite the evidence that urban residents are happier and healthier when they have access to green spaces of good quality, it remains unclear how residents prioritise biodiversity when considering the joint effects of other green space attributes, and how these priorities differ from those of landscape/ecology professionals. We used Adaptive Choice-Based Conjoint (ACBC) analysis to examine how biodiversity was prioritised in trade-offs with other important park attributes among residents and professionals. The ACBC study was conducted in Hangzhou (N = 187) and Shanghai (N = 194), two cities in eastern China. Utility values and average importances were estimated using Hierarchical Bayes (HB). While both residents and professionals preferred higher biodiversity levels, biodiversity improvements from poor to moderate yielded greater utility gains than from moderate to rich. Residents prioritised facilities over biodiversity when making trade-offs, whereas professionals prioritised biodiversity as the most important park attribute and valued it significantly more than residents. In both groups, preferences for higher biodiversity were associated with preferences for fewer facilities, denser tree cover, and low-maintenance, wild-looking landscapes. Urban park planning may prioritise biodiversity enhancement in biodiversity-poor sites over further enhancement in biodiversity-moderate sites to optimise resource allocation. Professionals should account for differences between their own preferences and those of residents, while recognising the importance of managing biodiversity-amenity trade-offs and supporting the coexistence of both objectives. © 2026

Authors: Kuo C.-C.; Wu C.-H.; Ni Y.-L.
Title: Why and when does leisure-time physical activity enhance hospitality employees’ job satisfaction
Abstract: Employee engagement in leisure-time physical activity has been associated with greater job satisfaction. However, the conditions under which and the reasons why leisure-time physical activity enhances job satisfaction need to be better understood. Drawing on the integrated perspective of proactivity and the work–home resources model, we propose that employees with lower levels of proactive personality particularly benefit from leisure-time physical activity because it helps them proactively manage their vitality, thereby increasing job satisfaction. Consistent with our expectations, the results from a sample of 197 hotel employees indicate that leisure-time physical activity positively predicted job satisfaction through proactive vitality management. Moreover, the mediating effect of proactive vitality management was more substantial among individuals with lower proactive personality. We discuss the theoretical and practical implications of these findings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: What impacts can intertemporal trading have on carbon markets across different development stages? An economy-wide analysis
Abstract: Carbon markets have encountered challenges such as limited flexibility and substantial price volatility. Intertemporal trading mechanisms, as one of the important ways of green finance, have been proposed as a potential solution to improve market efficiency. However, existing studies frequently overlook whether the intricate internal mechanisms of carbon markets are suitable for introducing intertemporal trading. To comprehensively analyze the effect of intertemporal trading, this study employs a computable general equilibrium model incorporating an intertemporal dynamic mechanism and a carbon market module. This study designs scenarios focusing on total quotas, sectoral coverage, quota allocation, and intertemporal trading to simulate and compare their macroeconomic impacts. The results suggest that intertemporal trading is particularly beneficial in carbon markets that prioritize later-stage reduction, experience rapid sectoral coverage, or have a high auction rate. Under these conditions, introducing intertemporal trading can help reduce long-term carbon prices while promoting the development of cumulative GDP and household welfare. It is noted that the output of sectors covered by the carbon market undergoes an initial contraction in the early stage, followed by a gradual increase in the later stage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Alhijawi B.
Author full names: Alhijawi, Bushra (57191223804)
Title: Evolution of recommender systems: Approaches, advances, paradigm shifts, and future directions
Abstract: Recommender systems are essential tools across numerous digital platforms, helping users discover relevant products, content, and services. Research has traditionally focused on prediction accuracy and relevance, relying primarily on collaborative filtering and matrix factorization techniques. With the increasing complexity of user behavior and data modalities, modern systems have moved beyond simple rating prediction to address additional objectives, including fairness, transparency, privacy, long-term engagement, and trustworthiness. This article systematically reviews the evolution of recommender systems, covering key stages from early predictive models to modern human-centered and trust-aware systems. Each stage is discussed in terms of methodological advances and practical applications. Emerging paradigms, including causal reasoning for bias mitigation, reinforcement learning for long-term optimization, federated and privacy-preserving learning, explainable recommendation techniques, and blockchain-based trust mechanisms, are analyzed. These developments illustrate a broader shift from static, correlation-driven predictions toward adaptive, context-aware, and human-centered intelligence. By organizing research into coherent clusters, this review provides a unified perspective on the field, highlights the connections between past and current approaches, and identifies promising directions for next-generation recommender systems that balance accuracy, user satisfaction, ethical considerations, and long-term system effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Author full names: Liu, Jian (55949814600); Zhong, Chen (55843593600); Meng, Fanlin (57213962702); Shank, Daniel B. (24503627700); Wunsch, Donald C. (7006706193)
Title: GenAI-enabled human–AI collaboration: An integrative review of local augmentation, hidden work, and governable synergy
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is becoming part of everyday knowledge work, where it can accelerate drafting, coding, summarization, ideation, customer communication, and other language-intensive tasks. Yet the organizational problem is conversion: local GenAI gains create organizational value only when they survive the full work system, including verification, coordination, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability. Drawing on 251 academic and practice-facing sources across information systems (IS), management, human–computer interaction, human factors, organizational theory, and responsible AI, this article synthesizes why GenAI-enabled work often produces local augmentation but less often yields governable organizational synergy. The review develops three findings. First, GenAI shifts the relevant unit of collaboration from a one-step task interaction to a recurrent production-and-revision workflow in which human framing, prompting, verification, correction, and reuse become part of the value-producing system. Second, the augmentation-to-synergy boundary is net work-system value: visible task gains and reallocation benefits must exceed work displaced across roles and time into verification, rework, coordination, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability. Third, durable synergy requires behavioral embedding and multi-outcome governance: prompts, memory, feedback traces, review routines, and escalation rules must improve local fit while keeping reliance, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability observable. The article contributes a work-system conversion account that distinguishes substitution, augmentation, and synergy as different organizational states; a trace-centered behavioral-embedding view of how recurring GenAI use becomes a persistent, history-dependent workflow state within established sociotechnical IS theory; and a governance-instrumentation account that evaluates visible gains together with hidden labor, learning, ownership, risk, reviewability, and accountability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A socio-technical maturity framework for design firms to enable the transition to design-out-waste in Indonesia's construction sector
Abstract: The construction sector remains a major driver of resource depletion and solid waste generation, with a substantial share traceable to early design-stage decisions. Design-out-Waste (DoW) strategies, including waste-efficient documentation, modern construction methods, and prefabrication, represent a proactive approach to enhancing lifecycle resource efficiency. However, their implementation remains fragmented, particularly in developing-country contexts, partly due to the lack of a structured framework for assessing organisational maturity. This study addresses this gap by developing an empirically grounded socio-technical maturity framework for DoW implementation in building design firms. The framework integrates five socio-technical dimensions into a single operational model encompassing processes & procedures, people & culture, industry structures, technology, and goals & incentives. Using data from 116 construction professionals, Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to validate the measurement and structural relationships, while Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) provided empirical importance values for weighting the maturity dimensions and attributes. These weights were subsequently integrated with a five-level maturity scoring scheme to operationalise the assessment framework. The results reveal an interdependent socio-technical structure, with Industry Structure emerging as the most influential dimension and an important upstream driver of other organisational capabilities. The resulting framework provides an empirically weighted basis for assessing organisational readiness, identifying capability priorities, and guiding DoW implementation towards circular construction. It also provides a structured basis for informing environmental assessment, project appraisal, and policy interventions aimed at improving resource efficiency and waste prevention. © 2026

Title: Robust optimization with decision dependent uncertainty for electric vehicle network expansion
Abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) is driving the need for charging infrastructure expansion, which in turn has significant implications for power system operations. Such expansion may also affect the EV-charging demand, making this uncertainty decision-dependent. This paper develops a two-stage robust optimization model that determines EV-charging station expansion decisions in the first stage and power system operational decisions in the second stage, while explicitly capturing decision-dependent uncertainty of charging demands to enhance planning robustness. To efficiently solve the resulting challenging optimization problem, we design a column-and-cut generation algorithm that obtains high-quality solutions quickly. Comprehensive numerical experiments demonstrate that generation availability and line congestion play critical roles in shaping optimal expansion decisions. © 2026

Authors: Wei H.; Yang F.; Yuan F.; Wu J.; Guo Y.; Ding Z.; Shen K.; Wu B.; Li L.; Qu Q.
Title: From surface coverage to biofilm involvement: Hyaluronic acid influences TiZr alloy corrosion under sterile and Staphylococcus aureus biofilm conditions
Abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is widely used for intra-articular injection to improve joint lubrication and mobility, but its influence on microbiologically influenced corrosion of joint implants remains unclear. Here, we investigated how HA affects the corrosion behavior of TiZr alloy in simulated body fluid (SBF) under sterile and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) biofilm conditions. Surface observations and chemical analysis indicated that HA-related surface coverage was formed on the TiZr surface and reduced surface damage under sterile conditions, suggesting a protective role of HA. However, in the presence of S. aureus biofilm, HA showed contrasting effects at different immersion stages, slightly reducing corrosion at the early stage compared with the S. aureus group but aggravating biofilm-associated localized damage after prolonged exposure. Contact angle analysis showed decreases of 68.1% and 57.1% within 1 min in the S. aureus + HA group on days 7 and 14, respectively, indicating that HA promoted rapid surface wetting and altered the interfacial wetting behavior in the biofilm environment. At these time points, electrochemical tests further confirmed corrosion acceleration, with the S. aureus + HA group showing the highest corrosion current densities among all groups, reaching 7.972 × 10-6 A cm-2 and 2.715 × 10-6 A cm-2, respectively. These results demonstrate that the effect of HA on TiZr alloy corrosion shifts from protection under sterile conditions to corrosion aggravation during prolonged S. aureus biofilm exposure. This finding suggests that HA-related effects on biofilm formation and implant corrosion should be considered when assessing the corrosion risk of TiZr joint implants under infection-related conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Energy-efficient beamforming design for sub-connected active RIS-assisted ISAC systems
Abstract: Active reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) can mitigate severe multiplicative fading through signal amplification, but fully-connected architectures consume substantial hardware power because each reflecting element requires a dedicated power amplifier (PA). This paper investigates a sub-connected active RIS (SC-ARIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where multiple reflecting elements share one PA, reducing active-hardware power consumption at the cost of lower amplification-control flexibility. We formulate a highly non-convex energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing the base station transmit beamforming, radar receive filter, and SC-ARIS reflection coefficients, subject to a minimum radar signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) requirement, power budgets, and hardware constraints. To solve it, we develop an alternating optimization framework combining Dinkelbach’s method and fractional programming. By exploiting the phase freedom of the radar receive filter, the non-convex radar SNR constraint is transformed into a linear constraint on the transmit beamformer for a fixed receive filter, while projection-based recovery yields hardware-feasible SC-ARIS coefficients. Simulations show that the proposed design achieves higher EE than fully-connected and random-phase baselines, although the fully-connected benchmark attains a higher communication sum-rate. These results demonstrate a favorable trade-off among EE, ISAC performance, and active-hardware complexity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Lin S.; Liu Q.
Title: “Crossing the river by feeling the stones”: Sub-national agency in China's highway maintenance marketisation
Abstract: Marketisation reforms in China are often described as an extension of Western New Public Management (NPM), yet their meanings and effects vary substantially across regions and remain poorly understood from the perspective of policymakers themselves. Drawing on document review and interviews with sub-national officials and practitioners involved in highway maintenance in two underdeveloped provinces, this study examines how marketisation is interpreted, justified, and enacted through a "learning by doing" process shaped by administrative legacies, political incentives, and constrained market environments. The analysis shows that NPM-related principles, such as competition and performance management, are selectively adapted rather than directly transplanted, producing hybrid arrangements that combine bureaucratic control with quasi-market practices dominated by state-owned enterprises. The study identifies four narrative frames through which policymakers explain and evaluate reforms, as well as the recurring strategy of deliberate inaction, which emerges as a pragmatic response to tensions between central expectations and local socio-economic realities. It also considers the broader implications of marketisation for highway service performance, public satisfaction, fiscal sustainability, and technical capacity, pointing to uneven outcomes and persistent governance tensions. By foregrounding sub-national agency and context-sensitive adaptation, the article contributes to understanding policy transfer, the institutional logics shaping China's state-led market reforms, and the prospects for more sustainable infrastructure governance in less developed regions. © 2026 The Authors.
