Title: Overcoming the sensitivity–selectivity trade-off in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) for uranium isotope analysis via joint spectral decomposition of single- and double-pulse spectra
Abstract: Reliable analysis of uranium isotopes (235U and 238U) is essential throughout the nuclear fuel cycle. Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) has emerged as a promising technique for rapid detection of uranium. However, its application to isotope analysis is hindered by a fundamental sensitivity-selectivity trade-off: High-energy laser pulses, while essential for enhancing sensitivity, exacerbate the overlap between closely spaced spectral features, thereby reducing isotope selectivity. To circumvent this dilemma, the present study proposes a joint spectral decomposition framework that integrates two complementary spectra obtained using single-pulse (SP) and double-pulse (DP) LIBS. SP spectra preserve the narrow spectral features required for isotope discrimination, whereas DP spectra provide enhanced emission intensity and detection sensitivity. By simultaneously fitting the SP and DP spectra under a shared isotope-ratio constraint, the proposed framework combines DP-enhanced sensitivity with SP-derived isotope selectivity, achieving a uranium limit of detection (LOD) of 0.008% in a soil matrix while keeping the isotope-quantification bias within approximately 1 percentage point. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed framework for improving the analytical performance of LIBS-based uranium isotope analysis and provide a basis for further validation toward rapid uranium isotope screening. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Accumulation and transfer behavior of typical heavy metals in Spirulina products: Implications for risk assessment
Abstract: This study investigated the exposure, bioaccumulation, migration, and associated risks of Pb, Cd, Hg and As throughout the Spirulina-based food supply chain. A total of 83 commercial Spirulina powder samples were analyzed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), followed by dietary risk assessment using Monte Carlo simulation. Controlled exposure system was established to evaluate heavy metal bioaccumulation during cultivation, and metal redistribution was tracked during phycocyanin production. The results showed that all four heavy metals were detected in commercial samples, with total As exhibiting the highest concentration level and exceedance rate, followed by Hg. Under the population-average intake scenario, the combined hazard index (HI) remained below 1. However, scenario-based recalculation using consumer-relevant Spirulina intake levels indicated that the HI could approach or exceed 1 under moderate-to-high and high supplement consumption. Under the controlled single-metal exposure conditions used in this study, Spirulina possessed significantly higher BCFs for Pb and Cd than for As and Hg, and that the soluble fraction served as the principal intracellular storage compartment. During processing, heavy metals were redistributed during crude extraction, ammonium sulfate precipitation, and dialysis, with approximately 30%-40% ultimately retained in the final phycocyanin product. Isothermal titration calorimetry further confirmed that all four metals could spontaneously bind to phycocyanin through exothermic interactions. This study reveals the transfer characteristics of heavy metals along the pathway of “water - algal biomass - algal powder - phycocyanin”, and provides a scientific basis for full-chain safety control and risk assessment of Spirulina-derived products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: “Looking at artifacts”: The development of visual aesthetic preferences
Abstract: Developmental aesthetics is an underexamined yet growing area of aesthetics research. Very few studies have investigated infants’ visual preferences for artifacts. Would a young child have visual preferences for artifacts, given their limited exposure to the world and with a developing brain? Revisiting our framework (Göksun et al., 2014), which was built on the aesthetic triad of Chatterjee and Vartanian (2014), we provide an overview of the current state of the field on early visual aesthetic preferences with a focus on art and architecture. After presenting evidence for perceptual primitives that may guide visual aesthetic preferences, we center on early artifact appreciation with infants and young children. Title: Identification and causal analysis of human factors in autonomous vessel accidents: An integrated transformer-DEMATEL approach
Abstract: This study proposes an integrated Transformer-DEMATEL framework to identify and analyse human factors in Maritime Autonomous Surface Ship (MASS) accidents based on the HFACS taxonomy and accident text mining. A corpus of investigation reports and academic literature is processed through semantic filtering, BERTopic topic modelling, and hierarchical classification to construct structured human-factor representations. A Transformer self-attention mechanism is introduced to extract causal influence matrices from textual data, reducing direct reliance on expert scoring in traditional DEMATEL analysis. Bayesian inference and sensitivity analysis are further applied to quantify causal propagation strength and inter-layer dependencies. Results indicate that organisational-level deficiencies, particularly the governance of system reliability, cybersecurity protocols, and cognitive resource allocation, form the core of the causal network. A clear dual-path mechanism of unsafe acts is revealed: action errors are primarily driven by systemic and environmental degradation, while routine violations are mainly associated with operator states and exhibit strong behavioural autonomy and weak system sensitivity. Moreover, supervisory and organisational failures demonstrate strong asymmetric cascading effects, where upstream deficiencies rapidly amplify downstream risks, while corrective interventions show limited and delayed mitigation effects. This explainable, data-driven framework hierarchically models human-factor causation in MASS accidents, advancing risk evaluation, system resilience, and safety management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: From revision to learning transfer: Self- and socially shared-regulated pathways in AI-assisted feedback
Abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has transformed feedback provision in writing practices. However, little is known about the mechanisms through which AI-mediated engagement and revision contribute to longer-term learning transfer. Research aims: Framed by theories of self-regulated learning (SRL), socially shared regulated learning (SSRL), and cognitive engagement, the study examined the relationship among engagement, immediate revision gains, and longer-term learning transfer in AI-assisted feedback. Methods: This 16-week cluster-randomized experiment involving 108 undergraduates in China compared two feedback modes: AI-assisted self-feedback and AI-assisted peer feedback. Analyses drew on 1100 writing samples (including pretests, four assignments with two drafts each, and posttests), and 432 reflection forms on AI feedback. Findings: Linear mixed models revealed a decoupling of learning and performance: while both conditions produced similarly strong second drafts, AI-assisted peer feedback demonstrated significantly greater learning transfer to subsequent tasks. In AI-assisted self-feedback, learning followed a performance-dependent SRL cycle in which AI engagement and revision improvements independently predicted learning. A threshold-like pattern further showed that benefits emerged only when students engaged constructively, measured by reflection forms, to internalize writing standards. Conversely, AI-assisted peer feedback was associated with stronger learning transfer that was less dependent on revision gains or engagement with AI, a pattern consistent with an SSRL perspective emphasizing interactive engagement and co-constructed understanding. Conclusion: These findings highlight the importance of revision mechanisms and depth of engagement across feedback contexts. The study contributes to theories of regulation and cognitive engagement and offers pedagogical and design implications for fostering meaningful learning through AI-assisted feedback. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Assessing urban carbon emissions from a water-energy-food nexus perspective: An intensity-structure-pressure framework for differentiated management in Chinese cities
Abstract: The classic Kaya identity lacks integration of water-energy-food (WEF) nexus elements, and conventional geographical zoning fails to capture the structural heterogeneity of urban carbon emissions. To address these gaps, this study extends the Kaya identity to construct an intensity–structure–pressure chain decomposition equation covering the energy-economy-agriculture-land-water system. A three-stage analytical framework, macro-driving decomposition, structure type identification, and conditional associations analysis, is then applied. Using city-level panel data from China (2000−2020) and integrating Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition, Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) clustering, and panel quantile regression, the study decomposes the structural factors of carbon emissions, identifies city clusters with homogeneous resource structures, and reveals heterogeneous factor associations across emission levels. The results indicate that: (1) Economic growth emerges as the dominant positive factor in carbon emission growth, with its decomposed proportion exhibiting significant north–south regional divergence; (2) cities can be classified into six distinct structural typologies in terms of resource use and emissions, high-emission clusters are typically constrained by a dilemma of improving efficiency while still expanding in scale, whereas low-carbon clusters have systematically entered a phase of decoupling economic growth from carbon emissions; and (3) regression analysis further suggests that the direction and magnitude of the conditional association of the same decomposition factor differ significantly between low- and high-carbon cities, with the marginal association of most factors diminishing as emission levels increase. This study provides a basis for transcending the limitations of geographical proximity and establishing intensity-structure-pressure-oriented, precise, and differentiated carbon management strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Yang S.; Zhao H.; Qin K.; Lv T.; Tang X.
Title: Thermal-hydraulic assessment of microencapsulated phase change material slurry for natural-circulation loops
Abstract: Natural-circulation is widely used in passive heat-removal systems for nuclear reactors. Microencapsulated phase change material (mPCM) slurry is a potential working fluid because it can couple latent heat storage with phase-change-induced density variation. However, the viscosity increase at higher mPCM concentrations may raise flow resistance and offset the heat-transfer benefit. To evaluate this trade-off, a calibrated plateau-viscosity correlation accounting for temperature and concentration effects was incorporated into a one-dimensional steady-state natural-circulation loop (NCL) program, termed NCLS1. The single-phase natural-circulation solver was verified against pure-water experimental data and the Vijayan correlation. The effects of mPCM concentration, heating power, loop height, and pipe diameter were evaluated using NCLS1. The results show that mPCM slurry does not always improve natural-circulation heat transfer. Cooling benefit appears only when a phase-change circulation is established, allowing the slurry to melt in the heater and solidify in the cooler. Under the investigated conditions, the favorable operating region occurred at heating powers of 10–20 W and mPCM mass concentrations of 5–10 wt%, where latent heat enhancement balanced viscosity-induced flow resistance. Increasing loop height broadened this region, whereas pipe diameter required careful selection to avoid boiling and low-shear conditions. These findings clarify the coupled effects of latent heat, buoyancy, and viscosity in mPCM slurry loops and provide guidance for evaluating candidate working fluids in passive nuclear heat-removal systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Transformation–conditioning Heckman-type selection models with extended skew-elliptical errors: mathematical characterization, computational aspects, and applications
Abstract: In bivariate sample-selection problems, the outcome is observed only for selected units, so misspecification of the joint selection–outcome error distribution can affect estimation and inference. Classical Heckman-type specifications are often based on Gaussian or symmetric error structures, which limits their ability to represent skewness, tail behavior, and support restrictions. We develop a transformation–conditioning, or hidden-truncation, construction for bivariate models that yields a unified extended skew-elliptical class, including skew-normal, skew-Student–t, log-skew-elliptical, Birnbaum–Saunders–elliptical, sinh-type, unit-type, and related distributions. The approach combines strictly monotone componentwise transformations, including support-changing cases, with hidden truncation in a single likelihood-based framework, and evaluates the hidden-truncation factor through the conditional distribution induced by the chosen elliptical generator rather than through a universal Gaussian-type standardization. This generator-aware formulation separates raw latent hidden-truncation quantities from the normalized effective parameters that enter the observed density, clarifying identifiability and the Gaussian-alignment case. We embed the resulting distribution in a Heckman-type threshold-selection model, derive the observed-data likelihood, and establish maximum-likelihood consistency and asymptotic normality under explicit regularity and population identification conditions. The reported implementation uses smooth reparameterizations, data-based multi-start optimization, and low-dimensional Gaussian or Student–t probability evaluations for the extended skew-normal (ESN) and extended skew-Student–t (EST) cases considered. Monte Carlo recovery experiments and synthetic benchmark comparisons with normal, symmetric Student–t, contaminated-normal, ESN, and EST Heckman specifications show a regime-dependent likelihood–penalty tradeoff. The results position the proposed class as an expanded modeling toolkit to be used alongside simpler benchmarks, with model choice guided by likelihood, information criteria, parsimony, convergence, and boundary diagnostics. An application to the Mroz87 dataset illustrates nesting, interpretation, and model comparison on a common likelihood scale. Title: Thermodynamics of soybean protein isolates dissolution in saline solutions
Abstract: The dissolution behaviors of two types of soybean protein isolates (SPI), DN and GN, in two salt solutions—KCl and CaCl2—were studied under various temperatures. The pseudo-critical concentration (CC) of SPI increased with temperature, indicating that the dissolution processes are endothermic. Followed by Hofmeister series, KCl exhibited a salting-out effect, whereas CaCl2 promoted a salting-in effect.Kinetic analysis revealed that the dissolution constants did not follow the Arrhenius formula. Thermodynamic parameters (ΔG, ΔH, and ΔS), evaluated via CC, show that ΔH is significantly smaller than that of protein crystallization, while ΔS is not. These findings suggest four key points: 1) a heterogeneous spatial mass distribution within SPI nanoparticles, 2) energy changes involvement of a trade-off among various bond-breaking processes, 3) a critical role of water molecules in thermodynamics through protein hydration, 4) inevitable protein conformational changes. These conformational changes were supported by two spectroscopic techniques, which yielded inconsistent results, further validating the heterogeneous spatial mass distribution. The nanoparticles (NPs) in SPI were characterized by their hydrodynamic radii (RH) and compactness (df). Structural variations associated with thermodynamic parameters were quantified via their correlation coefficients. However, the underlying reason why some of these coefficients exhibit opposite signs in KCl and CaCl2 solutions remains unclear. This study not only enhances understanding of food quality assessment and rational process development but also offers new insights into aggregate structure characterization. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Beyond exposure: familiarity and the ecology of food meaning in hierarchical environments – A military field study
Abstract: Familiarity is commonly assumed to enhance food acceptance and reduce waste through repeated exposure. However, in institutional environments shaped by hierarchical norms and operational constraints, repeated contact may influence not only sensory responses but also the meanings and practices associated with food. This study examined how food-related evaluations and practices differed across military career stages characterized by different levels of accumulated institutional experience. A focused ethnographic approach was conducted with 113 Brazilian Army personnel classified as Early-Career (EC), Mid-Career (MC), and Advanced-Career (AC). Contextual observations and semi-structured interviews were analyzed through thematic coding complemented by supervised AI-assisted sentiment classification. Negative sensory and physiological sentiment remained relatively stable across career stages, while patterns of expressing and managing dissatisfaction differed among career-stage groups. In early-career personnel, consumption remained closely shaped by supervision and institutional expectations. Mid-career personnel developed more detailed, peer-supported evaluations and engaged more frequently in selective consumption and food discard. By advanced career, dissatisfaction persisted, but participants routinely modified and combined ration components to make meals more practical and acceptable under field conditions. Career-stage differences were not consistent with progressively greater liking; rather, responses to persistent dissatisfaction differed across groups characterized by different levels of accumulated institutional experience. These findings support a multidimensional and contextual interpretation of familiarity and extend consumer research on food acceptance in constrained, high-demand institutional environments. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Differences in the orthographic expectation effect during auditory novel pseudo-character learning in Mandarin-speaking prelingually deaf children with cochlear implants
Abstract: While the orthographic expectation effect (OEE) is well-documented in alphabetic languages, its manifestation in logographic systems like Chinese, particularly among children with atypical auditory experience such as those with cochlear implants (CIs), remains unexplored. This study investigated whether Mandarin-speaking children can form orthographic expectations for Chinese characters through auditory exposure alone, comparing 36 prelingually deaf children with CIs and 36 age-matched children with normal hearing (NH). Using a novel-word learning paradigm, participants were auditorily exposed to pseudo-characters. Their reaction times in a subsequent lexical decision task were analyzed using Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Models (GLMM) to compare auditorily learned versus unlearned phonograms and non-phonograms, as well as predictable versus unpredictable phonetic radicals. Results revealed that both groups exhibited significantly faster reaction times for auditorily learned phonograms, and this expectation effect emerged robustly only when the phonetic radicals were highly predictable. However, children with CIs demonstrated markedly slower responses than their NH peers across all conditions. These findings demonstrate that Mandarin-speaking children can form robust orthographic expectations through auditory input regardless of hearing status. Although children with CIs exhibit slower baseline processing speeds due to underlying perceptual constraints, the magnitude of their orthographic expectation effect remains remarkably intact and comparable to their normal-hearing peers. Ultimately, this highlights the resilient nature of cross-modal reading acquisition, offering crucial neurocognitive insights for designing adaptive literacy interventions in clinical and educational settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Bioprinted core-shell living material platform for spatially controlled encapsulation of Bacillus subtilis and sustained metabolite exchange
Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents an escalating global health crisis, demanding alternative strategies to reduce resistant pathogen burden across environments. Microbe-based biocontrol is promising, yet effectively deploying it in practical settings remains challenging. In this study, we present a 3D bioprinted core-shell construct featuring a polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) shell with tunable nanoscale porosity, encapsulating germinable spores of the biocontrol agent Bacillus subtilis TH035. This configuration supports long-term spore viability while providing protection from common environmental stressors including UV-C irradiation, ethanol exposure, and desiccation over 4 weeks. The nanoporous PEGDA shell enables effective bacterial confinement while facilitating sufficient metabolite exchange for B. subtilis germination and growth, as well as suppression of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) growth by approximately one order of magnitude. This approach demonstrates the feasibility of embedding B. subtilis spores within engineered scaffolds for extended competitive functionality. The versatility and scalability of digital light processing (DLP) based bioprinting offers significant potential for tailored designs and high-throughput manufacturing. This proof-of-concept platform may find future applications in areas such as biomedical packaging, environmental sanitation, and built environment surface coatings, particularly in settings where intermittent moisture or nutrient availability can support spore germination and biocontrol activity. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Closed-loop versus conventional synchronization in spontaneously breathing adult patients– a randomized controlled study
Abstract: Background The IntelliSync+ [IS+] algorithm provides closed-loop synchronization by continuously analyzing airway pressure and flow waveforms in real time to optimize inspiratory and expiratory cycling. This study evaluated the efficacy of IS+ compared with conventional physician-tailored synchronization during noninvasive ventilation [NIV] in spontaneously breathing adult patients with ARF. Methods This multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled, single-blind crossover trial was conducted between March 2024 and May 2025 in two tertiary hospitals. Adult patients receiving NIV for ARF were randomized to start with either conventional synchronization or IS+. Each mode was applied for 30 min, separated by a 15-min washout period. The primary outcome was the Asynchrony Index [AI], defined as the number of asynchronous events per 100 breaths. Results Compared with conventional synchronization, IS+ significantly reduced the total AI [11.8 (7.9–22.4) vs. 25.5 (12.1–35.3) events/100 breaths, p < 0.001], as well as both major and minor asynchrony indices [8.3 (4.5–16.4) vs. 17.6 (7.5–25.6), p < 0.001; 3.4 (1.5–5.4) vs. 7.6 (3.4–13.6), p < 0.001, respectively]. Dyspnea scores were significantly reduced during IS+ [3 ± 1 vs. 5 ± 1, p = 0.0001], indicating improved comfort. Conclusions Closed-loop synchronization using IS+ significantly improved patient–ventilator interaction and comfort during NIV in adults with acute respiratory failure with no adverse events observed during the study period. This study demonstrates that synchrony during NIV can be enhanced using a closed-loop algorithm alone, solely through real-time waveform analysis, without the need for additional invasive monitoring. Authors: Hu X.; Ma P.; Yang K.; Li W.; Yang M.
Title: A structured and gated autoregressive Gaussian process for robust and efficient multi-fidelity learning
Abstract: Multi-fidelity learning with Gaussian processes (GPs) has become an effective strategy for improving predictive accuracy by leveraging inexpensive low-fidelity simulations to enhance high-fidelity inference. However, existing multi-fidelity GP methods often lack flexibility in representing heterogeneous cross-fidelity dependencies and remain vulnerable to negative transfer when cross-fidelity correlations become locally unreliable. Moreover, conventional Monte Carlo (MC)-based uncertainty propagation incurs a non-negligible computational cost. To address these limitations, we propose a structured and gated autoregressive GP (SGARGP) framework to improve robustness and computational efficiency in multi-fidelity learning. Specifically, a structured autoregressive kernel that combines linear and nonlinear components is introduced to capture diverse cross-fidelity relationships. A leave-one-out cross-validation–informed gating mechanism is further developed to adaptively downweight unreliable cross-fidelity transfer and mitigate localized negative transfer. In addition, a deterministic uncertainty propagation scheme (DGHUP) based on Gauss–Hermite quadrature is proposed to achieve an improved accuracy–cost trade-off compared with MC sampling. Comprehensive experiments on synthetic examples, benchmarks and two physics-based engineering applications demonstrate that the structured kernel improves robustness across linear-dominant, nonlinear-dominant, and mixed-dominant scenarios; the gating strategy effectively alleviates negative transfer without degrading performance in well-aligned cases; and DGHUP achieves predictive accuracy comparable to MC methods at significantly reduced computational cost. These results demonstrate that SGARGP provides a reliable and efficient probabilistic framework for multi-fidelity learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Ren L.; Zang Y.; Wang Z.; Liu G.; Li T.; Li Y.; Pan C.; Hu R.; Wu J.; Yang X.
Title: Spectral energy modeling for weighted graph anomaly detection
Abstract: Graph anomaly detection is critical for high-risk applications such as cancer gene identification and telecom fraud detection. However, traditional graph neural networks (GNNs) mainly focus on unweighted topology, while ignoring weight heterogeneity, i.e., differences in the strength of edge connections between nodes. Weight heterogeneity manifests as irregular interaction strengths between genes in biological networks and fraudulent behavior patterns in communication systems, both of which play a key role in graph anomaly detection. This study establishes a fundamental theoretical connection between weight heterogeneity and the spectral energy distribution of graphs. We theoretically show under a stylized random-weight model that weight heterogeneity induces the “flattening out” of spectral energy, in which energy shifts from the middle region and accumulates more prominently at the upper and lower bounds. This phenomenon is empirically validated on both synthetic graphs (Barabasi–Albert and Erdős–Renyi) and real-world datasets, including two protein–protein interaction networks (STRINGdb and CPDB) with cancer genes and two telecom graphs (Tele-Max and Tele-Min) with fraudsters. Motivated by this finding, we propose a Hierarchical-Perspective Graph Neural Network (HIPGNN), a novel framework that integrates spectral and spatial perspectives. HIPGNN not only captures variation in spectral energy distribution to mitigate the “flattening out” phenomenon, but also captures the detailed interaction strengths between nodes from a spatial perspective to address weight heterogeneity. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that HIPGNN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, validating the importance of modeling weight heterogeneity and spectral energy distribution for effective weighted graph anomaly detection. © 2026

Title: The impact of omni-channel strategies on consumer behavior in sport product purchases
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study addresses the gap in understanding sports consumers' behavior regarding omni-channel strategies, with a focus on the moderating roles of customer experience and brand trust. Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and commitment-trust theory, a quasi-experimental omnichannel retail setting was utilized with a sample of 166 sports product consumers. The results indicate that consumer outcomes differ significantly across strategies for repurchase intention, customer satisfaction, and brand loyalty (p < .001, partial η2 ranging from 0.454 to 0.521). Specifically, following the logical progression of the consumer journey, Webrooming emerged as the primary driver for repurchase intention (M = 4.94), whereas the Online-to-Offline configuration was most effective in enhancing customer satisfaction (M = 4.96) and brand loyalty (M = 4.96). Scheffé's post-hoc tests revealed several significant pairwise differences, confirming that channel advantages are outcome-specific: digital research excels in driving intent, while integrated physical touchpoints are essential for securing relational outcomes. Customer experience and brand trust both significantly moderated the effects of omni-channel strategies on all three outcomes. In both cases, differences between strategies were more pronounced among consumers with lower experience and trust.This study elucidates the differential impacts of omni-channel strategies on sports product consumers and highlights the importance of methodological rigor, specifically post-stratification weighting as a robustness check, in enhancing the generalizability of retailing research. The substantive conclusions remained unchanged when the same models were re-estimated on the raked, weighted sample, confirming the stability of the findings under post-stratification adjustment. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Park C.
Author full names: Park, Chankook (55516647000)
Title: One count, three processes: Rethinking administrative stability in Korea's fuel-cell and renewable licensing pipeline
Abstract: Administrative amendment counts conflate recurrent filings, schedule revisions, and changes in project ownership or specification. This article develops a Frequency-Magnitude-Type framework for interpreting incomplete development records and identifying the additional information needed for monitoring. Applied to Korea's RPS-era generation-licensing pipeline, it combines action-specific filing counts, planned-deadline displacement, and filing types over common project-age windows. Rebuilding the April 2001-June 2026 ledger yields 4804 records and a dated panel of 1813 projects; principal comparisons use 1018 projects with closed three-year windows. Fuel cells and onshore wind show no statistically detectable difference in extension incidence or intensity, whereas onshore wind has 1.44 times the adjusted deadline displacement among projects with positive movement. Project-level joint analysis adds distinctions that separate technology comparisons conceal. Twenty projects record positive deadline movement without a preparation-period extension, and projects with exactly one extension exhibit different displacement distributions. Ownership-transfer tags further distinguish administrative histories within the same frequency groups. Missing deadlines are retained as missing information rather than unchanged schedules. The resulting profiles describe administrative activity, not commissioning, and direct attention to the records needed to investigate it. The historical case thus provides a recording and interpretation framework for monitoring emerging development regimes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Generative AI use and sustainable pedagogical practices as predictors of 4Cs skill development: The mediating role of digital literacy among international postgraduate students in China
Abstract: This study examines how Generative AI Use (GAU) and Sustainable Pedagogical Practices (SPP) are associated with international postgraduate students’ critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and communication (4Cs), with Digital Literacy (DL) examined as a mediator. Using survey data from 369 international Master’s and PhD students at China’s C9 League universities, this study applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) analysis. The 4Cs were modeled as a higher-order construct comprising four lower-order dimensions. The results show that both GAU and SPP are positively associated with students’ 4Cs, with SPP showing the largest standardized direct association. GAU and SPP are also positively associated with DL, which in turn is positively associated with the 4Cs. Significant indirect associations of both GAU and SPP with the higher-order 4Cs construct were observed through DL. The ANN results provide complementary predictive evidence, with SPP showing the highest normalized predictive importance, followed by GAU and DL. Together, the findings support a technology–pedagogy–capability perspective in which pedagogical design shows the largest standardized direct association with 4Cs development, while DL functions as a learner-side information-processing capability linking AI-supported and sustainability-oriented learning experiences with competence development. For practice, the findings suggest that universities may benefit from embedding generative AI within structured, sustainability-oriented learning activities that emphasize information verification, responsible use, and collaborative problem solving. These findings should be interpreted in light of the cross-sectional, self-report design and the specific context of international postgraduate students at China’s C9 League universities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Cazorla-Calderón S.; Pedregosa-Fauste S.; Fernández-García E.; Barrientos-Trigo S.; García-Díaz F.; González-Concepción M.

Title: Nursing faculty perspectives on integrating emerging technologies in undergraduate nursing education: A qualitative descriptive study
Abstract: Background: Emerging technologies (ET), including virtual, augmented, mixed, and extended reality alongside simulation-based tools, are increasingly available for undergraduate nursing education, yet their institutional and pedagogical integration remains uneven. Nursing faculty are central to this process, but their own experiences and perceptions of adopting ET have received limited empirical attention. Aim: To explore nursing faculty's experiences and perceptions of integrating emerging technologies into undergraduate nursing education. Design: Qualitative descriptive study with a contextual quantitative component. Settings: Three university nursing faculties in Spain. Participants: Twenty-two nursing faculty members. Methods: Three focus groups were conducted and analyzed using template analysis, a form of thematic analysis. An ad hoc questionnaire provided descriptive data on participants' self-reported experience with specific technologies, used to contextualize the qualitative findings. Results: Three themes emerged: Resources and Integration, Teaching and Learning, and Navigating the Digital Divide in Nursing Education. Faculty recognized the pedagogical value of ET, particularly of well-established tools such as high-fidelity simulation, but identified limited institutional support, unequal training opportunities, and concerns about preserving humanistic and relational aspects of care as central barriers. Low-cost technologies already accessible to most institutions were seen as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, theoretical instruction. Conclusions: Nursing faculty view emerging technologies as pedagogically valuable but constrained by institutional support, training, and equity considerations. Because this study captures the perspective of faculty only, future research should examine how nursing students experience these same tensions. © 2026

Title: Ambient-condition photocatalytic conversion of synthetic polymers to methane via a dual-source carbon and hydrogen strategy
Abstract: Petrochemical wastes possess significant potential as “urban carbon resources,” and the sustainable production of methane (CH4) from these wastes represents an important strategy for addressing global energy supply challenges. In this study, the photocatalytic conversion of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), used as a water-soluble model polymer, into CH4 was investigated using TiO2 photocatalysts loaded with PtOx (x = 0, 1) or PdOx (x = 0, 1) co-catalysts under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Among the prepared photocatalysts, PtOx-TiO2 exhibited the highest CH4 production activity, achieving a CH4 concentration of 9.95 µmol L−1, which was more than ten times higher than that of PdOx-TiO2. Analysis of gaseous reaction products suggested that CH4 formation proceeded via the methanation of CO2 generated during the photocatalytic oxidation of PVA. Furthermore, deuterium-labeling experiments revealed that the hydrogen atoms in CH4 originated from both PVA and water. These findings provide a proof-of-concept for a sustainable reaction design that converts polymer-derived carbon resources into fuel molecules through coupled degradation and hydrogenation reactions within a single photocatalytic system. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Wang W.; Cheng P.; Yan X.; Guan Y.; Xu X.; Cao Z.
Title: Integrated stockyard allocation and handling scheduling in dry bulk ports with mixed storage
Abstract: Efficient dry bulk terminal operations are essential to global supply chains for raw materials such as coal and ores, yet fugitive dust from open storage and handling remains an environmental challenge. Enclosed silos can reduce dust dispersion, yet prolonged silo storage may cause self-heating and spontaneous-combustion risks, requiring preventive silo-to-yard transfers before temperatures exceed safety thresholds. This paper studies an integrated stockyard allocation and handling scheduling problem in dry bulk ports with mixed storage, where open stockyards and a silo complex coexist. The problem jointly determines storage allocation, handling schedules, inventory evolution, silo temperature dynamics, and preventive transfer decisions to minimize total task dwell time and environmental protection costs from open stockyard storage. We propose a novel space–time–state network (STSN)-based mathematical formulation for this problem. By embedding temporal, spatial, and temperature-state transitions into feasible network paths, the formulation reduces reliance on auxiliary logical variables and big-M constraints, thereby improving computational tractability. Numerical experiments show that the proposed model reduces the objective value by 16.5% on average relative to the rule-based benchmark across the instance set. Compared with the MIP formulation, the STSN-based model proves optimality for all tested instances and reduces end-to-end runtime by 70.3% on average for the instances where both models reach optimality. The trade-off and capacity-sizing analyses further show that the model can quantify the balance between operational efficiency and open-storage environmental costs and support case-specific evaluations of open stockyard capacity under specified operational conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: From expectations to experience: How tasting plant-based fermented foods shapes consumption intentions
Abstract: Increasing consumption of plant-based fermented foods (PBFF) is beneficial for both public health and environment, yet intake among Western meat-eaters remains low. This study examined how sensory exposure to PBFF (sourdough bread, plant-based fermented dairy and meat alternatives), the timing of sensory exposure, and expected and actual liking influence intentions to increase PBFF consumption, and whether food neophobia moderates these effects. Data were collected over three weeks via an online pre-survey (n = 143), a laboratory experiment (n = 143), and an online post survey (n = 127). In the laboratory, participants were randomly assigned to either report their consumption intentions before tasting PBFF (n = 70) or after tasting PBFF (n = 73). Results showed that tasting PBFF attenuated the negative association between food neophobia and intention to increase consumption of PBFF. Patterns in the data suggested that intentions shifted at the first measurement following sensory exposure: participants who tasted before reporting intentions, changed intentions in the laboratory, whereas for those who reported intentions prior to tasting, changed intentions at follow-up. Product-specific patterns were observed: tasting increased intentions for the well-liked sourdough bread, but decreased intentions for the lesser-liked plant-based fermented meat. Sensory liking of the specific PBFF product was the strongest predictor of intentions for sourdough bread and plant-based fermented dairy, beyond expectations, whereas effects for plant-based fermented meat were weaker and less consistent. These findings highlight the importance of positive sensory experiences in shaping intentions to increase consumption of plant-based fermented foods, particularly among more food-neophobic meat-eaters. © 2026 The Authors

Author full names: Liu, Kai-Wayne (61012947100); Pang, Ryan Tian En (61013130100); Durongbhan, Pholpat (57208707418)
Title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study
Abstract: Background The weighted rich-club coefficient tests whether a network's most strongly connected nodes are preferentially interconnected. Its interpretation depends on two often-implicit choices: how the randomised comparison networks are constructed, and whether the hubs are re-identified in each comparison network or held fixed at those of the observed network. When hubs are defined by connection strength, these choices change what the coefficient tests. New method We examined how these choices affect inference using resting-state EEG from 20 people with Alzheimer's disease and 20 controls. Holding the data fixed, we compared four analysis pipelines, crossing two ways of building the comparison networks (global weight reshuffle or strength-conditioned null) with the two hub choices, and ran a calibration study using data constructed to contain no preferential hub coupling beyond nodal strength. Results An apparent eyes-open group difference in rich-club organisation appeared only under the pipeline combining a global weight reshuffle with re-identified hubs. Under the empirical resampling ensemble, that pipeline reported a group difference in 43% of pseudo-studies, always higher in the Alzheimer's disease group, while the other three stayed near the expected 5%. Comparison with existing methods Unlike global weight reshuffling, strength-conditioned nulls approximately preserve nodal strengths; fixing observed hubs also retains the identity of the core being tested. Conclusions The same data can support or dissolve an apparent rich-club difference depending on these choices. No single choice is universally correct, but reporting which were made, and why they fit the question being asked, is essential to interpreting the result. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Meier E.; Dubosson M.; Fragnière E.

Title: Shared but feared: A vulnerability-sensitive account of consumer responses to post-crisis service environments
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Shared service environments are typically designed to facilitate comfort, efficiency, and positive consumer experiences. In post-crisis contexts, however, these environments may also be appraised through concerns about exposure, controllability, and personal vulnerability. Building on a context-specific refinement of the organismic component within the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, this research examines how residual infection-related fear is associated with consumer responses to shared service environments in a post-pandemic context. A two-study design was implemented within a single French-language survey (N = 425). Study 1 tested whether residual infection-related fear was associated with avoidance of public service environments through differentiated forms of health anxiety. Structural equation modeling showed that residual infection-related fear was positively associated with both personal and interpersonal health anxiety, but only personal health anxiety was associated with avoidance, yielding a significant indirect effect through the self-focused pathway. Study 2 experimentally manipulated store density (high vs. low) and sanitary signals (present vs. absent) to examine how servicescape cues influenced perceived crowding and shopping satisfaction. Results showed that higher density reduced satisfaction, but this negative effect was attenuated when sanitary signals were present. Perceived crowding did not mediate the density–satisfaction relationship. A separate exploratory analysis indicated that the overall association between sanitary signals and satisfaction was more positive among individuals reporting higher residual infection-related fear. Taken together, the findings suggest that post-crisis responses to shared service environments may reflect the interplay between situational cues and heterogeneous vulnerability orientations, consistent with a vulnerability-sensitive appraisal system. The research offers a context-specific contribution to servicescape theory by suggesting that, under residual health-threat salience, organismic processes may require a more differentiated specification in contexts marked by residual threat, and by highlighting how visible safety-related cues may improve evaluations of dense service environments. Exploratory evidence further suggests that the overall association between such cues and satisfaction is more positive among consumers who remain more sensitive to infection-related risk. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Long J.; Zhao J.; Lin Y.; Li S.; Guo W.
Title: Multi-period interval optimization of a renewable steam-methanol system for uncertainty-aware industrial decarbonization
Abstract: Deep decarbonization of industrial steam systems is fundamentally constrained by renewable intermittency, fluctuating steam demand, and tightly coupled interactions among energy, hydrogen, and carbon-management processes. This work presents a representative-month-based interval MINLP framework for uncertainty-aware planning and operation of a renewable-integrated steam–methanol co-production (RE-ISMP) system. The framework integrates wind power, solar steam generation, water electrolysis, CO2 capture and utilization (CCU), and methanol synthesis within a multi-pressure steam network. Interval parameter programming is employed to address uncertainties in renewable resources and steam demand without requiring probability distributions. An interval mixed-integer nonlinear optimization framework solved through an interactive boundary decomposition strategy is developed to coordinate equipment configuration and representative-period operation, while the ε-constraint method is used to quantify the economic–environmental trade-off. Application to a practical refinery case demonstrates favorable economic and plant-gate carbon performance, reveals a transition toward intensified CCU deployment, and highlights methanol valorization as an economic compensation pathway under uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: When perception meets reality: explaining measured food waste through consumer behavior in a university dining hall
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Food waste (FW) in university dining halls generates significant environmental and economic impacts, yet most studies rely on self-reported measures and rarely combine behavioral perceptions with objective waste data. This study investigates the determinants of consumer FW by integrating individual plate-waste measurements with behavioral and dining-related factors in a university dining hall setting. Data were collected from 422 diners using a 31-item questionnaire, along with individual measurements of avoidable plate waste after meals. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Kruskal–Wallis tests were applied to examine behavioral relationships and differences across demographic and meal-related groups. Average plate waste reached 51.5 g per person, with higher waste levels observed during lunch and among female diners. Self-perceived waste behavior, intention to reduce FW, and sensory satisfaction were directly associated with the measured amount of discarded food. In contrast, consumer knowledge, portion size perception, and available eating time influenced only perceived waste behavior, revealing a disconnect between awareness and objectively measured PW. The findings highlight the importance of dining context and meal satisfaction in shaping consumer FW and demonstrate the value of integrating subjective perceptions with objective waste measurements. By combining behavioral evidence with direct waste quantification, this study advances methodological approaches to consumer FW research and provides insights for designing more effective waste reduction strategies in institutional food services. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Fu R.; Tang L.; Tian H.; Xia X.; Li H.
Title: Universal speech steganalysis via coupled-domain progressive fusion
Abstract: Existing universal speech steganalysis methods are generally constrained by an inherent trade-off between detection generalization across multiple steganographic encoding domains and domain-specific discriminative performance. This limitation is particularly pronounced in scenarios where heterogeneous encoding domains and diverse embedding strategies coexist. To address this, we propose a novel universal speech steganalysis scheme based on Coupled-Domain Progressive Fusion (CDPF), which constructs a correlation-aware, multi-level fusion strategy to alleviate information drift while preserving domain-specific cues. The scheme is inspired by the biological perfusion process, in which beneficial substances are progressively transmitted through microcirculatory pathways in an adaptive manner. First, to determine an optimal propagation order of informative patterns across domains, inter-domain associations are quantitatively characterized using the maximal information coefficient and cosine correlation coefficient, providing guidance for CDPF’s progressive fusion. Second, to extract domain-specific representations, CDPF incorporates encoding-domain decoupling blocks built on liquid neural networks with closed-form dynamics, enabling effective modeling of temporal dependencies in speech signals. Third, to achieve fine-grained inter-domain coupling, extracted features are adaptively fused via perfusion blocks leveraging deformable convolutional networks, facilitating flexible feature alignment. Fourth, to enhance discriminative capability for hard-to-distinguish samples, a heavy-tail expansion and projection block is introduced. Finally, a domain-consistent classifier is employed to jointly optimize and unify cross-domain representations. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that CDPF achieves consistently superior performance in both multi-domain and specific-domain detection scenarios, confirming its effectiveness and robustness for universal speech steganalysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Özdilek Ü.

Title: Balancing structural life and digital technologies: global evidence for a preventive policy model
Abstract: Objectives: Everyday life is increasingly mediated by digital technologies. These systems improve access and convenience but can also replace movement, sleep-protective routines and in-person participation. We examined whether the activity-cognition index changed gradually or showed a rapid transition as digital mediation expanded, and whether the proposed three-parameter model performed better than simpler alternatives. Methods: We analysed global annual data for 2000–2024. An activity-cognition index combined adult mobility, metabolic integrity (inverse obesity), cognition-related health burden and international learning performance. A digitality index combined Internet and mobile-broadband access, digital payments and remote work/education anchors. We compared the study-specific quartic benchmark with linear, quadratic, spline, segmented, logistic, calendar-time and autoregressive models, and examined annual changes, serial dependence and detrended early-warning indicators. Results: The digitality index increased from 0.060 to 0.680. The benchmark fold was 0.456, first crossed in 2016; observed A first became negative in 2017, and the 2024 benchmark equilibrium was -0.220. A digitality-based logistic transition fitted best (RMSE 0.063; leave-one-year-out RMSE 0.074), but a calendar-time logistic model fitted nearly as well (leave-one-year-out RMSE 0.082), and digitality correlated 0.998 with year. Raw variance and autocorrelation increased around the transition period but weakened after detrending. Conclusions: The series shows a marked nonlinear change in the mid-2010s, but it does not establish a causal or universal digitality threshold. The framework should serve as an exploratory monitoring tool that makes scale, model and temporal uncertainty visible and can be tested with national, local and service-specific data. © 2026

Authors: Li R.; Bu B.; Gao J.
Title: A diffusion-based framework for probabilistic communication performance degradation prediction in train control systems
Abstract: Train-ground data communication is the only channel for safety-critical information exchange in train control systems, and its degradation can directly threaten operational reliability. However, degradation prediction is challenging due to cross-layer coupled indicators, strong uncertainty, and partial observability caused by missing monitoring data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a diffusion-based framework for probabilistic communication performance degradation prediction. The framework reformulates degradation prediction as a two-stage task consisting of probabilistic forecasting of degradation-sensitive indicators under incomplete observations and degradation risk probability prediction through degradation-index-based mapping. In Stage-I, a Multi-Granularity Token Conditional Diffusion Model (MTCDM) sequentially reconstructs incomplete multivariate historical observations and forecasts the probabilistic future trajectories of three degradation-sensitive indicators. In Stage-II, a Degradation Risk Probability Prediction (DRPP) module maps forecasts into interpretable degradation states and risk probabilities. Three degradation-sensitive indicators are selected to characterize degradation at the physical, service, and application levels. Experiments on a real-world railway communication dataset and a public benchmark demonstrate superior reconstruction, forecasting, and degradation-aware risk prediction performance compared with baselines. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective solution for risk-aware communication degradation monitoring and proactive warning in safety-critical train control systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Do influence tactics matter? investigating prompt framing effects in LLM code generation
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software engineering workflows, helping developers write, debug, test, and maintain code. While prompt wording and structure are known to influence model performance, the impact of psychologically inspired prompt framings remains unexplored. This study investigates whether different psychology-based communication strategies that humans use to persuade or motivate others can lead to more effective prompt framing, which may, in turn, affect LLM behaviour in coding tasks. Drawing on Yukl & Falbe’s well-known taxonomy, we operationalized eight influence tactics (like rational persuasion, ingratiation, and exchange) into reproducible prompt templates. These prompt templates were evaluated across five leading open-weight LLMs using two widely adopted benchmarks: LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench Verified. We assessed the resulting code output on four key software quality dimensions: functional correctness, quality, maintainability, and security. Our results show that certain influence-induced prompt framings, particularly those emphasizing urgency, were associated with reduced correctness and security. This work presents the first large-scale empirical study of influence-induced prompt framing in software engineering tasks, offering insights into how linguistic cues may shape LLM outputs. Title: Attribution, zonation, and simulation of spatiotemporal distribution of negative oxygen ions in mountainous megacity: A case study of Chongqing, China
Abstract: Negative oxygen ions (NOI) are key indicators of urban ecological quality. However, NOI dynamics in mountainous megacities remain poorly understood. A key challenge lies in translating complex environmental observations into interpretable knowledge for environmental planning rather than prediction alone. Therefore, we integrated few-shot learning, explainable AI (e.g., SHapley Additive exPlanations), and causal inference within an explainable GeoAI framework to identify NOI drivers and predict spatial patterns in Chongqing, China. Results revealed pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, with low concentrations in southwestern urbanized areas and high values in forested mountains and river valleys of northeastern Chongqing. Attribution analysis identified elevation, curvature, relative humidity (RH), NO₂, and aerosol optical depth (AOD) as dominant drivers with model-derived nonlinear response thresholds (AOD > 273.67; NO₂ > 15.42; RH > 90.95%), beyond which predicted NOI responses changed markedly. Additionally, DML-based analysis estimated a positive treatment effect of middle elevations on NOI (+0.179 per unit, p < 0.001). Scenario simulations demonstrated that humidity enhancement and the integrated scenario yielded stronger responses than pollution mitigation or greening alone, and achieved a mean ΔNOI of 130.12 cm−3 with 76.25% of the area displaying gains. However, the integrated scenario increased inequality despite maximizing population-weighted benefits (106.99 cm−3), favoring sparsely populated mountainous regions (Gain = −28.76 cm−3, Gini = 0.0835). These findings underscore the capacity of explainable GeoAI for adaptive urban planning by linking environmental response interpretation, intervention evaluation, and spatial equity assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Modelling temporal thermal taste responses: Variability, thermal taster subgroups and potential mechanisms
Abstract: Thermal taste is a phenomenon where some individuals perceive taste sensations when temperature is applied to the tongue. Reported tastes vary across individuals and temperature ranges, but limitations in earlier phenotyping methods made it difficult to explore underlying mechanisms. The RapCoTT approach addresses this by capturing real-time taste reports at the approximate stimulation temperature. This study analysed data from three RapCoTT studies (including previously published data in Botha et al., 2021) to examine relationships between reported tastes and temperature, using model-based clustering to identify patterns in thermal taster responses. From responses of 230 respondents, three distinct subgroups emerged. Cluster 1 (C1) often reported salty taste, either with any taste except metallic (State 4) or with metallic (State 2). Cluster 2 (C2) showed sour (State 2), savoury (State 4), and metallic (State 3) responses. Cluster 3 (C3) featured bitter taste combined with dominant sweet (State 2), metallic (State 5), or sour (State 3). By identifying critical temperatures where specific tastes or combinations occurred, this study highlighted potential temperature-sensitive receptor mechanisms underlying thermal tastes, in particular TRPA1 and TRPM5, but also TRPM4, TRPV4, TRPV1 and TMC4 and the need for research to understand potential variation in the identified receptors and thermal taste phenotype. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Conventional salmon or novel salmon alternatives? An evaluation of consumers' perceptions and stated willingness to eat across different salmon concepts in Switzerland
Abstract: In response to public concern about human health, fish welfare, and the environment, the salmon industry is seeking alternative ways of producing salmon with novel technologies such as land-based recirculated aquaculture systems, cell cultivation, and 3D printing. We conducted an online study to investigate consumers' attitudes towards different salmon production techniques. A total of 237 participants from Switzerland evaluated five salmon concepts (i.e., wild-caught, ocean-farmed, land-farmed 3D-printed cultured, and 3D-printed plant-based salmon), which were presented together with one of two final salmon product images (i.e., salmon fillet vs. sticks). Both qualitative data (initial association related to concerns and benefits) and quantitative data (evaluation facets) were assessed. The quantitative findings showed that the wild-caught salmon concept was the most favored with ocean- and land-based salmon concepts in second place. For the 3D-printed cultured and 3D-printed plant-based salmon concepts, participants stated the lowest stated willingness to eat. Fish attachment positively predicted stated willingness to eat for the land-based salmon concept. Concern about the environment and climate change positively predicted stated willingness to eat for the 3D-printed plant-based salmon concept. Food technology neophobia negatively predicted stated willingness to eat for the salmon alternative concepts. In addition, age was negatively associated with stated willingness to eat for the 3D-printed cultured and 3D-printed plant-based salmon concepts. Future salmon production and relevant research should therefore not only consider how to meet consumers' expectations on food healthiness, tastiness, and environmental friendliness but also focus on developing strategies for addressing food technology neophobia and building trust among consumers. © 2026

Title: Depressive symptoms, coping skills, and the perception of barriers to psychological treatment among college students
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: College students experience psychological symptoms at a concerning rate but infrequently access psychological treatment. However, research in this context has been incredibly limited, and the psychological factors related to perceptions of barriers to treatment are not well understood. We set out to provide an evaluation of the perceived prevalence of common barriers to psychological care, considering how perceptions of barriers are associated with depression symptoms and coping skills. Our findings were consistent with depressive symptoms being associated with greater perceived subjective and objective barriers. Interpersonal skills demonstrated small negative associations with stigma, treatment concerns, and perceived access barriers, and mindfulness skill was negatively associated with both stigma and perceived access barriers. Emotionally impaired coping was positively related to both stigma and treatment concerns. However, behavioral and cognitive skills were not correlated with any perceived barriers. We also considered how coping skills and depression symptoms interacted to predict perceptions of barriers. We found two significant interactions for perceived access barriers specifically. When cognitive or behavioral skills were greater, psychological symptoms were more strongly related to barrier perceptions. This suggests that those with greater coping skills perceive more barriers to treatment when experiencing elevated depressive symptoms compared to those with more limited coping skills. Findings from this study provide an initial characterization of barrier perceptions among college students and have the potential to inform efforts to increase treatment seeking among college students. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Authors: Qi G.; Liu G.; Zhao J.; Zhou Q.
Title: GLAM: Unifying global–local graph geometry via asymmetric mutual learning
Abstract: Real-world graphs exhibit both global homogeneity and rich local heterogeneity. Existing graph neural networks (GNNs) typically embed nodes into a single constant-curvature space, such as Euclidean or hyperbolic, ignoring geometric diversity and lacking sufficient modeling capacity for mixed structures. Although some works employ product or pseudo-Riemannian manifolds, these spaces remain homogeneous and cannot adapt to local geometric variations. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel Global–Local Asymmetric Mutual Learning Graph Neural Network (GLAM), comprising a local heterogeneous model (LeGNN), a global homogeneous model (GoGNN), and an asymmetric mutual learning module (AMLM). At the local level, LeGNN dynamically assigns each node a learnable constant-curvature Riemannian manifold via inter-layer smoothing constraints and achieves personalized modeling of microscopic topological patterns. At the global level, GoGNN efficiently utilizes a homogeneous manifold to characterize macroscopic structural patterns, providing a consistent topological view for the overall framework. Finally, AMLM performs a complementary fusion of geometric representations across multiple scales. Experiments on multiple benchmarks for node classification and link prediction show that GLAM performs competitively across both tasks, while exhibiting more pronounced advantages on link prediction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Uncovering emotion dynamics across human–AI interaction modes in programming: Evidence from facial expression and electrodermal activity
Abstract: Emotions play a fundamental role in learning by shaping learners' cognitive engagement and influencing learning outcomes. In generative AI (GAI)-supported programming, learners interact with AI in different ways. However, limited research has examined how different interaction modes are associated with learners' emotional dynamics. This study investigated students' emotions across three human–AI interaction modes (i.e., AI-reliant, AI-independent, and human–AI hybrid) during AI-assisted programming. A total of 150 undergraduate students completed programming tasks with access to ChatGPT, during which video recordings of their facial expressions and electrodermal activity (EDA) were collected. Facial expressions were analyzed to examine both emotion distributions and temporal transitions using lag sequential analysis, while EDA was used to measure affective arousal. Results reveal that none of the seven facial-expression categories differed significantly across the three modes. Lag sequential analysis uncovers that the three modes shared reciprocal anger ↔ disgust, fear ↔ surprise, and neutral ↔ sadness transitions. Descriptively, the AI-reliant mode showed transitions between positive and negative emotions, the AI-independent mode showed a relatively neutral-centered transition network, and the human-AI hybrid mode demonstrated a relatively surprise-centered transition network. However, none of the transition probabilities differed significantly across modes. In terms of EDA analysis, the hybrid mode exhibited significantly more skin conductance responses (SCRs) in total and significantly more SCRs per minute than the AI-reliant mode. These findings suggest that emotion states can serve as signals for understanding how learners engage with GAI during programming. The study highlights the importance of designing emotion-aware AI-supported programming environments that balance technological assistance and learners’ emotional engagement in problem-solving. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zeng G.; Fang Y.; Wu L.
Title: The impact of consumer culture positioning on multinational brand premium: The moderating role of global identity
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Multinational brands often charge higher prices in emerging markets than in their home markets. Although such multinational brand premiums can improve profitability, they may also invite consumers to compare prices across countries and evaluate the premium as unfair. This research examines how consumer culture positioning (CCP) shapes consumers' willingness to pay a multinational brand premium through price fairness perceptions, operationalized as perceived price unfairness, and how this process depends on consumers' global identity. Across a pretest and three experiments in China, we compare Global Consumer Culture Positioning (GCCP) with Local Consumer Culture Positioning (LCCP) in a multinational restaurant-brand context. Experiment 1 establishes the main effect of CCP and the mediating role of perceived price unfairness. Experiment 2 replicates this pathway and examines chronic global identity as a boundary condition. Experiment 3 further tests the moderation through situationally activated global versus local identity. The results generally show that GCCP, relative to LCCP, reduces perceived price unfairness and increases willingness to pay a premium. The fairness-based indirect effect becomes stronger as chronic global identity increases and when global identity is situationally activated. The findings integrate global branding and pricing research by showing when cultural positioning can make a higher price appear more acceptable rather than merely enhance brand image. The study also provides managerial implications for multinational and local brands operating in emerging retail and service markets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Geopolitical risk and tourism firm resilience: Global evidence
Abstract: This paper analyzes how geopolitical risk affects the performance of tourism firms and identifies the conditions under which its adverse effects are mitigated. Using a global panel of 1438 firms across 39 countries from 2007 to 2021, we find that heightened geopolitical risk significantly reduces firms’ market valuations. Drawing on risk perception theory, network theory, and institutional theory, we show that this effect is conditional rather than uniform. Specifically, firms located in countries with stronger international tourism network embeddedness experience weaker negative effects, as network connectivity facilitates demand diversification and adaptive responses. Similarly, higher institutional quality reduces the adverse impact of geopolitical risk by enhancing stability and policy credibility. These findings are robust to alternative measures and estimation methods. The paper provides new evidence on the transmission of geopolitical risk and highlights the role of structural and institutional factors in shaping resilience in the global tourism sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Complex post-traumatic stress disorder in patients initially diagnosed with idiopathic hypersomnia: a case series

Abstract: Objectives: The etiology of hypersomnia remains largely unknown, while the concept of complex post-traumatic stress disorder has recently emerged in the field of psychotraumatology. This case series comprises 17 consecutive patients previously diagnosed with idiopathic hypersomnia based on clinical and neurophysiological evaluations, all of whom underwent psychological and psychometric evaluations. Inferential comparisons between the CPTSD and non-CPTSD groups were exploratory and did not reach statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons. Descriptively, patients with CPTSD showed higher trauma-related and anger-related symptom scores. Dissociative symptoms also showed a descriptive difference, although interpretation was substantially limited by missing data in the non-CPTSD group. Conclusions: This case series suggests that some cases of pathological hypersomnolence might be associated with traumatic disorders. Hypersomnolence may represent a response to traumatic memories, particularly in patients with complex traumatic histories, such as childhood abuse. Title: Successful modal reasoning depends on WHAT went WHERE
Abstract: Modal reasoning requires quantifying over possibilities (e.g., categorizing events as necessary, possible, and impossible). This suite of abilities matures during the preschool years, but toddlers perform better in some modal reasoning tasks than others. We propose that these mixed findings reflect a cognitive distinction: toddlers perform worse when reasoning about ambiguous locations of objects (WHERE) than when reasoning about ambiguous kinds of objects (WHAT). In Experiments 1 and 2, we directly compared these forms of ambiguity using matched tasks. Consistent with the hypothesis, toddlers performed substantially better when reasoning about ambiguous kinds than ambiguous locations. Experiment 3 revealed a similar asymmetry in language comprehension, with preschool children showing better comprehension of modal terms such as “can” and “have to” in a What-based task than in a Where-based task. Thus, modal reasoning emerges earlier than previously suggested, and diversity in results reflects differences in how kind and location information are represented and processed. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A bladder microenvironment-adaptive ceria nanozyme hydrogel enables urea-responsive intravesical chemo-immunotherapy
Abstract: Bladder cancer intravesical therapy remains limited by rapid urinary washout, insufficient penetration across the bladder mucosal barrier, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we developed a bladder microenvironment-adaptive chemo-immunotherapy system, Gel/UCeNZ/Gem/CpG, to improve local bladder cancer treatment. In this system, urease-modified CeO2 nanozymes (UCeNZ), gemcitabine (Gem), and CpG oligodeoxynucleotide (CpG ODN) were incorporated into an injectable thermosensitive adhesive hydrogel. After intravesical administration, the hydrogel rapidly formed a mucosa-adherent depot, thereby prolonging bladder residence and enabling sustained therapeutic release. Meanwhile, UCeNZ responded to endogenous urinary urea to enhance particle transport and mucosal penetration, improving local drug exposure beyond passive instillation. Functionally, CeO2-mediated redox regulation amplified Gem-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, and immunogenic cell death-associated signaling, as evidenced by HMGB1 translocation/release, calreticulin exposure, and intracellular ATP dysregulation. CpG ODN further promoted dendritic cell maturation and strengthened T cell-mediated antitumor immunity. In an orthotopic bladder cancer model, Gel/UCeNZ/Gem/CpG significantly suppressed tumor progression, prolonged survival, increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, reduced regulatory T cells and M2-like macrophages, and enhanced memory/effector-like T cell activation without obvious systemic toxicity. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed coordinated regulation of oxidative stress, apoptosis, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling, T cell activation, PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint signaling, and p53-related tumor-suppressive pathways. Overall, this study presents a bladder-adaptive intravesical chemo-immunotherapy strategy that integrates mucosal retention, urea-responsive penetration, redox-amplified immunogenic chemotherapy, and immune microenvironment remodeling for bladder cancer treatment. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Lei Y.; Ma P.; Zhou W.; Cai H.; Chen C.; Wen J.
Title: LMGNN: Long-range graph modeling for recommender systems
Abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become a dominant paradigm for collaborative filtering by propagating signals over user–item interaction graphs. Yet, two fundamental issues remain: (i) shallow propagation fails to capture informative long-range collaborative signals, while deep propagation tends to homogenize representations and causes over-smoothing; and (ii) global attention can be computationally expensive and may weaken structural inductive bias. In this work, we propose a depth-adaptive long-range graph collaborative filtering framework that treats multi-hop GNN representations as an ordered sequence along the depth axis and learns node-specific fusion weights via a degree-conditioned Mamba depth-gating network. Moreover, to enhance robustness without perturbing the sparse interaction graph, we construct a contrastive view by perturbing only the depth-fusion gate rather than applying dropout to depth tokens. Concretely, in the common two-depth case, we reformulate depth fusion as a sigmoid gate and perform lightweight stochastic and adversarial perturbations on the gate logits, while reusing the same propagation content. The overall objective combines a pairwise ranking loss with regularization and an importance-sampled InfoNCE regularizer. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that LMGNN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines (up to 20.82%), validating the effectiveness of our proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
