Title: Predicting the future of retail services: Trends, technologies, and strategic imperatives for 2025–2035
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The rapid convergence of digital platforms and shifting consumer behaviors is driving an unprecedented structural transformation across the global retail landscape. This paper examines the systemic evolution of retail channel revenue distributions and operational capabilities, establishing the critical strategic imperatives required to navigate market disruption over the 2025–2035 horizons. The primary objective of this study is to empirically model the longitudinal shifts between traditional physical retail, e-commerce, and physical channels, while concurrently diagnosing the capability gaps across diverse corporate scales. Methodologically, this research deploys a mixed-methods empirical framework, integrating a quantitative survey of 418 retail industry professionals with qualitative interviews from 32 senior executives across six countries, analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA. The empirical findings reveal a definitive market polarization: traditional physical retail is projected to contract significantly from 54.3% to 30.8%, while e-commerce expands to claim a dominant 52.7% revenue share by 2035. Our multi-method analysis validates that digital-physical integration and AI-driven personalization (β = 0.38, p < .001) directly resolve post-pandemic operational vulnerabilities, emerging as the primary drivers of future performance outcomes. Longitudinal analysis confirms a steady decline in traditional commodity metrics, while scenario simulations warn that small and medium-sized enterprises face a severe (66.5%) market share loss under unmitigated polarization. To address this structural market polarization, this study provides a rigorous, data-driven defense by establishing the Retail Evolution Framework (REF) to explain how systemic retail survival requires aligning operational tools with shifting institutional norms. The study bridges the dynamic capabilities gap under the Resource-Based View while offering actionable strategies for ethical data governance. Practically, these insights provide an actionable investment roadmap for corporate managers to redirect capital allocations from physical footprint expansion into automated data ecosystems and cloud-based logistics architectures to maintain long-term competitive viability. © 2026

Title: Authentication and key agreement mechanisms for internet of drones: A novel taxonomy, critical review, and experimental performance analysis
Abstract: The continuous progress and distinct capabilities have led the Internet of Drones (IoD) to be a persuasive paradigm that offers promising advantages across various applications, spanning from defense to civilian uses. Despite its manifold benefits, it is essential to highlight that it also faces several challenges, and security remains a critical concern that can hold back its widespread adoption. Stringent authentication mechanism design has appeared as one of the favorable techniques for tackling distinct security attacks in IoD networks. This survey presents a detailed review of existing literature, focusing on authentication protocols explicitly designed for securing communication in IoD networks. Recognising the growing complexity and diversity of communication, we present a novel multi-layered taxonomy that offers a comprehensive roadmap for classifying authentication mechanisms across the IoD stack. The presented taxonomy interactively maps each authentication technique to its system roles, cryptographic foundations, and operational context within the IoD network to demonstrate a more holistic understanding of prevalent authentication mechanisms. Drawing from our presented taxonomy, we highlight the compelling contributions and acknowledge the potential limitations of the recent literature. We compare the security and resistance to common attacks of prevalent protocols while highlighting their advantages and limitations. Based on the security analysis, we shortlist protocols for full-scale implementation that exhibit the highest security coverage. We then present a detailed experimental analysis of these selected protocols against various metrics (i.e., CPU execution time, memory consumption, etc.) using a Holybro QAV250 quadcopter drone-based testbed setup. Title: Spectral-temporal dual view graph convolutional networks: A deep learning framework for dynamic bipartite graphs
Abstract: Dynamic bipartite graphs (DBGs) are widely used in real-world scenarios, where representation learning is particularly challenging due to the heterogeneity of node types and the temporal evolution of interactions. A key difficulty lies in jointly capturing non-stationary micro-level preference dynamics and macro-level stable structural evolution. Existing methods typically focus on either temporal dependency modeling or structural pattern extraction. For instance, recurrent or attention-based temporal models struggle to capture abrupt, short-term preference shifts, while spectral or structure-oriented approaches emphasize long-term regularities but overlook fine-grained dynamic variations. This imbalance becomes especially pronounced in scenarios with sparse interactions or sudden behavioral changes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a spectral-temporal dual-view framework, ST-DYB, for DBG representation learning. By explicitly decoupling macro-level structural evolution and micro-level preference dynamics, the model captures complementary heterogeneous patterns from two perspectives. A cross-view adaptive fusion mechanism further integrates these representations, enabling effective modeling of both implicit preference dependencies and temporal dynamics. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that ST-DYB consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in dynamic link prediction and node classification tasks, validating the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed dual-view modeling paradigm. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Do you need to add (con)text to the equation? Subject-related, linguistic, and contextual factors in competence-oriented assessment
Abstract: Background: The growing emphasis on competence-oriented school assessments requires tests with more complex descriptions of real-life situations. Aims: This study examines how linguistic, subject-related, and contextual task characteristics influence the empirical difficulty of reality-based assessment tasks. Sample: The participants were 786 lower secondary school pupils from three comprehensive schools in a federal state in Germany. Methods: In the experiment, three different language versions and three mathematical tasks were developed for 15 German-language factual texts and used in paper-and-pencil tests with a rotational design. Results: The results of the generalized linear mixed models showed that mathematical and linguistic task factors significantly affect empirical task difficulty, although no interactions were found. The real-life context of the tasks proved to be relevant, as students' interest in respective contexts significantly influenced task success. Title: Cognitive flexibility as a bridge between depressive symptoms and problematic smartphone use in adolescents: A two-wave network analysis across depression-severity groups
Abstract: The co-occurrence of depressive symptoms and problematic smartphone use (PSU) in adolescents poses a growing public health concern, but its component-level conditional associations, cross-wave patterns, and variation across depression-severity groups remain insufficiently understood. Using a two-wave observational design with a 12-month interval (N = 1200 students from one high school in a county of Gansu Province, China), this study integrated Gaussian graphical modeling (GGM), network comparison testing (NCT), and latent profile analysis (LPA). Cognitive Flexibility showed the largest absolute bridge expected influence at both waves, and the ranking was unchanged when the comparison was restricted to nodes measured at the same level of aggregation. NCT detected no significant global difference between the T1 and T2 contemporaneous networks, although several local cross-community edges differed between the two estimates. LPA retained four nearly parallel, severity-ordered classes at both waves, interpreted as depression-severity groups rather than qualitatively distinct profiles. Subgroup bootstrap analyses showed acceptable edge-weight accuracy; expected-influence CS coefficients ranged from 0.286 to 0.750, whereas all bridge-expected-influence CS coefficients were below 0.25, so the subgroup findings are confined to cross-community connectivity. Between-group differences in cross-community connectivity persisted after equal-n down-sampling. These findings should be interpreted in light of the observational design, single-school convenience sample, and reliance on self-report measures. Cognitive flexibility nevertheless emerged as a consistent cross-community correlate in the overall networks and warrants further longitudinal and intervention evaluation rather than being regarded as an established intervention target. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Survival of Contractor Consortiums in the Road Construction Industry during Economic Crisis

Abstract: Road construction industries worldwide are periodically exposed to economic crises, which are cyclical in nature and often characterized by high inflation, currency depreciation, resource shortages, and institutional inefficiencies. In such conditions, traditional procurement methods frequently struggle to maintain project continuity, prompting the emergence of local contractor consortiums as a more resilient alternative. This study examines how contractor consortiums in the road construction sector adapted to recent economic crises and sustained operations amid unprecedented challenges. A qualitative research approach was adopted, involving 14 semistructured interviews with industry experts. Manual content analysis identified key adaptive measures, including financial pooling, shared equipment and labor, agile internal coordination, and proactive engagement with public authorities. These mechanisms enabled many consortiums to continue project delivery despite severe economic and operational constraints. However, the effectiveness of these measures was constrained by rigid legal and contractual frameworks, limited digital integration, fragmented stakeholder collaboration, and delayed institutional responses. To enhance future resilience, the study recommends modernizing contractual systems, strengthening digital adoption, and improving public-private coordination. Title: Research on multi-objective optimization of hard-rock shield tunnelling parameters for cutterhead performance enhancement
Abstract: Hard-rock shield tunnelling involves inherent trade-offs among excavation efficiency, cutterhead loading, and energy consumption, making operational parameter selection a challenging multi-objective problem. This study develops an integrated prediction–interpretation–optimization–decision-making framework for cutterhead performance enhancement using field data from a hard-rock section of the Shenzhen–Shanwei Intercity Railway. Penetration per Revolution (PPR), Cutterhead Wear Pressure (CWP), and Total Cutterhead Power (TCP) are adopted to represent excavation efficiency, wear-related loading, and energy consumption, respectively. Bayesian Optimization-based Random Forest models establish nonlinear mappings between operational parameters and cutterhead responses, achieving testing-set R2 values of 0.9974, 0.9891, and 0.8228 for PPR, CWP, and TCP. SHAP analysis shows that advance rate and cutterhead rotational speed dominate PPR and TCP, whereas thrust-pressure distribution governs CWP. NSGA-II, MOEA/D, and MOPSO are jointly employed, and their Pareto solutions are integrated through non-dominated sorting to improve solution diversity and front coverage. TOPSIS identifies the final compromise solution. Compared with mean field conditions, the optimized scheme increases PPR by 67.1 % while reducing CWP and TCP by 1.56 % and 12.94 %, respectively, demonstrating effective coordinated optimization of cutterhead performance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Institutional resilience and land-acquisition governance: Participation and conflict-management mechanisms in the Jakarta–Bandung High-Speed Railway project

Buffering capacity and adaptive capacity were positively related to governance performance, while learning capacity showed no significant relationship. Title: Exploring the Dissolution-enhancement Functionality of Poloxamer 407 in Cilostazol Tablets Prepared by Different Manufacturing Techniques

Title: The location logic of informal retail: dual-scale evidence from street food vendors in Hangzhou
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Street food vendors (SFVs) form an important part of nighttime retail supply in cities. However, they operate without fixed premises and change locations over time. Understanding these patterns is essential for designating vending sites and planning the nighttime economy. Focusing on nighttime SFVs in the main urban districts of Hangzhou, this study applies an XGBoost, SHAP, and GAM framework with spatial autocorrelation analysis at the block and street scales. The analysis identifies associated factors, differences across scales, and spatial alignment between designated sites and actual SFV locations. At the block scale, SFV distribution is positively associated with working population density, shop rent, and metro accessibility, converging on mature commercial cores. At the street scale, associations shift toward micro-scale nodes such as metro entrances and parking facilities. Designated sites and actual locations align globally but diverge locally. These findings extend the discussion of classical retail location theory to informal retail. Fixed premises, rental arrangements, and purposive consumption may take different forms in informal settings. Their relevance therefore requires explicit consideration. The findings support a spatial guidance strategy combining block-scale zoning with street-scale site allocation, offering empirical grounding for nighttime economy planning and urban governance. © 2026

Title: TiDISC: A titans-inspired disentangled spectral memory-augmented contrastive model for dynamic graphs
Abstract: Dynamic graph representation learning is essential for modeling evolving dependencies in complex networks. Existing methods commonly encode temporal interactions as a unified sequence, which makes it difficult to distinguish slowly varying trends from rapidly varying event dynamics and increases vulnerability to shortcut patterns induced by repetitive interactions. To address these limitations, TiDISC, a Titans-inspired Disentangled Spectral Memory-augmented Contrastive model, is proposed. TiDISC first constructs adaptive leakage-safe historical contexts. Temporal Scaling Co-occurrence Attention (TSCA) then encodes recurrence-aware structural priors while discouraging excessive reliance on direct counting cues. The resulting tokens are organized into patches, and a Trend–Event Disentangled Filter (TEDF) constructs complementary trend-oriented and event-oriented representations through energy-guided spectral routing. A heterogeneous dual-stream encoder uses Titans-inspired implicit MLP attention to model long-range trends without reproducing the complete Titans memory system. A strictly causal convolutional branch captures short-term event bursts. A Trend–Event Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) decoder performs pair-specific routing between trend and event evidence for link prediction. Spectral-Augmented Contrastive Learning (SACL) further improves robustness through complementary structural perturbations and branch-specific spectral jitter. Experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that TiDISC achieves the strongest overall ranking under transductive evaluation and remains competitive across diverse inductive link prediction settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A soft computing-driven modelling approach to investigate Nipah virus transmitted diseases

Abstract: In this study, we have developed an integrated scientific machine-learning framework to characterize the hidden drivers of Nipah virus transmission, a zoonotic pathogen with complex multi-host ecology. We construct a deterministic compartmental model that captures the principal infection pathways and rigorously analyze its biological and structural properties. Numerical simulations using Python's odeint solver validate the theoretical results. To quantify the dominant forces shaping disease propagation, we perform a global sensitivity analysis based on partial rank correlation coefficients. We further employ a Multilayer Perceptron Neural Network (MLPNN) that learns the underlying vector field of the ODE system, enabling it to act as a computationally efficient surrogate operator that faithfully reproduces the mechanistic dynamics. This neural surrogate accurately reconstructs trajectories comparable to the classical solver, providing a flexible, data-driven tool for rapid prediction, simulation, and scenario exploration without repeatedly integrating the original ODEs. Augmenting this, a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based optimization procedure is used to minimize the basic reproduction number (R0) by tuning the dominant parameters, yielding control strategies that remain robust under variation in initial conditions. Title: Context matters in just culture: Translating formal just culture into lived near-miss reporting experience in maritime transportation
Abstract: In onboard environments characterised by high operational risk, near-miss reporting is an important mechanism for identifying latent risks, preventing accidents and supporting organisational improvement. However, there remains limited empirical understanding of whether the just culture advocated in formal systems can be translated into the lived reporting experience of seafarers who are willing, able and motivated to report near-miss incidents on a sustained basis. To address this issue, this study draws on semi-structured interviews with seafarers and shore-based managers. Six interrelated themes are identified: ease of reporting, motivation to report, trust, reporting independence, feedback and acknowledgement. The findings indicate that near-miss reporting is more likely to occur in organisational contexts where reporting is accessible, safe and worthwhile. Complicated procedures, paperwork burdens and hierarchical pressure weaken seafarers’ willingness to report, whereas simplified procedures, fair management, low exposure communication channels, timely feedback and positive acknowledgement help strengthen reporting willingness and promote experience sharing. This study provides context-specific empirical evidence on how formal just culture is translated into frontline reporting practice and offers practical insights that may inform efforts to improve near-miss reporting, reduce reporting concerns and strengthen closed-loop feedback in comparable organisational or cultural settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Peripheral arylation engineering for high-performance non-doped blue OLEDs based on phenanthroimidazole-anthracene hybrids
Abstract: Developing high-performance non-doped blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) remains a formidable challenge due to the trade-off among efficiency, color purity, and device stability. Title: Different knowledge, different aesthetic experiences (and vice versa)?
Abstract: Do different kinds of knowledge lead to different aesthetic experiences (and vice versa)? This paper addresses this question by examining the role of (art) knowledge within an interactionist perspective. Contemporary theories increasingly conceptualize aesthetic experience as emerging from the interaction between perceiver, stimuli, and contexts rather than from isolated properties of artworks or perceivers alone. Despite this theoretical shift, empirical research still often investigates knowledge as a characteristic of perceivers. We argue for a broader and more integrative understanding of knowledge that distinguishes between internal knowledge, residing within the perceiver, and external knowledge, provided by the environment. Internal knowledge encompasses prior experiences, competencies, and beliefs, whereas external knowledge includes information embedded in contextual features such as exhibition settings, curatorial texts, and other environmental cues. Drawing on empirical literature and illustrative findings from museum and laboratory studies, we show that aesthetic experiences are shaped by the continuous interaction between these two forms of knowledge. External knowledge can activate relevant internal knowledge, guide expectations, and support interpretation, while internal knowledge influences how viewers engage with artworks, seek additional information, and construct meaning. This reciprocal process can generate new insights that become incorporated into future knowledge structures, thereby influencing subsequent aesthetic encounters. Our perspective aligns with phenomenological perspectives emphasizing situated and embodied engagement with the world. We conclude that variations in aesthetic experiences give rise to differences in knowledge (and vice versa), and more specifically, that this is due to the interaction between internal and external forms of knowledge during aesthetic experiences. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Synergistic Integration of Building Information Modeling and Integrated Project Delivery using Multi-Criteria Decision-Making for Project Performance Evaluation: Case Studies in the Oil and Gas Industry

Abstract: Despite the prevalence of traditional project delivery methods such as Design-Bid-Build, these approaches often suffer from fragmentation between planning and construction phases, leading to inefficiencies. To address these limitations, Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) has emerged as a collaborative approach that, when combined with Building Information Modeling (BIM), can significantly enhance project outcomes. However, the application of this integrated approach in complex Oil, Gas, and Petrochemical projects remains underexplored. This research investigates the synergistic integration of BIM and IPD to develop a novel project delivery framework tailored for the OGP industry. The study utilizes a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making method, specifically TOPSIS, to evaluate Key Performance Indicators and validate the proposed framework. Title: Anger regulation scale for adolescents (ARS-A): Psychometric properties of the Portuguese version and its associations with emotion regulation, depression, and anxiety

Title: When health labels increase indulgent food purchase intention

Title: Managing Perils at Sea: a diagnostic analysis of occupational hazards among small-scale fishers in India’s southern coasts
Abstract: Marine fishing is a high-risk occupation that sustains the livelihoods of coastal communities worldwide. This study highlights the occupational hazards associated with marine fishing, drawing on an empirical case study of the high-intensity, multi-day offshore fishing sector in southern India. Following the FAO/ILO/IMO joint framework on occupational health and safety of fishers, our research revealed significant deficiencies in the adoption of safety devices, communication technologies, and navigation systems by sample fishers in the study areas. These gaps, compounded by weak regulatory enforcement and low insurance coverage, pose substantial risks, exacerbated by climate change. The findings underscore the need for targeted interventions—including awareness campaigns, training, and financial aid—to foster a robust safety culture and mitigate economic barriers, leading to improved fisher safety and well-being in the coastal regions of India. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Distributed maximum clique computation via clique-preserving partitioning and vertex replication
Abstract: The maximum clique problem is a fundamental NP-hard problem in graph theory. Despite advances in exact and heuristic solvers, their performance on large graphs is limited by irregular search spaces, strong sequential dependencies in pruning, and pronounced load imbalance. Parallel execution is therefore necessary to address these challenges, but achieving high performance without degrading solution quality is nontrivial. Additional experiments with a fundamentally different maximum clique solver indicate that the framework is largely independent of the underlying clique-search strategy. We further provide theoretical guarantees that characterize when graph partitioning preserves the maximum clique and quantify the replication required to recover cliques fragmented by partitioning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Mitigating cascading failures through intentional line removal: A conditional reinforcement learning approach
Abstract: Cascading failures in power networks pose critical challenges to system resiliency, as they can trigger widespread blackouts through the uncontrolled propagation of failures. This paper proposes a novel conditional reinforcement learning approach to mitigate cascading failures via strategic transmission line tripping. Our method combines: (1) an interaction learning module that quantifies failure dependencies between network lines, and (2) a deep Q-network (DQN) architecture that integrates real-time failure probabilities as conditional inputs for remedial action selection. This work advances the integration of physics-informed deep reinforcement learning by explicitly modeling inter-component dependencies to derive real-time mitigation strategies that improve power system resilience. We train the framework using a cascading failure simulator built on the IEEE 300-bus, 118-bus, and 57-bus systems, and evaluate line-tripping actions using DC optimal power-flow analysis. The proposed algorithm’s input is the state of the power network, and the output is the transmission line whose tripping mitigates the unfolding cascading failure. Experimental results demonstrate that our conditional reinforcement learning method reduces cascade sizes and failed power compared to no-action baselines, outperforming standard Q-learning in reducing cascade size. Furthermore, experimental evaluations under modified network topologies and AC power flow conditions verify the robustness of the proposed approach. Representative scenarios are also provided to illustrate the step-by-step mitigation process. Finally, an analysis of decision latency highlights the severe impact of delayed line tripping, underscoring the critical necessity for real-time control algorithms. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Bai X.; Liu J.; Su Y.; Wang X.; Zhang X.; Li J.
Title: Assessment of biomass resource utilization and greenhouse gas mitigation potential in Xinjiang
Abstract: Biomass energy offers a renewable pathway to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while supporting energy security. This study assesses the collectable, utilizable, and GHG mitigation potentials of five biomass resource categories (crop residues, forest residues, animal manure, municipal solid waste, and sewage sludge) in Xinjiang, China, from 2003 to 2050. Historical trends (2003–2020) were analyzed, and an ARIMA time-series model was developed to forecast collectable potential through 2050. Four scenarios combining planned/maximum utilization with/without carbon capture and storage (CCS) were designed, and life-cycle assessment (LCA) was applied to quantify GHG mitigation. Results show that Xinjiang's total collectable biomass potential will reach 1839.7 PJ by 2050, with crop residues accounting for 62.8%–74.6%. Under the maximum-potential-with-CCS scenario, the GHG mitigation potential reaches 298.90 Mt CO2e in 2050, with bio-liquid fuels and bio-electricity as the dominant contributors. These findings provide a dynamic, high-resolution basis for optimizing bioenergy deployment and supporting Xinjiang's dual-carbon transition and provides certain guidance for the development and utilization of biomass resources in Xinjiang and for mitigating global climate change. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Water footprint of low-tech digesters for bioenergy recovery from waste
Abstract: This study aimed to assess the water footprint of plastic tubular digesters to treat organic waste and recover bioenergy. Different scenarios in a small-scale dairy farm in Colombia were considered: i) scenario without the digester in which cow manure is piled up, and dairy wastewater is directly discharged into the environment, ii) scenario with a plastic tubular digester treating cow manure, and iii) scenario with a plastic tubular digester co-digesting cow manure with dairy wastewater. The ReCiPe 2016 – midpoint (H) method was used to assess the degradation of water bodies (i.e. eutrophication and ecotoxicity impact categories), while the AWARE 2.0 method was applied to evaluate the water scarcity impact category. Results showed that, in terms of water quality degradation, the co-digestion scenario exhibited impacts 10% to 45% lower than those of the other scenarios, depending on the impact category. In terms of water scarcity, the co-digestion scenario exhibited approximately 10% lower water scarcity than the other scenarios, which showed a similar water scarcity footprint. This indicates that implementing plastic tubular digesters, even under mono-digestion conditions, does not worsen water availability. These benefits are greater if co-digestion of different agri-food waste is applied, since it helps preserve water quality by valorising the intrinsic water content of food wastewater. It also decreases environmental impacts by reducing synthetic fertiliser use through the production of a higher-quality digestate. Overall, plastic tubular digesters provide a low-water footprint alternative to the direct discharge and uncontrolled storage of livestock waste and food-production wastewater in small-scale farms. © 2026 The Authors

Title: PinNet: Edge-optimized skin lesion segmentation
Abstract: Accurate skin lesion segmentation is an important prerequisite for computer-assisted dermoscopic image analysis, yet achieving reliable segmentation under stringent computational constraints remains challenging. Dermoscopic images frequently exhibit irregular lesion morphology, weak boundary contrast, heterogeneous pigmentation, and artifacts such as hair and illumination variations, whereas many high-performing segmentation networks incur substantial parameter and computational costs. To address this trade-off, we propose PinNet, a lightweight encoder–decoder network for skin lesion segmentation. PinNet incorporates a Morpho-Spectral Harmonic Layer (MSHL) that combines multi-scale Morphic Convolutions with frequency-domain feature modulation to capture irregular lesion structures while improving robustness to imaging variations. In addition, a Dual-perspective Block Attention Module (DBAM) jointly recalibrates channel-wise and spatial features and performs lightweight local refinement to improve boundary representation. Experiments on the ISIC2017 and ISIC2018 datasets demonstrate that PinNet achieves DSC scores of 88.47% and 90.10%, respectively, with only 0.050 M parameters and 0.068 GFLOPs. Under a unified training protocol, PinNet achieves a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off compared with the evaluated conventional and lightweight segmentation baselines. These results suggest that PinNet provides a compact solution for resource-constrained dermoscopic image segmentation. Authors: Zhu L.-T.; Li G.; Chen X.; Ruan S.-X.; Wu M.; Luo Z.-H.
Title: A review of tandem matching for chemical reactor design
Abstract: Reactor design is fundamental to chemical engineering, supporting controllable, efficient, and safe unit operations and chemical conversions. Tandem architecture can address inherent trade-offs among reaction stages in conventional reactors. Tandem matching, the core of its performance, governs the synergy between sequential processes across spatial and temporal domains. We review recent advances, current challenges, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled future directions of tandem matching for reactor design. We propose a unified hierarchical theoretical framework for tandem matching spanning molecular, catalyst, reactor, and system scales. It integrates transport-reaction matching that couples transport rates with reaction kinetics, and tandem thermodynamics-kinetics matching that coordinates thermodynamics and reaction kinetics as a novel conceptual insight. Together, they determine the efficiency, selectivity, and stability of tandem reactor systems, either in a zoned single reactor or cascaded multiple reactors. This framework offers a unified rationale for developing next-generation chemical reactors toward sustainable and intensified processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Tan J.; Ge C.; Li M.; Sun M.; Yang R.; Zhang H.
Title: Streaming algorithm for supply chain inventory optimization on the integer lattice
Source title: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: In a multi-echelon supply chain, to mitigate stockout risks and holding costs, the optimal inventory strategy can be transformed into an optimization problem that maximizes the difference between two DR-submodular functions. Specifically, let x denote the inventory level at each node (an integer variable), where g(x) represents the revenue from inventory meeting demand (DR-submodular, i.e., the marginal revenue of inventory diminishes as the inventory level increases), and h(x) denotes inventory holding costs (also DR-submodular). Maximizing g−h thus effectively mitigates stockout risks and cuts down inventory holding costs. In this paper, we design two algorithms for the problem of maximizing the difference of two DR-submodular function g−h (DDRS) on the integer lattice, where g(x) is monotone and non-negative DR-submodular, and h(x) is monotone and non-negative submodular with curvature ch. We first propose a one-pass streaming algorithm for the unconstrained problem. On this basis, we analyze the algorithm's performance and prove that it provides verifiable approximation guarantees. Second, we design a threshold streaming algorithm for the cardinality-constrained problem. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to verify the superiority of the proposed algorithms in terms of solution efficiency and approximation accuracy, further corroborating the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis and the practical application value of the algorithms. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Multi-granularity fusion network with mixed multi-hop graph convolution for hyperspectral image classification
Abstract: Effectively integrating spectral–spatial features under limited labeled samples remains a core challenge in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. Existing hybrid CNN–GCN methods often struggle to balance fine-grained local detail extraction and coarse-grained global relational modeling, frequently suffering from over-smoothing and inefficient cross-modal fusion. To address these issues, we propose a Multi-Granularity Fusion Network (MGF-Net) that systematically bridges coarse-grained structural contexts and fine-grained spatial details. Specifically, at the coarse granularity, a Mixed Multi-hop Graph Convolutional Network (MMGCN) operates on superpixel graphs, where the core Mixed k-hop blocks explicitly incorporate a parallel 0-hop branch to mitigate over-smoothing while capturing long-range dependencies. Concurrently, at the fine granularity, a Convolutional Feature Pyramid Network (CFPN) employs atrous blueprint separable convolutions to extract multi-scale pixel-level details with minimal parameter overhead. To seamlessly integrate these heterogeneous representations, a lightweight Hybrid Feature Fusion Module (HFFM) enforces early cross-granularity alignment via channel shuffle and group convolutions, offering an efficient alternative to heavy attention mechanisms. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that MGF-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance with statistical significance. Notably, the framework exhibits superior robustness under limited training samples and maintains the lowest theoretical computational complexity, offering a compelling accuracy–efficiency trade-off for practical HSI analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: KFS-CT: A physics-constrained hybrid network for broaching tool condition monitoring
Abstract: Tool condition monitoring (TCM) in industrial broaching faces significant challenges due to complex progressive multi-tooth geometries and cutting dynamics. To address these bottlenecks, this study proposes a physics-constrained hybrid expert network, termed the KFS-CT (Kalman Filtering Sparse-CNN-Transformer) framework, for multi-task decoupling of continuous full-teeth wear profiling and discrete transient chipping classification. In this framework, a macro-gating pipeline isolates the active cutting segments and partitions them kinematically, forming tooth-index-aligned interval matrices. Subsequently, a Kalman filtering sparse (KFS) separation operator is applied to decouple these segments into periodic degradation trends and transient shock components. Specifically, the framework employs a dual-branch feature fusion strategy: a multi-scale 1D-CNN branch directly processes the raw Spatio-Temporal signals, while a parallel physics-informed branch utilizes the KFS operator to decompose signals into periodic and transient components for extracting 16-dimensional expert physical fingerprints. Subsequently, the representations from both branches are concatenated, integrated with learnable positional encodings, and processed by a dual-layer spatial Transformer. Finally, a homoscedastic uncertainty loss is employed to dynamically balance the multi-task optimization objectives while incorporating physical mechanism constraints. Full-lifecycle industrial experiments demonstrate that KFS-CT achieves favorable diagnostic capabilities, limiting the full-teeth wear regression mean absolute error (MAE) to 0.0117 mm and yielding an 87.56% chipping classification F1-score. Concurrently, the computational latency of 2.84 s satisfies the requirements of quasi-real-time workshop deployment, offering a practical trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency in intelligent manufacturing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: UK bioenergy policies and implications for global land use change
Abstract: Bioenergy is central to UK decarbonisation policy, yet its reliance on imported biomass and crop-based biofuels raises concerns about land use change (LUC) and indirect land use change (ILUC) in supplier countries. This study provides a data-driven, ex-post assessment of land use implications associated with two UK bioenergy policy pathways: forestry-derived biomass supported by the Contract for Difference (CfD), and 1st generation biofuels supplied under the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation (RTFO). Import data for 2015–2022 were linked to forestry biomass productivity and country-specific crop yields to estimate direct land use footprints in major supplier countries. Wider ILUC-consistent signals were then assessed using observed land use, production and trade trends from 2000 to 2022, with particular focus on the US and Brazil. Results show that UK-bound forestry-derived biomass was mainly associated with land footprints in the US, Canada, Latvia and Estonia, while UK-bound 1st generation biofuel land demand became increasingly concentrated in the US and Brazil by 2022. Sensitivity analysis showed that lower productivity assumptions increased estimated land requirements, but did not alter the main supplier-country patterns. Overall, UK bioenergy imports represented a small share of total land use in major supplier countries. The study found no persistent national-scale ILUC signal detected in the US or Brazil. The findings suggest that ex-post land use monitoring can complement model-based ILUC assessment and improve the evidence base for bioenergy sustainability policy. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Governance transitions in underground infrastructure: Coordinating resilience enhancement of ageing metro systems
Abstract: As critical underground infrastructure, the resilience of ageing metro systems is fundamental to peoples’ safety and urban services. Its resilience failures extend far beyond technical origins; they arise from misaligned incentives, fragmented governance, and inefficient multi-stakeholder decision-making that derail technical implementation in complex urban settings. Here, we reconceptualize metro resilience as a socio-technical coordination problem rather than an exclusively technical one, developing a dynamic evolutionary game framework that reveals how service disruption constraints and stakeholder incentives determine whether cities escape low-resilience lock-in or achieve sustained adaptive capacity. We introduce a novel integration of life-cycle-informed, tripartite evolutionary game framework that integrates expert-based stakeholder salience identification with nonlinear dynamic modelling to capture long-term coordination in resilience enhancement decision-making. The results reveal that metro resilience is governed by sharp evolutionary tipping points: systems either remain trapped in low-resilience lock-in driven by short-term cost aversion or shift abruptly into stable high-resilience cooperation when institutional pressure, public supervision and risk reduction efficacy surpass critical thresholds. Beyond the ageing metro systems, this framework offers a transferable analytical lens for collaborative resilience decision-making in the comparable ageing urban underground infrastructures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Explainable grid informed model for power system transient stabilisation
Abstract: Demand response represents a cost-effective strategy for transient corrective control in power systems. However, evaluating transient scenarios that involve demand response programmes using traditional physical simulators is often computationally intensive, potentially resulting in suboptimal solutions. This paper proposes a data-driven grid informed approach to approximate transient stability based on the system initial conditions, fault information, and demand response control actions. First, a third-order structure-preserving model is introduced to capture transient dynamics. Second, the grid informed constraints incorporate both differential and algebraic constraints. Third, Shapley additive explanations are employed to interpret the contributions of different factors to final stability. Case studies conducted on the IEEE 9-bu, 39-bus, and 68-bus systems validate the proposed approach, demonstrating its high prediction accuracy and interpretability. © 2026

Title: DCET: Multi-scale decomposition and channel clustering enhanced multivariate time series forecasting
Abstract: Existing multivariate time series forecasting methods address multi-scale structures and channel heterogeneity by either enhancing model expressiveness with deeper and wider network architectures or by preprocessing sequences to attenuate certain frequency components. However, these approaches often lead to increased training costs, instability from over-reliance on model capacity, difficulty in handling multiple scales, and failure to consider differing structural relationships between channels. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel framework called DCET (Decomposition and channel Clustering Enhanced multivariate Time series Forecasting), which integrates a cascading two-stage decomposition process, channel clustering, and a ChebyKAN residual head within a single unified model. The main contribution of DCET lies in its ability to directly address multi-scale and channel heterogeneity in a more efficient manner by simplifying the model structure while preserving its expressiveness. Specifically, DCET introduces an unsupervised learning-based module for parameter sharing among similar variates, and applies the two-stage decomposition to capture multi-scale features. Nonlinear models are used to represent complex fluctuations, while linear models capture long-term trends. Moreover, a multi-objective training approach minimizes both the overall prediction error and the errors of decomposed components. We validate DCET through experiments on eight public datasets, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy, robustness, and flexibility in handling high-dimensional, heterogeneous time series with manageable model complexity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Culturally responsive cognitive-behavioral therapy for black populations: a scoping review
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the contributions of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to culturally responsive clinical practice addressing racial and ethnic issues, with an emphasis on the mental health of Black populations. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute and PRISMA-ScR guidelines and included systematic searches across multiple databases and complementary sources, resulting in 22 included publications. Findings revealed a predominance of studies conducted in the United States and a notable lack of empirical research in Latin American and African contexts. Conceptual heterogeneity emerged regarding how the cultural contextualization of CBT is defined and implemented, ranging from structured adaptations of standard protocols to culturally responsive therapeutic stances integrated into case conceptualization and clinical interactions. The most frequently reported intervention domains included cognitive restructuring, coping skills training, psychoeducation, and engagement in valued activities, often accompanied by explicit validation of racism-related experiences. The literature emphasized the centrality of culturally responsive therapeutic relationships and identified structural racism and healthcare mistrust as key barriers to access and engagement. Although the field demonstrates growing methodological and clinical maturity, theoretical fragmentation and the absence of integrative conceptual models remain significant gaps, underscoring the need for further empirical research in diverse sociocultural settings. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Title: Male DNA on underwear: Can Y- STR results help discriminate activities?
Abstract: This research is based on a case in which the complainant alleged that the defendant had removed her underwear, while the defendant claimed they had only danced together. To assist in resolving this issue, DNA was collected from the sides of the complainant’s underwear and Y-chromosome STR (Y-STR) analysis performed using the PowerPlex® Y23 System. As no published research were available on DNA recovered from the sides of underwear given the two alleged activities, 60 experiments were conducted to generate specific data on the expected results given underwear removal and given dancing. The underwear removal was simulated using a dummy, while the dancing experiments involved real participants. The paper discusses a principled approach to representing prior knowledge and combining it with the experimental observations when assigning probabilities to DNA recovery outcomes under the competing activity level propositions. To explore whether our LRs were calibrated, we applied our model to published ground truth studies. For the presence of a full Y-STR profile PP23, we show that our LRs in the order of 50 are robust. The prevalence of DNA from cohabitants was also studied. In our experiments, taking the cohabitant's Y-STR profile into account did not impact the value of the observations given activity level propositions. However, having access to the cohabitant reference sample increases the number of interpretable DNA mixtures and can provide relevant information. Title: Sustainable epoxy–polyurethane adhesives based on ionic liquids with high adhesion strength, low-temperature resistance, and direct adhesion on cold surfaces
Abstract: The exploration of the trade-off between adhesion performance and low-temperature resistance is essential for enabling the application of adhesive materials in cryogenic environments. However, simultaneously achieving strong adhesion, cryogenic tolerance, reusability, and stable adhesion directly on cold Surfaces remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a series of epoxy polyurethane adhesives regulated by ionic liquids (ILs), in which excellent low-temperature resistance and high adhesion are achieved through a crystallization-delayed self-reinforcement mechanism. The results demonstrate that the PU–E44 adhesive achieves an adhesion strength of 5.7 MPa at –40 ℃ and maintains a strength of 1.18 MPa even under liquid nitrogen conditions. Furthermore, this adhesive not only exhibits good adhesion properties at low temperatures and reusability, but also enables stable adhesion directly on cold surfaces. Such an adhesive, combining low-temperature durability, reusability, and direct adhesion to cold surfaces, offers new insights into the design and application of sustainable and recyclable adhesive systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Instructional approaches and content knowledge in teaching computational thinking: A large-scale study
Abstract: With the ongoing digitalization of society, educational curricula increasingly emphasize the development of learners' computational thinking. Yet, there is little consensus on how best to achieve this goal in classroom practice. This study investigates patterns in teachers' use of instructional approaches to foster computational thinking, focusing on approaches identified in the literature as effective: problem-based learning, cooperative learning, and direct instruction. Using data from the 2023 cycle of the International Computer and Information Literacy Study in Flanders, the analysis focuses on lower secondary school teachers teaching eighth-grade students. Latent profile analysis is used to identify teacher profiles. Three profiles are identified, distinguished primarily by the frequency rather than the type of instructional approaches employed. Direct instruction is most prevalent, though often combined with problem-based and cooperative learning. The study further examines the extent to which teachers' computational thinking content knowledge accounts for variation in their use of specific instructional approaches. To address this, a regression analysis is conducted. The findings reveal a significant negative association between teachers' computational thinking content knowledge and the use of problem-based and cooperative learning approaches, suggesting that teachers with higher levels of content knowledge tend to apply these approaches less frequently. No significant relationship is found between content knowledge and the use of direct instruction. Drawing on extensive large-scale data, the study offers valuable insights into teachers’ instructional approaches, underscoring the predominance of direct instruction and the nuanced role of content knowledge in shaping instructional practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A fairness-aware TabTransformer framework for credit scoring with high-cardinality regional bias
Abstract: This study examines whether fairness constraints must come at the expense of performance in credit risk models. We introduce a deep learning framework rooted in the TabTransformer architecture, integrating a Normalized Covariance Penalty into the loss function to mitigate regional bias over a high-cardinality sensitive attribute, the 27 Brazilian states. A real-world mortgage dataset of 1,529,211 contracts, under a strict unawareness-at-inference protocol and calibrated using Platt scaling, is benchmarked against industry standards and against fairness-aware alternatives from the pre-, in-, and post-processing families. The fairness-constrained model achieved an AUC of 0.751, above its unconstrained counterpart (0.745; DeLong p < .001) and Random Forest (0.735), while reducing the maximum True Positive Rate (TPR) gap across states to 0.445, against 0.499 for XGBoost, and reaching the lowest Demographic Parity difference among all evaluated models. XGBoost retains a statistically significant advantage in raw discrimination (ΔAUC (Formula presented)); among models that keep inference blind to the regional attribute, however, the proposed framework offers the most favorable fairness–performance profile and dominates the equity-constrained region of the empirical Pareto frontier. A decomposition across the 27 states shows that the penalty compresses the regional TPR distribution in both directions, raising the mean TPR of the three worst-served states, and a leakage audit confirms a measurable reduction in the regional information carried by the scores. Sensitivity analyses over the penalty weight and training seeds, module ablations, and replications on public credit datasets support the robustness of these findings. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Surgical treatment for idiopathic toe walkers gives good biomechanical and patient satisfaction outcomes
Abstract: Purpose: To assess the impact of bilateral surgical calf lengthening in patients with idiopathic toe walking (ITW) and calf contracture, including those with an autism diagnosis. Methods: Clinical assessment included passive range of motion and 3D gait analysis to capture kinematic and kinetic data. Temporal spatial parameters were measured. Gait Profile Scores (GPS) were calculated to evaluate gait normalcy, and Gait Variable Scores (GVS) identified the components of any change. Ankle push-off power was analysed. Patient satisfaction was assessed via questionnaires. Statistical analysis included paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results: Thirty-eight patients were included; 34 had complete kinematic and 30 had complete kinetic data. Mean age at surgery was 10.3 yrs and mean follow-up was 1.3 ± 0.4 yrs. Ankle dorsiflexion showed a significant improvement. Walking speed increased due to increased step length, while cadence was reduced. GPS improved from 11.4º from the norm preoperatively to 6.2º postoperatively (p < 0.001). GVS improved for ankle dorsiflexion (p < 0.001) and pelvic tilt (p < 0.005). Peak ankle power generation and work done during late stance significantly increased. Pain decreased postoperatively and patient satisfaction was high. There were no adverse biomechanical outcomes such as recurrence or overcorrection. Conclusion: Calf lengthening surgery for ITW has demonstrated improved clinical, kinematic and kinetic outcomes in gait analysis at one-year. High levels of satisfaction, with notable improvements in mobility and pain management postoperatively, were reported. However, longer-term follow-up to evaluate sustained benefits is needed. © 2026

Title: Coupling under-specification in functional resonance analysis method
Abstract: A growing body of research has combined the Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM) with network-analytic tools to derive quantitative insights about function importance and variability propagation in socio-technical systems. This article identifies a structural limitation shared by all the FRAM-network representations identified in the present review: the arcs between functions are treated as unspecified conduits through which variability propagates, without declaring the nature of the transmitted object or the mechanism of its distribution. This condition is termed “coupling under-specification”. This omission generates systematic ambiguities. Drawing on Borgatti's theory of network flows, the interpretation of propagation processes and the selection of appropriate network measures require the explicit specification of the nature of the transmitted good, the modality of its distribution, and the trajectory type of transmission processes. The problem is formalised through a PRISMA-compliant review of published studies combining FRAM and network models. An illustrative ontology for FRAM couplings based on three dimensions is proposed: coupling role, output nature, and transmission mechanism. The proposed ontology is illustrated through an industrial dairy packaging plant case study, an inter-rater reliability study examining the reproducibility of its application to a selected set of couplings, and a mapping between coupling classes and appropriate network measures. The results indicate that coupling under-specification is a validity condition of FRAM-derived network analyses rather than a defect of individual models, and that it constrains which network measures can be interpreted at all. The ontology is offered as one candidate means of supplying the missing specification, not as a validated instrument. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang T.; Lu S.; Wang M.; Liu B.
Title: Topology-aware dynamic co-evolution for robust graph learning
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success in learning from graph-structured data. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Building upon this decomposition, a fully differentiable attention-based architecture DeepGCN enables end-to-end optimization of the co-evolution process. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TADC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various attack settings, with particularly pronounced advantages under strong adversarial perturbations and high perturbation rates. Authors: Sha X.; Xu Z.; Park K.-S.; Su M.
Title: Urban economic resilience and low-altitude logistics industrial agglomeration: Implications for reliable deployment
Abstract: Low-altitude logistics (LAL) is a complex urban cyber-physical freight system comprising uncrewed aerial vehicles, eVTOL aircraft, airspace management, and ground infrastructure. Reliable deployment requires technical validation, regulatory compliance, and commercially sustainable operations, while urban socioeconomic conditions may provide supporting resources. This paper develops an interpretable causal learning framework to evaluate how urban economic resilience influences LAL industrial agglomeration, measured by the log-transformed stock of registered LAL-related enterprises. Utilizing panel data from 296 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2010–2024, we quantify urban economic resilience via an improved entropy-weighted TOPSIS model and integrate panel fixed-effects, double machine learning, causal forests, and SHAP attribution to estimate average effects under identifying assumptions and examine spatial heterogeneity and nonlinear predictive contributions. The results indicate that urban economic resilience significantly fosters LAL enterprise concentration, yet reveals a distinct resilience saturation pattern: mid-resilience cities exhibit the largest estimated effects on LAL industrial agglomeration, whereas marginal returns diminish in highly resilient metropolitan centers. SHAP decomposition reveals that household wealth accumulation, income levels, and fixed-asset investment are primary contributors to industrial presence. These findings identify urban economic conditions associated with LAL industrial agglomeration and offer implications for the economic foundations supporting reliable deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A self-supervised approach to malware classification using hybrid VAE-Swin Transformer models
Abstract: Malware detection and classification are critical in cybersecurity, where accurate identification of malware families enhances threat response and mitigation. Despite significant advances in malware image-based classification, challenges such as limited capture of local and global contextual dependencies, loss of spatial information, and high computational complexity continue to hinder robust malware family classification, particularly for diverse and imbalanced datasets. This paper introduces MalVEIT, a hybrid deep Variational Autoencoder (VAE) using an attention mechanism in the bottleneck of the model for malware classification under a self-supervised learning paradigm. Malware binaries are transformed into image representations, where the selected RGB formulation is adopted based on comparative evaluation against grayscale and other channel-construction alternatives. The VAE encoder then compresses these patches into a compact latent representation parameterized by learned mean and variance. Within the bottleneck layer of the VAE, shifted-window based self-attention mechanism is implemented using Swin Transformers for hierarchical feature extraction, enabling effective capture of both local structural patterns and global contextual dependencies. The refined features are sampled and reconstructed through a VAE decoder enforcing Kullback–Leibler divergence regularization to maintain a smooth distribution. The aggregated feature maps are then passed to a fully connected layer for malware family classification. The proposed model is evaluated on six benchmarked datasets, viz., Malimg, Malevis, Big-2015, Blended, Packed PE, and Obfuscation. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating robust multi-family malware classification across diverse datasets with data imbalance and outliers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: What are we measuring when we measure attractiveness?
Abstract: Facial attractiveness ratings are widely used as indicators of mate value and sexual preference in evolutionary aesthetics. Yet recent large-scale evidence reveals a robust Gender Attractiveness Gap (GAP): female faces are rated as more attractive than male faces across cultures, sexual orientations, age groups, and methodological contexts. This structural asymmetry has remained largely invisible despite being embedded in facial-attractiveness datasets for decades. It challenges the assumption that explicit attractiveness ratings map straightforwardly onto sexual desire. Rather, the GAP suggests that attractiveness judgments are outputs of a broader evaluative system in which female appearance occupies a privileged position. This article discusses the conceptual and methodological implications of this finding for measurement, theory construction, and future research on human aesthetic cognition. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Fetrati H.; Chan G.; Orji R.
Title: Design, development, and evaluation of STI Shield: A multi-chatbot mobile application for sexual health education and behavior change in African young adults
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a significant public health concern among African young adults, driven by limited knowledge, high-risk behaviors, stigma, and inadequate access to care. While mobile health (mHealth) interventions offer potential, many existing tools lack cultural relevance, theoretical grounding, and adaptability. This study presents STI Shield, a multi-chatbot mobile application designed to enhance STI awareness and encourage safer sexual behaviors. The app integrates rule-based and large language model (LLM)-based chatbots to deliver structured education and personalized counseling, drawing on the Health Belief Model and Persuasive System Design principles. A two-phase evaluation involving African participants living both in Africa and outside Africa, comprising pilot and in-the-wild studies, demonstrated high usability and acceptability, strong educational impact, high persuasiveness, and positive shifts in key behavior change determinants. Title: Aligning risk frameworks with fieldwork realities: extending Rasmussen’s model to scientific research settings
Abstract: Scientific fieldwork is an essential component of research across many academic disciplines. Fieldwork entails numerous risks, ranging from interpersonal to environmental risks, and can often result in physical and mental injury or illness. Despite these potential harms, standardized frameworks for understanding, managing, and responding to incidents in fieldwork remain underdeveloped. A limited understanding of incident causation in fieldwork contexts compounds this gap. In this article we propose that fieldwork, like other workplaces, operates as a complex socio-technical system in which people, cultural beliefs, governance, equipment, and the environment interact to create both safe and unsafe outcomes. To better understand the scientific fieldwork system, we conducted four focus groups to identify the people and institutions that constitute a fieldwork system and to characterize how these actors are organized within hierarchical levels. Through these sessions, we developed a classificatory scheme of variables that together influence safety outcomes. In total, 91 different actors across seven hierarchical levels and a contextual domain were identified. The resulting ActorMap and associated contributory factors offer a foundational framework for operationalizing safety and risk approaches, such as AcciMapping, in fieldwork settings. By incorporating these insights, we can enhance training, policy development, and institutional support structures to better equip researchers for the challenges of fieldwork. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Property-based testing in Python: empirical insights
Abstract: Property-Based Testing (PBT) automatically generates test inputs to validate properties of programs, shifting developers’ effort from writing examples to specifying invariants. While the technique has gained popularity in Python through the Hypothesis framework, little is known about how developers adopt and use it in practice. This paper reports on three empirical studies. First, we analyzed 367 PBTs from 244 Python projects, classifying them into nine property categories and quantifying their use of Hypothesis constructs. We found that Test Oracle properties dominate (29.97%), and that PBTs are generally concise (median 14 LOC), relying heavily on built-in strategies (75.20%), but also on external (22.62%) and internal (17.17%) ones. Second, we studied 213 Stack Overflow posts tagged with PBT, revealing that the main challenges developers face concern data generation strategies (36.62%), especially for composite and tabular data (24.36%). Finally, we evaluated Ghostwriter, Hypothesis’s automated test generator, against 203 tests from our dataset; only 18.23% were fully automatable, while most required partial adaptation (30.05%) or were incompatible (51.72%). Together, our findings provide the largest empirical characterization of PBT in Python to date, highlight developers’ difficulties in adopting the technique, and expose limitations of current tool support. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Field Assessment of the Safety Action Evaluation Protocol: Construction Safety Climate Focus
Source title: Journal of Structural Design and Construction Practice
Abstract: Frontline supervisors play a vital role in shaping the construction safety climate. Critical supervisory safety actions have been developed into the Safety Action Evaluation Protocol (SAEP) and a field assessment undertaken by frontline supervisors to evaluate its effectiveness and potential. A longitudinal field assessment was undertaken involving four stages of mixed-method inquiry to elicit both quantitative and qualitative data in a convergent design. Twelve frontline supervisors implemented the SAEP over a three-month period, embedding it into their daily work practices. Qualitative and quantitative data were collected at key stages and analyzed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. The frontline supervisors found the SAEP to be a useful and usable tool in the field that helped them prioritize and enhance safety. Allocation of suitable time to deliver the SAEP, and full organizational support and commitment, were felt to be critical for operational success. The SAEP was also considered a strong and well-balanced safety metric with potential as a safety management and monitoring tool in the future. The SAEP was evaluated as an effective tool to enhance the safety actions of frontline supervisors in the field. Future research will assess its use as a tool for safety monitoring and evaluation, completing the validation of the SAEP in the field. Title: Optimising construction health and safety training: the role of training design and firm size
Abstract: Background The construction industry is one of the most hazardous sectors globally, responsible for a disproportionate share of work-related injuries and fatalities. Construction health and safety (H&S) training is widely recognised as a critical component for improving workers’ H&S competence and reducing accident rates. Despite extensive investment in training programmes, research indicates that learning effectiveness varies across construction firms and may be associated with differences in training design and organisational context. However, empirical understanding of whether firm size moderates the relationship between specific training design dimensions and learning effectiveness is limited. Objective This study investigated the relationships between training design dimensions (training content relevance, facilitator competence, opportunity for practice, and learning environment) and learning effectiveness in construction H&S training while assessing the moderating role of firm size. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 80 construction professionals from medium- and large-scale firms. Data were collected using 5-point Likert scales to measure training design dimensions and learning effectiveness. Correlation analysis, multiple regression analysis, and moderation analysis using PROCESS were performed to test the hypothesised relationships. Results Multiple regression showed that the four training design dimensions jointly explained 64% of the variance in learning effectiveness ( R2 = 0.64, adjusted R2 = 0.62), with all four dimensions showing significant positive associations. Moderation analysis showed that firm size significantly moderated the relationship between training design quality and learning effectiveness (interaction B = 0.19, p = 0.033), with a stronger conditional effect among large firms ( b = 0.62) than medium-sized firms ( B = 0.43). Conclusions This study extends the training effectiveness literature by showing that the relationship between training design quality and learning effectiveness varies according to organisational context, with firm size representing a potential boundary condition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Organisational capability for digital health transformation in long-term care: development of a conceptual framework
Abstract: Background: Digital health transformation in long-term care (LTC) involves more than the adoption of digital technologies. Organisations must coordinate leadership, workforce capability, infrastructure, governance and implementation processes to sustain digital systems within continuing care environments. Existing implementation and digital maturity approaches address important aspects of digital transformation but provide less explanation of how organisational capabilities interact as a system within LTC. Objective: This study develops an evidence-informed organisational capability framework for digital health transformation in LTC and proposes relationships among capabilities potentially relevant to sustained digital system use. Methods: An evidence-informed framework development approach was used. Published evidence from digital health, healthcare management, implementation and organisational research was examined to identify recurring organisational mechanisms associated with digital transformation. Related mechanisms were grouped into capability domains, and proposed relationships among the domains were conceptualised. The resulting domains were integrated into the Long-Term Care Digital Capability and Alignment (LTC-DCA) framework. Results: LTC-DCA comprises seven interdependent organisational capability domains: strategic digital leadership, organisational readiness, workforce development systems, technology and data infrastructure alignment, governance and ethical oversight, implementation and integration mechanisms, and performance and learning systems. The framework conceptualises these domains as a connected capability system in which changes in one domain may influence others. Performance and organisational learning are proposed as feedback mechanisms that may support continued adjustment and alignment. Conclusions: LTC-DCA shifts attention from technology adoption towards the organisational capabilities potentially involved in integrating, sustaining and adapting digital systems within long-term care. The framework is evidence-informed and conceptually specified rather than empirically validated. Future research could examine its domains, proposed relationships and indicators across different LTC settings and investigate whether they are associated with sustained digital system use and organisational performance. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

Title: Supply-chain transmission and shared responsibility for multi-gas footprints across Chinese urban agglomerations
Abstract: Urban agglomerations connect the production, consumption, and governance of greenhouse gas emissions through interregional supply chains, yet existing studies often separate footprint accounting, emission drivers, supply-chain transmission, and responsibility sharing. This study examines 18 Chinese urban agglomerations comprising 204 cities using an integrated framework of environmentally extended multiregional input–output analysis (EE-MRIO), exact structural decomposition across all 120 factor-order permutations (SDA), structural path analysis (SPA), multi-gas emission-state diagnostics and a Shapley cooperative game. Consumption-based footprints of carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and aggregate greenhouse gases were assessed for 2012, 2015 and 2017. Per capita final demand increased emissions across all gases and periods, while the main mitigation source shifted from improvements in resource and emission intensity in 2012–2015 to changes in production structure in 2015–2017. For nitrous oxide, the −51.98% intensity effect in the earlier period was substantially offset by production restructuring and an expansion in final demand. Supply-chain pathways were gas-specific: carbon dioxide and aggregate greenhouse gases were transmitted mainly through electricity–industry–investment chains, whereas methane and nitrous oxide were more closely associated with agriculture, fuel exploitation and waste treatment. Title: Leaning into risk: How slanted typeface logos increase perceived risk of efficacious products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Marketing practice commonly uses slanted typeface logos on product packaging to convey movement and vitality, yet existing research has paid limited attention to the potential conflict between this low-level visual feature and the core claims of specific products. Drawing on the elaboration likelihood model (ELM), this research examines when and why slanted typeface logos on packaging increase consumers' perceived risk of efficacious products, revealing the underlying mechanism and boundary condition. Across three controlled experiments and one incentive-compatible experiment, this research manipulates the form of typeface logos on packaging and evaluates its effects and subsequent behavioral responses. Study 1 shows that, compared with an upright typeface logo, a slanted typeface logo increases consumers' perceived risk of efficacious products. Study 2 supports the mediating role of design instability: a slanted typeface logo triggers a visually perceived sense of imbalance, which further induces consumers’ risk inferences about the product; meanwhile, arousal, perceived movement, and perceptual fluency do not emerge as significant mediating mechanisms. Study 3 identifies the moderating role of cognitive load, showing that high cognitive load amplifies the effect of a slanted typeface logo on perceived risk. Study 4 further provides behavioral evidence through an incentive-compatible experiment, showing that consumers are less likely to choose the product in the slanted typeface logo condition. Overall, this research reveals a boundary of the visual marketing principle that “slanting implies vitality” in the context of efficacious products.
