Title: Regionalized life cycle assessment of NMC and LFP batteries across China-EU supply chain configurations under the EU Battery Regulation
Abstract: The EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 introduces stringent life cycle carbon footprint requirements that are expected to influence the regional organization of battery production. However, the carbon footprint implications of alternative China-EU supply chain configurations remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a regionalized life cycle assessment framework to evaluate the life cycle carbon footprints of lithium nickel‑manganese‑cobalt (NMC) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries under alternative regional supply chain configurations between China and the EU. The analysis follows the latest EU methodological guidance and combines proprietary industrial data from leading Chinese electric vehicle (EV) battery manufacturers. The boundary analysis showed that the calculated carbon footprints were sensitive to the life cycle stages included. Under the EU baseline, the carbon footprints of NMC and LFP batteries were 96.2 and 51.6 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 91/157/EEC-informed reference boundary, 95.9 and 81.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 2006/66/EC-informed reference boundary, and 142.9 and 128.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Regulation (EU) 2023/1542-aligned full life cycle boundary, respectively. Scenario analysis further indicated that regional supply chain reconfiguration can substantially narrow carbon footprint differences relative to Baseline-EU. For NMC batteries, the difference decreased from 59.3 gCO2e/kWh under the export (EX) scenario to 49.3 and 47.7 gCO2e/kWh under the overseas battery production (TB) scenario and partial material pre-processing in the EU (TBM) scenario, respectively. For LFP batteries, the corresponding values decreased from 74.1 to 49.4 and 47.1 gCO2e/kWh. These findings suggest that the regulatory context may encourage supply chain configurations with lower life cycle carbon footprints by altering the regional allocation of production stages. The findings highlight the importance of aligning regional production characteristics with decarbonization potential and provide policy-relevant evidence for coordinated China-EU battery supply chain strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Dalir N.
Title: Conductive polymer modified with nematic liquid crystal doped with graphene oxide for highly sensitive acetone sensing
Abstract: Acetone has been recognized as a critical biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring blood glucose levels in people having type II diabetes, and its measurement has been considered essential for maintaining human health. In this study, a highly sensitive gas sensor was developed in which a nanostructured polyaniline film was modified with a graphene oxide (GO)-doped nematic liquid crystal (NLC), and this composite layer was employed for acetone detection. The fabrication of the gas sensors was carried out through the electrosynthesis of polyaniline on interdigital electrodes (IDEs) under acidic conditions, after which the resulting films were modified using GO-doped NLC. Detection of chemical vapors was achieved by monitoring variations in the electrical resistance of the sensing layer, which were induced by orientational ordering transitions of GO and NLC, as well as by the absorption of analyte molecules onto LC droplets distributed across the polyaniline surface. The morphology of the polymeric films prior to and following modification was examined using scanning electron microscopy. The sensor responses (SRs) toward acetone were evaluated both in the presence and absence of GO, and enhanced sensitivity and improved selectivity toward acetone were observed when GO was incorporated. A detection limit of 0.27 ppm and a linear dynamic range of 1–10 ppm were obtained for acetone determination. Validating the method was carried out through the comparison of the sensor results with those obtained using gas chromatography. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A Block-Wise Updating Strategy for Approximate Duplicate Detection
Abstract: Approximate duplicate detection in data streams aims to determine whether an item is present within a small subsequence of the data stream. It is a fundamental query problem needed in several network applications, such as web crawling and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tag management. Most of the existing algorithms are not space-efficient as they overlook the distributional information of query frequency and membership likelihood. In this paper, we propose CEll Bloom Filter (CEBF) algorithm, a space-efficient data structure designed by adopting a block-wise updating strategy, to solve this problem, and two typical distributions are considered: two typical distributions: (1) uniform query frequency of items, and (2) uniform membership likelihood of items. For an arbitrary sliding window size n and an arbitrary average false positive rate ε ∈ (0, 1), the proposed algorithm needs approximately O(nlog2(1/ε)) bits, which is significantly less than the number of bits used in existing methods. Space lower bound is also derived for these two typical distributions, which demonstrates that the proposed algorithm is near-optimal in terms of space consumption. Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real datasets, and the experimental results clearly demonstrate that the proposed method is clearly and significantly more effective and promising compared to existing other methods. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Finding common and different factors in the motives underlying food choices across African and European countries
Abstract: Food Choice Questionnaires (FCQs) are widely used to assess consumers' food choice motives. Most validated versions originate from WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) countries and may not fully capture food environments in developing regions. This study applied a 39-item FCQ to urban consumers in four African countries (South Africa, Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia) and three European countries (Norway, Finland, France) (N = 500 per country). Urban populations were targeted because they are often early adopters of dietary trends. The assumed FCQ factor structure showed low reliability across countries. To identify shared food choice motives, a two-step approach was applied. First, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) was conducted separately in each country. Second, factor loadings were compared and clustered using the Tucker Incongruency Coefficient (TIC), enabling identification of factors with similar loading patterns across countries. Convenience and sustainability emerged as highly similar motives in all countries. Meat-related motives were also present across countries but showed greater heterogeneity in their factor structures. Emotional eating factors were identified in most countries. Gender differences were observed, with men placing greater emphasis on meat-related motives and women scoring higher on emotional eating. Despite substantial cultural and economic differences, the findings indicate the existence of shared food choice motives across low-, middle-, and high-income settings, although these motives appear to be expressed differently depending on context. The study introduces a novel methodological approach for comparing factor structures across cultures and may support the development of more context-sensitive measurement instruments, nutrition policies, and interventions tailored to diverse food environments. © 2026

Title: Quantifying the transient inertial and damping support of voltage-dependent loads: an analytical framework
Abstract: Declining system inertia necessitates quantifying intrinsic frequency support mechanisms. While load voltage dependency influences dynamics, its specific impacts on transient inertial and damping support remain under-quantified. This paper establishes an analytical framework to quantify voltage-dependent load contributions to the initial Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) and frequency nadir. By employing a Center of Inertia (CoI) framework to mathematically isolate load voltage dependence from network oscillations, closed-form expressions are derived for two physical mechanisms. First, the instantaneous power reduction from the subtransient voltage dip functions as an equivalent inertia, proportional to the system's base mechanical inertia and scaling linearly with grid impedance and load sensitivity. Second, load voltage sensitivity provides an effective damping torque that increases the damping ratio, suppressing the frequency nadir. Furthermore, the study reveals a critical trade-off with Automatic Voltage Regulators (AVR), where aggressive voltage recovery compromises this natural damping support. Time-domain simulations validate that voltage-dependent loads provide a self-regulating defense mechanism, particularly effective in weak grids. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Do Hopfield networks dream of stored patterns? A statistical–mechanical theory of dreaming in multidirectional associative memories
Abstract: We introduce the Dreaming L-directional Associative Memory (DLAM), a multi-layer Hebbian architecture in which off-line dreaming and supervised heteroassociative coupling coexist within a single cost function, placing our approach within the framework of energy-based models (EBMs). The replica-symmetric free energy, derived via the Guerra interpolation scheme, yields self-consistency equations governing the order parameters across the control-parameter space. The effective local field decomposes into signal, intra-layer dreaming noise, and inter-layer noise. Dreaming improves retrieval by differentially attenuating high-eigenvalue interference modes of the empirical correlation matrix, suppressing inter-pattern crosstalk while preserving the signal. Dreaming and inter-layer coupling prove synergistic, opening retrieval regions unreachable by either mechanism alone, as confirmed by Monte Carlo simulations for (Formula presented). Their interplay is most pronounced on pattern disentanglement: given a mixture state as input, the network splits the constituent patterns one-per-layer, recovering each modality-specific pattern from a common cue that simultaneously blends noisy evidence from all sensory channels. Phase diagrams are planar projections of the hyperspace (α, T, ρ, t)—where α is the storage load, T the fast-noise temperature, ρ the dataset entropy, and t the sleeping time. In the (ρ, t)-plane, the diagrams reveal a data–computation trade-off: off-line consolidation substitutes for additional training data, extending to heteroassociative architectures a phenomenon previously established for autoassociative networks. Enriching the standard Hopfield model with heteroassociativity and dreaming gives rise to EBMs capable of complex tasks beyond classical pattern recognition, contributing to a modern theory of neural information processing. Title: Modelling carbon price dynamics with jump-diffusion and higher-order hidden Markov switching
Abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic modelling framework that integrates a jump–diffusion process with a higher-order hidden Markov model, allowing carbon prices to exhibit both short-term volatility spikes and long-run regime memory. Motivated by the rapid expansion of emissions trading markets since the early 2000s, the framework captures the stylized facts of carbon prices, including non-stationary fluctuations, abrupt jump episodes, and discrete transitions across latent regimes. Monte Carlo experiments confirm the convergence and accuracy of the estimation procedure in offline and online implementations. For empirical validation, daily carbon price data from two representative markets—the European Union Emissions Trading System and China’s carbon market—are analyzed over the period from 2004 to 2024. Both point and interval forecasting performances are evaluated against benchmark models, including the autoregressive integrated moving average model, g eometric Brownian motion, extreme gradient boosting, and long short-term memory networks. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves improvements in model fitting and short-term forecasting performance. Title: Comparison of visual tasks for assessing attentional bias in cannabis users and non-users
Abstract: Attentional bias toward substance-related cues is a key feature of addiction and may contribute to the continued use of substances, such as cannabis. However, the sensitivity of different paradigms for detecting this bias remains underexplored. This study compared three visual attentional bias paradigms: dot probe (DP), eye movement (EM), and MouseView.js (MV) in detecting cannabis-related attentional biases among cannabis users and non-users. Linear mixed-effects models examined the effects of stimulus type, group, craving, and cannabis use severity. The EM and MV tasks revealed significant stimulus effects, with non-users showing greater attention to neutral images, while cannabis users exhibited more evenly distributed attention across stimuli. In the EM task, a significant stimulus × severity interaction indicated reduced attentional differentiation with increased cannabis use severity. MV results followed a similar, but less precise pattern. In contrast, the DP task showed minimal group or interaction effects and lacked sensitivity to detect attentional differences. These findings suggest that EM-based measures are more sensitive for detecting cannabis-related attentional biases, particularly when accounting for cannabis use severity. MV showed some alignment with EM patterns but demonstrated weaker effects. The DP task, despite its widespread use, may be insufficient for capturing cannabis-related attentional differences. Authors: Jang J.; Kim K.
Title: Where AI enters the product development process: Task orientation, human identity threat, and purchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly moving beyond analytical retail functions into product development, raising new questions about how consumers respond depending on where AI is positioned within the process. Across three studies with U.S. consumers in fashion-related contexts, this research examines how the task AI performs and how its role is framed shape consumer responses to products developed with AI involvement. Study 1 maps consumers’ perceptions of fashion-related tasks along a logic–intuition continuum and identifies trend forecasting as a logic-oriented task and design as an intuition-oriented task. Study 2 compares AI involvement in these two contrasting product-development tasks and finds lower purchase intention when AI is involved in design rather than trend forecasting, with heightened human identity threat accounting for part of this difference. Study 3 focuses on the intuition-oriented design context and shows that framing AI as complementing rather than replacing human designers is associated with lower identity threat and higher purchase intention. Together, the findings suggest that consumer responses depend not only on whether AI participates in product development, but also on where AI is positioned within the process and how its contribution relative to human creativity is framed. This research advances understanding of task-dependent responses to AI by identifying human identity threat as a mediator linking AI involvement to purchase intention and by showing how role framing can shape purchase intention when AI participates in creative work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Elucidating the relationship between fluidization dynamics and reactor performance in CO methanation via weakly-compressible DEM-CFD simulations
Abstract: Catalytic CO methanation is vital for synthetic natural gas production, yet its highly exothermic nature poses challenges for reactor design and thermal management. Macroscopic analyses show that, given sufficient gas–solid contact time, the CH4 production rate scales linearly with gas throughput up to 30umf without compromising the thermodynamic equilibrium yield. Despite substantial heat generation at high flow rates, particle circulation maintains pseudo-isothermal conditions throughout the bed. Mesoscopic analyses reveal a fundamental trade-off: low gas velocities promote premature reactant depletion near the gas inlet, whereas high gas velocities extend the kinetics-governed regime but induce localized convective mass-transfer limitation in the upper bed due to the formation of distinct dense and dilute regions. Consequently, an intermediate solid volume fraction ((Formula presented) –0.35) emerges as the optimal regime balancing catalyst holdup and reactant accessibility. These findings demonstrate that the governing rate-limiting mechanism is determined not only by reactor height but also by the local mesoscale structure. Therefore, disrupting phase separation through reactor internals or secondary gas injection represents a key strategy for improving catalyst utilization and optimizing industrial-scale fluidized-bed methanation reactors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Sensitivity analysis showed that selected medium risks could move to high risk after a one-level score increase. Title: Corporate strategy for the green transition: Are executive incentives effective?
Abstract: This paper examines whether green incentives embedded in executive compensation schemes are associated with a reorientation of firms' innovative activities toward environmentally sustainable technologies. Drawing on agency theory and the attention-based view of the firm, we conceptualize green incentives as governance and management-control devices that can mitigate managerial short-termism and channel executive attention toward long-horizon environmental objectives, thereby redirecting firms' technological search. These associations are weaker among firms experiencing a recent deterioration in carbon performance, and are strongest among continental European firms. Title: Macroprudential policies and dollarization: implications for the financial system and a cross-exchange rate regime analysis
Abstract: Macroprudential policy has gained prominence in promoting financial stability. This paper evaluates the effectiveness of macroprudential measures in curbing credit growth over a 22-year period across 129 countries. It further examines how macroprudential policy interacts with dollarization and other exchange rate regimes. Our findings indicate that tightening macroprudential measures are associated with lower credit growth within one quarter following implementation. The estimated associations are similar across the system and difference GMM specifications. Additionally, macroprudential policies are associated with significantly lower non-performing loan rates in dollarized economies compared to most other exchange rate regimes. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: High-throughput computational screening of metal–organic frameworks for CO2/H2 separation from biogas: Structure-property relationships and performance optimization under pressure- and vacuum-swing adsorption conditions
Abstract: Efficient CO2 capture from H2-rich biogas produced by dark fermentation requires adsorbents that preferentially retain CO2 to separate it from the gas mixtures. Here, we present a comprehensive guide to high-throughput computational screening of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) from the Computation-Ready Experimental (CoRE) MOF database to identify candidates for CO2/H2 separation. A systematic screening strategy based on geometric-structural and chemical criteria reduced the dataset to 137 candidate MOFs. Grand Canonical Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics simulations were employed to evaluate single-component gas adsorptivity, a 20:80 CO2/H2 binary mixture gas-adsorption selectivity, and diffusion selectivity at 298 K across pressure regimes from pressure- (PSA: 10 → 1 bar) and vacuum-swing adsorption (VSA: 1 → 0.1 bar). Structure-property analysis revealed that low-pressure CO2 uptake correlates strongly with structures having pore-limiting diameters < 6 Å and open metal sites, whereas high-pressure capacity is governed by accessible specific surface area. Confinement effects in microporous regions give rise to CO2-adsorption selectivity at low pressures, while diffusive selectivity favors H2 permeation in frameworks with restricted pore apertures. Screened MOFs were ranked according to overall performance score (OPS), which integrates CO2-adsorptivity, CO2/H2 separability, and CO2 recoverability. Top-performing MOFs for the VSA application tended to have adsorption performance scores that were twice those needed for PSA and were easily regenerated. Membrane profile analysis further confirmed that optimal H2-permeation selectivity emerges from balancing strong CO2-adsorption affinity with enhanced H2 diffusivity through size-selective pores. This work identifies promising MOFs for CO2 capture and biohydrogen purification and provides a computational framework to guide the rational design of new adsorbents. Copyright © 2026. Title: Idiosyncratic influences of hotel occupancy on energy consumption: Moderating effects of service style, hotel size, and hotel class
Abstract: With the growing attention to sustainability and energy management, understanding the dynamics of energy consumption in hotels has become increasingly important. We confirm that the utility expenses (e.g., electricity and water expenses) of a hotel generally follow a logarithmic increase with occupancy. A hotel's energy consumption rises rapidly when occupancy is relatively low but increases gradually once occupancy reaches a certain high level. In addition, full-service hotels exhibit a positive moderating effect at low occupancy rate but a negative moderating effect at high occupancy rate. Similar moderating effects are observed in large and high-class hotels. The findings indicate that full-service, large, and high-class hotels have opportunities for energy efficiency improvements when their occupancy rates are lower relative to those of limited-service, smaller, and lower-class hotels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Evaluation of cost reduction effects by sector-coupling synergies in timber processing and bioenergy for sustainable forestry in Japan
Abstract: The greenhouse gas sequestration capacity of forests is an important pillar in combating global warming; therefore establishing a forest resource circulation system is crucial. Forestry, which includes everything from cultivation to harvesting forests that store carbon dioxide as they grow, and the sawmill industry, which processes this timber, frequently face significant economic challenges. Consequently, proposals are needed to establish systems that improve these industries’ economic competitiveness while also ensuring the forest resources circulation. This study developed a model to evaluate the economic relationship between timber processing and energy consumption from a sector-coupling perspective using a prospective techno-economic analysis. It specifically defines wood utilization as a comprehensive forest resource circulation that includes production, planting, processing, energy utilization, and reforestation. It evaluates the economic interdependence between timber processing and energy utilization when all wood is harvested from forests and both uses are combined. The evaluation results show that combining energy utilization in sawmills processing over 36,000 m3 annually allows for full harvesting from forests, reducing forest residues, and lowering site preparation costs for reforestation. Additionally, using inexpensive electricity from biomass power generation for sawmilling lowers sawmill costs. It has become clear that, at sawmills of a certain size or larger, combining material utilization with energy utilization results in a slight decrease in sawmilling costs, while reducing forestry management costs; overall, this is an effective approach for wood utilization. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Lu J.; Zheng H.; Liu Z.; Li F.; Sun H.; Wu J.
Title: Robust optimization of emergency evacuation and supply allocation considering personnel demand heterogeneity and temporary shelters
Abstract: In emergency management, it is crucial to promptly evacuate affected people to shelters and allocate medical supply efficiently. Typically, these people have heterogeneous medical supply needs, with injured people requiring more medical supplies than uninjured ones. Additionally, their demand for medical supplies increases with evacuation time, which presents a significant challenge in emergency management. To address this, this paper proposes the novel idea of establishing temporary shelters to ensure the rapid evacuation of injured people and alleviate the resource burden. Considering the uncertainty in the proportion of injured people, we employ a robust optimization approach to jointly optimize emergency evacuation, supply allocation, and the establishment of temporary shelters. We then formulate a robust counterpart model and design a customized Benders decomposition algorithm to efficiently solve the model. For large-scale instances, we further incorporate a Branch-and-Cut procedure into the Benders decomposition framework to accelerate the solution process. Finally, we test our methodology using both a virtual example experiment and a Houston-based case, demonstrating the high performance of the designed algorithm and the advantages of establishing temporary shelters in reducing overall evacuation time and mitigating medical supply shortages. Based on these numerical results, we provide several valuable managerial insights for real-world applications. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Author full names: Gioia, Paul (59462574700); Ziegler, Johannes C. (7202576499); Deauvieau, Jérôme (16027993600)
Title: Strict phonics instruction outperforms mixed phonics: Evidence from a large-scale study
Abstract: Background: Learning to read is a foundational milestone in formal education, and a large body of research supports the effectiveness of systematic phonics instruction in early literacy development. However, much less is known about whether different implementations of phonics instruction influence children's reading outcomes. This study investigates whether variation within phonics-based instruction—specifically, strict versus mixed phonics approaches—is associated with differences in early reading development. Methods: We combine survey data from more than 9000 first-grade teachers with longitudinal assessment data for over 139,000 pupils in France. Teachers were classified according to the instructional approaches they reported using and the characteristics of the reading materials employed in their classrooms. Pupils’ reading fluency and reading comprehension were measured using nationally administered standardized assessments conducted during Grade 1 and at the beginning of Grade 2. Results: Multilevel analyses showed that pupils taught using strict phonics approaches achieved higher reading fluency and reading comprehension than those taught with mixed phonics approaches, with differences corresponding to approximately 0.11–0.16 standard deviations. These effects were substantially larger among pupils with weaker pre-reading skills and those attending socioeconomically disadvantaged schools. The findings remained robust across multiple complementary analyses designed to address potential selection effects and omitted-variable bias. Conclusion: The findings demonstrate that meaningful differences in reading outcomes may arise not only from whether systematic phonics instruction is provided, but also from how it is implemented. They further suggest that optimizing the coherence of early phonics instruction may be particularly beneficial for pupils most at risk of reading difficulties. © 2026 The Authors

Author full names: Zickmantel, Aidan (57223808682); Plácido, Francisco (60764408400); Portugal-Pereira, Joana (55799286600); Baptista, Patricia (16202135300); Ferrão, Paulo (6603743982)
Title: Where biomethane works: Geospatial and technical drivers of cost-effective deployment at municipal scale
Abstract: Biomethane produced from agricultural and agro-industrial residues can contribute to replacing fossil natural gas, yet national estimates alone do not reveal where production is technically and economically viable. This study developed a spatially explicit assessment of biomethane production across mainland Portugal, combining feedstocks, anaerobic co-digestion configurations, greenhouse gas accounting, feedstock and grid logistics, and techno-economic analysis at the municipal level. Results were aggregated to quantify national theoretical, technical and implementable potential while retaining the spatial detail needed to identify deployment constraints. Theoretical biomethane potential reached 0.643 bcm·yr−1, declining to a technical potential of 0.225 bcm·yr−1 after accounting for feedstock recovery rates and conversion losses. Once spatial, infrastructural and economic constraints were applied, implementable potential fell to 0.140–0.183 bcm·yr−1 across 81–133 sites, depending on carbon pricing, with resource-rich municipalities failing to qualify due to infrastructure inaccessibility. Transport, grid connection and feedstock logistics determine viability, producing geographically concentrated patterns. Under best available technology, net GHG abatement reached −1211 kt CO2eq·yr−1, while uncontrolled methane leakage more than halved it and left 9 to 12% of sites as net emitters under standard practice. 69% of avoided emissions originate from agricultural co-benefits (manure management and fertiliser displacement) rather than NG substitution, highlighting system boundary relevance. The median levelized cost of the implementable subset (€95 MWh−1 at the €80 PAB reference price) was competitive under current carbon pricing. Biomass availability, infrastructure coverage and carbon pricing shape an economic feasibility outcome that is inherently spatial and policy-sensitive. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Deng Q.
Author full names: Deng, Qinwen (59908407300)
Title: Market-driven or state strategic-driven? A hybrid driving paradigm and evolution of mission-oriented innovation ecosystems in aerospace engineering
Abstract: How national strategies and market forces jointly organize innovation for complex and uncertain space missions, such as deep space exploration, and why distinct driving logics retain their differences while incorporating governance mechanisms from one another remain important questions for research on mission-oriented innovation ecosystems. This study develops the Drive–Organization–Adaptation–Value (DOAV) analytical framework and conducts a longitudinal comparison of SpaceX's deep space exploration program and the China Manned Space Program, tracing stage-specific mission demands, local task gaps, mechanism entry, and coupling at task interfaces. The findings reveal a sequence of conditional relationships. First, mission mandates and resource conditions shape initial driving relations and produce distinct configurations of organization, adaptation, and value. Second, when stage-specific demands reach the configuration performance boundary, the leading actor can address local task gaps through internal adjustment or admit heterogeneous mechanisms when complementary capabilities and executable interfaces are available. Third, coupling at task interfaces links organization, adaptation, and value, encouraging convergence in governance mechanisms while leadership relations retain identifiable continuity at the defined long-term mission level. On this basis, the study distinguishes instrumental hybridization, asymmetric structural hybridization, and mission co-shaping according to mechanism embedding depth and the reach of governance feedback. Mission co-shaping is retained as a conditional theoretical extension within the process explanation of the DOAV dynamic adaptation mechanism. The findings inform the coordination of public objectives and firm innovation capabilities in major scientific and technological missions, including space exploration, and the design of collaborative rights, responsibilities, and verification arrangements in response to stage-specific tasks. © 2026 IAA. Title: Mass analysis of supercritical nitrous oxide and helium in a recompression Brayton cycle utilizing in-situ resources for lunar base energy system
Abstract: The Moon is the only natural satellite of the Earth and also the closest celestial body to the Earth. The Moon is regarded as an outpost of deep space exploration. The construction of lunar base infrastructure, polar exploration, and rovers constitutes the first step for humans to venture into the Moon. In the process of constructing a lunar base, it is essential to establish an energy system that can fully utilize local resources. This system will reduce the weight of materials transported from Earth and ultimately solve the energy shortage problem on the Moon. A recompression Brayton cycle that utilizes in-situ resources, with supercritical nitrous oxide and helium as the working media, and evaluates the mass of the energy system. A small modular reactor is applied to predict the minimum-mass reactor suitable for the given cycle conditions. The system mass and specific mass optimization explored the trade-offs among the reactor, radiation shield, Brayton cycle unit, recuperator, and radiator to obtain the minimum mass of the lunar base energy system. The results indicate that the specific mass of the energy system is 17.37 kg∙kWe−1. In addition, it is found that, by utilizing in-situ lunar base resources, the mass and volume of the radiation shield for the reactor can be reduced by 3.55% and 14.20%, respectively. In conclusion, the proposed energy system scheme offers several advantages, including light weight, high efficiency, and continuous electricity supply, for application in lunar bases. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: He R.; Wan M.; Luo H.; Yu H.; Zhou X.; Liu H.
Title: ST-JSCC: Synergizing structural and textural dependencies for robust and efficient image transmission
Abstract: Semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm for next-generation intelligent communications by prioritizing semantic fidelity over conventional bit-level accuracy. Although deep joint source-channel coding (JSCC) has demonstrated strong robustness under varying channel conditions, existing methods still face a trade-off between structural preservation and textural reconstruction. Most existing approaches rely on either convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or Transformers. CNN-based methods are effective at capturing local textures but struggle to model long-range structural dependencies, while Transformer-based methods capture global information yet often fail to preserve fine-grained textures under aggressive compression. To address these limitations, we propose Structural-Textural JSCC (ST-JSCC), a novel framework that jointly exploits structural and textural representations for robust image transmission. Specifically, a parallel architecture is designed, consisting of a linear attention branch for efficient global structure modeling and a CNN branch for local texture preservation. Furthermore, a Gated Fusion Module (GFM) is introduced to adaptively integrate complementary features from both branches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that ST-JSCC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, especially under low-SNR conditions. The source code will be made publicly available upon publication. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.

Authors: Sadeh N.
Author full names: Sadeh, Naomi (25626783600)
Title: A multilevel framework for distinguishing psychopathy from related disorders
Abstract: Although psychopathy is not a standalone diagnosis in current psychiatric classification systems, it remains widely used in forensic contexts and can have significant consequences for individuals within the legal system. Consequently, it is critical that the field be able to distinguish psychopathy from other mental disorders with over=lapping symptom presentations. This review proposes a multilevel theoretical framework for understanding how psychopathy differs from related disorders when mechanistic and dispositional factors are considered alongside behavioral symptoms. It illustrates how disorders overlapping with psychopathy at one level of analysis (e.g., chronic antisocial behavior and aggression) diverge from it at others, particularly the mechanistic level (e.g., attentional functioning, threat reactivity, empathy processing) and dispositional level (e.g., callous-unemotional traits). It further considers how contextual factors modulate whether psychopathic features are rewarded or criminalized and how this may affect their interpretation. By identifying features that distinguish psychopathy across levels of analysis, the framework clarifies what makes psychopathy a distinct construct, with implications for case formulation, treatment, and forensic assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Automatic behavior tree generation for enhanced human–robot collaborative task planning in industry 5.0: A systematic review
Abstract: In the context of Industry 5.0, scheduling heterogeneous resources, such as humans and robots, has become increasingly critical. Task allocation must balance human comfort, ergonomics, and trust with productivity and responsiveness to customer demands. This review explores recent advances and prospects in the automatic generation of schedules and action plans, particularly Behavior Trees (BTs), to improve human–robot collaboration. We examine the application of artificial intelligence techniques to classical production management problems, such as Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP) and Assembly Line Balancing Problems (ALBP), for autonomous task scheduling and robotic behavior design. This includes highlighting innovative scheduling approaches and the advantages of Behavior Trees over traditional models such as Hierarchical Task Networks (HTN) and Finite-State Machines (FSM). Behavior Trees offer a modular and reactive programming structure essential for executing complex tasks assigned to robots. The review also discusses human operators’ perception of robotic actions and identifies best practices for implementing collaborative solutions that prioritize both efficiency and safety. © 2026 The Authors. Title: IGPC: Multi-domain multimodal fake news detection via Info-Gini Weight Adaptation and Prototypical Multi-level Contrastive Learning
Abstract: Multi-domain multimodal fake news detection requires models to integrate textual and visual evidence while generalizing across diverse domains. Existing methods still struggle with multi-level data imbalance, weak class geometry in data-scarce domains, and transfer to held-out target domains. We propose Info-Gini Weight Adaptation and Prototypical Multi-level Contrastive Learning (IGPC), a method that decomposes imbalance into inter-domain, intra-domain, and global levels, and converts dataset statistics into stable training weights. It then learns a domain–label prototype space and applies multi-level contrastive learning to enforce compact intra-class clusters and clear inter-class margins. Finally, a prototype-based transfer enhancement, including a global class-prototype bridge and prediction fusion, improves robustness on held-out target domains without introducing extra loss terms. Experiments on Weibo (7723 experimental samples), Weibo-21,(6156 experimental samples), and FineFake (16,796 experimental samples) show that IGPC outperforms the strongest directly reproduced baseline by 1.06%, 1.48%, and 1.01% in overall F1 score, respectively. Authors: Piovesan F.; Frascaroli J.; Van de Cruys S.
Author full names: Piovesan, Francesca (58892537700); Frascaroli, Jacopo (57536030900); Van de Cruys, Sander (55338378700)
Title: Aesthetic taste in humans and machines
Abstract: Aesthetic taste remains an elusive phenomenon that has been comparatively underexplored in psychology. We argue that taste integrates four dimensions: sensitivity to fine-grained differences within a domain; valence, through which these differences come to matter affectively; orientation, the selective tendency to seek encounters that may further transform one's sensibility; and normativity, through which judgments of taste become shareable and contestable. These are not separate dimensions but faces of a single underlying capacity: continuously monitoring one's grip on the world and letting that monitoring modulate what happens next. This makes human engagement non-uniform. Throughout, we use current artificial intelligence as a contrast case, exploring how far it can model or replicate human taste. Machines can be sensitive to fine-grained distinctions, predict human preferences, generate apparently tasteful outputs, and shape the environments in which human taste develops. But they do not yet possess taste in the full human sense, because they lack the stake that makes human processing non-uniform: self-directed exploration, online self-transformation, and genuine normative vulnerability. The upshot is a systematic framework for the study of human taste and for assessing how AI may transform its formation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Advancing student mental health through AI-assisted group counseling in smart schools: A literature review
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), educational data analytics, and digital mental health technologies are rapidly transforming educational environments and creating new opportunities for student psychological support. Although substantial research has examined AI applications in education and mental health, limited attention has been devoted to the integration of AI-assisted group counseling within smart educational environments. This narrative literature review examines the role of artificial intelligence and educational data ecosystems in enhancing digital psychological support and group counseling in smart schools. Relevant studies were identified through major academic databases and synthesized using a thematic review approach. The analysis revealed three major themes: (1) emerging AI technologies for educational mental health, (2) AI-enhanced school counseling and group counseling, and (3) data-driven psychological support, ethical challenges, and governance considerations. The findings suggest that AI technologies, including machine learning, large language models, conversational AI, and educational analytics, can support psychological assessment, early identification of student needs, intervention planning, psychoeducation, and counseling decision-making. Emerging evidence also indicates that AI-assisted group counseling may enhance peer support, engagement, self-reflection, and student well-being through collaborative and data-informed interventions. Despite these opportunities, important concerns remain regarding privacy, transparency, explainability, algorithmic fairness, accountability, and human oversight. Based on the reviewed literature, this study proposes an Integrated Human-Centered Framework for AI-Assisted Group Counseling in Smart Schools that connects educational data ecosystems, AI-powered support systems, counseling processes, ethical governance, and student well-being outcomes. The review highlights the importance of human–AI collaboration and provides directions for future research and practice in AI-enabled educational mental health services. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Navigating public and private funding options for conservation measures: A cross-country comparison of western European farmers' preferences
Abstract: Evidence in economics highlights the importance of the design of agri-environmental contracts for farmers' participation. However, there is little evidence on Western European farmers' preferences between alternative public and private contracts and labels, and on their synergies with participation in farmer clusters. In addition, cultural or institutional differences may lead to variation in contract design preferences across countries. Thus, we apply a discrete choice experiment using an online survey to estimate farmers' preferences for the contract organiser (government, retailer, NGO), the payment method (fixed per hectare payment, price premium associated with a label), and participation in a farmer cluster including technical assistance by a facilitator as part of the contractual arrangement (no farmer cluster, optional participation, mandatory participation) in the United Kingdom, France and the Netherlands. Based on a sample of 767 farmers, respondents prefer, on average, government-organised contracts to contracts from retailers or NGOs. Farmers prefer fixed per hectare payments over price premiums associated with a label and contracts granting the option to join a farmer cluster. The results vary between farm types and countries. Authors: Kim S.-H.
Title: What makes human service distinctly human in the AI era? Conceptualizing and measuring authentic relational service competency
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) service agents increasingly simulate human interaction, the basis for distinguishing human service has become theoretically ambiguous. While prior research consistently identifies authenticity as a key limitation of AI-enabled service, authenticity remains underdeveloped as a uniquely human service capability. Addressing this gap, we introduce Authentic Relational Service (ARS) as a distinct form of service through which frontline employees create genuine, contextually responsive, and relationship-centered customer interactions. We further conceptualize authenticity as a competency-based capability and develop a measure of Authentic Relational Service Competency (ARSC), which enables frontline employees to enact ARS. Using established scale-development procedures, this study identifies and validates four dimensions of ARSC: perspective-taking, patience, creativity, and agility. By conceptualizing and operationalizing Authentic Relational Service as a distinct human service capability, this research advances theory on human-AI service differentiation and provides a foundation for understanding uniquely human value creation in service contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Developing instrument to measure the glass ceiling phenomenon among female academics in Indonesia
Abstract: The persistence of the glass ceiling phenomenon in academia indicates the necessity of developing a contextually valid and reliable measurement instrument, particularly within Indonesian higher education institutions. Instruments developed in different cultural settings are often unable to fully capture the structural and sociocultural dynamics influencing female academics' career advancement in Indonesia. This study aims to develop and validate a comprehensive measurement instrument that reflects these contextual specificities and improves measurement accuracy in assessing career advancement barriers. A quantitative research design was employed using a survey approach. Instrument development was conducted through the integration of two established questionnaires originating from India and Europe, followed by contextual adaptation. Data were collected from female lecturers employed at Catholic universities in Indonesia. The two preliminary questionnaires were administered to the same initial group of female academics. For the final validation, the integrated instrument was administered to the initial respondents together with additional participants, resulting in a larger validation sample. The measurement model was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with SmartPLS. Reliability and validity were assessed through composite reliability, Cronbach's alpha, average variance extracted, and discriminant validity criteria. The findings indicate that the newly developed instrument demonstrates strong reliability and validity across all dimensions, with acceptable thresholds achieved for composite reliability and convergent validity. Compared to the adapted international instruments, the final instrument exhibits higher cultural relevance and improved measurement precision. Several dimensions were more accurately captured, particularly those related to organizational culture, informal networks, and discriminatory promotion practices, indicating a stronger alignment with the Indonesian academic environment. The study contributes to the refinement of measurement approaches in gender-related research by providing a robust and context-sensitive instrument. The instrument is expected to support future empirical studies and institutional policy evaluations aimed at reducing gender disparities in academic career advancement and leadership positions in Indonesia, while also enabling more accurate diagnosis of structural and cultural barriers. Title: Hydrogen from pine wood waste via pyrolysis and autothermal steam reforming: technoeconomic and environmental performance of single and co-production pathways
Abstract: Biomass-based hydrogen production represents a promising pathway to reduce the environmental impacts associated with fossil-based hydrogen. In thermochemical pathways, biomass is typically converted into intermediate streams such as bio-oil prior to hydrogen production. However, in bio-oil reforming processes, a key unresolved question is whether hydrogen production should prioritize complete conversion of the pyrolysis liquid or selective upgrading of its aqueous fraction, recovering the organic fraction as a fuel co-product.In this work, the implications of both alternatives at industrial scale are systematically evaluated through an integrated techno-economic and environmental assessment, comparing two process configurations for hydrogen production from pine wood waste via fast pyrolysis coupled with autothermal reforming, and benchmarking them against conventional steam methane reforming.The results show that both biomass-based scenarios can reduce climate change impacts by approximately 80% compared to steam methane reforming. However, this benefit is accompanied by higher impacts in categories such as acidification and resource use (minerals and metals) due to electricity consumption and forest management. From an economic perspective, the configuration based on complete conversion of bio-oil leads to a levelized cost of hydrogen of 5.2 €2025/kg H2, which decreases to 2.8 €2025/kg H2 when the organic fraction is co-produced as fuel for industrial heat boilers.Overall, the results demonstrate that the choice of bio-oil valorization strategy for hydrogen production constitutes a critical design variable, introducing a trade-off between hydrogen yield, economic performance and environmental impacts. The co-production strategy enhances economic robustness, while environmental differences between the two scenarios remain minor, and depend on the allocation approach and the impact category considered. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Experiences of after-dark urban forest walks when using head torches: off-the-shelf vs customised
Abstract: During the dark season, electric lighting in urban forests can facilitate recreational activities and psychological restoration. However, the permanent presence of electric lighting causes light pollution, with detrimental effects for people and wildlife. This study explored the extent to which head torches could support pedestrian needs in a Nordic context where daylight hours are reduced during the winter season. The aim was to compare the pedestrian appraisal of an urban forest path under different lighting conditions: daylight (DL); regular off-the-shelf head torches (OHT); and customised head torches (CHT), with reduced light distribution and thereby less light pollution. The 75 participants completed structured walks with observer-based environmental assessments on site by means of questionnaires under DL, OHT or CHT light conditions. The results showed that participants experienced (appraised) the urban forest path similarly in the two head torch conditions in terms of visual accessibility, perceived safety, and the restorative potential of the forest setting. The behavioural intention to choose the path did not differ between head torches, but the intention to avoid the path was lower with OHT. No differences in comfort aspects of the light could be identified. As expected, the urban forest was rated higher for the environmental appraisals in DL, but retained its restorative potential even in the two head torch conditions. It is concluded that light sources with less ecological impact could be introduced without influencing pedestrians’ environmental experiences negatively. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Guan Q.; Gong T.; Wang Y.; Tang X.; Ji P.; Guo K.
Title: A Land-Sea integrated ecological compensation framework based on carbon sequestration service flows: Evidence from a Coastal City
Abstract: Ecological compensation (EC) is an important policy instrument for coordinating ecological conservation and economic development and promoting carbon neutrality. However, existing EC policies in coastal regions remain largely terrestrial-oriented, making it difficult to identify cross-regional dependence on land-sea carbon sequestration services (CSs) and the corresponding compensation responsibilities. Using Qingdao, China, as a case study, this study develops a land-sea integrated EC framework that combines random forest, the IPCC inventory method, and a spatial interaction model to identify land-sea CSs supply-demand patterns and carbon sequestration service flows (CSF), and to allocate EC responsibilities accordingly. The results show that: (1) from 2004 to 2023, the imbalance between CSs supply and demand continuously intensified, with pronounced spatial mismatches; (2) CSF exhibited clear land-sea coupling, with the sea area and coastal mountainous area (Laoshan District) serving as the major CSF sources. CSF outflows from the sea area accounted for 29.02%–47.81% of the total positive regional CSF and primarily flowed to the rapidly urbanizing area of Huangdao District; and (3) actual EC payments differed markedly from ideal responsibilities across county-level administrative units, while the sea area received 78.10% of total inter-county compensation receipts. The Ecological Compensation Priority Index (ECPI) further indicated that the sea area and key terrestrial CSs supply areas should be prioritized for compensation. By integrating land-sea ecological contributions, external CSs dependence, compensation responsibilities, and implementation priorities into a unified analysis, the framework can support more equitable and efficient EC decision-making in coastal regions. © 2026

Title: Kronecker product overdetermined independent vector analysis for online blind source separation
Abstract: Online blind source separation is essential for real-time speech communication and human-machine interaction. Among existing solutions, overdetermined independent vector analysis (OverIVA) has demonstrated superior separation performance by jointly exploiting source independence and the orthogonal constraint between the source and noise subspaces. However, when employed with large microphone arrays, the dimensionality of the separation filters grows rapidly, which poses significant challenges for reliable parameter estimation in online implementations. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a generalized Kronecker product decomposition for online OverIVA, in which each source extraction filter is represented as a sum of multiple Kronecker products of shorter sub-filters. The proposed formulation introduces an explicit Kronecker order that flexibly controls the model rank, enabling a smooth trade-off between representation capability and parameter efficiency. An efficient alternating optimization algorithm based on iterative projection is derived to estimate the structured extraction filters in an online manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved separation performance and enhanced robustness. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: ST-AHM: a soft-threshold sparse-attention hypergraph model with contrastive learning for session-based recommendation
Abstract: Session-based recommendation (SBR) predicts the next interaction from anonymous, short-lived behavioral sequences. A central challenge is to capture higher-order dependencies within sessions and collaborative information across related sessions while limiting weak contextual relations. We propose ST-AHM, a dual-channel model that jointly represents within-session and cross-session information. In the within-session channel, hypergraph convolution captures higher-order item dependencies. Hypergraph-specific sparse attention (HSPA) then averages scaled compatibility scores across attention heads before applying Sparsemax. This operation creates a consensus-based sparse support while retaining head-specific value projections, thereby reducing the propagation of weakly supported relations. An identity-free blank node summarizes the enhanced sequence and produces a context-dependent session-intent representation without relying directly on the last item. In the cross-session channel, Jaccard similarity between session item sets defines a relational graph. Relational graph convolution propagates collaborative information, and the blank-node representation acts as a blank-node-derived query for aggregating relevant cross-session context. A contrastive objective aligns valid interaction representations with the blank-node-augmented view of the same session and distinguishes them from shuffled representations. Across Tmall, Diginetica, and 30Music, ST-AHM outperformed the evaluated baselines, including DCL-BPM, DiffSBR, and MSGAT. Its average improvements were 19.23% for HR@10, 12.71% for HR@20, 23.19% for MRR@10, and 24.28% for MRR@20. These results support the joint modeling of within-session and cross-session information while reducing the influence of weak relations. Title: Mechanistic insights into tandem reaction kinetics in PMS activation by manganese-based poly(ionic liquid) for oxidative removal of dibenzothiophene
Abstract: A manganese-based polymeric ionic liquid catalyst, P[BVIM]MnCl3, was synthesized for PMS activation toward the deep oxidative removal of dibenzothiophene (DBT) under mild conditions. Unlike conventional endpoint evaluations, this study established a time-resolved GC–MS sampling strategy combined with consecutive first-order kinetic modeling, enabling the simultaneous determination of apparent rate constants, steady-state radical concentrations, and radical lifetimes from a single experiment. A global kinetic model incorporating radical consumption by the intermediate DBTO was further developed, revealing that intermediate accumulation-induced feedback inhibition is the key rate-limiting factor for overall desulfurization. Selective quenching experiments coupled with kinetic analysis demonstrated the differentiated roles of SO4•− and •OH: SO4•− dominated the initial DBT oxidation, contributing over 95%, whereas •OH mainly promoted DBTO oxidation to DBTO2. A radical generation efficiency parameter and multi-index evaluation system were established to elucidate the diminishing benefits and trade-offs associated with catalyst and PMS dosages. Under optimized conditions (30℃, 35 mg catalyst, and 0.5 g PMS), 97.3% desulfurization was achieved with an apparent activation energy of 17.1 kJ·mol−1. This work provides mechanistic insights into the Mn-based polymeric ionic liquid/PMS system and methodological guidance for the design and kinetic evaluation of oxidative desulfurization catalysts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Ma X.; Liu Q.; Ma S.; Wu L.; Li D.; Gao Y.
Title: Empowering adaptive MOOCs: A learning path recommendation model based on multi-level knowledge graphs and rule-guided path constraint optimization
Abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) provide abundant learning resources, yet their fixed instructional structures and limited adaptive support constrain learning effectiveness. Previous path recommendation approaches typically depend on predefined start and target nodes, offer limited dynamic adaptability, and insufficiently consider multi-hop dependencies among learning content. To address these challenges, this study proposes an adaptive learning path recommendation model based on a multi-level knowledge graph and rule-guided path constraint optimization (KGRRec). First, we design a multi-level knowledge graph framework that models course knowledge structures and integrates MOOC resources across three levels: instructional organization, knowledge representation, and resource aggregation. Second, building on this framework, we develop a rule-guided path constraint optimization method, which incorporates dynamic reasoning mechanisms, path constraint modeling, and learning gain simulation to deliver adaptive learning path recommendations. Implemented in a prototype integrating seven database-related MOOCs, KGRRec was evaluated through a one-group pretest-posttest study (34 students) and a randomized controlled study (59 students). Results showed KGRRec significantly outperformed eight baselines on Prerequisite, CogValidity-F, and expert ratings. Furthermore, it showed a trend toward improved learning performance and supported positive learning experiences. These findings provide preliminary evidence of the model’s effectiveness and a methodological reference for the future development of large-scale adaptive MOOCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wan L.; Liu G.; Su X.
Title: A systematic cost-effective assessment of multiple grassland restoration methods in China
Abstract: Extensive grassland restoration programs were being expanded nationwide in response to the pervasive and severe degradation of grasslands in China. However, there was a significant dearth of quantitative cost-effective analyses pertaining to grassland ecosystems. The lack hindered the selection of the most cost-effective approaches to achieve restoration goals. After reviewing 214 studies, we comprehensively analyzed the precise restoration costs (distinguishing one-time inputs and ongoing inputs) and effectiveness of 17 diverse grassland restoration methods across China's three most prevalent grassland types. One-time inputs refer to non-recurring expenditures during implementation, including machinery, seeds, fertilizers, fencing, and labor, accounting for over 50% of total costs for most methods. Ongoing inputs are annual recurring costs for maintenance, encompassing ecological compensation for herders, maintenance staff salaries, and opportunity costs. Results showed that: (1) grassland restoration enhanced biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality but 17 recovery methods had significant differences in effectiveness; (2) China's grassland restoration methods tended to be costly while grazing management was a low-cost approach; and (3) grazing management could be a viable and cost-effective approach across the main grasslands in China. Our results provided valuable insights for policy-makers aiming to enhance the cost-effectiveness of grassland restoration projects in China, thereby addressing the financial barriers associated with scaling up restoration efforts at a national level. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Transformations in nursing education: Voices of senior faculty members with decades of experience
Abstract: Background: Nursing education in Türkiye has undergone profound structural transformations over the past decades, driven by rapid program expansion, intensifying demands for research productivity, digitalization, and the erosion of academic-clinical continuity. Despite their centrality to educational quality, the lived experiences of senior nursing faculty members navigating these changes remain largely unexplored. Aim: To explore how senior nursing faculty members in Türkiye describe the major transformations in nursing education throughout their careers and how these changes have shaped their professional roles and academic identities. Design: Descriptive qualitative research design using thematic analysis. Settings: Multiple higher education institutions providing nursing education in Türkiye. Participants: Twelve senior nursing faculty members were recruited through purposive sampling with maximum variation, supplemented by snowball sampling to reach participants across diverse institutional contexts; the mean age was 54.67 years, with an average of 29.50 years of academic experience. Methods: Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth, online individual interviews. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis framework. Rigor was ensured through reflexive researcher positioning, collaborative analytic discussion, and member checking with six participants. Results: Three themes emerged: the transformation of academic nursing identity, characterized by growing distance from clinical practice and competing academic demands; shifting student cultures and the transformation of teaching, reflecting pedagogical alienation and decreased depth of learning; and the transformation of academic production from quality to quantity, characterized by metric-driven academic value, disconnection from nursing practice, and the burden of academic productivity. Conclusions: Senior nursing faculty members in Türkiye are navigating interlocking structural pressures that have destabilized the professional foundations of nursing academia. Urgent institutional responses are needed, including restructuring academic roles to protect clinical engagement, supporting pedagogical adaptation, and reconceptualizing promotion criteria to honor the full breadth of nursing scholarly contribution. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: On-Line Scheduling with A Non-Renewable Resource Under Periodic Supply
Abstract: This is the first paper to address an on-line scheduling problem with a non-renewable resource. Resource is supplied with known quantity periodically. The jobs arriving on-line over time have the same basic processing time and the same required quantity of resource. Each job is revealed until its release time, and a scheduler makes decision without the information of future jobs. If the available quantity of the resource satisfies the resource requirement, a job is processed with the basic processing time by consuming the resource requirement. Otherwise, the job can be processed with deterioration under a longer processing time by consuming the insufficient resource quantity. The objective is to minimize the makespan. For this problem on a single machine, we derive a lower bound on the competitive ratio by adversary strategy, and provide a best possible on-line algorithm with a competitive ratio of 1 + α, where α is the positive root of α2 + 3α = 1. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Using a UE5 Platform Based on Point Cloud to Develop the Digital Twin System of a Lianziya Scenic Spot in Xilingxia of the Yangtze River in China
Abstract: Addressing the challenges of complex terrain modeling and poor real-time interactivity in geologically sensitive areas, this study presents a digital twin system construction method based on the Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) platform. Taking the Lianziya dangerous rock mass in the Three Gorges area as a case study, high-precision terrain data were acquired using an unmanned aerial vehicle equipped with light detection and ranging, fused with oblique photography imagery. A cascade filtering pipeline was implemented to optimize point cloud quality, and the quadric error metrics algorithm was applied for model simplification. The results show that the method reduced the mesh polygon count by 50% while maintaining level of detail 4 accuracy, with a mean geometric error (Hausdorff distance) of only 0.018 m. The resulting system enables dynamic weather simulation and adaptive path planning, maintaining a stable frame rate of over 60 FPS at 4K resolution, effectively resolving rendering stalls in large-scale scenes. Title: Why (not) subscribe? Drivers and barriers of grocery replenishment subscriptions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Subscription models are gaining importance across retail sectors, yet a picture of consumers’ evaluations of replenishment subscriptions for regularly needed products, particularly groceries, is still lacking. Drawing on perceived value theory and technology acceptance research, this study proposes a value-risk framework for replenishment subscription adoption. It contrasts four value-related drivers (time efficiency, supply reliability, cognitive relief, and cost efficiency) with four corresponding risk-related barriers (time concerns, supply mismatch concerns, lock-in concerns, and financial concerns) and examines their effects on perceived usefulness, attitude, and ultimately usage intention. Two structural models, a ‘drivers model’ and a ‘barriers model’, were estimated using quota-representative surveys in Germany (N = 493) and the UK (N = 339), complemented by multigroup analysis. The results show that subscription evaluations are inherently ambivalent: positive and negative evaluations coexist, but drivers account for considerably more variance in perceived usefulness and attitude than barriers, while financial and supply mismatch concerns still exert strong negative effects. Convenience proves multidimensional: while cognitive relief outweighs time efficiency as a driver of perceived usefulness, distinct barrier facets also show different relevance. The cross-country comparison reveals common patterns alongside differences. Retailers are advised to communicate the benefits of subscriptions more concretely rather than through generic convenience claims. However, relying just on benefit communication is insufficient: adoption also hinges on actively mitigating perceived risks, with messaging tailored to a market's maturity and familiarity. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Foster J.A.; Yung K.L.
Title: Thermal property engineering of lunar regolith via spark plasma sintering
Abstract: The extreme logistical challenges of Lunar exploration and habitation encourage in situ resource utilisation. Spark Plasma Sintering is a technique capable of rapidly consolidating Lunar regolith without additives, leveraging the vacuum conditions of the Lunar surface. The manufactured components could be used for thermal energy storage, construction, or precision engineering, applications that are sensitive to how the thermal properties vary across the Lunar temperature range of −120°C to 120°C. Understanding how the sintering process influences the thermal properties is essential for optimal design and performance. This study investigates the effects of SPS process parameters on the coefficient of thermal expansion, heat capacity, and thermal conductivity of sintered regolith simulants. Both a mare and a highland simulant were sintered to expand the current body of knowledge with this data and with evaluation of the implications for in situ utilisation. The findings show that sintering temperature is the most influential factor affecting all three thermal parameters. Variations in thermal conductivity and heat capacity with density suggest that engineering trade-offs are necessary to optimise the thermal performance of thermal storage systems, structural materials, and precision components. Title: Consequence-driven active defense resource allocation for chemical park cyber-physical systems
Abstract: With the increasing deployment of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), the risk landscape in chemical industrial parks has progressively shifted from the physical domain to the cyber domain. This paradigm shift enables cyber adversaries to manipulate physical processes, thereby inducing catastrophic accidents. Traditional Industrial Control Systems (ICS) defense methods often isolate cyber vulnerability analysis from physical consequence analysis, failing to address this cross-domain threat. To bridge this gap, a hierarchical risk transmission model is established based on a three-layer architecture of chemical park CPS, spanning the information, cyber-physical, and physical layers. Attack graphs are utilized to quantify cross-layer attack paths, and Bayesian networks are employed to infer the severity of physical consequences. A coupling index is proposed to prioritize node defense resources under limited budgets. Furthermore, an attack-defense game model solved by a greedy algorithm is developed to realize a honeypot deployment scheme. The framework is validated using both a real cascaded water tank experimental platform and the non-linear Tennessee Eastman Process benchmark. Results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively intercepts unknown attacks originating from the information layer, thereby preventing catastrophic physical intrusions. Copyright © 2026. Title: Investigation of uncertainties associated with human judgment during the inspection and condition assessment of civil infrastructures
Abstract: Inspection of civil infrastructure components is a critical task to assess their condition states and plan for appropriate maintenance actions. The process of inspection, however, involves several sources of uncertainty that can influence how a component is rated by an inspector. Despite potential consequences, such uncertainties have remained largely unexplored. This motivated the current study to develop a holistic framework to first measure the agreement and consistency of condition state predictions provided by various inspectors through the inter-rater reliability and intra-class correlation methods. The study then advanced to understand how the provided condition ratings can be analyzed, updated, and aggregated, taking into consideration possible interactions among inspectors during an inspection task. The outcome was quantified based on the inclination of participating inspectors to make more conservative, realistic, or less conservative assessments. The cumulative prospect theory was then utilized to quantify how the risk tolerance of individual inspectors can influence the decision making process, both at the time of inspection and during the service life of civil infrastructure components subjected to inspection. In the absence of similar studies, this investigation’s findings helped improve how condition state ratings received from inspectors can be processed and incorporated into a decision making framework. While the exploration of the psychological roots of why various inspectors rate the same component differently remained outside the scope of this study, the quantification of contributing uncertainties is expected to guide future training programs to further enhance the quality of condition assessment and management decisions made based on inspection reports. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Enhancing fog performance through content replacement and caching strategies using Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has resulted in a significant increase in traffic sent to cloud data centers for processing. This event poses significant challenges, including network congestion, increased latency, and higher costs, which are particularly detrimental to real-time applications. Fog computing is a decentralized environment that utilizes Fog Nodes (FN) that are closer to users to process user requests, thereby improving latency, optimizing bandwidth utilization, and reducing costs. By implementing caching strategies within these FNs, we can further reduce response times, particularly for real-time applications. This paper presents a cooperative caching strategy with considering replacement for FNs and uses a Deep Learning (DL) method to predict popular content. Our goals include increasing the Cache Hit Ratio (CHR) while minimizing total delay and total cost to increase user satisfaction, and also answering all user requests by considering content replacement and distributing popular content among FNs to avoid duplication and improve resource usage. Since movie content has a significant contribution to the fronthaul load in fog computing networks, we utilize a real MovieLens dataset to evaluate our proposed method. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method has higher CHR, lower total delay, and lower total cost, while answering all requested content compared to traditional methods. Overall, this significantly improves the performance of fog computing. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Diversification or concentration? Supply chain configuration responses to decoupling risk
Abstract: This study investigates corporate supply chain configuration strategies in the context of perceived decoupling risk. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2023, we employ textual analysis to construct a firm-level index of perceived decoupling risk. Building on this index, we empirically examine its effect on corporate supply chain configuration strategies. The findings reveal that a higher level of perceived decoupling risk prompts firms to pursue greater supply chain diversification, leading to a significant decrease in supply chain concentration; notably, the diversification response is concentrated among firms facing high-intensity risk perception, while low-intensity risk perception is associated with minimal supply chain adjustment. Further analysis reveals that this negative association is attenuated by both executive risk preference and the level of corporate investment irreversibility. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the reduction in supply chain concentration is more pronounced for firms with high overseas revenue exposure, those in strategic emerging industries, and small-scale enterprises. Additionally, this impact is amplified during periods of heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly following the U.S.-China trade frictions in 2018, and is more pronounced in the upstream ends of supply chains. Finally, we find that the proactive supply chain diversification triggered by decoupling risk significantly enhances firms' operational resilience after a three-year adjustment period, demonstrating a long-term benefit for corporate stability. By quantifying firms’ subjective perception of decoupling risk and confirming its significant impact on supply chain configuration, this study provides novel micro-level evidence on firms’ supply chain behaviors in response to external environmental uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
