Authors: Lin H.; Jiang W.; Sun X.
Title: Industrial robotization and provincial green synergy performance in China: Coupling coordination, regional disparities, and dynamic responses
Abstract: Rapid industrial automation is becoming an important feature of production systems operating under economic and environmental constraints, while its observed performance implications may emerge with delay and differ across regions. This study examines whether industrial robotization and provincial green synergy performance evolve in tandem, where coordination disparities originate, and how their dynamic relationship unfolds. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provincial-level regions from 2006 to 2023, we employ a shift-share measure of robot installation density and estimate green synergy performance with a super-efficiency slacks-based measure integrating economic output, urban greening, industrial pollution, and carbon emissions. The coupling coordination degree evaluates the alignment of the two systems, the Dagum Gini decomposition identifies the sources of regional disparities, and a panel vector autoregression examines reciprocal temporal predictability and lagged responses. The national coordination degree increased from 0.4810 to 0.7740, while the overall Gini coefficient declined from 0.1685 to 0.1009. Between-region differences remained the largest component of disparity, accounting for 51.14% on average, with the eastern-western gap being the widest. Robotization predicted green synergy performance nationally and in eastern China, with a negative first-lag association followed by a positive second-lag association. By period 10, innovations in robotization accounted for 18.63% of the forecast-error variance in green synergy performance nationally and 34.02% in eastern China. These results reveal a stage-dependent and regionally uneven predictive relationship, although the research design does not identify structural causal effects. The findings highlight the value of coordinating robot deployment with green process redesign, region-specific technical support, and full-cycle performance monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Öztaş İ.; Demir E.; Yava A.
Title: Closing the gap or transforming the crisis? A qualitative study on the mentoring model as a sustainable solution to instructor shortage in surgical nursing education
Abstract: Background: Pressures on the global nursing education workforce and a growing shortage of clinical educators in surgical settings have placed preceptorship models at the heart of education. Viewing nursing education as a “revenue-generating commodity” raises concerns regarding the erosion of academic identity and the risk of disciplinary expertise being reduced to a technical craft. Aim: This study aimed to describe the effects of the mentorship model in surgical nursing education on academic identity, pedagogical processes, and workforce sustainability, based on the perceptions of academicians and clinical mentor nurses. Design: A study using a qualitative descriptive design was conducted to gather in-depth perspectives from stakeholders in academic and clinical fields. Method: Data were collected through semi-structured individual interviews; audio recordings were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using a self-reflective thematic analysis framework. The study involved 10 academics from the Department of Surgical Nursing and 10 preceptor nurses who supervise students in surgical clinics (Total N = 20). Findings: The analysis revealed four main themes: a shift in academic identity, highlighting the transition of academics from clinical expertise to administrative coordination; pedagogical tension, pointing to the risk of surgical nursing education devolving into the mere transfer of technical skills—or a “watch-and-do” model; a sustainability paradox, describing the invisible labor undertaken by clinical preceptors and the accompanying sense of burnout; and institutional disconnect, revealing—through the participants' own words—the gap between theory and clinical reality. Conclusions: The findings indicate that participants perceive a significant risk regarding the sustainability of the current preceptorship model. Key implications arising from these findings include the development of defined collaboration protocols between the university and the hospital, the recognition of the educational contributions made by clinical preceptor nurses, and the piloting of clinical-academic hybrid staffing models. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The effect of 3D printing technology in early childhood education: A systematic review
Abstract: The current landscape of early childhood education predominantly relies on traditional teaching methods, which may not fully address the diverse learning styles and developmental needs of young children. This systematic literature review examines the role of 3D printing technology as a potential tool to bridge this gap. Utilizing the PICOS framework and PRISMA model, a comprehensive search was conducted across five major databases, EBSCO, Springer, IEEE, ScienceDirect, and Scopus, resulting in the selection of 244 relevant studies based on strict inclusion and exclusion criteria. The findings reveal that 3D printing positively influences various domains of early childhood development, including cognitive growth, motor skills, creativity and design abilities, collaborative learning, educational integration, and foundational knowledge such as shapes, letters, and numbers. Although the current evidence is limited, this review highlights the promising potential of 3D printing to enhance creativity, spatial reasoning, and engagement among young learners. Nonetheless, significant gaps remain in understanding how to effectively integrate 3D printing into early learning environments. These include the need for developmentally appropriate pedagogical strategies, evaluation of long-term educational outcomes, and adequate preparation and training for educators. Addressing these gaps is crucial to fully harness the educational benefits of 3D printing while maintaining a balanced approach that complements traditional play-based learning. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Zhu J.; Jiang Y.; Zhu F.; Chai Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Target item identification for injection attacks in recommender systems via graph-enhanced user representations
Abstract: Recommender systems are increasingly threatened by profile injection attacks. However, most existing defenses focus on detecting fake users, which becomes unreliable as modern attacks generate highly concealed profiles and operational platforms often lack attacker labels or attack priors. To address this limitation, we propose TIGER (Target Item Identification via Graph-Enhanced Representations), a hybrid auditing-oriented framework that reframes the final defensive output from user-level fake user labels to item-level suspicious target item candidates. Importantly, TIGER does not eliminate user-side analysis; instead, it uses unsupervised suspicious user discovery as an intermediate support step for downstream auditing. Specifically, TIGER first leverages a small trusted reference set to learn stable item embeddings and aligns unknown data into a shared semantic space. It then constructs graph-enhanced user representations by integrating rating statistics, preference patterns, and item semantics, enabling the extraction of informative suspicious user candidates for target item auditing. Finally, suspicious target item candidates are flagged through a rank-shift auditing strategy that compares recommendation outcomes before and after reintroducing suspicious users. Extensive experiments on three widely used datasets under ten representative attack scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of TIGER. Across ten attacks, TIGER achieves average DR@5/DR@10 values of 0.4430/0.6120, 0.5550/0.7500, and 0.2670/0.3400 on ML-100K, ML-1M, and Automotive, outperforming the average results of the best baseline selected for each attack by 106.20%/28.25%, 72.36%/64.84%, and 154.29%/111.18%, respectively. These results indicate that TIGER provides a reliable auditing tool for identifying high-risk target item candidates in adversarial recommender systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Semiparametric Bayesian network classifiers
Abstract: Continuous Bayesian network classifiers are attractive because they provide probabilistic interpretability, but they face a trade-off between the computational efficiency of parametric modeling and the flexibility and computational cost of nonparametric density estimation. This paper studies whether semiparametric modeling can provide a better solution for continuous classification than purely Gaussian or kernel-based approaches. Therefore, we define a family of semiparametric Bayesian network classifiers in which each continuous node is modeled either parametrically or nonparametrically, and we instantiate this framework across seven established classifier structures. We propose efficient learning algorithms that automatically determine the best structure and distribution type (parametric or nonparametric) from data. Experiments on 25 UCI benchmark datasets using multiple predictive metrics, runtime analysis, and statistical significance testing show that the proposed models generally achieve better classification performance than their parametric counterparts, while incurring lower prediction-time costs than fully nonparametric alternatives. These results are relevant for researchers and practitioners who require interpretable probabilistic classifiers in settings where Gaussian assumptions may be too restrictive and uniformly nonparametric modeling may be computationally burdensome. More broadly, the findings suggest that adaptive node-wise distribution selection is a promising framework for probabilistic classification and motivate future work on mixed-type variables and alternative learning strategies. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Bridging Transparency Gaps in Construction Claims through Blockchain Integration
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The construction industry plays a vital role in Pakistan's economy, yet it continues to face persistent challenges in claim administration that hinder project performance, transparency, and trust among stakeholders. This study addresses these challenges by identifying the principal shortcomings of conventional claim management systems and developing a blockchain-based claims management application to improve security, traceability, and procedural efficiency. A three-stage research design was adopted. First, a systematic literature review was conducted to identify deficiencies in traditional claim management practices. This was followed by semistructured interviews with fifteen contract specialists involved in extension of time (EOT) claims to validate and refine the identified issues. Second, a decentralized application (DApp) was developed using React.js front-end and Solidity-based smart contracts and deployed on the Polygon test network to enable faster and more cost-effective transactions. Third, the developed system was evaluated through expert review involving 32 participants drawn from contracting, consulting, client organizations, and academia, followed by statistical analysis. The findings indicate that the proposed blockchain-based claims management system (B-CMS) improves data integrity, transparency, traceability, and timeliness in claim administration compared with traditional approaches. However, the system is not intended to replace professional judgment in highly subjective claim situations and is not suitable for capturing oral instructions or unstructured design and work-pattern changes. Despite these limitations, the study demonstrates the feasibility of B-CMS for construction claim administration in Pakistan and offers insights that may be relevant to comparable project environments internationally.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Xin Z.; Qiaoyun Y.; Jixuan H.; Jiao W.; Li W.
Title: eHealth literacy levels and associated factors among nursing students: A global systematic review and meta-analysis
Abstract: Background: The rapid digital transformation of healthcare highlights the importance of electronic health literacy (eHealth literacy) for nursing students. However, existing global evidence regarding their eHealth literacy levels and associated factors remains fragmented. Objective: To determine the overall level of e-health literacy among nursing students worldwide, analyze its associated factors and associations with health outcomes, and provide evidence-based support for nursing education reform in the digital age. Methods: A systematic search was conducted in eight Chinese and international databases, including PubMed, for cross-sectional studies published from the inception of each database through June 1, 2026. Study quality was assessed using the AHRQ scale, and random-effects meta-analyses and meta-regression analyses were performed using Stata 19.0. This systematic review protocol was registered in advance with PROSPERO (Registration No.: CRD420261418156). Results: A total of 20 cross-sectional studies involving 12,390 nursing students across 11 countries were ultimately included. The pooled eHEALS score for nursing students worldwide was29.51 (95% CI: 28.42–30.61), indicating an overall level slightly above average; however, there was extremely high heterogeneity among studies (I2 = 99.4%, P < 0.001). Senior-year students demonstrated significantly higher levels of literacy than junior-year students (SMD = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.41–0.59, P < 0.001); gender had no significant overall effect on literacy (SMD = −0.04, 95% CI: −0.35–0.27, P = 0.803). Regression analysis showed that living in an urban area (β = 4.24, P < 0.001) and having good economic conditions (β = 0.79, P < 0.001) were exploratory study-level indicators associated with higher literacy. Digital health literacy was moderately positively correlated with health-promoting behaviors (r = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.35–0.49, P < 0.001) and was significantly associated with lower levels of anxiety (OR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92–0.99, P = 0.006). Conclusions: Overall, the digital health literacy of nursing students worldwide is acceptable, but regional digital divides remain prominent. Systematic nursing education may help enhance digital health literacy, which is associated with more positive health behaviors and mental health outcomes. Institutions need to refine their digital health curriculum systems, focusing on cultivating students' abilities in information evaluation and AI-assisted decision-making to meet the evolving demands of digital healthcare and artificial intelligence. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Narrative-driven VR exergames for active older adults: Examining the impact of narrative styles and themes on motivation and user experience
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Older adults often face the dual challenge of insufficient physical activity and unmet psychological needs. Although exergames can promote physical activity, they often struggle to sustain motivation or adequately support psychological need satisfaction. This work explores the potential of integrating narrative into a VR cycling exergame, focusing on how narrative design can enhance motivation and fulfill psychological needs. Two experiments examined the impact of narrative styles with varying interactivity demands and different narrative themes (hedonic, eudaimonic, mixed-affective) on user experience. Study 1 (N=15) suggested that interactive narrative styles were associated with enhanced autonomy and relatedness, facilitated attentional dissociation from bodily fatigue, and led to higher psychological need satisfaction and lower perceived exertion, albeit at the cost of increased cognitive demands. Study 2 (N=36) compared hedonic, eudaimonic, and mixed-affective narratives. Hedonic narratives appeared to support flow and motivation with relatively low cognitive demands, whereas eudaimonic narratives were linked to deeper emotional and reflective engagement but imposed higher cognitive and emotional demands, leading to reduced replay intention. Mixed-affective narratives, by contrast, presented a potentially more balanced trade-off between motivational benefits and competence satisfaction. Interpreted through a Self-Determination Theory-informed perspective, these findings provide insights into how narrative styles and affective themes may be leveraged to design VR exergames that better align psychological engagement with older adults’ physical capacities. Overall, these exploratory findings highlight both the promise and the limitations of narrative-driven exergame design, and they offer implications for the development of adaptive, psychologically informed exergames for older adults. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Using reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a wine tasting service in Italy: Findings from a life cycle assessment application experience
Abstract: Wine tourism, including winery visits, tastings, and cultural events, boosts sustainable development but generates environmental impacts ranging from food and wine production to tasting services. This study applies Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), focused on Carbon Footprint (CF), to compare the use of reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a tasting service in an Apulian winery. A cradle-to-grave analysis reveals that, in baseline scenario, reusable plates showed a slightly higher CF than single-use plates (0.0668 vs. 0.0635 kgCO₂eq/person served, respectively). Based on the results obtained, process optimisation solutions were identified: it was found that using photovoltaic-powered energy-efficient dishwasher may reduce the CF of reusable plates by 67%, reducing the impact to 0.0179 kgCO₂eq/person served in the best-performing scenario. Five service configurations were then tested over a total of 2500 customers served in six months, assuming a constant optimal dishwasher loading efficiency (i.e., operating exclusively at full capacity). Whilst the absolute reuse rate of the plate stock inherently scales with customer volume (averaging approximately 73 uses per plate in the baseline period), the results showed that, without technological improvements, the lowest-impact option was to serve 500 people with reusable plates and 2000 with disposable plates. Overall, this study extends the application of Life Cycle Assessment from conventional production systems to experiential tourism services. The findings demonstrate that the environmental performance of tableware is not solely dictated by intrinsic material properties, but is fundamentally driven by the systemic operational configuration, including dishwashing efficiency, service volumes, and the carbon intensity of the electricity mix. Consequently, this study provides a novel, scalable methodological framework to support wineries and tourism operators in designing scientifically grounded, lower-impact tasting services. © 2026

Title: CCA-ID: Confidence-calibrated adaptive intrusion detection with selective routing for IoT networks
Abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has extended the cyber-attack surface. In resource-constrained IoT monitoring environments, maintaining always-on deep or ensemble-based intrusion detection can be challenging for high-rate, real-time traffic. This study presents CCA-ID, Confidence Calibrated Adaptive Intrusion Detection which integrates calibrated decision confidence with selective, resource-aware inference for IoT intrusion detection. CCA-ID combines an isotonic-calibrated logistic regression gate, heterogeneous heavy learners including DNN, XGBoost, and LightGBM, and a stacking meta-classifier within a class-specific confidence-driven routing mechanism. High-confidence samples are finalized by the lightweight calibrated gate, whereas low-confidence samples are selectively routed to the heavy ensemble for deeper analysis. The proposed CCA-ID is evaluated on the large-scale Gotham Dataset 2025, using a final experimental dataset comprising 7,792,438 packet-level samples across 18 traffic classes. Experimental results indicate that CCA-ID achieves 89.92% accuracy, 61.70% macro F1-score, and 98.93% macro ROC-AUC, while routing only 6.28% of samples to the heavy ensemble. The method also achieves an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 7.66%, showing improved confidence reliability for routing decisions. An inference-time analysis further indicates that CCA-ID achieves a 13.94 ×  speedup over the always-on heavy stack on a fixed stratified subset of the held-out test set. Overall, CCA-ID provides a calibrated trade-off between selective inference and heavy-model invocation for IoT intrusion detection. It reduces unnecessary heavy-model usage while maintaining strong threshold-free discriminative performance under severe class imbalance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: CrackLite: lightweight concrete crack segmentation with direction-guided topology aggregation and local geometry refinement
Abstract: Concrete crack segmentation in field inspection images remains challenging due to thin structures, weak contrast, irregular morphology, and confusing background patterns. This paper presents CrackLite, a lightweight topology-aware segmentation network for thin-crack pattern recognition. CrackLite introduces a Direction-Guided Topology Aggregation module to capture crack-oriented contextual dependencies and a Normal-Calibrated Local Geometry Refinement module to enhance local structural discrimination. A training-only auxiliary supervision scheme provides structural regularization without increasing inference-time complexity. Experiments on a self-collected Bridge Crack dataset and two public benchmarks show competitive segmentation accuracy with structure-sensitive behavior. Paired image-level analysis on Bridge Crack, zero-shot evaluation on PCHUN, and Jetson Orin NX profiling provide complementary evidence on performance differences, cross-domain transfer, and deployment efficiency under the evaluated protocols. Overall, CrackLite offers an accuracy–topology–efficiency trade-off for resource-constrained infrastructure crack segmentation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Dynamic event-triggered distributed control for predefined-time optimal energy management in microgrids
Abstract: A novel distributed control framework is developed for the optimal energy management (OEM) of microgrids, integrating a predefined-time control method and an event-triggered (ET) mechanism. Unlike conventional finite-time or fixed-time stability approaches, the upper bound of the convergence time is directly predefined by users, independent of initial conditions and system parameters. Title: Enhancing mass transfer and water drainage in proton exchange membrane fuel cells via active-passive synergistic composite flow channels

Abstract: Appropriate design and optimization of cathode flow fields are crucial for enhancing the overall performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Title: Client selection of multi-criteria and adaptive deadline in federated learning
Abstract: Edge computing-enabled federated learning (FL) is pivotal for privacy-preserving data-intensive applications, but data and system heterogeneity severely degrade global model performance, slow convergence, and induce fairness issues. Existing single-criterion client selection methods fail to handle strong data heterogeneity, while static timing controls exacerbate the dropout effect in heterogeneous environments. To address these critical challenges, we propose FedMA, a novel FL framework integrating Multi-Criteria Client Selection (MCCS) and Adaptive Deadline Determination (ADD). MCCS synthesizes three key metrics—data volume, data distribution (measured via Earth Mover’s Distance, EMD), and participation frequency—to ensure data quality and selection fairness, avoiding high-resource client dominance. ADD dynamically adjusts round deadlines using Deadline Efficiency (DDLE) and Round Utility, adapting to device computing/communication capabilities and training progress. Extensive experiments on FEMNIST, CIFAR-10, and GoogleSpeech datasets demonstrate FedMA’s effectiveness. On FEMNIST, FedMA attains the highest accuracy among all compared methods (81.45%); on CIFAR-10 (70.95%) and GoogleSpeech (71.51%) its accuracy is on par with the strongest baseline (Oort). Authors: Hu J.; Zhang H.; Zhou X.; Ye Y.; Tao L.
Title: Mirror-Smoothing: Leveraging historical data for enhanced utility in differentially private data stream release
Abstract: Data stream release enables real-time analysis across various applications but raises significant privacy concerns due to the risk of exposing sensitive user information. Although several studies leverage Differential Privacy (DP) to add noise to released statistics and protect privacy, existing methods face critical challenges, including sampling myopia, budget misallocation, and noise volatility, which degrade the utility of the released data. To address these challenges, we propose Mirror-Smoothing, a novel framework that incorporates three coordinated mechanisms: Sample-Mirror, Budget-Mirror, and Noise-Mirror. Sample-Mirror adjusts the sampling rate based on historical data, Budget-Mirror optimizes privacy budget allocation by learning from historical consumption, and Noise-Mirror generates temporally correlated noise by combining fresh and historical noise to mitigate volatility. By utilizing historical data to guide decisions on sampling, budget allocation, and noise generation, Mirror-Smoothing significantly improves data utility while ensuring rigorous privacy guarantees. Extensive experiments on both real-world and synthetic datasets show that Mirror-Smoothing achieves the best overall average performance among the compared methods across various utility metrics and privacy budgets, particularly under complex data stream patterns. Title: Contextualizing negotiation research: The unique dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations
Abstract: Effective buyer–supplier negotiations are important for organizations to attain their goals and for wider society to have a reliable supply of goods and services. These negotiations also have distinctive characteristics that differentiate them from other negotiation settings, such as personal buyer–seller negotiations, which have attracted much of the attention in the negotiation literature. Given the differences between professional buyer–supplier and personal buyer–seller negotiations, some findings from personal negotiations may have limited applicability in supply chain settings, while others hold across contexts. These findings have important implications for both negotiation research and education, calling for careful contextualization based on the type of negotiation. By reviewing recent studies in the supply chain management literature, this article highlights several common dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations and how they affect negotiation outcomes. These dynamics are broadly categorized into the non-exhaustive themes of power in ongoing buyer–supplier relationships, other relational factors (supply network complexity, cross-cultural relations, and AI adoption), and negotiation strategies in buyer–supplier relationships (distributive, integrative, and mixed strategies), providing scholars with an overview of selected recent research on buyer–supplier negotiations. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: LLMs’ reshaping of people, processes, products, and society in software development: a qualitative exploration with early adopters
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping software development, but their impact across the full software development lifecycle is underexplored. Existing work tends to focus on isolated activities such as code generation or testing, leaving open questions about how LLMs affect developers, processes, products, and the broader software ecosystem. We address this gap through semi-structured interviews with sixteen early-adopter software professionals who integrated LLM-based tools into their day-to-day work in early to mid-2023. We treat these interviews as early empirical evidence and compare participants’ accounts with recent work on LLMs in software engineering, noting which early patterns persist or shift. Using thematic analysis, we organize our findings around four dimensions: people, process, product, and society. Developers reported substantial productivity gains from reducing mundane tasks, streamlining search, and accelerating debugging, but also described a productivity-quality paradox: they frequently discarded generated code and shifted effort from writing code to critically evaluating and integrating it. LLM use was highly phase-dependent, with strong uptake in implementation and debugging but limited influence on requirements gathering and collaborative work. Participants developed new competencies to use LLMs effectively, including prompt engineering strategies, multi-layered verification, and security-conscious integration to protect proprietary data. They also anticipated changes in hiring expectations, team practices, and computing education, while emphasizing that human judgment and foundational software engineering skills remain essential. Our findings, consistent with evidence from large-scale studies, offer actionable implications for developers, organizations, educators, and tool designers seeking to integrate LLMs responsibly into professional software practice. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Multi-joint collaborative control for selective suppression of low-frequency chatter in robotic milling considering dynamic coupling
Abstract: Robotic milling has emerged as a cost-effective and flexible solution for machining large-scale complex components, yet its productivity is severely bottlenecked by low-frequency chatter (LFC) induced by joint flexibility. Existing joint-based vibration suppression strategies are typically confined to the Independent Joint Control (IJC) framework, which neglects inter-joint dynamic coupling and models each joint as an isolated single-input-single-output (SISO) system. Neglecting inter-joint dynamic coupling introduces massive unstructured modeling errors, forcing IJC-based H∞ controllers into extreme performance conservatism to guarantee robustness. Conversely, IJC-based DVF controller (or decentralized viscous damper) is inherently velocity-dependent, rendering it hypersensitive to high-frequency vibrations and ineffective for LFC suppression. To break these theoretical bottlenecks, this paper proposes a Multi-Joint Collaborative Control (MJCC) framework utilizing joint electromagnetic torsional actuators (ETAs). By explicitly establishing a coupled Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) structural dynamic model, the proposed approach eliminates the massive modeling errors inherent in IJC assumptions, fundamentally minimizing performance-robustness trade-offs. Furthermore, by exploiting the vibration directionality induced by dynamic coupling, an MJCC framework combining directional gain shaping with robust gain scaling is developed. The directional control gain is synthesized via the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) method in the modal space, which synergistically concentrates control energy on the targeted LFC mode to selectively suppress LFC with minimal control energy. Additionally, to address robustness challenges posed by residual modeling errors and control delays, a gain scaling factor is introduced to attenuate the intensity of the control action to ensure system robustness, which establishes an optimal trade-off between targeted performance and robustness through a fixed-structure H∞ controller synthesis. Finally, a series of experiments verified the physical feasibility, and large-scale milling experiments were conducted to compare MJCC with traditional IJC-based controllers, which verified the performance advantages of MJCC. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: When stigmatized workers become consumers
Abstract: Existing research on occupational stigma has focused primarily on workplace consequences, with less attention to how stigmatized service workers respond to service failures as consumers. Title: Educational legacies of christian missions: Evidence from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Abstract: This paper investigates the educational legacies of Christian missions established before independence, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, focusing on contemporary disparities in educational content, quality, access, and outcomes. Title: Newton-Cotes-based FIR smoothing for robust ECG segmentation: Integration with the Modified Varri method
Abstract: Reliable segmentation of electrocardiographic (ECG) signals is often compromised by noise and non-stationary artifacts, which can lead to unstable boundary detection. This study proposes a preprocessing strategy to enhance the robustness of the Modified Varri method using Newton–Cotes Moving Average (NCMA) filters. NCMA filters are symmetric, normalized FIR operators derived from closed Newton–Cotes quadrature rules. Their construction ensures unit DC gain, linear-phase behavior, and exact preservation of low-order polynomial trends in an integral sense. These properties make them suitable as structured smoothing operators for ECG signals, reducing noise variance while maintaining the underlying signal morphology. NCMA filters with 3, 5, and 7 points were evaluated on both synthetic signals and real recordings from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database using standard denoising metrics (MSE, SNR, and PRD) and a segmentation-specific Boundary Stability Index (BSI). Results show that the 5-point NCMA filter provides the best trade-off between noise reduction and signal fidelity, outperforming Savitzky–Golay smoothing of comparable length on synthetic data. On real recordings, while the 5-point filter balances signal fidelity and noise reduction, the 7-point configuration provides the highest segmentation stability (lowest BSI), despite greater morphological smoothing. Statistical validation across multiple noise realizations confirms the robustness of the proposed approach. These findings demonstrate that NCMA-based preprocessing offers a reliable and lightweight alternative to conventional SG filtering, enhancing ECG segmentation reliability in noisy environments. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: An improved algorithm for searching all minimal paths in networks using degree-2 chain compression and boundary-closure pruning
Abstract: Minimal paths (MPs) are fundamental to binary and multistate network reliability evaluation, but exhaustive MP search becomes computationally expensive as network size increases. To reduce redundant branch expansion in DFS-based MP search, this study develops an improved algorithm that eliminates redundant branches before and during the search process. First, an s–t core network is extracted by recursively removing source-sink-irrelevant leaf branches, and degree-2 chains are compressed to replace deterministic node-by-node traversal with endpoint jumps. The local-closure pruning rule is refined using a sink-side criterion, and the inherited first-bifurcation decomposition is implemented with spawn subprocesses. A formal correctness theorem establishes complete and duplicate-free MP enumeration under the combined preprocessing and pruning rules. Computational experiments on the reported benchmark and transportation-network cases show lower wall-clock time than the tested Bai and Zhou baselines where comparable results are available; the magnitude of the gain depends on network topology, terminal placement, and workload. Authors: Zhang D.-Y.; Qian H.-M.; Cao Y.
Title: Green energy transition in China's primary aluminum industry: Economic evaluation and pathways
Abstract: Propelled by China's dual carbon goals, the primary aluminum industry, which relies heavily on coal-fired electricity, is facing an urgent green energy transition for decarbonization. Particularly in major producing regions such as Inner Mongolia, Yunnan, and Shandong, achieving transition while ensuring economic viability is critical to the industry's sustainable development. This study applies cost‒benefit analysis to evaluate the economic performance of three transition pathways (distributed renewable self-supply, direct green power connection, and green power trading) in these three regions. Under current data conditions, green power trading yields negative financial returns in all three regions. In Yunnan, the remaining two pathways also lack economic feasibility considering Yunnan's already high share of hydropower and its associated low grid tariffs. In Inner Mongolia and Shandong, direct green power connection combined with self-owned power unit peak shaving emerges as the most cost-effective transition pathway. Sensitivity analysis reveals that economic viability is most sensitive to electricity prices of self-owned power plants and transmission and distribution tariffs, with sensitivity coefficients of ±2.89 and ± 1.48, respectively. This study delivers both data-driven references and practical insights for local primary aluminum producers, emphasizing that decarbonization pathways must be tailored to regional conditions and closely aligned with the policy landscape. Title: Life cycle assessment (LCA)-informed optimization framework with temporal fusion transformer for high-recovery hybrid semi-batch/batch reverse osmosis (HSBRO)

Title: A comprehensive survey on robust federated learning: From threat models to defense mechanisms
Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing raw data and has become an important paradigm for privacy-sensitive intelligent systems. Nevertheless, its distributed architecture, heterogeneous data, and unreliable participants introduce substantial robustness and security challenges, ranging from communication noise and system failures to poisoning, privacy inference, and Byzantine attacks. In this paper, we present a structured survey of robust federated learning. We first organize the literature through a threat-oriented taxonomy that covers poisoning attacks, privacy leakage risks, Byzantine behavior, and scenario-specific robustness challenges. We explicitly analyze stronger adversaries that collude, coordinate poisoning campaigns, replace models behind secure aggregation, and adapt their optimization to defense-specific weaknesses. We then review representative defense mechanisms, including robust aggregation, backdoor defense, privacy-preserving training, secure aggregation, and personalized robustness enhancement. Particular attention is given to three recurring tensions in the literature: robustness under Non-IID data, robustness-efficiency trade-offs, and robustness-privacy trade-offs. We further discuss robust federated learning in wireless and IoT environments, where communication uncertainty and resource constraints become first-order concerns. We examine how existing robustness mechanisms translate, or fail to translate, to foundation-model-based FL, federated fine-tuning of large language models, federated reinforcement learning, agentic federated systems, and federated retrieval-augmented generation. Finally, we summarize open challenges and outline future research directions for building more reliable, efficient, and deployable federated learning systems. Copyright © 2026. Title: Financial leverage in business sector profitability: A review
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between financial leverage and corporate profitability in a context of heightened economic uncertainty following the COVID-19 pandemic, a period during which organizations have been compelled to redefine their financing strategies in order to preserve sustainability and financial performance. The primary objective was to systematically analyze recent empirical evidence on the impact of financial leverage on corporate profitability. To this end, a systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, using the Scopus database. The search strategy incorporated terms related to financial leverage, financing, profitability, and firms, while the 2020–2025 period and the explicit inclusion of key topic-related concepts were established as the main eligibility criteria. From an initial total of 7,587 identified records, a rigorous screening process was carried out based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in the final selection of 36 articles for qualitative analysis. The study employed synthesis matrices, bibliometric analysis, and keyword co-occurrence networks, which made it possible to identify trends, predominant methodological approaches, and the main findings. The results indicate that companies rely on a combination of internal and external financing sources, including bank credit, bond issuance, informal financing, and fintech tools. In general, financial leverage has a positive effect on indicators such as ROA, ROE, and ROI, provided that adequate financial planning, cost control, and efficient debt management are in place. However, in SMEs or firms with high levels of indebtedness and limited managerial capacity, the impact may be negative or statistically insignificant. It is concluded that financial leverage constitutes a strategic tool for enhancing profitability, provided that it is managed prudently and within a comprehensive financial risk management framework. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Fast dynamic obstacle avoidance for quadruped robots via privileged state estimation and hierarchical reinforcement learning
Abstract: Avoiding fast, dynamic obstacles is a safety-critical capability for legged robots operating near people and in unstructured environments: the robot must infer an incoming object’s motion from brief noisy observations, generate a collision-free body motion, and execute it within tens of milliseconds. We present a hierarchical system for high-speed dynamic obstacle avoidance, instantiated and stress-tested on quadruped projectile evasion. A history-based Ball Estimator encodes short observation windows into an estimate of projectile motion that stays stable under observation noise, where simple differentiation degrades; a privileged High-Level Intention Modeling (HIM) Estimator aligns observation histories with future robot states to produce an intent latent for control. A lightweight planner searches over target body poses on a voxelized trunk model and outputs a collision-aware goal, which is tracked by a low-level policy trained with an asymmetric actor-critic and curriculum learning. In Isaac Gym, the method achieves a 76.3% success rate against 10 m/s projectiles and outperforms all baselines under the same training budget. We further deploy the trained policy on a Unitree Go1 and validate near-real-time execution of the planning and control stack under an external mocap-grade projectile-state input protocol with injected latency and noise; onboard visual perception is not evaluated in these hardware trials. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Jiang G.; Tang Q.; Zhang Z.; Cheng L.
Title: Multi-agent assisted co-evolutionary memetic algorithm for lot-streaming flexible job shop energy-efficient scheduling problem with asynchronous assembly
Abstract: Mass customization increasingly requires flexible manufacturing systems in which component processing, material transfer, and multi-station assembly must be coordinated simultaneously. This study investigates a lot-streaming flexible job shop energy-efficient scheduling problem with asynchronous assembly (LS-FJSEP-AA). It integrates lot streaming and flexible processing with inter-stage transportation and an unpaced assembly line subject to precedence and blocking constraints. A bi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model is formulated to minimize makespan and total energy consumption, with energy accounting for processing, setup, machine idle/on–off, transportation, assembly, and assembly-station idle states. Based on the cross-stage timing relationships, two structural properties are identified to guide critical-operation adjustment and assembly prioritization. To efficiently solve the resulting strongly coupled problem, a multi-agent assisted co-evolutionary memetic algorithm (MA-CoEA) is developed. MA-CoEA integrates offline GEP-assisted initialization, objective-oriented cooperative evolution, problem-specific neighborhood search, and DQN-based adaptive control. Computational experiments show that MA-CoEA achieves competitive solution quality and convergence performance against state-of-the-art algorithms, while exhibiting stable performance across independent runs on representative benchmark instances. An industrially inspired case further demonstrates the effectiveness of lot streaming and cross-stage schedule adjustment in improving the trade-off between makespan and energy consumption. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Physics-informed surrogates for multi-objective optimization of scraped falling-film plastic pyrolysis reactors
Abstract: Melt pyrolysis of mixed polyolefin waste is limited by slow, non-uniform heating of viscous, low-conductivity melts and coke formation on overheated or poorly wetted walls. Scraped falling-film reactors can alleviate these limitations by renewing thin melt films, but their design remains challenging because scraping simultaneously enhances heat transfer, alters residence time, and affects film stability. Here, we develop a physics-informed CFD–surrogate–optimization framework for a vertical scraped falling-film pyrolysis reactor. A two-phase volume-of-fluid CFD model, benchmarked against TG and batch pyrolysis data, couples endothermic cracking kinetics with a Danckwerts-type surface-renewal closure using a dimensionless scraping number, avoiding moving-mesh resolution of blade motion. The model reproduces batch oil yields at 440 and 480 °C with absolute deviations within 1.3 wt%. Mechanistic maps show that stronger scraping monotonically increases heat-transfer enhancement, whereas conversion enhancement peaks at intermediate intensity, revealing a non-monotonic balance between surface renewal and effective residence time. To accelerate design-space interrogation, a physics-informed neural-network surrogate constrained by energy and reaction-progress residuals is trained on CFD data; on 60 held-out cases, it achieves R2 = 0.83–0.98 for key scalar and field outputs. Coupling the surrogate with NSGA-III identifies Pareto trade-offs among oil yield, specific energy input, and coking risk. Balanced candidates cluster at 460–471 °C and scraping numbers of 11–14; within this region, B3–B4, corresponding to 466–469 °C and scraping numbers of 13–14, are predicted to deliver 80.9–81.4 wt% oil, defining a prioritized operating window within the design space. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhang Z.-M.; Xie B.-C.; Zhang S.; Su J.; Zhang X.-P.
Title: Multi-dimensional resilience assessment and spatio-temporal risk transmission in interconnected power grids under high-level renewable penetration
Abstract: Decarbonization is reshaping the structure and risk profile of power networks. Using complex network analysis and dynamic simulation, this study assesses the resilience of China’s provincial power grids under uncertainty. It combines historical data for 2005–2023 with scenario simulations for 2030–2060 to examine network evolution, risk propagation, and restoration during the energy transition. The results show that: (1) Interprovincial electricity dependence increases as the network evolves from dispersed connections to coordinated multipath transmission. High renewable-energy penetration strengthens block-structured dependencies and concentrates risk along critical transmission corridors; (2) The low-carbon transition provides only modest gains in initial disturbance resistance but more consistently reduces post-restoration residual and cumulative losses; (3) Resilience outcomes vary across regions and disturbance types because of differences in exposure, cascading propagation, and restoration benefits. Line failures are more recoverable, whereas persistent supply-side shocks cannot be fully mitigated through network reconfiguration alone; and (4) System losses depend on failure locations, cascading pathways, and restoration sequences rather than the scale of initial failures alone. Static topological indicators therefore cannot fully capture systemic risk. These findings support critical-corridor protection, system-wide topology optimization, flexible-resource deployment, and region-specific resilience planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ye Z.; Zhou X.; Xia Q.; Chen X.; Lu X.; Teng Q.; Ren T.; Tong X.; Chen Z.; Li Y.; Zhu L.; Wen C.; Lin J.; Ma J.
Title: Two-step K⁺/Rb⁺ ion exchange enabling high mechanical properties and brittle-ductile transition in 3D-printed dental lithium disilicate
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: To improve the mechanical reliability of thin-walled lithium disilicate (LD) veneers, this study developed a strengthening strategy that integrates vat photopolymerization (VP) with a two-step ion-exchange (IE) process. VP was employed to fabricate thin-walled LD structures, eliminating machining-induced damage, while a sequential K⁺/Rb⁺ IE process achieved both sufficient IE depth and compressive stress, overcoming their conventional trade-off. The two-step IE process increased the flexural strength of LD by 52.0% to 448.6 ± 31.5 MPa and improved the fracture toughness by 80.4% to 2.64 ± 0.10 MPa m1/2. The significant enhancement in mechanical performance was mainly attributed to a 349% increase in compressive stress (CS), reaching 141.9 ± 4.4 MPa. The atomic force microscope revealed that the ultrahigh CS was attributed to the volumetric expansion of an amorphous phase. Under scratching loads of 100 mN above the brittle-ductile transition threshold (∼70 mN), the coefficient of friction of IE-processed LD increased by nearly 50%, indicating a transition in energy dissipation from brittle crack initiation to localized plastic deformation. Overall, the VP-fabricated LD, after undergoing the two-step IE processing, exhibits markedly enhanced strength and toughness. This improved mechanical performance effectively resists crack initiation and propagation caused by sharp contacts, thereby contributing to the superior long-term reliability of the LD veneers in the oral masticatory environment. © 2026

Title: Economic consequences of climate change: Evidence from the Philippines
Abstract: This paper evaluates the economic implications of climate change in the Philippines. Data spanning two decades reveal that warmer temperatures increase out-migration, yet locations exposed to intense heat send fewer migrants to historically connected destinations. This pattern raises the question of how climate change affects the spatial allocation of economic activity when mobility is constrained. I employ a quantitative spatial equilibrium model in which rising temperatures and sea-level rise depress local amenities and productivity. Taking climate projections for 2100, I estimate aggregate welfare and output to fall by 15% and 12% respectively, with more prominent losses for high-skilled workers. Large-scale coastal protection can offset damages by up to 3 percentage points, but removing migration barriers attenuates welfare losses by as much as 13 percentage points. © 2026

Title: Exploring the relationships between problem and responsible gambling behaviors across time
Abstract: Recent legislative and technological changes have transformed the gambling landscape in the United States, underscoring the need to better understand both problem gambling and responsible gambling behaviors. The Positive Play framework conceptualizes responsible gambling from the player’s perspective, yet little is known about how these behaviors change over time. The present study examined longitudinal changes in Positive Play scores and problem gambling symptoms among a sample of adult gamblers (n = 2,942). Participants completed repeated assessments of the Positive Play Scale and the Problem Gambling Severity Index across five waves over approximately two years. Confirmatory factor analyses supported the original four-factor structure of the Positive Play Scale. Latent growth models indicated that scores across all Positive Play subscales increased over time, while problem gambling symptoms decreased. Notably, increases in gambling literacy scores were associated with greater reductions in problem gambling severity, whereas changes in other Positive Play domains were not. These findings suggest that gambling literacy, in particular, may be associated with reductions in gambling-related harm over time. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Hossin M.Z.; Chung Y.K.

Title: Operational constraints in professional kitchens: A theory of constraints perspective on food waste reduction
Abstract: Professional kitchens, where core foodservice operations occur, generate up to two-thirds of total food waste. Although recent research has increasingly acknowledged the managerial and operational dimensions of food waste, limited attention has been devoted to explaining how these constraints interact within an integrated operational system. Addressing this gap, this study applies the Theory of Constraints (TOC) and qualitative triangulation through structured observations and in-depth interviews with kitchen staff to identify and analyze waste reduction constraints across kitchen workflows. Four interrelated constraint dimensions were identified, and workflow-tracing analysis revealed a sequential constraint chain in which policy and market constraints appear to influence resource conditions that are reflected in behavioral constraints, where throughput constraints become most visible. Applying Goldratt's Five Focusing Steps across this chain generates prioritized interventions. The study reframes waste as a systemic outcome of upstream pressures and offers a structured diagnostic framework for effective intervention. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Data-driven modeling of toxic dyes adsorption onto human hair-activated carbon using artificial neural networks and Box–Behnken response surface methodology: mechanistic insights and cost evaluation
Abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of human hair activated carbon (HHAC) in removing Methylene Blue (MB) and Eriochrome Black T (EBT) from aqueous solutions using an integrated approach combining experimental analyses with kinetic, thermodynamic, and chemometric modeling. Parametric tests indicated that equilibrium was reached in 40 min, highlighting particularly rapid kinetics. MB adsorption was maximized in a basic environment, whereas EBT adsorption was favored in an acidic environment, confirming the decisive importance of electrostatic interactions. The Langmuir model provided the best fit among the tested isotherm models, particularly for MB, although the fit for EBT was comparatively weaker than that for MB. The pseudo-second-order kinetic models provided the best fits (R2 = 0.87–0.92 for EBT and 0.98 for MB), indicating a mechanism controlled by adsorbent–adsorbate interactions. Box–Behnken response surface modeling showed remarkable robustness (R2 = 0.998 and 0.996, p < 0.0001), identifying optimal conditions at pH 8.7, 65.45 mg L−1 of dye, and 0.25 g L−1 of adsorbent. Meanwhile, artificial neural networks showed slightly lower performance (R2 = 0.9868 for MB and 0.9938 for EBT), while confirming the intrinsic non-linearity of the system and revealing maximum capacities of 365.61 mg g−1 (MB) and 158.63 mg g−1 (EBT). The material retained its effectiveness after five thermal regeneration cycles, demonstrating its stability and potential for the sustainable treatment of colored effluents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhu S.; Niu K.; Li J.; Lu Y.; Liu Y.; Liu J.
Title: CRAFMark: Contrastive-driven robust adaptive frequency-aware video watermarking against H.265/HEVC compression
Abstract: Deep learning-based video watermarking has achieved notable progress in robustness and imperceptibility, yet it remains vulnerable to strong video compression such as H.265/HEVC. The main challenges arise from the non-differentiable operations in real encoders, including quantization, mode decision, and in-loop filtering, as well as the simulation-to-real domain gap between differentiable compression proxies and actual encoding pipelines. To address these issues, we propose CRAFMark, a Contrastive-driven Robust Adaptive Frequency-Aware Video Watermarking framework designed for robust watermarking under real-world H.265/HEVC compression. At the embedding stage, a Hierarchical Wavelet Frequency Modulation (HWFM) module guides watermark embedding toward compression-resilient frequency subbands, while a Motion-aware Temporal-Spatial Channel Attention (MTCA) module is introduced as a task-specific temporal-perceptual enhancement component to exploit motion information and spatiotemporal redundancy. To enable end-to-end optimization against real encoders, CRAFMark further incorporates a lightweight SAO-inspired Diff-SAO refinement module into the differentiable compression proxy to improve proxy fidelity. More importantly, CRAFMark introduces a Cross-domain Contrastive Compression Distillation (CCD) mechanism to align the latent features of proxy-decoded and real-decoded videos, thereby mitigating the proxy-to-real domain shift and encouraging compression-invariant decoding representations. Experiments on Kinetics-600 and UCF-101 demonstrate that CRAFMark achieves higher watermark extraction accuracy than existing methods under severe H.264/AVC and H.265/HEVC compression scenarios, while maintaining reasonable visual quality and temporal perceptual consistency. The proposed method also generalizes well across different video resolutions and frame lengths, indicating its applicability to intelligent and robust video watermarking for copyright protection in highly compressed distribution scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Audiovisual aesthetic matching enhances food evaluation by amplifying pleasure and perceived tastiness
Abstract: Aesthetic experiences can shape the evaluations of consumers, including in the case of food. While matching multisensory cues can enhance perception, such interventions have not always been shown to promote consumption as effectively as predicted. The present study examined whether and how the multisensory aesthetic match of food plating and background music can enhance consumers' hedonic evaluations and purchase intentions. In two studies, participants viewed or tasted foods with varying plating aesthetics, either with music matched or mismatched in aesthetic value (e.g., ugly vs. beautiful). The participants provided food evaluations before or after tasting. The results revealed that matched audiovisual aesthetics produced enhancement effects on expected evaluations across different aesthetic levels among female participants, whereas men's ratings were enhanced only for the less-aesthetic plating. In contrast, actual evaluations were amplified only for healthy food with less-aesthetic and unhealthy food with relatively high-aesthetic plating. The multisensory enhancement of aesthetic value occurred through distinct pathways, influencing pre- and post-tasting evaluations through pleasure and perceived tastiness. These findings reveal that the mechanisms of audiovisual aesthetic matching in enhancing food consumption depend on the type of food and the gender of the participant. Aesthetic cues can be applied to nudge emotional engagement and enrich sensory experiences in daily routines, and to promote health-oriented consumption across different goal orientations (e.g., encouraging or curbing consumption). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Early Termination Provisions in Public–Private Partnerships: Synthesizing Institutional Guidance into Process-Based Benchmarks
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Early termination provisions (ETPs) are critical risk management mechanisms in public–private partnership (PPP) contracts, defining the conditions, processes, and consequences under which contracts may be terminated before their expiry. While leading institutional guidance documents provide extensive and authoritative treatment of ETPs, their coverage is dispersed across different mandates, drafting styles, and levels of procedural detail, making it difficult to extract a coherent, operational benchmark directly from the guidance. The objective of this study is to systematically synthesize institutional PPP guidance into a unified, process-based benchmark for early termination. Using inductive qualitative content analysis methodology, the study examines guidance issued by five widely recognized institutions: the World Bank, the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), the European PPP Expertise Centre (EPEC), the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), and the US Federal Highway Administration (FHWA). The analysis identifies five principal ETP categories—private partner default, contracting authority default, voluntary termination, force majeure (FM), and uninsurability—and, where applicable, drives analytically grounded subcategories. These findings are translated into five benchmark flowcharts that operationalize early termination as a sequenced process structured around circumstances, procedures, and consequences. The results demonstrate that, despite differences in articulation and drafting depth, institutional guidance reflects a shared conceptual framework in which early termination is an exceptional outcome following the failure of cure, adaptation, or policy intervention mechanisms. The resulting benchmarks provide a practical reference for institutions to design, assess, and align ETP regimes in PPP contracts, supporting clearer risk allocation, improved governance, and more defensible termination practices. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: A system dynamics model for sugarcane-based alcohol-to-jet sustainable aviation fuel supply chains
Abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is a key pathway for decarbonizing aviation, but its deployment depends on integrating supply-chain, economic, and policy conditions. This study develops a generalized system dynamics model of a sugarcane alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) supply chain and demonstrates its application using Ecuador as a case study. The model integrates four subsystems: upstream (land allocation, sugar and ethanol production), midstream (ethanol allocation and ATJ conversion), downstream (SAF blending with fossil jet fuel and use), and finance (economic viability). Under baseline conditions, SAF production reaches 50 million liters, corresponding to a blend ratio of 9.7% at a minimum selling price (SAF MSP) of 1.8 USD/L. Sensitivity analysis identified sugarcane yield as the main production driver, while uncertainty analysis also identified ethanol price as the dominant driver of SAF MSP. Policy scenarios showed that stacked interventions, including ethanol price support and an incentive for SAF producers, improved financial viability. Monetizing the avoided emissions from SAF use could accelerate plant deployment, but only at carbon prices well above current levels. Alternative construction paradigms mainly reduced fixed capital investment (FCI), with limited direct effect on SAF MSP, although combining co-location with policy support increased the number of SAF plants that could potentially be deployed and reduced the time required to reach a positive net present value (NPV). The Ecuadorian case study results show that feedstock availability alone is insufficient to enable SAF industry growth, and project economics remain the main limiting factor. The model provides a dynamic framework for evaluating how ATJ industries may evolve under different structural and policy conditions. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Paying for the future? Cross-season pre-sale product launch strategy in hotels
Abstract: Traditional hotels face persistent seasonal demand imbalance, with weak off-peak demand and constrained peak-season capacity. Drawing on Contingency Theory, this study examines cross-season pre-sale as a context-dependent hotel revenue management configuration and investigates how different configurations (i.e., no pre-sale, self-run pre-sale, and platform-based pre-sale) fit varying operating conditions. Results show that cross-season pre-sale does not universally outperform conventional practices; its value depends on the balance among incremental demand, impacts on existing demand, and implementation costs. Moreover, neither self-run nor platform-based pre-sale always dominates, as their relative effectiveness depends on the trade-off between platform-enabled market reach and channel costs. The study identifies boundary conditions for effective cross-season demand coordination and offers practical guidance for configuration choice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Driving impact? How imperfect displacement shapes heterogeneous rebound in carsharing
Abstract: Green technologies, products, and services, such as carsharing, are commonly promoted as pathways to lower environmental impacts by increasing efficiency. Yet rebound effects, behavioral and economic responses to improved efficiency, may erode these environmental impact reductions. Many rebound studies assume perfect displacement, where a new technology or mode of service provision fully replaces an existing service on a one-to-one basis. While analytically convenient, this assumption overlooks real-world complexity and consumer heterogeneity. Using survey data from nearly 4500 Belgian carsharing users, we compare rebound estimates under perfect displacement with those based on reported shifts in mobility. Under the perfect displacement assumption, we find a 53% rebound effect. When accounting for imperfect displacement, however, rebound effects vary widely across users. While median effects remain positive (20%–46%), at the individual level rebound effects range from substantial net benefits to strong rebound (5th–95th percentile: −331% to 147%). A cluster analysis further reveals distinct user groups with systematically different impacts, underscoring that displacement patterns vary not only in scale but also in direction. These findings suggest that carsharing's environmental impact is highly user-dependent, and that relying on a single aggregate estimate may mask critical behavioral variations. As this case study demonstrates, accounting for imperfect displacement in rebound analysis is critical for advancing theory and for tailoring more effective policy interventions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Robust optimization of energy consumption and compliance risk for indirect electric-heating drying of particle-laden water in southern Xinjiang
Abstract: For high-sediment agricultural irrigation water-conveyance conditions in southern Xinjiang, the key drying process parameters of oven-drying-based sediment monitoring equipment have not yet been systematically optimized, which has constrained the measurement accuracy and field applicability of such equipment under complex sediment-laden conditions. Here, we develop a multi-objective framework that balances relative specific energy consumption against the probability of meeting a 0.5% residual-moisture criterion. Heating power, heating time, water-sediment mixture mass and sediment concentration were varied using a Box-Behnken design. Both response-surface models achieved R2 > 0.98. Sediment concentration exerted the strongest influence on residual moisture content and emerged as a key factor linking energy consumption with compliance risk. We then coupled support vector regression, calibrated logistic classification and Monte Carlo chance-constrained Pareto analysis to identify minimum-energy, minimum-risk and compromise knee-point regions. Independent validation experiments subsequently evaluated these regions. The minimum-risk region near 1492 W, 50 min and 400 g met the criterion at sediment concentrations of 1.0% and 17.5%. The knee-point region near 1079 W, 50 min and 400 g met the criterion at 15.0% and 16.5%, but marginally exceeded it at 3.5% (0.52489%). By contrast, the minimum-energy region near 1014 W, 50 min and 400 g failed the criterion at both tested concentrations. Thus, low-energy operation cannot be assumed to preserve compliance; operating conditions must instead reflect an explicit trade-off between energy use and compliance risk. This framework provides an experimentally informed basis for selecting operating conditions in automated gravimetric monitoring of high-sediment irrigation water. Copyright © 2026. Authors: Zhang T.-Q.; Lyu W.-M.; Wang X.-L.; Zhang Z.-L.; Li G.-C.; Wang X.-Y.; Jin J.-L.
Title: Quantitative analysis of causation in flight operation accidents: Event logic knowledge modeling and decoupled Bayesian network inference
Abstract: Aviation accident reports contain rich causal information for flight operation safety, yet existing methods cannot quantify multi-factor co-occurrence or cross-phase patterns, impeding phase-specific prevention. This makes a multi-state complex causation analysis framework theoretically valuable and practically urgent. A quantitative causal analysis framework for flight operation accidents is proposed. Multiple models are integrated to construct a multi-level event logic graph ontology, and core entities and relationships are extracted by evolutionary logic, forming a complete knowledge skeleton. A semi-automated strategy combining large language model pre-annotation with expert verification achieves low-cost, high-consistency transformation of unstructured texts into computable knowledge. Mapping rules from the event logic graph to the Bayesian network are established, decoupling multi-state nodes into binary nodes, enabling expression of multi-factor co-occurrence and joint conditional effects. Network parameters are learned in a data-driven manner, and the differential contributions of causal factors across flight phases are analyzed, providing quantitative foundations for differentiated safety management strategies. The innovative approach realizes an end-to-end transformation from semi-structured accident texts to probabilistic risk models and establishes a full-chain technical system encompassing ontology modeling, knowledge extraction, structure mapping, and probabilistic inference, offering a reusable methodological framework and engineering pathway for data-driven quantitative causation analysis. Authors: Huang C.; Zhang C.; Chen Y.; Fan Y.
Title: SPECTRA: Sequential prismatic ensemble and cross-domain transfer residual alignment for multimodal multi-domain fake news detection
Abstract: The task of multimodal multi-domain fake news detection is to identify the fake news from multiple domains with mixed textual and visual contents. Technically, the existing methods face the following problems: domain feature alignment bias, cross-domain negative transfer under long-tail distributions, and modality interaction vulnerability to domain interference. To address these problems, in this paper, we propose an approach with Sequential Prismatic Ensemble and Cross-domain Transfer Residual Alignment Network for this task, which is abbreviated as SPECTRA for clarity. Specifically, a domain-aware alignment mechanism in terms of Gaussian mixture model is built to perform the dynamic distribution alignment in the feature space. A sequential prismatic fusion network based on orthogonal latent variables is designed to capture concealed cross-modal logical misalignments. Moreover, a dynamic domain knowledge transfer strategy by using residual-query pattern is developed to ensure the effective reconstruction of features in sparse long-tail domains and overcome the phenomenon of cross-domain negative transfer. Experimental results on three real-world datasets demonstrate that SPECTRA outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, showing its effectiveness on fake news detection in complex multi-domain scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Data-driven Koopman predictive control for frequency regulation of power systems using black-box IBRs
Abstract: Model uncertainty of inverter-based resources (IBRs) presents significant challenges for power system control and stability. This work studies secondary frequency regulation in inverter-based power systems using a Data-driven Koopman Predictive Control (DKPC) framework. The method employs Koopman theory to lift the nonlinear system dynamics into a higher-dimensional space where they can be approximated as linear. Based on Willems’ fundamental lemma, a behavioral model is constructed directly from lifted input–output data. A receding-horizon predictive control formulation is then provided that operates entirely using observed data, without requiring a parametric model, while satisfying explicit constraints on the control input and system output. The proposed approach is particularly suited for IBRs with complex or uncertain dynamics. Numerical results demonstrate its effectiveness for frequency control as benchmarked against the Data-enabled Predictive Control (DeePC). The trade-off between tracking performance and control effort is illustrated through tuning of the weighting parameters. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Barriers and innovation pathways for Europe's circular bioeconomy: grassroots stakeholder insights from 43 multi-actor workshops
Abstract: The bioeconomy is a key pillar of the European Green Deal, yet its implementation remains constrained by entrenched linear value chains, fragmented logistics systems, and regulatory uncertainty. This paper examines how practitioners across Europe envision circular bioeconomy transitions, drawing on 43 harmonised multi-actor workshops conducted in 14 countries with 1078 participants from primary production, processing industries, technology provision, public authorities, and civil society. Using a structured participatory canvas and comparative thematic analysis, we analyse how stakeholders redesign existing value chains, which innovation pathways they prioritise, and which barriers they encounter in practice. Across agriculture, forestry, aquatic systems and bio-based industries, stakeholders consistently shift the focus from expanding biomass production toward better use of residues and side-streams. Dominant innovation pathways include residue valorisation, nutrient and water recycling, integrated bioenergy systems, and emerging biomaterials. Four interlinked barrier domains recur across countries and sectors: economic barriers, technological limitations, feedstock logistics and infrastructure constraints, and policy and regulatory challenges. The findings suggest that circular bioeconomy transitions are constrained less by a lack of innovation opportunities than by recurring economic, technological, infrastructural, regulatory, and knowledge-related barriers across countries and sectors. Providing one of the most extensive cross-country, practitioner-led analyses of circular bioeconomy transitions to date, the study offers insight into the conditions shaping circular bioeconomy development across Europe. The findings point to a policy agenda focused on regulatory clarification, coordinated investment in residue aggregation and pre-treatment infrastructure, while highlighting the need for complementary sustainability assessments to evaluate ecological effectiveness and broader socio-ecological implications. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Uncovering heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on stock returns using causal forest double machine learning
Abstract: Global uncertainty has become an important source of financial market instability, yet its effects are inherently heterogeneous and difficult to identify using conventional econometric models. Existing empirical studies primarily rely on linear and average-effect estimators, which may conceal substantial heterogeneity across economic conditions. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable causal machine learning framework that integrates Causal Forest Double Machine Learning (CF-DML) with SHAP explanations to estimate and interpret heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on industry-level stock returns. Using a balanced panel of six major industries listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange from 2011 to 2022, global uncertainty is measured by the World Uncertainty Index (WUI), while macroeconomic and financial variables are incorporated as lagged covariates. The CF-DML framework enables robust causal inference under high-dimensional confounding and nonlinear relationships, whereas SHAP values identify the main drivers of treatment-effect heterogeneity. The results show that the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) of global uncertainty is statistically insignificant, yet substantial heterogeneity exists across observations. Differences across industries are relatively modest, indicating that global uncertainty is transmitted primarily through time-varying macro-financial conditions rather than fixed sectoral characteristics. SHAP analysis identifies exchange-rate volatility, inflation, and market valuation as the dominant factors explaining heterogeneous responses. The study contributes to the literature by combining causal inference, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified framework for financial analysis. The findings suggest that global uncertainty should be viewed as a state-dependent macro-financial phenomenon, providing practical insights for portfolio risk management, macro-financial surveillance, and the design of policies aimed at enhancing financial resilience in emerging economies characterized by persistent inflation and exchange-rate volatility. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.
