Title: Design principles for advanced hydrides: A DFT and molecular dynamics study of tetragonal silicon-based A₂SiH₄ frameworks combining structural stability, ductility, and superior hydrogen storage metrics
Abstract: This work presents a comprehensive first-principles investigation of tetragonal A₂SiH₄ (A = Li, Na, Be, Mg) hydrides as promising solid-state hydrogen storage materials. Structural optimization, phonon dispersion, and ab initio molecular dynamics confirm their thermodynamic, mechanical, and thermal stability. All compounds exhibit near-isotropic elastic behavior, positive Cauchy pressures, and high Pugh ratios, indicating dominant ionic bonding and intrinsic ductility, which are critical for resisting mechanical degradation during hydrogen cycling. Hydrogen storage analysis reveals gravimetric capacities ranging from 4.99 to 8.76 wt% and volumetric densities up to 76.08 kg H₂/m³, exceeding DOE targets. Li₂SiH₄ delivers the highest gravimetric performance, while Be₂SiH₄ achieves maximum volumetric density. Formation enthalpies (–42 to –48 kJ/mol·H₂) indicate stronger hydrogen binding than previously estimated, placing these materials near the upper limit of the optimal thermodynamic window. Corresponding desorption temperatures (315–355 K) remain within practical ranges, although higher thermal input may be required, particularly for Li-based compounds. The observed trends highlight the key role of cation mass, ionic radius, and charge density in tuning structural compactness and hydrogen thermodynamics. Overall, A₂SiH₄ hydrides offer a versatile platform combining high storage capacity and mechanical resilience, while further optimization of thermodynamics and kinetics is necessary for practical deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The mediating effect of nursing students' academic resilience between the clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competency: A cross-sectional study
Abstract: Background: The clinical internship environment is crucial for developing nursing students' patient safety competency. While existing studies have confirmed their direct correlation, the underlying psychological mechanism remains unclear. Academic resilience, a key psychological resource for coping with clinical challenges, may serve as an important mediator, yet its specific role lacks empirical evidence. This study aims to address this gap. Objective: To examine the mediating role of academic resilience between the clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competency among nursing students. Methods: From February to March 2025, we used convenience sampling to recruit nursing students from two tertiary grade-A hospitals in Kaifeng, yielding 298 valid questionnaires. We collected data using a general information questionnaire, the Clinical Nursing Internship Environment Evaluation Scale, the Patient Safety Competency Scale, and the Nursing Student Academic Resilience Scale. We performed mediation analysis using the SPSS PROCESS macro. Results: We obtained survey data from 298 nursing students. The total scores for the clinical nursing internship environment evaluation, patient safety competency, and nursing student academic resilience were 94.0 (91.8, 110.0), 117.0 (114.5, 138.0), and 70.0 (68.0, 78.0), respectively, all in the medium-upper range. Correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlations among the total scores of the clinical nursing internship environment, patient safety competency, and academic resilience (r = 0.933–0.960, P < 0.01). Nursing students' clinical internship environment and academic resilience can directly and positively affect their level of patient safety competence; nursing students' academic resilience partially mediates the relationship between clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competence, with a mediating effect of 0.368 (95% CI: 0.1789–0.5108), accounting for 49.47% of the total effect. Conclusions: Nursing students' academic resilience mediates the relationship between the clinical nursing internship environment and patient safety competence. Nursing managers should focus on improving nursing students' academic resilience and adaptability to the practice environment during clinical practice to optimize the clinical practice environment, improve nursing students' safety competence, and ensure patient safety. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A study of difficulties in solving real-valued function problems: A systematic review
Abstract: The purpose of this study was to analyse and synthesise available scientific evidence regarding the difficulties students face when solving problems involving real-valued functions. Understanding real-valued functions poses a significant challenge in mathematics education due to difficulties interpreting concepts, establishing relationships between variables, coordinating different representations, and selecting appropriate problem-solving strategies. A systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines, involving the selection and analysis of 34 studies published between 1965 and 2026 that addressed mathematical problem-solving, the concept of a function, and learning difficulties associated with them. Despite the extensive body of research on the topic, the reviewed studies reveal persistent gaps in understanding how these difficulties manifest across different educational levels and instructional contexts. The results revealed that difficulties in solving problems involving real-valued functions are multidimensional, linked primarily to cognitive, conceptual, semiotic, procedural, didactic, and epistemological factors. Key findings included persistent difficulties in understanding the concept of a function, interpreting variables and dependency relationships, and converting between graphical, algebraic, tabular, and verbal representations; limitations in metacognition and a tendency toward the mechanical application of procedures were also identified. Furthermore, the data indicated that strategies based on contextualised problems, mathematical modelling, meaningful learning, metacognition, and the integrated use of multiple representations foster a deep understanding of functional thinking. Consequently, the study concludes that addressing these difficulties requires a comprehensive approach that goes beyond procedural instruction to promote conceptual understanding, interpretation, and mathematical argumentation; these findings thus offer valuable guidance for designing instructional strategies and conducting future research aimed at strengthening the learning of real-valued functions. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Jiao Z.; Wang C.; Hong Y.; Hao N.
Title: Efficient on-site treatment of kitchen waste using a microbial consortium: scale-up validation from laboratory to pilot system and mechanistic insights
Abstract: Exogenous microbial inoculation is widely regarded as an effective strategy for enhancing the treatment efficiency of kitchen waste (KW). This study systematically evaluated the performance of a laboratory-prepared composite microbial inoculant (LCI) in KW treatment through a stepwise scale-up strategy. In an 18 L laboratory-scale reactor, LCI achieved efficient liquefaction of KW, with removal efficiencies of 62.7% for COD, 50.7% for TP, 61.5% for TN, and 64.7% for NH4+-N, alongside substantial reduction in weight and volume by 88.3% and 86.5%, respectively. Upon scaling up to a 300 L pilot-scale system with the addition of fruitwood chips (FW) as a reinforcing agent, the LCI-FW configuration maintained stable and high treatment performance. No scale-up attenuation was observed compared with the laboratory-scale results, and the overall performance was superior to that of the commercial microbial inoculant (CI). High-throughput sequencing analysis revealed that LCI-FW significantly enriched dominant microbial taxa represented by Lactobacillus, forming a community structure more conducive to KW degradation. Functional prediction further indicated that, beyond enzymes associated with carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus metabolism, those linked to substrate uptake and environmental adaptation also showed higher predicted abundances, providing mechanistic insights into the enhanced treatment efficiency. Economic assessment demonstrated that LCI-FW achieved a 56.5% cost reduction compared with commercial products, indicating substantial economic advantages. Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of the LCI-FW synergistic reinforcement system for practical KW treatment. It also provides experimental evidence supporting the engineering application of microorganism–immobilized carrier strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Biogas-fueled oxy-fuel power system integrated with desalination and CO2 liquefaction: 4E analysis and multi-objective optimization
Abstract: This study proposes an integrated multi-generation system in which a multi-effect distillation (MED) unit is thermally coupled with a biogas-fueled oxy-fuel power plant, a transcritical CO2 cycle, and a CO2 capture and liquefaction subsystem. The system is comprehensively evaluated using thermodynamic (energy and exergy), economic (exergo-economic and net present value), and environmental (life cycle assessment-based exergo-environmental) analyses. An artificial neural network (ANNs) integrated with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) are subsequently employed for multi-objective optimization under four scenarios: exergy–cost, exergy–environment, cost–environment, and exergy–cost–environment. The three-objective optimization yields an exergy efficiency of 50.63%, a unit product cost of 29.73 $/GJ, and a specific exergo-environmental impact of 4309 mPts/GJ. At the optimized operating conditions, the system simultaneously produces 6939 m3/h of freshwater, 21,005 kW of net electricity, and 12,327 m3/h of liquefied CO2. In addition, optimum state indicates a net present value of 265.2 M$ with a payback period of 3.4 years. The results demonstrate that integrating biogas-based energy conversion with MED desalination and CO2 capture enhances resource utilization while reducing the environmental burden of energy and freshwater production. The proposed system therefore offers a promising pathway toward low-carbon and resource-efficient multi-generation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Optimizing Federated Incremental Learning: Efficient Malicious Data Removal for Big Data Analytics
Abstract: Federated incremental learning facilitates decentralized and continuous model updates across multiple clients, presenting a promising framework for big data analytics in distributed environments. However, the presence of poisoned or malicious data introduces significant challenges, including compromised model performance and system reliability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes an efficient and resource-aware machine unlearning method tailored for federated incremental learning. The approach utilizes a membership inference attack mechanism to accurately identify poisoned data based on prediction confidence levels. Once detected, a targeted forgetting mechanism is applied, leveraging fine-tuning techniques to erase the influence of the poisoned data while preserving the model’s incremental learning capabilities. By aligning the distributions of poisoned data with third-party datasets, the method achieves reliable unlearning without introducing excessive computational overhead. Extensive experiments conducted on diverse datasets validate the method’s effectiveness, demonstrating a significant reduction in forgetting time (up to 21.05× speedup compared with baseline approaches) while maintaining robust model performance in incremental learning tasks. This work offers a scalable and efficient solution to the data forgetting problem, advancing the reliability and practicality of federated incremental learning in distributed and resource-constrained scenarios. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Multi-technology synergic mechanism and integration pathways for regional organic waste-to-energy manufacturing utilization: A case study of China
Abstract: China generates more than 300 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually, with organic fractions representing over 50 percent of this volume. The conversion of organic waste to energy (OWtE) has emerged as a central pillar of China's circular economy strategy and its dual-carbon targets of peak emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. This paper examines the multi-technology synergic mechanisms underpinning regional OWtE systems in China, analyzing the technical, economic, environmental, and policy dimensions of four primary conversion pathways: anaerobic digestion (AD), incineration with energy recovery, pyrolysis, and gasification. Drawing on provincial data, life cycle assessment outcomes, and techno-economic evaluations, the study proposes an integrated framework for regional OWtE manufacturing utilization. The findings demonstrate that hybrid systems combining AD with thermal treatment can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 58 to 68 percent relative to landfilling while achieving levelized energy costs of 42 to 82 USD per MWh. Regional differentiation in technology deployment is driven by waste composition, economic development level, and feedstock availability. Policy coherence under the 14th Five-Year Plan and subsequent instruments has accelerated capacity development, though technology-region mismatches and digestate management gaps remain persistent barriers. This study provides an evidence-based roadmap for optimizing OWtE integration pathways across China's diverse regional contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Engineering hydrophobic membranes with tunable pore accessibility via selective swelling of SDS block copolymers for ethanol concentration
Abstract: The separation of ethanol from dilute aqueous solutions, such as fermentation broths, is critically important for biofuel production. Membrane distillation (MD) with porous membranes usually suffers from insufficient selectivity, while pervaporation (PV) with dense films is inadequate in permeability. To overcome this trade-off, we developed a novel hydrophobic membrane via the selective swelling of a polystyrene-b-polydimethylsiloxane-b-polystyrene triblock copolymer (SDS). By precisely controlling the swelling agent and duration, we engineered the optimal membrane with a tailored pore structure featuring interconnected nanopores and partially blind pores, along with a PDMS-enriched pore surface. This unique architecture enables a multipath permeation mechanism combing solution-diffusion and the transport pathway for molecules under vapor–liquid equilibrium within pore channels. The optimized membrane demonstrated an exceptional combination of high permeation flux and separation factor for a 5 wt% ethanol/water mixture at 50 °C, yielding a remarkable pervaporation separation index (PSI) of 38.2 kg·m−2·h−1. This performance surpasses many PDMS-based PV and conventional MD membranes. This work presents a simple and efficient strategy for fabricating high-performance membranes that simultaneously achieve high flux and selectivity, offering significant potential for advancing energy-efficient bioethanol recovery processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Revisiting topological bias in imbalanced graph learning: A Dual-Balanced Graph Neural Network approach
Abstract: Class imbalance in node classification can impair the discriminative capability of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) partly by limiting class-wise topological supervision reachability. While existing methods primarily focus on balancing sample quantities, we theoretically characterize, under a mean-field neighborhood-growth model and an exponential attenuation assumption for long-range message passing, how the effective supervision intensity of minority-class nodes can exhibit a power-law decay as the imbalance ratio increases. This conditional scaling result provides a theoretical explanation for how limited supervision reachability can constrain minority-class learning. Title: Stochastic optimization algorithms for biomedical image classification
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) remains the primary optimization method for training deep neural networks; however, its performance can deteriorate in the presence of noisy gradients or highly variable curvature. While momentum based and adaptive learning rate methods partially mitigate these challenges, they often rely on accumulated second moment estimates or exhibit sensitivity to hyperparameter choices, particularly when gradient statistics change over time. In this paper, we propose three stochastic optimization algorithms, SGD(New), SGD(We), and SGD(Was), which integrate three complementary mechanisms: Nesterov-type look ahead gradient evaluation, a normalized momentum update constructed from successive gradient differences, and an adaptive stepsize that scales inversely with the variability of gradient changes. By defining momentum in terms of directional consistency rather than gradient magnitude, and by adjusting the learning rate using curvature information implicitly inferred from gradient differences, the proposed methods yield stable and responsive updates under stochastic gradient feedback. Together, these components form a lightweight and principled optimization framework applicable to both standard i.i.d. training and more challenging learning scenarios. We evaluate the proposed algorithms against widely used baselines, including SGD with momentum, Adam, RAdam, and Adagrad, on four MedMNIST biomedical image classification datasets using an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 model. The empirical results demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve improved optimization stability and competitive performance across binary, multi-label, and multi-class medical image classification tasks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Dependence of high-temperature plastic deformation of fine-grained Y2O3 on the electric power density
Source title: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
Abstract: High-temperature plastic deformation behavior of two-step sintered, fine-grained Y2O3 polycrystals was examined under various direct current (DC) electric fields/currents. High-temperature flexural tests in the fine-grained Y2O3 body with an average grain size of 0.47 µm were conducted under DC electric fields of 0–1000 V·cm−1 and current density of 0–15 mA·mm−2 at 1000℃–1400℃ and strain rates of 2.4 × 10−5–1.0 × 10−4 s−1. Deformation of Y2O3 was athermally promoted by DC electric fields, with a maximum stress reduction of 36%, even when subtracting the thermal effect caused by Joule heating. In particular, the activation energy of the high-temperature plastic flow gradually decreased with increasing steady-state power density, which was amplified under a flash event and reached up to 225 mW·mm−3. Title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for energy-efficient cooperative UAV deployment in 5G networks
Abstract: The increasing demand for ubiquitous mobile connectivity and the rapid deployment of fifth generation (5G) networks have intensified the need for flexible communication infrastructures that can adapt to highly dynamic user distributions. In this context, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating as aerial base stations (BSs) have emerged as a promising solution for extending network coverage and capacity in scenarios where terrestrial infrastructure is unavailable, congested, or insufficient. However, determining efficient UAV deployment strategies remains a challenging optimization problem due to user mobility, network dynamics, and energy constraints. This paper presents a continuous-state multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for the cooperative deployment of UAV-based aerial BSs. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on grid-based mobility abstractions, the proposed framework incorporates force-based control dynamics to model UAV motion. Two representative MARL algorithms, namely multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) and monotonic value function factorization (QMIX), are evaluated under a centralized training and decentralized execution paradigm. Three independent and unweighted reward formulations are introduced, targeting network capacity maximization, relative capacity improvement, and energy-efficient data delivery, to isolate the impact of the reward structure and ensure that observed performance trade-offs are strictly attributable to the reward design. Bayesian hyperparameter optimization is applied independently to each configuration, while a functional ANOVA analysis demonstrates that hyperparameter sensitivity is inherently dependent on the algorithm and the reward. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed cooperative learning framework enables UAVs to learn coordinated deployment strategies that consistently outperform non-adaptive baseline approaches under diverse user mobility conditions, increased user density, intermittent position-report losses, and variations in action-force magnitude. Measured inference latency remains below one-fifth of the control interval on all evaluated hardware platforms, indicating that decentralized execution is feasible without an onboard accelerator. Among the evaluated configurations, reward shaping plays a critical role in balancing throughput and energy consumption, and MAPPO exhibits the most robust overall performance. These findings highlight the potential of adaptive MARL for efficient and energy-aware UAV-assisted 5G network deployment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Does retirement reduce household carbon emissions in China? Evidence from fuzzy regression discontinuity design
Abstract: This study examines the causal effect of household-head retirement on household carbon emissions (HCEs) in China. Combining multi-wave data from the China Family Panel Studies with household carbon accounting, we construct household-level total carbon emissions (TCEs), distinguishing between direct carbon emissions (DCEs) from household energy use and indirect carbon emissions (ICEs) embodied in the goods and services purchased by households. We estimate the local causal effect of retirement using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on China's statutory retirement age of 60 for urban male household heads. The results show that retirement significantly reduces TCEs by approximately 7.4–9.0 tCO₂ per household. This reduction is driven primarily by lower ICEs, while the estimated effect on DCEs is statistically insignificant. Point estimates are larger for households headed by individuals without tertiary education and for low-asset households, but formal bootstrap tests do not reject equality across education or asset groups. The mechanism results suggest that the decline in ICEs is mainly associated with a contraction in overall household consumption, particularly reductions in non-subsistence and work-related expenditure, with limited evidence of a broad shift in consumption composition. Disaggregated results further show that the emission reductions are concentrated in clothing, household facilities and services, and transportation and communication. These findings provide local causal evidence that retirement reshapes HCEs mainly through reductions in consumption-based indirect emissions rather than through changes in direct household energy use, highlighting the importance of life-course transitions for understanding demand-side emission dynamics in aging societies. © 2026

Title: An empirical study on the capability of LLMs in decomposing bug reports
Abstract: Bug reports are essential to the software development life cycle. They help developers track and resolve issues, but are often difficult to process due to their complexity, which can delay resolution and affect software quality. This study investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can assist developers in automatically decomposing complex bug reports into smaller, self-contained units, making them easier to understand and address. We first conducted an empirical study using 127 resolved privacy-related bug reports collected from Apache Jira. We evaluated ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V1 using zero-shot and few-shot prompting. Under zero-shot prompting, the models correctly decomposed only 10 and 11 reports, respectively. Few-shot prompting increased their true decomposition rates by 140% (10 vs. 24) and 163.64% (11 vs. 29), respectively, although the overall accuracy remained limited. To examine whether the findings generalize beyond privacy-related reports and to expand the dataset size, we further analyzed 127 security-related bug reports using GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. We compared zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and persona prompting. Few-shot prompting achieved the best performance for both models, correctly decomposing 89 reports with GPT-5.5 and 51 reports with DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Across the experiments, we identify a concrete failure taxonomy for LLM-based bug report decomposition, including over-decomposition, over-analysis, incorrect interpretation of solutions, lacking key information, and empty output. Over-decomposition is the most common failure mode, suggesting that LLMs often struggle to distinguish independent bug units from supporting information such as logs, code snippets, background context, and proposed fixes. Overall, LLMs show potential for automated bug report decomposition, but their reliability, prompt sensitivity, and adherence to decomposition instructions still require improvement. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Trade-offs between water storage and transport mediated by three percolating pores in subtropical red soils: X-ray CT evidence from an 11-year tillage experiment
Abstract: Red soils in subtropical regions are highly susceptible to structural degradation, resulting in poor water retention and restricted water transport. Although tillage strongly influences soil hydraulic properties, the pore-scale mechanisms governing these responses after long-term management remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how 11 years of no-tillage (NT), rotary tillage (RT), and deep ploughing (DP) reshaped pore architecture and regulated soil hydraulic behavior across a 0–40 cm red soil profile by integrating soil physical measurements, van Genuchten modeling, X-ray computed tomography (CT), and multivariate analyses. Relative to conventional rotary tillage (RT), DP reduced bulk density by 16.8% and increased saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ks) by 138.9–1248.2% and air permeability (Ka) by 25.9–167.0% within the 0–30 cm cultivated layer through enhanced macroporosity and pore connectivity. In contrast, NT maintained higher Ks and Ka in the 20–40 cm subsoil, reflecting the preservation of continuous biopore networks under long-term minimal disturbance. RT preferentially promoted mesopore (200–500 μm) development, resulting in the highest saturated water content, field moisture capacity, and plant-available water. Random forest analysis identified global pore connectivity (Γ), pore anisotropy (An) and pore size distribution, rather than total porosity, as the dominant predictors of hydraulic behavior. Correlation, principal component, and redundancy analyses consistently showed that macropores (>500 μm) primarily controlled water transmission, whereas meso- and micropores (60–200 and 200–500 μm) governed water retention. Structural equation modeling demonstrated that tillage regulated hydraulic function indirectly through pore architecture, with pore conductivity promoting hydraulic conductivity (standardized path coefficient: 0.38) and pore storage enhancing hydraulic storage (0.45), while revealing a strong antagonistic trade-off (-0.93) between conductivity and water storage. These findings establish pore architecture as the mechanistic link between long-term tillage and soil hydraulic function, providing a scientific basis for optimizing tillage strategies to improve water use efficiency and drought resilience in red soil agroecosystems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Research on icing thickness of transmission lines based on combinatorial correlation analysis and improved sparrow search algorithm to optimize support vector machine
Abstract: Extreme cold spells and freezing-rain events have become more frequent in recent years, increasing transmission-line ice accretion and compromising the stability of the power grid. To enhance the precision of ice accumulation level assessment and early warning capabilities, this paper constructs a feature analysis model integrating grey relational analysis and Spearman correlation using multidimensional micro-meteorological data from Northeast China. Specifically, the SCA coefficient and grey relational coefficient are integrated into a composite correlation index to screen key variables, and principal component analysis (PCA) is employed to generate orthogonal features for addressing multicollinearity issues. For icing-level recognition, a support vector machine (SVM) is adopted, and its hyperparameters are tuned by an improved sparrow search algorithm (SSA) that incorporates chaotic initialization, dynamic inertia weighting, and a Cauchy–Gaussian mutation operator to enhance global search performance. On the test set, the proposed model achieves 97.84 % accuracy, with recalls of 97.49 % and 99.11 % for light and moderate-to-heavy icing, respectively. Comparative experiments show that the proposed method consistently outperforms several benchmark models, providing a methodological basis for transmission-line icing early-warning systems and differentiated operation-and-maintenance strategies under extreme meteorological conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The emission-inequality nexus across stages of development
Abstract: Does a more unequal society emit more CO2? The nexus between carbon emissions and income inequality has been at the core of a vast literature yielding conflicting results. Here, we provide robust evidence of a non-linear relationship that depends on the structural composition of the economy. Specifically, we document a positive association between income inequality—measured using five different indicators, for both pre-tax and post-tax income—and per capita carbon emissions in highly tertiarized countries. By contrast, this relationship turns negative in non-service-intensive economies. We provide evidence for plausible mechanisms mediating this non-linear association. In particular, the investment carbon footprint of the top 1% and the size of the manufacturing sector emerge as key dimensions underlying the observed patterns. Our results point to the structural composition of the economy as a crucial factor shaping the emission-inequality nexus. As such, economic structure helps identify phases of development in which reducing inequality comes with climate-related benefits. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Rho J.; Guo R.; Li H.; Li C.
Title: Disengaged conversational behaviors and learning in student-AI dialogues for mathematical problem solving
Abstract: As the conversational AI agents become integrated into digital learning environments, students' interaction with these systems can show conversational disengagement, including mocking, misleading, or otherwise diverting the agents. Although task-based disengagement such as gaming the system and off-task actions are well documented, the nature of the consequences of this conversational disengagement in student-AI dialogue remains largely unexplored. This study examined how different types of conversational disengagement relate to middle-school students’ mathematical learning with an AI-powered teachable agent embedded in a large-scale platform. We coded 5522 utterances from 246 students into six conversational disengagement categories (False Answering, Mocking, Ghosting, Mirroring, Withholding, and Random/Noisy) versus engagement. Regression analyses showed that some disengagements (False Answering and Mocking) were positively associated with post-test scores after controlling for pre-test performance, although these associations did not replicate in a sensitivity analysis restricted to human-annotated utterances. To capture process-level dynamics, we modeled how conversational disengagement ends using a competing-risks approach and separately clustered students based on their turn-by-turn transition probabilities. Most conversational disengagement tended to end within the first few turns, whereas Withholding showed a strong tendency to continue. Students in the highest-performing cluster combined a moderate level of conversational disengagement with strong recovery pathways, whereas the lowest-performing cluster exhibited persistent self-loops without recovery. Together, these findings suggest that some apparent disengagement in conversation with AI may occur within interaction trajectories that subsequently return to productive engagement. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Wen Y.; Low Y.M.
Title: A hybrid deterministic-stochastic method for extreme sea level prediction incorporating tide-surge interaction
Abstract: Extreme sea levels driven by storm surges and high tides can have devastating impacts on coastal communities. Reliable prediction of these extremes is challenging due to site-specific nonlinear interactions between tide and surge, in addition to other complexities. Existing methods have drawbacks; for example block maxima suffers from data wastage, peaks-over-threshold introduces practitioner subjectivity, while joint probability methods rely on assumptions that are not always valid. To address these gaps, this paper develops a broadly applicable method for predicting extreme sea levels based on the crossing rate approach, by treating tide as deterministic and modeling surge as a tide-dependent stochastic process. The formulation makes minimal assumptions and rigorously models the salient problem characteristics including tide-surge interaction, non-Gaussian behavior, serial correlation and seasonality. Moreover, the method fully exploits the information embedded in the entire time series record, not only the peaks or maxima. The proposed method is demonstrated at three tide-gauge sites: Tanjong Pagar, San Franciso and Quarry Bay. The predicted upcrossing rates are in excellent agreement with observations. Cross-validation analysis by data splitting reveals that the proposed method is accurate for out-of-sample forecasting, with small predictive uncertainty and good statistical extrapolation. Overall, the proposed method is shown to be a powerful practical tool for reliable prediction of extreme sea levels. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Emergent collaborative scheduling in satellite swarms: A distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning approach with adaptive experience evolution
Abstract: Autonomous collaboration among multiple Earth observation satellites is essential for improving the performance of satellite swarms. However, this task is challenging because of limited onboard computing resources and unstable inter-satellite links, particularly when global coordination is required under communication constraints. Traditional centralized optimization methods often adapt poorly to dynamic observation requests, whereas existing multi-agent approaches may incur communication overhead that hinders practical deployment. To address this issue, we propose a distributed scheduling framework that enables emergent global coordination through local agent interactions and formulates the problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP). Specifically, we develop L-QTRAN, a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm that enables satellites to coordinate based on local observations with limited communication. To alleviate the non-stationarity inherent in dynamic swarm environments, we introduce an Adaptive Experience Evolution (AEE) mechanism. This mechanism follows the survival-of-the-fittest principle by selectively retaining elite transition experiences, thereby accelerating the development of cooperative strategies. Furthermore, a Random Segment Sampling (RSS) technique is introduced to improve training stability and convergence in high-dimensional solution spaces. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the baseline methods under weak-communication conditions and achieves sub-second response times, highlighting its potential for autonomous satellite swarms operating in dynamic environments. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The public funding of the New Space Economy. Confronting public procurement and public-private partnership
Abstract: This paper confronts public funding mechanisms in the New Space Economy (NSE). NSE refers to the rise of private actors’ activities in space; however, public funding remains crucial. Governments retain public control over space programmes on the one side, while private firms reduce risks on the other. Our results inform public decision-makers with a critical discussion on the advantages and disadvantages of the two models in the context of the NSE. The paper concludes that the supposed privatization of space is far from happening and that private actors would not have entered the space economy without public procurement. © 2026 IAA. Title: Disruption-induced spatial inequality in resilience loss of urban rail transit: A multi-agent simulation analysis
Abstract: With the rapid expansion of urban rail transit networks in large cities, operational disruptions occur more frequently, causing varying degrees of accessibility loss and shaping station-level resilience. From the network and spatial perspective, these differences manifest as inequalities in the distribution of transport capacity. To investigate these relationships, this study proposes a scenario-based dynamic simulation analysis framework and applies it to the Beijing urban rail transit system as a case study. High-resolution passenger travel processes are first generated using multi-agent simulation. Then, within a dynamic accessibility and resilience evaluation framework, a multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model is applied to examine accessibility, resilience, and equity under zero-load, normal operation, and disruption scenarios. The results show that variations in accessibility and resilience are highly sensitive to the location and characteristics of disruptions. Under severe disruptions, suburban corridors and key transfer segments form concentrated clusters of low resilience. MGWR analysis further reveals distinct spatial heterogeneity in the effects of structural attributes, passenger demand pressure, and spatial environmental factors, with different drivers operating at different spatial scales. Title: Exploring the influence of experiential learning on IA practice: Understanding IA professionals' views about the objectives and utility of strategic and regional assessments in subsequent project IAs
Abstract: Strategic and regional assessments (SAs/RAs) can inform and influence subsequent impact assessments (IAs) in various ways. While previous research has investigated perspectives about the goals and utility of SAs/RAs in project IAs, there has been no investigation of the basis for, and origins of, these views. Drawing on experiential learning theory, this study undertook statistical analyses of data from recent surveys of IA regulators and practitioners in Canada to investigate whether different forms of IA experience and knowledge help explain these perspectives. Title: Development, Optimization, and Evaluation of Chitosan Nanoparticles for Co-Delivery of Rivastigmine and Harmaline via Intranasal Route for Brain Targeting

Title: Differentiated instruction competency development among preservice primary teachers: A descriptive survey
Abstract: Differentiated instruction is important in primary teacher education because future teachers need to respond to students' diverse readiness levels, learning needs, interests, and learning pace. This study described differentiated instruction competency development among preservice primary teachers at a Vietnamese university. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted with 28 lecturers and 250 preservice primary teachers from the Primary Education program at Hung Vuong University. Data were collected using structured online questionnaires. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize lecturer ratings, student self-ratings, perceived goals, perceived pathways, and perceived related factors of differentiated instruction competency development. Lecturer ratings showed that differentiated instruction competency was highest among K19 students, followed by K20 and K21. Students' self-ratings showed a similar pattern, although students generally rated their own competency more positively than lecturers did. Both lecturers and students viewed differentiated instruction competency development as relevant to professional preparation, effective teaching in primary schools, and connecting theory with practice. Courses in the teacher education curriculum were identified by both groups as the main pathway for developing this competency. Lecturers emphasized lecturer competency, class size, and curriculum content as important related factors, whereas students gave the highest rating to their own awareness of the role of differentiated instruction competency. The findings suggest that differentiated instruction competency may be strengthened through an integrated approach that combines coursework, practice-based learning, self-study, student research, and lecturer guidance. Title: Steering the oxygen reduction pathway from 4e⁻ to 2e⁻ in surface-dominant CoNi/NC alloys for efficient H2O2 electrosynthesis
Abstract: Balancing the activity–selectivity trade-off in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e⁻ ORR) is essential for efficient electrochemical hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. Herein, constant-potential density functional theory calculations combined with experiments demonstrate that CoNi alloying regulates ORR branching through composition-dependent electronic interactions. Calculations on Co(111), CoNi(111), CoNi3(111), and Ni(111) show that Co(111) favors *OOH dissociation and thus the four-electron (4e⁻) pathway, whereas Ni(111) preferentially promotes H2O2 formation via the 2e⁻ pathway. In CoNi alloys, charge transfer from Co to Ni tunes the D-band center of Ni sites, which kinetically lowers the barrier for *OOH conversion to H2O2 while maintaining a comparatively high barrier for O–O bond cleavage. These effects kinetically favor the 2e⁻ branch over the competing 4e⁻ pathway. Guided by these insights, surface-dominant CoNi alloy nanoparticles with varying Ni contents were synthesized on N-doped carbon using a molten-salt-mediated method. Comprehensive characterizations support a surface-dominant CoNi alloy structure and electronic interactions between Co and Ni. Electrochemical measurements reveal a volcano-shaped dependence of H2O2 selectivity on alloy composition, with an optimized CoNi/NC catalyst achieving ~97% selectivity in 0.1 M HClO4. The catalyst also shows efficient and stable H2O2 electrosynthesis in flow cells, sustaining ~300 mA cm⁻2 for 100 h with 83–95% Faradaic efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Going beyond a stress reliever: A human-supported mindfulness intervention enhances daily psychological and behavioral functioning among hospitality employees
Abstract: Although mindfulness interventions have been found to play a critical role in improving employee well-being and job performance, empirical evidence from the hospitality industry remains scarce. Grounded in workplace mindfulness theory, this study explores how daily mindfulness interventions coupled with human coaching guidance influence psychological states (self-acceptance and serenity) and work behaviors (job crafting and helping behavior) among hospitality employees. Specifically, with the support of a human coach, employees participated in 10 consecutive days of systematic mindfulness intervention sessions, and the experience sampling method (ESM) was employed to assess the effects on psychological and behavioral outcomes. The multilevel modeling revealed that the intervention significantly enhanced participants’ psychological and behavioral functioning, with effects varying as a function of baseline levels. Based on these findings, hospitality managers are encouraged to adopt evidence-based mindfulness intervention programs to foster employees’ psychological well-being and proactive work behaviors. Authors: Cui L.; Zhang H.; Wu W.; Chen J.
Title: Attributing high-altitude multi-physics effects on distribution network resilience: A Shapley-based SOCP relaxation study
Abstract: High-altitude distribution networks face a tension that lower-altitude systems do not. Stronger solar irradiance raises photovoltaic output, but the same cold and snowy environment cuts mobile storage capacity, blocks the roads those units must travel, and thins the air that diesel generators rely on. When these effects pull in opposite directions, a single load-shedding figure says little about which one actually governs the result. We treat four altitude effects—PV gain, battery temperature loss, road mobility, and thermoelectric heating—as cooperating factors inside a post-disaster restoration model on the IEEE 33-bus feeder, and apply Shapley decomposition to assign each factor its share of the change in weighted load-shedding cost. The mixed-integer form of the problem did not converge reliably, so the attribution reported here rests on the continuous SOCP relaxation. PV altitude gain turns out to dominate the cost reduction: its base-case Shapley value is -2264 CNY, and the mean across ten quality-controlled fault sets is -2363 CNY with a coefficient of variation of only 0.59%. Cold-induced storage degradation is the largest adverse term (+159 CNY in the base case, positive in all ten sets, mean +139 CNY). Road and heating effects stay small and even flip sign from one fault scenario to the next. The planning implication is narrow but firm. Expanding PV capacity is the first-order resilience investment at altitude, yet without battery thermal management the cold penalty quietly erodes part of that gain. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Spatiotemporal patterns and nonlinear drivers of MSW carbon emissions from the perspective of consumption and industrial structure upgrading: An explainable machine learning approach
Abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) carbon emissions pose a major challenge to urban sustainable development, yet nonlinear drivers across different urban development contexts remain insufficiently understood. Based on consumption upgrading and industrial structure upgrading, this study classifies 284 prefecture-level and above cities in China into four development types, estimates MSW carbon emissions from treatment processes during 2010–2023, and constructs an XGBoost–SHAP model to identify key drivers, nonlinear thresholds, and interaction contributions. The results show that MSW carbon emissions followed an overall trajectory of “growth–decline–slight rebound,” with comprehensive upgrading cities, despite being the smallest group, maintaining the highest long-term emission levels. Urban construction scale and population size are identified as core drivers, whereas waste treatment structure upgrading shows a negative contribution. Comprehensive upgrading cities are characterized by joint drivers related to scale agglomeration, economic activity, and governance capacity; household consumption is a more prominent driver in consumption-led upgrading cities; environmental sanitation infrastructure emerges as a more prominent driver in industry-led upgrading cities; and scale-related factors remain the primary drivers in foundational cities. From the combined perspective of demand-side consumption changes and supply-side industrial structure adjustment, this study reveals heterogeneous drivers of MSW carbon emissions and provides insights for city-type-specific low-carbon MSW governance strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Isogeometric analysis for explicit wave propagation in poroelastic media
Source title: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
Abstract: For higher-order discretizations of explicit dynamics problems, Isogeometric Analysis (IGA) has several favorable properties as compared to classical Finite Element Analysis (FEA). While FEA produces spurious modes at orders beyond linear, this is not the case for IGA. Consequently, fewer degrees of freedom are required for comparable accuracy, larger timesteps can be taken, and the method is more robust for nonlinear problems. After eliminating outlier modes, the timestep even becomes virtually independent of the order. In this paper, we investigate how these advantages apply to the poroelastic continuum model.We consider both a primal formulation, wherein our variables are the displacement of the matrix material, the fluid displacement, and the pressure, as well as a reduced form wherein the pressure is eliminated. For our discretizations, we employ divergence-conforming spline spaces. Employing such spaces for the fluid displacement ensures inf-sup stability for the primal form, and exactly reproduces the kernel of the undamped problem in both forms. Furthermore, we prove and demonstrate that the two formulations coincide when both displacements are discretized with divergence-conforming spline spaces.Through spectral analysis, we find that the aforementioned benefits of IGA do carry over directly to the context of poroelasticity. In 1D, we split the discrete spectrum into fast and slow waves. When normalized against an analytical solution, each of these sub-spectra closely resembles results known in elasticity. Consequently, when poroelasticity is discretized with outlier-free IGA, the timestep is essentially independent of the order. We show this timestep scaling in 2D as well. Title: A domain-differentiated stress perspective on turnover intention
Abstract: This study examines the associations of job stress and work–family conflict with turnover intention among lecturers employed in private higher education institutions in Yunnan Province, China. Drawing on conservation of resources theory and a dual-stressor perspective, job stress and work–family conflict are conceptualized as distinct but potentially interrelated sources of resource depletion that may contribute to withdrawal cognition. Lecturers in Chinese private higher education institutions may face substantial teaching responsibilities, administrative demands, performance expectations, limited institutional resources, and employment uncertainty, making this an important context for examining turnover intention. Using a quantitative survey design, data were collected through the Wenjuanxing online platform. After data screening, 374 valid responses were retained. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to assess the measurement model, test the hypothesized relationships, and evaluate the model’s predictive relevance. The results showed that both job stress and work–family conflict were significantly and positively associated with turnover intention. Work–family conflict showed the stronger association, suggesting that difficulties reconciling professional and family responsibilities may play a particularly important role in lecturers’ intentions to leave. However, the interaction between job stress and work–family conflict was not statistically significant. Thus, the findings did not provide evidence that the association between work–family conflict and turnover intention varied across different levels of job stress. The model explained 62.1% of the variance in turnover intention, indicating substantial explanatory power. This study contributes to the literature by comparing the direct associations of work-domain and work–family-interface stressors with turnover intention in private higher education. The findings also suggest that workload management, family-supportive policies, and institutional support should be considered as complementary intervention targets. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Dynamic link prediction with community structure evolution modeling
Abstract: In dynamic graphs, future link formation is influenced by both structural evolution and temporal dependency. Many existing methods primarily focus on node-level dynamics or local interaction patterns, while insufficiently exploiting mesoscopic community structure and its evolution. To improve dynamic link prediction by learning mesoscopic evolution patterns of network community structure, a community-evolution-aware framework, termed CoEvoNet, is developed. Specifically, community assignments are explicitly learned from temporally encoded node states to extract mesoscopic organizational information beyond node-level dynamics. Title: From control to authorship: Exploring how user agency relates to generative presence and therapeutic self-attribution in AI-driven VR mindfulness
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: AI-driven interactivity is expanding the design space of virtual reality mindfulness-based interventions (VR-MBIs), but the experiential value of semantic co-creation remains unclear. We propose an agency-centered framework in which Generative Presence (GP) and Therapeutic Self-Attribution (TSA) represent potentially coupled experience- and belief-level pathways, with Emotional Resonance (ER) reflecting affective fit and responsiveness. In a mixed-methods pilot randomized controlled trial (N = 48), participants completed a 10-minute breath-focused session in either the generative condition (GEN) or a matched static active-control condition (STA). Semantic co-creation yielded higher covariate-adjusted post-session state mindfulness than pre-authored scene selection, whereas anxiety decreased in both conditions without a detectable between-condition difference. Exploratory differences were largest for the study-specific indicators of expressive control and authorship, while ER, therapeutic attribution, and spatial presence also favored GEN; broader established agency and attribution measures showed limited differentiation. Within GEN, authorship correlated with ER, and ER with post-session mindfulness—a pattern anticipated by the framework, although mediation and temporal ordering were not tested. Interviews (n = 12) identified two regulation modes: expressive control through attentional anchoring and meaning construction, and low-effort exposure through restorative absorption. The interviews further suggested that added agency could support engagement but also introduce evaluative pressure, whereas static exposure could reduce effort but was sometimes accompanied by boredom and rumination. These preliminary findings position semantic authorship as a conditional design resource that may support mindfulness by making the attentional object more personally meaningful and intention-linked, while its implications for immediate state anxiety regulation may vary with user–task fit. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Dynamic equivalent of IBR-dominated distribution networks through multi-port synthesis
Abstract: Distribution networks (DNs) are shifting from passive to active due to an ever-increasing share of inverter-based resources (IBRs), whose simulation is computationally demanding. To address this issue, we propose a distribution network (DN) reduction method that boosts simulation efficiency in two steps. First, the DN is synthesized as a multi-port circuit, with one port at the substation downstream of the transmission grid, and one for each grid-following IBR connected to the DN. Second, IBRs with a similar voltage dependency are clustered, and only a representative IBR per cluster is retained in the reduced DN. The method is compatible with DNs of any size (be them balanced or unbalanced, three-phase, single-phase, with or without neutral) and clusters IBRs through a numerical approach that hinges only on power flow and small-signal analysis. Thus, it is agnostic to the IBR model used and can suitably group IBRs with different power set-points and ratings. Title: Psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation influences safety behaviour: A moderated serial mediation of psychological safety climate, employee resilience, and ethical leadership
Abstract: Drawing on conservation of resources theory, this study examines the psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation is associated with employees’ safety behaviour in Ghana’s mining sector. Ethical leadership was found to moderate these relationships, strengthening the positive associations between digital transformation on psychological resources and behavioural outcomes. The study contributes to literature by extending conservation of resources theory to explain how technological, contextual, and personal resources interact in relation to safety behavior in high-risk work environments. Title: Unveiling the role of nanocrystallization in acousto-optic properties of Ge-Sb-S chalcogenide glasses

Abstract: Acousto-optic (AO) devices are essential in modern photonic systems and support applications such as optical communication and laser processing. Chalcogenide glasses (ChGs) have attracted considerable attention as promising AO materials, yet their AO performance optimization remains hindered by intrinsic trade-offs among key parameters. Abstract: Temporal graphs provide a useful model for many real-world networks. Unfortunately the majority of algorithmic problems we might consider on such graphs are intractable. Title: Differentially private encrypted-domain image retrieval with key-rotation robust token learning
Abstract: Cloud-based image retrieval should protect visual confidentiality without sacrificing search accuracy over outsourced image collections. Existing encrypted-domain (ED) methods limit direct content exposure, but encrypted descriptors and queries may still reveal statistical information. A Vision Transformer learns retrieval embeddings from privatized tokens, while key-rotation training improves robustness to unseen encryption keys and cipher-domain shifts. Repeated-query leakage is reduced through descriptor reuse, privacy-budget tracking, and fixed-size responses. Experiments on Corel10K-a, Corel10K-b, ImageNet100, and MIRFLICKR-25K demonstrate improved performance over reproduced ED baselines, reduced representation-level leakage, strong visual obfuscation, and limited latency under a configurable privacy-utility trade-off. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: “It's all just code”: How is responsibility embedded (or not) in the work of a team of software engineers?
Abstract: Recent research has documented how software can sometimes contribute to harm and inequality, affecting individuals, societies, and the environment. We argue that human values embedded in software, consciously or unconsciously during design and development, play a significant role in producing these outcomes. In other words, to understand responsibility in software engineering, it is crucial to understand how Software Engineers (SEs) incorporate responsibility into their practices, and if or how they reflect on the potential impact of their work. The research reported here probes this assertion by focusing on a team of research SEs involved in developing a commercial source code clone detection tool. Through reflexive thematic analysis of in-depth interviews, with meta-reflections from the SEs Principal Investigator, we offer a detailed account of the practices and artefacts referenced when these professionals reflect on responsibility in their work. Our analysis suggests that the team does not consider responsibility as a singular, unified concept. Instead, reflections on potential negative software impacts and mitigation strategies vary depending on whether they relate to the institutional/organisational context, the specific task, or the intended use. Overall, these SEs tend to perceive software as neutral or inherently beneficial, which, in turn, feeds into a lack of practice of engaging in speculation about the broader implications of the technologies they work with. To address these gaps, we propose a paradigm shift toward an infrastructural view of responsibility - interdisciplinary, sociotechnical, and situated – embedded within the diverse practices and organisational cultures of SE teams operating in different contexts. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Effect of AI authorship disclosure on purchase intention in cultural tourism souvenirs: The mediating roles of perceived effort and authenticity
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) expands in cultural tourism souvenir design and disclosure policies evolve, evidence remains limited on how AI authorship disclosure shapes responses across nationality groups and products. Drawing on signaling theory, two studies compared consumers from China and the U.S. across three disclosure conditions: unlabeled, human–AI co-created, and AI-generated. Study 1 used tourism postcard stimuli (N = 1110), and Study 2 used mug and tourism tote bag stimuli (N = 1255). Both studies found that disclosure affected purchase intention and interacted significantly with nationality. Differences across disclosure conditions were significant among participants from the U.S. but not among those from China. In Study 1, the unlabeled and human–AI co-created conditions did not differ, and both exceeded the AI-generated condition. In Study 2, the unlabeled condition exceeded both disclosed conditions for both products, whereas the latter two did not differ. AI-generated disclosure was consistently associated with lower purchase intention than no disclosure, whereas the relative position of human–AI co-created disclosure differed between studies. Parallel mediation analyses showed indirect effects through perceived effort and perceived authenticity. Perceived effort effects were significant for both comparisons with the unlabeled condition across three examined products, whereas the human–AI co-created versus unlabeled authenticity effect was nonsignificant in Study 1 but significant in Study 2. Nationality moderated some, but not all, indirect effects. Thus, firms should not assume that human–AI co-creation enhances responses and should consider clarifying human contribution and pretesting disclosure strategies across products and national markets. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Large language model-assisted modeling and optimization of high-purity Li2CO3 recovery from LFP recycling streams
Abstract: The downstream recovery of high-purity Li2CO3 from Li/K-rich solutions generated in Fe3+-based LFP recycling involves a strong trade-off between product purity (>99.5 %) and lithium recovery (>90 %). In this work, we develop a Large Language Model-Driven Multi-Agent Platform (LLM-MAP) based on GPT to guide the optimization of this method. LLM-MAP decomposes a complex task among role-defined agents and records intermediate outputs as structured summaries, thereby improving constraint retention and consistency during multi-stage, multi-objective process development. Using LLM-MAP, we jointly modeled the key precipitation and purification operations involved in Li2CO3 production via Fe3+ leaching, thereby accounting for the recovery losses that can arise when interdependent operations are optimized separately. Multi-objective optimization strategies implemented through the platform identified operating conditions that simultaneously achieved a product purity of 99.72 % and a recovery efficiency of 93.62 %. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Object identity in preschoolers: constraints in avoiding misidentification
Abstract: This study investigated whether preschool children act on the understanding that identical-looking objects can no longer be re-identified once their positions change unnoticed, using an everyday task assessing the ability to avoid misidentification and comparing their performance with that of adults. Although children aged 4 to 7 years (N = 66) reliably and repeatedly identified which of five identical-looking nuggets was a Playmobil figure’s “favorite”, the majority (56 %) nevertheless failed to separate it when tidying up the five nuggets into two opaque bags. In contrast, all adults (N = 66) did so. The fact that the majority of children failed to separate the verbally marked nugget, despite knowing “which one it was”, indicates that they struggle to anticipate that the identity of very similar objects can be maintained only as long as identity-relevant spatial information is available, pointing to a still-developing concept of object identity. Older preschoolers tended to be more successful in separating the figure’s favorite nugget than younger ones, suggesting a developmental progression in how spatial identity criteria for objects are conceptualized. In a condition in which the figure’s favorite nugget was perceptually distinct (different color), 64 % of another group of children (N = 66) packed it separately, even though this was not necessary, indicating that their behavior was strongly driven by perceptual salience. Taken together, these findings suggest that many preschool children still struggle to use spatial criteria of identity to guide their behavior, even in a context that minimizes memory, attentional, and linguistic demands. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Adaptive shuffle-boosting federated learning for imbalanced medical image analysis
Abstract: Medical image analysis is critical for clinical diagnosis, yet its application in federated learning remains constrained by class imbalance and inter-institutional heterogeneity. To address these challenges, we propose FedASB, a novel federated learning framework for imbalanced medical image analysis. This framework integrates two complementary modules: Adaptive Head Shuffle (AdaShuffle) and Dynamic Head Ensemble (DynEns) to enhance generalization capability and decision reliability in the presence of imbalanced and heterogeneous medical data. Specifically, we propose AdaShuffle, a dynamic head redistribution mechanism that assigns diversity classifier heads to different clients based on cross-client validation performance stored in a memory bank. By selectively excluding overfitted heads, AdaShuffle achieves an effective trade-off between global representation learning and client-specific adaptation. During inference, we propose DynEns to adaptively integrate predictions from multiple client-specific classifier heads via entropy-based confidence weighting, allowing reliable classifier heads to dominate the prediction while suppressing uncertain or overconfident outputs. Extensive experiments on multiple medical image benchmarks demonstrate that FedASB consistently outperforms existing federated learning methods under both imbalanced and heterogeneous conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: AI and negotiation: Facilitating learning or Fostering dependency?
Abstract: AI is being used in negotiation teaching and training both to promote learning and to facilitate planning for and executing a negotiation. This is a review of current empirical research on the relationships between AI negotiation interventions and learning and dependency. It categorizes AI negotiation interventions by practice, coaching, and feedback. It evaluates their effects on learning with respect to knowledge, satisfaction, behavior, and outcomes. Socratic coaching and post negotiation feedback and reflection appear to facilitate learning. However, interactive explicit AI coaching during planning or negotiation may risk dependency. Rather than dependency due to laziness, motivated students may defer to AI expertise. Alternatively, they may be overloaded by dynamic AI advice. The review concludes that there are many opportunities for future research on the question of if, why, and how AI can facilitate negotiators’ learning versus dependency. Research that looks broadly at learning, that compares separate versus packages of AI interventions, and that identifies mechanisms behind learning versus dependency is especially needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Author full names: Hu, Jingjing (56562102100); Gao, Xuesong (60697285700)
Title: Rethinking cultural awareness in think-aloud research
Abstract: Background: Think-aloud protocols have long been valued as a window into cognitive processes. However, insufficient attention has been paid to how culture shapes what participants articulate, how they do so, and what remains unspoken during think-aloud tasks. Purpose: This commentary re-examines think-aloud methodology on the basis of established theoretical, philosophical, and micro-linguistic foundations. Building on what has been achieved in this collection of studies, it aims to bolster cultural awareness in think-aloud research by proposing a reflective framework that foregrounds culture as integral to cognition rather than viewing it as methodological noise. Results: The developed reflective framework consists of five core dimensions of cultural awareness: (1) participant and researcher positionality; (2) the situatedness of tasks and materials; (3) cultural considerations in protocols and instructions; (4) cultural sensitivity in data analysis; and (5) the generalizability of research claims. Drawing on the studies in this special issue, each of these dimensions is detailed with an array of concrete, actionable aspects that operationalize cultural awareness across study design, data collection, analysis, and conclusion framing. The empirical practices featured throughout this special issue illuminate transformative horizons for future research, offering operational guidance to help researchers move beyond assumptions of procedural neutrality and treat verbal reports as culturally situated performances. Conclusions: Future think-aloud research should critically interrogate its methodological assumptions, foreground cultural dimensions throughout the analysis process, and ensure that theoretical claims are ecologically grounded in the data from which they are derived. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Approximating highly inapproximable problems on graphs of bounded twin-width
Source title: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: For any ε>0, we give a polynomial-time nε-approximation algorithm for MAX INDEPENDENT SET in graphs of bounded twin-width given with an O(1)-sequence. This result is derived from the following time-approximation trade-off: We establish an O(1)2-approximation algorithm running in time exp⁡(Oq(n2)), for every integer q⩾0. Guided by the same framework, we obtain similar approximation algorithms for MIN COLORING and MAX INDUCED MATCHING. In general graphs, all these problems are known to be highly inapproximable: for any ε>0, a polynomial-time n1−ε-approximation for any of them would imply that P=NP [Håstad, FOCS '96; Zuckerman, ToC '07; Chalermsook et al., SODA '13]. We generalize the algorithms for MAX INDEPENDENT SET and MAX INDUCED MATCHING to the independent (induced) packing of any fixed connected graph H. In contrast, we show that such approximation guarantees on graphs of bounded twin-width given with an O(1)-sequence are very unlikely for MIN INDEPENDENT DOMINATING SET, and somewhat unlikely for LONGEST PATH and LONGEST INDUCED PATH. Regarding the existence of better approximation algorithms, there is a (very) light evidence that the obtained approximation factor of nε for MAX INDEPENDENT SET may be best possible. This is the first in-depth study of the approximability of problems in graphs of bounded twin-width. Prior to this paper, essentially the only such result was a polynomial-time O(1)-approximation algorithm for MIN DOMINATING SET [Bonnet et al., ICALP '21]. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Variable time-step for power grid EMT simulations
Abstract: This paper presents a new variable time-step method for the electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation of power systems. Trapezoidal discretization with a constant time-step is commonly employed in EMT simulations of power systems. During an EMT simulation, power systems typically encounter high-frequency transients that demand small time-steps for accuracy, as well as low-frequency and steady-state conditions that allow larger time-steps for efficiency. With a fixed time-step, either the simulation accuracy or speed is compromised, and achieving a trade-off is not feasible for all cases. Consequently, this paper proposes a novel variable time-step strategy for maintaining both simulation accuracy and speed. The performance of the proposed method is verified through the WECC 240-bus system. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Picard approximation and stability analysis of generalized ϱ-Caputo stochastic fractional differential equations with application to a Black–Scholes-type model
Abstract: This paper investigates stochastic fractional differential equations involving the generalized ϱ-Caputo derivative of order β∈(1/2,1). Under global Lipschitz and linear growth conditions, existence and uniqueness are established through successive approximations. Explicit pointwise mean-square estimates are derived for the Picard approximation error and the continuous dependence of solutions on the initial data. Sufficient conditions for finite-time stability (F − T − S) and generalized Ulam–Hyers–Rassias (U − H − R) stability are also obtained, together with computable stability constants. For numerical illustration, a generalized Euler–Maruyama (E–M) scheme is adapted to time-dependent coefficients and applied to a stochastic fractional Black–Scholes-type model. Title: Mission reliability assessment and optimization of offshore wind farm inspection unmanned aerial vehicle swarm with coupled physical and data layers under multi-source uncertainties
Abstract: Mission reliability assessment and dynamic optimization are essential to ensure safe and efficient operation of offshore wind farm inspection unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms under multi-source uncertainties. However, existing methods remain limited in characterizing cross-layer coupling effects, including interactions between physical-layer energy consumption and data-layer transmission, and dependencies among environmental disturbances, equipment degradation, and communication channel variations. This paper proposes a mission reliability assessment and optimization method for offshore wind farm inspection UAV swarms under multi-source uncertainties, based on C-vine copula modeling and graph reinforcement learning. The method develops a coupled physical-data layer modeling framework incorporating battery degradation, offshore wind disturbance, and line-of-sight/non-line-of-sight (LoS/NLoS) channel variation to characterize swarm behavior in complex offshore inspection scenarios. Furthermore, a C-vine copula-based joint uncertainty model is established to capture nonlinear dependencies among key variables, supporting a dynamic reliability assessment framework that links battery capacity fade and hovering energy constraints to mission feasibility probability. A graph attention network-proximal policy optimization (GAT-PPO) algorithm is then proposed for dynamic task reassignment. Simulation results show that the proposed method reduces the reliability estimation deviation from 7.87% under the independence assumption to 0.82%. It further improves reliability by 3.1% and 3.5% over the best baseline under the most severe UAV failure and task revisit scenarios, respectively, demonstrating improvements in mission reliability and operational efficiency. Title: Identifying best candidates for busbar splitting
Abstract: Rising electricity demand and the growing integration of renewables are intensifying congestion in transmission grids. Grid topology optimization through busbar splitting (BuS) and optimal transmission switching can alleviate grid congestion and reduce the generation costs in a power system. However, BuS optimization requires a large number of binary variables, and analyzing all the substations for potential new topological actions is computationally intractable, particularly in large grids. To tackle this issue, we propose a set of metrics to identify and rank promising candidates for BuS, focusing on finding buses where topology optimization can reduce generation costs. To assess the effect of BuS on the identified buses, we use a combined mixed-integer convex-quadratic BuS model to compute the optimal topology and test it with the non-linear non-convex AC optimal power flow (OPF) simulation to show its AC feasibility and generation cost reduction compared to the AC-OPF simulations. By testing and validating the proposed metrics on test cases of different sizes, we show that they are able to identify busbars that reduce the total generation costs when their topology is optimized. Thus, the metrics enable effective selection of busbars for BuS, with no need to test every busbar in the grid, one at a time. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Boosting chemical looping hydrogen production over Cu–Al co-doped NiFe2O4: insights into lattice-oxygen activity and structural stability
Abstract: NiFe2O4 is a promising oxygen carrier for chemical looping hydrogen production, but its application is limited by the trade-off between lattice-oxygen activity and structural stability. Here, Cu- and Al-doped NiFe2O4 oxygen carriers were prepared to combine enhanced oxygen reactivity with improved cyclic durability. Structural characterization supported the incorporation of Cu and Al into the spinel framework and revealed higher defect-related oxygen fractions in the Cu-containing samples. At 850 °C, Cu0.2Ni0.8Fe1.8Al0.2O4 (CNFAO) achieved an H2 yield of 14.8 mmol·g−1 Fe2O3 and a production rate of 1.48 mmol·g−1 Fe2O3·min−1, while retaining 12.3 mmol·g−1 Fe2O3 after 80 cycles. Mechanistic analysis indicates that Cu doping enhances lattice-oxygen activity by promoting oxygen-vacancy formation and bulk lattice-oxygen diffusion, thereby improving reduction kinetics and hydrogen production. Meanwhile, Al stabilizes the spinel framework and suppresses phase separation, particle coalescence, and pore collapse. Their complementary effects enable CNFAO to balance high reactivity with long-term structural stability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Adaptive subsidy implementation for stakeholder-centric biofuel supply chains
Abstract: The transition to sustainable energy is hindered by the uncertain dynamics of biofuel supply chains, where traditional constant subsidy schemes frequently create fiscal inefficiencies and misaligned incentives. This work proposes a framework to formulate and implement adaptive subsidy plans for biofuel supply chains by highlighting the critical role of stakeholder engagement throughout the biofuel ecosystem. We introduce an agent-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework that describes stakeholder dynamics and adaptively explores subsidy policies. By simulating dynamic interactions across the biofuel value chain under uncertain transition dynamics, our framework learns policy schedules that dynamically align incentive timing with stakeholder readiness. Furthermore, stakeholder-targeted policy mitigates early adoption disparities across supply chain tiers without worsening the baseline emissions profile (preserving particulate matter reductions without escalating NOx penalties).
