Title: Pathways to plant-based meal consumption: A two-wave test of the health action process approach (HAPA)
Abstract: Despite well-documented health and environmental benefits, increasing plant-based meal consumption remains challenging in meat-centric societies, reflecting complex socio-cognitive processes in translating intention into action. While past behavior remained most strongly associated with plant-based meal consumption, the parsimonious model reaffirmed action planning as the key intention-behavior mediator. Title: Together or apart? Migration, education access, and intergenerational mobility in China
Abstract: This paper studies how hukou-based education wedges and child-arrangement costs jointly shape welfare and intergenerational educational mobility in China. I develop a quantitative spatial model with overlapping generations in which households sequentially choose education, migration, and child arrangement, and estimate it using census and household-survey data. Under a common financing rule, two child-targeted policies raise the co-migration rate to a similar extent but differ sharply in welfare and mobility. Subsidizing co-migrating families in high-cost destinations generates 1.4 times as much welfare per unit of government revenue as removing migrant children's education-access wedges. These gains concentrate on recipients. Removing the education-access wedges delivers over four times the mobility gain per unit of revenue, and the resulting human capital generates growing welfare gains across generations. Title: Bibliometric study of environmental education: Scientific architecture and the transition toward micro-educational and behavioral approaches
Abstract: Although scientific production in environmental education has grown steadily, fragmented approaches and limited interdisciplinary integration persist. Moreover, the transition from macronormative frameworks to microeducational approaches oriented toward behavioral change remains insufficiently characterized. The objective of this study was to comprehensively analyze the scientific architecture of environmental education, identifying its structural evolution, key actors, predominant sources, funding dynamics, thematic trends, and scientific production cycle, with particular attention to the shift toward microeducational and behavioral approaches. The study followed a rigorous and consolidated four-stage bibliometric method. A total of 4,952 documents indexed in Scopus were analyzed using the Bibliometrix software, examining six main indicators: (1) authors, (2) sponsors, (3) thematic evolution and conceptual structure, (4) sources, (5) documents, and (6) scientific production. The findings reveal sustained expansion in environmental education, with a productivity peak in 2025 and a projected stabilization toward 2032, confirming its advanced consolidation phase. An editorial structure concentrated in historical core journals—Environmental Education Research and Journal of Environmental Education—was identified, alongside growing interdisciplinary expansion toward sustainability, higher education, and technological innovation. Scientific leadership is concentrated in the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom, although emerging economies such as Brazil and China are gaining prominence. Thematically, macrostructural cores linked to sustainability and sustainable development persist; however, microeducational approaches such as pro-environmental behavior, outdoor environmental education, and environmental knowledge are emerging more strongly, indicating a shift toward the analysis of situated learning processes and behavioral change. Bibliometric findings were contrasted with evidence from other bibliometric studies and systematic reviews. It is concluded that environmental education has evolved from a paradigm centered on global normative frameworks toward a multidimensional model integrating experience, behavior, technological innovation, and community action. Title: The association between maternal acculturation, acculturative stress and factors related to child feeding in the Hispanic community health study/study of Latinos family lifestyle outcomes research (HCHS/SOL FLOR) study
Abstract: The acculturation process and its related stress have been associated with health declines among Hispanic/Latino immigrants in the US. However, the impact on caregiver feeding style and the home food environment are unknown. This study aimed to assess the associations between maternal acculturation and acculturation stress with both caregiver feeding style (n = 248) and the home food environment (n = 178) using data from mother-child dyads from the Family Lifestyle Outcomes Research ancillary study of the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos. Children were aged 3-9 years at the time of the study. Results suggest an association between greater maternal acculturative stress and greater odds of authoritative and authoritarian feeding styles. An association between greater acculturative stress and greater maternal demandingness in feeding was also observed. Additionally, greater language acculturation and greater length of time in the US were associated with more sweetened beverages and fewer fruits and vegetables reported in the home. These results highlight the importance of supporting Hispanic immigrants as they adapt to life in the US and developing culturally appropriate interventions that can address child feeding and food purchasing behaviors among immigrant parents. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Yang F.; Chen H.; Yu X.; Zhang M.; Xiao X.; Deng M.
Title: A survey on fake review detection: From pre-trained language models to large language models
Abstract: Online reviews shape consumer decisions, platform governance, and corporate reputation. Fake reviews compromise this information channel by injecting deceptive evidence into rating systems, recommendation pipelines, and public trust mechanisms. The rise of large language models, or LLMs, has changed the problem in two directions. LLMs can generate fluent and context-aware deceptive reviews, while pre-trained language models, or PLMs, and LLMs also provide stronger semantic representations for detection. This survey reviews fake review detection from an information fusion perspective, covering 211 studies published from 2018 to early 2026. We organize existing work by evidence source and fusion level, covering review text, sentiment, rating behavior, temporal metadata, user-product graphs, multimodal content, external knowledge, and LLM-generated signals. We trace the development from traditional machine learning and deep learning to PLM-based and LLM-based methods, and examine how different approaches combine textual, behavioral, structural, and multimodal evidence. We also analyze reported performance trends on widely used Amazon, Yelp, and OpSpam benchmark families, while noting the limitations caused by different label construction procedures, data splits, and evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems in adversarial generation, cross-domain transfer, uncertainty-aware fusion, missing-source robustness, interpretability, and trustworthy evaluation for AI-generated deceptive content. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: How can hotels strategically enhance competitive performance? Investigating the dynamic roles and impacts of service attributes on customer satisfaction and dissatisfaction
Abstract: This study examines the asymmetric impact of service attributes on customer satisfaction (CS) and dissatisfaction (DS) in the luxury and upper upscale hotel segments, utilizing Impact Asymmetry Analysis and Impact Asymmetry Competitor Analysis. Grounded by the two-factor theory, this study integrates insights from online review ratings and textual sentiment to gauge customer evaluations. The findings reveal that attributes have discrete impacts on CS and DS when comparing high and low performance consistency brands. Hotels exhibiting low performance consistency are advised to prioritize managing attributes such as rooms, followed by value and cleanliness in rating-based evaluations. Additionally, location is identified as a key competitive disadvantage requiring urgent action in sentiment-based assessments. This study extends the understanding of the two-factor theory by examining the distinct impacts of attributes on CS and DS under varying performance consistency, providing actionable insights for hoteliers to strategically enhance attribute-level performance that strengthens customer experience and competitive standing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Optimal generation expansion planning with weather-dependent generation and transmission
Abstract: Generation Expansion Planning is used to obtain future planning decisions that ensure the system reliability while minimizing cost. However, the past decade has seen an increase in weather-dependent faults in the electric grid, higher shares of weather-dependent renewable generation, and increased reliance on weather-dependent dynamic line ratings. To account for those dependencies, we propose a two-stage stochastic generation expansion planning model integrates leverages a spatial weather model to assess the generation and transmission line availability. This includes both variations of renewable generation capacity factors and dynamic line rating, and weather-dependent outage rates. The proposed framework is tested using a synthetic network, demonstrating that dynamic line rating outperforms static line ratings by reducing total operational costs and load shedding. © 2026

Title: EWiAR: Enhanced WiFi activity recognition using spectrogram analysis and cross-attention
Abstract: Driven by the development of wireless sensing, human activity recognition (HAR) based on WiFi channel state information (CSI) has attracted immense attention owing to its low-cost, device-free, and non-intrusive characteristics. Conventional approaches heavily rely on time-frequency analysis to generate spectrograms. However, fixed-window time-frequency transforms involve an inherent trade-off between temporal and frequency resolution, while residual noise and artifacts may obscure motion-related structures in the spectrograms. To tackle these challenges, we propose EWiAR, a framework designed for high-precision HAR. At its frontend, an Enhanced Spectrogram Analysis Network (ESAN) is introduced to mitigate resolution trade-offs. It leverages a multi-scale feature extraction (MSFE) bank to dynamically capture varying frequency resolutions, followed by a spectrogram refinement module (SRM) that actively purifies the representations from background interference. Rather than using standard classifiers, the backend employs a Time-Frequency Cross-Attention Transformer (TFAiT) to process these spectrograms. TFAiT orchestrates a dual-branch learning mechanism that concurrently models temporal motion dependencies via a bidirectional LSTM and extracts global spectral patterns using a vision transformer. These complementary features are fused through a dedicated Time-Frequency Cross-Attention mechanism. Comprehensive experiments across synthetic signals and three public datasets demonstrate that EWiAR achieves superior overall performance compared to eleven mainstream benchmarks. Specifically, it delivers accuracies of 98.6% on WiAR, 99.1% on UT-HAR and 98.9% on NTU-HAR, firmly validating its exceptional effectiveness for complex indoor environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Towards reliable intelligent decision-making systems: implicit and explicit correlation analysis with hypergraph neural networks
Abstract: Intelligent decision-making systems in autonomous operations require reliability analysis approaches capable of representing the complex, high-dimensional correlations among components, failure chains and decision measures. Conventional graph methods remain limited in describing both explicit structural dependencies and implicit influence pathways. This study proposes a Hypergraph Neural Network with Reversed Multi-Head Attention (HGNN-RMHA) that integrates explicit and implicit correlation modelling for interpretable and reliable decision support. The framework employs hyperedges to represent multi-node relations, while the Reversed Multi-Head Attention mechanism enhances sensitivity to low-frequency but crucial implicit features, enabling a unified representation of cross-layer dependencies. The Top-K adaptive association-rule mining approach further extracts semantically interpretable causal patterns, and comprehensive correlation analyses are conducted to reveal the intrinsic relationships between component failures and decision measures. Additionally, the Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) knowledge-enhancement strategy injects rule-level priors into large language models (LLMs), aligning structural reasoning with natural language inference for rule-driven interpretability. Experimental evaluations on multiple public datasets verify that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing baselines in node classification, link prediction, correlation interpretation, and rule-based reasoning. The integration of explicit and implicit correlation effectively captures the cross-layer failures­ propagation patterns, thereby improving the trustworthiness and interpretability of intelligent decision-making in safety­ critical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Primary care effectiveness, multimorbidity, and hospital use in public and private health-care systems in Brazil: a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2019–2021 Brazilian longitudinal study of aging
Abstract: Background: Whether patient-reported experiences in primary care modify the association between multimorbidity and emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations remains unclear. We examined these associations across public and private health system sectors among Brazilians aged ≥50 years. Methods: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the 2019–2021 Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Aging. Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of ≥2 of 13 chronic conditions. A 12-item patient-reported primary care effectiveness index captured access, continuity, communication, and coordination with participants’ usual source of healthcare. Primary outcomes were ED visits and hospitalizations in the past 12 months. Poisson regression models estimated associations with the outcomes, and assessed interactions among multimorbidity, primary care effectiveness, and health system sectors. Findings: Among 9058 participants (mean age = 66.3 ± 9.9 years; females = 55.3%; White race/ethnicity = 46.4%), 38.0% had multimorbidity. Overall, 12.5% reported an ED visit and 6.0% ≥ 1 hospitalization in the past 12 months. Multimorbidity was associated with approximately twice the prevalence of ED visits and three times the prevalence of hospitalizations. Primary care effectiveness modified these associations across health system sectors (three-way interaction p = 0.04 for ED visits and p < 0.001 for hospitalization). In the public system, higher primary care effectiveness attenuated the association between multimorbidity and hospitalization (interaction prevalence ratio [PR] = 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.63–0.87). In contrast, in the private system, higher primary care effectiveness strengthened the associations of multimorbidity with ED visits (interaction PR = 1.40, 95% CI = 1.18–1.66) and hospitalization (interaction PR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.22–2.50). Interpretation: Associations between multimorbidity and healthcare use varied according to patient-reported primary care experiences and health system sector. Title: Suppressed inquiry: The hidden toll of working with satisfaction-optimized AI
Abstract: LLMs have become thinking companions for hundreds of millions worldwide, and they often do remarkable work. But their satisfaction-optimized design produces suppressed inquiry: the tendency for LLMs to inhibit rather than facilitate users' questioning process. LLMs appear fluent, confident, and seemingly all-knowing, their near-instant and polished output making non-LLM work feel unacceptably tedious and less eloquent. They affirm rather than interrogate users' assumptions, producing output that is deceptively adequate—shallower, less original, and less carefully reasoned than it appears. Seemingly competent systems also reduce vigilance and the monitoring impulse that independent judgment requires. Their responses also confine users within the frame they establish, narrowing what users think to ask. These costs are self-concealing: detecting them requires the very engagement that they suppress. And repeated delegation gradually atrophies users' capacity to reason independently. Three converging pressures make correction difficult: commercial incentives that reward satisfaction over substance, LLMs’ tendency to revert to satisfaction-optimized defaults even when users push back, and a societal drift toward less-effortful engagement. We propose a research agenda to deepen the understanding of suppressed inquiry and how to counter it, to move closer to the remarkable thinking partners LLMs promised to be. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Luo W.; Zhou H.; Chen X.; Li N.
Title: Locus of morphological processing during visual L2 compound recognition: An ERP investigation
Abstract: The extent to which second language (L2) speakers process morphologically complex words through morphem-based processes remains debated, with conflicting evidence from behavioral studies suggesting that L2 learners may rely primarily on orthographic overlap rather than morphological structure. The present study employed morpho-semantic priming paradigm and event-related potentials (ERPs) to investigate whether and how Chinese-English bilinguals engage in morphological decomposition and morpho-semantic integration during real-time English compound word recognition. We manipulated two factors: Relatedness (primes semantically related vs. unrelated to the first constituent morpheme of the compound word) and Semantic Transparency (transparent vs. opaque compound words). In the N400 time window, a significant main effect of Relatedness emerged, with both transparent and opaque compound words showing comparable N400 attenuation, indicating early semantically blind morphological decomposition. In the late negativity window (800–1200 ms), a significant main effect of Semantic Transparency emerged, with opaque compounds eliciting greater negativity than transparent compounds, reflecting the late morpho-semantic integration process. These findings demonstrate a biphasic pattern of L2 morphological processing encompassing early obligatory morphological decomposition followed by late morpho-semantic integration. Overall, our findings suggest that Chinese-English bilinguals can engage in native-like morphological processing during recognition of English compound words. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Reinforcement learning for robust ageing-aware control of Li-ion battery systems with data-driven formal verification
Abstract: Rechargeable lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are a ubiquitous element of modern technology. In the last decades, the production and design of such batteries and their adjacent embedded charging and safety protocols, denoted by Battery Management Systems (BMS), has taken central stage. A fundamental challenge to be addressed is the trade-off between the speed of charging and the ageing behaviour, resulting in the loss of capacity in the battery cell. We rely on a high-fidelity physics-based battery model and propose an approach to data-driven charging and safety protocol design. Following a Counterexample-Guided Inductive Synthesis scheme, we combine Reinforcement Learning (RL) with recent developments in data-driven formal methods to obtain a hybrid control strategy: RL is used to synthesise the individual controllers, and a data-driven abstraction guides their partitioning into a switched structure, depending on the initial output measurements of the battery. The resulting discrete selection among RL-based controllers, coupled with the continuous battery dynamics, realises a hybrid system. When a design meets the desired criteria, the abstraction provides probabilistic guarantees on the closed-loop performance of the cell. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Cheng H.; Liu T.; Wang Q.; Sheng K.; Chen L.
Title: FinSA-MoE: A parameter-efficient mixture-of-experts framework for cross-domain Chinese financial sentiment analysis
Abstract: Financial sentiment signals from textual narratives are crucial for understanding market dynamics. However, heterogeneity across financial text sources introduces substantial cross-domain discrepancies in linguistic structure, noise patterns, and sentiment expression. In Chinese financial contexts, stylistic divergence between formal news and informal investor commentary further exacerbates these challenges, destabilizing representation learning in large language models. To address these challenges, we propose FinSA-MoE, a parameter-efficient mixture-of-experts framework for cross-domain Chinese financial sentiment analysis. Built upon a pre-trained large language model backbone, FinSA-MoE constructs domain-specific experts for financial news and stock commentary using lightweight low-rank adaptation adapters, while a mixture-of-experts routing mechanism dynamically selects appropriate experts to enable efficient and robust inference across heterogeneous financial domains. We design a composite training objective with regularization techniques to enhance training stability and cross-domain generalization by addressing class imbalance and uneven expert utilization. Furthermore, we introduce FinNF, a large-scale Financial News and Forum dataset comprising over 2.12 million high-quality Chinese financial news articles and stock commentary texts, which provides a solid data foundation for fine-tuning and evaluating financial sentiment analysis models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FinSA-MoE consistently outperforms existing deep learning approaches and financial large language models across multiple evaluation metrics on news, stock commentary, and mixed-domain benchmarks. The proposed framework effectively captures cross-domain financial sentiment characteristics and offers a scalable solution for Chinese financial text understanding. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: HGMG: Enhancing heterogeneous graph embedding by meta-graph learning
Abstract: Due to the ability of heterogeneous graph in modeling different types of objects and relationships in the real world, and the capability of graph embedding in extracting the effective features from graphs, heterogeneous graph embedding has received extensive attention in recent years. Heterogeneous graph embedding aims to learn low-dimensional node representations by capturing attribute information, structural information and semantic information of heterogeneous graph, facilitating downstream tasks, such as node classification, node clustering and link prediction. Meta-graphs, the powerful tool for expressing the complex composite semantic relationships between nodes, are widely combined with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and the attention mechanism to explore rich and meaningful semantic information hidden in heterogeneous graphs. Although existing meta-graph-based methods have achieved success, there remains considerable room for comprehensively exploring semantics in heterogeneous graphs, including selecting meta-graphs with rich semantics, learning meta-graph semantics, utilizing diverse node semantics. To address the above challenges, we propose a novel model for enhancing Heterogeneous Graph embedding by Meta-Graph learning (HGMG). Firstly, we propose a structure-aware meta-graph selection strategy for capturing rich semantics. Secondly, we design a meta-graph semantic learning mechanism for enhancing node embeddings. Finally, we present a semantic incorporating method for fusing the structural semantics and inherent semantics of nodes. Experimental results on real datasets demonstrate the proposed HGMG model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on three downstream tasks including node classification, node clustering and link prediction. The source code and implementation details of HGMG are available at https://github.com/kkkkajwjds/HGMG. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Full-scale experimental investigation of rockfall impact on EPS geofoam-cushioned composite vertical rigid barriers
Abstract: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) geofoam is a promising sacrificial cushioning material for rockfall protection, yet its full-scale performance in composite vertical rigid barriers remains insufficiently quantified. This study investigates the lateral rockfall impact response of an EPS-cushioned composite barrier through a full-scale L9 orthogonal test program. The barrier comprised a 1.8-m-thick EPS cushion, a reinforced-concrete load-distribution slab, force-sensor assemblies, and a rigid supporting wall. Rockfall mass and EPS density were selected as nominal factors. Transmitted force and block acceleration were measured synchronously, while impact velocity, rebound, and translational kinetic-energy change were derived from high-speed video. Results revealed a clear stiffness–deformability trade-off: higher-density EPS resisted local penetration more effectively but generally produced higher peak transmitted forces and lower translational kinetic-energy loss fractions. The measured kinetic-energy loss ranged from 35.92% to 47.56% and decreased consistently with increasing EPS density within each rockfall-mass group. The system response resulted from EPS compression and crushing, lateral load spreading, and subsequent load redistribution through the RC slab. These findings demonstrate the potential of replaceable EPS geofoam as an effective frontal sacrificial layer for improving the impact-mitigation performance of composite vertical rigid rockfall barriers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Bridging the Human-AI preference gap: A persuasion-oriented tripartite framework
Abstract: The remarkable performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems on a wide variety of complex tasks has fueled its rapid adoption in recent years. Yet, many individuals still exhibit a human-AI preference gap, such that they prefer human-generated over AI-generated outputs and follow recommendations made by generative AI (GenAI) less than human advice. We conceptualize the rejection of a superior AI system in favor of an inferior human as a persuasion failure that necessitates psychological rather than technological resolution. Recent research has identified various interventions that compress the human-AI preference gap. We codify these interventions by introducing a persuasion-oriented tripartite framework that delineates three distinct paths by which the preference gap between humans and AI systems may be narrowed: (1) AI-centric interventions, which directly bolster perceptions and evaluations of AI systems; (2) human-centric interventions, which reduce the (often inflated) perceptions and evaluations of humans; and (3) hybrid interventions, which offer an integrated or reformulated alternative that combines human and AI elements. Ultimately, our tripartite framework illustrates how different persuasion tactics fundamentally reshape beliefs and attitudes about both AI and humans, thereby informing system design elements and communication strategies that can bridge the human-AI preference gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Using physiological measures to assess and diagnose team performance: An interrogative approach
Abstract: Physiological measures have the potential to capture the dynamic nature of teamwork as it unfolds. Despite this potential, relatively few studies have applied physiological data in team contexts, leaving a gap in theory and practice. To address this gap, this work examines the following question: What are the emerging principles for using physiological measures to assess and diagnose team performance? To explore this question, we present an interrogative approach that structures the key considerations for applying physiological measures in team research. Specifically, this approach organizes considerations related to the purpose, context, personnel, timing, measurement selection, and implementation of using physiological measures to assess team performance. Building on prior guidance, we propose a set of emerging principles that synthesize best practices while introducing new considerations specific to the use of physiological data in team contexts. These principles provide practical guidance for researchers and practitioners seeking to leverage physiological measures, while emphasizing that their effective use depends on rigorous methodology, ethical safeguards, and integration with other validated assessment approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based Flow Splitting for Combinatorial Network Packet Routing Problem
Abstract: Due to the rising demand for Quality of Service (QoS) in the emerging network, this paper considers the routing problem of efficiently planning the transmission path of flow demands to balance the load of the network. Existing classical routing algorithms based on static decision-making are unable to adjust to dynamical scenarios with fluctuating flow. Traditional reinforcement learning-based methods face challenges in large-scale scenarios due to the vast state and action spaces. Besides, the neural networks used for policy generation also suffer from issues like rudimentary feature extraction and limited learning capability. In this paper, we first introduce RequestNet, a novel attention-based model designed to better leverage the information of network topology and feature correlations. We also propose a multi-agent modeling approach for the network packet routing problem, named RequestNet-MA, which treats pairs of edge routers as agents, allowing us to allocate traffic from the perspective of flow demands, thus significantly reducing the dimensions of state and action spaces and enhancing inter-agent communication and cooperation. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate that the proposed RequestNet-MA can reduce maximum link utilization and scale well to a large-scale network. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Metabolic cost, mechanical work and efficiency of lateral walking
Abstract: Purpose: Lateral walking is an asymmetrical gait, mainly used in sports or working tasks, characterised by higher oxygen demand compared to forward walking. Comprehensive analyses of its mechanical efficiency—the mechanical work produced over the metabolic cost—are lacking. The purpose of this work is to fill this gap of knowledge. Methods: Twenty-four healthy and active young adults (13 females, 11 males) completed controlled treadmill tests adjusted to their self-selected lateral walking speed (SSLWS) and free tests on a flat surface. Four treadmill speeds (±20%, SSLWS and +40% of SSLWS) were tested. Metabolic data were collected via indirect calorimetry, while mechanical work was estimated from 3D motion capture data. Data was analyzed by comparing the results at different speeds and using regression models. Results: Cardiorespiratory demand was moderate but, due to the low speed, the cost of transport (~7 J·kg⁻¹·m⁻¹) was more than double that of walking at self-selected speed. The mechanical work was comparable to walking, which resulted in lower estimates of mechanical efficiency (~12%). Treadmill trials showed higher metabolic demand than free overground lateral walking. Conclusion: In healthy young adults, the combination of modest absolute cardiorespiratory load with high metabolic cost per unit distance suggests that lateral walking may be useful for low-intensity training and merits further investigation as a rehabilitation gait in clinical populations, where metabolic demand without high cardiovascular stress is desired. © 2026

Author full names: Hou, Huiying (Cynthia) (57206935271); Lin, Minqi (57224471899); Sing, Michael C.P. (57189855171)
Title: Evaluating university campus open spaces through a resilience-based urban system lens: Integrating ecological, spatial and adaptive dimensions
Abstract: This study conceptualizes university campus open spaces as socio-ecological systems and develops an integrated evaluation framework combining spatial elements, ecological services, and adaptive capacities. Addressing the tendency for campus open spaces to be assessed through site-specific criteria, the study applies a resilience-based urban systems perspective to capture the interdependencies among environmental, spatial, and functional performance attributes. Using a case study at a Hong Kong university campus, questionnaire-based surveys were conducted with 220 users across ten open-space types, and Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was employed to examine how perceived importance of performance attributes shapes satisfaction with different open-space settings. The results reveal two distinct satisfaction pathways. For passive open spaces (courtyards, cafés, squares), satisfaction is predominantly driven by spatial elements (β = 0.507), indicating that perceptions of openness, scale, and aesthetic quality play a decisive role in shaping user experience, with ecological services exerting an indirect influence through spatial elements. In contrast, satisfaction with active open spaces (sport places) is primarily shaped by adaptive capacities (β = 0.268), such as accessibility, safety, and sociability, reflecting a more function-oriented appraisal. Across both pathways, ecological services emerge as a foundational dimension, significantly influencing spatial elements and adaptive capacities, and being directly associated with satisfaction in ecologically intensive settings such as rooftop gardens. By revealing differentiated satisfaction mechanisms and their structural relationships, this study advances the understanding of campus open spaces as integrated and resilient systems. The findings provide actionable guidance for campus planning and management, suggesting that investments should prioritize spatial quality in passive spaces while emphasizing functional accessibility and safety for active environments. © 2026 The Authors.

Author full names: Srivastava, Jigyasha (59310366600); Beri Gopinathan, Prakash Kumar (6505897975)
Title: Techno-economic study and sensitivity analysis- benefits of complex petrochemical waste refining
Abstract: For the petrochemical industry to maintain resource sustainability, complex waste must be treated effectively. In the previous work, the Aspen Hysys V12.0 modeling tool was used to analyze the regeneration of water, aromatics (BTX), and glycols (MEG, DEG, and TEG) from petrochemical effluent and the operating parameters were validated with experimental study. This study presents a techno-economic and environmental assessment of an integrated petrochemical wastewater treatment system with resource recovery. The process enables recovery of water (7.8 MM kg/year), aromatics such as benzene and toluene (468,000 kg/year each), and glycols (over 16.5 MM kg/year). The total capital investment is estimated at $42.4 MM, with annual operating costs of $8.46 MM and revenue of $18 MM. The system achieves a net present value (NPV) of $31.8 MM, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 19.9%, and a payback period of 4.87 years. Sensitivity analysis identified product price and electricity cost as key economic drivers. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) showed a 95% probability of positive NPV, indicating robust performance under uncertainty. The carbon footprint is estimated at 11,970 tons CO2/year (0.12 kg CO2/kg treated), representing an 87% reduction compared to conventional systems. Carbon pricing further enhances economic viability. The novelty of this work lies in integrating techno-economic analysis, uncertainty quantification, carbon footprint evaluation, and circular economy principles into a unified framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed system is a sustainable and economically viable solution for petrochemical wastewater management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Can visibility-based metrics predict soundscape perception in cities?
Abstract: Context plays a central role in soundscape perception within the ISO 12913 series framework. However, there is a lack of empirical evidence on how to identify operational, standardised proxy metrics for capturing ‘context’ in soundscape assessment and prediction. The study addresses this gap by deriving a set of visibility-based metrics from Isovist and Visibility Graph Analysis (VGA) and evaluating their effectiveness in a soundscape predictive model. An on-site soundscape data campaign was conducted in Bloomsbury, Central London., Isovist and VGA metrics were computed for each soundscape observation to obtain a high-resolution, geospatial soundscape dataset (N = 787). Key findings stand out: (1) Isovist and VGA metrics correlate strongly with pleasantness (PISO) but weakly with eventfulness (EISO); (2) four ‘visual-spatial’ clusters (ViSpID) are derived from the selected Isovist and VGA metrics: Highly connected streets, Moderately connected streets, Open spaces & poorly connected streets, and Enclosed spaces; and (3) a linear multilevel model predicting PISO that incorporates these clusters (ViSpID) with psychoacoustic predictors (R2 = 0.51) outperforms a psychoacoustics-only baseline model (R2 = 0.15). These findings demonstrate that Isovist and VGA metrics provide practical proxies for the structural visibility and spatial configuration dimensions of physical context and support a systematic and reproducible framework for integrating these effects into predictive modelling. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Locally constrained optimization of PC-SAFT parameters for reliable restricted group contribution calculations for associating fluids
Abstract: Accurate vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) prediction for associating fluids is paramount for chemical separation and carbon capture. However, systematic model parameter optimization across diverse equations of state (EoSs) remains limited. A fundamental challenge arises when transitioning from model parameters to a group contribution (GC) framework: the inherent trade-off between correlative accuracy and the linear additivity of groups. In this study, we first construct a high-precision model parameter database for 57 pure associating fluids using global optimization across PC-SAFT, SAFT-VR Mie, and CPA EoSs. SAFT-VR Mie demonstrates superior performance with an average absolute relative deviation (AARD%) below 0.42%. To reconcile the conflict between correlative accuracy and the linear additivity of groups, we propose an optimization strategy. This strategy yields model parameters that preserve both correlative fidelity and the linear additivity of groups. This framework enables the derivation of first- and second-order group parameters capable of resolving isomers, thereby substantially extending the applicability of PC-SAFT to complex associating systems with limited experimental data. Finally, we find that global optimization exhibits parameter compensation behavior, thereby achieving excellent fitting to experimental data. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Ye Z.; Wei B.; Deng L.; Zheng J.; Huang Y.
Title: Spatiotemporal resampling-based dynamic ensemble selection for nonstationary streams
Abstract: Classifying imbalanced data streams in nonstationary environments presents a substantial challenge, primarily due to the simultaneous presence of class imbalance and concept drift. Existing ensemble methods often struggle to balance the trade-off between preserving historical minority concepts and adapting to rapid distribution changes, thereby leading to performance degradation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel framework named the spatiotemporal resampling-based dynamic ensemble selection (STR-DES). First, a spatiotemporal weighted SMOTE (STW-SMOTE) is introduced, which synthesizes high-quality minority class instances by weighting historical neighbors according to both spatial proximity and temporal recency, ensuring alignment with the evolving data concept. Second, a stabilized dynamic ensemble selection strategy is developed, in which the competence region is constructed from multiple historical chunks to improve the robustness of local classifier evaluation under nonstationary environments. Third, a recall-biased ensemble management mechanism is introduced, combining a competence metric with recall emphasis and bounded specificity modulation with an oldest-worst pruning policy to suppress trivial classifiers while preserving discriminative ensemble members. Furthermore, a dual-threshold drift detection mechanism is integrated to adaptively distinguish between minor fluctuations and severe structural changes, triggering proportional model updates to effectively balance stability and plasticity. Evaluated on 10 synthetic and 5 real-world data streams, STR-DES achieves the lowest average rank (1.267) for both G-mean and Recall compared to nine baseline methods, ranking first across 12 and 11 streams, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wagemans J.
Author full names: Wagemans, Johan (7006148651)
Title: On the role of perception in the psychology of art: More than meets the eye of the beholder
Abstract: Perception is a cornerstone of aesthetic experience and the psychology of art, providing the primary means through which people engage with artworks and generate emotional and cognitive responses. Across theories of aesthetics, perception is the key process connecting the classic psychological triad of stimulus, person, and context, by integrating sensory information with situational influences. It encompasses factors ranging from low-level visual features, such as natural image statistics with broad appeal, to high-level influences related to familiarity with particular contents and artistic styles shaped by individual experience and sociocultural background. Crucially, mid-level perceptual processes are where perceptual, cognitive, emotional, and contextual factors interact most strongly, playing a central role in aesthetic appreciation and in explaining individual differences in artistic preferences. © 2026 The Author

Author full names: Kadıoğlu, Elif Nihan (58923609400); Atalay Eroğlu, Handan (57830207600); Akbal, Feryal (9239686500)
Title: Ion-specific capacity–rate–energy trade-offs in graphite-based capacitive deionization: Beyond gravimetric performance ranking
Abstract: This study systematically compares NaCl, NH4Cl, and CaCl2 on the same graphite-based electrode platform using a consistently defined operational endpoint and complementary gravimetric, molar, cation-equivalent, rate, and cell-electrical energy descriptors. The comparison addresses a key limitation of conventional capacitive deionization (CDI) benchmarking: although gravimetric salt adsorption capacity (SAC) is widely used as a performance metric, direct cross-electrolyte comparisons can be misleading when salts differ in molar mass and ionic valence. Moreover, SAC alone does not capture adsorption rate or electrical-energy demand, potentially altering the interpretation of electrolyte performance. At the reference condition of 0.10 N, 1.2 V, and 15 mL min−1, the 30-min mean SAC values were 64.87, 116.07, and 73.18 mg g−1 for NaCl, NH4Cl, and CaCl2, respectively. The corresponding operational endpoints occurred at 15, 10, and 30 min, yielding cation-equivalent uptake (qeq,op) values of 1.120, 2.170, and 1.319 meq g−1 and equivalent-normalized adsorption rates (ASAReq,op) of 0.075, 0.217, and 0.044 meq g−1 min−1, respectively. The corresponding cell-electrical specific energy consumption (SEC) values were 0.0212, 0.0153, and 0.0391 Wh L−1. Machine learning was retained as a secondary exploratory analysis, revealing strong observation-level interpolation but substantially weaker leave-one-condition-out transferability, thereby indicating limited generalization to unseen operating conditions. Overall, electrolyte performance depended on both the selected benchmarking metric and operating condition, demonstrating that gravimetric SAC alone is insufficient for robust cross-electrolyte evaluation. The coordinated assessment of adsorption capacity, equivalent-normalized uptake and rate, operational endpoint, and cell-electrical energy provides a more physically meaningful framework for CDI performance benchmarking across electrolytes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Psychometric properties and validity of the Family Accommodation Scale–Patient Version (FAS-PV) in adults with obsessive compulsive disorder: A French adaptation
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Background: Family accommodation (FA) is a common phenomenon in obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) and is associated with greater symptom severity, functional impairment, and poorer treatment outcomes. Assessing FA is therefore clinically relevant, yet no validated French-language instrument is currently available to assess accommodation from the patient’s perspective. Objective: The present study aimed to translate and validate a French version of the Family Accommodation Scale–Patient Version (FAS-PV) and to examine its psychometric properties in adults with OCD. Methods: Eighty-five adults diagnosed with OCD and 68 of their relatives were recruited in a specialized outpatient clinic. Patients completed the French FAS-PV alongside measures of OCD severity (Y-BOCS), relative-reported accommodation (FAS-SR), psychological distress, functional impairment, and family functioning. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted, and internal consistency, test–retest reliability, and convergent and divergent validity were examined. Results: The French FAS-PV demonstrated excellent internal consistency (McDonald’s ω = 0.89) and strong test–retest reliability (r = 0.89). Exploratory analyses supported a four-factor solution explaining 51.8 % of the variance, although item distribution partially diverged from the original theoretical structure. Confirmatory analyses provided partial support for the four-factor model, with adequate absolute fit but incremental indices slightly below conventional thresholds. Convergent validity was supported by significant associations with OCD severity, family accommodation, distress, and functional impairment, while divergent validity was confirmed by the absence of associations with impulsivity and age. Conclusions: The French FAS-PV demonstrates appreciable psychometric properties as an instrument for assessing family accommodation in adults with OCD and provides a useful tool for clinical practice and research in French-speaking contexts. © 2026 Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive. Authors: Fu L.; Shi Y.; Deng M.; Pan X.; You W.; Shi Y.; Zhang J.
Title: Crowd evacuation dynamics in a multi-exit room under the presence of simulated attackers: An experimental study
Abstract: In recent years, knife and axe violent attacks in crowded public places worldwide have occurred frequently. Such incidents easily trigger large-scale crowd physiological stress and stampede accidents, and have become one of the primary public safety risks threatening urban crowd. To reveal the physical-physiological coupling mechanism of crowd evacuation under knife attack scenarios, this study investigates evacuation dynamics in a multi-exit room under simulated attacker-induced threats through controlled experiments. Sixty-two participants completed 54 repeated runs across 27 experimental combinations, including 3 simulated attacker scenarios (0, 1, 2 simulated attackers) and 3 exit layout configurations (1, 2, 4 exits). High-precision trajectories were extracted using PeTrack software, and continuous physiological data were recorded by Apple Watch S7 devices. Results show that simulated attackers significantly exacerbate exit bottleneck deadlocks and the classic “faster-is-slower” effect with markedly prolonged peak time headway. They significantly increase crowd detour ratio by forcing evacuees to take longer alternative routes, reduce overall mean speed despite initial individual acceleration, elevate flow field turbulence intensity, and cause the fundamental speed-density relationship to deviate substantially from classical pedestrian flow laws. A distinct “physiological lag effect” is quantitatively verified, with peak heart rate consistently occurring after the completion of evacuation in most high-stress trials, and crowd danger increases stepwise with increasing attacker count. The findings of this study reveal the unique evacuation characteristics under dynamic threat conditions, providing critical scientific basis and empirical support for multi-exit architectural layout optimization, targeted emergency evacuation plan formulation, and proactive crowd safety management under violent attack scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ding S.; Pan X.; Zhou Z.; Deng H.; Tan J.; Sun L.
Title: A probabilistic model for situation awareness reliability assessment in uncertain environments
Abstract: Human error remains a major contributor to accidents in safety-critical systems, partly because operators may fail to establish effective situation awareness (SA) within critical time windows. Existing approaches to situation awareness reliability (SAR) often use SAGAT scores directly as reliability measures, conflating observed single-trial performance with the probability of successful SA formation under repeated conditions. They also lack a unified probabilistic framework integrating individual cognitive ability, task uncertainty, and available time. To address these limitations, this study applies the stress-strength interference principle from reliability engineering and models SA formation as a stochastic competition between cognitive strength and cognitive demand. A closed-form SAR expression with interpretable parameters is derived, forming the SAR-SSI model. The model was evaluated in a controlled experiment involving 29 participants and 1740 trials. Trial-level AUCs were 0.8032 for the full-sample fit and 0.8011 under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, indicating similar discrimination for held-out participants within the same experimental paradigm. Higher values of the task-related indicator C and longer available time were associated with higher SAR, whereas greater task uncertainty was associated with lower SAR and attenuated these relationships. The SAR-SSI model provides an interpretable probability-based tool for comparing how alternative information-presentation and task configurations may affect the likelihood of successful SA formation in controlled dynamic tasks. Authors: Shao Z.; Meng W.; Yang Y.; Li W.; Yao X.
Title: Cooperative operation of networked virtual power plants in low-carbon distribution systems
Abstract: Networked virtual power plants can create coordination gains while their emission and participation outcomes depend on the governing carbon and settlement rules. This study develops a DSO-coordinated mechanism that couples feeder-constrained two-stage stochastic dispatch, carbon-policy accounting, and coalition-stable settlement. The dispatch model coordinates renewable output, dispatchable generation, stationary storage, mobility-coupled electric vehicles, reserve, and scenario recourse. Risk is represented by six clustered empirical scenarios and one explicit tail scenario, with a 95% conditional value-at-risk term. The policy layer separates physical operational emissions, allocated allowances, carbon-valued accounting cost, and internal settlement. The settlement layer uses standard Shapley values to calibrate weighted-Nash gains and evaluates every coalition through core and least-core diagnostics. In a 168 h CAISO-eGRID case, cooperation under the same tiered carbon rule reduced total accounting cost from 52,566.65 to 50,349.19 USD and created 2217.47 USD of surplus. Physical emissions changed from 141.3554 to 144.5849 t CO2, an increase of 3.2294 t CO2 under the matched policy. Carbon prices produced a non-uniform physical response, whereas renewable expansion changed the feasible operating set directly. The integrated results identify the operating and governance conditions that support cost efficiency, carbon accountability, and stable participation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Li T.; Yu J.; Zhao J.; Xie Y.; Huang L.; Gao Q.
Title: Maximizing mutual information in multi-view representation learning for next POI prediction
Abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) prediction is a fundamental task in spatiotemporal data mining, aiming to facilitate personalized location-based services through modeling individual mobility trajectories. Despite recent advances in deep neural networks for capturing human mobility patterns from both short- and long-term trajectories, accurate POI prediction remains challenging due to the fragility of short-term intent representations and user preference drift. These challenges arise from intent inconsistency between stable long-term behavioral patterns and transient short-term contingencies, as well as the inherent stochasticity induced by sparse, noisy, and exploratory human mobility trajectories, ultimately causing biased or unstable future intention predictions. In this study, we propose MVMI, a Multi-View representation learning framework based on Mutual Information for next POI prediction. To improve the robustness of short-term intent representations, MVMI decomposes short-term trajectories into instantaneous and context-dependent intents and employs a Gaussian perturbation–based multi-view augmentation strategy to enhance the robustness of short-term intent representations against trajectory stochasticity. To address user preference drift, MVMI further introduces a mutual information (MI) constraint that aligns integrated user preferences with the ground-truth future intentions, where a dual-task learning paradigm is employed to enforce hierarchical spatial constraints at both the POI and region levels. Finally, experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that MVMI significantly outperforms representative baselines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Integrated simulation of forest dynamics and bioenergy utilization for GHG mitigation: A case study of Hyogo prefecture, Japan
Abstract: This study developed a dynamic simulation framework integrating forest growth, forest management, biomass supply, and energy utilization to jointly assess the supply potential and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of woody biomass energy, using Hyogo Prefecture, Japan, as a case study. Under conventional carbon-neutral accounting, GHG emissions from forest harvesting and forest residue utilization were 0.168 and 0.094 kg-CO2eq/kWh, respectively. When biogenic CO2 from combustion was included without subsequent forest uptake, these values increased to 2.660 and 2.586 kg-CO2eq/kWh. At the forest-system level, both woody biomass supply and the GHG balance were strongly influenced by forest age structure and harvesting regime. Under the baseline S3-a scenario, annual woody biomass harvest declined from approximately 84,000 BDT/yr in 2020 to 14,000 BDT/yr by 2050 and remained relatively stable thereafter, while cumulative net GHG emissions reached −60.492 million t-CO2eq by 2100. Increasing final felling enhanced woody biomass supply but weakened the long-term GHG balance. Among the scenarios examined, 10 km2/yr represented the highest final-felling level and approached the long-term forest-stock constraint, whereas 5 km2/yr maintained a substantially more favorable cumulative GHG balance than 10 km2/yr. These results demonstrate that maintaining forest growing stock and achieving a favorable GHG balance represent distinct management criteria, highlighting the importance of dynamically considering forest age structure, harvesting, regeneration, and subsequent growth when evaluating woody biomass energy utilization. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Feng Z.; Niu Y.; Zou H.
Title: Measurement scale for push and pull factors of Chinese pedestrian streets
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The concepts of push and pull theory have been proposed and extensively discussed in various studies, particularly in tourism research. However, push and pull theory in the field of pedestrian street is not addressed in the existing research. This study takes the perspective of pedestrian-street consumers, follows a systematic scale-development procedure, and uses samples from eight Chinese cities to develop and test a scale measuring perceived push and pull factors. The scale is composed of 11 dimensions for each of the push and pull domains. This study then examines the nomological validity by testing the associations between push and pull factors and revisit intention and recommendation intention. The results of the study support the nomological validity of the proposed relationships. This study does not propose push and pull as new constructs. Instead, it organizes and validates their context-specific manifestations within Chinese pedestrian streets and provides a culturally grounded measurement instrument for subsequent retail and consumer research. The evidence supports its initial applicability across the Chinese cities examined, while its cross-national applicability remains to be established. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Fu S.; Liu Z.; Niu Z.
Title: Product visual form and customer satisfaction: Multimodal evidence on affective value and functional diagnosis
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Product visual form conveys important aesthetic, quality, and use-related cues for functionally complex products. However, multimodal evidence from real-world retail settings remains limited regarding how product visual form relates to consumer evaluations in online reviews and satisfaction. Using data from 200 smart standing desks, 41951 valid reviews, and 200 product images, this study combined engineering-attribute encoding, CLIP image embeddings, and CLIP-text concept scores to construct a multilayer representation of product visual form. A large language model was used to extract affective and functional evaluations from the reviews, and the platform favorable rate served as a product-level proxy for satisfaction. Product-level path analysis showed that PC3 (Non-standard premium form) was positively associated with affective evaluation, and affective evaluation was positively associated with satisfaction. Together, these coefficients yielded a significant positive indirect association (indirect association = 0.075, 95% BCa CI [0.021, 0.156], FDR-Adj. p = 0.014). Functional evaluation, by contrast, was negatively associated with satisfaction (β = −0.254, p < 0.01). Further decomposition showed that this negative association was more closely related to functional-mention coverage than to overall polarity of functional evaluations. Noise control and Workspace size adequacy were the principal negative sources. These findings indicate that affective and functional evaluations relate to satisfaction in distinct ways. For online retailers and e-commerce platforms, combining analysis of product visual form with online-review monitoring can help identify design value, detect quality risks, and prioritize service recovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Experimental and simulation studies on plasma gasification of medical waste for the co-production of ammonia and urea
Abstract: This study explores the novel integration of plasma gasification and urea synthesis using medical waste as a feedstock, a research area largely unexplored compared to conventional plasma gasification applications. This investigation is designed to evaluate the technical and economic viability of producing hydrogen-rich syngas followed by the synthesis of ammonia and urea via advanced process simulation and experimental validation. Medical waste gasification occurs under a CO2 environment to increase syngas quality when using medical waste such as syringes, gloves, surgical masks, and drip sets. Although, the maximum value of lower heating value (LHV) (12.4  MJ/m3) was achieved by utilizing plasma at 1.25  kW, the highest energy efficiency of 53.8 % was obtained at 1.00 kW due to lower energy input. Residue content decreased from 19 wt% (0.75  kW), 14 wt% (1.0  kW), and 11 wt% (1.25  kW). A sensitivity analysis of the simulation indicates that increasing feed rates and plasma power improve syngas quality: CO reaches a maximum of 69 vol% and H2 rises to 31.1 vol%. Ammonia and urea units show N2 and CO2 conversion efficiencies of 87.6 % and 81.56 %, respectively, with maximum urea production of 2853  kg/h. Techno-economic analysis shows that a CAPEX of $32.9 million and OPEX of $4.49 million/year result in a competitive urea cost of $0.49/kg and annual revenue of $6.7 million. The cost analysis showed that a strong positive cash flow and net earnings in a period of 10 years confirm the long-term economic viability and sustainability of this waste utilization for fertilizer production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: RoC-GRL: A right-of-way communication graph reinforcement learning multi-agent decision-making method for mixed-traffic unsignalized intersection
Abstract: Safe cooperative control of connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) at unsignalized intersections in mixed traffic is an important foundation for advancing intelligent transportation toward collective intelligence. To address heterogeneous vehicle-interaction modeling and safe continuous-action exploration, we propose RoC-GRL, a graph reinforcement learning decision-making method integrating right-of-way constraints and communication topology. First, potential path conflicts, passing priorities, CAV perception information, and V2V communication topology are explicitly structured to construct a local right-of-way yielding graph and a global CAV communication graph. These graphs represent asymmetric yielding relationships among mixed-traffic participants and communication-based cooperation among CAVs, respectively. Second, a sequential graph representation learning architecture is designed. Multi-head attention extracts right-of-way-sensitive local interaction features, while communication-graph message passing aggregates global cooperative information, producing a high-level state representation for centralized multi-vehicle decision-making. Based on this representation, TD3 generates a centralized cooperative policy for multiple agents. To address high-risk exploration under potential conflicts, a behavioral exploration optimization mechanism jointly considering time-to-collision and yielding priority dynamically adjusts the action boundary of each CAV. The resulting behavioral-boundary deviation is incorporated into the policy loss, allowing execution-level safety constraints to influence policy learning. Risk-prioritized experience replay and a structured reward function considering safety, efficiency, and cooperation further enhance the learning of safety-critical experiences. Comprehensive experiments in a CARLA mixed-traffic environment demonstrate that RoC-GRL achieves stable training convergence and outperforms the baseline methods in traffic efficiency and safe cooperative decision-making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Bayat M.; Kharel S.; Li J.; Pan Q.; Mattingly S.; Shahandashti M.
Title: Leveraging Digital Twins for Bridge Maintenance Prioritization following Coastal Flood Events
Source title: Journal of Structural Design and Construction Practice
Abstract: Bridges are critical to the US transportation network and are essential components of our infrastructure systems. Coastal floods can disrupt these structures, isolating communities and highlighting the urgent need for effective maintenance and prioritization strategies. This study introduces a digital twin framework that evaluates the impacts of coastal floods on bridge substructures by integrating multisource data and employing spatial algorithms like inverse distance weighting and k-d tree methods to model flood severity. Using a generative adversarial network (GAN) with focal loss, the framework simulates preflood and postflood scenarios, generating synthetic data sets that reflect realistic damage patterns and evolving maintenance priorities. The GAN-enhanced model improved F1 scores (the harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a balance between the two metrics), particularly for Condition 4 (bridges with advanced section loss, deterioration, spalling, or scour), where the score increased from 0.63 to 0.87 preflood and from 0.63 to 0.88 postflood, effectively addressing class imbalances. It also enhanced macro and weighted average F1 scores, demonstrating robust predictive capabilities. Confusion matrices showed increased identification of bridges in Conditions 4 and 5, consistent with the model's emphasis on vulnerable infrastructure. The study's findings reveal shifts in maintenance priorities when flood severity is incorporated, emphasizing bridges with higher susceptibility to combined flooding and socioeconomic impacts. While the framework primarily focused on physical infrastructure impacts, it also highlighted potential disparities in resource allocation, suggesting the need for further research into equitable distribution strategies. The digital twin provides actionable insights for local and federal agencies, offering a valuable tool for managing and prioritizing infrastructure maintenance in response to extreme weather events while laying the groundwork for more inclusive resource planning.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Ren Y.; Cai X.; Li S.; Huo Y.; Yang M.; Wang M.; Hao C.
Title: Structure-dependent transport in ordered packed beds: pore-scale CFD analysis and Nusselt-number correlations
Abstract: Ordered packed beds can enhance particle-to-fluid heat transfer while reducing hydraulic resistance, but their thermo-hydraulic behavior depends on both porosity and packing architecture. This study investigates flow reorganization, pressure gradient, and convective heat transfer in cubic, orthorhombic, and rhombohedral ordered packed beds using pore-scale CFD. A particle-layer stacking model is introduced to quantify transverse packing and axial overlap, and 27 configurations with different normalized inter-particle spacings are analyzed. Results show that packing structure governs pore connectivity and flow pathways, producing distinct thermo-hydraulic responses among bed families. In cubic beds, decreasing transverse packing weakens particle-induced flow disturbance, reducing heat-transfer coefficients by up to 51.37 % while the pressure gradient decreases substantially (maximum 362.14 %). Orthorhombic beds exhibit weak thermal sensitivity, with heat-transfer variations of 0.42–6.75 % due to compensating flow accessibility. Rhombohedral beds show the strongest structure-induced transitions: connected axial passages cause abrupt flow redistribution, heat-transfer variations of 0.84–64.81 %, and pressure-gradient variations up to 48-fold. Although local heat transfer may decrease, the larger reduction in hydraulic resistance improves overall performance, with rhombohedral beds achieving the most favorable heat-transfer-to-pressure-drop trade-off. Structure-dependent Nusselt-number correlations are developed, incorporating packing-architecture effects, with maximum deviations of 14.49 %, 3.26 %, and 9.92 % for cubic, orthorhombic, and rhombohedral beds. These results highlight the limitations of porosity-based characterization and provide a structure-aware framework for predicting and optimizing ordered packed-bed performance in chemical and thermal processes. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A dispatch-aware framework for resource-efficient distributed electrification: A case study of photovoltaic-battery streetlights
Abstract: The rapid deployment of distributed electrification infrastructure requires assessment approaches that jointly consider operational carbon benefits, life-cycle environmental burdens, and public investment. Using photovoltaic (PV)-battery streetlights as a representative municipal application, this study develops a dispatch-aware framework integrating time-resolved PV-battery dispatch, regional load-side carbon accounting, life-cycle assessment, and public-cost evaluation. Using the observed 2024 operating year as a repeated benchmark over a nominal 20-year service life, the representative retrofit achieves an attributional operational emission reduction of 4.58 tCO₂e and retains 3.56 tCO₂e of net life-cycle abatement per streetlight. Within the modeled study set of 22 municipalities, operational emission reduction is more strongly associated with regional grid‑carbon intensity than with annual mean solar resource, with the contrast amplified by the outlying-island regions. Simplified national-average assumptions shift municipal rankings by up to 20 positions. Static 2030 and 2050 grid‑carbon stress tests retain reference dispatch and hardware over the same horizon, without forecasting grid evolution or future equipment life cycles. The results demonstrate that the environmental value of this PV–battery streetlight retrofit depends on both technology performance and the carbon intensity assigned to reduced grid purchases. The framework supports municipal screening under a common observed-year benchmark. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: A sight for restored minds: examining the impact of nature image exposure on perceived restorativeness and healthy food choices
Abstract: Nature exposure (including through images) offers physical and psychological benefits, including cognitive restoration. Growing evidence suggests it may also promote healthy food choices, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This pre-registered study examined whether perceived restorativeness (the perceived capacity of an environment for cognitive restoration) mediates the effect of nature image exposure on healthy food choices. Fruit and vegetable (FV) desirability was also examined as an alternative outcome. A total of 925 adults (M age = 39.46 y, SD = 15.67, 54.3% female) participated in an online between-subjects experiment and were exposed to a natural or urban image for 30 s. They then completed a food choice task – selecting a main course, side dish and drink (each from four options; two healthy, two unhealthy), followed by perceived restorativeness and FV desirability measures. There was a significant main effect of healthiness on the likelihood of choice (OR = 1.77, p < .001) and a significant healthiness × image exposure interaction (OR = 1.40, p < .001), indicating that healthy food choices were more likely following nature (vs. urban) image exposure. Additionally, nature (vs. urban) image exposure had a significant indirect effect on healthy food choices through perceived restorativeness (ACME = 0.04, p = .022). However, nature (vs. urban) image exposure did not significantly affect FV desirability (p = .087, d = 0.11). These findings suggest that nature image exposure can promote healthy food choices (though not FV desirability), an effect explained by enhanced perceived restorativeness. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Do digital platforms delocalise consumer activity? Platform services, retail agglomeration and the localisation of neighbourhood dining and shopping
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The platform economy is reshaping the relationship between digital service availability and physical retail activity. Yet how platform-service environments and physical retail provision are jointly associated with the localisation of dining and shopping visits, and whether these relationships vary across socioeconomic contexts, remains poorly understood. Using location-based service data from 6213 residential communities and more than 50 million dining and shopping records in Shenzhen, China, we measure local patronage as the share of each community's dining and shopping visits made to retailers within its proximate walking catchment. We combine income-stratified estimation using a heteroskedasticity-robust generalised method of moments spatial-error model (GMM-SEM) with gradient-boosted machine learning and SHAP interaction analysis to examine average, non-linear and interaction associations. Three findings emerge. First, greater food-delivery and instant-retail availability is consistently associated with lower physical-visit localisation, with the negative association for food delivery generally stronger in lower-income communities. Second, retail attractiveness and format show marked socioeconomic heterogeneity: restaurant ratings are more strongly positively associated with dining localisation in higher-income communities, whereas traditional markets are positively associated with shopping localisation across all income groups but most strongly in lower-income communities. Third, SHAP interaction analyses show that this negative platform–localisation association is conditional on physical retail provision: positive interaction contributions between platform-service availability and retail agglomeration emerge where restaurant and shopping-mall densities are high, consistent with a buffering role of dense local retail clusters. These findings show that relationships between platform-service environments and physical-visit localisation are conditional on retail agglomeration and neighbourhood socioeconomic context, with implications for retail location strategy, commercial real estate and neighbourhood retail planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Decentralized anaerobic digestion in emerging Indian cities: A systems perspective on urban waste management, bioenergy recovery, and circular economy transitions
Abstract: Rapid urbanization in emerging Indian urban cities is increasing the pressure on municipal solid waste management. This review evaluates anaerobic digestion as an integrated option for urban organic waste management, renewable energy recovery, and circular economy development. A structured narrative review was used to assess feedstock characteristics, digester configurations, operating conditions, and biogas uses. Policy support and reforms are discussed, followed by techno-economic evaluation of decentralized anaerobic digestion, along with opportunities to diversify income through bio-CNG, electricity, and bio-fertilizer production. Life cycle studies indicate a potential to reduce greenhouse gas through methane capture, fossil fuel substitution, and comparison with conventional methods. The reviewed evidence indicates that decentralized anaerobic digestion is most suitable if the waste is source-separated, moisture-rich, and available within a short distance. These work best if the local demand for energy and digestate exists. The economic performance of this technology depends substantially on digester scale, capacity utilization, feedstock availability, capital and operating and maintenance costs, etc. Direct thermal use may require lower treatment and conversion. At the same time, electricity generation and biomethane upgrading provide higher-value energy products, but the latter involves greater capital cost, operational complexity, and energy demand. Environmental benefits are higher when methane leakage is controlled, energy recovered replaces conventional energy resources, and digestate is used safely as a nutrient source. From a circular economy perspective, decentralized anaerobic digestion can reduce the disposal of biodegradable waste, promote energy and resource recovery, and support localized waste-to-resource systems. However, poor waste segregation, inconsistent feeding, limited capacity utilization, poor maintenance, and inadequate digestate management remain major barriers. This review article concludes that decentralized anaerobic digestion can support sustainable urban waste management in India only if technology selection, feedstock management, energy utilization, financing, policy support, and community participation are integrated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Threats to food security in rice farming: A scientific mapping of climate change impacts
Abstract: Climate change is severely disrupting many aspects of human life worldwide, particularly rice farming, as it feeds many people worldwide. In the absence of stable rice production, food security will is threatened for the global population. This paper examines how climate change is related to rice farming and what it means for overall food security. I used bibliometric analysis to examine the literature on this topic from 1998 to 2024, a 26-year period. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database using specific keywords, yielding 549 matching documents. Using VOSviewer helped visualize connections and identify trends in the research. Researchers have consistently focused on climate change, rice farming, and food security over time, but have not yet mapped the interrelationships between these variables. The findings suggest a reciprocal relationship. Agriculture produces greenhouse gases that exacerbate climate change, but climate change subsequently reverses itself and harms agricultural productivity. It is particularly difficult for rice to respond to changing temperatures, unusual rainfall patterns, and recurring extreme weather events. As a result, when crop yields decline, the availability of rice as a staple food decreases, directly impacting food security. These findings directly relate to Sustainable Development Goal 2, which aims to end hunger, making it urgent to find better ways to adapt agriculture to climate change and make it more sustainable. This necessary adaptation in rice farming aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 13, Climate Action. Therefore, this Action requires support from the government and the agricultural sector workforce to achieve food security and sustainable rice farming. © 2027, Malque Publishing.
