Title: Distributionally-robust heterogeneous graph neural networks via relation-aware grouping
Abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a key challenge for heterogeneous graph neural networks (HGNNs), which often exhibit substantial performance degradation under real-world distribution shifts. While Group Distributionally Robust Optimization (GroupDRO) has proven effective in promoting OOD generalization in various domains, its application to heterogeneous graphs remains largely unexplored. This gap stems from a fundamental obstacle: the complex, multi-relational nature of heterogeneous graphs renders conventional group definitions, which rely on explicit node attributes, inadequate. To bridge this gap, we propose DroHGNN, a GroupDRO-based framework for OOD generalization on heterogeneous graphs. DroHGNN introduces a relation-aware soft grouping mechanism coupled with a two-stage optimization procedure to enhance OOD robustness. Specifically, DroHGNN learns soft group assignments through learnable prototypes over relation-specific node representations. These assignments serve as optimization-oriented group proxies for GroupDRO, which minimizes worst-case group risk. To encourage structural coherence of the inferred assignments, we further introduce a heterogeneous graph structural consistency constraint that regularizes the group assignments of structurally connected target nodes. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world benchmarks show that DroHGNN consistently achieves strong OOD performance compared with competitive baselines. Notably, under degree-distribution shifts on the ArXiv dataset, DroHGNN outperforms NaiveDRO and the leading baseline CaNet by 23.3% and 6.5% in Macro-F1, respectively. Moreover, relative gains of up to 3.2% in average Macro-F1 under the inductive temporal setting further demonstrate its effectiveness under heterogeneous distribution shifts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Modeling Japanese consumers' acceptance and rejection of tech-enhanced foods
Abstract: To maintain the well-being of the global population, strengthening the food supply system is necessary. A promising solution is the development of new food manufacturing technologies related to the production, processing, and preservation of food. Foods produced with such technologies are referred to as tech-enhanced foods. While the promotion of tech-enhanced foods is important, they have yet to be widely used in Japan. An understanding of consumers' psychological reactions and related factors is considered useful when designing and promoting tech-enhanced foods. Thus, this research aimed to construct a model explaining the psychological factors pertaining to consumers' acceptance and rejection of four types of tech-enhanced foods: genetically modified (GM) foods, meat alternatives, cultured meats, and edible insects. The proposed psychological model was based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) framework and supplemented with elements from the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The analysis revealed that positive and negative affects emerge as the most significant factors associated with intake intention and rejection, respectively. Moreover, the potential damage and benefits of tech-enhanced foods, along with reliability of regulation, were found to be associated with emotional responses, rejection, and intake intention. These findings may provide useful insights for designing interventions aimed at promoting the acceptance of tech-enhanced foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhou J.; Guo X.; Zhang J.
Title: A novel lattice hydrodynamic model for bidirectional pedestrian flow considering the pedestrians’ anticipation effect of density difference
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: Pedestrians’ anticipation effect, which is a conscious or unconscious response to the surrounding environment, plays an important role in pedestrian flow, especially under high-density condition. In order to investigate the pedestrians’ anticipation effect of density difference, an extended lattice hydrodynamic model for bidirectional pedestrian flow is proposed in this paper. The stability condition of the proposed model is deduced using linear stability analysis and the analytical result reveals that the anticipation effect of density difference can significantly enlarge the stability region on the phase diagram. By the use of nonlinear analysis method, the time-dependent Ginzburg Landau (TDGL) equation is derived to describe the evolution of pedestrian flow near the critical point. The modified Korteweg-de Vries (MKdV) equation is also derived to characterize the kink-antikink waves in unstable region. The theoretical results indicate that jams can be effectively mitigated by considering the anticipation effect of density difference. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the accuracy of the theoretical findings. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: Activating competing goals: The dual effect of environmental fee
Abstract: While economic intervention is increasingly used to support environmental protection, its effectiveness in tourism contexts remains unclear. By introducing symbolic interactionism, this research examined how environmental fee cues influence tourists’ environmentally responsible behavior across different attraction types and quality levels. We conducted a field observation study (N = 500), two field surveys using questionnaires (total N = 765), and one online experiment (N = 293). Results showed that environmental fee cues increased environmentally responsible behavior in resource-based attractions by activating moral norm goals, but decreased environmentally responsible behavior in market-based attractions via thrift goal activation. Moreover, this study further refined the environmental fee strategy and examined its effectiveness and mechanism across all attraction quality levels. The findings provide novel theoretical insights and practical implications for designing adaptive environmental fee strategies. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Barriers and enablers to circular economy implementation in 3D concrete printing: A fuzzy decision-making approach
Abstract: The circular economy (CE) is increasingly emphasised in 3D concrete printing (3DCP), yet evidence remains limited on the key barriers to its implementation and the enablers needed to support practical uptake. This study addresses that gap through a sequential mixed-methods design combining a literature-informed review to identify initial barriers, ten semi-structured expert interviews to refine them and elicit corresponding enablers in the 3DCP context, and a questionnaire survey of 58 academic and industry specialists from multiple regions to prioritise their relative importance using a fuzzy synthetic evaluation approach. The findings show that CE implementation in 3DCP is constrained less by isolated technical limitations than by wider system conditions shaping approval, investment, knowledge translation, and supply-chain coordination. Regulatory and standardisation issues emerged as the most critical barrier theme, followed by financial and market constraints, while the gap between low-TRL academic research and high-TRL industrial implementation was identified as the most prominent item-level barrier. The most influential enablers were CE-oriented standards, cost-effective process maturation, targeted R&D support, and stronger validation and implementation pathways. By revealing convergence between academia and industry on the main priorities, the study contributes a context-specific methodological approach for investigating CE implementation in 3DCP and establishes a prioritised evidence base on the barriers and enablers shaping circular 3DCP. It also provides practical guidance for researchers, industry stakeholders, and policy actors by identifying where intervention is likely to be most effective, particularly in standards development, technology validation, investment support, and supply-chain coordination, to scale circular 3DCP in support of net-zero and zero-waste ambitions. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Su Y.; Li M.; Qu T.; Huang G.Q.
Title: Temporal-digital twin-network enabled Out-of-Order synchronized control for production-intralogistics considering disturbance propagation
Abstract: Dualistic production and intralogistics (DPiL) have inherently intricate spatio-temporal coupling relationships. Meanwhile, the occurrence of disturbance propagation further amplifies such complexity, aggravating operation control difficulty. This novel problem is summarized as the dualistic production and intralogistics synchronized control problem (DPiLSynC) considering disturbance propagation. Traditional production planning and control (PPC) methods overlook the impact of disturbance propagation, significantly compromising system stability. Fortunately, digital twin (DT) technology promises rapid identification of disturbances by physical-virtual interaction. The adverse effects of disturbances may diffuse across the manufacturing system, causing operational disruptions. But analyzing the spatio-temporal characteristics of disturbance propagation is challenging due to the unclear connection-interaction mechanism of multiple DT models in manufacturing systems. This paper proposes a temporal-digital twin-network (T-DT-N) enabled Out-of-Order (OoO) synchronized control approach. Firstly, the modified OoO framework with disturbance propagation analysis is designed to reconstruct the operation logic of DPiL. Secondly, T-DT-N is developed to reveal the spatio-temporal evolution patterns of disturbance propagation by introducing the temporal network to model connection-interaction relationships of DT models. Thirdly, OoO synchronized control using propagation analysis results is proposed, involving three distinct control phases, each considering multiple factors aiming to achieve resilient DPiL operation. Computation results indicate this approach achieves shorter order makespan, shopfloor throughput time, and waiting time, while decreasing the percentage tardy. Furthermore, it exhibits stability across varying queue lengths and uncertain levels, thereby validating its application in a dynamic environment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wu Z.; Zhang D.; Li Y.
Title: Respect your privacy: An identifiable and authorized privacy-preserving data retrieval protocol through decentralized identifier
Abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires personal data processing to satisfy both the principles of lawfulness and data minimization. However, existing privacy-preserving data retrieval protocols rarely meet both principles, especially at the batch scale. To solve these problems, we present IAPDR, an Identifiable and Authorized Privacy-Preserving Data Retrieval protocol that builds on Decentralised Identifier (DID) that focuses on data-subject privacy under GDPR compliance. IAPDR uses DIDs to provide verifiable, globally unique identities while preserving anonymity and self-sovereign management. It uses non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZKs) for anonymous authorization. The data controller can verify the lawfulness of each retrieval request without learning any personally identifiable data, thereby upholding data minimization. For scalable retrieval, IAPDR employs Private Set Intersection with Payload (PSI-Payload) to execute large-batch matching while keeping both identifiers and associated records confidential. We prove anonymity and unforgeability, and give a Universal Composability (UC) security analysis in the semi-honest model. Under the same dataset sizes and network settings on public benchmarks, IAPDR achieves an average 1.36 × improvement in computational efficiency and an average 3.62 × reduction in total communication compared with state-of-the-art schemes. These enhancements make GDPR compliant privacy-preserving data retrieval practically feasible. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Topology design of a 3D-printed reactor for CO elimination based on multi-objective optimization and its experimental evaluation
Abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) can accumulate rapidly in confined spaces during fires, fuel leaks, internal-combustion-engine emissions, and post-blasting operations, creating severe exposure risks. For independent CO purification devices, the reactor flow-channel structure directly affects CO transport, gas-catalyst contact, and flow resistance. This study develops a variable-density-based multi-objective topology optimization method for the internal flow-channel design of a CO elimination reactor. The CRITIC method is used to determine the weights of the domain-averaged reaction-rate objective and total power-dissipation objective, avoiding subjective weighting. Topology evolution and performance trade-offs are analyzed under different inlet flow conditions, and the selected topology-optimized structure is converted into a 3D-printed reactor prototype. Hopcalite is coated on the inner channel walls for experimental evaluation. Compared with a conventional parallel-channel reactor, Structure 2 increases the CO elimination efficiency by 54.1%, while the pressure drop increases by only 14.0%, resulting in a PECexp value of 1.35. The results demonstrate that topology optimization can improve CO elimination while controlling the flow-energy penalty, and that 3D printing provides a feasible route for fabricating complex optimized reactor channels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Automotive warranty intelligence through evidence-grounded graph retrieval and agentic reasoning
Abstract: Automotive warranty records contain detailed evidence on field failures, repeated repairs, and repair actions, but heterogeneous fields and fragmented vehicle–part–fault relations make reliability-oriented synthesis difficult. We introduce a confidential industrial protocol for automotive warranty intelligence and evaluate an evidence-grounded framework over 16,948 anonymized after-sales records. The full system achieved the highest blind-judge integrated quality score (4.224/5 versus 3.272 for the Flat Hybrid-RAG baseline) and reduced the hard-error rate from 48.7% to 22.0%. In a stratified double-rated expert review of 45 items, it also achieved the highest weighted score (4.237), exceeding the strongest competing configuration by 0.199 points (95% confidence interval, 0.115–0.281; Holm-adjusted p=0.0131). Within this controlled protocol using a test-reference-enriched GraphRAG index, the integrated configuration produced the strongest observed traceable warranty responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Thermal-hydraulic performance and multi-objective optimization of a V-shaped bifurcated honeycomb-fin cooling plate for large-format lithium-ion batteries
Abstract: Localized heat accumulation, non-uniform temperature distribution, and the trade-off between thermal performance and hydraulic penalty remain major challenges in large-capacity lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery modules. This study proposes a liquid cooling plate integrating dendritic hierarchical flow channels with honeycomb-inspired hexagonal fins for an eight-cell 280 Ah prismatic LiFePO4 module. A three-dimensional transient fluid–solid conjugate heat transfer model was established and experimentally validated, with maximum relative deviations below 3% for temperature and 4.79% for pressure drop. Comparative analyses identified the hexagonal-fin structure with the SIDO arrangement as the preferred configuration, followed by investigation of the nonlinear effects of porosity, fin arrangement, fin spacing, and Reynolds number on maximum temperature, maximum temperature difference, and pressure drop. A Kriging surrogate model based on 60 LHS–CFD samples was validated using five-fold cross-validation and 12 independent CFD points. Multiple NSGA-II runs and TOPSIS weight sensitivity analysis were then employed to identify the Pareto compromise region, followed by high-fidelity CFD screening. The recommended design (φ = 0.405, S = 5.48 mm, Re = 308) achieved Tmax = 34.336 °C, ΔTmax = 4.671 °C, and ΔP = 255.22 Pa. Compared with the baseline, Tmax and ΔTmax decreased by 0.699 °C and 0.441 °C, respectively, while ΔP increased from 143.29 to 255.22 Pa. Off-design simulations confirmed a stable thermal advantage across the investigated operating conditions. The results reveal a synergistic interaction between macroscopic flow redistribution and periodic regeneration of local thermal boundary layers, providing guidance for thermal–hydraulic trade-off design of large-capacity LiFePO4 liquid cooling systems. Title: Boundedness and large time behavior in a parabolic-parabolic-elliptic forager-exploiter model with competitive kinetics
Abstract: The parabolic-parabolic-elliptic forager-exploiter model with kinetic terms is investigated in a smoothly bounded domain of the n dimensional space. Title: Is state fragility a hindrance to trade openness in Africa?
Abstract: This paper analyses the effects of state fragility on trade openness in Africa, using panel data for 50 African countries over the period 1995–2018. We use the recent de facto trade openness indicators developed by Squalli and Wilson (2011) because it reflects the actual degree of trade and the Fraser Institute’s de jure Trade Freedom index. Estimates obtained using the feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) and the system generalized method of moments (system GMM) show that the inability of African states to provide basic public services and ensure high-quality institutions has a negative effect on these countries’ trade openness. However, the magnitude of the estimated effects varies considerably according to the different measures of trade openness used. Furthermore, the quantile regression approach shows that the effect of state fragility and its dimensions varies across the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th quintile. The results are also robust when distinguishing other measures of state fragility and trade openness. Based on these results, it would be worthwhile for African countries to strengthen state capacity and the quality of their institutions in order to ensure an effective and sustainable improvement in trade transactions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Advancing smart school initiatives: A case study of Zahedan city
Abstract: This mixed-methods case study evaluates Iran's Smart Schools Project in Zahedan, a socioeconomically heterogeneous city, to identify barriers and scalable interventions for technology-enhanced schooling in resource-constrained contexts. Data comprise structured surveys (n = 150), semi-structured interviews with policymakers (n = 10), and classroom observations across urban, semi-urban and rural schools. Findings reveal stark infrastructure and access gaps (rural device-sharing 1:175; chronic power outages; intermittent urban connectivity). Targeted, low-cost interventions (solar microgrids, offline learning-management systems, and Raspberry Pi deployments) produced measurable gains (rural literacy +25%; STEM engagement +18%). Cultural resistance was substantially reduced through engagement with religious leaders, raising parental approval from 20% to 65%. Analysis is situated within TPACK (Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge) and SAMR (Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition) frameworks. Policy implications include tiered funding that prioritizes rural allocation (proposed 60% share), promotion of domestic low-cost device manufacturing, and decentralized, context-sensitive teacher training. The study demonstrates that equity-driven, culturally attuned strategies can align national smart-school ambitions with local realities, offering a replicable model for other resource-limited regions seeking to close the urban–rural digital divide. © 2026 The Author.

Title: Achieving emotionally and factually grounded interactive comments through a large language model-driven adaptive dialogue engine
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce, online product comments have become a major reference point for consumers in making purchase decisions. However, current comment systems are challenged by uneven comment quality, limited accuracy in sentiment expression, and a lack of verification for factual information, which together reduce the usefulness and credibility of the comments. Grounded in dual process theory and adaptive control theory, this study proposes a large language model-driven adaptive dialogue engine framework that enables intelligent generation of interactive comments through an emotion-fact dual-anchoring mechanism. The framework dynamically adjusts its interaction strategy according to the dialogue state and user feedback, while preserving authentic emotional expression and ensuring the reliability of objective information. The findings show that interactive comments generated by large language models perform well in terms of content authenticity, emotional consistency, user satisfaction, and readability. This study offers an innovative solution to key limitations in e-commerce comment systems and is of significant importance for improving comment quality and user engagement on digital commerce platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Do platform and seller cues improve price prediction? A study on online food delivery platforms using machine learning
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study investigates value-based pricing on online food delivery platforms by examining the role of beyond-core service attributes—platform brand and Observed Restaurant Activity Duration—as observable platform- and restaurant-level cues. Drawing on signaling theory as a conceptual lens, we adopt a theory-guided predictive modeling approach to assess whether these cue-related variables improve the prediction of the final price paid per order under varying levels of order urgency. Using a dataset of 1536 cross-platform transactions in Vietnam and applying a broader model-benchmarking strategy, including Random Forest, linear regression, XGBoost, and other machine-learning models, we show that nonlinear machine-learning models provide stronger out-of-sample predictive accuracy than traditional linear estimation. XGBoost achieves the strongest overall predictive performance and is therefore used as the primary model for permutation feature-importance and hypothesis analyses, while Random Forest serves as a robustness benchmark. Both platform brand and restaurant activity duration emerge as meaningful predictive contributors beyond core service attributes. Importantly, platform brand shows a substantial increase in predictive importance under high-urgency conditions, whereas restaurant activity duration remains comparatively stable across urgency levels. Title: Beyond taste: how production-system information influences consumer liking of poultry meat from novel organic alternative production system
Abstract: Alternative food production systems may be unfamiliar to consumers, making communication of production-related credence attributes important for product understanding and evaluation. This study examined whether information about a novel dual-purpose poultry production system influenced consumer liking and preference when the chicken meat remained identical. In a within-subject repeated-measures design, consumers (n = 657) evaluated two identical chicken meat samples presented with either information about the production system or basic origin information only. Providing production-system information increased overall liking, taste liking, and texture liking, though samples were in fact identical. Preference responses showed that 50% preferred the sample with information, 24% preferred the sample without information, and 26% reported no preference. Across the whole sample, characteristics of the novel production system were generally rated as important, with minimal waste and outdoor access, specifically, receiving the highest importance ratings, while growth rate and price were rated lowest importance. In contrast, when participants selected broader grocery shopping values independent of the specific production system, price was most frequently prioritised, followed by animal welfare and taste. When stratified by preference, participants preferring the sample with information assigned greater importance to the novel production system characteristics compared with those reporting no preference, whereas general shopping values did not differ between groups. Overall, the findings indicate that information about food production systems can influence consumer evaluation of a food product even when sensory input is held constant, highlighting the potential role of communicating relevant credence attributes in supporting consumer acceptance of alternative food production systems. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Global research mapping of waste oil pyrolysis: Bibliometric analysis of technological trends, environmental impact, and SDG contributions (2015-2025)
Abstract: Global waste oil production from the automotive, industrial, and manufacturing sectors creates significant environmental challenges due to its persistent, toxic, and difficult-to-decompose characteristics. This study aims to analyze research trends, collaboration patterns, and global mapping on waste oil pyrolysis to identify technological trends, environmental impacts, and SDG contributions through a bibliometric approach. Bibliometric analysis was conducted on 167 Scopus-indexed publications from 2015 to 2025 using VOSviewer. Data were systematically processed to identify publication trends, author productivity, institutional networks, geographic patterns, subject area distribution, and funding patterns. The results of this study show a significant transformation from a niche topic to a mainstream topic in the global energy transition, marked by a 480% increase in publications (from 5 publications in 2015 to 29 publications in 2025) driven by postpandemic circular economy awareness, SDG commitments, and technological developments. Bibliometric analysis of 164 documents from 687 authors at 312 institutions from 45 countries reveals the structure of global collaboration. The temporal evolution shows progress from an initial exploration phase (2015-2017) focused on the feasibility of the basic process, to a consolidation phase (2018-2020) with systematic scale-up through catalytic pyrolysis, followed by an innovation phase (2021-2023) with the advent of hierarchical catalysts and the integration of machine learning, to a global phase (2024-2025) showing integration with the broader sustainable energy system through the coproduction of green hydrogen, biorefinery integration, and digital twinning, positioning waste oil pyrolysis as an integral component of future sustainable energy systems in the context of Industry 4.0 and the circular economy. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: SGRLCF: Supervision-guided reinforcement learning for rating prediction in collaborative filtering
Abstract: Collaborative Filtering (CF) is widely used for rating prediction in Recommender Systems (RSs). Traditional CF methods are highly sensitive to data sparsity, while recent Deep Learning (DL) based CF models enhance representation capacity by capturing complex nonlinear user–item interactions. However, most DL based CF methods rely on standard Supervised Learning (SL) and optimize prediction errors independently for each interaction. With sparse data, gradients estimated from limited observations may exhibit greater stochastic variability, leading to unstable optimization and suboptimal convergence in deep models. To address this issue, we propose a Supervision-Guided Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for rating prediction in CF, termed SGRLCF. Rather than minimizing only per-interaction regression errors, SGRLCF constructs reinforcement rewards from ground-truth labels to guide sequential optimization. Specifically, we design a dual-level reward scheme that jointly considers immediate prediction error and overall training improvement. Then, we introduce a validation-guided fusion strategy that incorporates a collaborative prior derived from the training data into the actor output, with the fusion weight selected on a held-out validation subset. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets show that SGRLCF achieves competitive or superior Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) in both single-domain and cross-domain scenarios. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Knowledge graph–based data governance for small and medium-sized enterprises: A systematic literature review and socio-technical framework
Abstract: Established data governance frameworks provide valuable guidance for large enterprises, yet their assumptions about stable funding, dedicated governance teams, and mature infrastructure often do not reflect the realities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Recent research has explored the use of semantic technologies and knowledge graphs to automate governance tasks, improve traceability, and support policy enforcement. Yet, whether these approaches effectively address SME-specific needs remains unclear. This paper presents a systematic literature review of knowledge-graph-based data governance approaches, focusing on their relevance to SMEs. Following the PRISMA method, we analyzed evidence from 43 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 through multiple lenses, including core data governance activities (Define, Implement, Monitor), components of the Data Governance Institute framework, and stages of the data lifecycle. Using thematic network analysis we synthesize recurring limitations and structural patterns across the literature. Our findings show that while semantic technologies demonstrate strong potential for automating policy enforcement, metadata integration, and interoperability, most approaches are designed for mature enterprises. They commonly assume formal governance hierarchies, specialized expertise, and sustained operational capacity, conditions that are often absent in SMEs. As a result, governance designs are skewed toward technical controls and early lifecycle stages, with limited attention to monitoring, organizational roles, decision rights, and end-to-end governance. Building on these findings, this study advances a socio-technical perspective on data governance in SME contexts by reframing governance as a lifecycle-embedded and practice-oriented capability rather than a purely technical implementation. It further conceptualizes knowledge graphs as boundary objects that mediate between governance intent, technical enforcement, and organizational practice. Our key contributions include a structured synthesis of knowledge-graph-based data governance research, identifies eight recurring gaps that hinder SME applicability, and derives nine design principles alongside a conceptual research framework to guide future research and the development of SME-suitable governance solutions. © 2026

Title: Fuel vs. food? Climate shocks, biofuel expansion, and the future of global food security
Abstract: The expansion of biofuel production has generated debate over its potential trade-off with food security, particularly regarding land diversion, rising food prices, and climate-related agricultural stress. This study utilizes panel data from 5 emerging (BRICS) and 7 advanced economies (G7) employing Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QR) and Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) for robustness to examine the association between biofuel production and agricultural total-factor productivity, crop value, and global food security during the period 2012-2022. Grounded in bioeconomy transition theory, induced innovation theory, the Porter hypothesis, and sustainable intensification, the empirical evidence indicates that biofuel expansion does not create a homogeneous food–fuel trade-off; instead, its associations vary across development and performance regimes. Biofuel production is positively associated with crop value in both groups but shows contrasting productivity associations, particularly across quantiles. Temperature anomalies exhibit heterogeneous associations with agricultural outcomes, while food prices are more strongly associated with food security. In line with induced innovation theory, innovation capacity is positively associated with several agricultural outcomes, while the climate–innovation interaction indicates heterogeneous adaptive associations across country groups. The differing associations of environmental policy stringency are broadly consistent with the conditional predictions of the Porter hypothesis, rather than indicating uniform regulatory benefits. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between biofuel expansion and food-system performance is conditional on development stage, climate exposure, innovation capacity, environmental policy stringency, and food-price conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Node-to-cluster contrastive learning with modularity maximization for graph clustering
Abstract: Attributed graph clustering has advanced significantly through self-supervised graph contrastive learning. However, existing methods often face two key limitations: (1) direct reliance on raw topology and features makes models susceptible to noise and representation collapse; (2) the lack of multi-granularity modeling prevents the effective integration of local node consistency, meso-scale cluster semantics, and macro-level community structures. To address these challenges, we propose Node-to-Cluster Contrastive Learning with Modularity Maximization (NC-MGC). Specifically, our model first executes a graph optimization strategy that reconstructs an attribute-augmented adjacency matrix via KNN refinement and employs a graph Laplacian filter to suppress high-frequency noise. Then, our approach builds upon contrastive learning by introducing a hierarchical structure that simultaneously optimizes node-level and cluster-level representations. While node-level alignment maintains local consistency, the cluster-level contrastive module provides meso-scale semantic guidance by attracting matched cluster prototypes and repelling dissimilar ones, thereby enhancing inter-class discriminability. Finally, a global modularity maximization objective is integrated to capture macro-level community interactions, ensuring the structural cohesiveness of the learned partitions. Extensive empirical evaluations on six benchmark datasets demonstrate that NC-MGC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Assessment of multi-stage telescopic control rods in a pebble bed reactor, Part I: Mechanical design, neutronic assessment, and economic analysis
Abstract: The low power density of Pebble-Bed Reactors (PBRs) results in larger Reactor Pressure Vessels (RPVs) and reactor buildings in comparison to other Generation IV concepts. Multi-stage Telescopic Control Rods (TCRs) have been proposed to reduce both the size and complexity of both the RPV and reactor building to reduce construction costs. This work seeks to explore the neutronic feasibility and economic impact of a three-stage TCR design in the 200 (Formula presented) Generic Pebble Bed Reactor (GPBR-200). Modeling of the reactor from startup to the equilibrium core was conducted using Serpent 2 and kugelpy. A wide range of TCR geometries using fresh boron carbide were found to bring the core to a subcritical state following a steam ingress scenario, assuming a uniform distribution of steam throughout the core and no prompt change in core temperatures. Loss of Boron-10 in the control rods was found to be insignificant up to 20 years but became neutronically significant by the reactor’s 30-year maintenance period. However, the depleted control rods were still capable of bringing the core to a subcritical state following a steam ingress scenario. A top-down economic analysis based on cost estimates from the Modular High Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor (MHTGR) program was then used to assess the economic impact of TCRs when introduced at various stages of reactor design completion. Subject to underlying assumptions, incorporation of TCRs resulted in an estimated 1.7%–4.3% savings, with earlier adoption of TCRs in the design phase resulting in greater savings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A vacation queueing model for the performance of blockchain systems by different transaction behaviors
Abstract: Performance bottlenecks have become a critical constraint hindering the further development of blockchain. Applying queueing theory to model blockchain systems provides an effective approach for performance analysis. As transactions serve as the core entities in blockchain systems, investigating the impact of transaction behaviors on system performance is of great necessity and significance. Firstly, considering the phenomena that transactions may suspend upon arrival or renege during waiting in the system, this study clarifies the transaction confirmation mechanism and constructs a multi-server vacation queueing model. A two-dimensional Markov process is established based on the states of transactions and miners. The steady-state solution is obtained via the successive over-relaxation method, and the key performance metric—transaction latency—is derived. Secondly, the influences of transaction suspension rate and reneging rate on latency are analyzed. Results show that higher suspension and reneging rates contribute to better system performance. Finally, simulation experiments and correlation analysis verify the model reliability, indicating an almost perfect consistency between theoretical and experimental results. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Coupling degree with self-supervised learning for multimodal recommendation
Abstract: Multimodal recommendation systems, leveraging multimodal data, demonstrate great potential in modeling user preferences and improving recommendation accuracy. However, due to the issues such as sparse interaction data, their performance typically deteriorates significantly, limiting their applicability. Existing works address this issue by using modality feature enhancement or self-supervised learning signal generation. The fusion features, which are derived from similar nodes with the original features, is suboptimal when enhancing user embedding features. To address these issues, we propose the Coupling Degree with Self-supervised Learning for Multimodal Recommendation (CDSSL). Title: Stakeholder acceptance and feasibility of REM, a multi-device medication reminder system for adults with hypertension
Abstract: Introduction: Medication non-adherence remains a major challenge in hypertension management among middle-aged and older adults. Reminder systems can support timely medication use, but many existing tools lack usability and healthcare workflow integration. REM, derived from the word ‘reminder’, was developed as an integrated medication adherence support system connecting patients, physicians, and pharmacists through a mobile application, smart pillbox, and wearable device. This study explored stakeholders’ perceived usefulness, ease of use, behavioral intention to use REM, and recommendations for improvement. Methods: This qualitative formative study used semi-structured interviews with hypertensive middle-aged and older adult patients (n = 20), physicians (n = 10), pharmacists (n = 10), and information technology (IT) experts (n = 10). The interview guide was informed by the Technology Acceptance Model and examined perceptions of system usefulness, ease of use, intention to use, feasibility, and recommended refinements. Data were coded and organized using MAXQDA. Results: Participants perceived the REM system as useful and easy to use for supporting medication adherence and patient monitoring. Most participants were willing to use or recommend REM, although acceptance depended on physician endorsement, affordability, insurance coverage, and workflow compatibility. Suggested refinements included secure communication, improved portability, offline functionality, and enhanced data security. Conclusion: REM was perceived as a useful and easy-to-use digital health intervention with potential to support medication adherence among middle-aged and older adults with hypertension. Findings highlight the importance of user-centered design, stakeholder integration, affordability, workflow compatibility, and robust data security in promoting future adoption and implementation. Public interest summary: Middle-aged to older adults with high blood pressure often forget to take their medication on time. To address this, the REM system was developed to improve their medication compliance. REM was derived from the word "reminder". The system consists of a mobile application, a smart pillbox, and a wearable device that work together to help patients remember their medication. Physicians and pharmacists can also access patients’ prescriptions and medication intake schedules to monitor their progress and compliance. In this study, patients, physicians, and pharmacists, including IT experts, were interviewed to express their thoughts about REM. Most participants were also willing to use and recommend REM for its usefulness. Suggested improvements included chat support, offline accessibility, portability, and stronger privacy and security features. In conclusion, the REM system shows potential as a user-friendly tool for improving medication adherence and supporting better health outcomes. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

Title: Research on interruption risk propagation in aircraft supply chain network: A multi-layer network coupling model
Abstract: The aircraft supply chain (ASC) is a core component of national high-end equipment manufacturing systems, which have complex network characteristics of strong coupling. Once an interruption occurs at any node, it will propagate to relevant enterprises along the supply-demand relationship. However, the propagation process of interruption risks is not merely a matter of physical transmission, it is typically accompanied by the spread of risk information and the adoption of preventive measures. Therefore, investigating the dynamic coupling characteristics among risk information diffusion, adoption of preventive measures, and interruption risk propagation is of great significance for exploring the interruption risk propagation mechanisms in ASC. Considering the above facts, this paper proposes a three-layer coupled network model. This model divides enterprises into multiple different states and innovatively proposes different network layer propagation mechanisms and interlayer coupling methods. Subsequently, the microscopic Markov chain approach is employed to establish state transition Eqs., and the mathematical characteristics of interruption risk outbreak are derived through theoretical deduction. The proposed model is applied to the risk propagation analysis of real ASC networks, and the proposed method and key findings were visually demonstrated. The research results provide decision-making references for risk management in the aviation industry chain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Proactive vs reactive destination revitalisation

Title: Towards exact temporal aggregation of time-coupled energy storage models via active constraint set identification and machine learning
Abstract: Time series aggregation (TSA) aims to construct temporally aggregated optimization models that accurately represent the output space of their full-scale counterparts while using a significantly reduced temporal dimensionality. Authors: Jeong J.; Lee H.; Kim S.; Yoon H.
Title: SafeBound: Safety-aware lower-bound learning for Remaining Useful Life prediction
Abstract: Deep learning-based prognostics for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction have achieved significant accuracy but often lack the reliability required for safety-critical systems. While recent risk-aware approaches employ asymmetric loss functions, they fundamentally treat safety as a soft penalty rather than a constraint-aware optimization, often failing to rule out hazardous overestimation at the instance level. To address this, we propose SafeBound ( Safe ty-Aware Bound ary Learner ), which reformulates RUL prediction from cost minimization to constraint-aware optimization. SafeBound decouples the prediction task into a conservative lower bound estimate and an accuracy-refining slack variable. By incorporating monotonic degradation as a domain-informed safety prior and a boundary-aware stabilization scheme, our method balances boundary tightness with feasibility, mitigating optimization instability. Extensive experiments on C-MAPSS, N-CMAPSS, and NASA Battery datasets demonstrate that SafeBound achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while maintaining low safety bound violation rates — as low as 2.4% on turbofan engines and below 1% on battery degradation — effectively addressing the trade-off between predictive accuracy and operational safety. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Asynchronous formation-containment flocking of multi-agent systems
Abstract: This paper develops an asynchronous distributed protocol for formation-containment flocking of discrete-time multi-agent systems, addressing moving leaders, cooperative-competitive interactions modeled by signed digraphs, and nonuniform private update schedules within a single design. Using only local neighbor information, each follower is driven to a prescribed barycentric position inside the translating convex hull of the leaders while aligning its velocity with the common leader velocity. Convergence is analyzed through the theory of infinite products of sub-stochastic matrices, which yields explicit conditions linking the network topology (positive-path reachability), the control gains, the signed interaction weights, and the inter-update bound, and guarantees geometric convergence. Title: Trends in access to basic sanitation services across Brazilian municipalities under a new legal framework
Abstract: Federal Law No. 14,026/2020 updated Brazil's sanitation legal framework, reinforcing universalization targets for water supply and sewage services. Title: Integration of meshed offshore HVDC grids in electricity markets under security constraints
Abstract: This paper compares the impact on operating costs and various economic indicators of integrating a meshed offshore HVDC grid into electricity markets under different security approaches. Authors: Jin Y.; Xu J.; Xiao T.; Lauwereyns J.
Title: Choice and goal framing effects in food evaluation: The roles of positive–negative asymmetry and decision sequence
Abstract: Food choices in everyday life are typically made as a sequence of repeated decisions rather than as isolated choices. We previously developed a sequential preference-based task and demonstrated consistent effects of choice framing on food choice behavior. Building upon that, the present study investigated two forms of framing: choice framing, by comparing Binary and Defer tasks, and goal framing, by contrasting Positive- and Negative-selection instructions. Participants completed a virtual food-shopping task in which food images were presented sequentially and each item was either accepted (“Take”), rejected (“Leave”), or, in some tasks, temporarily postponed (“Wait”). To characterize stage-specific and temporal dynamics of food choice, both aggregate and sequential analyses were conducted. Aggregate analyses replicated previous findings that “Take” decisions required longer processing times in both image viewing and evaluation stages than “Leave” decisions, whereas the “Wait” decision elicited the longest processing times, reflecting greater decision uncertainty. Furthermore, Negative-selection tasks elicited a reversed trend in different decision stages and higher between-participant variability for “Wait” decisions compared to Positive-selection tasks, despite identical task structures, supporting theories of positive–negative asymmetry. Sequential analyses further showed that response dynamics systematically evolved across Choice Sequences in Positive-selection tasks, whereas such temporal modulation was largely absent under Negative-selection, suggesting sustained cognitive demand throughout the task. These findings demonstrate that food choice is a dynamic, multi-stage process and illustrate how integrating stage-specific and sequential analyses can reveal cognitive mechanisms that remain hidden in conventional aggregate analyses. The present study highlights the value of integrating stage-specific and sequential analyses to advance understanding of consumer food decision-making. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Moderator analysis for single-case experimental design meta-analysis
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Moderator analysis in single-experimental design (SCED) meta-analysis allows for fine-grained analysis allowing explanation of variability in intervention effectiveness between studies in addition to between participants. This is desirable for the field of cognitive therapy as individual SCED study participant characteristics might explain participant's responsiveness to interventions. This stands in contrast to traditional group design meta-analysis in which moderator analysis is limited to exploring study level characteristics. If traditional meta-analytic techniques were to be used, as in group design studies (i.e., using study average moderators), then the unique benefits of synthesizing SCED studies are missed. In this manuscript, three-level meta-analysis for synthesis of SCED effect sizes with inclusion of moderators is introduced and an empirical demonstration using SCED studies focusing on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is provided. The goal is to provide applied SCED meta-analysis with appropriate methodology to conduct moderator analysis which can result in more fine-grained evidence. This approach can support a more comprehensive understanding of the conditions under which, and the participants for whom, interventions may be recommended. © 2026

Title: Monophily-aware graph pre-training for heterophilic graphs
Abstract: Graph pre-training algorithms aim to learn generic node embeddings without relying on labeled data. These models are typically designed based on the homophily assumption, which posits that connected nodes present similar features and same labels. However, this design limits their expressiveness and generalization ability on heterophilic graphs that exhibit dissimilar features and different labels between connected nodes and are prevalent in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we propose MAGNET, a novel Monophily-Aware Graph pre-traiNing for hETerophilic graphs, which unifies feature dimensionality across graphs and exploits latent similarity structures within graphs, enabling effective representation learning and robust cross-dataset generalization under heterophily. Specifically, we introduce a feature alignment mechanism that projects node features from different graphs into a consistent representation space with unified dimensionality, facilitating cross-dataset generalization. Based on the aligned features, we design a monophily-based message-passing mechanism that identifies and aggregates structurally similar two-hop neighbors to extract informative latent similarity information. This mechanism is further integrated into a dual-encoder architecture to capture complementary structural patterns and learn high-quality node representations on heterophilic graphs. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MAGNET significantly outperforms baselines on heterophilic graphs, achieving improvements of 6.75% on Crocodile and 4.49% on Cornell, while maintaining competitive performance on homophilic graphs. Title: Influence of temperature on the bio-oil production from biomass pyrolysis in a solar hybrid drop-tube/fixed-bed reactor
Abstract: Aviation remains a critical climate challenge in Europe, with emissions stubbornly high due to fossil fuel dependence, rising demand, and the slow adoption of low-carbon alternatives. The aim was to evaluate and optimize bio-oil yields, analyze products distribution (bio-oil, char, and gases) and elemental composition, and identify potential improvements to the solar reactor. The results showed that the bio-oil yield peaked at 500 °C, reaching 56 wt% when accounting for the “mass lost” required to close the mass balance, assuming that the missing mass consisted exclusively of liquid products. When considering only the measured mass, the bio-oil yield peaked at 600 °C, at 50 wt%. It declined at higher temperatures due to secondary cracking, while gas yield increased (12.5 - 20.4 wt%) and char yield remained stable (∼32 wt%) before slightly dropping at 700 °C. Compared to a Bubbling Fluidized Bed (BFB) reactor, the DTR produced less bio-oil (43 wt% for DTR vs. 62 wt% for BFB) and less gas (12 wt% for DTR vs. 17 wt% for BFB), but more char (32 wt% for DTR vs. 15 wt% for BFB), highlighting trade-offs tied to heat transfer and residence time. The study concludes that moderate temperatures (500 - 600 °C) favor bio-oil and char, while higher temperatures promote gasification, demonstrating the potential of solar-driven pyrolysis for scalable, carbon-neutral SAF production and circular biomass valorization. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Diagnosing ecosystem service mismatches through service flows and explainable AI: evidence from the Weihe River Basin, China
Abstract: Ecosystem service flows (ESFs) connect ecological supply with human demand, yet the links among service transmission, supply-demand imbalance, and nonlinear response thresholds remain difficult to diagnose in rapidly urbanizing regions. To provide a transferable diagnostic approach, we developed an explainable AI-assisted supply-demand-flow framework. We tested it in the Weihe River Basin, a representative ecological-economic transition zone of Northwest China, from 2000 to 2020. We quantified the supply, demand, and ecosystem service supply-demand ratios (ESDRs) for water yield, soil conservation, carbon sequestration, and food provision; simulated service-specific flows; and used XGBoost-SHAP-PDP to identify dominant drivers and threshold intervals. Ecological sources in the Qinling, Longshan and loess hilly regions remained separated from demand centers on the Guanzhong urban plain. Water yield supply increased from 9.41 to 11.99 billion m3, and soil conservation supply from 4.36 to 5.93 billion t, while their respective demands declined by 21.5% and 24.1%. Water and soil conservation flows were concentrated along terrain-controlled river corridors, carbon sequestration showed strong outward spillover and weak internal inflow, and food flows shifted toward a multi-center network linking eastern Gansu and the Guanzhong Plain. SHAP identified population density as the leading driver of water and food ESDRs and forestland proportion as the dominant driver of soil and carbon ESDRs. By coupling service-flow mechanisms with interpretable machine learning, the framework offers a reusable basis for environmental impact assessment, ecological compensation, corridor protection, demand-side regulation, and threshold-based territorial planning in comparable urbanizing regions. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Secondhand fashion subscription boxes: A necessary condition analysis of purchase intention determinants

Title: Mapping potential recurring risk of wildfire across Canada using artificial intelligence: Implications for human populations and tree species
Abstract: In response to the escalating global concern over increasing wildfire events and their extensive socioecological consequences, it is crucial to develop efficient and practical methods for reliably identifying high-risk wildfire zones to guide large-scale environmental management. In the present study, numerous deep learning architectures—including bidirectional recurrent neural network, encoder-decoder bidirectional recurrent neural network, deep neural network, recurrent neural network and long short-term memory—are applied to map wildfire susceptibility across Canada, with performance benchmarked against a comparatively low-complexity categorical boosting. Initially, a spatial database comprising 4,240 historically large wildfire occurrence locations across Canada from 2014 to 2023 was compiled. Next, we calculated the statistical Frequency and Likelihood of occurrence at 10,000 well-distributed points across Canada. Characteristics of 13 candidate wildfire-related hydrogeoclimatic parameters were extracted at the same points; feature selection retained 11 for Frequency and 10 for Likelihood as model inputs. Subsequently, potential recurring hazard and risk indices across Canada were calculated. To identify the effective predictor variables and optimal combinations, Boruta and classification and regression tree algorithms were used. Finally, the performance of models was evaluated using the error metrics including root mean squared error, mean absolute error and coefficient of determination. Results revealed that the bidirectional recurrent neural network gave the best value on five of the six test-set metrics across Frequency and Likelihood, while categorical boosting was weakest on five of six. According to the SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis, wind speed, climatic water deficit, shortwave radiation and potential evapotranspiration were the most influential predictors of large wildfire occurrence; higher climatic water deficit, shortwave radiation and potential evapotranspiration raised model predictions, whereas higher wind speed lowered them, consistent with its negative correlation with both targets. In terms of exposure to human populations, the metropolitan regions of Yellowknife, southwestern British Columbia, Winnipeg and Calgary were identified as facing the highest recurring risk of future wildfire impact. Regarding tree species, black spruce and jack pine were the tree species most frequently occurring in Canada’s high wildfire-risk regions. Title: From maritime near misses to recovery mechanisms: A Safety-II event-chain graph approach
Abstract: Maritime near misses are not only precursors of accidents, but also empirical traces of how hazardous situations are detected, coordinated, and controlled before escalation. However, existing near-miss studies have largely focused on risk identification and accident prediction, leaving limited quantitative evidence on the Safety-II-informed recovery patterns embedded in near-miss narratives. A Safety-II-informed event-chain graph framework is proposed to learn recovery-oriented patterns from maritime near-miss reports. A concept-level event-chain graph is constructed to represent links among antecedent contexts, hazardous situations, protective interventions, process mechanisms, and resilience outcomes. To capture response structures beyond ordinary pairwise relations, a stage-informed hypergraph is developed to preserve higher-order co-activation among protective functions. Time-to-clearance and restricted mean risk exposure time are examined as exploratory indicators of reported risk-exposure duration, while unadjusted (Raw), inverse probability weighting (IPW), and augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW) are compared to assess adjusted observational associations under comparable hazardous contexts. Cross-actor coordination showed the most stable adjusted association with risk removal/mitigation, whereas associations with high-quality recovery were more sensitive to narrative completeness. The proposed framework provides an interpretable approach for Safety-II learning from near-miss reports and supports maritime traffic governance, emergency response planning, and proactive safety management. Title: Software-defined vehicle ecosystems in transformation
Abstract: Context: The automotive industry is transitioning from hardware-centric development toward software-defined vehicles (SDVs), where software drives functionality, value creation, and competitive differentiation. This shift challenges proprietary software development, firm-centric innovation, and traditional supply chain models, giving rise to ecosystem-based collaboration. However, SDV transformation is primarily framed as a technical change, leaving its broader ecosystem implications insufficiently understood. Objective: This study explores the transformation of SDV ecosystems, their stakeholders, collaborative structures, roles and authority, and highlights associated challenges and opportunities. Methods: This systematic literature review collected 351 studies from six databases and selected 25 for detailed analysis. Results: Four interrelated shifts (from hardware-centric to software platforms, from supply chains to collaborative ecosystems, from proprietary to open and standard solutions, and from firm-level control to distributed governance) characterise the transformation, with six levels of collaboration involving twelve stakeholder groups. These collaborations are influenced by five dimensions of authority. The literature also highlights six core software development challenges and various organisational, industry and market, and regulatory, legal, and ethical challenges. It identifies five software development opportunities and various organisational, industry and market, and public value and ethical opportunities. Conclusion: The first contribution integrates previously fragmented literature on the SDV ecosystem transformation, demonstrating how SDVs are transforming the automotive industry through the four interrelated shifts driven by software advancements. Second, it proposes an SDV ecosystems model that integrates SDV architecture, stakeholder groups, collaboration structures, and governance levels to facilitate sustainable SDV ecosystems. Additionally, agendas for research and practice are outlined. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The effect of rosé wine color: A conceptual replication and a generation-based extension
Abstract: Recent research on crossmodal correspondences from Jaud et al. (2025) highlighted the role of rosé wine color in shaping consumer responses. Building on their work, this study aims to assess the robustness and generalizability of these findings while extending the original model in two ways. Specifically, by using a within-subjects experimental design conducted in the United States (N = 448), we replicate the model in a different cultural context by shifting from a French to a US sample. Further, we extend the underlying process by introducing perceived lightness as an additional mediating mechanism. Finally, we broaden the model by incorporating generational belonging (Generation Z vs. Generation Y) as a moderating variable. This approach enables us to assess both the robustness and the boundary conditions of previously identified effects of rosé wine color. Our findings contribute to the literature on crossmodal correspondences by demonstrating the stability of color-driven effects while highlighting generational differences in the relationship between perceived fruitiness and willingness to buy. They also offer practical insights for wine producers and distributors seeking to better align product presentation with the expectations of different generation-based consumer segments. © 2026

Title: Association of Dissociative Symptoms With Non-Suicidal Self-Injury and Repeated Suicide Attempts in Adolescents
Abstract: Background: Self-harm and suicidal behaviors are major mental health concerns among adolescents. Dissociative symptoms have recently been recognized as clinically relevant factors linking emotional dysregulation to self-injurious behaviors. However, empirical evidence supporting this association remains limited in Korean adolescent clinical populations. This study examined whether dissociative symptom severity was associated with frequent nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI) and suicide attempts among adolescents attending a psychiatric outpatient clinic. Methods: This retrospective chart review included 63 adolescents younger than 19 years who visited the Department of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry at Hallym University Sacred Heart Hospital between March 2020 and March 2023 and completed the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), and Korean Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fourth Edition. Dissociative symptoms were indexed using a summed score of six dissociation-related CBCL items and categorized as low (≤ 5 points) or high (≥ 6 points). NSSI frequency was classified as 0-5 versus ≥ 6 episodes, and suicide attempts as 0-1 versus ≥ 2 episodes. Sex, age, IQ, and depressive symptoms measured by the CES-D were included as covariates. Group differences were analyzed using independent samples t-tests and associations with high-frequency NSSI and repeated suicide attempts were examined using logistic regression. Results: Among the 63 participants, 26 were male (41.3%) and 37 were female (58.7%); the mean age was 15.4 years and the mean IQ was 88.0. Adolescents with high-frequency NSSI (≥ 6 episodes) had significantly higher CES-D and dissociation scores than those with 0-5 NSSI episodes (P = 0.008 and P = 0.003, respectively). In logistic regression, adolescents in the high-dissociation group had higher odds of high-frequency NSSI than those in the low-dissociation group (odds ratio [OR], 5.02; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34-18.81; P = 0.017). Similarly, adolescents with repeated suicide attempts (≥ 2 episodes) had higher CES-D and dissociation scores than those with 0-1 attempts (P = 0.006 and P = 0.039, respectively), and high dissociation was associated with higher odds of repeated suicidal attempts (OR, 5.33; 95% CI, 1.54-18.47; P = 0.008). Age, IQ, and sex were not significantly associated with either outcome. Conclusion: Dissociative symptoms were independently associated with both high-frequency NSSI and repeated suicide attempts among Korean adolescents receiving psychiatric outpatient care. Adolescents with elevated dissociation showed approximately five-fold higher odds of high-frequency NSSI and repeated suicide attempts, even after adjustment for depressive symptoms and demographic factors. These findings suggest that dissociation may be a clinically meaningful marker of elevated self-harm and suicide-related risk, supporting the routine assessment of dissociative experiences in adolescent mental health evaluations. © (2027), (Korean Academy of Medical Science). Title: Feasibility of an internet-based cognitive behavioral treatment for university students with depression and/or anxiety: A mixed-methods single arm repeated measures study
Source title: Journal of Behavioral and Cognitive Therapy
Abstract: Mental health problems are prevalent among university students, with anxiety and depression being the most common conditions. Despite available campus services, barriers to access persist, creating a substantial treatment gap. Internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) offers a scalable alternative, although evidence in university settings remains limited.This study assessed the feasibility and preliminary effects of VIVIM, an adapted iCBT program delivered through interactive eBooks for Spanish- and Catalan-speaking university students with anxiety and/or depression. It also evaluated the feasibility of conducting a future randomized controlled trial (RCT).Feasibility was evaluated through recruitment, retention, adherence, engagement, and acceptability. Thirty-three students from Rovira i Virgili University accessed the intervention over eight weeks.Recruitment targets were achieved within the planned timeframe, whereas retention was limited, with 45.45% and 39.39% of participants completing post-treatment and follow-up assessments, respectively. Adherence was low: only 12.12% of participants accessed all six predefined core eBooks, and 6.1% remained engaged throughout the intervention period. Nevertheless, participants who completed post-treatment assessments reported moderate-to-high levels of engagement and satisfaction.Completers and intention-to-treat sensitivity analyses showed significant improvements in depression and anxiety, although the uncontrolled single-arm design does not permit attribution of these changes to the intervention. Exploratory analyses suggested a possible association between greater eBooks use and larger symptom improvements, although findings were based on small subgroups and partly LOCF −imputed data.The findings suggest that both the intervention and study procedures require further optimization before progression to a full-scale RCT, despite encouraging preliminary evidence of improved mental health outcomes. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Masson SAS on behalf of Association Française de Therapie Comportementale et Cognitive.

Title: The grass is not always greener: The effects of local labor market information on search and employment
Abstract: We examine how information about local labor market conditions shapes search and employment outcomes for Indian job seekers. Participants were randomly shown information about either job postings, job applicants, or both from a popular job portal for their preferred city and occupation. Treated respondents are more likely to be employed seven months later. This overall effect varies considerably by baseline employment status. Among the initially employed, treatments reduce search off the portal and increase employment, with suggestive evidence of higher persistence in baseline jobs. In contrast, among the initially unemployed, treatments increase search activity but do not raise employment. Employment gains are concentrated among job seekers with less optimistic beliefs about labor market conditions. Title: Regional heterogeneity in the relationship between temperature and household electricity consumption across rural South Africa
Abstract: In this study we examine the heterogeneous effects of temperature on household electricity consumption using combined hourly electricity consumption and temperature data across several rural areas in South Africa. We apply a panel data regression model controlling for temperature bin dummies to capture nonlinear temperature effects, as well as a set of fixed effects to capture the unobserved heterogeneity across households and over time. We find that the temperature–consumption relationship varies across geographical locations and is characterised predominantly by inverse J-shaped and inverse U-shaped patterns, which differs from the typical U-shaped curve in the literature. This study deepens the understanding of the complex and heterogeneous effect of temperature on household electricity consumption in a developing-country context, highlighting substantial variation across climatic and geographic regions within the same country. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Exploring Lean-Integrated Circular Economy in the Built Environment Setting: Implications for Project Governance and Compliance
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The current study establishes how lean tenets contribute to the circular economy (CE) with exploration of lean tools with circular economy core principles and framework development. While there seem to be synergies between the concepts of lean and CE, the construction management research fraternity has not fully tapped the huge research potential in this domain. To address this gap, a two-phased exploratory qualitative research design is proposed. The first phase involves mapping lean tools with 10 dimensions of CE in the context of the built environment sector through content analysis and expert validation (n=3). Continuous improvement and added value tools of lean attained maximum realization of CE dimensions. The second phase involves semistructured interviews of experts (n=9) on an understanding of the synergies between lean and CE through thematic analysis (TA). The current study identifies predominant lean tools that realize CE dimensions and develops a conceptual model of a lean-driven circular economy (LdCE) framework for construction projects. Also, the lean tenets and their allied tools enabled value optimization through effective mapping of non-value-added processes and minimizing wasteful aspects. These findings are intended to inform engineers, construction managers, and legal practitioners about actionable strategies for promoting sustainable, legally compliant project execution. This study proves to accelerate sustainable construction through a lean and CE integrated framework in developing nations. Title: Polycaprolactone diol-mediated interfacial energy modulation for enhancing processability and thermal conductivity of highly filled epoxy/alumina composites
Source title: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
Abstract: The application of highly filled ceramic–epoxy composites is often limited by the rapid increase in viscosity at high filler loadings. Here, polycaprolactone diol (PCLD) is shown to function as a combined viscosity and interfacial modifier in alumina-filled epoxy composite systems, enabling effective flow control under high solid loading. PCLD content (0–15 wt%) and molecular weight (Mn = 530 and 2000 g·mol−1) were varied to evaluate rheological behavior and thermal transport. At 30 vol% alumina, 15 wt% PCLD (Mn 530) reduced viscosity from 57.8 to 5.3 Pa·s at 10 s−1, nearly one order of magnitude compared with the composite without PCLD. Under the same condition, thermal conductivity increased by 36%, from 0.60 to 0.82 W·m−1·K−1. PCLD altered the surface free energy of the epoxy matrix and reduced the estimated epoxy–alumina interfacial energy, consistent with improved filler wetting and changes in filler organization. These results indicate that the combined effects of bulk viscosity reduction and interfacial-energy modification can improve processability and heat transport in highly filled epoxy composites. However, the accompanying decreases in glass-transition temperature and tensile strength represent important trade-offs for application at elevated temperatures or under higher mechanical requirements. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Influence of environmental stimuli on sustainable food choices: the moderating role of AI-source disclosure
Abstract: Reducing meat consumption is necessary for public health and environmental sustainability. However, while the benefits of positively-valenced nature have been explored, the comparative behavioral effects and mediational patterns of positively-valenced and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli remain unclear. Across three studies, we examined how positively- and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli influence food choices. Study 1 showed that both types of environmental stimuli reduced meat-heavy meal choices compared to the control. Study 2 tested serial mediation models within a dual-system framework, and the results showed that positively-valenced stimuli were associated with stronger nature connectedness and greater consideration of future consequences (CFC), whereas negatively-valenced stimuli were associated with higher guilt and greater CFC. Study 3 manipulated AI-source disclosure for the environmental stimuli. Although AI-source disclosure did not significantly interact with environmental stimuli condition in predicting meat-heavy choices, it significantly attenuated the link between negatively-valenced stimuli and guilt, but did not attenuate the association between positively-valenced stimuli and nature connectedness. Title: Quantifying energy–cost–carbon tradeoffs in China's onshore wind expansion: A life cycle-based turbine design optimization
Abstract: China's onshore wind expansion must reconcile electricity generation, life-cycle cost, and life-cycle carbon emissions across heterogeneous wind regimes. We develop a region-specific assessment and turbine-design optimization framework linking rotor diameter and hub height to annual energy production, life-cycle cost, and greenhouse gas emissions from component manufacturing to grid delivery. Spatial screening identifies 2.61 million km2 of eligible land, representing 27.2% of China's land area. Under a uniform-design assessment using the reference wind speed, maximum geometric capacity reaches 10.1 TW, with gross generation of 30 PWh/yr and 10.6 PWh/yr after an idealized infinite-array adjustment. Separate national optimizations select turbine configurations across wind-speed zones under generation, cost, and carbon constraints, assuming full development of eligible land and using gross generation. The minimum-unit-cost solution generates 38.2 PWh/yr at 0.25 CNY/kWh and a carbon intensity of 15.0 g CO₂-eq/kWh. Minimizing carbon intensity lowers it to 13.3 g CO₂-eq/kWh but raises unit cost to 0.75 CNY/kWh, with generation of 40.2 PWh/yr. Selected turbine dimensions and rated powers generally decrease beyond their respective peaks in low-to-intermediate wind-speed zones; the minimum‑carbon-intensity solution generally favors larger rotors and higher-rated turbines. Title: Attribution of causality following service failure on online retail platforms: The roles of governance structure and recurring failures

Abstract: Online retail platforms are increasingly mediating customer–vendor interactions, yet research offers limited insight into how platform governance shapes service failure attribution, especially after recurring failures. Study 1 analyzes customer reviews using computational text analysis and shows that customers recognize governance structures and attribute causality to the platform more often under centralized than diffused governance. Title: Equilibrium of inorganic carbon species during photocatalytic CO2 reduction in TiO2 slurries: effect on the product yields and on the process kinetics
Abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction is a promising route for renewable fuel production, yet its efficiency remains limited by complex interactions between reaction conditions and carbon speciation. In aqueous systems, CO2 is in equilibrium with bicarbonate and carbonate species, with their distribution governed by pH, while only molecular CO2 is directly involved in photoreduction. This study systematically investigates the influence of carbon speciation on photocatalytic performance in TiO2 suspensions under UV-C irradiation. The highest yields of CO, CH4, and H2 were obtained in CO2-saturated NaHCO3 solution, which stabilized at about pH 6.7 and exhibited higher DIC and increased availability of dissolved CO2. In contrast, He-saturated NaHCO3 solution exhibited higher pH, significantly lower fractions of molecular CO2, and reduced product yields despite comparable DIC. A comprehensive reactor-scale kinetic model explicitly coupling inorganic carbon equilibrium with heterogeneous photocatalytic kinetics, radiation transport, and gas–liquid mass transfer showed good agreement with experimental data. This work demonstrates that photocatalytic performance is governed by the equilibrium concentration of molecular CO2 rather than the total carbon content, revealing a trade-off between CO2 capture capacity and reactive availability of CO2. These findings provide new insight into the role of carbon speciation in aqueous photocatalytic systems and offer a quantitative reactor–scale framework for process optimization and photoreactor simulation and design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
